persons.description: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Moses' brother, first high priest of Israel
persons.short: Aaron was Moses' older brother and served as the first high priest of Israel.
persons.article: Aaron was the older brother of Moses and Miriam, from the tribe of Levi. God appointed Aaron to be Moses' spokesman when Moses was called to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. Aaron performed signs before Pharaoh, including turning his staff into a snake. He assisted Moses during the Exodus, including holding up Moses' arms during the battle against the Amalekites. God chose Aaron and his descendants to serve as priests for the Israelites. Aaron was consecrated as the first high priest and wore special priestly garments. He was responsible for offering sacrifices, burning incense, and performing other priestly duties in the tabernacle. Aaron also played a role in several significant events, such as the golden calf incident and the rebellion of Korah. Aaron married Elisheba, and they had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. Aaron died at the age of 123 on Mount Hor, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as high priest. Despite his flaws, Aaron was a key figure in Israel's history and played a crucial role in establishing the priesthood.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.4.14 referred to as Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), or Aaron (Ἀαρών); son of Amram and Jochebed; a brother of Moses and Miriam; husband of Elisheba; father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 대제사장. Exo.4.14에 처음 언급되며 '아론'이라 불림. 아므람과 요게벳의 아들. 모세와 미리암의 형제. 엘리세바의 남편. 나답, 아비후, 이다말과 엘르아살의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아론은 모세의 형이며 이스라엘 최초의 대제사장으로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 아론은 모세와 미리암의 형이며 레위 지파에 속했다. 하나님은 모세가 이스라엘을 애굽에서 이끌어내도록 부름 받았을 때 아론을 모세의 대변인으로 세우셨다. 아론은 지팡이를 뱀으로 변하게 하는 것을 포함해 바로 앞에서 표적을 행했다. 그는 아말렉과의 전투에서 모세의 팔을 붙들어주는 것을 포함해 출애굽 과정에서 모세를 도왔다. 하나님은 아론과 그 후손을 이스라엘의 제사장으로 섬기도록 택하셨다. 아론은 첫 대제사장으로 성별되어 특별한 제사장 예복을 입었다. 그는 성막에서 제사를 드리고 향을 피우며 다른 제사장 직무를 수행하는 책임을 맡았다. 아론은 금송아지 사건과 고라의 반역 같은 여러 중요한 사건에서도 역할을 했다. 아론은 엘리세바와 결혼하여 나답, 아비후, 엘르아살, 이다말 네 아들을 두었다. 나답과 아비후는 여호와 앞에 허가받지 않은 불을 드려 죽었다. 아론은 호르산에서 백이십삼 세에 죽었고, 그의 아들 엘르아살이 대제사장직을 이었다. 결점에도 불구하고 아론은 이스라엘 역사의 핵심 인물이었으며 제사장직 확립에 중대한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of King Ahasuerus' seven eunuchs
persons.short: Abagtha was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.
persons.article: Abagtha was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus, the Persian king who ruled during the time of Esther. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, along with the other six eunuchs: Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Zethar, and Carcas. These eunuchs were tasked with bringing Queen Vashti before the king when he wanted to display her beauty to his guests.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.10 only referred to as Abagtha (אֲבַגְתָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '아박다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아박다는 아하수에로 왕을 섬긴 일곱 내시 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Adoram, who was over forced labor
persons.short: Abda was the father of Adoram (or 'Adoniram'), who was in charge of forced labor during Solomon's reign.
persons.article: Abda is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 1Ki.4.6, as the father of Adoram (or 'Adoniram'). He was one of King Solomon's officials, responsible for overseeing the forced labor used in Solomon's building projects.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.6 only referred to as Abda (עַבְדָּא); father of Adoram.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '압다'라 불림. 아도람의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 압다는 솔로몬 시대에 부역을 관장한 아도람(아도니람)의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shelemiah, an official under King Jehoiakim
persons.short: Abdeel was the father of Shelemiah, an official sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah.
persons.article: Abdeel is mentioned in Jer.36.26 as the father of Shelemiah, an official during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah. When Jeremiah's scribe, Baruch, read the prophet's warnings in the temple, King Jehoiakim ordered Jerahmeel, Seraiah, and Shelemiah to arrest both Baruch and Jeremiah. However, the Lord hid them from the officials.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.26 only referred to as Abdeel (עַבְדְּאֵל); father of Shelemiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '압디엘'이라 불림. 셀레마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 압디엘은 여호야김 왕이 바룩과 예레미야를 체포하러 보낸 관리 셀레먀의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite, ancestor of Ethan the musician
persons.short: Abdi, a Levite, was an ancestor of Ethan, one of the musicians appointed by David to serve in the temple.
persons.article: Abdi is mentioned in 1Ch.6.44 as a Levite and an ancestor of Ethan, one of the musicians appointed by King David to serve in the temple. Ethan, along with Heman and Asaph, was a leading musician and singer during David's reign (1Ch.15.19). Abdi is listed in the genealogy of the Levites, specifically within the lineage of Merari, one of the three main Levitical clans.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.44 only referred to as Abdi (עַבְדִּי); a son of Malluch; father of Kishi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.44에 처음 언급되며 '압디'라 불림. 말룩의 아들. 기시의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 압디는 레위인으로, 다윗이 성전 봉사자로 세운 음악가 중 한 사람인 에단의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Abdi, a Levite, was the father of Kish and served during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Abdi is mentioned in 2Ch.29.12 as a Levite who served during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He was the father of Kish, another Levite who participated in the purification of the temple ordered by Hezekiah. As part of Hezekiah's reforms, the Levites were tasked with cleansing the temple and restoring proper worship practices. Abdi's mention in this context suggests that he and his family played a role in supporting Hezekiah's religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12 only referred to as Abdi (עַבְדִּי); father of Kish.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12에 처음 언급되며 '압디'라 불림. 기스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 압디는 레위인으로 기스의 아버지였으며 히스기야 왕 시대에 활동했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Abdi, one of the descendants of Elam, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's time.
persons.article: Abdi is listed in Ezr.10.26 as one of the descendants of Elam who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was contrary to God's law and threatened the purity and identity of the Israelite community. Ezra called the people to repentance and required those who had married foreign wives to separate from them. Abdi was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives in obedience to Ezra's command.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.26 only referred to as Abdi (עַבְדִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '압디'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 압디는 엘람 자손 중 하나로, 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내를 내보내기로 동의한 사람들 가운데 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite leader
persons.short: Abdiel, son of Guni, was a chief of a Gadite family during the time of Jotham, king of Judah.
persons.article: Abdiel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.15 as a leader of the tribe of Gad during the time of Jotham, king of Judah. He is described as the son of Guni and a chief of his father's house. The Gadites were one of the Israelite tribes that settled east of the Jordan River. The mention of Abdiel in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles suggests that he was a significant figure among the Gadites and that his family held a prominent position within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.15 only referred to as Abdiel (עַבְדִּיאֵל); a son of Guni; father of Ahi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.15에 처음 언급되며 '압디엘'이라 불림. 구니의 아들. 아히의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 압디엘은 구니의 아들로, 유다 왕 요담 시대에 갓 지파 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ishpan@1Ch.8.22, Eber@1Ch.8.22, Eliel@1Ch.8.22, Zichri@1Ch.8.23, Hanan@1Ch.8.23, Hananiah@1Ch.8.24, Elam@1Ch.8.24, Anthothijah@1Ch.8.24, Iphdeiah@1Ch.8.25, Penuel@1Ch.8.25
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Shashak
persons.short: Abdon was a son of Shashak and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Abdon is listed in 1Ch.8.23 as one of the sons of Shashak, a descendant of Benjamin. He is mentioned in the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, which is given in the early chapters of 1 Chronicles. The genealogy traces the lineage of King Saul, who was from the tribe of Benjamin. Abdon's mention in this context suggests that he was part of the extended family of Saul, although his exact relationship to the king is not specified.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.23 only referred to as Abdon (עַבְדּוֹן); son of Shashak; a brother of Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah and Penuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.23에 처음 언급되며 '압돈'이라 불림. 사삭의 아들. 이스반, 에벨, 엘리엘, 시그리, 하난, 하나냐, 엘람, 안도디야, 이브드야와 브누엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 압돈은 사삭의 아들이며 베냐민 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Baal@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Ahio@1Ch.8.31-, Zecher@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-
persons.brief: Son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel') from Gibeon
persons.short: Abdon, the son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel') and brother of Ner, was a member of the Israelite community in Gibeon.
persons.article: Abdon is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Ch.8.30 and 1Ch.9.36. He was the son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), who is described as the "father of Gibeon," suggesting that he was the founder or a prominent figure in the Israelite community in Gibeon. Abdon is listed as a brother of Ner, who was the grandfather of King Saul. This places Abdon within the extended family of Saul, although his exact relationship to the king is not specified.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.30 only referred to as Abdon (עַבְדּוֹן); son of Abiel and Maacah; a brother of Kish, Ner, Zur, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher and Mikloth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.30에 처음 언급되며 '압돈'이라 불림. 아비엘과 마아가의 아들. 기스, 넬, 술, 바알, 나답, 그돌, 아효, 세겔과 미글롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 압돈은 아비엘(또는 여이엘)의 아들이자 넬의 형제로, 기브온의 이스라엘 공동체 일원이었다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: A minor judge of Israel from Ephraim
persons.short: Abdon, the son of Hillel the Pirathonite, was a minor Judge of Israel who led for eight years.
persons.article: Abdon, the son of Hillel the Pirathonite, is mentioned in Jdg.12.13-15 as a minor judge of Israel. He was from the tribe of Ephraim and succeeded Elon as a judge. Abdon judged Israel for eight years. He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys, which was a sign of wealth and status in ancient Israel. Abdon died and was buried in Pirathon, located in the hill country of the Amalekites within the territory of Ephraim.
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.12.13 only referred to as Abdon (עַבְדּוֹן); a son of Hillel.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.12.13에 처음 언급되며 '압돈'이라 불림. 힐렐의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 압돈은 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들로, 이스라엘의 사사로 팔 년간 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Adam and Eve's second son, killed by Cain
persons.short: Abel, the second son of Adam and Eve, was a shepherd who was killed by his brother Cain.
persons.article: Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve, born after his brother Cain. He was a shepherd, while Cain was a farmer. Both brothers brought offerings to God, but God accepted Abel's offering and rejected Cain's. This led to Cain's jealousy and anger, and he killed Abel in a field. God confronted Cain about Abel's murder, and as a result, Cain was cursed to be a wanderer on the earth. The New Testament references Abel as an example of faith (Heb.11.4 and as a righteous man whose blood cried out for justice )(Mat.23.35; Luk.11.51). Abel's blood is also contrasted with the blood of Jesus, which speaks of better things (Heb.12.24). After Abel's death, Adam and Eve had another son named Seth.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.4.2 referred to as Abel (הֶ֫בֶל), or Abel (Ἄβελ); son of Adam and Eve; a brother of Cain and Seth.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '아벨'이라 불림. 아담과 하와의 아들. 가인과 셋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아벨은 아담과 하와의 둘째 아들로 목자였으며 그의 형 가인에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Hezekiah of Judah
persons.short: Abi, also known as Abijah, was the mother of King Hezekiah and the daughter of Zechariah.
persons.article: Abi, also called Abijah, was the mother of King Hezekiah of Judah. She is mentioned in 2Ki.18.2 and 2Ch.29.1 as the daughter of Zechariah. Hezekiah, who reigned from approximately 715-686 BC, was known for his religious reforms and his trust in God (2Ki.18.5-6). The fact that Abi is mentioned by name suggests that she may have had a positive influence on her son Hezekiah. However, no further details about her life or character are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.2 referred to as Abi (אֲבִי), or Abijah (אֲבִיָּה); a daughter of Zechariah; wife of Ahaz; mother of Hezekiah and Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.18.2에 처음 언급되며 '아비'라 불림. 스가랴의 딸. 아하스의 아내. 히스기야와 마아세야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비(아비야라고도 함)는 히스기야 왕의 어머니이며 스가랴의 딸이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Wife of Hezron, who gave birth after he died
persons.short: Abiah was the wife of Hezron who bore Ashhur after her husband's death.
persons.article: Abiah or Abijah is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.2.24 as the wife of Hezron. The text states that Hezron's wife Abijah boor Abiah bore Ashhur to him after his death. The Hebrew is difficult, so it is uncertain whether Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah or whether this refers to Caleb and his wife Ephrathah,. This suggests that Abiah was conceived before Hezron's death but was born posthumously. Abiah is listed within the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, but no other information is provided about her life or descendants.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.24 only referred to as Abiah (אֲבִיָּה); wife of Hezron; mother of Ashhur.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.2.24에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림. 헤스론의 아내. 아스훌의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 헤스론의 아내로, 남편이 죽은 후 아스훌을 낳았다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, an Arbathite
persons.short: Abi-albon, also known as Abiel, was one of David's mighty men, an Arbathite.
persons.article: Abi-albon, also called Abiel, is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty men in 2Sa.23.31 and 1Ch.11.32. He is described as an Arbathite, indicating that he was from Beth-arabah, a town in the wilderness of Judah. As one of David's mighty men, Abi-albon would have been a skilled warrior who demonstrated exceptional bravery and loyalty to King David. The mighty men were an elite group of soldiers who played a significant role in David's military campaigns and in establishing his kingdom.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.31 referred to as Abi-albon (אֲבִי־עַלְבוֹן), or Abiel (אֲבִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.31에 처음 언급되며 '아비알본'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비알본(아비엘이라고도 함)은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 아르바 사람이었다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
persons.short: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, was a high priest who served during the reigns of David and Solomon.
persons.article: Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech, a priest at Nob. When King Saul ordered the execution of the priests at Nob, Abiathar was the only one who escaped and fled to David (1Sa.22.20-23). He brought with him the ephod, a sacred priestly garment used for seeking God's will (1Sa.23.6,9). Abiathar remained loyal to David throughout his reign, serving as one of his chief priests (2Sa.8.17; 15.24-36; 19.11; 20.25). However, near the end of David's life, Abiathar supported Adonijah's attempt to become king instead of Solomon (1Ki.1.7,19,25). When Solomon became king, he removed Abiathar from the priesthood, fulfilling the prophecy against the house of Eli (1Ki.2.26-27,35). Abiathar is also mentioned in the New Testament by Jesus, who referred to an incident during Abiathar's time as high priest (Mrk.2.26).
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.22.20 referred to as Abiathar (אֶבְיָתָר), or Abiathar (Ἀβιαθάρ); a son of Ahimelech; father of Ahimelech, Jonathan.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 대제사장. 1Sa.22.20에 처음 언급되며 '아비아달'이라 불림. 아히멜렉의 아들. 아히멜렉과 요나단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비아달은 아히멜렉의 아들로, 다윗과 솔로몬 시대에 대제사장으로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 아비아달은 놉의 제사장 아히멜렉의 아들이었다. 사울 왕이 놉의 제사장들을 처형하라고 명령했을 때 아비아달은 유일하게 도망쳐 다윗에게로 피신했다(삼상 22:20-23). 그는 하나님의 뜻을 구하는 데 사용되는 신성한 제사장 의복인 에봇을 가지고 왔다(삼상 23:6, 9). 아비아달은 다윗의 통치 내내 충성을 지키며 그의 수제사장 중 한 사람으로 섬겼다(삼하 8:17; 15:24-36; 19:11; 20:25). 그러나 다윗의 생애 말년에 아비아달은 솔로몬 대신 아도니야가 왕이 되려는 시도를 지지했다(왕상 1:7, 19, 25). 솔로몬이 왕이 되었을 때 그는 아비아달을 제사장직에서 제거하여 엘리 가문에 대한 예언을 성취했다(왕상 2:26-27, 35). 아비아달은 신약에서도 예수님에 의해 언급되는데, 그분은 아비아달이 대제사장이었을 때의 한 사건을 언급하셨다(막 2:26).

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Midian, grandson of Abraham
persons.short: Abida was a son of Midian and a grandson of Abraham through his concubine Keturah.
persons.article: Abida is mentioned in the genealogies of Abraham's descendants through his concubine Keturah. He was one of the sons of Midian, who was a son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen.25.4; 1Ch.1.33). The Midianites, named after Abida's father, are later mentioned in the Bible as a nomadic people living in the region near Canaan. However, no further information is provided about Abida himself or his specific role within the Midianite clan.
persons.summary: A man of the Midianites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.4 only referred to as Abida (אֲבִידָע); son of Midian; a brother of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch and Eldaah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '아비다'라 불림. 미디안의 아들. 에바, 에벨, 하녹과 엘다아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비다는 미디안의 아들이며, 아브라함이 첩 그두라를 통해 얻은 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus
persons.short: Abidan, son of Gideoni, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.
persons.article: Abidan, the son of Gideoni, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness after the Exodus from Egypt. He is mentioned several times in the book of Numbers. Abidan was one of the leaders who assisted Moses in taking a census of the Israelite population (Num.1.11). He also led the Benjamite tribe when the Israelites camped and marched in the wilderness (Num.2.22; 10.24). Additionally, Abidan presented the offering of the tribe of Benjamin during the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle (Num.7.60,65). Beyond these specific roles, no other details about Abidan's life or leadership are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.11 only referred to as Abidan (אֲבִידָן); a son of Gideoni.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.11에 처음 언급되며 '아비단'이라 불림. 기드오니의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아비단은 기드오니의 아들로, 이스라엘 백성이 광야를 지나는 동안 베냐민 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Abdon@1Ch.8.30-, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Baal@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Ahio@1Ch.8.31-, Zecher@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-, Gibeon@Jos.9.3-Ezk(f)
persons.brief: Father of Kish and grandfather of King Saul
persons.short: Abiel, also known as Jeiel, Ner, or Abigibeon (or '[re]-founder of Gibeon'), was the father of Kish and grandfather of King Saul.
persons.article: Abiel, also referred to as Jeiel, Ner, or Abigibeon (or '[re]-founder of Gibeon'), was a Benjaminite and the father of Kish, who was the father of King Saul, Israel's first king. In 1Sa.9.1, Abiel is mentioned as the father of Kish and is described as a mighty man of power. The genealogies in 1Chronicles 8 and 9 provide additional information about Abiel's family. In 1Ch.8.33 and 1Ch.9.39, he is called Ner, while in 1Ch.8.29 and 1Ch.9.35, he is referred to as Jeiel and Abigibeon or '[re]-founder of Gibeon'. These variations in names suggest that he may have been known by multiple names or that there might have been some discrepancies in the genealogical records. Abiel's son Kish became the father of Saul, who was anointed as the first king of Israel by the prophet Samuel.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.9.1 referred to as Abiel (אֲבִיאֵל), or Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל), or Ner (נֵר), or founder of Gibeon (אֲבִי גִבְעוֹן); a son of Zeror; husband of Maacah; father of Kish, Ner, Abdon, Zur, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher and Mikloth; founder of Gibeon.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.9.1에 처음 언급되며 '아비엘'이라 불림. 스롤의 아들. 마아가의 남편. 기스, 넬, 압돈, 술, 바알, 나답, 그돌, 아효, 세겔, 미글롯과 Gibeon의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비엘(여이엘, 넬, 또는 아비기브온이라고도 함)은 기스의 아버지이자 사울 왕의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hammolecheth, from the tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Abiezer, son of Hammolecheth, was a descendant of Manasseh and is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.
persons.article: Abiezer is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.7.18 as a son of Hammolecheth, who was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, which is given in the context of the census of the Israelites. No other information is provided about Abiezer's life, his role within the tribe, or any descendants he may have had. It is important to note that this Abiezer is a different individual from the Abiezer mentioned as one of David's mighty men.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.18 only referred to as Abiezer (אֲבִיעֶ֫זֶר); his mother was Hammolecheth; a brother of Ishhod and Mahlah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.18에 처음 언급되며 '아비에셀'이라 불림. 함몰레겟의 남편(이름 미상)와 함몰레겟의 아들. 이스홋과 말라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비에셀은 함몰레겟의 아들로 므낫세의 후손이며 그 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, from Anathoth
persons.short: Abiezer the Anathothite was one of David's mighty men and served as a commander in his army.
persons.article: Abiezer the Anathothite was one of David's mighty men, a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside King David. He was from Anathoth, a town in the territory of Benjamin (2Sa.23.27; 1Ch.11.28). Abiezer also served as one of the commanders of David's army, leading a division of 24,000 men during the ninth month of the year (1Ch.27.12). His inclusion in the lists of David's mighty men and his role as a commander indicate that he was a valiant and trusted soldier in David's service.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.27 only referred to as Abiezer (אֲבִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.27에 처음 언급되며 '아비에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아나돗 사람 아비에셀은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 그의 군대에서 지휘관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Clan of Manasseh, home of Gideon
persons.short: Abiezer, also known as Iezer, was a clan of the tribe of Manasseh and the home of Gideon, one of Israel's judges.
persons.article: Abiezer, also referred to as Iezer or the Abiezrites, was a clan within the tribe of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The clan was named after Abiezer, who was a son of Gilead and a grandson of Manasseh (Num.26.30; Jos.17.2). The Abiezrites settled in the region of Ophrah, which was located in the territory of Manasseh. Gideon, one of the judges of Israel, belonged to the clan of Abiezer (Jdg.6.11, 24). When Gideon was called by God to deliver Israel from the oppression of the Midianites, he gathered men from his clan and other tribes to form an army (Jdg.6.34). After Gideon's victory over the Midianites, he faced opposition from the men of Ephraim, who complained that they had not been called to join the battle earlier. Gideon tactfully responded, praising the Ephraimites and comparing their achievement to the grapes of Abiezer, implying that their contribution was greater than that of his own clan (Jdg.8.2). Gideon died and was buried in Ophrah of the Abiezrites (Jdg.8.32). The clan of Abiezer continued to play a role in the history of Israel, being mentioned in the genealogies of Manasseh (Num.26.30; Jos.17.2).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.30 referred to as Abiezer or Abiezrite (אֲבִיעֶ֫זֶר), or Iezer (אִיעֶזֶר), or Abiezrite (אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי), or Iezerite (אִיעֶזְרִי); son of Gilead; a brother of Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida and Hepher.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.30에 처음 언급되며 '아비에셀'이라 불림. 길르앗의 아들. 헬렉, 아스리엘, 세겜, 스미다와 헤벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비에셀(이에셀이라고도 함)은 므낫세 지파의 한 가문으로, 사사 기드온의 고향이었다.

persons.description: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Nabal, later married David
persons.short: Abigail, initially the wife of Nabal, became one of David's wives after Nabal's death and bore him a son named Chileab.
persons.article: Abigail was a wise and beautiful woman who was initially married to a wealthy but foolish man named Nabal. When David and his men were in the wilderness, Nabal refused to provide them with food and supplies. Abigail, learning of this, quickly gathered provisions and went to meet David, apologizing for her husband's behavior and urging David not to seek revenge. Impressed by her wisdom and courage, David accepted her appeal and spared Nabal's life. When Abigail told Nabal about this incident, he had a heart attack and died ten days later. After Nabal's death, David sent for Abigail and married her. Abigail became one of David's wives and bore him a son named Chileab, who is also known as Daniel (2Sa.3.3; 1Ch.3.1). She accompanied David during his time in Ziklag, where he sought refuge from King Saul (1Sa.27.3; 30.5). Abigail's story demonstrates her wisdom, diplomacy, and faith in God.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.25.3 only referred to as Abigail (אֲבִיגַ֫יִל, אֲבִיגַ֫ל); wife of David and Nabal; mother of Chileab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아내. 1Sa.25.3에 처음 언급되며 '아비가일'이라 불림. 다윗과 나발의 아내. 길르압의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비가일은 처음에 나발의 아내였으나 나발이 죽은 후 다윗의 아내가 되어 길르압이라는 아들을 낳았다.
persons.article_ko: 아비가일은 처음에 나발이라는 부유하지만 어리석은 사람과 결혼한 지혜롭고 아름다운 여인이었다. 다윗과 그의 부하들이 광야에 있을 때 나발은 그들에게 음식과 물자를 제공하기를 거부했다. 이를 알게 된 아비가일은 신속하게 물자를 모아 다윗을 만나러 가서 남편의 행동에 대해 사과하고 다윗에게 복수하지 말라고 촉구했다. 그녀의 지혜와 용기에 감명받은 다윗은 그녀의 호소를 받아들여 나발의 생명을 살려주었다. 아비가일이 나발에게 이 사건에 대해 말했을 때 그는 심장마비를 일으켜 열흘 후 죽었다. 나발이 죽은 후 다윗은 아비가일을 데려와 결혼했다. 아비가일은 다윗의 아내 중 한 사람이 되어 다니엘이라고도 불리는 길르압이라는 아들을 낳았다(삼하 3:3; 대상 3:1). 그녀는 다윗이 사울 왕을 피해 피신했던 시글락 시절 그와 동행했다(삼상 27:3; 30:5). 아비가일의 이야기는 그녀의 지혜, 외교술, 하나님에 대한 믿음을 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev(?), Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch(?), Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch(?), Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch(?), Nethanel@1Ch.2.14(?), Raddai@1Ch.2.14(?), Ozem@1Ch.2.15(?), Elihu@1Ch.27.18(?), Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch
persons.brief: Sister of David; mother of Amasa
persons.short: Abigail, David's sister, was the mother of Amasa, who became the commander of Absalom's army.
persons.article: Abigail was the daughter of Jesse and the sister of King David, as mentioned in 1Ch.2.16-17. She married a man named Jether, who was an Ishmaelite (2Sa.17.25). Abigail and Jether had a son named Amasa, who played a significant role during the rebellion of David's son Absalom. During Absalom's revolt against David, Absalom appointed Amasa as the commander of his army, replacing Joab, who had been David's military commander (2Sa.17.25). After Absalom's defeat and death, David offered Amasa the position of commander-in-chief to appease the supporters of Absalom. However, when David sent Amasa to gather the men of Judah, he took longer than expected. This delay prompted David to send Abishai and Joab to pursue the rebel Sheba. Joab, seeing Amasa as a threat to his position, killed him (2Sa.20.4-13). The biblical text does not provide further information about Abigail's life or her reaction to her son's death.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.17.25 referred to as Abigail (אֲבִיגַ֫יִל), or Abigal (אֲבִיגַ֫ל); daughter of Nahash and Nahash(?); a sister of David(?), Eliab(?), Abinadab(?), Shimeah(?), Nethanel(?), Raddai(?), Ozem(?), Zeruiah(?), and Elihu(?); wife of Jether; mother of Amasa.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 2Sa.17.25에 처음 언급되며 '아비가일'이라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 딸. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 삼마, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 엘리후와 스루야의 자매. 예델의 아내. 아마사의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비가일은 다윗의 누이로, 압살롬의 군대 지휘관이 된 아마사의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman of living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Abishur; mother of Ahban and Molid
persons.short: Abihail was the wife of Abishur and the mother of Ahban and Molid, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Abihail is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.2.29 as the wife of Abishur, who was a descendant of Judah. She is listed in the genealogy of Judah, which traces the lineage of David. Abihail and Abishur had two sons, Ahban and Molid.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.29 only referred to as Abihail (אֲבִיחַ֫יִל); wife of Abishur; mother of Ahban, Molid.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.2.29에 처음 언급되며 '아비하일'이라 불림. 아비술의 아내. 아반과 몰릿의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일은 아비술의 아내로 압반과 몰릿의 어머니였으며, 유다 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Michael@1Ch.5.13, Meshullam@1Ch.5.13, Sheba@1Ch.5.13, Jorai@1Ch.5.13, Jacan@1Ch.5.13, Zia@1Ch.5.13, Eber@1Ch.5.13
persons.brief: A Gadite leader from Gilead
persons.short: Abihail, a descendant of Guni, was a leader of the tribe of Gad who lived in Gilead.
persons.article: Abihail is mentioned in 1Ch.5.14 as a leader of the tribe of Gad. He is described as the son of Huri and a descendant of Guni. The Gadites lived in the region of Gilead, east of the Jordan River. As a tribal leader, Abihail would have had a prominent role in the affairs of the Gadites, but no specific details about his leadership or accomplishments are provided in the text. His mention in the genealogy highlights the importance of family lineage and leadership within the tribe of Gad.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.14 only referred to as Abihail (אֲבִיחַ֫יִל); a son of Huri; father of Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, Eber.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '아비하일'이라 불림. 후리의 아들. 미가엘, 므술람, 세바, 요래, 야간, 시아와 에벨의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일은 구니의 후손으로 길르앗에 거주한 갓 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of Rehoboam's wife Mahalath
persons.short: Abihail was the mother of Mahalath, who was one of King Rehoboam's wives and the daughter of David's son Jerimoth.
persons.article: Abihail is mentioned in 2Ch.11.18 as the mother of Mahalath, who became one of King Rehoboam's wives. Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and the first king of the southern kingdom of Judah after the division of the united monarchy. Mahalath's father was Jerimoth, one of David's sons. The marriage of Rehoboam to Mahalath was likely a political alliance, as it strengthened Rehoboam's connection to the Davidic dynasty.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.11.18 only referred to as Abihail (אֲבִיחַ֫יִל); a daughter of Eliab; wife of Jerimoth; mother of Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ch.11.18에 처음 언급되며 '아비하일'이라 불림. 엘리압의 딸. 여레못과 르호보암의 아내. 마할랏의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일은 다윗의 아들 여리못의 딸 마할랏의 어머니였으며, 마할랏은 르호보암 왕의 아내 중 하나가 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Esther (Hadassah)
persons.short: Abihail was the father of Esther (also known as Hadassah), who became Queen of Persia and saved the Jewish people from Haman's plot.
persons.article: Abihail is mentioned in the book of Esther as the father of Esther, also known as Hadassah (Est.2.15). Esther was a young Jewish woman living in Persia during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). After Queen Vashti was deposed, Esther was chosen to become the new queen. When Haman, a high-ranking official in the Persian court, plotted to destroy the Jewish people, Esther courageously intervened and saved her people. She revealed her Jewish identity to the king and exposed Haman's evil plan. As a result, Haman was executed, and the Jewish people were allowed to defend themselves against their enemies. Esther, along with her cousin and guardian Mordecai, wrote a letter to confirm the practices of Purim, a Jewish holiday commemorating the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's plot (Est.9.29). In this letter, Esther is referred to as "Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail."
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.2.15 only referred to as Abihail (אֲבִיחַ֫יִל); father of Esther.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.2.15에 처음 언급되며 '아비하일'이라 불림. 에스더의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일은 하닷사라고도 불린 에스더의 아버지로, 에스더는 페르시아의 왕비가 되어 하만의 음모에서 유대 민족을 구했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Zuriel, a Levite leader
persons.short: Abihail was the father of Zuriel, who was the leader of the Merarite clan of the Levites during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.article: Abihail is mentioned in Num.3.35 as the father of Zuriel, who was the leader of the Merarite clan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, alongside the Gershonites and the Kohathites. As the leader of the Merarites, Zuriel was responsible for overseeing the transportation and setup of the tabernacle's framework, including the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets (Num.3.36-37). The Merarites were under the overall leadership of Ithamar, one of Aaron's sons. No additional information is provided about Abihail himself in the biblical text, apart from being the father of Zuriel. His mention serves to identify Zuriel's lineage and his role within the Levitical clan structure.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.3.35 only referred to as Abihail (אֲבִיחַ֫יִל); father of Zuriel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.3.35에 처음 언급되며 '아비하일'이라 불림. 수리엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일은 수리엘의 아버지로, 광야 시절 레위 지파 므라리 가문의 지도자였던 수리엘을 낳았다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Aaron
persons.short: Abihu was a son of Aaron who served as a priest. (<ref="Exo.6.23">Exo.6.23</ref>)
persons.article: Abihu was the second son of Aaron and Elisheba, and the brother of Nadab, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exo.6.23; Num.3.2). He was consecrated as a priest along with his brothers to serve at the tabernacle (Exo.28.1). Abihu went up Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab and seventy elders of Israel to worship the Lord before He gave the tablets of the Testimony to Moses (Exo.24.1,9). However, Abihu and his brother Nadab offered unauthorized fire before the Lord, and fire came out from the presence of the Lord and consumed them, and they died (Lev.10.1-2; Num.3.4; 26.61). This occurred on the eighth day of the priests' consecration. Aaron and his surviving sons were not allowed to mourn their deaths (Lev.10.6). The sin of Abihu and Nadab was in offering "strange fire" which the Lord had not commanded (Lev.10.1). This may refer to offering incense that was not prepared according to God's instructions, or performing this in a wrong manner or at an inappropriate time. Their deaths served as a stern warning against improper worship. After this incident, God gave Aaron further regulations for priestly service and conduct (Lev.10.8-11). The genealogies record Aaron's descendants through his other sons Eleazar and Ithamar, since Nadab and Abihu had no children before their untimely deaths (Num.3.4; 1Ch.24.1-2).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.23 only referred to as Abihu (אֲבִיהוּא); son of Aaron and Elisheba; a brother of Nadab, Eleazar and Ithamar.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 제사장. Exo.6.23에 처음 언급되며 '아비후'라 불림. 아론과 엘리세바의 아들. 나답, 엘르아살과 이다말의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비후는 아론의 아들로 제사장으로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 아비후는 아론과 엘리세바의 둘째 아들이며 나답, 엘르아살, 이다말의 형제였다(출 6:23; 민 3:2). 그는 형제들과 함께 성막에서 섬기도록 제사장으로 성별되었다(출 28:1). 아비후는 여호와께서 모세에게 증거판을 주시기 전에 모세, 아론, 나답, 그리고 이스라엘의 칠십 장로와 함께 시내산에 올라가 여호와를 경배했다(출 24:1, 9). 그러나 아비후와 그의 형제 나답은 여호와 앞에 허가받지 않은 불을 드렸고, 여호와 앞에서 불이 나와 그들을 삼켜 그들이 죽었다(레 10:1-2; 민 3:4; 26:61). 이는 제사장 성별 여드레째 날에 일어났다. 아론과 그의 살아남은 아들들은 그들의 죽음을 애곡하는 것이 허락되지 않았다(레 10:6). 아비후와 나답의 죄는 여호와께서 명령하지 않으신 '다른 불'을 드린 데 있었다(레 10:1). 이는 하나님의 지시에 따라 준비되지 않은 향을 드리거나, 잘못된 방식으로 또는 부적절한 때에 이를 행한 것을 가리킬 수 있다. 그들의 죽음은 부적절한 예배에 대한 엄중한 경고가 되었다. 이 사건 이후 하나님은 아론에게 제사장 봉사와 행동에 관한 추가 규정을 주셨다(레 10:8-11). 족보는 나답과 아비후가 이른 죽음 이전에 자녀가 없었기 때문에 아론의 다른 아들들인 엘르아살과 이다말을 통한 후손을 기록한다(민 3:4; 대상 24:1-2).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ard@Num.26.40, Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Ezbon@1Ch.7.7, Uzzi@1Ch.7.7, Uzziel@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abishua@1Ch.8.4, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Bela, a Benjaminite
persons.short: Abihud was a son of Bela and a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.
persons.article: Abihud is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.8.3 as one of the sons of Bela, who was a son of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which is given in the context of the descendants of King Saul, Israel's first king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.3 only referred to as Abihud (אֲבִיהוּד); son of Bela; a brother of Ard, Naaman, Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abishua and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '아비훗'이라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 아릇, 나아만, 에스본, 웃시, 웃시엘, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비수아와 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비훗은 벨라의 아들로 베냐민 지파의 족보에 언급된 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a priestly division during David's reign
persons.short: Abijah was the head of the eighth priestly division established during King David's reign, and Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, belonged to this division.
persons.article: Abijah was the head of one of the twenty-four priestly divisions established during the reign of King David (1Ch.24.10). These divisions were responsible for serving in the temple in rotation. The priests were divided into twenty-four groups, each headed by a leading priest, and they would serve in the temple for a week at a time, twice a year. In the New Testament, Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, is mentioned as belonging to the priestly division of Abijah (Luk.1.5). This indicates that the priestly division named after Abijah continued to function even during the time of Jesus, several centuries after its establishment. Zechariah was serving in the temple when he received the announcement from the angel Gabriel that his wife Elizabeth would bear a son, John the Baptist, who would prepare the way for the Messiah (Luk.1.8-17).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.24.10 referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה), or Abijah (Ἀβιά).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.10에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 다윗 왕 시대에 세워진 여덟째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였으며, 세례 요한의 아버지 사가랴가 이 반차에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Joash@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: Son of Becher, a Benjaminite
persons.short: Abijah was a son of Becher and a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.
persons.article: Abijah is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.7.8 as one of the sons of Becher, who was a son of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which traces the descendants of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 요아스, 엘리에셀, 에료에내, 오므리, 여레못, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 베겔의 아들로 베냐민 지파의 족보에 언급된 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jeroboam I, died in childhood
persons.short: Abijah, the son of King Jeroboam I, fell ill and died in childhood, as prophesied by Ahijah the prophet.
persons.article: Abijah was the son of Jeroboam I, the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the division of the united monarchy. When Abijah fell sick, Jeroboam sent his wife in disguise to the prophet Ahijah to inquire about the child's fate (1Ki.14.1-3). Ahijah, guided by God, recognized Jeroboam's wife and delivered a message of judgment against Jeroboam's house for his idolatry and disobedience. The prophet also revealed that Abijah would die, and indeed, as soon as Jeroboam's wife returned home, the child died (1Ki.14.12-17). Ahijah prophesied that Abijah would be the only one of Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial because he was the only one in whom God found something good (1Ki.14.13). The death of Abijah was a sign of God's judgment against Jeroboam and his dynasty.
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.14.1 only referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה); son of Jeroboam; a brother of Nadab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림. 여로보암의 아들. 나답의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 여로보암 왕의 아들로, 선지자 아히야가 예언한 대로 어린 나이에 병들어 죽었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jeush@2Ch.11.19, Shemariah@2Ch.11.19, Zaham@2Ch.11.19, Attai@2Ch.11.20, Ziza@2Ch.11.20, Shelomith@2Ch.11.20
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam
persons.short: Abijah, the son of Rehoboam, reigned as king of Judah for three years and continued in the sins of his father.
persons.article: Abijah, also known as Abijam (1Ki.14.31, was the second king of Judah after the division of the united monarchy). He was the son of Rehoboam and Maacah, the daughter of Absalom (2Ch.11.20). Abijah reigned for three years in Jerusalem (2Ch.13.1-2; 1Ki.15.1-2). During his reign, there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam, the king of Israel (2Ch.13.3). In a battle at Mount Zemaraim, Abijah addressed the Israelites, emphasizing the legitimacy of the Davidic dynasty and the importance of the Levitical priesthood (2Ch.13.4-12). Despite being outnumbered, Judah prevailed against Israel because they relied on the Lord (2Ch.13.13-18). Abijah expanded his power, taking cities from Jeroboam and growing stronger (2Ch.13.19-21). However, like his father Rehoboam, Abijah did not fully follow the Lord and allowed idolatry to persist in Judah (1Ki.15.3). He walked in all the sins of his father and did not have a fully devoted heart like his ancestor David (1Ki.15.3). Abijah had fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters (2Ch.13.21). After his death, his son Asa succeeded him as king (1Ki.15.8; 2Ch.14.1). Abijah is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Mat.1.7.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.14.31 referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה), or Abijah (אֲבִיָּ֫הוּ), or Abijam (אֲבִיָּם), or Abijah (Ἀβιά); son of Rehoboam and Maacah; a brother of Attai, Ziza and Shelomith; father of Asa; half-brother of: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.14.31에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림. 르호보암과 마아가의 아들. 여우스, 스마랴, 사함, 앗대, 시사와 슬로밋의 형제. 아사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 르호보암의 아들로 유다 왕이 되어 삼 년간 다스렸으나 아버지의 죄를 그대로 따랐다.
persons.article_ko: 아비야(아비얌이라고도 함, 왕상 14:31)는 통일 왕국이 분열된 후 유다의 두 번째 왕이었다. 그는 르호보암과 압살롬의 딸 마아가의 아들이었다(대하 11:20). 아비야는 예루살렘에서 삼 년간 다스렸다(대하 13:1-2; 왕상 15:1-2). 그의 통치 기간 동안 아비야와 이스라엘 왕 여로보암 사이에 전쟁이 있었다(대하 13:3). 스마라임산에서의 전투에서 아비야는 이스라엘 백성에게 연설하며 다윗 왕조의 정당성과 레위 계열 제사장직의 중요성을 강조했다(대하 13:4-12). 수적으로 열세였음에도 유다는 여호와를 의지했기 때문에 이스라엘을 이겼다(대하 13:13-18). 아비야는 여로보암에게서 성읍들을 빼앗아 세력을 확장하며 더 강해졌다(대하 13:19-21). 그러나 그의 아버지 르호보암처럼 아비야는 여호와를 온전히 따르지 않았고 유다에 우상숭배가 지속되도록 허용했다(왕상 15:3). 그는 자기 아버지의 모든 죄를 따라 행하며 조상 다윗처럼 온전한 마음을 갖지 못했다(왕상 15:3). 아비야에게는 열네 명의 아내가 있었고 이십이 명의 아들과 열여섯 명의 딸을 낳았다(대하 13:21). 그가 죽은 후 그의 아들 아사가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다(왕상 15:8; 대하 14:1). 아비야는 또한 마태복음 1:7의 예수 그리스도 족보에도 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Samuel, a corrupt judge
persons.short: Abijah was one of Samuel's sons who served as a judge in Israel but did not follow his father's righteous ways.
persons.article: Abijah was one of the sons of Samuel, the last judge and a prominent prophet in Israel. Along with his brother Joel, Abijah was appointed by Samuel as a judge over Israel in his old age (1Sa.8.1-2). However, Abijah and his brother did not walk in the righteous ways of their father. They turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1Sa.8.3). The corrupt behavior of Abijah and Joel led the elders of Israel to demand a king to rule over them, rejecting the leadership of Samuel and his sons (1Sa.8.4-5). This event marked the transition from the period of the judges to the establishment of the monarchy in Israel. Abijah is also mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1Ch.6.28, confirming his lineage as a descendant of Levi through Samuel.
persons.summary: A Judge from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.8.2 only referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה); son of Samuel; a brother of Joel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Sa.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림. 사무엘의 아들. 요엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 사무엘의 아들 중 하나로 이스라엘의 사사로 섬겼으나 아버지의 의로운 길을 따르지 않았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Abijah was one of the priests who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time and was also listed among the priests who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Abijah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who sealed the covenant made by the people of Israel to follow God's law (Neh.10.7). This covenant was made during the time of Nehemiah, who led the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Abijah is also listed among the priests who returned from the Babylonian exile (Neh.12.4). In Neh.12.17, he is mentioned as the head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim, the high priest. This suggests that Abijah and his descendants continued to serve as priests in the restored community of Israel after the exile. The mention of Abijah in these passages highlights the importance of the priestly role in the spiritual life of Israel, both in the rebuilding of the temple and in the renewal of the covenant with God.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.7 only referred to as Abijah (אֲבִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.7에 처음 언급되며 '아비야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비야는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 인친 제사장 중 한 사람이었고, 바벨론 포로에서 귀환한 제사장 명단에도 올라 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
persons.short: Abimael was a descendant of Shem and one of the sons of Joktan, as mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Abimael is mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1 as one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah (Gen.10.28; 1Ch.1.22). Joktan and his descendants, including Abimael, are listed as part of the Table of Nations, which records the spread of Noah's descendants after the Flood. The descendants of Joktan are believed to have settled in the southern regions of the Arabian Peninsula. However, no further information is provided about Abimael or his specific role in the biblical narrative. His mention in the genealogies serves to trace the lineage of the Semitic peoples and to demonstrate the fulfillment of God's promise to Noah that his descendants would spread throughout the earth after the Flood (Gen.9.1,7).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.28 only referred to as Abimael (אֲבִימָאֵל); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.28에 처음 언급되며 '아비마엘'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비마엘은 셈의 후손으로 욕단의 아들 중 하나였으며, 창세기와 역대상의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Philistine king who interacted with Abraham and Isaac
persons.short: Abimelech was a Philistine king who had dealings with both Abraham and Isaac, involving incidents where the patriarchs claimed their wives were their sisters.
persons.article: Abimelech was a Philistine king who ruled in the region of Gerar. He is mentioned in several incidents involving the patriarchs Abraham and Isaac. In Genesis 20, Abraham moved to Gerar and, out of fear, claimed that his wife Sarah was his sister. Abimelech took Sarah into his household, but God warned him in a dream that she was Abraham's wife. Abimelech, who had not touched Sarah, pleaded his innocence, and God acknowledged that he had acted in integrity. Abimelech then restored Sarah to Abraham, along with gifts of livestock and servants, and allowed Abraham to settle in his land (Gen.20.1-18). Later, in Genesis 21, Abimelech and his commander Phicol made a treaty with Abraham at Beersheba, recognizing Abraham's right to a well he had dug (Gen.21.22-34). In Genesis 26, Isaac, like his father, claimed that his wife Rebekah was his sister while living in Gerar. Abimelech discovered the truth when he saw Isaac caressing Rebekah. He rebuked Isaac for the deception, fearing that one of his people might have slept with Rebekah and brought guilt upon them. Abimelech warned his people not to touch Isaac or Rebekah under penalty of death (Gen.26.1-11). Despite these incidents, Abimelech recognized the blessing of God upon Abraham and Isaac. He sought peace with them, and they made treaties together (Gen.21.22-34; 26.26-33). The interactions between Abimelech and the patriarchs highlight the challenges and tensions that existed between the people of God and the surrounding nations, as well as God's faithfulness in protecting and blessing His chosen people.
persons.summary: A king in Canaan living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.20.2 only referred to as Abimelech (אֲבִימֶ֫לֶךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.20.2에 처음 언급되며 '아비멜렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비멜렉은 블레셋 왕으로 아브라함, 이삭과 관계된 사건들, 곧 두 족장이 자기 아내를 누이라고 속인 일에 등장한다.
persons.article_ko: 아비멜렉은 그랄 지역을 다스린 블레셋 왕이었다. 그는 족장 아브라함과 이삭과 관련된 여러 사건에 언급된다. 창세기 20장에서 아브라함은 그랄로 이주했고, 두려움 때문에 자기 아내 사라를 자기 누이라고 주장했다. 아비멜렉은 사라를 자기 집에 데려갔으나, 하나님은 꿈에서 그녀가 아브라함의 아내라고 그에게 경고하셨다. 사라를 건드리지 않았던 아비멜렉은 자신의 결백을 호소했고, 하나님은 그가 정직하게 행동했음을 인정하셨다. 그런 다음 아비멜렉은 사라를 아브라함에게 돌려주며 가축과 종들의 선물도 함께 주었고, 아브라함이 자기 땅에 정착하도록 허락했다(창 20:1-18). 후에 창세기 21장에서 아비멜렉과 그의 지휘관 비골은 브엘세바에서 아브라함과 조약을 맺어 그가 판 우물에 대한 아브라함의 권리를 인정했다(창 21:22-34). 창세기 26장에서 이삭도 아버지처럼 그랄에 사는 동안 자기 아내 리브가를 자기 누이라고 주장했다. 아비멜렉은 이삭이 리브가를 애무하는 것을 보고 진실을 발견했다. 그는 자기 백성 중 한 사람이 리브가와 동침하여 그들에게 죄를 가져올 것을 두려워하여 속임수에 대해 이삭을 책망했다. 아비멜렉은 자기 백성에게 이삭이나 리브가를 건드리지 말라고 경고하며 죽음의 벌을 내리겠다고 했다(창 26:1-11). 이런 사건들에도 불구하고 아비멜렉은 아브라함과 이삭에게 임한 하나님의 축복을 인정했다. 그는 그들과 평화를 구했고 그들은 함께 조약을 맺었다(창 21:22-34; 26:26-33). 아비멜렉과 족장들 사이의 상호작용은 하나님의 백성과 주변 민족들 사이에 존재했던 도전과 긴장, 그리고 자신이 택하신 백성을 보호하고 축복하시는 하나님의 신실하심을 보여준다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Gideon, self-proclaimed king of Shechem
persons.short: Abimelech, a son of Gideon, declared himself king of Shechem but was eventually killed when a millstone was dropped on his head during the siege of Thebez.
persons.article: Abimelech was a son of Gideon, the judge of Israel, by his Shechemite concubine (Jdg.8.31). After Gideon's death, Abimelech conspired with his mother's family in Shechem to make himself king. He killed his seventy brothers, with only the youngest, Jotham, escaping (Jdg.9.1-6). Jotham confronted the people of Shechem with a parable, warning them of the consequences of their actions in supporting Abimelech (Jdg.9.7-21). After three years, tensions arose between Abimelech and the people of Shechem, who eventually rebelled against him. Abimelech defeated the Shechemites and destroyed their city, sowing it with salt (Jdg.9.22-49). Abimelech then attacked the city of Thebez. During the siege, a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head, severely wounding him. To avoid the disgrace of being killed by a woman, Abimelech ordered his armor-bearer to kill him with a sword (Jdg.9.50-54). His death was seen as God's judgment for his wickedness in killing his brothers (Jdg.9.56-57). Abimelech's story is a cautionary tale about the dangers of ambition, treachery, and the abuse of power. It also demonstrates the consequences of failing to follow God's leadership and the importance of loyalty and integrity in relationships. The death of Abimelech by a millstone is later referenced by David when he learns of the death of Uriah the Hittite in battle (2Sa.11.21, highlighting the ignominy associated with Abimelech's demise).
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.8.31 only referred to as Abimelech (אֲבִימֶ֫לֶךְ); son of Gideon; a brother of Jether and Jotham.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.8.31에 처음 언급되며 '아비멜렉'이라 불림. 기드온의 아들. 예델과 요담의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 기드온의 아들 아비멜렉은 스스로 세겜의 왕이라 선포했으나, 데베스 성 포위 중 한 여인이 던진 맷돌에 맞아 죽었다.
persons.article_ko: 아비멜렉은 이스라엘의 사사 기드온이 세겜 여인 첩에게서 낳은 아들이었다(삿 8:31). 기드온이 죽은 후 아비멜렉은 세겜에 있는 어머니의 가족과 공모하여 스스로 왕이 되고자 했다. 그는 자기 형제 일흔 명을 죽였고, 막내 요담만 도망쳤다(삿 9:1-6). 요담은 세겜 사람들에게 비유로 대면하여 아비멜렉을 지지한 것의 결과를 경고했다(삿 9:7-21). 삼 년 후 아비멜렉과 세겜 사람들 사이에 긴장이 발생했고, 그들은 결국 그를 대적하여 반역했다. 아비멜렉은 세겜 사람들을 물리치고 그 성읍을 파괴하며 소금을 뿌렸다(삿 9:22-49). 그런 다음 아비멜렉은 데베스 성을 공격했다. 포위 중 한 여인이 맷돌 위짝을 그의 머리에 던져 심하게 부상을 입혔다. 여인에게 죽임을 당하는 수치를 피하려고 아비멜렉은 자기 병기 든 자에게 칼로 자신을 죽이라고 명령했다(삿 9:50-54). 그의 죽음은 그가 자기 형제들을 죽인 악함에 대한 하나님의 심판으로 여겨졌다(삿 9:56-57). 아비멜렉의 이야기는 야심, 배신, 권력 남용의 위험성에 대한 경고 이야기다. 그것은 또한 하나님의 지도력을 따르지 않는 것의 결과와 관계에서 충성과 정직의 중요성을 보여준다. 아비멜렉이 맷돌에 맞아 죽은 사건은 후에 다윗이 헷 사람 우리야가 전투 중 죽었다는 소식을 들었을 때 언급되어, 아비멜렉의 죽음과 관련된 불명예를 부각시킨다(삼하 11:21).

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Solomon's son-in-law, an official in his government
persons.short: Abinadab, the son of Iddo, was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath and served as an official in Solomon's government, overseeing the region of Dor.
persons.article: Abinadab, the son of Iddo, was a high-ranking official during the reign of King Solomon. He was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath, which likely strengthened his position within the royal court (1Ki.4.11). As part of Solomon's administrative structure, Abinadab was appointed as one of the twelve officers who governed various regions of Israel. He was responsible for the region of Dor, located in the western part of the country near the Mediterranean coast (1Ki.4.11). These officers were tasked with providing provisions for the king and his household, each being responsible for supplying the royal court for one month out of the year (1Ki.4.7).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.11 only referred to as Abinadab (אֲבִינָדָב); father of Ben-abinadab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '아비나답'이라 불림. 벤아비나답의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비나답은 잇도의 아들로 솔로몬의 딸 다밧과 결혼했으며, 솔로몬의 관리로서 돌 지역을 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Malchi-shua@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Merab@1Sa.14.49-2Sa, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch, Armoni@2Sa.21.8, Mephibosheth@2Sa.21.8
persons.brief: Son of King Saul, killed in battle
persons.short: Abinadab, also known as Ishvi, was one of the sons of King Saul who died alongside his father and brothers in battle against the Philistines at Mount Gilboa.
persons.article: Abinadab, also referred to as Ishvi, was one of the sons of King Saul, the first king of Israel (1Sa.14.49; 1Ch.8.33; 9.39). He was the brother of Jonathan, Malchishua, and Esh-baal (also known as Ish-bosheth). Abinadab fought alongside his father and brothers in the battle against the Philistines at Mount Gilboa. In this battle, Saul and his sons, including Abinadab, were killed (1Sa.31.2; 1Ch.10.2). The Philistines found their bodies the following day and fastened Saul's body to the wall of Beth-shan, while the bodies of his sons were taken to Jabesh-gilead and buried there (1Sa.31.8-13). The death of Abinadab and his brothers marked the end of Saul's reign and paved the way for David to become king over Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.14.49 referred to as Abinadab (אֲבִינָדָב), or Ishvi (יִשְׁוִי); son of Saul and Ahinoam; a brother of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Merab and Michal; half-brother of: Ish-bosheth, Armoni and Mephibosheth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.14.49에 처음 언급되며 '아비나답'이라 불림. 사울과 아히노암의 아들. 요나단, 말기수아, 메랍, 미갈, 이스보셋, 알모니와 므비보셋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비나답(이스위라고도 함)은 사울 왕의 아들 중 하나로, 길보아산 전투에서 아버지와 형제들과 함께 죽었다.

persons.description: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Son of Jesse, brother of David
persons.short: Abinadab was one of the sons of Jesse and an older brother of King David, but he was not chosen to be anointed as king by Samuel.
persons.article: Abinadab was the second son of Jesse, a Bethlehemite, and an older brother of King David (1Sa.16.8; 1Ch.2.13). When the prophet Samuel came to Jesse's house to anoint one of his sons as the next king of Israel, Abinadab was presented to him. However, the Lord had not chosen Abinadab, and Samuel continued to inquire until David, the youngest son, was brought before him and anointed (1Sa.16.6-13). Abinadab, along with his brothers Eliab and Shammah, served in Saul's army during the war against the Philistines (1Sa.17.13). They were present when David, their youngest brother, arrived at the battlefront and challenged the Philistine champion Goliath (1Sa.17.17-28).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.16.8 only referred to as Abinadab (אֲבִינָדָב); son of Jesse; a brother of David, Eliab, Shimeah, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 형제. 1Sa.16.8에 처음 언급되며 '아비나답'이라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 아들. 다윗, 엘리압, 삼마, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 엘리후, 스루야와 아비가일의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비나답은 이새의 아들이자 다윗의 형이었으나 사무엘에게 왕으로 기름부음 받지 못했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Kept the ark of God in his house
persons.short: Abinadab, in whose house the ark of God was kept for 20 years.
persons.article: Abinadab was a man from Kiriath-jearim in whose house the ark of God was kept for twenty years after it was returned by the Philistines (1Sa.7.1). The ark had been captured by the Philistines in battle, but after God afflicted them with plagues, they sent it back to Israel (1Samuel 5-6). The men of Beth-shemesh, where the ark first arrived, were struck down by God for looking into the ark, so they sent messengers to Kiriath-jearim to take the ark away (1Sa.6.19-21). The ark remained in Abinadab's house until King David decided to bring it to Jerusalem. David and the Israelites went to Abinadab's house to retrieve the ark, placing it on a new cart driven by Abinadab's sons, Uzzah and Ahio (2Sa.6.3; 1Ch.13.7). However, when the oxen stumbled and Uzzah reached out to steady the ark, God struck him down for his irreverence (2Sa.6.6-7). After this incident, David left the ark in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months before successfully bringing it to Jerusalem (2Sa.6.10-12).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.7.1 referred to as Abinadab (אֲבִינָדָב); father of Eleazar, Uzzah, and Ahio.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.7.1에 처음 언급되며 '아비나답'이라 불림. 엘르아살, 웃사와 아효의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비나답의 집에는 하나님의 궤가 이십 년 동안 있었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Barak, the Israelite commander
persons.short: Abinoam was the father of Barak, the Israelite commander who, along with the prophetess Deborah, led the Israelites to victory against the Canaanite army led by Sisera.
persons.article: Abinoam was the father of Barak, an Israelite commander during the time of the judges. Barak was from Kedesh in Naphtali, a region in northern Israel (Jdg.4.6). When Israel was oppressed by Jabin, the king of Canaan, and his commander Sisera, the prophetess Deborah summoned Barak and instructed him to gather 10,000 men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun to mount an attack against Sisera's army (Jdg.4.6-7). Barak agreed to go only if Deborah would accompany him, to which she consented, but prophesied that the glory of the victory would go to a woman (Jdg.4.8-9). Barak and his army defeated Sisera's forces, and Sisera himself was killed by Jael, a woman who invited him into her tent and drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept (Jdg.4.12-24). After the victory, Deborah and Barak sang a song of praise to the Lord, recounting the events of the battle and celebrating the triumph of Israel over their oppressors (Jdg.5.1-31). In this song, Barak is referred to as the son of Abinoam (Jdg.5.12, emphasizing his lineage and his role in the victory).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.4.6 only referred to as Abinoam (אֲבִינֹ֫עַם); father of Barak.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '아비노암'이라 불림. 바락의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비노암은 여선지자 드보라와 함께 시스라가 이끄는 가나안 군대를 물리치고 이스라엘을 승리로 이끈 지휘관 바락의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Firstborn son of Hiel the Bethelite
persons.short: Abiram, the firstborn son of Hiel the Bethelite, died when his father laid the foundation of Jericho.
persons.article: Abiram was the firstborn son of Hiel the Bethelite, who lived during the reign of King Ahab of Israel. When Hiel rebuilt the city of Jericho, he laid the foundation at the cost of Abiram's life (1Ki.16.34). This fulfilled the prophecy spoken by Joshua after the conquest of Jericho, stating that whoever rebuilt the city would do so at the cost of his firstborn son (Jos.6.26). The death of Abiram as a consequence of his father's actions serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to God's commands and the seriousness of disregarding His warnings. It also highlights the enduring nature of God's word and the certainty of His judgments.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.16.34 only referred to as Abiram (אֲבִירָם); son of Hiel; a brother of Segub.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.16.34에 처음 언급되며 '아비람'이라 불림. 히엘의 아들. 스굽의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비람은 벧엘 사람 히엘의 맏아들로, 그의 아버지가 여리고 성의 기초를 놓을 때 죽었다.

persons.description: Aaron's adversary living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Reubenite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron
persons.short: Abiram, along with Korah and Dathan, led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed up by the earth.
persons.article: Abiram was a Reubenite, the son of Eliab, who joined Korah and Dathan in a rebellion against the leadership of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness (Num.16.1). When summoned by Moses, Abiram and Dathan refused to come, accusing Moses of failing to bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey and trying to make himself a prince over them (Num.16.12-14). In response to the rebellion, Moses proposed a test to demonstrate whom God had chosen. Korah and his followers were to present themselves before the Lord with censers, and God would show who was holy (Num.16.16-19). God warned Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from the rebels so that He could consume them, but Moses interceded for the people (Num.16.20-22). God then commanded the congregation to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Moses declared that if these men died a natural death, then the Lord had not sent him, but if the earth swallowed them up, then they had rejected the Lord (Num.16.23-30). As soon as Moses finished speaking, the ground split apart and swallowed up Korah, Dathan, Abiram, their households, and all their possessions (Num.16.31-33; Psalm Num.106.17). The sons of Korah, however, did not die (Num.26.11). The rebellion of Abiram and his co-conspirators served as a warning to the Israelites not to challenge God's appointed leaders (Deu.11.6). The New Testament also refers to this incident as an example of God's judgment against those who reject His authority (Jude 11).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.16.1 only referred to as Abiram (אֲבִירָם); son of Eliab; a brother of Dathan and Nemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 아론의 대적자. Num.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '아비람'이라 불림. 엘리압의 아들. 다단과 느무엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비람은 고라, 다단과 함께 모세와 아론을 대적하는 반역을 이끌다가 땅이 갈라져 삼켜졌다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Beautiful Shunammite who served King David
persons.short: Abishag, the beautiful Shunammite who served King David in his old age and was later sought as a wife by Adonijah.
persons.article: Abishag was a beautiful young woman from Shunem who was chosen to serve King David in his old age (1Ki.1.3). She was brought to the king to keep him warm and to attend to his needs, but David did not have sexual relations with her (1Ki.1.4). After David's death, his son Adonijah, who had previously attempted to claim the throne, approached Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. He requested that she ask King Solomon to give him Abishag as his wife (1Ki.2.17). However, Solomon perceived this request as a challenge to his kingship, as taking the king's concubine was a symbolic claim to the throne (2Sa.16.21-22). Solomon responded with anger, interpreting Adonijah's request as tantamount to asking for the kingdom itself. He vowed that Adonijah's request would cost him his life (1Ki.2.22-23). Subsequently, Solomon ordered Benaiah to execute Adonijah (1Ki.2.25). The incident with Abishag reveals the political intrigues and power struggles that occurred during the transition of power from David to Solomon. It also underscores the significance of the king's concubines in the context of royal succession in ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.1.3 only referred to as Abishag (אֲבִישַׁג).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.1.3에 처음 언급되며 '아비삭'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비삭은 다윗 왕의 노년에 그를 섬긴 아름다운 수넴 여인으로, 후에 아도니야가 그녀를 아내로 구했다.

persons.description: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: David's nephew, one of his mighty men and commanders
persons.short: Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and nephew of David, was a loyal commander and one of David's mighty men, known for his bravery and military prowess.
persons.article: Abishai was the son of Zeruiah, King David's sister, making him David's nephew (1Ch.2.16). He was the brother of Joab and Asahel, two other prominent figures in David's military ranks (2Sa.2.18). Abishai was one of David's mighty men and a trusted commander in his army. During David's flight from King Saul, Abishai accompanied him and showed his loyalty by offering to kill Saul when they found him sleeping in the camp (1Sa.26.6-9). However, David refused to allow Abishai to harm the Lord's anointed (1Sa.26.9-11). Abishai played a significant role in many of David's military campaigns. He fought alongside Joab against Abner and the forces of Ish-bosheth (2Sa.2.24). After Abner killed Asahel, Joab and Abishai pursued him but were convinced to halt their pursuit (2Sa.2.24-28). Later, Abishai supported Joab in avenging Asahel's death by killing Abner (2Sa.3.30). In the battle against the Ammonites, Abishai led a division of the army and helped secure victory for Israel (2Sa.10.10-14; 1Ch.19.11-15). He also accompanied David during the rebellion of Absalom and was one of the three commanders of David's forces (2Sa.18.2,5,12). Abishai intervened to save David's life when a giant named Ishbi-benob threatened to kill the king (2Sa.21.17). He was also known for his bravery and military exploits, being credited with killing three hundred men with his spear (2Sa.23.18; 1Ch.11.20). Throughout David's reign, Abishai remained a loyal and trusted commander, playing a crucial role in maintaining David's kingdom and defending Israel against its enemies.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.26.6 only referred to as Abishai (אֲבִישַׁי); his mother was Zeruiah; a brother of Joab and Asahel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 용사. 1Sa.26.6에 처음 언급되며 '아비새'라 불림. 스루야의 남편(이름 미상)와 스루야의 아들. 요압과 아사헬의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비새는 스루야의 아들이자 다윗의 조카로, 충성스러운 지휘관이자 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었으며 용맹함으로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 아비새는 다윗 왕의 누이 스루야의 아들로, 다윗의 조카였다(대상 2:16). 그는 다윗 군대의 다른 저명한 인물인 요압과 아사헬의 형제였다(삼하 2:18). 아비새는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이며 그의 군대에서 신뢰받는 지휘관이었다. 다윗이 사울 왕을 피해 도망 다닐 때 아비새는 그와 동행했고, 진영에서 잠자는 사울을 발견했을 때 그를 죽이겠다고 제안하며 충성심을 보였다(삼상 26:6-9). 그러나 다윗은 아비새가 여호와의 기름부음받은 자를 해치는 것을 허락하지 않았다(삼상 26:9-11). 아비새는 다윗의 많은 군사 원정에서 중요한 역할을 했다. 그는 요압과 함께 아브넬과 이스보셋의 군대를 대적하여 싸웠다(삼하 2:24). 아브넬이 아사헬을 죽인 후 요압과 아비새는 그를 추격했으나 추격을 멈추도록 설득당했다(삼하 2:24-28). 후에 아비새는 아사헬의 죽음에 대한 복수로 아브넬을 죽이는 것을 요압을 도왔다(삼하 3:30). 암몬 사람들을 대적하는 전투에서 아비새는 군대의 한 부대를 이끌었고 이스라엘의 승리를 확보하는 것을 도왔다(삼하 10:10-14; 대상 19:11-15). 그는 또한 압살롬의 반역 동안 다윗과 동행했고 다윗 군대의 세 지휘관 중 한 사람이었다(삼하 18:2, 5, 12). 아비새는 이스비브놉이라는 거인이 왕을 죽이려 위협했을 때 개입하여 다윗의 생명을 구했다(삼하 21:17). 그는 또한 자기 창으로 삼백 명을 죽인 것으로 인정받는 용맹함과 군사적 업적으로도 알려졌다(삼하 23:18; 대상 11:20). 다윗의 통치 내내 아비새는 충성스럽고 신뢰받는 지휘관으로 남아 다윗의 왕국을 유지하고 이스라엘을 원수들로부터 방어하는 데 중대한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Phinehas, grandson of Eleazar the high priest
persons.short: Abishua was the son of Phinehas and grandson of Eleazar, who served as high priests in the line of Aaron.
persons.article: Abishua was the son of Phinehas and the grandson of Eleazar, who was the son of Aaron, the first high priest of Israel (1Ch.6.4-5,50). He was part of the lineage of high priests who served in the tabernacle and, later, in the temple. As a descendant of Aaron, Abishua would have been part of the Levitical priesthood, although no specific details are given about his role or responsibilities. His mention in the genealogies serves to trace the line of high priests from Aaron to the time of the divided monarchy. Abishua is also mentioned in the genealogy of Ezra, the scribe and priest who led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem during the Persian period (Ezr.7.5). This genealogy demonstrates Ezra's priestly lineage and his connection to the line of high priests stretching back to Aaron, including Abishua.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.4 only referred to as Abishua (אֲבִישׁוּעַ); a son of Phinehas; father of Bukki.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 제사장. 1Ch.6.4에 처음 언급되며 '아비수아'라 불림. 비느하스의 아들. 북기의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비수아는 비느하스의 아들이자 엘르아살의 손자로, 아론 계열의 대제사장으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ard@Num.26.40, Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Ezbon@1Ch.7.7, Uzzi@1Ch.7.7, Uzziel@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abihud@1Ch.8.3, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendant of Benjamin, son of Bela
persons.short: Abishua was a descendant of Benjamin and one of the sons of Bela mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Abishua is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.8.4 as one of the sons of Bela, who was a son of Benjamin, the patriarch of one of the twelve tribes of Israel. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which traces the descendants of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.4 only referred to as Abishua (אֲבִישׁוּעַ); son of Bela; a brother of Ard, Naaman, Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abihud and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '아비수아'라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 아릇, 나아만, 에스본, 웃시, 웃시엘, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비훗과 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비수아는 베냐민 지파의 후손으로, 베냐민 족보에 나오는 벨라의 아들 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shammai, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Abishur, the son of Shammai, was a descendant of Judah; he married Abihail, and they had two sons, Ahban and Molid.
persons.article: Abishur was a descendant of Judah, the son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1Chronicles 2. Abishur was the son of Shammai, who was the son of Onam, a descendant of Jerahmeel, one of the sons of Hezron (1Ch.2.28). Abishur married a woman named Abihail, and together they had two sons, Ahban and Molid (1Ch.2.29). No further details are provided about Abishur's life or his role within the tribe of Judah. His mention in the genealogy serves to trace the lineage of the tribe and demonstrate the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would be numerous.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.28 only referred to as Abishur (אֲבִישׁוּר); son of Shammai; a brother of Nadab; husband of Abihail; father of Ahban and Molid.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.28에 처음 언급되며 '아비술'이라 불림. 삼매의 아들. 나답의 형제. 아비하일의 남편. 아반과 몰릿의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삼매의 아들 아비술은 유다의 후손으로, 아비하일과 결혼해 압반과 몰릿 두 아들을 낳았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's wives; mother of Shephatiah
persons.short: Abital was one of King David's wives and the mother of his son Shephatiah.
persons.article: Abital was one of the wives of King David, the second king of Israel. She is mentioned in the lists of David's wives and children in both 2Sa.3.4 and 1Ch.3.3. Abital gave birth to one of David's sons, named Shephatiah. The biblical text does not provide any further information about Abital's background, her relationship with David, or her role in the royal household. She is one of several wives mentioned in the genealogies, highlighting David's practice of polygamy, which was common among kings in the ancient Near East. Abital's son Shephatiah is listed among David's sons born in Hebron, where David reigned over Judah for seven years before becoming king over all Israel (2Sa.2.11; 5.5).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.4 only referred to as Abital (אֲבִיטָ֑ל); wife of David; mother of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 2Sa.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '아비달'이라 불림. 다윗의 아내. 스바댜의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아비달은 다윗 왕의 아내 중 한 사람으로 아들 스바댜의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jobab@1Ch.8.9, Zibia@1Ch.8.9, Mesha@1Ch.8.9, Malcam@1Ch.8.9, Jeuz@1Ch.8.10, Sachia@1Ch.8.10, Mirmah@1Ch.8.10, Elpaal@1Ch.8.11-
persons.brief: Son of Shaharaim, a Benjaminite
persons.short: Abitub was a son of Shaharaim, a Benjaminite, and is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Abitub is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.8.11 as one of the sons of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin. Shaharaim had two wives, Hushim and Baara, and Abitub is listed among the children born to him in the land of Moab after he had sent away his previous wives. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 traces the descendants of Benjamin, providing insight into the growth and development of the tribe. However, no further details are given about Abitub's life, his role within the tribe, or any significant events or accomplishments associated with him. His mention serves primarily to document the lineage of the Benjaminites.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.11 only referred to as Abitub (אֲבִיטוּב); son of Shaharaim and Hushim; a brother of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sachia, Mirmah and Elpaal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.11에 처음 언급되며 '아비둡'이라 불림. 사하라임과 후심의 아들. 요밥, 시비야, 메사, 말감, 여우스, 사갸, 미르마와 엘바알의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비둡은 베냐민 사람 사하라임의 아들로, 베냐민 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
