persons.article_ko: 아도니야는 다윗 왕의 넷째 아들로, 헤브론에서 태어났다(삼하 3:4; 대상 3:2). 그는 학깃의 아들이었고, 역시 다윗을 대적하여 반역했던 압살롬 다음에 태어났다. 다윗 왕이 늙고 노쇠했을 때 아도니야는 스스로를 높여 '내가 왕이 되리라'고 선언했다(왕상 1:5). 그는 병거와 말, 자기 앞에서 달릴 오십 명을 준비했고, 군대 지휘관 요압과 제사장 아비아달과 의논했는데 그들은 그를 따르고 지지했다. 그러나 그는 자기 대관식에 선지자 나단, 브나야, 용사들, 형제 솔로몬을 초청하지 않았다(왕상 1:7-10). 아도니야의 행동을 알게 된 나단은 솔로몬의 어머니 밧세바에게 다윗에게 알려 그의 뒤를 이어 솔로몬을 왕으로 세우겠다는 그의 맹세를 상기시키라고 조언했다. 이를 들은 다윗은 솔로몬을 선택한 것을 확인하고 그에게 기름을 부어 왕으로 선포하도록 명령했다(왕상 1:11-40). 아도니야와 그의 지지자들은 솔로몬이 왕으로 기름부음받았다는 소식을 듣고 두려워 도망쳤다. 아도니야는 보호를 구하며 제단 뿔을 붙잡았다. 솔로몬은 그가 합당한 사람임을 보이는 조건으로 그의 생명을 살려주었다(왕상 1:50-53). 그러나 다윗이 죽은 후 아도니야는 밧세바를 통해 다윗의 노년의 동반자였던 수넴 여인 아비삭을 아내로 달라고 요청했다. 솔로몬은 이 요청을 왕위에 대한 주장으로 인식하고 브나야에게 아도니야를 처형하라고 명령했다(왕상 2:13-25). 아도니야의 이야기는 야심과 반역에 대한 경고이며, 하나님이 택하신 지도력에 복종하는 것의 중요성과 불법적인 수단으로 권력을 추구하는 것의 결과를 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
persons.short: Adonijah was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God.
persons.article: Adonijah is listed in Neh.10.16 as one of the Levites who sealed the covenant made by the people of Israel during the time of Nehemiah. After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people made a solemn covenant to follow God's commandments and to maintain the worship and service in the temple. Nehemiah, the governor, along with the priests, Levites, and leaders of the people, signed and sealed this covenant as a binding commitment to God (Neh.9.38). Adonijah's inclusion in this list indicates his leadership role among the Levites and his dedication to the spiritual renewal of the community. The covenant included various obligations, such as observing the Sabbath, providing for the temple service, and refraining from intermarriage with the surrounding nations (Neh.10.28-39). By sealing the covenant, Adonijah and the other leaders pledged themselves and the people to follow these commitments faithfully. Apart from this mention in the list of those who sealed the covenant, no other information is provided about Adonijah's specific role, background, or personal life. His participation in this significant event, however, highlights the importance of the Levites' leadership and their commitment to the spiritual well-being of the community during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.16 only referred to as Adonijah (אֲדֹנִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.16에 처음 언급되며 '아도니야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아도니야는 느헤미야가 이끈 하나님의 율법을 따르기로 한 언약에 인친 레위인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Jewish exile whose descendants returned to Jerusalem
persons.short: Adonikam was one of the Jewish exiles whose descendants returned to Jerusalem from Babylon, as recorded in the lists in Ezra and Nehemiah.
persons.article: Adonikam is mentioned in the lists of Jewish exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon, as recorded in Ezr.2.13, Ezr.8.13, and Neh.7.18. These lists provide a record of the individuals and families who were part of the return, highlighting the restoration of the Jewish community in their homeland. In Ezr.2.13 and Neh.7.18, the descendants of Adonikam are numbered at 666 and 667, respectively, among those who returned with Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, during the first wave of the return from exile. In Ezr.8.13, the descendants of Adonikam are mentioned again among those who returned with Ezra, the priest and scribe, during the second wave of the return. In this passage, the last sons of Adonikam are specifically named as Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, along with 60 males. The variations in the numbers of Adonikam's descendants between the lists in Ezra and Nehemiah may be due to different counting methods or the inclusion of additional family members in one of the lists. The repeated mention of Adonikam's descendants in these lists emphasizes the continuity of the Jewish community and the importance of recording the genealogies of those who returned from exile. It also highlights the multi-generational impact of the exile and the restoration of the Jewish people to their homeland.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.13 only referred to as Adonikam (אֲדֹנִיקָם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.13에 처음 언급되며 '아도니감'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아도니감은 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 유대인 포로의 후손 중 한 사람으로, 에스라와 느헤미야의 명단에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: King living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Jerusalem who fought against Joshua
persons.short: Adoni-zedek, the king of Jerusalem, formed an alliance with other Amorite kings to fight against Joshua and the Israelites but was defeated and killed.
persons.article: Adoni-zedek was the king of Jerusalem during the time of Joshua's conquest of Canaan. He is mentioned in Jos.10.1 and Jos.10.3 as one of the Amorite kings who opposed the Israelites' advance into the Promised Land. When Adoni-zedek heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made a peace treaty with Israel, he became greatly alarmed. Gibeon was a significant city, and its alliance with Israel posed a threat to the other Amorite kings in the region. Adoni-zedek formed an alliance with four other Amorite kings: Hoham of Hebron, Piram of Jarmuth, Japhia of Lachish, and Debir of Eglon. Together, they attacked Gibeon to punish them for making peace with Israel (Jos.10.3-4). The Gibeonites sent word to Joshua, requesting help, and Joshua marched all night with his army to come to their aid. In the ensuing battle, the Lord threw the Amorite kings into confusion, and Israel defeated them with a great slaughter. The five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah (Jos.10.5-16). Joshua commanded that the cave be sealed until the battle was finished. After the victory, he brought the five kings out of the cave, and the Israelite commanders put their feet on the kings' necks, symbolizing their complete defeat. Joshua then struck and killed the kings, hanging their bodies on trees until evening (Jos.10.17-27). The defeat of Adoni-zedek and the other Amorite kings was a significant victory for Israel, demonstrating God's power and faithfulness in giving them the Promised Land. It also served as a warning to the other Canaanite kings who would oppose Israel's advance.
persons.summary: A king living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.10.1 only referred to as Adoni-zedek (אֲדֹנִי־צֶ֫דֶק).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 왕. Jos.10.1에 처음 언급되며 '아도니세덱'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아도니세덱은 예루살렘 왕으로, 다른 아모리 왕들과 동맹하여 여호수아와 이스라엘을 대적했으나 패하여 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Official in charge of forced labor under David and Solomon
persons.short: Adoram, also known as Adoniram or Hadoram, was an official in charge of forced labor during the reigns of David, Solomon, and Rehoboam.
persons.article: Adoram, also referred to as Adoniram or Hadoram, was a prominent official who served under three successive kings of Israel: David, Solomon, and Rehoboam. He is primarily known for his role in overseeing the forced labor used in various construction projects. During King David's reign, Adoram was mentioned as being in charge of the forced labor (2Sa.20.24). This suggests that he was responsible for organizing and supervising the workers conscripted for royal building projects. Under King Solomon, Adoram (called Adoniram in 1Ki.4.6 continued to hold the position of being in charge of the forced labor). Solomon undertook extensive building projects, including the construction of the temple and his royal palace, which required a significant workforce. Adoniram was tasked with managing the labor force, which included both Israelites and foreign workers (1Ki.5.13).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.20.24 referred to as Adoram (אֲדֹרָם), or Adoniram (אֲדֹנִירָם), or Hadoram (הֲדֹרָם); a son of Abda.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.20.24에 처음 언급되며 '아도람'이라 불림. 압다의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아도람(아도니람 또는 하도람이라고도 함)은 다윗, 솔로몬, 르호보암 시대에 부역을 관장한 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Assyrian god worshipped by Sepharvites in Samaria
persons.short: Adrammelech was an Assyrian deity worshipped by the Sepharvite people.
persons.article: Adrammelech was an Assyrian god mentioned in the Bible as one of the deities worshipped by the Sepharvite people who were brought to Samaria by the Assyrian king after the conquest of Israel. The Sepharvites burned their children as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.17.31 only referred to as Adrammelech (אַדְרַמֶּ֫לֶךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.17.31에 처음 언급되며 '아드람멜렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아드람멜렉은 스발와임 사람들이 섬긴 앗수르의 신이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Sennacherib who murdered his father
persons.short: Adrammelech, son of Assyrian king Sennacherib, assassinated his father.
persons.article: Adrammelech was one of the sons of Sennacherib, the king of Assyria. After Sennacherib's unsuccessful campaign against Jerusalem, he returned to Nineveh. While worshipping in the temple of his god Nisroch, Adrammelech and his brother Sharezer assassinated their father with the sword. They then escaped to the land of Ararat. Sennacherib's son Esarhaddon succeeded him as king. (2Ki.19.37; Isa.37.38).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.19.37 only referred to as Adrammelech (אַדְרַמֶּ֫לֶךְ); son of Sennacherib; a brother of Sharezer and Esarhaddon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.19.37에 처음 언급되며 '아드람멜렉'이라 불림. 산헤립의 아들. 사레셀과 에살핫돈의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아드람멜렉은 앗수르 왕 산헤립의 아들로, 자기 아버지를 암살했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Saul's son-in-law; husband of Merab
persons.short: Adriel married Saul's daughter Merab and had five sons.
persons.article: Adriel was the son of Barzillai the Meholathite. King Saul had promised his eldest daughter Merab to David, but instead gave her in marriage to Adriel. Merab bore Adriel five sons. During David's reign, these five sons were handed over to the Gibeonites and put to death to avenge Saul's earlier massacre of the Gibeonites, with whom Israel had a treaty. (1Sa.18.19; 2Sa.21.8).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.18.19 only referred to as Adriel (עַדְרִיאֵל); a son of Barzillai; husband of Merab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.18.19에 처음 언급되며 '아드리엘'이라 불림. 바실래의 아들. 메랍의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 아드리엘은 사울의 딸 메랍과 결혼하여 다섯 아들을 두었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Paralyzed man in Lydda healed by Peter
persons.short: Aeneas, paralyzed for eight years, was healed by Peter in Lydda.
persons.article: Aeneas was a man in Lydda who had been bedridden for eight years due to paralysis. When the apostle Peter visited Lydda, he found Aeneas and said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and roll up your mat." Immediately, Aeneas was healed and got up. This miracle led to many people in Lydda and Sharon turning to the Lord. (Act.9.33,34).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.9.33 only referred to as Aeneas (Αἰνέας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.9.33에 처음 언급되며 '애니아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 애니아는 팔 년 동안 중풍병자였는데, 룻다에서 베드로에게 고침을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Prophet who predicted famine and Paul's arrest
persons.short: Agabus, a prophet, foretold a famine and Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Agabus was a prophet from Jerusalem mentioned twice in the book of Acts. In the first instance, he came to Antioch and predicted through the Spirit that a severe famine would spread over the entire Roman world, which happened during the reign of Claudius. The disciples then decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea. (Act.11.28 Later, when Paul was visiting Philip the evangelist in Caesarea, Agabus came down from Judea). He took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet with it, and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'In this way the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and will hand him over to the Gentiles.'" This prophetic act foretold Paul's arrest in Jerusalem. (Act.21.10,11).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.11.28 only referred to as Agabus (Ἄγαβος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.11.28에 처음 언급되며 '아가보'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 아가보는 흉년이 들 것과 예루살렘에서 바울이 체포될 것을 예언했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Amalekite king captured and killed by Samuel
persons.short: Agag, king of the Amalekites, was spared by Saul but killed by Samuel.
persons.article: Agag was the king of the Amalekites during the reign of King Saul of Israel. God commanded Saul to attack the Amalekites and totally destroy everything, including Agag. Saul defeated the Amalekites but spared Agag and the best of the livestock. The prophet Samuel rebuked Saul for his disobedience and told him that God had rejected him as king. Samuel then summoned Agag and "hewed him in pieces before the Lord." (1Sa.15.8,9,20,32,33 The book of Esther mentions that Haman, the enemy of the Jews, was an Agagite, which suggests he may have been a descendant of Agag the Amalekite. )(Est.3.1,10; 8.3,5; 9.24).
persons.summary: A king of Amalakites living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.15.8 referred to as Agag (אֲגָג), or Agagite (אֲגָגִי), or Bougeon (Βουγαίου).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 1Sa.15.8에 처음 언급되며 '아각'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아말렉 왕 아각은 사울에게 죽임을 면했으나 사무엘에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: King mentioned in Balaam's oracle about Israel
persons.short: Agag, a king, is mentioned in Balaam's prophetic oracle about Israel's future.
persons.article: Agag is mentioned in the oracle of Balaam, a prophet hired by Balak, king of Moab, to curse Israel. In Balaam's third oracle, he prophesies about Israel's future, stating, "Their king shall be higher than Agag, and their kingdom shall be exalted." This suggests that Agag was a well-known, powerful king at the time.
persons.summary: A king of Amalakites living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.24.7 only referred to as Agag (אֲגָג).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.24.7에 처음 언급되며 '아각'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아각이라는 왕은 발람이 이스라엘의 미래에 대해 예언한 신탁에서 언급된다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Agee the Hararite was the father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Agee is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Shammah the Hararite, who was one of King David's mighty men. Shammah is known for his brave stand against the Philistines in a field of lentils, where he defended the field and struck down the Philistines, bringing about a great victory.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.11 only referred to as Agee (אָגֵא); father of Shammah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.11에 처음 언급되며 '아게'라 불림. 삼마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하랄 사람 아게는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 삼마의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Tetrarch who heard Paul's defense in Caesarea
persons.short: Tetrarch Agrippa heard Paul's defense and found no grounds for his imprisonment.
persons.article: Agrippa, also known as Herod Agrippa II, was the great-grandson of Herod the Great. He ruled over various territories in Judea during the time of Paul's imprisonment in Caesarea. Agrippa, along with his sister Bernice, visited Festus, the Roman governor. Festus presented Paul's case to Agrippa, who expressed his desire to hear Paul. (Act.25.13-27 The next day, Paul appeared before Agrippa and Bernice and made his defense, recounting his conversion and ministry). Agrippa, familiar with Jewish customs and controversies, listened intently. Paul appealed to Agrippa's belief in the prophets and challenged him to believe in Christ. Agrippa replied, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?" (Act.26.1-28).
persons.summary: Tetrarch Herod Agrippa II over Judea living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.25.13 referred to as Agrippa (Ἀγρίππας); a son of: Tetrarch Herod Agrippa I Male.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 분봉왕. Act.25.13에 처음 언급되며 '아그립바'라 불림. 헤롯의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 분봉왕 아그립바는 바울의 변론을 듣고 그를 가둘 근거가 없다고 판단했다.
persons.article_ko: 아그립바(헤롯 아그립바 2세라고도 함)는 헤롯대왕의 증손자였다. 그는 바울이 가이사랴에 투옥되었을 당시 유대의 여러 영토를 다스렸다. 아그립바는 누이 버니게와 함께 로마 총독 베스도를 방문했다. 베스도가 바울의 사건을 아그립바에게 제시하자 아그립바는 바울의 말을 듣고 싶다는 뜻을 밝혔다(행 25:13-27). 다음날 바울은 아그립바와 버니게 앞에 나아가 자신의 회심과 사역을 이야기하며 변론했다. 유대인의 관습과 논쟁에 익숙했던 아그립바는 주의 깊게 들었다. 바울은 선지자들에 대한 아그립바의 믿음에 호소하며 그리스도를 믿으라고 도전했다. 아그립바는 '네가 적은 말로 나를 권하여 그리스도인이 되게 하려 하는도다'라고 대답했다(행 26:1-28).

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Author of Proverbs 30, son of Jakeh
persons.short: Agur, son of Jakeh, is credited as the author of Proverbs 30.
persons.article: Agur is identified as the son of Jakeh and the author of the sayings recorded in Proverbs 30. He is described as the one "who spoke to Ithiel and Ucal." The text presents a collection of Agur's wise sayings and observations, which cover various topics such as the nature of God, the value of wisdom, and the dangers of foolishness and pride.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at Pro.30.1 only referred to as Agur (אָגוּר); a son of Jakeh.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Pro.30.1에 처음 언급되며 '아굴'이라 불림. 야게의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 야게의 아들 아굴은 잠언 30장의 저자로 알려져 있다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Wicked king of Israel; husband of Jezebel
persons.short: Ahab, son of Omri, reigned as king of Israel and did evil in the sight of the Lord.
persons.article: Ahab was the son of Omri and the seventh king of Israel, reigning for 22 years in Samaria. He did more evil in the eyes of the Lord than any of his predecessors. Ahab married Jezebel, daughter of the king of Sidon, and began to worship Baal. He built a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria and made an Asherah pole, provoking the anger of the Lord. (1Ki.16.28-33 During Ahab's reign, the prophet Elijah declared a drought in Israel). Later, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, proving the Lord to be the true God. (1Ki.17-18) Ahab fought wars against Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, with the Lord granting him victories. (1Ki.20).
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.28 only referred to as Ahab (אַחְאָב); a son of Omri; husband of Jezebel; father of Joash, Ahaziah, Joram, Athaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.16.28에 처음 언급되며 '아합'이라 불림. 오므리의 아들. 이세벨의 남편. 요아스, 아하시야, 요람과 아달랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오므리의 아들 아합은 이스라엘 왕으로 다스리며 여호와 보시기에 악을 행하였다.
persons.article_ko: 아합은 오므리의 아들이며 이스라엘의 일곱 번째 왕으로, 사마리아에서 이십이 년간 다스렸다. 그는 그 이전 어떤 왕보다도 여호와 보시기에 더 많은 악을 행했다. 아합은 시돈 왕의 딸 이세벨과 결혼하여 바알을 숭배하기 시작했다. 그는 사마리아에 바알을 위한 신전과 제단을 짓고 아세라 목상을 만들어 여호와의 진노를 일으켰다(왕상 16:28-33). 아합의 통치 기간 동안 선지자 엘리야는 이스라엘에 가뭄을 선포했다. 후에 엘리야는 갈멜산에서 바알 선지자들에게 도전하여 여호와가 참 하나님이심을 증명했다(왕상 17-18장). 아합은 아람 왕 벤하닷을 대적하여 전쟁을 치렀는데, 여호와께서 그에게 승리를 허락하셨다(왕상 20장).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: False prophet during the Babylonian exile
persons.short: Ahab, son of Kolaiah, was a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
persons.article: Ahab, the son of Kolaiah, was a false prophet among the Judean exiles in Babylon during the time of Jeremiah. The Lord declared that He would deliver Ahab and another false prophet, Zedekiah, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who would execute them. Their fate would become a curse used by the exiles, saying, "May the Lord make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire." This judgment was due to their wickedness and adultery committed in the Lord's name. (Jer.29.21,22).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.29.21 only referred to as Ahab (אַחְאָב); a son of Kolaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.29.21에 처음 언급되며 '아합'이라 불림. 골라야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 골라야의 아들 아합은 바벨론 포로 중에 있던 거짓 선지자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Harum, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Aharhel was a son of Harum, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Aharhel is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah as a son of Harum. He is listed among the descendants of Coz. No further information about Aharhel is provided in the Bible. (1Ch.4.8).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.8 only referred to as Aharhel (אֲחַרְחֵל); a son of Harum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.8에 처음 언급되며 '아하헬'이라 불림. 하룸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아하르헬은 유다의 후손인 하룸의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Ahasbai the Maachathite was the father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Ahasbai is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Eliphelet the Maachathite, who was one of King David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside David and were renowned for their military prowess.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.34 only referred to as Ahasbai (אֲחַסְבַּי); father of Eliphelet.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.34에 처음 언급되며 '아하스배'라 불림. 엘리벨렛의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아가 사람 아하스배는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 엘리벨렛의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Emperor Xerxes I, living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian Emperor (probably Xerxes I); husband of Esther
persons.short: Ahasuerus, Emperor of Persia (probably Xerxes I), chose Esther as his queen and issued decrees impacting the Jews.
persons.article: Ahasuerus, probably Xerxes I, was the king of Persia during the events described in the book of Esther. He ruled over a vast empire from India to Ethiopia. In the third year of his reign, Ahasuerus held a lavish banquet and requested the presence of his queen, Vashti. When she refused to come, the king deposed her. (Est.1) A search was made for a new queen, and Esther, a young Jewish woman, was chosen. Esther kept her Jewish identity secret. (Est.2) Later, Haman, a high official, plotted to destroy the Jews due to his hatred for Mordecai, Esther's cousin. Haman convinced Ahasuerus to issue a decree allowing the annihilation of the Jews. (Est.3). Esther revealed her Jewish identity to Ahasuerus and exposed Haman's plot. The king ordered Haman's execution and issued a new decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves. (Est.7-8) The Jews were victorious over their enemies, and Ahasuerus promoted Mordecai to a high position in the kingdom. (Est.9-10). Ahasuerus is also mentioned in Ezr.4.6, where his reign is associated with opposition to the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and in Dan.9.1, as the father of Darius the Mede. Xerxes I ruled 486 to 465.
persons.summary: An emperor of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.4.6 referred to as Ahasuerus (אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ); a son of Darius; husband of Vashti; father of Artaxerxes and Darius; .
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 황제 크세르크세스 1세(아하수에로). Ezr.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '아하수에로'라 불림. 다리오의 아들. 와스디의 남편. 아닥사스다와 다리오의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아하수에로는 페르시아 황제(아마도 크세르크세스 1세)로, 에스더를 왕비로 택했고 유대인들에게 영향을 준 여러 조서를 내렸다.
persons.article_ko: 아하수에로(아마도 크세르크세스 1세)는 에스더서에 묘사된 사건들 당시 페르시아 왕이었다. 그는 인도부터 에티오피아까지 광대한 제국을 다스렸다. 통치 삼 년째에 아하수에로는 성대한 잔치를 베풀고 왕비 와스디를 부르러 보냈다. 그녀가 오기를 거부하자 왕은 그녀를 폐위시켰다(에스더 1장). 새 왕비를 찾는 일이 있었고, 젊은 유대인 여성 에스더가 선택되었다. 에스더는 자기의 유대인 정체를 비밀로 했다(에스더 2장). 후에 고위 관리 하만은 에스더의 사촌 모르드개에 대한 증오 때문에 유대인들을 멸하려는 음모를 꾸몄다. 하만은 아하수에로를 설득하여 유대인 학살을 허용하는 조서를 내리게 했다(에스더 3장). 에스더는 아하수에로에게 자신의 유대인 정체를 밝히고 하만의 음모를 폭로했다. 왕은 하만의 처형을 명령하고 유대인들이 스스로를 방어할 수 있도록 허락하는 새 조서를 내렸다(에스더 7-8장). 유대인들은 원수들을 이겼고, 아하수에로는 모르드개를 나라의 높은 지위로 승진시켰다(에스더 9-10장). 아하수에로는 또한 에스라 4:6에도 언급되는데, 그의 통치가 예루살렘 재건에 대한 반대와 연관되어 있으며, 다니엘 9:1에서는 메대 사람 다리오의 아버지로 언급된다. 크세르크세스 1세는 기원전 486년부터 465년까지 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Saul and Jonathan
persons.short: Ahaz was a descendant of Saul and Jonathan, from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Ahaz is mentioned in the genealogy of Saul, the first king of Israel, from the tribe of Benjamin. He was the son of Micah and the father of Jehoadah (also known as Jarah). Ahaz is listed among the descendants of Jonathan, Saul's son. No further details about his life or role are provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.8.35,36; 9.42).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.35 only referred to as Ahaz (אָחָז); son of Micah; a brother of Pithon, Melech and Tarea; father of Jehoaddah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.35에 처음 언급되며 '아하스'라 불림. 미가의 아들. 비돈, 멜렉과 다레아의 형제. 여호앗다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아하스는 베냐민 지파 사울과 요나단의 후손이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Jotham
persons.short: Ahaz, son of Jotham, reigned as king of Judah for 16 years.
persons.article: Ahaz was the son of Jotham and the eleventh king of Judah. He reigned for 16 years in Jerusalem, beginning at the age of 20. Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the Lord, but followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even burned his son as an offering and sacrificed to idols on the high places. (2Ki.16.1-4; 2Ch.28.1-4 During his reign, Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, king of Israel, attacked Jerusalem but could not conquer it. )(2Ki.16.5; Isa.7.1 The prophet Isaiah encouraged Ahaz to trust in the Lord, but Ahaz instead sought help from Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, offering him tribute. )(2Ki.16.7-9; Isa.7.3-12). Ahaz adopted pagan practices, including building a new altar based on a design from Damascus and offering sacrifices on it. He cut up the temple articles and closed the doors of the Lord's temple. (2Ki.16.10-18; 2Ch.28.24 Ahaz faced military defeats and became increasingly unfaithful to the Lord. )(2Ch.28.5-8,16-25). Hezekiah, Ahaz's son, succeeded him as king. Hezekiah repaired and purified the temple, which had been neglected during Ahaz's reign. (2Ch.29.3-19 The reign of Ahaz was marked by idolatry and unfaithfulness to God, leading to political turmoil and religious decline in Judah. )(2Ki.16.2-4; 2Ch.28.1-4,22-25).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.38 referred to as Ahaz (אָחָז), or Ahaz (Ἀχάζ); a son of Jotham; husband of Abi; father of Hezekiah and Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.38에 처음 언급되며 '아하스'라 불림. 요담의 아들. 아비의 남편. 히스기야와 마아세야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요담의 아들 아하스는 유다 왕으로 십육 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 아하스는 요담의 아들이며 유다의 열한 번째 왕이었다. 그는 이십 세에 시작하여 예루살렘에서 십육 년간 다스렸다. 아하스는 여호와 보시기에 정직한 것을 행하지 않고 이스라엘 왕들의 길을 따랐다. 그는 심지어 자기 아들을 제물로 불태우고 산당에서 우상들에게 제사를 드렸다(왕하 16:1-4; 대하 28:1-4). 그의 통치 기간 동안 시리아 왕 르신과 이스라엘 왕 베가가 예루살렘을 공격했으나 정복하지 못했다(왕하 16:5; 사 7:1). 선지자 이사야는 아하스에게 여호와를 신뢰하라고 격려했으나, 아하스는 대신 앗수르 왕 디글랏빌레셀에게 도움을 구하며 조공을 바쳤다(왕하 16:7-9; 사 7:3-12). 아하스는 다메섹의 설계를 본뜬 새 제단을 만들고 그 위에 제사를 드리는 것을 포함해 이방 관습을 채택했다. 그는 성전 기구들을 자르고 여호와의 성전 문을 닫았다(왕하 16:10-18; 대하 28:24). 아하스는 군사적 패배에 직면했고 점점 여호와께 신실하지 못하게 되었다(대하 28:5-8, 16-25). 아하스의 아들 히스기야가 그를 이어 왕이 되었다. 히스기야는 아하스 통치 기간 동안 방치되었던 성전을 수리하고 정결하게 했다(대하 29:3-19). 아하스의 통치는 우상숭배와 하나님께 대한 신실치 못함으로 특징지어져 유다에 정치적 혼란과 종교적 쇠퇴를 가져왔다(왕하 16:2-4; 대하 28:1-4, 22-25).

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel, son of Ahab
persons.short: Ahaziah, son of Ahab, reigned as king of Israel for two years.
persons.article: Ahaziah was the son of Ahab and the eighth king of Israel. He reigned for two years in Samaria, doing evil in the sight of the Lord and following the ways of his father and mother, Jezebel. (1Ki.22.51-53 During his reign, Ahaziah formed an alliance with Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, to build ships to go to Tarshish). However, the ships were wrecked, and the venture failed. (1Ki.22.48-49; 2Ch.20.35-37). Ahaziah suffered a severe injury when he fell through the lattice of his upper room. He sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, about his recovery. The prophet Elijah confronted the messengers and prophesied that Ahaziah would die due to his idolatry. Ahaziah sent captains with their fifties to seize Elijah, but fire from heaven consumed them. Elijah then went to Ahaziah and delivered the message of his impending death. (2Ki.1.2-17 Ahaziah died according to the word of the Lord spoken by Elijah, and his brother Jehoram succeeded him as king, as Ahaziah had no son. )(2Ki.1.17-18).
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.40 only referred to as Ahaziah (אֲחַזְיָ֫הוּ); son of Ahab and Jezebel; a brother of Joash, Joram and Athaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.22.40에 처음 언급되며 '아하시야'라 불림. 아합과 이세벨의 아들. 요아스, 요람과 아달랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아합의 아들 아하시야는 이스라엘 왕으로 이 년간 다스렸다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah
persons.short: Ahaziah (also called Jehoahaz), son of Jehoram, reigned as king of Judah for one year.
persons.article: Ahaziah, also known as Jehoahaz, was the son of Jehoram and Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab. He became the sixth king of Judah at the age of 22 and reigned for one year in Jerusalem. Ahaziah did evil in the sight of the Lord, walking in the ways of the house of Ahab, as his mother Athaliah counseled him to do wickedly. (2Ki.8.25-27; 2Ch.22.1-4 Ahaziah joined his uncle Joram, king of Israel, in a battle against Hazael, king of Syria, at Ramoth Gilead). Joram was wounded and returned to Jezreel to recover. Ahaziah went to visit Joram in Jezreel, where he encountered Jehu, who had been anointed to destroy the house of Ahab. Jehu pursued Ahaziah, and Ahaziah was wounded at the ascent of Gur. He fled to Megiddo, where he died. His servants brought his body to Jerusalem, and he was buried with his fathers in the City of David. (2Ki.8.28-29; 9.16,21-28; 2Ch.22.5-9 After Ahaziah's death, his mother Athaliah seized the throne and destroyed all the royal heirs, except for Joash, who was hidden by Jehosheba. )(2Ki.11.1-3; 2Ch.22.10-12 The short reign of Ahaziah was marked by the influence of his mother Athaliah and the house of Ahab, leading to his downfall and the near extinction of the Davidic line).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.8.24 referred to as Ahaziah (אֲחַזְיָ֫הוּ), or Ahaziah (עֲזַרְיָ֫הוּ), or Ahaziah or Jehoahaz (יְהוֹאָחָז); son of Jehoram and Athaliah; a brother of Jehosheba; husband of Zibiah; father of Joash.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.8.24에 처음 언급되며 '아하시야'라 불림. 여호람과 아달랴의 아들. 여호세바의 형제. 시비아의 남편. 요아스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아하시야(여호아하스라고도 함)는 여호람의 아들로 유다 왕으로 일 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 아하시야(여호아하스라고도 함)는 여호람과 아합의 딸 아달랴의 아들이었다. 그는 이십이 세에 유다의 여섯 번째 왕이 되어 예루살렘에서 일 년간 다스렸다. 아하시야는 그의 어머니 아달랴가 그에게 악을 행하도록 조언한 대로 아합 가문의 길을 따라 여호와 보시기에 악을 행했다(왕하 8:25-27; 대하 22:1-4). 아하시야는 삼촌 이스라엘 왕 요람과 함께 시리아 왕 하사엘을 대적하는 전투를 위해 라못길르앗에 합류했다. 요람은 부상을 입어 회복을 위해 이스르엘로 돌아갔다. 아하시야는 이스르엘로 요람을 방문하러 갔다가 그곳에서 아합의 집을 멸하도록 기름부음을 받았던 예후를 만나게 되었다. 예후는 아하시야를 추격했고 아하시야는 구르 비탈에서 부상을 입었다. 그는 므깃도로 도망쳤고 그곳에서 죽었다. 그의 신하들은 그의 시신을 예루살렘으로 가져와 다윗 성에 그의 조상들과 함께 장사했다(왕하 8:28-29; 9:16, 21-28; 대하 22:5-9). 아하시야가 죽은 후 그의 어머니 아달랴는 왕위를 찬탈하여 요아스를 제외한 모든 왕족 상속자를 멸했는데, 요아스는 여호세바에 의해 숨겨졌다(왕하 11:1-3; 대하 22:10-12). 아하시야의 짧은 통치는 그의 어머니 아달랴와 아합 가문의 영향으로 특징지어져 그의 몰락과 다윗 혈통의 거의 멸절로 이어졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Abishur, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Ahban was the son of Abishur, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Ahban is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah. He was the son of Abishur and his wife Abihail. Ahban had a brother named Molid. No further information about Ahban's life or role is provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.2.29).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.29 only referred to as Ahban (אַחְבָן); son of Abishur and Abihail; a brother of Molid.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.29에 처음 언급되며 '아반'이라 불림. 아비술과 아비하일의 아들. 몰릿의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 압반은 유다의 후손인 아비술의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shemer, from the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Aher was a son of Shemer, a descendant of Asher.
persons.article: Aher is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher. He was the son of Shemer, who was a descendant of Asher through Beriah. No further details about Aher's life or role are provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.7.12).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.12 only referred to as Aher (אַחֵר); father of Hushim.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.12에 처음 언급되며 '아헬'이라 불림. 후심의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아헬은 아셀의 후손인 세멜의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Abdiel, a Gadite chief
persons.short: Ahi, son of Abdiel, was a chief of the Gadites.
persons.article: Ahi is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad. He was the son of Abdiel and is described as the chief of his father's household. This suggests that Ahi held a leadership position among the Gadites.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.15 only referred to as Ahi (אֲחִי); a son of Abdiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.15에 처음 언급되며 '아히'라 불림. 압디엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아히는 압디엘의 아들로 갓 지파의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shomer, from the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Ahi (or "brother") was a son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), a descendant of Asher.
persons.article: Ahi, whose name means "brother," is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher. He was the son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), who was a descendant of Asher through Heber. The biblical text does not provide any additional details about Ahi's life, role, or the significance of his name. (1Ch.7.34).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.34 only referred to as Ahi (אֲחִי); son of Shomer; a brother of Rohgah, Jehubbah and Aram.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.34에 처음 언급되며 '아히'라 불림. 소멜의 아들. 로가, 호바와 아람의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히('형제'라는 뜻)는 아셀의 후손인 소멜(또는 사멜)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
persons.short: Ahiah was a priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Ahiah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who sealed the covenant made by the people of Israel after their return from Babylonian exile. The covenant involved a commitment to follow the Law of God, given through Moses. Ahiah, along with other priests, Levites, and leaders, signed this covenant, pledging to uphold its principles and guide the people in obedience to God.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.26 only referred to as Ahiah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아히야는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 인친 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, son of Sharar
persons.short: Ahiam, son of Sharar the Hararite, was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Ahiam was one of the mighty men who served under King David. He was the son of Sharar the Hararite. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors known for their bravery and military prowess. They played a significant role in David's military campaigns and helped establish and defend his kingdom. Ahiam is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty men found in both 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles, but no specific details about his individual exploits are recorded in the Bible. (2Sa.23.33; 1Ch.11.35).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.33 only referred to as Ahiam (אֲחִיאָם); a son of Sharar.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.33에 처음 언급되며 '아히암'이라 불림. 사랄의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하랄 사람 사랄의 아들 아히암은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Shemidah, from the tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Ahian was a son of Shemidah, a descendant of Manasseh.
persons.article: Ahian is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh. He was one of the sons of Shemidah, who was a descendant of Manasseh through his son Gilead. No further details about Ahian's life or role are provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.7.19).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.19 only referred to as Ahian (אַחְיָן); son of Shemida; a brother of Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.19에 처음 언급되며 '아히안'이라 불림. 스미다의 아들. 세겜, 릭히와 아니암의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히안은 므낫세의 후손인 스미다의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Ahiezer was a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Ahiezer is mentioned as one of the Benjamite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. Along with his fellow Benjamites, Ahiezer is described as a brave warrior, armed with a bow, and able to shoot arrows and sling stones with either his right or left hand. (1Ch.12.1-2 These skilled warriors aligned themselves with David and provided valuable military support during his time of exile). The biblical text does not provide any further details about Ahiezer's specific role or exploits in David's army. (1Ch.12.3).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Ahiezer (אֲחִיעֶ֫זֶר); son of Shemaah; a brother of Joash.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '아히에셀'이라 불림. 스마아의 아들. 요아스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히에셀은 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 베냐민 지파의 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader from the tribe of Dan during the Exodus
persons.short: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, was a leader of the tribe of Dan during the Exodus.
persons.article: Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, was a prominent leader from the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. He was appointed by God as the head of his tribe and played a significant role in the census and organization of the Israelite camp. (Num.1.12; 2.25) Ahiezer's tribe was positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Asher and Naphtali. (Num.2.25 He presented his tribe's offering at the dedication of the tabernacle, which included a silver plate, a silver basin, and various animals for sacrifice. )(Num.7.66,71 As a tribal leader, Ahiezer was responsible for leading the Danites in their journey and ensuring their obedience to God's commands. )(Num.10.25)
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.12 only referred to as Ahiezer (אֲחִיעֶ֫זֶר); a son of Ammishaddai.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.12에 처음 언급되며 '아히에셀'이라 불림. 암미삿대의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 암미삿대의 아들 아히에셀은 출애굽 당시 단 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ehud, from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Ahihud was a son of Ehud, a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Ahihud is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He was one of the sons of Ehud, who was a descendant of Benjamin through his son Bela. The genealogy traces the lineage of several prominent Benjamite families, but no specific details are given about Ahihud's life or role within the tribe. (1Ch.8.7).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.7 only referred to as Ahihud (אֲחִיחֻד); son of Ehud; a brother of Naaman, Ahijah, Gera and Uzza.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '아히훗'이라 불림. 에훗의 아들. 나아만, 아히야, 게라와 웃사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히훗은 베냐민의 후손인 에훗의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader from the tribe of Asher for land allocation
persons.short: Ahihud, son of Shelomi, was a leader from the tribe of Asher appointed to help allocate the Promised Land.
persons.article: Ahihud, the son of Shelomi, was a leader chosen from the tribe of Asher to assist in the allocation of the Promised Land among the Israelite tribes. After the conquest of Canaan, God instructed Moses to appoint leaders from each tribe to help divide the land as an inheritance for the Israelites. (Num.34.16-29 Ahihud was selected as the representative for the tribe of Asher in this important task). His role was to work alongside Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the other tribal leaders to ensure a fair and orderly distribution of the land according to God's direction.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.27 only referred to as Ahihud (אֲחִיהוּד); a son of Shelomi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.27에 처음 언급되며 '아히훗'이라 불림. 슬로미의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 슬로미의 아들 아히훗은 약속의 땅을 분배하는 일을 돕도록 임명된 아셀 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, the Pelonite
persons.short: Ahijah the Pelonite was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Ahijah the Pelonite is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men, a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside King David. The mighty men were known for their bravery and military prowess, and they played a significant role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. Ahijah is specifically identified as a Pelonite, which may refer to his place of origin or his family lineage. No further details about Ahijah's specific exploits or role in David's army are provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.11.36).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.36 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.36에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 블로니 사람 아히야는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jerahmeel, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Ahijah was a son of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Ahijah is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He was one of the sons of Jerahmeel, who was a descendant of Judah through his son Hezron. The genealogy lists Ahijah among Jerahmeel's children, along with Ram, Bunah, Oren, and Ozem. No further information about Ahijah's life or role within the tribe is provided in the biblical text. (1Ch.2.25).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.25 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ); son of Jerahmeel; a brother of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.25에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림. 여라므엘과 여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 람, 브나, 오렌, 오셈과 오남의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히야는 유다의 후손인 여라므엘의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite in charge of the treasuries of the temple
persons.short: Ahijah, a Levite, was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God.
persons.article: Ahijah is mentioned briefly in the context of the organization of the Levites during the reign of King David. He was a Levite appointed to oversee the treasuries of the house of God. The Levites were responsible for various duties related to the tabernacle and, later, the temple. These duties included managing the treasuries, which contained the dedicated gifts and offerings brought by the people. Ahijah's specific role was to ensure the proper care and administration of these treasuries.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.20 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.26.20에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 아히야는 하나님 집의 곳간을 맡아 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ehud, from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Ahijah was a son of Ehud, a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Ahijah is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He was one of the sons of Ehud, who was a descendant of Benjamin through his son Bela. The genealogy traces the lineage of several prominent Benjamite families, but no specific details are given about Ahijah's life or role within the tribe. (1Ch.8.7).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.7 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ); son of Ehud; a brother of Naaman, Gera, Uzza and Ahihud.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림. 에훗의 아들. 나아만, 게라, 웃사와 아히훗의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히야는 베냐민의 후손인 에훗의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet from Shiloh who prophesied to Jeroboam
persons.short: Ahijah the Shilonite was a prophet who foretold Jeroboam's rise to power and the division of the kingdom.
persons.article: Ahijah was a prophet from Shiloh who lived during the reigns of Solomon and Jeroboam I. He is best known for his prophecy to Jeroboam, foretelling the division of the kingdom and Jeroboam's rise as king over ten tribes of Israel. (1Ki.11.29-39 Ahijah encountered Jeroboam and symbolically tore his new garment into twelve pieces, giving ten to Jeroboam to represent the ten tribes he would rule). Ahijah also prophesied the downfall of Solomon's dynasty due to idolatry. (1Ki.11.29-39). Later, when Jeroboam's son Abijah fell ill, Jeroboam sent his wife in disguise to seek Ahijah's counsel. Ahijah, now blind, received a message from God and predicted the child's death and the destruction of Jeroboam's house for his idolatry. (1Ki.14.2-18 Ahijah's prophecies concerning the division of the kingdom and the rise of Jeroboam came to pass, as recorded in both 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles. )(1Ki.12.15; 2Ch.10.15 His writings are mentioned as a source for the acts of Solomon. )(2Ch.9.29)
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.11.29 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 선지자. 1Ki.11.29에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 실로 사람 선지자 아히야는 여로보암이 권력을 잡을 것과 왕국이 나뉠 것을 예언했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Baasha, king of Israel
persons.short: Ahijah was the father of Baasha, who became king of Israel and ruled for 24 years.
persons.article: Ahijah is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Baasha, who became the third king of Israel after Jeroboam I. Baasha, the son of Ahijah, was from the tribe of Issachar and reigned over Israel for 24 years. (1Ki.15.27,33 During his reign, Baasha did evil in the sight of the Lord and walked in the ways of Jeroboam, leading Israel into sin. )(1Ki.15.34 The prophet Jehu, son of Hanani, prophesied against Baasha and his house, declaring that they would meet a fate similar to that of Jeroboam's house. )(1Ki.16.1-4 Ahijah is mentioned in the context of God's judgment against the house of Baasha, as God declared that He would bring disaster upon Baasha and his house, making it like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat. )(1Ki.21.22; 2Ki.9.9)
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.15.27 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ); father of Baasha.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.15.27에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림. 바아사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아히야는 이스라엘 왕이 되어 이십사 년간 다스린 바아사의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Seraiah (or 'Shisha'), a scribe during Solomon's reign
persons.short: Ahijah, son of Seraiah (or 'Shisha'), served as a scribe during King Solomon's reign.
persons.article: Ahijah, the son of Seraiah (or 'Shisha'), is mentioned as one of the scribes who served during the reign of King Solomon. Along with his brother Elihoreph, Ahijah held the important position of recording and documenting the king's decrees, correspondence, and other official matters. Scribes in ancient Israel were highly educated individuals who played a crucial role in the administration of the kingdom. No further details about Ahijah's life or specific duties are provided in the Bible. (1Ki.4.3).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.3 only referred to as Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ); son of Seraiah; a brother of Elihoreph.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.3에 처음 언급되며 '아히야'라 불림. 스라야의 아들. 엘리호렙의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스라야(또는 시사)의 아들 아히야는 솔로몬 왕 시대에 서기관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shaphan, protected Jeremiah from death
persons.short: Ahikam, son of Shaphan, was an official during the reigns of Josiah and Jehoiakim, and he protected Jeremiah from death.
persons.article: Ahikam was the son of Shaphan the scribe and an important official during the reigns of King Josiah and King Jehoiakim of Judah. He first appears in the biblical narrative when Josiah sends him, along with other officials, to consult the prophetess Huldah regarding the book of the Law discovered in the temple. (2Ki.22.12-14; 2Ch.34.20 Later, during the reign of Jehoiakim, Ahikam uses his influence to protect the prophet Jeremiah from being put to death when Jeremiah's prophecies anger the officials and the people. )(Jer.26.24). After the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians, the Babylonian captain of the guard appoints Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, as governor over the cities of Judah. (2Ki.25.22 Jeremiah is released from captivity and entrusted to Gedaliah's care. )(Jer.39.14; 40.5-6) Gedaliah establishes his headquarters at Mizpah and encourages the remaining people in Judah to serve the Babylonians. (Jer.40.7-12 However, Ishmael, a member of the royal family, murders Gedaliah and those with him, causing the people to flee to Egypt out of fear of Babylonian reprisal. )(Jer.41.1-18 Ahikam's role in protecting Jeremiah and his son's appointment as governor highlight the family's importance during this turbulent period in Judah's history).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.22.12 only referred to as Ahikam (אֲחִיקָם); son of Shaphan; a brother of Elasah and Gemariah; father of Gedaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.22.12에 처음 언급되며 '아히감'이라 불림. 사반의 아들. 엘라사와 그마랴의 형제. 그달리야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사반의 아들 아히감은 요시야와 여호야김 시대의 관리였으며, 예레미야를 죽음에서 보호했다.
persons.article_ko: 아히감은 서기관 사반의 아들이며 유다 왕 요시야와 여호야김 통치 기간의 중요한 관리였다. 그는 요시야가 성전에서 발견된 율법책에 관해 여선지자 훌다에게 자문을 구하도록 그를 다른 관리들과 함께 보낼 때 성경 이야기에 처음 등장한다(왕하 22:12-14; 대하 34:20). 후에 여호야김 통치 기간에 아히감은 예레미야의 예언이 관리들과 백성을 분노하게 했을 때 자신의 영향력을 사용하여 그가 죽임을 당하지 않도록 보호했다(렘 26:24). 예루살렘이 바벨론 사람들에게 함락된 후 바벨론 시위대장은 아히감의 아들 그달랴를 유다 성읍들을 다스리는 총독으로 임명했다(왕하 25:22). 예레미야는 포로 생활에서 풀려나 그달랴의 보호에 맡겨졌다(렘 39:14; 40:5-6). 그달랴는 미스바에 본부를 세우고 유다에 남은 백성에게 바벨론을 섬기라고 격려했다(렘 40:7-12). 그러나 왕족의 일원인 이스마엘이 그달랴와 그와 함께 있던 사람들을 살해하여, 백성이 바벨론의 보복을 두려워하여 애굽으로 도망치게 만들었다(렘 41:1-18). 예레미야를 보호한 아히감의 역할과 그의 아들이 총독으로 임명된 것은 유다 역사의 이 격동의 시기에 그 가문의 중요성을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jehoshaphat and Baana, officials under David and Solomon
persons.short: Ahilud was the father of Jehoshaphat, David's recorder, and Baana, one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
persons.article: Ahilud is mentioned in the Bible as the father of two important officials who served under King David and King Solomon. His first son, Jehoshaphat, held the position of recorder during David's reign. (2Sa.8.16; 1Ch.18.15 The recorder was responsible for maintaining official records and documents of the kingdom). Ahilud's second son, Baana, served as one of the twelve district governors during Solomon's reign. (1Ki.4.12 These governors were appointed by Solomon to oversee the administration and provision of resources for the king's household, each being responsible for a specific region of Israel). The fact that both of Ahilud's sons held significant positions in the royal administration suggests that Ahilud himself may have been a prominent figure or had a close relationship with the royal family. However, no further details about Ahilud's life or role are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.16 only referred to as Ahilud (אֲחִילוּד); father of Jehoshaphat, Baana.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '아힐룻'이라 불림. 여호사밧과 바아나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아힐룻은 다윗의 사관 여호사밧과 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 한 사람인 바아나의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Solomon's son-in-law, governor of Naphtali
persons.short: Ahimaaz, who was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath, served as the governor of Naphtali during Solomon's reign.
persons.article: Ahimaaz is mentioned briefly in the context of King Solomon's administration. He was one of Solomon's twelve district governors, responsible for providing resources for the king's household. Ahimaaz was assigned to the region of Naphtali, located in the northern part of Israel. (1Ki.4.7,15 Notably, Ahimaaz was married to Basemath, one of Solomon's daughters). This marriage alliance suggests that Ahimaaz was a trusted official and had a close relationship with the royal family. The practice of marrying daughters to high-ranking officials was common in ancient times to strengthen political alliances and ensure loyalty.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.15 only referred to as Ahimaaz (אֲחִימַ֫עַץ); husband of Basemath.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.15에 처음 언급되며 '아히마아스'라 불림. 바스맛의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 아히마아스는 솔로몬의 딸 바스맛과 결혼했으며, 솔로몬 시대에 납달리 지역의 관장으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Saul's wife Ahinoam
persons.short: Ahimaaz was the father of Ahinoam, who was the wife of King Saul.
persons.article: Ahimaaz is briefly mentioned in the Bible as the father of Ahinoam, who became the wife of King Saul, the first king of Israel. Ahinoam was one of Saul's two wives, the other being Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. (1Sa.14.50 The mention of Ahimaaz in this context suggests that he may have been a prominent figure or had some connection to the royal family). However, no further information about Ahimaaz's life, occupation, or role is provided in the biblical text. His significance lies primarily in his relationship to Ahinoam and, by extension, to King Saul.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.14.50 only referred to as Ahimaaz (אֲחִימַ֫עַץ); father of Ahinoam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.14.50에 처음 언급되며 '아히마아스'라 불림. 아히노암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아히마아스는 사울 왕의 아내가 된 아히노암의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zadok the priest, a messenger for David
persons.short: Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, was a messenger who helped David during Absalom's rebellion and brought news of Absalom's death.
persons.article: Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok, the high priest during the reign of King David. He played a significant role as a messenger and loyal supporter of David during the rebellion of David's son Absalom. Along with Jonathan, son of Abiathar, Ahimaaz stayed outside Jerusalem to relay information about Absalom's plans to David. (2Sa.15.27,36; 17.17) When David's forces defeated Absalom's army, Ahimaaz wanted to bring the news to David, but Joab initially sent a Cushite messenger instead. Ahimaaz persisted and was allowed to run, overtaking the Cushite. He reported the victory to David but withheld the news of Absalom's death, which the Cushite messenger revealed. (2Sa.18.19-29 In the genealogy of the Levites, Ahimaaz is listed as the son of Zadok and the father of Azariah, who served as priests in the temple built by Solomon. )(1Ch.6.8,9,53 Ahimaaz's loyalty to David and his role in supporting the rightful king showcase his importance during this tumultuous period in Israel's history).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.15.27 only referred to as Ahimaaz (אֲחִימַ֫עַץ); a son of Zadok; father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 제사장. 2Sa.15.27에 처음 언급되며 '아히마아스'라 불림. 사독의 아들. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독의 아들 아히마아스는 압살롬의 반역 때 다윗을 도운 전령으로, 압살롬의 죽음을 알리는 소식을 전했다.
persons.article_ko: 아히마아스는 다윗 왕 통치 기간의 대제사장 사독의 아들이었다. 그는 다윗의 아들 압살롬의 반역 동안 전령이며 충성스러운 다윗 지지자로서 중요한 역할을 했다. 아비아달의 아들 요나단과 함께 아히마아스는 예루살렘 밖에 머물며 압살롬의 계획에 관한 정보를 다윗에게 전달했다(삼하 15:27, 36; 17:17). 다윗의 군대가 압살롬의 군대를 물리쳤을 때 아히마아스는 그 소식을 다윗에게 전하고 싶어했으나 요압은 처음에 구스 사람 전령을 대신 보냈다. 아히마아스는 고집하여 달려가는 것을 허락받았고 그 구스 사람을 앞질렀다. 그는 다윗에게 승리를 보고했으나 압살롬의 죽음에 대한 소식은 삼갔는데, 이는 구스 사람 전령이 밝혔다(삼하 18:19-29). 레위인 족보에서 아히마아스는 사독의 아들이며 솔로몬이 지은 성전에서 제사장으로 섬긴 아사랴의 아버지로 열거된다(대상 6:8-9, 53). 다윗에 대한 아히마아스의 충성과 정당한 왕을 지지하는 그의 역할은 이스라엘 역사의 이 격동의 시기에 그의 중요성을 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign
persons.short: Ahiman was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper during the reign of David.
persons.article: Ahiman is mentioned briefly in a list of Levites who served as gatekeepers during the reign of King David. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple. They ensured that only authorized individuals entered the sacred premises and maintained order. Ahiman is listed along with other gatekeepers, including Shallum, Akkub, and Talmon. These Levites and their descendants were entrusted with the important task of keeping watch over the gates of the house of the Lord. (1Ch.9.17-19 No further details about Ahiman's specific duties or life are provided in the Bible). His mention in this context highlights the significance of the gatekeeper role in maintaining the sanctity and security of the tabernacle and temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.17 only referred to as Ahiman (אֲחִימַן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.17에 처음 언급되며 '아히만'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아히만은 다윗 시대에 문지기로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: One of the giant descendants of Anak in Hebron
persons.short: Ahiman was one of the three giant descendants of Anak who lived in Hebron and were driven out by Caleb.
persons.article: Ahiman was one of the three sons of Anak, a group of giants who inhabited the city of Hebron in the land of Canaan. When Moses sent twelve spies to scout out the land, they reported seeing the descendants of Anak, including Ahiman, who appeared as giants in their eyes. This report discouraged the Israelites from entering the land. (Num.13.22,28,33 During the conquest of Canaan under Joshua's leadership, Caleb, one of the faithful spies, was given Hebron as his inheritance). He drove out the three sons of Anak, including Ahiman, from the city. (Jos.15.13,14). The book of Judges reiterates that Judah and Simeon fought against the Canaanites in Hebron and defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak. (Jdg.1.10 Ahiman and his brothers were known for their great stature and strength, which initially intimidated the Israelites). However, with God's help, they were eventually defeated, allowing the Israelites to claim the land promised to them.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.13.22 only referred to as Ahiman (אֲחִימַן); son of Anak; a brother of Sheshai and Talmai.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.22에 처음 언급되며 '아히만'이라 불림. 아낙의 아들. 세새와 달매의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히만은 헤브론에 살던 아낙의 세 거인 후손 중 한 사람으로, 갈렙에게 쫓겨났다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: High Priest at Nob who helped David, killed by Saul
persons.short: Ahimelech, the High Priest at Nob, gave David consecrated bread and Goliath's sword but was later killed by Saul for aiding David.
persons.article: Ahimelech, also known as Ahijah, was the priest at Nob during the reign of King Saul. He was the son of Ahitub and the father of Abiathar. When David was fleeing from Saul, he came to Ahimelech at Nob seeking help. Ahimelech, unaware of the conflict between David and Saul, provided David with the consecrated bread and the sword of Goliath. (1Sa.21.1-9 Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul's servants, witnessed this interaction and reported it to Saul). Saul summoned Ahimelech and the other priests, accusing them of conspiring with David against him. Despite Ahimelech's defense of his actions, Saul ordered the execution of the priests. Doeg carried out the order, killing Ahimelech and eighty-four other priests. (1Sa.22.9-19). Abiathar, Ahimelech's son, was the only one who escaped the massacre. He fled to David and brought with him the ephod, a priestly garment used for seeking God's guidance. (1Sa.22.20-23; 23.6; 30.7) The story of Ahimelech's tragic fate is also referenced in Psalm 52, which is attributed to David when Doeg informed Saul about Ahimelech's assistance to David. The psalm reflects on the consequences of those who trust in evil and contrasts them with those who trust in God's steadfast love. (Psa.52.1)
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.14.3 referred to as Ahimelech (אֲחִימֶ֫לֶךְ), or Ahijah (אֲחִיָּ֫הוּ); a son of Ahitub; father of Abiathar.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 대제사장. 1Sa.14.3에 처음 언급되며 '아히멜렉'이라 불림. 아히둡의 아들. 아비아달의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 놉의 대제사장 아히멜렉은 다윗에게 진설병과 골리앗의 칼을 내주었으나, 다윗을 도왔다는 이유로 후에 사울에게 죽임을 당했다.
persons.article_ko: 아히멜렉(아히야라고도 함)은 사울 왕 통치 기간에 놉의 제사장이었다. 그는 아히둡의 아들이며 아비아달의 아버지였다. 다윗이 사울을 피해 도망치고 있을 때 그는 도움을 구하러 놉에 있는 아히멜렉에게 왔다. 다윗과 사울 사이의 갈등을 알지 못했던 아히멜렉은 다윗에게 성별된 떡과 골리앗의 칼을 제공했다(삼상 21:1-9). 사울의 종 중 한 사람인 에돔 사람 도엑은 이 상호작용을 목격하고 사울에게 보고했다. 사울은 아히멜렉과 다른 제사장들을 불러 다윗과 함께 자신을 대적하여 공모했다고 고발했다. 아히멜렉이 자신의 행동을 변호했음에도 사울은 제사장들의 처형을 명령했다. 도엑은 그 명령을 수행하여 아히멜렉과 다른 제사장 여든네 명을 죽였다(삼상 22:9-19). 아히멜렉의 아들 아비아달만이 유일하게 그 학살에서 도망쳤다. 그는 다윗에게로 도망쳐 하나님의 인도를 구하는 데 사용되는 제사장 의복인 에봇을 가지고 왔다(삼상 22:20-23; 23:6; 30:7). 아히멜렉의 비극적인 운명 이야기는 시편 52편에도 언급되는데, 이는 도엑이 아히멜렉이 다윗을 도운 것을 사울에게 알렸을 때 다윗이 지은 것으로 여겨진다. 그 시편은 악을 신뢰하는 자들의 결과를 성찰하며 그들을 하나님의 한결같은 사랑을 신뢰하는 자들과 대조한다(시 52:1).

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ahitub, a Hittite warrior who joined David
persons.short: Ahimelech the Hittite was one of David's warriors who accompanied him to Saul's camp while Saul was pursuing David.
persons.article: Ahimelech the Hittite is briefly mentioned as one of the warriors who accompanied David when he infiltrated Saul's camp. During this time, Saul was pursuing David, seeking to kill him out of jealousy and fear for his own kingship. David, along with Ahimelech and Abishai, snuck into Saul's camp while Saul and his men were sleeping. Abishai suggested killing Saul, but David refused, choosing to spare Saul's life as he was the Lord's anointed. Instead, David took Saul's spear and water jug, which were near Saul's head, and left the camp undetected. (1Sa.26.6-12 Ahimelech's presence alongside David demonstrates his loyalty and support for the future king, even in the face of danger). As a Hittite, Ahimelech's allegiance to David also shows that David's followers came from various backgrounds, not just Israelites.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.26.6 only referred to as Ahimelech (אֲחִימֶ֫לֶךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 1Sa.26.6에 처음 언급되며 '아히멜렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헷 사람 아히멜렉은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로, 사울이 다윗을 쫓을 때 그와 동행했다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Abiathar, a priest during David's reign
persons.short: Ahimelech, son of Abiathar, served as a priest during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Ahimelech, the son of Abiathar, was a priest who served during the reign of King David. He is mentioned alongside Zadok, another prominent priest, suggesting that they held important positions in the priestly hierarchy. (2Sa.8.17; 1Ch.18.16 In the context of organizing the priestly divisions, Ahimelech is listed among the descendants of Ithamar, one of Aaron's sons). The priests were divided into groups to carry out their duties in the tabernacle and later in the temple. (1Ch.24.3,6). Ahimelech's father, Abiathar, had a significant role in David's life, supporting him during his flight from Saul and later serving as a priest and advisor to David. (1Sa.22.20-23; 2Sa.15.24-29 Although not much is recorded about Ahimelech's specific actions, his position as a priest during David's reign indicates that he played a role in the religious life of Israel and in serving the king).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.17 son of Abiathar; brother of JonathanI); called Ahimelech (אֲחִימֶ֫לֶךְ); or Ahimelech (אֲבִימֶ֫לֶךְ)
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 제사장. 2Sa.8.17에 처음 언급되며 '아히멜렉'이라 불림. 아비아달의 아들. 요나단의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아비아달의 아들 아히멜렉은 다윗 왕 시대에 제사장으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite descendant of Kohath, son of Elkanah
persons.short: Ahimoth, also known as Mahath, was a Levite descended from Kohath, the son of Elkanah.
persons.article: Ahimoth, also referred to as Mahath, is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites, specifically in the lineage of Kohath. He was the son of Elkanah, who was a descendant of Kohath, one of the three sons of Levi. (1Ch.6.25,35 The Kohathites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the Gershonites and Merarites). They were responsible for the care and transportation of the most sacred items in the tabernacle, including the Ark of the Covenant, the table of showbread, the lampstand, and the altars. (Num.3.27-32 Ahimoth's mention in the genealogy highlights the importance of the Levitical lineage and their roles in serving in the tabernacle and later in the temple). However, no specific details about Ahimoth's life or duties are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.25 referred to as Ahimoth (אֲחִימוֹת), or Mahath (מַ֫חַת); a son of Amasai; father of Elkanah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.25에 처음 언급되며 '아히못'이라 불림. 아마새의 아들. 엘가나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아히못(마핫이라고도 함)은 엘가나의 아들 고핫 계열의 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Iddo, a governor under Solomon
persons.short: Ahinadab, the son of Iddo, was one of Solomon's twelve governors, responsible for providing provisions for the king's household.
persons.article: Ahinadab, the son of Iddo, is mentioned briefly in the context of King Solomon's administration. He was one of the twelve governors appointed by Solomon to oversee the twelve districts of Israel. Each governor was responsible for providing provisions for the king's household for one month out of the year. (1Ki.4.7 Ahinadab was assigned to the district of Mahanaim, a region east of the Jordan River. )(1Ki.4.14 His role as a governor involved ensuring that the necessary supplies were collected and delivered to the royal court during his assigned month). The appointment of governors over districts was part of Solomon's strategy to organize his kingdom efficiently and to ensure a steady supply of resources for the royal household.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.14 only referred to as Ahinadab (אֲחִינָדָב); a son of Iddo.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.14에 처음 언급되며 '아히나답'이라 불림. 잇도의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 잇도의 아들 아히나답은 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 한 사람으로, 왕실에 필요한 양식을 공급하는 책임을 맡았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Malchi-shua@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Merab@1Sa.14.49-2Sa, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch
persons.brief: Wife of King Saul, daughter of Ahimaaz
persons.short: Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz, was one of King Saul's wives.
persons.article: Ahinoam is mentioned briefly in the Bible as one of the wives of King Saul, the first king of Israel. She was the daughter of Ahimaaz, but no further information is provided about her father. (1Sa.14.50 Saul had two wives mentioned in the biblical text: Ahinoam and Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. )(2Sa.3.7 Ahinoam was the mother of several of Saul's children, including his eldest son Jonathan, who became a close friend of David. )(1Sa.14.49 Despite her status as the wife of the king, little is recorded about Ahinoam's life or her role in the royal court). The biblical narrative focuses primarily on Saul's reign, his conflicts with David, and his eventual downfall. The mention of Ahinoam in the genealogy of Saul's family establishes her as an important figure in the royal lineage, although her personal character and influence are not elaborated upon in the Bible.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.14.50 only referred to as Ahinoam (אֲחִינֹ֫עַם); a daughter of Ahimaaz; wife of Saul; mother of Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchi-shua, Merab, Ish-bosheth and Michal.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Sa.14.50에 처음 언급되며 '아히노암'이라 불림. 아히마아스의 딸. 사울의 아내. 요나단, 아비나답, 말기수아, 메랍, 미갈과 이스보셋의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아히마아스의 딸 아히노암은 사울 왕의 아내 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of David, from Jezreel; mother of Amnon
persons.short: Ahinoam of Jezreel was one of David's wives and the mother of his firstborn son, Amnon.
persons.article: Ahinoam of Jezreel was one of the wives of King David. She became David's wife after he fled from King Saul and settled in the wilderness of Paran. (1Sa.25.43 Ahinoam accompanied David during his time in Ziklag, a city given to him by Achish, the king of Gath. )(1Sa.27.3 When the Amalekites raided Ziklag and took captive the women and children, including Ahinoam, David pursued the raiders and rescued all who had been captured. )(1Sa.30.5,18). After Saul's death, David and his wives, including Ahinoam, moved to Hebron, where David was anointed king over Judah. (2Sa.2.2-4 Ahinoam gave birth to David's firstborn son, Amnon, in Hebron. )(2Sa.3.2; 1Ch.3.1 As one of David's wives, Ahinoam held an important position in the royal household). However, the biblical text does not provide further details about her life or her relationship with David beyond her role as the mother of Amnon.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.25.43 only referred to as Ahinoam (אֲחִינֹ֫עַם); wife of David; mother of Amnon.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Sa.25.43에 처음 언급되며 '아히노암'이라 불림. 다윗의 아내. 암논의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 이스르엘 여인 아히노암은 다윗의 아내 중 한 사람으로, 다윗의 맏아들 암논의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Arad@1Ch.8.15, Shashak@1Ch.8.14-, Jeremoth@1Ch.8.14, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.15, Eder@1Ch.8.15, Michael@1Ch.8.16, Ishpah@1Ch.8.16, Joha@1Ch.8.16
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, a Benjamite
persons.short: Ahio was a son of Elpaal and a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Ahio is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He was a son of Beriah, son of Elpaal, who was a descendant of Benjamin through his son Shaharaim. (1Ch.8.8-14 The genealogy lists several of Elpaal's family, including Ahio, but does not provide any additional information about their lives or roles within the tribe). The purpose of the genealogy is to trace the lineage of significant Benjamite families and individuals. As a member of the tribe of Benjamin, Ahio would have been part of the Israelite community, but the biblical text does not record any specific events or contributions associated with him.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.14 only referred to as Ahio (אַחְיוֹ); son of Beriah; a brother of Arad, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Eder, Michael, Ishpah and Joha.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.8.14에 처음 언급되며 '아히요'라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 아랏, 사삭, 여레못, 스바댜, 에델, 미가엘, 이스바와 요하의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히오는 베냐민의 후손인 엘바알의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Abdon@1Ch.8.30-, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Baal@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Zecher@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-
persons.brief: Son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), a Benjamite
persons.short: Ahio was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), a Benjamite who was the re-founder of Gibeon.
persons.article: Ahio is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), who was the father or re-founder of Gibeon. Abiel (or 'Jeiel') and his wife Maakah had several children, including Ahio. (1Ch.8.29-31; 9.35-37) The genealogies in 1Chronicles 8 and 9 provide a detailed record of the Benjamite families who lived in Gibeon, a city located north of Jerusalem. These chapters aim to establish the lineage and settlement of the Benjamites in the post-exilic period. Apart from being listed among Jeiel's sons, no further information is given about Ahio's life, occupation, or role within the Benjamite community in Gibeon. His mention in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and the population of Gibeon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.31 only referred to as Ahio (אַחְיוֹ); son of Abiel and Maacah; a brother of Kish, Ner, Abdon, Zur, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Zecher and Mikloth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.31에 처음 언급되며 '아히오'라 불림. 아비엘과 마아가의 아들. 기스, 넬, 압돈, 술, 바알, 나답, 그돌, 세겔과 미글롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히오는 기브온을 재건한 베냐민 사람 아비엘(여이엘)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Abinadab, accompanied the ark from Kiriath-jearim
persons.short: Ahio, along with his brother Uzzah, drove the cart carrying the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
persons.article: Ahio was the son of Abinadab, in whose house the ark of God had been kept for many years after it was returned by the Philistines. When David decided to bring the ark to Jerusalem, Ahio and his brother Uzzah were tasked with transporting it. They placed the ark on a new cart, with Uzzah walking alongside the ark and Ahio going before it. (2Sa.6.3,4; 1Ch.13.7 However, during the journey, when the oxen stumbled, Uzzah reached out to steady the ark and was struck down by God for his irreverent act. )(2Sa.6.6-7; 1Ch.13.9-10 The biblical text does not mention Ahio's reaction to his brother's death or provide any further details about his life). His role in the story is primarily as one of the two men entrusted with the responsibility of transporting the ark, which highlights the importance and sacredness of the ark in Israelite worship.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.6.3 only referred to as Ahio (אַחְיוֹ); son of Abinadab; a brother of Eleazar and Uzzah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.6.3에 처음 언급되며 '아효'라 불림. 아비나답의 아들. 엘르아살과 웃사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아히오는 그의 형제 웃사와 함께 기럇여아림에서 하나님의 궤를 실은 수레를 몰았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Exodus
persons.short: Ahira, son of Enan, was the leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.
persons.article: Ahira, the son of Enan, was a prominent leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Israelites' exodus from Egypt and their subsequent journey through the wilderness. He was appointed by God as the head of his tribe and played a significant role in the organization and leadership of the Israelite community. (Num.1.15 In the arrangement of the Israelite camp, Ahira and the tribe of Naphtali were positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Dan and Asher. )(Num.2.29). As a tribal leader, Ahira was responsible for presenting the offerings of the tribe of Naphtali during the dedication of the altar. He brought his offering on the twelfth day, which included various silver and gold utensils, as well as animals for sacrifices. (Num.7.78,83 When the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai, Ahira and the tribe of Naphtali were part of the rearguard, marching last among the tribal divisions. )(Num.10.27 Throughout the wilderness journey, Ahira would have played a crucial role in leading his tribe, ensuring their obedience to God's commands, and representing their interests before Moses and the other tribal leaders). However, no further specific details about his life or leadership are recorded in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.15 only referred to as Ahira (אֲחִירַע); a son of Enan.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.15에 처음 언급되며 '아히라'라 불림. 에난의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 에난의 아들 아히라는 이스라엘 백성이 광야를 지나는 동안 납달리 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Bela@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Becher@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ashbel@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Naaman@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Muppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Huppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ard@Gen.46.21, Jediael@1Ch.7.6-
persons.brief: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ahiramite clan
persons.short: Ahiram, also known as Aharah or Ehi, was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ahiramite clan.
persons.article: Ahiram, also referred to as Aharah or Ehi, was one of the sons of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin, which trace the lineage of the Israelites after their exodus from Egypt. In the census taken in the wilderness, the descendants of Ahiram are listed as the Ahiramite clan, indicating that he was the founder of this Benjamite family. (Num.26.38 The variations in his name )(Aharah in 1Ch.8.1 and Ehi in Gen.46.21 may be due to different traditions or textual transmissions). However, all three names refer to the same individual, a son of Benjamin. Apart from being mentioned in the genealogies, no further details about Ahiram's life or specific role within the tribe of Benjamin are provided in the biblical text. His significance lies in his place in the family line of Benjamin and his role as the progenitor of the Ahiramite clan.
