persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 이스마엘 사람. 2Sa.17.25에 처음 언급되며 '아마사'라 불림. 예델과 아비가일의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 예델과 다윗의 누이 아비가일의 아들 아마사는 압살롬 밑에서 군 지휘관으로 섬기다가 후에 다윗을 섬겼으나 요압에게 죽임을 당했다.
persons.article_ko: 아마사는 이스마엘 사람 이델의 아들이며 다윗 왕의 누이 아비가일의 아들이었다. 그는 다윗의 군 지휘관 요압의 사촌이었다(삼하 17:25; 대상 2:17). 압살롬이 다윗을 대적하여 반역하는 동안 아마사는 압살롬 군대의 지휘관으로 임명되었다(삼하 17:25). 압살롬이 패하여 죽은 후 다윗은 반역 세력들과 화해하고자 요압을 대신하여 아마사에게 자기 군대의 지휘관 자리를 제안했다(삼하 19:13). 그러나 다윗이 아마사에게 세바가 이끄는 반역을 진압하기 위해 유다 사람들을 소집하라고 명령했을 때 아마사는 정해진 시간보다 오래 걸렸다. 그러자 다윗은 아비새를 보내 세바를 추격하게 했고, 요압과 그의 부하들이 뒤따랐다(삼하 20:4-7). 아마사가 그들을 따라잡았을 때 요압은 그를 맞이하는 척하며 다가갔으나 대신 칼로 그를 죽였다. 요압은 그런 다음 세바 추격을 계속했다(삼하 20:8-13). 요압의 아마사 살해는 아마 시기심과 다윗의 군 지휘관으로서 자신의 지위를 유지하려는 욕망에서 비롯되었을 것이다. 그러나 다윗은 이 행위를 배신으로 여겼고 후에 아들 솔로몬에게 아마사와 아브넬의 죽음에 대해 요압에게 심판을 내리라고 지시했다(왕상 2:5-6). 아마사의 이야기는 다윗 가족과 그의 왕국 내의 복잡한 관계와 권력 다툼을 보여준다. 그것은 또한 왕궁 안에서 충성, 배신, 권력을 위한 투쟁의 결과를 보여준다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Chief of thirty who joined David
persons.short: Amasai, a chief of thirty mighty men, joined David at Ziklag while he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Amasai was a chief of thirty mighty men who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. When David was in the wilderness, a group of men came to him, and the Spirit came upon Amasai, who was their leader. Amasai pledged his allegiance to David, saying, "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Success, success to you, and success to those who help you, for your God will help you." David received them and made them leaders of his troops.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.18 only referred to as Amasai (עֲמָשַׂי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.18에 처음 언급되며 '아마새'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삼십 용사의 우두머리 아마새는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest who blew the trumpet
persons.short: Amasai, a priest, was among those who blew the trumpet when the Ark of the Covenant was brought to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Amasai was a priest who participated in the procession when the Ark of the Covenant was brought to Jerusalem during the reign of King David. He was one of the priests who blew the trumpet during this solemn and joyous occasion. The blowing of trumpets was a significant part of religious ceremonies and celebrations in ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.15.24 only referred to as Amasai (עֲמָשַׂי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.24에 처음 언급되며 '아미새'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 아마새는 언약궤가 예루살렘으로 옮겨질 때 나팔을 분 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite descendant of Kohath
persons.short: Amasai, a Levite descended from Kohath, was an ancestor of the prophet Samuel.
persons.article: Amasai was a Levite who belonged to the Kohathite clan. He was a descendant of Kohath, the son of Levi. Amasai is mentioned in the genealogy of the prophet Samuel, indicating that he was one of Samuel's ancestors. As a Levite, Amasai would have been involved in the religious duties and services in the tabernacle or temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.25 only referred to as Amasai (עֲמָשַׂי); a son of Elkanah; father of Ahimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.25에 처음 언급되며 '아마새'라 불림. 엘가나의 아들. 아히못의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 아마새는 고핫의 후손으로, 선지자 사무엘의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped purify the temple
persons.short: Amasai, a Levite of the sons of Merari, helped purify the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Amasai was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari. During the reign of King Hezekiah, when the temple was being purified and restored, Amasai was one of the Levites who participated in this important task. The purification of the temple was a significant event in Hezekiah's religious reforms, as he sought to restore proper worship and eliminate idolatry in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12 only referred to as Amasai (עֲמָשַׂי); father of Mahath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12에 처음 언급되며 '아마새'라 불림. 마핫의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므라리 자손 레위인 아마새는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Commander who volunteered for God's service
persons.short: Amasiah, the son of Zichri, was a commander who willingly offered himself for the service of the Lord during the reign of King Jehoshaphat.
persons.article: Amasiah was the son of Zichri and served as a commander during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He is described as a man who willingly offered himself for the service of the Lord. This suggests that Amasiah was a devoted follower of God and was committed to serving Him faithfully. As a commander, Amasiah likely played a significant role in Jehoshaphat's army and in the defense of the kingdom of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.16 only referred to as Amasiah (עֲמַסְיָה); a son of Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.16에 처음 언급되며 '아마시야'라 불림. 시그리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 시그리의 아들 아마시야는 여호사밧 왕 시대에 자원하여 여호와를 섬긴 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite, son of Joshah
persons.short: Amaziah, the son of Joshah, was a descendant of Simeon.
persons.article: Amaziah was a descendant of Simeon, the son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He was the son of Joshah and is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.34 only referred to as Amaziah (אֲמַצְיָ֫הוּ); father of Joshah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.34에 처음 언급되며 '아마샤'라 불림. 요사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요사의 아들 아마샤는 시므온의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite, son of Hilkiah
persons.short: Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah, was a Levite of the family of Merari during the time of David.
persons.article: Amaziah was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari. He was the son of Hilkiah and lived during the reign of King David. As a Levite, Amaziah would have been involved in the religious duties and services in the tabernacle or temple. The Merarites were responsible for the tabernacle's structural components, such as its frames, crossbars, posts, and bases.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.45 only referred to as Amaziah (אֲמַצְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Hilkiah; father of Hashabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.45에 처음 언급되며 '아마샤'라 불림. 힐기야의 아들. 하사뱌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 힐기야의 아들 아마샤는 다윗 시대 므라리 가문의 레위인이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Joash
persons.short: Amaziah, son of Joash, was the ninth king of Judah who reigned for 29 years.
persons.article: Amaziah was the son of Joash and the ninth king of Judah. He began his reign at the age of 25 and reigned for 29 years in Jerusalem. Amaziah did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, but not wholeheartedly like his ancestor David. He executed the officials who had murdered his father, but spared their children in obedience to the law of Moses. Amaziah also defeated the Edomites in battle, capturing Sela and renaming it Joktheel. However, he later challenged King Jehoash of Israel to battle and was defeated, resulting in the plundering of the temple and palace in Jerusalem. Amaziah outlived Jehoash by 15 years. He was eventually conspired against and killed in Lachish, and his son Uzziah succeeded him as king.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.12.21 referred to as Amaziah (אֲמַצְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Joash and Jehoaddan; husband of Jecoliah; father of Uzziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.12.21에 처음 언급되며 '아마샤'라 불림. 요아스와 여호앗단의 아들. 여골리아의 남편. 웃시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아스의 아들 아마샤는 유다의 아홉째 왕으로 이십구 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 아마샤는 요아스의 아들이며 유다의 아홉 번째 왕이었다. 그는 이십오 세에 통치를 시작하여 예루살렘에서 이십구 년간 다스렸다. 아마샤는 여호와 보시기에 정직한 것을 행했으나 그의 조상 다윗처럼 온전한 마음으로는 아니었다. 그는 자기 아버지를 살해한 관리들을 처형했으나, 모세의 율법에 순종하여 그들의 자녀들은 살려주었다. 아마샤는 또한 전투에서 에돔 사람들을 물리치고 셀라를 점령하여 욕드엘이라 개명했다. 그러나 그는 후에 이스라엘 왕 요아스에게 싸움을 걸었다가 패배하여 예루살렘의 성전과 왕궁이 약탈당했다. 아마샤는 요아스보다 십오 년을 더 살았다. 그는 결국 라기스에서 반역 음모로 죽임을 당했고, 그의 아들 웃시야가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest of Bethel during Amos' ministry
persons.short: Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, opposed the prophet Amos and told him to leave the kingdom of Israel.
persons.article: Amaziah was a priest who served at the sanctuary in Bethel during the reign of Jeroboam II, king of Israel. When the prophet Amos came to Bethel and prophesied against the kingdom of Israel, Amaziah opposed him. He sent a message to King Jeroboam, accusing Amos of conspiracy and claiming that the land could not bear his words. Amaziah also told Amos to flee to the land of Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy there, but not to prophesy anymore at Bethel, as it was the king's sanctuary and a temple of the kingdom. Amos responded by affirming that he was not a professional prophet, but a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs, and that the Lord had called him to prophesy to Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Amo.7.10 only referred to as Amaziah (אֲמַצְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Amo.7.10에 처음 언급되며 '아마샤'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 벧엘의 제사장 아마샤는 선지자 아모스를 대적하며 이스라엘 땅을 떠나라고 말했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Family of Solomon's servants
persons.short: The descendants of Ami (or Amon) were among the returned exiles who were servants of Solomon.
persons.article: Ami, also known as Amon, was the head of a family whose descendants were among the returned exiles from Babylon. They were listed among the servants of Solomon, suggesting that their ancestors had been assigned by King Solomon to perform specific duties or services. The descendants of Ami were part of the group that returned to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel, as recorded in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah. They likely played a role in the rebuilding of the temple and the restoration of Jewish worship in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.57 referred to as Ami (אָמִי), or Amon (אָמוֹן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.57에 처음 언급되며 '아미'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아미(또는 아몬)의 후손은 솔로몬의 종이었던 포로 귀환자 명단에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of the prophet Jonah
persons.short: Amittai was the father of Jonah, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
persons.article: Amittai was the father of the prophet Jonah, who was from Gath-hepher in the region of Zebulun. Jonah, the son of Amittai, prophesied during the reign of Jeroboam II, king of Israel. He predicted that Jeroboam would restore the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, which came to pass according to the word of the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.14.25 only referred to as Amittai (אֲמִתַּי); father of Jonah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.14.25에 처음 언급되며 '아밋대'라 불림. 요나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아밋대는 가드헤벨 출신 선지자 요나의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Shemaiah@1Ch.26.4-, Jehozabad@1Ch.26.4, Joah@1Ch.26.4, Sachar@1Ch.26.4, Nethanel@1Ch.26.4, Issachar@1Ch.26.5, Peullethai@1Ch.26.5
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign
persons.short: Ammiel was a Levite gatekeeper during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Ammiel was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper during the reign of King David. He is mentioned in the context of the organization of the gatekeepers, who were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple. Ammiel was among the Levites appointed to this important role, ensuring the security and sanctity of the house of the Lord.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.5 only referred to as Ammiel (עַמִּיאֵל); son of Obed-edom; a brother of Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Issachar and Peullethai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.5에 처음 언급되며 '암미엘'이라 불림. 오벧에돔의 아들. 스마야, 여호사밧, 요아, 사갈, 느다넬, 잇사갈과 브울래대의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 암미엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 문지기로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Machir, David's ally
persons.short: Ammiel was the father of Machir, who provided assistance to David during his flight from Absalom.
persons.article: Ammiel was the father of Machir, a man from Lo-debar who played a significant role in the life of King David. When David inquired about the whereabouts of Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, he was told that Mephibosheth was living in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar. Later, during Absalom's rebellion, when David fled from Jerusalem, Machir, along with Shobi and Barzillai, brought supplies to David and his people, including beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, curds, sheep, and cheese.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.9.4 only referred to as Ammiel (עַמִּיאֵל); father of Machir.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '암미엘'이라 불림. 마길의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미엘은 다윗이 압살롬을 피해 도망할 때 그를 도운 마길의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Spy from the tribe of Dan
persons.short: Ammiel, the son of Gemalli, was the representative from the tribe of Dan among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Ammiel, the son of Gemalli, was a member of the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. When Moses sent twelve spies to explore the land of Canaan, one from each tribe, Ammiel was chosen to represent the tribe of Dan. He was among the group that spent forty days scouting the land and brought back a report to Moses, Aaron, and the entire congregation of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.12 only referred to as Ammiel (עַמִּיאֵל); a son of Gemalli.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.12에 처음 언급되며 '암미엘'이라 불림. 그말리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 그말리의 아들 암미엘은 모세가 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 명 중 단 지파 대표였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem
persons.short: Ammihud, a descendant of Judah, was among those who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Ammihud was a descendant of Judah mentioned in the genealogical records of those who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is listed among the descendants of Perez, one of the sons of Judah. The record in 1Chronicles 9 provides insight into the resettlement of Jerusalem following the return from exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.4 only referred to as Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד); a son of Omri; father of Uthai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '암미훗'이라 불림. 오므리의 아들. 우대의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유다의 후손 암미훗은 포로 귀환 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Talmai, king of Geshur
persons.short: Ammihud (or Ammihur) was the father of Talmai, the king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after killing his brother Amnon.
persons.article: Ammihud, also known as Ammihur, was the father of Talmai, the king of Geshur. After Absalom, the son of King David, killed his brother Amnon, he fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. Absalom stayed with Talmai for three years before returning to Jerusalem. Geshur was a small Aramean kingdom located northeast of the Sea of Galilee.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.13.37 referred to as Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד), or Ammihur (עַמִּיהוּד); father of Talmai, king of Geshur.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.13.37에 처음 언급되며 '암미훗'이라 불림. 달매의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗(암미훌이라고도 함)은 압살롬이 형제 암논을 죽인 후 도망간 그술 왕 달매의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Elishama, leader of Ephraim
persons.short: Ammihud was the father of Elishama, the leader of the tribe of Ephraim during the wilderness journey.
persons.article: Ammihud was an Ephraimite, the father of Elishama, who was a prominent leader during the Israelites' wilderness journey. Elishama, the son of Ammihud, was the leader of the people of Ephraim and one of the tribal chiefs who assisted Moses in the census of the Israelites. He was also in charge of the camp of Ephraim, which included the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin. Additionally, Elishama presented the offering of the tribe of Ephraim during the dedication of the tabernacle. Ammihud is also mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim in the book of Chronicles.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.10 only referred to as Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד); a son of Ladan; father of Elishama.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '암미훗'이라 불림. 라단의 아들. 엘리사마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗은 광야 시절 에브라임 지파 지도자였던 엘리사마의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Shemuel, leader from Simeon
persons.short: Ammihud was the father of Shemuel, the leader from the tribe of Simeon appointed to help divide the land of Canaan.
persons.article: Ammihud was the father of Shemuel, a leader from the tribe of Simeon. When the Lord commanded Moses to appoint leaders from each tribe to help divide the land of Canaan among the Israelites, Shemuel son of Ammihud was chosen to represent the tribe of Simeon in this important task.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.20 only referred to as Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד); father of Shemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.20에 처음 언급되며 '암미훗'이라 불림. 스므엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗은 가나안 땅 분배를 돕도록 임명된 시므온 지파 지도자 스무엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Pedahel, leader from Naphtali
persons.short: Ammihud was the father of Pedahel, the leader from the tribe of Naphtali appointed to help divide the land of Canaan.
persons.article: Ammihud was the father of Pedahel, a leader from the tribe of Naphtali. Pedahel son of Ammihud was selected by the Lord to be the representative from Naphtali who would assist in dividing the land of Canaan among the Israelite tribes. This was a significant responsibility, as it involved ensuring a fair distribution of the Promised Land.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.28 only referred to as Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד); father of Pedahel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.28에 처음 언급되며 '암미훗'이라 불림. 브다헬의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗은 가나안 땅 분배를 돕도록 임명된 납달리 지파 지도자 브다헬의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite leader during the Ark's transfer
persons.short: Amminadab was a Levite leader from the Uzzielite clan who participated in the transfer of the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Amminadab was a Levite leader who belonged to the clan of Uzziel. During the reign of King David, when the Ark of the Covenant was being brought to Jerusalem, Amminadab was one of the Levites appointed to oversee the transportation of the Ark. He, along with his relatives, was sanctified to carry out this sacred task, ensuring that the Ark was handled with the utmost reverence and care.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.10 only referred to as Amminadab (עַמִּינָדָב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.10에 처음 언급되며 '암미나답'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 암미나답은 웃시엘 가문 출신 레위인 지도자로, 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮기는 일에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father-in-law of Aaron, ancestor of David
persons.short: Amminadab was the father of Elisheba, who married Aaron, and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Amminadab was a prominent figure in the genealogy of the Israelites. He was the father of Elisheba, who married Aaron, the first high priest of Israel. Amminadab's son Nahshon was a leader of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness wanderings. Nahshon was in charge of the Judahite division and made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle. Amminadab is also mentioned in the genealogy of King David, being his great-great-grandfather. This makes Amminadab an ancestor of Jesus Christ as well, as seen in the genealogies recorded in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke. The consistency of Amminadab's mention in various genealogical records highlights his significance in the lineage of important biblical figures, from the time of Moses to the earthly life of Jesus.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.23 referred to as Amminadab (עַמִּינָדָב), or Amminadab (Ἀμιναδάβ); a son of Ram; father of Elisheba and Nahshon.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Exo.6.23에 처음 언급되며 '암미나답'이라 불림. 람의 아들. 엘리세바와 나손의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미나답은 아론과 결혼한 엘리세바의 아버지이며, 다윗 왕과 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Noble mentioned in a love song
persons.short: Amminadib is mentioned in a poetic passage in the Song of Solomon, possibly referring to a noble or prince.
persons.article: Amminadib is a name that appears in the Song of Solomon, a poetic book in the Old Testament. The context suggests that Amminadib may have been a noble or prince, but the exact identity of this individual is not clear. The passage in which Amminadib is mentioned is part of a love song, and the reference to this person is likely symbolic or metaphorical, rather than a historical figure.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at Sng.6.12 only referred to as Amminadib (עַמִּי נָדִיב).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Sng.6.12에 처음 언급되며 '암미나디브'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 암미나딥은 아가서의 한 시적인 구절에서 언급되는데, 아마 귀족이나 왕자를 가리키는 것으로 보인다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Ahiezer, leader of Dan
persons.short: Ammishaddai was the father of Ahiezer, the leader of the tribe of Dan during the wilderness journey.
persons.article: Ammishaddai was the father of Ahiezer, a prominent leader from the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, was appointed as the leader of the Danites and was responsible for overseeing the census of his tribe. He also led the tribe of Dan when the Israelites were encamped and during their journey. Additionally, Ahiezer presented the offering of the tribe of Dan at the dedication of the tabernacle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.12 only referred to as Ammishaddai (עַמִּישַׁדָּ֑י); father of Ahiezer.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.12에 처음 언급되며 '암미삿대'라 불림. 아히에셀의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암미삿대는 광야 시절 단 지파 지도자였던 아히에셀의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Ammizabad was the son of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men, and served as his father's second-in-command.
persons.article: Ammizabad was the son of Benaiah, one of King David's mighty men and the commander of his bodyguard. Benaiah was a valiant warrior known for his heroic deeds. Ammizabad served as his father's second-in-command, assisting him in his duties and responsibilities. This suggests that Ammizabad was also a skilled and trusted military leader, following in his father's footsteps.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.6 only referred to as Ammizabad (עַמִּיזָבָד); a son of Benaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.27.6에 처음 언급되며 '암미사밧'이라 불림. 브나야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 암미사밧은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 브나야의 아들로, 아버지의 부관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shimon, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Amnon was a son of Shimon and a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Amnon was a descendant of Judah through his son Shimon. He is mentioned in the genealogical record of the tribe of Judah in 1Chronicles 4.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.20 only referred to as Amnon (אַמְנוֹן); son of Shimon; a brother of Rinnah, Ben-hanan , Tilon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.20에 처음 언급되며 '암논'이라 불림. 시몬의 아들. 린나, 벤하난과 딜론의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 암논은 유다의 후손인 시몬의 아들이었다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: David's firstborn son, killed by Absalom
persons.short: Amnon, David's firstborn son, raped his half-sister Tamar and was later killed by her brother Absalom.
persons.article: Amnon was the firstborn son of King David, born to him in Hebron. His mother was Ahinoam of Jezreel. Amnon is primarily known for his infamous act of raping his half-sister Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. After the incident, Amnon's love for Tamar turned to hatred, and he sent her away in shame. Absalom, enraged by Amnon's actions, waited two years before exacting revenge. He invited Amnon to a sheep-shearing feast and had his servants kill Amnon when he was drunk. This led to a rift between Absalom and his father, David, and ultimately to Absalom's rebellion against the king. The story of Amnon highlights the tragic consequences of sexual violence and the far-reaching effects it can have on families and relationships.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.2 only referred to as Amnon (אַמְנוֹן); a son of David and Ahinoam; half-brother of: Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.3.2에 처음 언급되며 '암논'이라 불림. 다윗과 아히노암의 아들. 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다윗의 맏아들 암논은 이복누이 다말을 범하였고, 후에 그녀의 오라비 압살롬에게 죽임을 당했다.
persons.article_ko: 암논은 다윗 왕의 맏아들로, 헤브론에서 그에게 태어났다. 그의 어머니는 이스르엘 사람 아히노암이었다. 암논은 주로 압살롬의 자매인 이복누이 다말을 강간한 악명 높은 행위로 알려져 있다. 그 사건 이후 다말에 대한 암논의 사랑은 미움으로 변했고, 그는 그녀를 수치스럽게 내쫓았다. 암논의 행동에 격분한 압살롬은 복수를 하기까지 이 년을 기다렸다. 그는 암논을 양털 깎는 잔치에 초대하여 그가 취했을 때 자기 종들에게 그를 죽이게 했다. 이는 압살롬과 그의 아버지 다윗 사이의 균열로 이어졌고, 결국 왕을 대적하는 압살롬의 반역으로 이어졌다. 암논의 이야기는 성적 폭력의 비극적인 결과와 그것이 가족과 관계에 미칠 수 있는 광범위한 영향을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Amok was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and signed the covenant under Nehemiah.
persons.article: Amok was a priest who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the list of priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Later, during the time of Nehemiah, Amok is recorded as one of the priests who signed the covenant to follow the Law of God and to keep themselves separate from the neighboring peoples.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.12.7 only referred to as Amok (עָמוֹק).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.7에 처음 언급되며 '아목'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아목은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아와 느헤미야의 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Governor of Samaria during Ahab's reign
persons.short: Amon was the governor of Samaria during the reign of King Ahab of Israel.
persons.article: Amon was the governor of the city of Samaria during the reign of King Ahab of Israel. When the prophet Micaiah prophesied against Ahab, the king ordered Amon to put Micaiah in prison and feed him only bread and water until Ahab returned safely from battle. This event demonstrates Ahab's rejection of the true prophetic message and his preference for the false prophets who spoke favorably of him.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.26 only referred to as Amon (אָמוֹן).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.22.26에 처음 언급되며 '아몬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아몬은 이스라엘 왕 아합 시대에 사마리아의 성주였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Manasseh
persons.short: Amon, the son of Manasseh, was the 15th king of Judah who reigned for two years before being assassinated by his servants.
persons.article: Amon was the son of Manasseh and the 15th king of Judah. He began his reign at the age of 22 and ruled for two years in Jerusalem. Amon followed the evil practices of his father Manasseh, worshiping idols and doing what was evil in the sight of the Lord. He did not humble himself before the Lord as his father had done. Amon's servants conspired against him and assassinated him in his palace. However, the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place. Amon was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. The prophets Jeremiah and Zephaniah began their ministries during the reign of Josiah, Amon's son. Amon is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.21.18 referred to as Amon (אָמוֹן), or Amon (Ἀμών), or Amos (Ἀμώς); a son of Manasseh and Meshullemeth; husband of Jedidah; father of Josiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.21.18에 처음 언급되며 '아몬'이라 불림. 므낫세와 므술레멧의 아들. 여디다의 남편. 요시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므낫세의 아들 아몬은 유다의 열다섯째 왕으로 이 년간 다스리다가 신하들에게 암살당했다.
persons.article_ko: 아몬은 므낫세의 아들이며 유다의 열다섯 번째 왕이었다. 그는 이십이 세에 통치를 시작하여 예루살렘에서 이 년간 다스렸다. 아몬은 자기 아버지 므낫세의 악한 관행을 따라 우상을 숭배하며 여호와 보시기에 악을 행했다. 그는 자기 아버지가 그랬던 것처럼 여호와 앞에서 스스로를 겸비하게 하지 않았다. 아몬의 신하들이 그를 대적하여 음모를 꾸며 그의 왕궁에서 그를 암살했다. 그러나 그 땅의 백성은 아몬 왕을 대적하여 음모를 꾸민 자들을 모두 죽였고, 그의 아들 요시야를 대신하여 왕으로 세웠다. 아몬은 웃사의 동산에 있는 자기 무덤에 묻혔다. 선지자 예레미야와 스바냐는 아몬의 아들 요시야의 통치 기간에 사역을 시작했다. 아몬은 또한 마태복음의 예수 그리스도 족보에도 언급된다.

persons.description: People from Amor(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Canaanite people group, enemies of Israel
persons.short: The Amorites were a Canaanite people group who lived in the hill country and were among the enemies the Israelites faced when entering the Promised Land.
persons.article: The Amorites were one of the Canaanite peoples who inhabited the land promised to the Israelites. They are first mentioned in the Table of Nations as descendants of Canaan, the son of Ham. The Amorites lived in the hill country and were known for their military prowess. During the time of Abraham, the Amorites were one of the groups living in Canaan. God promised Abraham that his descendants would inherit the land when the iniquity of the Amorites reached its full measure. When the Israelites left Egypt and approached the Promised Land, the Amorites were among the peoples they were told to dispossess. The Amorite kings Sihon and Og, who ruled over the territories east of the Jordan River, were defeated by the Israelites under Moses' leadership. After the conquest of Canaan under Joshua, the Amorites were among the groups that the Israelites failed to completely drive out. They remained a significant presence in the land, often oppressing the Israelites during the time of the judges. The Amorites are mentioned throughout the historical books of the Old Testament as one of the primary enemies of Israel. Their presence in the land was a result of the Israelites' disobedience to God's command to completely remove them. The prophets Ezekiel and Amos also refer to the Amorites, using them as an example of the wickedness that Israel had adopted. The complete destruction of the Amorites was a sign of God's judgment against their sinful practices.
persons.summary: A person from Amor(?), first mentioned at Gen.10.16 only referred to as Amorites (אֱמֹרִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 아모리 족속. Gen.10.16에 처음 언급되며 '아모리'라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓, 스말과 하맛의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 아모리 족속은 산지에 살던 가나안 족속으로, 이스라엘이 약속의 땅에 들어갈 때 맞선 대적 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet from Tekoa who prophesied to Israel
persons.short: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, called by God as a prophet to Israel.
persons.article: Amos was a prophet from Tekoa who prophesied during the reigns of Uzziah, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel (Amo.1.1). He was originally a shepherd and fig grower before being called by God to deliver His message (Amo.7.14-15). Amos prophesied against the sins of Israel, warning them of impending judgment (Amo.7.8; 8.2). His prophecies were met with opposition from Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, who told him to stop prophesying and leave (Amo.7.10-13). However, Amos remained faithful to his calling and continued to proclaim God's word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Amo.1.1 only referred to as Amos (עָמוֹס).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Amo.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '아모스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드고아 출신 목자 아모스는 하나님의 부르심을 받아 이스라엘의 선지자가 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Naum in Jesus' genealogy
persons.short: Amos, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Naum.
persons.article: Amos is mentioned in Luk.3.25 as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in his genealogy. He was the son of Naum.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.25 only referred to as Amos (Ἀμώς); a son of Nahum; father of Mattathias.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '아모스'라 불림. 나훔의 아들. 맛다디아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아모스는 예수님의 조상으로 나훔의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Isaiah's father living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of the prophet Isaiah
persons.short: Amoz, the father of the prophet Isaiah.
persons.article: Amoz was the father of the prophet Isaiah (Isa.1.1; 2.1). He lived during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (Isa.1.1). Isaiah often mentions his father's name when introducing himself or his prophecies (Isa.2.1; 13.1; 20.2). Amoz was also mentioned in connection with the historical records of Uzziah's reign (2Ch.26.22 and Hezekiah's reign )(2Ch.32.32). His name appears in the narrative of Hezekiah's illness and recovery, as Isaiah, the son of Amoz, was sent to deliver messages from God to the king (2Ki.19.2,20; 20.1; Isa.37.2,21; 38.1).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.19.2 only referred to as Amoz (אָמוֹץ); father of Isaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 이사야의 아버지. 2Ki.19.2에 처음 언급되며 '아모스'라 불림. 이사야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아모스는 선지자 이사야의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 아모스(아모스 선지자와는 다른 인물)는 선지자 이사야의 아버지였다(사 1:1; 2:1). 그는 유다 왕 웃시야, 요담, 아하스, 히스기야 통치 기간에 살았다(사 1:1). 이사야는 자신이나 자신의 예언을 소개할 때 종종 아버지의 이름을 언급한다(사 2:1; 13:1; 20:2). 아모스는 또한 웃시야의 통치(대하 26:22)와 히스기야의 통치(대하 32:32)의 역사적 기록과 관련하여 언급된다. 그의 이름은 히스기야의 병과 회복 이야기에도 나오는데, 아모스의 아들 이사야가 왕에게 하나님의 메시지를 전달하도록 보내졌다(왕하 19:2, 20; 20:1; 사 37:2, 21; 38:1).

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer greeted by Paul in Rome
persons.short: Ampliatus, a beloved fellow believer greeted by Paul in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Ampliatus is mentioned in Rom.16.8 as a believer in Rome whom Paul greets and describes as "my beloved in the Lord." This brief mention suggests that Ampliatus was a dear friend or fellow worker of Paul and a member of the Christian community in Rome.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.8 only referred to as Ampliatus (Ἀμπλίας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.8에 처음 언급되며 '암블리아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 암블리아는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 사랑받는 동료 신자였다.

persons.description: Moses' father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
persons.short: Amram was the father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, and a member of the tribe of Levi.
persons.article: Amram was a Levite, the son of Kohath and father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam (Exo.6.18,20; Num.26.58,59; 1Ch.6.2,3; 23.12,13). He married his father's sister Jochebed (Exo.6.20). Amram's family belonged to the Kohathite branch of Levites (Num.3.19,27; 1Ch.6.18; 24.20; 26.23). As the father of Moses and Aaron, Amram played a significant role in the history of Israel, although little is recorded about his own life.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.18 referred to as Amram (עַמְרָם), or Amramite (עַמְרָמִי); son of Kohath; a brother of Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel; husband of Jochebed; father of Moses, Aaron and Miriam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 모세의 아버지. Exo.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '아므람'이라 불림. 그핫의 아들. 이스할, 헤브론과 웃시엘의 형제. 요게벳의 남편. 모세, 아론과 미리암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아므람은 모세, 아론, 미리암의 아버지이며 레위 지파에 속했다.
persons.article_ko: 아므람은 레위인으로, 고핫의 아들이며 모세, 아론, 미리암의 아버지였다(출 6:18, 20; 민 26:58-59; 대상 6:2-3; 23:12-13). 그는 아버지의 자매 요게벳과 결혼했다(출 6:20). 아므람의 가족은 레위인의 고핫 계열에 속했다(민 3:19, 27; 대상 6:18; 24:20; 26:23). 모세와 아론의 아버지로서 아므람은 이스라엘 역사에서 중요한 역할을 했지만, 그 자신의 삶에 대해서는 거의 기록되어 있지 않다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Amram was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the Exile and agreed to put her away.
persons.article: Amram is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. When Ezra called the people to repentance and to put away their foreign wives, Amram was among those who agreed to do so, demonstrating his willingness to obey God's law and maintain the purity of the Israelite community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.34 only referred to as Amram (עַמְרָם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.34에 처음 언급되며 '아므람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아므람은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그 아내를 내보내기로 동의한 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Shinar, ally of Chedorlaomer
persons.short: Amraphel, king of Shinar, was one of the four kings who joined forces with Chedorlaomer in the battle against the five kings of the Plain.
persons.article: Amraphel was the king of Shinar (Babylonia) during the time of Abraham. He was one of the four kings who formed an alliance with Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a battle against the five kings of the cities of the Plain, including Sodom and Gomorrah. The four kings, led by Chedorlaomer, emerged victorious in this conflict. Some scholars have suggested that Amraphel might be an alternate name for Hammurabi, the famous Babylonian king, but this identification remains uncertain.
persons.summary: A king in Mesopotamia living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.1 only referred to as Amraphel (אַמְרָפֶל).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '아므라벨'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 시날 왕 아므라벨은 그돌라오멜과 연합하여 평지 다섯 왕과 싸운 네 왕 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician, descendant of Merari
persons.short: Amzi, a descendant of Merari, was a Levite who served as a musician in the temple.
persons.article: Amzi was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1Chronicles 6. As a descendant of Merari, Amzi would have been responsible for the musical duties in the temple, such as singing and playing instruments during worship services.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.46 only referred to as Amzi (אַמְצִי); a son of Bani; father of Hilkiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.46에 처음 언급되며 '암시'라 불림. 바니의 아들. 힐기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므라리의 후손 암시는 성전에서 음악가로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest in Jerusalem after the Exile
persons.short: Amzi was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Amzi was a priest who resided in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the list of priests and Levites who settled in Jerusalem, as recorded in the book of Nehemiah. As a priest, Amzi would have been responsible for performing religious duties in the rebuilt temple and serving the spiritual needs of the people.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.12 only referred to as Amzi (אַמְצִי); a son of Zechariah; father of Pelaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 제사장. Neh.11.12에 처음 언급되며 '암시'라 불림. 스가랴의 아들. 블라야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암시는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Horite, father of Oholibamah, Esau's wife
persons.short: Anah was a Horite, the father of Oholibamah, one of Esau's wives, and the discoverer of hot springs in the wilderness.
persons.article: Anah was a Horite, a descendant of Seir, who lived in the land of Edom. He was the father of Oholibamah, one of Esau's wives. Anah is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau and Seir, both in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. One notable event associated with Anah is his discovery of hot springs in the wilderness while he was grazing his father's donkeys. This discovery suggests that Anah was an observant and resourceful individual. Anah is also referred to as a Hivite in one passage, which may indicate that the Horites and Hivites were related or that Anah had a connection to both groups. As the father-in-law of Esau, Anah played a role in the intermarriage between the Edomites and the Horites, which had significant implications for the history of the region.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.2 only referred to as Anah (עֲנָה); a son of Zibeon; father of Oholibamah and Dishon.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.2에 처음 언급되며 '아나'라 불림. 시브온의 아들. 아야의 형제. 디손과 오홀리바마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아나는 호리 사람으로, 에서의 아내 중 하나인 오홀리바마의 아버지이며 광야에서 온천을 발견한 자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant
persons.short: Anaiah was a priest who signed the covenant of faithfulness to God during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Anaiah was a priest who lived in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. He is listed among the priests who sealed the covenant, a solemn agreement made by the people to follow God's laws and commandments. By signing this covenant, Anaiah demonstrated his commitment to God and his willingness to lead the people in obedience to the Law. His participation in this significant event highlights his role as a spiritual leader within the priestly community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.22 only referred to as Anaiah (עֲנָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '아나야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아나야는 느헤미야 시대에 하나님께 대한 신실한 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law
persons.short: Anaiah was one of the men who stood beside Ezra when he read the Book of the Law to the people.
persons.article: Anaiah was a prominent figure during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. He is mentioned as one of the men who stood beside Ezra on the platform when the scribe read the Book of the Law to the assembled people in Jerusalem. This event took place after the completion of the city wall and marked a significant moment of spiritual renewal for the returned exiles. Anaiah's presence on the platform alongside Ezra suggests that he held a respected position within the community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Anaiah (עֲנָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '아나야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아나야는 에스라가 백성에게 율법책을 낭독할 때 그 곁에 섰던 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Ancestor of giant people in Canaan
persons.short: Anak was the ancestor of the Anakim, a race of giants who inhabited Canaan before the Israelite conquest.
persons.article: Anak was the progenitor of the Anakim, a race of giants who lived in Canaan prior to the Israelite conquest. The Anakim were known for their great height and strength, which struck fear into the hearts of the Israelite spies who were sent to scout out the land. The spies reported that the descendants of Anak were among the inhabitants of Canaan, comparing them to the Nephilim, another race of giants. During the conquest of Canaan under Joshua's leadership, the Israelites fought against the Anakim and gradually drove them out of the land. Caleb, one of the faithful spies, was given Hebron as his inheritance, which was formerly known as Kiriath-arba and was associated with Anak. Caleb successfully expelled the descendants of Anak from Hebron. The Anakim were also mentioned as having lived in the land of Moab and Edom, where they were known as Emim and Rephaim, respectively. These giant peoples were gradually displaced or destroyed by the Israelites and the surrounding nations. The memory of the Anakim and their formidable presence in Canaan served as a reminder of God's faithfulness in giving the land to His people, despite the challenges they faced.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.13.22 referred to as Anak (עֲנָק), or Anakim (עֲנָקִי); a son of Arba; father of Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.22에 처음 언급되며 '아낙'이라 불림. 아르바의 아들. 아히만, 세새와 달매의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아낙은 이스라엘이 가나안을 정복하기 전 그 땅에 살던 거인 족속 아낙 자손의 조상이었다.
persons.article_ko: 아낙은 이스라엘 정복 이전 가나안에 살던 거인 족속인 아낙 자손의 조상이었다. 아낙 자손은 그들의 큰 키와 힘으로 알려졌으며, 이는 그 땅을 정탐하러 보내진 이스라엘 정탐꾼들의 마음에 두려움을 심어주었다. 정탐꾼들은 아낙의 후손이 가나안 주민들 가운데 있다고 보고하며 그들을 또 다른 거인 족속인 네피림에 비유했다. 여호수아의 지도 아래 가나안 정복 동안 이스라엘 백성은 아낙 자손을 대적하여 싸워 점차 그들을 그 땅에서 몰아냈다. 신실한 정탐꾼 중 한 사람인 갈렙은 이전에 기럇아르바로 알려졌고 아낙과 관련이 있던 헤브론을 자기 기업으로 받았다. 갈렙은 헤브론에서 아낙의 후손을 성공적으로 쫓아냈다. 아낙 자손은 또한 모압과 에돔 땅에도 살았던 것으로 언급되는데, 그곳에서 그들은 각각 엠 족속과 르바 족속으로 알려졌다. 이 거인 민족들은 이스라엘 백성과 주변 민족들에 의해 점차 밀려나거나 멸망당했다. 아낙 자손과 가나안에서 그들의 위협적인 존재에 대한 기억은 그들이 직면한 어려움에도 불구하고 자기 백성에게 그 땅을 주시는 하나님의 신실하심에 대한 상기가 되었다.

persons.description: People from Anam(?)
persons.siblings: Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Pathrusim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Casluhim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Caphtorim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
persons.short: The Anamim were a people group descended from Mizraim, the son of Ham, and are listed among the nations in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: The Anamim were a people group mentioned in the Table of Nations, a genealogical record found in both Genesis and 1 Chronicles. They are listed as descendants of Mizraim, who was a son of Ham and grandson of Noah. The Table of Nations provides insight into the various people groups that emerged after the Flood and their geographical distribution. Little is known about the specific identity or location of the Anamim, as they are not mentioned elsewhere in the Bible. Some scholars suggest that they may have settled in the region of North Africa, possibly in the area of modern-day Libya or Tunisia, based on their association with other descendants of Mizraim. However, due to the lack of further biblical or historical evidence, the exact identity and location of the Anamim remain uncertain.
persons.summary: People from Anam(?) of the Egyptians, first mentioned at Gen.10.13 only referred to as Anamim (עֲנָמִים); descended from Egypt along with Ludim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim and Caphtorim.
persons.summary_ko: 아나밈. Gen.10.13에 처음 언급되며 '아나밈'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 루딤, 르하빔, 납두힘, 바드루심, 가슬루힘과 갑도림의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 아나밈은 함의 아들 미스라임의 후손으로, 민족 계보에 열거된 족속이다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Assyrian deity worshiped by Sepharvites
persons.short: Anammelech was an Assyrian deity worshiped by the Sepharvites, who were among the foreign peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king.
persons.article: Anammelech was an Assyrian deity mentioned in the Bible as one of the gods worshiped by the Sepharvites. The Sepharvites were a people group from the Assyrian Empire who were brought to Samaria by the Assyrian king after the deportation of the Israelites. They settled in the cities of Samaria and continued to worship their own gods, including Anammelech. The worship of Anammelech involved child sacrifice, as the Sepharvites were known to "burn their children in the fire" as part of their religious practices. This abhorrent act was strongly condemned by God and was one of the reasons for His judgment against the foreign nations who had been settled in Samaria. The name "Anammelech" is believed to mean "Anu is king" or "Anu is prince," referring to the Mesopotamian sky god Anu. This connection suggests that Anammelech may have been a local deity or a manifestation of Anu worshiped by the Sepharvites. The worship of foreign gods, including Anammelech, was a violation of God's covenant with Israel and demonstrated the syncretistic practices that led to the downfall of the Northern Kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.17.31 only referred to as Anammelech (עֲנַמֶּ֫לֶךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.17.31에 처음 언급되며 '아남멜렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아남멜렉은 앗수르 왕이 사마리아에 이주시킨 스발와임 사람들이 섬긴 신이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Signer of the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Anan was one of the leaders who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Anan is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the leaders who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. The covenant was a solemn agreement made by the people of Israel to follow God's laws and commandments faithfully. By signing the covenant, Anan demonstrated his commitment to God and his support for the spiritual and social reforms initiated by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.26 only referred to as Anan (עָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '아난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아난은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Hodaviah@1Ch.3.24, Eliashib@1Ch.3.24, Pelaiah@1Ch.3.24, Akkub@1Ch.3.24, Johanan@1Ch.3.24, Delaiah@1Ch.3.24
persons.brief: Descendant of King David
persons.short: Anani was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Anani is listed in the genealogy of King David found in 1Chronicles 3. He is mentioned as one of the descendants of David, specifically from the line of Solomon. The genealogy traces David's lineage after the Babylonian exile, indicating that Anani lived during the post-exilic period. Apart from his mention in this genealogical record, no other information is provided about Anani in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.24 only referred to as Anani (עֲנָנִי); son of Elioenai; a brother of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan and Delaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '아나니'라 불림. 에료에내의 아들. 호다위야, 엘리아십, 블라야, 악굽, 요하난과 들라야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아나니는 역대상 족보에 기록된 다윗 왕의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repairer of the wall in Jerusalem
persons.short: Ananiah made repairs to a section of the wall near his house during the rebuilding of Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership.
persons.article: Ananiah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who participated in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem. During the time of Nehemiah, the city's walls were in disrepair, leaving the inhabitants vulnerable. Nehemiah organized the people to work on different sections of the wall. Ananiah is specifically noted for making repairs to the section of the wall near his own house. His participation in this important project demonstrates his commitment to the restoration of Jerusalem and his willingness to contribute to the community's well-being.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.23 only referred to as Ananiah (עֲנַנְיָה); father of Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '아나냐'라 불림. 마아세야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아나냐는 느헤미야의 지휘 아래 예루살렘 성벽을 재건할 때 자기 집 근처 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: High priest during Paul's trial
persons.short: Ananias, the high priest, presided over Paul's trial and ordered him to be struck on the mouth for his defense.
persons.article: Ananias was the high priest during the time of Paul's trial in Jerusalem. When Paul was brought before the Sanhedrin to face accusations from the Jewish leaders, Ananias presided over the proceedings. During Paul's defense, Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth. Paul, unaware that Ananias was the high priest, rebuked him for commanding him to be struck contrary to the law. Later, when Paul was brought before Felix the governor, Ananias, along with some elders and an orator named Tertullus, presented their case against Paul, accusing him of being a troublemaker and a ringleader of the Nazarene sect.
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.23.2 only referred to as Ananias (Ἀνανίας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 대제사장. Act.23.2에 처음 언급되며 '아나니아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 대제사장 아나니아는 바울의 재판을 주재하며 그의 변론에 대해 입을 치라고 명령했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Husband of Sapphira, lied about offering proceeds
persons.short: Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, lied to the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property and faced divine judgment.
persons.article: Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, was a member of the early Christian church in Jerusalem. They sold a piece of property and brought a portion of the proceeds to the apostles, claiming it was the full amount. However, they had conspired to keep back part of the money for themselves. When confronted by the Apostle Peter about their deception, Ananias fell down and died instantly. Later, when Sapphira came in, unaware of her husband's fate, she also lied about the transaction and met the same judgment. Their story serves as a stark warning against lying and hypocrisy within the church community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.5.1 only referred to as Ananias (Ἀνανίας); husband of Sapphira.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.5.1에 처음 언급되며 '아나니아'라 불림. 삽비라의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 아나니아는 그의 아내 삽비라와 함께 재산 판 값에 대해 사도들에게 거짓말을 했다가 하나님의 심판을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Disciple in Damascus, baptized Saul (Paul)
persons.short: Ananias, a disciple in Damascus, was sent by God to heal and baptize Saul (later known as Paul) after his conversion on the road to Damascus.
persons.article: Ananias was a disciple of Jesus Christ living in Damascus. After Saul's dramatic encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus, Saul was left blind and was directed to go into the city to await further instructions. In a vision, the Lord told Ananias to go to the house where Saul was staying and lay hands on him to restore his sight. Initially hesitant due to Saul's reputation as a persecutor of the church, Ananias obeyed the Lord's command. He went to Saul, laid his hands on him, and conveyed the message that Jesus had sent him to restore Saul's sight and to fill him with the Holy Spirit. Ananias then baptized Saul, who later became known as Paul, the great apostle to the Gentiles. Ananias played a crucial role in the early days of Paul's Christian life, demonstrating faith and obedience to God's call.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.9.10 only referred to as Ananias (Ἀνανίας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.9.10에 처음 언급되며 '아나니아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다메섹의 제자 아나니아는 다메섹 도상에서 회심한 사울(후의 바울)을 고치고 세례를 주도록 하나님이 보내신 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shamgar, a judge of Israel
persons.short: Anath was the father of Shamgar, one of the judges who delivered Israel from oppression.
persons.article: Anath is mentioned in the book of Judges as the father of Shamgar, one of the judges who delivered Israel from their enemies. Shamgar, the son of Anath, is described as having killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad, which was a farming implement used to guide and control oxen. This heroic act brought deliverance to Israel during a time of oppression. Anath is also mentioned in the Song of Deborah, where it is stated that in the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, the highways were abandoned, and travelers had to take winding paths, indicating a time of insecurity and danger in Israel.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.3.31 only referred to as Anath (עֲנָת); father of Shamgar.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.3.31에 처음 언급되며 '아낫'이라 불림. 삼갈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아낫은 이스라엘을 압제에서 건져낸 사사 중 한 사람인 삼갈의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Joash@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: Son of Becher, descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Anathoth was a son of Becher and a descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Anathoth is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Chronicles 7. He is mentioned as one of the sons of Becher, who was a son of Benjamin. The genealogy provides a record of the descendants of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Anathoth, son of Becher, in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Anathoth (עֲנָתוֹת); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '아나돗'이라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 요아스, 엘리에셀, 에료에내, 오므리, 여레못, 아비야와 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아나돗은 베냐민의 후손인 베겔의 아들로, 베냐민 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Signer of the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Anathoth was one of the leaders who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Anathoth is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the leaders who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. The covenant was a solemn agreement made by the people of Israel to follow God's laws and commandments faithfully. By signing the covenant, Anathoth demonstrated his commitment to God and his support for the spiritual and social reforms initiated by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.19 only referred to as Anathoth (עֲנָתוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.19에 처음 언급되며 '아나돗'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아나돗은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Apostle, brother of Simon Peter
persons.short: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ and played a significant role in the early church.
persons.article: Andrew was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ and the brother of Simon Peter. He was originally a disciple of John the Baptist but later followed Jesus after hearing John's testimony about Him. Andrew is known for bringing his brother Peter to Jesus, recognizing Him as the Messiah. Throughout the Gospels, Andrew is mentioned several times, often in connection with his brother Peter. He was present at significant events, such as the feeding of the five thousand, where he brought a boy with five loaves and two fish to Jesus. Andrew was also among the disciples who asked Jesus about the signs of His coming and the end of the age. After Jesus' ascension, Andrew continued to play a role in the early church. He was present in the upper room with the other disciples as they waited for the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost. According to church tradition, Andrew preached the gospel in various regions, including Greece and Asia Minor, and was martyred by crucifixion on an X-shaped cross, which has become known as St. Andrew's Cross. His faithfulness and dedication to spreading the message of Christ have made him an important figure in Christian history.
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.4.18 only referred to as Andrew (Ἀνδρέας); son of John; a brother of Peter.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '안드레'라 불림. 요한의 아들. 베드로의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 안드레는 시몬 베드로의 형제로, 예수 그리스도의 열두 사도 중 한 사람이었으며 초대교회에서 중요한 역할을 했다.
persons.article_ko: 안드레는 예수 그리스도의 열두 사도 중 한 사람이며 시몬 베드로의 형제였다. 그는 원래 세례 요한의 제자였으나 요한이 예수님에 대해 증언한 것을 들은 후 그분을 따르게 되었다. 안드레는 자기 형제 베드로를 예수님께 데려와 그분을 메시아로 인정한 것으로 알려져 있다. 복음서 전체에서 안드레는 여러 번 언급되며, 종종 그의 형제 베드로와 관련하여 나온다. 그는 오병이어의 기적 같은 중요한 사건들에 있었는데, 그곳에서 그는 떡 다섯 개와 물고기 두 마리를 가진 소년을 예수님께 데려왔다. 안드레는 또한 예수님의 오심과 세상 끝의 징조에 대해 예수님께 질문한 제자 중 한 사람이었다. 예수님의 승천 후 안드레는 계속해서 초대교회에서 역할을 했다. 그는 오순절 날 성령이 부어지기를 기다리는 동안 다른 제자들과 함께 다락방에 있었다. 교회 전승에 따르면 안드레는 그리스와 소아시아를 포함한 여러 지역에서 복음을 전했고 X자 모양의 십자가에서 순교했는데, 이는 '성 안드레의 십자가'로 알려지게 되었다. 그리스도의 메시지를 전파하는 데 대한 그의 신실함과 헌신은 그를 그리스도교 역사에서 중요한 인물로 만들었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Fellow prisoner with Paul, outstanding among the apostles
persons.short: Andronicus, along with Junia, was a fellow prisoner with Paul and was noted as outstanding among the apostles.
persons.article: Andronicus is mentioned by Paul in his letter to the Romans as one of his fellow prisoners and kinsmen. Along with Junia, Andronicus is described as being "outstanding among the apostles" and having been "in Christ" before Paul himself. This suggests that Andronicus and Junia were well-known and respected members of the early Christian community, possibly having been converted to Christianity before Paul's own conversion. Paul's greeting to them in his letter indicates a close relationship and high regard for their faith and service in the gospel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.7 only referred to as Andronicus (Ἀνδρόνικος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.7에 처음 언급되며 '안드로니고'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 안드로니고는 유니아와 함께 바울의 동료 죄수였으며, 사도들 중에서 뛰어난 자로 언급되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Amorite ally of Abram
persons.short: Aner was an Amorite, one of the allies of Abram, who joined him in the battle against the kings who had taken Lot captive.
persons.article: Aner was an Amorite, mentioned in the book of Genesis as one of the three allies of Abram (later known as Abraham). Along with his brothers Mamre and Eshcol, Aner joined forces with Abram to pursue and defeat the kings who had taken Abram's nephew Lot captive. After the successful rescue of Lot and the recovery of the goods that had been taken, Abram gave a tenth of the spoils to Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High. Aner, along with Eshcol and Mamre, received their share of the remaining spoils, as they had fought alongside Abram in the battle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.13 only referred to as Aner (עָנֵר); a brother of Mamre.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.14.13에 처음 언급되며 '아넬'이라 불림. 마므레의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 마므레와 에스골의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아넬은 아모리 사람으로, 아브람의 동맹자 중 한 사람으로 롯을 사로잡아 간 왕들과의 전투에 함께했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Shemida, descendant of Manasseh
persons.short: Aniam was a son of Shemida and a descendant of Manasseh, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Aniam is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, found in 1Chronicles 7. He is listed as one of the sons of Shemida, who was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Aniam in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.19 only referred to as Aniam (אֲנִיעָם); son of Shemida; a brother of Ahian, Shechem and Likhi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.19에 처음 언급되며 '아니암'이라 불림. 스미다의 아들. 아히안, 세겜과 릭히의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아니암은 므낫세의 후손인 스미다의 아들로, 므낫세 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Prophetess who witnessed Jesus' dedication in the temple
persons.short: Anna, a prophetess and widow, witnessed the dedication of the infant Jesus in the temple and spoke about Him to all who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Anna was a prophetess mentioned in the Gospel of Luke. She was the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. At the time of Jesus' birth, Anna was an elderly widow who had been married for seven years before her husband died, and she had remained a widow for eighty-four years. She was known for her devotion to God, as she never left the temple but worshiped day and night, fasting and praying. When Mary and Joseph brought the infant Jesus to the temple to dedicate Him according to the law, Anna was present. Upon seeing Jesus, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the child to all who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem. Her prophetic insight allowed her to recognize Jesus as the long-awaited Messiah, and she shared this knowledge with others who were eagerly anticipating God's redemptive work through Him.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.2.36 only referred to as Anna (Ἄννα); a daughter of Phanuel.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Luk.2.36에 처음 언급되며 '안나'라 불림. 바누엘의 딸.
persons.short_ko: 여선지자이며 과부인 안나는 아기 예수가 성전에 봉헌될 때 그 자리에 있었고, 예루살렘의 구속을 기다리는 모든 사람에게 그분에 대해 말했다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
persons.short: Annas, a high priest, played a significant role in the events surrounding Jesus' arrest, trial, and crucifixion, as well as in the early persecution of the apostles.
persons.article: Annas was a high priest during the time of Jesus' ministry and played a significant role in the events surrounding Jesus' arrest and trial. He served as high priest from AD 6 to 15 and was succeeded by his son-in-law Caiaphas. However, even after his tenure, Annas retained significant influence and was still referred to as high priest. After Jesus' arrest, He was first brought before Annas for questioning. Annas then sent Jesus to Caiaphas, the current high priest, who presided over the Sanhedrin trial that condemned Jesus to death. Following Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection, Annas continued to oppose the early Christian church. When the apostles Peter and John were arrested for preaching in Jesus' name, they were brought before the Sanhedrin, where Annas was present as a member of the ruling council. Annas' involvement in the events surrounding Jesus' trial and the persecution of the early church highlights the significant influence he held, even though he was no longer the official high priest. His actions demonstrate the religious establishment's opposition to Jesus and the growing Christian movement in the early days of the church.
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.3.2 only referred to as Annas (Ἄννας); father in law of Caiaphas.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 대제사장. Luk.3.2에 처음 언급되며 '안나스'라 불림. 안나스의 딸(이름 미상)의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 대제사장 안나스는 예수님의 체포와 재판, 십자가 처형 및 초기 사도들에 대한 박해에서 중요한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ishpan@1Ch.8.22, Eber@1Ch.8.22, Eliel@1Ch.8.22, Abdon@1Ch.8.23, Zichri@1Ch.8.23, Hanan@1Ch.8.23, Hananiah@1Ch.8.24, Elam@1Ch.8.24, Iphdeiah@1Ch.8.25, Penuel@1Ch.8.25
persons.brief: Son of Shashak, descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Anthothijah was a descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Anthothijah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, found in 1Chronicles 8. He is listed as one of the sons of Shashak, who was a descendant of Benjamin through his son Beriah. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Anthothijah in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.24 only referred to as Anthothijah (עַנְתֹתִיָּה); son of Shashak; a brother of Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Iphdeiah and Penuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.24에 처음 언급되며 '안도디야'라 불림. 사삭의 아들. 이스반, 에벨, 엘리엘, 압돈, 시그리, 하난, 하나냐, 엘람, 이브드야와 브누엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 안도디야는 베냐민의 후손으로, 베냐민 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Faithful martyr in Pergamum
persons.short: Antipas, described as Christ's faithful witness, was martyred in Pergamum, where Satan's throne was said to be.
persons.article: Antipas is mentioned in the book of Revelation as a faithful witness of Christ who was martyred in the city of Pergamum. In the letter to the church in Pergamum, Jesus acknowledges the difficult circumstances the believers faced, living in a city "where Satan's throne is." Despite the intense persecution, Antipas remained faithful to Christ, even to the point of death. Jesus commends the church for holding fast to His name and not denying their faith, even in the face of martyrdom, as exemplified by Antipas. This brief mention of Antipas serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made by early Christians and the importance of remaining faithful to Christ in the face of adversity.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rev.2.13 only referred to as Antipas (Ἀντίπας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rev.2.13에 처음 언급되며 '안디바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그리스도의 신실한 증인이라 불린 안디바는 사탄의 왕좌가 있다고 하는 버가모에서 순교했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Coz, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Anub was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Anub is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, found in 1Chronicles 4. He is listed as one of the sons of Coz, who was a descendant of Judah through his son Ashhur. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Judah, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Anub in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.8 only referred to as Anub (עָנוּב); son of Koz; a brother of Zobebah and Harum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.8에 처음 언급되며 '아눕'이라 불림. 고스의 아들. 소베바, 하룸과 야베스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아눕은 유다의 후손으로, 유다 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Approved in Christ, greeted by Paul
persons.short: Apelles, described as "approved in Christ," was among those greeted by Paul in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Apelles is mentioned by Paul in his letter to the Romans as one of the individuals to whom he sends greetings. Paul describes Apelles as being "approved in Christ," indicating that he was a respected and trustworthy member of the Christian community in Rome. This commendation suggests that Apelles had demonstrated his faith and commitment to Christ in a notable way, earning the recognition and approval of the apostle. Beyond this brief mention and commendation, no further details about Apelles' life or ministry are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.10 only referred to as Apelles (Ἀπελλῆς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.10에 처음 언급되며 '아벨레'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아벨레는 '그리스도 안에서 인정받은 자'로 묘사되며, 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of King Saul, a Benjamite
persons.short: Aphiah, a Benjamite, was an ancestor of King Saul, the first king of Israel.
persons.article: Aphiah is mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul, the first king of Israel, found in the first book of Samuel. He is described as a Benjamite, indicating that he belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. Aphiah is listed as an ancestor of Saul, though the exact relationship is not specified. The genealogy traces Saul's lineage back several generations, highlighting his Benjamite heritage. This brief mention of Aphiah serves to provide context for Saul's family background and his connection to the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.9.1 only referred to as Aphiah (אֲפִיחַ); father of Becorath.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.9.1에 처음 언급되며 '아비아'라 불림. 베고랏의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 사람 아비아는 이스라엘의 첫 왕 사울의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Eloquent Jewish Christian from Alexandria, co-worker with Paul
persons.short: Apollos, an eloquent and learned Jewish Christian from Alexandria, was an important figure in the early church who worked alongside Paul in spreading the gospel.
persons.article: Apollos was a prominent Jewish Christian from Alexandria, known for his eloquence, knowledge of the Scriptures, and effectiveness in preaching the gospel. He is first mentioned in the book of Acts as a learned man who spoke with great fervor and taught about Jesus accurately, though he knew only the baptism of John. After receiving further instruction from Priscilla and Aquila in Ephesus, Apollos went to Achaia and greatly helped the believers there, vigorously refuting the Jews in public debate and proving from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Messiah. In Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, Apollos is mentioned as one of the leaders that some of the Corinthian believers were aligning themselves with, alongside Paul and Cephas (Peter). Paul clarifies that both he and Apollos are merely servants through whom the Corinthians came to believe, each serving the role God had assigned to them. Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God made it grow. Paul also mentions Apollos as a positive example when discussing the need for humility and unity among believers. Later, in Paul's letter to Titus, Apollos is mentioned again as someone Paul encourages Titus to help on his journey, together with Zenas the lawyer. This suggests that Apollos continued to be actively involved in ministry and was a valued co-worker in spreading the gospel message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.18.24 only referred to as Apollos (Ἀπολλῶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.18.24에 처음 언급되며 '아볼로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 알렉산드리아 출신의 언변 좋고 학식 있는 유대인 그리스도인 아볼로는 초대교회의 중요한 인물로, 바울과 함께 복음을 전하는 일을 했다.

persons.description: People from Aph(?)
persons.brief: Son of Nadab, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Appaim was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Appaim is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, found in 1Chronicles 2. He is listed as one of the sons of Nadab, who was a descendant of Judah through his son Jerahmeel. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Judah, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Appaim in the biblical text.
persons.summary: People from Aph(?) from the tribe of Judah, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.30 only referred to as Appaim (אַפַּיִם); descended from Nadab along with Seled; progenitors of Ishi.
persons.summary_ko: 압바임. 1Ch.2.30에 처음 언급되며 '압바임'이라 불림. 나답의 자녀. 셀렛의 동기. 이시의 부모.
persons.short_ko: 압바임은 유다의 후손으로, 유다 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Recipient of Paul's letter to Philemon
persons.short: Apphia, likely a member of Philemon's household, was one of the recipients of Paul's letter to Philemon.
persons.article: Apphia is mentioned in the opening of Paul's letter to Philemon as one of the recipients of the letter, along with Philemon and Archippus. Paul addresses her as "our sister," indicating that she was a fellow believer and likely a member of Philemon's household. Some scholars suggest that Apphia may have been Philemon's wife, but this is not explicitly stated in the text. The letter to Philemon is a personal appeal from Paul regarding Onesimus, a runaway slave who had become a Christian under Paul's ministry.
