Paul sends Onesimus back to Philemon, his master, with this letter, urging Philemon to receive Onesimus back not as a slave, but as a beloved brother in Christ. By addressing the letter to Apphia and Archippus as well, Paul emphasizes the communal nature of the request and the shared responsibility of the Christian community in welcoming Onesimus. Beyond this mention in the letter to Philemon, no further details about Apphia's life or role in the early church are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Phm.1.2 only referred to as Apphia (Ἀπφία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Phm.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '압비아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 압비아는 빌레몬 집안의 일원으로 보이며, 바울이 빌레몬에게 보낸 편지의 수신자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Jewish Christian tentmaker, co-worker with Paul
persons.short: Aquila, along with his wife Priscilla, was a Jewish Christian who worked as a tentmaker and played a significant role in the early church, partnering with Paul in his ministry.
persons.article: Aquila was a Jewish Christian from Pontus who, along with his wife Priscilla, played a significant role in the early church. He is first mentioned in the book of Acts as a tentmaker who had recently come to Corinth from Italy due to the emperor Claudius' decree expelling all Jews from Rome. Paul, also a tentmaker, stayed and worked with Aquila and Priscilla during his time in Corinth. When Paul left Corinth, Aquila and Priscilla accompanied him to Ephesus. There, they met Apollos, an eloquent Jewish Christian from Alexandria who knew only the baptism of John. Aquila and Priscilla took Apollos aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately, enabling him to continue his effective ministry. In Paul's letter to the Romans, he sends greetings to Aquila and Priscilla, commending them as his co-workers in Christ Jesus who risked their lives for him. Paul also mentions that the church met in their house, indicating their significant role in hosting and supporting the local Christian community. Aquila and Priscilla are mentioned again in Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, where he sends greetings from them and the church that meets at their house. Finally, in Paul's second letter to Timothy, he asks Timothy to greet Aquila and Priscilla, demonstrating their ongoing involvement in the ministry and their close relationship with Paul and his associates.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.18.2 only referred to as Aquila (Ἀκύλας); husband of Priscilla.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.18.2에 처음 언급되며 '아굴라'라 불림. 브리스길라의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 아굴라는 그의 아내 브리스길라와 함께 천막을 만드는 일을 한 유대인 그리스도인으로, 초대교회에서 바울의 사역에 동역자로서 중요한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jether, descendant of Asher
persons.short: Ara was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
persons.article: Ara is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, found in 1Chronicles 7. He is listed as one of the sons of Jether, who was a descendant of Asher through his son Beriah. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Ara in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.38 only referred to as Ara (אֲרָא); son of Ithran; a brother of Jephunneh and Pispa.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.38에 처음 언급되며 '아라'라 불림. 이드란의 아들. 여분네와 비스바의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아라는 아셀의 후손으로, 아셀 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ahio@1Ch.8.14, Shashak@1Ch.8.14-, Jeremoth@1Ch.8.14, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.15, Eder@1Ch.8.15, Michael@1Ch.8.16, Ishpah@1Ch.8.16, Joha@1Ch.8.16
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Beriah.
persons.short: Arad was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Beriah.
persons.article: Arad is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 1Ch.8.15, as one of the sons of Beriah, a Benjamite. He is listed among the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. No further information is provided about Arad in the biblical text. His name means "wild donkey" in Hebrew.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.15 only referred to as Arad (עֲרָד); son of Beriah; a brother of Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Eder, Michael, Ishpah and Joha.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.8.15에 처음 언급되며 '아랏'이라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 아효, 사삭, 여레못, 스바댜, 에델, 미가엘, 이스바와 요하의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아랏은 베냐민 사람으로, 브리아의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shual, an Asherite
persons.short: Arah, the son of Shual ('Ulla'), was a descendant of Asher.
persons.article: Arah is mentioned in 1Ch.7.39 as one of the sons of Shual ('Ulla'), who was a descendant of Asher. He is listed among the members of the tribe of Asher in the genealogical records.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.39 only referred to as Arah (אָרַח); son of Shual; a brother of Hanniel and Rizia.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.39에 처음 언급되며 '아라'라 불림. 수알의 아들. 한니엘과 리시아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아라(수알 또는 울라의 아들)는 아셀의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite
persons.short: Arah, whose daughter was married to Shechaniah, was the father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite.
persons.article: Arah is mentioned in Neh.6.18 as the father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite, who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. Arah's daughter was married to a man named Shechaniah, and this marriage alliance created a connection between Tobiah and some of the Jewish nobles. This relationship complicated Nehemiah's efforts to restore and protect Jerusalem, as Tobiah used his influence to undermine Nehemiah's authority.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.5 only referred to as Arah (אָרַח).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.5에 처음 언급되며 '아라'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아라는 스가냐와 결혼한 딸을 두었고, 암몬 사람 도비야의 장인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Jewish leader whose daughter married Tobiah's son.
persons.short: Arah's daughter was married to the son of Tobiah the Ammonite.
persons.article: Arah is briefly mentioned in Neh.6.18 as a Jewish leader whose daughter was married to the son of Tobiah the Ammonite. Tobiah was one of the enemies who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem (Neh). Neh.2.10, 19; 4.3, 7. The marriage between Arah's daughter and Tobiah's son suggests that some Jewish nobles had formed alliances with foreign adversaries. This connection may have complicated Nehemiah's task of leading the Jewish people and rebuilding Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.18 only referred to as Arah (אָרַח); father of Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '아라'라 불림. 스가냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아라의 딸은 암몬 사람 도비야의 아들과 결혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shemer, descendant of Asher
persons.short: Aram was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
persons.article: Aram is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, found in 1Chronicles 7. He is listed as the son of Shemer, who was a descendant of Asher through his son Beriah. The genealogy provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Aram, son of Shemer, in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.34 only referred to as Aram (אֲרָם); son of Shomer; a brother of Ahi, Rohgah and Jehubbah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.34에 처음 언급되며 '아람'이라 불림. 소멜의 아들. 아히, 로가와 호바의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아람은 아셀의 후손으로, 아셀 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Shem, ancestor of the Arameans
persons.short: Aram, a son of Shem and ancestor of the Aramean people.
persons.article: Aram is mentioned in Gen.10.22,23 and 1Ch.1.17 as one of the sons of Shem, the son of Noah. He is listed among the descendants of Shem and is identified as the ancestor of the Arameans, a Semitic people who inhabited the regions of Syria and Mesopotamia. The Arameans played a significant role in the history of the ancient Near East, and their language, Aramaic, became a common language of trade and diplomacy. Aram's descendants spread throughout the region, establishing various Aramean kingdoms and city-states.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.22 only referred to as Aram (אֲרָם); son of Shem; a brother of Asshur, Elam, Arpachshad and Lud; father of Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '아람'이라 불림. 셈의 아들. 앗수르, 엘람, 아르박삿과 룻의 형제. 우스, 훌, 게델과 마스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아람은 셈의 아들이며 아람 족속의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Kemuel, nephew of Abraham
persons.short: Aram was the son of Kemuel, who was the son of Abraham's brother Nahor.
persons.article: Aram is mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's family, found in Genesis 22. He is listed as the son of Kemuel, who was the son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his wife Milcah. This makes Aram the nephew of Abraham. The genealogy is provided in the context of Abraham sending his servant to find a wife for his son Isaac from among his relatives in Mesopotamia. Apart from this mention in the genealogical list, no further information is given about Aram, son of Kemuel, in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.21 only referred to as Aram (אֲרָם); a son of Kemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.21에 처음 언급되며 '아람'이라 불림. 그무엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아람은 아브라함의 형제 나홀의 아들 그무엘의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Concubine of Manasseh; mother of Asriel
persons.short: An Aramitess, who was a concubine of Manasseh, gave birth to Machir and Asriel..
persons.article: An unnamed Aramitess is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, found in 1Chronicles 7. She is described as a concubine of Manasseh, one of the sons of Joseph and a patriarch of one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The Aramitess gave birth to Asriel, who is listed among the descendants of Manasseh. The term "Aramitess" indicates that she was from Aram, a region in ancient Syria. Her inclusion in the genealogy suggests that intermarriage between the Israelites and the Arameans was not uncommon. Apart from this brief mention, no further information is provided about this Aramitess concubine of Manasseh in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A concubine of Syria living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.14 only referred to as Aramitess (אֲרַמִּי); concubine of Manasseh; mother of Machir and Asriel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.7.14에 처음 언급되며 '아람'이라 불림. 므낫세의 아내. 마길과 아스리엘의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 므낫세의 아람 여인 첩은 마길과 아스리엘을 낳았다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Dishan, descendant of Seir the Horite
persons.short: Aran was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau's family and the Horite clans.
persons.article: Aran is mentioned in the genealogies found in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1, which record the descendants of Esau and the Horite clans. He is listed as one of the sons of Dishan, who was a son of Seir the Horite. The Horites were the original inhabitants of the land of Seir, which was later inhabited by the descendants of Esau, also known as the Edomites. The genealogies provide a record of the family lines and clans that lived in the region. Apart from these mentions in the genealogical lists, no further information is given about Aran, son of Dishan, in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.28 only referred to as Aran (אֲרָן); son of Dishan; a brother of Uz.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.28에 처음 언급되며 '아란'이라 불림. 디산의 아들. 우스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아란은 세일 호리 사람의 후손으로, 에서 가문과 호리 족속의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Canaanite living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Anak, former name of Hebron
persons.short: Arba was the father of Anak and the namesake of Kiriath-arba, which was the former name of Hebron.
persons.article: Arba is mentioned in the book of Joshua as the father of Anak and the namesake of Kiriath-arba, which was the former name of the city of Hebron. Hebron was a significant city in the hill country of Judah, later assigned to Caleb as part of his inheritance. The text states that Hebron's former name was Kiriath-arba, which means "the city of Arba." Arba is described as the greatest man among the Anakim, a group of people known for their large stature and strength. The Anakim were descendants of Anak and were considered a formidable enemy by the Israelites during their conquest of Canaan. The renaming of the city from Kiriath-arba to Hebron marks a significant shift in the region's history as the Israelites claimed the land promised to them by God. Apart from this mention in Joshua, no further information is provided about Arba himself in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.14.15 only referred to as Arba (אַרְבַּע); father of Anak.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 가나안 사람. Jos.14.15에 처음 언급되며 '아르바'라 불림. 아낙의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아르바는 아낙의 아버지이며, 헤브론의 옛 이름인 기럇아르바의 어원이 된 인물이었다.

persons.description: Ethnarch living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Son of Herod the Great, Ethnarch of Judea
persons.short: Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, Ethnarch over Judea, causing Joseph to fear returning there with Mary and the child Jesus.
persons.article: Archelaus was the son of Herod the Great, who ruled as king over Judea at the time of Jesus' birth. After Herod's death, his kingdom was divided among his sons, with Archelaus receiving the rule over Judea, Samaria, and Idumea. However, Archelaus' reign was marked by cruelty and tyranny, leading to his eventual banishment by the Roman emperor. In the context of Jesus' early life, Archelaus is mentioned in Mat.2.22. After the visit of the magi and the family's flight to Egypt, Joseph was warned in a dream not to return to Judea because Archelaus was ruling there in place of his father Herod. Fearing for the child's safety, Joseph instead took Mary and Jesus to the region of Galilee, settling in Nazareth. This decision, guided by divine intervention, led to the fulfillment of the prophecy that the Messiah would be called a Nazarene.
persons.summary: Ethnarch Herod Archelaus over Israel living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Mat.2.22 only referred to as Archelaus (Ἀρχέλαος); son of Herod 'the Great'; a brother of Herod Antipas, Herod Philip I and Herod Philip II.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 민족장. Mat.2.22에 처음 언급되며 '아켈라오'라 불림. 헤롯의 아들. 헤롯, 빌립과 빌립의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤롯대왕의 아들 아켈라오는 유대 지역의 분봉왕이 되었고, 이로 인해 요셉이 마리아와 아기 예수를 데리고 그곳으로 돌아가기를 두려워했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Fellow soldier and minister in Colossae
persons.short: Archippus, addressed as a fellow soldier by Paul, was urged to complete the ministry he had received in the Lord.
persons.article: Archippus was a member of the early Christian church, mentioned by Paul in his letters to the Colossians and to Philemon. In the letter to the Colossians, Paul instructs the church to tell Archippus, "See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord" (Col. 4:17). This suggests that Archippus held a position of responsibility within the church at Colossae and that Paul wanted to encourage him to fulfill his duties faithfully. In the letter to Philemon, Archippus is addressed alongside Philemon and Apphia as a "fellow soldier" (Phm. 1:2). This military metaphor indicates that Archippus was a committed and active member of the Christian community, working alongside others to advance the gospel message. The inclusion of Archippus in the opening of this personal letter also suggests a close relationship between him and Paul, as well as with Philemon and Apphia. While no further details about Archippus' life or specific ministry are provided in the biblical text, these brief mentions highlight his importance within the early church and Paul's desire to encourage and support him in his Christian service.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Col.4.17 only referred to as Archippus (Ἄρχιππος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Col.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '아킵보'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바울에게 '함께 병사된 자'로 불린 아킵보는 주 안에서 받은 직분을 다하도록 권면을 받았다.

persons.description: People from Arach(?)
persons.brief: Inhabitants of a region near Bethel
persons.short: The Archites were a people group mentioned in relation to the boundaries of Ephraim's territory and as the origin of Hushai, King David's friend and advisor.
persons.article: The Archites were a people group mentioned in the Old Testament, primarily in connection with the region near Bethel, a city located on the border between the territories of Ephraim and Benjamin. In Jos.16.2, the boundary of Ephraim's territory is described as extending from Bethel to Luz and going down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, reaching to Jericho and the Jordan River. This suggests that the Archites inhabited a region in the vicinity of Bethel. The most prominent Archite mentioned in the Bible is Hushai, who is described as King David's friend and advisor. During Absalom's rebellion against David, Hushai remained loyal to the king and acted as a spy in Absalom's court. He successfully countered the advice of Ahithophel, Absalom's counselor, and played a crucial role in helping David regain the throne (2Samuel 15-17). Hushai's loyalty and wisdom were highly valued by David, as evidenced by his inclusion among the king's chief officials (1Ch.27.33). Apart from these mentions, little is known about the Archites as a people group. Their association with the region near Bethel and the prominence of Hushai in David's court suggest that they may have been a significant clan or tribe within Israel during the time of the United Monarchy.
persons.summary: A person from Arach(?), first mentioned at Jos.16.2 only referred to as Archites (אַרְכִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 아렉 족속. Jos.16.2에 처음 언급되며 '아렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아렉 족속은 에브라임 지경의 경계와 관련해 언급되며, 다윗 왕의 친구이자 모사인 후새의 출신지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Bela@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Becher@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ashbel@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Naaman@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Muppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Huppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ahiram@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Jediael@1Ch.7.6-
persons.brief: Son of Benjamin, brother of Bela
persons.short: Ard, a son of Benjamin, is listed among the descendants of Jacob who went to Egypt during the famine.
persons.article: Ard is mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'), in Gen.46.21. He is listed as a son of Bela, who was one of Benjamin's sons. This genealogy is given in the context of Jacob's family migrating to Egypt during the time of famine, at the invitation of Joseph, who had risen to a position of authority in Egypt. The mention of Ard in this genealogy serves to highlight the growth and development of the Israelite clan, even as they prepared to leave their homeland for Egypt. It also emphasizes the continuity of God's promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as their descendants multiplied and began to fulfill the divine plan for their nation. Apart from this mention in the genealogy, no further information is provided about Ard in the biblical text. His inclusion in the record of Benjamin's descendants suggests that he was part of the foundation for the future tribe of Benjamin within the nation of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Gen.46.21 only referred to as Ard (אַרְדְּ); son of Benjamin; a brother of Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ahiram, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, Ahiram and Jediael.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.21에 처음 언급되며 '아릇'이라 불림. 베냐민의 아들. 벨라, 베겔, 아스벨, 게라, 나아만, 로스, 뭅빔, 훔빔, 에히와 여디아엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민의 아들 아릇은 흉년 때 애굽으로 내려간 야곱의 후손 명단에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Ezbon@1Ch.7.7, Uzzi@1Ch.7.7, Uzziel@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abihud@1Ch.8.3, Abishua@1Ch.8.4, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
persons.short: Ard, a grandson of Benjamin, is mentioned in the census of the Israelites taken in the wilderness of Moab.
persons.article: Ard is mentioned in the book of Numbers as one of the descendants of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). In the census of the Israelites taken in the wilderness of Moab, near the end of their forty years of wandering, Ard is listed as a grandson of Benjamin through his son Bela (Num.26.40). The purpose of this census was to determine the military strength of each tribe and to prepare for the allocation of the Promised Land among the tribes. The mention of Ard in this context highlights the continuity of the Benjamite clan and their place within the nation of Israel as they prepared to enter and possess the land promised to their forefathers. This reference to Ard in the book of Numbers is consistent with his mention in the genealogy of Benjamin in Gen.46.21, confirming his place in the family line. Apart from these two mentions, no further details about Ard's life or role within the tribe of Benjamin are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.26.40 referred to as Ard (אַרְדְּ), or Ardite (אַרְדִּי); son of Bela; a brother of Naaman, Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.40에 처음 언급되며 '아릇'이라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 나아만, 에스본, 웃시, 웃시엘, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비훗, 아비수아와 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민의 손자 아릇은 모압 광야에서 실시된 이스라엘 인구조사에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Jesher@1Ch.2.18, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Mesha@1Ch.2.42, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Sheva@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: Son of Caleb, brother of Jether and Mered
persons.short: Ardon was a son of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Ardon is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, found in 1Chronicles 2. He is listed as one of the sons of Caleb, along with his brothers Jether and Mered. Caleb was a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah, known for his faithfulness to God during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the descendants of Judah, highlighting the important families and individuals within the tribe. Apart from this mention in the genealogical record, no further information is provided about Ardon in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.18 only referred to as Ardon (אַרְדּוֹן); son of Caleb and Azubah; a brother of Hur, Jesher, Shobab, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez, Sheber, Tirhanah, Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Shaaph, Sheva and Achsah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '아르돈'이라 불림. 갈렙과 아수바의 아들. 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아르돈은 갈렙의 아들로, 유다의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ziphion@Gen.46.16-Num, Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num, Shuni@Gen.46.16-Num, Ezbon@Gen.46.16-Num, Eri@Gen.46.16-Num, Arod@Gen.46.16-Num
persons.brief: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob
persons.short: Areli, a son of Gad, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jacob and the census of the Israelites in the wilderness.
persons.article: Areli is mentioned in the Old Testament as one of the sons of Gad, who was one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). In Gen.46.16, Areli is listed among the descendants of Jacob who went down to Egypt during the time of famine. This genealogical record emphasizes the growth of the Israelite clan and the fulfillment of God's promise to make them a great nation. Areli is also mentioned in the book of Numbers, during the census of the Israelites taken in the wilderness of Moab, near the end of their forty years of wandering. In Num.26.17, the descendants of Areli are listed as a clan within the tribe of Gad. This census was taken to determine the military strength of each tribe and to prepare for the allocation of the Promised Land among the tribes. Apart from these mentions in the genealogical records and census, no further details about Areli's life or his descendants are provided in the biblical text. His inclusion in these lists highlights the continuity of the Israelite tribes and their growth as a nation, in fulfillment of God's promises to their forefathers.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.16 referred to as Areli or Arelite (אַרְאֵלִי); son of Gad; a brother of Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri and Arod.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.16에 처음 언급되며 '아렐리'라 불림. 갓의 아들. 시뵨, 학기, 수니, 에스본, 에리와 아롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아렐리는 갓의 아들로, 야곱의 족보와 광야에서의 이스라엘 인구조사에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: King of the Nabataeans in Damascus
persons.short: Aretas, the king of the Nabataeans, governed Damascus and tried to arrest Paul.
persons.article: Aretas is mentioned in the New Testament, in 2Co.11.32, where Paul recounts his escape from Damascus. According to Paul, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of Damascus in order to arrest him. This event likely occurred shortly after Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus, as he had begun preaching the gospel and faced opposition from both Jewish and Gentile authorities. Aretas IV Philopatris was the king of the Nabataeans, an Arab kingdom centered in Petra (in modern-day Jordan), from roughly 9 BC to AD 40. The Nabataeans controlled the trade routes in the region, and their influence extended to Damascus during this period. The exact date of Paul's escape from Damascus is uncertain, but it is generally believed to have taken place in the mid-30s AD, during the reign of Aretas IV. The mention of Aretas in 2 Corinthians provides historical context for Paul's early ministry and the challenges he faced as he spread the gospel message. It also demonstrates the political complexity of the region, with various authorities, both Jewish and Gentile, opposing the growing Christian movement.
persons.summary: A king living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Co.11.32 only referred to as Aretas (Ἀρέτας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 왕. 2Co.11.32에 처음 언급되며 '아레다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 나바테아 왕 아레다는 다메섹을 다스리며 바울을 체포하려 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Officer of King Pekahiah of Israel
persons.short: Argob, along with Arieh, was with King Pekahiah when Pekah conspired against him and assassinated him.
persons.article: Argob is briefly mentioned in 2Ki.15.25 as one of the officers of King Pekahiah of Israel. Pekahiah was the son and successor of Menahem, ruling over the northern kingdom of Israel in the 8th century BC. During Pekahiah's reign, one of his officers, Pekah son of Remaliah, conspired against him. Pekah, along with fifty men from Gilead, attacked and killed Pekahiah in the citadel of the royal palace in Samaria. The text mentions that Argob and Arieh were with Pekahiah at the time of the assassination. The brief mention of Argob in this context suggests that he was a high-ranking officer or official in Pekahiah's court. However, no further details about his role, responsibilities, or fate after the assassination are provided in the biblical text. The assassination of Pekahiah and the usurpation of the throne by Pekah occurred during a period of political instability and turmoil in the northern kingdom of Israel, which ultimately led to its downfall and exile at the hands of the Assyrian Empire.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.15.25 only referred to as Argob (אַרְגֹּב).

persons.brief: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
persons.short: Aridai was one of the ten sons of Haman, who were killed and hanged after their father's downfall.
persons.article: Aridai is mentioned in the book of Esther as one of the ten sons of Haman, the chief antagonist in the story. Haman, a high-ranking official in the Persian court, plotted to destroy all the Jews in the empire due to his hatred for Mordecai, a Jew who refused to bow down to him. However, Haman's plan was thwarted by Queen Esther, who revealed her Jewish identity to King Ahasuerus and exposed Haman's evil scheme. As a result, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king issued a decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves against their enemies. On the appointed day, the Jews throughout the empire fought against those who sought to harm them. In Susa, the capital, they killed five hundred men and also killed Haman's ten sons, including Aridai (Est.9.9). After this victory, Queen Esther requested that the bodies of Haman's sons be hanged on the gallows, further emphasizing the complete defeat of Haman and his family (Est.9.13-14). The mention of Aridai and his brothers' deaths serves to underscore the reversal of fortune and the triumph of the Jewish people over their enemies, as well as the downfall of those who sought to destroy them.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.9.9 only referred to as Aridai (אֲרִידַי); son of Haman; a brother of Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai and Vaizatha.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.9.9에 처음 언급되며 '아리대'라 불림. 하만과 세레스의 아들. 바산다다, 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새와 왜사다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아리대는 하만의 열 아들 중 한 사람으로, 아버지가 몰락한 후 죽임을 당해 매달렸다.

persons.description: Warriors living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Two lion-like men of Moab killed by Benaiah
persons.short: Ariel refers to two lion-like men of Moab who were killed by Benaiah, one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: In 2Sa.23.20 and 1Ch.11.22, the term "Ariel" is used to describe two warriors from Moab who were killed by Benaiah, one of King David's mighty men. The passage states that Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was a valiant fighter from Kabzeel who performed great exploits. Among his notable achievements, he struck down two "Ariel" of Moab. The term "Ariel" in this context is not a proper name but rather a descriptive term meaning "lion of God" or "lion-like." It is used to emphasize the strength, courage, and ferocity of these Moabite warriors. The fact that Benaiah defeated two of these formidable fighters highlights his exceptional skill and bravery as a warrior in David's army. Apart from this brief mention, no further details are provided about the identity, background, or specific circumstances surrounding Benaiah's encounter with these Moabite warriors. The passage serves to showcase Benaiah's prowess and loyalty to King David, as well as to illustrate the might of David's elite group of warriors known as "The Thirty."
persons.summary: A group of warriors living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.20 referred to as Ariel or "hero" (אֲרִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 용사들. 2Sa.23.20에 처음 언급되며 '아리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아리엘은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 브나야에게 죽임을 당한 모압의 사자 같은 두 용사를 가리킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the leaders summoned by Ezra
persons.short: Ariel was one of the leaders summoned by Ezra to assist in the return of the exiles to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Ariel is mentioned in Ezr.8.16 as one of the leaders summoned by Ezra to assist in the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem. Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a group of Israelites back to Jerusalem during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, with the purpose of teaching and enforcing the Law of Moses among the people. In preparation for the journey, Ezra gathered leading men to accompany him. Ariel is listed among these leaders, along with Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. Ezra sent these men to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, to request the assistance of Levites and temple servants for the house of God in Jerusalem. The mention of Ariel in this context highlights his role as a trusted leader among the exiles and his willingness to support Ezra in the important task of restoring worship and religious practices in Jerusalem. However, beyond this brief mention, no further details about Ariel's background, family, or specific contributions are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.16 only referred to as Ariel (אֲרִיאֵל).

persons.short_ko: 아리엘은 에스라가 포로 귀환을 돕도록 소집한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard
persons.short: Arioch, the captain of King Nebuchadnezzar's guard, was commanded to execute the wise men of Babylon but brought Daniel before the king to interpret his dream.
persons.article: Arioch is mentioned in the book of Daniel as the captain of King Nebuchadnezzar's guard during the time of the Babylonian exile. In Daniel 2, Nebuchadnezzar had a troubling dream and demanded that his wise men not only interpret the dream but also tell him what he had dreamed. When they were unable to do so, the king ordered Arioch to execute all the wise men of Babylon. Daniel, a young Jewish exile, requested time from Arioch to interpret the king's dream. Arioch brought Daniel before Nebuchadnezzar, and Daniel was able to reveal both the content of the dream and its interpretation, which concerned the rise and fall of future kingdoms and the ultimate establishment of God's eternal kingdom. Arioch's role in this narrative highlights the danger faced by Daniel and his friends, as well as the power and authority of the Babylonian king. Arioch's willingness to grant Daniel's request and bring him before Nebuchadnezzar also demonstrates the respect and trust that Daniel had earned in the Babylonian court, even as a young exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Dan.2.14 only referred to as Arioch (Aramiac אֲרְיוֹךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Dan.2.14에 처음 언급되며 '아리옥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느부갓네살 왕의 시위대장 아리옥은 바벨론의 지혜자들을 죽이라는 명령을 받았으나, 다니엘을 왕 앞으로 데려와 그의 꿈을 해석하게 했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Ellasar, ally of Chedorlaomer
persons.short: Arioch, king of Ellasar, was one of the four kings who joined forces with Chedorlaomer in the battle against the five kings of the plain.
persons.article: Arioch is mentioned in Genesis 14 as the king of Ellasar, one of the four kings who allied with Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a battle against five kings in the region of Sodom and Gomorrah. The other kings allied with Chedorlaomer were Amraphel king of Shinar and Tidal king of Goiim. The biblical account states that these four kings had previously subjugated the five kings of the plain (Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela) for twelve years. In the thirteenth year, the five kings rebelled against Chedorlaomer's rule. As a result, Chedorlaomer and his allies, including Arioch, went to war against the rebellious kings. Arioch's kingdom, Ellasar, is not definitively identified but is believed to be located in the region of Mesopotamia. His participation in this battle alongside Chedorlaomer suggests that he was a powerful ruler and had a significant military force at his disposal. The four kings, led by Chedorlaomer, defeated the five kings and captured Lot, Abraham's nephew, along with his possessions. Upon hearing of Lot's capture, Abraham mobilized his trained men and pursued the victorious kings. Abraham successfully defeated Chedorlaomer and his allies, including Arioch, and rescued Lot and his belongings. Apart from this event, no further information is provided about Arioch or his kingdom in the biblical text. His mention serves to provide historical context for the political and military dynamics of the ancient Near East during the time of Abraham.
persons.summary: A king in Mesopotamia living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.1 only referred to as Arioch (אַרְיוֹךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '아리옥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘라살 왕 아리옥은 그돌라오멜과 연합하여 평지 다섯 왕과 싸운 네 왕 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Macedonian companion of Paul, fellow prisoner
persons.short: Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was a faithful companion of Paul during his missionary journeys and imprisonment.
persons.article: Aristarchus was a Macedonian Christian from Thessalonica who became a close companion and fellow worker of the apostle Paul. He is mentioned several times in the New Testament, providing insight into his dedication to the gospel and his support of Paul's ministry. In Act.19.29, during the riot in Ephesus, Aristarchus and Gaius are described as Paul's traveling companions who were seized by the mob. This incident highlights the dangers faced by early Christians as they spread the gospel message. Aristarchus is later mentioned as one of the delegates who accompanied Paul on his journey to Jerusalem (Act.20.4, demonstrating his commitment to supporting Paul and the church). In Act.27.2, we learn that Aristarchus was also with Paul during his voyage to Rome as a prisoner, further emphasizing his loyalty and willingness to face hardships for the sake of the gospel. In Paul's letters, Aristarchus is described as a fellow prisoner (Col). Act.4.10 and a fellow worker (Phm). Act.1.24. These references suggest that Aristarchus not only traveled with Paul but also shared in his sufferings and labored alongside him in ministry. Aristarchus' consistent presence in Paul's life, from his missionary journeys to his imprisonment, testifies to his unwavering faith and dedication to the spread of the gospel. His example serves as an encouragement to believers to remain faithful and committed to serving Christ, even in the face of adversity.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.19.29 only referred to as Aristarchus (Ἀρίσταρχος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.19.29에 처음 언급되며 '아리스다고'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 데살로니가 출신 마게도냐 사람 아리스다고는 바울의 선교여행과 투옥 기간 동안 그와 신실하게 동행한 동료였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer in Rome, greeted by Paul
persons.short: Paul sends greetings to those who belong to the household of Aristobulus, suggesting that Aristobulus was a prominent believer in Rome.
persons.article: Aristobulus is mentioned briefly in Paul's letter to the Romans, where the apostle sends greetings to "those who belong to the household of Aristobulus" (Rom. 16:10). This greeting suggests that Aristobulus was a prominent member of the Christian community in Rome, and that his household, which likely included family members, servants, and slaves, had also embraced the Christian faith. The fact that Paul specifically mentions Aristobulus' household implies that Aristobulus himself was a well-known figure, either within the church or in Roman society. However, beyond this brief greeting, no further information is provided about Aristobulus' background, conversion, or role in the early church. Some scholars speculate that Aristobulus may have been a member of Herod's family or a prominent Jewish figure in Rome, but there is no conclusive evidence to support these theories. The mention of his name in Paul's letter serves as a reminder of the diversity within the early church and the spread of the gospel message across various social and cultural boundaries.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.10 only referred to as Aristobulus (Ἀριστόβουλος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.10에 처음 언급되며 '아리스도불로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바울은 아리스도불로 집안에 속한 사람들에게 문안했는데, 이는 아리스도불로가 로마에서 신망 있는 신자였음을 시사한다.

persons.description: People from Arak(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Canaanite people group descended from Canaan
persons.short: The Arkites were one of the Canaanite tribes descended from Canaan, the son of Ham, and are mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: The Arkites were a Canaanite people group mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1. They are listed among the descendants of Canaan, the son of Ham and grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:17; 1Chr. 1:15). The Table of Nations in Genesis 10 provides a genealogical record of the spread of Noah's descendants after the Flood, highlighting the various people groups and nations that emerged from them. The Arkites are mentioned alongside other Canaanite tribes, such as the Sidonians, Hivites, and Jebusites, indicating their shared ancestry and geographic proximity in the region of Canaan. Beyond their inclusion in the Table of Nations, no further information is provided about the Arkites in the biblical text. Their mention serves to demonstrate the diversity of people groups that inhabited the land of Canaan prior to the Israelite conquest under Joshua. Some scholars suggest that the Arkites may have been associated with the ancient city of Arqa, located in present-day Lebanon, approximately 25 kilometers northeast of Tripoli. However, this connection remains uncertain due to the lack of conclusive historical and archaeological evidence. The Arkites, along with the other Canaanite tribes, were among the people groups that the Israelites were commanded to dispossess as they entered the Promised Land (Deut. 20:17). The presence of these Canaanite nations underscores the challenges faced by the Israelites as they sought to establish their own nation in obedience to God's covenant promises.
persons.summary: People from Arak(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at Gen.10.17 only referred to as Arkites (עַרְקִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 알가 족속. Gen.10.17에 처음 언급되며 '알가'라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 신, 아르왓, 스말과 하맛의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 알가 족속은 함의 아들 가나안의 후손인 가나안 족속 중 하나로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.siblings: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Malchi-shua@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Merab@1Sa.14.49-2Sa, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch, Mephibosheth@2Sa.21.8
persons.brief: Son of Saul by Rizpah, killed by Gibeonites
persons.short: Armoni was a son of Saul by his concubine Rizpah, killed by the Gibeonites (<ref="2Sa.21.8">2Sa.21.8</ref>).
persons.article: Armoni was one of the two sons of King Saul of Israel by his concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. After Saul's death, to avert a famine, David handed over Armoni and his brother Mephibosheth to the Gibeonites, who killed them in retribution for Saul's earlier attempt to annihilate the Gibeonites. Their bodies were left exposed until Rizpah took sackcloth and spread it on a rock, keeping the birds and wild animals away, until David had their bones buried in Saul's family tomb.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.21.8 only referred to as Armoni (אַרְמֹנִי); son of Saul and Rizpah; a brother of Mephibosheth; half-brother of: Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchi-shua, Merab, Michal and Ish-bosheth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.21.8에 처음 언급되며 '알모니'라 불림. 사울과 리스바의 아들. 요나단, 아비나답, 말기수아, 메랍, 미갈, 이스보셋과 므비보셋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아르모니는 사울이 첩 리스바를 통해 낳은 아들로, 기브온 사람들에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of David's son Solomon
persons.short: Arnan was a descendant of David's son Solomon (<ref="1Ch.3.21">1Ch.3.21</ref>).
persons.article: Arnan was a descendant of King David of Israel through his son Solomon, appearing in a genealogy in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Rephaiah, the son of Jeshaiah, the son of Hananiah, the son of Zerubbabel, who led the first group of exiles back from Babylon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.21 only referred to as Arnan (אַרְנָן); son of Hananiah; a brother of Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Obadiah and Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.21에 처음 언급되며 '아르난'이라 불림. 하나냐의 아들. 블라댜, 여사야, 르바야, 오바댜와 스가냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아르난은 다윗의 아들 솔로몬의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ziphion@Gen.46.16-Num, Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num, Shuni@Gen.46.16-Num, Ezbon@Gen.46.16-Num, Eri@Gen.46.16-Num, Areli@Gen.46.16-Num
persons.brief: Son of Gad and founder of the Arodite clan
persons.short: Arod, son of Gad, was the founder of the Arodite clan (<ref="Gen.46.16; Num.26.17">Gen.46.16; Num.26.17</ref>).
persons.article: Arod was a son of Gad and grandson of Israel (or 'Jacob'), listed among the 70 members of Jacob's family who moved to Egypt during the famine. He was the founder of the Arodite clan within the tribe of Gad. In the census taken in the wilderness, the Arodite clan numbered 40,500 men age 20 and up, showing God's fulfillment of his promise to make Abraham's descendants as numerous as the stars.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.16 referred to as Arod (אֲרוֹד), or Arodi or Arodite (אֲרוֹדִי); son of Gad; a brother of Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri and Areli.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.16에 처음 언급되며 '아롯'이라 불림. 갓의 아들. 시뵨, 학기, 수니, 에스본, 에리와 아렐리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아롯은 갓의 아들로 아롯 가문의 시조였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Shem, ancestor of Abraham
persons.short: Arpachshad, son of Shem, was born two years after the flood and was an ancestor of Abraham (<ref="Gen.10.22,24; 11:10-13; 1Ch.1.17-18,24; Luke 3:36">Gen.10.22,24; 11:10-13; 1Ch.1.17-18,24; Luke 3:36</ref>).
persons.article: Arpachshad, also spelled Arphaxad, was a son of Shem and grandson of Noah. He was born two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old. At age 35, Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. He lived 403 years after Shelah's birth and had other sons and daughters. Arpachshad was an ancestor of Abraham and is listed in both the genealogies in Genesis and in Jesus' genealogy in Luke 3. His name is of uncertain meaning but may be related to the region of Arrapḫa in Assyria.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.22 referred to as Arpachshad (אַרְפַּכְשַׁד), or Arphaxad (Ἀρφαξάδ); son of Shem; a brother of Asshur, Elam, Lud and Aram; father of Cainan.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '아르박삿'이라 불림. 셈의 아들. 앗수르, 엘람, 룻과 아람의 형제. 가이난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아르박삿은 셈의 아들로 홍수 후 이 년 만에 태어났으며 아브라함의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Artaxerxes Longimanus, an emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian king during Ezra and Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Artaxerxes was the Persian king who allowed Ezra and Nehemiah to return to Jerusalem (<ref="Ezra 7:1,11-12,21; Neh.2.1; 5:14">Ezra 7:1,11-12,21; Neh.2.1; 5:14</ref>).
persons.article: Artaxerxes was a Persian king who ruled during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. In the seventh year of his reign, he authorized Ezra the priest and scribe to lead a group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem. Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter granting him authority to teach the law, appoint magistrates and judges, and requisition supplies from the provincial treasuries. In Artaxerxes' twentieth year, his cupbearer Nehemiah learned that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and asked the king for permission to return and rebuild them. Artaxerxes sent Nehemiah to Judah as governor, with letters authorizing him to obtain timber for the walls. He is probably to be identified with Artaxerxes I Longimanus, who ruled the Persian Empire from 465 to 424 BC.
persons.summary: A king living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.4.7 (though some think this is another Artaxerxes) referred to as Artaxerxes (אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׂתָּא), or Artaxerxes (Aramiac אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׂתְּא); son of Xerxes I or Ahasuerus and Vashti; brother of Darius.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 황제 아닥사스다 롱기마누스. Ezr.4.7에 처음 언급되며 '아닥사스다'라 불림. 아하수에로와 와스디의 아들. 다리오의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아닥사스다는 에스라와 느헤미야가 예루살렘으로 돌아가도록 허락한 페르시아 왕이었다.
persons.article_ko: 아닥사스다는 에스라와 느헤미야 시대에 다스린 페르시아 왕이었다. 그의 통치 칠 년째에 그는 제사장이며 서기관인 에스라가 유대인 포로 무리를 예루살렘으로 이끌도록 허락했다. 아닥사스다는 에스라에게 율법을 가르치고 관리와 재판관을 임명하며 지방 곳간에서 물자를 조달할 권한을 부여하는 편지를 주었다. 아닥사스다 통치 이십 년째에 그의 술 맡은 관원 느헤미야는 예루살렘 성벽이 무너졌다는 것을 알고 돌아가서 그것을 재건할 허락을 왕에게 요청했다. 아닥사스다는 느헤미야를 유다의 총독으로 보내며 성벽을 위한 목재를 얻을 권한을 부여하는 편지들을 주었다. 그는 아마 기원전 465년부터 424년까지 페르시아 제국을 다스린 아닥사스다 1세 롱기마누스와 동일 인물로 여겨진다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Companion of Paul, potential replacement for Titus
persons.short: Artemas was a companion of Paul who could potentially replace Titus in Crete (<ref="Titus 3:12">Titus 3:12</ref>).
persons.article: Artemas was a Christian mentioned by Paul in his letter to Titus. Paul stated that he might send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus, presumably to assist or replace him in his work on the island of Crete. This suggests that Artemas was a trusted colleague of Paul and capable of handling important responsibilities in the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Tit.3.12 only referred to as Artemas (Ἀρτεμάς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Tit.3.12에 처음 언급되며 '아데마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아데마는 바울의 동역자로, 그레데에서 디도를 대신할 수 있는 사람이었다.

persons.description: People from Arvad(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Canaanite descendants of Canaan, son of Ham
persons.short: The Arvadites were a Canaanite People from Canaan, son of Ham (<ref="Gen.10.18; 1Ch.1.16">Gen.10.18; 1Ch.1.16</ref>).
persons.article: The Arvadites were a Canaanite people group descended from Arvad, one of the sons of Canaan, who was a son of Ham and grandson of Noah. They are mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1, which describe the spreading out of Noah's descendants after the flood. The Arvadites likely lived in the city of Arvad, an island city located off the coast of modern-day Syria. Arvad was known for its maritime trade and was a significant Phoenician port city.
persons.summary: People from Arvad(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at Gen.10.18 only referred to as Arvadites (אַרְוָדִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 아르왓 족속. Gen.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '아르왓'이라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 스말과 하맛의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 아르왓 족속은 함의 아들 가나안의 후손인 가나안 족속이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Steward of King Elah's household in Tirzah
persons.short: Arza was the steward of King Elah's household in Tirzah (<ref="1Ki.16.9">1Ki.16.9</ref>).
persons.article: Arza was the steward of the household of Elah, king of Israel. Elah was the son of Baasha and became king in the twenty-sixth year of Asa, king of Judah. However, Elah's reign was short-lived. While Elah was drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza in Tirzah, his servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspired against him and killed him. This fulfilled the prophecy against Baasha's house due to his evil ways.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.16.9 only referred to as Arza (אַרְצָא).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.16.9에 처음 언급되며 '아르사'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아르사는 디르사에서 엘라 왕의 왕궁을 관리하던 신하였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper who resettled in Jerusalem
persons.short: Asa was a Levite gatekeeper who resettled in Jerusalem (<ref="1Ch.9.16">1Ch.9.16</ref>).
persons.article: Asa was a Levite mentioned in a list of people who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was a gatekeeper and the son of Berechiah, the son of Asa. The Levites were responsible for various duties in the temple, including serving as gatekeepers. Asa's mention in this context suggests that he was part of the group of Levites who returned to Jerusalem to help restore worship at the temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.16 only referred to as Asa (אָסָא); a son of Elkanah; father of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.16에 처음 언급되며 '아사'라 불림. 엘가나의 아들. 베레갸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아사는 예루살렘에 재정착한 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Abijah; father of Jehoshaphat
persons.short: Asa was a king of Judah who reigned for 41 years, known for his religious reforms (1Kings 15; 2Chr 14-16).
persons.article: Asa was the third king of Judah, son of Abijah (or 'Abijam') and grandson of Rehoboam. He reigned for 41 years, from the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel. Asa did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, removing idols, male cult prostitutes, and high places from Judah. He even deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an obscene image of Asherah. Asa faced an invasion by Zerah the Ethiopian but defeated him with God's help after crying out to the Lord. In his later years, Asa sought help from Ben-Hadad king of Syria against Baasha king of Israel instead of relying on God and imprisoned the seer Hanani for rebuking him. Asa developed a severe foot disease but did not seek the Lord's help. He died and was succeeded by his son Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.15.8 referred to as Asa (אָסָא), or Asaph (Ἀσά); a son of Abijah; husband of Azubah; father of Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.15.8에 처음 언급되며 '아사'라 불림. 아비야의 아들. 아수바의 남편. 여호사밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아사는 유다 왕으로 사십일 년간 다스렸으며 종교개혁으로 알려져 있다.
persons.article_ko: 아사는 유다의 세 번째 왕이며 아비야(아비얌이라고도 함)의 아들이고 르호보암의 손자였다. 그는 이스라엘 왕 여로보암 통치 이십 년째부터 사십일 년간 다스렸다. 아사는 여호와 보시기에 정직히 행하여 우상과 남색하는 자들, 산당을 유다에서 제거했다. 그는 심지어 할머니 마아가가 아세라의 흉측한 목상을 만들었기 때문에 그녀를 태후의 자리에서 폐위시켰다. 아사는 구스 사람 세라의 침공에 직면했으나 여호와께 부르짖은 후 하나님의 도우심으로 그를 물리쳤다. 말년에 아사는 하나님을 의지하는 대신 이스라엘 왕 바아사를 대적하기 위해 시리아 왕 벤하닷의 도움을 구했고, 그를 책망한 선견자 하나니를 투옥했다. 아사는 심한 발병에 걸렸으나 여호와의 도움을 구하지 않았다. 그는 죽었고 그의 아들 여호사밧이 뒤를 이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Asahel was a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in Judah (<ref="2Ch.17.8">2Ch.17.8</ref>).
persons.article: Asahel was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. As part of Jehoshaphat's reforms, Asahel was one of the Levites sent out to teach the Book of the Law in all the towns of Judah. This educational mission aimed to instruct the people in the ways of the Lord and strengthen their commitment to God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Asahel (עֲשָׂהאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '아사헬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아사헬은 여호사밧이 유다에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite in charge of tithes under Hezekiah
persons.short: Asahel was a Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute the tithes and dedicated things (<ref="2Ch.31.13">2Ch.31.13</ref>).
persons.article: Asahel was a Levite who served during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. As part of Hezekiah's reforms to restore proper worship, Asahel was appointed as one of the overseers in charge of distributing the tithes and dedicated things brought to the Temple. These contributions were used to support the priests and Levites serving in the Temple. Asahel's appointment suggests he was a trusted and responsible individual capable of handling these important duties.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Asahel (עֲשָׂהאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '아사헬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아사헬은 히스기야가 십일조와 봉헌물을 분배하도록 임명한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, killed by Abner
persons.short: Asahel, son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, was a fast runner killed by Abner during a battle (<ref="2Sam 2; 3:27, 30; 23:24; 1Ch.2.16; 11:26; 27:7">2Sam 2; 3:27, 30; 23:24; 1Ch.2.16; 11:26; 27:7</ref>).
persons.article: Asahel was the youngest son of Zeruiah, David's sister, and the brother of Joab and Abishai. He was known for his speed and agility, being described as fleet-footed as a wild gazelle. During the battle between the forces of David and Ish-Bosheth at Gibeon, Asahel pursued Abner, the commander of Ish-Bosheth's army. Despite Abner's warnings to turn aside, Asahel refused, and Abner killed him with the butt of his spear. Joab and Abishai later avenged their brother's death by murdering Abner when he came to support David. Asahel was one of David's mighty men and was placed in charge of a division in David's army.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.2.18 only referred to as Asahel (עֲשָׂהאֵל); his mother was Zeruiah; a brother of Abishai and Joab; father of Zebadiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 동료. 2Sa.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '아사헬'이라 불림. 스루야의 남편(이름 미상)와 스루야의 아들. 아비새와 요압의 형제. 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스루야의 아들이자 요압의 형제 아사헬은 발이 빠른 자였으나 전투 중 아브넬에게 죽임을 당했다.
persons.article_ko: 아사헬은 다윗의 누이 스루야의 막내아들이며 요압과 아비새의 형제였다. 그는 들노루처럼 발이 빠른 것으로 묘사되며 속도와 민첩함으로 알려졌다. 기브온에서 다윗과 이스보셋의 군대 사이의 전투 동안 아사헬은 이스보셋 군대의 지휘관 아브넬을 추격했다. 비켜서라는 아브넬의 경고에도 불구하고 아사헬은 거부했고, 아브넬은 그를 창 뒤 끝으로 죽였다. 요압과 아비새는 후에 아브넬이 다윗을 지지하러 왔을 때 그를 살해하여 형제의 죽음을 복수했다. 아사헬은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었고 다윗 군대의 한 부대를 맡았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Opposed Ezra's dissolution of mixed marriages
persons.short: Asahel, along with Jahzeiah, opposed Ezra's plan to dissolve mixed marriages among the returned exiles (<ref="Ezra 10:15">Ezra 10:15</ref>).
persons.article: Asahel was one of two individuals mentioned in Ezra 10 who opposed Ezra's plan to dissolve the mixed marriages among the Jewish people who had returned from Babylonian exile. When Ezra called for the people to separate from their foreign wives and children, Asahel and Jahzeiah stood against this decision. However, the assembly ultimately agreed with Ezra, and the mixed marriages were ended.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.15 only referred to as Asahel (עֲשָׂהאֵל); father of Jonathan.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '아사헬'이라 불림. 요나단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아사헬은 야스야와 함께 포로 귀환자들의 이방인 혼인을 해소하려는 에스라의 계획에 반대했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite leader who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem
persons.short: Asaiah was a Levite leader who assisted in bringing the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem during David's reign (<ref="1Ch.15.6, 11">1Ch.15.6, 11</ref>).
persons.article: Asaiah was a Levite leader during the reign of King David. When David gathered the Levites to bring the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem, Asaiah was one of the leaders mentioned. He was part of the clan of Merari, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. David instructed Asaiah and other Levite leaders to appoint their relatives as musicians and singers to accompany the procession of the ark. Asaiah's leadership role in this significant event demonstrates his importance among the Levites and his involvement in the worship life of Israel.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.6 only referred to as Asaiah (עֲשָׂיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.6에 처음 언급되며 '아사야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아사야는 다윗 왕 시대에 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮기는 일을 도운 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Asaiah was a Simeonite leader during the reign of King Hezekiah (<ref="1Ch.4.36">1Ch.4.36</ref>).
persons.article: Asaiah was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He is mentioned in a genealogy of Simeon in 1Chronicles 4. The passage describes how some of the Simeonites, including Asaiah, sought new pasture lands for their flocks and migrated to Gedor, where they found rich, good pasture. They also destroyed the Hamites and Meunites who lived there and settled in their place. Asaiah's mention as a leader suggests he played a significant role in this expansion of Simeonite territory.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.36 only referred to as Asaiah (עֲשָׂיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.36에 처음 언급되며 '아사야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아사야는 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Merarite Levite, ancestor of Ethan the singer
persons.short: Asaiah was a Merarite Levite, an ancestor of Ethan the singer (<ref="1Ch.6.30">1Ch.6.30</ref>).
persons.article: Asaiah was a Levite of the Merari clan, mentioned in the genealogy of Ethan, a renowned singer in the time of King David. Asaiah is listed as the son of Haggiah and the father of Joel in this lineage. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and later the temple. As an ancestor of Ethan, Asaiah was part of a family line known for their musical abilities and service in worship.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.30 only referred to as Asaiah (עֲשָׂיָה); a son of Haggiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.30에 처음 언급되며 '아사야'라 불림. 학기야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아사야는 므라리 계열 레위인으로, 노래하는 자 에단의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem
persons.short: Asaiah, a descendant of Judah, lived in Jerusalem (<ref="1Ch.9.5">1Ch.9.5</ref>).
persons.article: Asaiah was a descendant of Judah mentioned in a list of people who lived in Jerusalem, recorded in 1Chronicles 9. He is described as "the firstborn of the Shilonites," which likely refers to a branch of the tribe of Judah. The context suggests that this list represents those who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. As a descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem, Asaiah was part of the group that helped repopulate the city and restore its community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.5 only referred to as Asaiah (עֲשָׂיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.5에 처음 언급되며 '아사야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 유다의 후손 아사야는 예루살렘에 거주했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Servant of King Josiah during Book of Law discovery
persons.short: Asaiah was a servant of King Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah about the Book of the Law (<ref="2Ki.22.12, 14; 2Ch.34.20">2Ki.22.12, 14; 2Ch.34.20</ref>).
persons.article: Asaiah was a servant of King Josiah of Judah during the time when the Book of the Law was discovered in the Temple. When the book was read to Josiah, he tore his robes in distress and sent Asaiah, along with several others, to inquire of the Lord through the prophetess Huldah. Huldah confirmed that the curses written in the book would come upon Judah for their idolatry but that Josiah would not see this judgment because of his humble response. Asaiah's involvement in this event suggests he was a trusted servant of the king and played a role in Josiah's religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.22.12 only referred to as Asaiah (עֲשָׂיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.22.12에 처음 언급되며 '아사야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아사야는 요시야 왕의 신하로, 율법책에 관해 여선지자 훌다에게 문의하도록 보냄을 받았다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician, psalmist, and ancestor of temple singers
persons.article: Asaph was a prominent Levite musician and psalmist during the reign of King David. He was appointed by David as one of the leaders of music in the tabernacle and later in the temple. Asaph, along with Heman and Ethan, was responsible for leading the musical worship and prophesying with lyres, harps, and cymbals. He also composed and collected psalms, with 12 psalms (50, 73-83) attributed to him in the Book of Psalms. Asaph's descendants continued to serve as temple singers and musicians for generations, as evidenced by their mention in the reigns of subsequent kings and in the post-exilic period. The "sons of Asaph" are often referred to as a distinct group of temple singers, highlighting the enduring legacy of Asaph's musical contributions to Israelite worship.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.39 only referred to as Asaph (אָסָף); a son of Berechiah; father of Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asharelah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.6.39에 처음 언급되며 '아삽'이라 불림. 베레갸의 아들. 삭굴, 요셉, 느다니야와 아사렐라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아삽은 다윗 왕 시대의 레위인 음악가이자 시편 기자였으며, 그 후손들은 성전에서 노래하는 자로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 아삽은 다윗 왕 시대의 저명한 레위인 음악가이며 시편 기자였다. 그는 다윗에 의해 성막, 후에는 성전에서 음악을 이끄는 지도자 중 한 사람으로 임명되었다. 아삽은 헤만, 에단과 함께 음악 예배를 이끌고 수금과 비파, 심벌즈로 예언하는 책임을 맡았다. 그는 또한 시편을 작곡하고 편집했는데, 시편에서 열두 편(50편, 73-83편)이 그의 것으로 여겨진다. 아삽의 후손은 여러 세대 동안 계속해서 성전 노래하는 자이며 음악가로 섬겼는데, 이는 후대 왕들의 통치 기간과 포로 이후 시대에 언급된 것에서 알 수 있다. '아삽의 자손'은 종종 성전 노래하는 자들의 뚜렷한 집단으로 언급되며, 이는 이스라엘 예배에 대한 아삽의 음악적 기여의 지속적인 유산을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite descendant who resettled in Jerusalem
persons.short: Asaph was a Levite descendant who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile (<ref="1Ch.9.15; Neh.11.17">1Ch.9.15; Neh.11.17</ref>).
persons.article: Asaph is mentioned in the lists of Levites who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, recorded in 1Chronicles 9 and Nehemiah 11. He is described as a descendant of Gershom, one of the sons of Levi. In the parallel passage in Nehemiah, he is called "Zabdi the son of Asaph." These lists highlight the importance of the Levites in restoring worship and community life in Jerusalem after the exile. As a Levite descendant living in Jerusalem, Asaph would have likely been involved in the various duties and responsibilities assigned to the Levites in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.15 only referred to as Asaph (אָסָף); father of Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.15에 처음 언급되며 '아삽'이라 불림. 시그리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아삽은 포로 귀환 후 예루살렘에 재정착한 레위인 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Recorder during King Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Asaph served as the recorder during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah (<ref="2Ki.18.18, 37; Isa.36.3, 22">2Ki.18.18, 37; Isa.36.3, 22</ref>).
persons.article: Asaph was an official who served as the recorder during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. When the Assyrian king Sennacherib invaded Judah and threatened Jerusalem, Hezekiah sent a delegation, including Asaph, to meet with the Assyrian officials. The Assyrian representative, the Rabshakeh, delivered a threatening message, urging the people of Jerusalem to surrender. Asaph, along with the other officials, tore their clothes in distress and reported the message to Hezekiah. As the recorder, Asaph likely had responsibilities related to official records and correspondence in the royal court.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.18 only referred to as Asaph (אָסָף); father of Joah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.18.18에 처음 언급되며 '아삽'이라 불림. 요아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아삽은 유다 왕 히스기야 시대에 사관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Keeper of the king's forest during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Asaph was the keeper of the king's forest during Nehemiah's time (<ref="Neh.2.8">Neh.2.8</ref>).
persons.article: Asaph is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the keeper of the king's forest. When Nehemiah requested permission from King Artaxerxes to return to Jerusalem and rebuild its walls, he also asked for letters to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, to obtain timber for the construction. As the keeper of the king's forest, Asaph was likely responsible for managing and protecting the royal forest lands and overseeing the distribution of timber resources. His cooperation was essential for Nehemiah to secure the necessary materials for the rebuilding project in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.2.8 only referred to as Asaph (אָסָף).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.2.8에 처음 언급되며 '아삽'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아삽은 느헤미야 시대에 왕의 삼림을 관리하는 자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jehallelel, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Asarel was a son of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah (<ref="1Ch.4.16">1Ch.4.16</ref>).
persons.article: Asarel is briefly mentioned in 1Chronicles 4 as one of the sons of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah. He is listed along with his brothers Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel. This genealogy is part of a larger record of the descendants of Judah, providing a glimpse into the family lines within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.16 only referred to as Asarel (אֲשַׂרְאֵל); son of Jehallelel; a brother of Ziph, Ziphah and Tiria.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.16에 처음 언급되며 '아사렐'이라 불림. 여할렐렐의 아들. 십, 시바와 디리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아사렐은 유다의 후손인 여할렐렐의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
persons.short: Asen was an ancestor of 223 individuals who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Asen was the ancestor of a group of people who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian captivity (Neh. 7:24). According to the records, 223 individuals from Asen's family were among those who made the journey back to their homeland. The return of the exiles to Jerusalem was a significant event in Jewish history, as it marked the beginning of the restoration of their religious and cultural identity after decades of captivity in Babylon. The mention of Asen and the number of his descendants highlights the importance of family lineage and the preservation of ancestral records among the returning exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.19 only referred to as Asen (Ἀσέν).
persons.note: LXX(70인역) 전용 인명, 개역개정 본문에 없음
persons.summary_ko: Neh.7.24에 처음 언급되며 'Asen'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아센은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 223명의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Egyptian wife of Joseph; mother of Manasseh and Ephraim
persons.short: Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, was given to Joseph as his wife by Pharaoh (<ref="Gen.41.45, 50; 46:20">Gen.41.45, 50; 46:20</ref>).
persons.article: Asenath was an Egyptian woman who became the wife of Joseph, the son of Israel (or 'Jacob'), during his rise to power in Egypt. She was the daughter of Potiphera, a priest of On (Heliopolis), and was given to Joseph by Pharaoh as a wife when he was appointed as the second-in-command over Egypt. Asenath bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, who would later become the patriarchs of two of the twelve tribes of Israel. As the wife of Joseph and the mother of two important tribal leaders, Asenath played a significant role in the history of Israel, despite her Egyptian background.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.41.45 only referred to as Asenath (אָֽסְנַת); a daughter of Potiphera; wife of Joseph; mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.41.45에 처음 언급되며 '아스낫'이라 불림. 보디베라의 딸. 요셉의 아내. 므낫세와 에브라임의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 온의 제사장 보디베라의 딸 아스낫은 바로에 의해 요셉의 아내로 주어졌다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician appointed by David to prophesy with lyres
persons.short: Asharelah (or Jesharelah) was a Levite musician appointed by David to prophesy with lyres (<ref="1Ch.25.2, 14">1Ch.25.2, 14</ref>).
persons.article: Asharelah, also known as Jesharelah, was a Levite musician during the reign of King David. He was one of the sons of Asaph, a prominent Levite musician and psalmist. Asharelah was appointed by David to lead a group of musicians who prophesied with lyres, along with his brothers. This role involved using music as a means of prophetic worship and declaring the words of the Lord. Asharelah's inclusion in this list of musicians highlights the importance of music and prophetic worship in the Israelite culture during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.2 referred to as Asharelah (אֲשַׂרְאֵ֫לָה), or Jesharelah (יְשַׂרְאֵ֫לָה); son of Asaph; a brother of Zaccur, Joseph and Nethaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.2에 처음 언급되며 '아사렐라'라 불림. 아삽의 아들. 삭굴, 요셉과 느다니야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아사렐라(여사렐라라고도 함)는 다윗이 수금으로 예언하도록 임명한 레위인 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Bela@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Becher@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Naaman@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Muppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Huppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ard@Gen.46.21, Ahiram@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Jediael@1Ch.7.6-
persons.brief: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ashbelite clan
persons.short: Ashbel was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ashbelite clan (<ref="Gen.46.21; Num.26.38; 1Ch.8.1">Gen.46.21; Num.26.38; 1Ch.8.1</ref>).
persons.article: Ashbel was one of the sons of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is mentioned in the genealogies of Benjamin in Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles. Ashbel was among the 70 members of Jacob's household who went down to Egypt during the famine. He became the founder of the Ashbelite clan within the tribe of Benjamin. In the census taken in the wilderness, the Ashbelite clan was numbered among the descendants of Benjamin. As one of the grandsons of Jacob and a progenitor of a clan, Ashbel played a role in the growth and development of the Israelite people.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.21 referred to as Ashbel (אַשְׁבֵּל), or Ashbelite (אַשְׁבֵּלִי); son of Benjamin; a brother of Bela, Becher, Gera, Naaman, Ahiram, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, Ard, Ahiram and Jediael.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.21에 처음 언급되며 '아스벨'이라 불림. 베냐민의 아들. 벨라, 베겔, 게라, 나아만, 로스, 뭅빔, 훔빔, 아릇, 에히와 여디아엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아스벨은 베냐민의 아들로 아스벨 가문의 시조였다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Dan@Gen.30.6-1Ch, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev
persons.brief: Son of Jacob and Zilpah, founder of the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Asher was the eighth son of Jacob, born to Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, and became the founder of the tribe of Asher (<ref="Gen.30.13; 46:17; Deu.33:24; Jos.19:24-34; Luke 2.36">Gen.30.13; 46:17; Deu.33:24; Jos.19:24-34; Luke 2.36</ref>).
persons.article: Asher was the eighth son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and the second son of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant. He was born in Paddan-aram and was one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Asher's descendants formed the tribe of Asher, which was allocated territory in the northern part of Canaan, along the Mediterranean coast. The tribe of Asher was known for its fertile land and abundance of olive oil. In the blessings of Jacob and Moses, Asher was described as being blessed with rich food and providing royal delicacies. During the period of the judges, Asher was criticized for not joining the fight against Sisera. The tribe of Asher was among those taken into Assyrian captivity. In the New Testament, Anna, a prophetess, is mentioned as being from the tribe of Asher. In the book of Revelation, 12,000 from the tribe of Asher are sealed as servants of God.
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Asher living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.30.13 referred to as Asher (אָשֵׁר), or Asherite or "pine" (אָשֵׁרִי), or Ashurite (אֲשׁוּרִי), or Asher (Ἀσήρ); son of Israel and Zilpah; a brother of Gad; half-brother of: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Issachar, Zebulun, Dinah, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah and Serah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.30.13에 처음 언급되며 '아셀'이라 불림. 이스라엘과 실바의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 단, 납달리, 갓, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 임나, 이스와, 이스위, 브리아와 세라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아셀은 야곱의 여덟째 아들로, 레아의 여종 실바에게서 태어났으며 아셀 지파의 시조가 되었다.
