persons.article: Azmaveth is mentioned in 1Ch.12.3 as the father of two of the Benjamite warriors, Jeziel and Pelet, who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. The fact that Azmaveth's sons were among David's supporters suggests that they had chosen to align themselves with David, even though their family was closely associated with Saul. The genealogies in Chronicles serve to trace the lineage of important individuals and to demonstrate the continuity of the people of Israel, even during times of political transition. when he was fleeing from King Saul. During this time, David had taken refuge among the Philistines, and a group of warriors from various tribes of Israel came to support him. Azmaveth, along with other skilled archers and slingers from the tribe of Benjamin, pledged their allegiance to David and fought alongside him. The fact that these warriors were willing to leave their homes and families to support David demonstrates their belief in his leadership and their commitment to his cause. The support of these warriors was crucial to David's eventual success in establishing his kingdom and uniting the tribes of Israel under his rule.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Azmaveth (עַזְמָ֫וֶת); father of Jeziel, Pelet.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '아스마'라 불림. 여시엘과 벨렛의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 용사 아스마웻은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of royal treasuries under King David
persons.short: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of King David's treasuries (<ref="1Ch.27.25">1Ch.27.25</ref>).
persons.article: Azmaveth, the son of Adiel, is mentioned in 1Ch.27.25 as the overseer of King David's treasuries. This chapter lists the various officials and administrators who served in David's government, and Azmaveth is identified as the one responsible for managing the royal treasuries. This position would have involved overseeing the collection, storage, and distribution of the wealth and resources of the kingdom. The fact that Azmaveth was entrusted with this important role indicates that he was a trusted and capable individual who had earned the confidence of King David. The effective management of the royal treasuries was crucial for the stability and prosperity of the kingdom, and Azmaveth's appointment to this position highlights the importance of wise financial administration in the reign of King David.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.25 only referred to as Azmaveth (עַזְמָ֫וֶת); a son of Adiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.25에 처음 언급되며 '아스마'라 불림. 아디엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아디엘의 아들 아스마웻은 다윗 왕의 곳간을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah
persons.short: Azmaveth, a descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah..
persons.article: Azmaveth is mentioned in 1Ch.8.36 and 1Ch.9.42 as a descendant of Saul, the first king of Israel. He is listed in the genealogy of Saul's family, which is given in two parallel passages in the book of Chronicles.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.36 only referred to as Azmaveth (עַזְמָ֫וֶת); son of Jehoaddah; a brother of Alemeth and Zimri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.36에 처음 언급되며 '아스마'라 불림. 여호앗다의 아들. 알레멧과 시므리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아스마웻은 사울의 후손으로 여호앗다의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, a Barhumite
persons.short: Azmaveth the Barhumite was one of David's mighty men, known for his valor (<ref="2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33">2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33</ref>).
persons.article: Azmaveth the Barhumite is mentioned in 2Sa.23.31 and 1Ch.11.33 as one of David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of elite warriors who served under King David and were renowned for their bravery and military prowess. Azmaveth is described as a Barhumite, indicating his place of origin or family lineage. His inclusion in the list of mighty men suggests that he had distinguished himself in battle and had earned a reputation for his valor and loyalty to King David. The mighty men played a significant role in establishing and maintaining David's kingdom, and their individual acts of heroism were celebrated in Israelite history.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.31 only referred to as Azmaveth (עַזְמָ֫וֶת).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.31에 처음 언급되며 '아스마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바하룸 사람 아스마웻은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 용맹함으로 알려졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy of Matthew
persons.short: Azor was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in the genealogy of Matthew (<ref="Matt 1:13, 14">Matt 1:13, 14</ref>).
persons.article: Azor is mentioned in Mat.1.13-14 as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy recorded in the Gospel of Matthew. This genealogy traces the lineage of Jesus from Abraham through his earthly father, Joseph. Azor is listed as the son of Eliakim and the father of Zadok, placing him in the period after the Babylonian exile. The inclusion of Azor in the genealogy of Jesus emphasizes the continuity of the Messianic line and the fulfillment of God's promises through the generations. The genealogy in Matthew serves to establish Jesus' legal claim to the throne of David and to demonstrate his connection to the patriarchs and prophets of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Mat.1.13 only referred to as Azor (Ἀζώρ); a son of Eliakim; father of Zadok.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Mat.1.13에 처음 언급되며 '아소르'라 불림. 엘리야김의 아들. 사독의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아솔은 마태복음의 예수 그리스도 족보에 언급된 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ruler of the tribe of Naphtali under David
persons.short: Azriel son of Jeremoth was the ruler of the tribe of Naphtali during the reign of King David (<ref="1Ch.27.19">1Ch.27.19</ref>).
persons.article: Azriel, the son of Jeremoth, is mentioned in 1Ch.27.19 as the ruler of the tribe of Naphtali during the reign of King David. This chapter lists the leaders of each tribe who were responsible for overseeing their respective tribes in various administrative and military matters. Azriel's position as the ruler of Naphtali suggests that he was a trusted and capable leader who had earned the confidence of King David. The tribe of Naphtali was located in the northern part of Israel, and its leaders would have been responsible for governing the people, maintaining order, and organizing the tribe's military forces when necessary. The mention of Azriel and the other tribal leaders demonstrates the importance of effective leadership and organization in the administration of David's kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.19 only referred to as Azriel (עַזְרִיאֵל); father of Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.19에 처음 언급되며 '아스리엘'이라 불림. 여레못의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여레못의 아들 아스리엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 납달리 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
persons.short: Azriel was a head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead (<ref="1Ch.5.24">1Ch.5.24</ref>).
persons.article: Azriel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.24 as one of the heads of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh that settled in Gilead. The chapter describes the genealogies and territories of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, who lived on the east side of the Jordan River. Azriel is listed along with other leaders of Manasseh who are described as valiant warriors, famous men, and heads of their fathers' houses. This suggests that Azriel was a prominent figure within his tribe, known for his military prowess and leadership abilities. The mention of Azriel and the other leaders highlights the importance of family structure and tribal organization in the allocation of land and the defense of Israel's territories.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.24 only referred to as Azriel (עַזְרִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.24에 처음 언급되며 '아스리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아스리엘은 길르앗에 있던 므낫세 반 지파의 가문 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Official sent to arrest the prophet Jeremiah
persons.short: Azriel was one of the officials sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest the prophet Jeremiah (<ref="Jer.36.26">Jer.36.26</ref>).
persons.article: Azriel is mentioned in Jer.36.26 as one of the officials sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest the prophet Jeremiah and his scribe, Baruch. The chapter describes how Jeremiah had dictated a prophecy to Baruch, warning of the impending judgment on Judah, and Baruch had read the scroll in the temple. When King Jehoiakim heard the words of the prophecy, he burned the scroll and ordered the arrest of Jeremiah and Baruch. Azriel, along with two other officials, Jerahmeel and Shelemiah, was tasked with carrying out this order. However, the text notes that the Lord had hidden Jeremiah and Baruch, and they were not found. The incident highlights the opposition and persecution faced by Jeremiah in delivering God's message to a rebellious nation and the protection provided by God for his faithful servants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.26 only referred to as Azriel (עַזְרִיאֵל); father of Seraiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '아스리엘'이라 불림. 스라야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아스리엘은 여호야김 왕이 선지자 예레미야를 체포하러 보낸 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of David through Jehoiachin.
persons.short: Azrikam was a descendant of David through Jehoiachin.
persons.article: Azrikam was a descendant of King David through the line of Jehoiachin, who was taken captive to Babylon. He is mentioned in the genealogy found in 1Ch.3.23 as one of the sons or descendants of Neariah, who was himself a descendant of David through Solomon and the kings of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.23 only referred to as Azrikam (עַזְרִיקָם); son of Neariah; a brother of Elioenai and Hizkiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '아스리감'이라 불림. 느아랴의 아들. 에료에내와 히스기야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아스리감은 여호야긴을 통한 다윗의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Saul and Jonathan.
persons.short: Azrikam was a descendant of Saul and Jonathan.
persons.article: Azrikam was a descendant of King Saul and his son Jonathan, as recorded in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Ch.8.38 and 1Ch.9.44. He was one of the six sons of Azel, who was a descendant of Jonathan. The genealogies trace Azrikam's lineage back through several generations to Saul, Israel's first king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.38 only referred to as Azrikam (עַזְרִיקָם); son of Azel; a brother of Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.38에 처음 언급되며 '아스리감'이라 불림. 아셀의 아들. 보그루, 이스마엘, 스아랴, 오바댜와 하난의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아스리감은 사울과 요나단의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite living in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Azrikam was a Levite who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Azrikam was a Levite who lived in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah, after the return from Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in two parallel lists of the inhabitants of Jerusalem found in 1Ch.9.14 and Neh.11.15. In both passages, Azrikam is identified as a Levite and a descendant of Hashabiah. The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the temple services. Azrikam's presence in Jerusalem suggests he may have had duties related to the temple worship that was being reestablished at that time.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.14 only referred to as Azrikam (עַזְרִיקָם); a son of Hashabiah; father of Hasshub.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.14에 처음 언급되며 '아스리감'이라 불림. 하사뱌의 아들. 핫숩의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아스리감은 예루살렘에 거주한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An official in King Ahaz's household.
persons.short: Azrikam was an official in charge of King Ahaz's palace.
persons.article: Azrikam was an official who served in the royal court of King Ahaz of Judah. He held the position of being in charge of the palace, which was an important role in the king's administration. 2Ch.28.7 records that Azrikam was killed by Zichri, a mighty warrior from Ephraim, during a time of war between Judah and Israel. This occurred when Ahaz was facing military threats from both Israel and Syria, and had turned away from fully following the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.7 only referred to as Azrikam (עַזְרִיקָם).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.28.7에 처음 언급되며 '아스리감'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아스리감은 아하스 왕궁을 관리하는 관리였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Caleb and mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
persons.short: Azubah was Caleb's wife and the mother of his sons Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
persons.article: Azubah was the wife of Caleb, who was a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah. She is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah recorded in 1Ch.2.18-19. The passage states that Caleb had sons by Azubah his wife, and then lists their names as Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon. After this, it notes that Azubah died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.18 only referred to as Azubah (עֲזוּבָה); wife of Caleb; mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '아수바'라 불림. 갈렙의 아내. 아르돈, 예셀과 소밥의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아수바는 갈렙의 아내이며 그 아들 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: The mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.short: Azubah was the mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.article: Azubah was the wife of King Asa and the mother of King Jehoshaphat, who ruled over the Kingdom of Judah. She is mentioned in 1Ki.22.42 and 2Ch.20.31, which provide the introductory information about Jehoshaphat as he became king. Both passages state that Jehoshaphat's mother's name was Azubah, and identify her as the daughter of Shilhi.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.42 only referred to as Azubah (עֲזוּבָה); a daughter of Shilhi; wife of Asa; mother of Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.22.42에 처음 언급되며 '아수바'라 불림. 실히의 딸. 아사의 아내. 여호사밧의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 아수바는 유다 왕 여호사밧의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Paltiel, a leader from the tribe of Issachar.
persons.short: Azzan was the father of Paltiel, a leader from Issachar chosen to help divide Canaan.
persons.article: Azzan was an Israelite man from the tribe of Issachar. He is mentioned in Num.34.26 as the father of Paltiel. Paltiel was chosen as the leader from the tribe of Issachar to work with Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and one leader from each of the other tribes to divide the land of Canaan fairly among the Israelites. Being selected for this role suggests that Paltiel was respected within his tribe. By identifying Paltiel as the son of Azzan, the text implies that Azzan was also a man of good reputation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.26 only referred to as Azzan (עַזָּן); father of Paltiel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.26에 처음 언급되며 '앗산'이라 불림. 발디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 앗산은 잇사갈 지파에서 가나안 분배를 돕도록 선택된 지도자 발디엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of the wicked prince Jaazaniah.
persons.short: Azzur was the father of Jaazaniah, one of the wicked princes Ezekiel saw in a vision.
persons.article: Azzur is mentioned in Ezk.11.1 as the father of Jaazaniah, one of the twenty-five men Ezekiel saw in a vision at the entrance of the temple gate. These men are described as "princes of the people" and are portrayed as wicked leaders who were giving bad advice and plotting violence in Jerusalem. Ezekiel was brought to them in the vision to prophesy against them and announce the Lord's judgment on their evil plans. The text notes that another man named Pelatiah died as Ezekiel was prophesying, confirming the seriousness of God's message. Azzur is not directly accused of wrongdoing but is identified to specify which Jaazaniah was being condemned.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezk.11.1 only referred to as Azzur (עַזּוּר); father of Jaazaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezk.11.1에 처음 언급되며 '앗술'이라 불림. 야아사냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 앗술은 에스겔이 환상 중에 본 악한 방백 중 한 사람인 야아사냐의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of the false prophet Hananiah.
persons.short: Azzur was the father of Hananiah, a false prophet who opposed Jeremiah.
persons.article: Azzur was the father of Hananiah, a false prophet who prophesied against Jeremiah. In Jer.28.1, Hananiah is introduced as "the son of Azzur." Hananiah contradicted Jeremiah's prophecies about submitting to Babylon, claiming that God would break Babylon's yoke and restore the temple treasures within two years. Jeremiah denounced Hananiah's message as false, warning that he would die that year for promoting rebellion against the Lord. Hananiah died two months later, confirming he was not a true prophet. Identifying Hananiah as Azzur's son implies his family was known, though Azzur is not mentioned again.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.28.1 only referred to as Azzur (עַזּוּר); father of Hananiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.28.1에 처음 언급되며 '앗술'이라 불림. 하나냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 앗술은 예레미야를 대적한 거짓 선지자 하나냐의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Azzur was one of the leaders who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.article: Azzur is listed in Neh.10.17 as one of the leaders of the people who sealed the covenant made in the time of Nehemiah. After the Israelites had returned from exile in Babylon and rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, they gathered to confess their sins and commit to obeying God's law. Nehemiah 10 records the names of those who signed this agreement, including leaders, priests, Levites, and others. Azzur's presence on this list indicates he held some position of authority and influence among the people. By sealing the covenant, he was pledging to uphold its commitments.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.17 only referred to as Azzur (עַזּוּר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.17에 처음 언급되며 '앗술'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 앗술은 느헤미야의 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Reuben.
persons.short: Baal was a descendant of Reuben, the firstborn son of Jacob.
persons.article: Baal is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.5.5 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben. He is described as the son of Reaiah, who was the son of Micah, who was the son of Shimei. This lineage traces Baal's ancestry back to Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy is given in the context of describing the clans and leaders of Reuben, suggesting that Baal and his family were part of this tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.5 only referred to as Baal (בַּ֫עַל); a son of Reaiah; father of Beerah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.5에 처음 언급되며 '바알'이라 불림. 르아야의 아들. 브에라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바알은 야곱의 맏아들 르우벤의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Abdon@1Ch.8.30-, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Ahio@1Ch.8.31-, Zecher@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-
persons.brief: A son of Abiel and descendant of Benjamin.
persons.short: Baal was a son of Abiel and a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Baal is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Ch.8.30 and 1Ch.9.36. He was one of the sons of Abiel, who was a descendant of Benjamin. The genealogy traces Baal's lineage back to the patriarch Benjamin, showing his connection to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Baal had several brothers, including Ner, the grandfather of King Saul. This places Baal within the extended family of Israel's first king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.30 only referred to as Baal (בַּ֫עַל); son of Abiel and Maacah; a brother of Kish, Ner, Abdon, Zur, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher and Mikloth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.30에 처음 언급되며 '바알'이라 불림. 아비엘과 마아가의 아들. 기스, 넬, 압돈, 술, 나답, 그돌, 아효, 세겔과 미글롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바알은 아비엘의 아들로 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An overseer of olive and sycamore trees under David.
persons.short: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands under David's reign.
persons.article: Baal-hanan the Gederite was one of the officials who served under King David. In 1Ch.27.28, he is described as being in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands, which were likely the coastal plains and foothills of Judah. This was an important role, as olive oil and sycamore fruit were valuable crops in ancient Israel. Baal-hanan's title "the Gederite" suggests he was from the town of Geder or had an association with that place.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.28 only referred to as Baal-hanan (בַּ֫עַל חָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.28에 처음 언급되며 '바알하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 게델 사람 바알하난은 다윗 왕 시대에 평지의 감람나무와 뽕나무를 관리했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A king of Edom.
persons.short: Baal-hanan was a king of Edom who reigned before Israel had kings.
persons.article: Baal-hanan was one of the kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had kings. He is mentioned in the lists of Edomite kings found in Gen.36.38-39 and 1Ch.1.49-50. Baal-hanan is described as the son of Achbor, and he succeeded Shaul as king of Edom. After his death, Hadad became king in his place. The text does not provide any details about the length or events of Baal-hanan's reign. His name, which means "Baal is gracious," suggests that the Canaanite deity Baal was worshiped in Edom at that time.
persons.summary: A king of Edom living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.38 only referred to as Baal-hanan (בַּ֫עַל חָנָן); a son of Achbor.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.36.38에 처음 언급되며 '바알하난'이라 불림. 악볼의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바알하난은 이스라엘에 왕이 있기 전 다스린 에돔 왕이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of the Ammonites during the Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Baalis, the king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael to assassinate Gedaliah the governor.
persons.article: Baalis was the king of the Ammonites during the time of the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in Jer.40.14 in connection with a plot to assassinate Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians over the remnant of Judah. According to the text, Johanan warned Gedaliah that Baalis had sent a man named Ishmael to kill him. Gedaliah did not believe the warning and was subsequently murdered by Ishmael, causing the remaining Jews to flee to Egypt out of fear. This incident reveals that Baalis was opposed to the Babylonian-appointed governor and was willing to use violence to disrupt the fragile peace in Judah after the exile. The Ammonites, led by Baalis, were long-time enemies of Israel and may have seen Judah's weakened state as an opportunity to gain power in the region.
persons.summary: A king of the Ammonites living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.40.14 only referred to as Baalis (בַּעֲלִיס).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. Jer.40.14에 처음 언급되며 '바알리스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 암몬 왕 바알리스는 이스마엘을 보내 총독 그달랴를 암살하게 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Philistine god worshiped at Ekron.
persons.short: Baal-zebub was the god of Ekron whom Ahaziah consulted about his illness.
persons.article: Baal-zebub, meaning "Lord of the Flies," was the god of the Philistine city of Ekron. In 2Kings 1, King Ahaziah of Israel sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub whether he would recover from an illness. This action provoked God's anger, and the prophet Elijah confronted the king, prophesying that he would die for seeking guidance from a pagan god rather than the Lord. The narrative presents Baal-zebub as a false god whose worship was forbidden for Israelites. Consulting this deity was seen as a direct violation of the commandment to worship only the one true God. The passage also demonstrates the futility of trusting in false gods, as Baal-zebub had no power to heal Ahaziah or overturn God's decree of judgment.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.1.2 only referred to as Baal-zebub (בַּעַל זְבוּב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '바알세붑'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바알세붑은 아하시야가 자신의 병에 대해 물어본 에그론의 신이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
persons.short: Baana son of Ahilud was one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
persons.article: Baana son of Ahilud was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to oversee the territories of Israel. According to 1Ki.4.12, Baana's district included Taanach, Megiddo, and the region of Beth-shan near Zarethan. As a governor, Baana would have been responsible for administering his district, collecting taxes, and supplying provisions for the king's household. The twelve governors are listed as part of a description of Solomon's officials and the prosperity of his reign. Baana's position indicates he was a trusted official in Solomon's administration, helping to manage the kingdom's resources and maintain order in his assigned territory.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.12 only referred to as Baana (בַּעֲנָא); son of Ahilud; a brother of Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.12에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림. 아힐룻의 아들. 여호사밧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아힐룻의 아들 바아나는 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
persons.short: Baana son of Hushai governed the territory of Asher and Aloth under Solomon.
persons.article: Baana son of Hushai was another of the twelve district governors who served under King Solomon. He is mentioned in 1Ki.4.16 as being in charge of the territory of Asher and Aloth. Like the other governors, Baana would have had administrative duties in his district, ensuring the smooth running of local affairs and the collection of resources for the king. The fact that he was the son of Hushai suggests he may have been from a prominent family, as Hushai was a close advisor to King David. Baana's role as a governor reflects the organized structure of Solomon's kingdom and the king's delegation of authority to trusted officials.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.16 only referred to as Baana (בַּעֲנָא); a son of Hushai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.16에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림. 후새의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 후새의 아들 바아나는 솔로몬 치하에서 아셀과 알롯 지역을 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A man who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Baana son of Zadok made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Baana son of Zadok is briefly mentioned in Neh.3.4 as one of the people who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem. During the time of Nehemiah, the city's walls were in disrepair, leaving the inhabitants vulnerable. Nehemiah organized a massive rebuilding effort, with different individuals and families taking responsibility for specific sections. Baana worked on restoring a portion of the wall alongside Meremoth son of Uriah. The text does not provide any further details about Baana's background or role in the community. However, his participation in the wall rebuilding project suggests he was a man of some means and influence who was willing to contribute to the important task of fortifying Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.4 only referred to as Baana (בַּעֲנָא); father of Zadok.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림. 사독의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독의 아들 바아나는 예루살렘 성벽의 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from Netophah.
persons.short: Baanah the Netophathite was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Baanah the Netophathite is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty warriors found in 2Sa.23.29 and 1Ch.11.30. He is described as being from Netophah, a town in Judah. The mighty warriors were a group of elite soldiers who fought alongside David and were known for their exceptional skill and bravery in battle. Baanah's inclusion in this list indicates that he was a distinguished warrior who had proven his loyalty and valor in service to King David.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.29 only referred to as Baanah (בַּעֲנָה); father of Heleb.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.29에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림. 헬렙의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 느도바 사람 바아나는 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: David's compatriots living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A captain who murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.
persons.short: Baanah and his brother Rechab assassinated Ish-bosheth, hoping to gain favor with David.
persons.article: Baanah was one of the two captains who assassinated Ish-bosheth, the son of King Saul. After Saul's death, Ish-bosheth had been proclaimed king over Israel, while David ruled over Judah. According to 2Samuel 4, Baanah and his brother Rechab, who were Benjamites from Beeroth, entered Ish-bosheth's house while he was resting and killed him. They brought his head to David, hoping to be rewarded. However, David condemned their treacherous act and ordered their execution. The text describes Baanah and Rechab as wicked men who murdered an innocent person. Their actions were motivated by self-interest rather than loyalty. David's response demonstrated his integrity and respect for Saul's family, as he refused to condone violence against his rivals.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.4.2 only referred to as Baanah (בַּעֲנָה); son of Rimmon; a brother of Rechab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 동료들. 2Sa.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림. 림몬의 아들. 레갑의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바아나와 그의 형제 레갑은 다윗의 환심을 사려고 이스보셋을 암살했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Baanah was one of the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylon to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Baanah is listed among the leaders who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile, as recorded in Ezr.2.2 and Neh.7.7. He was part of the group that accompanied Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, in the first wave of returnees. The lists in Ezra and Nehemiah provide a record of the individuals and families who made the journey back to their homeland to rebuild the temple and the city of Jerusalem. Baanah's presence among the leaders suggests he held a position of responsibility and influence within the community of exiles. The text does not provide any further information about his specific role or contributions to the resettlement process.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.2 only referred to as Baanah (בַּעֲנָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.2에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바아나는 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Baanah was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Baanah is mentioned in Neh.10.27 as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant made during the time of Nehemiah. After the Israelites had returned from Babylonian exile and rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, they gathered to confess their sins and commit to obeying God's law. Nehemiah 10 records the names of those who signed this agreement, including leaders, priests, Levites, and others. Baanah's presence on this list indicates he held a position of authority and influence among the people. By sealing the covenant, he publicly declared his commitment to follow God's commandments and to support the spiritual and social reforms initiated by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.27 only referred to as Baanah (בַּעֲנָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '바아나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바아나는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A wife of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
persons.short: Baara was one of the wives of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Baara is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.8.8 as one of the wives of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin. The passage is part of a genealogy tracing the lineage of the tribe of Benjamin. It states that Shaharaim had children by his wives Hushim and Baara in the country of Moab, after he had divorced them. No further details are provided about Baara's life or her children. The mention of Moab suggests that Shaharaim may have lived there for a period of time, either voluntarily or as a result of exile. The genealogy serves to establish the Benjamite heritage of Shaharaim and his descendants.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.8 only referred to as Baara (בַּעֲרָא); wife of Shaharaim.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.8.8에 처음 언급되며 '바아라'라 불림. 사하라임의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 바아라는 베냐민의 후손인 사하라임의 아내 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite in the lineage of Gershom.
persons.short: Baaseiah was a Levite descended from Gershom, the son of Levi.
persons.article: Baaseiah is mentioned in 1Ch.6.40 as part of a genealogy of the Levites, specifically the descendants of Gershom, one of the sons of Levi. The Levites were the tribe designated to assist the priests in the tabernacle and temple worship. The genealogy traces the lineage of several prominent Levitical families. Baaseiah is listed as the father of Michael and the son of Malchijah. Beyond this genealogical information, no other details are provided about Baaseiah's life or specific role within the Levitical community. The inclusion of his name in the genealogy serves to establish the continuity and legitimacy of the Levitical priesthood across generations.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.40 only referred to as Baaseiah (בַּעֲשֵׂיָה); a son of Malchijah; father of Michael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.40에 처음 언급되며 '바아세야'라 불림. 말기야의 아들. 미가엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바아세야는 레위의 아들 게르솜을 통한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Third king of Israel who ruled for 24 years.
persons.short: Baasha, son of Ahijah, became king of Israel and reigned for 24 years.
persons.article: Baasha was the third king of the northern kingdom of Israel, ruling for 24 years (1Ki.15.33). He came to power by assassinating Nadab, the son of Jeroboam, and then proceeded to kill off all of Jeroboam's family (1Ki.15.27-29). Despite this, Baasha continued in the sinful ways of Jeroboam (1Ki.15.34). He engaged in warfare with Asa, king of Judah, who bribed Ben-hadad of Syria to attack Israel (1Ki.15.16-22; 2Ch.16.1-6). The prophet Jehu pronounced judgment on Baasha's dynasty, predicting its downfall (1Ki.16.1-4). After Baasha's death, his son Elah became king (1Ki.16.6). Years later, Baasha's sins were remembered alongside those of other wicked kings (1Ki.21.22; 2Ki.9.9). Jer.41.9 mentions a pit made by Baasha during his war with Asa, which was later used to dispose of bodies.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.15.16 only referred to as Baasha (בַּעְשָׁא); a son of Ahijah; father of Elah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.15.16에 처음 언급되며 '바아사'라 불림. 아히야의 아들. 엘라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아히야의 아들 바아사는 이스라엘 왕이 되어 이십사 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 바아사는 북이스라엘 왕국의 세 번째 왕으로, 이십사 년간 다스렸다(왕상 15:33). 그는 여로보암의 아들 나답을 암살하고 권력을 잡았으며, 그런 다음 여로보암 가문 전체를 죽였다(왕상 15:27-29). 그럼에도 바아사는 여로보암의 죄악된 길을 계속 이어갔다(왕상 15:34). 그는 유다 왕 아사와 전쟁을 치렀는데, 아사는 시리아의 벤하닷에게 뇌물을 주어 이스라엘을 공격하게 했다(왕상 15:16-22; 대하 16:1-6). 선지자 예후는 바아사의 왕조에 대한 심판을 선포하며 그 몰락을 예언했다(왕상 16:1-4). 바아사가 죽은 후 그의 아들 엘라가 왕이 되었다(왕상 16:6). 여러 해 후 바아사의 죄는 다른 악한 왕들의 죄와 함께 기억되었다(왕상 21:22; 왕하 9:9). 예레미야 41:9은 바아사가 아사와의 전쟁 중에 만든 구덩이를 언급하는데, 이는 후에 시신들을 처리하는 데 사용되었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Bakbakkar was a Levite who resided in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Bakbakkar is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.9.15 as one of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem. The context suggests that this was during the time of the return from Babylonian exile. The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the temple service.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.15 only referred to as Bakbakkar (בַּקְבַּקַּר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.15에 처음 언급되며 '박박갈'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 박박갈은 예루살렘에 거주한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Bakbuk was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
persons.article: Bakbuk is mentioned in Ezr.2.51 and Neh.7.53 as the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. The lists in Ezra and Nehemiah record the names of the families who returned to Judah to resettle and rebuild the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.51 only referred to as Bakbuk (בַּקְבּוּק).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.51에 처음 언급되며 '박북'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 박북은 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who served in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Bakbukiah was a Levite who held leadership roles in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Bakbukiah was a Levite who served in various roles in Jerusalem after the return from Babylonian exile. In Neh.11.17, he is described as the second among his brothers and one who gave thanks in prayer. This suggests he had a leadership role in worship. In Neh.12.9, Bakbukiah is listed along with other Levites who had responsibilities over the thanksgiving choirs. Later, in Neh.12.25, he is mentioned as one of the gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates. These references indicate that Bakbukiah was a prominent Levite who held multiple positions related to temple service and worship in the post-exilic community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.11.17 only referred to as Bakbukiah (בַּקְבֻּקְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.17에 처음 언급되며 '박부갸'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 박부갸는 포로 이후 예루살렘에서 지도적 역할을 맡은 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A prophet hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.
persons.short: Balaam was a pagan prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel, but he blessed them instead.
persons.article: Balaam was a pagan prophet from Pethor near the Euphrates River (Num.22.5). Balak, king of Moab, hired him to curse the Israelites as they approached Moabite territory (Num.22.6). Despite initial resistance, Balaam agreed to go with Balak's messengers after God permitted him, but only to speak what God told him (Num.22.7-21). On the way, Balaam's donkey saw the Angel of the Lord and saved Balaam from being killed (Num.22.22-35). In three oracles, Balaam blessed Israel instead of cursing them (Numbers 23-24). Later, Balaam was killed in Israel's battle against Midian (Num.31.8). He had advised the Midianites to entice Israel into idolatry and immorality (Num.31.16; Rev.2.14). Balaam's story is remembered as an example of God's sovereignty (Deu.23.4-5; Jos.24.9-10; Neh.13.2; Mic.6.5 and as a warning against greed and false teaching )(2Pe.2.15; Jud.1.11).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.22.5 referred to as Balaam (בִּלְעָם), or Balaam (Βαλαάμ); a son of Beor.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 선지자. Num.22.5에 처음 언급되며 '발람'이라 불림. 브올의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 발람은 발락에게 고용되어 이스라엘을 저주하려 했던 이방 선지자였으나 오히려 그들을 축복했다.
persons.article_ko: 발람은 유프라테스강 근처 브돌 출신의 이방 선지자였다(민 22:5). 모압 왕 발락은 이스라엘 백성이 모압 지역에 가까이 왔을 때 그들을 저주하도록 그를 고용했다(민 22:6). 처음에는 저항했으나 발람은 하나님이 허락하신 후 발락의 사신들과 함께 가기로 동의했다. 다만 하나님이 그에게 말씀하신 것만 말하는 조건이었다(민 22:7-21). 도중에 발람의 나귀가 여호와의 사자를 보고 발람이 죽임을 당하지 않도록 구했다(민 22:22-35). 세 번의 신탁에서 발람은 이스라엘을 저주하는 대신 축복했다(민수기 23-24장). 후에 발람은 이스라엘이 미디안을 대적하는 전투에서 죽임을 당했다(민 31:8). 그는 미디안 사람들에게 이스라엘을 우상숭배와 부도덕함으로 유혹하도록 조언했었다(민 31:16; 계 2:14). 발람의 이야기는 하나님의 주권의 본보기로 기억되며(신 23:4-5; 수 24:9-10; 느 13:2; 미 6:5) 탐욕과 거짓 가르침에 대한 경고로도 기억된다(벧후 2:15; 유 1:11).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Babylonian king Merodach-baladan (or 'Berodach-baladan').
persons.short: Baladan was the father of Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon.
persons.article: Baladan is mentioned in 2Ki.20.12 and Isa.39.1 as the father of Merodach-baladan (also known as Berodach-baladan), who was the king of Babylon. Merodach-baladan sent letters and a present to King Hezekiah of Judah after hearing of his illness and recovery. This diplomatic gesture led to Hezekiah showing the Babylonian envoys all his treasures, which the prophet Isaiah warned would one day be carried off to Babylon. Baladan is not mentioned in any other context, and no further information is provided about his life or role in Babylonian history. He is known only as the father of the king who initiated contact with Hezekiah. Merodach-baladan is likely the Babylonian king known outside the Bible as Marduk-apla-iddina II, who ruled Babylon in the late 8th century BC.
persons.summary: A king of Babylon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.20.12 only referred to as Baladan (בַּלְאֲדָן); father of Merodach-baladan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.20.12에 처음 언급되며 '발라단'이라 불림. 부로닥발라단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 발라단은 바벨론 왕 므로닥발라단의 아버지였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
persons.short: Balak, son of Zippor, was the king of Moab who tried to curse Israel through Balaam.
persons.article: Balak was the king of Moab during the time when the Israelites were approaching the Promised Land (Num.22.4). Fearing the large number of Israelites, Balak hired the pagan prophet Balaam to curse them (Num.22.5-6). Despite Balak's repeated attempts and offerings, Balaam could only bless Israel as God commanded (Numbers 23-24). Balak became angry with Balaam for not cursing Israel and sent him away (Num.24.10-11). Balak is mentioned in the farewell speeches of Joshua (Jos.24.9 and Jephthah )(Jdg.11.25 as an example of how God protected Israel from their enemies). The prophet Micah also refers to Balak's story as a reminder of God's righteousness (Mic.6.5). In Rev.2.14, Balak is associated with Balaam's scheme to entice Israel into idolatry and immorality. Balak's actions demonstrate the futility of opposing God's plan and people.
persons.summary: A king in Moab living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.22.2 referred to as Balak (בָּלָק), or Balak (Βαλάκ); a son of Zippor.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.22.2에 처음 언급되며 '발락'이라 불림. 십볼의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 십볼의 아들 발락은 모압 왕으로, 발람을 통해 이스라엘을 저주하려 했다.
persons.article_ko: 발락은 이스라엘 백성이 약속의 땅에 가까이 왔을 때 모압을 다스린 왕이었다(민 22:4). 이스라엘 백성의 많은 수를 두려워한 발락은 이방 선지자 발람을 고용하여 그들을 저주하게 했다(민 22:5-6). 발락의 거듭된 시도와 예물에도 불구하고 발람은 하나님이 명령하신 대로 이스라엘을 축복할 수밖에 없었다(민수기 23-24장). 발락은 발람이 이스라엘을 저주하지 않은 것에 분노하여 그를 돌려보냈다(민 24:10-11). 발락은 여호수아(수 24:9)와 입다(삿 11:25)의 고별 연설에서 하나님이 어떻게 이스라엘을 원수들에게서 보호하셨는지에 대한 본보기로 언급된다. 선지자 미가도 하나님의 의로우심을 상기시키기 위해 발락의 이야기를 언급한다(미 6:5). 요한계시록 2:14에서 발락은 이스라엘을 우상숭배와 부도덕함으로 유혹하려는 발람의 계략과 관련하여 언급된다. 발락의 행동은 하나님의 계획과 백성을 대적하는 것의 헛됨을 보여준다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite musician in the time of David.
persons.short: Bani was a Levite who served as a musician during David's reign.
persons.article: Bani is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.6.46 as a Levite who served as a musician during the reign of King David. The context of the passage is a genealogy of the Levites, specifically the family of Merari, one of the three main Levitical clans. Bani is listed as the son of Shemer (or 'Shamer') and the father of Amzi. The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the tabernacle and temple worship, and many of them were appointed as musicians (1Ch.15.16-24). Bani's inclusion in this genealogy suggests that he was part of a family line that served in this musical role.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.46 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי); a son of Shemer; father of Amzi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.46에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림. 세멜의 아들. 암시의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 다윗 왕 시대에 음악가로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Bani, a descendant of Perez, was among those who settled in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Bani is mentioned in 1Ch.9.4 as one of the descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Perez was one of the twin sons of Judah (Gen.38.29 and an ancestor of the royal line of David )(Rut.4.18-22). The context of 1Chronicles 9 is a list of the families who resettled in Jerusalem and the surrounding towns. Bani's inclusion in this list indicates that he was part of the tribe of Judah and among those who returned from exile to rebuild the city and restore the community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.4 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי); father of Imri.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림. 이므리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베레스의 후손 바니는 예루살렘에 정착한 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from the tribe of Gad.
persons.short: Bani the Gadite was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Bani the Gadite is mentioned in 2Sa.23.36 as one of David's mighty warriors. The mighty warriors were a group of elite soldiers known for their exceptional skill and bravery in battle. Bani is described as a Gadite, indicating that he was from the tribe of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The Gadites were known for their military prowess and loyalty to David (1Ch.12.8-15). Bani's inclusion in the list of mighty warriors suggests that he had distinguished himself in service to King David, likely through his courage and feats in battle.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.36 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.36에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갓 사람 바니는 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife.
persons.short: Bani was one of the men who had married foreign women and agreed to put them away.
persons.article: Bani is listed in Ezr.10.34 among the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples (Ezr.9.1-2). This was seen as a violation of God's command not to intermarry with the idolatrous nations (Deu.7.3-4). Ezra called the people to repentance and urged them to separate from their foreign wives (Ezr.10.10-11). Bani was one of those who agreed to put away his foreign wife in obedience to God's law. This act demonstrated a commitment to holiness and a desire to maintain the distinct identity of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.34 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.34에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그 아내를 내보내기로 동의한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A family group that had married foreign women.
persons.short: The sons of Bani were among those who had married foreign women during Ezra's time.
persons.article: In Ezr.10.38, the sons of Bani are mentioned among the groups that had married foreign women. The context is Ezra's call for the people to repent and separate from their foreign wives, which was seen as a violation of God's law (Ezr.10.10-11). The term "sons" here likely refers to a family group or clan rather than a specific individual named Bani. This family group is listed along with others who had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. By agreeing to put away their foreign wives, the sons of Bani demonstrated a willingness to obey God's commands and maintain the purity of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.38 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.38에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니의 아들들은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람들 가운데 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Bani was the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Bani is mentioned in Ezr.2.10 and Neh.7.15 as the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile. The lists in these passages record the names of the families who journeyed back to their homeland to resettle and rebuild. In Ezr.8.10, a descendant of Bani named Shelomith is mentioned among those who returned with Ezra. Later, in Ezr.10.29, another descendant of Bani is listed among those who had married foreign women and pledged to put them away in response to Ezra's call for repentance. The repeated mention of Bani's descendants suggests that his family played a role in the restoration of Jewish life and worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.10 referred to as Bani (בָּנִי), or Binnui (בִּנּוּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.10에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 바벨론 포로에서 유다로 돌아온 한 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Bani was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Bani is mentioned in Neh.10.14 as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant made during the time of Nehemiah. After the Israelites had returned from Babylonian exile and rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, they gathered to confess their sins and commit to obeying God's law. Nehemiah 10 records the names of those who signed this agreement, including leaders, priests, Levites, and others. Bani's presence on this list indicates he held a position of authority and influence among the people. By sealing the covenant, he publicly declared his commitment to follow God's commandments and to support the spiritual and social reforms initiated by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.14 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite overseer in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.short: Bani was a Levite who served as an overseer in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Bani is briefly mentioned in Neh.11.22 as a Levite who served as an overseer in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. The context of the passage is a list of people who resettled in Jerusalem and the surrounding towns after the exile. Bani is described as "the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem." This role likely involved supervising the Levites' duties and ensuring the proper functioning of the temple service. The mention of Bani's oversight responsibility suggests he was a trusted leader within the Levitical community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.22 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי); a son of Hashabiah; father of Uzzi.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.22에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림. 하사뱌의 아들. 웃시의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 예루살렘에서 감독으로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Bani, a Levite, made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Bani is mentioned in Neh.3.17 as one of the Levites who participated in repairing the wall of Jerusalem. During the time of Nehemiah, the city's walls were in disrepair, leaving the inhabitants vulnerable. Nehemiah organized a massive rebuilding effort, with different individuals and groups taking responsibility for specific sections (Neh.3.1-32). Bani worked on a portion of the wall alongside Hashabiah, the leader of half the district of Keilah. The Levites' involvement in the wall reconstruction demonstrates their commitment to the well-being and security of the community, as well as their support for Nehemiah's leadership.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.17 only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי); father of Rehum.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.17에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림. 르훔의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 바니는 예루살렘 성벽의 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who taught the Law and led prayers.
persons.short: Bani (Binnui) was a Levite involved in teaching the Law and leading prayers during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Bani, also known as Binnui, was a Levite who played a significant role in the spiritual renewal of Israel during the time of Nehemiah. In Neh.8.7, Bani is listed among the Levites who helped explain the Law to the people as Ezra read it aloud. This teaching ministry was crucial for the people to understand and apply God's Word. Later, in Neh.9.4-5, Bani is one of the Levites who led the people in a prayer of confession and worship. He stood on the stairs with other Levites and cried out to God, acknowledging the nation's sins and God's faithfulness. Bani is also mentioned in Neh.10.9 as one of the Levites who signed the covenant to obey God's law. In Neh.12.8, he is listed among the Levites who participated in the dedication of the wall. These references highlight Bani's involvement in various aspects of spiritual leadership, including teaching, prayer, and covenant renewal.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.8.7 referred to as Bani (בָּנִי), or Binnui (בִּנּוּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니(빈누이)는 느헤미야 시대에 율법을 가르치고 기도를 인도한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who led prayers and sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Bani was a Levite who led prayers of confession and sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Bani is mentioned in Neh.9.4 and Neh.10.13 as a Levite who played a significant role in the spiritual renewal of Israel during the time of Nehemiah. In Neh.9.4, Bani is one of the Levites who stood on the stairs and led the people in a prayer of confession. This prayer acknowledged the nation's sins, God's faithfulness, and the people's commitment to obey God's law. Later, in Neh.10.13, Bani is listed among the Levites who sealed the covenant, publicly declaring their dedication to follow God's commandments. These references highlight Bani's involvement in leading the people in prayer and covenant renewal, demonstrating his spiritual leadership within the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.9.4b only referred to as Bani (בָּנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.9.4b에 처음 언급되며 '바니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바니는 느헤미야 시대에 회개의 기도를 인도하고 언약에 서명한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A notorious prisoner released instead of Jesus.
persons.short: Barabbas, a notorious prisoner, was released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.
persons.article: Barabbas was a notorious prisoner mentioned in all four Gospels (Mat.27.16-26; Mrk.15.7-15; Luk.23.18-25; Jhn.18.40). He was in custody during the trial of Jesus before Pontius Pilate. According to the Gospel accounts, it was customary during the Passover feast for the Roman governor to release a prisoner chosen by the crowd. Pilate offered the people a choice between releasing Jesus or Barabbas. The chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude to ask for Barabbas and demand Jesus' crucifixion. Pilate, although convinced of Jesus' innocence, yielded to the crowd's pressure and released Barabbas while condemning Jesus to death. Some manuscripts of Mat.27.16-17 refer to Barabbas as "Jesus Barabbas," suggesting that he may have also been called Jesus. Barabbas is described as a notorious criminal, with Mark and Luke mentioning that he had committed murder during an insurrection. His release in place of Jesus highlights the irony and injustice of the situation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.27.16 referred to as Barabbas (Βαραββᾶς) or Jesus Barabbas.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.27.16에 처음 언급되며 '바라바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 악명 높은 죄수 바라바는 무리의 요구에 따라 빌라도가 예수님 대신 풀어준 자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: The father of Elihu, one of Job's friends.
persons.short: Barachel the Buzite was the father of Elihu, one of the men who spoke to Job.
persons.article: Barachel is mentioned in Job.32.2 and Job.32.6 as the father of Elihu, one of the men who engaged in a dialogue with Job. Barachel is described as a Buzite, indicating that he was from the region of Buz, possibly located in northern Arabia or southern Edom. Elihu, his son, is introduced as a younger man who had been listening to the conversation between Job and his three friends (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar). After the three friends had finished speaking, Elihu became angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God and with the friends for not refuting Job's arguments effectively. Elihu then proceeded to present his own perspective on Job's situation and God's justice. Apart from being Elihu's father and a Buzite, no other information is provided about Barachel himself.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Job.32.2 only referred to as Barachel (בָּרַכְאֵל); father of Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Job.32.2에 처음 언급되며 '바라겔'이라 불림. 엘리후의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 부스 사람 바라겔은 욥에게 말한 사람 중 하나인 엘리후의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: An Israelite commander who defeated Canaanite forces with Deborah.
persons.short: Barak, son of Abinoam, led the Israelites to victory against Canaanite forces under Deborah's leadership.
persons.article: Barak was an Israelite commander from the tribe of Naphtali who played a significant role in the victory over the Canaanite forces led by Sisera (Judges 4). Deborah, a prophetess and judge of Israel, summoned Barak and instructed him to gather troops from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun to fight against Sisera's army. Barak agreed to go only if Deborah accompanied him, to which she consented but prophesied that the honor of the victory would go to a woman. Barak led the Israelite forces to Mount Tabor, where they decisively defeated Sisera's army. The victory was celebrated in the Song of Deborah and Barak (Judges 5), which praises their leadership and God's deliverance. Barak is later mentioned in 1Sa.12.11 as one of the deliverers sent by God to save Israel from their enemies. The New Testament also commends Barak's faith in Heb.11.32, listing him among the examples of those who through faith conquered kingdoms and administered justice.
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.4.6 referred to as Barak (בָּרָק), or Barak (בְּדָן), or Barak (Βαράκ); a son of Abinoam.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '바락'이라 불림. 아비노암의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아비노암의 아들 바락은 드보라의 지도 아래 가나안 군대를 물리치고 이스라엘을 승리로 이끌었다.
persons.article_ko: 바락은 납달리 지파 출신 이스라엘 지휘관으로, 시스라가 이끄는 가나안 군대를 이긴 승리에서 중요한 역할을 했다(사사기 4장). 여선지자이며 이스라엘의 사사인 드보라는 바락을 불러 시스라의 군대를 대적하여 싸우도록 납달리와 스불론 지파에서 군대를 모으라고 지시했다. 바락은 드보라가 동행할 경우에만 가겠다고 동의했고, 그녀는 이를 승낙했으나 승리의 영예가 한 여인에게 돌아갈 것이라고 예언했다. 바락은 이스라엘 군대를 다볼산으로 이끌었고, 그곳에서 그들은 시스라의 군대를 결정적으로 물리쳤다. 그 승리는 드보라와 바락의 노래(사사기 5장)에서 기념되는데, 이는 그들의 지도력과 하나님의 구원을 찬양한다. 바락은 후에 사무엘상 12:11에서 이스라엘을 원수들에게서 구원하도록 하나님이 보내신 구원자 중 한 사람으로 언급된다. 신약도 히브리서 11:32에서 바락의 믿음을 칭찬하며, 그를 믿음으로 나라들을 이기고 정의를 행한 자들의 본보기 명단에 포함시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of David through the line of Solomon.
persons.short: Bariah was a descendant of King David through Solomon's line.
persons.article: Bariah is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.3.22 as one of the descendants of King David through the line of Solomon. The context of the passage is a genealogy tracing the royal lineage from David to several generations after the Babylonian exile. Bariah is listed as one of the sons of Shemaiah, who was a descendant of Shecaniah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.22 only referred to as Bariah (בָּרִיחַ); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Hattush, Igal, Neariah and Shaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.22에 처음 언급되며 '바리야'라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 핫두스, 이갈, 느아랴와 사밧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바리아는 솔로몬 계열을 통한 다윗의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Jewish sorcerer who opposed Paul and Barnabas.
persons.short: Bar-Jesus, also known as Elymas, was a Jewish sorcerer who tried to hinder Paul and Barnabas' ministry.
persons.article: Bar-Jesus, also called Elymas, was a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet encountered by Paul and Barnabas during their missionary journey on the island of Cyprus (Act.13.6-12). He was associated with Sergius Paulus, the proconsul of the island, who had summoned Paul and Barnabas to hear the word of God. However, Elymas opposed the apostles and tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith. Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, rebuked Elymas for his deceit and obstruction of the truth, declaring that he would be temporarily blinded. Immediately, Elymas lost his sight, and the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed and was astonished at the teaching about the Lord. The name "Elymas" is said to mean "magician" or "sorcerer," while "Bar-Jesus" means "son of Jesus" or "son of Joshua." This incident demonstrates the power of the gospel over spiritual opposition and the consequences of resisting God's message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.13.6 referred to as Bar-jesus (Βαριησοῦς), or Elymas (Ἐλύμας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.13.6에 처음 언급되며 '바예수'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바예수(엘루마라고도 함)는 바울과 바나바의 사역을 방해하려 한 유대인 마술사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Barkos was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Barkos is mentioned in Ezr.2.53 and Neh.7.55 as the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. The lists in Ezra and Nehemiah record the names of the families who returned to Judah to resettle and rebuild the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.53 only referred to as Barkos (בַּרְקוֹס).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.53에 처음 언급되며 '바르고스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바르고스는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Levite from Cyprus who accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.
persons.short: Barnabas, also known as Joseph or Joses, was a Levite from Cyprus who played a significant role in the early church and accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.
persons.article: Barnabas, whose original name was Joseph or Joses, was a prominent figure in the early Christian church. He was a Levite from the island of Cyprus (Act.4.36 who sold his land and brought the money to the apostles, demonstrating his generosity and commitment to the faith). Barnabas played a crucial role in introducing the newly converted Paul to the apostles in Jerusalem, vouching for his sincerity (Act.9.27). The church in Jerusalem later sent Barnabas to Antioch, where he encouraged the believers and brought Paul to minister there (Act.11.22-26). Barnabas and Paul were then commissioned by the Holy Spirit to embark on a missionary journey (Act.13.2, during which they preached the gospel and established churches in various cities). Barnabas was also involved in the dispute concerning the acceptance of Gentile believers and accompanied Paul to the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15). He later separated from Paul due to a disagreement over taking Mark on another journey (Act.15.36-39). Barnabas continued his ministry with Mark, while Paul chose Silas as his new companion. In the New Testament epistles, Barnabas is mentioned as a fellow laborer and an example of one who worked for the gospel without relying on financial support from the churches (1Co.9.6). He was recognized as a pillar of the church alongside James and Peter (Gal.2.9). Barnabas' ministry was characterized by encouragement, generosity, and a commitment to spreading the gospel message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.4.36 referred to as Barnabas (Βαρνάβας), or Joseph (Ἰωσήφ), or Joses (Ἰωσῆς); his mother was Mary ; a brother of Mary.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 레위인. Act.4.36에 처음 언급되며 '바나바'라 불림. 바나바의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 마리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바나바(요셉 또는 요세라고도 함)는 구브로 출신 레위인으로, 초대교회에서 중요한 역할을 했으며 바울과 함께 선교여행에 동행했다.
persons.article_ko: 원래 이름이 요셉 또는 요세였던 바나바는 초대 그리스도교 교회의 저명한 인물이었다. 그는 구브로 섬 출신 레위인으로(행 4:36) 자기 밭을 팔아 그 돈을 사도들에게 가져와 그의 관대함과 신앙에 대한 헌신을 보여주었다. 바나바는 새로 회심한 바울을 예루살렘의 사도들에게 소개하는 데 중요한 역할을 하며 그의 진실함을 보증했다(행 9:27). 예루살렘 교회는 후에 바나바를 안디옥으로 보냈고, 그곳에서 그는 신자들을 격려하고 바울을 데려와 그곳에서 섬기게 했다(행 11:22-26). 그런 다음 바나바와 바울은 성령에 의해 선교여행을 떠나도록 위임받았고(행 13:2), 그 여정에서 그들은 복음을 전하고 여러 성읍에 교회를 세웠다. 바나바는 또한 이방인 신자들의 수용에 관한 논쟁에 관여했고 바울과 함께 예루살렘 공의회에 동행했다(사도행전 15장). 그는 후에 마가를 또 다른 여행에 데려가는 것에 대한 의견 차이로 바울과 갈라섰다(행 15:36-39). 바나바는 마가와 함께 사역을 계속했고, 바울은 실라를 새로운 동반자로 선택했다. 신약 서신서에서 바나바는 동역자이며 교회들의 재정적 지원에 의존하지 않고 복음을 위해 일한 본보기로 언급된다(고전 9:6). 그는 야고보, 베드로와 함께 교회의 기둥으로 인정받았다(갈 2:9). 바나바의 사역은 격려, 관대함, 복음 메시지 전파에 대한 헌신으로 특징지어졌다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ.
persons.short: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
persons.article: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles selected by Jesus Christ to be part of His inner circle (Mat.10.3; Mrk.3.18; Luk.6.14). He is always mentioned in the lists of the apostles, indicating his importance within the group. However, beyond his inclusion in these lists, no specific details about his background, life, or ministry are provided in the New Testament. Bartholomew is also named in Act.1.13 as one of the apostles gathered in the upper room after Jesus' ascension, praying and waiting for the coming of the Holy Spirit. Some scholars suggest that Bartholomew may be the same person as Nathanael, who is mentioned in John's Gospel (Jhn.1.45-51; 21.2, but this identification is not conclusively established in the biblical text). Tradition holds that Bartholomew preached the gospel in various regions, including India and Armenia, and suffered martyrdom for his faith, but these accounts are not recorded in the New Testament.
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.10.3 only referred to as Bartholomew (Βαρθολομαῖος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '바돌로매'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바돌로매는 예수님이 택하신 열두 사도 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A blind beggar healed by Jesus near Jericho.
persons.short: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was healed by Jesus as He was leaving Jericho.
persons.article: Bartimaeus was a blind beggar mentioned in Mrk.10.46-52. He was the son of Timaeus and sat by the roadside near Jericho. When he heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by, he began to cry out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" Despite the crowd's attempts to silence him, Bartimaeus persisted in calling out to Jesus. Jesus stopped and asked for Bartimaeus to be brought to Him. When asked what he wanted, Bartimaeus replied, "Rabbi, I want to see." Jesus told him, "Go your way; your faith has made you well." Immediately, Bartimaeus received his sight and followed Jesus on the way. This miracle demonstrates Jesus' compassion and power to heal, as well as the importance of faith and persistence in seeking His help. Bartimaeus' story is an example of how Jesus responded to the needs of the marginalized and restored them physically and spiritually.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Mrk.10.46 only referred to as Bartimaeus (Βαρτιμαῖος); a son of Timaeus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mrk.10.46에 처음 언급되며 '바디매오'라 불림. 디매오의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바디매오는 눈먼 거지로, 예수님이 여리고를 떠나실 때 고침을 받았다.

persons.description: Jeremiah's servant living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Jeremiah's scribe who recorded and delivered his prophecies.
persons.short: Baruch, son of Neriah, served as Jeremiah's scribe and faithfully recorded and delivered his prophecies.
persons.article: Baruch, son of Neriah, was the faithful scribe and companion of the prophet Jeremiah. He played a significant role in recording and delivering Jeremiah's prophecies to the people of Judah. In Jeremiah 36, Baruch wrote down Jeremiah's words on a scroll and read them in the temple, as the prophet was restricted from going there himself. When King Jehoiakim destroyed the scroll, Baruch rewrote the prophecies with additional messages from Jeremiah. Baruch also served as a witness to Jeremiah's purchase of a field, symbolizing God's promise of future restoration (Jer.32.12-16). He accompanied Jeremiah to Egypt after the fall of Jerusalem, despite the prophet's warnings (Jer.43.3-6). In Jeremiah 45, God spoke directly to Baruch, reassuring him of divine protection amidst the impending judgment on Judah. Baruch's unwavering support for Jeremiah, even in the face of opposition and personal risk, demonstrates his commitment to God's message and his loyalty to the prophet.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.32.12 only referred to as Baruch (בָּרוּךְ); son of Neriah; a brother of Seraiah; a servant of Jeremiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 예레미야의 종. Jer.32.12에 처음 언급되며 '바룩'이라 불림. 네리야의 아들. 스라야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 네리야의 아들 바룩은 예레미야의 서기관으로 섬기며 그의 예언을 충실히 기록하고 전달했다.
persons.article_ko: 네리야의 아들 바룩은 선지자 예레미야의 신실한 서기관이며 동반자였다. 그는 예레미야의 예언을 기록하고 유다 백성에게 전달하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다. 예레미야 36장에서 바룩은 예레미야의 말을 두루마리에 기록했고, 선지자 자신이 성전에 가는 것이 금지되었기 때문에 그곳에서 그것을 낭독했다. 여호야김 왕이 그 두루마리를 태웠을 때 바룩은 예레미야로부터 받은 추가 메시지와 함께 예언을 다시 기록했다. 바룩은 또한 미래의 회복에 대한 하나님의 약속을 상징하는 예레미야의 밭 매입에 증인으로 섬겼다(렘 32:12-16). 그는 예루살렘 함락 이후 선지자의 경고에도 불구하고 예레미야와 함께 애굽으로 갔다(렘 43:3-6). 예레미야 45장에서 하나님은 바룩에게 직접 말씀하셔서 유다에 대한 임박한 심판 가운데서도 신적 보호를 확신시키셨다. 반대와 개인적 위험에 직면해서도 예레미야에 대한 바룩의 흔들리지 않는 지지는 하나님의 메시지에 대한 그의 헌신과 선지자에 대한 그의 충성을 보여준다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Baruch was a priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Baruch is mentioned in Neh.10.6 as one of the priests who sealed the covenant made during the time of Nehemiah. After the Israelites had returned from Babylonian exile and rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, they gathered to confess their sins and commit to obeying God's law. Nehemiah 10 records the names of those who signed this agreement, including leaders, priests, and Levites. Baruch's presence on this list indicates that he was a member of the priestly family and held a position of authority within the religious community. By sealing the covenant, Baruch publicly declared his commitment to follow God's commandments and to support the spiritual and social reforms initiated by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.6 only referred to as Baruch (בָּרוּךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.6에 처음 언급되며 '바룩'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바룩은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Judah who settled in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Baruch, a descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah, settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Baruch is briefly mentioned in Neh.11.5 as one of the descendants of Perez, a son of Judah, who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. The context of the passage is a list of people from various tribes and families who resettled in Jerusalem and the surrounding towns. Baruch is described as "the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni." This genealogy traces his lineage back to Perez, establishing him as a member of the tribe of Judah. The resettlement of Jerusalem was an important step in the restoration of Jewish life and worship after the exile. Baruch's presence in the city suggests that he was part of this process and contributed to the reestablishment of the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Baruch (בָּרוּךְ); a son of Col-hozeh ; father of Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '바룩'이라 불림. 골호세의 아들. 마아세야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유다 지파 베레스의 후손 바룩은 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A man who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Baruch, son of Zabbai, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Baruch, the son of Zabbai, is mentioned in Neh.3.20 as one of the individuals who participated in repairing the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time. He is described as having "earnestly repaired" another section of the wall, starting from the angle and extending to the door of the house of Eliashib, the high priest. This suggests that Baruch was a dedicated worker who took his responsibility seriously and went beyond his assigned portion. The rebuilding of the wall was a significant project that required the cooperation and effort of various people from different families and professions. Baruch's contribution, along with that of others, helped to restore the physical and spiritual integrity of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.20 only referred to as Baruch (בָּרוּךְ); a son of Zabbai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.20에 처음 언급되며 '바룩'이라 불림. 삽배의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 삽배의 아들 바룩은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽의 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gileadite who provided for David during Absalom's rebellion.
persons.short: Barzillai the Gileadite supplied provisions to David during his flight from Absalom and was later honored by the king.
persons.article: Barzillai was a wealthy Gileadite from Rogelim who provided essential support to King David during his flight from his son Absalom's rebellion (2Sa.17.27-29). Along with others, Barzillai generously supplied food and provisions for David and his men. After Absalom's defeat, when David returned to Jerusalem, Barzillai accompanied him to the Jordan River (2Sa.19.31-39). Due to his advanced age of eighty, Barzillai declined David's invitation to join him in Jerusalem, but he sent his son Chimham in his place. David blessed Barzillai and promised to show kindness to his family. Later, on his deathbed, David instructed Solomon to show favor to Barzillai's descendants (1Ki.2.7). Barzillai's loyalty and generosity during David's time of need were remembered and honored by the king. In Ezr.2.61 and Neh.7.63, a priestly family is mentioned who traced their lineage to Barzillai, indicating the enduring impact of his devotion to David.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.17.27 only referred to as Barzillai (בַּרְזִלַּי).
