Cainan's inclusion in this genealogy is notable because he is not mentioned in the genealogies found in Genesis 11 and 1Chronicles 1, which list Shelah as the direct son of Arphaxad. Some scholars suggest that the name Cainan may have been added to Luke's genealogy based on the Septuagint (Greek Old Testament) translation, which includes Cainan in Genesis 11. The presence of Cainan in Luke's genealogy highlights the importance of genealogical records in establishing Jesus' lineage and fulfilling messianic prophecies.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Luk.3.36 only referred to as Cainan (Καϊνάν, Καϊνάμ); a son of Arpachshad; father of Shelah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Luk.3.36에 처음 언급되며 '가이난'이라 불림. 아르박삿의 아들. 셀라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아르박삿의 아들 가이난은 누가복음 족보에 따르면 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zerah, grandson of Judah
persons.short: Calcol, a son of Zerah, was a grandson of Judah.
persons.article: Calcol is mentioned in 1Ch.2.6 as one of the five sons of Zerah, who was a son of Judah. The other sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, and Dara. This genealogy traces the descendants of Judah, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'), and highlights the family line of David, who would later become king of Israel. Calcol's inclusion in this genealogy demonstrates his connection to the tribe of Judah and his place in the ancestral line of important figures in Israel's history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.6 only referred to as Calcol (כַּלְכֹּל); son of Zerah; a brother of Zabdi, Ethan, Heman and Dara.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '갈골'이라 불림. 세라의 아들. 삽디, 에단, 헤만과 다라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세라의 아들 갈골은 유다의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wise man Solomon was compared to
persons.short: Calcol was a wise man to whom Solomon's wisdom was compared.
persons.article: Calcol is mentioned in 1Ki.4.31 as one of the wise men to whom Solomon's wisdom was compared. The verse states that Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt, including the wisdom of Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, who were known for their wisdom. The comparison highlights the exceptional nature of Solomon's God-given wisdom, which was greater than that of the most renowned wise men of his time.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.31 only referred to as Calcol (כַּלְכֹּל); son of Mahol; a brother of Ethan, Heman and Darda.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.31에 처음 언급되며 '갈골'이라 불림. 마홀의 아들. 에단, 헤만과 다르다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 갈골은 솔로몬의 지혜와 비교된 지혜로운 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.partners: Azubah@1Ch.2.18-, Jerioth@1Ch.2.18, Ephrathah@Rut.1.2-1Ch, Ephah@1Ch.2.46, Maacah@1Ch.2.48, Jahdai@1Ch.2.47(?)
persons.offspring: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Jesher@1Ch.2.18, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Ardon@1Ch.2.18, Mesha@1Ch.2.42, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Sheva@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: Son of Hezron, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Caleb (Chelubai), the son of Hezron, was a descendant of Judah and the father of Hur.
persons.article: Caleb, also known as Chelubai, is mentioned in the genealogies of Judah in 1Chronicles 2 and 4:1. He was the son of Hezron and the father of Hur (1Chr. 2:9, 18-19). Caleb's wives included Azubah and Ephrathah (1Chr. 2:18-19). Through his son Hur, Caleb was the grandfather of Uri and the great-grandfather of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman who worked on the tabernacle (1Chr. 2:20; Ex. 31:2). Caleb's descendants, known as the Calebites, settled in the region of Hebron and played a significant role in the tribe of Judah (1Chr. 2:42-55). This Caleb is a different person from Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who was one of the twelve spies. The similar names and their connection to the tribe of Judah may have led to some confusion in the genealogical records.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.9 referred to as Caleb (כָּלֵב), or Carmi (כַּרְמִי), or Chelubai (כְּלוּבָ֑י); son of Hezron; a brother of Ram, Jerahmeel, Segub and Ashhur; husband of Azubah, Jerioth, Ephrathah, Ephah and Maacah; father of Hur, Jesher, Shobab, Ardon, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez, Sheber, Tirhanah, Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Sheva and Achsah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.9에 처음 언급되며 '글루배'라 불림. 헤스론과 헤스론의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 람, 여라므엘, 스굽과 아스훌의 형제. 아수바, 여리옷, 에브랏, 에바, 마아가와 야대의 남편. 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압, 스와와 악사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤스론의 아들 갈렙(글루배)은 유다의 후손이며 훌의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
persons.brief: Faithful spy, given Hebron as inheritance
persons.short: Caleb, one of the twelve spies, remained faithful to God and was granted Hebron as his inheritance.
persons.article: Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:6). Along with Joshua, Caleb stood firm in his faith and trust in God's promise, encouraging the Israelites to enter the land despite the other spies' negative report (Num. 13:30; 14:6-9). As a result, God commended Caleb for his faithfulness and promised that he would inherit the land he had explored (Num. 14:24, 30, 38; Deut. 1:36). After the conquest of Canaan, Caleb requested and received Hebron as his inheritance (Josh. 14:6-15; 15:13-19; 21:12; Judg. 1:12-15, 20). He drove out the Anakim giants from Hebron and offered his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever conquered Kirjath Sepher (Josh. 15:14-17; Judg. 1:12-13). Caleb's descendants settled in the Negev region and in the cities of Hebron (1Sam. 30:14; 1Chr. 4:15; 6:56). His faith, courage, and obedience to God made him a prominent figure in Israel's history, and his story is remembered as an example of unwavering trust in God's promises (Num. 32:12; Judg. 3:9).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest, first mentioned at Num.13.6 referred to as Caleb (כָּלֵב), or Calebite (כָּלִבִּי); son of Jephunneh; a brother of Kenaz; father of Achsah, Iru, Elah, Naam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야·정복시대 여호수아의 동료. Num.13.6에 처음 언급되며 '갈렙'이라 불림. 여분네의 아들. 그나스의 형제. 악사, 이루, 엘라와 나암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람인 갈렙은 하나님께 신실했으며 그 상으로 헤브론을 기업으로 받았다.
persons.article_ko: 여분네의 아들 갈렙은 모세가 가나안 땅을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람이었다(민 13:6). 여호수아와 함께 갈렙은 하나님의 약속에 대한 믿음과 신뢰 안에 굳게 서서, 다른 정탐꾼들의 부정적인 보고에도 불구하고 이스라엘 백성에게 그 땅에 들어가라고 격려했다(민 13:30; 14:6-9). 그 결과 하나님은 갈렙의 신실함을 칭찬하시며 그가 정탐한 땅을 유업으로 받을 것이라고 약속하셨다(민 14:24, 30, 38; 신 1:36). 가나안 정복 이후 갈렙은 헤브론을 자기 기업으로 요청하여 받았다(수 14:6-15; 15:13-19; 21:12; 삿 1:12-15, 20). 그는 헤브론에서 아낙 거인들을 쫓아냈고 기럇세벨을 정복하는 자에게 딸 악사를 아내로 주겠다고 제안했다(수 15:14-17; 삿 1:12-13). 갈렙의 후손은 네게브 지역과 헤브론 성읍들에 정착했다(삼상 30:14; 대상 4:15; 6:56). 그의 믿음, 용기, 하나님께 대한 순종은 그를 이스라엘 역사의 저명한 인물로 만들었고, 그의 이야기는 하나님의 약속에 대한 흔들리지 않는 신뢰의 본보기로 기억된다(민 32:12; 삿 3:9).

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Ham; father of Sidon and Heth
persons.short: Canaan, the son of Ham, was the father of Sidon, Heth, and other Canaanite tribes.
persons.article: Canaan was the fourth son of Ham and the grandson of Noah (Gen. 9:18, 22; 10:6; 1Chr. 1:8). He became the progenitor of the Canaanite tribes, which inhabited the land that would later be promised to Abraham and his descendants (Gen. 10:15-19; 1Chr. 1:13-16). Canaan's sons included Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth, the ancestor of the Hittites. Other descendants of Canaan included the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. After Noah's drunkenness, Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers (Gen. 9:22). In response, Noah cursed Canaan, stating that he would be a servant to his brothers (Gen. 9:25-27). This curse was likely a prophetic declaration about the future subjugation of the Canaanite tribes by the Israelites. The land of Canaan became synonymous with the region God promised to Abraham, and the Canaanites were among the inhabitants the Israelites were to displace and conquer (Gen. 12:5-7; Ex. 3:8; Deut. 7:1-3).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.9.18 only referred to as Canaan (כְּנַ֫עַן); son of Ham; a brother of Cush, Egypt and Put; father of Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.9.18에 처음 언급되며 '가나안'이라 불림. 함의 아들. 구스, 미스라임과 붓의 형제. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓, 스말과 하맛의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함의 아들 가나안은 시돈, 헷 및 다른 가나안 족속들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Shaul's mother, a Canaanite woman
persons.short: Shaul's mother was a Canaanite woman, according to the genealogies of Simeon.
persons.article: The Canaanite woman mentioned in Gen.46.10 and Exo.6.15 is the mother of Shaul, who was a son of Simeon. In the genealogies of Simeon, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'), Shaul is distinguished from his brothers by the fact that his mother was a Canaanite woman. This detail suggests that Simeon married a woman from the Canaanite people, who were the inhabitants of the land of Canaan before the Israelites. The mention of Shaul's mother's Canaanite origin is significant because it shows that intermarriage between the Israelites and the Canaanites did occur, despite the general prohibition against such unions (Deut). Exo.7.3. The inclusion of this information in the genealogies also highlights the importance of maternal lineage in the biblical record.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.46.10 only referred to as Canaanite woman (כְּנַעֲנִי); mother of Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '가나안 여인'이라 불림. 시므온의 아내. 사울의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 시므온 족보에 따르면 사울의 어머니는 가나안 여인이었다.

persons.description: People from Caphtor (Crete)
persons.siblings: Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Anamim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Pathrusim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Casluhim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendants of Mizraim who displaced the Avvim
persons.short: The Caphtorim, descendants of Mizraim, displaced the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza.
persons.article: The Caphtorim are mentioned in Gen.10.14, Deu.2.23, and 1Ch.1.12 as descendants of Mizraim, who was a son of Ham and grandson of Noah. They are listed among the peoples who descended from Egypt (Mizraim is the Hebrew name for Egypt). According to Deu.2.23, the Caphtorim came from Caphtor and destroyed the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, and settled in their place. This event occurred before the Israelites entered the Promised Land. The exact location of Caphtor is uncertain, but it is often associated with the island of Crete or the region of Cilicia in modern-day Turkey. The Caphtorim's displacement of the Avvim is one of several examples in the Bible of people groups migrating and conquering new territories.
persons.summary: People from Caphtor (Crete) of the Egyptians, first mentioned at Gen.10.14 only referred to as Caphtorim (כַּפְתֹּרִי); descended from Egypt along with Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim and Casluhim.
persons.summary_ko: 갑돌(크레타) 사람. Gen.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '갑도림'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 루딤, 아나밈, 르하빔, 납두힘, 바드루심과 가슬루힘의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 미스라임의 후손 갑돌 사람들은 가사에 이르기까지 마을에 살던 아위 족속을 쫓아냈다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Eunuch in King Ahasuerus' court
persons.short: Carkas was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.
persons.article: Carkas was one of the seven eunuchs who served in the court of King Ahasuerus, also known as Xerxes, the Persian ruler (Est.1.10). Eunuchs were often employed in royal courts as trusted officials and servants due to their loyalty and inability to establish a rival dynasty. During a royal feast, when King Ahasuerus was in high spirits from drinking wine, he commanded the seven eunuchs, including Carkas, to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing her royal crown. The king wanted to display her beauty to the people and nobles, but Queen Vashti refused to come (Est.1.11-12). This refusal led to the king's anger and ultimately to Vashti's removal as queen, setting the stage for the rise of Esther. Carkas' mention as one of the eunuchs highlights the opulence and power dynamics within the Persian court during the time of Esther.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.10 only referred to as Carkas (כַּרְכַּס).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '가르가스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갈가스는 아하수에로 왕을 섬긴 일곱 내시 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Reuben; father of the Carmites
persons.short: Carmi, the son of Reuben, was the father of the Carmite clan.
persons.article: Carmi was the son of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.46.9; Exo.6.14; 1Ch.5.3). He was the progenitor of the Carmite clan within the tribe of Reuben (Num.26.6). The Carmites were one of the families descended from Reuben, as recorded in the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai and the plains of Moab. Carmi's inclusion in the genealogies of Reuben highlights the importance of family lineage and the organization of the Israelite tribes according to their ancestral heritage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.9 referred to as Carmi (כַּרְמִי), or Carmite (כַּרְמִי); son of Reuben; a brother of Pallu, Hezron and Hanoch.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.9에 처음 언급되며 '갈미'라 불림. 르우벤의 아들. 발루, 헤스론과 하녹의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 르우벤의 아들 갈미는 갈미 가문의 시조였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Achan, who stole devoted things
persons.short: Carmi, the son of Zabdi, was the father of Achan, who took devoted things from Jericho.
persons.article: Carmi, the son of Zabdi, was a member of the tribe of Judah and the father of Achan (Jos.7.1, 18; 1Ch.2.7). After the Israelites conquered Jericho, Achan took some of the devoted things from the city, which were supposed to be dedicated to God. This act of disobedience brought God's anger upon the Israelites, causing them to suffer defeat in their next battle against Ai. When Joshua sought the Lord's guidance, God revealed that someone had taken from the devoted things. Through a process of elimination, Achan was identified as the culprit. Achan confessed his sin and was punished by being stoned to death along with his family and livestock, and their remains were burned (Jos.7.19-26). Carmi's mention in this narrative serves to identify Achan's lineage and emphasize the consequences of disobedience to God's commands.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.7.1 only referred to as Carmi (כַּרְמִי); a son of Zabdi; father of Achan.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jos.7.1에 처음 언급되며 '갈미'라 불림. 삽디의 아들. 아간의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삽디의 아들 갈미는 여리고에서 온전히 바친 물건을 취한 아간의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Paul's friend in Troas
persons.short: Carpus was a friend of Paul in Troas, with whom Paul left his cloak, books, and parchments.
persons.article: Carpus was a resident of Troas, a city located on the northwest coast of Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey). He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 2Ti.4.13, where the apostle Paul asks Timothy to bring the cloak, books, and parchments that he had left with Carpus in Troas. This request suggests that Carpus was a trusted friend or associate of Paul, who had provided lodging or assistance to the apostle during his travels. The fact that Paul left important personal belongings with Carpus indicates a level of familiarity and trust between them. Although no further details about Carpus are provided in the Bible, his brief mention in Paul's letter to Timothy offers a glimpse into the network of believers and supporters that sustained Paul's ministry in the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.4.13 only referred to as Carpus (Κάρπος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.4.13에 처음 언급되며 '가보'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 가보는 드로아에서 바울의 친구로, 바울이 그에게 겉옷과 책, 양피지를 맡겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prince in King Ahasuerus' court
persons.short: Carshena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus' presence.
persons.article: Carshena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who served in the court of King Ahasuerus, also known as Xerxes (Est.1.14). These princes were the closest advisors to the king and had the privilege of direct access to his presence. They were known for their knowledge of the law and their understanding of the times. When Queen Vashti refused to appear before the king during a royal feast, Ahasuerus consulted with his wise men, including Carshena, to determine the appropriate response according to the law (Est.1.15). The inclusion of Carshena among the named princes highlights his high status and influence within the Persian court during the events described in the book of Esther.
persons.summary: A prince of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Carshena (כַּרְשְׁנָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '가르스나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갈스나는 아하수에로 왕을 알현할 수 있었던 페르시아와 메대의 일곱 방백 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: People from Casluch(?)
persons.siblings: Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Anamim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Pathrusim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Caphtorim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendants of Mizraim, ancestor of Philistines
persons.short: The Casluhim, descendants of Mizraim, were the ancestors of the Philistines.
persons.article: The Casluhim are mentioned in Gen.10.14 and 1Ch.1.12 as descendants of Mizraim, who was a son of Ham and grandson of Noah. They are listed among the peoples who descended from Egypt (Mizraim is the Hebrew name for Egypt). According to Gen.10.14, the Casluhim were the ancestors of the Philistines, a prominent enemy of the Israelites in the Old Testament. The Philistines are known to have migrated from the region of the Aegean Sea to the coastal plain of Canaan, where they established a powerful confederation of city-states. The connection between the Casluhim and the Philistines suggests a possible Egyptian origin or influence on the Philistine people. However, the exact nature of this relationship is not clearly defined in the biblical text.
persons.summary: People from Casluch(?) of the Egyptians, first mentioned at Gen.10.14 only referred to as Casluhim (כַּסְלֻחִים); descended from Egypt along with Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim and Caphtorim; progenitors of the Philistine.
persons.summary_ko: 가슬루힘. Gen.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '가슬루힘'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 루딤, 아나밈, 르하빔, 납두힘, 바드루심과 갑도림의 동기. 블레셋의 부모.
persons.short_ko: 미스라임의 후손 가슬루힘은 블레셋 사람들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Elam, led coalition against Sodom and Gomorrah
persons.short: Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, led a coalition of kings against Sodom and Gomorrah and was later defeated by Abraham.
persons.article: Chedorlaomer was the king of Elam, a powerful nation located east of Mesopotamia, during the time of Abraham (Gen.14.1, 4, 5, 9, 17). He formed a coalition with three other kings: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of Goiim. For twelve years, the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, and others in the region served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year, they rebelled. In response, Chedorlaomer and his allies waged war against the rebellious cities, defeating them and taking captives, including Abraham's nephew Lot. When Abraham learned of Lot's capture, he gathered his 318 trained men and pursued Chedorlaomer's army. With God's help, Abraham defeated Chedorlaomer and his allies, rescuing Lot and recovering the stolen goods. This event showcases Abraham's military prowess and his loyalty to his family, as well as God's faithfulness in granting victory to Abraham and his small force against a powerful coalition of kings.
persons.summary: A king in Mesopotamia living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.1 only referred to as Chedorlaomer (כְּדׇרְלָעֹמֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '그돌라오멜'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘람 왕 그돌라오멜은 소돔과 고모라를 대적하는 왕들의 연합을 이끌었으나 후에 아브라함에게 패했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife during Ezra's time
persons.short: Chelal was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Chelal is mentioned in Ezr.10.30 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, contrary to God's commands (Ezr.9.1-2). This intermarriage was seen as a violation of the covenant and a threat to the spiritual purity of the nation. Ezra called for a national assembly, where the people confessed their sin and agreed to separate from their foreign wives (Ezr.10.10-12). Chelal was among those who had taken foreign wives and pledged to put them away, demonstrating repentance and a commitment to obey God's laws. The inclusion of Chelal's name in this account highlights the importance of maintaining spiritual purity and the need for individuals to take responsibility for their actions in light of God's covenant with His people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.30 only referred to as Chelal (כְּלָ֑ל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.30에 처음 언급되며 '글랄'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글랄은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of King David's farm workers
persons.short: Chelub the Ishmaelite was in charge of King David's farm workers.
persons.article: Chelub the Ishmaelite is mentioned in 1Ch.27.26 as one of King David's officials. He was responsible for overseeing the agricultural workers who tilled the soil. This Chelub is distinguished from the Chelub in 1Ch.4.11 by his Ishmaelite lineage and his role in David's administration.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.26 only referred to as Chelub (כְּלוּב); father of Ezri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.26에 처음 언급되며 '글룹'이라 불림. 에스리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이스마엘 사람 그룹은 다윗 왕의 농장 일꾼들을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Caleb's brother, son of Hezron
persons.short: Chelub, Caleb's brother and Hezron's son, was Mehir's father.
persons.article: Chelub, mentioned in 1Ch.4.11, was the brother of Caleb and the son of Hezron. He was the father of Mehir.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.11 only referred to as Chelub (כְּלוּב); a brother of Shuhah; father of Mehir.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '글룹'이라 불림. 수하의 형제. 므힐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 갈렙의 형제이자 헤스론의 아들인 글룹은 므힐의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A man who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Cheluhi was among those who married foreign women during the Exile.
persons.article: Cheluhi is briefly mentioned in Ezr.10.35 as one of the men who had married foreign women during the Babylonian Exile. He was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives and children in response to Ezra's call for repentance and obedience to God's law.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.35 only referred to as Cheluhi (כְּלוּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.35에 처음 언급되며 '글루히'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글루히는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jeush@1Ch.7.10, Benjamin@1Ch.7.10, Ehud@1Ch.7.10, Zethan@1Ch.7.10, Tarshish@1Ch.7.10, Ahishahar@1Ch.7.10
persons.brief: Son of Bilhan, descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Chenaanah was a son of Bilhan and descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Chenaanah is mentioned in 1Ch.7.10 as one of the sons of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin. He is listed among the heads of families in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. This Chenaanah is different from the false prophet Zedekiah son of Chenaanah mentioned in 1Kings 22 and 2Chronicles 18.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.10 only referred to as Chenaanah (כְּנַעֲנָה); son of Bilhan; a brother of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.10에 처음 언급되며 '그나아나'라 불림. 빌한의 아들. 여우스, 베냐민, 에훗, 세단, 달시스와 아히사할의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 그나아나는 빌한의 아들로 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: False prophet who opposed Micaiah
persons.short: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was a false prophet who opposed Micaiah.
persons.article: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was a false prophet who lived during the reign of King Ahab of Israel. He is mentioned in the context of the battle at Ramoth-gilead, where he, along with other false prophets, encouraged Ahab to go to war against the Arameans. Zedekiah made iron horns and claimed that Ahab would gore the Arameans until they were destroyed. When the true prophet Micaiah prophesied Ahab's defeat, Zedekiah struck him on the cheek and questioned the source of his prophecy. Micaiah responded by saying that Zedekiah would go into an inner chamber to hide when his false prophecy was exposed. The biblical account portrays Zedekiah as a false prophet who opposed God's true message delivered through Micaiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.11 only referred to as Chenaanah (כְּנַעֲנָה); father of Zedekiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.22.11에 처음 언급되며 '그나아나'라 불림. 시드기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 그나아나의 아들 시드기야는 미가야를 대적한 거짓 선지자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who led the people in confession
persons.short: Chenani was a Levite who led the people in confession and worship.
persons.article: Chenani is mentioned in Neh.9.4 as one of the Levites who stood on the stairs and led the people in a prayer of confession and worship during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. He is listed alongside other Levites such as Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani. The prayer they led acknowledged God's faithfulness, recounted Israel's history, and confessed the nation's sins.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.9.4 only referred to as Chenani (כְּנָנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '그나니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그나니는 백성이 자백하고 예배드리도록 이끈 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite leader of singing and administration under David
persons.short: Chenaniah was a Levite leader in charge of singing and administration during David's reign.
persons.article: Chenaniah was a Levite who served during the reign of King David. He had a leadership role in directing the singing when the ark of the covenant was brought to Jerusalem (1Ch.15.22,27). Chenaniah was skilled in this task and instructed others in singing to the Lord. Later, he was also appointed as an administrator over Israel's external business (1Ch.26.29). These passages highlight Chenaniah's musical abilities and his trusted position in David's administration.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.22 only referred to as Chenaniah (כְּנַנְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.22에 처음 언급되며 '그나냐'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그나냐는 다윗 왕 시대에 노래와 행정을 맡은 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Dishon, descendant of Esau
persons.short: Cheran was a son of Dishon and a descendant of Esau.
persons.article: Cheran is mentioned in Gen.36.26 and 1Ch.1.41 as one of the sons of Dishon, who was a descendant of Esau. Esau was the son of Isaac and the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The passages list the descendants of Esau, who became the Edomites, and Cheran is named among the clan leaders.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.26 only referred to as Cheran (כְּרָ֑ן); son of Dishon; a brother of Eshban, Ithran and Hemdan.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '그란'이라 불림. 디손의 아들. 에스반, 이드란과 헴단의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 그란은 디손의 아들로 에서의 후손이었다.

persons.description: People from Chereth(?)
persons.brief: Philistine tribe, often serving as royal guard
persons.short: The Cherethites were a Philistine tribe that often served as royal guards.
persons.article: The Cherethites were a Philistine tribe mentioned in several passages in the Old Testament. In 1Sa.30.14, they are described as living in the Negev region, and their territory was raided by the Amalekites. The Cherethites, along with the Pelethites, often served as royal guards and soldiers for Israelite kings, particularly during the reigns of David and Solomon (2Sa.8.18; 15.18; 20.7; 1Ki.1.38,44). In prophetic oracles, Ezk.25.16 and Zep.2.5 mention the Cherethites as one of the Philistine groups facing God's judgment for their hostility towards Israel. The Cherethites are closely associated with the Philistines and were likely one of the major Philistine tribes settled in Canaan.
persons.summary: A person from Chereth(?), first mentioned at 1Sa.30.14 only referred to as Cherethites (כְּרֵתִי).
persons.summary_ko: 그렛 사람. 1Sa.30.14에 처음 언급되며 '그렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그렛 족속은 흔히 왕의 호위병으로 섬긴 블레셋 지파였다.

persons.description: A military group in the Old Testament
persons.brief: Member of Philistine tribe serving as royal guard
persons.short: The Cherethites were a Philistine tribe that served as royal guards for Israelite kings.
persons.article: The Cherethites, along with the Pelethites, were a group of Philistine warriors who served as loyal guards and soldiers for Israelite kings, particularly during the reigns of David and Solomon. They are mentioned multiple times in the books of Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles. During David's reign, the Cherethites and Pelethites were part of his royal bodyguard and army (2Sa.8.18; 15.18; 20.7, 23). They remained loyal to David during Absalom's rebellion (2Sa.15.18 and helped suppress the revolt led by Sheba )(2Sa.20.7). When Solomon ascended to the throne, the Cherethites and Pelethites supported him and played a role in securing his kingship against Adonijah's attempted coup (1Ki.1.38, 44). They continued to serve in the royal guard during Solomon's reign (1Ki.11.4; 2Ki.11.19). The Cherethites' consistent loyalty and military support for the Davidic kings suggest that they were a trusted and elite group of warriors, likely drawn from the Philistine tribe of the same name.
persons.summary: A group of warriors, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.18 referred to as Cherethite (כְּרֵתִי), or Carite or Cherethite (כָּרִי).
persons.summary_ko: 구약의 한 군사 집단. 2Sa.8.18에 처음 언급되며 '그렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그렛 족속은 이스라엘 왕들의 호위병으로 섬긴 블레셋 지파였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor, Abraham's nephew
persons.short: Chesed was a son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and Milcah.
persons.article: Chesed is mentioned in Gen.22.22 as one of the eight sons of Nahor and Milcah. Nahor was Abraham's brother, making Chesed Abraham's nephew. The passage lists the descendants of Nahor, providing context for the family background of Abraham.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.22 only referred to as Chesed (כֶּ֫שֶׂד); son of Nahor and Milcah; a brother of Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel; half-brother of: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.22에 처음 언급되며 '게셋'이라 불림. 나홀과 밀가의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 그세드는 아브라함의 형제 나홀과 밀가의 아들이었다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: Son of David and Abigail the Carmelitess
persons.short: Chileab, also known as Daniel, was David's son by Abigail the Carmelitess.
persons.article: Chileab, also known as Daniel, was one of King David's sons, born to him by Abigail the Carmelitess. Abigail was originally the wife of Nabal, but after Nabal's death, she became David's wife (1Samuel 25). In the list of David's sons born in Hebron, Chileab is mentioned as the second son (2Sa.3.3, while in the parallel passage in 1Ch.3.1, he is called Daniel). The reason for this difference in names is not explicitly stated in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.3 referred to as Chileab (כִּלְאָב), or Daniel (דָּנִיֵּאל, דָּנִאֵל); a son of David and Abigail; half-brother of: Amnon, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.3.3에 처음 언급되며 '길르압'이라 불림. 다윗과 아비가일의 아들. 암논, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 길르압(다니엘이라고도 함)은 갈멜 여인 아비가일을 통해 낳은 다윗의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Elimelech and Naomi; husband of Orpah
persons.short: Chilion was the son of Elimelech and Naomi, and the husband of Orpah.
persons.article: Chilion was the son of Elimelech and Naomi, from Bethlehem in Judah. He had a brother named Mahlon. During a famine, Elimelech, Naomi, and their two sons went to live in the country of Moab (Rut.1.1-2). While in Moab, Chilion married a Moabite woman named Orpah, and Mahlon married Ruth (Rut.1.4). Tragically, Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon died in Moab, leaving Naomi, Ruth, and Orpah as widows (Rut.1.3,5). When Naomi decided to return to Judah, Orpah remained in Moab, while Ruth chose to accompany her mother-in-law (Rut.1.6-18). Later, when Boaz redeemed the land that had belonged to Elimelech, he also acquired the right to marry Ruth and continue the lineage of Mahlon and Chilion (Rut.4.9-10).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.1.2 only referred to as Chilion (כִּלְיוֹן); son of Elimelech and Naomi; a brother of Mahlon; husband of Orpah.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Rut.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '기룐'이라 불림. 엘리멜렉과 나오미의 아들. 말론의 형제. 오르바의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 기룐은 엘리멜렉과 나오미의 아들이며 오르바의 남편이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Barzillai's son, accompanied David to Jerusalem
persons.short: Chimham, son of Barzillai, accompanied David to Jerusalem after Absalom's rebellion.
persons.article: Chimham was the son of Barzillai the Gileadite, who was a wealthy man from Rogelim. During Absalom's rebellion against King David, Barzillai provided support for David and his followers when they fled from Jerusalem (2Sa.17.27-29). After Absalom's defeat, when David returned to Jerusalem, Barzillai accompanied him to the Jordan River. Due to his advanced age, Barzillai declined David's invitation to come with him to Jerusalem. Instead, he sent his son Chimham to go with the king (2Sa.19.37-38). David showed kindness to Chimham and promised to do for him whatever Barzillai requested (2Sa.19.38). Chimham then went on with David to Jerusalem (2Sa.19.40). This act of loyalty and the king's favor suggests that Chimham held a special place in David's court.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.19.37 only referred to as Chimham (כִּמְהָם).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.19.37에 처음 언급되며 '김함'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바르실래의 아들 김함은 압살롬의 반역 이후 다윗과 함께 예루살렘으로 갔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Elidad, a leader from Benjamin
persons.short: Chislon was the father of Elidad, a leader from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Chislon is mentioned in Num.34.21 as the father of Elidad, who was appointed as a leader from the tribe of Benjamin. Elidad was one of the representatives chosen to help divide the land of Canaan among the Israelite tribes after the conquest. Each tribe had a designated leader for this task, and Elidad was selected from Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.21 only referred to as Chislon (כִּסְלוֹן); father of Elidad.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.21에 처음 언급되며 '기슬론'이라 불림. 엘리닷의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 기슬론은 베냐민 지파 지도자 엘리닷의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer whose household reported divisions in Corinthian church
persons.short: Chloe's household informed Paul about divisions in the Corinthian church.
persons.article: Chloe is mentioned in 1Co.1.11 as a believer whose household members reported to Paul about the divisions and quarrels in the church at Corinth. The fact that Paul cites her household as the source of this information suggests that Chloe was a prominent member of the Corinthian church, and her household had direct knowledge of the problems within the congregation. Paul's mention of Chloe's name indicates that she was known to the Corinthians and that her report was credible.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 1Co.1.11 only referred to as Chloe (Χλόη).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. 1Co.1.11에 처음 언급되며 '글로에'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글로에의 집 사람들은 고린도 교회의 분쟁에 대해 바울에게 알렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Herod's steward, whose wife Joanna supported Jesus
persons.short: Chuza, Herod's steward, was the husband of Joanna, who supported Jesus' ministry.
persons.article: Chuza is mentioned in Luk.8.3 as the steward of Herod Antipas, the ruler of Galilee. Chuza's wife, Joanna, is named among the women who supported Jesus and His disciples out of their own means. The fact that Chuza held a prominent position in Herod's court suggests that he and Joanna were wealthy and influential. Joanna's devotion to Jesus, despite her husband's role in Herod's service, indicates her deep faith and commitment.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.8.3 only referred to as Chuza (Χουζᾶς); husband of Joanna.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '구사'라 불림. 요안나의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 헤롯의 청지기 구사는 예수님의 사역을 도운 요안나의 남편이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer in Rome who sent greetings to Timothy
persons.short: Claudia, along with others, sent greetings to Timothy in Paul's letter.
persons.article: Claudia is mentioned in 2Ti.4.21 as one of the believers in Rome who sent greetings to Timothy through Paul's letter. She is listed alongside Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, and "all the brethren." The inclusion of her name suggests that she was a prominent member of the Roman church and known to both Paul and Timothy. As Paul was writing from prison in Rome, Claudia's greeting indicates her support and concern for both Paul and Timothy.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.4.21 only referred to as Claudia (Κλαυδία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. 2Ti.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '글라우디아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글라우디아는 다른 이들과 함께 바울의 편지를 통해 디모데에게 문안했다.

persons.description: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Roman emperor during Paul's ministry
persons.short: Claudius was the Roman emperor during part of Paul's ministry.
persons.article: Claudius, also referred to as Caesar, was the Roman emperor during a significant portion of Paul's ministry. He is mentioned in several contexts throughout the book of Acts. In Act.11.28, the prophet Agabus foretold a great famine that would occur during the reign of Claudius, which prompted the disciples to send relief to the believers in Judea. Act.18.2 mentions that Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, which led Aquila and Priscilla to move to Corinth, where they met Paul. In Act.17.7, the accusers of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica claimed that they were acting against the decrees of Caesar, likely referring to Claudius. During Paul's trial in Acts 25-26, Claudius is mentioned as the emperor to whom Paul appealed for justice (Act.25.8,10,11,12,21; 26.32). In Act.27.24, an angel told Paul that he must stand before Caesar, referring to Claudius or his successor. Finally, in Act.28.19, Paul stated that he was compelled to appeal to Caesar because of the Jews' opposition. These references to Claudius provide historical context for the events in Acts and demonstrate the Roman Empire's significant influence on the early Christian church.
persons.summary: An emperor of Rome living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.11.28 referred to as Claudius (Κλαύδιος), or Caesar (Καῖσαρ).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 황제. Act.11.28에 처음 언급되며 '글라우디오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글라우디오는 바울 사역의 한 시기에 로마 황제였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Fellow laborer with Paul in the gospel
persons.short: Clement was a fellow laborer with Paul, whose name was in the Book of Life.
persons.article: Clement is mentioned in Php.4.3 as one of Paul's fellow laborers in the gospel. Paul describes Clement, along with others, as having his name in the Book of Life, indicating his faithful service and commitment to Christ. Paul's appeal to the Philippians to help these individuals suggests that they had faced some challenges or conflicts in their ministry. The mention of Clement's name implies that he was known to the Philippian church and had played a significant role in spreading the gospel alongside Paul. No further details about Clement's life or specific ministry activities are provided in the Bible. Some early church traditions identify this Clement as the same person as Clement of Rome, an early church father, but this connection cannot be conclusively established from the biblical text alone.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Php.4.3 only referred to as Clement (Κλήμης).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Php.4.3에 처음 언급되며 '글레멘트'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글레멘드는 바울의 동역자로, 그 이름이 생명책에 기록되어 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Maaseiah, who settled in Jerusalem
persons.short: Col-hozeh was an ancestor of Maaseiah, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Col-hozeh is mentioned in Neh.11.5 as an ancestor of Maaseiah, a descendant of Judah who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Maaseiah is described as the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh. This Col-hozeh is likely a different individual from the father of Shallun mentioned in Neh.3.15, given the different context and time period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Col-hozeh (כׇּל־חֹזֶה); a son of Hazaiah; father of Baruch.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '골호세'라 불림. 하사야의 아들. 바룩의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 골호세는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착한 마아세야의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Shallum, who repaired the Fountain Gate
persons.short: Col-hozeh was the father of Shallum (or 'Shallun'), who repaired the Fountain Gate.
persons.article: Col-hozeh is mentioned in Neh.3.15 as the father of Shallum (or 'Shallun'), who was responsible for repairing the Fountain Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall. Shallum, the son of Col-hozeh, is described as the leader of the district of Mizpah. This suggests that Col-hozeh's family held a prominent position in the region.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.15 only referred to as Col-hozeh (כׇּל־חֹזֶה); father of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.15에 처음 언급되며 '골호세'라 불림. 살룸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 골호세는 샘문을 수리한 살룸(살룬)의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite in charge of offerings during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Conaniah, a Levite, was in charge of the offerings and distributions during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Conaniah was a Levite who served during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He was appointed as one of the officials in charge of the contributions, tithes, and dedicated gifts brought to the Temple (2Ch.31.12). Along with his brother Shimei and other Levites, Conaniah was responsible for ensuring the proper distribution of these offerings to the priests and Levites (2Ch.31.13). Later, during the Passover celebration in Hezekiah's reign, Conaniah, along with other Levite leaders, contributed a large number of animals for the Passover sacrifices (2Ch.35.9). This demonstrates Conaniah's ongoing commitment to the Temple service and his leadership role among the Levites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.31.12 only referred to as Conaniah (כּוֹנַנְיָ֫הוּ); a brother of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.12에 처음 언급되며 '고나냐'라 불림. 고나냐의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 시므이의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 고나냐는 히스기야 왕 시대에 헌물과 분배를 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Centurion, first Gentile convert to Christianity
persons.short: Cornelius, a centurion, was the first Gentile convert to Christianity through Peter's ministry.
persons.article: Cornelius was a Roman centurion stationed in Caesarea. He is described as a devout man who feared God, gave alms generously, and prayed regularly (Act.10.1-2). Despite his piety, Cornelius was not a convert to Judaism. In a vision, an angel instructed Cornelius to send for Peter, who was staying in Joppa (Act.10.3-8). Meanwhile, Peter had a vision in which God revealed that he should not consider anything unclean that God had made clean, preparing him to accept Gentile believers (Act.10.9-16). When Peter arrived at Cornelius' house, Cornelius gathered his relatives and close friends to hear Peter's message (Act.10.24-27). As Peter shared the gospel, the Holy Spirit fell upon the Gentile listeners, confirming that God had accepted them (Act.10.44-46). This event marked a significant turning point in the early church, as it demonstrated that the gospel was for both Jews and Gentiles. Peter then ordered that Cornelius and the other believing Gentiles be baptized (Act.10.47-48). The conversion of Cornelius and his household was a pivotal moment in the spread of Christianity, paving the way for the inclusion of Gentiles in the church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.10.1 only referred to as Cornelius (Κορνήλιος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.10.1에 처음 언급되며 '고넬료'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 백부장 고넬료는 베드로의 사역을 통해 그리스도교로 개종한 최초의 이방인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
persons.short: Cosam is listed as an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Cosam is mentioned in Luk.3.28 as one of the ancestors of Jesus Christ in the genealogy traced through Joseph, Jesus' legal father. He is listed as the son of Elmadam and the father of Addi. The genealogy in Luke's Gospel goes back from Joseph to Adam, the son of God, highlighting Jesus' connection to all of humanity. Cosam's inclusion in the genealogy helps to establish Jesus' lineage and his ties to the Davidic line, as well as his relationship to key figures in Israel's history. However, no additional information about Cosam's life or role is provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.28 only referred to as Cosam (Κωσάμ); a son of Elmadam; father of Addi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.28에 처음 언급되며 '고삼'이라 불림. 엘마담의 아들. 앗디의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 고삼은 누가복음 족보에서 예수님의 조상으로 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Midianite woman killed for immorality with an Israelite
persons.short: Cozbi, a Midianite woman, was killed along with an Israelite man for their immorality.
persons.article: Cozbi was a Midianite woman, the daughter of Zur, a tribal head in Midian. During Israel's stay in Shittim, Cozbi engaged in sexual immorality with Zimri, an Israelite man from the tribe of Simeon. This act of defiance against God's commands occurred in the sight of Moses and the entire congregation of Israel, who were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting due to a plague that had broken out as a result of the people's immorality and idolatry. Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, took a spear and followed Zimri into his tent, where he found him with Cozbi. Phinehas drove the spear through both of them, killing them and halting the plague that had claimed the lives of 24,000 Israelites. God commended Phinehas for his zeal and granted him a covenant of perpetual priesthood. Cozbi's name is mentioned again in Num.25.18, where God instructs Moses to treat the Midianites as enemies and attack them because of their treachery and the incident involving Cozbi, which led Israel into sin.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.25.15 only referred to as Cozbi (כָּזְבִי); a daughter of Zur.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Num.25.15에 처음 언급되며 '고스비'라 불림. 술의 딸.
persons.short_ko: 미디안 여인 고스비는 부도덕한 행위로 한 이스라엘 남자와 함께 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Companion of Paul who went to Galatia
persons.short: Crescens, a companion of Paul, went to Galatia during Paul's imprisonment.
persons.article: Crescens is mentioned briefly in 2Ti.4.10 as one of Paul's companions who had left him during his imprisonment in Rome. Paul states that Crescens had gone to Galatia, a region in Asia Minor where Paul had previously ministered and established churches. The reason for Crescens' departure is not specified, but it is possible that he went to Galatia to continue ministry work or to attend to personal matters. Paul's mention of Crescens, along with others who had left him, highlights the challenges and loneliness he faced during his final imprisonment. Despite this, Paul remained committed to his faith and the spread of the gospel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.4.10 only referred to as Crescens (Κρήσκης).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.4.10에 처음 언급되며 '그레스게'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 그레스게는 바울의 동역자로, 바울이 옥에 갇혔을 때 갈라디아로 갔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Synagogue leader in Corinth who believed in Jesus
persons.short: Crispus, the synagogue leader in Corinth, believed in Jesus and was baptized by Paul.
persons.article: Crispus was the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth during Paul's ministry there. According to Act.18.8, Crispus believed in the Lord, along with his entire household, after hearing Paul's preaching. This conversion was significant, as Crispus held a prominent position in the Jewish community. Following his conversion, Crispus was baptized by Paul, as mentioned in 1Co.1.14. Paul specifically notes that he personally baptized Crispus, along with Gaius, emphasizing the importance of their conversions. The fact that Paul baptized Crispus himself underscores the significance of this synagogue leader coming to faith in Christ. Crispus' conversion likely had a considerable impact on the Jewish community in Corinth and may have encouraged other Jews and Gentiles to consider Paul's message more closely. His story demonstrates the power of the gospel to transform lives, even among those in positions of religious authority.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.18.8 only referred to as Crispus (Κρίσπος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.18.8에 처음 언급되며 '그리스보'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고린도 회당장 그리스보는 예수님을 믿게 되어 바울에게 세례를 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Seba@Gen.10.7-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.7-1Ch, Sabtah@Gen.10.7-1Ch, Raamah@Gen.10.7-1Ch, Sabteca@Gen.10.7-1Ch, Nimrod@Gen.10.8-Mic
persons.brief: Son of Ham; father of Nimrod and other descendants
persons.short: Cush, a son of Ham, was the father of Nimrod and other descendants who became nations.
persons.article: Cush is mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1 as one of the sons of Ham, the son of Noah. He is listed alongside his brothers Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. Several descendants of Cush are named, including Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons, Sheba and Dedan, are also mentioned. These descendants of Cush are associated with various regions and peoples, mostly located in Africa and Arabia. One of the most notable descendants of Cush is Nimrod, who is described as a mighty hunter before the Lord and the founder of the first kingdoms on earth, including Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar (Babylonia). Nimrod is also credited with building Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah, and Resen in Assyria. The Cushites, descendants of Cush, are often associated with the region of Nubia, south of Egypt. In later biblical texts, Cush is used as a geographical term referring to the land south of Egypt, including parts of modern-day Sudan and Ethiopia. The genealogy of Cush and his descendants in Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1 provides insight into the early spread of nations and the origins of various people groups in the ancient Near East and Africa.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.6 only referred to as Cush (כּוּשׁ); son of Ham; a brother of Canaan, Egypt and Put; father of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabteca and Nimrod.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.6에 처음 언급되며 '구스'라 불림. 함의 아들. 가나안, 미스라임과 붓의 형제. 스바, 하윌라, 삽다, 라아마, 삽드가와 니므롯의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함의 아들 구스는 니므롯과 여러 민족이 된 다른 후손들의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite mentioned in the title of Psalm 7
persons.short: Cush, a Benjamite, is mentioned in the title of Psalm 7, which David sang to the Lord.
persons.article: Cush, a Benjamite, is mentioned in the title of Psalm 7, which provides the context for David's composition of this psalm. The title states that David sang this song to the Lord concerning the words of Cush, a Benjamite. This suggests that Cush had spoken against David in some manner, possibly through slander, false accusations, or threats. The content of Psalm 7 reveals that David faced persecution and opposition, and he sought God's protection and justice against those who attacked him without cause. David affirms his innocence and trusts in God to judge righteously, knowing that God is a righteous judge who feels indignation every day. Although no further details are provided about Cush or his specific words against David, the psalm's title and content indicate that Cush's actions prompted David to seek refuge and vindication from the Lord. This incident demonstrates David's reliance on God in the face of adversity and his confidence in God's justice.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at Psa.7.1 only referred to as Cush (כּוּשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Psa.7.1에 처음 언급되며 '구시'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 사람 구시는 다윗이 여호와께 부른 시편 7편의 표제에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel
persons.short: Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, oppressed Israel for eight years until Othniel defeated him.
persons.article: Cushan-rishathaim was the king of Mesopotamia (Aram-naharaim) who oppressed the Israelites for eight years after they had done evil in the sight of the Lord. As a result of their disobedience, the Lord sold the Israelites into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim. In response to the Israelites' cry for help, God raised up Othniel, the son of Kenaz and Caleb's younger brother, as a deliverer. Othniel was empowered by the Spirit of the Lord and went to war against Cushan-rishathaim. The Lord gave Cushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and he prevailed over the Mesopotamian king. As a result of Othniel's victory, the land had rest for forty years until Othniel's death. This event is part of the recurring cycle in the book of Judges, where the Israelites fall into sin, face oppression from foreign rulers, cry out to God, and are delivered by a God-appointed judge.
persons.summary: A king of Mesopotamia living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.3.8 only referred to as Cushan-rishathaim (כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַ֫יִם).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 왕. Jdg.3.8에 처음 언급되며 '구산리사다임'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 메소보다미아 왕 구산리사다임은 팔 년 동안 이스라엘을 압제했으나 옷니엘에게 패했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jehudi, who read Jeremiah's scroll
persons.short: Cushi was the great grandfather of Jehudi, who was sent to fetch Baruch to read Jeremiah's scroll.
persons.article: Cushi is mentioned in Jer.36.14 as the father of Jehudi, a man involved in the events surrounding Jeremiah's prophetic scroll. When Micaiah informed the officials about the contents of the scroll that Baruch had read in the people's hearing, the officials sent Jehudi to summon Baruch and bring the scroll. Jehudi's task was to fetch Baruch, who had written down Jeremiah's prophecies, and have him read the scroll before the officials. This event took place during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah when Jeremiah's prophecies were causing concern among the royal officials. Apart from being identified as Jehudi's father, no other information is provided about Cushi in the Bible. His name suggests that he or his ancestors may have had a connection to the land of Cush, but this is not explicitly stated in the text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.14 only referred to as Cushi (כּוּשִׁי); father of Shelemiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.14에 처음 언급되며 '구시'라 불림. 셀레마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 구시는 예레미야의 두루마리를 읽도록 바룩을 데려오라는 명을 받은 여후디의 증조부였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet
persons.short: Cushi was an ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet, mentioned in his genealogy.
persons.article: Cushi is mentioned in Zep.1.1 as part of the prophet Zephaniah's genealogy. He is listed as the son of Gedaliah and the grandson of Amariah, who was the son of Hezekiah. This genealogy serves to introduce Zephaniah and establish his lineage. The name Cushi may indicate that he or his ancestors had a connection to the land of Cush, which is associated with the region south of Egypt, including parts of modern-day Sudan and Ethiopia. However, it is not uncommon for names to be passed down through generations, and the name itself does not necessarily imply that Cushi himself was from that region. Apart from being mentioned in Zephaniah's genealogy, no other details about Cushi's life or role are provided in the Bible. His inclusion in the genealogy helps to establish Zephaniah's background and family heritage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Zep.1.1 only referred to as Cushi (כּוּשִׁי); a son of Gedaliah; father of Zephaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Zep.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '구스'라 불림. 그달리야의 아들. 스바니야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 구시는 선지자 스바냐의 족보에 언급된 조상이었다.

persons.description: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian Emperor who decreed the rebuilding of the Temple
persons.short: Cyrus, Emperor of Persia, issued a decree allowing the Jews to return and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Cyrus, also known as Cyrus the Great, was the Emperor of Persia who played a significant role in the history of Israel. He is mentioned in several books of the Bible, including 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Isaiah, and Daniel. According to 2Ch.36.22-23 and Ezr.1.1-2, in the first year of his reign, Cyrus issued a proclamation allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple. This decree fulfilled the prophecy of Jeremiah concerning the end of the Babylonian captivity after 70 years. Cyrus also returned the articles of the Temple that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem (Ezr.1.7-8). The returning exiles, led by Zerubbabel, began to rebuild the Temple with the support of Cyrus (Ezr.3.7). The prophets Isaiah and Daniel both mention Cyrus by name. Isa.44.28 and Isa.45.1 refer to Cyrus as the Lord's "anointed" and the one who would carry out God's purpose in rebuilding Jerusalem and the Temple. Dan.1.21 and Dan.10.1 indicate that Daniel lived until the reign of Cyrus, and Dan.6.28 mentions Cyrus as the king who succeeded Darius the Mede. Ezr.4.3-5 records the opposition faced by the Jews in rebuilding the Temple during the reigns of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes. However, Ezr.5.13-17 and Ezr.6.3-14 recount how Cyrus' original decree was rediscovered during the reign of Darius, leading to the completion of the Temple reconstruction. Historically, Cyrus was the founder of the Achaemenid Persian Empire. His conquest of Babylon in 539 BC and his subsequent policy of allowing captive peoples to return to their homelands and rebuild their temples made him a significant figure in Jewish history and a fulfillment of biblical prophecy.
persons.summary: An emperor Persia living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.36.22 referred to as Cyrus (כּ֫וֹרֶשׁ), or Cyrus (Aramiac כּ֫וֹרֶשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 황제. 2Ch.36.22에 처음 언급되며 '고레스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 페르시아 황제 고레스는 유대인들이 돌아가 예루살렘 성전을 재건하도록 허락하는 조서를 내렸다.
persons.article_ko: 고레스(대왕이라고도 함)는 이스라엘 역사에서 중요한 역할을 한 페르시아 황제였다. 그는 역대하, 에스라, 이사야, 다니엘서를 포함한 성경의 여러 책에 언급된다. 역대하 36:22-23과 에스라 1:1-2에 따르면 그의 통치 원년에 고레스는 유대인들이 예루살렘으로 돌아가 성전을 재건하도록 허락하는 조서를 내렸다. 이 조서는 칠십 년 후 바벨론 포로의 종말에 관한 예레미야의 예언을 성취했다. 고레스는 또한 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에서 가져간 성전 기구들을 돌려주었다(스 1:7-8). 스룹바벨이 이끄는 돌아온 포로들은 고레스의 지원으로 성전을 재건하기 시작했다(스 3:7). 선지자 이사야와 다니엘 모두 고레스를 이름으로 언급한다. 이사야 44:28과 45:1은 고레스를 여호와의 '기름부음받은 자'이며 예루살렘과 성전을 재건하는 하나님의 목적을 수행할 자로 언급한다. 다니엘 1:21과 10:1은 다니엘이 고레스 통치 시대까지 살았음을 나타내고, 다니엘 6:28은 고레스를 메대 사람 다리오를 이은 왕으로 언급한다. 에스라 4:3-5는 고레스, 다리오, 아닥사스다 통치 기간 동안 유대인들이 성전 재건에서 직면한 반대를 기록한다. 그러나 에스라 5:13-17과 6:3-14는 다리오 통치 기간 동안 고레스의 원래 조서가 재발견되어 성전 재건 완성으로 이어진 과정을 이야기한다. 역사적으로 고레스는 아케메네스 페르시아 제국의 창시자였다. 기원전 539년 그의 바벨론 정복과 포로가 된 백성들이 고향으로 돌아가 자신들의 성전을 재건하도록 허락하는 그 후의 정책은 그를 유대인 역사의 중요한 인물이며 성경 예언의 성취로 만들었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Parshandatha@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Parmashta@Est.9.9, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9, Vaizatha@Est.9.9
persons.brief: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
persons.short: Dalphon was one of the ten sons of Haman who were killed and hanged.
persons.article: Dalphon is mentioned in Est.9.7 as one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews in the Persian Empire during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). Haman had plotted to destroy all the Jews in the empire, but his plan was thwarted by Queen Esther and her cousin Mordecai. After Haman's downfall and execution, the king granted the Jews the right to defend themselves against their enemies. On the 13th day of the month of Adar, the Jews fought against those who sought to harm them. They defeated their enemies, and among those killed were the ten sons of Haman, including Dalphon. Following their deaths, the bodies of Haman's sons were hanged on the gallows, likely the same gallows Haman had prepared for Mordecai (Est.9.13-14). This act served as a public display of the Jews' victory over their enemies and the downfall of Haman's family. Apart from being listed as one of Haman's sons, no other details about Dalphon's life or actions are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.9.7 only referred to as Dalphon (דַּלְפוֹן); son of Haman; a brother of Parshandatha, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.9.7에 처음 언급되며 '달본'이라 불림. 하만과 세레스의 아들. 바산다다, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새, 아리대와 왜사다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 달본은 죽임을 당해 매달린 하만의 열 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Woman who believed Paul's message in Athens
persons.short: Damaris was a woman who believed Paul's message in Athens and joined him.
persons.article: Damaris is mentioned in Act.17.34 as one of the people who believed Paul's message when he preached at the Areopagus in Athens. After hearing Paul's discourse on the "Unknown God" and the resurrection of Jesus, some of the Athenians mocked him, while others expressed interest in hearing more. Among those who joined Paul and believed were Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris. The fact that Damaris is specifically named alongside Dionysius suggests that she was a person of some prominence or significance in the Athenian society. No further details about Damaris' life, background, or role in the early church are provided in the biblical text. However, her conversion is an example of how Paul's message reached people from various backgrounds, including women, and how the gospel spread in the intellectual and philosophical center of Athens.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.17.34 only referred to as Damaris (Δάμαρις).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Act.17.34에 처음 언급되며 '다마리'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다마리는 아덴에서 바울의 메시지를 믿고 그와 함께한 여인이었다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev, Asher@Gen.30.13-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev
persons.brief: Fifth son of Jacob, founder of Israelite tribe
persons.short: Dan was the fifth son of Jacob and the founder of the Israelite tribe bearing his name.
persons.article: Dan was the fifth son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and the firstborn of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant. His birth is recorded in Gen.30.6, where Rachel, who had been unable to conceive, gave Bilhah to Jacob as a concubine to bear children on her behalf. When Bilhah gave birth to a son, Rachel named him Dan, saying, "God has vindicated me; he has listened to my plea and given me a son." As one of Israel's twelve sons, Dan became the founder of the Israelite tribe bearing his name. In Gen.46.23, when Israel and his family moved to Egypt, Dan's son Hushim is mentioned as part of the household. In Israel's blessing to his sons before his death (Gen.49.16-17, Dan is described as one who will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel). Jacob also compares Dan to a serpent by the roadside, an adder along the path, foreshadowing the tribe's future role in the Promised Land. The tribe of Dan was allocated territory in the northern part of Canaan during the conquest under Joshua. However, they later migrated northward and settled in the city of Laish, which they renamed Dan (Judges 18). In 1Ch.2.2, Dan is listed among the twelve tribes of Israel, confirming his status as one of the founding fathers of the nation. Throughout the Old Testament, the tribe of Dan is mentioned alongside the other Israelite tribes, although they are sometimes associated with idolatry and apostasy.
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Dan living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.30.6 only referred to as Dan (דָּן); son of Israel and Bilhah; a brother of Naphtali; half-brother of: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Dinah, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Hushim.
persons.brief_ko: 야곱과 빌하의 아들, 단 지파 시조
persons.short_ko: 단은 야곱과 라헬의 여종 빌하 사이에서 태어난 아들로 이스라엘 12지파 중 단 지파의 시조가 되었다.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.30.6에 처음 언급되며 '단'이라 불림. 이스라엘과 빌하의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 납달리, 갓, 아셀, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 후심의 아버지.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prophet in Babylon, known for wisdom and visions
persons.short: Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was a prophet in Babylon known for his wisdom, integrity, and interpretation of dreams and visions.
persons.article: Daniel, whose Babylonian name was Belteshazzar, was a prominent Jewish prophet during the Babylonian exile. He was among the young nobles taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar and brought to Babylon to serve in the king's court (Daniel 1). Known for his wisdom, integrity, and ability to interpret dreams and visions, Daniel served under several Babylonian kings, including Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar, and Darius the Mede. He is mentioned alongside Noah and Job in Ezk.14.14,20 as an example of righteousness. Throughout his life, Daniel received several visions and revelations from God, which are recorded in the Book of Daniel. These visions include the interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar's dreams (Daniel 2; 4), the handwriting on the wall during Belshazzar's feast (Daniel 5), and visions concerning future kingdoms and the end times (Daniel 7-12). Daniel's faithfulness to God was tested when he was thrown into the lions' den for praying to God instead of King Darius (Daniel 6). However, God protected him, and his faith and integrity were vindicated. In the New Testament, Jesus refers to the "abomination of desolation" spoken of by the prophet Daniel (Mat.24.15; Mrk.13.14, indicating the continued significance of Daniel's prophecies). Daniel's life and ministry demonstrate the importance of faith, prayer, and obedience to God, even in the face of persecution and adversity. His visions and prophecies provide insight into God's sovereign plan for the nations and the coming of the Messiah.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezk.14.14 referred to as Daniel (דָּנִיֵּאל, דָּנִאֵל), or Daniel (Aramiac דָּנִיֵּאל, דָּנִאֵל), or Belteshazzar (בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר), or Belteshazzar (Aramiac בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר) or Daniel (Δανιήλ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Ezk.14.14에 처음 언급되며 '다니엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다니엘(벨드사살이라고도 함)은 바벨론의 선지자로, 지혜와 정직함, 꿈과 환상 해석으로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 다니엘(바벨론 이름은 벨드사살)은 바벨론 포로 시대의 저명한 유대인 선지자였다. 그는 느부갓네살에게 사로잡혀 바벨론으로 끌려온 젊은 귀족 중 한 사람으로, 왕궁에서 섬기게 되었다(다니엘 1장). 지혜와 정직함, 꿈과 환상을 해석하는 능력으로 알려진 다니엘은 느부갓네살, 벨사살, 메대 사람 다리오를 포함한 여러 바벨론 왕들을 섬겼다. 그는 에스겔 14:14, 20에서 노아, 욥과 함께 의로움의 본보기로 언급된다. 그의 생애 동안 다니엘은 하나님으로부터 여러 환상과 계시를 받았는데, 이는 다니엘서에 기록되어 있다. 이 환상들에는 느부갓네살의 꿈 해석(다니엘 2장, 4장), 벨사살 잔치 때의 벽에 쓴 글씨(다니엘 5장), 미래 왕국들과 종말에 관한 환상들(다니엘 7-12장)이 포함된다. 다니엘의 하나님께 대한 신실함은 다리오 왕 대신 하나님께 기도했다는 이유로 사자굴에 던져졌을 때 시험받았다(다니엘 6장). 그러나 하나님은 그를 보호하셨고, 그의 믿음과 정직함이 입증되었다. 신약에서 예수님은 선지자 다니엘이 말한 '멸망의 가증한 것'을 언급하셔서(마 24:15; 막 13:14) 다니엘의 예언들이 계속해서 중요함을 나타내신다. 다니엘의 생애와 사역은 박해와 역경에도 불구하고 믿음, 기도, 하나님께 대한 순종의 중요성을 보여준다. 그의 환상과 예언은 민족들에 대한 하나님의 주권적 계획과 메시아의 오심에 대한 통찰을 제공한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Daniel, a priest, was among those who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Daniel is mentioned in Ezr.8.2 and Neh.10.6 as a priest who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. In Ezr.8.2, he is listed among the descendants of Ithamar, one of Aaron's sons, indicating his priestly lineage. This Daniel was part of the group that returned to Jerusalem with Ezra, who led a significant return of exiles during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia. In Neh.10.6, Daniel is mentioned again as one of the priests who signed the covenant to follow the Law of God. This covenant was made after Ezra had read the Book of the Law to the people, and they had confessed their sins and committed to obeying God's commands. The fact that Daniel is mentioned in both Ezra and Nehemiah suggests that he played a role in the religious life of the Jewish community after the exile. As a priest, he would have been involved in the Temple service and in teaching the people the Law of God. Apart from these two references, no other details about this Daniel's life or ministry are provided in the Bible. It is important to note that this Daniel is a different person from the more well-known prophet Daniel, who lived earlier during the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.8.2 only referred to as Daniel (דָּנִיֵּאל, דָּנִאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '다니엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 다니엘은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zerah, grandson of Judah
persons.short: Dara was a son of Zerah and grandson of Judah.
persons.article: Dara is mentioned in 1Ch.2.6 as one of the five sons of Zerah, along with Zimri, Ethan, Heman, and Calcol. Zerah was one of the twin sons of Judah, born to Tamar (Gen.38.30). As a grandson of Judah, Dara was part of the tribe of Judah, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The tribe of Judah played a significant role in Israel's history, as it was prophesied that the Messiah would come from this tribe (Gen.49.10). Apart from being listed in the genealogy of Judah, no other details about Dara's life or role are provided in the Bible. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles trace the lineage of the tribes of Israel, demonstrating the importance of family heritage and the fulfillment of God's promises through the generations.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.6 only referred to as Dara (דָּרַע); son of Zerah; a brother of Zabdi, Ethan, Heman and Calcol.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '다라'라 불림. 세라의 아들. 삽디, 에단, 헤만과 갈골의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다라는 세라의 아들이며 유다의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wise man surpassed by Solomon's wisdom
persons.short: Darda was a wise man, but Solomon's wisdom surpassed his.
persons.article: Darda is mentioned in 1Ki.4.31 as one of the wise men whom King Solomon's wisdom surpassed. He is listed alongside Ethan the Ezrahite and the sons of Mahol, suggesting that he was a well-known figure renowned for his wisdom during that time. The context of this passage emphasizes the exceptional wisdom that God had granted to Solomon, stating that his wisdom was greater than that of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt. By comparing Solomon's wisdom to that of Darda and the other wise men, the text highlights the unparalleled nature of Solomon's God-given wisdom. Apart from this single mention, no other details about Darda's life, background, or specific areas of wisdom are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.31 only referred to as Darda (דַּרְדַּע); son of Mahol; a brother of Ethan, Heman and Calcol.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.31에 처음 언급되며 '다르다'라 불림. 마홀의 아들. 에단, 헤만과 갈골의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다르다는 지혜로운 사람이었으나 솔로몬의 지혜가 그를 능가했다.

persons.description: Ruler living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Mede who became Emperor over Babylon
persons.short: Darius the Mede received the Empire of Babylon and ruled over it.
persons.article: Darius the Mede is mentioned in the Book of Daniel as the ruler who took over the Babylonian kingdom after the fall of Babylon to the Medo-Persian Empire. He is first introduced in Dan.5.31, which states that Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of sixty-two. In Daniel 6, Darius is portrayed as the king who was manipulated by his officials into issuing a decree that prohibited prayer to anyone but him for thirty days. This decree led to Daniel being thrown into the lions' den when he was caught praying to God. However, God protected Daniel, and Darius, upon discovering Daniel's miraculous survival, issued a new decree acknowledging the power of Daniel's God (Dan.6.25-28). Darius is also mentioned in Dan.9.1, which sets the context for Daniel's prayer of confession and supplication for his people. The chapter begins by stating that this event took place in the first year of Darius' reign. In Dan.11.1, an angelic messenger refers to the first year of Darius the Mede, indicating that he had been supporting and protecting the prince of Persia. The identity of Darius the Mede has been a subject of debate among scholars, as there is no clear historical record of a Median king ruling Babylon between the reigns of Belshazzar and Cyrus the Great. Some scholars suggest that Darius may have been a subordinate ruler or a governor under Cyrus, while others propose that the name may be a title or a reference to Cyrus himself. Despite the uncertainty surrounding his identity, the biblical account presents Darius the Mede as a significant figure in the early days of the Medo-Persian Empire and in the life of Daniel.
persons.summary: Ruler living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Dan.5.31 referred to as Darius (דָּֽרְיָ֫וֶשׁ), or Darius (Aramiac דָּֽרְיָ֫וֶשׁ); son of Ahasuerus and Vashti; brother of Artaxerxes.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 통치자. Dan.5.31에 처음 언급되며 '다리오'라 불림. 아하수에로와 와스디의 아들. 아닥사스다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 메대 사람 다리오는 바벨론 제국을 이어받아 다스렸다.

persons.description: Emperor Darius I, 'the Great', living at the time of Exile and Return
