persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Eliashib was an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Eliashib is mentioned in Ezr.10.27 as one of the descendants of Zattu who had married foreign women. During the time of Ezra, many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan inhabitants of the land. Ezra called for a reform, urging those who had married foreign wives to separate from them. Eliashib was among the Israelites who had taken foreign wives, contrary to God's law. As part of the reform, Eliashib and the other Israelites pledged to put away their foreign wives and children.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.27 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아십'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리아십은 에스라의 개혁 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼한 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Another Israelite who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Eliashib was another Israelite who married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Eliashib is mentioned in Ezr.10.36 as one of the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women. During the time of Ezra, many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan inhabitants of the land. Ezra called for a reform, urging those who had married foreign wives to separate from them. Eliashib was among the Israelites who had taken foreign wives, contrary to God's law. As part of the reform, Eliashib and the other Israelites pledged to put away their foreign wives and children.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.36 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.36에 처음 언급되며 '에랴십'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리아십은 에스라의 개혁 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼한 또 다른 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest during Ezra's time, associated with Jehohanan's chamber
persons.short: Eliashib was a priest during Ezra's time who was associated with Jehohanan's chamber.
persons.article: Eliashib is mentioned in Ezr.10.6 as a priest associated with the chamber of Jehohanan, the son of Eliashib. This reference occurs in the context of Ezra's reforms, particularly addressing the issue of intermarriage between the Israelites and foreign women. Ezra went to the chamber of Jehohanan to fast and mourn over the unfaithfulness of the exiles who had married foreign women. The chamber of Jehohanan likely refers to a room within the temple complex.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.6 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב); father of Jehohanan.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.6에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아십'이라 불림. 여호하난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리아십은 에스라 시대에 여호하난의 방과 관련된 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: High priest, father of Joiada and ancestor of Jaddua
persons.short: Eliashib was the high priest, father of Joiada, and ancestor of Jaddua, who served as high priest during the time of Alexander the Great.
persons.article: Eliashib is mentioned in Neh.12.10, 22, 23 as a high priest in the lineage of the high priesthood. He was the father of Joiada and the ancestor of Jaddua, who served as high priest during the time of Alexander the Great (Neh.12.22). The text provides a genealogy of the high priests, tracing the line from Jeshua to Jaddua, with Eliashib being a key figure in this lineage. Eliashib's mention in this context highlights the importance of the high priesthood and its succession throughout the generations. The text also notes that one of Eliashib's grandsons married a daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, a prominent opponent of Nehemiah (Neh.13.28).
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.12.10 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב); a son of Joiakim; father of Joiada.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 제사장. Neh.12.10에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아십'이라 불림. 요야김의 아들. 요야다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 대제사장 엘리아십은 요야다의 아버지이며, 알렉산더 대왕 시대에 대제사장으로 섬긴 얏두아의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who prepared a room for Tobiah in the temple
persons.short: Eliashib, a priest, had ties to Tobiah the Ammonite and prepared a room for him in the temple courts.
persons.article: Eliashib, a priest, is mentioned in Neh.13.4, 7 in relation to his ties with Tobiah the Ammonite, an opponent of Nehemiah. Prior to Nehemiah's return to Jerusalem, Eliashib had been put in charge of the storerooms in the temple (Neh.13.4). However, he allied himself with Tobiah and prepared a large room for him in the temple courts, which had previously been used to store grain offerings, incense, and temple articles (Neh.13.5). Upon learning of this, Nehemiah was greatly displeased and threw out Tobiah's household goods from the room (Neh.13.7-8). This incident highlights the challenges Nehemiah faced in restoring proper worship and order in the temple, even among the priestly ranks.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.13.4 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.13.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아십'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 엘리아십은 암몬 사람 도비야와 친분이 있어 성전 뜰에 그를 위한 방을 마련해주었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: High priest during Nehemiah's time, involved in rebuilding Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Eliashib, the high priest during Nehemiah's time, participated in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Eliashib, the high priest, is mentioned in Neh.3.1, 20, 21 as one of the prominent figures involved in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem. He, along with his fellow priests, rebuilt the Sheep Gate and consecrated it (Neh.3.1). Eliashib's involvement in the rebuilding project highlights the importance of religious leadership in the restoration of Jerusalem. The text also mentions that Eliashib's grandson, Meremoth, was responsible for repairing two sections of the wall (Neh.3.20, 21). Eliashib's participation in the rebuilding effort demonstrates his commitment to the physical and spiritual restoration of the city and the temple.
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.3.1 only referred to as Eliashib (אֶלְיָשִׁיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아십'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느헤미야 시대의 대제사장 엘리아십은 예루살렘 성벽 재건에 참여했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: Son of Heman, appointed as a musician in David's time
persons.short: Eliathah, a son of Heman, was appointed as a musician during King David's reign.
persons.article: Eliathah is mentioned in 1Ch.25.4, 27 as one of the sons of Heman, a prominent musician during the reign of King David. Heman, along with Asaph and Jeduthun, was appointed by David to lead the music in the house of the Lord (1Ch.25.1). Eliathah, along with his brothers, was skilled in music and was appointed to serve as a musician under the direction of his father, Heman (1Ch.25.4). The text also mentions that Eliathah and his brothers were assigned the twentieth turn in the musical rotation (1Ch.25.27). Eliathah's inclusion in this list highlights the importance of music in Israelite worship during David's reign.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Eliathah (אֳלִיאָ֫תָה); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘리아다'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤만의 아들 엘리아다는 다윗 왕 시대에 음악가로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Chislon, leader from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Elidad, the son of Chislon, was a leader from the tribe of Benjamin chosen to help divide the Promised Land.
persons.article: Elidad, the son of Chislon, is mentioned in Num.34.21 as the leader chosen from the tribe of Benjamin to assist in dividing the Promised Land. After the Israelites had conquered the land of Canaan, God instructed Moses to appoint leaders from each tribe to help divide the land as an inheritance among the tribes (Num.34.16-29). Elidad was selected as the representative from the tribe of Benjamin. His role, along with the other appointed leaders, was to ensure a fair and equitable distribution of the land based on the size of each tribe. Elidad's appointment demonstrates the importance of tribal representation and organization in the allocation of the Promised Land.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.21 only referred to as Elidad (אֱלִידָד); a son of Chislon.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.21에 처음 언급되며 '엘리닷'이라 불림. 기슬론의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 기슬론의 아들 엘리닷은 약속의 땅 분배를 돕도록 선택된 베냐민 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Son of Meshelemiah, a gatekeeper in David's time
persons.short: Eliehoenai, a son of Meshelemiah, was a gatekeeper during King David's reign.
persons.article: Eliehoenai is mentioned in 1Ch.26.3 as one of the sons of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper during the reign of King David. Meshelemiah and his sons were appointed as gatekeepers for the house of the Lord, ensuring the security and order of the temple. Eliehoenai, along with his brothers, was assigned to guard the gates and maintain the sacred space. The mention of Eliehoenai in this context highlights the importance of the gatekeepers' role in the temple service during David's time.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.3 only referred to as Eliehoenai (אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam and Jehohanan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.3에 처음 언급되며 '엘여호에내'라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 스가랴, 여디아엘, 스바댜, 야드니엘, 엘람과 여호하난의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 므셀레먀의 아들 엘여호에내는 다윗 왕 시대에 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Pahath-Moab who returned with Ezra
persons.short: Eliehoenai, a descendant of Pahath-Moab, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Eliehoenai is mentioned in Ezr.8.4 as one of the descendants of Pahath-Moab who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. During the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, Ezra led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem to restore worship and reinforce the Jewish community (Ezr.7.1-10). Eliehoenai was part of this group, which included various families and individuals from different tribes and backgrounds. The mention of Eliehoenai in this list highlights the diverse composition of the returnees and their shared commitment to rebuilding Jerusalem and the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.4 only referred to as Eliehoenai (אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי); a son of Zerahiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘여호에내니'라 불림. 스라히야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압의 후손 엘여호에내는 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: The Mahavite, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Eliel the Mahavite was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Eliel the Mahavite is mentioned in 1Ch.11.46 as one of David's mighty men. The mighty men were an elite group of warriors known for their exceptional military skills and bravery. They played a crucial role in David's military campaigns and helped establish his kingdom. Eliel's association with Mahavite suggests that he may have been from a place or family known as Mahavah, although the exact location is not specified in the text.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.46 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.46에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마하위 사람 엘리엘은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men from Meholah
persons.short: Eliel from Meholah was another one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned in 1Ch.11.47 as one of David's mighty men. He is described as being from Meholah, which was a town in the Jordan Valley, possibly associated with the tribe of Issachar. The mighty men were an elite group of warriors known for their exceptional military skills and bravery. They played a crucial role in David's military campaigns and helped establish his kingdom.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.47 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.47에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므홀랏 사람 엘리엘은 다윗의 또 다른 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Eliel was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned in 1Ch.12.11 as one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag. The Gadites were known for their bravery and military prowess. They joined David while he was seeking refuge from King Saul, who sought to kill him. The text describes the Gadites as men of valor, trained for battle, and skilled with shield and spear. Eliel, along with the other Gadite warriors, provided valuable support to David during his time of need.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.11 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.11에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갓 지파 용사 엘리엘은 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite leader who assisted in bringing the ark to Jerusalem
persons.short: Eliel, a Levite leader, assisted in bringing the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem during David's reign.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned in 1Ch.15.9, 11 as one of the Levite leaders during the reign of King David. He, along with other Levite leaders, was appointed to assist in bringing the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. The ark, which symbolized God's presence among His people, had been neglected for many years. David sought to restore proper worship by bringing the ark to Jerusalem. Eliel, as a Levite leader, played a significant role in this sacred task. The Levites were responsible for carrying the ark and ensuring its safe transportation. Eliel's involvement in this event highlights the importance of the Levites in the religious life of Israel during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.9 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.9에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 지도자 엘리엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮기는 일을 도왔다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Leader from the half-tribe of Manasseh during David's reign
persons.short: Eliel was a leader from the half-tribe of Manasseh during King David's reign.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.24 as one of the leaders from the half-tribe of Manasseh during the reign of King David. He is described as a mighty man of valor and a leader of his father's house. The half-tribe of Manasseh settled in the region of Gilead, east of the Jordan River. Eliel, along with the other leaders mentioned, played a significant role in the military and political affairs of their tribe. The text highlights their bravery and leadership qualities, which contributed to the strength and success of the tribe during David's reign.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.24 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.5.24에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 므낫세 반 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jakim@1Ch.8.19, Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Zabdi@1Ch.8.19, Elienai@1Ch.8.20, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21, Shimrath@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: Descendant of Shimei from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Eliel was a descendant of Shimei from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.8.20 as one of the descendants of Shimei, who was a member of the tribe of Benjamin. This genealogical record traces the lineage of the Benjamites, providing a list of names without much additional information. Eliel's mention in this context serves to highlight the continuity of the Benjamite lineage and their presence in the post-exilic community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.20 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל); son of Shimei; a brother of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.20에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 야김, 시그리, 삽디, 엘리에내, 실르대, 아다야, 브라야와 시므랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리엘은 베냐민 지파 시므이의 후손이었다.

persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.22에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림. 사삭의 아들. 이스반, 에벨, 압돈, 시그리, 하난, 하나냐, 엘람, 안도디야, 이브드야와 브누엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리엘은 베냐민 지파 사삭의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who served as an overseer during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Eliel was a Levite who served as an overseer during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Eliel is mentioned briefly in 2Ch.31.13 as one of the Levites who served as an overseer during the reign of King Hezekiah. Hezekiah was known for his religious reforms and his efforts to restore proper worship in Judah. As part of these reforms, Hezekiah appointed Levites to oversee the collection and distribution of tithes and offerings brought to the temple. Eliel was one of the Levites entrusted with this responsibility. His role as an overseer highlights the importance of the Levites in maintaining the temple's functioning and ensuring the proper use of the offerings.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '엘리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 엘리엘은 히스기야 왕 시대에 감독으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jakim@1Ch.8.19, Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Zabdi@1Ch.8.19, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Eliel@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21, Shimrath@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: A Benjamite descendant of Shimei.
persons.short: Elienai was a Benjamite, a descendant of Shimei.
persons.article: Elienai was a Benjamite mentioned in the genealogy of Shimei (1Ch.8.20). He was one of the descendants of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 lists the heads of families and clans in the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.20 only referred to as Elienai (אֱלִיעֵינַי); son of Shimei; a brother of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.20에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에내'라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 야김, 시그리, 삽디, 실르대, 엘리엘, 아다야, 브라야와 시므랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘여내는 베냐민 사람으로 시므이의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A priest who blew trumpets before the ark.
persons.short: Eliezer was a priest who blew trumpets before the ark of God.
persons.article: Eliezer is mentioned as one of the priests who blew trumpets before the ark of God when David brought it to Jerusalem (1Ch.15.24). He was part of a procession that included Levites carrying the ark, singers, and other musicians. The blowing of trumpets was a significant part of Israelite worship and was used to signal important events.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.15.24 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.24에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 엘리에셀은 하나님의 궤 앞에서 나팔을 불었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Leader of the tribe of Reuben under David.
persons.short: Eliezer was the leader of the tribe of Reuben during King David's reign.
persons.article: Eliezer is listed as the leader of the tribe of Reuben during King David's reign (1Ch.27.16). He was one of the twelve tribal leaders appointed by David to oversee the administration of the kingdom. Each leader was responsible for the affairs of their tribe for one month of the year. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Eliezer's life or role as the leader of Reuben.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.16 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר); a son of Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.16에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림. 시그리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 다윗 왕 시대에 르우벤 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Joash@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8

persons.short: Eliezer was a descendant of Benjamin; son of Becher.
persons.article: Eliezer is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Ch.7.8. He was a ; son of Becher, who was one of the sons of Benjamin. The genealogy lists the heads of families and clans in the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Joash, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 요아스, 에료에내, 오므리, 여레못, 아비야, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 베겔의 아들로 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet who rebuked King Jehoshaphat.
persons.short: Eliezer was a prophet who rebuked King Jehoshaphat for his alliance with Ahaziah.
persons.article: Eliezer was a prophet who rebuked King Jehoshaphat of Judah for his alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel (2Ch.20.37). Jehoshaphat had joined forces with Ahaziah to build ships to go to Tarshish, but Eliezer prophesied against this alliance, declaring that God had destroyed Jehoshaphat's works because of his partnership with Ahaziah. As a result, the ships were wrecked and never set sail to Tarshish. The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliezer or his prophetic ministry.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.20.37 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר); a son of Dodavahu.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.20.37에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림. 도다와후의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 엘리에셀은 여호사밧 왕이 아하시야와 동맹한 것을 책망했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Moses and Zipporah.
persons.short: Eliezer was the second son of Moses and Zipporah.
persons.article: Eliezer was the second son of Moses and Zipporah (Exo.18.4). His name, which means "my God is help," was given by Moses because God had delivered him from Pharaoh's sword (Exo.18.4). Eliezer and his brother Gershom were born during Moses' exile in Midian. In the genealogies of the Levites, Eliezer is listed as a son of Moses (1Ch.23.15,17). He had a son named Rehabiah, who had many descendants (1Ch.23.17; 26.25). The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliezer's life or role.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.18.4 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר); son of Moses and Zipporah; a brother of Gershom; father of Rehabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Exo.18.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림. 모세와 십보라의 아들. 게르솜의 형제. 르하뱌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 모세와 십보라의 둘째 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Eliezer was a priest who married a foreign woman during the exile.
persons.article: Eliezer is mentioned as one of the priests who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.18). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was a violation of God's command not to intermarry with the pagan nations. Eliezer was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra. The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliezer's life or priestly service.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.18 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Eliezer was a Levite who married a foreign woman during the exile.
persons.article: Eliezer is mentioned as one of the Levites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.23). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites, including Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was a violation of God's command not to intermarry with the pagan nations. Eliezer was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra. The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliezer's life or role as a Levite.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.23 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.23에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Eliezer was an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile.
persons.article: Eliezer is listed among the descendants of Harim who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.31). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was a violation of God's command not to intermarry with the pagan nations. Eliezer was one of those who had taken a foreign wife, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Eliezer's life or family.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.31 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.31에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader summoned by Ezra.
persons.short: Eliezer was one of the leaders summoned by Ezra to the river Ahava.
persons.article: Eliezer was one of the leaders summoned by Ezra to the river Ahava during the return of the exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezr.8.16). Ezra had gathered the people at the river and discovered that there were no Levites among them. He then sent for Eliezer and other leaders to bring Levites and temple servants to accompany them on their journey. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Eliezer's role or status among the returning exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.16 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 에스라가 아하와 강가로 소집한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Of Damascus, Abraham's servant and potential heir.
persons.short: Eliezer of Damascus was Abraham's servant and potential heir before the birth of Ishmael and Isaac.
persons.article: Eliezer of Damascus was a servant in Abraham's household who was mentioned as a potential heir to Abraham's estate before the birth of Ishmael and Isaac (Gen.15.2). In a conversation with God, Abraham lamented his lack of children and named Eliezer as the steward of his house and the one who would inherit his possessions. However, God promised Abraham that he would have a son of his own, and this promise was fulfilled through the births of Ishmael and Isaac.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.15.2 only referred to as Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.15.2에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다메섹 사람 엘리에셀은 아브라함의 종으로, 이스마엘과 이삭이 태어나기 전 잠재적 상속자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
persons.short: Eliezer was an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Eliezer is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.29). He was an ancestor of Jesus, listed in the lineage from David to Joseph, the husband of Mary. The genealogy in Luke traces Jesus' ancestry through his mother Mary.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.29 only referred to as Eliezer (Ἐλιέζερ); a son of Jorim; father of Joshua.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.29에 처음 언급되며 '엘리에서'라 불림. 요림의 아들. 여호수아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리에셀은 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A scribe of King Solomon.
persons.short: Elihoreph was one of King Solomon's scribes.
persons.article: Elihoreph is mentioned as one of the scribes of King Solomon (1Ki.4.3). He served alongside Ahiah, another scribe, during Solomon's reign. Scribes were important officials in the royal court, responsible for writing and maintaining official documents, correspondence, and records. The mention of Elihoreph and Ahiah as Solomon's scribes highlights the king's administrative organization and the importance of record-keeping in his kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.3 only referred to as Elihoreph (אֱלִיחֹ֫רֶף); son of Seraiah; a brother of Ahijah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.3에 처음 언급되며 '엘리호렙'이라 불림. 스라야의 아들. 아히야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리호렙은 솔로몬 왕의 서기관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Manassite who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Elihu was one of the Manassites who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Elihu is listed as one of the Manassites who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul (1Ch.12.20). Along with several other warriors from the tribe of Manasseh, Elihu defected to David's side and helped him fight against the raiding bands. These Manassites were described as brave warriors, commanders, and expert with shield and spear. The Bible does not provide any additional details about Elihu's life or his role in David's army.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.20 only referred to as Elihu (אֱלִיהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.20에 처음 언급되며 '엘리후'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리후는 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 므낫세 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A gatekeeper of the temple, son of Shemaiah.
persons.short: Elihu was one of the sons of Shemaiah, a gatekeeper of the temple.
persons.article: Elihu is mentioned as one of the sons of Shemaiah, who was a gatekeeper of the temple during the reign of King David (1Ch.26.7). Elihu and his brothers were described as capable men with the strength to do the work. They served in the role of gatekeepers, which involved guarding the entrances to the temple and ensuring that only authorized individuals were allowed to enter. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elihu's life or his specific duties as a gatekeeper.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.7 only referred to as Elihu (אֱלִיהוּ); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad and Semachiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.7에 처음 언급되며 '엘리후'라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 오드니, 르바엘, 오벳, 엘사밧과 스마갸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리후는 성전 문지기 스마야의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Leader of the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Elihu, David's brother, was the leader of the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Elihu, identified as King David's brother, is mentioned as the leader of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.27.18). He was one of the twelve tribal leaders appointed by David to oversee the administration of the kingdom. Each leader was responsible for the affairs of their tribe for one month of the year. The fact that Elihu is called David's brother suggests that he may have been a close relative or a member of the extended royal family. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Elihu's life or his role as the leader of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.18 only referred to as Elihu (אֱלִיהוּ); son of Jesse; a brother of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Shimeah, Nethanel, Raddai, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Ozem.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 형제. 1Ch.27.18에 처음 언급되며 '엘리후'라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 아들. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 삼마, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 스루야와 아비가일의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다윗의 형 엘리후는 유다 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Samuel.
persons.short: Elihu, also known as Eliel, was an ancestor of the prophet Samuel.
persons.article: Elihu, also referred to as Eliel, is mentioned in the genealogies of the Kohathite Levites as an ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1Sa.1.1; 1Ch.6.27,34). He was the son of Tohu (1Sa.1.1 or Toah )(1Ch.6.34 and the father of Jeroham, who was the father of Elkanah, Samuel's father). The variations in the names (Elihu, Eliel, and Eliab) may be due to scribal differences or alternative names for the same individual. The Bible does not provide any further information about Elihu's life or role as a Levite.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.1.1 referred to as Elihu (אֱלִיהוּ), or Eliab (אֱלִיאָב), or Eliel (אֱלִיאֵל); a son of Tohu; father of Jeroham.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Sa.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '엘리후'라 불림. 도후의 아들. 여로함의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리후(엘리엘이라고도 함)는 선지자 사무엘의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A young man who spoke to Job.
persons.short: Elihu, a young man from the family of Ram, spoke to Job and his friends.
persons.article: Elihu is a character in the Book of Job who speaks to Job and his three friends after they had finished their dialogue (Job.32-37). He is described as a young man from the family of Ram, and he became angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God and with Job's friends for not finding an answer to Job's complaints (Job.32.2-3). Elihu waited to speak until after the older men had finished, showing respect for their age (Job.32.4-6). In his speeches, Elihu emphasizes God's justice, sovereignty, and wisdom, arguing that God uses suffering to discipline and purify people (Job.33-37). He also asserts that God is greater than human understanding and that people should submit to His will (Job.36-37). After Elihu's speech, God Himself addresses Job out of the whirlwind (Job.38.1). The Bible does not provide any further information about Elihu's life or background.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Job.32.2 only referred to as Elihu (אֱלִיהוּ); a son of Barachel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Job.32.2에 처음 언급되며 '엘리후'라 불림. 바라겔의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 람 가문의 젊은이 엘리후는 욥과 그의 친구들에게 말했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Jeroham.
persons.short: Elijah was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Jeroham.
persons.article: Elijah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Jeroham (1Ch.8.27). This genealogy lists the descendants of Benjamin, tracing the lineage of King Saul. Apart from being named as a son of Jeroham, no additional information is provided about this Elijah in the Bible. He should not be confused with the prominent prophet Elijah, as they are different individuals.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.27 only referred to as Elijah (אֵלִיָּה); son of Jeroham; a brother of Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah and Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.27에 처음 언급되며 '엘리야'라 불림. 여로함의 아들. 삼스래, 스하랴, 아달랴, 야아레시야와 시그리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리야는 베냐민 사람으로 여로함의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet during the reigns of Ahab and Ahaziah.
persons.short: Elijah was a prominent prophet in Israel during the reigns of Ahab and Ahaziah, known for his miracles and confrontations with the prophets of Baal.
persons.article: Elijah was a prominent prophet in Israel during the reigns of King Ahab and his son Ahaziah (1Ki.17-2Ki.2). He is introduced as a Tishbite from Gilead, who proclaimed a drought in Israel as a judgment from God (1Ki.17.1). During the drought, God miraculously provided for Elijah through ravens and a widow in Zarephath (1Ki.17.2-16). Elijah famously confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, demonstrating the power of the true God and exposing the false prophets (1Ki.18). He also confronted King Ahab and Queen Jezebel for their wickedness, particularly in the case of Naboth's vineyard (1Ki.21). Elijah anointed Elisha as his successor and was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, leaving behind his mantle for Elisha (2Ki.2). He is mentioned in the New Testament as a forerunner to John the Baptist (Mat.11.14; Luk.1.17 and as appearing with Moses at Jesus' transfiguration )(Mat.17.3-4; Mrk.9.4-5; Luk.9.30-33). Elijah is also referenced as an example of powerful prayer (Jas.5.17-18 and as a prophet whom God had preserved a remnant of faithful Israelites )(Rom.11.2-4). The prophet Malachi foretold that Elijah would return before the coming of the Messiah (Mal.4.5-6).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.17.1 referred to as Elijah (אֵלִיָּה) or Elijah (Ἡλίας).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 1Ki.17.1에 처음 언급되며 '엘리야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리야는 아합과 아하시야 왕 시대의 저명한 이스라엘 선지자로, 기적과 바알 선지자들과의 대결로 알려져 있다.
persons.article_ko: 엘리야는 아합 왕과 그 아들 아하시야의 통치 기간 동안 이스라엘의 저명한 선지자였다(왕상 17장-왕하 2장). 그는 하나님의 심판으로 이스라엘에 가뭄을 선포한 길르앗 사람 디셉 사람으로 소개된다(왕상 17:1). 가뭄 동안 하나님은 까마귀들과 사르밧의 한 과부를 통해 기적적으로 엘리야를 부양하셨다(왕상 17:2-16). 엘리야는 갈멜산에서 바알 선지자들을 대적하여 유명한 대결을 벌였고, 참 하나님의 능력을 나타내며 거짓 선지자들의 정체를 드러냈다(왕상 18장). 그는 또한 나봇의 포도원 사건에서 특히 아합 왕과 이세벨 왕비의 악함을 대적했다(왕상 21장). 엘리야는 엘리사에게 기름을 부어 후계자로 삼았고 회오리바람을 타고 하늘로 올라가며 엘리사에게 자기 겉옷을 남겨두었다(왕하 2장). 그는 신약에서 세례 요한의 선구자로 언급되며(마 11:14; 눅 1:17) 예수님의 변화산에서 모세와 함께 나타난다(마 17:3-4; 막 9:4-5; 눅 9:30-33). 엘리야는 또한 능력 있는 기도의 본보기로 언급되며(약 5:17-18) 하나님이 신실한 이스라엘 사람의 남은 자를 보존하셨던 선지자로도 언급된다(롬 11:2-4). 선지자 말라기는 메시아가 오시기 전에 엘리야가 돌아올 것이라고 예언했다(말 4:5-6).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Elijah was a descendant of Harim who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Elijah is mentioned in the Book of Ezra as one of the descendants of Harim who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.21). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, which was against God's command. Elijah was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra. The Bible does not provide any further details about this Elijah's life or family.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.21 only referred to as Elijah (אֵלִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '엘리야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리야는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 하림의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Elijah was a descendant of Elam who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Elijah is listed in the Book of Ezra as one of the descendants of Elam who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.26). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many Israelites had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, which was a violation of God's command. Elijah was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.26 only referred to as Elijah (אֵלִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '엘리야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리야는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 엘람의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A Harodite, one of David's mighty men.
persons.short: Elika the Harodite was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Elika the Harodite is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men, a group of elite warriors who fought alongside King David (2Sa.23.25). The mighty men were known for their exceptional bravery, strength, and military prowess. Elika is described as a Harodite, which likely refers to his place of origin or clan affiliation.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.25 only referred to as Elika (אֱלִיקָא).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.25에 처음 언급되며 '엘리가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하롯 사람 엘리가는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Naomi's husband from Bethlehem.
persons.short: Elimelech was Naomi's husband from Bethlehem who died in Moab.
persons.article: Elimelech was a man from Bethlehem in Judah, the husband of Naomi and the father of Mahlon and Chilion (Rut.1.2). During a time of famine, Elimelech and his family moved to the country of Moab (Rut.1.1-2). While in Moab, Elimelech died, leaving Naomi a widow (Rut.1.3). Naomi's sons, Mahlon and Chilion, married Moabite women named Ruth and Orpah, but they also died after about ten years (Rut.1.4-5). After the death of her husband and sons, Naomi decided to return to Bethlehem, and her daughter-in-law Ruth accompanied her (Rut.1.6-22). Elimelech's family had owned land in Bethlehem, which was later acquired by Boaz, a relative who married Ruth (Rut.4.3,9). Through this marriage, Elimelech's lineage was preserved, and his family's property remained within the clan.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.1.2 only referred to as Elimelech (אֱלִימֶ֫לֶךְ); son of Salma; husband of Naomi; father of Mahlon, Chilion.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Rut.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '엘리멜렉'이라 불림. 살마의 아들. 나오미의 남편. 말론과 기룐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리멜렉은 베들레헴 출신 나오미의 남편으로, 모압에서 죽었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Hodaviah@1Ch.3.24, Eliashib@1Ch.3.24, Pelaiah@1Ch.3.24, Akkub@1Ch.3.24, Johanan@1Ch.3.24, Delaiah@1Ch.3.24, Anani@1Ch.3.24
persons.brief: A descendant of David through Jeconiah.
persons.short: Elioenai was a descendant of David through Jeconiah, mentioned in the genealogy.
persons.article: Elioenai is mentioned in the genealogy of King David's descendants, particularly in the line of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), who was one of the last kings of Judah before the Babylonian exile (1Ch.3.23,24). Elioenai is listed as one of the sons of Neariah, who was a descendant of Shealtiel, the son of Jeconiah. This genealogy demonstrates the continuation of David's lineage after the exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.3.23 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי); son of Neariah; a brother of Hizkiah and Azrikam; father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '에료에내'라 불림. 느아랴의 아들. 히스기야와 아스리감의 형제. 호다위야, 엘리아십, 블라야, 악굽, 요하난, 들라야와 아나니의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 여고냐를 통한 다윗의 후손으로, 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.short: Elioenai was a Simeonite leader during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Elioenai is mentioned as one of the leaders of the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah (1Ch.4.36). He is listed among the Simeonites who expanded their territory by conquering the land of the Amalekites. This event likely took place during Hezekiah's religious reforms and military campaigns against the enemies of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.36 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.36에 처음 언급되며 '엘료에내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Joash@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Becher.
persons.short: Elioenai was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Becher.
persons.article: Elioenai is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Becher (1Ch.7.8). Becher was a son of Benjamin, making Elioenai a grandson of the patriarch Benjamin. This genealogy records the heads of families and clans within the tribe of Benjamin. Apart from being mentioned as a son of Becher, no additional information is provided about Elioenai's life or role in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '엘료에내'라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 요아스, 엘리에셀, 오므리, 여레못, 아비야, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 베냐민 사람으로 베겔의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Elioenai was a priest who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Elioenai is mentioned in the Book of Ezra as one of the priests who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.22). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, which was against God's command. Elioenai was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elioenai's life or priestly duties.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.22 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '엘료에내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Elioenai was an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Elioenai is listed in the Book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.27). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many Israelites had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, which was a violation of God's command. Elioenai was among those who had taken foreign wives, but he agreed to put away his wife as part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.27 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '엘료에내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Elioenai was a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Elioenai is mentioned as one of the priests who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.12.41). After the completion of the wall's reconstruction, Nehemiah organized a grand dedication ceremony that involved two large choirs processing on top of the wall. Elioenai was part of the group of priests who blew trumpets during this celebration. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elioenai's life or priestly responsibilities.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.41 only referred to as Elioenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.41에 처음 언급되며 '엘료에내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘여에내는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men, son of Ur.
persons.short: Eliphal, son of Ur, was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Eliphal, the son of Ur, is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men (1Ch.11.35). The mighty men were a group of elite warriors who fought alongside King David and were known for their exceptional bravery, strength, and military prowess. Eliphal is listed among these distinguished warriors, indicating that he played a significant role in David's military campaigns and battles. However, no further details about Eliphal's specific exploits or life are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.35 only referred to as Eliphal (אֱלִיפָל); a son of Ur.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.35에 처음 언급되며 '엘리발'이라 불림. 울의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 울의 아들 엘리발은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Teman@Gen.36.11-Job, Omar@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Zepho@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Amalek@Gen.36.12-, Korah@Gen.36.16
persons.brief: The firstborn son of Esau.
persons.short: Eliphaz was the firstborn son of Esau and the father of several Edomite clans.
persons.article: Eliphaz was the firstborn son of Esau, born to his wife Adah (Gen.36.4). He became the father of several sons, including Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, and Amalek (through his concubine Timna) (Gen.36.11-12). These sons grew into clans within the Edomite nation, with Eliphaz's descendants being listed among the chiefs of Edom (Gen.36.15-16). Eliphaz's lineage is also recorded in the genealogy of Esau in 1Ch.1.35-36. As the firstborn of Esau, Eliphaz played a significant role in the establishment and growth of the Edomite people, who were the descendants of Esau. The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliphaz's life or personal characteristics.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.4 only referred to as Eliphaz (אֱלִיפַז); a son of Esau and Adah; half-brother of: Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah; husband of Timna; father of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Amalek and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘리바스'라 불림. 에서와 아다의 아들. 르우엘, 여우스, 얄람과 고라의 형제. 딤나와 엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편. 데만, 오말, 스보, 가담, 그나스, 아말렉과 고라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리바스는 에서의 맏아들이며 여러 에돔 족속의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A Temanite, one of Job's three friends.
persons.short: Eliphaz the Temanite was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him during his affliction.
persons.article: Eliphaz the Temanite was one of the three friends who visited Job during his time of suffering (Job.2.11). He is described as coming from Teman, an area known for its wisdom (Jer.49.7). Eliphaz, along with Bildad and Zophar, engaged in a series of dialogues with Job, attempting to explain the reasons behind Job's afflictions (Job.4-25). In his speeches, Eliphaz emphasizes the justice and sovereignty of God, suggesting that Job's suffering is a result of sin and urging him to repent (Job.4.1; 15.1; 22.1). However, at the end of the book, God rebukes Eliphaz and his two friends for not speaking what is right about Him, unlike Job (Job.42.7). God instructs them to offer sacrifices and have Job pray for them to be forgiven (Job.42.9). The Bible does not provide any further information about Eliphaz's life outside of his interactions with Job.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Job.2.11 only referred to as Eliphaz (אֱלִיפַז).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Job.2.11에 처음 언급되며 '엘리바스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 데만 사람 엘리바스는 욥의 고난 중 그를 위로하러 온 세 친구 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite musician during David's reign.
persons.short: Eliphelehu was a Levite musician who played the harp during the transfer of the ark to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Eliphelehu is mentioned as one of the Levite musicians who participated in the procession when King David brought the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem (1Ch.15.18,21). He was appointed, along with other skilled musicians, to play the harp during the celebration. The Levites were responsible for the musical aspects of worship in ancient Israel, and Eliphelehu's inclusion in this important event highlights his musical abilities and his role in the Levitical service. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Eliphelehu's life or other responsibilities as a Levite.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Eliphelehu (אֱלִיפְלֵ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '엘리블레후'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 음악가 엘리블레후는 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮길 때 수금을 연주했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.short: Eliphelet was a descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Eliphelet is mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul's descendants from the tribe of Benjamin (1Ch.8.39). He is listed as one of the sons of Eshek, who was a descendant of Saul's son Jonathan. This genealogy demonstrates the continuation of Saul's lineage after his death and the establishment of David's kingdom. The Bible does not provide any further information about Eliphelet's life, role, or significance within the tribe of Benjamin or the kingdom of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.39 only referred to as Eliphelet (אֲלִיפֶ֫לֶט); son of Eleasah; a brother of Ulam and Jeush.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.39에 처음 언급되며 '엘리벨렛'이라 불림. 엘르아사의 아들. 울람과 여우스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리벨렛은 베냐민 지파 사울 왕의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, one of David's mighty men.
persons.short: Eliphelet, son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Eliphelet, the son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men (2Sa.23.34). The mighty men were a group of elite warriors who fought alongside King David and were known for their exceptional bravery, strength, and military prowess. Eliphelet's inclusion in this list indicates that he was a skilled warrior who played a significant role in David's military campaigns. His father, Ahasbai, is described as a Maacathite, suggesting that Eliphelet may have had ties to the region of Maacah, located near the border of Israel and Syria.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.34 only referred to as Eliphelet (אֲלִיפֶ֫לֶט); a son of Ahasbai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.34에 처음 언급되며 '엘리벨렛'이라 불림. 아하스배의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마아가 사람 아하스배의 아들 엘리벨렛은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: A son of David born in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Eliphelet was a son of David born to him in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Eliphelet is mentioned in the lists of King David's children born to him in Jerusalem (2Sa.5.16; 1Ch.3.8; 14.7). He was born after David had established himself as king over Israel and had conquered the city of Jerusalem. Eliphelet is consistently named among David's sons in these passages, confirming his place in the royal family. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Eliphelet's life, role, or significance in the kingdom of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.5.16 only referred to as Eliphelet (אֱלִיפָֽלֶט); son of David; a brother of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.5.16에 처음 언급되며 '엘리벨렛'이라 불림. 다윗과 예루살렘의 아내들의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리벨렛은 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile.
persons.short: Eliphelet was an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Eliphelet is listed among the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.33). After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra the priest discovered that many of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples, which was against God's command. Eliphelet was one of those who had taken a foreign wife. As part of the covenant renewal led by Ezra, Eliphelet and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives to demonstrate their commitment to following God's law. The Bible does not provide any further information about Eliphelet's life, family, or role in the community of the returned exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.33 only referred to as Eliphelet (אֲלִיפֶ֫לֶט).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.33에 처음 언급되며 '엘리벨렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리벨렛은 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the descendants of Adonikam who returned from Babylon.
persons.short: Eliphelet was one of the descendants of Adonikam who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Eliphelet is mentioned in the list of the descendants of Adonikam who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.8.13). He was part of the group that accompanied Ezra, the priest and scribe, on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem. This return was part of the larger Jewish restoration to their homeland following the decree of King Cyrus of Persia. The Bible does not provide any additional details about Eliphelet's life, family, or role in the community of the returned exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.13 only referred to as Eliphelet (אֲלִיפֶ֫לֶט).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.13에 처음 언급되며 '엘리벨렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘리벨렛은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 아도니감의 후손 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet who succeeded Elijah.
persons.short: Elisha was a prophet who performed many miracles and served as a spiritual leader in Israel after Elijah.
persons.article: Elisha was a prophet in Israel who succeeded Elijah (1Ki.19.16). He was the son of Shaphat and was from Abel-meholah (1Ki.19.16,19). Elisha became Elijah's servant and disciple after Elijah threw his cloak around him while he was plowing (1Ki.19.19). When Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elisha took up his cloak and received a double portion of his spirit (2Ki.2.9-13). Elisha performed many miracles, including parting the Jordan River (2Ki.2.14, purifying water )(2Ki.2.19-22, multiplying a widow's oil )(2Ki.4.1-7, raising a Shunammite woman's son from the dead )(2Ki.4.8-37, and healing Naaman's leprosy )(2Ki.5). He also prophesied and gave counsel to kings, such as Jehoshaphat and Joram (2Ki.3). Elisha's ministry spanned the reigns of several kings of Israel, including Joram, Jehu, Jehoahaz, and Joash (2Ki.2-13). He died during the reign of King Joash (2Ki.13.14-20). Jesus mentioned Elisha as an example of a prophet who was sent to heal a foreigner, Naaman the Syrian (Luk.4.27).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.19.16 referred to as Elisha (אֱלִישָׁע), or Elisha (Ἐλισσαῖος); a son of Shaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 1Ki.19.16에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사'라 불림. 사밧의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사는 엘리야를 이어 이스라엘에서 여러 기적을 행하며 영적 지도자로 섬긴 선지자였다.
persons.article_ko: 엘리사는 엘리야를 이은 이스라엘의 선지자였다(왕상 19:16). 그는 사밧의 아들이며 아벨므홀라 출신이었다(왕상 19:16, 19). 엘리사는 밭을 갈고 있을 때 엘리야가 자기 겉옷을 그에게 두른 후 엘리야의 종이며 제자가 되었다(왕상 19:19). 엘리야가 회오리바람을 타고 하늘로 올라갈 때 엘리사는 그의 겉옷을 취하여 그의 영을 갑절이나 받았다(왕하 2:9-13). 엘리사는 요단강을 가르는 것(왕하 2:14), 물을 정결하게 하는 것(왕하 2:19-22), 과부의 기름을 늘리는 것(왕하 4:1-7), 수넴 여인의 아들을 죽음에서 살리는 것(왕하 4:8-37), 나아만의 나병을 고치는 것(왕하 5장)을 포함한 많은 기적을 행했다. 그는 또한 여호사밧과 요람 같은 왕들에게 예언하고 조언했다(왕하 3장). 엘리사의 사역은 요람, 예후, 여호아하스, 요아스를 포함한 이스라엘의 여러 왕의 통치 기간에 걸쳐 있었다(왕하 2-13장). 그는 요아스 왕 통치 기간에 죽었다(왕하 13:14-20). 예수님은 엘리사를 이방인 시리아 사람 나아만을 고치도록 보내진 선지자의 본보기로 언급하셨다(눅 4:27).

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A son of Javan, who is grandson of Noah.
persons.short: Elishah was a son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah.
persons.article: Elishah is mentioned in the genealogy of the nations descended from Noah (Gen.10.4; 1Ch.1.7). He was a son of Javan, who was a son of Japheth, one of Noah's three sons. Elishah and his brothers, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim (or Rodanim), are associated with the coastal regions and islands of the Mediterranean Sea (Gen.10.5). The descendants of Javan are believed to have settled in various parts of Greece and the Aegean Sea. The name Elishah may be associated with Alashiya, an ancient name for Cyprus, or with the region of Elis in Greece. However, the exact location and extent of the territory associated with Elishah are not specified in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man of the Greeks living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.4 only referred to as Elishah (אֱלִישָׁה); son of Javan; a brother of Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.4에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사'라 불림. 야완의 아들. 달시스, 깃딤과 도다님의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사는 야완의 아들이며 노아의 증손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Jerahmeel from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Elishama was a descendant of Jerahmeel from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Elishama is mentioned in the genealogy of Jerahmeel, a clan from the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.41). He was the son of Jekamiah and is listed among the descendants of Judah. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of Judah, focusing on the clans of Jerahmeel, Hezron, and others. Apart from being mentioned in this genealogical record, no further information is provided about Elishama's life or role within the clan of Jerahmeel or the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.41 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע); a son of Jekamiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.41에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림. 여가먀의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사마는 유다 지파 여라므엘의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law.
persons.short: Elishama was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Elishama is mentioned as one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Law in the cities of Judah (2Ch.17.8). During Jehoshaphat's reign, he initiated a program to instruct the people in the Law of the Lord. He sent officials, Levites, and priests throughout the cities of Judah to teach the people from the Book of the Law. Elishama was one of the Levites chosen for this task, indicating his knowledge and understanding of the Law. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Elishama's background, life, or other responsibilities as a Levite.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 엘리사마는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법을 가르치도록 보낸 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Ishmael, who assassinated Gedaliah.
persons.short: Elishama was the grandfather of Ishmael, who assassinated Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians.
persons.article: Elishama is mentioned as the grandfather of Ishmael, a member of the royal family who assassinated Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem (2Ki.25.25; Jer.41.1). Ishmael was the son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama. The Bible describes Elishama as being "of the royal family," indicating his connection to the Davidic line. Apart from this familial connection, no further details are provided about Elishama's life or role. His grandson Ishmael's actions led to political instability and the flight of many Judeans to Egypt, fearing Babylonian retaliation (2Ki.25.26; Jer.41.16-18).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.25 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע); father of Nethaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.25.25에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림. 느다니야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사마는 바벨론 사람들이 임명한 총독 그달랴를 암살한 이스마엘의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: A son of King David born in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Elishama was a son of King David born to him in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Elishama was one of the sons of King David born to him in Jerusalem (2Sa.5.16; 1Ch.3.8; 14.7). He was born after David had established himself as king over Israel and had conquered the city of Jerusalem. Elishama is consistently listed among David's sons born in Jerusalem, confirming his place in the royal family. However, the Bible does not provide any additional information about Elishama's life, role, or significance in the kingdom of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.5.16 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע); son of David; a brother of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.5.16에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림. 다윗과 예루살렘의 아내들의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사마는 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗 왕의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A secretary during Jehoiakim's reign.
persons.short: Elishama the secretary was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign in Judah.
persons.article: Elishama the secretary was an official during the reign of King Jehoiakim in Judah (Jer.36.12,20,21). He is mentioned in the context of Jeremiah's prophecies being read before the officials of Judah. When Micaiah reported the words of Jeremiah's scroll to the officials in the secretary's chamber, Elishama was present (Jer.36.12). Later, when King Jehoiakim demanded to hear the words of the scroll, Jehudi brought the scroll from Elishama's chamber and read it before the king (Jer.36.20,21). Elishama's role as a secretary suggests that he was responsible for record-keeping and administrative duties in the royal court. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elishama's life or his reaction to Jeremiah's prophecies.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.36.12 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.12에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 서기관 엘리사마는 유다 왕 여호야김 시대의 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Ephraim.
persons.short: Elishama was a leader from the tribe of Ephraim during the wilderness journey.
persons.article: Elishama was a leader from the tribe of Ephraim during the Israelites' wilderness journey after the Exodus from Egypt. He was the son of Ammihud (Num.1.10 and grandfather of Joshua )(1Ch.7.26). Elishama was appointed as the leader of the Ephraimites and was responsible for organizing and leading the tribe in the census, encampment, and offerings (Num.1.10; 2.18; 7.48,53; 10.22). As a tribal leader, he played a significant role in the administrative and military organization of the Israelites during their time in the wilderness. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elishama's life or leadership.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.10 only referred to as Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע); a son of Ammihud; father of Nun.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사마'라 불림. 암미훗의 아들. 눈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사마는 광야 시절 에브라임 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of the captains who helped Jehoiada overthrow Athaliah.
persons.short: Elishaphat was one of the captains who helped Jehoiada the priest overthrow Queen Athaliah.
persons.article: Elishaphat is mentioned as one of the captains who assisted Jehoiada the priest in overthrowing Queen Athaliah and installing Joash as the rightful king of Judah (2Ch.23.1). After the death of King Ahaziah, Athaliah seized power and ruled over Judah for six years. In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest organized a coup to remove Athaliah and restore the Davidic line to the throne. Elishaphat, along with other captains and Levites, gathered the people and supported Jehoiada in his plan. They crowned Joash as king and executed Athaliah, effectively ending her reign. The Bible does not provide any additional information about Elishaphat's background, life, or role beyond his involvement in this significant event in Judah's history.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.23.1 only referred to as Elishaphat (אֱלִישָׁפָט); a son of Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.23.1에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사밧'이라 불림. 시그리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사밧은 제사장 여호야다를 도와 아달랴 여왕을 폐한 지휘관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Aaron's wife and Nahshon's daughter.
persons.short: Elisheba was the wife of Aaron and the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon.
persons.article: Elisheba is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites as the wife of Aaron, the first High Priest of Israel (Exo.6.23). She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon, who was the leader of the tribe of Judah during the Exodus (Num.1.7). Elisheba married Aaron and bore him four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Her sons served as priests alongside their father, Aaron. Elisheba's marriage to Aaron highlights the connection between the priestly Levites and the royal tribe of Judah. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elisheba's life or her role as the wife of the High Priest.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Exo.6.23 only referred to as Elisheba (אֱלִישֶׁ֫בַע); daughter of Amminadab; a sister of Nahshon; wife of Aaron; mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Exo.6.23에 처음 언급되며 '엘리세바'라 불림. 암미나답의 딸. 나손의 자매. 아론의 아내. 나답, 아비후, 엘르아살과 이다말의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 엘리세바는 아론의 아내이며 암미나답의 딸이자 나손의 자매였다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
