persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zabad, in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.short: Ephlal was the son of Zabad, who was a descendant of Judah through Jerahmeel.
persons.article: Ephlal is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah as the son of Zabad (1Ch.2.37). The genealogy traces the descendants of Judah through his son Jerahmeel, and Ephlal is listed as part of this lineage. Zabad, Ephlal's father, is identified as the son of Nathan, who was a descendant of Sheshan (1Ch.2.36). No further information is provided about Ephlal's life, his role within the family, or any descendants he may have had. The repetition of Ephlal's name in the same verse (1Ch.2.37 is likely for emphasis or clarity in the genealogical record). The inclusion of Ephlal in the genealogy serves to provide a comprehensive account of Judah's descendants and to showcase the continuity of the family line through multiple generations. The mention of Ephlal and his father Zabad demonstrates the importance of documenting even the lesser-known individuals within the genealogies, as they contribute to the overall understanding of the family structure and the relationships between members of the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.37 only referred to as Ephlal (אֶפְלָל); a son of Zabad; father of Obed.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.37에 처음 언급되며 '에블랄'이라 불림. 사밧의 아들. 오벳의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에블랄은 여라므엘을 통한 유다의 후손인 사밧의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.short: Ephod son of Hanniel was appointed as the leader from the tribe of Manasseh to assist in dividing the land of Canaan.
persons.article: Ephod, the son of Hanniel, is mentioned in the book of Numbers as the appointed leader from the tribe of Manasseh who assisted in dividing the land of Canaan among the Israelite tribes (Num.34.23). After the Israelites had conquered the land of Canaan under the leadership of Joshua, representatives from each tribe were chosen to help allocate the land according to the instructions given by God. Ephod was selected as the representative for the tribe of Manasseh, highlighting his leadership skills and the trust placed in him by his tribe. The division of the land was a crucial task, ensuring that each tribe received its allotted portion and that the distribution was fair and equitable. Ephod's role in this process demonstrates his importance and the responsibility he held within his tribe. No further details are provided about Ephod's life, his family, or his other contributions to the tribe of Manasseh. His mention in this context serves to highlight the organization and cooperation among the tribes during the allocation of the Promised Land and to recognize the significant individuals who played a role in this important event in Israel's history.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.23 only referred to as Ephod (אֵפֹד); father of Hanniel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.23에 처음 언급되며 '에봇'이라 불림. 한니엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 한니엘의 아들 에봇은 가나안 땅 분배를 돕도록 임명된 므낫세 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Shuthelah@Num.26.35-1Ch, Becher@Num.26.35, Tahan@Num.26.35, Ezer@1Ch.7.21, Elead@1Ch.7.21, Beriah@1Ch.7.23
persons.brief: Second son of Joseph, and a tribe of Israel.
persons.short: Ephraim was the second son of Joseph, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel, often playing a prominent role in the nation's history.
persons.article: Ephraim was the second son of Joseph, born to him in Egypt by his wife Asenath (Gen.41.52). He and his older brother Manasseh were adopted by Israel (or 'Jacob') and blessed, with Ephraim receiving the greater blessing (Gen.48). Ephraim's descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and they were often grouped with the tribe of Manasseh under the collective name "Joseph" (Num.1.32,33; 26.28,35,37). The tribe of Ephraim settled in the central region of Canaan (Jos.16.4,5,8,9,10 and played a significant role throughout Israel's history). They were known for their military prowess (Jdg.5.14; Psa.78.9 and produced several notable leaders, including Joshua )(Num.13.8, Abdon )(Jdg.12.15, and Samuel )(1Sa.1.1). However, they also exhibited pride and a rebellious spirit at times (Jdg.8.1,2; 12.1; 2Sa.20.21). Ephraim, along with the other northern tribes, separated from Judah after Solomon's reign and formed the northern kingdom of Israel (1Ki.12.25). The prophets often addressed Ephraim, warning them of judgment for their idolatry and unfaithfulness (Isa.7.2,5,8,9; Jer.31.18,20; Hos.4.17; 5). However, there were also promises of restoration and blessing (Jer.31.6,9; Ezk.37.16,19). In the New Testament, Ephraim is mentioned in the context of Jesus withdrawing to a village called Ephraim before his final entry into Jerusalem (Jdg.12.6; 1Ch.12.30; 27.20; 2Ch.25.7; Psa.78.9; 2Ch.13.19; 1Ki.11.26; 1Sa.1.1).
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Ephraim, living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.41.52 referred to as Ephraim or Ephraimite (אֶפְרַ֫יִם), or Ephron (עֶפְרוֹן), or Ephraimite or Ephrathite (אֶפְרָתִי); son of Joseph and Asenath; a brother of Manasseh; father of Shuthelah, Becher, Tahan, Ezer, Elead and Beriah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 요셉의 아들. Gen.41.52에 처음 언급되며 '에브라임'이라 불림. 요셉과 아스낫의 아들. 므낫세의 형제. 수델라, 베겔, 다한, 에셀, 엘르앗과 브리아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에브라임은 요셉의 둘째 아들로, 그 후손이 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나를 이루었고 이스라엘 역사에서 자주 중요한 역할을 했다.
persons.article_ko: 에브라임은 요셉의 둘째 아들로, 애굽에서 아내 아스낫에게서 태어났다(창 41:52). 그와 형 므낫세는 이스라엘(야곱)에게 입양되어 축복을 받았는데, 에브라임이 더 큰 축복을 받았다(창 48장). 에브라임의 후손은 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나를 이루었으며, 종종 므낫세 지파와 함께 '요셉'이라는 집합적 이름으로 묶였다(민 1:32-33; 26:28, 35, 37). 에브라임 지파는 가나안 중부 지역에 정착했고(수 16:4-5, 8-10) 이스라엘 역사 전체에서 중요한 역할을 했다. 그들은 군사적 용맹으로 알려졌으며(삿 5:14; 시 78:9) 여호수아(민 13:8), 압돈(삿 12:15), 사무엘(삼상 1:1) 등 여러 저명한 지도자를 배출했다. 그러나 때로 교만과 반역적인 태도를 보이기도 했다(삿 8:1-2; 12:1; 삼하 20:21). 에브라임은 다른 북부 지파들과 함께 솔로몬 통치 후 유다에서 분리되어 북이스라엘 왕국을 형성했다(왕상 12:25). 선지자들은 종종 에브라임에게 우상숭배와 신실치 못함에 대한 심판을 경고했다(사 7:2, 5, 8-9; 렘 31:18, 20; 호 4:17; 5장). 그러나 회복과 축복의 약속도 있었다(렘 31:6, 9; 겔 37:16, 19). 신약에서 에브라임은 예수님이 예루살렘에 마지막으로 들어가시기 전 물러가신 에브라임이라는 마을과 관련하여 언급된다(요 11:54).

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A wife of Caleb and founder of Bethlehem.
persons.short: Ephrathah (through her son Hur or grandon Salma) was the founder of Bethlehem.
persons.article: Ephrathah was first the wife of Hezron then of Caleb. Her descendents gave her name to the area around Bethlehem, the city in Judah where David and Jesus were born. In several passages, Bethlehem is referred to as "Bethlehem Ephrathah" (Rut.1.2; 1Sa.17.12), indicating that Ephrathah was either an alternate name for the city or a region encompassing it. The name Ephrathah is also mentioned in the genealogies of Judah in connection with Caleb, a prominent figure in the tribe. Ephrathah is listed as the wife of Caleb (1Ch.2.19, and their descendants, including Hur and Salma, are associated with the founding or settlement of Bethlehem )(1Ch.2.50; 4.4). The dual usage of the name Ephrathah suggests a possible link between the person and the place, although the exact nature of this connection is not explicitly stated in the Bible. The association of Ephrathah with Bethlehem highlights the significance of this city in Israel's history, as it was the birthplace of key figures like David and Jesus.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.19 referred to as Ephrathah (אֶפְרָ֫תָה), or Ephrath (אֶפְרָת), or Ephrathite (אֶפְרָתִי); wife of Hezron and Hezron; mother of Hur and Ram; ; then married to Caleb and bore Ashhur.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Rut.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '에브랏'이라 불림. 헤스론과 갈렙의 아내. 훌과 람의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 에브랏(그 아들 훌 또는 손자 살마를 통해)은 베들레헴의 창설자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A Hittite who sold a burial site to Abraham.
persons.short: Ephron the Hittite sold the cave of Machpelah to Abraham as a burial site for Sarah.
persons.article: Ephron was a Hittite man who lived in the city of Hebron during the time of Abraham. He owned a field containing the cave of Machpelah, which Abraham sought to purchase as a burial place for his wife Sarah (Gen.23). When Sarah died, Abraham approached the Hittites and requested to buy a burial site. Ephron was present at the meeting and offered to give the field and the cave to Abraham as a gift (Gen.23.8-11). However, Abraham insisted on paying the full price, and Ephron named a price of 400 shekels of silver (Gen.23.14-15). Abraham agreed to the price and paid Ephron in the presence of witnesses, securing the field and the cave as a permanent possession for burial (Gen.23.16-20). The cave of Machpelah later became the burial place for Abraham himself, as well as Isaac, Rebekah, Israel (or 'Jacob'), and Leah (Gen.25.9; 49.29,30; 50.13). Ephron's interaction with Abraham demonstrates the legal and social customs of property transactions in the ancient Near East. It also highlights Abraham's desire to establish a permanent burial place for his family in the land of Canaan, foreshadowing the future possession of the land by his descendants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.23.8 only referred to as Ephron (עֶפְרוֹן); a son of Zohar.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '에브론'이라 불림. 소할의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 헷 사람 에브론은 사라의 매장지로 막벨라 굴을 아브라함에게 팔았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Judah's grandson, ancestor of linen workers.
persons.short: Er was Judah's grandson, ancestor of linen workers at Beth-ashbea.
persons.article: Er was the son of Shelah, son of Judah. Unlike his uncle with the same name, he had descendants, and these became the linen workers at Beth-ashbea.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.21 only referred to as Er (עֵר); son of Shelah; a brother of Laadah, Jokim, Joash and Saraph; father or founder of Lecah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '에르'라 불림. 셀라의 아들. 라아다, 요김, 요아스와 사랍의 형제. 레가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에르는 유다의 손자로, 벧아스베아 세마포 짜는 자들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Judah's firstborn son, killed by God for his wickedness.
persons.short: Er, Judah's firstborn son, was killed by God because of his wickedness.
persons.article: Er was the firstborn son of Judah and his Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shua (Gen. 38:3; 1Ch. 2:3). He married Tamar, but the Lord put him to death because of his wickedness (Gen. 38:6-7). The nature of his wickedness is not specified in the text. After Er's death, Judah instructed his second son, Onan, to marry Tamar and produce offspring for his deceased brother, a practice known as levirate marriage (Gen. 38:8). However, Onan also displeased the Lord and was put to death (Gen. 38:9-10). Er is mentioned again in the genealogy of Judah (Gen. 46:12; Num. 26:19; 1Ch. 2:3), which highlights the significance of his lineage despite his early death. His inclusion in these genealogies emphasizes the importance of Judah's descendants, particularly in light of the Messianic promise that would ultimately be fulfilled through this tribe (Gen. 49:10).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.38.3 only referred to as Er (עֵר); son of Judah and Bath-shua; a brother of Onan and Shelah; half-brother of: Perez and Zerah; husband of Tamar.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.38.3에 처음 언급되며 '엘'이라 불림. 유다와 딸의 아들. 오난, 셀라, 베레스와 세라의 형제. 다말의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 유다의 맏아들 에르는 그의 악함으로 인해 하나님께 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus
persons.short: Er is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus as the son of Joshua.
persons.article: Er is a name that appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luk.3.28. He is listed as the son of Joshua and an ancestor of Jesus. No further information is provided about Er in the biblical text. His inclusion in the genealogy highlights the importance of tracing Jesus' lineage and affirming his descent from the royal line of David.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.28 only referred to as Er (Ἤρ); a son of Joshua; father of Elmadam.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.28에 처음 언급되며 '에르'라 불림. 여호수아의 아들. 엘마담의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에르는 예수님의 족보에서 여호수아의 아들로 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Shuthelah, grandson of Ephraim; head of clan.
persons.short: Eran was a son of Shuthelah and grandson of Ephraim, who became the head of the Eranite clan.
persons.article: Eran was a son of Shuthelah and a grandson of Ephraim (Num.26.36). He was the head of the Eranite clan, which was named after him. The Eranites were counted among the descendants of Ephraim during the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.36).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.26.36 referred to as Eran (עֵרָן), or Eranite (עֵרָנִי); son of Shuthelah; a brother of Bered.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.36에 처음 언급되며 '에란'이라 불림. 수델라의 아들. 베렛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에란은 수델라의 아들이며 에브라임의 손자로, 에란 가문의 우두머리가 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Companion of Paul; served as city treasurer in Corinth.
persons.short: Erastus was a companion of Paul who served as the city treasurer in Corinth.
persons.article: Erastus was a companion of the apostle Paul, mentioned in several New Testament passages. He was sent by Paul, along with Timothy, from Ephesus to Macedonia (Act.19.22). In his letter to the Romans, Paul mentions that Erastus, the city treasurer, sends his greetings (Rom.16.23, indicating that he held an important position in Corinth). Later, in his second letter to Timothy, Paul writes that Erastus stayed in Corinth (2Ti.4.20). These references suggest that Erastus was a trusted associate of Paul and played a significant role in the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.19.22 only referred to as Erastus (Ἔραστος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.19.22에 처음 언급되며 '에라스도'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에라스도는 고린도의 재무관으로 섬긴 바울의 동역자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ziphion@Gen.46.16-Num, Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num, Shuni@Gen.46.16-Num, Ezbon@Gen.46.16-Num, Arod@Gen.46.16-Num, Areli@Gen.46.16-Num
persons.brief: Son of Gad; head of the Erite clan.
persons.short: Eri was a son of Gad and the head of the Erite clan.
persons.article: Eri was one of the sons of Gad, who was among the seventy members of Jacob's family that went down to Egypt (Gen.46.16). He became the head of the Erite clan, which was named after him. The Erites were counted among the descendants of Gad during the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.16).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.16 referred to as Eri (עֵרִי), or Erite (עֵרִי); son of Gad; a brother of Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Arod and Areli.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.16에 처음 언급되며 '에리'라 불림. 갓의 아들. 시뵨, 학기, 수니, 에스본, 아롯과 아렐리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에리는 갓의 아들로 에리 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Assyria; son and successor of Sennacherib.
persons.short: Esarhaddon was the king of Assyria, the son and successor of Sennacherib.
persons.article: Esarhaddon (681-669 BC) was the king of Assyria, the son and successor of Sennacherib. He is mentioned in the Bible as the king to whom Sennacherib's assassins escaped after killing their father (2Ki.19.37; Isa.37.38). Esarhaddon is also credited with resettling people in the cities of Samaria (Ezr.4.2, which suggests that he was involved in the deportation and relocation of conquered populations, a common practice among Assyrian kings). Historically, Esarhaddon is known for rebuilding Babylon, which his father had destroyed, and for his military campaigns, including the conquest of Egypt.
persons.summary: A king of Assyria living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.19.37 only referred to as Esarhaddon (אֵסַר־חַדּוֹן); son of Sennacherib; a brother of Adrammelech and Sharezer.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.19.37에 처음 언급되며 '에살핫돈'이라 불림. 산헤립의 아들. 아드람멜렉과 사레셀의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에살핫돈은 앗수르 왕으로, 산헤립의 아들이며 그 뒤를 이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Isaac's firstborn son; sold birthright to Jacob; became Edom.
persons.short: Esau, also called Edom, was Isaac's firstborn son who sold his birthright to his twin brother Jacob and became the father of the Edomites.
persons.article: Esau, also known as Edom, was the firstborn son of Isaac and Rebekah and the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.25.25-26). He was a skillful hunter and his father's favorite son (Gen.25.27-28). Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew when he was famished (Gen.25.29-34). He married two Hittite women, causing grief to his parents (Gen.26.34-35). Esau lost his father's blessing to Jacob through deception (Genesis 27). He held a grudge against Jacob but later reconciled with him (Genesis 32-33). Esau settled in the hill country of Seir, which became known as Edom (Gen.36.8-9). He had five sons and became the father of the Edomites (Gen.36.1-43). The Edomites were later considered enemies of Israel (Num.20.14-21; 1Sa.14.47; 2Sa.8.13-14). God's love for Jacob and His rejection of Esau is used as an example of His sovereignty (Mal.1.2-3; Rom.9.13).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.25 referred to as Esau (עֵשָׂו), or Esau (Ἠσαῦ), or Edom (אֱדוֹם), or Esau (עֵשָׂו), or Esau (Ἠσαῦ); son of Isaac and Rebekah; a brother of Israel; husband of Oholibamah, Judith, Adah and Mahalath; father of Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah; founded nation of Edom.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.25.25에 처음 언급되며 '에서'라 불림. 이삭과 리브가의 아들. 이스라엘의 형제. 오홀리바마, 유딧, 아다와 마할랏의 남편. 엘리바스, 르우엘, 여우스, 얄람과 고라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에서(에돔이라고도 함)는 이삭의 맏아들로, 쌍둥이 형제 야곱에게 장자권을 팔았고 에돔 족속의 조상이 되었다.
persons.article_ko: 에서(에돔이라고도 함)는 이삭과 리브가의 맏아들이며 이스라엘(야곱)의 쌍둥이 형제였다(창 25:25-26). 그는 능숙한 사냥꾼이었고 아버지가 가장 사랑하는 아들이었다(창 25:27-28). 에서는 굶주렸을 때 죽 한 그릇에 자기 장자권을 야곱에게 팔았다(창 25:29-34). 그는 두 헷 여인과 결혼하여 부모에게 근심을 안겨주었다(창 26:34-35). 에서는 속임수를 통해 야곱에게 아버지의 축복을 빼앗겼다(창세기 27장). 그는 야곱에게 원한을 품었으나 후에 그와 화해했다(창세기 32-33장). 에서는 세일의 산지에 정착했고, 그 지역은 에돔으로 알려지게 되었다(창 36:8-9). 그는 다섯 아들을 두었고 에돔 사람들의 조상이 되었다(창 36:1-43). 에돔 사람들은 후에 이스라엘의 원수로 여겨졌다(민 20:14-21; 삼상 14:47; 삼하 8:13-14). 야곱에 대한 하나님의 사랑과 에서에 대한 그분의 거절은 그분의 주권의 본보기로 사용된다(말 1:2-3; 롬 9:13).

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Dishon, a Horite chief in Seir.
persons.short: Eshban was a son of Dishon and a Horite chief who lived in the land of Seir.
persons.article: Eshban was a son of Dishon, a Horite chief who lived in the land of Seir (Gen.36.26; 1Ch.1.41). The Horites were the original inhabitants of Seir before the descendants of Esau dispossessed them (Deu.2.12).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.26 only referred to as Eshban (אֶשְׁבָּן); son of Dishon; a brother of Hemdan, Ithran and Cheran.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '에스반'이라 불림. 디손의 아들. 헴단, 이드란과 그란의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스반은 디손의 아들이며 세일 땅에 살던 호리 사람 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Amorite ally of Abram; valley named after him.
persons.short: Eshcol was an Amorite, an ally of Abram, and the valley of Eshcol was named after him.
persons.article: Eshcol was an Amorite and one of the three allies of Abram (later called Abraham) mentioned in Gen.14.13,24. He, along with Mamre and Aner, joined forces with Abram to rescue his nephew Lot, who had been taken captive by King Chedorlaomer and his allies (Gen.14.14-16). The valley of Eshcol, known for its abundant grape clusters, was named after him (Num.13.23-24). This valley was later part of the land allocated to the tribe of Judah (Num.13.23; 32.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.13 only referred to as Eshcol (אֶשְׁכֹּל); a brother of Mamre and Aner.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.14.13에 처음 언급되며 '에스골'이라 불림. 마므레의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 마므레와 아넬의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스골은 아모리 사람으로 아브람의 동맹자였으며, 에스골 골짜기가 그의 이름을 따서 지어졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mehir; father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah.
persons.short: Eshton was the son of Mehir and the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah.
persons.article: Eshton was a descendant of Judah through Chelub, mentioned in 1Ch.4.11-12. He was the son of Mehir and the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. Tehinnah was noted as the father of Ir-nahash.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.4.11 only referred to as Eshton (אֶשְׁתּוֹן); a son of Mehir; father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, Tehinnah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '에스돈'이라 불림. 므힐의 아들. 베드라바, 바세아와 드힌나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에스돈은 므힐의 아들이며 벧라바, 바세아, 드힌나의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
persons.short: Esli was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in His genealogy.
persons.article: Esli is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luk.3.25. He was the son of Naggai and the father of Nahum. Esli was part of the lineage traced from David to Jesus through Nathan, David's son.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.25 only referred to as Esli (Ἐσλί); a son of Naggai; father of Nahum.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '에슬리'라 불림. 낙개의 아들. 나훔의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에슬리는 예수 그리스도의 족보에 언급된 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Jewish queen of Persia; saved her people from genocide.
persons.short: Esther, also known as Hadassah, was a Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people from genocide.
persons.article: Esther, born Hadassah, was a Jewish woman who became the queen of Persia during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). She was an orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai (Est.2.7). Esther was chosen to be queen after Ahasuerus deposed Queen Vashti (Est.2.17). When Haman, a high-ranking official, plotted to exterminate the Jews, Esther risked her life by approaching the king uninvited to expose Haman's plot (Esther 4-5). As a result, Haman was hanged, and the Jews were given the right to defend themselves, leading to their deliverance (Esther 7-8). Esther and Mordecai instituted the Feast of Purim to commemorate this event (Est.9.29-32). Her story exemplifies courage, faith, and God's providence in protecting His people.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.2.7 referred to as Esther (אֶסְתֵּר), or Hadassah (הֲדַסָּה); a daughter of Abihail.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Est.2.7에 처음 언급되며 '에스더'라 불림. 아비하일의 딸.
persons.short_ko: 에스더(하닷사라고도 함)는 페르시아의 유대인 왕비로, 그녀의 백성을 대학살에서 구했다.
persons.article_ko: 하닷사라는 이름으로 태어난 에스더는 아하수에로 왕(크세르크세스 1세) 통치 기간에 페르시아의 왕비가 된 유대인 여성이었다. 그녀는 사촌 모르드개에게 길러진 고아였다(에 2:7). 에스더는 아하수에로가 와스디 왕비를 폐위시킨 후 왕비로 선택되었다(에 2:17). 고위 관리인 하만이 유대인들을 몰살하려는 음모를 꾸몄을 때 에스더는 초청받지 않은 채 왕에게 나아가 하만의 음모를 폭로함으로써 자기 목숨을 걸었다(에스더 4-5장). 그 결과 하만은 교수형을 당했고, 유대인들은 스스로를 방어할 권리를 받아 구원받았다(에스더 7-8장). 에스더와 모르드개는 이 사건을 기념하기 위해 부림절을 제정했다(에 9:29-32). 그녀의 이야기는 용기, 믿음, 그리고 자기 백성을 보호하시는 하나님의 섭리를 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zerah; grandson of Judah.
persons.short: Ethan was a son of Zerah and a grandson of Judah.
persons.article: Ethan was one of the five sons of Zerah, who was a son of Judah (1Ch.2.6). He was a grandson of Judah and is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah's descendants (1Ch.2.8).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.6 only referred to as Ethan (אֵיתָן); son of Zerah; a brother of Zabdi, Heman, Calcol and Dara; father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '에단'이라 불림. 세라의 아들. 삽디, 헤만, 갈골과 다라의 형제. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에단은 세라의 아들이며 유다의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wise man; Ezrahite; author of Psalm 89.
persons.short: Ethan the Ezrahite was a wise man and the author of Psalm 89.
persons.article: Ethan the Ezrahite was a wise man during the time of King Solomon. He was known for his wisdom, although not as wise as Solomon himself (1Ki.4.31). Ethan was also a skilled musician and is credited with authoring Psalm 89, a psalm that reflects on God's covenant with David and the challenges faced by the Davidic dynasty (Psalm 1Ki.89.1). The psalm demonstrates Ethan's deep understanding of God's faithfulness and sovereignty.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.4.31 only referred to as Ethan (אֵיתָן); son of Mahol; a brother of Heman, Calcol and Darda.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.31에 처음 언급되며 '에단'이라 불림. 마홀의 아들. 헤만, 갈골과 다르다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스라 사람 에단은 지혜로운 사람이며 시편 89편의 저자였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Sidon; father of Jezebel.
persons.short: Ethbaal was the king of Sidon and the father of Jezebel, who married King Ahab of Israel.
persons.article: Ethbaal was the king of Sidon, a Phoenician city-state. He was the father of Jezebel, who became the wife of King Ahab of Israel (1Ki.16.31). Ethbaal's reign is estimated to have been around 878-847 BC. By arranging the marriage of his daughter Jezebel to Ahab, Ethbaal likely sought to strengthen political and economic ties between Sidon and Israel. Jezebel's influence led to the promotion of Baal worship in Israel, which had significant consequences for the nation (1Ki.16.32-33).
persons.summary: A king of Sidon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.16.31 only referred to as Ethbaal (אֶתְבַּ֫עַל); father of Jezebel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.16.31에 처음 언급되며 '엣바일'이라 불림. 이세벨의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엣바알은 시돈의 왕이며 이스라엘 왕 아합과 결혼한 이세벨의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Hepher@1Ch.4.6, Temeni@1Ch.4.6, Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6, Zereth@1Ch.4.7, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Koz@1Ch.4.8
persons.brief: Son of Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.
persons.short: Ethnan was a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur'), the  father (ie founder) of Tekoa.
persons.article: Ethnan is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah (1Ch.4.7). He was one of the sons of Ashhur (or 'Ashur'), who was known as the father (ie founder) of Tekoa, a town in Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.7 only referred to as Ethnan (אֶתְנַן); son of Ashhur and Helah; a brother of Haahashtari, Zereth, Izhar and Koz; half-brother of: Ahuzzam, Hepher and Temeni.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.7에 처음 언급되며 '에드난'이라 불림. 아스훌과 헬라의 아들. 아훗삼, 헤벨, 데므니, 하아하스타리, 세렛, 이스할과 고스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에드난은 드고아의 창설자(아버지)인 아스훌(아술)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Greeted by Paul in his letter to Timothy.
persons.short: Eubulus was a Christian who sent greetings to Timothy through Paul's letter.
persons.article: Eubulus is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Paul's second letter to Timothy (2Ti.4.21). He is one of several individuals who sent greetings to Timothy through Paul. The mention of Eubulus alongside other believers suggests that he was a member of the Christian community known to both Paul and Timothy.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.4.21 only referred to as Eubulus (Εὔβουλος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '으불로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 유불로는 바울의 편지를 통해 디모데에게 문안한 그리스도인이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Mother of Timothy; a Jewish believer.
persons.short: Eunice was the mother of Timothy and a Jewish believer.
persons.article: Eunice was the mother of Timothy, a young Christian leader and companion of Paul (2Ti.1.5). She was a Jewish believer married to a Greek man (Act.16.1). Eunice, along with her mother Lois, had a sincere faith that greatly influenced Timothy's spiritual development (2Ti.1.5). Paul's mention of Eunice's faith suggests that she played a significant role in Timothy's early education in the Scriptures and his growth as a Christian (2Ti.3.15).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.1.5 only referred to as Eunice (Εὐνίκη); her mother was Lois; mother of Timothy.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. 2Ti.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '유니게'라 불림. 유니게의 아버지(이름 미상)와 로이스의 딸. 디모데의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아내. 디모데의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 유니게는 디모데의 어머니이며 유대인 신자였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian woman in Philippi; urged by Paul to reconcile.
persons.short: Euodia was a Christian woman in Philippi whom Paul urged to reconcile with Syntyche.
persons.article: Euodia was a Christian woman in the church at Philippi. In his letter to the Philippians, Paul specifically addresses Euodia and another woman named Syntyche, urging them to reconcile and be of the same mind in the Lord (Php.4.2). The fact that Paul mentions them by name and calls them his co-workers suggests that they were prominent members of the church who had labored alongside him in spreading the gospel (Php.4.3). The disagreement between Euodia and Syntyche was significant enough for Paul to address it directly, emphasizing the importance of unity and harmony within the church.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Php.4.2 only referred to as Euodia (Εὐοδία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Php.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '유오디아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 유오디아는 빌립보의 그리스도인 여성으로, 바울이 순두게와 화해하도록 권면했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Young man in Troas; fell from window; restored by Paul.
persons.short: Eutychus was a young man in Troas who fell from a window and was restored to life by Paul.
persons.article: Eutychus was a young man who attended a gathering in Troas where Paul was preaching (Act.20.9). As Paul prolonged his message late into the night, Eutychus, who was sitting in a window, fell asleep and fell from the third story. He was picked up dead, but Paul went down, embraced him, and declared that he was alive (Act.20.10). This miraculous restoration of Eutychus's life demonstrated God's power working through Paul. The incident also highlights the length and depth of Paul's teachings, which could extend late into the night.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.20.9 only referred to as Eutychus (Εὔτυχος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.20.9에 처음 언급되며 '유두고'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 유두고는 드로아의 청년으로, 창문에서 떨어졌으나 바울에 의해 다시 살아났다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: First woman; wife of Adam; tempted by the serpent.
persons.short: Eve was the first woman, created as Adam's wife, who was tempted by the serpent and ate the forbidden fruit.
persons.article: Eve was the first woman, created by God as a companion for Adam (Gen.2.22). She was formed from one of Adam's ribs and was named "Eve" because she would become the mother of all living (Gen.3.20). Eve was tempted by the serpent to eat the fruit from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which God had forbidden (Gen.3.1-6). She ate the fruit and gave some to Adam, resulting in their disobedience and the introduction of sin into the world (Gen.3.6-7). As a consequence, Eve experienced pain in childbirth and a desire for her husband, while Adam had to labor to provide for them (Gen.3.16-19). Despite this, Eve is recognized as the mother of the human race (Gen.4.1). Paul references Eve's deception as a warning against false teachers (2Co.11.3 and notes that Adam was created first, then Eve )(1Ti.2.13).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.3.20 referred to as Eve (חַוָּה), or Eve (Εὖα); wife of Adam; mother of Cain, Abel and Seth.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 여성. Gen.3.20에 처음 언급되며 '하와'라 불림. 아담의 자매. 아담의 아내. 가인, 아벨과 셋의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 하와는 최초의 여자로 아담의 아내로 창조되었으나, 뱀의 유혹을 받아 금지된 열매를 먹었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Midianite king killed in battle against Israel.
persons.short: Evi was one of the Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.
persons.article: Evi was one of the five kings of Midian who were defeated and killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses (Num.31.8). These kings were allies of the Moabites and had played a role in leading the Israelites into idolatry and sexual immorality (Num.25.1-9). As a result, God commanded Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites (Num.31.1-2). Evi and the other Midianite kings were slain in battle, along with Balaam the son of Beor (Num.31.8). The Midianite kings, including Evi, are also mentioned as having been defeated by the Israelites in Jos.13.21, where they are described as "princes of Sihon" and "rulers in the land."
persons.summary: A king living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.31.8 only referred to as Evi (אֱוִי).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.31.8에 처음 언급되며 '에위'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에위는 모세 시대에 이스라엘 사람들에게 죽임을 당한 미디안 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Babylon; released Jehoiachin from prison.
persons.short: Evil-merodach was a king of Babylon who released Jehoiachin, the former king of Judah, from prison.
persons.article: Evil-merodach was a king of Babylon who reigned from 562 to 560 BC. He was the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar II, the Babylonian king who had conquered Judah and destroyed Jerusalem. In the 37th year of the exile of Jehoiachin, the former king of Judah, Evil-merodach showed him kindness by releasing him from prison (2Ki.25.27; Jer.52.31). He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon (2Ki.25.28; Jer.52.32). Evil-merodach also provided Jehoiachin with regular food allowances for the rest of his life (2Ki.25.29-30; Jer.52.33-34). This act of mercy toward the exiled king of Judah is the only event recorded in the Bible about Evil-merodach's reign.
persons.summary: A king in Babylon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.27 only referred to as Evil-merodach (אֱוִיל מְרֹדַךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.25.27에 처음 언급되며 '에윌므로닥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에윌므로닥은 바벨론 왕으로, 유다의 전왕 여호야긴을 감옥에서 풀어주었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Naarai, one of David's mighty men.
persons.short: Ezbai was the father of Naarai, who was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Ezbai is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 1Ch.11.37. He was the father of Naarai, who was one of King David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of elite warriors who played a significant role in David's military campaigns and in establishing his kingdom (2Sa.23.8-39; 1Ch.11.10-47). Naarai, son of Ezbai, is listed among these mighty men, indicating that he was a skilled and valiant warrior.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.37 only referred to as Ezbai (אֶזְבָּ֑י); father of Naarai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.37에 처음 언급되며 '에스배'라 불림. 나아래의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에스배는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 나아래의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ard@Num.26.40, Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Uzzi@1Ch.7.7, Uzziel@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abihud@1Ch.8.3, Abishua@1Ch.8.4, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
persons.short: Ezbon was a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin.
persons.article: Ezbon is mentioned in 1Ch.7.7 as one of the sons of Bela, who was a son of Benjamin. Benjamin was one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') and the founder of the Israelite tribe of Benjamin. Ezbon was part of the second generation of Benjamites born in Egypt. He is listed along with his brothers Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri as the heads of their ancestral houses and mighty warriors (1Ch.7.7). The descendants of Bela, including Ezbon, are described as valiant men who were skilled with the bow (1Ch.8.40).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.7 only referred to as Ezbon (אֶצְבּוֹן); son of Bela; a brother of Ard, Naaman, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.7에 처음 언급되며 '에스본'이라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 아릇, 나아만, 웃시, 웃시엘, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비훗, 아비수아와 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스본은 벨라의 아들이며 베냐민의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ziphion@Gen.46.16-Num, Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num, Shuni@Gen.46.16-Num, Eri@Gen.46.16-Num, Arod@Gen.46.16-Num, Areli@Gen.46.16-Num
persons.brief: Son of Gad; head of the Oznite clan.
persons.short: Ezbon, also known as Ozni, was a son of Gad and the head of the Oznite clan.
persons.article: Ezbon, also referred to as Ozni, was one of the sons of Gad, the founder of the Israelite tribe of Gad (Gen.46.16; Num.26.16). He was born to Gad during the time the Israelites lived in Egypt. Ezbon became the head of the Oznite clan, one of the clans within the tribe of Gad (Num.26.16). The Oznites were named after him and were counted among the descendants of Gad in the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.15-18).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.16 referred to as Ezbon (אֶצְבּוֹן), or Ozni (אׇזְנִי), or Oznite (אׇזְנִי); son of Gad; a brother of Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Eri, Arod and Areli.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.16에 처음 언급되며 '에스본'이라 불림. 갓의 아들. 시뵨, 학기, 수니, 에리, 아롯과 아렐리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스본(오스니라고도 함)은 갓의 아들이며 오스니 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prophet during Babylonian exile; author of the Book of Ezekiel.
persons.short: Ezekiel was a prophet during the Babylonian exile who authored the Book of Ezekiel and served as a sign to the people of Israel.
persons.article: Ezekiel was a priest and prophet who lived during the time of the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Buzi and was among the captives taken to Babylon by King Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC (Ezk.1.3). Ezekiel received visions and messages from God while in exile, which he recorded in the Book of Ezekiel. His prophecies included warnings of judgment against Israel and the surrounding nations, as well as messages of hope and restoration for God's people. Ezekiel's life and actions often served as symbolic signs to the people of Israel, such as his unusual behavior during his wife's death, which was meant to illustrate the coming destruction of Jerusalem (Ezk.24.24). His ministry spanned approximately 22 years, from the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's captivity until at least the 27th year (Ezk.1.2; 29.17).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezk.1.3 only referred to as Ezekiel (יְחֶזְקֵאל); a son of Buzi.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Ezk.1.3에 처음 언급되며 '에스겔'이라 불림. 부시의 아들. 에스겔의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 에스겔은 바벨론 포로 시대의 선지자로, 에스겔서를 저술했으며 이스라엘 백성에게 표징이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite warrior; joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Ezer was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.
persons.article: Ezer is mentioned in 1Ch.12.9 as one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. The Gadites were known for their bravery and skill in battle, and they were among the first to support David during his time of exile (1Ch.12.8). Ezer and his fellow Gadites were described as "mighty and experienced warriors" who were "expert with shield and spear" (1Ch.12.8). They played a significant role in helping David establish his kingdom and were known for their loyalty and valor.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.9 only referred to as Ezer (עֵ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.9에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갓 지파 용사 에셀은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch, Shobal@1Ch.2.50-, Salma@1Ch.2.51-, Hareph@1Ch.2.51, Jezreel@1Ch.4.3, Ishma@1Ch.4.3, Idbash@1Ch.4.3, Hazzelelponi@1Ch.4.3, Penuel@1Ch.4.4
persons.brief: Father or founder of Hushah, of Ephrathah.
persons.short: Ezer was the father or founder of Hushah and a son of Hur of Ephrathah.
persons.article: Ezer is mentioned in 1Ch.4.4 as a son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah. Ephrathah was the wife of Caleb, son of Hezron (1Ch.2.19, 50). Ezer is identified as the father of Hushah, which could refer to either an individual or a place associated with him.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.4 only referred to as Ezer (עֵ֫זֶר); son of Hur; a brother of Uri, Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Jezreel, Ishma, Idbash, Hazzelelponi and Penuel; father or founder of Hushah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.4에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림. 훌의 아들. 우리, 소발, 살마, 하렙, 이스르엘, 이스마, 잇바스, 하술렐보니와 브누엘의 형제. 후사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에셀은 에브랏의 아들 훌을 통해 후사의 아버지 또는 창설자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Ephraim; killed by the men of Gath.
persons.short: Ezer was a son of Ephraim who was killed by the men of Gath while attempting to steal their livestock.
persons.article: Ezer was one of the sons of Ephraim, the son of Joseph (1Ch.7.21). He was born in Egypt before the Israelites' exodus. Ezer, along with his brother Elead, was killed by the men of Gath when they went to raid the livestock of the Gathites (1Ch.7.21). This event caused great grief to their father, Ephraim, who mourned for many days. The incident highlights the ongoing conflicts between the Israelites and the inhabitants of Canaan during their early history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.21 referred to as Ezer (עֶ֫זֶר); son of Ephraim; a brother of Shuthelah, Becher, Tahan, Elead and Beriah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.21에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림. 에브라임의 아들. 수델라, 베겔, 다한, 엘르앗과 브리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에셀은 에브라임의 아들로, 가드 사람들의 가축을 훔치려다 그들에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Lotan@Gen.36.20-1Ch, Shobal@Gen.36.20-1Ch, Zibeon@Gen.36.2-1Ch, Dishon@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Dishan@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch
persons.brief: Horite chief in Seir; son of Seir the Horite.
persons.short: Ezer was a Horite chief in the land of Seir, a son of Seir the Horite.
persons.article: Ezer was one of the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land of Seir before the descendants of Esau (Gen.36.21; 1Ch.1.38). He was a Horite chief and is mentioned among the leaders of the Horite clans (Gen.36.30; 1Ch.1.42). The Horites were the original inhabitants of Seir, but they were later dispossessed by the descendants of Esau (Deu.2.12). Ezer had three sons: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan (Gen.36.27; 1Ch.1.42).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.21 only referred to as Ezer (אֵ֫צֶר); son of Seir; a brother of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Dishon, Dishan and Timna; father of Bilhan, Zaavan, Akan.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.21에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림. 세일의 아들. 로단, 소발, 시브온, 디손, 디산과 딤나의 형제. 빌한, 사아완과 야아간의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에셀은 세일 땅에 살던 세일 사람 호리의 아들이며 호리 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite; participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Ezer was a Levite who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Ezer is mentioned in Neh.12.42 as one of the Levites who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall. The dedication ceremony was a significant event that celebrated the completion of the wall's reconstruction and the restoration of Jerusalem's security and spiritual life. Ezer, along with other Levites, played a role in the musical aspect of the dedication, which included singing and playing instruments such as trumpets, cymbals, harps, and lyres (Neh.12.27, 35-36). The Levites' involvement in the dedication highlights their important role in the worship and spiritual life of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Ezer (עֵ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.42에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 에셀은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ruler of Mizpah; repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Ezer, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall near the armory.
persons.article: Ezer, the ruler of Mizpah, is mentioned in Neh.3.19 as one of the individuals who helped repair Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah. He repaired a section of the wall near the armory, which was located at the angle of the wall. This suggests that Ezer was responsible for a strategically important part of the city's defenses. As the ruler of Mizpah, Ezer likely had significant influence and resources, which he used to contribute to the rebuilding efforts. His participation in the wall's restoration demonstrates the unity and cooperation among the Jewish leaders and people in the face of opposition and challenges.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.19 only referred to as Ezer (עֵ֫זֶר); a son of Jeshua.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.19에 처음 언급되며 '에셀'이라 불림. 예수아의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 미스바의 관장 에셀은 병기고 근처의 예루살렘 성벽 다른 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: People from Ezni(?)
persons.brief: Adino the Eznite; one of David's mighty men.
persons.short: Adino the Eznite, also known as Josheb-Basshebeth, was one of David's mighty men who wielded his spear against eight hundred men.
persons.article: The Eznites are mentioned in 2Sa.23.8 in reference to Adino, one of David's mighty men. The verse states that "Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahkemonite, was chief of the Three; he raised his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter." Some translations render "Josheb-Basshebeth" as "Adino the Eznite," suggesting that he was from a place or clan called Eznite. The exact location or meaning of Eznite is not clear from the biblical text. Adino's feat of killing eight hundred men with his spear in a single battle highlights his exceptional skill and bravery as one of David's elite warriors.
persons.summary: People from Ezni(?), only mentioned at 2Sa.23.8 only referred to as Eznites (עֵצֶן).
persons.summary_ko: 에센 사람. 2Sa.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '에센'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에센 사람 아디노(요셉밧세벳이라고도 함)는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 창을 휘둘러 팔백 명을 죽였다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest; scribe; led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem.
persons.short: Ezra was a priest and scribe who led a group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem and played a key role in the spiritual reformation of the people.
persons.article: Ezra was a prominent Jewish priest and scribe who lived during the Persian period. He was a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest of Israel (Ezr.7.1-5). Ezra was known for his devotion to the study and teaching of the Law of Moses (Ezr.7.6, 10). He led a group of Jewish exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes of Persia (Ezr.7.7-8). Upon arriving in Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many of the Jews, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land (Ezr.9.1-2). Ezra prayed and confessed the sins of the people, leading to a spiritual reformation and the dissolution of the mixed marriages (Ezra 10). Ezra also played a significant role in teaching the Law to the people and leading them in a covenant renewal ceremony (Nehemiah 8). He worked closely with Nehemiah, the governor of Judah, in rebuilding Jerusalem and restoring the spiritual life of the Jewish community (Neh.12.26, 36).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.7.1 referred to as Ezra (עֶזְרָא), or Ezra (Aramiac עֶזְרָא); son of Seraiah; a brother of Jehozadak.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 제사장. Ezr.7.1에 처음 언급되며 '에스라'라 불림. 스라야의 아들. 여호사닥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 에스라는 제사장이며 서기관으로, 유대인 포로 무리를 이끌고 예루살렘으로 돌아와 백성의 영적 개혁에 중요한 역할을 했다.
persons.article_ko: 에스라는 페르시아 시대에 살았던 저명한 유대인 제사장이며 서기관이었다. 그는 이스라엘의 첫 대제사장 아론의 후손이었다(스 7:1-5). 에스라는 모세의 율법을 연구하고 가르치는 것에 대한 헌신으로 알려졌다(스 7:6, 10). 그는 페르시아 왕 아닥사스다 통치 칠 년째에 유대인 포로 무리를 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 이끌었다(스 7:7-8). 예루살렘에 도착했을 때 에스라는 제사장과 레위인을 포함한 많은 유대인이 그 땅의 이방 민족들과 통혼했다는 것을 발견했다(스 9:1-2). 에스라는 기도하고 백성의 죄를 자백하여 영적 개혁과 혼합 결혼의 해소로 이어졌다(에스라 10장). 에스라는 또한 백성에게 율법을 가르치고 언약 갱신 의식을 인도하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다(느헤미야 8장). 그는 유다 총독 느헤미야와 긴밀히 협력하여 예루살렘을 재건하고 유대 공동체의 영적 생활을 회복시켰다(느 12:26, 36).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest; returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel; participated in wall dedication.
persons.short: Ezra was a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Ezra, mentioned in Neh.12.1, 13, and 33, was a priest who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, during the reign of King Cyrus of Persia. He was among the first group of exiles to return to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple and the city (Ezr.2.1-2). Ezra is listed as the head of a priestly family (Neh.12.13, indicating his leadership role within the priestly community). He also participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, where he led one of the two processions of thanksgiving on top of the wall (Neh.12.33). This Ezra should not be confused with the more prominent Ezra, the priest and scribe, who led a later group of exiles back to Jerusalem and initiated a spiritual reformation among the people.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.12.1 only referred to as Ezra (עֶזְרָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.1에 처음 언급되며 '에스라'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에스라는 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 돌아온 제사장으로, 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Chelub; mentioned in Judah's genealogy.
persons.short: Ezrah was a son of Chelub, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Ezrah is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.17 as a son of Chelub. He is listed in the genealogy of Judah, but no further information is provided about his life or role within the tribe. The genealogical record in this passage focuses on the descendants of Judah, particularly through the line of Caleb, and Ezrah is one of the many names mentioned without additional details.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.17 only referred to as Ezrah (עֶזְרָה); father of Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '에스라'라 불림. 예델, 메렛, 에벨과 얄론의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에스라는 유다의 족보에 언급된 글룹의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of David's agricultural workers.
persons.short: Ezri was the overseer of King David's agricultural workers who tilled the soil.
persons.article: Ezri is mentioned in 1Ch.27.26 as the overseer of King David's agricultural workers who tilled the soil. He was responsible for managing the laborers who worked in the fields, likely ensuring that the king's lands were properly cultivated and productive. This brief mention of Ezri provides insight into the organization and administration of David's kingdom, showing that he had appointed officials to oversee various aspects of the economy and agriculture.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.26 only referred to as Ezri (עֶזְרִי); a son of Chelub.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.26에 처음 언급되며 '에스리'라 불림. 글룹의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 에스리는 다윗 왕의 밭을 경작하는 일꾼들을 감독했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case.
persons.short: Felix was a Roman governor of Judea who heard the case against Paul and kept him in custody for two years.
persons.article: Felix was a Roman procurator (governor) of Judea who served from approximately 52 to 60 AD. He is mentioned in the book of Acts in connection with the apostle Paul's imprisonment and trial. Paul was brought before Felix in Caesarea after being accused by the Jewish leaders of being a troublemaker and inciting riots (Act.23.24, 26). During the hearing, Paul defended himself against the charges and spoke about his faith in Christ (Act.24.10-21). Felix, who was well-informed about Christianity, postponed making a decision and kept Paul in custody, hoping to receive a bribe from him (Act.24.22-26). Felix also heard Paul speak about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, which caused him to be afraid (Act.24.25). However, Felix left Paul in prison for two years until his successor, Porcius Festus, took office (Act.24.27). The account of Paul's interaction with Felix highlights the challenges faced by early Christians in the face of Roman authority and the corruption within the judicial system.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.23.24 only referred to as Felix (Φῆλιξ); husband of Drusilla.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.23.24에 처음 언급되며 '벨릭스'라 불림. 드루실라의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 벨릭스는 유대의 로마 총독으로, 바울에 대한 소송을 듣고 그를 이 년간 구금했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case; sent him to Rome.
persons.short: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as the Roman governor of Judea and heard Paul's case, ultimately sending him to Rome for trial.
persons.article: Porcius Festus was a Roman procurator (governor) of Judea who succeeded Felix around 60 AD (Act.24.27). He is mentioned in the book of Acts in relation to the apostle Paul's ongoing legal case. Upon taking office, Festus was confronted with the charges against Paul that had been left unresolved by Felix (Act.25.1-2). Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem for trial, but Paul appealed to Caesar, asserting his rights as a Roman citizen (Act.25.9-12). Festus, unsure how to handle the case, consulted with King Agrippa II and his sister Bernice, who came to Caesarea to pay their respects to the new governor (Act.25.13-22). Paul was brought before Festus, Agrippa, and Bernice to present his defense (Act.25.23-26:32). After hearing Paul's testimony, Festus exclaimed that Paul's great learning had driven him insane (Act.26.24). Agrippa, however, believed that Paul could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar (Act.26.32). Festus then sent Paul to Rome for trial, as he had requested (Act.27.1). The account of Festus's involvement in Paul's case illustrates the complexities of the Roman legal system and the challenges faced by early Christians in navigating it.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.24.27 referred to as Festus (Φῆστος), or Porcius (Πόρκιος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.24.27에 처음 언급되며 '베스도'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 보르기오 베스도는 벨릭스를 이어 유대의 로마 총독이 되어 바울의 사건을 듣고 결국 로마로 재판을 보냈다.
persons.article_ko: 베스도(보르기오 베스도)는 기원전 60년경 벨릭스를 이어 유대의 로마 총독(방백)이 되었다(행 24:27). 그는 사도 바울의 계속되는 소송 사건과 관련하여 사도행전에 언급된다. 부임하자마자 베스도는 벨릭스가 해결하지 않고 남겨둔 바울에 대한 고발에 직면했다(행 25:1-2). 유대인들에게 호의를 베풀고자 한 베스도는 바울에게 재판을 위해 예루살렘으로 가겠느냐고 물었으나, 바울은 로마 시민으로서의 권리를 주장하며 가이사에게 상소했다(행 25:9-12). 사건을 어떻게 처리해야 할지 확신이 없었던 베스도는 새 총독에게 인사하러 가이사랴에 온 아그립바 2세 왕과 그의 누이 버니게와 상의했다(행 25:13-22). 바울은 베스도, 아그립바, 버니게 앞에 끌려나와 변론했다(행 25:23-26:32). 바울의 증언을 들은 후 베스도는 바울의 많은 학식이 그를 미치게 했다고 외쳤다(행 26:24). 그러나 아그립바는 바울이 가이사에게 상소하지 않았더라면 풀려날 수 있었을 것이라고 믿었다(행 26:32). 베스도는 그 후 바울이 요청한 대로 그를 재판을 위해 로마로 보냈다(행 27:1). 바울의 사건에 대한 베스도의 관여 기록은 로마 법 체계의 복잡함과 초대 그리스도인들이 그것을 헤쳐나가는 데 직면한 어려움을 보여준다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Corinthian Christian; visited Paul in Ephesus.
persons.short: Fortunatus was a Corinthian Christian who, along with Stephanas and Achaicus, visited Paul in Ephesus and refreshed his spirit.
persons.article: Fortunatus is mentioned in 1Co.16.17 as one of the Corinthian Christians who visited Paul during his stay in Ephesus. He, along with Stephanas and Achaicus, are described as having refreshed Paul's spirit and supplying what was lacking from the Corinthian church. This suggests that they brought news, encouragement, and possibly financial support from Corinth to Paul. Their presence was a source of joy and comfort to Paul, who was facing challenges in his ministry. The mention of Fortunatus and his companions highlights the importance of fellowship and support among early Christians, even across different cities and regions.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at 1Co.16.17 referred to as Fortunatus (Φορτουνᾶτος).
persons.short_ko: 브드나도는 아가이고, 스데바나와 함께 에베소로 바울을 찾아가 고린도전서를 전달했다.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 1Co.16.17에 처음 언급되며 '브드나도'라 불림.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ebed; led a revolt against Abimelech.
persons.short: Gaal, the son of Ebed, led a revolt against Abimelech, the ruler of Shechem, but was defeated and driven out of the city.
persons.article: Gaal, the son of Ebed, appears in Judges 9 as the leader of a revolt against Abimelech, the ruler of Shechem. After Abimelech had ruled Shechem for three years, Gaal arrived in the city and gained the trust of the people (Jdg.9.26-29). He challenged Abimelech's authority and encouraged the people to follow him instead. When Abimelech was informed of Gaal's actions, he devised a plan to attack the city (Jdg.9.30-33). Gaal and his followers went out to fight against Abimelech but were defeated and driven out of Shechem (Jdg.9.34-41). Abimelech then destroyed the city and scattered salt over it, symbolizing its complete destruction (Jdg.9.45). The story of Gaal's failed revolt illustrates the internal conflicts and power struggles that occurred during the period of the judges in Israel.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.9.26 only referred to as Gaal (גַּ֫עַל); a son of Ebed.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.9.26에 처음 언급되며 '가알'이라 불림. 에벳의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 에벳의 아들 가알은 세겜의 통치자 아비멜렉에 대한 반역을 이끌었으나 패배하여 성에서 쫓겨났다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Gabbai was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Gabbai is mentioned briefly in Neh.11.8 as one of the Benjamite leaders who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is described as coming after Sallu, another Benjamite leader. The context suggests that Gabbai was among the first to resettle in Jerusalem and played a role in the city's repopulation and rebuilding. However, no further details are provided about his specific duties or contributions. The mention of Gabbai in this passage highlights the importance of the Benjamites in the restoration of Jerusalem and the Jewish community after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.8 only referred to as Gabbai (גַּבַּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.8에 처음 언급되며 '갑배'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갑배는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착한 베냐민 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
persons.short: Gad was a prophet who advised King David and wrote a book of his acts.
persons.article: Gad was a prophet who served during the reigns of King David and his son Solomon. He first appears in 1Sa.22.5, where he advises David to leave his stronghold in Moab and return to the land of Judah. Gad played a significant role in the events surrounding David's census of Israel (2Samuel 24; 1Chronicles 21). After David had sinned by taking the census, Gad was sent by God to offer David a choice of three punishments: three years of famine, three months of fleeing from enemies, or three days of plague (2Sa.24.11-14; 1Ch.21.9-13). David chose the plague, and Gad instructed him to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite to stop the plague (2Sa.24.18-19; 1Ch.21.18-19). Gad is described as David's seer (2Sa.24.11; 1Ch.21.9 and is credited with writing a book about David's acts )(1Ch.29.29). He was also involved in organizing the music and worship in the tabernacle (2Ch.29.25). Gad's ministry as a prophet spanned the latter years of David's reign and continued into the early years of Solomon's reign.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.22.5 only referred to as Gad (גָּד).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 선지자. 1Sa.22.5에 처음 언급되며 '갓'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갓은 다윗 왕에게 조언한 선지자로, 그의 행적을 기록한 책을 썼다.
persons.article_ko: 갓은 다윗 왕과 그 아들 솔로몬의 통치 기간 동안 섬긴 선지자였다. 그는 사무엘상 22장 5절에 처음 등장하는데, 그곳에서 그는 다윗에게 모압에 있는 요새를 떠나 유다 땅으로 돌아가라고 조언한다. 갓은 다윗이 이스라엘 인구조사를 실시한 사건에서 중요한 역할을 했다(사무엘하 24장; 역대상 21장). 다윗이 인구조사를 함으로써 죄를 지은 후 갓은 하나님께 보냄을 받아 다윗에게 세 가지 벌 중 하나를 선택하게 했다: 삼 년의 흉년, 석 달간 원수들에게 쫓기는 것, 또는 사흘간의 전염병(삼하 24:11-14; 대상 21:9-13). 다윗은 전염병을 선택했고, 갓은 그에게 전염병을 멈추기 위해 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당에 제단을 쌓으라고 지시했다(삼하 24:18-19; 대상 21:18-19). 갓은 다윗의 선견자로 묘사되며(삼하 24:11; 대상 21:9) 다윗의 행적에 관한 책을 저술한 것으로 인정받는다(대상 29:29). 그는 또한 성막에서 음악과 예배를 조직하는 데 관여했다(대하 29:25). 선지자로서 갓의 사역은 다윗 통치 후기부터 솔로몬 통치 초기까지 걸쳐 있었다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Dan@Gen.30.6-1Ch, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Asher@Gen.30.13-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev

persons.brief: Israelite tribe; descended from Gad, son of Jacob.
persons.short: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Gad, the son of Jacob, and known for their military prowess and settlement east of the Jordan River.
persons.article: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, named after Gad, the seventh son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Zilpah, Leah's maidservant (Gen.30.11; 35.26). The tribe of Gad played a significant role throughout Israel's history. During the Exodus, the tribe of Gad was counted among the Israelites (Num.1.14, 24-25 and was positioned on the south side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Reuben and Simeon )(Num.2.14). The tribe of Gad, along with Reuben and half of Manasseh, settled in the region east of the Jordan River (Numbers 32; Jos.13.24-28). They were known for their military prowess and bravery (1Ch.12.8, 14). The Gadites were among the first to help David when he was hiding from Saul (1Ch.12.8-15). They also supported David during the census and the purchase of the threshing floor for the temple (2Sa.24.5; 1Ch.21.2). The Gadites were blessed by Moses for their faithfulness and strength (Deu.33.20-21). The tribe of Gad was allotted cities and pasturelands in the region of Gilead (Jos.13.24-28; 1Ch.6.63, 80). They, along with the other tribes east of the Jordan, built an altar as a witness to their unity with the rest of Israel (Joshua 22). The Gadites were among the first tribes to be taken into captivity by the Assyrians (1Ch.5.26). In Ezekiel's vision of the restored Israel, the tribe of Gad is allotted a portion of land in the far north (Ezk.48.27-28, 34). In the book of Revelation, Gad is mentioned as one of the tribes with 12,000 sealed servants of God (Rev.7.5).
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Gad living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.30.11 referred to as Gad or Gadite (גָּד), or Gad or Gadite (גָּדִי), or Gad (Γάδ); son of Israel and Zilpah; a brother of Asher; half-brother of: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Issachar, Zebulun, Dinah, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arod and Areli.
persons.brief_ko: 야곱과 실바의 아들, 갓 지파 시조
persons.short_ko: 갓은 야곱과 레아의 여종 실바 사이에서 태어난 아들로 갓 지파의 시조가 되었다.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.30.11에 처음 언급되며 '갓'이라 불림. 이스라엘과 실바의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 단, 납달리, 아셀, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 시뵨, 학기, 수니, 에스본, 에리, 아롯과 아렐리의 아버지.
persons.article_ko: 갓은 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나로, 이스라엘(야곱)과 레아의 여종 실바의 일곱째 아들 갓의 이름을 따서 지어졌다(창 30:11; 35:26). 갓 지파는 이스라엘 역사 전반에 걸쳐 중요한 역할을 했다. 출애굽 당시 갓 지파는 이스라엘 백성 가운데 계수되었고(민 1:14, 24-25) 르우벤, 시므온 지파와 함께 성막 남쪽에 배치되었다(민 2:14). 갓 지파는 르우벤, 므낫세 반 지파와 함께 요단강 동편 지역에 정착했다(민 32장; 수 13:24-28). 그들은 군사적 용맹과 담대함으로 알려졌다(대상 12:8, 14). 갓 사람들은 다윗이 사울을 피해 숨어 있을 때 그를 도운 최초의 사람들 중에 속했다(대상 12:8-15). 그들은 또한 인구조사와 성전을 위한 타작마당 구매 당시 다윗을 지지했다(삼하 24:5; 대상 21:2). 갓 사람들은 그들의 신실함과 힘 때문에 모세에게 축복을 받았다(신 33:20-21). 갓 지파는 길르앗 지역의 성읍들과 목초지를 받았다(수 13:24-28; 대상 6:63, 80). 그들은 요단강 동편의 다른 지파들과 함께 나머지 이스라엘과의 하나됨을 증거하는 제단을 세웠다(여호수아 22장). 갓 사람들은 앗수르에게 처음으로 포로로 끌려간 지파 중에 속했다(대상 5:26). 회복된 이스라엘에 대한 에스겔의 환상에서 갓 지파는 극북 지역의 땅을 분배받는다(겔 48:27-28, 34). 요한계시록에서 갓은 하나님의 인침 받은 종 만 이천 명이 있는 지파 중 하나로 언급된다(계 7:5).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Susi; representative of Manasseh among the spies.
persons.short: Gaddi, the son of Susi, was the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Gaddi, the son of Susi, is mentioned in Num.13.11 as the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. The spies were tasked with scouting out the land, assessing its resources, and gathering information about its inhabitants (Num.13.17-20). Gaddi was one of the ten spies who brought back a negative report, emphasizing the strength of the Canaanites and the challenges of conquering the land (Num.13.31-33). Only Joshua and Caleb, the other two spies, gave a positive report and encouraged the Israelites to trust in God's promise (Num.14.6-9). As a result of the people's unbelief and rebellion, God declared that the generation who had witnessed the Exodus would not enter the Promised Land, except for Joshua and Caleb (Num.14.20-35).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.11 only referred to as Gaddi (גַּדִּי); a son of Susi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.11에 처음 언급되며 '갓디'라 불림. 수시의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 수시의 아들 갓디는 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 므낫세 지파 대표였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Sodi; representative of Zebulun among the spies.
persons.short: Gaddiel, the son of Sodi, was the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Gaddiel, the son of Sodi, is mentioned in Num.13.10 as the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. The spies were chosen from each of the twelve tribes of Israel to scout out the land, assess its resources, and gather information about its inhabitants (Num.13.17-20). Gaddiel was one of the ten spies who brought back a negative report, emphasizing the strength of the Canaanites and the challenges of conquering the land (Num.13.31-33). Only Joshua and Caleb, the other two spies, gave a positive report and encouraged the Israelites to trust in God's promise (Num.14.6-9). As a result of the people's unbelief and rebellion, God declared that the generation who had witnessed the Exodus would not enter the Promised Land, except for Joshua and Caleb (Num.14.20-35).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.10 only referred to as Gaddiel (גַּדִּיאֵל); a son of Sodi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.10에 처음 언급되며 '갓디엘'이라 불림. 소디의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 소디의 아들 갓디엘은 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 스불론 지파 대표였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Menahem, king of Israel.
persons.short: Gadi was the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum.
persons.article: Gadi is mentioned in 2Ki.15.14, 17 as the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel during a time of political instability. Menahem, the son of Gadi, assassinated Shallum, who had previously overthrown Zechariah to become king (2Ki.15.10, 14). Menahem then reigned as king of Israel for ten years (2Ki.15.17). During his reign, Menahem faced the threat of the Assyrian king Pul (Tiglath-Pileser III) and paid him a large tribute to gain his support and strengthen his hold on the kingdom (2Ki.15.19-20). Menahem's reign was marked by violence and oppression, as he brutally suppressed any opposition to his rule (2Ki.15.16).
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.14 only referred to as Gadi (גָּדִי); father of Menahem.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.15.14에 처음 언급되며 '가디'라 불림. 므나헴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 가디는 살룸을 암살하고 이스라엘 왕이 된 므나헴의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor and Reumah.
persons.short: Gaham was one of the sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah.
persons.article: Gaham is mentioned briefly in Gen.22.24 as one of the sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah. Nahor and Reumah had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. This information is provided in the context of the genealogy of Abraham's family, highlighting the relatives of the patriarch. The mention of Nahor's children by his concubine demonstrates the practice of polygamy among the patriarchs and their extended family.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.24 only referred to as Gaham (גַּ֫חַם); son of Nahor and Reumah; a brother of Tebah, Tahash and Maacah; half-brother of: Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.24에 처음 언급되며 '가함'이라 불림. 나홀과 르우마의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 가함은 아브라함의 형제 나홀이 첩 르우마를 통해 얻은 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Gahar was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Gahar is mentioned in Ezr.2.47 and Neh.7.49 as an ancestor of a group of temple servants, also known as Nethinim, who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. The Nethinim were a class of temple personnel who assisted the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple (Ezr.8.20). They were likely descendants of the Gibeonites who were assigned by Joshua to serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the altar of the Lord (Jos.9.23, 27). In the lists of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel (Ezra 2) and Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7), the descendants of Gahar are counted among the Nethinim. This suggests that Gahar's descendants had faithfully carried out their duties in the temple service, even during the exile, and were part of the group who returned to restore worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.47 only referred to as Gahar (גַּ֫חַר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '가할'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 가할은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자(느디님) 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Recipient of John's third epistle; commended for his faithfulness.
persons.short: Gaius, the recipient of John's third epistle, was commended for his faithfulness to the truth and his hospitality to traveling missionaries.
persons.article: Gaius is the recipient of John's third epistle, a short letter in which the apostle commends him for his faithfulness and hospitality. John addresses Gaius as a dear friend whom he loves in the truth (3Jn.1.1). He expresses his joy upon hearing that Gaius is walking in the truth and supporting the work of the gospel (3Jn.1.3-4). John specifically praises Gaius for his hospitality towards traveling missionaries, even though they were strangers to him (3Jn.1.5-8). This hospitality was essential for the spread of the gospel, as these missionaries relied on the support of believers like Gaius. John also mentions a certain Diotrephes who was causing problems in the church and refusing to welcome the missionaries (3Jn.1.9-10). In contrast, John encourages Gaius to continue doing what is good and not to imitate what is evil (3Jn.1.11). The letter to Gaius provides insight into the challenges and importance of hospitality and support within the early Christian community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 3Jn.1.1 only referred to as Gaius (Γάϊος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 3Jn.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '가이오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 가이오는 요한삼서의 수신자로, 진리에 대한 신실함과 여행하는 선교사들에 대한 환대로 칭찬받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Macedonian; Paul's traveling companion; caught in Ephesian riot.
persons.short: Gaius, a Macedonian and traveling companion of Paul, was seized along with Aristarchus during the riot in Ephesus.
persons.article: Gaius, a Macedonian, was one of Paul's traveling companions during his third missionary journey. In Act.19.29, Gaius and Aristarchus, another Macedonian, were seized by the mob during the riot in Ephesus. The riot was instigated by Demetrius, a silversmith who made shrines of Artemis, because he felt threatened by Paul's preaching and the spread of Christianity in the city. The mob dragged Gaius and Aristarchus into the theater, but Paul was prevented from entering by his disciples and some officials of the province of Asia who were his friends. The incident highlights the opposition and dangers faced by Paul and his companions as they spread the gospel in pagan cities.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.19.29 only referred to as Gaius (Γάϊος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.19.29에 처음 언급되며 '가이오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마게도냐 사람이며 바울의 여행 동반자인 가이오는 에베소 소요 사건 때 아리스다고와 함께 붙잡혔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Derbean; accompanied Paul on his journey to Jerusalem.
persons.short: Gaius of Derbe accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem, along with several others.
persons.article: Gaius of Derbe is mentioned in Act.20.4 as one of the men who accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem. After spending three months in Greece, Paul decided to return through Macedonia due to a plot against him by the Jews. He was accompanied by Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia. These men went ahead and waited for Paul and his companions at Troas. The mention of Gaius and the others demonstrates the unity and support among the early Christians from different regions as they worked together to spread the gospel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.20.4 only referred to as Gaius (Γάϊος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.20.4에 처음 언급되며 '가이오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 더베 사람 가이오는 여러 사람과 함께 그리스에서 예루살렘으로 가는 바울의 여정에 동행했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Corinthian believer; host to Paul and the church.
persons.short: Gaius, a Corinthian believer baptized by Paul, hosted Paul and the whole church in his home.
persons.article: Gaius, mentioned in Rom.16.23 and 1Co.1.14, was a believer from Corinth who played a significant role in the early church. In his letter to the Romans, Paul sends greetings from Gaius, describing him as his host and the host of the whole church. This suggests that Gaius was a wealthy and generous man who opened his home for Christian gatherings and provided hospitality to Paul and other believers. In 1 Corinthians, Paul mentions that he personally baptized Gaius, along with Crispus and the household of Stephanas. This indicates that Gaius was one of the early converts in Corinth and had a close relationship with Paul. Gaius' example of hospitality and support for the church was crucial for the growth and unity of the early Christian community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Rom.16.23 only referred to as Gaius (Γάϊος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.23에 처음 언급되며 '가이오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바울에게 세례받은 고린도 신자 가이오는 자기 집에서 바울과 온 교회를 대접했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite musician; descendant of Asaph; lived in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Asaph, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Galal is mentioned in 1Ch.9.15 as one of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was a descendant of Asaph, one of the chief musicians appointed by David to lead worship in the temple (1Ch.6.39). Galal's inclusion in this list suggests that he, like his ancestor Asaph, was a skilled musician who served in the temple. The Levites were responsible for various duties in the temple, including music, singing, and assisting the priests (1Ch.23.28-32). The mention of Galal and other Levites living in Jerusalem after the exile demonstrates the importance of restoring worship and maintaining the temple services as the Jewish community rebuilt their lives in the land.
