persons.article: Gog is mentioned in 1Ch.5.4 as a descendant of Reuben, the eldest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is listed in the genealogy as the son of Joel, who was the son of Shemaiah, the son of Joel, the son of Reaiah, the son of Baal, the son of Reuben.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.4 only referred to as Gog (גּוֹג); a son of Shemaiah; father of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.5.4에 처음 언급되며 '곡'이라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 곡은 르우벤의 후손으로, 역대상 5장 4절 르우벤 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: People from Goy(?)
persons.brief: A king of Goyim who fought alongside Chedorlaomer.
persons.short: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.
persons.article: Goiim, meaning "nations," appears in the Bible as a place name or a title. In Gen.14.1 and Gen.14.9, Tidal is mentioned as the king of Goiim (also spelled Goyim). He was one of the four kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer and his allies in the Battle of the Vale of Siddim. The exact location of Goiim is uncertain, but it is thought to refer to a region or a confederation of peoples, rather than a specific city or nation. In Jos.12.23, the king of Goiim in Gilgal is listed among the kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. This suggests that Goiim may have been a region or a group of people living in the area of Gilgal.
persons.summary: People from Goy(?), first mentioned at Gen.14.1 only referred to as Goiim (גּוֹיִם).
persons.summary_ko: 고임. Gen.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '고임'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고임(민족들)의 왕 디달은 창세기 14장에서 그돌라오멜과 연합하여 싸운 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A Philistine giant defeated by David.
persons.short: Goliath was the Philistine champion from Gath who was defeated by David in a battle.
persons.article: Goliath was a Philistine warrior from the city of Gath who fought against the Israelites during the reign of King Saul. He is described as a giant, standing at six cubits and a span (approximately 9 feet 9 inches or 3 meters) tall, and wearing heavy bronze armor (1Sa.17.4-7). Goliath challenged the Israelites to send a champion to face him in single combat, but no one dared to accept the challenge until David, a young shepherd, volunteered. With a sling and a stone, David defeated Goliath, striking him on the forehead and killing him (1Sa.17.48-50). David then cut off Goliath's head with the giant's own sword (1Sa.17.51). This event is significant in David's life, as it marked the beginning of his rise to prominence in Israel. The sword of Goliath was kept as a trophy, and David later retrieved it from the tabernacle at Nob when he was fleeing from Saul (1Sa.21.9, 22:10). In 2Sa.21.19 and 1Ch.20.5, there is mention of another Goliath, also from Gath, who was killed by Elhanan, one of David's warriors. Some scholars believe this may refer to a brother or relative of the Goliath killed by David.
persons.summary: A gigantic man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.17.4 only referred to as Goliath (גׇּלְיַת); son of Rapha; a brother of Ishbi-benob, Saph, Lahmi, huge man.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 거인. 1Sa.17.4에 처음 언급되며 '골리앗'이라 불림. Rapha의 아들. 이스비브놉, 삽, 라흐미와 거인의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 골리앗은 가드 출신 블레셋의 장수로, 전투에서 다윗에게 패했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth; father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
persons.short: Gomer, a son of Japheth, was the father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah, as listed in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Gomer is mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10.2-3, 1 Chronicles Gen.1.5-6 as one of the sons of Japheth, the son of Noah). He is listed alongside his brothers Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer is also named as the father of three sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. The descendants of Gomer are believed to have settled in the region around the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, possibly in the area of modern-day Turkey, Armenia, and parts of Eastern Europe. In Ezk.38.6, Gomer is mentioned along with Beth-togarmah as one of the allies of Gog, a future enemy of Israel. This suggests that the descendants of Gomer were still recognized as a distinct people group during the time of Ezekiel's prophecy. Some scholars have proposed a connection between Gomer and the ancient Cimmerians, a nomadic people who inhabited the region north of the Black Sea in the 8th and 7th centuries BC, but this identification remains uncertain.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Gomer (גֹּ֫מֶר); son of Japheth; a brother of Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; father of Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '고멜'이라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 마곡, 마대, 야완, 두발, 메섹과 디라스의 형제. 아스그나스, 리밧과 도갈마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 고멜은 야벳의 아들로, 민족 계보에 나오는 아스그나스, 리밧, 도갈마의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Hosea's wife, a promiscuous woman.
persons.short: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea.
persons.article: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea, as mentioned in Hos.1.3. God commanded Hosea to marry Gomer, who was described as a promiscuous woman or a prostitute, to illustrate Israel's unfaithfulness to God. Gomer bore Hosea three children: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, and Lo-ammi, whose names were symbolic of God's judgment and rejection of Israel due to their disobedience. Despite Gomer's continued unfaithfulness, Hosea was commanded to love her and redeem her, just as God continued to love and seek to redeem Israel. The story of Hosea and Gomer serves as an allegory of God's relationship with Israel, emphasizing God's steadfast love and mercy in the face of Israel's sin and disobedience.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Hos.1.3 only referred to as Gomer (גֹּ֫מֶר); a daughter of Diblaim; wife of Hosea; mother of Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi H3818).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. Hos.1.3에 처음 언급되며 '고멜'이라 불림. 디블라임의 딸. 호세아의 아내. 이스르엘, 로루하마와 로암미의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 디블라임의 딸 고멜은 선지자 호세아의 아내였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Gad; father of Abdiel.
persons.short: Guni, a descendant of Gad, was the father of Abdiel, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad.
persons.article: In 1Ch.5.15, Guni is mentioned as a descendant of Gad, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is described as the son of Abdiel and the father of Ahi, who was the chief of their ancestral house. This Guni is mentioned in the context of the genealogy of the tribe of Gad, which settled east of the Jordan River.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.15 only referred to as Guni (גּוּנִי); father of Abdiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.15에 처음 언급되며 '구니'라 불림. 압디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 구니는 갓의 후손으로, 갓 족보에 나오는 압디엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob.
persons.short: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.
persons.article: Guni is mentioned in Gen.46.24 and Num.26.48 as one of the sons of Naphtali, who was one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). In the genealogy of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt during the famine, Guni is listed among the sons of Naphtali. The descendants of Guni are referred to as the Gunites in Num.26.48, where they are counted as part of the tribe of Naphtali in the census taken in the wilderness. In 1Ch.7.13, Guni is again mentioned in the genealogy of Naphtali's descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Naphtali living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.24 referred to as Guni (גּוּנִי), or Gunite (גּוּנִי); son of Naphtali; a brother of Jahzeel, Jezer and Shillem.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.24에 처음 언급되며 '구니'라 불림. 납달리의 아들. 야스엘, 예셀과 실렘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 구니는 납달리의 아들이며 야곱의 손자로, 창세기와 민수기 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Hepher@1Ch.4.6, Temeni@1Ch.4.6, Zereth@1Ch.4.7, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Ethnan@1Ch.4.7, Koz@1Ch.4.8
persons.brief: A descendant of Judah through Hezron.
persons.short: Haahashtari was a descendant of Judah through Hezron, as listed in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Haahashtari is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.6 as one of the sons of Naarah, who was one of the wives of Ashhur, a descendant of Judah through Hezron. The name Haahashtari appears only once in the Bible, and no other information is provided about him or his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.6 only referred to as Haahashtari (אֲחַשְׁתָּרִי); son of Ashhur and Naarah; a brother of Ahuzzam, Hepher and Temeni; half-brother of: Zereth, Izhar, Ethnan and Koz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '하아하스타리'라 불림. 아스훌과 나아라의 아들. 아훗삼, 헤벨, 데므니, 세렛, 이스할, 에드난과 고스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하아하스다리는 헤스론을 통한 유다의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest whose descendants were unable to prove their lineage.
persons.short: Habaiah was a priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood due to insufficient genealogical records.
persons.article: Habaiah is mentioned in Ezr.2.61 and Neh.7.63 as one of the priests who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. However, when the genealogies of the priests were examined, the descendants of Habaiah were unable to prove their priestly lineage. As a result, they were considered unclean and were excluded from serving as priests. The governor ordered them not to eat from the most holy things until a priest with the Urim and Thummim could resolve the matter. The Urim and Thummim were sacred objects used to determine the will of God. The fact that the descendants of Habaiah could not provide clear genealogical records suggests that their priestly lineage may have been lost or compromised during the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.61 referred to as Habaiah or Hobaiah (חֲבַיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.61에 처음 언급되며 '하바야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하바야는 그 후손들이 족보 기록 부족으로 제사장직에서 제외된 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet who questioned God's justice.
persons.short: Habakkuk, a prophet, wrote the book bearing his name, which records his dialogue with God about justice and faith.
persons.article: Habakkuk was a prophet who lived in Judah, likely during the late 7th century BC, before the Babylonian exile. The book of Habakkuk, which bears his name, records a unique dialogue between the prophet and God. Habakkuk questioned God's justice, asking why evil seemed to go unpunished and the righteous suffered (Hab.1.2-4). God responded by revealing His plan to use the Babylonians to punish Judah's wickedness (Hab.1.5-11). Habakkuk then struggled with the idea of God using a wicked nation to punish His people (Hab.1.12-2:1). God assured Habakkuk that the Babylonians would also face judgment for their sins, and that the righteous would live by faith (Hab.2.2-20). The book concludes with a prayer of Habakkuk, in which he expresses his trust in God despite the difficult circumstances (Hab.3.1-19). Habakkuk's message emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in God, even when His ways are difficult to understand.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Hab.1.1 only referred to as Habakkuk (חֲבַקּוּק).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. Hab.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '하박국'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 하박국은 정의와 믿음에 대한 하나님과의 대화를 기록한 자신의 이름을 딴 책을 썼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Jaazaniah, a Rechabite leader.
persons.short: Habazziniah was the grandfather of Jaazaniah, a leader of the Rechabites during Jeremiah's time.
persons.article: Habazziniah is mentioned in Jer.35.3 as the grandfather of Jaazaniah, who was a leader of the Rechabites during the time of the prophet Jeremiah. The Rechabites were a nomadic tribe known for their strict adherence to the commands of their ancestor, Jonadab son of Rechab. They abstained from drinking wine, planting crops, and living in permanent dwellings (Jer.35.6-7). Jeremiah used the Rechabites' obedience to their ancestor's commands as an example to contrast with the disobedience of the people of Judah to God's commands (Jer.35.12-19).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.35.3 only referred to as Habazziniah (חֲבַצִּנְיָה); father of Jeremiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.35.3에 처음 언급되며 '하바시냐'라 불림. 예레미야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하바시냐는 예레미야 시대에 레갑 족속의 지도자였던 야아사냐의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Nehemiah, the governor of Judah.
persons.short: Hacaliah was the father of Nehemiah, who served as the governor of Judah during the Persian period.
persons.article: Hacaliah is mentioned in Neh.1.1 and Neh.10.1 as the father of Nehemiah, the main character of the book of Nehemiah. Nehemiah served as the cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia (Neh.1.11 before being appointed as the governor of Judah )(Neh.5.14). Nehemiah played a crucial role in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem and instituting religious and social reforms among the Jewish people who had returned from exile. Apart from being Nehemiah's father, no other details are provided about Hacaliah's life or role in the biblical narrative.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.1.1 only referred to as Hacaliah (חֲכַלְיָה); father of Nehemiah, Hanani.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '하가랴'라 불림. 느헤미야와 하나니의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하가랴는 페르시아 시대에 유다 총독으로 섬긴 느헤미야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jehiel, one of David's family servants.
persons.short: Hachmoni was the father of Jehiel who, with Jonathan attended King David's sons.
persons.article: Hachmoni is mentioned in 1Ch.27.32 as the father of Jehiel who looked after King David's sons along with David's counselor, Jonathan. (1Ch.27.32).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.32 only referred to as Hachmoni (חַכְמוֹנִי); father of Jehiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.32에 처음 언급되며 '학모니'라 불림. 여히엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 학모니는 요나단과 함께 다윗 왕의 아들들을 섬긴 여히엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: People from Hachmon or Tahchemon(?)
persons.brief: A clan or family known for their mighty warriors.
persons.short: The Hachmonites, also known as the Tahchemonites, were a clan or family that produced some of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: The Hachmonites, also referred to as the Tahchemonites, were a clan or family mentioned in the context of King David's mighty warriors. In 2Sa.23.8, Josheb-Basshebeth, one of David's mighty men, is called the Tahchemonite, which suggests that he may have been a member of this clan. Similarly, in 1Ch.11.11, Jashobeam, another of David's mighty warriors, is described as the son of a Hachmonite. These references indicate that the Hachmonites or Tahchemonites were known for producing skilled and valiant warriors who served in David's army. However, no further details are provided about the history or origins of this clan in the Bible.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Hachmon or Tahchemon(?), first mentioned at 2Sa.23.8 referred to as Hachmonites (חַכְמוֹנִי), or Tahchemonite (תַּחְכְּמֹנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 학몬 또는 다그몬 족속(추정). 2Sa.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '학모니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 학몬 족속(다그몬 족속이라고도 함)은 다윗의 용사 몇 명을 배출한 가문이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: An Edomite prince who opposed Solomon.
persons.short: Hadad, an Edomite prince, fled to Egypt and later became an adversary to King Solomon.
persons.article: Hadad was an Edomite prince who became an adversary to King Solomon of Israel (1Ki.11.14-22). When King David conquered Edom, Hadad was a young boy. He fled to Egypt with some Edomite servants of his father and found favor with Pharaoh, who gave him a house, land, and provisions. Pharaoh also gave Hadad his sister-in-law, the sister of Queen Tahpenes, as a wife. Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, who was raised in Pharaoh's palace. After the deaths of David and Joab, Hadad returned to Edom and became an adversary to Solomon, causing trouble for Israel. The Bible does not provide further details about Hadad's actions against Solomon or the outcome of their conflict.
persons.summary: A king of Edom of the Egyptians living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.11.14 referred to as Hadad (הֲדַד), or Hadad (אֲדַד); husband of sister of Tahpenes; father of Genubath.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.11.14에 처음 언급되며 '하닷'이라 불림. 다브네스의 자매(이름 미상)의 남편. 그누밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에돔 왕자 하닷은 애굽으로 도망쳤고 후에 솔로몬 왕의 대적자가 되었다.

persons.description: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mibsam@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Massa@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Jetur@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Mahalath@Gen.28.9-
persons.brief: A son of Ishmael, Abraham's son.
persons.short: Hadad was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son.
persons.article: Hadad is mentioned in Gen.25.15 and 1Ch.1.30 as one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, who was the son of Abraham and Hagar. Ishmael's sons, including Hadad, are described as tribal rulers, suggesting that they became leaders of their own clans or tribes. The listing of Ishmael's sons in these passages is part of the genealogical record of Abraham's descendants.
persons.summary: A man of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.15 referred to as Hadad (חֲדַד), or Hadad (חֲדַר); son of Ishmael; a brother of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah and Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 아라비아 사람. Gen.25.15에 처음 언급되며 '하닷'이라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 밉삼, 미스마, 두마, 맛사, 데마, 여둘, 나비스, 게드마와 마할랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하닷은 아브라함의 아들 이스마엘의 열두 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Edom, succeeded Husham.
persons.short: Hadad, son of Bedad, became king of Edom after Husham's death.
persons.article: Hadad, son of Bedad, was a king of Edom mentioned in Gen.36.35-36 and 1Ch.1.46-47. He succeeded Husham as king of Edom. Hadad defeated the Midianites in the country of Moab, which suggests that during his reign, Edom had a military conflict with Midian. The city of Avith is mentioned as the place where Hadad reigned, but its exact location is unknown.
persons.summary: A king of Edom living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.35 only referred to as Hadad (הֲדַד); a son of Bedad.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.36.35에 처음 언급되며 '하닷'이라 불림. 브닷의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 브닷의 아들 하닷은 후삼이 죽은 후 에돔 왕이 되었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: The last king of Edom before Israelite rule.
persons.short: Hadad, also known as Hadar, was the last king of Edom before the Israelites established their monarchy.
persons.article: Hadad, also referred to as Hadar in some passages, was the last king of Edom mentioned in the Bible before the Israelites established their own monarchy (Gen.36.39, 1 Chronicles Gen.1.50-51). He was the successor of Baal-hanan, son of Achbor. Hadad's wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Me-zahab. The city where Hadad reigned was Pau, but its exact location is unknown. The mention of Hadad as the last king suggests that after his reign, Edom came under the rule of the Israelites.
persons.summary: A king of Edom living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.39 referred to as Hadad (הֲדַד), or Hadar (הֲדַר); husband of Mehetabel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.36.39에 처음 언급되며 '하닷'이라 불림. 므헤다벨의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 하닷(하달이라고도 함)은 이스라엘에 왕정이 세워지기 전 에돔의 마지막 왕이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Zobah, defeated by David.
persons.short: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, was defeated by King David in battle, and his allies, the Arameans, became subject to Israel.
persons.article: Hadadezer was the king of Zobah, an Aramean kingdom, during the reign of King David of Israel. He is mentioned in 2Samuel 8, 10, and 1Chronicles 18, 19. Hadadezer went to restore his control along the Euphrates River, but David defeated him, capturing many of his chariots, horsemen, and foot soldiers (2Sa.8.3-4, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.18.3-4). David also took gold shields from Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem (2Sa.8.7, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.18.7). When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David defeated them as well, and they became subject to Israel (2Sa.8.5-6, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.18.5-6). Later, when David's messengers were mistreated by the Ammonites, Hadadezer sent his army to help the Ammonites fight against Israel (2Sa.10.16, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.19.16). However, Joab and Abishai, David's commanders, defeated the Arameans and the Ammonites. After this defeat, Hadadezer's allies made peace with Israel and became subject to them (2Sa.10.19, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.19.19). The biblical account portrays Hadadezer as a powerful king who posed a significant threat to Israel, but was ultimately defeated by David and his army.
persons.summary: A king of Zobah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.3 referred to as Hadadezer (הֲדַרְעֶ֫זֶר), or Hadadezer (הֲדַדְעֶ֫זֶר); a son of Rehob.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 2Sa.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '하닷에셀'이라 불림. 르흡의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 소바 왕 하닷에셀은 다윗 왕에게 전투에서 패했고, 그의 동맹인 아람 사람들이 이스라엘에 복속되었다.
persons.article_ko: 하닷에셀은 이스라엘 왕 다윗 통치 기간의 아람 왕국인 소바의 왕이었다. 그는 사무엘하 8장, 10장과 역대상 18장, 19장에 언급된다. 하닷에셀은 유프라테스강을 따라 자신의 지배권을 회복하러 갔으나 다윗이 그를 물리쳐 그의 병거와 기병, 보병 다수를 사로잡았다(삼하 8:3-4; 대상 18:3-4). 다윗은 또한 하닷에셀의 관리들에게서 금 방패를 빼앗아 예루살렘으로 가져왔다(삼하 8:7; 대상 18:7). 다메섹의 아람 사람들이 하닷에셀을 도우러 왔을 때 다윗은 그들도 물리쳤고, 그들은 이스라엘에 복속되었다(삼하 8:5-6; 대상 18:5-6). 후에 다윗의 사신들이 암몬 사람들에게 학대당했을 때 하닷에셀은 암몬 사람들이 이스라엘을 대적하여 싸우는 것을 돕도록 자기 군대를 보냈다(삼하 10:16; 대상 19:16). 그러나 다윗의 지휘관 요압과 아비새는 아람 사람들과 암몬 사람들을 물리쳤다. 이 패배 후 하닷에셀의 동맹들은 이스라엘과 화친하고 그들에게 복속되었다(삼하 10:19; 대상 19:19). 성경 기록은 하닷에셀을 이스라엘에게 중대한 위협이 되었으나 결국 다윗과 그의 군대에게 패배한 강력한 왕으로 묘사한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah.
persons.short: Hadlai was the father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz.
persons.article: Hadlai is mentioned in 2Ch.28.12 as the father of Amasa, who was one of the leaders of Ephraim during the reign of King Ahaz of Judah. When Pekah, king of Israel, attacked Judah and took captives, some leaders of Ephraim, including Amasa son of Hadlai, opposed this action. They stood against the army of Israel and urged them to release the captives, as they believed that the Lord's fierce anger was already against Israel. The army listened to their plea and released the captives, providing them with clothing, food, and medical care before sending them back to Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.12 only referred to as Hadlai (חַדְלָ֑י); father of Amasa.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.28.12에 처음 언급되며 '하들래'라 불림. 아마사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하들래는 아하스 왕 시대에 유다 포로를 잡아오는 것을 반대한 아마사의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem.
persons.short: Hadoram was a son of Joktan and a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Hadoram is mentioned in the genealogies found in Gen.10.27 and 1Ch.1.21 as one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah. Joktan's descendants are listed as part of the Table of Nations, which records the spread of Noah's descendants after the flood. The descendants of Joktan are believed to have settled in the southern regions of the Arabian Peninsula. No further details are provided about Hadoram's life or his specific role in the family line. His mention in the genealogies serves to trace the lineage of Shem and to demonstrate the fulfillment of God's promise to Noah that his descendants would spread throughout the earth after the flood.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.27 only referred to as Hadoram (הֲדוֹרָם); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '하도람'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하도람은 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들로, 창세기와 역대상 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Hagab was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra.
persons.article: Hagab is mentioned in Ezr.2.46 as one of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity under the leadership of Zerubbabel. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. They were not of Israelite descent but were likely descendants of the Gibeonites who had been assigned by Joshua to serve in the tabernacle (Jos.9.27). Hagab and the other temple servants are listed among those who returned to help rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.2.46 only referred to as Hagab (חָגָב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.46에 처음 언급되며 '하갑'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하갑은 에스라서에 기록된 대로 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Hagabah, also known as Hagaba, was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Hagabah, also referred to as Hagaba, is mentioned in Ezr.2.45 and Neh.7.48 as one of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. They were not of Israelite descent but were likely descendants of the Gibeonites who had been assigned by Joshua to serve in the tabernacle (Jos.9.27). Hagabah and the other temple servants are listed among those who returned to help rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.45 referred to as Hagabah (חֲגָבָה), or Hagaba (חֲגָבָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.45에 처음 언급되며 '하가바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하가바(하가바라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Sarah's Egyptian maidservant; mother of Ishmael.
persons.short: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, bore Abraham a son named Ishmael and is also mentioned in Paul's allegory in Galatians.
persons.article: Hagar was an Egyptian maidservant of Sarah, Abraham's wife. When Sarah was unable to conceive, she gave Hagar to Abraham as a concubine to bear a child on her behalf, following the custom of the time (Gen.16.1-3). Hagar conceived and gave birth to a son named Ishmael (Gen.16.15). However, tensions arose between Hagar and Sarah, leading Sarah to mistreat Hagar, who then fled into the wilderness (Gen.16.4-6). An angel of the Lord appeared to Hagar, instructing her to return and submit to Sarah, and promising that her descendants would be greatly multiplied (Gen.16.7-10). Years later, after Isaac was born to Sarah, Hagar and Ishmael were sent away by Abraham at Sarah's insistence (Gen.21.9-14). God heard Ishmael's cry in the wilderness and provided for him and Hagar, promising to make Ishmael into a great nation (Gen.21.17-21). In the New Testament, Paul uses Hagar and Sarah as an allegory, with Hagar representing the old covenant of slavery under the law, and Sarah representing the new covenant of freedom through Christ (Gal.4.24-25). Hagar's story illustrates God's care for the oppressed and His faithfulness to His promises, even to those outside the primary line of Abraham's descendants.
persons.summary: A concubine living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.16.1 referred to as Hagar (הָגָר), or Hagar (Ἄγαρ); concubine of Abraham; mother of Ishmael.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '하갈'이라 불림. 아브라함의 아내. 이스마엘의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 사라의 애굽인 여종 하갈은 아브라함에게 이스마엘이라는 아들을 낳아주었고, 바울의 갈라디아서 비유에도 언급된다.
persons.article_ko: 하갈은 아브라함의 아내 사라의 애굽인 여종이었다. 사라가 잉태할 수 없었을 때 그녀는 당시의 관습에 따라 자신을 대신해 아이를 낳게 하려고 하갈을 아브라함에게 첩으로 주었다(창 16:1-3). 하갈은 잉태하여 이스마엘이라는 아들을 낳았다(창 16:15). 그러나 하갈과 사라 사이에 긴장이 발생하여 사라가 하갈을 학대하게 되었고, 그녀는 광야로 도망쳤다(창 16:4-6). 여호와의 사자가 하갈에게 나타나 돌아가 사라에게 복종하라고 지시하며 그녀의 후손이 크게 번성할 것이라고 약속했다(창 16:7-10). 여러 해 후 사라에게서 이삭이 태어난 후 하갈과 이스마엘은 사라의 고집으로 아브라함에게서 쫓겨났다(창 21:9-14). 하나님은 광야에서 이스마엘의 울음을 들으시고 그와 하갈을 돌보시며 이스마엘을 큰 민족이 되게 하시겠다고 약속하셨다(창 21:17-21). 신약에서 바울은 하갈과 사라를 비유로 사용하는데, 하갈은 율법 아래 종노릇하는 옛 언약을, 사라는 그리스도를 통한 자유의 새 언약을 나타낸다(갈 4:24-25). 하갈의 이야기는 압제받는 자들에 대한 하나님의 돌보심과 아브라함 후손의 주요 혈통 밖에 있는 이들에게조차 그분의 신실하심을 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A prophet who encouraged the rebuilding of the temple.
persons.short: Haggai, a prophet during the post-exilic period, urged the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Haggai was a prophet who lived in Jerusalem during the post-exilic period, after the Jews had returned from Babylonian captivity. He is mentioned in the book bearing his name and in Ezr.5.1 and Ezr.6.14. Haggai, along with the prophet Zechariah, played a crucial role in encouraging the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem, which had been destroyed by the Babylonians. In the second year of King Darius of Persia, Haggai delivered a series of messages to the governor of Judah, Zerubbabel, and the high priest, Joshua, urging them to resume the work on the temple (Hag.1.1, 3, 12). He confronted the people about their misplaced priorities, as they had focused on building their own houses while neglecting the house of God (Hag.1.4, 9). Haggai's prophecies also included messages of hope, assuring the people that God would bless them and that the glory of the new temple would surpass that of the former (Hag.2.9). As a result of Haggai's exhortations, the people obeyed, and the work on the temple resumed (Hag.1.12-15). The temple was eventually completed in the sixth year of King Darius (Ezr.6.14-15).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.5.1 referred to as Haggai (חַגַּי), or Haggai (Aramiac חַגַּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Ezr.5.1에 처음 언급되며 '학개'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 학개는 포로 이후 시대에 백성에게 예루살렘 성전을 재건하도록 권면했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest mentioned in Nehemiah's time.
persons.short: Haggedolim was a priest during the time of Nehemiah, mentioned in the list of priests and Levites.
persons.article: Haggedolim is mentioned briefly in Neh.11.14 as one of the priests who lived in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. He is described as a leader among his fellow priests. The name Haggedolim means "the great ones" or "the mighty ones" in Hebrew.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.14 only referred to as Haggedolim (גָּדוֹל); father of Zabdiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.14에 처음 언급되며 '하그돌림'이라 불림. 삽디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 학그돌림은 느헤미야 시대에 제사장과 레위인 명단에 언급된 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ziphion@Gen.46.16-Num, Shuni@Gen.46.16-Num, Ezbon@Gen.46.16-Num, Eri@Gen.46.16-Num, Arod@Gen.46.16-Num, Areli@Gen.46.16-Num
persons.brief: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob.
persons.short: Haggi was a son of Gad and a grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.
persons.article: Haggi is mentioned in Gen.46.16 and Num.26.15 as one of the sons of Gad, who was one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). In the genealogy of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt during the famine, Haggi is listed among the sons of Gad. The descendants of Haggi are referred to as the Haggites in Num.26.15, where they are counted as part of the tribe of Gad in the census taken in the wilderness.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.16 referred to as Haggi or Haggite (חַגִּי); son of Gad; a brother of Ziphion, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arod and Areli.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.16에 처음 언급되며 '학기'라 불림. 갓의 아들. 시뵨, 수니, 에스본, 에리, 아롯과 아렐리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 학기는 갓의 아들이며 야곱의 손자로, 창세기와 민수기 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite, descendant of Merari.
persons.short: Haggiah, a Levite descended from Merari, is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Haggiah is mentioned in 1Ch.6.30 as part of the genealogy of the Levites, specifically the descendants of Merari, one of the three sons of Levi. He is listed as the son of Shimea and the father of Asaiah. The Levites were the tribe chosen by God to assist the priests in the tabernacle and temple services. The descendants of Merari were responsible for the structural components of the tabernacle, such as the frames, crossbars, posts, and bases (Num.3.36).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.30 only referred to as Haggiah (חַגִּיָּה); a son of Shimea; father of Asaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.30에 처음 언급되며 '학기야'라 불림. 시므아의 아들. 아사야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 학기야는 므라리를 통한 레위인 후손으로, 역대상 레위인 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's wives; mother of Adonijah.
persons.short: Haggith was one of King David's wives and the mother of Adonijah, who attempted to claim the throne.
persons.article: Haggith was one of King David's wives and the mother of Adonijah, who was David's fourth son (2Sa.3.4, 1 Chronicles 2Sa.3.2). Adonijah was born in Hebron during the early years of David's reign. After the death of his older brothers Amnon and Absalom, Adonijah considered himself the heir to the throne and attempted to claim it while David was still alive (1Ki.1.5). He gained the support of Joab, the commander of the army, and Abiathar, the priest (1Ki.1.7). However, David had promised Bathsheba that their son Solomon would be the next king (1Ki.1.17). When David was informed of Adonijah's actions, he ordered Solomon to be anointed as king (1Ki.1.32-35). Fearing for his life, Adonijah sought asylum by clinging to the horns of the altar (1Ki.1.50). Solomon spared his life on the condition that he would show himself to be a worthy man (1Ki.1.52-53). Later, Adonijah made a request to Solomon through Bathsheba, asking for Abishag, David's nurse, to be given to him as a wife (1Ki.2.13-17). Solomon perceived this as a threat to his throne and ordered Adonijah to be put to death (1Ki.2.23-25).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.4 only referred to as Haggith (חַגִּית); wife of David; mother of Adonijah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 2Sa.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '학깃'이라 불림. 다윗의 아내. 아도니야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 학깃은 다윗 왕의 아내 중 한 사람으로, 왕위를 차지하려 한 아도니야의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite, father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men.
persons.short: Hagri was the father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men from the tribe of Gad.
persons.article: Hagri is mentioned in 1Ch.11.38 as the father of Mibhar, who was one of King David's mighty men. Mibhar is described as a Gadite, indicating that Hagri was also from the tribe of Gad. The Gadites were known for their bravery and military prowess, as they were among the first to join David when he was fleeing from King Saul (1Ch.12.8-15).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.5.10 referred to as Hagri or Hagrite (הַגְרִי); father of Mibhar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.5.10에 처음 언급되며 '하갈'이라 불림. 밉할의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하그리는 갓 지파 출신 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 미브할의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Johanan, a leader who returned from Babylon.
persons.short: Hakkatan was the father of Johanan, a leader who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hakkatan is mentioned in Ezr.8.12 as the father of Johanan, who was one of the leaders that returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile. Johanan is described as "of the sons of Azgad" and was accompanied by 110 males. The return from exile was a significant event in Jewish history, as it marked the end of the Babylonian captivity and the beginning of the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple. Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem and was instrumental in teaching the people the Law of Moses and instituting religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.12 only referred to as Hakkatan (קָטָן); father of Johanan.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.12에 처음 언급되며 '학가단'이라 불림. 요하난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 학갓단은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자 요하난의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A priest in the time of David.
persons.short: Hakkoz was a priest who served during the reign of King David, as mentioned in the priestly divisions.
persons.article: Hakkoz is mentioned in 1Ch.24.10 as one of the priests who served during the reign of King David. He was the head of the seventh priestly division, as organized by David. The priests were divided into 24 divisions, each responsible for serving in the temple for a week at a time, twice a year. This system ensured that all the priestly families had an opportunity to serve and that the temple services were conducted in an orderly manner.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.10 only referred to as Hakkoz (הַקוֹץ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.10에 처음 언급되며 '학고스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 학고스는 다윗 왕 시대 제사장 반차 명단에 언급된 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A post-exilic priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood.
persons.short: Hakkoz was a priest whose descendants were unable to prove their priestly lineage after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hakkoz is mentioned in Ezr.2.61 and Neh.7.63 as one of the priests who returned from the Babylonian exile. However, when the genealogies of the priests were examined, the descendants of Hakkoz were unable to prove their priestly lineage. As a result, they were considered unclean and were excluded from serving as priests. The governor ordered them not to eat from the most holy things until a priest with the Urim and Thummim could resolve the matter. The Urim and Thummim were sacred objects used to determine the will of God. The fact that the descendants of Hakkoz could not provide clear genealogical records suggests that their priestly lineage may have been lost or compromised during the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.61 only referred to as Hakkoz (הַקוֹץ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.61에 처음 언급되며 '학고스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 학고스는 바벨론 포로 이후 그 후손들이 제사장 족보를 증명하지 못한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Hakkoz, a priest, was involved in repairing sections of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Hakkoz is mentioned in Neh.3.4 and Neh.3.21 as one of the priests who participated in repairing the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. In Neh.3.4, Hakkoz is described as one of the priests who made repairs to a section of the wall. Later, in Neh.3.21, Meremoth, the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, is mentioned as repairing another section of the wall near his house. The rebuilding of the wall was a significant event in the history of Jerusalem, as it provided security and stability for the city and its inhabitants after the return from Babylonian exile. The participation of priests like Hakkoz in the rebuilding effort demonstrates the importance of the project and the unity of the people in working towards a common goal.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.3.4 only referred to as Hakkoz (הַקוֹץ); father of Uriah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '학고스'라 불림. 우리아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 학고스는 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽의 일부를 수리하는 일에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Hakupha was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Hakupha is mentioned in Ezr.2.51 and Neh.7.53 as one of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. They were not of Israelite descent but were likely descendants of the Gibeonites who had been assigned by Joshua to serve in the tabernacle (Jos.9.27). Hakupha and the other temple servants are listed among those who returned to help rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.51 only referred to as Hakupha (חֲקוּפָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.51에 처음 언급되며 '하그바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하굽바는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Hallohesh was the father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Hallohesh is mentioned in Neh.3.12 and Neh.10.24 as the father of Shallum, who was a leader during the time of Nehemiah. In Neh.3.12, Shallum, the son of Hallohesh, is described as the leader of half the district of Jerusalem. He and his daughters participated in repairing a section of the wall of Jerusalem. The rebuilding of the wall was a significant event in the history of Jerusalem, as it provided security and stability for the city and its inhabitants after the return from Babylonian exile. In Neh.10.24, Hallohesh is listed among the leaders who sealed the covenant to follow the Law of God. This covenant was a solemn agreement by the people to obey God's commands and to support the temple service.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.3.12 only referred to as Hallohesh (הַלּוֹחֵשׁ); father of Shallum.
persons.short_ko: 할로헤스는 느헤미야 시대 예루살렘 지방 절반을 다스리며 성벽 중수를 이끌었다.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.12에 처음 언급되며 '할로헤스'라 불림. 살룸의 아버지.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: One of Noah's three sons, father of Canaan.
persons.short: Ham, one of Noah's three sons, was the father of Canaan and the ancestor of various nations.
persons.article: Ham was one of the three sons of Noah, along with Shem and Japheth (Gen.5.32; 6.10). He and his wife were among the eight people who survived the great flood in Noah's ark (Gen.7.13). After the flood, Ham became the father of Canaan (Gen.9.18). An incident occurred in which Ham saw his father Noah naked and informed his brothers (Gen.9.22). When Noah awoke and learned of Ham's actions, he pronounced a curse on Canaan, Ham's son (Gen.9.24-25). Ham is also mentioned as the ancestor of various nations, including the Cushites, Egyptians, Put, and Canaanites (Gen.10.6-20). These nations are often referred to as the "sons of Ham" and are generally associated with the regions of Africa and the Middle East. In the Table of Nations (Genesis 10), Ham's descendants are listed, providing insight into the geographical distribution of ancient people groups. Ham's significance in the Bible lies primarily in his role as the father of Canaan and the ancestor of nations that would later play important roles in the history of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.5.32 only referred to as Ham (חָם); son of Noah; a brother of Shem and Japheth; father of Canaan, Cush, Egypt and Put.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.5.32에 처음 언급되며 '함'이라 불림. 노아와 나아마의 아들. 셈과 야벳의 형제. 가나안, 구스, 미스라임과 붓의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함은 노아의 세 아들 중 한 사람이며 가나안의 아버지이자 여러 민족의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.offspring: Parshandatha@Est.9.7, Dalphon@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Parmashta@Est.9.9, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9, Vaizatha@Est.9.9
persons.brief: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
persons.short: Haman, a high-ranking Persian official, conspired to kill all the Jews in the empire but was ultimately thwarted by Queen Esther and Mordecai.
persons.article: Haman is the primary antagonist in the book of Esther. He was an Agagite, a descendant of the Amalekite kings, and a high-ranking official in the Persian Empire during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). Haman was promoted to a position of authority and commanded all the royal officials to bow down to him (Est.3.1-2). However, Mordecai, a Jew, refused to bow to Haman (Est.3.2-4). Enraged, Haman plotted to destroy not only Mordecai but all the Jews in the empire (Est.3.5-6). He convinced the king to issue a decree ordering the extermination of the Jews (Est.3.8-15). Haman also had a gallows built to hang Mordecai (Est.5.14). However, Haman's plans were thwarted by Queen Esther, who revealed her Jewish identity to the king and exposed Haman's plot (Est.7.1-6). The king ordered Haman to be hanged on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai (Est.7.7-10). Haman's ten sons were also executed (Est.9.10-14). The king then issued a new decree, allowing the Jews to defend themselves against their enemies (Est.8.1-14). Haman's story serves as a powerful example of how God can use individuals to protect His people and bring about justice, even in the face of great adversity.
persons.summary: A man of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.3.1 only referred to as Haman (הָמָן); a son of Hammedatha; husband of Zeresh; father of Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, Vaizatha.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 페르시아 사람. Est.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '하만'이라 불림. 함므다다의 아들. 세레스의 남편. 바산다다, 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새, 아리대와 왜사다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함은 고위 페르시아 관리로, 제국의 모든 유대인을 죽이려 음모했으나 에스더 왕비와 모르드개에 의해 좌절되었다.
persons.article_ko: 하만은 에스더서의 주요 적대자였다. 그는 아각 사람으로 아말렉 왕들의 후손이며, 아하수에로 왕(크세르크세스 1세) 통치 기간 동안 페르시아 제국의 고위 관리였다. 하만은 권세 있는 지위로 승진하여 모든 왕실 관리에게 자신에게 절하라고 명령했다(에 3:1-2). 그러나 유대인 모르드개는 하만에게 절하기를 거부했다(에 3:2-4). 격분한 하만은 모르드개뿐 아니라 제국의 모든 유대인을 멸하려는 음모를 꾸몄다(에 3:5-6). 그는 왕을 설득하여 유대인 학살을 명령하는 조서를 내리게 했다(에 3:8-15). 하만은 또한 모르드개를 매달 교수대를 세웠다(에 5:14). 그러나 하만의 계획은 에스더 왕비에 의해 좌절되었는데, 그녀는 왕에게 자신의 유대인 정체를 밝히고 하만의 음모를 폭로했다(에 7:1-6). 왕은 하만이 모르드개를 위해 준비한 바로 그 교수대에 그를 매달도록 명령했다(에 7:7-10). 하만의 열 아들도 처형되었다(에 9:10-14). 그런 다음 왕은 유대인들이 원수들을 대적하여 스스로를 방어할 수 있도록 허락하는 새 조서를 내렸다(에 8:1-14). 하만의 이야기는 하나님이 큰 역경 속에서도 자기 백성을 보호하고 정의를 이루시기 위해 사람들을 사용하실 수 있다는 강력한 본보기가 된다.

persons.description: People from Hamath(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: A Canaanite people group descended from Canaan.
persons.short: The Hamathites were a Canaanite people group descended from Canaan, son of Ham.
persons.article: The Hamathites were a Canaanite people group mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10.18; 1Ch.1.16). They were descendants of Canaan, the son of Ham and grandson of Noah. The Hamathites were named after the city of Hamath, located in modern-day Syria, which was their primary settlement. Hamath was an important city-state in ancient times, known for its strategic location along trade routes. The Hamathites were one of the many Canaanite groups that inhabited the region before the Israelites settled in the land. In later biblical history, Hamath is mentioned as one of the kingdoms that bordered Israel during the reigns of David and Solomon (2Sa.8.9-10; 1Ki.8.65). The Hamathites, along with other Canaanite groups, were eventually conquered and assimilated by the Israelites as they took possession of the Promised Land.
persons.summary: People from Hamath(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at Gen.10.18 only referred to as Hamathites (חֲמָתִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites and Zemarites.
persons.summary_ko: 하맛 족속. Gen.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '하맛'이라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓과 스말의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 하맛 족속은 함의 아들 가나안의 후손인 가나안 족속이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Kenite clan, descendants of Salma.
persons.short: Hammath was a Kenite clan, listed among the descendants of Salma, the  father (ie founder) of Bethlehem.
persons.article: Hammath is mentioned in 1Ch.2.55 as one of the Kenite clans descended from Salma, the father (ie founder) of Bethlehem. The Kenites were a nomadic tribe closely associated with the Israelites, particularly during the time of Moses and the Exodus. Some Kenites, such as Jethro (Moses' father-in-law), played important roles in Israel's history. The mention of Hammath in the genealogy of Judah suggests that this Kenite clan had integrated with the tribe of Judah and settled in or near Bethlehem.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.55 only referred to as Hammath (חַמַּת); father or founder of Rechabites.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.55에 처음 언급되며 '함맛'이라 불림. 레갑의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함맛은 베들레헴의 창설자 살마의 후손 명단에 나오는 겐 족속 가문이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: The father of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.
persons.short: Hammedatha was the father of Haman, the Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews in the book of Esther.
persons.article: Hammedatha is mentioned in the book of Esther as the father of Haman, the primary antagonist who plotted to destroy the Jews in the Persian Empire. He is identified as an Agagite (Est.3.1, which suggests that he may have been a descendant of Agag, the Amalekite king who was defeated by King Saul )(1Samuel 15). Hammedatha's son, Haman, rose to a high position in the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) and used his influence to persuade the king to issue a decree ordering the extermination of all Jews in the empire (Est.3.8-15). However, Queen Esther and her cousin Mordecai ultimately thwarted Haman's plans, leading to his downfall and execution, along with his ten sons (Esther 7-9). The mention of Hammedatha in the book of Esther serves to provide background information on Haman's lineage and to emphasize the long-standing enmity between the Amalekites and the Israelites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.3.1 only referred to as Hammedatha (הַמְּדָתָא); father of Haman.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '함므다다'라 불림. 하만의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함므다다는 에스더서에서 유대인을 멸하려 음모한 페르시아 관리 하만의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials during Jeremiah's time.
persons.short: Hammelech, meaning "the king," was the father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials mentioned in the book of Jeremiah.
persons.article: Hammelech, which means "the king" in Hebrew, is mentioned in Jer.36.26 and Jer.38.6 as the father of two officials during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah. In Jer.36.26, Jerahmeel, the son of Hammelech, is identified as one of the officials sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet after the king burned the scroll containing Jeremiah's prophecies. In Jer.38.6, Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), another son of Hammelech, is mentioned as one of the officials who threw Jeremiah into a cistern at the request of the princes who opposed the prophet's message. The use of the term "Hammelech" in these passages has led some scholars to believe that it may be a title rather than a proper name, indicating that Jerahmeel and Malchiah were royal officials. However, the exact nature of their roles and their relationship to the king remains unclear.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.36.26 only referred to as Hammelech (הַמֶּלֶךְ); father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah. also translated "the king";
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '왕'이라 불림. 여라므엘과 말기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: '왕'이라는 뜻의 함멜렉은 예레미야서에 언급된 관리 여라므엘과 말기야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Sister of Gilead; mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
persons.short: Hammolecheth, the sister of Gilead, was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
persons.article: Hammolecheth is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.7.18 as the sister of Gilead, who was a descendant of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. She is described as the mother of three individuals: Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah. Abiezer is notable as the clan from which Gideon, one of the judges of Israel, descended (Jdg.6.11, 24). The name Hammolecheth is unusual, as it is a feminine form of the Hebrew word "melech," meaning "king." Some scholars suggest that this name may indicate a position of authority or leadership held by Hammolecheth within her family or clan. However, no further details about her life or role are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.18 only referred to as Hammolecheth (הַמֹּלֶכֶת); daughter of Machir; a sister of Gilead, daughter of Machir, Peresh and Sheresh; mother of Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.7.18에 처음 언급되며 '함몰레겟'이라 불림. 마길과 마아가의 딸. 길르앗, 마길의 딸(이름 미상), 베레스와 세레스의 자매. 함몰레겟의 남편(이름 미상)의 아내. 이스홋, 아비에셀과 말라의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 길르앗의 자매 함몰레겟은 이스홋, 아비에셀, 마흘라의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mishma, a descendant of Simeon.
persons.short: Hammuel, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Mishma.
persons.article: Hammuel is mentioned in 1Ch.4.26 as a descendant of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. He is identified as the son of Mishma and is listed in the genealogy of Simeon. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles provide a record of the families and clans within each of the Israelite tribes, highlighting their lineage and descent from the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The mention of Hammuel in this genealogy serves to demonstrate the continuity of Simeon's lineage and to provide a historical record of his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.26 only referred to as Hammuel (חַמּוּאֵל); a son of Mishma; father of Zaccur.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.26에 처음 언급되며 '함무엘'이라 불림. 미스마의 아들. 삭굴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함무엘은 시므온의 후손으로 미스마의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A Hivite prince, father of Shechem.
persons.short: Hamor, a Hivite prince, was the father and founder of Shechem and negotiated with Jacob's sons after Shechem's assault on Dinah.
persons.article: Hamor was a Hivite who founded the city of Shechem during the time of the patriarchs. His son was called Shechem, after whom the city was named (Gen.33.19). When Israel (or 'Jacob') and his family settled near Shechem, Hamor's son Shechem assaulted Jacob's daughter Dinah (Gen.34.2). Hamor and Shechem sought to arrange a marriage between Shechem and Dinah and proposed that their people intermarry with Jacob's family (Gen.34.8-10). Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, deceitfully agreed on the condition that all the men of Shechem be circumcised (Gen.34.13-24). However, while the men of Shechem were recovering from the circumcision, Simeon and Levi attacked the city, killed Hamor and Shechem, and rescued Dinah (Gen.34.25-29). The land that Jacob had purchased from Hamor became a possession of the Israelites and was later allocated to the tribe of Manasseh (Jos.24.32). In the time of the judges, Gaal son of Ebed challenged Abimelech's rule in Shechem, invoking the memory of Hamor as the city's ancestral leader (Jdg.9.28). In Act.7.16, Stephen mentions that Abraham bought a tomb from the sons of Hamor in Shechem, which may refer to the same transaction or a separate one.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.33.19 referred to as Hamor (חֲמוֹר), or Hamor (Ἐμμόρ); father of Shechem; founder of Shechem.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.33.19에 처음 언급되며 '하몰'이라 불림. 세겜과 세겜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 히위 사람 방백 하몰은 세겜의 아버지이자 창설자로, 세겜이 디나를 범한 후 야곱의 아들들과 협상했다.
persons.article_ko: 하몰은 족장 시대에 세겜 성읍을 세운 히위 사람이었다. 그의 아들은 세겜이라 불렸는데, 그 이름을 따서 성읍의 이름이 지어졌다(창 33:19). 이스라엘(야곱)과 그의 가족이 세겜 근처에 정착했을 때 하몰의 아들 세겜은 야곱의 딸 디나를 강간했다(창 34:2). 하몰과 세겜은 세겜과 디나의 결혼을 주선하고자 했고 그들의 백성이 야곱의 가족과 통혼하자고 제안했다(창 34:8-10). 야곱의 아들들인 시므온과 레위는 세겜의 모든 남자가 할례를 받는다는 조건으로 속임수를 써서 동의했다(창 34:13-24). 그러나 세겜 사람들이 할례에서 회복되는 동안 시므온과 레위는 그 성을 공격하여 하몰과 세겜을 죽이고 디나를 구출했다(창 34:25-29). 야곱이 하몰에게서 산 땅은 이스라엘 백성의 소유가 되었고 후에 므낫세 지파에게 분배되었다(수 24:32). 사사 시대에 에벳의 아들 가알은 아비멜렉의 세겜 통치에 도전하며 그 성읍의 조상 지도자로서 하몰을 언급했다(삿 9:28). 사도행전 7:16에서 스데반은 아브라함이 세겜에 있는 하몰의 아들들에게서 무덤을 샀다고 언급하는데, 이는 같은 거래이거나 별도의 거래를 가리킬 수 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Perez, grandson of Judah.
persons.short: Hamul was a son of Perez and a grandson of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Hamul was a son of Perez and a grandson of Judah, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.46.12; 1Ch.2.5). He was born to Perez, who was the son of Judah and Tamar (Gen.38.29). Hamul is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which is recorded in the book of Genesis when Jacob and his family moved to Egypt during the famine (Gen.46.12). He is also listed in the census of the Israelites taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.21). The descendants of Hamul, known as the Hamulites, are mentioned as one of the clans of the tribe of Judah (Num.26.21).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.12 referred to as Hamul (חָמוּל), or Hamulite (חָמוּלִי); son of Perez; a brother of Hezron.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.12에 처음 언급되며 '하물'이라 불림. 베레스의 아들. 헤스론의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하물은 베레스의 아들이며 유다의 손자로, 창세기와 민수기, 역대상 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, kings of Judah.
persons.short: Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, was the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, two kings of Judah.
persons.article: Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah and the mother of two kings of Judah: Jehoahaz and Zedekiah (2Ki.23.31; 24.18). Jehoahaz, also known as Shallum, became king after the death of his father, King Josiah (1Ch.3.15). However, he reigned for only three months before being deposed by Pharaoh Necho of Egypt (2Ki.23.31-34). Zedekiah, Hamutal's other son, was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile. He was appointed as king by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, after the deportation of his nephew, King Jehoiachin (2Ki.24.17-18). Zedekiah reigned for eleven years but ultimately rebelled against Babylon, leading to the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple (2Ki.25.1-10). The mention of Hamutal in the genealogies of the kings of Judah highlights the importance of maternal lineage in the royal succession and provides insight into the political dynamics of the time.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.23.31 referred to as Hamutal (חֲמוּטַל); a daughter of Jeremiah; wife of Josiah; mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.23.31에 처음 언급되며 '하무달'이라 불림. 예레미야의 딸. 요시야의 아내. 여호아하스와 시드기야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 립나 사람 예레미야의 딸 하무달은 유다 왕 여호아하스와 시드기야의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Jeremiah's cousin, from whom he bought a field.
persons.short: Hanamel, Jeremiah's cousin, sold a field to the prophet as a sign of future restoration during the Babylonian siege.
persons.article: Hanamel was the cousin of the prophet Jeremiah and is mentioned in the context of Jeremiah's purchase of a field during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem (Jer.32.7-12). While Jeremiah was imprisoned in the court of the guard, the word of the Lord came to him, revealing that Hanamel would come and offer to sell him a field in Anathoth, Jeremiah's hometown (Jer.32.7-8). As prophesied, Hanamel visited Jeremiah and offered to sell him the field, which was Jeremiah's right to redeem as a close relative (Jer.32.8). Jeremiah purchased the field, weighed out the money, signed and sealed the deed, and had it witnessed (Jer.32.9-12). This transaction served as a symbolic act, demonstrating Jeremiah's faith in God's promise that houses, fields, and vineyards would once again be bought in the land of Judah, despite the impending Babylonian conquest (Jer.32.15). The purchase of the field from Hanamel was a sign of hope and future restoration for the people of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.32.7 only referred to as Hanamel (חֲנַמְאֵל); a son of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.32.7에 처음 언급되며 '하나멜'이라 불림. 살룸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 예레미야의 사촌 하나멜은 바벨론 포위 기간 동안 미래의 회복을 상징하는 표징으로 그에게 밭을 팔았다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Maacah.
persons.short: Hanan, the son of Maacah, was one of King David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Hanan, the son of Maacah, is mentioned in 1Ch.11.43 as one of King David's mighty warriors. The mighty warriors were a group of elite soldiers who served under David and were renowned for their bravery, strength, and military prowess. They played a crucial role in establishing and maintaining David's kingdom, fighting in various battles and campaigns. The mention of Hanan in this list highlights his exceptional skills as a warrior and his loyalty to King David.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.43 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן); a son of Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.43에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림. 마아가의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마아가의 아들 하난은 다윗 왕의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ishpan@1Ch.8.22, Eber@1Ch.8.22, Eliel@1Ch.8.22, Abdon@1Ch.8.23, Zichri@1Ch.8.23, Hananiah@1Ch.8.24, Elam@1Ch.8.24, Anthothijah@1Ch.8.24, Iphdeiah@1Ch.8.25, Penuel@1Ch.8.25
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Shashak.
persons.short: Hanan, a Benjamite, was the son of Shashak, as mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.8.23 as a son of Shashak, a Benjamite. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which is recorded in the book of 1 Chronicles. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles provide a record of the families and clans within each of the Israelite tribes, highlighting their lineage and descent from the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The mention of Hanan in this genealogy serves to demonstrate the continuity of Benjamin's lineage and to provide a historical record of his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.23 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן); son of Shashak; a brother of Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah and Penuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.23에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림. 사삭의 아들. 이스반, 에벨, 엘리엘, 압돈, 시그리, 하나냐, 엘람, 안도디야, 이브드야와 브누엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 사람 하난은 사삭의 아들로, 역대상 베냐민 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Azel, a descendant of King Saul.
persons.short: Hanan, a descendant of King Saul, was the son of Azel, as mentioned in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned in 1Ch.8.38 and 1Ch.9.44 as one of the sons of Azel, a descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of Saul's family, which is recorded in the book of 1 Chronicles. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles provide a record of the families and clans within each of the Israelite tribes, highlighting their lineage and descent from notable figures such as King Saul. The mention of Hanan in this genealogy serves to demonstrate the continuity of Saul's lineage and to provide a historical record of his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.38 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן); son of Azel; a brother of Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah and Obadiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.38에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림. 아셀의 아들. 아스리감, 보그루, 이스마엘, 스아랴와 오바댜의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사울의 후손 하난은 아셀의 아들로, 역대상 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Hanan was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned in Ezr.2.46 and Neh.7.49 as one of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. They were not of Israelite descent but were likely descendants of the Gibeonites who had been assigned by Joshua to serve in the tabernacle (Jos.9.27). Hanan and the other temple servants are listed among those who returned to help rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.46 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.46에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하난은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Igdaliah, associated with the Rechabites.
persons.short: Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, was associated with the Rechabites and had a chamber in the temple during Jeremiah's time.
persons.article: Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, is mentioned in Jer.35.4 in connection with the Rechabites. The Rechabites were a nomadic tribe known for their commitment to abstaining from wine, living in tents, and following the commands of their ancestor, Jonadab son of Rechab. During the reign of King Jehoiakim, Jeremiah was instructed by God to bring the Rechabites to the temple and offer them wine to drink. The Rechabites refused, demonstrating their steadfast obedience to their ancestor's commands. The chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, was used for this encounter. Hanan is described as "the man of God," indicating his prophetic or priestly role. The location of this chamber in the temple suggests that Hanan held a position of importance or respect within the religious community. The association of Hanan with the Rechabites and the use of his chamber for Jeremiah's test highlights the significance of the Rechabites' commitment to their principles and their role as an example of obedience to God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.35.4 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן); a son of Igdaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.35.4에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림. 익다랴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 익다랴의 아들 하난은 레갑 족속과 관련이 있었으며 예레미야 시대에 성전에 방을 가지고 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Hanan, a Levite, was among those who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow God's Law.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned in Neh.10.22 as one of the Levites who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God. After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a solemn covenant to obey God's commandments and to support the temple service (Nehemiah 9-10). The covenant was sealed by the signatures of the leaders, priests, and Levites, including Hanan. This event demonstrated the commitment of the post-exilic community to God and their determination to live according to His laws.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.22 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 하난은 느헤미야가 이끈 하나님의 율법을 따르는 언약에 서명했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Another Levite who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.short: Hanan, a Levite, was among the signatories of the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow God's Law.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned in Neh.10.26 as another Levite who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God. This Hanan is listed separately from the Hanan mentioned in Neh.10.22, indicating that they were two different individuals. After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a solemn covenant to obey God's commandments and to support the temple service (Nehemiah 9-10). The covenant was sealed by the signatures of the leaders, priests, and Levites, including this Hanan. This event demonstrated the commitment of the post-exilic community to God and their determination to live according to His laws.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.26 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 하난은 느헤미야가 이끈 언약에 서명한 또 다른 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A treasurer appointed by Nehemiah for the storehouses.
persons.short: Hanan, the son of Zaccur, was appointed by Nehemiah as one of the treasurers responsible for the storehouses.
persons.article: Hanan, the son of Zaccur, is mentioned in Neh.13.13 as one of the treasurers appointed by Nehemiah to oversee the storehouses. Nehemiah assigned four reliable men, including Hanan, to distribute the portions due to the priests and Levites from the tithes and offerings collected in the storehouses. This appointment was made to ensure the fair distribution of resources and to support the temple service. Nehemiah's choice of Hanan and the other treasurers was based on their trustworthiness and integrity. The appointment of dedicated individuals like Hanan helped maintain the proper functioning of the temple and the support of its personnel in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.13.13 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן); a son of Zaccur.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림. 삭굴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 삭굴의 아들 하난은 느헤미야가 곳간을 관리하도록 임명한 재무관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who helped explain the Law to the people.
persons.short: Hanan, a Levite, assisted Ezra in teaching the Law to the people during the post-exilic period.
persons.article: Hanan is mentioned in Neh.8.7 as one of the Levites who helped Ezra, the priest and scribe, in explaining the Law to the people. After the return from Babylonian exile, Ezra read the Book of the Law to the assembled Israelites during the Feast of Tabernacles (Neh.8.1-3). Hanan, along with several other Levites, stood beside Ezra and helped the people understand the Law, translating and explaining it clearly (Neh.8.7-8). This event marked a significant moment in the spiritual revival of the post-exilic community, as the people rediscovered and recommitted themselves to the teachings of the Law. In Neh.10.10, Hanan is also listed among the Levites who signed the covenant to follow the Law of God, demonstrating his commitment to the spiritual renewal of the people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.8.7 only referred to as Hanan (חָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 하난은 포로 이후 시대에 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 가르치는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: A musician in the temple during David's reign.
persons.short: Hanani was a temple musician during King David's reign, assigned to the twenty-fifth division.
persons.article: Hanani is mentioned in 1Ch.25.4 and 1Ch.25.25 as one of the temple musicians during the reign of King David. He was among the sons of Heman, the king's seer, who were appointed to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals in the temple service. Hanani and his brothers were skilled musicians, trained in singing to the Lord. In the organization of the temple musicians, Hanani was assigned to the twenty-fifth division (1Ch.25.25). The temple musicians played a crucial role in the worship services, providing music and leading the people in praise to God. The mention of Hanani in this context highlights the importance of music and worship in the temple during David's reign.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Hanani (חֲנָנִי); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
persons.short_ko: 하나니는 헤만의 열넷 아들 중 한 명으로 성전에서 음악을 담당했다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '하나니'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A seer who prophesied during the reign of Asa.
persons.short: Hanani, a seer, prophesied during the reigns of Asa and Jehoshaphat, kings of Judah.
persons.article: Hanani was a seer who prophesied during the reigns of King Asa and King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He first appears in 1Ki.16.1, where he delivered a message from God to King Baasha of Israel, warning him of judgment for his evil deeds. Later, during the reign of King Asa of Judah, Hanani rebuked the king for relying on the king of Aram instead of trusting in the Lord (2Ch.16.7). As a result, Asa became angry and imprisoned Hanani. Despite this, Hanani's prophecy came true, and Asa suffered from a severe foot disease in his old age (2Ch.16.12). Hanani is also mentioned in connection with King Jehoshaphat, Asa's son. After Jehoshaphat formed an alliance with King Ahab of Israel, Hanani's son, Jehu, prophesied against Jehoshaphat (2Ch.19.2). The account of Jehoshaphat's reign, including his accomplishments and the events during his time, was recorded in the annals of Hanani the seer (2Ch.20.34). Hanani's prophetic ministry spanned multiple generations, and his messages focused on the importance of trusting in God and the consequences of disobedience.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.1 only referred to as Hanani (חֲנָנִי); father of Jehu.
persons.short_ko: 하나니는 선지자 예후의 아버지로 유다 왕 아사를 책망한 선견자다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 1Ki.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '하나니'라 불림. 예후의 아버지.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A returnee from Babylon who had married a foreign wife.
persons.short: Hanani was among the returnees from Babylon who had married foreign wives during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Hanani is mentioned in Ezr.10.20 as one of the men who had returned from the Babylonian exile and had married foreign wives. During the time of Ezra, the Israelites who had returned to Jerusalem were found to have intermarried with the neighboring peoples, going against God's command to maintain their purity and separation. Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a reform to address this issue. He called an assembly and urged the people to confess their sin and separate themselves from their foreign wives. Hanani was among those listed who had taken foreign wives and pledged to put them away. This event demonstrates the importance of obedience to God's laws and the need for the returned exiles to maintain their distinct identity as God's chosen people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.20 only referred to as Hanani (חֲנָנִי).
persons.brief_ko: 이방 여인과 결혼했다가 돌려보낸 제사장 자손
persons.short_ko: 하나니는 에스라 시대 이방 여인을 아내로 삼았다가 돌려보낸 임멜 자손 중 한 명이다.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.20에 처음 언급되며 '하나니'라 불림.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Nehemiah's brother, who reported on Jerusalem's condition.
persons.short: Hanani, Nehemiah's brother, brought a report about the dire situation in Jerusalem, prompting Nehemiah to take action.
