He, along with Malchijah, repaired another section of the wall and the Tower of the Ovens. Pahath-moab was likely a family or clan name, indicating that Hasshub belonged to this group. His participation in the rebuilding of the wall demonstrates the involvement of various families and individuals in the restoration of Jerusalem. (Neh.3.11).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.11 only referred to as Hasshub (חַשּׁוּב); a son of Pahath-moab.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.11에 처음 언급되며 '핫숩'이라 불림. 바핫모압의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압의 아들 핫숩은 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A repairer of Jerusalem's wall opposite his house.
persons.short: Hasshub repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall opposite his house.
persons.article: Hasshub is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped repair Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah. He repaired a section of the wall opposite his house, along with Benjamin. This suggests that Hasshub lived in Jerusalem and had a personal stake in the city's restoration. His participation in the rebuilding of the wall demonstrates the involvement of various individuals in the restoration of Jerusalem. (Neh.3.23).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.23 only referred to as Hasshub (חַשּׁוּב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '핫숩'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 핫숩은 자기 집 맞은편 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Hasupha was an ancestor of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hasupha is mentioned as an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a class of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. In the lists of returnees recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Hasupha are mentioned among the temple servants. No further information about Hasupha is provided in the Bible. (Ezr.2.43; Neh.7.46).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.43 only referred to as Hasupha (חֲשׂוּפָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.43에 처음 언급되며 '하수바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하수바는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A eunuch in the court of King Ahasuerus.
persons.short: Hathach was a eunuch who served Queen Esther and acted as a messenger between her and Mordecai.
persons.article: Hathach was a eunuch who served in the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) of Persia during the time of Queen Esther. He is mentioned in the book of Esther as a messenger between Esther and her cousin Mordecai. When Mordecai learned of a plot to destroy the Jews, he sent word to Esther through Hathach, urging her to intervene with the king on behalf of her people. Hathach faithfully delivered messages between Esther and Mordecai, playing a crucial role in the communication that ultimately led to the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's evil plan. (Est.4.5,6,9,10).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.4.5 only referred to as Hathach (הֲתָךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.4.5에 처음 언급되며 '하닥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하닥은 에스더 왕비를 섬긴 내시로, 그녀와 모르드개 사이의 전령 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Othniel, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Hathath was a son of Othniel, the son of Kenaz, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Hathath is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in the book of 1 Chronicles. He was a son of Othniel, who was the son of Kenaz. Othniel was a notable figure in the tribe of Judah, known for his military prowess and for being the first judge of Israel after the death of Joshua. No further information is provided about Hathath in the Bible. (1Ch.4.13).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.13 only referred to as Hathath (חֲתַת); son of Othniel whose wife was Achsah; a brother of Meonothai(?).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.4.13에 처음 언급되며 '하닷'이라 불림. 옷니엘과 악사의 아들. 므오노대의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하닷은 그나스의 아들 옷니엘의 아들로 유다 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Hatipha was an ancestor of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hatipha is mentioned as an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The temple servants were a class of people assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. In the lists of returnees recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Hatipha are mentioned among the temple servants. No further information about Hatipha is provided in the Bible. (Ezr.2.54; Neh.7.56).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.54 only referred to as Hatipha (חֲטִיפָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.54에 처음 언급되며 '하디바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하디바는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of gatekeepers who returned from exile.
persons.short: Hatita was an ancestor of gatekeepers who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hatita is mentioned as an ancestor of a group of gatekeepers who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the gates of the temple and maintaining order within its precincts. In the lists of returnees recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Hatita are mentioned among the gatekeepers. No further information about Hatita is provided in the Bible. (Ezr.2.42; Neh.7.45).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.42 only referred to as Hatita (חֲטִיטָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.42에 처음 언급되며 '하디다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하디다는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 문지기 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Hattil was an ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Hattil is mentioned as an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity. Solomon's servants were a class of people who were assigned to various duties in the service of the king and the temple. In the lists of returnees recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Hattil are mentioned among Solomon's servants. No further information about Hattil is provided in the Bible. (Ezr.2.57; Neh.7.59).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.57 only referred to as Hattil (חַטִּיל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.57에 처음 언급되며 '하딜'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 핫딜은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 솔로몬의 종들 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah.
persons.short: Hattush was a descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah.
persons.article: Hattush was a descendant of King Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin) of Judah. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the royal line of Judah recorded in the book of 1 Chronicles. Hattush was one of the sons of Shemaiah, who was a descendant of Jeconiah through Pedaiah. Jeconiah was one of the last kings of Judah before the Babylonian exile, and his descendants played a role in the restoration of Jewish life after the return from exile. No other information is provided about Hattush in the Bible. (1Ch.3.22).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.22 only referred to as Hattush (חַטּוּשׁ); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.22에 처음 언급되며 '핫두스'라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 이갈, 바리야, 느아랴와 사밧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 핫두스는 유다 왕 여고냐(여호야긴)의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of David, who returned from exile.
persons.short: Hattush, a descendant of David, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Hattush, a descendant of David, is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. He is listed among the descendants of David, indicating his royal lineage. The return led by Ezra was a significant event in the restoration of Jewish life in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. No further information is provided about this Hattush in the Bible. (Ezr.8.2).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.2 only referred to as Hattush (חַטּוּשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '핫두스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다윗의 후손 핫두스는 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who sealed the covenant and returned with Zerubbabel.
persons.short: Hattush was a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah and returned with Zerubbabel.
persons.article: Hattush was a priest who lived during the time of Nehemiah. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. This covenant was a solemn agreement made by the people of Israel to follow God's laws and commandments. Hattush is also listed among the priests who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, indicating that he was among the first group of exiles to return from Babylon. As a priest, Hattush would have had important responsibilities in the religious life of the community. (Neh.10.4; 12.2).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.4 only referred to as Hattush (חַטּוּשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.4에 처음 언급되며 '핫두스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 핫두스는 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 서명하고 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Hashabneiah, a repairer of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Hattush, son of Hashabneiah, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Hattush, the son of Hashabneiah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped repair Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah. He repaired a section adjacent to the portion repaired by Jedaiah, the son of Harumaph. Hashabneiah, Hattush's father, is also mentioned as a participant in the wall repair. Hattush's involvement in this important project demonstrates his commitment to the restoration of Jerusalem. (Neh.3.10).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.10 only referred to as Hattush (חַטּוּשׁ); a son of Hashabneiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.10에 처음 언급되며 '핫두스'라 불림. 하삽느야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하삽느야의 아들 핫두스는 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem.
persons.short: Havilah was a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Havilah is mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as a son of Joktan, who was a descendant of Shem, one of Noah's three sons. The Table of Nations is a genealogical record of the descendants of Noah's sons after the Great Flood, representing the known nations and peoples of the ancient world. Joktan's descendants, including Havilah, are associated with the peoples of the Arabian Peninsula. No further information is provided about this Havilah in the Bible. (Gen.10.29; 1Ch.1.23).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.29 only referred to as Havilah (חֲוִילָה); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.29에 처음 언급되며 '하윌라'라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌과 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하윌라는 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A son of Cush, descendant of Ham.
persons.short: Havilah was a son of Cush, a descendant of Ham, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Havilah is mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as a son of Cush, who was a son of Ham, one of Noah's three sons. The Table of Nations is a genealogical record of the descendants of Noah's sons after the Great Flood, representing the known nations and peoples of the ancient world. No further information is provided about this Havilah in the Bible. (Gen.10.7; 1Ch.1.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.7 only referred to as Havilah (חֲוִילָה); son of Cush; a brother of Seba, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabteca and Nimrod.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.7에 처음 언급되며 '하윌라'라 불림. 구스의 아들. 스바, 삽다, 라아마, 삽드가와 니므롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하윌라는 함의 후손 구스의 아들로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Aram (Syria), anointed by Elijah.
persons.short: Hazael, king of Aram, was anointed by Elijah and fought against Israel and Judah.
persons.article: Hazael was the king of Aram (Syria) during the reigns of Jehoram, Jehu, Jehoahaz, and Jehoash of Israel, and Ahaziah and Joash of Judah. He was anointed by the prophet Elijah as the future king of Aram (1Ki.19.15, 17). Hazael became king after the death of Ben-Hadad II, whom he had murdered (2Ki.8.15). During his reign, Hazael fought against Israel and Judah, capturing cities and inflicting heavy casualties (2Ki.8.28-29; 9.14-15; 10.32; 12.17-18; 13.3, 22). He also oppressed Israel during the reign of Jehoahaz (2Ki.13.3, 22). However, Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, recaptured some cities from Hazael's son, Ben-Hadad III (2Ki.13.24-25). The prophet Amos prophesied against Hazael and his dynasty for their cruelty against Israel (Amo.1.4).
persons.summary: A king in Syria living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.19.15 only referred to as Hazael (חֲזָהאֵל); father of Ben-hadad.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.19.15에 처음 언급되며 '하사엘'이라 불림. 벤하닷의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아람 왕 하사엘은 엘리야에게 기름부음을 받았고 이스라엘과 유다를 대적해 싸웠다.
persons.article_ko: 하사엘은 이스라엘의 여호람, 예후, 여호아하스, 여호아스와 유다의 아하시야, 요아스 통치 기간의 아람(시리아) 왕이었다. 그는 선지자 엘리야에게 아람의 미래 왕으로 기름부음을 받았다(왕상 19:15, 17). 하사엘은 자신이 살해한 벤하닷 2세가 죽은 후 왕이 되었다(왕하 8:15). 그의 통치 기간 동안 하사엘은 이스라엘과 유다를 대적하여 싸워 성읍들을 점령하고 큰 인명 피해를 입혔다(왕하 8:28-29; 9:14-15; 10:32; 12:17-18; 13:3, 22). 그는 또한 여호아하스 통치 기간 동안 이스라엘을 압제했다(왕하 13:3, 22). 그러나 여호아하스의 아들 여호아스는 하사엘의 아들 벤하닷 3세에게서 일부 성읍을 되찾았다(왕하 13:24-25). 선지자 아모스는 이스라엘에 대한 잔인함 때문에 하사엘과 그의 왕조를 대적하여 예언했다(암 1:4).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Hazaiah was an ancestor of Maaseiah, a leader who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Hazaiah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as an ancestor of Maaseiah, a leader who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Maaseiah is listed among the descendants of Judah who settled in Jerusalem. No further information is provided about Hazaiah in the Bible. (Neh.11.5).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Hazaiah (חֲזָיָה); a son of Adaiah; father of Col-hozeh.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '하사야'라 불림. 아다야의 아들. 골호세의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 하사야는 예루살렘에 거주한 지도자 마아세야의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem.
persons.short: Hazarmaveth was a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Hazarmaveth is mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as a son of Joktan, who was a descendant of Shem, one of Noah's three sons. The Table of Nations is a genealogical record of the descendants of Noah's sons after the Great Flood, representing the known nations and peoples of the ancient world. Joktan's descendants, including Hazarmaveth, are associated with the peoples of the Arabian Peninsula. The name Hazarmaveth is believed to be preserved in the name of the region of Hadhramaut in southern Arabia. No further information is provided about Hazarmaveth in the Bible. (Gen.10.26; 1Ch.1.20).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.26 only referred to as Hazarmaveth (חֲצַרְמָ֫וֶת); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '하살마웻'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하살마웻은 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite of the family of Shimei.
persons.short: Haziel was a Levite of the family of Shimei during the time of David.
persons.article: Haziel was a Levite who lived during the reign of King David. He belonged to the family of Shimei, one of the sons of Levi. In the organization of the Levites for the service of the tabernacle, Haziel and his brothers were assigned duties under the leadership of Jahath. No further information is provided about Haziel in the Bible. (1Ch.23.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.23.9 only referred to as Haziel (חֲזִיאֵל); son of Shimei; a brother of Zimmah, Shelomoth and Haran.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.9에 처음 언급되며 '하시엘'이라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 심마, 슬로못과 하란의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하시엘은 다윗 시대 시므이 가문 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother.
persons.short: Hazo was a son of Nahor, the brother of Abraham.
persons.article: Hazo is mentioned in the book of Genesis as one of the sons of Nahor, who was the brother of Abraham. Nahor and his family lived in the city of Haran, which was located in Mesopotamia. Hazo is listed among the twelve sons of Nahor and his concubine, Reumah. No further information is provided about Hazo in the Bible. (Gen.22.22).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.22 only referred to as Hazo (חֲזוֹ); son of Nahor and Milcah; a brother of Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel; half-brother of: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.22에 처음 언급되며 '하소'라 불림. 나홀과 밀가의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 하소는 아브라함의 형제 나홀의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch, Shobal@1Ch.2.50-, Salma@1Ch.2.51-, Hareph@1Ch.2.51, Jezreel@1Ch.4.3, Ishma@1Ch.4.3, Idbash@1Ch.4.3, Penuel@1Ch.4.4, Ezer@1Ch.4.4
persons.brief: A woman mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.short: Hazzelelponi was a woman mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Hazzelelponi is a woman mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. She is listed among the descendants of Judah, along with her brothers Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. No further information is provided about Hazzelelponi in the Bible, and her name is not mentioned elsewhere in the Scriptures. (1Ch.4.3).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.3 only referred to as Hazzelelponi (הַצְּלֶלְפּוֹנִי); daughter of Hur; a sister of Uri, Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Jezreel, Ishma, Idbash, Penuel and Ezer.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.4.3에 처음 언급되며 '하술렐보니'라 불림. 훌의 딸. 우리, 소발, 살마, 하렙, 이스르엘, 이스마, 잇바스, 브누엘과 에셀의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 하슬렐보니는 유다 족보에 언급된 여인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mered, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Heber was a son of Mered, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Heber is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as a son of Mered. Mered was married to Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh, and had two sons, Miriam and Shammai, in addition to Heber. No further information is provided about this Heber in the Bible. (1Ch.4.18).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.18 only referred to as Heber (חֶ֫בֶר); son of Mered(?) and Jehudijah; a brother of Jered and Jekuthiel; half-brother of: Miriam(?), Shammai(?) and Ishbah(?); father or founder of Soco.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 메렛과 여후디야의 아들. 예렛, 여구디엘, 미리암, 삼매와 이스바의 형제. 소고의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤벨은 므렛의 아들로 유다 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Eber@1Ch.8.12, Misham@1Ch.8.12, Shemed@1Ch.8.12, Beriah@1Ch.8.13-, Shema@1Ch.8.13, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.17, Meshullam@1Ch.8.17, Hizki@1Ch.8.17, Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18, Izliah@1Ch.8.18, Jobab@1Ch.8.18
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Elpaal.
persons.short: Heber was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal.
persons.article: Heber is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles as one of the sons of Elpaal. Elpaal was a descendant of Shaharaim and had several children, including Heber. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 lists the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. No further information is provided about this Heber in the Bible. (1Ch.8.17).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.17 only referred to as Heber (חֶ֫בֶר); son of Elpaal; a brother of Eber, Misham, Shemed, Beriah, Shema, Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.17에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 엘바알의 아들. 에벨, 미삼, 세멧, 브리아, 세마, 스바댜, 므술람, 히스기, 이스므래, 이슬리아와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤벨은 베냐민 사람으로 엘바알의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, grandson of Asher.
persons.short: Heber was a son of Beriah and grandson of Asher.
persons.article: Heber was a son of Beriah and a grandson of Asher, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Israel). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher in Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles. In Numbers, the descendants of Heber are referred to as the Heberite clan. Heber's sister was Jael, and his brother was Malchiel. No further information is provided about Heber in the Bible. (Gen.46.17; Num.26.45; 1Ch.7.31,32).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.17 referred to as Heber (חֶ֫בֶר), or Heberite (חֶבְרִי); son of Beriah; a brother of Malchiel; father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham and Shua.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.17에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 말기엘의 형제. 야블렛, 소멜, 호담과 수아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤벨은 브리아의 아들이며 아셀의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: A Kenite; husband of Jael.
persons.short: Heber the Kenite; husband of Jael. He had separated from the Kenites and allied with Jabin, king of Hazor.
persons.article: Heber was a Kenite, a descendant of Moses' father-in-law, Hobab. He had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent in the plain of Zaanaim, near Kedesh. Heber had made peace with Jabin, the king of Hazor, who was oppressing Israel at that time. Heber's wife, Jael, played a significant role in the defeat of Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army. When Sisera fled from the battle and sought refuge in Jael's tent, she killed him by driving a tent peg through his temple while he slept. Jael's actions are praised in the Song of Deborah for bringing deliverance to Israel. (Jdg.4.11,17; 5.24).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.4.11 only referred to as Heber (חֶ֫בֶר); husband of Jael.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 야엘의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 겐 사람 헤벨은 야엘의 남편으로, 겐 족속에서 갈라져 나와 하솔 왕 야빈과 동맹했다.

persons.description: Eber@Gen.10.21-Luk   עֵבֶר (Eber, H5677)   People from Eber@Gen.10.21-Luk
persons.brief: An ethnic group descended from Abraham.
persons.short: The Hebrews were an ethnic group descended from Abraham, also known as Israelites or Jews.
persons.article: The Hebrews were an ethnic group descended from Abraham, also known as Israelites or Jews. The term "Hebrew" first appears in the Bible in reference to Abraham (Gen.14.13 and is later used to refer to his descendants, the Israelites, throughout the Old Testament). The Hebrews were distinct from the Egyptians (Gen.43.32; Exo.1.15,16,19 and other nations, and they were often oppressed or enslaved )(Exo.1.11-14; 5.3). God identified Himself as the God of the Hebrews (Exo.3.18; 5.3; 7.16; 9.1,13; 10.3) and gave them laws and commandments to follow (Exo.21.2; Deu.15.12). The Hebrews were also known for their language, Hebrew (Luk.23.38; Act.6.1, and their religious practices). In the New Testament, the term "Hebrew" is used to refer to Jewish Christians who spoke Hebrew or Aramaic (Act.6.1 and to emphasize the Jewish heritage of some early Christians )(2Co.11.22; Php.3.5).
persons.summary: People from Eber, first mentioned at Gen.10.21 referred to as Hebrews (עִבְרִי), or Hebrew (Ἑβραῖος).
persons.summary_ko: 에벨 자손. Gen.14.13에 처음 언급되며 '히브리인'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 히브리인은 아브라함의 후손인 민족으로, 이스라엘 사람 또는 유대인이라고도 불린다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mareshah, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Hebron was a son of Mareshah, a descendant of Caleb from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Hebron is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as a son of Mareshah. Mareshah was a descendant of Caleb, who was from the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.42,43). Hebron is also the name of the town founded by his father Mareshah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.42 only referred to as Hebron (חֶבְרוֹן); a son of Mareshah; father of Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, Shema.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.42에 처음 언급되며 '헤브론'이라 불림. 마레사의 아들. 고라, 답부아, 레겜과 세마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤브론은 유다 지파 갈렙의 후손 마레사의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi.
persons.short: Hebron was a son of Kohath and grandson of Levi, and his descendants were known as the Hebronites.
persons.article: Hebron was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in Exodus, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles. Hebron's brothers were Amram, Izhar, and Uzziel (Exo.6.18; Num.3.19; 1Ch.6.2,18). His descendants were known as the Hebronites, who were assigned various duties in the service of the tabernacle and the temple (Num.3.27; 26.58; 1Ch.26.23,30,31). Some of the notable Hebronites included Jeriah, the chief of the Hebronites during the time of David (1Ch.23.19; 26.31), and Hashabiah, a leader during the time of David (1Ch.15.9).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.18 referred to as Hebron (חֶבְרוֹן), or Hebronite (חֶבְרוֹנִי); son of Kohath; a brother of Amram, Izhar and Uzziel; father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel and Jekameam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Exo.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '헤브론'이라 불림. 그핫의 아들. 아므람, 이스할과 웃시엘의 형제. 여리야, 아마랴, 야하시엘과 여가므암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤브론은 고핫의 아들이며 레위의 손자로, 그 후손은 헤브론 족속으로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 헤브론은 고핫의 아들이며 레위의 손자였다. 그는 출애굽기, 민수기, 역대상의 레위인 족보에 언급된다. 헤브론의 형제들은 아므람, 이스할, 웃시엘이었다(출 6:18; 민 3:19; 대상 6:2, 18). 그의 후손은 헤브론 사람들로 알려졌으며, 성막과 성전 봉사에서 다양한 직무를 부여받았다(민 3:27; 26:58; 대상 26:23, 30-31). 저명한 헤브론 사람으로는 다윗 시대 헤브론 사람들의 우두머리였던 여리야(대상 23:19; 26:31)와 다윗 시대의 지도자 하사뱌(대상 15:9)가 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A eunuch in charge of King Ahasuerus' harem.
persons.short: Hegai was a eunuch in charge of King Ahasuerus' harem, responsible for preparing Esther for her night with the king.
persons.article: Hegai was a eunuch who served in the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) of Persia. He was in charge of the king's harem, which was the living quarters for the king's concubines and prospective brides. When Esther was brought into the king's harem, Hegai was responsible for her care and preparation (Est.2.3,8). He provided Esther with cosmetics, special food, and seven choice maidservants from the king's palace (Est.2.9). Hegai was also instrumental in advising Esther on how to approach the king and win his favor (Est.2.15). Esther found favor with Hegai and received the best place in the harem (Est.2.9. )(Est.2.3,8,15).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.2.3 only referred to as Hegai (הֵגֵא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.2.3에 처음 언급되며 '헤개'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헤개는 아하수에로 왕의 후궁을 관리하는 내시로, 에스더가 왕과 밤을 보내도록 준비시켰다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of the two wives of Ashhur.
persons.short: Helah was one of the two wives of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Helah is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as one of the two wives of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa. Ashhur's other wife was Naarah (1Ch.4.5). Helah gave birth to Zereth, Izhar, Ethnan, and Koz (1Ch.4.7). No further information is provided about Helah in the Bible. (1Ch.4.5,7).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.4.5 only referred to as Helah (חֶלְאָה); wife of Ashhur; mother of Zereth, Izhar, Ethnan and Koz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.4.5에 처음 언급되며 '헬라'라 불림. 아스훌의 아내. 세렛, 이스할, 에드난과 고스의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 헬라는 유다 지파 드고아의 아버지 아스훌의 두 아내 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A returned exile who helped crown Joshua.
persons.short: Heldai (or Helem), a returned exile, was one of those who provided silver and gold to make a crown for Joshua the high priest.
persons.article: Heldai, also known as Helem, was one of the returned exiles mentioned in the book of Zechariah. He, along with Tobijah and Jedaiah, came from Babylon and stayed at the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah. Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah provided silver and gold to make a crown for Joshua the high priest, symbolizing the Messiah who would be both priest and king (Zec.6.10,14). This event took place during the time of the prophet Zechariah, who encouraged the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. (Zec.6.10,14).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Zec.6.10 referred to as Heldai (חֶלְדַּי), or Helem (חֵ֫לֶם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '헬대'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헬대(헬렘이라고도 함)는 포로에서 돌아온 자로, 대제사장 여호수아의 면류관을 만들 은과 금을 제공한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors.
persons.short: Heleb (also known as Heldai or Heled) was one of David's mighty warriors, a Netophathite.
persons.article: Heleb, also known as Heldai or Heled, was one of King David's mighty warriors. He was a Netophathite, indicating that he was from the town of Netophah in Judah. Heleb is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty men in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles (2Sa.23.29; 1Ch.11.30). In 1Ch.27.15, he is mentioned as the officer in charge of the twelfth division of David's army, which served in the twelfth month of the year. Heleb's inclusion in these lists suggests that he was a skilled and valiant warrior who played a significant role in David's military campaigns. (2Sa.23.29; 1Ch.27.15; 11.30).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.29 referred to as Heleb (חֵ֫לֶב), or Heldai (חֶלְדַּי), or Heled (חֵ֫לֶד); a son of Baanah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.29에 처음 언급되며 '헬렙'이라 불림. 바아나의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 헬렙(헬대 또는 헬렛이라고도 함)은 느도바 사람으로 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Gilead, ancestor of the Helekites.
persons.short: Helek was a son of Gilead and ancestor of the Helekite clan in the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Helek was a son of Gilead, who was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Manasseh in Numbers and Joshua (Num.26.30; Jos.17.2). Helek's descendants were known as the Helekites, one of the clans within the tribe of Manasseh. The Helekites, along with the other clans of Manasseh, received their inheritance in the Promised Land under the leadership of Joshua (Jos.17.2). No further information is provided about Helek himself in the Bible. (Num.26.30; Jos.17.2).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.30 referred to as Helek (חֵ֫לֶק), or Helekite (חֶלְקִי); son of Gilead; a brother of Abiezer, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida and Hepher.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.30에 처음 언급되며 '헬렉'이라 불림. 길르앗의 아들. 아비에셀, 아스리엘, 세겜, 스미다와 헤벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헬렉은 길르앗의 아들이며 므낫세 지파 헬렉 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Jerahmeel from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Helez was a descendant of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Helez is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron (1Ch.2.39). He was the son of Azariah and the father of Eleasah. This genealogy traces the lineage of some of the notable clans and individuals within the tribe of Judah. No further information is provided about this Helez in the Bible, and he is not to be confused with Helez, one of David's mighty warriors. (1Ch.2.39).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.39 only referred to as Helez (חֶ֫לֶץ); a son of Azariah; father of Eleasah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.39에 처음 언급되며 '헬레스'라 불림. 아사랴의 아들. 엘르아사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헬레스는 헤스론의 아들 여라므엘의 후손으로 유다 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from Pelet.
persons.short: Helez the Paltite (or Pelonite) was one of David's mighty warriors and commander of his army division for the seventh month.
persons.article: Helez was one of King David's mighty warriors, mentioned in the lists of David's mighty men in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles (2Sa.23.26; 1Ch.11.27). He was from Pelet (or Pelon) and was known as Helez the Paltite or Pelonite. In 1Ch.27.10, Helez is mentioned as the commander of David's army division for the seventh month. This suggests that he was a skilled warrior and leader, entrusted with significant responsibilities in David's military. No further information is provided about Helez's specific exploits or life events in the Bible. (2Sa.23.26; 1Ch.11.27; 27.10).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.26 only referred to as Helez (חֶ֫לֶץ).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.26에 처음 언급되며 '헬레스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 발디 사람(블로니 사람) 헬레스는 다윗의 용맹한 용사이며 일곱째 달 군대의 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Father of Mary and maternal grandfather of Jesus.
persons.short: Heli was the father of Mary and the maternal grandfather of Jesus.
persons.article: Heli is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke. He is identified as the father of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and thus, the maternal grandfather of Jesus (Luk.3.23). In the genealogy, Luke traces Jesus' lineage back to Adam through his mother Mary's side of the family, while Matthew's genealogy (Matt 1.1-17 follows Joseph's lineage). The mention of Heli provides insight into Jesus' family background and affirms his connection to the Davidic line through his mother. No further information is given about Heli in the Bible. (Luk.3.23).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.3.23 only referred to as Heli (Ἡλί); a son of Matthat; father of Mary and Salome (?).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '헬리'라 불림. 맛닷의 아들. 헬리의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편. 마리아와 살로매의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헬리는 마리아의 아버지이며 예수님의 외할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest during the time of Joiakim.
persons.short: Helkai was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim the high priest.
persons.article: Helkai was a priest who lived during the time of Joiakim, the high priest in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the list of priests and Levites who served in the days of Joiakim (Neh.12.15). This list was compiled to record the heads of the priestly families who returned to Jerusalem and served in the temple. Helkai's mention suggests that he was a prominent priest during this period and led a priestly family. No other details about Helkai's life or specific responsibilities are provided in the Bible. (Neh.12.15).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.15 only referred to as Helkai (חֶלְקָ֑י).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.15에 처음 언급되며 '헬개'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헬개는 대제사장 요야김 시대에 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Eliab, a leader from the tribe of Zebulun.
persons.short: Helon was the father of Eliab, a leader from the tribe of Zebulun during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.article: Helon was an Israelite from the tribe of Zebulun who lived during the time of Moses. He was the father of Eliab, a prominent leader within the tribe (Num.1.9). Eliab was chosen as the leader of the Zebulunites during the census and organization of the Israelite camp in the wilderness (Num.2.7). He also represented his tribe when the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the tabernacle altar (Num.7.24,29). Additionally, Eliab led the Zebulunites in the order of march when the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai (Num.10.16). Helon's mention in connection with his son Eliab suggests that he was a respected member of the tribe of Zebulun. (Num.1.9; 2.7; 7.24,29; 10.16).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.9 only referred to as Helon (חֵלֹן); father of Eliab.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.9에 처음 언급되며 '헬론'이라 불림. 엘리압의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헬론은 광야 시절 스불론 지파 지도자 엘리압의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A descendant of Seir the Horite.
persons.short: Hemam was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau.
persons.article: Hemam is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau, the son of Isaac and brother of Israel (or 'Jacob'), in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. He was a descendant of Seir the Horite, the original inhabitants of the land of Seir (Edom) before Esau's descendants settled there (Gen.36.22; 1Ch.1.39). The Horites were a people group that lived in the region of Seir prior to the Edomites. Hemam is listed among the sons of Lotan, one of the sons of Seir. No further details about Hemam's life or role are provided in the Bible. (1Ch.1.39; Gen.36.22).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.22 referred to as Hemam (הוֹמָ֑ם), or Hemam (הֵימָם); son of Lotan; a brother of Hori.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.22에 처음 언급되며 '호맘'이라 불림. 로단의 아들. 호리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤맘은 세일 사람 호리의 후손으로, 에서의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandson of Judah through Zerah.
persons.short: Heman was a grandson of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Heman is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Zerah, who was one of the twin sons of Judah and Tamar (Gen.38.30). Heman's brothers were Zimri, Ethan, Calcol, and Dara (1Ch.2.6). This genealogy traces the descendants of Judah, highlighting some of the notable figures in the tribe's history. No further information is provided about Heman's life or role in the Bible. (1Ch.2.6).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.6 only referred to as Heman (הֵימָן); son of Zerah; a brother of Zabdi, Ethan, Calcol and Dara.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '헤만'이라 불림. 세라의 아들. 삽디, 에단, 갈골과 다라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤만은 유다의 족보에 언급된 유다의 손자였다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-, Jehuel@2Ch.29.14, Shimei@2Ch.29.14
persons.brief: A Levite and chief musician in David's time.
persons.short: Heman, a Levite, was a chief musician appointed by David to lead worship in the tabernacle.
persons.article: Heman was a prominent Levite and musician during the reign of King David. He was a descendant of Kohath, one of the sons of Levi (1Ch.6.33). Heman, along with Asaph and Ethan, was appointed by David to lead the music and worship in the tabernacle (1Ch.15.17,19; 16.41,42). He was known for his skill in playing the cymbal (1Ch.16.42). Heman had fourteen sons and three daughters, all of whom were under his direction in providing music for the house of the Lord (1Ch.25.1,4-6). During the reign of Solomon, Heman and his fellow musicians participated in the dedication of the temple (2Ch.5.12). Later, during the reigns of Hezekiah and Josiah, Heman's descendants continued to serve as musicians in the temple (2Ch.29.14; 35.15). Heman's significant role in the tabernacle and temple worship highlights the importance of music in Israelite worship. (1Ch.6.33; 15.17,19; 16.41,42; 25.1,4-6; 2Ch.5.12; 29.14; 35.15).
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.33 only referred to as Heman (הֵימָן); a son of Joel; father of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth, Jehuel, Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.6.33에 처음 언급되며 '헤만'이라 불림. 요엘의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디, 호딜, 마하시옷, 여후엘과 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 헤만은 다윗이 성막에서 예배를 인도하도록 임명한 수석 음악가였다.
persons.article_ko: 헤만은 다윗 왕 통치 기간의 저명한 레위인이며 음악가였다. 그는 레위의 아들 중 한 사람인 고핫의 후손이었다(대상 6:33). 헤만은 아삽, 에단과 함께 다윗에 의해 성막에서 음악과 예배를 이끄는 자로 임명되었다(대상 15:17, 19; 16:41-42). 그는 심벌즈 연주 실력으로 알려졌다(대상 16:42). 헤만에게는 열네 아들과 세 딸이 있었는데, 모두 여호와의 집을 위한 음악을 제공하는 데 있어 그의 지도 아래 있었다(대상 25:1, 4-6). 솔로몬 통치 기간 동안 헤만과 그의 동료 음악가들은 성전 봉헌식에 참여했다(대하 5:12). 후에 히스기야와 요시야 통치 기간 동안 헤만의 후손은 계속해서 성전에서 음악가로 섬겼다(대하 29:14; 35:15). 성막과 성전 예배에서 헤만의 중요한 역할은 이스라엘 예배에서 음악의 중요성을 부각시킨다(대상 6:33; 15:17, 19; 16:41-42; 25:1, 4-6; 대하 5:12; 29:14; 35:15).

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A wise man during Solomon's time.
persons.short: Heman was known for his wisdom, though not as wise as Solomon.
persons.article: Heman is mentioned in the book of 1 Kings as one of the wise men during the reign of King Solomon. He is described as a man of great wisdom, along with Ethan the Ezrahite and the sons of Mahol (1Ki.4.31). However, the passage also states that Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of all these men, indicating that Heman, while wise, was not as wise as Solomon himself. The comparison serves to highlight the exceptional wisdom that God had granted to Solomon. Heman the Ezrahite was a psalmist and musician mentioned in the title of Psalm 88. He is described as "Heman the Ezrahite," indicating that he was a descendant of Zerah, one of the sons of Judah (Gen.38.30; 1Ch.2.6). Psalm 88, which is attributed to Heman, is a deeply sorrowful and introspective psalm, expressing the psalmist's anguish and despair. The psalm is unique in that it does not end with the usual expression of hope or praise found in most other psalms. This has led some scholars to suggest that Heman may have composed the psalm during a time of great personal distress or national crisis.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.4.31 only referred to as Heman (הֵימָן); son of Mahol; a brother of Ethan, Calcol and Darda.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.31에 처음 언급되며 '헤만'이라 불림. 마홀의 아들. 에단, 갈골과 다르다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤만은 지혜로 알려졌으나 솔로몬만큼 지혜롭지는 않았다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A descendant of Seir the Horite.
persons.short: Hemdan was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Esau.
persons.article: Hemdan is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau, the son of Isaac and brother of Israel (or 'Jacob'), in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. He was a descendant of Seir the Horite, the original inhabitants of the land of Seir (Edom) before Esau's descendants settled there (Gen.36.26; 1Ch.1.41). The Horites were a people group that lived in the region of Seir prior to the Edomites. Hemdan is listed among the sons of Dishon, one of the sons of Seir. No further details about Hemdan's life or role are provided in the Bible. (Gen.36.26; 1Ch.1.41).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.26 referred to as Hemdan (חֶמְדָּן), or Hemdan (חַמְרָן); son of Dishon; a brother of Eshban, Ithran and Cheran.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '헴단'이라 불림. 디손의 아들. 에스반, 이드란과 그란의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헴단은 세일 사람 호리의 후손으로, 에서의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite whose sons assisted in rebuilding the temple.
persons.short: Henadad was a Levite whose descendants helped rebuild the temple and signed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Henadad was a Levite who lived during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. His sons and descendants played a significant role in the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem (Ezr.3.9). They worked alongside the Levites under the leadership of Jeshua, Kadmiel, and Binnui to supervise the laborers and the rebuilding efforts. Later, during the time of Nehemiah, the descendants of Henadad are mentioned among the Levites who signed the covenant to follow the Law of God (Neh.10.9). This covenant was a solemn agreement to obey God's commandments and maintain the purity of the Jewish community. Henadad's descendants' involvement in both the temple reconstruction and the signing of the covenant highlights their commitment to the restoration of the Jewish faith and community after the exile. (Ezr.3.9; Neh.10.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.3.9 only referred to as Henadad (חֵנָדָד).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.3.9에 처음 언급되며 '헤나닷'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헤나닷은 그 후손들이 성전 재건을 돕고 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Binnui, a Levite who repaired the wall.
persons.short: Henadad, son of Binnui, was a Levite who repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Henadad, son of Binnui, was a Levite who participated in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem under the leadership of Nehemiah. He is specifically mentioned as repairing a section of the wall, along with his brothers (Neh.3.18). The rebuilding of the wall was a significant project undertaken by Nehemiah to restore the security and integrity of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Henadad's involvement in this project demonstrates the participation of the Levites in the physical restoration of the city, in addition to their spiritual and religious duties. No further information is provided about this specific Henadad in the Bible. (Neh.3.18).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.18 only referred to as Henadad (חֵנָדָד); father of Bavvai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.18에 처음 언급되며 '헤나닷'이라 불림. 바왜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 빈누이의 아들 헤나닷은 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Bani, a Levite who repaired the wall.
persons.short: Henadad, son of Bani, was a Levite who repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Henadad, son of Bani, was a Levite who participated in the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem under the leadership of Nehemiah. He is specifically mentioned as repairing a section of the wall, along with Binnui, son of Henadad (Neh.3.24). The rebuilding of the wall was a significant project undertaken by Nehemiah to restore the security and integrity of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Henadad's involvement in this project demonstrates the participation of the Levites in the physical restoration of the city, in addition to their spiritual and religious duties. No further information is provided about this specific Henadad in the Bible. (Neh.3.24).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.24 only referred to as Henadad (חֵנָדָד); father of Binnui.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '헤나닷'이라 불림. 빈누이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바니의 아들 헤나닷은 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Mecherathite, one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.short: Hepher the Mecherathite was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Hepher the Mecherathite is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles. He is described as one of the valiant warriors who supported David and fought alongside him (1Ch.11.36). The term "Mecherathite" likely refers to his place of origin or clan affiliation, although the exact location is unknown. Being included in the list of David's mighty men suggests that Hepher was a skilled and loyal soldier who played a significant role in David's military campaigns. No further details about his specific accomplishments or life events are provided in the Bible. (1Ch.11.36).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.36 only referred to as Hepher (חֵ֫פֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.36에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므게랏 사람 헤벨은 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Temeni@1Ch.4.6, Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6, Zereth@1Ch.4.7, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Ethnan@1Ch.4.7, Koz@1Ch.4.8
persons.brief: A son of Ashhur, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Hepher was a son of Ashhur, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Hepher is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was one of the sons of Ashhur, who was a descendant of Judah through Caleb (1Ch.4.6). Ashhur's wife was named Naarah, and they had several children, including Hepher. No further information is provided about Hepher's life or role in the Bible. (1Ch.4.6).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.6 only referred to as Hepher (חֵ֫פֶר); son of Ashhur and Naarah; a brother of Ahuzzam, Temeni and Haahashtari; half-brother of: Zereth, Izhar, Ethnan and Koz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 아스훌과 나아라의 아들. 아훗삼, 데므니, 하아하스타리, 세렛, 이스할, 에드난과 고스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헤벨은 유다의 후손인 아스훌의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Gilead, ancestor of the Hepherites.
persons.short: Hepher was a son of Gilead and ancestor of the Hepherite clan in the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Hepher was a son of Gilead, who was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Manasseh in Numbers and Joshua (Num.26.32; Jos.17.2). Hepher's descendants were known as the Hepherites, one of the clans within the tribe of Manasseh (Num.26.32). The daughters of Zelophehad, who were descendants of Hepher, played a significant role in establishing inheritance rights for women in the absence of male heirs (Num.27.1; Jos.17.3). They brought their case before Moses and the leaders, and God instructed that they should receive an inheritance among their father's relatives. This event set a precedent for inheritance laws in Israel. (Num.26.32,33; 27.1; Jos.17.2,3).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.32 referred to as Hepher (חֵ֫פֶר), or Hepherite (חֶפְרִי); son of Gilead; a brother of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem and Shemida; father of Zelophehad.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.32에 처음 언급되며 '헤벨'이라 불림. 길르앗의 아들. 아비에셀, 헬렉, 아스리엘, 세겜과 스미다의 형제. 슬로브핫의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤벨은 길르앗의 아들이며 므낫세 지파 헤벨 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: The mother of King Manasseh of Judah.
persons.short: Hephzibah was the mother of King Manasseh, who ruled over Judah.
persons.article: Hephzibah is mentioned in the Bible as the mother of King Manasseh, who ruled over Judah. She was the wife of King Hezekiah (2Ki.21.1). Manasseh, born to Hezekiah and Hephzibah, succeeded his father as king at the age of twelve and reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. Manasseh's reign was marked by idolatry and wickedness, as he undid many of the religious reforms his father had implemented. He even practiced child sacrifice and consulted mediums and spiritists. Despite this, God showed mercy to Manasseh when he humbled himself and prayed for forgiveness. No further details about Hephzibah's life or character are provided in the Bible. (2Ki.21.1).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.21.1 only referred to as Hephzibah (חֶפְצִי־בָהּ); wife of Hezekiah; mother of Manasseh.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.21.1에 처음 언급되며 '헵시바'라 불림. 히스기야의 아내. 므낫세의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 헵시바는 유다를 다스린 므낫세 왕의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Heresh was a Levite who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Heresh is mentioned in the list of Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is identified as one of the Levites who settled in the city during the time of Nehemiah (1Ch.9.15). The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the temple service and had various duties related to the maintenance and operation of the temple. Heresh's presence in Jerusalem suggests that he was involved in these responsibilities, although his specific role is not mentioned. No further details about Heresh's life or activities are provided in the Bible. (1Ch.9.15).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.15 only referred to as Heresh (חֶ֫רֶשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.15에 처음 언급되며 '헤레스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헤레스는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Christian in Rome greeted by Paul.
persons.short: Hermes was a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Hermes is mentioned in the Bible as one of the Christians in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans. He is listed along with several other believers, including Asyncritus, Phlegon, and Hermas (Rom.16.14). The fact that Paul specifically mentions Hermes in his greetings suggests that he was a notable member of the Roman Christian community. However, no further information is provided about Hermes' background, conversion, or role in the church. The name Hermes was common in the Greco-Roman world, and it is not clear whether this Hermes had any connection to the Greek god of the same name. (Rom.16.14).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.14 referred to as Hermes or Hermas (Ἑρμῆς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.14a에 처음 언급되며 '허메'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 허메는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Christian in Rome greeted by Paul.
persons.short: Hermas was a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Hermas is mentioned in the Bible as one of the Christians in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans. He is listed along with several other believers, including Asyncritus, Phlegon, and Hermes (Rom.16.14). The fact that Paul specifically mentions Hermas in his greetings suggests that he was a notable member of the Roman Christian community. However, no further information is provided about Hermas' background, conversion, or role in the church. Some scholars have suggested that this Hermas may be the same person as the author of the early Christian work "The Shepherd of Hermas," but this identification is uncertain and not universally accepted. (Rom.16.14).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.14 referred to as Hermas (Ἑρμᾶς), or Hermes (Ἑρμῆς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.14b에 처음 언급되며 '허마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 허마는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A believer who deserted Paul in Asia.
persons.short: Hermogenes was one of the believers in Asia who deserted Paul during his imprisonment.
persons.article: Hermogenes is mentioned briefly in Paul's second letter to Timothy as one of the believers in Asia who deserted Paul during his imprisonment. Along with Phygellus, Hermogenes is cited as an example of those who turned away from Paul in his time of need (2Ti.1.15). The exact circumstances of this desertion are not specified, but it likely occurred during Paul's final imprisonment in Rome. Paul's mention of Hermogenes' abandonment serves as a contrast to the faithfulness of Onesiphorus, who diligently sought out Paul and refreshed him (2Ti.1.16-18). No other details about Hermogenes' background, conversion, or reasons for deserting Paul are provided in the Bible. (2Ti.1.15).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.1.15 only referred to as Hermogenes (Ἑρμογένης).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.1.15에 처음 언급되며 '허모게네'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 허모게네는 바울이 옥에 갇혔을 때 그를 버린 아시아의 신자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Tetrarch who persecuted the early church.
persons.short: Herod Agrippa I was a king who persecuted the early church, killing James and imprisoning Peter.
persons.article: Herod Agrippa I was the grandson of Herod the Great and ruled as king over Judea, Samaria, and other regions from 41 to 44 AD. In the book of Acts, he is portrayed as a persecutor of the early Christian church. Herod Agrippa I had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword (Act.12.1-2). Seeing that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter as well, intending to bring him out for public trial after the Passover (Act.12.3-4). However, an angel miraculously freed Peter from prison (Act.12.6-11). When Herod Agrippa I discovered Peter's escape, he had the guards executed (Act.12.19). Later, Herod Agrippa I was involved in a dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon (Act.12.20). On the appointed day, he delivered a public address to them, and the people shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man!" (Act.12.21-22). Immediately, an angel of the Lord struck him down because he did not give glory to God, and he was eaten by worms and died (Act.12.23. )(Act.12.1-23).
persons.summary: Tetrarch Herod Agrippa I over Judea living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.12.1 only referred to as Herod (Ἡρώδης); a brother of Herodias; father of: Tetrarch Agrippa II.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 분봉왕. Act.12.1에 처음 언급되며 '헤롯'이라 불림. 헤로디아의 형제. 아그립바의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤롯 아그립바 1세는 초대교회를 박해하여 야고보를 죽이고 베드로를 옥에 가둔 왕이었다.

persons.description: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry.
persons.short: Herod Antipas was the tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry and played a role in Jesus' trial.
persons.article: Herod Antipas was the son of Herod the Great and ruled as tetrarch of Galilee and Perea during the time of Jesus' ministry. He is mentioned in the Gospels in connection with the imprisonment and execution of John the Baptist (Mat.14.3,6; Mrk.6.17-29; Luk.3.19-20). Herod Antipas had married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, which John the Baptist condemned as unlawful. In retaliation, Herodias's daughter danced for Herod Antipas and requested the head of John the Baptist as a reward. Herod, though reluctant, fulfilled her request and had John beheaded. During Jesus' ministry, Herod Antipas heard about Jesus' miracles and teachings and was perplexed, thinking that John the Baptist had risen from the dead (Mat.14.1-2; Mrk.6.14-16; Luk.9.7-9). Later, during Jesus' trial, Pontius Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem at the time (Luk.23.7-12). Herod Antipas questioned Jesus, hoping to see a miracle, but Jesus remained silent. Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus, dressed him in an elegant robe, and sent him back to Pilate. This encounter between Herod Antipas and Jesus is unique to the Gospel of Luke.
persons.summary: Tetrarch Herod Antipas I living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.14.1 only referred to as Herod (Ἡρώδης); son of Herod 'the Great'; a brother of Ethnarch Herod Archelaus, Herod Philip I and Herod Philip II; husband of Herodias.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 분봉왕. Mat.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '헤롯'이라 불림. 헤롯의 아들. 아켈라오, 빌립과 빌립의 형제. 헤로디아의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 헤롯 안디바는 예수님의 사역 당시 갈릴리의 분봉왕이었으며 예수님의 재판에 관여했다.
persons.article_ko: 헤롯 안디바는 헤롯대왕의 아들로, 예수님의 사역 당시 갈릴리와 베레아의 분봉왕으로 다스렸다. 그는 세례 요한의 투옥과 처형과 관련하여 복음서에 언급된다(마 14:3, 6; 막 6:17-29; 눅 3:19-20). 헤롯 안디바는 자기 형제 빌립의 아내였던 헤로디아와 결혼했는데, 세례 요한은 이를 불법이라고 정죄했다. 이에 대한 보복으로 헤로디아의 딸은 헤롯 안디바 앞에서 춤을 추고 그 상으로 세례 요한의 머리를 요청했다. 헤롯은 내키지 않았으나 그녀의 요청을 이행하여 요한을 참수시켰다. 예수님의 사역 기간 동안 헤롯 안디바는 예수님의 기적과 가르침에 대해 듣고 당황하며 세례 요한이 죽은 자 가운데서 살아났다고 생각했다(마 14:1-2; 막 6:14-16; 눅 9:7-9). 후에 예수님의 재판 동안 본디오 빌라도는 당시 예루살렘에 있던 헤롯 안디바에게 예수님을 보냈다(눅 23:7-12). 헤롯 안디바는 기적을 보기를 바라며 예수님을 심문했으나 예수님은 침묵을 지키셨다. 헤롯과 그의 군인들은 예수님을 조롱하며 화려한 옷을 입혀 빌라도에게 돌려보냈다. 헤롯 안디바와 예수님 사이의 이 만남은 누가복음에만 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: King Herod the Great: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: The Great, Roman-appointed king of Judea during Jesus' birth.
persons.short: Herod the Great was the Roman-appointed king of Judea who ruled during the time of Jesus' birth.
persons.article: Herod, also known as Herod the Great, was the Roman-appointed king of Judea during the time of Jesus' birth. He was an Idumean (Edomite) by birth and was appointed as king by the Roman Senate in 40 BC. Herod was known for his ambitious building projects, including the expansion and renovation of the Second Temple in Jerusalem. In the Bible, Herod is portrayed as a cruel and paranoid ruler. When the wise men from the East inquired about the birth of the "king of the Jews," Herod saw this as a threat to his power (Mat.2.1-8). After the wise men failed to report back to him, Herod ordered the massacre of all male children aged two and under in Bethlehem and the surrounding region (Mat.2.16-18). This event, known as the "Massacre of the Innocents," reflects Herod's ruthless nature and his determination to eliminate any perceived threats to his rule. Herod's death is mentioned in Mat.2.19, which allowed Joseph, Mary, and Jesus to return from Egypt, where they had fled to escape Herod's wrath. (Mat.2; Luk.1.5).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.2.1 only referred to as Herod (Ἡρώδης); father of Ethnarch Herod Archelaus, Herod Antipas I, Herod Philip I, Herod Philip II.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 통치자 헤롯대왕. Mat.2.1에 처음 언급되며 '헤롯'이라 불림. 아켈라오, 헤롯, 빌립과 빌립의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤롯대왕은 예수님의 탄생 당시 로마가 임명한 유대의 왕이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Wife of Herod Antipas who had John beheaded.
persons.short: Herodias was the wife of Herod Antipas, who had John the Baptist beheaded at her request.
persons.article: Herodias was the wife of Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee during the time of Jesus' ministry. She was originally married to Herod Philip, the half-brother of Herod Antipas, but later divorced him to marry Herod Antipas (Mat.14.3; Mrk.6.17; Luk.3.19). John the Baptist openly condemned this marriage as unlawful, which led to his imprisonment by Herod Antipas (Mat.14.3-4; Mrk.6.17-18; Luk.3.19-20). Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to have him killed, but Herod Antipas feared the multitude who regarded John as a prophet (Mat.14.5; Mrk.6.19-20). On Herod Antipas's birthday, Herodias's daughter danced before the guests, pleasing Herod Antipas, who promised to give her whatever she asked (Mat.14.6-7; Mrk.6.21-23). Prompted by her mother Herodias, the daughter asked for the head of John the Baptist on a platter (Mat.14.8; Mrk.6.24-25). Although reluctant, Herod Antipas fulfilled the request and had John beheaded in prison (Mat.14.9-11; Mrk.6.26-28).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.14.3 only referred to as Herodias (Ἡρωδιάς); wife of Herod Antipas I and Herod Philip I; mother of Salome; a sister of Tetrarch Herod Agrippa.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Mat.14.3에 처음 언급되며 '헤로디아'라 불림. 헤롯의 자매. 헤롯과 빌립의 아내. 살로매의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 헤로디아는 헤롯 안디바의 아내로, 그녀의 요청으로 세례 요한이 참수되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A relative of Paul in Rome.
persons.short: Herodion was a relative of Paul in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.
persons.article: Herodion is mentioned briefly in Paul's letter to the Romans as one of Paul's fellow Jews and relatives in Rome. In his closing greetings, Paul sends a personal greeting to Herodion, along with a few others (Rom.16.11). The fact that Paul specifically mentions Herodion as his relative suggests that they were kinsmen, possibly from the same tribe or family lineage. However, no further details about Herodion's background, conversion, or role in the Roman church are provided in the Bible. The name Herodion may indicate that he was a freedman or descendant of someone from the Herodian household, but this is not certain. (Rom.16.11).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.11 only referred to as Herodion (Ἡρωδίων).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.11에 처음 언급되며 '헤로디온'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 헤로디온은 로마에 있던 바울의 친척으로, 바울이 그에게 문안했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A district overseer under Solomon.
persons.short: Hesed was one of the twelve district overseers who provided supplies for King Solomon and his household.
persons.article: Hesed is mentioned in the Bible as one of the twelve district overseers appointed by King Solomon to provide supplies for the king and his household. Each overseer was responsible for provisioning the royal court for one month out of the year (1Ki.4.7). Hesed was in charge of the district of Arubboth (1Ki.4.10). These district overseers were responsible for collecting and delivering the necessary provisions, such as food, drink, and other supplies, to support the king's vast household and administration. The appointment of these overseers reflects Solomon's wise governance and the organization of his kingdom. No other information about Hesed's personal life or background is provided in the Bible. (1Ki.4.10).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.10 only referred to as Hesed (חֶ֫סֶד); father of Ben-hesed.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.10에 처음 언급되며 '헤셋'이라 불림. 벤헤셋의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤셋은 솔로몬 왕과 왕실에 필요한 물자를 공급한 열두 지방관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Canaan and ancestor of the Hittites.
persons.short: Heth was a son of Canaan and the ancestor of the Hittites, a prominent people group in the ancient Near East.
persons.article: Heth, also known as the Hittites, was a descendant of Canaan, the son of Ham, according to the Table of Nations in Genesis 10 (Gen.10.15; 1Ch.1.13). The Hittites were a prominent people group in the ancient Near East, and they are frequently mentioned throughout the Old Testament. Abraham had dealings with the Hittites when he purchased the cave of Machpelah as a burial site for his wife Sarah (Gen.23). This cave later became the burial place for Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.25.9-10; 49.29-32; 50.13). Esau, Isaac's son, married two Hittite women, which caused grief for his parents (Gen.26.34-35; 27.46). The Hittites are listed among the inhabitants of the Promised Land that God would drive out before the Israelites (Exo.3.8,17; 13.5; 23.23,28; 33.2; 34.11; Deu.7.1; 20.17; Jos.1.4; 3.10; 9.1; 11.3; 12.8; 24.11; Jdg.3.5; 1Ki.9.20; 2Ch.8.7; Ezr.9.1; Neh.9.8). During the time of the united monarchy, the Hittites are mentioned in connection with David's reign, particularly in the story of Uriah the Hittite, one of David's mighty men (2Sa.11; 23.39; 1Ch.11.41). Solomon had trade relations with the Hittites and even married Hittite women (1Ki.10.29; 11.1; 2Ch.1.17). The Hittites are also mentioned in the prophetic books as a point of comparison or as part of a list of nations (Isa.1.1; Ezk.16.3,45).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.15 referred to as Heth or Hittite (חֵת), or Hittite (חִתִּי); son of Canaan; a brother of Sidon, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '헷'이라 불림. 가나안의 아들. 시돈, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓, 스말과 하맛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 헷은 가나안의 아들이며 고대 근동의 유력한 민족 헷 족속의 조상이었다.
persons.article_ko: 헷(헷 족속이라고도 함)은 창세기 10장의 민족 계보에 따르면 함의 아들 가나안의 후손이었다(창 10:15; 대상 1:13). 헷 족속은 고대 근동의 저명한 민족이었으며 구약 전체에서 자주 언급된다. 아브라함은 아내 사라의 매장지로 막벨라 굴을 살 때 헷 족속과 거래했다(창 23장). 이 굴은 후에 아브라함, 이삭, 리브가, 레아, 이스라엘(야곱)의 매장지가 되었다(창 25:9-10; 49:29-32; 50:13). 이삭의 아들 에서는 두 헷 여인과 결혼하여 부모에게 근심을 안겨주었다(창 26:34-35; 27:46). 헷 족속은 하나님이 이스라엘 앞에서 쫓아내실 약속의 땅 주민 명단에 열거되어 있다(출 3:8, 17; 13:5; 23:23, 28; 33:2; 34:11; 신 7:1; 20:17; 수 1:4; 3:10; 9:1; 11:3; 12:8; 24:11; 삿 3:5; 왕상 9:20; 대하 8:7; 스 9:1; 느 9:8). 통일왕국 시대에 헷 족속은 다윗의 통치와 관련하여 언급되는데, 특히 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 헷 사람 우리야의 이야기에서 그러하다(삼하 11장; 23:39; 대상 11:41). 솔로몬은 헷 족속과 무역 관계를 맺었고 심지어 헷 여인들과 결혼했다(왕상 10:29; 11:1; 대하 1:17). 헷 족속은 예언서에서도 비교 대상이나 민족 목록의 일부로 언급된다(사 1:1; 겔 16:3, 45).

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A righteous king of Judah.
persons.short: Hezekiah was a king of Judah who instituted religious reforms and trusted in God during the Assyrian invasion.
persons.article: Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz and the 13th king of Judah. He reigned for 29 years (2Ki.18.2; 2Ch.29.1). Hezekiah is known for his religious reforms and his trust in God during the Assyrian invasion. He removed the high places, broke down the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles (2Ki.18.4; 2Ch.31.1). He also cleansed and restored the temple, and reinstituted the Passover celebration (2Ch.29-30). When Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invaded Judah, Hezekiah trusted in God and sought the counsel of the prophet Isaiah (2Ki.18-19; 2Ch.32; Isa.36-37). As a result, God delivered Jerusalem from the Assyrian army (2Ki.19.35-36; 2Ch.32.21; Isa.37.36-37). Hezekiah also faced a severe illness, but after he prayed, God granted him 15 more years of life (2Ki.20.1-11; 2Ch.32.24-26; Isa.38). However, Hezekiah's pride led him to show the Babylonian envoys all his treasures, which prompted Isaiah to prophesy the future Babylonian captivity (2Ki.20.12-19; 2Ch.32.27-31; Isa.39). Despite this, Hezekiah is remembered as a king who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord (2Ki.18.3; 2Ch.29.2). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat.1.9-10 and is also referenced in the books of Jeremiah, Hosea, and Micah )(Jer.15.4; 26.18-19; Hos.1.1; Mic.1.1).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.16.20 referred to as Hezekiah (חִזְקִיָּהוּ), or Hezekiah (יְחִזְקִיָּה), or Hezekiah (Ἐζεκίας); son of Ahaz and Abi; a brother of Maaseiah; husband of Hephzibah; father of Manasseh.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.16.20에 처음 언급되며 '히스기야'라 불림. 아하스와 아비의 아들. 마아세야의 형제. 헵시바의 남편. 므낫세의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 히스기야는 유다 왕으로 종교개혁을 이루었고 앗수르의 침공 중 하나님을 신뢰했다.
persons.article_ko: 히스기야는 아하스의 아들이며 유다의 열세 번째 왕이었다. 그는 이십구 년간 다스렸다(왕하 18:2; 대하 29:1). 히스기야는 종교개혁과 앗수르 침공 기간 동안 하나님께 대한 신뢰로 알려져 있다. 그는 산당을 제거하고 신성한 기둥들을 부수며 아세라 목상들을 찍어냈다(왕하 18:4; 대하 31:1). 그는 또한 성전을 정결하게 하고 회복시켰으며 유월절 축제를 재실시했다(대하 29-30장). 앗수르 왕 산헤립이 유다를 침공했을 때 히스기야는 하나님을 신뢰하며 선지자 이사야의 조언을 구했다(왕하 18-19장; 대하 32장; 사 36-37장). 그 결과 하나님은 예루살렘을 앗수르 군대에서 구원하셨다(왕하 19:35-36; 대하 32:21; 사 37:36-37). 히스기야는 또한 심각한 병에 걸렸으나 그가 기도한 후 하나님은 그에게 십오 년의 생명을 더 허락하셨다(왕하 20:1-11; 대하 32:24-26; 사 38장). 그러나 히스기야의 교만함은 바벨론 사신들에게 자신의 모든 보물을 보여주게 했고, 이는 이사야가 미래의 바벨론 포로를 예언하도록 이끌었다(왕하 20:12-19; 대하 32:27-31; 사 39장). 그럼에도 히스기야는 여호와 보시기에 정직히 행한 왕으로 기억된다(왕하 18:3; 대하 29:2). 그는 예수님의 족보에 언급되며(마 1:9-10) 예레미야, 호세아, 미가서에도 언급된다(렘 15:4; 26:18-19; 호 1:1; 미 1:1).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem.
persons.short: Hezekiah was an ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Hezekiah is briefly mentioned as an ancestor in the list of people returned from exile (Ezr.2.16; Neh.7.21).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.16 referred to as Hezekiah (חִזְקִיָּהוּ), or Hezekiah (יְחִזְקִיָּה); a son of Ater.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.16에 처음 언급되며 '히스기야'라 불림. 아델의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 히스기야는 예루살렘으로 돌아온 포로들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A clan leader who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Hezekiah was a clan leader among the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
persons.article: Hezekiah is mentioned in the lists of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. He is identified as the leader of a clan that numbered 98 people (Ezr.2.16; Neh.7.21). These lists were compiled to record the individuals and families who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. Hezekiah's presence in these lists suggests that he played a leadership role among the returning exiles and was responsible for his clan during the journey and resettlement in Jerusalem. No other details about this Hezekiah are provided in the Bible. (Ezr.2.16; Neh.7.21).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.17 only referred to as Hezekiah (חִזְקִיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.17에 처음 언급되며 '히스기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 히스기야는 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 포로들 중 한 가문의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah
persons.short: Hezekiah was an ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah.
persons.article: Hezekiah is mentioned in Zep.1.1 as an ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah. He is listed as the great-great-grandfather of Zephaniah, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah. No other details are provided about this Hezekiah. He is not to be confused with King Hezekiah of Judah, who lived earlier. The mention of Hezekiah in Zephaniah's genealogy helps to establish the prophet's lineage and time period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Zep.1.1 only referred to as Hezekiah (חִזְקִיָּהוּ); father of Amariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Zep.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '히스기야'라 불림. 아마랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 히스기야는 선지자 스바냐의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Ben-Hadad, king of Aram.
persons.short: Hezion was the grandfather of Ben-Hadad I, the king of Aram during the reign of Asa, king of Judah.
persons.article: Hezion is mentioned in 1Ki.15.18 as the grandfather of Ben-Hadad, the king of Aram (Syria) during the reign of King Asa of Judah. The verse states that there was a treaty between Asa's father and Hezion, which Asa sought to renew with Ben-Hadad. His mention in this context suggests that he was a significant figure in the history of Aram, likely a former king or ruler, who had established a treaty with the kingdom of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.15.18 only referred to as Hezion (חֶזְיוֹן); father of Tabrimmon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '헤시온'이라 불림. 다브림몬의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 헤시온은 유다 왕 아사 시대의 아람 왕 벤하닷 1세의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A priest in the time of David.
persons.short: Hezir was a priest who was assigned the 17th division of priestly service in the time of King David.
persons.article: Hezir is mentioned in 1Ch.24.15 as a priest during the reign of King David. He was the head of the 17th division of the priestly service, which was established by David when he organized the priests into 24 divisions for their service in the temple. Each division was responsible for serving in the temple for a week at a time, twice a year.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.15 only referred to as Hezir (חֵזִיר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.15에 처음 언급되며 '헤실'이라 불림.
