Jahdai is mentioned among these descendants (1Ch.2.47, indicating that he was part of Caleb's lineage and a member of the tribe of Judah). No other specific details are provided about Jahdai's life, occupation, or role within the family or tribe. His inclusion in this genealogical record, however, serves to highlight the importance of family lineage and the preservation of ancestral records among the Israelites, particularly within the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.47 only referred to as Jahdai (יַהְדַּי); wife of Caleb; mother of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '야대'라 불림. 갈렙의 아내. 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바와 사압의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 야대는 여분네의 아들 갈렙의 후손 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mighty warrior and head of a father's house in Manasseh.
persons.short: Jahdiel was a mighty warrior and head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh, east of the Jordan.
persons.article: Jahdiel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.24 as one of the mighty warriors and heads of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh, east of the Jordan. This passage is part of a genealogical record of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, who settled in the region of Gilead (1Ch.5.1-26). The half-tribe of Manasseh, along with the tribes of Reuben and Gad, had requested to settle in the land east of the Jordan, as it was suitable for their abundant livestock (Num.32.1-5). Moses granted their request on the condition that they would help their fellow Israelites.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.24 only referred to as Jahdiel (יַחְדִּיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.5.24에 처음 언급되며 '야디엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야디엘은 요단 동편 므낫세 반 지파의 용맹한 용사이며 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Buz, a Gadite
persons.short: Jahdo, a son of Buz, was a descendant of Gad and a clan head.
persons.article: Jahdo is mentioned in 1Ch.5.14 as a son of Buz, who was a descendant of Gad. He is listed among the clan heads of the Gadites during the reign of King Jotham of Judah and King Jeroboam II of Israel. This suggests that Jahdo held a leadership position within the tribe of Gad during this period. The biblical text does not provide any further details about Jahdo's life or specific role as a clan head.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.14 only referred to as Jahdo (יַחְדּוֹ); a son of Buz; father of Jeshishai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '야도'라 불림. 부스의 아들. 여시새의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 부스의 아들 야흐도는 갓의 후손이며 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Zebulun, grandson of Jacob, and a clan leader.
persons.short: Jahleel, son of Zebulun, was a grandson of Jacob and a clan leader.
persons.article: Jahleel was one of the sons of Zebulun and a grandson of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen. 46:14). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt during the time of Joseph. Later, in the census taken in the wilderness, Jahleel is listed as one of the clans of Zebulun (Num. 26:26). The Jahleelites, his descendants, are counted among the clans of Zebulun. Apart from these two mentions in the genealogies and census, no other details about Jahleel's life or specific role are provided in the Bible. His inclusion in these lists highlights his place in the lineage of Zebulun and his status as a clan leader within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Zebulun living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.14 referred to as Jahleel (יַחְלְאֵל), or Jahleelite (יַחְלְאֵלִי); son of Zebulun; a brother of Sered and Elon.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.14에 처음 언급되며 '얄르엘'이라 불림. 스불론의 아들. 세렛과 엘론의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스불론의 아들 야흘르엘은 야곱의 손자이며 가문의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Tola, an Issacharite
persons.short: Jahmai, a son of Tola, was a descendant of Issachar and a clan head.
persons.article: Jahmai is mentioned in 1Ch.7.2 as one of the sons of Tola, who was a descendant of Issachar. He is listed among the clan heads of Issachar, indicating that he held a leadership position within the tribe. The biblical text describes Jahmai and his brothers as valiant warriors, suggesting that they were known for their military prowess.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.2 only referred to as Jahmai (יַחְמַי); son of Tola; a brother of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Ibsam and Shemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.2에 처음 언급되며 '야매'라 불림. 돌라의 아들. 웃시, 르바야, 여리엘, 입삼과 스므엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 돌라의 아들 야매는 잇사갈의 후손이며 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob, and a clan leader.
persons.short: Jahzeel (or Jahziel), son of Naphtali, was a grandson of Jacob and a clan leader.
persons.article: Jahzeel, also known as Jahziel, was one of the sons of Naphtali and a grandson of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen. 46:24; 1Ch. 7:13). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt during the time of Joseph. In the census taken in the wilderness, Jahzeel is listed as one of the clans of Naphtali (Num. 26:48). The Jahzeelites, his descendants, are counted among the clans of Naphtali. Apart from these mentions in the genealogies and census, no other details about Jahzeel's life or specific role are provided in the Bible. His inclusion in these lists highlights his place in the lineage of Naphtali and his status as a clan leader within the tribe. The variation in the spelling of his name (Jahzeel or Jahziel) occurs in different passages, but both refer to the same individual.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Naphtali living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.24 referred to as Jahzeel (יַחְצְאֵל), or Jahzeelite (יַחְצְאֵלִי), or Jahziel (יַחְצִיאֵל); son of Naphtali; a brother of Guni, Jezer and Shillem.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.24에 처음 언급되며 '야스엘'이라 불림. 납달리의 아들. 구니, 예셀과 실렘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 납달리의 아들 야스엘(야시엘이라고도 함)은 야곱의 손자이며 가문의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Opposed Ezra's command for Israelites to divorce foreign wives.
persons.short: Jahzeiah, along with three others, opposed Ezra's order for Israelites to divorce their foreign wives.
persons.article: Jahzeiah, son of Tikvah, is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezr.10.15. He was one of the four men who opposed Ezra's command for the Israelites to divorce their foreign wives. After the Babylonian exile, Ezra led a reform to purify the Jewish community by separating from foreign influences. As part of this reform, he ordered the men of Israel to divorce their foreign wives. Jahzeiah, along with Jonathan son of Asahel, Meshullam, and Shabbethai, stood against this decision. However, their opposition was to no avail, and many innocent women and children were sent away. The name Jahzeiah means "Yahweh sees" in Hebrew, combining the shortened form of the divine name "Yah" with the verb "haza," meaning "to see" or "have a vision."
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.15 only referred to as Jahzeiah (יַחְזְיָה); a son of Tikvah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '야스야'라 불림. 디과의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 야스야는 다른 세 사람과 함께 에스라가 이스라엘 사람들에게 이방인 아내와 이혼하라고 한 명령을 반대했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest in postexilic Jerusalem
persons.short: Jahzerah was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Jahzerah is mentioned in 1Ch.9.12 as one of the priests who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was a descendant of Immer, who was a priest during the time of King David (1Ch.24.14). The text provides no further information about Jahzerah's life or role in the postexilic community. His inclusion in the list of priests suggests that he played a part in reestablishing the temple worship and religious practices in Jerusalem following the return from exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 only referred to as Jahzerah (יַחְזֵרָה); a son of Meshullam; father of Adiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '야세라'라 불림. 므술람의 아들. 아디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야스라는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Mordecai's father, a Benjamite
persons.short: Jair was the father of Mordecai, a Benjamite mentioned in the book of Esther.
persons.article: Jair is briefly mentioned in Est.2.5 as the father of Mordecai, one of the main characters in the book of Esther. Jair was a Benjamite, indicating that he belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. The text states that Jair's ancestors, Kish and Shimei, had been exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon during the time of King Jeconiah of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.2.5 only referred to as Jair (יָאִיר); a son of Shimei; father of Mordecai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.2.5에 처음 언급되며 '야일'이라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 모르드개의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야일은 에스더서에 언급된 베냐민 사람 모르드개의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Gileadite judge who led Israel
persons.short: Jair the Gileadite was a judge who led Israel for twenty-two years.
persons.article: Jair the Gileadite is introduced in Jdg.10.3-5 as a judge who led Israel for twenty-two years. He came after Tola and was succeeded by Jephthah. Jair had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys and controlled thirty towns in Gilead, which were called Havvoth-jair. This suggests that Jair and his family held significant influence and power in the region. The text does not provide any further details about Jair's leadership or accomplishments during his time as a judge. After his death, Jair was buried in Kamon, a location likely within Gilead.
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.10.3 only referred to as Jair (יָאִיר).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '야일'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 길르앗 사람 야일은 이스라엘을 이십이 년간 다스린 사사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Manassite leader who captured Gilead
persons.short: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captured the region of Gilead.
persons.article: Jair was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, who played a significant role in the conquest and settlement of the region east of the Jordan River. According to Num.32.41 and Deu.3.14, Jair captured the settlements in Gilead and named them Havvoth-jair, which means "the towns of Jair." 1Ch.2.22 states that Jair controlled twenty-three cities in Gilead. In 2Sa.20.26, a person named Ira the Jairite is mentioned as one of David's officials, possibly indicating that Jair's descendants continued to hold influential positions. 1Ki.4.13 refers to the towns of Jair in the context of Solomon's administrative districts, suggesting that the region remained associated with Jair's name long after his lifetime.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.32.41 referred to as Jair (יָאִיר), or Jairite (יָאִרִי); a son of Segub.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.32.41에 처음 언급되며 '야일'이라 불림. 스굽의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 므낫세의 후손 야일은 길르앗 지역을 점령했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Synagogue leader whose daughter Jesus healed
persons.short: Jairus, a synagogue leader, sought Jesus to heal his dying daughter.
persons.article: Jairus was a synagogue leader mentioned in the Gospels of Mark and Luke. He approached Jesus desperately seeking help for his critically ill daughter, who was about twelve years old. In Mrk.5.22-23, Jairus fell at Jesus' feet and pleaded earnestly with him to come and lay hands on his daughter, believing that Jesus could heal her. While Jesus was on his way to Jairus' house, they received news that the girl had died. However, Jesus encouraged Jairus to have faith and continued to his home. There, Jesus took the girl by the hand and commanded her to get up, miraculously bringing her back to life (Mrk.5.41-42; Luk.8.54-55). This event demonstrated Jesus' power over death and his compassion for those in need.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mrk.5.22 only referred to as Jairus (Ἰάειρος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mrk.5.22에 처음 언급되며 '야이로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 회당장 야이로는 죽어가는 딸을 고쳐달라고 예수님을 찾아왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Agur, the author of Proverbs 30
persons.short: Jakeh was the father of Agur, the author of Proverbs 30.
persons.article: Jakeh is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Pro.30.1, as the father of Agur, the author of the sayings in this chapter. The text provides no further information about Jakeh's life, occupation, or place of origin. His name suggests that he may have been a non-Israelite, possibly from a neighboring region. The inclusion of Agur's sayings in the book of Proverbs indicates that Jakeh's son was recognized for his wisdom and that his teachings were deemed valuable enough to be included in the biblical canon.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at Pro.30.1 only referred to as Jakeh (יָקֶה); father of Agur.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Pro.30.1에 처음 언급되며 '야게'라 불림. 아굴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야게는 잠언 30장의 저자 아굴의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of the 12th priestly division
persons.short: Jakim was the head of the 12th priestly division during David's reign.
persons.article: Jakim is mentioned in 1Ch.24.12 as the head of the 12th priestly division during the reign of King David. David organized the priests into 24 divisions to ensure a systematic rotation of their duties in the temple. Each division was responsible for serving in the temple for a week at a time, twice a year. As the head of his division, Jakim would have been responsible for overseeing the priestly duties and ensuring that the temple services were carried out according to the prescribed regulations.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.12 only referred to as Jakim (יָקִים).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.12에 처음 언급되며 '야김'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야김은 다윗 왕 시대에 열두 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Zabdi@1Ch.8.19, Elienai@1Ch.8.20, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Eliel@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21, Shimrath@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: Benjamite, son of Shimei
persons.short: Jakim was a Benjamite, the son of Shimei, mentioned in a genealogy.
persons.article: Jakim is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.8.19 as part of a genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He is listed as one of the sons of Shimei, along with his brothers Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel. No further information is provided about Jakim's life or role within the tribe of Benjamin. The genealogy in this chapter traces the descendants of Benjamin, focusing on the family of Saul, Israel's first king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.19 only referred to as Jakim (יָקִים); son of Shimei; a brother of Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.19에 처음 언급되며 '야김'이라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 시그리, 삽디, 엘리에내, 실르대, 엘리엘, 아다야, 브라야와 시므랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야김은 시므이의 아들로 베냐민 사람이며, 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
persons.short: Jalam was a son of Esau and Oholibamah, and a chief of Edom.
persons.article: Jalam was one of the sons born to Esau, the son of Isaac, and his wife Oholibamah, as recorded in Gen.36.5, 14, and 18, and 1Ch.1.35. Esau, also known as Edom, settled in the region of Seir and became the ancestor of the Edomites. Jalam and his brothers, Jeush and Korah, were born in Canaan before Esau moved to Seir. Gen.36.18 lists Jalam as one of the chiefs of Edom, indicating that he and his descendants held a position of authority within the Edomite tribal structure.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.5 only referred to as Jalam (יַעְלָם); son of Esau and Oholibamah; a brother of Jeush and Korah; half-brother of: Eliphaz and Reuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.5에 처음 언급되며 '얄람'이라 불림. 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들. 엘리바스, 르우엘, 여우스와 고라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 얄람은 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들이며 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ezrah, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Jalon was a son of Ezrah, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Jalon is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.17 as one of the sons of Ezrah, along with his brothers Jether and Mered. Ezrah was a descendant of Judah, the son of Israel (or 'Jacob'), through Perez. The text does not provide any further information about Jalon's life, occupation, or role within the tribe of Judah. His mention in the genealogy suggests that he was an ancestor of some of the families within the tribe of Judah, although no specific details are given about his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.17 only referred to as Jalon (יָלוֹן); son of Ezrah; a brother of Jether, Mered and Epher.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '얄론'이라 불림. 에스라의 아들. 예델, 메렛과 에벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 얄론은 유다 지파 에스라의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Egyptian magician who opposed Moses
persons.short: Jambres was an Egyptian magician who, along with Jannes, opposed Moses.
persons.article: Jambres is mentioned in 2Ti.3.8 as one of two Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses during the events of the Exodus. Along with Jannes, Jambres is said to have resisted Moses, likely referring to the magicians' attempts to duplicate the miracles performed by Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh (Exodus 7-8). Although not named in the Old Testament, Jewish tradition identified these two magicians and passed down their names. Paul's use of these names in 2 Timothy suggests that the story of Jannes and Jambres was well-known among his audience and served as an example of those who resist the truth. The text does not provide any further details about Jambres' life or the extent of his opposition to Moses.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Exodus, only mentioned at 2Ti.3.8 only referred to as Jambres (Ἰαμβρῆς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.3.8에 처음 언급되며 '얌브레'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 얌브레는 얀네와 함께 모세를 대적한 애굽의 마술사였다.

persons.description: Father of an apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Father of Judas, an Apostles
persons.short: James, father of Judas who was also know as Thaddaeus, one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus.
persons.article: James the father of Judas who was usually known as Thaddaeus to distinguish him from Judas Iscariot. He was the father of one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus, as recorded in Luk.6.15 and Act.1.13. Beyond the name of his son, the Bible provides no further information about his background, ministry, or fate.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.6.16 only referred to as James (Ἰάκωβος); father of Judas.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도의 아버지. Luk.6.16에 처음 언급되며 '야고보'라 불림. 유다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야고보는 다대오라고도 불린 유다의 아버지로, 예수님이 택하신 열두 사도 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: James "the Less", son of Alphaeus
persons.short: James son of Alphaeus, known as "James the Less"was one of the Twelve Apostles.
persons.article: James was later known as "James the Less" to distinguishe him from James "the Great" and James "the Just". He was a son of Alphaeus, one of the Twelve Apostles. In the lists of the apostles provided in Mat.10.3, Mrk.3.18, Luk.6.15, and Act.1.13,"
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.10.3 only referred to as James (Ἰάκωβος); a son of Alphaeus and probably Mary; brother of Joses and possibly Matthew.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '야고보'라 불림. 알패오와 마리아의 아들. 요세와 마태의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 알패오의 아들 야고보('작은 야고보'라고도 함)는 열두 사도 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Jesus' brother, leader in the Jerusalem church
persons.short: James, the brother of Jesus, was a leader in the Jerusalem church and authored the epistle of James.
persons.article: James was one of the brothers of Jesus, along with Joses, Judas, and Simon (Mat.13.55; Mrk.6.3). During Jesus' ministry, James and his brothers did not believe in Him (Jhn.7.5). However, after Jesus' resurrection, James became a believer and a prominent leader in the early church in Jerusalem. He was one of the individuals to whom Jesus appeared after His resurrection (1Co.15.7). In the early church, James played a significant role in the Jerusalem Council, which addressed the issue of Gentile believers and the Mosaic Law (Act.15.13-21). He also received Paul and his companions during their visits to Jerusalem (Act.21.18; Gal.1.19; 2.9). James authored the New Testament epistle that bears his name, in which he emphasizes practical faith and good works (Jam 1.1). He is often referred to as "James the Just" due to his reputation for righteousness and his strict observance of the Jewish law. According to early church tradition, James was martyred in Jerusalem around 62 AD.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.13.55 only referred to as James (Ἰάκωβος); son of Joseph and Mary; a brother of Jesus, Joses, Simon and Jude.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.13.55에 처음 언급되며 '야고보'라 불림. 요셉과 마리아의 아들. 예수, 요세, 시몬과 유다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예수님의 형제 야고보는 예루살렘 교회의 지도자였으며 야고보서를 저술했다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve Apostles
persons.short: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, was one of the Twelve Apostles and a member of Jesus' inner circle.
persons.article: James, the son of Zebedee and brother of John, was one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus. He was a fisherman by trade and was called by Jesus, along with his brother, to follow Him (Mat.4.21; Mrk.1.19). James, John, and Peter formed Jesus' inner circle and were present at significant events such as the Transfiguration (Mat.17.1; Mrk.9.2; Luk.9.28 and Jesus' agony in the Garden of Gethsemane )(Mrk.14.33). Jesus surnamed James and John "Boanerges," meaning "Sons of Thunder" (Mrk.3.17, possibly referring to their zealous and passionate nature). James and his brother also asked Jesus for positions of honor in His kingdom (Mrk.10.35-41). After Jesus' ascension, James continued to play a prominent role in the early church (Act.1.13). He was the first of the Twelve Apostles to be martyred, executed by Herod Agrippa I around 44 AD (Act.12.2).
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.4.21 only referred to as James (Ἰάκωβος); son of Zebedee; a brother of John.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '야고보'라 불림. 세베대와 살로매의 아들. 요한의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세베대의 아들이자 요한의 형제인 야고보는 열두 사도 중 한 사람이며 예수님의 측근 제자였다.
persons.article_ko: 세베대의 아들이며 요한의 형제인 야고보는 예수님이 택하신 열두 사도 중 한 사람이었다. 그는 어부였으며 형제와 함께 예수님을 따르도록 부름받았다(마 4:21; 막 1:19). 야고보, 요한, 베드로는 예수님의 측근 그룹을 이루었고 변화산(마 17:1; 막 9:2; 눅 9:28)과 겟세마네 동산에서의 예수님의 고뇌(막 14:33) 같은 중요한 사건들에 함께했다. 예수님은 야고보와 요한에게 '보아너게' 곧 '우레의 아들'이라는 별명을 붙이셨는데(막 3:17), 이는 아마 그들의 열정적이고 격정적인 성격을 가리키는 것으로 보인다. 야고보와 그의 형제는 또한 예수님의 나라에서 영예로운 자리를 요청했다(막 10:35-41). 예수님의 승천 후 야고보는 계속해서 초대교회에서 저명한 역할을 했다(행 1:13). 그는 열두 사도 중 가장 먼저 순교한 사람으로, 서기 약 44년경 헤롯 아그립바 1세에게 처형당했다(행 12:2).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ram, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Jamin was a son of Ram and a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Jamin is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.2.27 as one of the sons of Ram, along with his brothers Bunah, Oren, and Ozem. Ram was a descendant of Judah through Hezron and Jerahmeel. The genealogy in this chapter traces the lineage of Judah, focusing on the descendants of Hezron. No further information is provided about Jamin's life or his role within the tribe of Judah. His mention in the genealogy suggests that he was an ancestor of some of the families within the tribe, although no specific details are given about his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.27 only referred to as Jamin (יָמִין); son of Ram; a brother of Maaz and Eker.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.27에 처음 언급되며 '야민'이라 불림. 람의 아들. 마아스와 에겔의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야민은 람의 아들로 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Simeon, grandson of Jacob
persons.short: Jamin was a son of Simeon and a grandson of Jacob.
persons.article: Jamin was one of the sons of Simeon, the second son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah, as recorded in Gen.46.10, Exo.6.15, and 1Ch.4.24. He was born in Canaan and went down to Egypt with his father and grandfather as part of the seventy members of Jacob's household (Gen.46.27). In Num.26.12, Jamin is mentioned as one of the clans of Simeon, suggesting that his descendants formed a significant subgroup within the tribe. The Bible does not provide any further details about Jamin's life or his role in the events of the Israelites' history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.10 referred to as Jamin (יָמִין), or Jaminite (יָֽמִינִי); son of Simeon; a brother of Jemuel, Ohad, Jachin, Zerah and Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '야민'이라 불림. 시므온과 시므온의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 여무엘, 오핫, 야긴, 세라와 사울의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야민은 시므온의 아들이며 야곱의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
persons.short: Jamin was a Levite who helped explain the Law to the people during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah.
persons.article: Jamin is mentioned in Neh.8.7 as one of the Levites who helped explain the Law to the people during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. After the return from the Babylonian exile, Ezra the scribe read the Book of the Law to the assembled Israelites during the Feast of Tabernacles. As he read, the Levites, including Jamin, helped the people understand the Law by translating and interpreting it for them. This event marked a significant moment in the spiritual reformation of the Israelites as they recommitted themselves to following God's commandments. The text does not provide any further details about Jamin's life or his specific role among the Levites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.7 only referred to as Jamin (יָמִין).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '야민'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 야민은 에스라와 느헤미야 시대에 백성에게 율법을 설명하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Jamlech was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Jamlech is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.34 as one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He is listed along with other Simeonite leaders, including Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, and others. These leaders are described as having gone to the region of Gedor, east of the valley, in search of pasture for their flocks. This event likely took place during a time of peace and prosperity in Judah, as Hezekiah was known for his religious reforms and his trust in God (2Chronicles 29-31).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.34 only referred to as Jamlech (יַמְלֵךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.34에 처음 언급되며 '야믈렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야믈렉은 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite leader who settled in Bashan
persons.short: Janai was a leader from the tribe of Gad who settled in the region of Bashan.
persons.article: Janai is mentioned in 1Ch.5.12 as one of the leaders from the tribe of Gad who settled in the region of Bashan, along with his fellow leaders Joel, Shapham, and Shaphat. The Gadites are described as mighty warriors, famous men, and heads of their families. They settled in the land of Gilead in Bashan, extending as far as Salecah, due to the abundance of pasture for their livestock. This settlement likely took place during the early period of Israel's history, after the conquest of Canaan and the allocation of tribal territories.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.12 only referred to as Janai (יַעֲנַי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.12에 처음 언급되며 '야내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야내는 바산 지역에 정착한 갓 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
persons.short: Jannai was an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Jannai is mentioned in Luk.3.24 as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy traced through Joseph, Jesus' legal father. He is listed as the son of Joseph and the father of Melchi. The genealogy in Luke's Gospel traces Jesus' lineage back to Adam, emphasizing His humanity and connection to all mankind. No further information is provided about Jannai's life or his role in the family line that eventually led to Jesus. His inclusion in the genealogy highlights the importance of family heritage and the fulfillment of God's plan through the generations.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.24 only referred to as Jannai (Ἰαννά); a son of Joseph; father of Melchi.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '얀나'라 불림. 요셉의 아들. 멜기의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 얀내는 누가복음 족보에 언급된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Egyptian magician who opposed Moses
persons.short: Jannes was an Egyptian magician who, along with Jambres, opposed Moses.
persons.article: Jannes is mentioned in 2Ti.3.8 as one of two Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses during the events of the Exodus. Along with Jambres, Jannes is said to have resisted Moses, likely referring to the magicians' attempts to duplicate the miracles performed by Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh (Exodus 7-8). Although not named in the Old Testament, Jewish tradition identified these two magicians and passed down their names. Paul's use of these names in 2 Timothy suggests that the story of Jannes and Jambres was well-known among his audience and served as an example of those who resist the truth. The text does not provide any further details about Jannes' life or the extent of his opposition to Moses.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Exodus, only mentioned at 2Ti.3.8 only referred to as Jannes (Ἰαννῆς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.3.8에 처음 언급되며 '얀네'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 얀네는 얌브레와 함께 모세를 대적한 애굽의 마술사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Noah, ancestor of Indo-European peoples
persons.short: Japheth was one of Noah's three sons and the ancestor of the Indo-European peoples.
persons.article: Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah, along with Shem and Ham, as recorded in Gen.5.32 and Gen.6.10. He and his brothers were born before the Great Flood. Japheth, his wife, and his brothers and their wives entered the ark with Noah and survived the Flood (Gen.7.13). After the Flood, Noah blessed Japheth, saying, "May God extend Japheth's territory; may Japheth live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be the slave of Japheth" (Gen.9.27). Japheth's descendants are listed in Gen.10.2-5 and 1Ch.1.5-7, and they are generally associated with the Indo-European peoples, including the Greeks, Medes, and Thracians. The name Japheth means "enlargement" or "expansion," which is fitting given the widespread distribution of his descendants. Japheth's offspring played a significant role in the repopulation of the earth after the Flood and the development of various nations and cultures.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.5.32 only referred to as Japheth (יֶ֫פֶת); son of Noah; a brother of Shem and Ham; father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras. See ambiguities here<https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WI5gOd0O-wfPf5rjuRPW5yhxNFoedx2fssmgOQGYj7o/edit?tab=t.0#A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.5.32 only referred to as Japheth (יֶ֫פֶת); son of Noah; a brother of Shem and Ham; father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.5.32에 처음 언급되며 '야벳'이라 불림. 노아와 나아마의 아들. 셈과 함의 형제. 고멜, 마곡, 마대, 야완, 두발, 메섹과 디라스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야벳은 노아의 세 아들 중 한 사람이며 인도유럽 민족의 조상이었다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: Son of David, born in Jerusalem
persons.short: Japhia was one of King David's sons, born to him in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Japhia is mentioned in 2Sa.5.15 and 1Ch.3.7 and 1Ch.14.6 as one of the sons born to King David in Jerusalem. He was born after David had conquered the city and established it as his capital. Japhia's mother is not named, but he was one of several children born to David through his various wives. The Bible does not provide any further information about Japhia's life, his relationship with his father or siblings, or any roles he may have played in the royal court. His inclusion in the lists of David's sons emphasizes the importance of family lineage and the growth of David's household during his reign in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.5.15 only referred to as Japhia (יָפִיעַ); son of David; a brother of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.5.15에 처음 언급되며 '야비아'라 불림. 다윗과 예루살렘의 아내들의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야비아는 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗 왕의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Lachish, defeated by Joshua
persons.short: Japhia was the king of Lachish, one of the Amorite cities defeated by Joshua.
persons.article: Japhia is mentioned in Jos.10.3 as the king of Lachish, one of the Amorite cities that formed an alliance against the Israelites during the conquest of Canaan. When the people of Gibeon made a peace treaty with Israel, Japhia joined forces with Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, and three other Amorite kings to attack Gibeon. In response, Joshua and the Israelite army came to Gibeon's defense and, with the help of God, defeated the Amorite kings and their armies (Jos.10.1-27). Lachish, along with the other Amorite cities, was conquered by Joshua and the Israelites. The text does not provide any further details about Japhia's life or his fate after the battle.
persons.summary: A king in Canaan living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at Jos.10.3 only referred to as Japhia (יָפִיעַ).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 왕. Jos.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '야비아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야비아는 여호수아에게 패배한 아모리 성읍 중 하나인 라기스의 왕이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Asher, son of Heber
persons.short: Japhlet was a descendant of Asher and the son of Heber.
persons.article: Japhlet is mentioned in 1Ch.7.32-33 as one of the sons of Heber, who was a descendant of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Japhlet had three sons: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. The text does not provide any further details about Japhlet's life or his role within the tribe of Asher. His mention in the genealogy suggests that he was an ancestor of some of the families within the tribe, although no specific details are given about his descendants. In Jos.16.3, a place called the "border of Beth-horon the lower" is described as extending to the "border of the Japhletites," possibly indicating that Japhlet's descendants inhabited a specific region within the territory of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.16.3 referred to as Japhlet (יַפְלֵט), or Japhletite (יַפְלֵטִי); son of Heber; a brother of Shomer, Hotham and Shua; father of Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jos.16.3에 처음 언급되며 '야블렛'이라 불림. 헤벨의 아들. 소멜, 호담과 수아의 형제. 바삭, 빔할과 아스왓의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야블렛은 아셀의 후손이며 헤벨의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Ancestor of Noah; father of Enoch
persons.short: Jared was an ancestor of Noah and the father of Enoch, who walked with God.
persons.article: Jared is mentioned in the genealogies of Gen.5.15-20 and 1Ch.1.2 as a descendant of Seth, the third son of Adam and Eve. He was the son of Mahalalel and the father of Enoch. Jared lived to the age of 962 years, making him the second-longest-lived person mentioned in the Bible after Methuselah. He was born when Mahalalel was 65 years old and had other sons and daughters in addition to Enoch. Jared's life is notable for being the father of Enoch, who is described as walking with God and being taken by God without experiencing death (Gen.5.22-24). In Luk.3.37, Jared is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, emphasizing the continuity of God's plan from creation to the coming of the Messiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.5.15 referred to as Jared (יֶ֫רֶד), or Jared (Ἰάρεδ); a son of Mahalalel; father of Enoch; founder of Gedor.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.5.15에 처음 언급되며 '야렛'이라 불림. 마할랄렐의 아들. 에녹의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야렛은 노아의 조상이며, 하나님과 동행한 에녹의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Egyptian living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Egyptian servant who married Sheshan's daughter
persons.short: Jarha was an Egyptian servant who married the daughter of Sheshan, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Jarha is mentioned in 1Ch.2.34-35 as an Egyptian servant who married the daughter of Sheshan, a descendant of Judah. Sheshan had no sons, only daughters, so he gave one of his daughters in marriage to his servant Jarha. This marriage between an Israelite woman and an Egyptian servant was unusual, as it deviated from the typical practice of marrying within one's tribe or nation. The text does not provide any further details about Jarha's life or his relationship with Sheshan's daughter. However, their marriage resulted in the continuation of Sheshan's lineage, as Jarha's son Attai is listed among the descendants of Judah. This inclusion of Jarha in the genealogy of Judah demonstrates that God's plan can work through unexpected means and that one's background does not limit their potential to be part of God's people.
persons.summary: A man of Egypt living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.34 only referred to as Jarha (יַרְחָע); husband of Ahlai; father of Attai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 애굽 사람. 1Ch.2.34에 처음 언급되며 '야르하'라 불림. 알래의 남편. 앗대의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야하는 유다의 후손 세산의 딸과 결혼한 애굽인 종이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Jarib was a priest who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Jarib is mentioned in Ezr.10.18 as one of the priests who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from the Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land. This was a violation of God's command to maintain their holiness and avoid the idolatrous practices of the surrounding nations. Ezra called for a solemn assembly, during which the people confessed their sin and agreed to separate from their foreign wives. Jarib is listed among the priests who had married foreign women and pledged to put them away. The text does not provide any further details about Jarib's life or the specific circumstances of his marriage. However, his inclusion in this list serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining purity and obedience to God's commands, even for those in positions of spiritual leadership.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.18 only referred to as Jarib (יָרִיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '야립'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야립은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader sent by Ezra to find Levites
persons.short: Jarib was one of the leaders sent by Ezra to find Levites to serve in the Temple.
persons.article: Jarib is mentioned in Ezr.8.16 as one of the leaders sent by Ezra to the place called Casiphia to find Levites and Temple servants to bring back to Jerusalem. After returning from the Babylonian exile, Ezra was tasked with reestablishing proper worship in the Temple. To accomplish this, he needed Levites to perform the necessary duties. Ezra sent Jarib, along with other leaders, to Casiphia, where there was a community of Levites. The text does not provide any further details about Jarib's life or his specific role in this mission. However, his inclusion in the list of leaders suggests that he was a trusted and capable individual who could help Ezra in his efforts to restore the Temple worship.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.16 only referred to as Jarib (יָרִיב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '야립'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야립은 성전에서 섬길 레위인을 찾도록 에스라가 보낸 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite, son of Gilead
persons.short: Jaroah was a Gadite, the son of Gilead, mentioned in a genealogy.
persons.article: Jaroah is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.5.14 as part of a genealogy of the tribe of Gad. He is listed as the son of Gilead, who was a descendant of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. No further information is provided about Jaroah's life or his role within the tribe of Gad. The genealogy in this chapter traces the descendants of Gad, focusing on the families that settled in the region of Gilead. Jaroah's mention in the genealogy suggests that he was an ancestor of some of the Gadite families that lived in this area.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.14 only referred to as Jaroah (יָרוֹחַ); a son of Gilead; father of Huri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '야로아'라 불림. 길르앗의 아들. 후리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야로아는 길르앗의 아들이며 갓 사람으로, 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancient Hebrew book mentioned in the Old Testament
persons.short: Jashar was an ancient Hebrew book mentioned in the Old Testament, but not included in the biblical canon.
persons.article: Jashar, also known as the "Book of Jashar" or the "Book of the Upright," is mentioned twice in the Old Testament (Jos.10.13 and 2Sa.1.18). It appears to have been an ancient Hebrew collection of poetry or historical accounts that was known to the authors of the biblical texts. In Jos.10.13, the book of Jashar is referenced in connection with the miraculous event of the sun and moon standing still during Joshua's battle against the Amorite kings. In 2Sa.1.18, David's lament over the deaths of Saul and Jonathan is said to be written in the Book of Jashar. These references suggest that the Book of Jashar was a recognized source of poetry and historical information, although the book itself is not included in the biblical canon. The exact content and date of the Book of Jashar are unknown, and no copies of the book have been discovered.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.10.13 only referred to as Jashar (יָשָׁר).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jos.10.13에 처음 언급되며 '야살'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야살은 구약에 언급되었으나 성경 정경에는 포함되지 않은 고대 히브리 책이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of some of David's mighty men
persons.short: Jashen, also known as Hashem, was the father of some of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Jashen, also referred to as Hashem, is mentioned in 2Sa.23.32 and 1Ch.11.34 as the father of some of David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors who served under King David and played a significant role in his military campaigns and the establishment of his kingdom. The sons of Jashen are listed among these mighty men, indicating that they were valiant and capable soldiers. The text does not provide any further details about Jashen's life. The variation in the name between "Jashen" and "Hashem" may be due to textual differences or scribal errors in the transmission of the biblical text.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.32 referred to as Jashen (יָשֵׁן), or Hashem (הָשֵׁם).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.32에 처음 언급되며 '야센'이라 불림. 야센의 아들(이름 미상)의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야센(하솀이라고도 함)은 다윗의 용사 몇 명의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Korahite who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Jashobeam was a Korahite who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Jashobeam is mentioned in 1Ch.12.6 as one of the Korahites who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. The Korahites were a Levitical family known for their role in the music and worship of the tabernacle and temple. During David's time of exile, many skilled warriors from various tribes came to support him, recognizing him as the rightful king of Israel. Jashobeam, along with other Korahites, was among these supporters. The text describes them as brave warriors, trained for battle and able to handle the shield and spear. Their presence at Ziklag demonstrates their loyalty to David and their willingness to stand with him during a difficult time. This Jashobeam is likely a different person from the mighty man of the same name mentioned in other passages, as the context and tribal affiliation differ.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.6 only referred to as Jashobeam (יָשׇׁבְעָם).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.6에 처음 언급되며 '야소브암'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고라 사람 야소브암은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Chief of David's mighty men, Hachmoni's son
persons.short: Jashobeam, also known as Josheb-basshebet, was the chief of David's mighty men and the son of Hachmoni.
persons.article: Jashobeam, also referred to as Josheb-basshebet, was a prominent figure among David's mighty men. He is mentioned in 1Ch.11.11 and 1Ch.27.2, as well as 2Sa.23.8. Jashobeam was the son of Hachmoni and is described as the chief of the mighty men. In 1Ch.11.11, it is recorded that he wielded his spear against 300 men and killed them in a single encounter. This feat demonstrates his exceptional skill and bravery as a warrior. In 1Ch.27.2, Jashobeam is listed as the leader of the first division of David's army, which served the king in the first month of each year. This position indicates that he held a high rank and was trusted with significant military responsibilities. The variations in his name, "Jashobeam" and "Josheb-basshebet," may be due to textual differences or scribal errors in the transmission of the biblical text.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.8 referred to as Jashobeam (יָשׇׁבְעָם), or Josheb-basshebeth (יֹשֵׁב בַּשֶּׁ֫בֶת); a son of Zabdiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '야소브암'이라 불림. 삽디엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 야소브암(요셉밧세벳이라고도 함)은 학모니의 아들이며 다윗 용사들의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Jashub was an Israelite who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Jashub is mentioned in Ezr.10.29 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from the Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land, which was a violation of God's command to maintain their holiness and avoid idolatry. Ezra called for a solemn assembly, during which the people confessed their sin and agreed to separate from their foreign wives. Jashub is listed among those who had taken foreign wives and pledged to put them away. The text does not provide any further details about Jashub's life or the specific circumstances of his marriage. His inclusion in this list serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining purity and obedience to God's commands.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.29 only referred to as Jashub (יָשׁוּב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.29에 처음 언급되며 '야숩'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야숩은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Issachar, grandson of Jacob
persons.short: Jashub, also known as Yob, was a son of Issachar and a grandson of Jacob.
persons.article: Jashub, also referred to as Yob, was one of the sons of Issachar, as recorded in Num.26.24, 1 Chronicles Num.7.1, and Gen.46.13. He was born to Issachar, the ninth son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah, during the time when the Israelites lived in Canaan. In Gen.46.13, Jashub is mentioned as one of the descendants of Jacob who went down to Egypt during the famine, along with his father and brothers. The name "Yob" appears to be an alternate spelling or pronunciation of his name. In Num.26.24, Jashub is listed as one of the clans of Issachar during the census taken in the wilderness. This suggests that his descendants formed a significant subgroup within the tribe of Issachar. The Bible does not provide any further details about Jashub's life or his role in the events of Israel's history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.13 referred to as Jashub (יָשׁוּב), or Jashubite (יָשֻׁבִי), or Yob (יוֹב); son of Issachar; a brother of Tola, Puah and Shimron.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.13에 처음 언급되며 '야숩'이라 불림. 잇사갈의 아들. 돌라, 부와와 시므론의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야숩(욥이라고도 함)은 잇사갈의 아들이며 야곱의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Paul's host in Thessalonica; relative of Paul
persons.short: Jason was Paul's host in Thessalonica and a relative of Paul mentioned in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Jason is mentioned in Act.17.5-9 as the host of Paul and Silas during their visit to Thessalonica. He provided lodging for the missionaries while they preached in the city. However, their presence caused an uproar among the Jews who were jealous of Paul's success in converting people to Christianity. A mob formed and attacked Jason's house, seeking to bring Paul and Silas before the city authorities. When they could not find the missionaries, they dragged Jason and some other believers before the city officials, accusing them of harboring those who were defying Caesar's decrees. The officials took security from Jason and the others before releasing them. In Rom.16.21, Paul mentions a Jason as one of his fellow workers and relatives who send greetings to the church in Rome. It is unclear whether this is the same Jason who hosted Paul in Thessalonica, but the shared name and association with Paul suggest that it could be the same person.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.17.5 only referred to as Jason (Ἰάσων).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.17.5에 처음 언급되며 '야손'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 야손은 데살로니가에서 바울을 대접한 사람이며, 로마서에서 바울의 친척으로 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign
persons.short: Jathniel was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jathniel is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.26.2 as one of the gatekeepers from the Levites during the reign of King David. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple. They ensured that only authorized individuals entered the sacred spaces and maintained order and security. Jathniel is listed as the fourth son of Meshelemiah, who was one of the chief gatekeepers. The text does not provide any further details about Jathniel's life or his specific duties as a gatekeeper. His mention in the list of gatekeepers suggests that he was a trusted and reliable individual who served faithfully in this important role.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.2 only referred to as Jathniel (יַתְנִיאֵל); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Elam, Jehohanan and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.2에 처음 언급되며 '야드니엘'이라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 스가랴, 여디아엘, 스바댜, 엘람, 여호하난과 엘여호에내의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 야드니엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 문지기로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth; ancestor of Greek people
persons.short: Javan, the ancestor of the Greek people, was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah.
persons.article: Javan is mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10.2,4; 1Ch.1.5,7 as one of the sons of Japheth and grandsons of Noah). He is considered the ancestor of the Greek people, and his name is often used in the Bible as a reference to Greece or the Greek people. In the Old Testament, Javan is associated with the trading of slaves (Jol.3.6, suggesting that the Greeks were involved in the slave trade). In the New Testament, the term "Greeks" (Hellenes) is used to refer to non-Jewish people, particularly those influenced by Greek culture. The Greeks are mentioned in various contexts, such as seeking Jesus (Jhn.12.20, attending synagogues )(Act.14.1; 17.4; 18.4, and being among the first Gentile converts to Christianity )(Act.16.1,3). The inclusion of Greeks in the early church underscores the universal nature of the gospel message (Rom.1.16; 10.12; Gal.3.28). The Greeks are also depicted as seekers of wisdom (1Co.1.22 and are contrasted with the Jews in terms of their religious and cultural background )(Rom.1.14; 2.9-10; 1Co.10.32; 12.13). In Mrk.7.26, a Syrophoenician woman is described as a Greek, highlighting the widespread influence of Greek culture in the region.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 referred to as Javan (יָוָן), or Greek (יְוָנִי=יְוָנִי), Gentile or Greek (Ἕλλην=Ἕλλην), or Gentile ; son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; father of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '야완'이라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마곡, 마대, 두발, 메섹과 디라스의 형제. 엘리사, 달시스, 깃딤과 도다님의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 야완은 그리스 민족의 조상으로, 야벳의 아들이며 노아의 손자였다.
persons.article_ko: 야완은 민족 계보(창 10:2, 4; 대상 1:5, 7)에서 야벳의 아들이며 노아의 손자 중 한 사람으로 언급된다. 그는 그리스 민족의 조상으로 여겨지며, 그의 이름은 성경에서 종종 그리스나 그리스 사람들을 가리키는 데 사용된다. 구약에서 야완은 노예 무역과 관련되어 언급되는데(욜 3:6), 이는 그리스인들이 노예 무역에 관여했음을 시사한다. 신약에서 '헬라인'(헬레네스)이라는 용어는 유대인이 아닌 사람들, 특히 그리스 문화의 영향을 받은 사람들을 가리키는 데 사용된다. 헬라인들은 예수님을 찾는 것(요 12:20), 회당에 참석하는 것(행 14:1; 17:4; 18:4), 그리스도교로 개종한 최초의 이방인 중 하나였던 것(행 16:1, 3) 등 다양한 맥락에서 언급된다. 초대교회에 헬라인들이 포함된 것은 복음 메시지의 보편적인 성격을 강조한다(롬 1:16; 10:12; 갈 3:28). 헬라인들은 또한 지혜를 구하는 자들로 묘사되며(고전 1:22) 종교적, 문화적 배경 면에서 유대인들과 대조된다(롬 1:14; 2:9-10; 고전 10:32; 12:13). 마가복음 7:26에서 수로보니게 여인은 헬라인으로 묘사되어, 그 지역에서 그리스 문화의 광범위한 영향을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Hagrite in charge of David's flocks
persons.short: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of King David's flocks.
persons.article: Jaziz the Hagrite is mentioned in 1Ch.27.31 as the individual responsible for overseeing King David's flocks. He was one of the officials appointed by David to manage various aspects of his kingdom. The Hagrites were a nomadic people who lived in the region east of Gilead, and they were known for their skill in tending livestock. Jaziz's appointment to this position suggests that he had expertise in animal husbandry and was trusted by David to manage this important resource. The text does not provide any further details about Jaziz's life or his role in David's administration.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.31 only referred to as Jaziz (יָזִיז).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.31에 처음 언급되며 '야시스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하갈 사람 야시스는 다윗 왕의 양떼를 관리했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite, son of Zerah, ancestor of Asaph
persons.short: Jeatherai, also known as Ethni, was a Levite, the son of Zerah, and an ancestor of Asaph.
persons.article: Jeatherai, also referred to as Ethni, is mentioned in 1Ch.6.21 and 1Ch.6.41 as part of the genealogy of the Levites. He was the son of Zerah and is listed as an ancestor of Asaph, one of the principal musicians and psalmists in King David's court. In verse 21, he is called Jeatherai, while in verse 41, he is referred to as Ethni. This discrepancy may be due to variations in spelling or copying of the text over time. As a Levite, Jeatherai would have been part of the tribe dedicated to assisting the priests in the tabernacle and temple services. The genealogies in 1Chronicles 6 trace the lineage of the Levites, particularly those who served as musicians and singers in the temple worship.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.21 referred to as Jeatherai (יְאָֽתְרַי), or Ethni (אֶתְנִי); a son of Zerah; father of Malchijah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.21에 처음 언급되며 '여아드래'라 불림. 세라의 아들. 말기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여아드래(에드니라고도 함)는 세라의 아들이며 아삽의 조상인 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Witness to Isaiah's prophecy about Maher-shalal-hash-baz
persons.short: Jeberechiah was a witness to Isaiah's prophecy concerning his son Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
persons.article: Jeberechiah is mentioned in Isa.8.2 as one of the reliable witnesses called by the prophet Isaiah to attest to his prophecy concerning his son Maher-shalal-hash-baz. The name Maher-shalal-hash-baz means "swift is the booty, speedy is the prey," and was given as a sign of the impending Assyrian invasion and conquest of Damascus and Samaria. Isaiah was instructed to write this name on a large scroll and have it confirmed by reliable witnesses, including Jeberechiah and Uriah the priest. The presence of these witnesses served to validate the prophecy and emphasize its importance.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Isa.8.2 only referred to as Jeberechiah (יְבֶרֶכְיָ֫הוּ); father of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Isa.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '여베레기야'라 불림. 스가랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여베레갸는 이사야가 그의 아들 마헬살랄하스바스에 관해 예언할 때 증인이 되었다.

persons.description: People from Jebus(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Zemarites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Canaanite tribe inhabiting Jerusalem before David's conquest
persons.short: The Jebusites were a Canaanite tribe that inhabited Jerusalem before King David conquered the city.
persons.article: The Jebusites were one of the Canaanite tribes that inhabited the land promised to the Israelites by God. They are first mentioned in Gen.10.16 and Gen.15.21 as descendants of Canaan, the grandson of Noah. When the Israelites left Egypt, God promised to drive out the Jebusites and other Canaanite tribes from the land (Exo.3.8, 17; 13.5; 23.23; 33.2; 34.11). During the conquest of Canaan under Joshua, the Jebusites were among the tribes that the Israelites were commanded to utterly destroy (Deu.7.1; 20.17). However, the Jebusites proved to be formidable opponents, and the Israelites were unable to completely drive them out of Jerusalem (Jos.15.63; Jdg.1.21). The Jebusites continued to live among the Israelites during the time of the judges (Jdg.3.5; 19.11). It was not until the reign of King David that the Jebusites were finally defeated, and Jerusalem was captured and made the capital of Israel (2Sa.5.6-8; 1Ch.11.4-6). After their defeat, some Jebusites remained in the land and were subjected to forced labor by Solomon (1Ki.9.20; 2Ch.8.7). The site where the temple was built, Mount Moriah, was purchased by David from Araunah the Jebusite (2Sa.24.16-18; 1Ch.21.15-28; 2Ch.3.1). The Jebusites are mentioned among the foreign peoples with whom the Israelites intermarried, contrary to God's command (Ezr.9.1). In Zec.9.7, there is a prophetic promise that the Jebusites will be incorporated into God's people, symbolizing the inclusion of Gentiles in the future messianic kingdom.
persons.summary: People from Jebus(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at Gen.10.16 only referred to as Jebusites (יְבוּסִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 여부스 족속. Gen.10.16에 처음 언급되며 '여부스'라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓, 스말과 하맛의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 여부스 족속은 다윗 왕이 예루살렘을 정복하기 전 그곳에 살던 가나안 족속이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Uzziah (Azariah) of Judah
persons.short: Jecoliah was the mother of King Uzziah (also known as Azariah) of Judah.
persons.article: Jecoliah is mentioned in 2Ki.15.2 and 2Ch.26.3 as the mother of King Uzziah, who is also referred to as Azariah. She was from Jerusalem, but no further information is provided about her background or family. Jecoliah's son Uzziah became king of Judah at the age of sixteen and reigned for fifty-two years. He is described as a king who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, although he did not remove the high places where people offered sacrifices and burned incense. Uzziah's reign was marked by military successes and a strengthening of Judah's defenses. However, when he attempted to burn incense in the temple, which was a task reserved for the priests, he was struck with leprosy and had to live in isolation until his death. Jecoliah's mention as Uzziah's mother highlights the importance of maternal lineage in the royal succession and the historical record of Judah's kings.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.2 referred to as Jecoliah or Jecoliah (יְכָלְיָהוּ); wife of Amaziah; mother of Uzziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.15.2에 처음 언급되며 '여골리아'라 불림. 아마샤의 아내. 웃시야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여골리야는 유다 왕 웃시야(아사랴라고도 함)의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a priestly division during David's reign
persons.short: Jedaiah was the head of the second priestly division during King David's reign and his descendants returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned in 1Ch.24.7 as the head of the second priestly division during the reign of King David. David organized the priests into twenty-four divisions to ensure a systematic and orderly approach to temple service. Jedaiah's division was the second to serve in the temple rotation. In Ezr.2.36 and Neh.7.39, the descendants of Jedaiah are listed among the priests who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. This indicates that Jedaiah's family continued to serve as priests throughout the generations, even during the exile. The return of Jedaiah's descendants highlights the continuity of the priestly lineage and the importance of the temple service in the restoration of Jewish worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.24.7 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדַעְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.7에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 다윗 왕 시대에 두 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였으며, 그 후손은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Simeon
persons.short: Jedaiah was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in a genealogy.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.37 as part of a genealogy of the descendants of Simeon. He is listed as the son of Shimri, but no further information is provided about his life or role within the tribe of Simeon. The genealogy in this chapter traces the lineage of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and highlights some of the notable individuals and families within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.37 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדָיָה); a son of Shimri; father of Allon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.37에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림. 시므리의 아들. 알론의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 시므온의 후손으로, 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Jedaiah was a priest who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile and served in the temple.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned in 1Ch.9.10, Neh.11.10, and Neh.12.6,19 as a priest who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. In 1Chronicles 9 and Nehemiah 11, he is listed among the priests who settled in Jerusalem, indicating his role in reestablishing the temple worship and the spiritual life of the community. Neh.12.6 identifies him as one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel, the first group of exiles to return to Jerusalem. In Neh.12.19, Jedaiah is mentioned as the head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim, the high priest. These references suggest that Jedaiah and his descendants played a significant role in the priestly duties and the restoration of temple worship in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.10 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדַעְיָה); a son of Joiarib.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.10에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림. 요야립의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착하여 성전에서 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel
persons.short: Jedaiah was a priest who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and signed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned in Neh.12.7 and Neh.12.21 as one of the priests who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, the leader of the first group of exiles to return from Babylon. In verse 7, he is listed among the priests who came back to Jerusalem, indicating his role in the restoration of temple worship and the spiritual life of the community. In verse 21, Jedaiah is mentioned again in the context of the priests who served during the time of Joiakim, the high priest. This suggests that Jedaiah and his descendants continued to serve as priests in the generations following the return from exile. The repeated mention of Jedaiah in the context of the post-exilic priesthood highlights the importance of his family in maintaining the priestly duties and the continuity of temple service.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.12.7 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדַעְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.7에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 스룹바벨과 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아와 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Jedaiah made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall near his house during Nehemiah's rebuilding project.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned in Neh.3.10 as one of the individuals who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. He is described as making repairs to a section of the wall next to his house. The fact that Jedaiah worked on the wall near his own residence suggests that he had a personal stake in the security and restoration of Jerusalem. Nehemiah 3 records the various individuals and groups who contributed to the rebuilding effort, highlighting the unity and dedication of the Jewish people in restoring their city after returning from Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.10 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדָיָה); a son of Harumaph.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.10에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림. 하루맙의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 느헤미야의 재건 사업 당시 자기 집 근처 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Returned exile who provided silver and gold for crowns
persons.short: Jedaiah was a returned exile who provided silver and gold for the crowns placed on Joshua's head.
persons.article: Jedaiah is mentioned in Zec.6.10 and Zec.6.14 as one of the returned exiles who provided silver and gold for the crowns that were to be placed on the head of Joshua, the high priest. In a symbolic act, Zechariah was instructed to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had recently arrived from Babylon. The prophet was to make crowns from the precious metals and set them on Joshua's head, signifying the coming of the Branch (the Messiah) who would build the temple of the Lord and rule as both priest and king. The crowns were to be kept in the temple as a memorial to Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah. This prophetic act emphasizes the importance of the priesthood and the anticipation of the Messiah's coming, who would fulfill the roles of both priest and king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Zec.6.10 only referred to as Jedaiah (יְדַעְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '여다야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여다야는 포로에서 돌아온 자로, 여호수아의 머리에 씌울 면류관을 만들 은과 금을 제공했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men from the tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Jediael the son of Shimri was one of David's mighty men from the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Jediael, the son of Shimri, is mentioned in 1Ch.11.45 as one of David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside King David and played a crucial role in establishing and defending his kingdom. Jediael is specifically identified as being from the tribe of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Although no further details are provided about his specific achievements or exploits, his inclusion in the list of mighty men suggests that he was a valiant and capable warrior who demonstrated exceptional loyalty and bravery in service to King David.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.45 only referred to as Jediael (יְדִיעֲאֵל); son of Shimri; a brother of Joha.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.45에 처음 언급되며 '여디아엘'이라 불림. 시므리의 아들. 요하의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시므리의 아들 여디아엘은 므낫세 지파 출신 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Manassite who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Jediael was one of the Manassites who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Jediael is mentioned in 1Ch.12.20 as one of the Manassites who joined David at Ziklag when he was seeking refuge from King Saul. During this time, David was gathering support from various tribes as he was being pursued by Saul, who sought to kill him. The Manassites, including Jediael, are described as defecting to David and offering their support. They are characterized as brave warriors, commanders of thousands in Manasseh, who provided valuable military assistance to David. The text does not provide any further details about Jediael's specific role or actions during this period. However, his presence among the Manassites who allied with David suggests that he was a loyal and capable warrior who recognized David as the rightful king of Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.20 only referred to as Jediael (יְדִיעֲאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.20에 처음 언급되며 '여디아엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여디아엘은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 므낫세 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper, son of Meshelemiah
persons.short: Jediael was a Levite gatekeeper, the second son of Meshelemiah, during the time of David.
persons.article: Jediael is mentioned in 1Ch.26.2 as one of the sons of Meshelemiah, a Levite gatekeeper during the reign of King David. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple, ensuring that only authorized individuals entered the sacred spaces and maintaining order and security. Jediael is listed as the second son of Meshelemiah, suggesting that he held a position of responsibility within the gatekeeping duties. The text does not provide any further details about Jediael's specific role or the duration of his service. However, his mention in the context of the gatekeepers highlights the importance of this function in the maintenance and protection of the holy places during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.2 only referred to as Jediael (יְדִיעֲאֵל); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Zechariah, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.2에 처음 언급되며 '여디아엘'이라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 스가랴, 스바댜, 야드니엘, 엘람, 여호하난과 엘여호에내의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여디아엘은 다윗 시대 므셀레먀의 둘째 아들로, 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Bela@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Becher@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ashbel@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Naaman@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Muppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Huppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch, Ard@Gen.46.21, Ahiram@Gen.46.21-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Benjamin, head of a clan
persons.short: Jediael was a son of Benjamin and the head of a Benjamite clan.
persons.article: Jediael is mentioned in 1Ch.7.6, 10-11 as one of the sons of Benjamin and the head of a Benjamite clan. Benjamin was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and this chapter provides a genealogical record of his descendants. Jediael is listed along with his brothers Bela and Becher as the three sons of Benjamin. The text further states that Jediael had three sons: Bilhan, Jeush, and Benjamin. The descendants of Jediael are described as mighty warriors and expert archers, numbering 17,200 men ready for battle. This information suggests that Jediael's clan was known for its military prowess and played a significant role in the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.7.6 only referred to as Jediael (יְדִיעֲאֵל); son of Benjamin; a brother of Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ahiram, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, Ard and Ahiram; father of Bilhan.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.6에 처음 언급되며 '여디아엘'이라 불림. 베냐민의 아들. 벨라, 베겔, 아스벨, 게라, 나아만, 로스, 뭅빔, 훔빔, 아릇과 에히의 형제. 빌한의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여디아엘은 베냐민의 아들이며 베냐민 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Josiah of Judah
persons.short: Jedidah was the mother of King Josiah of Judah and the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
persons.article: Jedidah is mentioned in 2Ki.22.1 as the mother of King Josiah of Judah. She was the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath, a town in the Shephelah region of Judah. Jedidah's son, Josiah, became king at the age of eight and reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. He is known for his religious reforms and his efforts to restore the worship of the Lord in Judah. The text does not provide any further information about Jedidah's life or her role in Josiah's upbringing. However, her mention as the mother of a significant king in Judah's history highlights the importance of maternal lineage in the royal succession.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.22.1 only referred to as Jedidah (יְדִידָה); a daughter of Adaiah; wife of Amon; mother of Josiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.22.1에 처음 언급되며 '여디다'라 불림. 아다야의 딸. 아몬의 아내. 요시야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여디다는 유다 왕 요시야의 어머니이며 보스갓 사람 아다야의 딸이었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Obed-edom@2Sa.6.10-2Ch, Mattithiah@1Ch.15.18-, Gedaliah@1Ch.25.3-, Zeri@1Ch.25.3-, Jeshaiah@1Ch.25.3-, Hashabiah@1Ch.25.3-, Shemaiah@2Ch.29.14, Uzziel@2Ch.29.14
persons.brief: Levitical musician and singer during David's reign
persons.short: Jeduthun, also known as Ethan, was a Levitical musician and singer during the reign of King David.
