persons.article: Jeduthun, also referred to as Ethan, was a prominent Levitical musician and singer during the reign of King David. He is mentioned numerous times in 1 Chronicles and 2 Chronicles, as well as in the titles of several psalms. Jeduthun was one of the three principal musicians appointed by David to lead the music and singing in the tabernacle, alongside Asaph and Heman (1Ch.16.41-42; 25.1, 6). He and his sons were skilled in playing the harp, lyre, and cymbals (1Ch.16.42; 25.3). Jeduthun's descendants continued to serve as musicians in the temple during the reigns of subsequent kings, such as Solomon (2Ch.5.12 and Hezekiah )(2Ch.29.14; 35.15). Three psalms (Psalms 39, 62, and 77) are attributed to Jeduthun, indicating his role in composing or leading the music for these hymns. In 1Ch.6.44 and 1Ch.15.17, 19, he is referred to as Ethan, suggesting that this was either an alternate name or a title. Jeduthun's significant role in the musical worship of ancient Israel highlights the importance of music and singing in the religious life of the nation.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.44 referred to as Jeduthun (יְדוּתוּן), or Ethan (אֵיתָן); a son of Kishi; father of Obed-edom, Mattithiah, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.6.44에 처음 언급되며 '여두둔'이라 불림. 기시의 아들. 오벧에돔, 맛디디야, 그달리야, 스리, 여사야, 하사뱌, 스마야와 웃시엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여두둔(에단이라고도 함)은 다윗 왕 시대에 레위인 음악가이며 노래하는 자였다.
persons.article_ko: 여두둔(에단이라고도 함)은 다윗 왕 통치 기간의 저명한 레위인 음악가이며 노래하는 자였다. 그는 역대상과 역대하 여러 곳, 그리고 여러 시편의 표제에도 언급된다. 여두둔은 다윗이 아삽, 헤만과 함께 성막에서 음악과 노래를 인도하도록 임명한 세 명의 주요 음악가 중 한 사람이었다(대상 16:41-42; 25:1, 6). 그와 그의 아들들은 수금, 비파, 심벌즈 연주에 능숙했다(대상 16:42; 25:3). 여두둔의 후손은 솔로몬(대하 5:12)과 히스기야(대하 29:14; 35:15) 같은 후대 왕들의 통치 기간 동안 계속 성전에서 음악가로 섬겼다. 세 편의 시편(39편, 62편, 77편)이 여두둔의 것으로 여겨지는데, 이는 이 찬송들의 음악을 작곡하거나 인도하는 데 있어 그의 역할을 나타낸다. 역대상 6:44과 15:17, 19에서 그는 에단이라 불리는데, 이는 이것이 다른 이름이거나 칭호였음을 시사한다. 고대 이스라엘의 음악 예배에서 여두둔의 중요한 역할은 그 민족의 종교 생활에서 음악과 노래의 중요성을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper and singer in post-exilic Jerusalem
persons.short: Jeduthun was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper and singer in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jeduthun is mentioned in 1Ch.9.16 and Neh.11.17 as a Levite who served in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. In 1Ch.9.16, he is described as a gatekeeper, belonging to the Levites who were responsible for guarding the entrances to the temple and maintaining order. In Neh.11.17, Jeduthun is identified as a singer, along with Bakbukiah and Abda, who led the thanksgiving songs in prayer. This suggests that he had a dual role in the post-exilic community, serving both as a gatekeeper and a musician in the temple. The text does not provide any further details about Jeduthun's life or his specific contributions to the rebuilding and restoration of Jerusalem after the exile. However, his mention in these passages highlights the importance of the Levites in maintaining the temple services and leading the worship of the community.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.16 referred to as Jeduthun or Jeduthun (יְדוּתוּן); father of Galal.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.16에 처음 언급되며 '여두둔'이라 불림. 갈랄의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여두둔은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에서 문지기이며 노래하는 자로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Elah, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Jehallelel was a son of Elah and a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Jehallelel is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.4.16 as one of the sons of Elah, who was a descendant of Judah. The genealogy in this chapter traces the lineage of some of the clans and families within the tribe of Judah. Jehallelel is listed along with his brothers Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel. No further information is provided about Jehallelel's life, his occupation, or his role within the clan. The mention of his name in this genealogical record serves to document the family lines and the descendants of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.16 only referred to as Jehallelel (יְהַלֶּלְאֵל); father of Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, Asarel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.16에 처음 언급되며 '여할렐렐'이라 불림. 엘라의 아들. 그나스의 형제. 십, 시바, 디리아와 아사렐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여할렐렐은 엘라의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped purify the temple under Hezekiah
persons.short: Jehallelel, a Levite from the Merari clan, helped purify the temple during King Hezekiah's religious reforms.
persons.article: Jehallelel is mentioned in 2Ch.29.12 as one of the Levites who participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He is identified as a member of the Merari clan, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. When Hezekiah became king, he initiated a series of religious reforms aimed at restoring the worship of the Lord and cleansing the temple, which had been neglected and defiled during the reign of his father, Ahaz. Jehallelel, along with other Levites from the clans of Kohath and Gershon, responded to the king's command and took part in the purification process. They cleansed the temple, removed the unclean items, and prepared it for proper worship. The text does not provide any further details about Jehallelel's specific role or contributions during this event. However, his participation in the temple purification highlights the importance of the Levites in maintaining the sanctity of the temple and assisting in the religious reforms initiated by the king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12 only referred to as Jehallelel (יְהַלֶּלְאֵל); father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12에 처음 언급되며 '여할렐렐'이라 불림. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므라리 가문 레위인 여할렐렐은 히스기야 왕의 종교개혁 기간 동안 성전을 정결하게 하는 일을 도왔다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite descendant of Amram during David's reign
persons.short: Jehdeiah was a Levite descendant of Amram who served during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jehdeiah is mentioned in 1Ch.24.20 as a descendant of Amram, who was a Levite. This chapter describes the divisions of the Levites and their duties during the reign of King David. Jehdeiah is listed among the Levites who were appointed to serve in the temple. The text does not provide any further details about Jehdeiah's specific role or responsibilities. However, his inclusion in this list suggests that he was a member of the Levitical family and participated in the various tasks assigned to the Levites in the temple service.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.20 only referred to as Jehdeiah (יֶחְדְּיָ֫הוּ); a son of Shebuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.24.20에 처음 언급되며 '예드야'라 불림. 스브엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여드야는 아므람의 후손인 레위인으로, 다윗 왕 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Officer in charge of King David's donkeys
persons.short: Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of King David's donkeys.
persons.article: Jehdeiah the Meronothite is mentioned in 1Ch.27.30 as the officer in charge of King David's donkeys. This chapter lists the various officials and administrators who were responsible for overseeing different aspects of David's kingdom. Jehdeiah's specific role was to manage the king's donkeys, which were likely used for transportation and agricultural purposes. The fact that he was from Meronoth, a town believed to be located in Judah, suggests that he may have had expertise in animal husbandry. The text does not provide any further information about Jehdeiah's background or his other duties in the royal administration.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.30 only referred to as Jehdeiah (יֶחְדְּיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.30에 처음 언급되며 '예드야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므로놋 사람 여드야는 다윗 왕의 나귀들을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of the 20th priestly division under David
persons.short: Jehezkel was the head of the 20th priestly division during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jehezkel is mentioned in 1Ch.24.16 as the head of the 20th priestly division during the reign of King David. This chapter describes the organization of the priests into 24 divisions, each responsible for serving in the temple for a specific period. Jehezkel was chosen by lot to lead the 20th division. The priests were descendants of Aaron and were responsible for offering sacrifices, maintaining the temple, and performing other religious duties. The text does not provide any additional information about Jehezkel's life or his specific responsibilities as the head of his division. However, his inclusion in this list highlights the importance of the priestly role in the religious life of ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.16 only referred to as Jehezkel (יְחֶזְקֵאל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.16에 처음 언급되며 '여헤스겔'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여헤스겔은 다윗 왕 시대에 스무 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levitical musician during the reign of King David
persons.short: Jehiel was a Levitical musician who played the harp and lyre during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in 1Ch.15.18, 20, and 1Ch.16.5 as one of the Levitical musicians who served during the reign of King David. In 1Chronicles 15, Jehiel is listed among the Levites chosen to play the harp and lyre when the Ark of the Covenant was brought to Jerusalem. He is described as a "second-degree" musician, suggesting a level of skill and experience in his role. In 1Ch.16.5, Jehiel is mentioned again as one of the musicians who ministered before the Ark of the Covenant with harps, lyres, and cymbals. This chapter describes the celebration and worship that took place when the Ark was placed in the tent David had prepared for it. Jehiel's inclusion in these passages highlights the importance of music and worship in the religious life of ancient Israel and the significant role played by skilled musicians like Jehiel in the temple service.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 여히엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 수금과 비파를 연주하는 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King David's uncle and counselor
persons.short: Jehiel, King David's uncle, was a counselor and a scribe.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in 1Ch.27.32 as King David's uncle and counselor. He is described as a wise and understanding man who served as a scribe in the royal court. In this context, a scribe was not merely a writer but an educated and knowledgeable person who could provide advice and guidance to the king. The fact that Jehiel was David's uncle suggests that he was a trusted family member who had a close relationship with the king. His role as a counselor highlights the importance of wise advisors in the administration of the kingdom. The text does not provide any further details about Jehiel's life or his specific contributions to David's reign. However, his mention in this passage indicates that he held a significant position in the royal court and played a role in shaping the decisions and policies of the kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.32 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל); a son of Hachmoni.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.32에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림. 학모니의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 다윗 왕의 삼촌 여히엘은 조언자이며 서기관이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite leader during the reign of King David
persons.short: Jehiel, also known as Jahath, was a Levite leader who served during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jehiel, also referred to as Jahath, is mentioned in several passages in 1 Chronicles as a Levite leader during the reign of King David. In 1Ch.23.8, Jehiel is listed as one of the sons of Ladan, who was a descendant of Gershon. This chapter describes the organization of the Levites and their duties in the temple service. In 1Ch.29.8, Jehiel is mentioned as one of the leaders of the Levites who received the donations of precious stones for the construction of the temple. This suggests that he held a position of responsibility and trust within the Levitical community. In 1Ch.26.21-22, Jehiel is identified as the father of Zetham and Joel, who were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord. This passage also refers to him as Jehieli, possibly indicating a variant spelling of his name. The text does not provide any further details about Jehiel's life or his specific role as a Levite leader. However, his repeated mention in these passages highlights his importance and the significance of the Levites in the administration and service of the temple during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.8 referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל), or Jehieli (יְחִיאֵלִי), or Jahath (יַ֫חַת); son of Libni ; a brother of Zetham and Joel; father of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.20에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림. 립니의 아들. 세담과 요엘의 형제. 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여히엘(야핫이라고도 함)은 다윗 왕 시대에 섬긴 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jehoram@1Ki.22.50-Mat, Azariah@2Ch.21.2, Zechariah@2Ch.21.2, Azariahu@2Ch.21.2, Michael@2Ch.21.2, Shephatiah@2Ch.21.2
persons.brief: Son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah
persons.short: Jehiel was one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in 2Ch.21.2 as one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He is listed along with his brothers Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. The text states that Jehoshaphat gave his sons many gifts of silver, gold, and valuable possessions, as well as fortified cities in Judah. However, the kingdom was given to Jehoram, Jehoshaphat's firstborn son. The passage does not provide any further information about Jehiel's life or his role in the royal family. His mention in this context serves to highlight the wealth and power of Jehoshaphat's reign and the practice of providing for the king's sons, even though the firstborn would inherit the throne.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.21.2 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל); son of Jehoshaphat; a brother of Jehoram, Azariah, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.21.2에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림. 여호사밧의 아들. 여호람, 아사랴, 스가랴, 아사랴, 미가엘과 스바댜의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여히엘은 유다 왕 여호사밧의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite appointed by King Hezekiah to distribute offerings
persons.short: Jehiel was a Levite appointed by King Hezekiah to distribute the offerings and tithes in the temple.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in 2Ch.31.13 as one of the Levites appointed by King Hezekiah to oversee the distribution of offerings and tithes in the temple. This chapter describes Hezekiah's reforms and his efforts to restore proper worship and support for the priests and Levites. Jehiel is listed along with other Levites such as Azaziah, Nahath, and Benaiah, who were chosen to serve as officers and overseers in the temple. Their role was to ensure that the contributions from the people were properly collected, stored, and distributed to the priests and Levites according to their divisions. The text does not provide any further details about Jehiel's background or his specific duties in this role. However, his appointment by Hezekiah suggests that he was a trusted and capable Levite who could handle the important task of managing the temple's resources and supporting the religious leaders of the nation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 여히엘은 히스기야 왕이 성전 헌물과 십일조를 분배하도록 임명한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Temple officer during King Josiah's Passover celebration
persons.short: Jehiel, along with Zechariah and Jehiel, was a temple officer who gave animals for King Josiah's Passover offerings.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in 2Ch.35.8 as one of the officers of the temple during the reign of King Josiah. Along with Zechariah and another Jehiel, he gave animals for the Passover offerings. This chapter describes Josiah's celebration of the Passover, which was carried out with great zeal and in accordance with the Law of Moses. The officers of the temple, including Jehiel, contributed sheep, goats, and cattle for the Passover sacrifices, demonstrating their support for the king's religious reforms and their dedication to the proper observance of the festival. The text does not provide any additional information about this Jehiel's background or his specific role in the temple administration. However, his contribution to the Passover offerings highlights the importance of the temple officers in facilitating the religious celebrations and ensuring that the necessary resources were available for the sacrifices.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.35.8 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.35.8에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여히엘은 스가랴, 여히엘과 함께 요시야 왕의 유월절 제물로 짐승을 내준 성전 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, was guilty of marrying a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Jehiel was a member of the clan of Elam who returned from the Babylonian exile. He was one of the men found guilty of marrying foreign women, which was a violation of the Mosaic Law. Ezra the priest confronted the returned exiles about this issue (Ezr.10.2). Jehiel is not mentioned again in the biblical record.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.2 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל); father of Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림. 스가냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘람의 후손 여히엘은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼한 죄를 지었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile
persons.short: Jehiel, one of the descendants of Harim, was a priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
persons.article: Jehiel is mentioned in Ezr.10.21 as one of the priests who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. This chapter lists the names of the men who had taken foreign wives, including priests, Levites, and other Israelites. Jehiel is identified as one of the descendants of Harim, a priestly family. The fact that priests had married foreign women was particularly problematic, as they were expected to maintain ritual purity and set an example for the people. In response to Ezra's call for repentance, these men agreed to put away their foreign wives and children, demonstrating their commitment to following the Law of Moses and maintaining the distinct identity of the Israelite community. The text does not provide any additional information about Jehiel's background or his specific role as a priest.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.21 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하림의 후손 여히엘은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile
persons.short: Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, married a foreign woman during the Exile but agreed to put her away.
persons.article: Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, is mentioned in Ezr.10.26 among the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. This chapter lists the names of the men who had taken foreign wives, including representatives from various families and clans. Jehiel's inclusion in this list suggests that he, like many others, had married a woman from one of the surrounding nations, which was contrary to the Law of Moses. In response to Ezra's call for repentance and reform, these men agreed to put away their foreign wives and children, demonstrating their willingness to follow Ezra's leadership and to restore their obedience to God's law. The text does not provide any further details about Jehiel's life or his role in the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.26 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 엘람의 또 다른 후손 여히엘은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했으나 그녀를 내보내기로 동의했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra
persons.short: Jehiel, son of Shechaniah, was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Jehiel, the son of Shechaniah, is mentioned in Ezr.8.9 as one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. This chapter lists the heads of families who joined Ezra in his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem, intending to restore worship and obedience to the Law of Moses. Jehiel is listed along with other leaders such as Zechariah, Sherebiah, and Obadiah, each accompanied by a number of men from their respective families. The text does not provide any further details about Jehiel's background or his role in the community. However, his inclusion in this list suggests that he was a prominent figure among the returnees and had a significant number of people under his leadership. Ezra's return to Jerusalem was a crucial event in the history of Israel, as it marked the beginning of a new era of religious and social reform after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.9 only referred to as Jehiel (יְחִיאֵל); father of Obadiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '여히엘'이라 불림. 오바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스가냐의 아들 여히엘은 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ephraimite leader who opposed taking Judean captives
persons.short: Jehizkiah, an Ephraimite leader, opposed taking Judean captives during the reign of King Ahaz of Judah.
persons.article: Jehizkiah is mentioned in 2Ch.28.12 as one of the leaders of the tribe of Ephraim who opposed the actions of the Israelite army during the reign of King Ahaz of Judah. The army had just returned from a successful campaign against Judah, bringing back a large number of captives and plunder. However, Jehizkiah, along with Azariah, Berechiah, and Amasa, confronted the army and urged them not to bring the captives into Samaria, warning that this would only add to Israel's guilt before God. They argued that the army's actions had already provoked God's anger and that taking the captives would further incur his wrath. As a result of their intervention, the army released the captives, provided them with clothing and food, and sent them back to Judah. Jehizkiah's actions demonstrate his concern for righteousness and his willingness to stand up against wrongdoing, even in the face of military success.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.12 only referred to as Jehizkiah (יְחִזְקִיָּה); a son of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.28.12에 처음 언급되며 '여히스기야'라 불림. 살룸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여히스기야는 아하스 왕 시대에 유다 포로를 잡아오는 것을 반대한 에브라임 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of King Saul
persons.short: Jehoaddah, also known as Jarah, was a descendant of King Saul mentioned in the genealogies of Benjamin.
persons.article: Jehoaddah, also referred to as Jarah, is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Ch.8.36 and 1Ch.9.42. He is listed as one of the descendants of King Saul, Israel's first king. In both passages, his name appears in the genealogy of Saul's descendants, suggesting that he was a member of the royal family. However, no further information is provided about his life, his role in the family, or his place in the history of Israel. The fact that he is mentioned by two different names, Jehoaddah and Jarah, suggests that one may have been a variant spelling or a nickname. The inclusion of his name in the genealogies serves to trace the lineage of Saul and to highlight the continuing presence of his descendants among the people of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.36 referred to as Jehoaddah (יְהוֹעַדָּה), or Jarah (יַעְרָה); a son of Ahaz; father of Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.36에 처음 언급되며 '여호앗다'라 불림. 아하스의 아들. 알레멧, 아스마와 시므리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호앗다(야라라고도 함)는 베냐민 족보에 언급된 사울 왕의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Amaziah of Judah
persons.short: Jehoaddan was the mother of King Amaziah of Judah and was from Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jehoaddan is mentioned in 2Ch.25.1 and 2Ki.14.2 as the mother of King Amaziah of Judah. She was from Jerusalem, but no further information is provided about her background or family. Jehoaddan's son, Amaziah, became king at the age of 25 and reigned for 29 years in Jerusalem. The text does not give any details about Jehoaddan's role in her son's life or reign, but her mention in the context of Amaziah's accession to the throne suggests that the mother of the king was considered a significant figure. The fact that her place of origin, Jerusalem, is specifically mentioned may also indicate that she was from an influential family or had connections to the royal court.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.14.2 referred to as Jehoaddan or Jehoaddin (יְהוֹעַדָּן); wife of Joash; mother of Amaziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.14.2에 처음 언급되며 '여호앗단'이라 불림. 요아스의 아내. 아마샤의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여호앗단은 유다 왕 아마샤의 어머니이며 예루살렘 출신이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel, son of Jehu
persons.short: Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, was king of Israel and reigned for seventeen years.
persons.article: Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, was a king of Israel who reigned for seventeen years, as recorded in 2Ki.10.35 and 2Ki.13.1. He succeeded his father, Jehu, on the throne of Israel. During his reign, Israel faced oppression from the Arameans, led by King Hazael and his son Ben-hadad III(2Ki.13.3, 22). The text states that Jehoahaz did evil in the sight of the Lord, following the sins of Jeroboam, which led to Israel's suffering (2Ki.13.2). However, when Jehoahaz sought the Lord's favor, God provided a deliverer for Israel, allowing them to escape from the Arameans (2Ki.13.4-5). Despite this, Israel continued to face military challenges, and their army was greatly reduced (2Ki.13.7). Jehoahaz's reign was marked by ongoing conflict with the Arameans and the consequences of Israel's disobedience to God. After his death, his son Jehoash (also known as Joash) succeeded him as king (2Ki.13.9).
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.10.35 referred to as Jehoahaz (יְהוֹאָחָז), or Joahaz (יוֹאָחָז); a son of Jehu; father of Joash.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.10.35에 처음 언급되며 '여호아하스'라 불림. 예후의 아들. 요아스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 예후의 아들 여호아하스는 이스라엘 왕으로 십칠 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 예후의 아들 여호아하스는 열왕기하 10:35과 13:1에 기록된 대로 십칠 년간 다스린 이스라엘 왕이었다. 그는 아버지 예후를 이어 이스라엘 왕위에 올랐다. 그의 통치 기간 동안 이스라엘은 하사엘 왕과 그의 아들 벤하닷 3세가 이끄는 아람 사람들에게서 압제를 당했다(왕하 13:3, 22). 본문은 여호아하스가 여로보암의 죄를 따라 여호와 보시기에 악을 행하여 이스라엘의 고통을 초래했다고 말한다(왕하 13:2). 그러나 여호아하스가 여호와의 은총을 구했을 때 하나님은 이스라엘에 구원자를 보내주셔서 그들이 아람 사람들에게서 벗어날 수 있게 하셨다(왕하 13:4-5). 그럼에도 이스라엘은 계속 군사적 어려움에 직면했고 그들의 군대는 크게 줄어들었다(왕하 13:7). 여호아하스의 통치는 아람 사람들과의 계속된 갈등과 하나님께 대한 이스라엘의 불순종의 결과로 특징지어졌다. 그가 죽은 후 그의 아들 여호아스(요아스라고도 함)가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다(왕하 13:9).

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Josiah
persons.short: Jehoahaz, also known as Johanan, was a king of Judah and the son of Josiah.
persons.article: Jehoahaz, also known as Johanan, was a king of Judah and the son of Josiah, as mentioned in 2Ki.23.30-31, 2 Chronicles 2Ki.36.1-2, and 1Ch.3.15. After the death of his father Josiah, the people of the land made Jehoahaz king in Jerusalem, even though he was not the eldest son (2Ki.23.30, 2 Chronicles 2Ki.36.1). He was twenty-three years old when he became king and reigned for only three months (2Ki.23.31, 2 Chronicles 2Ki.36.2). However, Pharaoh Necho of Egypt removed Jehoahaz from the throne, imposed a heavy tribute on Judah, and made his brother Eliakim (later renamed Jehoiakim) king in his place (2Ki.23.33-34, 2 Chronicles 2Ki.36.3-4). Pharaoh Necho took Jehoahaz captive to Egypt, where he died (2Ki.23.34). The brief reign of Jehoahaz was marked by the increasing influence of Egypt over Judah and the beginning of a period of political instability and foreign domination.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.23.30 referred to as Jehoahaz (יְהוֹאָחָז), or Jehoahaz (יוֹאָחָז), or Johanan (יוֹחָנָן); son of Josiah and Hamutal; a brother of Zedekiah; half-brother of: Jehoiakim and Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.23.30에 처음 언급되며 '여호아하스'라 불림. 요시야와 하무달의 아들. 여호야김, 시드기야와 살룸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여호아하스(요하난이라고도 함)는 요시야의 아들이며 유다 왕이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during the reign of David
persons.short: Jehohanan was a Levite gatekeeper during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in 1Ch.26.3 as one of the gatekeepers from the Levites during the reign of King David. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple. They ensured that only authorized individuals entered the sacred spaces and maintained order and security. Jehohanan is listed among the descendants of Korah who were assigned to this important role. The text does not provide any further details about Jehohanan's specific duties or the duration of his service. However, his inclusion in the list of gatekeepers highlights the significance of this function in the organization of the Levites and the importance of maintaining the sanctity of the tabernacle during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.3 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.3에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 스가랴, 여디아엘, 스바댜, 야드니엘, 엘람과 엘여호에내의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 다윗 왕 시대에 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Military commander under King Jehoshaphat of Judah
persons.short: Jehohanan was a military commander from Judah during the reign of King Jehoshaphat.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in 2Ch.17.15 as one of the military commanders of Judah during the reign of King Jehoshaphat. He is described as a leader of 280,000 mighty warriors, indicating his significant role in the army of Judah. The passage lists several commanders and the number of troops under their command, highlighting the military strength of Judah during Jehoshaphat's reign. Jehoshaphat is known for his reforms and his efforts to strengthen the spiritual and military foundation of the kingdom. The presence of capable military leaders like Jehohanan would have been essential for maintaining the security and stability of Judah. The text does not provide any further information about Jehohanan's background, his specific military achievements, or his role in the battles and conflicts of the time. However, his inclusion in this list of commanders suggests that he was a trusted and competent leader in Jehoshaphat's army.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.15 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.15에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 여호사밧 왕 시대에 유다 출신 군 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Ishmael, a military leader under Jehoiada
persons.short: Jehohanan was the father of Ishmael, one of the military leaders who supported Jehoiada in his coup against Athaliah.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in 2Ch.23.1 as the father of Ishmael, one of the military leaders who supported the priest Jehoiada in his coup against Queen Athaliah. Athaliah had seized the throne of Judah after the death of her son, King Ahaziah, and had ordered the execution of all the royal heirs. However, Jehoiada and his wife, Jehosheba, managed to rescue the young prince Joash and hide him in the temple for six years. In the seventh year, Jehoiada gathered the military leaders, including Ishmael, son of Jehohanan, and revealed the existence of the rightful heir to the throne. The military leaders pledged their support to Joash and helped Jehoiada execute a plan to overthrow Athaliah and install Joash as king. The text does not provide any further information about Jehohanan himself, but his son's involvement in this significant event suggests that the family may have held a prominent position in the military or royal court.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.23.1 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן); father of Ishmael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.23.1에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림. 이스마엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 아달랴를 대적하여 여호야다를 도운 군 지도자 중 한 사람인 이스마엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile
persons.short: Jehohanan, one of the descendants of Bebai, married a foreign woman during the Exile but pledged to put her away.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in Ezr.10.28 as one of the descendants of Bebai who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. This chapter lists the names of the men who had taken foreign wives, including representatives from various families and clans. Jehohanan's inclusion in this list suggests that he, like many others, had married a woman from one of the surrounding nations, which was contrary to the Law of Moses. In response to Ezra's call for repentance and reform, these men pledged to put away their foreign wives and children, demonstrating their willingness to follow Ezra's leadership and to restore their obedience to God's law. The text does not provide any further details about Jehohanan's life or his role in the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.28 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.28에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 브배의 후손 여호하난은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했으나 그녀를 내보내기로 서약했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Eliashib, a priest during Ezra's time
persons.short: Jehohanan was the son of Eliashib, a priest during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in Ezr.10.6 as the son of Eliashib, a priest during the time of Ezra. The passage describes Ezra's response to the issue of intermarriage between the Israelites and the surrounding nations. Upon learning of this problem, Ezra tore his garments, pulled out some of his hair and beard, and sat down in shock. He then went to the chamber of Jehohanan, son of Eliashib, where he spent the night, mourning and fasting because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles. The text does not provide any further details about Jehohanan himself, but the mention of his chamber suggests that he may have held a significant position within the temple or the priesthood. The fact that Ezra chose to spend the night in Jehohanan's chamber may also indicate a close relationship or a shared concern for the spiritual well-being of the community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.6 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן); a son of Eliashib.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.6에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림. 엘리아십의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 엘리아십의 아들로, 에스라 시대의 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Head of a priestly family during the high priesthood of Joiakim
persons.short: Jehohanan was the head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in Neh.12.13 as the head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua. This chapter lists the priests and Levites who served in Jerusalem during the high priesthood of Joiakim, providing a record of the religious leadership after the return from the Babylonian exile. Jehohanan is listed among the heads of the priestly families, indicating that he was a prominent figure in the priestly hierarchy. The text does not provide any further details about Jehohanan's specific role or responsibilities, but his position as the head of a priestly family suggests that he would have been involved in the various duties associated with the temple service, such as offering sacrifices, teaching the law, and maintaining the sacred space. The mention of Jehohanan in this context helps to establish the continuity of the priestly lineage and the restoration of the temple worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.13 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.13에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 예수아의 아들 요야김 시대에 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest during the dedication of Jerusalem's walls
persons.short: Jehohanan was one of the priests who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's walls during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in Neh.12.42 as one of the priests who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's walls during the time of Nehemiah. This chapter describes the grand celebration that took place after the completion of the city's fortifications, with two large choirs marching on top of the walls and giving thanks to God. Jehohanan is listed among the priests who were involved in this ceremony, along with other notable figures such as Maaseiah, Shemaiah, and Eleazar. The text does not provide any further details about Jehohanan's specific role in the dedication or his background, but his inclusion in this list suggests that he was a part of the priestly leadership in Jerusalem at that time. The dedication of the walls was a significant event that marked the restoration of Jerusalem and the renewal of the people's commitment to God, and Jehohanan's participation in this ceremony highlights the important role of the priests in the spiritual life of the community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.42에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Ammonite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father-in-law of Tobiah, an opponent of Nehemiah
persons.short: Jehohanan was the father-in-law of Tobiah, an opponent of Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
persons.article: Jehohanan is mentioned in Neh.6.18 as the father-in-law of Tobiah, one of the main opponents of Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. Tobiah, along with Sanballat and Geshem, actively tried to hinder and discourage Nehemiah's efforts to reconstruct the city's defenses. The passage notes that many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah, son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam, son of Berechiah. These family connections suggest that Tobiah had significant influence and support among some of the Jewish nobles, which made it more difficult for Nehemiah to carry out his mission. The text does not provide any further information about Jehohanan himself, but his relationship to Tobiah and his marriage into another prominent family highlight the complex social and political dynamics that Nehemiah had to navigate during the rebuilding process.
persons.summary: A man of the Ammonites living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.18 only referred to as Jehohanan (יְהוֹחָנָן); a son of Tobiah; husband of daughter of Meshullam.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 암몬 사람. Neh.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '여호하난'이라 불림. 도비야와 스가냐의 딸(이름 미상)의 아들. 므술람의 딸(이름 미상)의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 여호하난은 느헤미야의 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 반대한 도비야의 장인이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Jehoiakim
persons.short: Jehoiachin, also known as Jeconiah, Coniah, or Shallum, was a king of Judah who reigned for three months before being exiled to Babylon.
persons.article: Jehoiachin, also referred to as Jeconiah, Coniah, or Shallum, was a king of Judah who reigned for a brief period of three months and ten days (2Ch.36.9). He was the son of King Jehoiakim and ascended to the throne at the age of eighteen (2Ki.24.8). However, during his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon besieged Jerusalem, and Jehoiachin surrendered to him (2Ki.24.12). As a result, Jehoiachin, along with his family, nobles, and skilled workers, was taken captive to Babylon (2Ki.24.15-16; Jer.24.1; 27.20; 29.2; Ezk.1.2). Nebuchadnezzar appointed Jehoiachin's uncle, Mattaniah (later renamed Zedekiah), as the new king of Judah (2Ki.24.17; Jer.37.1). During his captivity in Babylon, Jehoiachin was imprisoned for 37 years until Evil-merodach, the new king of Babylon, released him and treated him kindly (2Ki.25.27-30; Jer.52.31-34). Jehoiachin's descendants, including Shealtiel and Zerubbabel, are mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ (1Ch.3.17; Mat.1.11-12). The prophet Jeremiah prophesied about Jehoiachin, referring to him as "Coniah" and declaring that none of his descendants would prosper on the throne of David (Jer.22.24-30). Despite this prophecy, Jehoiachin's release from prison and the favor shown to him by the Babylonian king suggest that God had not forgotten him or his family.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.24.6 referred to as Jehoiachin (יְהוֹיָכִין), or Jehoiachin (יוֹיָכִין), or Jeconiah (יְכוֹנְיָה), or Coniah (כׇּנְיָהוּ), or Shallum (שַׁלּוּם), or Jechoniah (Ἰεχονίας); a son of Jehoiakim and Nehushta; father of Zedekiah (?) and Shealtiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.24.6에 처음 언급되며 '여호야긴'이라 불림. 여호야김과 느후스다의 아들. 시드기야와 스알디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호야긴(여고냐, 고니야, 또는 살룸이라고도 함)은 유다 왕으로 삼 개월간 다스리다가 바벨론으로 유배되었다.
persons.article_ko: 여호야긴(여고냐, 고니야, 살룸이라고도 함)은 삼 개월 열흘이라는 짧은 기간 동안 다스린 유다 왕이었다(대하 36:9). 그는 여호야김 왕의 아들이며 십팔 세에 왕위에 올랐다(왕하 24:8). 그러나 그의 통치 기간 동안 바벨론 왕 느부갓네살이 예루살렘을 포위했고 여호야긴은 그에게 항복했다(왕하 24:12). 그 결과 여호야긴은 가족, 귀족들, 숙련된 기술자들과 함께 바벨론으로 포로로 끌려갔다(왕하 24:15-16; 렘 24:1; 27:20; 29:2; 겔 1:2). 느부갓네살은 여호야긴의 삼촌 맛다냐(후에 시드기야로 개명)를 유다의 새 왕으로 임명했다(왕하 24:17; 렘 37:1). 바벨론 포로 생활 동안 여호야긴은 삼십칠 년간 투옥되었다가 바벨론의 새 왕 에윌므로닥이 그를 풀어주고 친절히 대우할 때까지 감옥에 있었다(왕하 25:27-30; 렘 52:31-34). 스알디엘과 스룹바벨을 포함한 여호야긴의 후손들은 예수 그리스도의 족보에 언급된다(대상 3:17; 마 1:11-12). 선지자 예레미야는 여호야긴을 '고니야'라 부르며 그의 후손 중 아무도 다윗의 왕좌에서 형통하지 못할 것이라고 예언했다(렘 22:24-30). 이 예언에도 불구하고 여호야긴이 감옥에서 풀려나고 바벨론 왕에게서 은총을 받은 것은 하나님이 그와 그의 가족을 잊지 않으셨음을 시사한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Counselor to King David after Ahithophel
persons.short: Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, succeeded Ahithophel as King David's counselor.
persons.article: Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, is mentioned in 1Ch.27.34 as a counselor to King David. This chapter lists the various officials and administrators who served during David's reign, including the counselors who advised the king. Jehoiada is specifically noted as the successor to Ahithophel, who had been David's previous counselor before he defected to support Absalom's rebellion (2Sa.15.12, 31). The fact that Jehoiada is identified as the son of Benaiah suggests that he may have been the grandson of the high priest Jehoiada.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.34 only referred to as Jehoiada (יְהוֹיָדָע); a son of Benaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.34에 처음 언급되며 '여호야다'라 불림. 브나야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 브나야의 아들 여호야다는 아히도벨을 이어 다윗 왕의 모사가 되었다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: High priest who overthrew Athaliah and crowned Joash
persons.short: Jehoiada, also known as Barachiah, was a high priest who led a revolt against Queen Athaliah and crowned Joash as king of Judah.
persons.article: Jehoiada, also referred to as Barachiah in Mat.23.35, was a high priest during the reign of King Joash of Judah. He played a crucial role in preserving the Davidic lineage and restoring the worship of Yahweh in Judah. When Athaliah, the mother of the deceased king Ahaziah, seized the throne and ordered the execution of all the royal heirs, Jehoiada and his wife Jehosheba rescued the infant Joash and hid him in the temple for six years (2Ki.11.1-3; 2Ch.22.11-12). In the seventh year, Jehoiada gathered the military leaders and Levites, revealing the existence of the rightful heir and orchestrating a coup against Athaliah (2Ki.11.4-12; 2Ch.23.1-11). Joash was crowned king, and Athaliah was executed (2Ki.11.13-16; 2Ch.23.12-15). During Joash's reign, Jehoiada served as his advisor and guided him in the ways of the Lord (2Ki.12.2). Jehoiada also initiated repairs to the temple and oversaw the collection of funds for this purpose (2Ki.12.7-16; 2Ch.24.4-14). He died at the age of 130 and was buried among the kings in the City of David, a testament to his significant role in the history of Judah (2Ch.24.15-16). After Jehoiada's death, Joash turned away from the Lord and even ordered the execution of Jehoiada's son, Zechariah, for speaking out against the king's disobedience (2Ch.24.17-22; Mat.23.35). This act of betrayal led to the downfall of Joash and the kingdom of Judah.
persons.summary: A high priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.11.4 referred to as Jehoiada (יְהוֹיָדָע), or Barachiah (Βαραχίας); husband of Jehosheba; father of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 대제사장. 2Ki.11.4에 처음 언급되며 '여호야다'라 불림. 여호세바의 남편. 스가랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호야다(바라갸라고도 함)는 대제사장으로, 아달랴 여왕을 대적하는 반역을 이끌어 요아스를 유다 왕으로 세웠다.
persons.article_ko: 마태복음 23:35에서 바라갸라고도 불리는 여호야다는 유다 왕 요아스 통치 기간의 대제사장이었다. 그는 다윗 혈통을 보존하고 유다에서 여호와 예배를 회복하는 데 중대한 역할을 했다. 죽은 왕 아하시야의 어머니 아달랴가 왕위를 찬탈하여 모든 왕족 상속자들을 처형하라고 명령했을 때 여호야다와 그의 아내 여호세바는 아기 요아스를 구출하여 육 년 동안 성전에 숨겼다(왕하 11:1-3; 대하 22:11-12). 일곱째 해에 여호야다는 군 지휘관들과 레위인들을 모아 정당한 상속자의 존재를 밝히고 아달랴를 대적하는 쿠데타를 조직했다(왕하 11:4-12; 대하 23:1-11). 요아스는 왕으로 즉위했고 아달랴는 처형되었다(왕하 11:13-16; 대하 23:12-15). 요아스의 통치 기간 동안 여호야다는 그의 조언자로 섬기며 여호와의 길로 그를 인도했다(왕하 12:2). 여호야다는 또한 성전 수리를 시작하고 이를 위한 자금 모금을 감독했다(왕하 12:7-16; 대하 24:4-14). 그는 백삼십 세에 죽어 다윗 성에 있는 왕들 가운데 묻혔는데, 이는 유다 역사에서 그의 중요한 역할을 증거한다(대하 24:15-16). 여호야다가 죽은 후 요아스는 여호와에게서 돌아섰고 심지어 왕의 불순종에 대해 목소리를 낸 여호야다의 아들 스가랴를 처형하라고 명령했다(대하 24:17-22; 마 23:35). 이 배신 행위는 요아스와 유다 왕국의 몰락으로 이어졌다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of one of David's warriors, Benaiah
persons.short: Jehoiada was the father  of one of David's warriors who commanded the Kerethites and Pelethites;
persons.article: Jehoiada was the father of one of David's warriors who commanded the Kerethites and Pelethites - the elite kings' guard. He first appears in 2Sa.8.18, and 1Ch.27.5 he is called a "priest". However this probably means some kind of non-religious official, in the same way that David's sons are described as "priests" in 2Sa.8.18.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.18 only referred to as Jehoiada (יְהוֹיָדָע); father of Benaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 동료. 2Sa.8.18에 처음 언급되며 '여호야다'라 불림. 브나야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호야다는 그렛 사람과 블렛 사람을 지휘한 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 여호야다는 왕의 정예 호위대인 그렛 사람과 블렛 사람을 지휘한 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람의 아버지였다. 그는 사무엘하 8:18에 처음 등장하며, 역대상 27:5에서 '제사장'이라 불린다. 그러나 이는 아마 다윗의 아들들이 사무엘하 8:18에서 '제사장'으로 묘사된 것과 같은 방식으로, 종교적 직분이 아닌 어떤 비종교적 관리를 의미하는 것으로 보인다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer in the house of the Lord
persons.short: Jehoiada was appointed as an overseer in the house of the Lord during the time of Jeremiah.
persons.article: Jehoiada is mentioned in Jer.29.26 as an overseer in the house of the Lord. In a letter sent from the false prophet Shemaiah to the priest Zephaniah, Shemaiah criticizes Zephaniah for not rebuking Jeremiah and appointing Jehoiada as an overseer in the temple. The context suggests that Jehoiada was a contemporary of Jeremiah and held a position of authority in the temple. However, the text does not provide any further details about Jehoiada's background, his specific duties, or his relationship with Jeremiah. The mention of his name in this letter indicates that he was a known figure in the religious establishment of Jerusalem during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.29.26 only referred to as Jehoiada (יְהוֹיָדָע).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.29.26에 처음 언급되며 '여호야다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호야다는 예레미야 시대에 여호와의 집에서 감독으로 임명되었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Josiah
persons.short: Jehoiakim, also known as Eliakim, was a king of Judah who reigned for eleven years before being succeeded by his son Jehoiachin.
persons.article: Jehoiakim, also known as Eliakim, was a king of Judah who reigned for eleven years (609-598 BC). He was the second son of King Josiah and became king after his younger brother Jehoahaz was deposed by Pharaoh Necho II of Egypt (2Ki.23.34; 2Ch.36.4). Necho changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim and imposed a heavy tribute on Judah (2Ki.23.35). During Jehoiakim's reign, Judah became a vassal state of Egypt and later Babylon (2Ki.24.1). Jehoiakim initially served Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon but later rebelled against him (2Ki.24.1). This rebellion led to the first Babylonian invasion of Judah, during which some of the temple treasures and members of the royal family and nobility were taken to Babylon (2Ch.36.6-7; Dan.1.1-2). The prophet Jeremiah prophesied during Jehoiakim's reign, warning the king and the people of Judah about the impending Babylonian judgment (Jer.1.3; 25.1; 26.1). Jehoiakim opposed Jeremiah, burning the scroll containing the prophet's warnings (Jeremiah 36) and persecuting those who followed Jeremiah's message (Jer.26.20-23). Jehoiakim died before the final Babylonian invasion and was succeeded by his son Jehoiachin (2Ki.24.6). The circumstances of his death are not clearly stated in the biblical text, but Jeremiah prophesied that he would be buried like a donkey, dragged and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem (Jer.22.18-19; 36.30).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.23.34 referred to as Jehoiakim (יְהוֹיָקִים), or Eliakim (אֶלְיָקִים); a son of Josiah and Zebidah; half-brother of: Jehoahaz, Zedekiah and Shallum; husband of Nehushta; father of Jehoiachin.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.23.34에 처음 언급되며 '여호야김'이라 불림. 요시야와 스비다의 아들. 여호아하스, 시드기야와 살룸의 형제. 느후스다의 남편. 여호야긴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호야김(엘리아김이라고도 함)은 유다 왕으로 십일 년간 다스렸고, 그 아들 여호야긴이 뒤를 이었다.
persons.article_ko: 여호야김(엘리아김이라고도 함)은 십일 년간(기원전 609-598년) 다스린 유다 왕이었다. 그는 요시야 왕의 둘째 아들로, 동생 여호아하스가 애굽 바로 느고 2세에게 폐위된 후 왕이 되었다(왕하 23:34; 대하 36:4). 느고는 엘리아김의 이름을 여호야김으로 바꾸고 유다에 무거운 조공을 부과했다(왕하 23:35). 여호야김의 통치 기간 동안 유다는 애굽의, 그리고 후에 바벨론의 봉신국이 되었다(왕하 24:1). 여호야김은 처음에는 바벨론 왕 느부갓네살을 섬겼으나 후에 그를 대적하여 반역했다(왕하 24:1). 이 반역은 첫 번째 바벨론의 유다 침공으로 이어졌고, 그 과정에서 성전 보물 일부와 왕족 및 귀족들이 바벨론으로 끌려갔다(대하 36:6-7; 단 1:1-2). 선지자 예레미야는 여호야김의 통치 기간 동안 예언하며 왕과 유다 백성에게 임박한 바벨론의 심판에 대해 경고했다(렘 1:3; 25:1; 26:1). 여호야김은 예레미야를 대적하여 그의 경고가 담긴 두루마리를 불태웠고(예레미야 36장) 예레미야의 메시지를 따르는 자들을 박해했다(렘 26:20-23). 여호야김은 마지막 바벨론 침공 이전에 죽었고 그의 아들 여호야긴이 뒤를 이었다(왕하 24:6). 그의 죽음의 정황은 성경 본문에 명확히 언급되지 않지만, 예레미야는 그가 나귀처럼 매장되어 예루살렘 성문 밖으로 끌려나가 던져질 것이라고 예언했다(렘 22:18-19; 36:30).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a priestly division during David's reign
persons.short: Jehoiarib was the head of the first priestly division organized by King David.
persons.article: Jehoiarib is mentioned in 1Ch.24.7 as the head of the first priestly division organized by King David. As part of David's reforms, the priests were divided into 24 groups to serve in the temple on a rotating basis. The order of service was determined by casting lots, and Jehoiarib's division was selected first. This suggests that Jehoiarib and his descendants held a prominent position among the priestly families. The text does not provide any further information about Jehoiarib's background or his specific role in the priestly duties. However, the organization of the priestly divisions was a significant step in establishing a structured and efficient system for temple service, ensuring that the worship of God was carried out regularly and in an orderly manner.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.7 only referred to as Jehoiarib (יְהוֹיָרִיב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.7에 처음 언급되며 '여호야립'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호야립은 다윗 왕이 조직한 첫 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Jehonathan was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Jehonathan is mentioned in 2Ch.17.8 as one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. This chapter describes Jehoshaphat's efforts to strengthen the spiritual foundation of his kingdom by sending out teachers to instruct the people in the ways of the Lord. Jehonathan is listed among the Levites who were chosen for this important task, along with Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, and Tobijah. The text does not provide any further details about Jehonathan's background or his specific role in the teaching mission. However, his inclusion in this list suggests that he was a trusted and knowledgeable Levite who was capable of communicating the principles of God's law to the people. The sending out of these teachers demonstrates Jehoshaphat's commitment to the spiritual well-being of his subjects and his desire to foster a deeper understanding of God's word throughout the kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Jehonathan (יְהוֹנָתָן).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '여호나단'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호나단은 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Head of a priestly family during the high priesthood of Joiakim
persons.short: Jehonathan was the head of the priestly family of Shemaiah during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua.
persons.article: Jehonathan is mentioned in Neh.12.18 as the head of the priestly family of Shemaiah during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua. This chapter lists the priests and Levites who served in Jerusalem during the high priesthood of Joiakim, providing a record of the religious leadership after the return from the Babylonian exile. Jehonathan is listed among the heads of the priestly families, indicating that he was a prominent figure in the priestly hierarchy. The text does not provide any further details about Jehonathan's specific role or responsibilities, but his position as the head of a priestly family suggests that he would have been involved in the various duties associated with the temple service, such as offering sacrifices, teaching the law, and maintaining the sacred space. The mention of Jehonathan in this context helps to establish the continuity of the priestly lineage and the restoration of the temple worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.18 only referred to as Jehonathan (יְהוֹנָתָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.18에 처음 언급되며 '여호나단'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호나단은 예수아의 아들 요야김 시대에 스마야 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of N. Israel, son of Ahab
persons.short: Joram (or Jehoram), the son of Ahab, was king of Northern Israel for twelve years.
persons.article: Joram, also known as Jehoram, was the king of Northern Israel and the son of King Ahab. He became king after the death of his brother Ahaziah who had no son (2 Kings 1:17). He began his reign in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and ruled for twelve years from Samaria (2 Kings 3:1). Joram was not as wicked as his parents, for he removed the pillar of Baal, but he still continued in the sinful ways of Jeroboam by allowing the worship of golden calves. During his reign, Joram formed alliances with the kings of Judah, Jehoshaphat and later Ahaziah, who were also his relatives by marriage (2 Kings 8:16, 25). These alliances led to joint military campaigns, including a war against Moab and, most notably, a battle against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth Gilead (2 Kings 3:6; 8:28. ¶ In the battle at Ramoth Gilead, Joram was wounded and returned to Jezreel to recover )(2 Kings 8:29; 2 Chronicles 22:6). While he was recovering, Jehu, who had been anointed by a prophet to destroy the house of Ahab, led a revolt against him (2 Kings 9:14, 16). Joram went out to meet Jehu, but Jehu killed him with an arrow and threw his body on the field of Naboth, fulfilling the prophecy of judgment against Ahab’s family (2 Kings 9:21-26). Joram’s death marked the end of the Omride dynasty and the beginning of Jehu’s rule over Israel (2 Kings 9:29; 2 Chronicles 22:7). His life is a story of political alliances, battles, and the fulfillment of God’s judgment on a royal house that had turned away from the Lord.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.1.17 referred to as Joram (יוֹרָם), or Joram or Jehoram (יְהוֹרָם); son of Ahab and Jezebel; a brother of Joash, Ahaziah and Athaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.1.17에 처음 언급되며 '요람'이라 불림. 아합과 이세벨의 아들. 요아스, 아하시야와 아달랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요람(여호람이라고도 함)은 아합의 아들로 북이스라엘 왕으로 십이 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 요람(여호람이라고도 함)은 북이스라엘의 왕이며 아합 왕의 아들이었다. 그는 아들이 없었던 형제 아하시야가 죽은 후 왕이 되었다(왕하 1:17). 그는 유다 왕 여호사밧 통치 십팔 년째에 통치를 시작하여 사마리아에서 십이 년간 다스렸다(왕하 3:1). 요람은 부모만큼 악하지는 않았는데, 바알의 기둥을 제거했으나 여전히 금송아지 숭배를 허용하며 여로보암의 죄악된 길을 이어갔다. 그의 통치 기간 동안 요람은 유다 왕 여호사밧, 그리고 후에는 결혼으로 그의 친척이 된 아하시야와 동맹을 맺었다(왕하 8:16, 25). 이 동맹은 모압을 대적하는 전쟁과, 특히 라못길르앗에서 시리아 왕 하사엘을 대적하는 전투를 포함한 공동 군사작전으로 이어졌다(왕하 3:6; 8:28). 라못길르앗 전투에서 요람은 부상을 입어 회복을 위해 이스르엘로 돌아갔다(왕하 8:29; 대하 22:6). 그가 회복하는 동안 아합의 집을 멸하도록 한 선지자에게 기름부음을 받은 예후가 그를 대적하는 반역을 이끌었다(왕하 9:14, 16). 요람은 예후를 만나러 나갔으나 예후는 화살로 그를 죽이고 그의 시신을 나봇의 밭에 던져 아합 가문에 대한 심판의 예언을 성취했다(왕하 9:21-26). 요람의 죽음은 오므리 왕조의 끝과 예후의 이스라엘 통치의 시작을 나타냈다(왕하 9:29; 대하 22:7). 그의 삶은 정치적 동맹, 전투, 그리고 여호와에게서 돌아선 왕가에 대한 하나님의 심판이 이루어지는 이야기다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Azariah@2Ch.21.2, Jehiel@2Ch.21.2, Zechariah@2Ch.21.2, Azariahu@2Ch.21.2, Michael@2Ch.21.2, Shephatiah@2Ch.21.2
persons.brief: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
persons.short: Jehoram, also known as Joram, was the son of Jehoshaphat and king of Judah.
persons.article: Jehoram, also known as Joram, was the son of Jehoshaphat and became king of Judah. He reigned for eight years in Jerusalem. Jehoram married Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. He followed the evil ways of the kings of Israel and did what was wrong in the eyes of the Lord. During his reign, Edom revolted against Judah's rule. Jehoram engaged in battle with Edom but was surrounded. He managed to break through during the night. The Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels, and he died in great pain. His son Ahaziah succeeded him as king.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.50 referred to as Jehoram (יְהוֹרָם), or Joram (יוֹרָם), or Joram (Ἰωράμ); son of Jehoshaphat; a brother of Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah; husband of Athaliah; father of Ahaziah and Jehosheba.
persons.short_ko: 여호람은 유다 왕 여호사밧의 아들이자 이스라엘 왕 아합의 아들로, 동명의 두 왕이 같은 시대에 있었다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.22.50에 처음 언급되며 '여호람'이라 불림. 여호사밧의 아들. 아사랴, 여히엘, 스가랴, 아사랴, 미가엘과 스바댜의 형제. 아달랴의 남편. 아하시야와 여호세바의 아버지.
persons.article_ko: 여호람(요람이라고도 함)은 여호사밧의 아들이며 유다 왕이 되었다. 그는 예루살렘에서 팔 년간 다스렸다. 여호람은 아합과 이세벨의 딸 아달랴와 결혼했다. 그는 이스라엘 왕들의 악한 길을 따라 여호와 보시기에 악을 행했다. 그의 통치 기간 동안 에돔이 유다의 통치를 대적하여 반역했다. 여호람은 에돔과 전투를 벌였으나 포위당했다. 그는 밤중에 간신히 뚫고 나왔다. 여호와는 여호람을 고칠 수 없는 창자병으로 치셨고, 그는 극심한 고통 속에서 죽었다. 그의 아들 아하시야가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach.
persons.short: Jehoram was a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in Judah.
persons.article: Jehoram was a Levite who was sent by King Jehoshaphat of Judah to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. He was part of a group of Levites, officials, and priests tasked with instructing the people in the ways of the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Jehoram (יְהוֹרָם).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '여호람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호람은 여호사밧이 유다에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Jehoram@1Ki.22.50-Mat, Azariah@2Ch.21.2, Jehiel@2Ch.21.2, Zechariah@2Ch.21.2, Azariahu@2Ch.21.2, Michael@2Ch.21.2, Shephatiah@2Ch.21.2
persons.brief: Son of Asa, king of Judah.
persons.short: Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa and became a powerful and righteous king of Judah.
persons.article: Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa and became king of Judah at the age of 35. He reigned for 25 years in Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat did what was right in the eyes of the Lord and followed the ways of his father Asa. He removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah and sent officials to teach the Book of the Law throughout the land. Jehoshaphat became very wealthy and held great honor. He allied himself with Ahab, king of Israel, through marriage and military campaigns. After a prophet rebuked him for helping the wicked Ahab, Jehoshaphat continued to seek the Lord. When faced with a vast army of Moabites, Ammonites, and Meunites, Jehoshaphat prayed for deliverance, and the Lord caused the enemy forces to destroy each other. He enjoyed peace for the remainder of his reign. Jehoshaphat died and was buried in the City of David, and his son Jehoram succeeded him as king.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.15.24 referred to as Jehoshaphat (יְהוֹשָׁפָט), or Jehoshaphat (Ἰωσαφάτ); a son of Asa and Azubah; father of Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.15.24에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 아사와 아수바의 아들. 여호람, 아사랴, 여히엘, 스가랴, 아사랴, 미가엘과 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧은 아사의 아들로 유다의 강력하고 의로운 왕이 되었다.
persons.article_ko: 여호사밧은 아사의 아들이며 삼십오 세에 유다 왕이 되었다. 그는 예루살렘에서 이십오 년간 다스렸다. 여호사밧은 여호와 보시기에 정직히 행하며 그의 아버지 아사의 길을 따랐다. 그는 유다에서 산당과 아세라 목상을 제거했고 온 땅에 율법책을 가르치도록 관리들을 보냈다. 여호사밧은 큰 부와 큰 영예를 누렸다. 그는 결혼과 군사 원정을 통해 이스라엘 왕 아합과 동맹을 맺었다. 한 선지자가 악한 아합을 도운 것에 대해 그를 책망한 후에도 여호사밧은 계속 여호와를 찾았다. 모압, 암몬, 므운 사람들의 큰 군대에 직면했을 때 여호사밧은 구원을 위해 기도했고, 여호와께서는 원수 군대가 서로를 멸하게 하셨다. 그는 통치 나머지 기간 동안 평안을 누렸다. 여호사밧은 죽어 다윗 성에 장사되었고, 그의 아들 여호람이 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Solomon's officer, son of Paruah.
persons.short: Jehoshaphat, son of Paruah, was one of Solomon's twelve officers responsible for providing food for the king and his household.
persons.article: Jehoshaphat, the son of Paruah, was one of the twelve officers appointed by King Solomon to oversee the provision of food for the king and his household. Each officer was responsible for supplying provisions for one month of the year. Jehoshaphat's district was Issachar.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.17 only referred to as Jehoshaphat (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); a son of Paruah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 바루아의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바루아의 아들 여호사밧은 솔로몬 왕과 왕실을 위한 양식을 공급하도록 임명된 열두 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jehu, king of Israel.
persons.short: Jehoshaphat was the father of Jehu, who became king of Israel.
persons.article: Jehoshaphat was the father of Jehu, who was anointed by Elisha's servant to become king of Israel. Jehu was a commander in the army of Joram, king of Israel, when he was anointed. Jehoshaphat's son Jehu went on to fulfill the prophecy against the house of Ahab by destroying Joram and the royal family of Israel.
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.9.2 only referred to as Jehoshaphat (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); a son of Nimshi; father of Jehu.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.9.2에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 님시의 아들. 예후의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧은 이스라엘 왕이 된 예후의 아버지였다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Recorder for David and Solomon.
persons.short: Jehoshaphat served as a recorder for King David and his son Solomon.
persons.article: Jehoshaphat was an official who served as a recorder during the reigns of King David and his son Solomon. The role of a recorder was to keep records of important events and decisions in the kingdom. Jehoshaphat is mentioned alongside other key officials in David and Solomon's administrations.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.16 only referred to as Jehoshaphat (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); son of Ahilud; a brother of Baana.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 동료. 2Sa.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 아힐룻의 아들. 바아나의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧은 다윗 왕과 그 아들 솔로몬 시대에 사관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Jehoram, saved Joash from Athaliah's massacre.
persons.short: Jehosheba, also known as Jehoshabeath, was the daughter of King Jehoram and the wife of Jehoiada the priest; she saved the infant Joash from Athaliah's massacre of the royal family.
persons.article: Jehosheba, also known as Jehoshabeath, was the daughter of King Jehoram of Judah and the sister of King Ahaziah. She was married to Jehoiada, the high priest. When Athaliah, Jehosheba's mother, attempted to kill all the royal heirs after Ahaziah's death, Jehosheba rescued the infant Joash, Ahaziah's son, and hid him in the temple for six years. Later, Jehoiada and Jehosheba orchestrated the coronation of Joash and the overthrow of Athaliah.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.11.2 referred to as Jehosheba (יְהוֹשֶׁבַע), or Jehoshabeath (יְהוֹשַׁבְעַת); daughter of Jehoram and Athaliah; a sister of Ahaziah; wife of Jehoiada; mother of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.11.2에 처음 언급되며 '여호세바'라 불림. 여호람과 아달랴의 딸. 아하시야의 자매. 여호야다의 아내. 스가랴의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여호세바(여호사브앗이라고도 함)는 여호람 왕의 딸이며 제사장 여호야다의 아내로, 아달랴의 왕족 학살에서 아기 요아스를 구했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Shemaiah@1Ch.26.4-, Joah@1Ch.26.4, Sachar@1Ch.26.4, Nethanel@1Ch.26.4, Ammiel@1Ch.26.5, Issachar@1Ch.26.5, Peullethai@1Ch.26.5
persons.brief: Son of Obed-edom, a gatekeeper for the ark.
persons.short: Jehozabad was one of the sons of Obed-edom who served as a gatekeeper for the ark of the covenant.
persons.article: Jehozabad was one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite who was entrusted with the care of the ark of the covenant. Jehozabad, along with his brothers, was appointed as a gatekeeper for the ark. They were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tent that housed the ark and ensuring that only authorized personnel could enter.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.4 only referred to as Jehozabad (יְהוֹזָבָד); son of Obed-edom; a brother of Shemaiah, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar and Peullethai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.4에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 오벧에돔의 아들. 스마야, 요아, 사갈, 느다넬, 암미엘, 잇사갈과 브울래대의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧은 오벧에돔의 아들 중 한 사람으로 언약궤의 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Commander of 180,000 warriors under Jehoshaphat.
persons.short: Jehozabad was a commander who led 180,000 warriors under King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.article: Jehozabad was one of the commanders in King Jehoshaphat's army. He led a force of 180,000 warriors who were equipped for battle. Jehozabad's large contingent was part of Jehoshaphat's military might, which was established during his reign as he sought to strengthen Judah's defenses and maintain peace in the region.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.18 only referred to as Jehozabad (יְהוֹזָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.18에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧은 유다 왕 여호사밧 밑에서 십팔만 용사를 이끈 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Moabite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shomer, killed King Joash of Judah.
persons.short: Jehozabad, the son of Shomer, was one of the servants who conspired against and killed King Joash of Judah.
persons.article: Jehozabad, the son of Shomer, was one of the servants who conspired against King Joash of Judah. Along with Jozabad, the son of Shimeath, Jehozabad murdered Joash in his bed as revenge for the execution of Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest. The assassination took place at the house of Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla. Joash's son Amaziah succeeded him as king and executed the conspirators.
persons.summary: A man of the Moabites living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.12.21 only referred to as Jehozabad (יְהוֹזָבָד); a son of Shomer.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 모압 사람. 2Ki.12.21에 처음 언급되며 '여호사밧'이라 불림. 소멜의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 소멜의 아들 여호사밧은 유다 왕 요아스를 암살하는 음모에 가담한 신하 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Joshua the high priest during the exile.
persons.short: Jehozadak (or Jozadak) was the father of Joshua, the high priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and helped rebuild the temple.
persons.article: Jehozadak, also known as Jozadak, was the father of Joshua, the high priest who served during the time of the Babylonian exile and the return to Jerusalem. Jehozadak was the son of Seraiah, the high priest who was executed by Nebuchadnezzar when Jerusalem fell. Jehozadak was taken into captivity in Babylon, where his son Joshua was born. After the exile, Joshua returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and helped to rebuild the temple and restore the worship of God. Jehozadak is mentioned in the genealogies of the high priests and in the accounts of the rebuilding of the temple.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.14 referred to as Jehozadak (יְהוֹצָדָק), or Jozadak (יוֹצָדָק), or Jozadak (Aramiac יוֹצָדָק); son of Seraiah; a brother of Ezra; father of Joshua.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 대제사장. 1Ch.6.14에 처음 언급되며 '여호사닥'이라 불림. 스라야의 아들. 에스라의 형제. 여호수아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호사닥(요사닥이라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아와 성전 재건을 도운 대제사장 여호수아의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 여호사닥(요사닥이라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로 시대와 예루살렘 귀환 시기에 섬긴 대제사장 여호수아의 아버지였다. 여호사닥은 예루살렘이 함락되었을 때 느부갓네살에게 처형된 대제사장 스라야의 아들이었다. 여호사닥은 바벨론으로 포로로 끌려갔고, 그곳에서 그의 아들 여호수아가 태어났다. 포로 이후 여호수아는 스룹바벨과 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아와 성전 재건과 하나님 예배 회복을 도왔다. 여호사닥은 대제사장 족보와 성전 재건 기록에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Jehu was one of the Benjamite archers and slingers who joined David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul.
persons.article: Jehu, a Benjamite warrior, was among the skilled archers and slingers who joined David at Ziklag while he was seeking refuge from King Saul. These warriors, including Jehu, were ambidextrous and could shoot arrows and sling stones with either hand. They pledged their allegiance to David during this time of his exile, demonstrating their support for the future king of Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Jehu (יֵהוּא).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '예후'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 예후는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 베냐민 궁수와 물매꾼 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Obed, a descendant of Judah.
persons.short: Jehu was a descendant of Judah through Obed, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jehu, the son of Obed, is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was a descendant of Hezron, one of the sons of Perez, who was a son of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.38 only referred to as Jehu (יֵהוּא); a son of Obed; father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.38에 처음 언급되며 '예후'라 불림. 오벳의 아들. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 예후는 오벧을 통한 유다의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Joshibiah, a descendant of Simeon.
persons.short: Jehu, the son of Joshibiah, was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jehu, the son of Joshibiah, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles. He was part of the family of Asiel, a descendant of Simeon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.35 only referred to as Jehu (יֵהוּא); a son of Joshibiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.35에 처음 언급되며 '예후'라 불림. 요시비야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여시비야의 아들 예후는 시므온의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hanani, prophet during the reign of Baasha and Jehoshaphat.
persons.short: Jehu, the son of Hanani, was a prophet who prophesied against Baasha, king of Israel, and later rebuked Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, for his alliance with Ahab.
persons.article: Jehu, the son of Hanani, was a prophet who lived during the reigns of Baasha, king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He delivered a message from God to Baasha, condemning him for his evil ways and announcing the downfall of his dynasty. Later, Jehu rebuked Jehoshaphat for his alliance with Ahab, the wicked king of Israel. He warned Jehoshaphat that his actions had brought God's wrath upon him. Jehu also wrote a record of the events during Jehoshaphat's reign, which was included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.1 only referred to as Jehu (יֵהוּא); a son of Hanani.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '예후'라 불림. 하나니의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하나니의 아들 선지자 예후는 이스라엘 왕 바아사를 대적하여 예언했고, 후에 아합과 동맹한 여호사밧을 책망했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel, destroyed Ahab's dynasty.
persons.short: Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, was anointed king of Israel by Elisha's servant; he destroyed the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal, but continued in the sins of Jeroboam.
persons.article: Jehu, the son of Jehoshaphat, was a commander in the army of Israel during the reign of Joram. He was anointed king by a servant of Elisha the prophet, who instructed him to destroy the house of Ahab. Jehu carried out this mission zealously, killing Joram, Ahaziah (king of Judah), Jezebel, and all the descendants of Ahab. He also eradicated the worship of Baal in Israel. However, Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, continuing the worship of the golden calves. His dynasty lasted for four generations, as promised by God, but Israel suffered losses to the Arameans during his reign. Jehu's story is recorded in the books of 1 and 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and Hosea.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.19.16 only referred to as Jehu (יֵהוּא); a son of Jehoshaphat; father of Jehoahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.19.16에 처음 언급되며 '예후'라 불림. 여호사밧의 아들. 여호아하스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호사밧의 아들 예후는 엘리사의 종에게 기름부음을 받아 이스라엘 왕이 되었고, 아합의 집과 바알 숭배를 멸했으나 여로보암의 죄를 계속 따랐다.
persons.article_ko: 여호사밧의 아들 예후는 요람 왕 시대에 이스라엘 군대의 지휘관이었다. 그는 선지자 엘리사의 종에게 기름부음을 받아 왕이 되었는데, 그 종은 그에게 아합의 집을 멸하라고 지시했다. 예후는 이 사명을 열심히 수행하여 요람, 아하시야(유다 왕), 이세벨, 그리고 아합의 모든 후손을 죽였다. 그는 또한 이스라엘에서 바알 숭배를 근절했다. 그러나 예후는 여로보암의 죄에서 돌이키지 않고 계속 금송아지 숭배를 이어갔다. 그의 왕조는 하나님이 약속하신 대로 사대에 걸쳐 지속되었으나, 이스라엘은 그의 통치 기간 동안 아람 사람들에게 손실을 입었다. 예후의 이야기는 열왕기상하, 역대하, 호세아서에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Asher.
persons.short: Jehubbah was a descendant of Asher mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jehubbah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), who was a descendant of Beriah, one of the sons of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.34 only referred to as Jehubbah (חֻבָּה); son of Shomer; a brother of Ahi, Rohgah and Aram.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.34에 처음 언급되며 '호바'라 불림. 소멜의 아들. 아히, 로가와 아람의 형제.
