persons.short_ko: 여훕바는 아셀의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An official during Zedekiah's reign, opposed Jeremiah.
persons.short: Jehucal (or Jucal) was an official during King Zedekiah's reign who opposed the prophet Jeremiah and sought his punishment.
persons.article: Jehucal, also known as Jucal, was an official during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah. He, along with Zephaniah the priest, was sent by the king to the prophet Jeremiah to request his prayers for the nation. However, later, Jehucal is mentioned as one of the officials who opposed Jeremiah and sought to have him punished for his prophecies. He, along with other officials, urged the king to put Jeremiah to death, accusing him of discouraging the people and not seeking the welfare of the nation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.37.3 referred to as Jehucal (יְהוּכַל), or Jucal (יוּכַל); a son of Shelemiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.37.3에 처음 언급되며 '여후갈'이라 불림. 셀레마의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여후갈(유갈이라고도 함)은 시드기야 왕 시대의 관리로, 선지자 예레미야를 대적하여 그의 처벌을 구했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An official who read Jeremiah's scroll to Jehoiakim.
persons.short: Jehudi was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign who read Jeremiah's scroll to the king, who then burned it piece by piece.
persons.article: Jehudi was an official during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah. He was the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi. When Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, read the prophet's scroll in the temple, the officials sent Jehudi to summon Baruch and have him bring the scroll. Jehudi then read the scroll to the officials, who decided to report its contents to the king. Jehudi was then sent to read the scroll to King Jehoiakim. As Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut off the portion with a scribe's knife and threw it into the fire until the entire scroll was burned. Despite the warnings in the scroll, neither the king nor his officials showed any fear or repentance.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.36.14 only referred to as Jehudi (יְהוּדִי); a son of Nethaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.14에 처음 언급되며 '여후디'라 불림. 느다니야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여후디는 여호야김 왕 시대의 관리로, 예레미야의 두루마리를 왕에게 읽었고 왕은 그것을 조각조각 태웠다.

persons.description: Woman descended from Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev
persons.brief: Wife of Mered; mother of Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel.
persons.short: Jehudijah (or the Judahite) was the wife of Mered and the mother of Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Jehudijah, also referred to as the Judahite, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles. She was the wife of Mered, a descendant of Judah. Jehudijah gave birth to three sons: Jered, who was the father of Gedor; Heber, the father of Soco; and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.18 only referred to as Jehudijah (יְהֻדִיָּה); wife of Mered(?); mother of Jered, Heber and Jekuthiel.
persons.summary_ko: 유다의 여성 후손. 1Ch.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '여후디야'라 불림. 메렛의 아내. 예렛, 헤벨과 여구디엘의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여후디야(유다 여인이라는 뜻)는 므렛의 아내이며, 유다 족보에 기록된 예렛, 헤벨, 여구디엘의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who helped cleanse the temple under Hezekiah.
persons.short: Jehuel was a Levite from the family of Heman who participated in the cleansing of the temple during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Jehuel was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He was a member of the family of Heman, one of the three principal musicians appointed by David. When Hezekiah ordered the cleansing and rededication of the temple, Jehuel was among the Levites who helped in this process, purifying themselves and working to restore the temple for proper worship.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.14 only referred to as Jehuel (יְחִיאֵל); son of Heman; a brother of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 2Ch.29.14에 처음 언급되며 '여후엘'이라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 시므이의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여후엘은 헤만 가문 출신 레위인으로, 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일에 참여했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men from Mahavite.
persons.short: Jeiel the Mahavite was listed among David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeiel the Mahavite is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles. He was one of the warriors who fought alongside David and demonstrated exceptional valor and military skill. However, no additional information is provided about Jeiel's background or specific accomplishments.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.44 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל); son of Hotham; a brother of Shama.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.44에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림. 호담의 아들. 사마의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마하위 사람 여이엘은 역대상에서 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 언급된다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite musician and gatekeeper during David's reign.
persons.short: Jeiel (or Jehiah) was a Levite who served as a musician and gatekeeper during the time of David, particularly in the transportation of the ark to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jeiel, also known as Jehiah, was a Levite who lived during the reign of King David. He was appointed as one of the musicians to play the harp when the ark of the covenant was brought to Jerusalem. Jeiel was also among the Levites who blew trumpets before the ark during its journey. Additionally, he served as a gatekeeper for the ark, ensuring its safety and proper handling. Jeiel's responsibilities as a musician and gatekeeper highlight the importance of worship and reverence in the presence of the ark of the covenant.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל), or Jehiah (יְחִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여이엘(여히야라고도 함)은 다윗 시대에 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮길 때 음악가이며 문지기로 섬긴 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a Reubenite family.
persons.short: Jeiel was the head of a family in the tribe of Reuben, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeiel is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben in 1 Chronicles. He was the head of a family within the tribe, but no further details are provided about him or his family in the biblical record.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.7 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.7에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여이엘은 르우벤 지파의 한 가문의 우두머리로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite during Jehoshaphat's reign.
persons.short: Jeiel was the grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite who prophesied during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.article: Jeiel is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as the grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. When Jehoshaphat and his army faced a formidable enemy alliance, the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jahazielin the midst of the assembly. Jahaziel prophesied victory and encouragement to the king and his people, assuring them of God's presence and deliverance in the upcoming battle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.20.14 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל); a son of Mattaniah; father of Benaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.20.14에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림. 맛다냐의 아들. 브나야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여이엘은 유다 왕 여호사밧 시대에 예언한 레위인 야하시엘의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A scribe in King Uzziah's army.
persons.short: Jeiel was the scribe who recorded the number of soldiers in King Uzziah's army.
persons.article: Jeiel is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as a scribe during the reign of King Uzziah of Judah. He was responsible for recording the number of soldiers in Uzziah's army, which was organized by Maaseiah the officer under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders. Jeiel's role as a scribe highlights the importance of record-keeping and organization in the military during Uzziah's prosperous reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.26.11 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.26.11에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여이엘은 웃시야 왕의 군대 병력 수를 기록한 서기관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who contributed to Josiah's Passover celebration.
persons.short: Jeiel was one of the Levites who generously provided animals for King Josiah's Passover celebration.
persons.article: Jeiel is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as one of the Levites who contributed to the Passover celebration during the reign of King Josiah of Judah. Along with other Levitical leaders, Jeiel generously provided sheep, lambs, and goats for the Passover offerings. This act of generosity demonstrated the Levites' support for Josiah's religious reforms and their commitment to the proper observance of the Passover festival.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.35.9 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.35.9에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여이엘은 요시야 왕의 유월절 행사에 짐승을 아낌없이 제공한 레위인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife.
persons.short: Jeiel, a descendant of Nebo, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.
persons.article: Jeiel is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the descendants of Nebo who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. When Ezra learned of the widespread intermarriage between the Israelites and the neighboring peoples, he called for repentance and reform. Jeiel was among those who agreed to send away their foreign wives and children, demonstrating their commitment to obey God's law and maintain the purity of the Israelite community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.43 only referred to as Jeiel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.43에 처음 언급되며 '여이엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느보의 후손 여이엘은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그녀를 내보내기로 동의했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A Levite, son of Hebron.
persons.short: Jekameam was a Levite, the son of Hebron, mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jekameam is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Hebron, who was a descendant of Kohath, one of the sons of Levi. Jekameam is listed among the Levites who were appointed to various duties in the service of the tabernacle during the time of David. The genealogical record in 1 Chronicles emphasizes the importance of the Levitical lineage and their roles in the worship and service of God.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.19 only referred to as Jekameam (יְקַמְעָם); son of Hebron; a brother of Jeriah, Amariah and Jahaziel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.19에 처음 언급되며 '여가므암'이라 불림. 헤브론의 아들. 여리야, 아마랴와 야하시엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여가므암은 헤브론의 아들이며 레위인으로, 역대상 레위인 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shallum, a descendant of Judah.
persons.short: Jekamiah was a descendant of Judah through Shallum, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jekamiah is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Shallum, who was a descendant of Sheshan, from the clan of Jerahmeel. The genealogy traces Jekamiah's lineage back to Judah, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob').
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.41 only referred to as Jekamiah (יְקַמְיָה); a son of Shallum; father of Elishama.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.41에 처음 언급되며 '여가먀'라 불림. 살룸의 아들. 엘리사마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여가먀는 살룸을 통한 유다의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Jeconiah, a descendant of David.
persons.short: Jekamiah was a descendant of Jeconiah and a descendant of David, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jekamiah is mentioned in the genealogy of David in 1 Chronicles. He was one of the descendant of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), the king of Judah who was taken captive by the Babylonians. Jekamiah is listed among the descendants of David after the exile, indicating that the royal lineage continued even during the captivity.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.18 only referred to as Jekamiah (יְקַמְיָה); son of Shealtiel(?); a brother of Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.18에 처음 언급되며 '여가먀'라 불림. 스알디엘의 아들. 말기람, 브다야, 세낫살, 호사마와 느다뱌의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여가먀는 여고냐를 통한 다윗의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mered, founder of Zanoah.
persons.short: Jekuthiel was the son of Mered and the  father (ie founder) of Zanoah, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jekuthiel is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Mered, who was a descendant of Judah. Jekuthiel's mother was Jehudijah (or the Judahite woman), one of Mered's wives. Jekuthiel is described as the father (or founder) of Zanoah, which probably refers to a town associated with his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.18 only referred to as Jekuthiel (יְקוּתִיאֵל); son of Mered(?) and Jehudijah; a brother of Jered and Heber; half-brother of: Miriam, Shammai and Ishbah; father or founder of Zanoah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '여구디엘'이라 불림. 메렛과 여후디야의 아들. 예렛, 헤벨, 미리암, 삼매와 이스바의 형제. Zanoah의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여구디엘은 므렛의 아들이며 유다 족보에 나오는 사노아의 창설자(아버지)였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: One of Job's daughters born after his restoration.
persons.short: Jemimah was the first of three daughters born to Job after God restored his fortunes, as recorded in the book of Job.
persons.article: Jemimah is mentioned in the book of Job as one of the three daughters born to him after God restored his fortunes. She was the first daughter, followed by Keziah and Keren-happuch. The name Jemimah means "dove" or "warm," possibly signifying the peace and comfort that came to Job's life after his trials. The Bible notes that Job's daughters were the most beautiful women in all the land, and he granted them an inheritance along with their brothers, which was unusual in that culture. Jemimah's presence in the story emphasizes the completeness of Job's restoration and the blessings he received after his period of suffering.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Job.42.14 only referred to as Jemimah (יְמִימָה); daughter of Job; a sister of Keziah, Keren-happuch.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Job.42.14에 처음 언급되며 '여미마'라 불림. 욥의 딸. 긋시야와 게렌합북의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 여미마는 욥기에서 하나님이 욥의 재산을 회복시키신 후 태어난 세 딸 중 첫째였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Simeon, also known as Nemuel.
persons.short: Jemuel (or Nemuel) was a son of Simeon and a founder of the Nemuelite clan, as recorded in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jemuel, also known as Nemuel, was one of the sons of Simeon, the second son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah. He is mentioned in the lists of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt during the famine and in the census of the Israelites in the wilderness. In Numbers, the descendants of Jemuel are referred to as the Nemuelite clan, indicating that he was the founder of this family group within the tribe of Simeon. The variations in his name (Jemuel and Nemuel) may be due to textual transmission or linguistic differences. Beyond these genealogical references, no further information is provided about Jemuel's life or role in the family history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.10 referred to as Jemuel (יְמוּאֵל), or Nemuel (נְמוּאֵל), or Nemuelite (נְמוּאֵלִי); son of Simeon; a brother of Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zerah and Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '여무엘'이라 불림. 시므온과 시므온의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 야민, 오핫, 야긴, 세라와 사울의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여무엘(느무엘이라고도 함)은 시므온의 아들로, 느무엘 가문의 창설자였다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: A judge of Israel, known for his tragic vow.
persons.short: Jephthah was a judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the Ammonites but made a tragic vow that resulted in the sacrifice of his daughter.
persons.article: Jephthah was a judge of Israel during the period between the conquest of Canaan and the establishment of the monarchy. He was the son of Gilead and a prostitute, and his half-brothers drove him away from the family inheritance. Jephthah fled to the land of Tob, where he gathered a group of warriors around him. When the Ammonites attacked Israel, the elders of Gilead asked Jephthah to lead them in battle, promising him leadership if he succeeded. Jephthah made a vow to God, pledging to sacrifice the first thing that came out of his house to meet him if he were victorious. Jephthah defeated the Ammonites, but tragically, his daughter was the first to greet him upon his return. Jephthah fulfilled his vow, and his daughter willingly submitted to her fate. Jephthah judged Israel for six years before his death. His story highlights the importance of making wise vows and the consequences of rash decisions. Despite his tragic vow, Jephthah is commended in the New Testament for his faith and is listed among the heroes of faith in Hebrews 11.
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.11.1 referred to as Jephthah (יִפְתָּח), or Jephthah (Ἰεφθάε); a son of Gilead.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.11.1에 처음 언급되며 '입다'라 불림. 길르앗의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 입다는 이스라엘의 사사로 이스라엘을 암몬 사람들에게서 구원했으나, 비극적인 서원으로 인해 그의 딸을 제물로 바치는 결과를 낳았다.
persons.article_ko: 입다는 가나안 정복과 왕정 수립 사이 시기의 이스라엘 사사였다. 그는 길르앗과 창녀 사이에서 태어난 아들이었고, 그의 이복형제들은 그를 가족 유산에서 쫓아냈다. 입다는 돕 땅으로 도망쳐 그곳에서 자기 주변에 용사 무리를 모았다. 암몬 사람들이 이스라엘을 공격했을 때 길르앗의 장로들은 입다에게 전투에서 그들을 이끌어달라고 요청하며 성공하면 지도력을 주겠다고 약속했다. 입다는 하나님께 서원하여, 만약 자신이 승리한다면 자기 집에서 자신을 맞으러 나오는 첫 번째 것을 제물로 바치겠다고 맹세했다. 입다는 암몬 사람들을 물리쳤으나, 비극적으로 그가 돌아왔을 때 그를 처음 맞이한 것은 그의 딸이었다. 입다는 자기 서원을 지켰고, 그의 딸은 기꺼이 자기 운명에 순종했다. 입다는 죽기 전 육 년간 이스라엘을 다스렸다. 그의 이야기는 지혜로운 서원을 하는 것의 중요성과 경솔한 결정의 결과를 부각시킨다. 그의 비극적인 서원에도 불구하고 입다는 신약에서 그의 믿음으로 칭찬받으며 히브리서 11장의 믿음의 영웅들 명단에 포함되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Asher.
persons.short: Jephunneh is mentioned in the genealogy of Asher in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jephunneh is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles. He is listed as one of the sons of Jether, a descendant of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.38 only referred to as Jephunneh (יְפֻנֶּה); son of Ithran; a brother of Pispa and Ara.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.38에 처음 언급되며 '여분네'라 불림. 이드란의 아들. 비스바와 아라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여분네는 역대상 아셀 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Caleb's father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: The Kenizzite, father of Caleb the spy.
persons.short: Jephunneh, a Kenizzite, was the father of Caleb, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Jephunneh, a Kenizzite, was the father of Caleb, a prominent figure in the Old Testament. Caleb was chosen as one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. Along with Joshua, Caleb was one of the two spies who brought back a positive report and encouraged the Israelites to trust in God and take possession of the land. As a result, Caleb and Joshua were the only two adults from their generation permitted to enter Canaan. Jephunneh's Kenizzite background suggests that he may have been a descendant of the Kenizzites, a non-Israelite tribe that was later absorbed into the tribe of Judah. Caleb's inheritance in the Promised Land, including Hebron and its surrounding areas, is mentioned multiple times in connection with Jephunneh, emphasizing the faithfulness and obedience of this father-son duo.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.13.6 only referred to as Jephunneh (יְפֻנֶּה); father of Caleb, Kenaz.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 갈렙의 아버지. Num.13.6에 처음 언급되며 '여분네'라 불림. 갈렙과 그나스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 그니스 사람 여분네는 모세가 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람인 갈렙의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 그니스 사람 여분네는 구약의 저명한 인물인 갈렙의 아버지였다. 갈렙은 모세가 가나안 땅을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람으로 선택되었다. 여호수아와 함께 갈렙은 긍정적인 보고를 가져와 이스라엘 백성에게 하나님을 신뢰하고 그 땅을 차지하라고 격려한 두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람이었다. 그 결과 갈렙과 여호수아는 그 세대에서 가나안에 들어가는 것이 허락된 유일한 두 성인이었다. 여분네의 그니스 사람 배경은 그가 후에 유다 지파에 흡수된 비이스라엘 부족인 그니스 족속의 후손이었을 수 있음을 시사한다. 헤브론과 그 주변 지역을 포함한 약속의 땅에서의 갈렙의 기업은 여분네와 관련하여 여러 번 언급되어, 이 아버지와 아들 콤비의 신실함과 순종을 강조한다.

persons.brief: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem.
persons.short: Jerah was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, as recorded in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jerah is mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah. Joktan's descendants are believed to have settled in the southern Arabian Peninsula, suggesting that Jerah and his brothers may have been associated with the ancient peoples of that region. However, no further details are provided about Jerah's life or the specific territory he and his descendants inhabited.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.26 only referred to as Jerah (יֶ֫רַח); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '예라'라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예라는 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들 중 한 사람으로, 창세기와 역대상 민족 계보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite of the Merari clan.
persons.short: Jerahmeel was a Levite of the family of Merari, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jerahmeel is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles. He is described as a descendant of Merari, one of the three main clans of the Levites. The Merarites were responsible for the transportation and maintenance of the tabernacle's framework and related items during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings. However, no specific details are provided about Jerahmeel's role or life within the Merari clan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.29 only referred to as Jerahmeel (יְרַחְמְאֵל); a son of Kish.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.24.29에 처음 언급되며 '여라므엘'이라 불림. 기스의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여라므엘은 므라리 가문 출신 레위인으로, 역대상 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.offspring: Ram@1Ch.2.25-, Bunah@1Ch.2.25, Oren@1Ch.2.25, Ozem@1Ch.2.25, Ahijah@1Ch.2.25, Onam@1Ch.2.26-
persons.brief: Son of Hezron, a descendant of Judah.
persons.short: Jerahmeel was the son of Hezron and a prominent figure in the genealogy of Judah, with his descendants being called the Jerahmeelites.
persons.article: Jerahmeel was the son of Hezron, a descendant of Judah, and is mentioned in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles. He had two wives, Atarah and Ahijah, and several children who became the founders of various clans within the tribe of Judah. Jerahmeel's descendants, known as the Jerahmeelites, are mentioned in connection with David's time as a fugitive from King Saul. David sent gifts to the Jerahmeelites, among others, after defeating the Amalekites who had raided Ziklag. This suggests that the Jerahmeelites were a significant clan within Judah and had a friendly relationship with David. The Jerahmeelites' territory was likely located in the Negev region, south of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.27.10 referred to as Jerahmeel (יְרַחְמְאֵל), or Jerahmeelite (יְרַחְמְאֵלִי); son of Hezron; a brother of Ram, Caleb, Segub and Ashhur; husband of Atarah; father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, Ahijah and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Sa.27.10에 처음 언급되며 '여라므엘'이라 불림. 헤스론과 헤스론의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 람, 갈렙, 스굽과 아스훌의 형제. 아다라와 여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편. 람, 브나, 오렌, 오셈, 아히야와 오남의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여라므엘은 헤스론의 아들이며 유다 족보의 주요 인물로, 그 후손은 여라므엘 족속이라 불렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hammelech, sent to arrest Jeremiah.
persons.short: Jerahmeel, the son of Hammelech, was one of the officers sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch.
persons.article: Jerahmeel, the son of Hammelech (which means "the king"), was an officer in the court of King Jehoiakim of Judah. When Jeremiah's scribe, Baruch, read the prophet's words in the temple, the officials reported the incident to the king. Jehoiakim ordered Jerahmeel, along with two other officers, to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. However, the Lord hid them from the king's men. This event demonstrates the tension between the prophetic message and the royal authority, as well as God's protection of His faithful servants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.26 only referred to as Jerahmeel (יְרַחְמְאֵל); son of Hammelech; a brother of Malchijah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.26에 처음 언급되며 '여라므엘'이라 불림. 왕의 아들. 말기야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 함멜렉의 아들 여라므엘은 여호야김 왕이 예레미야와 바룩을 체포하도록 보낸 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mered, founder of Gedor.
persons.short: Jered was the son of Mered and the  father (ie founder) of Gedor, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jered is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Mered and his wife Jehudijah (or the Judahite woman). Jered is described as the father (ie founder) of Gedor, which may refer to a person or a town associated with his descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.18 only referred to as Jered (יֶ֫רֶד); son of Mered and Jehudijah; a brother of Heber and Jekuthiel; half-brother of: Miriam(?), Shammai(?) and Ishbah(?); founder of Gedor.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '예렛'이라 불림. 메렛과 여후디야의 아들. 헤벨, 여구디엘, 미리암, 삼매와 이스바의 형제. 그돌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 예렛은 므렛의 아들이며 유다 족보에 나오는 그돌의 창설자(아버지)였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife.
persons.short: Jeremai, a descendant of Hashum, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.
persons.article: Jeremai is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the descendants of Hashum who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. When Ezra learned of the widespread intermarriage between the Israelites and the neighboring peoples, he called for repentance and reform. Jeremai was among those who agreed to send away their foreign wives and children, demonstrating their commitment to obey God's law and maintain the purity of the Israelite community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.33 only referred to as Jeremai (יְרֵמַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.33에 처음 언급되며 '여레매'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하숨의 후손 여레매는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그녀를 내보내기로 동의했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Jeremiah was one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.
persons.article: Jeremiah is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was seeking refuge from King Saul. He is described as a brave warrior and is listed alongside other Gadite men who were known for their military prowess and loyalty to David. These warriors helped David during his time of exile and played a significant role in his eventual rise to power as king of Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.10 only referred to as Jeremiah (יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.10에 처음 언급되며 '예레미야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 예레미야는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 갓 지파 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
persons.short: Jeremiah was one of the leaders of the half-tribe of Manasseh during the time of the Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeremiah is briefly mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of the leaders of the half-tribe of Manasseh. He is described as a valiant warrior and is listed alongside other leaders such as Hodaviah and Jahdiel. These leaders are mentioned in the context of the genealogies and the military prowess of the tribes of Israel. However, no specific details are provided about Jeremiah's life or his role in the events of the time.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.24 only referred to as Jeremiah (יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.24에 처음 언급되며 '예레미야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 예레미야는 역대기 시대 므낫세 반 지파 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hilkiah, the prophet during Judah's final days.
persons.short: Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, was a prophet who ministered during the reigns of the last kings of Judah, warning of the Babylonian exile and calling for repentance.
persons.article: Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, was one of the major prophets of the Old Testament. He lived and prophesied during the reigns of the last kings of Judah, including Josiah, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah. Jeremiah's ministry spanned over 40 years, during which he warned the people of Judah about the impending Babylonian exile and called them to repentance and faithfulness to God. Jeremiah faced significant opposition and persecution for his messages, which often contradicted the false hopes and political ambitions of the kings and people of Judah. He was threatened, imprisoned, and even thrown into a cistern. Despite these challenges, Jeremiah remained faithful to his prophetic calling and continued to deliver God's words to the nation. Jeremiah's prophecies also included messages of hope and restoration, foretelling the eventual return of the exiles to their homeland and the establishment of a new covenant between God and His people. His writings, which include the book of Jeremiah and the book of Lamentations, provide a detailed account of the events leading up to the fall of Jerusalem and the Babylonian captivity, as well as his personal struggles and faith in God. Jeremiah's prophecies are referenced in the New Testament, and he is considered a significant figure in both Jewish and Christian traditions. His life and message continue to inspire and challenge readers to remain faithful to God in the face of adversity and to trust in His ultimate plan for redemption and restoration.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.35.25 referred to as Jeremiah (יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ), or Jeremiah or Jeremiah (Ἱερεμίας); a son of Hilkiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 2Ch.35.25에 처음 언급되며 '예레미야'라 불림. 힐기야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 힐기야의 아들 선지자 예레미야는 유다 마지막 왕들의 통치 기간 동안 사역하며 바벨론 포로를 경고하고 회개를 촉구했다.
persons.article_ko: 힐기야의 아들 예레미야는 구약의 주요 선지자 중 한 사람이었다. 그는 요시야, 여호야김, 여호야긴, 시드기야를 포함한 유다의 마지막 왕들 시대에 살며 예언했다. 예레미야의 사역은 사십 년 넘게 이어졌으며, 그 기간 동안 그는 유다 백성에게 임박한 바벨론 포로에 대해 경고하고 회개와 하나님께 대한 신실함을 촉구했다. 예레미야는 유다 왕들과 백성의 거짓된 소망과 정치적 야심과 종종 상반되는 메시지 때문에 상당한 반대와 박해에 직면했다. 그는 위협받고 투옥되었으며 심지어 구덩이에 던져지기도 했다. 이러한 어려움에도 불구하고 예레미야는 자신의 예언적 소명에 신실하게 남아 계속해서 그 민족에게 하나님의 말씀을 전했다. 예레미야의 예언에는 소망과 회복의 메시지도 포함되어 있었는데, 포로들이 결국 고향으로 돌아올 것과 하나님과 그 백성 사이의 새 언약이 세워질 것을 예고했다. 예레미야서와 예레미야애가를 포함한 그의 저작은 예루살렘 함락과 바벨론 포로에 이르는 사건들, 그리고 그의 개인적인 고뇌와 하나님에 대한 믿음을 상세히 기록한다. 예레미야의 예언은 신약에서도 언급되며, 그는 유대교와 그리스도교 전통 모두에서 중요한 인물로 여겨진다. 그의 삶과 메시지는 역경 속에서도 하나님께 신실하게 남고 구속과 회복에 대한 그분의 궁극적인 계획을 신뢰하도록 독자들에게 계속해서 영감을 주고 도전한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father-in-law of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah
persons.short: Jeremiah of Libnah was the father of Hamutal, who was the mother of King Jehoahaz and King Zedekiah of Judah.
persons.article: Jeremiah of Libnah is mentioned in the books of 2 Kings and Jeremiah as the father of Hamutal, who was the wife of King Josiah and the mother of two kings of Judah: Jehoahaz and Zedekiah. Libnah was a city in the Shephelah region of Judah, suggesting that Jeremiah was from this area. Beyond this familial connection, no further information is provided about Jeremiah's life or role in the royal court.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.23.31 only referred to as Jeremiah (יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ); father of Hamutal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.23.31에 처음 언급되며 '예레미야'라 불림. 하무달의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 립나 사람 예레미야는 유다 왕 여호아하스와 시드기야의 어머니인 하무달의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Habazziniah, a Rechabite.
persons.short: Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, was a Rechabite who was tested by the prophet Jeremiah for his obedience to his ancestor's commands.
persons.article: Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, is mentioned in the book of Jeremiah as a member of the Rechabite clan. The Rechabites were a nomadic group known for their strict adherence to the commands of their ancestor, Jonadab son of Rechab. They abstained from drinking wine, building houses, sowing seed, and planting vineyards. The prophet Jeremiah was instructed by God to test the Rechabites' obedience. He brought them into the temple and offered them wine to drink. However, the Rechabites, including Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, refused to drink the wine, stating that they were following the commands of their ancestor Jonadab. The prophet Jeremiah then used the Rechabites' obedience as a contrast to the disobedience of the people of Judah. He praised the Rechabites for their faithfulness and declared that they would always have a descendant to serve God because of their commitment to their ancestor's commands. This event highlights the importance of obedience and faithfulness to God, even in the face of societal pressure to conform.

persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Ch.11.18에 처음 언급되며 '여리못'이라 불림. 다윗과 예루살렘의 아내들의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛과 노가의 형제. 아비하일의 남편. 마할랏의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여리못은 다윗 왕과 그의 형 엘리압의 딸 아비하일 사이에서 태어난 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite overseer during Hezekiah's temple restoration.
persons.short: Jerimoth was a Levite appointed as an overseer during King Hezekiah's restoration of the temple and its services.
persons.article: Jerimoth is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as one of the Levites who served as an overseer during the reign of King Hezekiah. When Hezekiah initiated a restoration of the temple and its services, he appointed Levites to oversee the collection and distribution of the tithes and offerings brought by the people. Jerimoth, along with several other Levites, was entrusted with this responsibility, ensuring that the contributions were properly managed and used for the support of the priests and Levites. This appointment demonstrates the important role of the Levites in the administration of the temple and the trust placed in them by the king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Jerimoth (יְרֵמוֹת, יְרִימוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '여리못'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 여리못은 히스기야 왕이 성전과 그 예배를 회복할 때 감독으로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Caleb; mother of unnamed children.
persons.short: Jerioth was one of the wives of Caleb, and she bore him some unnamed children, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jerioth is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as one of the wives of Caleb, the son of Hezron. The passage states that Caleb had children by his wife Azubah, and after her death, he married Ephrath. It then mentions that Caleb also had children by Jerioth. The wording at 1Chr 2.18 makes it possible this was another name for Azubah who had Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.18 only referred to as Jerioth (יְרִיעוֹת); wife of Caleb; mother of Mesha(?).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '여리옷'이라 불림. 갈렙의 아내. 메사의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여리옷은 갈렙의 아내 중 한 사람으로, 역대상 유다 족보에서 이름 없는 자녀들을 낳았다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
persons.short: Jeroboam I was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the split of the united monarchy following Solomon's reign.
persons.article: Jeroboam I was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the united monarchy split following the reign of King Solomon. He was an Ephraimite and a former official in Solomon's administration. The prophet Ahijah predicted that Jeroboam would rule over ten tribes of Israel, and when Solomon sought to kill him, Jeroboam fled to Egypt. After Solomon's death, Jeroboam returned and led the northern tribes in a revolt against Solomon's son, Rehoboam. He established his capital in Shechem and set up two golden calves in Bethel and Dan to prevent the people from worshipping in Jerusalem. This act of idolatry became known as the "sin of Jeroboam" and was condemned by the prophets. Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, during which he constantly fought against the southern kingdom of Judah. He was succeeded by his son Nadab. The kings of Israel who followed Jeroboam continued in his idolatrous practices, leading to the eventual downfall and exile of the northern kingdom.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.11.26 only referred to as Jeroboam (יָֽרָבְעָם); a son of Nebat and Zeruah; father of Abijah, Nadab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일·분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.11.26에 처음 언급되며 '여로보암'이라 불림. 느밧과 스루아의 아들. 아비야와 나답의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로보암 1세는 솔로몬 통치 이후 분열된 왕국에서 북이스라엘의 첫 왕이었다.
persons.article_ko: 여로보암 1세는 솔로몬 왕 통치 이후 통일 왕국이 분열된 후 북이스라엘 왕국의 첫 왕이었다. 그는 에브라임 사람이며 솔로몬 행정부의 전직 관리였다. 선지자 아히야는 여로보암이 이스라엘 열 지파를 다스릴 것이라고 예언했고, 솔로몬이 그를 죽이려 하자 여로보암은 애굽으로 도망쳤다. 솔로몬이 죽은 후 여로보암은 돌아와서 북부 지파들을 이끌고 솔로몬의 아들 르호보암에 대한 반역을 일으켰다. 그는 세겜에 수도를 세웠고 백성이 예루살렘에서 예배하는 것을 막기 위해 벧엘과 단에 금송아지 두 개를 세웠다. 이 우상숭배 행위는 '여로보암의 죄'로 알려지게 되었고 선지자들에게 정죄받았다. 여로보암은 이십이 년간 다스렸으며, 그 기간 동안 계속해서 남유다 왕국과 싸웠다. 그의 아들 나답이 그를 이었다. 여로보암을 이은 이스라엘 왕들은 그의 우상숭배 관행을 계속 이어가 결국 북이스라엘 왕국의 몰락과 유배로 이어졌다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel, son of Jehoash.
persons.short: Jeroboam II was a king of Israel who reigned for 41 years, restoring some of Israel's former territories.
persons.article: Jeroboam II was a king of Israel who reigned for 41 years, from around 786 to 746 BC. He was the son of Jehoash and the grandson of Jehoahaz. During his reign, Jeroboam II was able to restore some of Israel's former territories, extending the kingdom's boundaries to the "entrance of Hamath," as predicted by the prophet Jonah. Despite his military successes, Jeroboam II continued in the idolatrous practices of his predecessors, maintaining the worship of the golden calves in Bethel and Dan. The prophets Amos and Hosea, who were active during his reign, condemned the social injustice, religious corruption, and moral decay prevalent in Israel at the time. Jeroboam II's reign was marked by prosperity and stability, but this was followed by a period of decline and political turmoil after his death. His son Zechariah succeeded him but was assassinated after only six months on the throne.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.13.13 only referred to as Jeroboam (יָֽרָבְעָם); a son of Joash; father of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '여로보암'이라 불림. 요아스의 아들. 스가랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로보암 2세는 이스라엘 왕으로 사십일 년간 다스리며 이스라엘의 옛 영토 일부를 회복했다.
persons.article_ko: 여로보암 2세는 대략 기원전 786년부터 746년까지 사십일 년간 다스린 이스라엘 왕이었다. 그는 여호아스의 아들이며 여호아하스의 손자였다. 그의 통치 기간 동안 여로보암 2세는 선지자 요나가 예언한 대로 이스라엘의 이전 영토 일부를 회복하여 왕국의 경계를 '하맛 어귀'까지 확장시킬 수 있었다. 군사적 성공에도 불구하고 여로보암 2세는 벧엘과 단에서 금송아지 숭배를 유지하며 그의 전임자들의 우상숭배 관행을 이어갔다. 그의 통치 기간에 활동했던 선지자 아모스와 호세아는 당시 이스라엘에 만연했던 사회적 불의, 종교적 부패, 도덕적 타락을 정죄했다. 여로보암 2세의 통치는 번영과 안정으로 특징지어졌으나, 그의 죽음 이후 쇠퇴와 정치적 혼란의 시기가 뒤따랐다. 그의 아들 스가랴가 그를 이었으나 왕위에 오른 지 여섯 달 만에 암살당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Jeroham was a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of the Benjamite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was seeking refuge from King Saul. He is described as a brave warrior and is listed alongside his fellow Benjamite, Joelah. These warriors helped David during his time of exile and played a significant role in his eventual rise to power as king of Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.7 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); father of Joelah, Zebadiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.7에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 요엘라와 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 베냐민 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Dan.
persons.short: Jeroham was a leader from the tribe of Dan during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a leader from the tribe of Dan during the reign of King David. He is listed among the tribal leaders who were responsible for overseeing their respective tribes and assisting in the administration of the kingdom. The mention of Jeroham in this context highlights the importance of tribal organization and leadership in ancient Israel, as well as the role of these leaders in supporting the king and maintaining order within their tribes.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.22 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); father of Azarel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.22에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 아사렐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 다윗 왕 시대 단 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Shamsherai@1Ch.8.26, Shehariah@1Ch.8.26, Athaliah@1Ch.8.26, Jaareshiah@1Ch.8.27, Elijah@1Ch.8.27, Zichri@1Ch.8.27
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Jeshaiah.
persons.short: Jeroham was a Benjamite, the son of Jeshaiah, mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles as the son of Jeshaiah. He is listed among the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.27 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); father of Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah and Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.27에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 삼스래, 스하랴, 아달랴, 야아레시야, 엘리야와 시그리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 여사야의 아들이며 베냐민 사람으로, 역대상 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest, father of Adaiah.
persons.short: Jeroham was a priest, the father of Adaiah, who served in the temple during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah as a priest, the father of Adaiah. Adaiah was one of the priests who served in the temple during the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. He was a descendant of Malchijah, one of the priestly families. Jeroham's mention in these passages highlights the importance of priestly lineage and the role of the priests in the restoration of the temple and its services.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); a son of Pelaliah; father of Adaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 블라야의 아들. 아다야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 느헤미야 시대에 성전에서 섬긴 제사장 아다야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjamite, father of Ibneiah.
persons.short: Jeroham was a Benjamite, the father of Ibneiah, mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles as the father of Ibneiah. Ibneiah is listed among the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.8 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); father of Ibneiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.8에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 이브느야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 베냐민 사람으로, 역대상 족보에 나오는 이브느야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: An Ephraimite, father of Elkanah and grandfather of Samuel.
persons.short: Jeroham was an Ephraimite, the father of Elkanah and grandfather of the prophet Samuel.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned in 1 Samuel and 1 Chronicles as an Ephraimite, the father of Elkanah and grandfather of the prophet Samuel. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was a descendant of Kohath, one of the sons of Levi. Jeroham's son Elkanah was married to Hannah, who prayed for a child and dedicated her son Samuel to serve in the tabernacle. Jeroham's lineage is significant, as it establishes Samuel's Levitical heritage and his family's connection to the priestly line.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.1.1 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); a son of Elihu; father of Elkanah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Sa.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 엘리후의 아들. 엘가나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 에브라임 사람으로, 엘가나의 아버지이며 선지자 사무엘의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Azariah, who supported Jehoiada's coup.
persons.short: Jeroham was the father of Azariah, one of the commanders who supported Jehoiada in overthrowing Athaliah and installing Joash as king.
persons.article: Jeroham is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as the father of Azariah, one of the commanders who supported the priest Jehoiada in overthrowing Queen Athaliah and installing Joash as the rightful king of Judah. Athaliah had seized power after the death of her son, King Ahaziah, and had ordered the execution of the royal family. However, Joash, the youngest son of Ahaziah, was rescued and hidden by Jehoiada. When Joash was seven years old, Jehoiada gathered support from the commanders, including Azariah son of Jeroham, to overthrow Athaliah and restore the Davidic line to the throne. This event highlights the importance of loyalty to the Davidic dynasty and the role of key individuals in preserving the lineage of David.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.23.1 only referred to as Jeroham (יְרֹחָם); father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.23.1에 처음 언급되며 '여로함'이라 불림. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여로함은 여호야다를 도와 아달랴를 폐하고 요아스를 왕으로 세운 지휘관 중 한 사람인 아사랴의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18(?), Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-
persons.brief: Wives David took in Jerusalem
persons.short: The unnamed wives David took in Jerusalem, who bore him more sons and daughters.
persons.article: 2Sa.5.13 mentions that King David took more wives in Jerusalem after he had conquered the city and made it his capital. These wives, whose names are not recorded in the Bible, bore David additional sons and daughters. The practice of kings having multiple wives was common in ancient Near Eastern societies, often serving to establish political alliances and ensure the continuation of the royal lineage. However, the Bible also records instances where having many wives led to spiritual and moral challenges, as in the case of Solomon. The unnamed wives of David in Jerusalem played a role in expanding his family and solidifying his dynasty, even though their individual stories are not detailed in the biblical narrative.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, implied at 2Sa.5.13 ; only referred to as Jerusalem_wives (.); wife of David; mother of Eliada, Eliphelet, Elpelet, Elishama, Elishua, Ibhar, Japhia, Jerimoth(?), Nepheg, Nogah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 2Sa.5.13에 처음 언급되며 '예루살렘의 아내들'이라 불림. 다윗의 아내. 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 엘리벨렛, 엘리사마, 엘리수아, 입할, 야비아, 여레못, 네벡과 노가의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 다윗이 예루살렘에서 얻은 이름 없는 아내들은 그에게 더 많은 아들딸을 낳아주었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Jotham of Judah.
persons.short: Jerusha was the mother of King Jotham of Judah and the daughter of Zadok.
persons.article: Jerusha is mentioned in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles as the mother of King Jotham of Judah. She was the daughter of Zadok, although no further information is provided about her father. Jerusha's son Jotham became king at the age of 25 and reigned for 16 years in Jerusalem. He is described as a righteous king who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, following the example of his father Uzziah. The mention of Jerusha in the biblical record highlights the importance of maternal lineage in the royal families of Judah and the role of queen mothers in the life of their sons.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.33 referred to as Jerusha or Jerushah (יְרוּשָׁא, יְרוּשָׁה); a daughter of Zadok; wife of Uzziah; mother of Jotham.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.15.33에 처음 언급되며 '여루사'라 불림. 사독의 딸. 웃시야의 아내. 요담의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여루사는 유다 왕 요담의 어머니이며 사독의 딸이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite, son of Jeduthun the musician.
persons.short: Jeshaiah was a Levite, the son of Jeduthun, and a musician appointed by King David to serve in the tabernacle choir.
persons.article: Jeshaiah is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of the sons of Jeduthun, a Levite and one of the chief musicians appointed by King David to serve in the tabernacle choir. Jeduthun, along with Asaph and Heman, was responsible for leading the music and praise in the tabernacle. Jeshaiah, along with his brothers, was a skilled musician and singer, and he was appointed by lot to serve in the choir. The mention of Jeshaiah in this context highlights the importance of music and worship in ancient Israelite culture and the role of the Levites in facilitating these practices.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.3 only referred to as Jeshaiah (יְשַׁעְיָ֫הוּ); son of Jeduthun; a brother of Obed-edom, Mattithiah, Gedaliah, Zeri, Hashabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.3에 처음 언급되며 '여사야'라 불림. 여두둔의 아들. 오벧에돔, 맛디디야, 그달리야, 스리와 하사뱌의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여사야는 여두둔의 아들이며 레위인으로, 다윗 왕이 성막 성가대에서 섬기도록 임명한 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Shecaniah from the line of David.
persons.short: Jeshaiah was a descendant of Shecaniah, from the royal line of David, mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeshaiah is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the descendants of King David in 1 Chronicles. He is listed as one of the sons or descendants of Shecaniah, who was a descendant of David through the line of Solomon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.21 only referred to as Jeshaiah (יְשַׁעְיָה); son of Hananiah; a brother of Pelatiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah and Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.21에 처음 언급되며 '여사야'라 불림. 하나냐의 아들. 블라댜, 르바야, 아르난, 오바댜와 스가냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여사야는 다윗 왕가 스가냐의 후손으로, 역대상 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who accompanied Ezra to Jerusalem.
persons.short: Jeshaiah was a Levite who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jeshaiah is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Levites who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem. Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a group of Israelites back to Jerusalem to restore the temple and reinstitute the Law of Moses. Jeshaiah, along with other Levites, was sent by Ezra to find ministers for the house of God. The Levites played a crucial role in the temple service, and their presence in Ezra's group underscores the importance of restoring proper worship in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.19 only referred to as Jeshaiah (יְשַׁעְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.19에 처음 언급되며 '여사야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 여사야는 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 가는 에스라의 여정에 동행했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Elam who returned with Ezra.
persons.short: Jeshaiah, a descendant of Elam, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Jeshaiah is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the descendants of Elam who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. After the Babylonian exile, Ezra led a group of Israelites back to Jerusalem to restore the temple and reinstitute the Law of Moses. Jeshaiah was among this group, which also included priests, Levites, and other Israelites. The mention of Jeshaiah in this context highlights the importance of the return from exile and the restoration of Jewish worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.7 only referred to as Jeshaiah (יְשַׁעְיָה); a son of Athaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '여사야'라 불림. 아달랴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 엘람의 후손 여사야는 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Jeshaiah, a descendant of Benjamin, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jeshaiah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is listed among the leaders of the people who settled in the city. The resettlement of Jerusalem was a significant event in the history of Israel, as it marked the restoration of Jewish presence in the holy city after decades of exile. The mention of Jeshaiah in this context highlights the importance of the Benjamite tribe in the post-exilic period and their role in the reestablishment of Jewish life in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.7 only referred to as Jeshaiah (יְשַׁעְיָה); father of Ithiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.7에 처음 언급되며 '여사야'라 불림. 이디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여사야는 베냐민의 후손으로, 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of the fourteenth priestly division.
persons.short: Jeshebeab was the head of the fourteenth division of priests during the time of David.
persons.article: Jeshebeab is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as the head of the fourteenth division of priests during the time of King David. David organized the priests into twenty-four divisions, each responsible for serving in the temple for a specific period. Jeshebeab's division was the fourteenth in the order of service. This organization of the priesthood ensured that the temple services were carried out efficiently and that all the priestly families had an opportunity to serve. The mention of Jeshebeab in this context highlights the importance of the priestly duties and the structured nature of temple worship during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.13 only referred to as Jeshebeab (יֶֽשֶׁבְאָב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.13에 처음 언급되며 '예세브압'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여세브압은 다윗 시대에 열네 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Ardon@1Ch.2.18, Mesha@1Ch.2.42, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Sheva@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: A son of Caleb and Azubah.
persons.short: Jesher was one of the sons of Caleb and his wife Azubah, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jesher is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles as one of the sons of Caleb and his wife Azubah. The passage states that Caleb had children by his wife Azubah, and after her death, he married Ephrath. It then lists Jesher, along with his brothers Shobab and Ardon, as the sons of Caleb and Azubah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.18 only referred to as Jesher (יֶ֫שֶׁר); son of Caleb and Azubah(?); a brother of Hur, Shobab, Ardon, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez, Sheber, Tirhanah, Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Shaaph, Sheva and Achsah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '예셀'이라 불림. 갈렙과 아수바의 아들. 훌, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예셀은 갈렙과 그의 아내 아수바 사이에서 태어난 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Gadite leaders.
persons.short: Jeshishai was an ancestor of the Gadite leaders who lived in Bashan, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jeshishai is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad in 1 Chronicles. He is listed as an ancestor of the Gadite leaders who lived in the region of Bashan, known for its fertile land and pastures. The Gadites were one of the Israelite tribes that settled east of the Jordan River. The mention of Jeshishai in this genealogy highlights the importance of family lineage and the connection between the Gadites and their ancestral heritage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.14 only referred to as Jeshishai (יְשִׁישַׁי); a son of Jahdo; father of Michael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '여시새'라 불림. 야도의 아들. 미가엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여시새는 바산에 살던 갓 지파 지도자들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Simeon.
persons.short: Jeshohaiah was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the time of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Jeshohaiah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles. He is listed among the leaders of the Simeonites during the reign of King Hezekiah. The Simeonites were one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and they were known for their warriors and their role in the conquest of Canaan. The mention of Jeshohaiah in this context highlights the importance of tribal leadership and the participation of the Simeonites in the events of Hezekiah's reign.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.36 only referred to as Jeshohaiah (יְשׁוֹחָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.36에 처음 언급되며 '여소하야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여소하야는 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of a priestly family that returned from exile.
persons.short: Jeshua was the head of a priestly family that returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned in Ezra, Nehemiah, and 1 Chronicles as the head of a priestly family that returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. He is listed among the priests who settled in Jerusalem and served in the rebuilt temple. Jeshua's family was responsible for the eleventh division of priestly duties, as organized during the time of King David. The return of Jeshua and other priests was crucial for the restoration of temple worship and the spiritual life of the Jewish community after the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.24.11 referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); a son of Jozadak.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.11에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 요사닥의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 예수아는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.short: Jeshua was a Levite who served during the reign of King Hezekiah and assisted in distributing offerings to his fellow Levites.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned briefly in 2 Chronicles as a Levite who served during the reign of King Hezekiah. He was one of the Levites appointed to distribute the offerings and tithes to his fellow Levites in their cities. This distribution was part of Hezekiah's reforms to restore and strengthen the worship practices in Judah. The mention of Jeshua in this context highlights the important role of the Levites in managing the temple's resources and supporting the religious life of the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.15 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.15에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 예수아는 히스기야 왕 시대에 동료 레위인들에게 헌물을 분배하는 것을 도운 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A prominent Levite leader during the post-exilic period.
persons.short: Jeshua was a prominent Levite leader who played a significant role in the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned in Ezra and Nehemiah as a prominent Levite leader during the post-exilic period. He was among the first group of exiles who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel. Jeshua, along with his fellow Levites, was involved in various aspects of the restoration process, including the rebuilding of the temple, the reading of the Law, and the celebration of religious feasts. He is also listed among the Levites who signed the covenant to follow the Law of God during the time of Nehemiah. Jeshua's leadership and dedication were crucial in reestablishing the spiritual life of the Jewish community after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.40 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); a son of Azaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.40에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 아사냐의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 예수아는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘과 성전 재건에 중요한 역할을 한 저명한 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader of a group that returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Jeshua was the leader of a group of Israelites who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned in Ezra and Nehemiah as the leader of a group of Israelites who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. He is listed among the first group of exiles who returned under the decree of King Cyrus of Persia. Jeshua's group, along with others, helped to resettle Jerusalem and the surrounding towns. The return of these exiles was a significant event in the history of Israel, as it marked the beginning of the restoration of Jewish life in the land after decades of captivity in Babylon.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.6 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); son of Pahath-moab ; a brother of Joab.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 바핫모압의 아들. 요압의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예수아는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 이스라엘 무리의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who received the temple treasures.
persons.short: Jeshua was a priest who received the temple treasures brought back from Babylon during the return from exile.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned briefly in Ezra as one of the priests who received the temple treasures that were brought back from Babylon. These treasures, which included gold and silver vessels, had been taken from the temple by the Babylonians during the conquest of Jerusalem. When the exiles returned, they brought these treasures back to be used in the rebuilt temple. Jeshua, along with other priests, was responsible for ensuring that the treasures were properly accounted for and stored until the temple was ready for use.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.33 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); father of Jozabad.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.33에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 요사밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 예수아는 포로 귀환 시기에 바벨론에서 가져온 성전 보물을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite leader during Nehemiah's time.
persons.short: Jeshua was a Levite leader who served during the time of Nehemiah and participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jeshua is mentioned in Nehemiah as one of the Levite leaders who served during the time of Nehemiah. He is listed among the Levites who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, which had been rebuilt under Nehemiah's leadership. The dedication ceremony was a significant event that marked the completion of the wall and the restoration of Jerusalem's defenses. Jeshua's presence at this event highlights the important role of the Levites in the religious life of the community and their support for the leadership of Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.24 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); a son of Kadmiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.24에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 갓미엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 예수아는 느헤미야 시대에 섬기며 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여한 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Jozadak, who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, was a high priest who helped rebuild a section of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, is mentioned in Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped rebuild a section of Jerusalem's wall. He was a high priest during the post-exilic period and is also mentioned in the book of Ezra. Jeshua worked alongside other leaders and volunteers to repair and fortify the city's defenses, which had been destroyed during the Babylonian conquest. The rebuilding of the wall was a significant event in the restoration of Jerusalem and a symbol of the Jewish people's determination to reclaim their homeland.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.19 only referred to as Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ); father of Ezer.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.19에 처음 언급되며 '예수아'라 불림. 에셀의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요사닥의 아들 예수아는 대제사장으로, 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 재건하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Simeon.
persons.short: Jesimiel was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Jesimiel is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles. He is listed among the leaders of the Simeonites during the reign of King Hezekiah. The Simeonites were one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and they were known for their warriors and their role in the conquest of Canaan. The mention of Jesimiel in this context highlights the importance of tribal leadership and the participation of the Simeonites in the events of Hezekiah's reign.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.36 only referred to as Jesimiel (יְשִׁימִאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.36에 처음 언급되며 '여시미엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여시미엘은 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Father of King David.
persons.short: Jesse was the father of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Jesse was a Bethlehemite from the tribe of Judah and the father of King David. He is first mentioned in the book of Ruth as the son of Obed and the grandson of Boaz and Ruth. Jesse had eight sons, the youngest of whom was David, who was anointed by the prophet Samuel to be king over Israel. Jesse is described as an old man during the time of David's youth, and he sent David to take supplies to his older brothers who were fighting in Saul's army against the Philistines. Later, when David was on the run from Saul, he expressed concern for his parents' safety, and he arranged for them to stay with the king of Moab. Jesse is also mentioned in the genealogies of Jesus Christ in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke, emphasizing the Messianic lineage from Jesse through David. The prophet Isaiah foretold that the Messiah would come from the "stump of Jesse," symbolizing the humble origins of the Davidic dynasty.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.4.17 referred to as Jesse (יִשַׁי), or Jesse (Ἰεσσαί); a son of Obed; father of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Shimeah, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아버지. Rut.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '이새'라 불림. 오벳의 아들. 나하스의 남편. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 삼마, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 엘리후, 스루야와 아비가일의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이새는 다윗 왕의 아버지이며 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.
persons.article_ko: 이새는 유다 지파 출신 베들레헴 사람이며 다윗 왕의 아버지였다. 그는 룻기에서 오벳의 아들이며 보아스와 룻의 손자로 처음 언급된다. 이새에게는 여덟 아들이 있었는데, 그중 막내가 선지자 사무엘에게 이스라엘 왕으로 기름부음을 받은 다윗이었다. 이새는 다윗의 젊은 시절 노인으로 묘사되며, 사울의 군대에서 블레셋을 대적하여 싸우던 형들에게 물자를 가져다주도록 다윗을 보냈다. 후에 다윗이 사울을 피해 도망 다닐 때 그는 부모의 안전을 염려하여 그들이 모압 왕과 함께 지내도록 주선했다. 이새는 또한 마태복음과 누가복음의 예수 그리스도 족보에 언급되어, 이새로부터 다윗을 거친 메시아적 혈통을 강조한다. 선지자 이사야는 메시아가 '이새의 줄기'에서 나올 것이라고 예언했는데, 이는 다윗 왕조의 겸손한 기원을 상징한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: The Son of God and Savior of the world.
persons.short: Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity, is the Son of God who became incarnate, died for the sins of humanity, and rose from the dead, providing salvation for all who believe in Him.
persons.article: Jesus Christ is the central figure of the New Testament and the foundation of the Christian faith. He is the eternal Son of God who became incarnate, being born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem. Jesus lived a sinless life and performed many miracles, demonstrating His divine power and authority. He taught with wisdom and authority, proclaiming the Kingdom of God and calling people to repentance and faith. Jesus faced opposition from religious leaders and was ultimately crucified under Pontius Pilate. However, on the third day, He rose from the dead, appearing to His disciples and commissioning them to spread the gospel message. Jesus ascended into heaven and is now seated at the right hand of God the Father, interceding for believers. He is the Savior of the world, offering forgiveness of sins and eternal life to all who put their faith in Him. The New Testament also teaches that Jesus will return in glory to judge the living and the dead and to establish His eternal Kingdom. He is the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies concerning the Messiah and is the perfect revelation of God's love and grace to humanity.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.1.1 referred to as Jesus (Ἰησοῦς), or Christ (Χριστός), or Christian (Χριστιανός), or Immanuel (עִמָּנוּאֵל), or Immanuel (Ἐμμανουήλ); son of Joseph and Mary; a brother of James, Joses, Simon and Jude.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Isa.7.14에 처음 언급되며 '예수'라 불림. 요셉과 마리아의 아들. 야고보, 요세, 시몬과 유다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예수 그리스도는 그리스도교의 중심 인물로, 육신을 입으신 하나님의 아들이며 인류의 죄를 위해 죽으시고 부활하셔서 믿는 모든 자에게 구원을 주셨다.
persons.article_ko: 예수 그리스도는 신약의 중심 인물이며 그리스도교 신앙의 기초이다. 그분은 영원하신 하나님의 아들로 육신이 되셔서 베들레헴에서 동정녀 마리아에게서 태어나셨다. 예수님은 죄 없는 삶을 사셨고 많은 기적을 행하시어 그분의 신적 권능과 권위를 나타내셨다. 그분은 지혜와 권위로 가르치시며 하나님 나라를 선포하시고 사람들에게 회개와 믿음을 촉구하셨다. 예수님은 종교 지도자들의 반대에 직면하셨고 결국 본디오 빌라도 아래에서 십자가에 처형되셨다. 그러나 사흘째 되는 날 그분은 죽음에서 부활하셔서 제자들에게 나타나시고 복음 메시지를 전파하도록 그들에게 사명을 맡기셨다. 예수님은 하늘로 승천하셔서 지금은 하나님 아버지 우편에 앉으셔서 믿는 자들을 위해 중보하고 계신다. 그분은 세상의 구주로, 그분을 믿는 모든 이에게 죄 사함과 영생을 제공하신다. 신약은 또한 예수님이 산 자와 죽은 자를 심판하시고 그분의 영원한 나라를 세우시기 위해 영광 중에 다시 오실 것이라고 가르친다. 그분은 메시아에 관한 구약 예언의 성취이시며 인류를 향한 하나님의 사랑과 은혜의 완전한 계시이시다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A son of Jada from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Jether was a son of Jada, a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles.
persons.article: Jether is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles. He is listed as one of the sons of Jada within the tribe of Judah. The genealogies in Chronicles serve to establish the lineage and heritage of important figures in Israel's history and to demonstrate God's faithfulness to His promises through the generations.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.32 only referred to as Jether (יֶ֫תֶר); son of Jada; a brother of Jonathan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.32에 처음 언급되며 '예델'이라 불림. 야다의 아들. 요나단의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예델은 야다의 아들이며 유다의 후손으로, 역대상 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ezrah; brother of Mered, Epher and Jalon
persons.short: Jether, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Jether is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.4.17. He is listed as the brother of Mered, Epher and Jalon, though the genealogy is complex.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.17 only referred to as Jether (יֶ֫תֶר); son of Ezrah; a brother of Mered, Epher and Jalon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '예델'이라 불림. 에스라의 아들. 메렛, 에벨과 얄론의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예델은 유다의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: An Ishmaelite, father of Amasa.
persons.short: Jether, also known as Ithra, was an Ishmaelite and the father of Amasa, who was Absalom's commander and later killed by Joab.
persons.article: Jether, also known as Ithra, was an Ishmaelite and the father of Amasa. Amasa was the son of Jether and Abigail, who was David's sister. Despite being David's nephew, Amasa sided with Absalom during his rebellion against David and was appointed as the commander of Absalom's army. After Absalom's death, David offered Amasa the position of commander over his army, replacing Joab. However, when Amasa failed to mobilize the troops quickly enough, David sent Abishai to pursue the rebel Sheba. Joab, who had been demoted, accompanied Abishai and took the opportunity to kill Amasa, viewing him as a threat to his position. The fact that Jether is described as an Ishmaelite suggests that he was not an Israelite, which may have contributed to Amasa's complex loyalties within David's family and kingdom.
persons.summary: A man of the Ishmaelites living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.17.25 referred to as Jether (יֶ֫תֶר), or Ithra (יִתְרָא); husband of Abigail; father of Amasa.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 이스마엘 사람. 2Sa.17.25에 처음 언급되며 '예델'이라 불림. 아비가일의 남편. 아마사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 예델(이드라라고도 함)은 이스마엘 사람으로, 압살롬의 지휘관이었다가 후에 요압에게 죽임을 당한 아마사의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Gideon's firstborn son who refused to kill captives.
persons.short: Jether was Gideon's firstborn son who was commanded to kill Zebah and Zalmunna but was too young and fearful to do so.
persons.article: Jether was the firstborn son of Gideon, the judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from Midianite oppression. After Gideon defeated the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna, he commanded Jether to kill them. However, Jether was still a youth and was afraid to carry out the execution. As a result, Gideon himself killed the Midianite kings. This incident highlights Jether's youth and inexperience, as well as Gideon's role as a strong leader and warrior.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at Jdg.8.20 only referred to as Jether (יֶ֫תֶר); son of Gideon; a brother of Abimelech and Jotham.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.8.20에 처음 언급되며 '여델'이라 불림. 기드온의 아들. 아비멜렉과 요담의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예델은 기드온의 맏아들로, 세바와 살문나를 죽이라는 명령을 받았으나 너무 어리고 두려워 하지 못했다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A chief of Edom
persons.short: Jetheth, one of the chiefs of Edom.
persons.article: Jetheth is mentioned in the lists of the chiefs of Edom in Gen.36.40 and 1Ch.1.51. He is identified as one of the chiefs who came from the Edomite clans.
