persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.40 only referred to as Jetheth (יְתֵת).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.40에 처음 언급되며 '여뎃'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 예데는 에돔 족장 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Midianite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian
persons.short: Jethro, also known as Reuel, was Moses' father-in-law and a priest of Midian.
persons.article: Jethro, also referred to as Reuel, was Moses' father-in-law and a priest of Midian. He is first mentioned in Exo.2.18, where his daughters tell him about Moses defending them at a well. Later, in Exo.3.1, Moses is described as tending Jethro's flock when he encounters the burning bush. After the Exodus, Jethro visits Moses in the wilderness, bringing along Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons (Exo.18.1-6). Jethro praises God for the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt (Exo.18.9-10 and offers sacrifices to God )(Exo.18.12). Observing Moses' heavy workload in judging the people, Jethro advises him to appoint capable men to share the burden (Exo.18.13-23). Moses follows this advice and bids farewell to Jethro, who returns to his own land (Exo.18.24-27). In Num.10.29, Moses invites Hobab, identified as Reuel's son, to join the Israelites on their journey, suggesting a continued relationship between Moses and Jethro's family.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.2.18 referred to as Jethro (יִתְרוֹ), or Jethro (יֶ֫תֶר), or Jothor (LXX) (Ιωθώρ), or Reuel or Reuel (רְעוּאֵל); father of Zipporah and Hobab.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 미디안 사람. Exo.2.18에 처음 언급되며 '이드로'라 불림. 십보라와 호밥의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이드로(르우엘이라고도 함)는 모세의 장인이며 미디안의 제사장이었다.
persons.article_ko: 이드로(르우엘이라고도 함)는 모세의 장인이며 미디안의 제사장이었다. 그는 출애굽기 2:18에 처음 언급되는데, 그곳에서 그의 딸들은 모세가 우물에서 자신들을 지켜준 일을 그에게 이야기한다. 후에 출애굽기 3:1에서 모세는 불타는 떨기나무를 만날 때 이드로의 양떼를 치고 있는 것으로 묘사된다. 출애굽 이후 이드로는 모세의 아내 십보라와 그들의 두 아들을 데리고 광야에서 모세를 방문한다(출 18:1-6). 이드로는 이스라엘 백성이 애굽에서 구원받은 것에 대해 하나님을 찬양하고(출 18:9-10) 하나님께 제사를 드린다(출 18:12). 모세가 백성을 재판하는 무거운 업무를 관찰한 이드로는 그에게 능력 있는 사람들을 임명하여 그 부담을 나누라고 조언한다(출 18:13-23). 모세는 이 조언을 따르고 이드로에게 작별을 고하며, 이드로는 자기 땅으로 돌아간다(출 18:24-27). 민수기 10:29에서 모세는 르우엘의 아들로 확인되는 호밥을 이스라엘 백성의 여정에 합류하도록 초청하는데, 이는 모세와 이드로 가족 사이의 계속되는 관계를 시사한다.

persons.description: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mibsam@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Massa@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Mahalath@Gen.28.9-
persons.brief: Son of Ishmael
persons.short: Jetur, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael.
persons.article: Jetur is mentioned in the genealogies of Ishmael in Gen.25.15 and 1Ch.1.31. He is listed as one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar. The Ishmaelites, including Jetur and his brothers, are described as living in the region from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt (Gen.25.18).
persons.summary: A man of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.15 only referred to as Jetur (יְטוּר); son of Ishmael; a brother of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Naphish, Kedemah and Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 아라비아 사람. Gen.25.15에 처음 언급되며 '여둘'이라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 밉삼, 미스마, 두마, 맛사, 하닷, 데마, 나비스, 게드마와 마할랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여둘은 이스마엘의 열두 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Zerah
persons.short: Jeuel, a descendant of Zerah, settled in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jeuel is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.9.6 as one of the descendants of Zerah who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is listed among the members of the tribe of Judah who returned to Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.6 only referred to as Jeuel (יְעוּאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.6에 처음 언급되며 '여우엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여우엘은 세라의 후손으로 예루살렘에 정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who helped cleanse the temple
persons.short: Jeuel, a Levite who assisted in cleansing the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Jeuel is mentioned in 2Ch.29.13 as one of the Levites who participated in the cleansing and rededication of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He is listed among the Levites from the Elizaphan clan who were involved in this important task. The purification of the temple was a significant event in Hezekiah's religious reforms, which aimed to restore proper worship practices in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.13 only referred to as Jeuel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.13에 처음 언급되며 '여우엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여우엘은 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일을 도운 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Adonikam who returned from exile
persons.short: Jeuel, a descendant of Adonikam, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Jeuel is briefly mentioned in Ezr.8.13 as one of the descendants of Adonikam who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile. He is listed among the men who accompanied Ezra on his journey to Jerusalem, which took place during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.13 only referred to as Jeuel (יְעִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.13에 처음 언급되며 '여우엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여우엘은 아도니감의 후손으로, 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A Levite, son of Shimei or Shubael
persons.short: Jeush, a Levite, was a son of Shimei (or Shubael) during David's reign.
persons.article: Jeush is mentioned in 1Ch.23.10-11 as one of the sons of Shimei (or Shubael), a Levite who served during the reign of King David. In the organization of the Levites for temple service, Jeush and his brothers were appointed to various duties. The text notes that Jeush and his brother Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family in the Levitical divisions.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.10 only referred to as Jeush (יְעוּשׁ); son of Shimei; a brother of Jahath, Zizah and Beriah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.10에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 야핫, 시사와 브리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 다윗 왕 시대에 시므이(수바엘이라고도 함)의 아들인 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Benjamin@1Ch.7.10, Ehud@1Ch.7.10, Chenaanah@1Ch.7.10, Zethan@1Ch.7.10, Tarshish@1Ch.7.10, Ahishahar@1Ch.7.10
persons.brief: A descendant of Bilhan from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Jeush, a Benjamite, was a descendant of Bilhan.
persons.article: Jeush is mentioned in 1Ch.7.10 as one of the sons of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which is given in the context of the census taken during the reign of King David.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.10 only referred to as Jeush (יְעוּשׁ); son of Bilhan; a brother of Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.10에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 빌한의 아들. 베냐민, 에훗, 그나아나, 세단, 달시스와 아히사할의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 베냐민 사람으로 빌한의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Eleasah from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Jeush, a Benjamite, was a son of Eleasah (or 'Eshek').
persons.article: Jeush is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.8.39 as one of the sons of Eleasah (or 'Eshek'), a descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of Saul's family, which is given in the context of the Benjamite clans that settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.39 only referred to as Jeush (יְעוּשׁ); son of Eleasah; a brother of Ulam and Eliphelet.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.39에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 엘르아사의 아들. 울람과 엘리벨렛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 베냐민 사람으로 엘르아사(에섹이라고도 함)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Abijah@1Ki.14.31-Mat, Shemariah@2Ch.11.19, Zaham@2Ch.11.19, Attai@2Ch.11.20, Ziza@2Ch.11.20, Shelomith@2Ch.11.20
persons.brief: Son of King Rehoboam and Mahalath
persons.short: Jeush was a son of King Rehoboam and his wife Mahalath.
persons.article: Jeush is mentioned in 2Ch.11.19 as one of the sons born to King Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, and his wife Mahalath. Mahalath was the daughter of David's son Jerimoth and Abihail, the daughter of Eliab, who was David's brother.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.11.19 only referred to as Jeush (יְעוּשׁ); son of Rehoboam and Mahalath; a brother of Shemariah, Zaham; half-brother of: Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 르호보암과 마할랏의 아들. 아비야, 스마랴, 사함, 앗대, 시사와 슬로밋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 르호보암 왕과 그의 아내 마할랏의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
persons.short: Jeush, a son of Esau and Oholibamah, was a chief of Edom.
persons.article: Jeush was one of the sons of Esau, the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob'), and Esau's wife Oholibamah, as recorded in Gen.36.5,14 and 1Ch.1.35. He is listed among the chiefs of Edom who descended from Esau. As a grandson of Isaac and great-grandson of Abraham, Jeush was part of the Edomite clan that settled in the region of Seir.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.5 referred to as Jeush (יְעוּשׁ), or Jeush (יְעִישׁ); son of Esau and Oholibamah; a brother of Jalam and Korah; half-brother of: Eliphaz and Reuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.5에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들. 엘리바스, 르우엘, 얄람과 고라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들이며 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jobab@1Ch.8.9, Zibia@1Ch.8.9, Mesha@1Ch.8.9, Malcam@1Ch.8.9, Sachia@1Ch.8.10, Mirmah@1Ch.8.10, Abitub@1Ch.8.11, Elpaal@1Ch.8.11-
persons.brief: A descendant of Shaharaim from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Jeuz was a Benjamite, born to Shaharaim in the country of Moab.
persons.article: Jeuz is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.8.10 as one of the sons of Shaharaim, a Benjamite. The text states that Shaharaim had children in the country of Moab after he had divorced his wives Hushim and Baara. Jeuz is listed among the children born to Shaharaim in Moab.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.10 only referred to as Jeuz (יְעוּץ); son of Shaharaim and Hodesh; a brother of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Sachia, Mirmah, Abitub and Elpaal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.10에 처음 언급되며 '여우스'라 불림. 사하라임과 호데스의 아들. 요밥, 시비야, 메사, 말감, 사갸, 미르마, 아비둡과 엘바알의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여우스는 베냐민 사람으로 모압 땅에서 사하라임에게서 태어났다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader of the Judean forces
persons.short: Jezaniah, also known as Azariah, was a leader of the Judean forces after the fall of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Jezaniah, also referred to as Azariah, was one of the leaders of the Judean forces who survived the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem. In Jer.40.8, he is mentioned among the commanders who came to Gedaliah, the appointed governor of Judah, at Mizpah. Later, in Jer.42.1, Jezaniah and the other leaders approached Jeremiah to seek guidance from the Lord regarding their plan to flee to Egypt. However, when Jeremiah delivered God's message, warning them not to go to Egypt, Jezaniah (called Azariah in this passage) and another leader, Johanan, accused Jeremiah of falsely prophesying and led the people to Egypt despite the divine warning (Jer.43.2).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.23 referred to as Jezaniah (יְזַנְיָה), or Jezaniah or Jaazaniah (יַאֲזַנְיָ֫הוּ), or Azariah (עֲזַרְיָה); a son of Hoshaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.25.23에 처음 언급되며 '여사냐'라 불림. 호사야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여사냐(아사랴라고도 함)는 예루살렘 함락 이후 유다 군대의 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Queen living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Queen of Israel; wife of King Ahab
persons.short: Queen Jezebel, the Phoenician wife of King Ahab, promoted Baal worship and persecuted the prophets of God.
persons.article: Jezebel was the Phoenician princess who became the wife of King Ahab of Israel (1Ki.16.31). She zealously promoted the worship of the Canaanite god Baal and persecuted the prophets of the Lord (1Ki.18.4,13,19). Her conflict with the prophet Elijah is notably recorded in 1Kings 18-19, where Elijah confronts the prophets of Baal and Jezebel threatens Elijah's life. Jezebel's wickedness is further demonstrated in her plot to have Naboth killed so that Ahab could seize his vineyard (1Ki.21). Her actions led to divine judgment, as pronounced by Elijah (1Ki.21.23). Years later, during the reign of Ahab's son Joram, Jezebel met her demise as prophesied. Jehu, anointed as king of Israel, had her thrown from a window, and her body was consumed by dogs, fulfilling Elijah's prophecy (2Ki.9.30-37). In Rev.2.20, the name "Jezebel" is used symbolically to describe a false prophetess who led people astray in the church of Thyatira, drawing a parallel to the idolatry and immorality promoted by Ahab's queen.
persons.summary: A queen of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.31 referred to as Jezebel (אִיזֶבֶל), or Jezebel (Ἰεζαβήλ); a daughter of Ethbaal; wife of Ahab; mother of Athaliah, Joash, Ahaziah and Joram.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕비. 1Ki.16.31에 처음 언급되며 '이세벨'이라 불림. 엣바일의 딸. 아합의 아내. 아달랴, 요아스, 아하시야와 요람의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 이세벨 여왕은 아합 왕의 페니키아인 아내로, 바알 숭배를 조장하고 하나님의 선지자들을 박해했다.
persons.article_ko: 이세벨은 이스라엘 왕 아합의 아내가 된 페니키아 공주였다(왕상 16:31). 그녀는 가나안 신 바알 숭배를 열심히 조장하고 여호와의 선지자들을 박해했다(왕상 18:4, 13, 19). 그녀와 선지자 엘리야의 갈등은 열왕기상 18-19장에 특히 기록되어 있는데, 그곳에서 엘리야는 바알 선지자들과 대결하고 이세벨은 엘리야의 생명을 위협한다. 이세벨의 악함은 아합이 나봇의 포도원을 빼앗을 수 있도록 그를 죽이려는 그녀의 음모에서 더욱 드러난다(왕상 21장). 그녀의 행동은 엘리야가 선포한 대로 신적 심판으로 이어졌다(왕상 21:23). 여러 해 후 아합의 아들 요람 통치 기간에 이세벨은 예언된 대로 최후를 맞았다. 이스라엘 왕으로 기름부음받은 예후는 그녀를 창문에서 던지게 했고, 그녀의 시신은 개들에게 먹혀 엘리야의 예언을 성취했다(왕하 9:30-37). 요한계시록 2:20에서 '이세벨'이라는 이름은 두아디라 교회에서 사람들을 잘못된 길로 이끈 거짓 여선지자를 상징적으로 묘사하는 데 사용되어, 아합의 왕비가 조장한 우상숭배와 부도덕함에 비유된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Naphtali, founder of the Jezerite clan
persons.short: Jezer, a son of Naphtali, was the ancestor of the Jezerite clan.
persons.article: Jezer was one of the sons of Naphtali, as listed in the genealogies of Gen.46.24, Num.26.49, and 1Ch.7.13. He was born during the period when Israel (or 'Jacob') and his family lived in Canaan, before their migration to Egypt. Jezer became the founder of the Jezerite clan within the tribe of Naphtali. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, the Jezerite clan is mentioned as one of the clans descended from Naphtali (Num.26.49).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Naphtali living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.24 referred to as Jezer (יֵ֫צֶר), or Jezerite (יִצְרִי); son of Naphtali; a brother of Jahzeel, Guni and Shillem.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.24에 처음 언급되며 '예셀'이라 불림. 납달리의 아들. 야스엘, 구니와 실렘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 예셀은 납달리의 아들이며 예셀 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Jeziel, a Benjamite, was one of the warriors who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Jeziel is mentioned in 1Ch.12.3 as one of the Benjamite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. Along with his fellow Benjamites, Jeziel is described as a brave warrior and an archer who could shoot arrows and sling stones with either his right or left hand. These skilled warriors provided valuable support to David during his time of exile and later when he became king over Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Jeziel (יְזִיאֵל); son of Azmaveth; a brother of Pelet.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '여시엘'이라 불림. 아스마의 아들. 벨렛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여시엘은 베냐민 사람으로, 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader of the singers at the wall dedication
persons.short: Jezrahiah was one of the leaders of the singers during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Jezrahiah is briefly mentioned in Neh.12.42 as one of the leaders of the singers during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. After the completion of the wall's reconstruction under Nehemiah's leadership, a great celebration was held to dedicate the wall. Jezrahiah, along with other leaders, is named as directing the singers and musicians who provided joyful praise during the dedication ceremony.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Jezrahiah (יִזְרַחְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.42에 처음 언급되며 '예스라히야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 이스라히야는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식 때 노래하는 자들의 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch, Shobal@1Ch.2.50-, Salma@1Ch.2.51-, Hareph@1Ch.2.51, Ishma@1Ch.4.3, Idbash@1Ch.4.3, Hazzelelponi@1Ch.4.3, Penuel@1Ch.4.4, Ezer@1Ch.4.4
persons.brief: A son of Hur in the genealogy of Judah
persons.short: Jezreel was a son of Hur, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Jezreel is mentioned in 1Ch.4.3 as one of the sons of Hur in the genealogy of Judah, though the text is difficult to interpret. He is listed along with his brothers Ishma and Idbash, as well as their sister Hazzelelponi.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.3 only referred to as Jezreel (יִזְרְעֶאל); son of Hur; a brother of Uri, Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Ishma, Idbash, Hazzelelponi, Penuel and Ezer.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.3에 처음 언급되며 '이스르엘'이라 불림. 훌의 아들. 우리, 소발, 살마, 하렙, 이스마, 잇바스, 하술렐보니, 브누엘과 에셀의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 이스르엘은 훌의 아들로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A symbolic name given to Hosea's son
persons.short: Jezreel was the name given to Hosea's son as a sign of God's judgment on the house of Jehu.
persons.article: In Hos.1.4, God instructs the prophet Hosea to name his son Jezreel as a symbolic act representing divine judgment. The name Jezreel is associated with the valley of Jezreel, where Jehu, a former king of Israel, had carried out a massacre (2Ki.9-10). God declares that he will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel and bring an end to the kingdom of Israel. The child's name serves as a prophetic sign of the coming judgment and the end of Jehu's dynasty.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Hos.1.4 only referred to as Jezreel (יִזְרְעֶאל); son of Hosea and Gomer; a brother of Lo-ruhamah , Lo-ammi H3818).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Hos.1.4에 처음 언급되며 '이스르엘'이라 불림. 호세아와 고멜의 아들. 로루하마와 로암미의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 이스르엘은 여호와께서 예후의 집을 심판하실 표징으로 호세아의 아들에게 지어준 이름이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor and Milcah
persons.short: Jidlaph, a son of Nahor and Milcah, was Abraham's nephew.
persons.article: Jidlaph is mentioned in Gen.22.22 as one of the eight sons of Nahor and Milcah. Nahor was Abraham's brother, making Jidlaph Abraham's nephew. The passage lists the children born to Nahor and Milcah in Paddan Aram, providing insight into Abraham's extended family.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.22 only referred to as Jidlaph (יִדְלָ֑ף); son of Nahor and Milcah; a brother of Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash and Bethuel; half-brother of: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.22에 처음 언급되며 '이들랍'이라 불림. 나홀과 밀가의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 브두엘, 데바, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 이들랍은 나홀과 밀가의 아들이며 아브라함의 조카였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Seraiah, founder of Ge-harashim
persons.short: Joab, the son of Seraiah, was the  father (ie founder) of Ge-harashim.
persons.article: Joab, mentioned in 1Ch.4.14, was the son of Seraiah from the tribe of Judah. He is described as the father (ie founder) of Ge-harashim, which likely refers to a place or a group of craftsmen.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.14 only referred to as Joab (יוֹאָב); a son of Seraiah; founder of Ge-harashim.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.14에 처음 언급되며 '요압'이라 불림. 스라야의 아들. Ge-harashim의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스라야의 아들 요압은 게하라심의 창설자(아버지)였다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army
persons.short: Joab, David's nephew and commander of his army, was a key figure in David's reign, known for his military prowess and loyalty.
persons.article: Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was King David's nephew and the commander of his army. He first appears in 1Sa.26.6, accompanying David on a mission to Saul's camp. Joab played a significant role in David's rise to power and the establishment of his kingdom (2Sa.2-3; 8.16; 1Ch.11.6,8). As a military commander, Joab led David's forces in various battles against the Ammonites, Syrians, and other enemies (2Sa.10; 12.26-27; 1Ch.19). He also helped quell Absalom's rebellion and was instrumental in defeating Sheba's revolt (2Sa.18; 20). However, Joab's loyalty to David was sometimes overshadowed by his own ambition and ruthlessness. He killed Abner, Saul's former commander, in revenge for his brother Asahel's death (2Sa.3). He also disobeyed David's orders by killing Absalom (2Sa.18) and supported Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne (1Ki.1.7,19). Despite his flaws, Joab remained a key figure in David's reign until the end. He was involved in the census that brought God's judgment upon Israel (2Sa.24; 1Ch.21) and was eventually killed by Benaiah on Solomon's orders for his support of Adonijah (1Ki.2.28-35).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.26.6 only referred to as Joab (יוֹאָב); his mother was Zeruiah; a brother of Abishai and Asahel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 동료. 1Sa.26.6에 처음 언급되며 '요압'이라 불림. 스루야의 남편(이름 미상)와 스루야의 아들. 아비새와 아사헬의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다윗의 조카이며 그의 군대 지휘관인 요압은 다윗의 통치에서 중요한 인물로, 군사적 기량과 충성으로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 스루야의 아들 요압은 다윗 왕의 조카이며 그의 군대 지휘관이었다. 그는 삼상 26:6에서 다윗을 따라 사울의 진영으로 가는 임무에 동행한 것으로 처음 등장한다. 요압은 다윗의 권력 상승과 왕국 확립에 중요한 역할을 했다(삼하 2-3장; 8:16; 대상 11:6, 8). 군 지휘관으로서 요압은 암몬, 시리아 및 다른 원수들을 대적하는 다양한 전투에서 다윗의 군대를 이끌었다(삼하 10장; 12:26-27; 대상 19장). 그는 또한 압살롬의 반역을 진압하는 것을 돕고 세바의 반역을 무찌르는 데 중요한 역할을 했다(삼하 18장; 20장). 그러나 요압의 다윗에 대한 충성은 때때로 자신의 야심과 무자비함으로 가려졌다. 그는 형제 아사헬의 죽음에 대한 복수로 사울의 전 지휘관 아브넬을 죽였다(삼하 3장). 그는 또한 다윗의 명령을 어기고 압살롬을 죽였고(삼하 18장) 아도니야가 왕위를 찬탈하려는 시도를 지지했다(왕상 1:7, 19). 결점에도 불구하고 요압은 다윗의 통치 끝까지 핵심 인물로 남았다. 그는 이스라엘에 하나님의 심판을 초래한 인구조사에 관여했고(삼하 24장; 대상 21장) 결국 아도니야를 지지한 것 때문에 솔로몬의 명령으로 브나야에게 죽임을 당했다(왕상 2:28-35).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family that returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Joab was the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Joab is mentioned in Ezr.2.6 and Neh.7.11 as the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile. The descendants of Joab are listed among the returnees who settled in Jerusalem and the surrounding towns. The count of Joab's descendants varies slightly between the two passages, with Ezra recording 2,812 and Nehemiah listing 2,818.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.6 only referred to as Joab (יוֹאָב); son of Pahath-moab; a brother of Jeshua.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '요압'이라 불림. 바핫모압의 아들. 예수아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요압은 바벨론 포로에서 유다로 돌아온 한 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A descendant of Pahath-Moab who returned with Ezra
persons.short: Joab, a descendant of Pahath-Moab, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: In Ezr.8.9, Joab is mentioned as one of the descendants of Pahath-Moab who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. He is listed among the men who joined Ezra's expedition from Babylon to Jerusalem during the reign of King Artaxerxes. The passage records that 218 men from the family of Joab of Pahath-Moab were part of this group.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.9 only referred to as Joab (יוֹאָב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '요압'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압의 후손 요압은 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 사람 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Shemaiah@1Ch.26.4-, Jehozabad@1Ch.26.4, Sachar@1Ch.26.4, Nethanel@1Ch.26.4, Ammiel@1Ch.26.5, Issachar@1Ch.26.5, Peullethai@1Ch.26.5
persons.brief: A son of Obed-edom, a gatekeeper of the temple
persons.short: Joah, a son of Obed-edom, was one of the gatekeepers assigned to guard the temple.
persons.article: Joah is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.26.4 as one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite who served as a gatekeeper for the tabernacle during King David's reign. Obed-edom and his family were entrusted with the responsibility of guarding the temple gates. Joah is listed among Obed-edom's eight sons, who are described as capable men with the strength to do the work.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.4 only referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח); son of Obed-edom; a brother of Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar and Peullethai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.4에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 오벧에돔의 아들. 스마야, 여호사밧, 사갈, 느다넬, 암미엘, 잇사갈과 브울래대의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요아는 오벧에돔의 아들로 성전을 지키는 문지기 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gershonite Levite, son of Zimmah
persons.short: Joah (or Ethan), a Gershonite Levite, was the son of Zimmah in the genealogy of Levi.
persons.article: Joah (or Ethan) is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites, specifically the Gershonite clan, in 1Ch.6.21 and 1Ch.6.42. He is identified as the son of Zimmah and is listed among the ancestors of Asaph, a prominent Levitical musician in King David's time. The name Joah is used in verse 21, while Ethan is used in verse 42, suggesting that these two names refer to the same individual.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.21 referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח), or Ethan (אֵיתָן); a son of Zimmah; father of Iddo.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.21에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 심마의 아들. 잇도의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아(에단이라고도 함)는 레위 족보에서 짐마의 아들인 게르손 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who helped cleanse the temple under Hezekiah
persons.short: Joah, a Levite of the Gershonites, assisted in the purification of the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Joah, son of Zimmah, a Levite belonging to the Gershonite clan, is mentioned in 2Ch.29.12 as one of the Levites who participated in the cleansing and consecration of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. When Hezekiah ascended to the throne, he initiated a reformation to restore proper worship in Judah. As part of this process, he called upon the Levites to purify the temple, which had fallen into disrepair and defilement during the reign of the previous kings. Joah, along with other Levites from various clans, responded to this call and took part in the cleansing and sanctification of the temple, ensuring that it was ready for the proper worship of God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12a only referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח); a son of Zimmah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12a에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 심마의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 게르손 계열 레위인 요아는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who helped purify the temple
persons.short: Joah son of Joahaz was a Kohathite Levite who helped purify the temple under King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Joah son of Joahaz was a Levite of the Kohath clan who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He took part in the purification and rededication of the temple as ordered by Hezekiah, working with other Levites to complete the cleansing rites (2Ch.29.12). No other information is provided in the biblical text about Joah's responsibilities or experiences.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12b only referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח); father of Eden.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12b에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 에덴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아하스의 아들 요아는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일을 도운 고핫 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Joahaz, King Josiah's secretary
persons.short: Joah, the son of Joahaz, served as King Josiah's secretary during the temple repairs.
persons.article: Joah, the son of Joahaz, held the position of King Josiah's secretary during the king's reign in Judah. He is mentioned in 2Ch.34.8, which describes the events surrounding the repair and restoration of the temple. Joah, along with Shaphan the scribe and Maaseiah the governor of the city, was entrusted by Josiah to oversee the distribution of funds to the workers involved in the temple repairs. This event took place in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, as part of the king's efforts to restore proper worship in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.8 only referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח); a son of Joahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.8에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 요아하스의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 요아하스의 아들 요아는 성전 수리 기간 동안 요시야 왕의 서기관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Asaph, King Hezekiah's secretary
persons.short: Joah, the son of Asaph, served as King Hezekiah's secretary during the Assyrian invasion.
persons.article: Joah, the son of Asaph, was a high-ranking official in King Hezekiah's court, serving as the king's secretary. He is mentioned in the context of the Assyrian invasion of Judah during Hezekiah's reign. When the Assyrian envoys came to Jerusalem to demand the city's surrender, Joah was one of the three officials sent by Hezekiah to meet with them (2Ki.18.18; Isa.36.3). Along with Eliakim and Shebna, Joah sought to negotiate with the Assyrians and asked them to speak in Aramaic rather than Hebrew, so the people on the wall would not understand (2Ki.18.26; Isa.36.11). After the Assyrian envoys delivered their threatening message, Joah and his colleagues reported back to Hezekiah, tearing their clothes in distress (2Ki.18.37; Isa.36.22).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.18 only referred to as Joah (יוֹאָח); a son of Asaph.
persons.short_ko: 요아는 아삽의 아들로 히스기야 왕 때 사관을 지냈다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.18.18에 처음 언급되며 '요아'라 불림. 아삽의 아들.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Joah, King Josiah's secretary
persons.short: Joahaz was the father of Joah, who served as King Josiah's secretary during the temple repairs.
persons.article: Joahaz is briefly mentioned in 2Ch.34.8 as the father of Joah, who held the position of King Josiah's secretary during the king's reign in Judah. Joah, along with Shaphan the scribe and Maaseiah the governor of the city, was entrusted by Josiah to oversee the distribution of funds to the workers involved in the temple repairs. This event took place in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, as part of the king's efforts to restore proper worship in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.8 only referred to as Joahaz (יוֹאָחָז); father of Joah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.8에 처음 언급되며 '요아하스'라 불림. 요아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아하스는 성전 수리 기간 동안 요시야 왕의 서기관으로 섬긴 요아의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Joanan is listed as an ancestor of Jesus in the genealogy recorded by Luke.
persons.article: Joanan is mentioned in Luk.3.27 as one of the ancestors of Jesus Christ in the genealogy traced through Joseph, Jesus' legal father. He is listed as the son of Rhesa and the father of Joda, although no further details about his life or role in the family line are provided. The genealogy in Luke's Gospel spans from Jesus back to Adam, emphasizing Jesus' connection to all of humanity.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.27 only referred to as Joanan (Ἰωαννᾶς); a son of Rhesa; father of Joda.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.27에 처음 언급되며 '요아난'이라 불림. 레사의 아들. 맛다디아요의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아난은 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A follower of Jesus who supported His ministry
persons.short: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, was one of the women who followed and supported Jesus during His earthly ministry.
persons.article: Joanna is mentioned in Luk.8.3 and Luk.24.10 as one of the women who followed Jesus and supported His ministry. She is described as the wife of Chuza, who was a steward in Herod's household. Along with other women, including Mary Magdalene and Susanna, Joanna provided financial support for Jesus and His disciples out of her own means. Joanna was also among the women who witnessed Jesus' crucifixion and later went to His tomb on the morning of His resurrection. In Luk.24.10, she is named as one of the women who reported the news of the empty tomb and the angels' message to the apostles. Her presence at these key moments in Jesus' life and her support of His ministry indicate her devotion and faith.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.8.3 only referred to as Joanna (Ἰωάννα, Ἰωανάν); wife of Chuza.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Luk.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '요안나'라 불림. 구사의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 구사의 아내 요안나는 예수님의 지상 사역 동안 그분을 따르며 섬긴 여인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Joash, the son of Shemaah the Gibeathite, was a Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Joash, the son of Shemaah the Gibeathite, is mentioned in 1Ch.12.3 as one of the Benjaminite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul. Along with his brother Jeziel, Joash is described as a skillful archer and slingshot user. These warriors from the tribe of Benjamin provided valuable military support to David during his time of exile and later when he became king over Israel.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ); son of Shemaah; a brother of Ahiezer.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 스마아의 아들. 아히에셀의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 기브아 사람 스마아의 아들 요아스는 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 베냐민 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An official in charge of David's olive and sycamore trees
persons.short: Joash the Abiezrite was responsible for King David's olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah.
persons.article: Joash the Abiezrite is mentioned in 1Ch.27.28 as one of the officials in charge of King David's agricultural resources. Specifically, he was responsible for overseeing the olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah, a region of low hills between the central mountains and the coastal plain of Judah. This information provides insight into the organization and management of the king's resources during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.28 only referred to as Joash (יוֹעָשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.28에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아비에셀 사람 요아스는 평지에서 다윗 왕의 감람나무와 뽕나무를 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A descendant of Shelah in the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Joash was a descendant of Shelah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Joash is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.4.22 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, specifically the descendants of Shelah. He is described as one of the "ancient things" or "ancient records" associated with the lineage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.22 only referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ); son of Shelah; a brother of Er, Laadah, Jokim and Saraph.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.22에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 셀라의 아들. 엘, 라아다, 요김과 사랍의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요아스는 셀라의 후손으로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: A descendant of Benjamin through Becher
persons.short: Joash was a descendant of Benjamin through Becher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.
persons.article: Joash is mentioned in 1Ch.7.8 as one of the sons of Becher, a descendant of Benjamin. He is listed along with his brothers Zemira, Zemirah, and Eliezer. This genealogical record provides insight into the family structure within the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Joash (יוֹעָשׁ); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 엘리에셀, 에료에내, 오므리, 여레못, 아비야, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요아스는 베겔을 통한 베냐민의 후손으로, 그 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of King Ahab of Israel
persons.short: Joash, the son of King Ahab, was imprisoned by his father for a prophecy against him.
persons.article: Joash, the son of King Ahab of Israel, is mentioned briefly in 1Ki.22.26 and 2Ch.18.25. During a joint military campaign with King Jehoshaphat of Judah, Ahab sought advice from his prophets regarding the battle against the Arameans at Ramoth-gilead. When the prophet Micaiah prophesied Ahab's defeat and death, the king ordered Joash to imprison Micaiah until his safe return from the battle. However, Ahab was killed in the battle, fulfilling Micaiah's prophecy.
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.26 only referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ); son of Ahab; a brother of Ahaziah, Joram and Athaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.22.26에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 아합과 이세벨의 아들. 아하시야, 요람과 아달랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아합 왕의 아들 요아스는 그에 대한 예언 때문에 아버지에게 투옥되었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Ahaziah
persons.short: Joash (Jehoash), son of Ahaziah, became king of Judah at age seven and reigned for forty years.
persons.article: Joash, also known as Jehoash, was the king of Judah and the son of Ahaziah. He became king at the age of seven, after being hidden by his aunt Jehosheba for six years following the usurpation of the throne by Athaliah (2Ki.11.2; 2Ch.22.11). During his forty-year reign (2Ki.12.1; 2Ch.24.1, Joash initiated repairs to the temple of the Lord, which had fallen into disrepair )(2Ki.12.4-7; 2Ch.24.4). However, after the death of his mentor, Jehoiada the priest, Joash turned away from the Lord and allowed the worship of idols (2Ch.24.17-18). When Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada, prophesied against this wickedness, Joash ordered his execution (2Ch.24.20-22). Consequently, Judah faced military defeats and Joash was wounded (2Ch.24.23-24). He was eventually assassinated by his own servants and succeeded by his son Amaziah (2Ki.12.20-21; 2Ch.24.25-27). Joash's reign was marked by both early reforms and later apostasy, highlighting the importance of godly leadership and the consequences of turning away from the Lord.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.11.2 referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ), or Jehoash (יְהוֹאָשׁ); a son of Ahaziah and Zibiah; husband of Jehoaddan; father of Amaziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.11.2에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 아하시야와 시비아의 아들. 여호앗단의 남편. 아마샤의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아스(여호아스)는 아하시야의 아들로, 일곱 살에 유다 왕이 되어 사십 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 요아스(여호아스라고도 함)는 유다 왕이며 아하시야의 아들이었다. 그는 아달랴가 왕위를 찬탈한 후 이모 여호세바에게 육 년간 숨겨진 후 일곱 살에 왕이 되었다(왕하 11:2; 대하 22:11). 사십 년간의 통치 기간 동안(왕하 12:1; 대하 24:1) 요아스는 방치되었던 여호와의 성전 수리를 시작했다(왕하 12:4-7; 대하 24:4). 그러나 그의 스승인 제사장 여호야다가 죽은 후 요아스는 여호와에게서 돌아서서 우상숭배를 허용했다(대하 24:17-18). 여호야다의 아들 스가랴가 이 악행을 대적하여 예언했을 때 요아스는 그를 처형하라고 명령했다(대하 24:20-22). 그 결과 유다는 군사적 패배에 직면했고 요아스는 부상을 입었다(대하 24:23-24). 그는 결국 자기 신하들에게 암살당했고 그의 아들 아마샤가 뒤를 이었다(왕하 12:20-21; 대하 24:25-27). 요아스의 통치는 초기의 개혁과 후기의 배교로 특징지어지며, 경건한 지도력의 중요성과 여호와에게서 돌아서는 것의 결과를 부각시킨다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel, son of Jehoahaz
persons.short: Joash (Jehoash), son of Jehoahaz, reigned as king of Israel for sixteen years.
persons.article: Joash, also known as Jehoash, was the king of Israel and the son of Jehoahaz. He reigned for sixteen years (2Ki.13.10; 14.23) and, like his predecessors, did evil in the sight of the Lord (2Ki.13.11). During his reign, the prophet Elisha fell ill and died, but not before prophesying that Joash would defeat the Arameans three times (2Ki.13.14-19). Joash successfully recaptured cities from the Arameans that had been lost during his father's reign (2Ki.13.25). He also engaged in a war with Amaziah, king of Judah, after Amaziah challenged him to battle (2Ki.14.8-14; 2Ch.25.17-24). Joash defeated Amaziah, captured him, and broke down a portion of the wall of Jerusalem. The reigns of Joash and his son Jeroboam II were marked by military successes and the restoration of Israel's borders (2Ki.14.23-27). However, despite these victories, the biblical text emphasizes that Joash and the kings of Israel continued in the sins of Jeroboam I, leading to the eventual downfall of the northern kingdom (2Ki.14.24). The prophets Hosea and Amos prophesied during the time of Joash (Hos.1.1; Amo.1.1, warning of the consequences of Israel's disobedience).
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.13.9 referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ), or Jehoash (יְהוֹאָשׁ); a son of Jehoahaz; father of Jeroboam.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.13.9에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 여호아하스의 아들. 여로보암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요아스(여호아스)는 여호아하스의 아들로 이스라엘 왕으로 십육 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 요아스(여호아스라고도 함)는 이스라엘 왕이며 여호아하스의 아들이었다. 그는 십육 년간 다스렸고(왕하 13:10; 14:23), 그의 전임자들처럼 여호와 보시기에 악을 행했다(왕하 13:11). 그의 통치 기간 동안 선지자 엘리사가 병들어 죽었으나, 그전에 요아스가 아람을 세 번 물리칠 것이라고 예언했다(왕하 13:14-19). 요아스는 아버지 통치 기간에 잃었던 성읍들을 아람에게서 성공적으로 되찾았다(왕하 13:25). 그는 또한 유다 왕 아마샤가 그에게 전투를 걸어온 후 그와 전쟁을 치렀다(왕하 14:8-14; 대하 25:17-24). 요아스는 아마샤를 물리치고 그를 사로잡았으며 예루살렘 성벽의 일부를 헐었다. 요아스와 그의 아들 여로보암 2세의 통치는 군사적 성공과 이스라엘 국경의 회복으로 특징지어졌다(왕하 14:23-27). 그러나 이러한 승리에도 불구하고 성경 본문은 요아스와 이스라엘 왕들이 계속 여로보암 1세의 죄를 이어갔음을 강조하며, 이는 결국 북이스라엘 왕국의 몰락으로 이어졌다(왕하 14:24). 선지자 호세아와 아모스는 요아스 시대에 예언하며(호 1:1; 암 1:1) 이스라엘의 불순종의 결과를 경고했다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: The father of Gideon, a judge of Israel
persons.short: Joash, the father of Gideon, supported his son's actions in tearing down the altar of Baal.
persons.article: Joash, an Abiezrite from the tribe of Manasseh, was the father of Gideon, one of the judges of Israel. He first appears in Jdg.6.11, where the Angel of the Lord visits Gideon while he is threshing wheat in Joash's winepress to hide from the Midianites. When Gideon tears down the altar of Baal and the Asherah pole beside it, the men of the city demand that Joash surrender his son to be put to death (Jdg.6.29-30). However, Joash defends Gideon, saying that if Baal is truly a god, he can defend himself (Jdg.6.31). This event earns Gideon the name Jerubbaal, meaning "Let Baal contend against him." Joash is mentioned again in Jdg.7.14, where the Midianites interpret a dream as a sign that God has given them into the hand of Gideon, the son of Joash. After Gideon's victory over the Midianites, he returns to his father's house in Ophrah (Jdg.8.13,29). Joash dies at a good old age and is buried in the tomb of his father in Ophrah (Jdg.8.32).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.6.11 only referred to as Joash (יוֹאָשׁ); father of Gideon.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.6.11에 처음 언급되며 '요아스'라 불림. 기드온의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 기드온의 아버지 요아스는 아들이 바알의 제단을 헐어버린 행동을 지지했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A righteous man who endured great suffering
persons.short: Job, a blameless and upright man from Uz, endured severe trials and maintained his faith in God.
persons.article: Job was a man from the land of Uz, described as blameless, upright, and one who feared God and shunned evil (Job.1.1). He was blessed with seven sons, three daughters, and great wealth (Job.1.2-3). However, God allowed Satan to test Job's faith through a series of severe trials, including the loss of his children, wealth, and health (Job.1.6-2.10). Throughout his suffering, Job maintained his integrity and did not sin against God (Job.1.22; 2.10). He engaged in a lengthy dialogue with his three friends - Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar - who came to comfort him but ultimately accused him of wrongdoing (Job.2.11-31.40). A fourth friend, Elihu, also spoke to Job, emphasizing God's justice and sovereignty (Job.32-37). Finally, God spoke to Job, challenging him to understand the mysteries of creation and divine wisdom (Job.38-41). Job acknowledged God's power and repented of his questioning (Job.42.1-6). In the end, God restored Job's fortunes, giving him twice as much as he had before, and blessed him with seven more sons and three more daughters (Job.42.10-17). Job's story is a testament to faith in the face of adversity, and he is mentioned alongside Noah and Daniel as an example of righteousness (Ezk.14.14,20). His perseverance is also commended in the New Testament (Jas.5.11). The book of Job grapples with the question of suffering and the sovereignty of God, ultimately showcasing God's wisdom and the importance of trust in Him.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Job.1.1 referred to as Job (אִיּוֹב), or Job (Ἰώβ); father of Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Job.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '욥'이라 불림. 여미마, 긋시야와 게렌합북의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우스 땅 출신의 흠 없고 정직한 사람 욥은 극심한 시련을 견디며 하나님에 대한 믿음을 지켰다.
persons.article_ko: 욥은 우스 땅 출신 사람으로, 흠 없고 정직하며 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 자로 묘사된다(욥 1:1). 그는 일곱 아들과 세 딸, 그리고 큰 부를 축복받았다(욥 1:2-3). 그러나 하나님은 사탄이 욥의 자녀와 재산, 건강을 잃는 것을 포함한 일련의 심한 시련을 통해 그의 믿음을 시험하도록 허락하셨다(욥 1:6-2:10). 고난 내내 욥은 자신의 온전함을 지켰고 하나님께 범죄하지 않았다(욥 1:22; 2:10). 그는 자신을 위로하러 온 세 친구 엘리바스, 빌닷, 소발과 긴 대화를 나누었으나, 결국 그들은 그를 잘못했다고 비난했다(욥 2:11-31:40). 넷째 친구 엘리후도 욥에게 말하며 하나님의 정의와 주권을 강조했다(욥 32-37장). 마침내 하나님이 욥에게 말씀하시며 창조의 신비와 신적 지혜를 이해하라고 도전하셨다(욥 38-41장). 욥은 하나님의 권능을 인정하고 자신의 질문을 회개했다(욥 42:1-6). 결국 하나님은 욥의 재산을 회복시키셔서 이전보다 두 배로 주셨고, 일곱 아들과 세 딸을 더 축복하셨다(욥 42:10-17). 욥의 이야기는 역경 앞에서의 믿음에 대한 증거이며, 그는 노아, 다니엘과 함께 의로움의 본보기로 언급된다(겔 14:14, 20). 그의 인내는 신약에서도 칭찬받는다(약 5:11). 욥기는 고난과 하나님의 주권이라는 질문과 씨름하며, 궁극적으로 하나님의 지혜와 그분을 신뢰하는 것의 중요성을 보여준다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Eber@1Ch.8.12, Misham@1Ch.8.12, Shemed@1Ch.8.12, Beriah@1Ch.8.13-, Shema@1Ch.8.13, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.17, Meshullam@1Ch.8.17, Hizki@1Ch.8.17, Heber@1Ch.8.17, Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18, Izliah@1Ch.8.18
persons.brief: A son of Elpaal, descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Jobab, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Elpaal.
persons.article: Jobab is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.8.18 as one of the sons of Elpaal, a descendant of Benjamin. He is listed among Elpaal's eighteen sons in the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin. This genealogy traces the lineage of King Saul and provides insight into the family structure within the tribe. However, no further information is given about Jobab's life or his specific role within the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.18 only referred to as Jobab (יוֹבָב); son of Elpaal; a brother of Eber, Misham, Shemed, Beriah, Shema, Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai and Izliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.18에 처음 언급되며 '요밥'이라 불림. 엘바알의 아들. 에벨, 미삼, 세멧, 브리아, 세마, 스바댜, 므술람, 히스기, 헤벨, 이스므래와 이슬리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요밥은 베냐민의 후손으로 엘바알의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zibia@1Ch.8.9, Mesha@1Ch.8.9, Malcam@1Ch.8.9, Jeuz@1Ch.8.10, Sachia@1Ch.8.10, Mirmah@1Ch.8.10, Abitub@1Ch.8.11, Elpaal@1Ch.8.11-
persons.brief: A son of Shaharaim and Hodesh
persons.short: Jobab was one of the sons born to Shaharaim and his wife Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin.
persons.article: Jobab is mentioned in 1Ch.8.9 as one of the sons of Shaharaim and his wife Hodesh. This information is provided in the context of the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. Shaharaim had sent away his wives Hushim and Baara, and he had children with Hodesh in the country of Moab. Jobab is listed among the seven sons born to Shaharaim and Hodesh.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.9 only referred to as Jobab (יוֹבָב); son of Shaharaim and Hodesh; a brother of Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sachia, Mirmah, Abitub and Elpaal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '요밥'이라 불림. 사하라임과 호데스의 아들. 시비야, 메사, 말감, 여우스, 사갸, 미르마, 아비둡과 엘바알의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요밥은 사하라임이 그의 아내 호데스에게서 낳은 아들 중 한 사람으로, 베냐민 족보에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
persons.short: Jobab, a descendant of Shem through Joktan, is mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Jobab is mentioned in Gen.10.29 and 1Ch.1.23 as one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem. He is listed among the thirteen sons of Joktan in the genealogical record known as the Table of Nations. This record provides insight into the peoples and nations that descended from Noah's sons after the Flood. The descendants of Joktan are believed to have settled in the southern regions of the Arabian Peninsula.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.29 only referred to as Jobab (יוֹבָב); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir and Havilah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.29에 처음 언급되며 '요밥'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌과 하윌라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요밥은 셈의 후손 욕단을 통한 후손으로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A king of Edom, son of Zerah of Bozrah
persons.short: Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, was an early king of Edom who reigned before Israel had a king.
persons.article: Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, is mentioned in Gen.36.33-34 and 1Ch.1.44-45 as one of the early kings of Edom. He ruled after the death of King Bela, son of Beor, and was succeeded by Husham of the land of the Temanites. These kings reigned in Edom before any king ruled over the Israelites, indicating that the Edomite monarchy was established earlier than that of Israel. The mention of Jobab and other Edomite kings in these passages provides historical context for the relationship between Edom and Israel, as well as insight into the political structure of the region during the patriarchal period. However, no additional details are given about Jobab's reign or personal life.
persons.summary: A king of Edom living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.33 only referred to as Jobab (יוֹבָב); a son of Zerah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.36.33에 처음 언급되며 '요밥'이라 불림. 세라의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 보스라 사람 세라의 아들 요밥은 이스라엘에 왕이 있기 전 에돔을 다스린 초기 왕이었다.

persons.description: King living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Madon, who joined forces against Joshua
persons.short: Jobab, the king of Madon, was one of the northern kings who allied against Israel during the conquest of Canaan.
persons.article: Jobab, the king of Madon, is mentioned in Jos.11.1 as one of the northern Canaanite kings who formed an alliance against Israel during the conquest of Canaan. When Jabin, king of Hazor, called for the northern kings to unite against Joshua and the Israelites, Jobab joined forces with him, along with the kings of Shimron and Achshaph. This coalition gathered their troops and encamped together at the Waters of Merom to fight against Israel. However, Joshua and the Israelite army launched a surprise attack and defeated them, pursuing and striking them down until no survivors were left (Jos.11.7-8).
persons.summary: A king in Canaan living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at Jos.11.1 only referred to as Jobab (יוֹבָב).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 왕. Jos.11.1에 처음 언급되며 '요밥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마돈 왕 요밥은 가나안 정복 당시 이스라엘을 대적하여 동맹한 북부 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
persons.short: Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, married her nephew Amram and became the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
persons.article: Jochebed, meaning "Yahweh is glory," was the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. She is mentioned in Exo.6.20 and Num.26.59 in the genealogical records of the Levites. Jochebed was the daughter of Levi, born to him in Egypt. She married her nephew Amram, the son of her brother Kohath. This marriage took place before the laws prohibiting such unions were given (Lev.18.12). Jochebed gave birth to three children who would play significant roles in Israel's history: Miriam, the eldest, followed by Aaron and Moses. According to Exo.2.1-10, when Moses was born, Jochebed hid him for three months to protect him from Pharaoh's edict to kill all male Hebrew babies. When she could no longer hide him, she placed him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile River, where he was found and adopted by Pharaoh's daughter. Jochebed's faith and courage in protecting her son led to Moses being raised in the Egyptian court, ultimately preparing him for his future role as Israel's deliverer.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.20 only referred to as Jochebed (יוֹכֶ֫בֶד); daughter of Levi; a sister of Gershon, Kohath and Merari; wife of Amram; mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Exo.6.20에 처음 언급되며 '요게벳'이라 불림. 레위의 딸. 게르손, 그핫과 므라리의 자매. 아므람의 아내. 모세, 아론과 미리암의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 레위의 딸 요게벳은 조카 아므람과 결혼하여 모세, 아론, 미리암의 어머니가 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Joda is listed as an ancestor of Jesus in the genealogy recorded by Luke.
persons.article: Joda is mentioned in Luk.3.26 as one of the ancestors of Jesus Christ in the genealogy traced through Joseph, Jesus' legal father. He is listed as the son of Joanan and the father of Josech. This genealogy spans from Jesus back to Adam, emphasizing Jesus' connection to all of humanity. The genealogy in Luke's Gospel differs from the one recorded in Matthew's Gospel, as Luke traces Jesus' lineage through David's son Nathan, while Matthew traces it through Solomon. The two genealogies converge at Zerubbabel and Shealtiel, after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.26 only referred to as Joda (Ἰωδά); a son of Joanan; father of Josech.
persons.summary_ko: Luk.3.26에 처음 언급되며 '맛다디아요'라 불림. 요아난의 아들. 맛다디아요의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요다는 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjaminite who resettled in Jerusalem
persons.short: Joed, a Benjaminite, was among those who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Joed is mentioned in Neh.11.7 as one of the Benjaminites who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Following the return of the Jewish exiles to their homeland, Nehemiah, the governor of Judah, took steps to repopulate Jerusalem. He gathered the leaders, nobles, and people to be registered by genealogy, and Joed is listed among the descendants of Benjamin who chose to reside in the holy city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.7 only referred to as Joed (יוֹעֵד); a son of Pedaiah; father of Meshullam.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.7에 처음 언급되며 '요엣'이라 불림. 브다야의 아들. 므술람의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요엣은 베냐민 사람으로, 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 재정착한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: The brother of Nathan, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Joel, the brother of Nathan, was one of the mighty men who fought valiantly for King David.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.11.38 as one of the mighty men who served under King David. He is described as the brother of Nathan, another of David's mighty warriors. The mighty men were a group of elite soldiers known for their exceptional bravery, skill, and loyalty to the king. They played a crucial role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. The inclusion of Joel in this list indicates his prowess as a warrior and his dedication to serving King David. However, no further details are provided about his specific accomplishments or the nature of his relationship with his brother Nathan.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.38 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); a brother of Nathan.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.38에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 나단의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 나단의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 나단의 형제 요엘은 다윗 왕을 위해 용맹하게 싸운 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gershomite Levite during the reign of David
persons.short: Joel, a Levite of the Gershomite clan, was appointed by David to help transport the ark of the covenant.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.15.7 and 1Ch.15.11 as a Levite of the Gershomite clan during the reign of King David. When David decided to bring the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem, he gathered the Levites and instructed them to consecrate themselves and carry the ark according to the proper procedures. Joel, along with his fellow Gershomites, was appointed to this sacred task. The Gershomites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, responsible for assisting in the transportation and care of the tabernacle and its furnishings. Joel's inclusion in this narrative highlights the importance of the Levites' role in maintaining the proper worship of God and the significance of the ark's journey to Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.7 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.7에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 게르솜 가문 레위인 요엘은 다윗이 언약궤를 옮기는 일을 돕도록 임명했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gershonite Levite during David's organization of the Levites
persons.short: Joel, a descendant of Ladan from the Gershonite clan, was a Levite during David's time.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.23.8 and 1Ch.26.22 as a Levite belonging to the Gershonite clan during the reign of King David. In 1Chronicles 23, David organizes the Levites and assigns them their duties. Joel is listed as one of the sons of Ladan, a descendant of Gershon. The Gershonites were responsible for the care and transportation of the tabernacle and its furnishings. In 1Chronicles 26, Joel is mentioned again in the context of the gatekeepers and treasurers appointed by David. The sons of Jehieli, including Zetham and Joel, were entrusted with the treasuries of the house of the Lord. This responsibility included managing the dedicated gifts and offerings brought to the temple. Joel's inclusion in these passages highlights the various roles and responsibilities held by the Levites in maintaining the worship and administration of the temple during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.8 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); son of Libni; a brother of Zetham and Jehiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 립니의 아들. 여히엘과 세담의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 라단의 후손 게르손 계열 레위인 요엘은 다윗 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
persons.short: Joel was appointed as the ruler over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during David's reign.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.27.20 as the ruler over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during the reign of King David. In this chapter, David organizes his administration and appoints various officials and rulers over the tribes of Israel. Joel is specifically assigned to govern the region of Gilead, which was allocated to the half-tribe of Manasseh. This appointment reflects David's efforts to establish a structured and efficient governance system throughout his kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.20 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); a son of Pedaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.20에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 브다야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 길르앗에 있는 므낫세 반 지파를 다스리는 자로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
persons.short: Joel is listed in the genealogy of Judah as a descendant of Simeon.
persons.article: Joel is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.4.35 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He is listed among the descendants of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The inclusion of Simeonite names within the genealogy of Judah suggests that some members of the tribe of Simeon may have been absorbed into Judah or lived within their territory.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.35 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.35에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 유다 족보에서 시므온의 후손으로 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite chief in Bashan
persons.short: Joel was a chief of the Gadites who lived in the territory of Bashan.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.12 as one of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad who lived in the region of Bashan. He is listed alongside Shapham, the chief, and Janai and Shaphat, who were also in Bashan. The Gadites were one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and they settled in the area east of the Jordan River. The mention of Joel and the other chiefs provides insight into the leadership structure within the tribe of Gad during their time in Bashan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.12 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.12에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 바산 땅에 살던 갓 지파 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of Reuben
persons.short: Joel is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben as a descendant of Shemaiah.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.4 as a descendant of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is listed in the genealogical record of the tribe of Reuben as the son of Shemaiah and the father of Gog. This genealogy traces the lineage of the Reubenites, who settled east of the Jordan River.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.4 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); father of Shemaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.4에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 스마야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 르우벤 지파 족보에서 스마야의 후손으로 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shema living in Reubenite lands
persons.short: Joel, a father of Shema who lived in Reuben and also neighbouring Gad.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.5.8 among Reubenite genealogies (1Chr 5.3-10). His son Shema lived in and area that stretched from Reuben into neighbouring Gad..
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.8 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); father of Shema.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.8에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 세마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 르우벤과 인접한 갓 땅에 살던 세마의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A son of Izrahiah from the tribe of Issachar
persons.short: Joel was one of the five sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar, known for their bravery.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 1Ch.7.3 as one of the sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar. He is listed alongside his brothers Michael, Obadiah, Ishiah, and Shimron. The five brothers were described as mighty warriors and heads of their fathers' houses. The chronicler notes that during the reign of King David, their census records showed a total of 22,600 mighty warriors. This information highlights the military strength and leadership within the tribe of Issachar.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.3 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); son of Izrahiah; a brother of Michael, Obadiah and Isshiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.7.3에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 이스라히야의 아들. 미가엘, 오바댜와 잇시야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 잇사갈의 후손인 이스라히야의 다섯 아들 중 한 사람으로, 용맹함으로 알려졌다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Samuel's firstborn son who judged Israel
persons.short: Joel, the firstborn son of Samuel, served as a judge in Israel but did not walk in his father's ways.
persons.article: Joel was the firstborn son of the prophet and judge Samuel, as mentioned in 1Sa.8.2. Along with his brother Abijah, Joel was appointed by Samuel to serve as a judge in Israel. However, unlike their father, Joel and Abijah did not walk in the ways of the Lord. They turned aside after dishonest gain, accepted bribes, and perverted justice (1Sa.8.3). This corruption in leadership led the elders of Israel to demand a king to rule over them, ultimately resulting in the anointing of Saul as the first king of Israel (1Sa.8.4-5). The failure of Joel and Abijah to uphold the standards of righteous judgment set by their father had significant consequences for the nation of Israel.
persons.summary: A Judge from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.8.2 referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל), or "second" (וַשְׁנִי); son of Samuel; a brother of Abijah; father of Heman.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Sa.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 사무엘의 아들. 아비야의 형제. 헤만의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사무엘의 맏아들 요엘은 이스라엘의 사사로 섬겼으나 아버지의 길을 따르지 않았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Kohathite Levite during Hezekiah's temple restoration
persons.short: Joel, a Levite of the Kohathite clan, participated in the purification of the temple during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Joel is mentioned in 2Ch.29.12 as one of the Levites who participated in the purification and restoration of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. Hezekiah, a righteous king of Judah, initiated a series of religious reforms, which included cleansing the temple and reinstating proper worship practices. Joel, along with other Levites from the clans of Kohath, Merari, and Gershon, responded to the king's command and took part in the temple purification process. The Kohathites, Joel's clan, were traditionally responsible for the care and transportation of the most sacred items in the tabernacle and temple. Joel's participation in this significant event demonstrates the Levites' commitment to restoring and maintaining the proper worship of God in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); a son of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 아사랴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 고핫 계열 레위인 요엘은 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile
persons.short: Joel was among the Israelites who had married foreign women and pledged to put them away during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Joel is briefly mentioned in Ezr.10.43 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. After the return of the exiles to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra, it was discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was in violation of God's command to maintain their holiness and avoid the pagan practices of the surrounding nations. Ezra called for a assembly, where the people confessed their sin and pledged to put away their foreign wives and children. Joel is listed among those who had taken this step of obedience in response to Ezra's reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.43 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.43에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요엘은 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그녀를 내보내기로 서약한 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet of Judah and the author of the Book of Joel
persons.short: Joel, the son of Pethuel, was a prophet of Judah who delivered a message of judgment and hope.
persons.article: Joel, the son of Pethuel, was a prophet of Judah and the author of the Old Testament book that bears his name. Little is known about Joel's personal life or the exact time of his ministry, as the book does not provide specific historical references. However, based on the themes and content of his prophecy, scholars generally place him in the post-exilic period, possibly during the late 5th or early 4th century BC. In his prophetic message, Joel describes a devastating locust plague and drought that had struck Judah, using this calamity as a metaphor for the coming Day of the Lord. He calls the people to repentance and promises restoration and blessing for those who turn back to God. Joel's prophecy also includes a powerful vision of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon all people, regardless of age, gender, or social status (Jol.2.28-32). This prophecy is notably quoted by the apostle Peter in his sermon on the Day of Pentecost (Act.2.16-21, indicating its fulfillment in the early days of the Church). Joel's message, though rooted in the specific challenges faced by Judah in his time, carries a timeless call to repentance, hope in God's mercy, and the promise of the Holy Spirit's transformative power.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jol.1.1 referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל), or Joel (Ἰωήλ); a son of Pethuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. Jol.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 브두엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 브두엘의 아들 선지자 요엘은 유다에 심판과 소망의 메시지를 전했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjaminite leader in Jerusalem after the Exile
persons.short: Joel, the son of Zichri, was a Benjaminite leader in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Joel, the son of Zichri, is mentioned in Neh.11.9 as a leader of the Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Following the return of the exiles and the rebuilding of the city walls, Nehemiah organized the repopulation of Jerusalem. He appointed leaders from various tribes to reside in the holy city and help maintain its security and prosperity. Joel is identified as the second-in-command to Judah, the son of Hassenuah, who was the chief of the Benjaminites in Jerusalem. This leadership role indicates Joel's importance and responsibility within the Benjaminite community during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.9 only referred to as Joel (יוֹאֵל); a son of Zichri.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.9에 처음 언급되며 '요엘'이라 불림. 시그리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 시그리의 아들 요엘은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘의 베냐민 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Joelah, a Benjaminite warrior, was among those who joined David at Ziklag while he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Joelah is mentioned in 1Ch.12.7 as one of the Benjaminite warriors who joined David at Ziklag while he was fleeing from King Saul. Along with his brother Zebadiah, Joelah is described as a brave warrior and a leader among the Benjaminites. They were part of a group of skilled archers and slingers who came to support David during this difficult period in his life. The chronicler emphasizes the military prowess and loyalty of these men, noting that they were "brave warriors, ready for battle and able to handle the shield and spear" (1Ch.12.8). Joelah's decision to align himself with David demonstrates his faith in David's divine appointment as the future king of Israel, even while Saul was still on the throne.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.7 only referred to as Joelah (יוֹעֵאלָה); son of Jeroham; a brother of Zebadiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.7에 처음 언급되며 '요엘라'라 불림. 여로함의 아들. 스바댜의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 용사 요엘라는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Joezer, a Korahite warrior, was among the Benjaminites who joined David at Ziklag while he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Joezer is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.12.6 as one of the Benjaminite warriors who joined David at Ziklag while he was seeking refuge from King Saul. He is described as a Korahite, which may indicate that he belonged to the Levitical clan of Korah. Joezer was part of a group of skilled archers and slingers from the tribe of Benjamin who came to support David during this challenging time. The chronicler highlights the bravery and military expertise of these men, noting that they were "armed with bows and were able to shoot arrows or to sling stones right-handed or left-handed" (1Ch.12.2). Joezer's presence among David's supporters demonstrates his loyalty to the future king and his belief in David's divine appointment, even while Saul was still in power.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.6 only referred to as Joezer (יוֹעֶ֫זֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.6에 처음 언급되며 '요에셀'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고라 사람 용사 요에셀은 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 베냐민 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A leader from the tribe of Dan
persons.short: Jogli, the son of Bukki, was a leader from the tribe of Dan appointed to help divide the Promised Land.
persons.article: Jogli, the son of Bukki, is mentioned in Num.34.22 as one of the leaders appointed to help divide the Promised Land among the tribes of Israel. He was chosen as the representative from the tribe of Dan. This appointment took place near the end of the Israelites' wilderness wanderings, as they prepared to enter and possess the land of Canaan. Jogli's selection as a leader indicates his importance and respect within his tribe. Along with leaders from the other tribes, he was entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing the fair distribution of the land, ensuring that each tribe received its allotted portion as decreed by God. This division of the land was a significant moment in Israel's history, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give them a homeland.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.22 only referred to as Jogli (יׇגְלִי); father of Bukki.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.22에 처음 언급되며 '요글리'라 불림. 북기의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 북기의 아들 요글리는 약속의 땅 분배를 돕도록 임명된 단 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from the Tizite clan
persons.short: Joha the Tizite was one of David's mighty warriors, known for his bravery and military skill.
persons.article: Joha the Tizite is mentioned in 1Ch.11.45 as one of David's mighty warriors. He is listed among the group of soldiers known for their exceptional bravery, strength, and military prowess. The mighty warriors were an elite group of soldiers who played a crucial role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. Joha's inclusion in this list indicates that he was recognized for his outstanding skills as a warrior and his loyalty to King David. The designation "Tizite" likely refers to his place of origin or clan affiliation, although the exact location of Tiz is unknown. No further details are provided about Joha's specific accomplishments or his role in David's military campaigns.
