persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.24 only referred to as Joseph (Ἰωσήφ); a son of Mattathias; father of Jannai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림. 맛다디아의 아들. 얀나의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 맛다디아의 아들 요셉은 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Joseph, the son of Jonam, is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Joseph, the son of Jonam, is mentioned in Luk.3.30 as part of the genealogy of Jesus Christ. This genealogy traces Jesus' lineage through his mother Mary's family line. Joseph is listed as the son of Jonam and the father of Judah. The genealogy spans several centuries, from Jesus back to Adam, demonstrating Jesus' connection to the ancestral line of David and the fulfillment of messianic prophecies. However, no additional information is provided about Joseph's life or the specific time period in which he lived. His inclusion in the genealogy helps establish Jesus' lineage and ancestral heritage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.30 only referred to as Joseph (Ἰωσήφ); a son of Jonam; father of Judah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.30에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림. 요남의 아들. 유다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요남의 아들 요셉은 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Mary's husband living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Husband of Mary and earthly father of Jesus
persons.short: Joseph was the husband of Mary and the earthly father of Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Joseph was the husband of Mary and the earthly father of Jesus Christ. He was a descendant of David (Mat.1.16, 20; Luk.1.27; 2.4 and lived in Nazareth )(Luk.2.4). Joseph was betrothed to Mary when she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit (Mat.1.18; Luk.1.27). Being a righteous man, he planned to divorce her quietly, but an angel appeared to him in a dream, telling him to take Mary as his wife and name the child Jesus (Mat.1.19-21, 24-25). Joseph obeyed and took care of Mary and Jesus. He was present at Jesus' birth in Bethlehem (Luk.2.4-7, 16 and later took his family to Egypt to escape Herod's persecution )(Mat.2.13-15, 19-23). Joseph is last mentioned in the Gospels when Jesus was 12 years old, and the family visited Jerusalem for the Passover (Luk.2.41-51). He is referred to as Jesus' father (Luk.2.33, 48; 4.22; Jhn.1.45; 6.42 and was a carpenter by trade )(Mat.13.55). Joseph is not mentioned during Jesus' adult ministry, suggesting he may have died before that time.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Mat.1.16 referred to as Joseph or "father" or "parents" (Ἰωσήφ); son of Jacob; a brother of: Alphaeus (?); husband of Mary; father of Jesus, James, Joses, Simon and Jude.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 마리아의 남편. Mat.1.16에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림. 야곱의 아들. 알패오의 형제. 마리아의 남편. 예수, 야고보, 요세, 시몬과 유다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요셉은 마리아의 남편이며 예수 그리스도의 지상 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 요셉은 마리아의 남편이며 예수 그리스도의 지상 아버지였다. 그는 다윗의 후손이며(마 1:16, 20; 눅 1:27; 2:4) 나사렛에 살았다(눅 2:4). 요셉은 마리아가 성령으로 잉태한 것이 발견되었을 때 그녀와 약혼한 상태였다(마 1:18; 눅 1:27). 의로운 사람이었던 그는 그녀를 조용히 이혼시키려 했으나, 천사가 꿈에 그에게 나타나 마리아를 아내로 맞고 그 아이의 이름을 예수라 지으라고 말했다(마 1:19-21, 24-25). 요셉은 순종하여 마리아와 예수님을 돌보았다. 그는 베들레헴에서 예수님이 태어나실 때 함께 있었고(눅 2:4-7, 16) 후에 헤롯의 박해를 피해 가족을 애굽으로 데려갔다(마 2:13-15, 19-23). 요셉은 예수님이 열두 살이었을 때 가족이 유월절을 위해 예루살렘을 방문한 것을 마지막으로 복음서에 언급된다(눅 2:41-51). 그는 예수님의 아버지로 언급되며(눅 2:33, 48; 4:22; 요 1:45; 6:42) 목수였다(마 13:55). 요셉은 예수님의 성인 사역 동안에는 언급되지 않는데, 이는 그가 그 전에 죽었을 수 있음을 시사한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Of Arimathea, buried Jesus in his own tomb
persons.short: Joseph of Arimathea was a wealthy disciple who buried Jesus in his own new tomb.
persons.article: Joseph of Arimathea was a wealthy and prominent member of the Jewish council (Mat.27.57; Mrk.15.43). He was a disciple of Jesus but secretly out of fear of the Jewish leaders (Jhn.19.38). Joseph is described as a good and righteous man who had not consented to the council's decision to condemn Jesus (Luk.23.50-51). After Jesus' crucifixion, Joseph boldly asked Pilate for Jesus' body (Mrk.15.43; Jhn.19.38). He took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and placed it in his own new tomb, which had been cut out of rock (Mat.27.59-60; Mrk.15.46; Luk.23.53). The tomb was then sealed with a large stone (Mat.27.60). Joseph's actions fulfilled the prophecy that the Messiah would be buried with the rich (Isa.53.9). His selfless act provided a proper burial for Jesus and demonstrated his devotion and respect for the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.27.57 only referred to as Joseph (Ἰωσήφ).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.27.57에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아리마대 사람 요셉은 부유한 제자로, 예수님을 자신의 새 무덤에 장사했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Head of the priestly family of Shebaniah
persons.short: Joseph was the head of the priestly family of Shebaniah during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.article: Joseph is mentioned in Neh.12.14 as the head of the priestly family of Shebaniah during the days of Joiakim, the high priest. This was during the post-exilic period in Jerusalem, likely in the 5th century BC. The priests were organized into divisions or families, each with a designated leader. Nehemiah 12 lists the heads of priestly families in the generation following the return from Babylonian exile under Jeshua (Neh.12.1-7 and then during the time of Joiakim )(Neh.12.12-21).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.14 only referred to as Joseph (יוֹסֵף).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.14에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요셉은 요야김 대제사장 시절에 스바냐 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Representative of Issachar among the spies
persons.short: Joseph son of Igal represented the tribe of Issachar among the twelve spies sent to Canaan.
persons.article: Joseph, the son of Igal, was a member of the tribe of Issachar and one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num.13.7). The twelve spies, one from each tribe, were chosen to assess the land and its inhabitants before the Israelites entered the Promised Land (Num.13.1-2). After forty days of scouting the land, the spies returned with their report (Num.13.25). While Joshua and Caleb encouraged the people to trust God and take possession of the land, the other ten spies, including Joseph, brought back a discouraging report, emphasizing the strength of the land's inhabitants and cities (Num.13.26-33). This led to the people's rebellion against Moses and their refusal to enter the land (Num.14.1-4). As a result, God declared that the generation who had seen His miracles would not enter the Promised Land, except for Joshua and Caleb (Num.14.20-24).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.7 only referred to as Joseph (יוֹסֵף); father of Igal.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.7에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림. 이갈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이갈의 아들 요셉은 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 잇사갈 지파 대표였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Brother of Jesus and son of Mary
persons.short: Joses (or Joseph) was one of Jesus' brothers and a son of Mary.
persons.article: Joses, also known as Joseph, was one of the brothers of Jesus Christ and a son of Mary. He is mentioned by name in the Gospels of Mark and Matthew. In Mrk.6.3 and Mat.13.55, Joses/Joseph is listed along with James, Judas (or Jude), and Simon as Jesus' brothers. He was likely born after Jesus, as Jesus is referred to as Mary's firstborn (Luk.2.7).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.13.55 referred to as Joses (Ἰωσῆς), or Joseph (Ἰωσήφ); son of Joseph and Mary; a brother of Jesus, James, Simon and Jude.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.13.55에 처음 언급되며 '요셉'이라 불림. 요셉과 마리아의 아들. 예수, 야고보, 시몬과 유다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요세(요셉이라고도 함)는 예수님의 형제 중 한 사람으로 마리아의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Brother of James "the Less" and son of the "other" Mary
persons.short: Joses (or Joseph) was brother of James "the Less" who was an apostle.
persons.article: Joses, also known as Joseph, was one of the sons of "the other" Mary (Matt 28.1 with Mrk.16.1). He is the brother of James "the Less" (or "the younger" - Mrk.15.40 who is traditionally identified with James the son of Alphaeus, who would therefore be Mary's husband). Thsi may be the same Alphaeus who is the father of Matthew, though this is uncertain. His mother Mary was present at the crucifixion, burial, and discovery of the empty tomb (Mat.27.56; Mrk.15.40, 47).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.27.56 referred to as Joses (Ἰωσῆς), or Joseph (Ἰωσήφ); a son of Mary and probably Alphaeus ; brother of James and possibly Matthew.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.27.56에 처음 언급되며 '요세'라 불림. 알패오와 마리아의 아들. 야고보와 마태의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요세(요셉이라고도 함)는 사도 '작은 야고보'의 형제였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Joshah was one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Joshah is mentioned in 1Ch.4.34 as one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. The context of the passage is the genealogy and history of the tribe of Simeon (1Ch.4.24-43). During Hezekiah's reign, some Simeonites, including Joshah, migrated to the region of Gedor in search of pasture for their flocks (1Ch.4.39). They also attacked and displaced the Hamites and Meunites who were living there (1Ch.4.40-41). These events likely took place in the late 8th century BC, during the religious and political reforms of King Hezekiah (2Chronicles 29-32).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.34 only referred to as Joshah (יוֹשָׁה); a son of Amaziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.34에 처음 언급되며 '요사'라 불림. 아마샤의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 요사는 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from Mithan
persons.short: Joshaphat the Mithnite was listed among David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Joshaphat the Mithnite is mentioned in 1Ch.11.43 as one of David's mighty warriors. The context is a list of David's elite soldiers known for their military prowess and loyalty (1Ch.11.10-47). These warriors played a significant role in establishing and expanding David's kingdom during his reign as king of Israel, which lasted from approximately 1010 to 970 BC. The descriptor "Mithnite" likely refers to Joshaphat's place of origin or clan affiliation, but no further details are provided about its location or significance.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.43 only referred to as Joshaphat (יוֹשָׁפָט).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.43에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 미덴 사람 요사밧은 다윗의 용맹한 용사 명단에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A priest who blew trumpets before the ark
persons.short: Joshaphat, along with other priests, blew trumpets before the ark of the covenant during its transfer to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Joshaphat is mentioned in 1Ch.15.24 as one of the priests who blew trumpets before the ark of the covenant as it was being brought to Jerusalem. This event took place during the reign of King David, as he sought to establish Jerusalem as the religious and political center of Israel (1Ch.15.1-16:3). The ark, which symbolized God's presence among His people, was carried by the Levites and accompanied by musicians and singers. The priests, including Joshaphat, played a special role in this procession by blowing trumpets, which were used in religious ceremonies and to signal important events (Num.10.1-10).
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.15.24 only referred to as Joshaphat (יוֹשָׁפָט).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.24에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요사밧은 다른 제사장들과 함께 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮길 때 나팔을 불었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from Eliahba's sons
persons.short: Joshaviah, a son of Elnaam, was listed among David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Joshaviah, son of Elnaam, is mentioned in 1Ch.11.46 as one of David's mighty warriors. The context is a list of David's elite soldiers known for their military skills and bravery (1Ch.11.10-47). These warriors were instrumental in establishing and defending David's kingdom during his reign as king of Israel, which lasted from approximately 1010 to 970 BC. Joshaviah is specifically identified as a son of Elnaam, but no further information is provided about his family background or place of origin. The text does not give any details about Joshaviah's specific military exploits or his role among David's mighty warriors.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.46 only referred to as Joshaviah (יוֹשַׁוְיָה); son of Elnaam; a brother of Jeribai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.46에 처음 언급되며 '요사위야'라 불림. 엘라암의 아들. 여리배의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 엘남의 아들 요사위야는 다윗의 용맹한 용사 명단에 기록되어 있다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: A son of Heman, a musician in David's time
persons.short: Joshbekashah, one of Heman's sons, was a musician appointed by King David to lead worship.
persons.article: Joshbekashah is mentioned in 1Ch.25.4 and 1Ch.25.24 as one of the sons of Heman, a prominent Levitical musician during the reign of King David. Heman, along with Asaph and Jeduthun, was appointed by David to lead the music and worship in the house of the Lord (1Ch.25.1). Joshbekashah, along with his brothers, was set apart for the ministry of prophesying with musical instruments (1Ch.25.2). He was among those who were assigned duties by casting lots, ensuring a fair distribution of responsibilities (1Ch.25.8).
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Joshbekashah (יׇשְׁבְּקָ֫שָׁה); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '요스브가사'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 말로디, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 여호벡가사는 헤만의 아들 중 한 사람으로, 다윗 왕이 예배를 인도하도록 임명한 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Joshibiah was one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Joshibiah is mentioned in 1Ch.4.35 as one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. The context of the passage is the genealogy and history of the tribe of Simeon (1Ch.4.24-43). During Hezekiah's reign, some Simeonites, including Joshibiah, migrated to the region of Gedor in search of pasture for their flocks (1Ch.4.39). They also attacked and displaced the Hamites and Meunites who were living there (1Ch.4.40-41). These events likely took place in the late 8th century BC, during the religious and political reforms of King Hezekiah (2Chronicles 29-32).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.35 only referred to as Joshibiah (יוֹשִׁבְיָה); a son of Seraiah; father of Jehu.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.35에 처음 언급되며 '요시비야'라 불림. 스라야의 아들. 예후의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요시비야는 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Owner of a field in Beth-shemesh
persons.short: The ark of the covenant was placed on a rock in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
persons.article: Joshua is mentioned in 1Sa.6.14 and 1Sa.6.18 as a resident of Beth-shemesh, a town in Judah. The context of the passage is the return of the ark of the covenant to Israel after it had been captured by the Philistines (1Samuel 4-6). The Philistines, afflicted by plagues because of the ark's presence, sent it back to Israel on a cart pulled by two cows (1Sa.6.7-12). The cart carrying the ark came to the field of Joshua in Beth-shemesh, where the people were reaping their wheat harvest (1Sa.6.13). The cows pulling the cart stopped beside a large rock in Joshua's field (1Sa.6.14). The people of Beth-shemesh then split up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the Lord (1Sa.6.14). The large rock in Joshua's field, where the ark was placed, is mentioned again in 1Sa.6.18 as a marker or boundary stone.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.6.14 only referred to as Joshua (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.6.14에 처음 언급되며 '여호수아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 언약궤는 벧세메스 사람 여호수아의 밭에 있는 바위 위에 놓였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Governor of Jerusalem during Josiah's reign
persons.short: Joshua was the governor of Jerusalem during the reign of King Josiah.
persons.article: Joshua is mentioned in 2Ki.23.8 as the governor of Jerusalem during the reign of King Josiah. The context of the passage is Josiah's religious reforms, which took place in the late 7th century BC (2Kings 22-23). As part of these reforms, Josiah removed pagan worship sites and practices from Judah and Jerusalem. The high places that the kings of Judah had made at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city, were among those removed. These high places were likely dedicated to pagan deities and were located near Joshua's official residence or administrative building.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.23.8 only referred to as Joshua (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '여호수아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 여호수아는 요시야 왕 시대에 예루살렘의 성주였다.

persons.description: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
persons.brief: Moses' assistant who led Israel into Canaan
persons.short: Joshua, the son of Nun, was Moses' assistant and successor who led the Israelites into the Promised Land.
persons.article: Joshua, the son of Nun, was a prominent figure in the Old Testament who served as Moses' assistant and later succeeded him as the leader of the Israelites. He was from the tribe of Ephraim (Num.13.8 and was originally named Hoshea, but Moses changed his name to Joshua )(Num.13.16). Joshua was one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan (Num.13.8, and he and Caleb were the only ones who brought back a positive report and encouraged the people to trust God )(Num.14.6-9). As a result, Joshua and Caleb were the only adults from their generation permitted to enter the Promised Land (Num.14.30, 38). Before Moses' death, God appointed Joshua to succeed him as the leader of Israel (Num.27.18-23; Deu.31.7-8, 14, 23). After Moses' death, Joshua led the Israelites across the Jordan River and into the land of Canaan (Joshua 1-4). He oversaw the conquest of Jericho (Joshua 6), Ai (Joshua 8), and numerous other cities and territories (Joshua 10-12). Joshua also led the Israelites in renewing their covenant with God (Jos.8.30-35; 24.1-28). Under Joshua's leadership, the land of Canaan was divided among the tribes of Israel as their inheritance (Joshua 13-21). In his old age, Joshua gave a farewell address to the Israelites, encouraging them to remain faithful to God (Joshua 23-24). He died at the age of 110 and was buried in his inheritance at Timnath-serah (Jos.24.29-30; Jdg.2.8-9). Joshua is remembered as a courageous leader, a faithful servant of God, and a key figure in Israel's history who led the people into the Promised Land and helped establish them as a nation.
persons.summary: A Judge from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest, first mentioned at Exo.17.9 referred to as Joshua (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), or Hoshea or Joshua (הוֹשֵׁעַ), or Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ), or Joshua (Ἰησοῦς); a son of Nun.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야·정복시대 사사. Exo.17.9에 처음 언급되며 '여호수아'라 불림. 눈의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 눈의 아들 여호수아는 모세의 조수이며 후계자로, 이스라엘 백성을 약속의 땅으로 이끌었다.
persons.article_ko: 눈의 아들 여호수아는 모세의 조수로 섬기다가 후에 이스라엘 백성의 지도자로 그를 계승한 구약의 저명한 인물이었다. 그는 에브라임 지파에 속했고(민 13:8) 원래 이름은 호세아였으나 모세가 여호수아로 개명했다(민 13:16). 여호수아는 가나안 땅을 정탐하도록 보내진 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람이었고(민 13:8), 그와 갈렙만이 긍정적인 보고를 가져와 백성에게 하나님을 신뢰하라고 격려했다(민 14:6-9). 그 결과 여호수아와 갈렙은 그 세대에서 약속의 땅에 들어가는 것이 허락된 유일한 성인이었다(민 14:30, 38). 모세가 죽기 전 하나님은 여호수아를 이스라엘의 지도자로 그를 계승하도록 임명하셨다(민 27:18-23; 신 31:7-8, 14, 23). 모세가 죽은 후 여호수아는 이스라엘 백성을 이끌고 요단강을 건너 가나안 땅으로 들어갔다(수 1-4장). 그는 여리고(수 6장), 아이(수 8장), 그리고 다른 수많은 성읍과 영토의 정복을 감독했다(수 10-12장). 여호수아는 또한 이스라엘 백성이 하나님과의 언약을 갱신하도록 이끌었다(수 8:30-35; 24:1-28). 여호수아의 지도 아래 가나안 땅은 이스라엘 지파들에게 그들의 기업으로 분배되었다(수 13-21장). 노년에 여호수아는 이스라엘 백성에게 고별 연설을 하며 하나님께 신실하게 남아있으라고 격려했다(수 23-24장). 그는 백십 세에 죽어 자기 기업인 딤낫세라에 묻혔다(수 24:29-30; 삿 2:8-9). 여호수아는 용감한 지도자이며 하나님의 신실한 종이자, 백성을 약속의 땅으로 이끌고 그들을 한 민족으로 세우는 데 도움을 준 이스라엘 역사의 핵심 인물로 기억된다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: High priest during the rebuilding of the temple
persons.short: Joshua (or Jeshua), the son of Jehozadak, was the high priest who led the rebuilding of the temple after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Joshua, also known as Jeshua, was the high priest who played a significant role in the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Jehozadak (or Jozadak) and is mentioned in the books of Haggai, Zechariah, Ezra, and Nehemiah. Joshua is first mentioned among the leaders who returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezr.2.2; Neh.7.7). He worked alongside Zerubbabel to rebuild the altar and lay the foundation of the temple (Ezr.3.2, 8). When the temple construction faced opposition, Joshua and Zerubbabel successfully petitioned the Persian authorities to allow the work to continue (Ezr.5.2). The prophets Haggai and Zechariah delivered messages of encouragement and support to Joshua during the temple reconstruction (Hag.1.1, 12, 14; 2.2, 4; Zec.3.1-9; 6.11). In a vision, Zechariah saw Joshua standing before the angel of the Lord, with Satan accusing him. The Lord rebuked Satan and affirmed His choice of Joshua as the high priest (Zec.3.1-5). Joshua was also given a symbolic crown and a promise of the coming "Branch," a messianic figure (Zec.6.11-13). Joshua continued to serve as high priest during the early years of the restored Jewish community in Jerusalem (Neh.12.1, 7, 10, 26). His leadership, along with that of Zerubbabel, was instrumental in the completion of the temple and the reestablishment of Jewish worship in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.2 referred to as Joshua (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), or Jeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ), or Jeshua (Aramiac יֵשׁוּעַ); a son of Jehozadak; father of Joiakim.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 대제사장. Ezr.2.2에 처음 언급되며 '여호수아'라 불림. 여호사닥의 아들. 요야김의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호사닥의 아들 여호수아(예수아라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로 이후 성전 재건을 이끈 대제사장이었다.
persons.article_ko: 여호수아(예수아라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘 성전 재건에 중대한 역할을 한 대제사장이었다. 그는 여호사닥(요사닥)의 아들이며 학개, 스가랴, 에스라, 느헤미야서에 언급된다. 여호수아는 스룹바벨과 함께 포로에서 돌아온 지도자 중에 처음 언급된다(스 2:2; 느 7:7). 그는 스룹바벨과 함께 제단을 재건하고 성전의 기초를 놓는 일을 했다(스 3:2, 8). 성전 건축이 반대에 직면했을 때 여호수아와 스룹바벨은 페르시아 당국에 성공적으로 청원하여 그 일을 계속하도록 허락받았다(스 5:2). 선지자 학개와 스가랴는 성전 재건 기간 동안 여호수아에게 격려와 지지의 메시지를 전했다(학 1:1, 12, 14; 2:2, 4; 슥 3:1-9; 6:11). 환상 중에 스가랴는 여호수아가 여호와의 사자 앞에 서 있고 사탄이 그를 고발하는 것을 보았다. 여호와는 사탄을 책망하시고 대제사장으로서 여호수아를 택하신 것을 확인하셨다(슥 3:1-5). 여호수아는 또한 상징적인 면류관과 오실 '싹'이라는 메시아적 인물에 대한 약속을 받았다(슥 6:11-13). 여호수아는 예루살렘의 회복된 유대 공동체 초기 시절에 계속 대제사장으로 섬겼다(느 12:1, 7, 10, 26). 그의 지도력은 스룹바벨의 지도력과 함께 성전 완공과 포로 이후 시대 유대인 예배의 재확립에 중요한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Joshua (or Jose) is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Joshua, also known as Jose, is mentioned in Luk.3.29 as part of the genealogy of Jesus Christ. This genealogy traces Jesus' lineage through His mother Mary's family line. Joshua/Jose is listed as the son of Eliezer and the father of Er. The genealogy spans several centuries, from Jesus back to Adam, demonstrating Jesus' connection to the ancestral line of David and the fulfillment of messianic prophecies. However, no additional information is provided about Joshua/Jose's life or the specific time period in which he lived. The variation in names (Joshua/Jose) may reflect different traditions or translations of the name.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.29 referred to as Joshua (Ἰησοῦς), or Jose (Ἰωσή); a son of Eliezer; father of Er.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.29에 처음 언급되며 '예수'라 불림. 엘리에셀의 아들. 엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여호수아(요세라고도 함)는 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 조상 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah known for his religious reforms
persons.short: Josiah was a king of Judah who instituted significant religious reforms and repaired the temple.
persons.article: Josiah was a king of Judah who reigned from approximately 640 to 609 BC. He was the son of Amon and the grandson of Manasseh (2Ki.21.24, 26; 1Ch.3.14). Josiah became king at the age of eight and reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem (2Ki.22.1; 2Ch.34.1). Josiah is best known for his religious reforms and his commitment to following the Law of the Lord. In the eighteenth year of his reign, Josiah initiated repairs to the temple (2Ki.22.3-7; 2Ch.34.8-13). During these repairs, the Book of the Law was discovered (2Ki.22.8-13; 2Ch.34.14-21). Upon hearing the words of the Law, Josiah tore his clothes in repentance and sought the guidance of the prophetess Huldah (2Ki.22.11-20; 2Ch.34.22-28). Josiah then led a comprehensive religious reform, removing pagan worship sites, idols, and practices from Judah and Jerusalem (2Ki.23.1-25; 2Ch.34.29-35:19). He renewed the covenant between the people and God and celebrated the Passover with great dedication (2Ki.23.21-23; 2Ch.35.1-19). Josiah's reign and reforms were praised by the prophets, including Jeremiah and Zephaniah (Jer.1.2; 3.6; 22.11, 18; 25.1, 3; 26.1; 35.1; 36.1-2, 9; Zep.1.1). However, Josiah's life came to a tragic end when he confronted Pharaoh Necho of Egypt at Megiddo and was killed in battle (2Ki.23.29-30; 2Ch.35.20-27). He was succeeded by his son Jehoahaz (2Ki.23.30; 2Ch.36.1). Despite the reforms Josiah implemented, Judah's unfaithfulness persisted, and the nation ultimately faced the Babylonian exile (2Ki.23.26-27; Jer.25.1-14). Nonetheless, Josiah is remembered as a righteous king who sought to turn the nation back to God.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.13.2 referred to as Josiah (יֹאשִׁיָּ֫הוּ), or Josiah (Ἰωσίας); a son of Amon and Jedidah; husband of Hamutal and Zebidah; father of Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.13.2에 처음 언급되며 '요시야'라 불림. 아몬과 여디다의 아들. 하무달, 스비다와 요시야의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편. 여호아하스, 여호야김, 시드기야와 살룸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요시야는 중요한 종교개혁을 이루고 성전을 수리한 유다 왕이었다.
persons.article_ko: 요시야는 대략 기원전 640-609년에 다스린 유다 왕이었다. 그는 아몬의 아들이며 므낫세의 손자였다(왕하 21:24, 26; 대상 3:14). 요시야는 여덟 살에 왕이 되어 예루살렘에서 삼십일 년간 다스렸다(왕하 22:1; 대하 34:1). 요시야는 종교개혁과 여호와의 율법을 따르려는 그의 헌신으로 가장 잘 알려져 있다. 통치 십팔 년째에 요시야는 성전 수리를 시작했다(왕하 22:3-7; 대하 34:8-13). 이 수리 기간 동안 율법책이 발견되었다(왕하 22:8-13; 대하 34:14-21). 율법의 말씀을 듣고 요시야는 회개하며 자기 옷을 찢고 여선지자 훌다의 지도를 구했다(왕하 22:11-20; 대하 34:22-28). 그런 다음 요시야는 유다와 예루살렘에서 이방 예배 처소와 우상, 관행을 제거하는 포괄적인 종교개혁을 이끌었다(왕하 23:1-25; 대하 34:29-35:19). 그는 백성과 하나님 사이의 언약을 갱신했고 큰 헌신으로 유월절을 지켰다(왕하 23:21-23; 대하 35:1-19). 요시야의 통치와 개혁은 예레미야와 스바냐를 포함한 선지자들에게 칭찬받았다(렘 1:2; 3:6; 22:11, 18; 25:1, 3; 26:1; 35:1; 36:1-2, 9; 습 1:1). 그러나 요시야의 삶은 그가 므깃도에서 애굽 왕 바로 느고와 대적하다가 전투에서 죽으면서 비극적인 종말을 맞았다(왕하 23:29-30; 대하 35:20-27). 그의 아들 여호아하스가 뒤를 이었다(왕하 23:30; 대하 36:1). 요시야가 실시한 개혁에도 불구하고 유다의 신실치 못함은 계속되었고, 그 민족은 결국 바벨론 포로에 직면했다(왕하 23:26-27; 렘 25:1-14). 그럼에도 불구하고 요시야는 민족을 하나님께로 돌이키고자 한 의로운 왕으로 기억된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who provided silver and gold for a crown
persons.short: Josiah (or Hen), along with others, provided silver and gold for a crown in a symbolic act during Zechariah's time.
persons.article: Josiah, also known as Hen, is mentioned in Zec.6.10 and Zec.6.14 in the context of a symbolic act during the prophet Zechariah's ministry. Zechariah was instructed to take silver and gold from the returned exiles, specifically from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had come from Babylon (Zec.6.10). Josiah (or Hen) is mentioned as the son of Zephaniah, in whose house the silver and gold were to be stored until they were used to make a crown (Zec.6.10, 14). The crown was then to be placed on the head of Joshua, the high priest, as a symbol of the coming "Branch," a messianic figure who would build the temple and rule as both priest and king (Zec.6.11-13). The name "Josiah" is used in verse 10, while "Hen" is used in verse 14. This variation may reflect different traditions or translations of the name.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Zec.6.10 referred to as Josiah (יֹאשִׁיָּ֫הוּ), or Hen (חֵן); a son of Zephaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '요시야'라 불림. 스바니야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 요시야(헨이라고도 함)는 스가랴 시대에 상징적인 행동으로 다른 이들과 함께 면류관을 만들 은과 금을 제공했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Shelomith, a returning exile
persons.short: Josiphiah was the father of Shelomith, who was among the exiles who returned with Ezra to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Josiphiah is mentioned only in Ezr.8.10. He is the father of a man whose descendants returned from the Babylonian exile. His son (referred to as Ben-Josiphiah, meaning "son of Josiphiah") led 160 males who accompanied Ezra on the return journey to Jerusalem. This return occurred during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia. The name appears in a list of family heads who participated in this important return to Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.10 only referred to as Josiphiah (יוֹסִפְיָה); father of Shelomith.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.10에 처음 언급되며 '요시뱌'라 불림. 슬로밋의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요시비야는 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 포로 중 하나였던 슬로밋의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Regem@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch(?), Jesher@1Ch.2.18(?), Shobab@1Ch.2.18(?), Ardon@1Ch.2.18(?), Mesha@1Ch.2.42(?), Haran@1Ch.2.46(?), Moza@1Ch.2.46(?), Gazez@1Ch.2.46a(?), Sheber@1Ch.2.48(?), Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48(?), Shaaph@1Ch.2.49(?), Sheva@1Ch.2.49(?), Achsah@1Ch.2.49(?)
persons.brief: A son of Jahdai, a Calebite
persons.short: Jotham was a son of Jahdai, who was a wife of Caleb.
persons.article: Jotham is mentioned in 1Ch.2.47 as one of the sons of Jahdai. The context of the passage is the genealogy of Caleb, one of the leaders of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.42-55). Caleb's descendants are listed, including his great-grandson Jahdai (1Ch.2.47). Jotham is named as one of the six sons of Jahdai, along with Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1Ch.2.47). No further information is provided about Jotham's life, occupation, or role within the family or tribe. His mention serves to complete the genealogical record of Caleb's descendants.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.47 only referred to as Jotham (יוֹתָם); son of Caleb and Jahdai; a brother of Regem, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, Shaaph, Hur(?), Jesher(?), Shobab(?), Ardon(?), Mesha(?), Haran(?), Moza(?), Gazez(?), Sheber(?), Tirhanah(?), Shaaph(?), Sheva(?) and Achsah(?).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '요단'이라 불림. 갈렙과 야대의 아들. 레겜, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요담은 갈렙의 아내였던 야대의 아들이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah and son of Uzziah
persons.short: Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was a king of Judah who reigned for sixteen years.
persons.article: Jotham was a king of Judah who reigned for sixteen years, from approximately 750 to 735 BC (2Ki.15.32-33; 2Ch.27.1). He was the son of Uzziah (also known as Azariah) and succeeded him as king (2Ki.15.7; 2Ch.26.23). Jotham became co-regent with his father Uzziah when Uzziah was struck with leprosy for burning incense in the temple (2Ki.15.5; 2Ch.26.21). After Uzziah's death, Jotham assumed full control of the kingdom (2Ki.15.7; 2Ch.26.23). During his reign, Jotham is described as doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord, following the example of his father Uzziah (2Ki.15.34; 2Ch.27.2). He rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple and carried out construction projects on the wall at Ophel (2Ch.27.3). Jotham also successfully waged war against the Ammonites, subjecting them to tribute (2Ch.27.5). He became powerful because he walked steadfastly before the Lord his God (2Ch.27.6). The prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah prophesied during Jotham's reign (Isa.1.1; Hos.1.1; Mic.1.1). Jotham died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and his son Ahaz succeeded him as king (2Ki.15.38; 2Ch.27.7, 9).
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.5 referred to as Jotham (יוֹתָם), or Jotham (Ἰωάθαμ); a son of Uzziah and Jerusha; father of Ahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.5에 처음 언급되며 '요담'이라 불림. 웃시야와 여루사의 아들. 아하스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야의 아들 요담은 유다 왕으로 십육 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 요담은 대략 기원전 750년부터 735년까지 십육 년간 다스린 유다 왕이었다(왕하 15:32-33; 대하 27:1). 그는 웃시야(아사랴라고도 함)의 아들이며 그를 이어 왕이 되었다(왕하 15:7; 대하 26:23). 요담은 웃시야가 성전에서 분향한 것 때문에 나병에 걸렸을 때 아버지와 함께 섭정왕이 되었다(왕하 15:5; 대하 26:21). 웃시야가 죽은 후 요담은 왕국을 완전히 통제하게 되었다(왕하 15:7; 대하 26:23). 그의 통치 기간 동안 요담은 아버지 웃시야의 본을 따라 여호와 보시기에 정직한 것을 행한 것으로 묘사된다(왕하 15:34; 대하 27:2). 그는 성전의 윗문을 재건하고 오벨 성벽에 건축 사업을 수행했다(대하 27:3). 요담은 또한 암몬 사람들을 성공적으로 대적하여 그들을 조공을 바치게 했다(대하 27:5). 그는 자기 하나님 여호와 앞에서 굳건히 행했기 때문에 강성해졌다(대하 27:6). 선지자 이사야, 호세아, 미가는 요담의 통치 기간에 예언했다(사 1:1; 호 1:1; 미 1:1). 요담은 죽어 다윗 성에 그의 조상들과 함께 묻혔고, 그의 아들 아하스가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다(왕하 15:38; 대하 27:7, 9).

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Youngest son of Gideon who escaped Abimelech's massacre
persons.short: Jotham, the youngest son of Gideon, was the only one to escape when Abimelech killed his seventy brothers.
persons.article: Jotham was the youngest of Gideon's seventy sons (Jdg.9.5). After Gideon's death, Abimelech, another of Gideon's sons, conspired to become king and killed his seventy brothers on one stone (Jdg.9.5). However, Jotham escaped by hiding (Jdg.9.5). Jotham went to Mount Gerizim and delivered a parable to the men of Shechem, warning them of the consequences of their actions in supporting Abimelech (Jdg.9.7-21). In the parable, the trees sought to anoint a king over them, but the worthy trees (olive, fig, and vine) refused, while the bramble accepted and threatened to devour the cedars of Lebanon (Jdg.9.8-15). Jotham then fled to Beer and remained there, fearing Abimelech (Jdg.9.21). Later, God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, causing them to turn against each other (Jdg.9.22-25). This ultimately led to Abimelech's downfall and death, which was seen as a fulfillment of Jotham's curse (Jdg.9.57).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.9.5 only referred to as Jotham (יוֹתָם); son of Gideon; a brother of Jether and Abimelech.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.9.5에 처음 언급되며 '요담'이라 불림. 기드온의 아들. 예델과 아비멜렉의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 기드온의 막내아들 요담은 아비멜렉이 그의 형제 칠십 명을 죽일 때 유일하게 도망친 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Manassite leader who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: One of two men called Jozabad who, along with other Manassite leaders, joined David at Ziklag when he was returning to fight against the Philistines.
persons.article: Jozabad is one of two men of that name in 1Ch.12.20 who were leaders from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag. The context of the passage is the listing of the warriors who allied themselves with David during his time of exile and conflict with King Saul (1Ch.12.1-22). When David was returning to Ziklag, after being dismissed by the Philistine commanders who were suspicious of his loyalty, several Manassite leaders deserted Saul's army and joined David (1Ch.12.19-20). Jozabad is named among these leaders, along with Adnah, Michael, Jediael, Elihu, and Zillethai (1Ch.12.20). These Manassite leaders were described as mighty men of valor and commanders in the army (1Ch.12.21). They provided significant military support to David, helping him in his raids against the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites, who had attacked and plundered Ziklag (1Ch.12.21; 1Sa.30.1-20).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.20a only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.20a에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요사밧이라는 이름의 두 사람 중 한 사람으로, 다른 므낫세 지도자들과 함께 다윗이 블레셋과 싸우러 돌아올 때 시글락에서 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Manassite leader who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: One of two men called Jozabad who, along with other Manassite leaders, joined David at Ziklag when he was returning to fight against the Philistines.

persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.20b에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요사밧이라는 이름의 다른 한 사람으로, 다른 므낫세 지도자들과 함께 다윗이 블레셋과 싸우러 돌아올 때 시글락에서 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Jozabad, a Benjamite warrior, was one of the mighty men who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in 1Ch.12.4 as one of the Benjamite warriors who joined David at Ziklag. The context of the passage is the listing of the mighty men who supported David during his time of exile and conflict with King Saul (1Ch.12.1-22). Jozabad, along with other Benjamite warriors such as Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty, joined David at Ziklag while David was still a fugitive from Saul (1Ch.12.1-4). These men were described as brave warriors, trained for battle and skilled with the bow, and able to shoot arrows and sling stones with either the right or left hand (1Ch.12.2). The passage highlights the support David received from various tribes, including Benjamin, Saul's own tribe (1Ch.12.29).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.4 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.4에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 용사 요사밧은 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite appointed as an overseer during Hezekiah's reign
persons.short: Jozabad, a Levite, was one of the overseers appointed by King Hezekiah to distribute the contributions to the priests and Levites.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in 2Ch.31.13 as one of the Levites appointed by King Hezekiah to oversee the distribution of contributions to the priests and Levites. The context of the passage is Hezekiah's religious reforms and the restoration of proper worship in Judah (2Ch.31.1-21). After the people brought in abundant contributions, tithes, and dedicated gifts (2Ch.31.5-6, Hezekiah appointed officers to oversee the distribution of these offerings). Jozabad, along with Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah, was appointed as an overseer under the direction of Conaniah and his brother Shimei, the chief officers (2Ch.31.12-13). These overseers were entrusted with the task of ensuring that the contributions were faithfully distributed to the priests and Levites according to their divisions and duties (2Ch.31.14-19).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 요사밧은 히스기야 왕이 제사장과 레위인들에게 헌물을 분배하도록 임명한 감독 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who contributed to the Passover celebration
persons.short: Jozabad, along with other Levitical leaders, generously provided animals for the Passover offerings during King Josiah's reign.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in 2Ch.35.9 as one of the Levitical leaders who contributed to the Passover celebrations during the reign of King Josiah. The context of the passage is Josiah's restoration of the Passover observance as part of his religious reforms (2Ch.35.1-19). In preparation for the Passover, the Levitical leaders generously provided animals for the offerings. Jozabad, along with Conaniah, Shemaiah, Nethanel, and his brothers Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, gave 5,000 lambs and young goats and 500 oxen from their own possessions for the Passover offerings (2Ch.35.9). This contribution demonstrated the Levitical leaders' support for Josiah's reforms and their commitment to the proper observance of the Passover.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.35.9 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.35.9에 처음 언급되며 '요사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요사밧은 다른 레위인 지도자들과 함께 요시야 왕의 유월절 제물로 짐승을 아낌없이 제공했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Jozabad was one of the priests who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to put them away.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in Ezr.10.22 as one of the priests who had married foreign women during the post-exilic period. The context of the passage is Ezra's reforms and the issue of intermarriage between the Israelites and the pagan peoples of the land (Ezra 9-10). Upon learning of the widespread intermarriage, Ezra led the people in confession and repentance (Ezr.9.1-10:4). The Israelites made a covenant to put away their foreign wives and children (Ezr.10.5). Jozabad is listed among the priests who had married foreign women and agreed to send them away (Ezr.10.18-22). This event highlights the importance of maintaining religious and cultural purity among the Israelites, especially in the post-exilic period when they were re-establishing their identity and covenant relationship with God.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who weighed the silver and gold offerings
persons.short: Jozabad, along with Noadiah, was a priest appointed to weigh the silver, gold, and vessels brought as offerings to the temple.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in Ezr.8.33 as one of the priests appointed to weigh the silver, gold, and vessels brought as offerings to the temple in Jerusalem. The context of the passage is Ezra's journey from Babylon to Jerusalem, during which he and his companions transported these offerings (Ezr.8.24-34). Upon their arrival in Jerusalem, the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed and entrusted to the care of specific priests and Levites. Jozabad, son of Jeshua, along with Noadiah, son of Binnui, were the priests appointed to weigh and record the offerings (Ezr.8.33). The careful weighing and recording of the offerings demonstrated the importance of accountability and stewardship in handling the resources dedicated to the temple.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.33 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד); a son of Jeshua.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite leader in charge of outside work
persons.short: Jozabad, one of the leaders of the Levites, was in charge of the outside work of the house of God.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in Neh.11.16 as one of the leaders of the Levites who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God. The context of the passage is the listing of the people who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.1-36). Jozabad, along with Shabbethai, is described as being in charge of the outside work of the house of God (Neh.11.16). This likely involved overseeing maintenance, repairs, and other tasks related to the exterior of the temple complex. The mention of Jozabad's role highlights the various responsibilities of the Levites in maintaining and serving in the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.16 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
persons.short: Jozabad was one of the Levites who helped the people understand the Law as Ezra read it aloud.
persons.article: Jozabad is mentioned in Neh.8.7 as one of the Levites who helped the people understand the Law of Moses as it was being read aloud by Ezra. The context of the passage is the public reading of the Law during the Feast of Tabernacles, after the Israelites had returned from Babylonian exile (Neh.8.1-18). As Ezra read from the Book of the Law, the Levites, including Jozabad, instructed the people and helped them understand the meaning of the text (Neh.8.7-8). This involved translating or explaining the Law, as many of the people may have been unfamiliar with the original Hebrew after years in exile. The Levites' role in teaching and interpreting the Law was crucial for the spiritual renewal of the Israelites as they sought to re-establish their covenant relationship with God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.7 only referred to as Jozabad (יוֹזָבָד).

persons.description: Ammonite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of the servants who killed King Joash
persons.short: Jozacar (or Zabad), along with Jehozabad, was one of the servants who conspired against and killed King Joash of Judah.
persons.article: Jozacar, also known as Zabad, is mentioned in 2Ki.12.22 and 2Ch.24.26 as one of the servants who conspired against and killed King Joash of Judah. The context of the passage is the assassination of Joash and the succession of his son Amaziah (2Ki.12.20-21; 2Ch.24.25-27). Jozacar, the son of Shimeath, along with Jehozabad, the son of Shomer, plotted against King Joash and struck him down at Beth-millo (2Ki.12.21; 2Ch.24.26). The reason for their conspiracy is not explicitly stated, but it may have been related to Joash's earlier abandonment of the Lord's ways and his ordering the execution of the priest Zechariah (2Ch.24.17-22). After killing Joash, the servants buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings (2Ch.24.25). Joash's son Amaziah succeeded him as king (2Ki.12.21; 2Ch.24.27).
persons.summary: A man of the Ammonites living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.12.21 referred to as Jozacar (יוֹזָכָר), or Jozacar (יוֹזָבָד), or Zabad (זָבָד); a son of Shimeath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 암몬 사람. 2Ki.12.21에 처음 언급되며 '요사갈'이라 불림. 시므앗의 남편(이름 미상)와 시므앗의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 요사갈(사밧이라고도 함)은 여호사밧과 함께 유다 왕 요아스를 암살하는 음모에 가담한 신하 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest whose descendants married foreign women
persons.short: Among the descendants of Jozadak, some priests were found to have married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Jozadak is mentioned in Ezr.10.18 in the context of the priests who had married foreign women during the post-exilic period. The passage is part of Ezra's reforms and his efforts to address the issue of intermarriage between the Israelites and the pagan peoples of the land (Ezra 9-10). In the list of priests who had married foreign women, some of the descendants of Jozadak are mentioned (Ezr.10.18). This indicates that even among the priestly families, there were those who had violated the commandment to refrain from intermarrying with the surrounding nations (Deu.7.3-4). As part of the covenant made under Ezra's leadership, these priests agreed to put away their foreign wives and children (Ezr.10.19). This event underscores the importance of maintaining religious and cultural purity among the Israelites, particularly in the post-exilic period when they were re-establishing their identity and covenant relationship with God.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.18 only referred to as Jozadak (יוֹצָדָק); father of Jeshua.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '요사닥'이라 불림. 예수아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요사닥의 후손 중 일부 제사장은 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼한 것으로 밝혀졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Father of musicians who play the lyre and pipe
persons.short: Jubal was the father of all who play the lyre and pipe.
persons.article: Jubal is mentioned in Gen.4.21 as the son of Lamech and Adah, and the brother of Jabal. He is described as the father of all who play the lyre and pipe, indicating his role in the early development of musical instruments. The context of the passage is the genealogy of Cain, Adam and Eve's firstborn son. Jubal is part of the seventh generation from Adam, and his mention highlights the advancement of culture and the arts in the pre-flood world. As the father of musicians, Jubal's influence likely extended to the invention or popularization of stringed and wind instruments. His legacy suggests that music played a significant role in ancient societies, even in the earliest stages of human history. No further details are provided about Jubal's life, family, or specific musical achievements. His brief mention serves to demonstrate the development of human skills and the diversification of occupations among the descendants of Cain.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time before the Flood, only mentioned at Gen.4.21 only referred to as Jubal (יוּבָ֑ל); son of Lamech and Adah; a brother of Jabal, Tubal-cain, Naamah.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '유발'이라 불림. 라멕과 아다의 아들. 야발, 두발가인과 나아마의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 유발은 수금과 퉁소를 잡는 모든 자의 조상이었다.

persons.brief: Israelite tribe, kingdom, and province
persons.short: Judah, also known as the Jews or Judea, refers to the Israelite tribe, the southern kingdom, and the Roman province in various biblical contexts.
persons.article: Judah, Jews, and Judea are terms used throughout the Bible to refer to the Israelite tribe, the southern kingdom, and the Roman province, depending on the historical context. Judah was the fourth son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah (Gen.29.35 and became the founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel). The tribe of Judah played a prominent role in Israel's history, with notable figures such as Caleb, Othniel, and King David coming from this tribe. After the reign of Solomon, the kingdom of Israel split into two: the northern kingdom of Israel and the southern kingdom of Judah (1Kings 12). The southern kingdom, which included the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, remained loyal to the Davidic dynasty and the worship of God in Jerusalem. The kingdom of Judah lasted from about 930 BC until the Babylonian conquest in 586 BC. Following the Babylonian exile, many Jews returned to the land of Judah, now a province of the Persian Empire (Ezra 1-6). During the Second Temple period, Judea became a province of the Roman Empire. In the New Testament, the terms "Jews" and "Judea" are often used to refer to the Jewish people and the region they inhabited. The history of Judah, the Jews, and Judea is a central focus of the biblical narrative, with many of the key events, prophecies, and teachings revolving around this people and their relationship with God. The prophets, such as Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel, often addressed their messages to Judah and warned of judgment for disobedience while also offering hope for restoration. In the New Testament, Jesus Christ, the Messiah, is born in Judea and is recognized as the King of the Jews (Mat.2.2). The early Christian church began in Jerusalem, and many of the first converts were Jews (Acts 2). Throughout the Bible, God's covenant relationship with the people of Judah, the Jews, and the inhabitants of Judea remains a central theme, highlighting His faithfulness, judgment, and redemptive purposes for all nations through the Jewish Messiah, Jesus Christ.
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Judah living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.29.35 referred to as Judah (יְהוּדָה), or Judah (Aramiac יְהוּד), or Jew or Jewish or Judean or "those of Judah" (יְהוּדִי), or Jew (Aramiac יְהוּדַי), or Judah (Ἰουδά), or Judah (Ἰούδας), or Jew or Jewish people or "of Judea" (Ἰουδαῖος), or Jew (Ἰουδαΐζω), or Jewish (Ἰουδαϊκός), or Jew (Ἰουδαϊκῶς); son of Israel and Leah; a brother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah; half-brother of: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph and Benjamin; husband of Bath-shua and Tamar; father of Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.29.35에 처음 언급되며 '유다'라 불림. 이스라엘과 레아의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 단, 납달리, 갓, 아셀, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 딸과 다말의 남편. 엘, 오난, 셀라, 베레스와 세라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유다(유대인 또는 유대라고도 함)는 여러 성경 문맥에서 이스라엘 지파, 남유다 왕국, 로마의 유대 속주를 가리킨다.
persons.article_ko: 유다, 유대인, 유대는 성경 전체에서 역사적 맥락에 따라 이스라엘 지파, 남유다 왕국, 로마 속주를 가리키는 데 사용되는 용어다. 유다는 이스라엘(야곱)과 레아의 넷째 아들이었으며(창 29:35) 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나의 창설자가 되었다. 유다 지파는 이스라엘 역사에서 두드러진 역할을 했으며, 갈렙, 옷니엘, 다윗 왕 같은 저명한 인물들이 이 지파에서 나왔다. 솔로몬 통치 이후 이스라엘 왕국은 북이스라엘 왕국과 남유다 왕국 둘로 나뉘었다(열왕기상 12장). 유다와 베냐민 지파를 포함한 남왕국은 다윗 왕조와 예루살렘에서의 하나님 예배에 계속 충성했다. 유다 왕국은 대략 기원전 930년부터 기원전 586년 바벨론 정복까지 지속되었다. 바벨론 포로 이후 많은 유대인이 이제 페르시아 제국의 한 속주가 된 유다 땅으로 돌아왔다(에스라 1-6장). 제2성전 시대에 유대는 로마 제국의 한 속주가 되었다. 신약에서 '유대인'과 '유대'라는 용어는 종종 유대 민족과 그들이 거주한 지역을 가리키는 데 사용된다. 유다, 유대인, 유대의 역사는 성경 이야기의 중심 초점으로, 많은 핵심 사건, 예언, 가르침이 이 백성과 그들의 하나님과의 관계를 중심으로 전개된다. 이사야, 예레미야, 에스겔 같은 선지자들은 종종 그들의 메시지를 유다에게 전하며 불순종에 대한 심판을 경고하는 동시에 회복에 대한 소망도 제시했다. 신약에서 메시아이신 예수 그리스도는 유대에서 태어나셨고 유대인의 왕으로 인정받으신다(마 2:2). 초대 그리스도교 교회는 예루살렘에서 시작되었고, 최초 개종자 중 많은 사람이 유대인이었다(사도행전 2장). 성경 전체에서 유다 백성, 유대인, 유대 거주민들과의 하나님의 언약 관계는 중심 주제로 남아, 유대인 메시아 예수 그리스도를 통한 모든 민족에 대한 그분의 신실하심, 심판, 구속의 목적을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Judah is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Judah is mentioned in Luk.3.30 as part of the genealogy of Jesus Christ. This genealogy traces Jesus' lineage through His mother Mary's family line, back to Adam. In the genealogy, Judah is listed as the father of Simeon and the son of Joseph. He is one of the ancestors in the period between David and the Babylonian exile. The inclusion of Judah in the genealogy demonstrates Jesus' connection to the tribe of Judah and the fulfillment of the messianic prophecies, which indicated that the Messiah would come from the line of David and the tribe of Judah (Gen.49.10; Isa.11.1-5; Mic.5.2). No additional information is provided about this specific Judah's life or the historical context in which he lived. His mention serves primarily to establish Jesus' lineage and to affirm His messianic identity.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.30 only referred to as Judah (Ἰούδας); a son of Joseph; father of Simeon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.30에 처음 언급되며 '유다'라 불림. 요셉의 아들. 시므온의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유다는 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader of Judahites living in Jerusalem
persons.short: Judah was a leader of the people of Judah living in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Judah is identified as the son of Senuah in a list of leaders living in Jerusalem after some of the Jewish exiles returned from Babylon (Neh.11.9). He is described as being "second over the city," likely indicating a position of authority under the primary city official. The people under his leadership were from the tribe of Judah. No other details are provided about Judah's life or achievements. He is not to be confused with the patriarch Judah, son of Israel (or 'Jacob'), or the tribe and kingdom that bore his name.

persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.9에 처음 언급되며 '유다'라 불림. 핫스누아의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 유다는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 유다 백성의 지도자였다.
