persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 아론의 대적자. Exo.6.21에 처음 언급되며 '고라'라 불림. 이스할의 아들. 네벡, 시그리와 슬로밋의 형제. 앗실, 엘가나와 에비아삽의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 고라는 모세와 아론을 대적하여 반역한 레위인으로, 그 후손은 성전 음악가와 문지기가 되었다.
persons.article_ko: 고라는 광야에서 모세와 아론을 대적하는 반역을 이끈 레위인이었다(민수기 16장). 그는 고핫 가문 출신 이스할의 아들이었다(출 6:21, 24). 고라는 다단, 아비람, 그리고 저명한 공동체 지도자 이백오십 명과 함께 모세와 아론이 회중 위에 스스로를 높인다고 고발했다(민 16:1-3). 고라의 추종자들이 향 예물을 드렸을 때 여호와는 불로 그들을 멸하셨다(민 16:35). 땅이 갈라져 고라와 다단, 아비람, 그리고 그들의 가족을 삼켰다(민 16:31-33). 그러나 고라의 아들들은 죽지 않았다(민 26:11). 반역자들의 놋 향로는 여호와를 대적하여 반역하지 말라는 상기물로 제단을 덮는 데 사용되었다(민 16:38-40). 고라의 후손은 성전 음악가(대상 6:22, 37; 시 42-49편; 84-88편)와 문지기(대상 9:19; 26:1, 19)가 되었다. 일부는 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 용맹한 용사였고(대상 12:6), 다른 이들은 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착했다(대상 9:31). 고라 사람들은 또한 여호사밧 통치 기간에 노래했고(대하 20:19) 레위인 가문 명단에 올라 있다(민 26:58).

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Teman@Gen.36.11-Job, Omar@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Zepho@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Amalek@Gen.36.12-
persons.brief: Edomite chief, descendant of Eliphaz
persons.short: Korah, an Edomite chief, descendant of Eliphaz, son of Esau.
persons.article: Korah was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Eliphaz, the son of Esau (Gen.36.16). He was one of the clan leaders of Edom.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.36.16 only referred to as Korah (קֹ֫רַח); son of Eliphaz; a brother of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz and Amalek.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.16에 처음 언급되며 '고라'라 불림. 엘리바스와 엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 데만, 오말, 스보, 가담, 그나스와 아말렉의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 고라는 에서의 아들 엘리바스를 통한 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Esau
persons.short: Korah, son of Esau and Oholibamah
persons.article: Korah was a son of Esau and his wife Oholibamah (Gen.36.5, 18; 1Ch.1.35). He was born in Canaan before Esau moved his family to Seir (Gen.36.5-8). Korah was a grandson of Zibeon the Hivite (Gen.36.14). He became one of the chiefs of Edom (Gen.36.18).
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.5 only referred to as Korah (קֹ֫רַח); son of Esau and Oholibamah; a brother of Jeush and Jalam; half-brother of: Eliphaz and Reuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.5에 처음 언급되며 '고라'라 불림. 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들. 엘리바스, 르우엘, 여우스와 얄람의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 고라는 에서와 오홀리바마의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper
persons.short: Kore, a Levite gatekeeper, descendant of Korah
persons.article: Kore was a Levite gatekeeper, a descendant of Korah (1Ch.9.19). He belonged to the Korahite clan, which was responsible for guarding the thresholds of the tent of meeting (1Ch.9.19). Kore and his relatives were also in charge of guarding the entrance to the temple during David's reign (1Ch.26.1). They faithfully carried out their duties as gatekeepers.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.19 only referred to as Kore (קוֹרֵא); son of Ebiasaph; a brother of Assir.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.19에 처음 언급되며 '고레'라 불림. 에비아삽의 아들. 앗실의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 고레는 고라의 후손인 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite in charge of freewill offerings
persons.short: Kore, a Levite in charge of distributing freewill offerings during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Kore, the son of Imnah the Levite, was appointed by King Hezekiah to be in charge of distributing the freewill offerings, contributions, and dedicated gifts brought to the temple (2Ch.31.14). He served at the East Gate and was responsible for ensuring that the offerings were properly distributed among the priests and Levites according to their divisions (2Ch.31.15). Kore's appointment demonstrates Hezekiah's efforts to restore proper worship and support for the Levites during his reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.14 only referred to as Kore (קוֹרֵא); a son of Imnah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.14에 처음 언급되며 '고레'라 불림. 임나의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 고레는 히스기야 왕 시대에 자원 예물 분배를 담당한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Hepher@1Ch.4.6, Temeni@1Ch.4.6, Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6, Zereth@1Ch.4.7, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Ethnan@1Ch.4.7
persons.brief: Son of Ashhur, a Judahite
persons.short: Koz, a descendant of Judah through Ashhur.
persons.article: Koz was a son of Ashhur and a descendant of Judah (1Ch.4.8). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, but no additional information is provided about him in the Bible. Koz lived during the period of the judges or the early monarchy in Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.8 only referred to as Koz (קוֹץ); son of Ashhur and Helah; a brother of Haahashtari, Zereth, Izhar and Ethnan; half-brother of: Ahuzzam, Hepher and Temeni; father of Anub, Zobebah, Harum and Jabez(?).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.8에 처음 언급되며 '고스'라 불림. 아스훌과 헬라의 아들. 아훗삼, 헤벨, 데므니, 하아하스타리, 세렛, 이스할과 에드난의 형제. 아눕, 소베바, 하룸과 야베스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 고스는 아스훌을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Shelah, a Judahite
persons.short: Laadah, a son of Shelah and descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Laadah was a son of Shelah and a descendant of Judah (1Ch.4.21). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically in the family line of Shelah. Laadah was likely born in the land of Canaan during the period of the patriarchs or the early settlement of the tribes.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.21 only referred to as Laadah (לַעְדָּה); son of Shelah; a brother of Er, Jokim, Joash and Saraph; father or founder of Mareshah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '라아다'라 불림. 셀라의 아들. 엘, 요김, 요아스와 사랍의 형제. 마레사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라아다는 셀라의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Brother of Rebekah; father of Leah and Rachel
persons.short: Laban, the brother of Rebekah and father of Jacob's wives, Leah and Rachel.
persons.article: Laban was the son of Bethuel and the brother of Rebekah, Isaac's wife (Gen.24.29). He lived in Paddan Aram, where he welcomed Abraham's servant who sought a wife for Isaac (Gen.24.29-51). Years later, Laban hosted his nephew Israel (or 'Jacob'), who fled from his brother Esau (Gen.27.43; 28.2,5). Laban arranged for Jacob to marry his daughters, Leah and Rachel, in exchange for fourteen years of labor (Gen.29). Laban also gave his maidservants, Zilpah and Bilhah, to Jacob as concubines (Gen.30.9,22). Jacob's wives bore him eleven sons and a daughter while living with Laban (Gen.29.31-30.24; 46.18,25). Laban and Jacob had a tense relationship due to Laban's deception and Jacob's prosperity (Gen.30-31). After Jacob fled with his family, Laban pursued them but ultimately made a covenant with Jacob before departing (Gen.31). Laban is last mentioned when Jacob sent messengers to Esau, stating that he had stayed with Laban (Gen.32.4).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.24.29 only referred to as Laban (לָבָן); son of Bethuel; a brother of Rebekah; father of Rachel and Leah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.24.29에 처음 언급되며 '라반'이라 불림. 브두엘의 아들. 리브가의 형제. 라헬과 레아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라반은 리브가의 형제이며 야곱의 아내 레아와 라헬의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 라반은 브두엘의 아들이며 이삭의 아내 리브가의 형제였다(창 24:29). 그는 밧단아람에 살았고, 그곳에서 이삭을 위해 아내를 구하러 온 아브라함의 종을 환대했다(창 24:29-51). 여러 해 후 라반은 형제 에서를 피해 도망친 조카 이스라엘(야곱)을 대접했다(창 27:43; 28:2, 5). 라반은 야곱이 그의 딸들인 레아와 라헬과 결혼하도록 주선했는데, 그 대가로 십사 년간 일하도록 했다(창세기 29장). 라반은 또한 자기 여종들인 실바와 빌하를 야곱에게 첩으로 주었다(창 30:9, 22). 야곱의 아내들은 라반과 함께 사는 동안 그에게 열한 아들과 딸 하나를 낳아주었다(창 29:31-30:24; 46:18, 25). 라반의 속임수와 야곱의 번영으로 인해 라반과 야곱은 긴장된 관계를 가졌다(창세기 30-31장). 야곱이 가족과 함께 도망친 후 라반은 그들을 추격했으나 결국 떠나기 전 야곱과 언약을 맺었다(창세기 31장). 라반은 야곱이 에서에게 사신을 보내며 자신이 라반과 함께 머물렀다고 말할 때 마지막으로 언급된다(창 32:4).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Descendant of Ephraim
persons.short: Ladan, a descendant of Ephraim.
persons.article: Ladan was a descendant of Ephraim, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim (1Ch.7.26). He was the son of Tahan and the father of Ammihud. Ladan lived during the period of the judges or the early monarchy in Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.26 only referred to as Ladan (לַעְדָּן); a son of Tahan; father of Ammihud.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.26에 처음 언급되며 '라단'이라 불림. 다한의 아들. 암미훗의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라단은 에브라임의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Eliasaph, a Gershonite Levite
persons.short: Lael, the father of Eliasaph, a leader of the Gershonite Levites.
persons.article: Lael was the father of Eliasaph, who was a leader of the Gershonite clan of the Levites during the wilderness wanderings (Num.3.24). The Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, and hangings (Num.3.25-26). Lael's son, Eliasaph, was appointed as the chief of the Gershonite families (Num.3.24).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.3.24 only referred to as Lael (לָאֵל); father of Eliasaph.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '라엘'이라 불림. 엘리아삽의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라엘은 게르손 계열 레위인 지도자 엘리아삽의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jahath, a Judahite
persons.short: Lahad, a descendant of Judah through Jahath.
persons.article: Lahad was a son of Jahath and a descendant of Judah (1Ch.4.2). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, but no additional information is provided about him in the Bible. Lahad likely lived during the period of the judges or the early monarchy in Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.2 only referred to as Lahad (לָ֑הַד); son of Jahath; a brother of Ahumai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '라핫'이라 불림. 야핫의 아들. 아후매의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 라핫은 야핫을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Brother of Goliath the Gittite
persons.short: Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, was killed by Elhanan the Bethlehemite.
persons.article: Lahmi was the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the Philistine champion who was killed by David (1Ch.20.5). In another account, he is referred to as "the brother of Goliath the Gittite" (2Sa.21.19). Lahmi was killed by Elhanan, son of Jair the Bethlehemite, during a battle between the Israelites and the Philistines at Gob (2Sa.21.19; 1Ch.20.5). The exact timing of this event is unclear, but it likely occurred during the reign of David. Lahmi's death, along with the defeat of other Philistine warriors, demonstrated the Israelites' military prowess under David's leadership.
persons.summary: A gigantic man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.21.19 referred to as Lahmi or [brother of] Goliath (לַחְמִי); son of Rapha; a brother of Goliath, Ishbi-benob, Saph, huge man.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 거인. 2Sa.21.16에 처음 언급되며 '라흐미'라 불림. Rapha의 아들. 골리앗, 이스비브놉, 삽과 거인의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 라흐미는 골리앗의 형제로, 베들레헴 사람 엘하난에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Michal's husband Palti (or 'Paltiel')
persons.short: Laish, the father of Palti (or 'Paltiel'), to whom Saul gave his daughter Michal in marriage.
persons.article: Laish was the father of Palti (or 'Paltiel'), a man from Gallim (1Sa.25.44). King Saul gave his daughter Michal, who was previously married to David, to Palti as a wife (1Sa.25.44). After Saul's death, David demanded that Michal be returned to him as part of a political agreement with Abner, the commander of Saul's army (2Sa.3.12-16). Paltiel followed Michal, weeping, as she was taken back to David, until Abner ordered him to return home (2Sa.3.15-16).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.25.44 referred to as Laish (לוּשׁ), or Laish (לַ֫יִשׁ); father of Palti.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.25.44에 처음 언급되며 '라이스'라 불림. 발디의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라이스는 사울이 딸 미갈을 아내로 준 발디(발디엘이라고도 함)의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Descendant of Cain; first polygamist mentioned in the Bible
persons.short: Lamech, a descendant of Cain, was the first polygamist mentioned in the Bible.
persons.article: Lamech was a descendant of Cain, the son of Adam and Eve (Gen.4.18). He was the father of Jabal, Jubal, and Tubal-cain (Gen.4.20-22). Lamech is notable for being the first polygamist mentioned in the Bible, having married two women, Adah and Zillah (Gen.4.19). He is also known for his speech to his wives, in which he boasted about killing a man for wounding him and claimed that he would be avenged seventy-sevenfold, in contrast to the sevenfold vengeance promised to Cain (Gen.4.23-24). This speech suggests a progression of violence and a disregard for the sanctity of human life among Cain's descendants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.4.18 only referred to as Lamech (לֶ֫מֶךְ); a son of Methushael; husband of Adah and Zillah; father of Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, Naamah.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '라멕'이라 불림. 므드사엘의 아들. 아다와 씰라의 남편. 야발, 유발, 두발가인과 나아마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라멕은 가인의 후손으로, 성경에 언급된 최초의 일부다처자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Father of Noah; lived 777 years
persons.short: Lamech, the father of Noah, lived 777 years.
persons.article: Lamech was the son of Methuselah and the father of Noah (Gen.5.25,28-29). He was born when Methuselah was 187 years old (Gen.5.25). Lamech named his son Noah, saying, "This one will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed" (Gen.5.29). Lamech lived 595 years after the birth of Noah and had other sons and daughters (Gen.5.30). He died at the age of 777, making him the second-oldest person mentioned in the Bible after his father, Methuselah (Gen.5.31). Lamech is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.36 and in the genealogy of Adam in the book of Chronicles )(1Ch.1.3). His life and legacy are significant in the context of the pre-flood world and the lineage of the patriarchs leading to Noah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.5.25 referred to as Lamech (לֶ֫מֶךְ), or Lamech (Λάμεχ); a son of Methuselah; father of Noah.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.5.25에 처음 언급되며 '라멕'이라 불림. 므두셀라의 아들. 노아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라멕은 노아의 아버지로 칠백칠십칠 년을 살았다.

persons.description: Woman living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Husband of Deborah the prophetess and judge
persons.short: Lappidoth, the husband of Deborah, a prophetess and judge in Israel.
persons.article: Lappidoth was the husband of Deborah, a prophetess and judge who led Israel during a time of oppression by the Canaanites (Jdg.4.4). No further information is provided about Lappidoth in the Bible, and he is not mentioned in the account of Deborah's leadership and the victory over the Canaanite army led by Sisera (Jdg.4-5). It is possible that Lappidoth supported Deborah in her role as a judge and prophetess, but the biblical text does not provide any specific details about his life or their relationship.
persons.summary: A woman living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at Jdg.4.4 only referred to as Lappidoth (לַפִּידוֹת); wife of Deborah.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 여성. Jdg.4.4에 처음 언급되며 '랍비돗'이라 불림. 드보라의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 랍비돗은 여선지자이며 사사인 드보라의 남편이었다.

persons.description: Mary's brother living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Brother of Mary and Martha; raised from the dead
persons.short: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, was raised from the dead by Jesus (<ref="Jhn.11.1-44; 12.1-2,9-11">Jhn.11.1-44; 12.1-2,9-11</ref>).
persons.article: Lazarus was the brother of Mary and Martha, who lived in the village of Bethany (Jhn.11.1). Jesus loved Lazarus and his sisters (Jhn.11.5). When Lazarus fell ill, his sisters sent word to Jesus, but by the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been dead for four days (Jhn.11.6,17). Jesus went to the tomb and called for Lazarus to come out, and Lazarus emerged, still wrapped in burial cloths (Jhn.11.43-44). This miraculous sign led many to believe in Jesus (Jhn.11.45). Later, Jesus visited Lazarus' home, where Martha served a meal and Mary anointed Jesus' feet with perfume (Jhn.12.1-3). The chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus because his resurrection caused many to believe in Jesus (Jhn.12.9-11). Lazarus' story demonstrates Jesus' power over death and foreshadows His own resurrection.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Jhn.11.1 only referred to as Lazarus (Λάζαρος); a brother of Martha and Mary.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 마리아의 형제. Jhn.11.1에 처음 언급되며 '나사로'라 불림. 나사로의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 마르다와 마리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마리아와 마르다의 형제 나사로는 예수님에 의해 죽음에서 살아났다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man
persons.short: Lazarus, a poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus (<ref="Luk.16.20-25">Luk.16.20-25</ref>).
persons.article: Lazarus is the name given to the poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus (Luk.16.19-31). In the parable, Lazarus is described as a beggar covered with sores who longed to eat the crumbs falling from the rich man's table (Luk.16.20-21). When both men died, Lazarus was carried by angels to Abraham's side in heaven, while the rich man found himself in Hades, in torment (Luk.16.22-23). The rich man called out to Abraham, asking him to send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool his tongue (Luk.16.24). However, Abraham replied that a great chasm separated them and that it was impossible for anyone to cross from one side to the other (Luk.16.25-26). The parable emphasizes the reversal of fortunes in the afterlife and the importance of caring for the poor and needy in this life.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.16.20 only referred to as Lazarus (Λάζαρος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.16.20에 처음 언급되며 '나사로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 나사로는 예수님의 부자와 나사로의 비유에 나오는 가난한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-
persons.brief: Wife of Jacob; mother of six sons and Dinah
persons.short: Leah, the first wife of Jacob and mother of six of his sons and his daughter Dinah.
persons.article: Leah was the elder daughter of Laban, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's mother (Gen.29.16). Israel (or 'Jacob') agreed to work for Laban for seven years to marry Rachel, Leah's younger sister (Gen.29.18). However, Laban deceived Jacob and gave him Leah instead, requiring him to work another seven years for Rachel (Gen.29.23-28). Leah bore Jacob six sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, as well as a daughter, Dinah (Gen.29.32-35; 30.17-21). Despite being the less favored wife, Leah hoped to gain Jacob's affection through childbearing (Gen.29.32). Leah accompanied Jacob when he left Laban's household and reconciled with his brother Esau (Gen.31.4,14; 33.1-2,7). She is last mentioned as being buried with Jacob in the cave of Machpelah (Gen.49.31). Leah's sons became the ancestors of six of the twelve tribes of Israel (Gen.35.23; 46.15; 49.1-28).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.29.16 only referred to as Leah (לֵאָה); daughter of Laban; a sister of Rachel; wife of Israel; mother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.29.16에 처음 언급되며 '레아'라 불림. 라반의 딸. 라헬의 자매. 이스라엘의 아내. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 잇사갈, 스불론과 디나의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 레아는 야곱의 첫 아내이며 그의 여섯 아들과 딸 디나의 어머니였다.
persons.article_ko: 레아는 야곱의 어머니 리브가의 형제인 라반의 맏딸이었다(창 29:16). 이스라엘(야곱)은 레아의 여동생 라헬과 결혼하기 위해 라반을 위해 칠 년간 일하기로 동의했다(창 29:18). 그러나 라반은 야곱을 속여 대신 레아를 주었고, 라헬을 위해 다시 칠 년을 더 일하도록 요구했다(창 29:23-28). 레아는 야곱에게 여섯 아들 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 잇사갈, 스불론과 딸 디나를 낳아주었다(창 29:32-35; 30:17-21). 덜 사랑받는 아내였음에도 레아는 자녀를 낳음으로써 야곱의 애정을 얻기를 바랐다(창 29:32). 레아는 야곱이 라반의 집을 떠나 형제 에서와 화해할 때 그와 동행했다(창 31:4, 14; 33:1-2, 7). 그녀는 야곱과 함께 막벨라 굴에 묻힌 것으로 마지막으로 언급된다(창 49:31). 레아의 아들들은 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 여섯 지파의 조상이 되었다(창 35:23; 46:15; 49:1-28).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Lebanah or Lebana, whose descendants were among the temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Lebanah, also known as Lebana, was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.45; Neh.7.48). The temple servants were assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple (Ezr.8.20). Lebanah's descendants were among the 392 Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezr.2.43,45; Neh.7.46,48).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.45 referred to as Lebanah or Lebana (לְבָנָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.45에 처음 언급되며 '르바나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르바나(레바나라고도 함)의 후손은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중에 있었다.

persons.description: Man or town at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Er, a Judahite
persons.short: Lecah, a descendant of Judah through Er.
persons.article: Lecah was a son of Er and a descendant of Judah (1Ch.4.21). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically in the line of Shelah. No additional information is provided about Lecah in the Bible. He likely lived during the period of the patriarchs or the early settlement of the tribes in Canaan.
persons.summary: A man or town of the tribe of Judah at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.21 only referred to as Lecah (לֵכָה); a son of Er.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 인물 또는 지명. 1Ch.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '레가'라 불림. 엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레가는 에르를 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: People from Lehab
persons.siblings: Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Anamim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Pathrusim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Casluhim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Caphtorim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Mizraim; progenitor of a people group
persons.short: Lehabim, a son of Mizraim and progenitor of a people group.
persons.article: Lehabim was one of the sons of Mizraim, who was a son of Ham (Gen.10.13; 1Ch.1.11). He is mentioned in the Table of Nations, which records the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. Lehabim is listed among the descendants of Ham, specifically as a son of Mizraim, who is associated with Egypt. The Lehabim are believed to be the ancestors of the Libyans, a people group that inhabited the region west of Egypt in North Africa. However, the exact relationship between the Lehabim and the historical Libyans is not certain.
persons.summary: People from Lehab first mentioned at Gen.10.13 only referred to as Lehabim (לְהָבִים); descended from Egypt along with Ludim, Anamim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim and Caphtorim.
persons.summary_ko: 르합 사람. Gen.10.13에 처음 언급되며 '르하빔'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 루딤, 아나밈, 납두힘, 바드루심, 가슬루힘과 갑도림의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 르하빔은 미스라임의 아들이며 한 민족의 조상이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: King mentioned in Proverbs; his mother taught him wisdom
persons.short: Lemuel, a king whose wise sayings are recorded in Proverbs 31, as taught by his mother.
persons.article: Lemuel is mentioned in the opening verse of Proverbs 31 as a king to whom the sayings in this chapter are attributed (Pro.31.1). The chapter contains the words of King Lemuel, which were taught to him by his mother (Pro.31.1). In her teaching, Lemuel's mother warns him against giving his strength to women and urges him not to drink wine or strong drink, as it is not fitting for kings (Pro.31.3-7). She also instructs him to speak up for the mute, defend the rights of the poor and needy, and judge righteously (Pro.31.8-9). The identity and reign of King Lemuel are not specified in the Bible, and he is not mentioned elsewhere in the scriptures. Some scholars suggest that Lemuel may have been a non-Israelite king or a symbolic name representing a wise and righteous ruler. The chapter concludes with a description of a virtuous wife, often referred to as the "Proverbs 31 woman" (Pro.31.10-31).
persons.summary: A king living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at Pro.31.1 only referred to as Lemuel (לְמוּאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. Pro.31.1에 처음 언급되며 '르무엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르무엘은 그의 어머니가 가르친 지혜로운 말이 잠언 31장에 기록된 왕이었다.

persons.description: People from Letush(?)
persons.brief: Son of Dedan, descendant of Abraham and Keturah
persons.short: Letushim, a son of Dedan and descendant of Abraham and Keturah.
persons.article: Letushim was one of the sons of Dedan, who was a son of Jokshan, born to Abraham and his wife Keturah (Gen.25.3). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's descendants through Keturah, which is recorded after the death of Sarah. The Letushim are listed among the descendants of Jokshan, along with the Asshurim and Leummim. No further information is provided about Letushim or his descendants in the biblical record. It is likely that they became a tribe or clan that settled in the region of Arabia, as many of Abraham's descendants through Keturah are associated with Arab tribes.
persons.summary: People from Letush(?) of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.25.3 only referred to as Letushim (לְטוּשִׁם); descended from Dedan along with Asshurim and Leummim.
persons.summary_ko: 르두시 족속. Gen.25.3에 처음 언급되며 '르두시'라 불림. 드단의 자녀. 앗수르와 르움미의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 르두심은 드단의 아들이며 아브라함과 그두라를 통한 후손이었다.

persons.description: People from Leumm(?)
persons.brief: Son of Dedan, descendant of Abraham and Keturah
persons.short: Leummim, a son of Dedan and descendant of Abraham and Keturah.
persons.article: Leummim was one of the sons of Dedan, who was a son of Jokshan, born to Abraham and his wife Keturah (Gen.25.3). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's descendants through Keturah, which is recorded after the death of Sarah. The Leummim are listed among the descendants of Jokshan, along with the Asshurim and Letushim. No further information is provided about Leummim or his descendants in the biblical record. It is likely that they became a tribe or clan that settled in the region of Arabia, as many of Abraham's descendants through Keturah are associated with Arab tribes.
persons.summary: People from Leumm(?) of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.25.3 only referred to as Leummim (לְאֻמִּ֑ים); descended from Dedan along with Asshurim and Letushim.
persons.summary_ko: 르움미 족속. Gen.25.3에 처음 언급되며 '르움미'라 불림. 드단의 자녀. 앗수르와 르두시의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 르움미는 드단의 아들이며 아브라함과 그두라를 통한 후손이었다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Dan@Gen.30.6-1Ch, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev, Asher@Gen.30.13-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev
persons.brief: Son of Jacob; progenitor of the Levites
persons.short: Levi, son of Jacob and Leah, was the progenitor of the Levites, the priestly tribe of Israel.
persons.article: Levi was the third son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah (Gen.29.34). Along with his brother Simeon, he took revenge on the Shechemites for the rape of their sister Dinah (Gen.34.25-31). Jacob rebuked them for this act on his deathbed (Gen.49.5-7). Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari (Gen.46.11; Exo.6.16). His descendants, the Levites, were set apart as the priestly tribe (Exo.32.26-29; Num.3.5-13). They were responsible for the tabernacle and its services (Num.1.47-54; 3.14-39; 4.1-49; 8.5-26). The Levites were given cities throughout Israel, but no territorial inheritance (Num.35.1-8; Jos.21.1-42). Notable Levites include Moses, Aaron, and Samuel. The Levites are frequently mentioned in the historical and prophetic books of the Old Testament, as well as in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles. In the New Testament, Levites are mentioned in connection with the temple and its services (Luk.10.32; Jhn.1.19; Act.4.36). The Levitical priesthood is contrasted with the superior priesthood of Christ (Heb.7.1-28).
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Levi living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.29.34 referred to as Levi or Levite (לֵוִי), or Levite (Aramiac לֵוָי), or Levi or Levite or Levitical (לֵוִי), or Levi (Λευΐ), or Levite (Λευΐτης), or Levitical (Λευϊτικός); son of Israel and Leah; a brother of Reuben, Simeon, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah; half-brother of: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Gershon, Kohath, Merari and Jochebed.
persons.brief_ko: 야곱과 레아의 아들, 레위 지파 시조
persons.short_ko: 레위는 야곱과 레아의 셋째 아들로 제사장 지파인 레위 지파의 시조가 되었다.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.29.34에 처음 언급되며 '레위'라 불림. 이스라엘과 레아의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 유다, 단, 납달리, 갓, 아셀, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 게르손, 그핫, 므라리와 요게벳의 아버지.
persons.article_ko: 레위는 이스라엘(야곱)과 레아의 셋째 아들이었다(창 29:34). 형제 시므온과 함께 그는 자매 디나를 강간한 것에 대한 복수로 세겜 사람들에게 보복했다(창 34:25-31). 야곱은 임종 시 이 행동에 대해 그들을 책망했다(창 49:5-7). 레위에게는 게르손, 고핫, 므라리 세 아들이 있었다(창 46:11; 출 6:16). 그의 후손인 레위인은 제사장 지파로 구별되었다(출 32:26-29; 민 3:5-13). 그들은 성막과 그 봉사에 대한 책임을 맡았다(민 1:47-54; 3:14-39; 4:1-49; 8:5-26). 레위인은 이스라엘 전역에 성읍들을 받았으나 영토적 기업은 받지 않았다(민 35:1-8; 수 21:1-42). 저명한 레위인으로는 모세, 아론, 사무엘이 있다. 레위인은 구약의 역사서와 예언서, 그리고 역대상의 족보에 자주 언급된다. 신약에서 레위인은 성전과 그 봉사와 관련하여 언급된다(눅 10:32; 요 1:19; 행 4:36). 레위 계열 제사장직은 그리스도의 더 우월한 제사장직과 대조된다(히 7:1-28).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus
persons.short: Levi, son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.24">Luk.3.24</ref>).
persons.article: Levi, the son of Melchi, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.24). He was an ancestor of Jesus, but no additional information is provided about his life or role in the biblical narrative. Levi lived sometime between the Babylonian exile and the birth of Christ.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.24 only referred to as Levi (Λευΐ); a son of Melchi; father of Matthat.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '레위'라 불림. 멜기의 아들. 맛닷의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위는 멜기의 아들이며 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus
persons.short: Levi, son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.29">Luk.3.29</ref>).
persons.article: Levi, the son of Simeon, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.29). He was an ancestor of Jesus, but no additional information is provided about his life or role in the biblical narrative. Levi lived sometime between the patriarchal period and the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.29 only referred to as Levi (Λευΐ); a son of Simeon; father of Matthat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.29에 처음 언급되며 '레위'라 불림. 시므온의 아들. 맛닷의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위는 시므온의 아들이며 누가복음 족보에 기록된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Grandson of Merari; grandson of Levi
persons.short: Libni, a grandson of Merari and grandson of Levi.
persons.article: Libni was a grandson of Merari and a grandson of Levi (1Ch.6.29). He is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles. No additional information is provided about his life or role in the biblical narrative. As a descendant of Merari, Libni would have been part of the Levitical clan responsible for the framework, pillars, bases, and other structural elements of the tabernacle (Num.3.36-37; 4.29-33).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.29 only referred to as Libni (לִבְנִי); son of Mahli; a brother of Eleazar and Kish; father of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.29에 처음 언급되며 '립니'라 불림. 마흘리의 아들. 엘르아살과 기스의 형제. 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 리브니는 므라리의 아들이며 레위의 손자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Gershon; grandson of Levi
persons.short: Libni or Ladan, a son of Gershon and grandson of Levi.
persons.article: Libni, also known as Ladan, was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi (Exo.6.17; Num.3.18; 1Ch.6.17,20). He was the brother of Shimei (Exo.6.17; Num.3.18; 1Ch.6.17,20; 23.7). Libni's descendants, the Libnites, were one of the Levitical clans (Num.3.21; 26.58). During the time of David, the Libnites were counted among the Levites and given duties in the service of the tabernacle (1Ch.23.7-9). The sons of Libni, Jehiel and Zetham, along with their relatives, were given charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord (1Ch.26.21-22).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.17 referred to as Libni (לִבְנִי), or Libnite (לִבְנִי), or Ladan (לַעְדָּן); son of Gershon; a brother of Shimei; father of Jehiel, Zetham, Joel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Exo.6.17에 처음 언급되며 '립니'라 불림. 게르손의 아들. 시므이의 형제. 여히엘, 세담과 요엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 리브니(라단이라고도 함)는 게르손의 아들이며 레위의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Shemida, a Manassite
persons.short: Likhi, a son of Shemida and descendant of Manasseh.
persons.article: Likhi was a son of Shemida, who was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph (1Ch.7.19). He is mentioned in the genealogy of the half-tribe of Manasseh, but no additional information is provided about his life or role in the biblical narrative. Likhi likely lived during the period of the judges or the early monarchy in Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.19 only referred to as Likhi (לִקְחִי); son of Shemida; a brother of Ahian, Shechem and Aniam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.19에 처음 언급되며 '릭히'라 불림. 스미다의 아들. 아히안, 세겜과 아니암의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 리기는 스미다의 아들이며 므낫세의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian in Rome; greeted by Paul
persons.short: Linus, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.
persons.article: Linus was a Christian who lived in Rome during the time of Paul's second imprisonment (2Ti.4.21). In Paul's second letter to Timothy, he asked Timothy to greet Linus, along with other believers such as Eubulus, Pudens, and Claudia. This suggests that Linus was a member of the Christian community in Rome and likely known to both Paul and Timothy. Some early church traditions identify Linus as the second bishop of Rome, succeeding Peter, but this cannot be confirmed from the biblical text alone.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.4.21 only referred to as Linus (Λίνος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '리노'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 리노는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Symbolic name of Hosea's son; represents God's rejection of Israel
persons.short: Lo-ammi, meaning "not my people," was the symbolic name given to Hosea's son, representing God's rejection of Israel.
persons.article: Lo-ammi was the symbolic name given to the son of the prophet Hosea and his wife Gomer (Hos.1.9). The name Lo-ammi means "not my people" in Hebrew. This name, along with the names of Hosea's other children, Jezreel and Lo-ruhamah, was used by God to convey a message to the people of Israel. The name Lo-ammi symbolized God's rejection of Israel due to their unfaithfulness and idolatry. God declared that He would no longer consider Israel as His people and would withdraw His mercy from them (Hos.1.9). This message was part of Hosea's prophecy, which called the Israelites to repentance and warned of the consequences of their disobedience. The symbolic names of Hosea's children served as a powerful visual reminder of God's judgment and the broken relationship between God and His people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Hos.1.9 only referred to as Lo-ammi (לֹא עַמִּי); son of Hosea and Gomer; a brother of Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Hos.1.9에 처음 언급되며 '로암미'라 불림. 호세아와 고멜의 아들. 이스르엘과 로루하마의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 로암미('내 백성이 아니다'라는 뜻)는 하나님이 이스라엘을 거부하심을 상징하는 이름으로 호세아의 아들에게 지어졌다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Grandmother of Timothy; commended for her faith
persons.short: Lois, the grandmother of Timothy, was commended by Paul for her sincere faith.
persons.article: Lois was the grandmother of Timothy, a young Christian leader and companion of the apostle Paul (2Ti.1.5). In Paul's second letter to Timothy, he mentioned Lois and her daughter Eunice, Timothy's mother, commending them for their sincere faith. Paul noted that this faith first dwelt in Lois before being passed down to Eunice and then to Timothy. This suggests that Lois played a significant role in the spiritual upbringing and nurturing of her grandson, Timothy. It is likely that Lois, along with Eunice, taught Timothy the Scriptures from a young age, laying a strong foundation for his faith and future ministry (2Ti.3.14-15). Although no other details are provided about Lois in the Bible, her legacy of faith and her influence on Timothy's life serve as a testament to the importance of passing on spiritual values from one generation to the next.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at 2Ti.1.5 only referred to as Lois (Λωΐς); mother of Eunice.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. 2Ti.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '로이스'라 불림. 유니게의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아내. 유니게의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 디모데의 할머니 로이스는 바울에게 그녀의 진실한 믿음으로 칭찬받았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Symbolic name of Hosea's daughter; represents God's withdrawal of mercy
persons.short: Lo-ruhamah, meaning "not pitied," was the symbolic name given to Hosea's daughter, representing God's withdrawal of mercy from Israel.
persons.article: Lo-ruhamah was the symbolic name given to the daughter of the prophet Hosea and his wife Gomer (Hos.1.6). The name Lo-ruhamah means "not pitied" or "not shown mercy" in Hebrew. This name, along with the names of Hosea's other children, Jezreel and Lo-ammi, was used by God to convey a message to the people of Israel. The name Lo-ruhamah symbolized God's decision to withdraw His mercy and compassion from Israel due to their persistent unfaithfulness (Hos.1.6). God declared that He would no longer show love to the house of Israel or forgive them (Hos.1.6,8). This message was part of Hosea's prophecy, which called the Israelites to repentance and warned of the consequences of their disobedience. The symbolic names of Hosea's children served as a powerful visual reminder of God's judgment and the broken relationship between God and His people.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Hos.1.6 only referred to as Lo-ruhamah (לֹא רֻחָ֫מָה); daughter of Hosea and Gomer; a sister of Jezreel, Lo-ammi H3818).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. Hos.1.6에 처음 언급되며 '로루하마'라 불림. 호세아와 고멜의 딸. 이스르엘과 로암미의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 로루하마('긍휼히 여김을 받지 못하다'라는 뜻)는 하나님이 이스라엘에게서 자비를 거두심을 상징하는 이름으로 호세아의 딸에게 지어졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Abraham's nephew; rescued from Sodom's destruction
persons.short: Lot, the nephew of Abraham, was rescued from Sodom before its destruction.
persons.article: Lot was the son of Haran and the nephew of Abraham (Gen.11.27,31). He traveled with Abraham from Ur to Canaan (Gen.12.4-5). Due to strife between their herdsmen, Lot chose to settle in the plain of Jordan near Sodom (Gen.13.1-13). Lot was captured when Sodom was invaded, but Abraham rescued him (Gen.14.12,16). Despite the wickedness of Sodom, Lot continued living there (Gen.19.1). When God revealed His plan to destroy the city, Abraham pleaded for Lot's safety (Gen.18.16-33). Two angels warned Lot to flee Sodom with his family (Gen.19.1-22). Lot's wife disobeyed and was turned into a pillar of salt (Gen.19.26; Luk.17.32). Lot and his daughters escaped to Zoar and later settled in a cave (Gen.19.30). Lot's daughters, believing they were the last survivors, got him drunk and slept with him, resulting in the births of Moab and Ammon (Gen.19.31-38; Psa.83.8). The New Testament describes Lot as a righteous man distressed by the debauchery of Sodom (2Pe.2.7). Jesus used Lot's story as a warning about the suddenness of His return (Luk.17.28-29).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.11.27 referred to as Lot (לוֹט), or Lot (Λώτ); son of Haran; a brother of Milcah and Iscah; father of daughter1 of Lot, daughter2 of Lot, Moab, Ben-ammi.
persons.short_ko: 롯은 아브라함의 조카로 소돔에 살다가 그 성이 멸망할 때 천사의 도움으로 구원받았다.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.11.27에 처음 언급되며 '롯'이라 불림. 하란의 아들. 밀가와 이스가의 형제. 롯의 아내(이름 미상), 롯의 딸(이름 미상)와 롯의 딸(이름 미상)의 남편. 롯의 딸(이름 미상), 롯의 딸(이름 미상), 모압과 벤암미의 아버지.
persons.article_ko: 롯은 하란의 아들이며 아브라함의 조카였다(창 11:27, 31). 그는 아브라함과 함께 우르에서 가나안까지 여행했다(창 12:4-5). 그들의 목자들 사이의 다툼 때문에 롯은 소돔 근처 요단 평지에 정착하기로 선택했다(창 13:1-13). 소돔이 침공당했을 때 롯은 사로잡혔으나 아브라함이 그를 구출했다(창 14:12, 16). 소돔의 악함에도 불구하고 롯은 계속 그곳에 살았다(창 19:1). 하나님이 그 성읍을 멸하실 계획을 밝히셨을 때 아브라함은 롯의 안전을 위해 간청했다(창 18:16-33). 두 천사가 롯에게 가족과 함께 소돔에서 도망치라고 경고했다(창 19:1-22). 롯의 아내는 불순종하여 소금 기둥이 되었다(창 19:26; 눅 17:32). 롯과 그의 딸들은 소알로 도망쳤다가 후에 굴에 정착했다(창 19:30). 롯의 딸들은 자신들이 마지막 생존자라고 믿어 그를 취하게 하고 그와 동침했고, 그 결과 모압과 암몬이 태어났다(창 19:31-38; 시 83:8). 신약은 롯을 소돔의 방탕함으로 괴로워한 의로운 사람으로 묘사한다(벧후 2:7). 예수님은 롯의 이야기를 그분의 재림의 갑작스러움에 대한 경고로 사용하셨다(눅 17:28-29).

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Shobal@Gen.36.20-1Ch, Zibeon@Gen.36.2-1Ch, Dishon@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Ezer@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Dishan@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Seir the Horite; chief of Edom
persons.short: Lotan, a son of Seir the Horite and a chief of Edom.
persons.article: Lotan was a son of Seir the Horite and a chief of the land of Edom (Gen.36.20,29; 1Ch.1.38). He had a sister named Timna (Gen.36.22; 1Ch.1.39). Lotan is listed among the descendants of Esau who settled in the region of Seir (Gen.36.20-30; 1Ch.1.38-42). The Horites were the original inhabitants of Seir before Esau's descendants displaced them (Deut 2.12). As a chief of Edom, Lotan likely held a position of authority and influence among his people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.20 only referred to as Lotan (לוֹטָן); son of Seir; a brother of Shobal, Zibeon, Dishon, Ezer, Dishan and Timna; father of Hori, Hemam.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.20에 처음 언급되며 '로단'이라 불림. 세일의 아들. 소발, 시브온, 디손, 에셀, 디산과 딤나의 형제. 호리와 호맘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 로단은 세일 사람 호리의 아들이며 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch.
persons.short: Lucius of Cyrene was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch who was involved in sending Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey.
persons.article: Lucius of Cyrene is mentioned in Act.13.1 as one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, alongside Barnabas, Simeon (called Niger), Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul (later known as Paul). Cyrene was a city in modern-day Libya, North Africa, indicating that Lucius may have been of African origin. As a prophet and teacher, Lucius would have been involved in proclaiming God's word and instructing the believers in Antioch. It was during a time of worship and fasting that the Holy Spirit called Barnabas and Saul to be set apart for the work of spreading the gospel to the Gentiles. Lucius, along with the other leaders, laid their hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them off on their first missionary journey, which marked a significant expansion of the early Christian church. Additionally, Lucius is mentioned in Rom.16.21 as a companion of Paul who sends greetings to the church in Rome, further indicating his involvement in the ministry of the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.13.1 only referred to as Lucius (Λούκιος).
persons.short_ko: 누기오는 구레네 출신으로 안디옥 교회의 선지자 겸 교사였다.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.13.1에 처음 언급되며 '루기오'라 불림.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Shem; progenitor of the Lydians
persons.short: Lud, a son of Shem and progenitor of the Lydians.
persons.article: Lud was one of the sons of Shem, the son of Noah (Gen.10.22; 1Ch.1.17). He is mentioned in the Table of Nations, which records the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. Lud is considered the ancestor of the Lydians, a people group that inhabited the region of Lydia in western Anatolia (modern-day Turkey). The Lydians were known for their military prowess and are mentioned as allies or mercenaries of Tyre and Egypt (Ezk.27.10; 30.5; Jer.46.9). The prophet Isaiah also includes Lud among the nations that will come to know the glory of the Lord (Isa.66.19). Although the connection between the biblical Lud and the historical Lydians is not explicitly stated, it is generally accepted based on the similarity of the names and the geographic location associated with Lud's descendants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.22 referred to as Lud or Lud or Lud (לוּד), or Lud (לוּדִי); son of Shem; a brother of Asshur, Elam, Arpachshad and Aram.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '룻'이라 불림. 셈의 아들. 앗수르, 엘람, 아르박삿과 아람의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 룻은 셈의 아들이며 루디아 사람들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: People from Lud
persons.siblings: Anamim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Pathrusim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Casluhim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Caphtorim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Mizraim; progenitor of a people group
persons.short: Ludim, a son of Mizraim and progenitor of a people group.
persons.article: Ludim was one of the sons of Mizraim, who was a son of Ham (Gen.10.13; 1Ch.1.11). He is mentioned in the Table of Nations, which records the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. Ludim is listed among the descendants of Ham, specifically as a son of Mizraim, who is associated with Egypt. The Ludim are believed to be the ancestors of the Lydians, a people group that inhabited the region of Lydia in western Anatolia (modern-day Turkey). However, the exact relationship between the Ludim and the historical Lydians is not certain.
persons.summary: People from Lud, first mentioned at Gen.10.13 only referred to as Ludim (לוּדִי); descended from Egypt along with Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim and Caphtorim.
persons.summary_ko: 룻 사람. Gen.10.13에 처음 언급되며 '루딤'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 아나밈, 르하빔, 납두힘, 바드루심, 가슬루힘과 갑도림의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 루딤은 미스라임의 아들이며 한 민족의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Physician; companion of Paul; author of Luke and Acts
persons.short: Luke, a physician and companion of Paul, was the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts.
persons.article: Luke was a physician (Col.4.14 and a close companion of the apostle Paul )(2Ti.4.11; Phm.1.24). He is best known as the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts. Although not mentioned by name in these books, early church tradition unanimously attributes them to Luke. His writings suggest that he was well-educated and had a keen eye for historical detail. Luke accompanied Paul on several missionary journeys, as evidenced by the "we" passages in Acts (Act.16.10-17; 20.5-21.18; 27.1-28.16). He remained with Paul during his imprisonment in Rome (2Ti.4.11). In Paul's letters, Luke is described as a beloved friend and fellow worker in the gospel (Col.4.14; Phm.1.24). His medical background may have been helpful during Paul's travels and ministry. Luke's Gospel emphasizes the humanity of Jesus, His compassion for the marginalized, and the universal scope of His message. The Book of Acts records the growth of the early church and the spread of the gospel from Jerusalem to Rome.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at 2Co.13.14 only referred to as Luke (Λουκᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Co.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '누가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 의사이며 바울의 동역자였던 누가는 누가복음과 사도행전의 저자였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Seller of purple goods; converted by Paul in Philippi
persons.short: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, was converted by Paul in Philippi and hosted the church in her home.
persons.article: Lydia was a businesswoman from the city of Thyatira who sold purple goods (Act.16.14). She was living in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia, when she encountered the apostle Paul and his companions. Lydia is described as a worshiper of God, suggesting that she was a Gentile who followed the Jewish faith. When Paul preached the gospel, the Lord opened her heart to respond to his message (Act.16.14). Lydia and her household were baptized, becoming the first recorded converts in Europe (Act.16.15). She then invited Paul and his companions to stay at her home, demonstrating her hospitality and eagerness to support the spreading of the gospel (Act.16.15). After Paul and Silas were released from prison, they visited Lydia's house and met with the believers before departing from Philippi (Act.16.40). Lydia's conversion and her role in hosting the early church in Philippi highlight the importance of women in the early Christian movement and the gospel's appeal to people from various backgrounds.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.16.14 only referred to as Lydia (Λυδία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Act.16.14에 처음 언급되며 '루디아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 루디아는 두아디라 출신의 자색 옷감 장수로, 빌립보에서 바울에 의해 회심하여 자기 집에서 교회를 대접했다.

persons.description: Tetrarch of Abilene living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Tetrarch of Abilene during John the Baptist's ministry
persons.short: Lysanias, the tetrarch of Abilene, ruled during the time of John the Baptist's ministry (<ref="Luk.3.1">Luk.3.1</ref>).
persons.article: Lysanias was the tetrarch of Abilene, a region located in the Anti-Lebanon mountains, during the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar (Luk.3.1). He is mentioned in the Gospel of Luke as one of the rulers in power when John the Baptist began his ministry. The title "tetrarch" indicates that Lysanias governed a portion of a divided territory. Historical records suggest that he may have been a descendant of an earlier Lysanias who ruled Chalcis and was executed by Mark Antony in 36 BC. Apart from this brief mention in Luke's Gospel, no further details about Lysanias' life or rule are provided in the Bible. His inclusion in the list of rulers helps to establish the historical and political context of John the Baptist's ministry and the beginning of Jesus' public ministry.
persons.summary: Tetrarch of Abilene living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.3.1 only referred to as Lysanias (Λυσανίας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 아빌레네 분봉왕. Luk.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '루사니아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아빌레네의 분봉왕 루사니아는 세례 요한의 사역 당시 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Roman commander who rescued Paul from a Jewish mob
persons.short: Claudius Lysias, the Roman commander in Jerusalem, rescued Paul from a Jewish mob and sent him to Felix.
persons.article: Claudius Lysias was a Roman tribune (commander) stationed in Jerusalem during the time of Paul's arrest (Act.23.26). When Paul was attacked by a Jewish mob in the temple, Lysias intervened with his soldiers and took Paul into custody (Act.21.30-33). Upon learning of a plot to kill Paul, Lysias arranged for him to be transferred to Caesarea under armed guard to appear before Felix, the governor (Act.23.12-35). In his letter to Felix, Lysias explained the circumstances of Paul's arrest and his decision to send him to the governor for judgment (Act.23.26-30). Lysias admitted that he had initially arrested Paul thinking he was a rebel, but later learned that the charges against him were related to Jewish religious disputes (Act.23.28-29). Lysias' actions demonstrate his commitment to maintaining order and ensuring that Paul received a fair trial under Roman law. His letter to Felix also serves as an official record of the events surrounding Paul's arrest and transfer to Caesarea.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.23.26 referred to as Lysias (Λυσίας), or Claudius (Κλαύδιος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.23.26에 처음 언급되며 '루시아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 글라우디오 루시아는 예루살렘의 로마 지휘관으로, 유대인 폭도에게서 바울을 구출하여 벨릭스에게 보냈다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Hanan, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Maacah was the father of Hanan, one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Maacah was the father of Hanan, who was one of King David's mighty men (1Ch.11.43). Hanan is listed among the warriors who joined David during his reign. The mighty men were known for their bravery, loyalty, and military prowess (2Sa.23.8-39; 1Ch.11.10-47). They played a significant role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. No further details are provided about Maacah himself in the biblical narrative. His mention as the father of one of David's mighty men suggests that he may have been a person of some influence or status within the tribe of Benjamin. The inclusion of Shephatiah in the list of mighty men highlights the important role that individual warriors played in the success of David's reign and the establishment of the Israelite monarchy.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.43 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); father of Hanan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.43에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 하난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아가는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 하난의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Caleb's concubine; mother of Sheber and Tirhanah
persons.short: Maacah, Caleb's concubine, was the mother of Sheber and Tirhanah.
persons.article: Maacah was a concubine of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1Ch.2.48). She is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically in the line of Caleb. Maacah gave birth to two sons, Sheber and Tirhanah. No further information is provided about Maacah or her sons in the biblical record. Her inclusion in the genealogy highlights the complex family structures of the period and the importance of documenting lineage in ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A concubine from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.48 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); concubine of Caleb; mother of Sheber, Tirhanah, Shaaph, Sheva.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.2.48에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 갈렙의 아내. 세벨, 디르하나, 사압과 스와의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 갈렙의 첩 마아가는 세벨과 디르하나의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shephatiah, leader of the Simeonites under David
persons.short: Maacah was the father of Shephatiah, the leader of the Simeonites during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Maacah was the father of Shephatiah, who was appointed as the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King David (1Ch.27.16). Shephatiah's mention in the list of tribal leaders suggests that he held a position of authority and responsibility within the tribe of Simeon. The tribal leaders were responsible for overseeing the affairs of their respective tribes and representing their interests before the king. No further information is provided about Maacah himself in the biblical record. His mention as the father of a tribal leader indicates that he may have been a person of influence within the tribe of Simeon. The inclusion of Shephatiah in the list of tribal leaders highlights the importance of tribal organization and leadership during the reign of King David.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.16 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); father of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.16에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아가는 다윗 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자 스바댜의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Sister of Huppim and Shuppim; mother of Peresh and Sheresh
persons.short: Maacah, the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, was the wife of Machir and mother of Peresh and Sheresh.
persons.article: Maacah was the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, who were descendants of Benjamin (1Ch.7.15). She married Machir, the son of Manasseh, and gave birth to two sons, Peresh and Sheresh (1Ch.7.16). Machir was known for being the father of Gilead, a region east of the Jordan River (Num.26.29; 1Ch.7.14). The marriage of Maacah to Machir represents an intermarriage between the tribes of Benjamin and Manasseh. No further details are provided about Maacah or her sons in the biblical narrative. Her mention in the genealogy underscores the interconnectedness of the Israelite tribes and the significance of marriage alliances in the early history of Israel.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.7.15 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); daughter of Ir; a sister of Shuppim and Huppim; wife of Machir; mother of Hammolecheth, Gilead, daughter of Machir, Peresh, Sheresh.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.7.15에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 일의 딸. 숩빔과 훔빔의 자매. 마길의 아내. 함몰레겟, 길르앗, 마길의 딸(이름 미상), 베레스와 세레스의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 훕빔과 숩빔의 자매 마아가는 마길의 아내이며 브레스와 세레스의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Abdon@1Ch.8.30-, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Baal@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Ahio@1Ch.8.31-, Zecher@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-
persons.brief: Grandmother of Saul
persons.short: Maacah, the mother of Kish, the father of Saul.
persons.article: Maacah was the wife of a man variously called Jeiel and elsewhere called Abiel or Ner (1Ch.8.29; 9.35). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin, specifically in the line of Saul. Her husband re-established Gibeon as an important city and religious centre.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.29 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); wife of Abiel; mother of Kish, Ner, Abdon, Zur, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher, Mikloth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.8.29에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 아비엘의 아내. 기스, 넬, 압돈, 술, 바알, 나답, 그돌, 아효, 세겔과 미글롯의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마아가는 사울의 아버지 기스의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Abishalom; wife of Rehoboam; mother of Abijah
persons.short: Maacah, also known as Micaiah, the daughter of Abishalom (Absalom), was the wife of Rehoboam and mother of Abijah, king of Judah.
persons.article: Maacah, also referred to as Micaiah, was the daughter of Abishalom (likely Absalom, the son of David) and the wife of King Rehoboam of Judah (1Ki.15.2; 2Ch.11.20-21). She was the mother of Abijah, who succeeded Rehoboam as king (1Ki.15.2; 2Ch.11.22; 13.2). Maacah held the influential position of queen mother during the reigns of Rehoboam and Abijah. However, she was removed from this role by her grandson, King Asa, because she had made an obscene image of Asherah (1Ki.15.13; 2Ch.15.16). Maacah's story illustrates the political significance of the queen mother in the Judean monarchy and the religious reforms undertaken by King Asa to purge idolatry from the land.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.15.2 referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה), or Micaiah (מִיכָיָ֫הוּ); a daughter of Uriel and Tamar; wife of Rehoboam; mother of Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.15.2에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 우리엘과 다말의 딸. 르호보암의 아내. 아비야, 앗대, 시사와 슬로밋의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마아가(미가야라고도 함)는 압살롬의 딸로, 르호보암의 아내이며 유다 왕 아비야의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Talmai; wife of David; mother of Absalom
persons.short: Maacah, the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur, was one of David's wives and the mother of Absalom.
persons.article: Maacah was the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur, a region located northeast of the Sea of Galilee (2Sa.3.3; 1Ch.3.2). She became one of King David's wives and bore him a son named Absalom. Maacah's marriage to David likely served as a political alliance between Israel and Geshur. Absalom, her son, would later flee to Geshur after murdering his half-brother Amnon and remained there for three years (2Sa.13.37-38). Although not mentioned by name, Maacah was likely the mother of Tamar, who was raped by her half-brother Amnon (2Sa.13.1-22). Maacah's role in the biblical narrative is primarily as the mother of Absalom, whose rebellion against David and subsequent death had a profound impact on the king and his reign (2Sa.15-18). Her inclusion in the genealogies of David's family underscores the importance of maternal lineage in the royal line of Judah.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.3 referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); a daughter of Talmai; wife of David; mother of Absalom and Tamar.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 2Sa.3.3에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 달매의 딸. 다윗의 아내. 압살롬과 다말의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 그술 왕 달매의 딸 마아가는 다윗의 아내 중 한 사람이며 압살롬의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother
persons.short: Maacah, a concubine of Nahor, was the mother of Nahor's son Tebah.
persons.article: Maacah was a concubine of Nahor, who was the brother of Abraham (Gen.22.24). She is mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's family, which lists the children born to Nahor and his wife Milcah, as well as his concubine Reumah. Maacah is identified as the mother of Tebah, one of Nahor's sons. No further information is provided about Maacah or her son Tebah in the biblical record. Her inclusion in the genealogy highlights the complex family structures of the patriarchal period and the importance of documenting lineage in the ancient Near East.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.24 only referred to as Maacah (מַעֲכָה); son of Nahor and Reumah; a brother of Tebah, Gaham and Tahash; half-brother of: Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.24에 처음 언급되며 '마아가'라 불림. 나홀과 르우마의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 가함과 다하스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 나홀의 첩 마아가는 나홀의 아들 데바의 어머니였다.

persons.description: People descended from Maacat(?)
persons.brief: Son of Hodiah, grandson of Naham's sister
persons.short: An unnamed son of Hodiah, who was the grandson of Naham's sister.
persons.article: 1Ch.4.19 mentions an unnamed man who was the son of Hodiah. Hodiah's father was married to Naham's sister, making this unnamed man the grandson of Naham's sister. No further details are provided about his life, character, or accomplishments. His inclusion in the genealogy of Judah underscores the importance of family lineage and the recording of generations in ancient Israelite society, even when individuals' names and deeds were not specifically noted.
persons.summary: People descended from Maacat(?) living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.19 only referred to as Maacathites (גַּרְמִי); ; founded Eshtemoa.
persons.summary_ko: 마아가 사람. 2Sa.23.34에 처음 언급되며 '마아갓'이라 불림. 이스바와 호디야의 아들. Eshtemoa의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 호디야의 이름 없는 아들은 나함의 자매의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the men who married foreign women during Ezra's time
persons.short: Maadai was one of the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Maadai is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the men who had married foreign women during the post-exilic period (Ezr.10.34). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon, Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a religious reform to purify the community and restore adherence to the Law of Moses. Part of this reform involved addressing the issue of intermarriage with foreign women, which was seen as a violation of God's commandments (Deut 7.3-4). Maadai was among those who had taken foreign wives and was required to separate from them as part of the community's repentance and renewal of the covenant with God (Ezr.10.10-44). No further details are provided about Maadai's life or family in the biblical text. His inclusion in the list of those who had married foreign women highlights the challenges faced by the Jewish community in maintaining their religious and cultural identity during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.34 only referred to as Maadai (מַעֲדַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.34에 처음 언급되며 '마아대'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마아대는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Zechariah@Neh.12.35, Shemaiah@Neh.12.36, Azarel@Neh.12.36, Milalai@Neh.12.36, Gilalai@Neh.12.36, Nethanel@Neh.12.36, Judah@Neh.12.36, Hanani@Neh.12.36
persons.brief: Levite musician who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Maai, a Levite musician, participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maai was a Levite musician who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.12.36). After the completion of the wall's reconstruction, Nehemiah organized a grand dedication ceremony that involved two large choirs processing around the city on top of the wall (Neh.12.27-43). Maai is listed among the Levite musicians who played instruments and sang during this celebratory event. The participation of Levite musicians in the dedication ceremony highlights the importance of music and worship in the religious life of the Jewish community. No further information is provided about Maai's specific role or personal life in the biblical text. His inclusion in the list of musicians demonstrates the significance of the Levites' musical duties in the context of religious celebrations and the restoration of Jerusalem during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.36 only referred to as Maai (מָעַי); son of Jonathan; a brother of Zechariah, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.36에 처음 언급되며 '마애'라 불림. 요나단의 아들. 스가랴, 스마야, 아사렐, 밀랄래, 길랄래, 느다넬, 유다와 하나니의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 음악가 마애는 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest during the time of David and Nehemiah
persons.short: Maasai, also known as Amashsai, was a priest who served during the time of  Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maasai, also referred to as Amashsai, was a priest mentioned in the genealogies of the priestly families during and Nehemiah (1Ch.9.12; Neh.11.13). In the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles, Maasai is listed as a descendant of Adiel, who was a descendant of Immer, one of the priestly clans (1Ch.9.12). This suggests that Maasai belonged to the priestly lineage that served in the temple during the reign of David. In the book of Nehemiah, Amashsai (likely the same person as Maasai) is mentioned as the son of Azarel and a leader among the priests who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.13). The inclusion of Maasai/Amashsai in both the pre-exilic and post-exilic records highlights the continuity of the priestly families and their service in the temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 referred to as Maasai (מַעֲשַׂי), or Amashsai (עֲמַשְׁסַי); a son of Adiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '마아새'라 불림. 아디엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마아새(아맛새라고도 함)는 느헤미야 시대에 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during the reign of David
persons.short: Maaseiah, a Levite gatekeeper, served during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper during the reign of King David (1Ch.15.18,20). He is mentioned in the context of the transportation of the Ark of the Covenant from the house of Obed-Edom to Jerusalem. David organized a grand procession involving Levites, priests, and musicians to accompany the Ark (1Ch.15.1-28). Maaseiah is listed among the gatekeepers who were appointed to carry the Ark and to play musical instruments, such as harps and lyres, during the procession (1Ch.15.18,20). The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple, ensuring that only authorized personnel could enter (1Ch.9.17-27). Maaseiah's participation in the transportation of the Ark and his role as a gatekeeper highlight the importance of the Levites' duties in the worship and service of God during David's reign.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 문지기 마아세야는 다윗 왕 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest involved in Joash's coronation
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, assisted in the coronation of King Joash during the reign of Athaliah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who played a role in the coronation of King Joash of Judah (2Ch.23.1). During the reign of Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, who had usurped the throne and killed the royal heirs, Jehoiada the priest organized a coup to restore the Davidic line (2Ch.22.10-23.21). Maaseiah, along with other leaders and Levites, was part of the group that Jehoiada gathered to support the young prince Joash and overthrow Athaliah. The coup was successful, and Joash was crowned king at the age of seven (2Ch.24.1). Maaseiah's involvement in this event highlights the importance of the priesthood in maintaining the religious and political stability of the kingdom of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.23.1 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); a son of Adaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.23.1에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 아다야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 마아세야는 아달랴 시대에 요아스 왕의 대관식을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Army officer during King Uzziah's reign
persons.short: Maaseiah, an army officer, served under King Uzziah of Judah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was an army officer who served during the reign of King Uzziah of Judah (2Ch.26.11). Uzziah, also known as Azariah, was a powerful and prosperous king who strengthened the kingdom's military and fortifications (2Ch.26.1-15). Maaseiah is mentioned as one of the officers who was in charge of the army under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders. This suggests that Maaseiah held a position of authority and responsibility within the military structure of Judah. The mention of his name in the context of Uzziah's military achievements highlights the importance of the army in maintaining the security and stability of the kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.26.11 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).

persons.short_ko: 군 지휘관 마아세야는 유다 왕 웃시야 밑에서 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ahaz's son killed by Zichri, an Ephraimite warrior
persons.short: Maaseiah, a son of King Ahaz of Judah, was killed by Zichri, an Ephraimite warrior, during a war between Judah and Israel.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a son of King Ahaz of Judah who was killed during a war between Judah and Israel (2Ch.28.7). During the reign of Ahaz, Judah faced military threats from neighboring kingdoms, including Israel and Syria (2Ch.28.1-15). In one battle, Zichri, a mighty warrior from the tribe of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah, along with Azrikam, the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, who was second to the king. The death of Maaseiah and other high-ranking officials demonstrates the severity of the defeat suffered by Judah and the consequences of Ahaz's unfaithfulness to God (2Ch.28.19). This event also highlights the political and military tensions between the kingdoms of Israel and Judah during this period.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.7 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); son of Ahaz; a brother of Hezekiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.28.7에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 아하스와 아비의 아들. 히스기야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 유다 왕 아하스의 아들 마아세야는 유다와 이스라엘의 전쟁 중 에브라임 용사 시그리에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Servant of King Josiah involved in temple repairs
persons.short: Maaseiah, a servant of King Josiah, was involved in the repair and restoration of the temple.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a servant of King Josiah of Judah who was involved in the repair and restoration of the temple (2Ch.34.8). During Josiah's reign, a book of the Law was discovered in the temple, prompting the king to initiate religious reforms and repairs to the temple (2Ch.34.1-33). Maaseiah, along with Shaphan the secretary and Joah the recorder, was sent by Josiah to Hilkiah the high priest to assess the money collected for the temple repairs and to oversee the work. This demonstrates Maaseiah's trusted position within the royal court and his involvement in the religious and administrative affairs of the kingdom. The restoration of the temple and the rediscovery of the Law were significant events in Josiah's reign, leading to a renewed commitment to the worship of God and the observance of His commandments.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.8 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.8에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 요시야 왕의 신하 마아세야는 성전 수리와 재건에 관여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who was found to have married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra (Ezr.10.18). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon, Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a religious reform to purify the community and restore adherence to the Law of Moses (Ezr.7-10). One of the issues addressed in this reform was the problem of intermarriage with foreign women, which was seen as a violation of God's commandments (Deut 7.3-4). Maaseiah was among the priests who had taken foreign wives, and he is listed along with others who pledged to put away their wives and offer a ram as a guilt offering (Ezr.10.18-19). This event highlights the importance of maintaining religious purity and the challenges faced by the Jewish community in the post-exilic period. The inclusion of priests among those who had married foreign women underscores the pervasive nature of the problem and the need for spiritual leadership in the restoration of the community.
persons.summary: A piest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.18 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 마아세야는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Maaseiah, an Israelite, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Maaseiah was an Israelite who was found to have married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra (Ezr.10.21). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon, Ezra led a religious reform to address the issue of intermarriage with foreign women, which was seen as a violation of God's commandments (Ezr.9-10). Maaseiah is listed among the descendants of Harim who had taken foreign wives (Ezr.10.21). As part of the reform, those who had married foreign women were required to separate from their wives and children (Ezr.10.44). This event highlights the importance of maintaining religious and ethnic purity within the Jewish community during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.21 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).

persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who was found to have married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra (Ezr.10.22). During the religious reform led by Ezra, which addressed the issue of intermarriage with foreign women, Maaseiah is listed among the descendants of Pashhur who had taken foreign wives (Ezr.10.22). The priests were expected to maintain a higher standard of religious purity and serve as examples to the community. The presence of priests among those who had married foreign women underscores the pervasive nature of the problem and the need for spiritual leadership in the restoration of the community. As part of the reform, those who had married foreign women were required to separate from their wives and children (Ezr.10.44).

persons.short_ko: 또 다른 제사장 마아세야도 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.
