persons.short: Maaseiah, an Israelite, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Maaseiah was an Israelite who was found to have married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra (Ezr.10.30). He is listed among the descendants of Pahath-Moab who had taken foreign wives (Ezr.10.30). During the religious reform led by Ezra, which addressed the issue of intermarriage with foreign women, those who had married foreign women were required to separate from their wives and children (Ezr.10.44). This event highlights the importance of maintaining religious and ethnic purity within the Jewish community during the post-exilic period. The inclusion of Maaseiah and others in the list of those who had married foreign women demonstrates the widespread nature of the problem and the need for repentance and restoration.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest during the reigns of Zedekiah and Jehoiakim
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, served during the reigns of Kings Zedekiah and Jehoiakim of Judah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who served during the reigns of Kings Zedekiah and Jehoiakim of Judah (Jer.21.1; 29.25; 37.3). He was the father of Zephaniah, who was also a priest (Jer.21.1; 29.25; 37.3). During the reign of Zedekiah, Maaseiah and his son Zephaniah were sent by the king to inquire of the prophet Jeremiah concerning the Babylonian invasion (Jer.21.1; 37.3). Maaseiah is also mentioned in a letter sent by Jeremiah to the exiles in Babylon, where he is referred to as the second priest under Jehoiada, the high priest (Jer.29.25). This suggests that Maaseiah held a significant position within the priestly hierarchy. The biblical text does not provide further details about Maaseiah's personal life or his other priestly duties.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.21.1 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); father of Zephaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.21.1에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 스바니야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 마아세야는 유다 왕 시드기야와 여호야김 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: False prophet during the Babylonian exile
persons.short: Maaseiah, along with Ahab, was a false prophet who prophesied lies to the exiles in Babylon.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a false prophet who, along with Ahab, prophesied lies to the Jewish exiles in Babylon (Jer.29.21). In a letter sent by the prophet Jeremiah to the exiles, he warned them about the false prophecies of Ahab and Maaseiah, who were leading the people astray (Jer.29.20-23). Jeremiah prophesied that these false prophets would be punished by God, and they would be killed by Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon (Jer.29.21). The presence of false prophets like Maaseiah among the exiles demonstrates the spiritual challenges faced by the Jewish community during the Babylonian captivity.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.29.21 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); father of Zedekiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.29.21에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 시드기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 아합과 함께 바벨론 포로들에게 거짓을 예언한 거짓 선지자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jaazaniah; associated with the Rechabites
persons.short: Maaseiah was an ancestor of Jaazaniah, who was associated with the Rechabites during the reign of Jehoiakim.
persons.article: Maaseiah is mentioned as an ancestor of Jaazaniah, who was associated with the Rechabites during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah (Jer.35.4). The Rechabites were a nomadic clan known for their adherence to the commands of their ancestor, Jonadab son of Rechab, which included abstaining from wine, not building houses, and not sowing crops (Jer.35.6-7). In the biblical account, Jeremiah uses the Rechabites' faithfulness to their ancestor's commands as a contrast to the disobedience of the people of Judah (Jer.35.12-19). Maaseiah's connection to the Rechabites through his descendant Jaazaniah suggests that he may have been part of this clan or associated with them in some way.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.35.4 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); a son of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.35.4에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 살룸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 여호야김 시대에 레갑 사람들과 관련이 있던 야아사냐의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Maaseiah was among those who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was one of the individuals who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.10.25). After the reading of the Law and the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commandments and to separate themselves from the surrounding nations (Neh.9-10). Maaseiah is listed among the leaders, Levites, and priests who signed and sealed this covenant, pledging to uphold its terms (Neh.10.1-27). The sealing of the covenant was a significant act of commitment and dedication to God, demonstrating the people's desire to live according to His will.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.25 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.25에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Shiloni; lived in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Maaseiah, a descendant of Shiloni, lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a descendant of Shiloni who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.5). He is mentioned in the list of people who resettled in Jerusalem, which was compiled by Nehemiah as part of his efforts to repopulate the city (Neh.11.1-36). Maaseiah is identified as a descendant of Judah through the lineage of Shiloni. The resettlement of Jerusalem was an important step in the restoration of the Jewish community and the reestablishment of their presence in the holy city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); a son of Baruch.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 바룩의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 실로니의 후손 마아세야는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주했다.

persons.brief: Descendant of Benjamin; lived in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Maaseiah, a descendant of Benjamin, lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.7). He is mentioned in the list of people who resettled in Jerusalem, which was compiled by Nehemiah as part of his efforts to repopulate the city (Neh.11.1-36). Maaseiah is identified as a member of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the two remaining tribes of Israel after the exile. The resettlement of Jerusalem was an important step in the restoration of the Jewish community and the reestablishment of their presence in the holy city.

persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.7에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 이디엘의 아들. 골라야의 아버지.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.12.41). After the completion of the wall's reconstruction, Nehemiah organized a grand dedication ceremony that involved two large choirs processing around the city on top of the wall (Neh.12.27-43). Maaseiah is listed among the priests who blew trumpets during this celebratory event, along with other priests and Levites. The dedication of the wall was a significant moment in the restoration of Jerusalem, marking the completion of a major project and the reestablishment of the city's defenses. Maaseiah's participation in this event highlights the role of the priests in the religious and civic life of the community.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.41 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Maaseiah, a priest, was among those who sang during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.12.42). He is mentioned among the priests who sang and gave thanks during the celebratory procession on the wall (Neh.12.42). The dedication ceremony was a significant event marking the completion of the wall's reconstruction and the restoration of Jerusalem. The involvement of priests like Maaseiah in singing and giving thanks highlights the importance of worship and praise in the religious life of the community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).

persons.short_ko: 제사장 마아세야는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에서 노래한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Maaseiah, an Israelite, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near his house during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was an Israelite who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.3.23). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon, Nehemiah led the effort to reconstruct the city's walls and gates (Neh.1-7). Maaseiah is mentioned as one of the individuals who repaired a section of the wall near his house, working alongside Baruch the son of Zabbai (Neh.3.23). The rebuilding of the wall was a significant event in the restoration of Jerusalem and the reestablishment of the Jewish community in the post-exilic period. The participation of Maaseiah and others in this project demonstrates their commitment to the physical and spiritual renewal of their homeland.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.23 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ); a son of Ananiah; father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.23에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림. 아나냐의 아들. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 느헤미야 시대에 자기 집 근처 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
persons.short: Maaseiah, a Levite, was among those who assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.8.4). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate to hear Ezra read from the Book of the Law (Neh.8.1-3). Maaseiah is listed among the Levites who stood beside Ezra on a raised platform and helped to explain the Law to the people (Neh.8.4,7). The reading of the Law was a significant event in the spiritual renewal of the Jewish community, as they recommitted themselves to the covenant with God and the observance of His commandments. The involvement of Maaseiah and other Levites in this event highlights their role as teachers and interpreters of the Law, guiding the people in their understanding and application of God's word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '마아세야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 마아세야는 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 낭독하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
persons.short: Maaseiah, a Levite, assisted in explaining the Law to the people during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maaseiah was a Levite who helped explain the Law to the people during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.8.7). After the reading of the Law by Ezra, Maaseiah was among the Levites who instructed the people and helped them understand the meaning of the words (Neh.8.7-8). The Levites' role in teaching and interpreting the Law was crucial for the spiritual renewal of the Jewish community, as they sought to reestablish their covenant relationship with God. Maaseiah's involvement in this event demonstrates the importance of the Levites as teachers and spiritual guides for the people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.7 only referred to as Maaseiah (מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Maath is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ as recorded in the Gospel of Luke.
persons.article: Maath is a name that appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.26). He is listed as the son of Mattathias and the father of Naggai, making him a distant ancestor of Jesus. The genealogy in Luke traces Jesus' lineage back to Adam, emphasizing His connection to all of humanity. Maath's inclusion in this genealogy highlights the importance of family lines and ancestral heritage in Jewish culture. However, no further information is provided about Maath's life, occupation, or role in the biblical narrative. His presence in the genealogy serves primarily to establish Jesus' lineage and to affirm His descent from the royal line of David, as well as His connection to the broader human family.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.26 only referred to as Maath (Μαάθ); a son of Mattathias; father of Naggai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.26에 처음 언급되며 '마앗'이라 불림. 맛다디아의 아들. 낙개의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마앗은 누가복음에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ram, from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Maaz was a son of Ram, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Maaz was a son of Ram, who was a descendant of Judah, as recorded in the genealogy found in 1Chronicles 2 (1Ch.2.27). He is mentioned only in this genealogical list and no further information is provided about his life or role in the biblical narrative. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of Judah, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and highlights the descendants of Ram, who was a grandson of Judah. Maaz's inclusion in this list serves to establish the continuity of the tribe of Judah and its prominent figures. As with many individuals mentioned in biblical genealogies, the lack of additional details about Maaz suggests that the primary purpose of his mention is to maintain the historical record of the family line.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.27 only referred to as Maaz (מַ֫עַץ); son of Ram; a brother of Jamin and Eker.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.27에 처음 언급되며 '마아스'라 불림. 람의 아들. 야민과 에겔의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마아스는 람의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest who served in the 24th division
persons.short: Maaziah was the head of the 24th priestly division during the time of David.
persons.article: Maaziah was a priest who served as the head of the 24th division of priests during the reign of King David (1Ch.24.18). As part of David's organization of the priesthood, the priests were divided into 24 divisions, each responsible for serving in the temple for a specific period (1Ch.24.1-19). Maaziah's division was the 24th in the order of service. The establishment of this system ensured a structured and orderly approach to the priestly duties in the temple. No further details are provided about Maaziah's personal life or his specific responsibilities as the head of his division. His inclusion in the list of priestly divisions highlights the importance of the priesthood in maintaining the religious life of ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.18 only referred to as Maaziah (מַעַזְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.18에 처음 언급되며 '마아시야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마아시야는 다윗 시대에 스물네 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Maaziah, also known as Maadiah or Moadiah, was a priest who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Maaziah, also referred to as Maadiah or Moadiah, was a priest who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon (Neh.10.8; 12.5,17). He is mentioned among the priests who sealed the covenant, a solemn agreement made by the people of Israel to follow God's law and to maintain the temple worship (Neh.10.1-29). Maaziah's inclusion in this list indicates his prominence and leadership role within the priestly community. He is also listed among the priests who returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Neh.12.1-7 and among the heads of the priestly families during the high priesthood of Joiakim )(Neh.12.12-21). These multiple mentions of Maaziah in the context of priestly service and leadership underscore the significance of the priesthood in the restoration of Jewish worship and community life after the exile.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.8 referred to as Maaziah (מַעַזְיָהוּ), or Maadiah (מַעֲדְיָה), or Moadiah (מוֹעַדְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.8에 처음 언급되며 '마아시야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마아시야(마아댜 또는 모아댜라고도 함)는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Machbannai, a Gadite warrior, was one of the men who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: Machbannai was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag, along with several other warriors from the tribe of Gad (1Ch.12.8-13). The Gadites are described as brave warriors, trained for battle and skilled with the shield and spear (1Ch.12.8). Machbannai and his fellow Gadites defected to David during the time when he was fleeing from King Saul and seeking refuge in the wilderness (1Sa.22.1-2). The support of these warriors was crucial for David as he navigated the challenges of this period and eventually established his kingdom. Machbannai's presence among David's supporters demonstrates the loyalty and military prowess that David inspired among his followers.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.13 only referred to as Machbannai (מַכְבַּנַּי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.13에 처음 언급되며 '막반내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 갓 지파 용사 막반내는 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman or town of at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter or town founded by Sheva
persons.short: Machbenah was a descendant or town of Caleb, the son of Hezron, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Machbenah is mentioned as a daughter or a town of Sheva in the genealogy of Caleb, the son of Hezron, who was a descendant of Judah (1Ch.2.49). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of Judah and highlights the descendants of Hezron, including Caleb. Machbenah is listed as one of the descendants of Caleb, along with several other individuals and clans. No further information is provided about Machbenah's life, occupation, or role in the biblical narrative. The mention of Machbenah in this genealogical record serves to establish the continuity of Caleb's lineage and the growth of his clan within the tribe of Judah. As with many individuals mentioned in biblical genealogies, the lack of additional details about Machbenah suggests that the primary purpose of the mention is to maintain the historical record of the family line.
persons.summary: A woman or town of the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.49 only referred to as Machbenah (מַכְבֵּנָה); founded or fathered by Sheva; a sister of Gibea.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성 또는 지명. 1Ch.2.49에 처음 언급되며 '막베나'라 불림. 스와의 딸. 기브아의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 막베나는 유다 지파 헤스론의 아들 갈렙의 후손이거나 그가 세운 성읍이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Geuel, from the tribe of Gad
persons.short: Machi was the father of Geuel, a scout from the tribe of Gad sent to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Machi is mentioned in the book of Numbers as the father of Geuel, who was one of the twelve scouts sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num.13.15). Each scout was chosen as a leader from their respective tribes, and Geuel represented the tribe of Gad. The scouts were tasked with surveying the land, assessing its fertility, and gathering information about the inhabitants (Num.13.17-20). Upon their return, the scouts reported that the land was bountiful but the inhabitants were powerful, which discouraged the Israelites and led to their refusal to enter the land (Num.13.25-33). As a result, God condemned the generation to wander in the wilderness for forty years (Num.14.26-35).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.15 only referred to as Machi (מָכִי); father of Geuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.15에 처음 언급되며 '마기'라 불림. 그우엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마기는 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 갓 지파 정탐꾼 그우엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ammiel's son who hosted Mephibosheth
persons.short: Machir, the son of Ammiel, hosted Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, in Lo-debar and later provided supplies to David during Absalom's rebellion.
persons.article: Machir, the son of Ammiel, was a resident of Lo-debar who played a significant role in the life of Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan (2Sa.9.4,5). After the deaths of Saul and Jonathan, Mephibosheth was taken to the house of Machir in Lo-debar, where he found refuge and support. When King David sought to show kindness to the remaining descendants of Saul, he learned that Mephibosheth was living in the house of Machir (2Sa.9.4). David summoned Mephibosheth and restored to him all the land that had belonged to Saul, ensuring his well-being (2Sa.9.7-13). Later, during Absalom's rebellion against David, Machir, along with Shobi and Barzillai, provided essential supplies to David and his followers, including beds, basins, wheat, barley, flour, and other provisions (2Sa.17.27-29). Machir's actions demonstrate his loyalty and support for both Mephibosheth and King David during challenging times.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.9.4 only referred to as Machir (מָכִיר); a son of Ammiel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '마길'이라 불림. 암미엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 암미엘의 아들 마길은 로데발에서 요나단의 아들 므비보셋을 대접했고, 후에 압살롬의 반역 때 다윗에게 물자를 공급했다.

persons.description: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.offspring: Gilead@Num.26.29-1Ch, Gilead@Gen.31.21-Zec(f), daughter_of_Machir@1Ch.2.21, Peresh@1Ch.7.16, Sheresh@1Ch.7.16, Hammolecheth@1Ch.7.18
persons.brief: Son of Manasseh; father (ie re-founder) of Gilead
persons.short: Machir, the son of Manasseh, was the father  (ie re-founder) of Gilead and a prominent figure in the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Machir was the son of Manasseh and the father (ie re-founder) of Gilead, making him a significant ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh (Gen.50.23; Num.26.29; 1Ch.7.14). He is mentioned numerous times throughout the Old Testament, often in relation to the settlement and inheritance of the tribe of Manasseh. Machir's descendants, known as the Machirites, formed a substantial portion of the tribe (Num.26.29; Jos.17.1). They were known for their military prowess and were praised in the Song of Deborah (Jdg.5.14). The Machirites, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, conquered and settled in the land of Gilead, east of the Jordan River (Num.32.39-40; Deu.3.15; Jos.13.31). Machir's daughters, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah, appealed to Moses for the right to inherit their father's property in the absence of male heirs, setting a precedent for inheritance laws (Num.27.1; 36.1; Jos.17.3). Machir's descendants continued to play a role in the tribe of Manasseh, with some even marrying into the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.21,23).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.50.23 referred to as Machir (מָכִיר), or Machirite (מָכִירִי); son of Manasseh and Aramitess; a brother of Asriel; husband of Maacah; father or founder of Gilead, daughter of Machir, Peresh, Sheresh and Hammolecheth; founder of Gilead.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 므낫세의 아들. Gen.50.23에 처음 언급되며 '마길'이라 불림. 므낫세와 아람의 아들. 아스리엘의 형제. 마아가의 남편. 길르앗, 길르앗, 마길의 딸(이름 미상), 베레스, 세레스와 함몰레겟의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므낫세의 아들 마길은 길르앗의 창설자(재건자)였으며 므낫세 지파의 저명한 인물이었다.
persons.article_ko: 마길은 므낫세의 아들이며 길르앗의 창설자(재건자)로, 그를 므낫세 지파의 중요한 조상으로 만든다(창 50:23; 민 26:29; 대상 7:14). 그는 구약 전체에서 여러 번 언급되며, 종종 므낫세 지파의 정착과 기업과 관련이 있다. 마길의 후손인 마길 사람들은 그 지파의 상당 부분을 이루었다(민 26:29; 수 17:1). 그들은 군사적 용맹으로 알려졌고 드보라의 노래에서 칭찬받는다(삿 5:14). 마길 사람들은 르우벤 사람, 갓 사람과 함께 요단강 동편의 길르앗 땅을 정복하고 정착했다(민 32:39-40; 신 3:15; 수 13:31). 마길의 딸들인 마흘라, 노아, 호글라, 밀가, 디르사는 남자 상속자가 없는 상황에서 아버지의 재산을 상속받을 권리를 모세에게 청원하여 상속법의 선례를 세웠다(민 27:1; 36:1; 수 17:3). 마길의 후손은 계속해서 므낫세 지파에서 역할을 했으며, 일부는 유다 지파와도 혼인했다(대상 2:21, 23).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of those who married foreign women
persons.short: Machnadebai was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Machnadebai is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the men who had married foreign women during the post-exilic period (Ezr.10.40). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon, Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a religious reform to address various issues, including intermarriage with foreign women (Ezr.9-10). This practice was seen as a violation of God's commandments and a threat to the religious and cultural identity of the Jewish community. Machnadebai is listed among those who pledged to put away their foreign wives and children, following the counsel of Ezra and the leaders (Ezr.10.44). The inclusion of Machnadebai in this list highlights the widespread nature of the issue and the importance of maintaining religious purity and obedience to God's laws in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.40 only referred to as Machnadebai (מַכְנַדְבַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.40에 처음 언급되며 '막나드배'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 막나드배는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth; progenitor of the Medes
persons.short: Madai, a son of Japheth, is considered the ancestor of the Medes.
persons.article: Madai is mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10) and the genealogy of Chronicles (1Ch.1) as one of the sons of Japheth, the son of Noah. He is considered the ancestor of the Medes, an ancient Iranian people who inhabited the region of Media in western Iran. The Medes played a significant role in the ancient Near East, forming a powerful empire and later contributing to the Persian Empire. In the Bible, the Medes are known for their role in the fall of Babylon, as prophesied by Isaiah and Jeremiah (Isa.13.17; Jer.51.11,28). The inclusion of Madai in the Table of Nations and the genealogy of Chronicles emphasizes the biblical understanding of the origins and relationships of the various nations and people groups in the ancient world. As a descendant of Japheth, Madai is part of the lineage that spread out and populated the coastlands and islands, as described in Genesis 10.5.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Madai (מָדַי); son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Magog, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '마대'라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마곡, 야완, 두발, 메섹과 디라스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마대는 야벳의 아들이며 메대 사람들의 조상으로 여겨진다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Caleb, son of Hezron
persons.short: Madmannah was a descendant of Caleb, the son of Hezron, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Madmannah is mentioned in the genealogy of Caleb, the son of Hezron, who was a descendant of Judah (1Ch.2.49). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of Judah and highlights the descendants of Hezron, including Caleb. Madmannah is listed as one of the descendants of Caleb, along with several other individuals and clans. No further information is provided about Madmannah's life, occupation, or role in the biblical narrative. The mention of Madmannah in this genealogical record serves to establish the continuity of Caleb's lineage and the growth of his clan within the tribe of Judah. As with many individuals mentioned in biblical genealogies, the lack of additional details about Madmannah suggests that the primary purpose of the mention is to maintain the historical record of the family line.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.49 only referred to as Madmannah (מַדְמַנָּה); a son of Shaaph.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.49에 처음 언급되며 '맛만나'라 불림. 사압의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 맛만나는 유다 지파 헤스론의 아들 갈렙의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Edomite chief descended from Esau
persons.short: Magdiel was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Esau, the son of Isaac.
persons.article: Magdiel is mentioned in the lists of Edomite chiefs found in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1. He is identified as one of the chiefs of Edom, a descendant of Esau, the son of Isaac and the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.36.43; 1Ch.1.54). The Edomites were the descendants of Esau who settled in the region of Seir, south of the Dead Sea. The lists of Edomite chiefs provide a record of the political and social structure of Edom, highlighting the importance of family lineage and tribal leadership. Magdiel's inclusion in these lists suggests that he held a position of authority and influence within the Edomite community. However, no further details are provided about his personal life, achievements, or the specific period of his leadership. The mention of Magdiel in these genealogical records serves to establish the continuity of Esau's descendants and their role in the history of the region.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.43 only referred to as Magdiel (מַגְדִּיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.43에 처음 언급되며 '막디엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 막디엘은 이삭의 아들 에서의 후손인 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth; progenitor of a people group
persons.short: Magog, a son of Japheth, is considered the ancestor of a people group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy.
persons.article: Magog is mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10) and the genealogy of Chronicles (1Ch.1) as one of the sons of Japheth, the son of Noah. He is considered the ancestor of a people group that bore his name. In the Bible, the name Magog appears in the prophetic context of Ezekiel 38-39, where Magog is described as a land ruled by Gog, a powerful leader who will lead a coalition of nations against Israel in the end times. The exact identity of the Magog people and their geographical location is uncertain, but some scholars suggest that they may have been associated with the Scythians, a nomadic people who inhabited the region north of the Black Sea. The inclusion of Magog in the Table of Nations and the genealogy of Chronicles emphasizes the biblical understanding of the origins and relationships of the various nations and people groups in the ancient world. As a descendant of Japheth, Magog is part of the lineage that spread out and populated the coastlands and islands, as described in Genesis 10.5.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Magog (מָגוֹג); son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '마곡'이라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마대, 야완, 두발, 메섹과 디라스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마곡은 야벳의 아들이며, 에스겔의 예언에 언급된 한 민족의 조상으로 여겨진다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Magpiash was among those who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Magpiash is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.10.20). After the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon and the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, the people gathered to renew their commitment to God and His laws (Neh.8-10). As part of this renewal, a covenant document was prepared and signed by the leaders, Levites, and priests (Neh.10.1-27). Magpiash is listed among the leaders who sealed this covenant, pledging to follow God's commandments and to support the temple service (Neh.10.28-39). The sealing of the covenant was a significant act of dedication and commitment to God, demonstrating the people's desire to live according to His will in the post-exilic period. No further details are provided about Magpiash's personal life or his specific role in the community. His inclusion in the list of those who sealed the covenant highlights the importance of collective responsibility and unity in the spiritual life of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.20 only referred to as Magpiash (מַגְפִּיעָשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.20에 처음 언급되며 '막비아스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 막비아스는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Descendant of Seth; ancestor of Noah
persons.short: Mahalalel was a descendant of Seth and an ancestor of Noah, living before the flood.
persons.article: Mahalalel is mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis 5, 1Chronicles 1, and Luke 3 as a descendant of Seth, the third son of Adam and Eve. He is an ancestor of Noah and is part of the lineage that leads to Abraham, David, and ultimately, Jesus Christ. According to Genesis 5, Mahalalel was the son of Kenan and the father of Jared (Gen.5.12,15). He lived for 895 years, which was typical of the long lifespans recorded for the pre-flood patriarchs (Gen.5.13,16,17). The genealogies in Genesis 5 and 1Chronicles 1 focus on the line of descent from Adam to Noah, highlighting the continuity of the godly lineage before the flood. The genealogy in Luke 3 traces Jesus' ancestry back to Adam, emphasizing His connection to all of humanity. Mahalalel's inclusion in these genealogies serves to establish the historical and theological context of God's plan of redemption through the descendants of Seth, ultimately leading to the birth of Jesus Christ.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.5.12 referred to as Mahalalel (מַהֲלַלְאֵל), or Mahalaleel (Μαλελεήλ); a son of Kenan; father of Jared.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.5.12에 처음 언급되며 '마할랄렐'이라 불림. 게난의 아들. 야렛의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마할랄렐은 셋의 후손이며 노아의 조상으로, 홍수 이전에 살았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Perez; lived in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Mahalalel, a descendant of Perez, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Mahalalel is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.4). He is listed among the people who resettled in Jerusalem as part of Nehemiah's efforts to repopulate the city (Neh.11.1-36). Mahalalel belonged to the tribe of Judah, specifically the clan of Perez, which was one of the prominent families in Judah. The resettlement of Jerusalem was a significant step in the restoration of the Jewish community and the reestablishment of their presence in the holy city after the exile. No further details are provided about Mahalalel's personal life or his specific contributions to the community in the post-exilic period. His inclusion in the list of residents highlights the importance of family lineage and tribal identity in the social and religious life of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.4 only referred to as Mahalalel (מַהֲלַלְאֵל); father of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.4에 처음 언급되며 '마할랄렐'이라 불림. 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마할랄렐은 베레스의 후손으로, 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Rehoboam's wife, granddaughter of David
persons.short: Mahalath was one of King Rehoboam's wives, a granddaughter of David through his son Jerimoth.
persons.article: Mahalath is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as one of the wives of King Rehoboam, the son of Solomon and the first king of the Kingdom of Judah after the division of the united monarchy (2Ch.11.18). She was the daughter of Jerimoth, who was a son of David, making her a granddaughter of King David. Rehoboam's marriage to Mahalath, along with his other wife Abihail, is recorded in the context of his family life and his establishment of his royal household (2Ch.11.18-23). The chronicler notes that Rehoboam loved Mahalath and Abihail more than his other wives and concubines (2Ch.11.21). This marriage alliance with a descendant of David likely served to strengthen Rehoboam's claim to the throne and his connection to the Davidic dynasty. No further details are provided about Mahalath's personal life or her influence in the royal court. Her inclusion in the biblical record highlights the importance of marital alliances and family lineage in the political and social structure of the Judean monarchy.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.11.18 only referred to as Mahalath (מַחֲלַת); a daughter of Jerimoth and Abihail; wife of Rehoboam; mother of Jeush, Shemariah, Zaham.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ch.11.18에 처음 언급되며 '마할랏'이라 불림. 여레못과 아비하일의 딸. 르호보암의 아내. 여우스, 스마랴와 사함의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마할랏은 르호보암 왕의 아내 중 한 사람으로, 다윗의 아들 여리못을 통한 다윗의 손녀였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mibsam@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Massa@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Jetur@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch
persons.brief: Esau's wife, daughter of Ishmael
persons.short: Mahalath, also known as Basemath, was one of Esau's wives, a daughter of Ishmael.
persons.article: Mahalath, also referred to as Basemath, was one of the wives of Esau, the son of Isaac and the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.28.9; 36.3). She was the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son with Hagar, making her Esau's cousin (Gen.28.9). Esau married Mahalath in addition to his other wives, who were Hittite women (Gen.26.34; 28.8-9). This marriage likely strengthened the ties between Esau's descendants, the Edomites, and the Ishmaelites. Mahalath is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau, which list his wives, children, and descendants (Gen.36.4,10,13,17). These genealogies emphasize the importance of family lineage and the relationships between different people groups in the ancient Near East. The Bible does not provide further details about Mahalath's personal life or her role in the family dynamics of Esau's household. Her inclusion in the biblical record primarily serves to document Esau's marital alliances and the ancestry of the Edomites.
persons.summary: A woman of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.28.9 referred to as Mahalath (מַחֲלַת), or Basemath (בָּֽשְׂמַת); daughter of Ishmael; a sister of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah; wife of Esau; mother of Reuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.28.9에 처음 언급되며 '마할랏'이라 불림. 이스마엘의 딸. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 밉삼, 미스마, 두마, 맛사, 하닷, 데마, 여둘, 나비스와 게드마의 자매. 에서의 아내. 르우엘의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마할랏(바스맛이라고도 함)은 에서의 아내 중 한 사람으로 이스마엘의 딸이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from Netophah
persons.short: Maharai the Netophathite was one of David's mighty warriors and served as a commander in his army.
persons.article: Maharai the Netophathite is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty warriors in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles (2Sa.23.28; 1Ch.11.30). He was from Netophah, a town in Judah, and was among the elite group of soldiers who fought alongside David and demonstrated exceptional bravery and military prowess. The mighty warriors were instrumental in establishing and maintaining David's kingdom, as they provided military support and leadership. In addition to being listed among the mighty warriors, Maharai is also mentioned in the records of David's military organization (1Ch.27.13). He served as the commander over the tenth division of the army, which consisted of 24,000 men and was responsible for military service during the tenth month of the year. This suggests that Maharai held a significant leadership position within David's army and was entrusted with important military responsibilities. No further details are provided about Maharai's personal life or his specific exploits as a warrior. His inclusion in the biblical record highlights the importance of military strength and loyalty in the establishment and maintenance of the Davidic kingdom.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.28 only referred to as Maharai (מַהֲרַי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.28에 처음 언급되며 '마하래'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느도바 사람 마하래는 다윗의 용맹한 용사이며 그의 군대에서 지휘관으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped purify the temple under Hezekiah
persons.short: Mahath, a Levite, participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Mahath is mentioned in 2 Chronicles as one of the Levites who participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah (2Ch.29.12). Hezekiah initiated a religious reform that included the cleansing and restoration of the temple, which had fallen into disrepair and neglect under the previous kings (2Ch.29.3-11). Mahath, along with other Levites from the clans of Kohath and Merari, was summoned by the king to assist in this important task (2Ch.29.12). The Levites played a crucial role in the temple's purification, as they were responsible for removing the unclean items, carrying them outside the city, and preparing the temple for proper worship (2Ch.29.15-19). Mahath's participation in this event highlights the significance of the Levites in maintaining the religious life of Judah and their dedication to restoring proper worship practices. No further details are provided about Mahath's personal life or his other responsibilities as a Levite. His inclusion in the biblical record emphasizes the importance of religious reform and the collective effort required to maintain the purity and sanctity of the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.12 only referred to as Mahath (מַ֫חַת); a son of Amasai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.12에 처음 언급되며 '마핫'이라 불림. 아마새의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 마핫은 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 일에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who assisted in distributing tithes during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.short: Mahath, a Levite, helped distribute tithes in Hezekiah's time.
persons.article: Mahath was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He was appointed as one of the assistants to oversee the distribution of tithes and offerings brought by the people to the Temple. This event took place during Hezekiah's religious reforms, when he sought to restore proper worship and support for the Levites and priests (2Ch.31.13).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.31.13 only referred to as Mahath (מַ֫חַת).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.13에 처음 언급되며 '마핫'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 마핫은 히스기야 시대에 십일조를 분배하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Warriors from or of Mahav(?)
persons.brief: Some of David's mighty men, possibly from Mahavim.
persons.short: The Mahavites were represented among David's mighty men.
persons.article: The Mahavites are mentioned in the context of listing David's mighty men, a group of elite warriors who fought alongside him. In 1Ch.11.46, the Mahavites are listed among these warriors, suggesting that at least one of David's mighty men came from a place or clan called Mahavim. However, no further information is provided about their identity or location.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Mahav(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.11.46 only referred to as Mahavites (מַחֲוִים).
persons.summary_ko: 마하위 사람. 1Ch.11.46에 처음 언급되며 '마하위'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마하위 족속은 다윗의 용사 중에 대표되었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: Son of Heman, a musician in David's time.
persons.short: Mahazioth, a son of Heman, served as a musician during David's reign.
persons.article: Mahazioth was one of the fourteen sons of Heman, a prominent musician and seer in King David's court. He was appointed by David to serve in the Temple as a musician, along with his brothers. Mahazioth and his brothers were skilled in music and were responsible for providing musical accompaniment during religious services. They were divided into twenty-four groups, each responsible for their duties in rotation (1Ch.25.4, 30).
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Mahazioth (מַחֲזִיאֹת); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '마하시옷'이라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디와 호딜의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마하시옷은 헤만의 아들 중 한 사람으로, 다윗 왕 시대에 음악가로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Symbolic name given to Isaiah's son, meaning "swift is booty, speedy is prey."
persons.short: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning "swift is booty, speedy is prey," was the symbolic name given to Isaiah's son.
persons.article: Maher-shalal-hash-baz was the name given to the son of the prophet Isaiah. The name, which means "swift is booty, speedy is prey," was a prophetic message about the impending Assyrian invasion of Syria and Israel. God instructed Isaiah to write this name on a large scroll and have it witnessed by reliable people. When Isaiah's wife, the prophetess, conceived and gave birth to a son, God commanded Isaiah to name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz. The child's name was a sign that before he would be old enough to say "father" or "mother," the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria would be carried away by the king of Assyria (Isa.8.1, 3).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Isa.8.1 only referred to as Maher-shalal-hash-baz (מַהֵר שָׁלָל חָשׁ בַּז); son of Isaiah; a brother of Shear-jashub.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Isa.8.1에 처음 언급되며 '마헬살랄하스바스'라 불림. 이사야의 아들. 스알야숩의 형제.
persons.short_ko: '노략이 속하고 탈취가 빠르다'는 뜻의 마헬살랄하스바스는 선지자 이사야의 아들에게 지어진 상징적인 이름이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad's sister.
persons.short: Mahlah was the daughter of Zelophehad's sister.
persons.article: Mahlah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh. She was the daughter of Zelophehad's sister, who is not named in the text.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.18 only referred to as Mahlah (מַחְלָה); her mother was Hammolecheth; a sister of Ishhod and Abiezer.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.7.18에 처음 언급되며 '말라'라 불림. 함몰레겟의 남편(이름 미상)와 함몰레겟의 딸. 이스홋과 아비에셀의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 마흘라는 슬로브핫의 자매의 딸이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad, who received an inheritance among her brothers.
persons.short: Mahlah, a daughter of Zelophehad, received an inheritance among her brothers.
persons.article: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, a man from the tribe of Manasseh. Zelophehad had no sons, and according to the law, his inheritance would pass to his brothers. However, Mahlah and her sisters approached Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. They argued that their father's name should not disappear from his clan because he had no sons and that they should receive an inheritance among their father's relatives. Moses brought their case before God, who agreed with the daughters and instructed Moses to give them property as an inheritance among their father's relatives, setting a precedent for cases where a man died without sons. Mahlah and her sisters received an inheritance in the land of Canaan (Num.26.33; 27.1; 36.11; Jos.17.3).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.33 only referred to as Mahlah (מַחְלָה); daughter of Zelophehad; a sister of Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Num.26.33에 처음 언급되며 '말라'라 불림. 슬로브핫의 딸. 노아, 호글라, 밀가와 디르사의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 슬로브핫의 딸 마흘라는 그녀의 형제들 사이에서 유산을 받았다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Mushi, grandson of Merari.
persons.short: Mahli, a son of Mushi and grandson of Merari, was a Levite during the time of David.
persons.article: Mahli was a Levite who lived during the reign of King David. He was a son of Mushi and a grandson of Merari. Mahli and his brothers were appointed by David to serve in various roles in the temple. They were part of the division of Levites responsible for the service of the house of the Lord (1Ch.6.47; 23.23; 24.30).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.47 only referred to as Mahli (מַחְלִי); son of Mushi; a brother of Eder and Jerimoth; father of Shemer.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.47에 처음 언급되며 '말리'라 불림. 무시의 아들. 에델과 여레못의 형제. 세멜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마흘리는 무시의 아들이며 므라리의 손자로, 다윗 시대의 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Merari, grandson of Levi.
persons.short: Mahli, a son of Merari and grandson of Levi, was an ancestor of the Mahlites.
persons.article: Mahli was one of the sons of Merari and a grandson of Levi. He was an ancestor of the Levitical clan known as the Mahlites. Mahli's descendants were responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and later in the temple. They were counted in the census of the Levites during the time of Moses and were given specific responsibilities in the transportation and setup of the tabernacle
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.19 referred to as Mahli (מַחְלִי), or Mahlite (מַחְלִי); son of Merari; a brother of Mushi and Jaaziah; father of Libni, Eleazar and Kish.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Exo.6.19에 처음 언급되며 '마흘리'라 불림. 므라리의 아들. 무시와 야아시야의 형제. 립니, 엘르아살과 기스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마흘리는 므라리의 아들이며 레위의 손자로, 마흘리 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Husband of Ruth, son of Elimelech and Naomi.
persons.short: Mahlon, the son of Elimelech and Naomi, married Ruth but died in Moab.
persons.article: Mahlon was the son of Elimelech and Naomi from Bethlehem in Judah. He had a brother named Chilion. Due to a famine in Judah, Elimelech took his family to live in the country of Moab. There, Mahlon married a Moabite woman named Ruth. However, Elimelech, Mahlon, and Chilion all died in Moab, leaving Naomi and her daughters-in-law as widows. When Naomi decided to return to Judah, Ruth chose to go with her. In Bethlehem, Boaz, a relative of Elimelech, acted as a kinsman-redeemer. He married Ruth and bought the property that had belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon to maintain their inheritance (Rut.1.2, 5; 4.9, 10).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.1.2 only referred to as Mahlon (מַחְלוֹן); son of Elimelech and Naomi; a brother of Chilion; husband of Ruth.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Rut.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '말론'이라 불림. 엘리멜렉과 나오미의 아들. 기룐의 형제. 룻의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 엘리멜렉과 나오미의 아들 말론은 룻과 결혼했으나 모압에서 죽었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of wise men surpassed in wisdom by Solomon.
persons.short: Mahol was the father of wise men whom Solomon surpassed in wisdom.
persons.article: Mahol is mentioned in the context of describing King Solomon's wisdom. He was the father of Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, who were known for their wisdom. However, Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of these men and all the wisdom of Egypt.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.31 only referred to as Mahol (מָחוֹל); father of Ethan, Heman, Calcol, Darda.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.31에 처음 언급되며 '마홀'이라 불림. 세라의 아들. 에단, 헤만, 갈골과 다르다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마홀은 솔로몬이 그 지혜를 능가했던 지혜로운 사람들의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe.
persons.short: Mahseiah was the grandfather of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe.
persons.article: Mahseiah is mentioned as the grandfather of Baruch, who served as the scribe and assistant to the prophet Jeremiah. In one instance, Baruch was tasked with writing down Jeremiah's words on a scroll and reading them in the temple (Jer.32.12). Later, Baruch accompanied Seraiah, the quartermaster, on a journey to Babylon, carrying a message from Jeremiah (Jer.51.59).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.32.12 only referred to as Mahseiah (מַחְסֵיָה); father of Neriah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.32.12에 처음 언급되며 '마세아'라 불림. 네리야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마아세야는 예레미야의 서기관 바룩의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prophet who wrote the book bearing his name.
persons.short: Malachi, a prophet, received the word of the Lord to Israel.
persons.article: Malachi was a prophet of the Lord who delivered a message to the people of Israel after their return from Babylonian exile. The opening verse of the book bearing his name states that the word of the Lord came to Israel through Malachi. The name "Malachi" means "my messenger" in Hebrew. Malachi confronted the people about their spiritual apathy, their neglect of proper worship, and their disobedience to God's laws. He also foretold the coming of a messenger who would prepare the way for the Lord (Mal.1.1).
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Mal.1.1 only referred to as Malachi (מַלְאָכִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Mal.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '말라기'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 말라기는 이스라엘에 대한 여호와의 말씀을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jobab@1Ch.8.9, Zibia@1Ch.8.9, Mesha@1Ch.8.9, Jeuz@1Ch.8.10, Sachia@1Ch.8.10, Mirmah@1Ch.8.10, Abitub@1Ch.8.11, Elpaal@1Ch.8.11-
persons.brief: Son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
persons.short: Malcam was a son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, born in Moab.
persons.article: Malcam is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He was one of the sons of Shaharaim, who had sent away his wives Hushim and Baara. Shaharaim had children in the country of Moab, including Malcam.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.9 only referred to as Malcam (מַלְכָּם); son of Shaharaim and Hodesh; a brother of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Jeuz, Sachia, Mirmah, Abitub and Elpaal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '말감'이라 불림. 사하라임과 호데스의 아들. 요밥, 시비야, 메사, 여우스, 사갸, 미르마, 아비둡과 엘바알의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 말감은 베냐민 사람 사하라임이 모압 땅에서 낳은 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Pashur, involved in plot against Jeremiah.
persons.short: Malchiah, son of Pashur, was involved in a plot against Jeremiah.
persons.article: Malchiah was the son of Pashur, a priest during the time of the prophet Jeremiah. He was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's message in the temple court and reported it to the other officials. Later, Malchiah was among those who plotted against Jeremiah and had him thrown into a cistern, leaving him to die. However, Ebed-Melech, an Ethiopian eunuch, rescued Jeremiah from the cistern (Jer.38.1, 6; 21.1).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.21.1 referred to as Malchiah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ); father of Pashhur.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.21.1에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림. 바스훌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바스훌의 아들 말기야는 예레미야를 대적하는 음모에 가담했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, grandson of Asher.
persons.short: Malchiel, son of Beriah and grandson of Asher, was the ancestor of the Malchielites.
persons.article: Malchiel was a son of Beriah and a grandson of Asher, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher. Malchiel's descendants were known as the Malchielites and were counted in the census of the Israelites during the time of Moses. They formed one of the clans within the tribe of Asher (Gen.46.17; Num.26.45; 1Ch.7.31).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.17 referred to as Malchiel (מַלְכִּיאֵל), or Malchielite (מַלְכִּיאֵלִי); son of Beriah; a brother of Heber; father or founder of Birzaith.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.17에 처음 언급되며 '말기엘'이라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 헤벨의 형제. 비르사잇의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 말기엘은 브리아의 아들이며 아셀의 손자로, 말기엘 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Head of the fifth priestly division in David's time.
persons.short: Malchijah was the head of the fifth priestly division during David's reign.
persons.article: Malchijah was a priest who served during the reign of King David. He was appointed as the head of the fifth division of the priestly order when David organized the priests into 24 divisions for their service in the temple (1Ch.24.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.9 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.24.9에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 말기야는 다윗 시대에 다섯 번째 제사장 반차의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ethni, a Gershonite Levite.
persons.short: Malchijah, a son of Ethni, was a Gershonite Levite.
persons.article: Malchijah was a Levite who belonged to the Gershonite clan, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. He was the son of Ethni and is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites (1Ch.6.40).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.40 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ); a son of Jeatherai; father of Baaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.40에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림. 여아드래의 아들. 바아세야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 말기야는 에드니의 아들로 게르손 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.short: Malchijah was a priest who served during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Malchijah was a priest who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the return of the Jews from Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the lists of priests and Levites who settled in Jerusalem (1Ch.9.12; Neh.11.12).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ); a brother of Jerahmeel; a son of Hammelech; father of Pashhur.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림. 왕의 아들. 여라므엘의 형제. 바스훌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 말기야는 느헤미야 시대에 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Parosh, who divorced his foreign wife.
persons.short: Malchijah, a descendant of Parosh, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Malchijah was a man from the family of Parosh who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. As part of Ezra's reforms to purify the Jewish community, Malchijah and others who had married foreign wives were required to divorce them (Ezr.10.25). The presence of two similar men in the same verse named Malchijah in this list either indicates that it was a common name during this period, or a scribal error.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.25 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.25a에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바로스의 후손 말기야는 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 이혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Parosh, who divorced his foreign wife.
persons.short: Malchijah, known as Hashabiah in the LXX, a descendant of Parosh, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Malchijah (or Malkijah in the NIV) was a man from the family of Parosh who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. He has a brother who is also called Malchijah, so some BIbles translate his name as Hashabiah as in the LXX. As part of Ezra's reforms to purify the Jewish community, Malchijah and others who had married foreign wives were required to divorce them (Ezr.10.25). The presence of two similar men in the same verse named Malchijah in this list either indicates that it was a common name during this period, or a scribal error.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.25 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.25b에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 칠십인역에서는 하사뱌로 불리는 바로스의 후손 말기야도 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 이혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Harim, who divorced his foreign wife.
persons.short: Malchijah, a descendant of Harim, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Malchijah was a man from the family of Harim who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. As part of Ezra's reforms to purify the Jewish community, Malchijah and others who had married foreign wives were required to divorce them (Ezr.10.31).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.31 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.31에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하림의 후손 말기야는 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 이혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Malchijah, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Malchijah was a priest who was among the leaders that sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. This covenant was made between the people of Israel and God, in which they pledged to follow the Law of Moses, keep the Sabbath holy, and support the temple service. Malchijah, along with other priests, Levites, and leaders, signed this covenant as a representative of the people (Neh.10.3).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.3 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 말기야는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Malchijah, a priest, participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Malchijah was a priest who lived during the time of Nehemiah. He was among the priests and Levites who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after it had been rebuilt. During the dedication ceremony, Malchijah and other priests played musical instruments and offered thanksgiving to God (Neh.12.42).
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.42에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 말기야는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Harim, helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Malchijah, son of Harim, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Malchijah, the son of Harim, was one of the people who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. He worked on rebuilding a section of the wall, alongside Hashub, the son of Pahath-Moab (Neh.3.11).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.11 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ); a son of Harim.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.11에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림. 하림의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하림의 아들 말기야는 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Rechab, repaired the Dung Gate in Jerusalem.
persons.short: Malchijah, son of Rechab, repaired the Dung Gate during Nehemiah's wall restoration.
persons.article: Malchijah, the son of Rechab, was a ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem. He participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. Malchijah was responsible for repairing the Dung Gate, one of the gates in the city wall (Neh.3.14).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.14 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ); a son of Rechab.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.14에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림. 레갑의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레갑의 아들 말기야는 느헤미야의 성벽 재건 사업 당시 분문을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Goldsmith who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Malchijah, a goldsmith, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near the Levites.
persons.article: Malchijah, a goldsmith, was among those who worked on repairing the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. He restored a section of the wall next to the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate and as far as the room above the corner (Neh.3.31).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.31 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.31에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 금장색 말기야는 레위인들 근처의 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law.
persons.short: Malchijah, a priest, stood beside Ezra as he read the Law to the people.
persons.article: Malchijah was a priest who lived during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. When Ezra read the Book of the Law to the assembled people in Jerusalem, Malchijah was one of the priests who stood beside him on the platform. This event took place during the Feast of Tabernacles, after the Jews had returned from Babylonian exile (Neh.8.4).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Malchijah (מַלְכִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '말기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 말기야는 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 낭독할 때 그 곁에 섰다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah.
persons.short: Malchiram was a descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah.
persons.article: Malchiram was one of the descendant of King Jeconiah, also known as Jehoiachin, who ruled over the Kingdom of Judah. Jeconiah was taken captive by the Babylonians and spent many years in exile. Malchiram is mentioned in the genealogy of the kings of Judah, but no further details about his life are provided (1Ch.3.18).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.18 only referred to as Malchiram (מַלְכִּירָם); son of Shealtiel(?); a brother of Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.18에 처음 언급되며 '말기람'이라 불림. 스알디엘의 아들. 브다야, 세낫살, 여가먀, 호사마와 느다뱌의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 말기람은 유다 왕 여고냐(여호야긴)의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Merab@1Sa.14.49-2Sa, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch, Armoni@2Sa.21.8, Mephibosheth@2Sa.21.8
persons.brief: Son of King Saul, killed in battle against the Philistines.
persons.short: Malchi-shua, a son of King Saul, was killed in battle against the Philistines.
persons.article: Malchi-shua was one of the sons of King Saul, the first king of Israel. He was a brother of Jonathan, Abinadab, and Ishvi. Malchi-shua fought alongside his father and brothers in the battles against the Philistines. In a fierce battle on Mount Gilboa, the Philistines overwhelmed the Israelite army. Malchi-shua, along with his brothers Jonathan and Abinadab, was killed in the battle. King Saul, upon seeing his sons dead and facing imminent capture, took his own life by falling on his sword (1Sa.14.49; 31.2; 1Ch.8.33; 9.39; 10.2).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.14.49 only referred to as Malchi-shua (מַלְכִּישׁוּעַ); son of Saul and Ahinoam; a brother of Jonathan, Abinadab, Merab and Michal; half-brother of: Ish-bosheth, Armoni and Mephibosheth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.14.49에 처음 언급되며 '말기수아'라 불림. 사울과 아히노암의 아들. 요나단, 아비나답, 메랍, 미갈, 이스보셋, 알모니와 므비보셋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사울 왕의 아들 말기수아는 블레셋과의 전투에서 죽었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: High priest's servant whose ear was cut off by Peter.
persons.short: Malchus, the high priest's servant, had his ear cut off by Peter during Jesus' arrest.
persons.article: Malchus was a servant of the high priest during the time of Jesus' arrest in the Garden of Gethsemane. When the crowd, led by Judas Iscariot, came to arrest Jesus, Simon Peter drew his sword and struck Malchus, cutting off his right ear. Jesus rebuked Peter for his violent act and healed Malchus' ear, demonstrating his compassion and willingness to show love even to his enemies (Jhn.18.10).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Jhn.18.10 only referred to as Malchus (Μάλχος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Jhn.18.10에 처음 언급되며 '말고'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 대제사장의 종 말고는 예수님이 체포되실 때 베드로에게 귀가 잘렸다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: Son of Heman, a musician in David's court.
persons.short: Mallothi, a son of Heman, was a musician in David's court.
persons.article: Mallothi was one of the sons of Heman, a prominent musician in King David's court. Heman, along with Asaph and Jeduthun, was appointed by David to lead the music and thanksgiving in the tabernacle. Mallothi and his brothers were skilled musicians who prophesied with lyres, harps, and cymbals. They were assigned by lot to serve in the tabernacle, with Mallothi being the nineteenth in order (1Ch.25.4, 26).
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Mallothi (מַלּוֹתִי); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Hothir, Mahazioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '말로디'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 말로디는 헤만의 아들로 다윗 궁정의 음악가였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hashabiah, a Merarite Levite.
persons.short: Malluch, a son of Hashabiah, was a Merarite Levite.
persons.article: Malluch was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari. He was the son of Hashabiah and is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites (1Ch.6.44).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.44 only referred to as Malluch (מַלּוּךְ); a son of Hashabiah; father of Abdi.

persons.short_ko: 하사뱌의 아들 말룩은 므라리 가문 레위인이었다.

persons.short: Malluch, a descendant of Bani, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Malluch was a man from the family of Bani who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. As part of Ezra's reforms to purify the Jewish community, Malluch and others who had married foreign wives were required to divorce them (Ezr.10.29).

persons.short_ko: 바니의 후손 말룩은 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 이혼했다.
