persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Malluch was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Malluch was one of the individuals who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. This covenant was made between the people of Israel and God, in which they pledged to follow the Law of Moses, keep the Sabbath holy, and support the temple service. Malluch, along with other leaders and people, signed this covenant as a commitment to obey God's commands (Neh.10.27).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.27 only referred to as Malluch (מַלּוּךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '말룩'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 말룩은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Malluch, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Malluch was a priest who lived during the time of Nehemiah. He was among the leaders who sealed the covenant between the people of Israel and God, pledging to follow the Law of Moses, keep the Sabbath holy, and support the temple service (Neh.10.4). Malluch is also mentioned in the list of priests who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Neh.12.2 and in the list of priestly families during the high priesthood of Joiakim )(Neh.12.14).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.4 referred to as Malluch (מַלּוּךְ), or Mallichi (מְלִיכוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.4에 처음 언급되며 '말룩'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 말룩은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Amorite, ally of Abraham.
persons.short: Mamre was an Amorite and an ally of Abraham.
persons.article: Mamre was an Amorite who lived during the time of Abraham. He was described as an ally or confederate of Abraham, along with his brothers Eshcol and Aner. When Abraham learned that his nephew Lot had been captured by a coalition of kings, he gathered his trained servants and pursued them. Mamre and his brothers joined Abraham in this rescue mission, demonstrating their loyalty and support for Abraham (Gen.14.13).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.14.13 only referred to as Mamre (מַמְרֵא); a brother of Eshcol and Aner.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.14.13에 처음 언급되며 '마므레'라 불림. 마므레의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 에스골과 아넬의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마므레는 아모리 사람이며 아브라함의 동맹자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch.
persons.short: Manaen, a prophet and teacher, was part of the church at Antioch.
persons.article: Manaen was a prophet and teacher in the early Christian church at Antioch. He is mentioned alongside other prominent figures such as Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, and Saul (later known as Paul). Manaen is described as having been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, indicating that he may have had a connection to the Herodian royal family. As a prophet and teacher, Manaen played a role in the worship, instruction, and leadership of the church at Antioch (Act.13.1).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.13.1 only referred to as Manaen (Μαναήν).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.13.1에 처음 언급되며 '마나엔'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자이며 교사인 마나엔은 안디옥 교회의 일원이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Shobal, a Horite.
persons.short: Manahath was a son of Shobal, a Horite.
persons.article: Manahath was a Horite, a descendant of Seir, who lived in the land of Edom. He was the son of Shobal and is mentioned in the genealogies of the Horites (Gen.36.23; 1Ch.1.40).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.23 referred to as Manahath (מָנַ֫חַת), or Manahathite (מָנַ֫חַת), or "half the Manahathites" (חֲצִי הַמְּנַחְתִּי ); son of Shobal; a brother of Alvan, Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.23에 처음 언급되며 '마나핫'이라 불림. 소발의 아들. 알완, 에발, 스보와 오남의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마나핫은 호리 사람 소발의 아들이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, son of Hezekiah.
persons.short: Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, was a king of Judah who reigned for 55 years.
persons.article: Manasseh was the fourteenth king of Judah, succeeding his father, Hezekiah. He began his reign at the age of twelve and ruled for fifty-five years, making him the longest-reigning king of Judah. However, Manasseh's reign was marked by evil and idolatry. He rebuilt the high places that his father had destroyed, erected altars for Baal, and made an Asherah pole. He even sacrificed his own son and practiced sorcery and divination. Manasseh's actions led the people of Judah astray, and they did more evil than the nations that God had destroyed before the Israelites. As a result, God announced judgment on Judah and Jerusalem, stating that He would wipe them out like a dish, turning it upside down. Manasseh also shed much innocent blood, filling Jerusalem from end to end. However, when Manasseh was captured by the Assyrians and taken to Babylon, he humbled himself before God and prayed. God heard his prayer and restored him to Jerusalem, where Manasseh acknowledged the Lord as God and attempted to undo some of the evil he had done. Despite this, the damage to Judah was severe, and the nation continued to face the consequences of Manasseh's sins even after his death. Manasseh was buried in his palace garden, and his son Amon succeeded him as king.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.20.21 referred to as Manasseh (מְנַשֶּׁה), or Manasseh (Μανασσῆς); a son of Hezekiah and Hephzibah; husband of Meshullemeth; father of Amon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.20.21에 처음 언급되며 '므낫세'라 불림. 히스기야와 헵시바의 아들. 므술레멧의 남편. 아몬의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 히스기야의 아들 므낫세는 유다 왕으로 오십오 년간 다스렸다.
persons.article_ko: 므낫세는 유다의 열네 번째 왕으로 아버지 히스기야를 이었다. 그는 십이 세에 통치를 시작하여 오십오 년간 다스려 유다 왕 중 가장 오랜 기간 통치한 왕이 되었다. 그러나 므낫세의 통치는 악함과 우상숭배로 얼룩졌다. 그는 아버지가 헐어버린 산당들을 다시 세우고 바알을 위한 제단들을 세웠으며 아세라 목상을 만들었다. 그는 심지어 자기 아들을 제물로 바치고 마술과 점술을 행했다. 므낫세의 행동은 유다 백성을 잘못된 길로 이끌었고, 그들은 하나님이 이스라엘 백성 앞에서 멸하신 민족들보다 더 많은 악을 행했다. 그 결과 하나님은 유다와 예루살렘에 대한 심판을 선언하시며 그들을 접시처럼 씻어 엎으시겠다고 말씀하셨다. 므낫세는 또한 무죄한 피를 심히 많이 흘려 예루살렘을 이 끝에서 저 끝까지 채웠다. 그러나 므낫세가 앗수르 사람들에게 사로잡혀 바벨론으로 끌려갔을 때 그는 하나님 앞에서 스스로를 겸비하게 하고 기도했다. 하나님은 그의 기도를 들으시고 그를 예루살렘으로 회복시키셨고, 그곳에서 므낫세는 여호와가 하나님이심을 인정하며 자신이 행한 악의 일부를 되돌리려 했다. 그럼에도 유다에 대한 피해는 심각했고, 그 민족은 므낫세가 죽은 후에도 계속 그의 죄의 결과에 직면했다. 므낫세는 자기 왕궁 정원에 묻혔고 그의 아들 아몬이 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.

persons.description: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Firstborn son of Joseph, blessed by Jacob.
persons.short: Manasseh, Joseph's firstborn, was blessed by Jacob and became a tribe of Israel.
persons.article: Manasseh was the firstborn son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt before the famine. When Israel (or 'Jacob') blessed Joseph's sons, he gave the greater blessing to Ephraim, the younger son, despite Joseph's objection. The tribe of Manasseh, along with Ephraim, became one of the twelve tribes of Israel. During the Exodus, the tribe of Manasseh was counted in the census and arranged in the camp under their standard. They had a significant population and contributed to the army. Notable descendants of Manasseh include Gaddi, who was among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan, and Zelophehad's daughters, who received an inheritance among their uncles due to their father's lack of sons. When the Promised Land was divided, half of the tribe of Manasseh settled east of the Jordan River, while the other half settled west of the Jordan. The eastern portion of Manasseh, along with Reuben and Gad, assisted in the conquest of Canaan before returning to their inheritance. The western portion of Manasseh received cities and territories, including the city of refuge, Golan. Throughout Israel's history, the tribe of Manasseh played significant roles. They participated in the conquest of Canaan, fought alongside Gideon against the Midianites, and joined David's army. However, they also faced challenges, such as incomplete conquest of their territories and occasional conflicts with other tribes. In later prophecies, Manasseh is mentioned as part of the restored Israel. The tribe is also listed among the sealed servants of God in the Book of Revelation. Manasseh is also used to refer to the territory allotted to the tribe of Manasseh. The tribe's inheritance was divided between the eastern and western portions of the Promised Land. The eastern portion of Manasseh's territory was conquered by Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, and was named Havvoth-jair. This region was known for its small towns and villages. The western portion of Manasseh's territory was located in the heart of Canaan. It included cities such as Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo, along with their villages. However, the Manassites were unable to drive out the Canaanites from these cities completely. Manasseh's territory also included the city of refuge, Golan, in the region of Bashan. This city was designated as a place of asylum for those who unintentionally caused the death of another person. The territory of Manasseh is mentioned in the context of the conquest of Canaan, the division of the land among the tribes, and the establishment of cities of refuge. It is also noted in the description of the regions that remained loyal to the house of David during the reign of King Pekah of Israel.
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.41.51 referred to as Manasseh or Manassite (מְנַשֶּׁה), or Manassite or Manassite (מְנַשִּׁי), or Manasseh (Μανασσῆς); son of Joseph and Asenath; a brother of Ephraim; had an Aramitess concubine; father of Machir and Asriel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 요셉의 아들. Gen.41.51에 처음 언급되며 '므낫세'라 불림. 요셉과 아스낫의 아들. 에브라임의 형제. 아람의 남편. 마길과 아스리엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 요셉의 맏아들 므낫세는 야곱에게 축복을 받아 이스라엘의 한 지파가 되었다.
persons.article_ko: 므낫세는 요셉과 아스낫의 맏아들로, 흉년이 오기 전 애굽에서 태어났다. 이스라엘(야곱)이 요셉의 아들들을 축복할 때, 요셉의 반대에도 불구하고 동생 에브라임에게 더 큰 축복을 주었다. 므낫세 지파는 에브라임과 함께 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나가 되었다. 출애굽 당시 므낫세 지파는 인구조사에 포함되어 진영에서 그들의 깃발 아래 배치되었다. 그들은 상당한 인구를 가졌고 군대에 기여했다. 므낫세의 저명한 후손으로는 가나안을 정탐하도록 보내진 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람인 갓디, 그리고 아버지에게 아들이 없어 숙부들 사이에서 유산을 받은 슬로브핫의 딸들이 있다. 약속의 땅이 분배될 때 므낫세 지파의 절반은 요단강 동편에, 나머지 절반은 요단강 서편에 정착했다. 므낫세의 동편 부분은 르우벤과 갓과 함께 가나안 정복을 도운 후 자기 기업으로 돌아갔다. 므낫세의 서편 부분은 도피성 골란을 포함한 성읍들과 영토를 받았다. 이스라엘 역사 전반에 걸쳐 므낫세 지파는 중요한 역할을 했다. 그들은 가나안 정복에 참여하고, 기드온과 함께 미디안을 대적하여 싸웠으며, 다윗의 군대에 합류했다. 그러나 그들은 자기 영토의 불완전한 정복이나 다른 지파들과의 간헐적인 갈등 같은 어려움도 겪었다. 후기 예언에서 므낫세는 회복된 이스라엘의 일부로 언급된다. 그 지파는 요한계시록에서 하나님의 인침 받은 종들 명단에도 포함된다. 므낫세라는 이름은 므낫세 지파에게 분배된 영토를 가리키는 데도 사용된다. 그 지파의 기업은 약속의 땅의 동편과 서편으로 나뉘었다. 므낫세 영토의 동편 부분은 므낫세의 후손 야일이 정복했고 하봇야일이라 불렸다. 이 지역은 작은 마을과 촌락들로 알려졌다. 므낫세 영토의 서편 부분은 가나안 중심부에 있었다. 그곳에는 벧산, 이블르암, 돌, 엔돌, 다아낙, 므깃도와 그 주변 마을들이 포함되었다. 그러나 므낫세 사람들은 이 성읍들에서 가나안 사람들을 완전히 몰아내지 못했다. 므낫세의 영토에는 바산 지역의 도피성 골란도 포함되었다. 이 성읍은 실수로 다른 사람의 죽음을 초래한 자들을 위한 피난처로 지정되었다.

persons.description: Samson's father living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Samson, from the tribe of Dan.
persons.short: Manoah, Samson's father from the tribe of Dan, was visited by the Angel of the Lord who announced Samson's birth.
persons.article: Manoah was an Israelite from the tribe of Dan, and he was the father of Samson. Manoah's wife was barren, but the Angel of the Lord appeared to her and announced that she would conceive and give birth to a son who would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. The Angel instructed her to follow specific guidelines during her pregnancy and to raise the child as a Nazirite. Manoah prayed for the Angel to return and teach them how to raise the child, and the Angel appeared again, reiterating the instructions. Manoah offered a young goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, and the Angel ascended in the flame of the altar, confirming his divine nature. Manoah and his wife named their son Samson, and the Lord blessed him as he grew. After Samson's death, he was buried in the tomb of his father, Manoah, between Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 13; 16:31).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.13.2 only referred to as Manoah (מָנוֹחַ); father of Samson.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 삼손의 아버지. Jdg.13.2에 처음 언급되며 '마노아'라 불림. 삼손의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 단 지파 출신 삼손의 아버지 마노아는 여호와의 사자로부터 삼손의 탄생을 예고받았다.
persons.article_ko: 마노아는 단 지파 출신 이스라엘 사람으로, 삼손의 아버지였다. 마노아의 아내는 불임이었으나, 여호와의 사자가 그녀에게 나타나 그녀가 잉태하여 블레셋에게서 이스라엘을 구원하기 시작할 아들을 낳을 것이라고 알려주었다. 그 사자는 그녀에게 임신 중 특정한 지침을 따르고 그 아이를 나실인으로 기르라고 지시했다. 마노아는 그 사자가 다시 와서 아이를 어떻게 기를지 가르쳐달라고 기도했고, 그 사자는 다시 나타나 지침을 반복했다. 마노아는 여호와께 어린 염소를 제물로 드렸고, 그 사자는 제단의 불꽃 속에서 올라가 그의 신적 본성을 확인해주었다. 마노아와 그의 아내는 그들의 아들을 삼손이라 이름 짓고, 그가 자라면서 여호와께서 그를 축복하셨다. 삼손이 죽은 후 그는 소라와 에스다올 사이에 있는 그의 아버지 마노아의 무덤에 묻혔다(사사기 13장; 16:31).

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Achish, king of Gath.
persons.short: Maoch (or Maacah) was the father of Achish, king of Gath, to whom David fled.
persons.article: Maoch, also known as Maacah, was the father of Achish, the king of Gath, a Philistine city. When David was fleeing from King Saul, he sought refuge with Achish in Gath. Achish, the son of Maoch, received David and his men, allowing them to settle in the city. Later, when David was king of Israel, two of his servants fled to Achish, the son of Maacah, in Gath (1Sa.27.2; 1Ki.2.39). The variation in the name (Maoch or Maacah) may indicate different spellings or translations of the same name.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.27.2 referred to as Maoch (מָעוֹךְ), or Maacah (מַעֲכָה); father of Achish.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.27.2에 처음 언급되며 '마옥'이라 불림. 아기스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마옥(마아가라고도 함)은 다윗이 도망간 가드 왕 아기스의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shammai, a descendant of Caleb.
persons.short: Maon, a son of Shammai, was a descendant of Caleb.
persons.article: Maon was a descendant of Caleb, the son of Hezron, from the tribe of Judah. He was the son of Shammai and is mentioned in the genealogy of Caleb's descendants (1Ch.2.45).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.45 only referred to as Maon (מָעוֹן); a son of Shammai; founder of Beth-zur.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.45에 처음 언급되며 '마온'이라 불림. 삼매의 아들. Beth-zur의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마온은 삼매의 아들이며 갈렙의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Mesha, re-founder of Hebron.
persons.short: Mareshah, a son of Mesha, was the father and re-founder of Hebron.
persons.article: Mareshah was a son of Mesha, son of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, from the tribe of Judah. He restored and re-founded Hebron which had been given to his father (Josh 14.3 who removed the Anakim who inhabited it )(Jdg.1.20). Mareshah is mentioned in the genealogy of Caleb's descendants (1Ch.2.42).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.42 only referred to as Mareshah (מָרֵשָׁה); son of Mesha; father and re-founder of Hebron.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.42에 처음 언급되며 '마레사'라 불림. 메사의 아들. 헤브론의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마레사는 메사의 아들이며 헤브론의 아버지이자 재건자였다.

persons.description: Man or town at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son or town of Laadah in Judah.
persons.short: Mareshah, a son or town of Laadah,  a descendant of Shelah from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Mareshah was a descendant or town of Mareshah, who is mentioned in the genealogy of the descendants of Shelah (1Ch.4.21).
persons.summary: A man or town of the tribe of Judah at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.21 only referred to as Mareshah (מָרֵשָׁה); a son of Laadah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 인물 또는 지명. 1Ch.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '마레사'라 불림. 라아다의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마레사는 유다 지파 셀라의 후손인 라아다의 아들 또는 그가 세운 성읍이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Cousin of Barnabas, companion of Paul, author of Gospel.
persons.short: Mark (also called John), Barnabas' cousin and Paul's companion, was the author of the Gospel of Mark.
persons.article: Mark, also known as John Mark, was a prominent figure in the early Christian church. He was the son of Mary, whose house in Jerusalem served as a meeting place for the believers (Act.12.12). Mark was also the cousin of Barnabas (Col.4.10 and accompanied Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey )(Act.12.25; 13.5). However, he left them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem (Act.13.13, which later caused a disagreement between Paul and Barnabas )(Act.15.37-39). Despite this, Mark remained active in ministry, as evidenced by Paul's later references to him as a fellow worker (Phm.1.24; 2Ti.4.11). He also worked closely with Peter, who referred to him as "my son Mark" (1Pe.5.13). Tradition holds that Mark wrote the Gospel that bears his name based on Peter's teachings, making it one of the earliest written accounts of Jesus' life and ministry.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.12.12 referred to as Mark (Μάρκος), or John (Ἰωάννης); his mother was Mary.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 레위인. Act.12.12에 처음 언급되며 '마가'라 불림. 마리아의 남편(이름 미상)와 마리아의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마가(요한이라고도 함)는 바나바의 사촌이며 바울의 동역자로, 마가복음의 저자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
persons.short: Marsena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advised King Ahasuerus.
persons.article: Marsena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus' presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom. These princes were consulted by the king when he sought advice regarding the appropriate response to Queen Vashti's refusal to appear before him and his guests (Est.1.14). The counsel of these princes led to the king's decision to remove Vashti as queen and seek a new queen to replace her.
persons.summary: A prince of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Marsena (מַרְסְנָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '마르스나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마르스나는 아하수에로 왕에게 조언한 페르시아와 메대의 일곱 방백 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, hosted Jesus.
persons.short: Martha, the sister of Mary and Lazarus, hosted Jesus in her home.
persons.article: Martha was a woman from Bethany who, along with her siblings Mary and Lazarus, was a close friend of Jesus. When Jesus visited their home, Martha welcomed Him and busied herself with serving, while her sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet, listening to His teachings. Martha complained to Jesus that Mary was not helping her, but Jesus gently reminded her that Mary had chosen the better part by focusing on His words (Luk.10.38-42). Later, when Lazarus fell ill and died, Martha went out to meet Jesus and expressed her faith in Him, saying that if He had been there, her brother would not have died. Jesus reassured her that Lazarus would rise again and proclaimed Himself as the resurrection and the life (Jhn.11.1-44). After Lazarus was raised from the dead, Martha served a meal for Jesus and His disciples, demonstrating her love and gratitude (Jhn.12.2).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.10.38 only referred to as Martha (Μάρθα); a sister of Mary and Lazarus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Luk.10.38에 처음 언급되며 '마르다'라 불림. 나사로의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 마리아와 나사로의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 마리아와 나사로의 자매 마르다는 자기 집에서 예수님을 대접했다.
persons.article_ko: 마르다는 베다니 출신 여성으로, 형제자매인 마리아, 나사로와 함께 예수님의 가까운 친구였다. 예수님이 그들의 집을 방문하셨을 때 마르다는 그분을 맞이하며 섬기는 일로 분주했고, 그녀의 자매 마리아는 예수님의 발치에 앉아 그분의 가르침을 들었다. 마르다는 마리아가 자신을 돕지 않는다고 예수님께 불평했으나, 예수님은 온화하게 마리아가 그분의 말씀에 집중함으로써 더 좋은 부분을 택했다고 상기시키셨다(눅 10:38-42). 후에 나사로가 병들어 죽었을 때 마르다는 예수님을 맞으러 나가 그분이 그곳에 계셨더라면 그녀의 형제가 죽지 않았을 것이라며 그분에 대한 믿음을 표현했다. 예수님은 나사로가 다시 살아날 것이라고 안심시키시며 자신이 부활이요 생명이라고 선포하셨다(요 11:1-44). 나사로가 죽음에서 살아난 후 마르다는 예수님과 그 제자들을 위해 식사를 섬겨 그녀의 사랑과 감사를 나타냈다(요 12:2).

persons.description: Barnabus' relative living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Mother of John Mark; hosted prayer meeting.
persons.short: Mary, the mother of John Mark, hosted a prayer meeting in her house.
persons.article: Mary was a woman living in Jerusalem and the mother of John Mark, who later became a companion of Paul and Barnabas. When Peter was miraculously released from prison, he went to Mary's house, where many believers had gathered to pray for him. This indicates that Mary's home served as a meeting place for the early church in Jerusalem (Act.12.12). Her son, John Mark, would later accompany Paul and Barnabas on their missionary journeys and was a source of disagreement between the two leaders (Act.12.25; 15.37-39). Tradition holds that John Mark wrote the Gospel that bears his name based on Peter's teachings.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.12.12 only referred to as Mary (Μαρία); a sister of Barnabas; mother of Mark.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 바나바의 친척. Act.12.12에 처음 언급되며 '마리아'라 불림. 바나바의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 바나바의 자매. 마리아의 남편(이름 미상)의 아내. 마가의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 요한 마가의 어머니 마리아는 자기 집에서 기도 모임을 대접했다.

persons.description: Lazarus' sister living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet.
persons.short: Mary, the sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet and anointed Him with perfume.
persons.article: Mary was a woman from Bethany, the sister of Martha and Lazarus, and a close friend of Jesus. When Jesus visited their home, Mary sat at His feet, listening intently to His teachings, while her sister Martha was busy serving. When Martha complained that Mary was not helping, Jesus commended Mary for choosing the better part by focusing on His words (Luk.10.39, 42). After the death of Lazarus, Mary fell at Jesus' feet, expressing her grief and faith in Him. Jesus was deeply moved by her sorrow and wept with her before raising Lazarus from the dead (Jhn.11.1-44). Later, during a meal at their home, Mary took a pound of expensive perfume and anointed Jesus' feet, wiping them with her hair. This act of devotion and love was criticized by Judas Iscariot, but Jesus defended her, stating that she had anointed Him for His burial (Jhn.12.3-8).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.10.39 only referred to as Mary (Μαρία); a sister of Martha and Lazarus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 나사로의 자매. Luk.10.39에 처음 언급되며 '마리아'라 불림. 나사로의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 마르다와 나사로의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 마르다와 나사로의 자매 마리아는 예수님의 발치에 앉았고 향유를 부어 그분에게 발랐다.

persons.description: Jesus' mother living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Mother of Jesus; wife of Joseph.
persons.short: Mary, the mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph, was a virgin when she conceived by the Holy Spirit.
persons.article: Mary, the mother of Jesus, was a young Jewish woman from Nazareth betrothed to Joseph, a descendant of David. She was likely a sister of Salome (see Jhn.19.25 and Gosple of Thomas but contra Diatessaron). Before their marriage, an angel appeared to Mary, announcing that she would conceive a child by the Holy Spirit and name Him Jesus. Mary humbly accepted this divine plan, and the virgin birth of Jesus fulfilled the prophecy of the Messiah (Mat.1.16, 18, 20; Luk.1.26-38). After Jesus' birth in Bethlehem, Mary and Joseph presented Him at the temple, where Simeon prophesied that a sword would pierce her soul (Luk.2.5, 16, 19, 34). Mary treasured these events in her heart. She and Joseph raised Jesus in Nazareth, and He was known as the son of Mary (Mat.13.55; Mrk.6.3). During Jesus' crucifixion, Mary stood near the cross with other women, including her sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene (Mat.27.56, 61; Mrk.15.40, 47). After Jesus' resurrection, Mary was among the women who went to the tomb and later informed the disciples (Mat.28.1; Mrk.16.1; Luk.24.10). In the early church, Mary joined the disciples in prayer as they awaited the coming of the Holy Spirit (Act.1.14).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.1.16 only referred to as Mary (Μαρία); daughter of Heli; a sister of Salome (?); wife of Joseph; mother of Jesus, James, Joses, Simon and Jude.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 예수님의 어머니. Mat.1.16에 처음 언급되며 '마리아'라 불림. 헬리와 헬리의 아내(이름 미상)의 딸. 살로매의 자매. 요셉의 아내. 예수, 야고보, 요세, 시몬과 유다의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 예수님의 어머니이며 요셉의 아내인 마리아는 성령으로 잉태했을 때 처녀였다.
persons.article_ko: 예수님의 어머니 마리아는 다윗의 후손인 요셉과 약혼한 나사렛 출신의 젊은 유대인 여성이었다. 그녀는 아마 살로메의 자매였을 것이다(요 19:25 및 도마복음 참조, 그러나 디아테사론과는 상반됨). 결혼 전에 한 천사가 마리아에게 나타나 그녀가 성령으로 아이를 잉태하여 그 이름을 예수라 지을 것이라고 알렸다. 마리아는 겸손하게 이 신적 계획을 받아들였고, 예수님의 동정녀 탄생은 메시아에 대한 예언을 성취했다(마 1:16, 18, 20; 눅 1:26-38). 예수님이 베들레헴에서 태어나신 후 마리아와 요셉은 그분을 성전에 드렸고, 그곳에서 시므온은 칼이 그녀의 영혼을 찌를 것이라고 예언했다(눅 2:5, 16, 19, 34). 마리아는 이 사건들을 마음에 새겼다. 그녀와 요셉은 예수님을 나사렛에서 길렀고, 그분은 마리아의 아들로 알려졌다(마 13:55; 막 6:3). 예수님의 십자가 처형 동안 마리아는 그녀의 자매인 글로바의 아내 마리아, 막달라 마리아를 포함한 다른 여인들과 함께 십자가 근처에 서 있었다(마 27:56, 61; 막 15:40, 47). 예수님의 부활 후 마리아는 무덤에 가서 후에 제자들에게 알린 여인 중 한 사람이었다(마 28:1; 막 16:1; 눅 24:10). 초대교회에서 마리아는 성령의 오심을 기다리며 제자들과 함께 기도했다(행 1:14).

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Wife of Cleopas (or 'Alphaeus'), present at Jesus' crucifixion.
persons.short: Mary, the wife of Cleopas (or 'Alphaeus'), was present at Jesus' crucifixion.
persons.article: Mary, the wife of Cleopas (or 'Alphaeus'), was one of the women present at the crucifixion of Jesus. She stood near the cross along with Jesus' mother, Mary, and Mary Magdalene. This brief mention in John's Gospel provides insight into the group of faithful women who witnessed Jesus' suffering and death (Jhn.19.25). In Catholic theology, where Mary the mother of Jesus remains a virgin, Mary the wife of Cleopas is the mother of Jesus' brothers, so her sons James and Joses are identical to the James and Joses who are listed as 'brothers' of Jesus along with Simon and Judas who are therefore also her sons (Mat.13.55)
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Jhn.19.25 only referred to as Mary (Μαρία); wife of Cleopas aka Alphaeus; mother of James, Joses. and Matthew.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Mat.27.56에 처음 언급되며 '마리아'라 불림. 알패오의 아내. 야고보, 요세와 마태의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 글로바(알패오라고도 함)의 아내 마리아는 예수님의 십자가 처형 현장에 있었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A woman who worked hard for the church in Rome.
persons.short: Mary was a woman who worked very hard for the church in Rome.
persons.article: Mary was a woman mentioned by Paul in his letter to the Romans. He commended her for working very hard for the church in Rome, indicating that she was a dedicated and diligent member of the Christian community there.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.6 only referred to as Mary (Μαρία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Rom.16.6에 처음 언급되며 '마리아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마리아는 로마 교회를 위해 매우 수고한 여인이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Follower of Jesus, first witness of His resurrection.
persons.short: Mary Magdalene, a follower of Jesus, was the first to witness His resurrection.
persons.article: Mary Magdalene was a devoted follower of Jesus Christ. She was from the town of Magdala and had been healed by Jesus of seven demons (Luk.8.2). Mary Magdalene was one of the women who supported Jesus' ministry financially and followed Him even to the cross. She witnessed His crucifixion along with other women, including Jesus' mother Mary (Mat.27.56; Mrk.15.40; Jhn.19.25). After Jesus' death, Mary Magdalene and other women prepared spices to anoint His body and went to the tomb on the first day of the week. They found the stone rolled away and the tomb empty. Mary Magdalene was the first to see the risen Jesus and was instructed by Him to tell the disciples of His resurrection (Mat.28.1; Mrk.16.1, 9; Luk.24.10; Jhn.20.1, 11-18). As a result, she became known as the "apostle to the apostles" for being the first to witness and proclaim the resurrection of Jesus.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.27.56 only referred to as Mary Magdalene (Μαρία).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Mat.27.56에 처음 언급되며 '막달라 마리아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 막달라 마리아는 예수님을 따른 여인으로, 그분의 부활을 처음 목격했다.
persons.article_ko: 막달라 마리아는 예수 그리스도의 헌신적인 추종자였다. 그녀는 막달라 마을 출신이었고 예수님에 의해 일곱 귀신에게서 고침을 받았다(눅 8:2). 막달라 마리아는 예수님의 사역을 재정적으로 지원하고 십자가까지 그분을 따른 여인 중 한 사람이었다. 그녀는 예수님의 어머니 마리아를 포함한 다른 여인들과 함께 그분의 십자가 처형을 목격했다(마 27:56; 막 15:40; 요 19:25). 예수님이 죽으신 후 막달라 마리아와 다른 여인들은 그분의 시신에 바를 향품을 준비하여 주간 첫날 무덤으로 갔다. 그들은 돌이 굴려져 있고 무덤이 비어있는 것을 발견했다. 막달라 마리아는 부활하신 예수님을 처음으로 본 사람이었고 그분에게서 제자들에게 그분의 부활을 알리라는 지시를 받았다(마 28:1; 막 16:1, 9; 눅 24:10; 요 20:1, 11-18). 그 결과 그녀는 예수님의 부활을 처음으로 목격하고 선포했다는 이유로 '사도들에게 보낸 사도'로 알려지게 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Aram, grandson of Shem.
persons.short: Mash (or Meshech), a son of Aram, was a grandson of Shem.
persons.article: Mash, also known as Meshech, was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, the son of Noah. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood (Gen.10.23; 1Ch.1.17). The name Mash is used in Genesis, while Meshech is used in 1 Chronicles, referring to the same individual.
persons.summary: A man of the Syrians living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.23 referred to as Mash (מַשׁ), or Meshech (מֶ֫שֶׁךְ); son of Aram; a brother of Uz, Hul and Gether.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.23에 처음 언급되며 '마스'라 불림. 아람의 아들. 우스, 훌과 게델의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마스(메섹이라고도 함)는 아람의 아들이며 셈의 손자였다.

persons.description: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mibsam@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Jetur@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Mahalath@Gen.28.9-
persons.brief: Son of Ishmael, grandson of Abraham.
persons.short: Massa, a son of Ishmael, was a grandson of Abraham.
persons.article: Massa was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Ishmael's descendants (Gen.25.14; 1Ch.1.30). As a grandson of Abraham, Massa was part of the Ishmaelite tribes that settled in the Arabian Peninsula.
persons.summary: A man of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.14 only referred to as Massa (מַשָּׂא); son of Ishmael; a brother of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah and Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 아라비아 사람. Gen.25.14에 처음 언급되며 '맛사'라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 밉삼, 미스마, 두마, 하닷, 데마, 여둘, 나비스, 게드마와 마할랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 맛사는 이스마엘의 아들이며 아브라함의 손자였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Mother of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, king of Edom.
persons.short: Matred was the mother of Mehetabel, who was the wife of Hadar, king of Edom.
persons.article: Matred was a woman mentioned in the genealogies of the kings of Edom. She was the mother of Mehetabel, who became the wife of Hadar (or Hadad), the last king of Edom mentioned before the monarchy of Israel (Gen.36.39; 1Ch.1.50).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.39 only referred to as Matred (מַטְרֵד); a daughter of Mezahab; mother of Mehetabel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.36.39에 처음 언급되며 '마드렛'이라 불림. 메사합의 딸. 마드렛의 남편(이름 미상)의 아내. 므헤다벨의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마드렛은 에돔 왕 하달의 아내 므헤다벨의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Saul's ancestral clan from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.short: The Matrite (or Matri) clan was Saul's ancestral clan from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: The Matrite, also known as Matri, was a clan within the tribe of Benjamin. When Saul was chosen to be the first king of Israel, the selection process involved casting lots among the tribes, clans, and families. The lot fell on the tribe of Benjamin, then on the Matrite clan, and finally on Saul, the son of Kish (1Sa.10.21). This indicates that Saul's family belonged to the Matrite clan within the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.10.21 only referred to as Matri or a Matrite (מַטְרִי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '마드리'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 마드리(마드라이라고도 함) 가문은 베냐민 지파 사울의 조상 가문이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest of Baal, killed during Jehoiada's reforms.
persons.short: Mattan, a priest of Baal, was killed during Jehoiada's religious reforms.
persons.article: Mattan was a priest of Baal during the reign of Athaliah, the queen mother of Judah. When Jehoiada the priest led a revolt to overthrow Athaliah and restore the rightful king, Joash, to the throne, the temple of Baal was destroyed. Mattan, as a priest of Baal, was killed in front of the altars of his pagan temple (2Ki.11.18; 2Ch.23.17). This event marked a significant moment in Jehoiada's religious reforms, which aimed to restore the worship of the Lord and eliminate idolatry in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.11.18 only referred to as Mattan (מַתָּן).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.11.18에 처음 언급되며 '맛단'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바알의 제사장 맛단은 여호야다의 종교개혁 기간 동안 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shephatiah, an opponent of Jeremiah.
persons.short: Mattan was the father of Shephatiah, one of the officials who opposed the prophet Jeremiah.
persons.article: Mattan was the father of Shephatiah, a prominent official during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah. Shephatiah, along with other officials, accused the prophet Jeremiah of discouraging the people and urged the king to put him to death. As a result, Jeremiah was thrown into a cistern, where he sank into the mud. However, Ebed-Melech, an Ethiopian eunuch, rescued Jeremiah with the king's permission (Jer.38.1-13). Mattan is only mentioned in this context as the father of Shephatiah, one of Jeremiah's opponents.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.38.1 only referred to as Mattan (מַתָּן); father of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.38.1에 처음 언급되며 '맛단'이라 불림. 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 맛단은 선지자 예레미야를 대적한 관리 중 한 사람인 스바댜의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Uzziel@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: Son of Heman, a musician in David's court.
persons.short: Mattaniah, a son of Heman, was a musician in King David's court.
persons.article: Mattaniah was one of the sons of Heman, a prominent musician in King David's court. Heman, along with Asaph and Jeduthun, was appointed by David to lead the music and praise in the tabernacle (1Ch.25.1). Mattaniah, along with his brothers, was chosen by lot to serve as a musician and singer in the temple. He was the ninth son of Heman and was responsible for the ninth division of musicians (1Ch.25.4, 16). The presence of Mattaniah and his brothers in the temple music ministry highlights the importance of worship and the role of skilled musicians in ancient Israelite culture.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 only referred to as Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '맛다냐'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 웃시엘, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 맛다냐는 헤만의 아들로 다윗 궁정의 음악가였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite singer and gatekeeper during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.short: Mattaniah, a Levite singer and gatekeeper, served during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Mattaniah was a Levite who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. He served as a singer and gatekeeper in the temple. In the genealogies of the Levites, Mattaniah is listed as a descendant of Asaph, one of the chief musicians appointed by David (1Ch.9.15). During the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Mattaniah was among the Levites who led the people in praise and thanksgiving to God (Neh.11.17; 12.8, 25). His role as a singer and gatekeeper highlights the importance of worship and service in the restored community of Israel.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.15 only referred to as Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Mica.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.15에 처음 언급되며 '맛다냐'라 불림. 미가의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 노래하는 자이며 문지기인 맛다냐는 느헤미야 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite, grandfather of Jahaziel, who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign.
persons.short: Mattaniah, a Levite, was the grandfather of Jahaziel, who prophesied during King Jehoshaphat's reign.
persons.article: Mattaniah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He was the grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite who was filled with the Spirit of the Lord and prophesied before the king and the people of Judah. Jahaziel encouraged Jehoshaphat and the people not to fear the approaching armies of the Moabites, Ammonites, and Meunites, assuring them that the battle belonged to the Lord. As a result, Jehoshaphat and the people worshipped the Lord, and the next day, they witnessed the Lord's deliverance as their enemies turned against each other (2Ch.20.14-24). Mattaniah is only mentioned in this context as the father of the prophet Jahaziel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.20.14 only referred to as Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ); father of Jeiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.20.14에 처음 언급되며 '맛다냐'라 불림. 여이엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 맛다냐는 여호사밧 왕 시대에 예언한 야하시엘의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped cleanse the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.short: Mattaniah, a Levite, helped cleanse the temple during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Mattaniah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. When Hezekiah initiated a reformation to restore proper worship in Judah, he ordered the cleansing and consecration of the temple, which had been neglected and defiled during the reign of his father, Ahaz. Mattaniah was among the Levites who participated in this cleansing process, removing the unclean items from the temple and preparing it for proper worship (2Ch.29.13). This event marked a significant turning point in Judah's spiritual life, as Hezekiah sought to lead the nation back to the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.13 only referred to as Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.13에 처음 언급되며 '맛다냐'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 맛다냐는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Zattu, who divorced his foreign wife.
persons.short: Mattaniah, a descendant of Zattu, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Mattaniah was a man from the family of Zattu who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra. As part of Ezra's reforms to purify the Jewish community after their return from Babylonian exile, Mattaniah and others who had married foreign wives were required to divorce them (Ezr.10.26). This action was taken to ensure that the Israelites remained faithful to the Lord and did not fall into the same sins that had led to their exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.26 only referred to as Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '맛다냐'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삿두의 후손 맛다냐는 에스라의 개혁 때 이방인 아내와 이혼했다.

persons.short: Mattaniah, a Levite singer and descendant of Asaph, served during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Mattaniah was a Levite who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. He was a descendant of Asaph, one of the chief musicians appointed by David. Mattaniah served as a singer in the temple (Neh.11.22). During the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Mattaniah was among the Levites who led the people in praise and thanksgiving to God (Neh.12.35). His role as a singer highlights the importance of worship and the role of skilled musicians in the restored community of Israel.

persons.article: Mattaniah was a Levite who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. Mattaniah's role as a treasurer demonstrates the importance of proper administration and support for those serving in the house of God.

persons.short: Mattatha was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in His genealogy.
persons.article: Mattatha is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in the Gospel of Luke. He is listed as the son of Nathan and the father of Menna (Luk.3.31). This genealogy traces Jesus' lineage through His mother, Mary, back to David and ultimately to Adam. Mattatha's inclusion in this genealogy highlights the human ancestry of Jesus and His connection to the royal line of David.

persons.article: Mattenai was a priest who lived during the time of Joiakim, the high priest who served after the Babylonian exile. In the list of priests and Levites who returned to Jerusalem, Mattenai is mentioned as the head of the priestly family of Joiarib (Neh.12.19). This suggests that Mattenai was a prominent figure among the priests during this period of Jewish history, as the Israelites sought to reestablish their religious practices and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

persons.short: This is one of the ancestors of Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus.
persons.article: Matthan is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in the Gospel of Matthew. He was the son of Eleazar and an ancestor or father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus (Mat.1.15). His son and a few generations after him are anonymous placeholders unnamed missing individuals that are necessray to increase the number of generations in Jesus' genealogy as recorded in Matthew to become the same as the number of generations in Luke. Matthew is known to deliberately miss out some individuals (kings Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah) so it is likely he also missed out others, in order to create three sets of 14 generations (Mat.1.17).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Mat.1.15 only referred to as Matthan (Ματθάν); a son of Eleazar; ancestor of Jacob.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Apostle, tax collector, author of the Gospel of Matthew.
persons.short: Matthew, also known as Levi, was a tax collector who became one of Jesus' twelve apostles and authored the Gospel of Matthew.
persons.article: Matthew, also known as Levi, was a tax collector in Capernaum before being called by Jesus to become one of His twelve apostles. As a tax collector, Matthew would have been considered a sinner and an outcast by the Jewish community. However, Jesus saw beyond his profession and called him to follow Him (Mat.9.9; Mrk.2.14; Luk.5.27). Matthew responded immediately, leaving his tax booth and hosting a great feast for Jesus in his home, inviting other tax collectors and sinners (Luk.5.29). As an apostle, Matthew witnessed Jesus' ministry, death, and resurrection. He is also traditionally attributed as the author of the Gospel of Matthew, which emphasizes Jesus as the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies and the long-awaited Messiah (Mat.10.3; Mrk.3.18; Luk.6.15; Act.1.13).
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.9.9 referred to as Matthew (Ματθαῖος), or Levi (Λευΐ), or Levi (Λευΐ); a son of Alphaeus and possibly Mary; possibly brother of James and Joses.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.9.9에 처음 언급되며 '마태'라 불림. 알패오와 마리아의 아들. 요세와 야고보의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 마태(레위라고도 함)는 세리였으나 예수님의 열두 사도 중 한 사람이 되어 마태복음을 저술했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Apostle chosen to replace Judas Iscariot.
persons.short: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles.
persons.article: Matthias was a disciple of Jesus who was chosen to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles after Judas' betrayal and death. In the days following Jesus' ascension, the apostles gathered to pray and choose a replacement for Judas. The criteria for the new apostle were that he had to have been with Jesus from His baptism by John until His ascension and be a witness to His resurrection. Two men were proposed: Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias. After praying, the apostles cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias, who was then numbered with the eleven apostles (Act.1.21-26). Although not much is known about Matthias' life and ministry after this event, his selection as an apostle demonstrates the importance of maintaining the twelve as the foundation of the early church, representing the twelve tribes of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.1.23 only referred to as Matthias (Ματθίας, Μαθθίας).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.1.23에 처음 언급되며 '맛디아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 맛디아는 제비뽑기로 선택되어 가룟 유다를 대신하여 열두 사도 중 한 사람이 되었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician during the time of David.
persons.short: Mattithiah, a Levite, served as a musician during the time of King David.
persons.article: Mattithiah was a Levite who served as a musician during the reign of King David. He was among the Levites appointed by David to lead the music and praise in the tabernacle (1Ch.15.18, 21). Mattithiah is specifically mentioned as a harpist, playing the harp to accompany the singing of psalms and hymns (1Ch.16.5). He was also one of the sons of Jeduthun, a chief musician in David's court, and was responsible for leading the fourteenth division of musicians (1Ch.25.3, 21). Mattithiah's role as a musician highlights the importance of worship and the use of music in the Israelite religious practices during David's reign.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Mattithiah (מַתִּתְיָ֫הוּ); son of Jeduthun; a brother of Obed-edom, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '맛디디야'라 불림. 여두둔의 아들. 오벧에돔, 그달리야, 스리, 여사야와 하사뱌의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 맛디디아는 다윗 왕 시대에 음악가로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite in charge of baking bread in the temple.
persons.short: Mattithiah, a Levite, was in charge of baking bread in the temple.
persons.article: Mattithiah was a Levite who was appointed to oversee the baking of the showbread in the temple. The showbread, also known as the bread of the Presence, was a sacred offering that was placed on a table in the Holy Place of the tabernacle or temple. It consisted of twelve loaves, representing the twelve tribes of Israel, and was replaced every Sabbath. Mattithiah's responsibility was to ensure that the bread was properly prepared and presented according to the divine instructions (1Ch.9.31).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.31 only referred to as Mattithiah (מַתִּתְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.31에 처음 언급되며 '맛디디야'라 불림. 살룸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 맛디디아는 성전에서 떡 굽는 일을 맡았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law.
persons.short: Mattithiah, a Levite, assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people.
persons.article: Mattithiah was a Levite who lived during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile. When Ezra read the Book of the Law to the people in Jerusalem, Mattithiah was one of the Levites who stood beside him on the platform (Neh.8.4). The Levites were responsible for helping the people understand the Law as it was being read. This event marked a significant moment in the spiritual reformation of the Israelites, as they recommitted themselves to follow God's commandments and covenant.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Mattithiah (מַתִּתְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '맛디디야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 맛디디아는 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 낭독하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Warriors from or of Mecherath(?)
persons.brief: Clan or inhabitants of an unknown place called Mecherah.
persons.short: The Mecherathites were a clan or inhabitants of an unknown place called Mecherah.
persons.article: The Mecherathites are mentioned in the list of David's mighty men, specifically in reference to Hepher the Mecherathite (1Ch.11.36). The term "Mecherathite" likely refers to an individual from a place called Mecherah, but the exact location of this place is unknown. It is possible that Mecherah was a small town or village in Israel, and that Hepher was a skilled warrior from that community who joined David's army. However, due to the lack of additional information in the Bible, the identity and location of the Mecherathites remain uncertain.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Mecherath(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.11.36 only referred to as Mecherathites (מְכֵרָתִי).
persons.summary_ko: 므게랏 사람. 1Ch.11.36에 처음 언급되며 '므게랏'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므게랏 족속은 알려지지 않은 므게라라는 곳의 주민 또는 가문이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Eldad's companion who prophesied in the Israelite camp.
persons.short: Medad, along with Eldad, prophesied in the Israelite camp, though they had not gone to the tent of meeting.
persons.article: Medad was an Israelite who, along with Eldad, received the Spirit and prophesied in the camp during the time of Moses. When Moses appointed seventy elders to assist him in leading the people, the Lord took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. However, Eldad and Medad, who were listed among the elders but had not gone to the tent of meeting, began prophesying in the camp. When Joshua urged Moses to stop them, Moses responded, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord's people were prophets and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" (Num.11.26-29). This event demonstrates that the Spirit of God can work through individuals unexpectedly and that God's power is not limited to human structures or expectations.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.11.26 only referred to as Medad (מֵידָד).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.11.26에 처음 언급되며 '메닷'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 메닷은 엘닷과 함께 회막에 가지 않았음에도 이스라엘 진영에서 예언했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Ishmael@Gen.16.11-Psa, Isaac@Gen.17.19-Jas, Zimran@Gen.25.2-1Ch, Jokshan@Gen.25.2-1Ch, Midian@Gen.25.2-1Ch, Ishbak@Gen.25.2-1Ch, Shuah@Gen.25.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Abraham and Keturah.
persons.short: Medan was a son of Abraham and his concubine Keturah.
persons.article: Medan was one of the sons born to Abraham and his concubine Keturah after the death of Sarah. Along with his brothers Zimran, Jokshan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah, Medan was sent away by Abraham with gifts to the land of the east, separating them from Isaac, Abraham's son with Sarah (Gen.25.1-6). Medan is also mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's descendants in 1Ch.1.32. Little else is known about Medan or his descendants, as they are not mentioned further in the biblical narrative.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.2 only referred to as Medan (מְדָן); son of Abraham and Keturah; half-brother of: Ishmael and Isaac; a brother of Zimran, Jokshan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.25.2에 처음 언급되며 '므단'이라 불림. 아브라함과 그두라의 아들. 이스마엘, 이삭, 시므란, 욕산, 미디안, 이스박과 수아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 므단은 아브라함이 첩 그두라를 통해 얻은 아들이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Hadar, king of Edom.
persons.short: Mehetabel was the wife of Hadar, a king of Edom.
persons.article: Mehetabel was the wife of Hadar (or Hadad), who was the last king of Edom mentioned in the genealogy of Esau. She was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-zahab (Gen.36.39; 1Ch.1.50). The Edomites were descendants of Esau, the twin brother of Israel (or 'Jacob'), and they settled in the region southeast of Judah. The mention of Mehetabel in the genealogy suggests that she held a significant position as the queen of Edom during her husband's reign. However, no further details about her life or role are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.39 only referred to as Mehetabel (מְהֵיטַבְאֵל); her mother was Matred; wife of Hadad.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.36.39에 처음 언급되며 '므헤다벨'이라 불림. 마드렛의 남편(이름 미상)와 마드렛의 딸. 하닷의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 므헤다벨은 에돔 왕 하달의 아내였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Shemaiah, who opposed Nehemiah.
persons.short: Mehetabel was an ancestor of Shemaiah, who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild Jerusalem's walls.
persons.article: Mehetabel is mentioned in the context of Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Shemaiah, a man described as "the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel," was hired by Nehemiah's enemies, Sanballat and Tobiah, to intimidate Nehemiah and hinder the work on the wall. Shemaiah invited Nehemiah to meet with him in the temple and suggested that they close the doors, claiming that there was a plot to kill Nehemiah. However, Nehemiah perceived that Shemaiah was not sent by God and that his prophecy was intended to frighten Nehemiah and discredit him (Neh.6.10-13). Mehetabel's role in this narrative is limited to being mentioned as an ancestor of Shemaiah, providing context for Shemaiah's background and family lineage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.10 only referred to as Mehetabel (מְהֵיטַבְאֵל); father of Delaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '므헤다벨'이라 불림. 들라야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므헤다벨은 느헤미야의 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 반대한 스마야의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Mehida was an ancestor of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Mehida is mentioned in the lists of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity under the leadership of Zerubbabel. The descendants of Mehida were among the temple servants, also known as Nethinim, who were assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple (Ezr.2.52; Neh.7.54). The Nethinim were a group of people who had been dedicated to the service of the temple, possibly descendants of the Gibeonites who were assigned by Joshua to be woodcutters and water carriers for the house of God (Jos.9.27). The inclusion of Mehida's descendants in the list of returning exiles highlights the importance of the temple servants in the restoration of worship in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.52 only referred to as Mehida (מְחִידָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.52에 처음 언급되며 '므히다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므히다는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자(느디님) 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Chelub.
persons.short: Mehir was the son of Chelub.
persons.article: Mehir is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically as the son of Chelub (1Ch.4.11). No further information is provided about Mehir or his descendants in the biblical text. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles often serve to establish the lineage and inheritance rights of prominent families in Israel, particularly in the context of the post-exilic period when these records were compiled. However, due to the lack of additional details, Mehir's role and significance in the family of Judah remain unknown.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.11 only referred to as Mehir (מְחִיר); a son of Chelub; father of Eshton.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '므힐'이라 불림. 글룹의 아들. 에스돈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므힐은 글룹의 아들이었다.

persons.description: People from Meholath(?)
persons.brief: People from Abel-meholah, including Adriel and Barzillai.
persons.short: The Meholathites were people from Abel-meholah, including Adriel, who married Saul's daughter Merab, and Barzillai, whose son married Saul's daughter Michal.
persons.article: The Meholathites were inhabitants of Abel-meholah, a town in the Jordan Valley, possibly located in the territory of Issachar or Manasseh. Two individuals are specifically identified as Meholathites in the Bible. The first is Adriel, who was married to Saul's daughter Merab, although she had originally been promised to David (1Sa.18.19). The second is Barzillai, whose son married Saul's daughter Michal after she was taken from David and given to another man (2Sa.21.8). The Meholathites' connection to Saul's family suggests that they may have been influential in the region during the early monarchical period in Israel.
persons.summary: People from Meholath(?), first mentioned at 1Sa.18.19 only referred to as Meholathites (מְחֹלָתִי).
persons.summary_ko: 므훌랏 사람. 1Sa.18.19에 처음 언급되며 '므홀랏'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므홀랏 족속은 아벨므홀라 출신 사람들로, 사울의 딸 메랍과 결혼한 아드리엘과 그 아들이 사울의 딸 미갈과 결혼한 바르실래가 포함된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Descendant of Cain; father of Methushael.
persons.short: Mehujael was a descendant of Cain and the father of Methushael.
persons.article: Mehujael is mentioned in the genealogy of Cain, the son of Adam and Eve who was cursed for murdering his brother Abel. Mehujael was the son of Irad and the father of Methushael (Gen.4.18). The genealogy in Genesis 4 traces the descendants of Cain, highlighting the development of civilization and the increasing wickedness of humanity, which eventually led to the judgment of the flood. Mehujael's name is of Hebrew origin and can be translated as "smitten by God" or "blot out that Jah is God," possibly reflecting the growing rebellion against God among Cain's descendants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.4.18 only referred to as Mehujael (מְחוּיָאֵל); a son of Irad; father of Methushael.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '므후야엘'이라 불림. 이랏의 아들. 므드사엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므후야엘은 가인의 후손이며 므두사엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of King Ahasuerus' seven eunuchs.
persons.short: Mehuman was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.
persons.article: Mehuman was one of the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus, the Persian king who ruled over a vast empire from India to Ethiopia. In the book of Esther, King Ahasuerus summoned these seven eunuchs—Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas—to bring Queen Vashti before him during a great feast, so that he could display her beauty to the people and nobles (Est.1.10-11). However, Queen Vashti refused to come, leading to her removal as queen and the search for a new queen, which ultimately led to Esther becoming queen. Mehuman's role in this narrative highlights the power and influence of the eunuchs in the Persian court, as they had direct access to the king and were entrusted with carrying out his commands.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.10 only referred to as Mehuman (מְהוּמָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '므후만'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므후만은 아하수에로 왕을 섬긴 일곱 내시 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Gibeonite who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
persons.short: Melatiah the Gibeonite helped repair a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding project.
persons.article: Melatiah the Gibeonite is mentioned in the context of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under the leadership of Nehemiah. He was one of the individuals who took responsibility for repairing a specific section of the wall, alongside Jadon the Meronothite and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah (Neh.3.7). The Gibeonites were descendants of the Hivites who had deceived Joshua into making a treaty with them, and as a result, they were assigned as servants to the Israelites (Joshua 9). Melatiah's participation in the rebuilding project demonstrates that the Gibeonites, despite their history, were still involved in the affairs of Israel and contributed to the restoration of Jerusalem in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.7 only referred to as Melatiah (מְלַטְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.7에 처음 언급되며 '믈라댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 기브온 사람 믈라댜는 느헤미야의 재건 사업 당시 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
persons.short: Melchi, mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
persons.article: Melchi is a name that appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.24). He is listed as an ancestor of Jesus, but no additional information about him is provided in the biblical text. His name suggests he was likely of Jewish descent.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.24 only referred to as Melchi (Μελχί); a son of Jannai; father of Levi.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '멜기'라 불림. 얀나의 아들. 레위의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 멜기는 누가복음의 예수님 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
persons.short: Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy.
persons.article: Melchi is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ found in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.28). He is listed as an ancestor of Jesus, but the biblical text does not provide any further details about his life or role in the family line. Based on his inclusion in the genealogy, he was likely of Jewish heritage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.28 only referred to as Melchi (Μελχί); a son of Addi; father of Neri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.28에 처음 언급되며 '멜기'라 불림. 앗디의 아들. 네리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 멜기는 누가복음 족보에 언급된 예수님의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Salem and priest of God Most High.
persons.short: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham.
persons.article: Melchizedek was the king of Salem and a priest of God Most High (Gen.14.18). He blessed Abraham and received a tithe from him after Abraham's victory over Chedorlaomer and his allies. Melchizedek brought out bread and wine, demonstrating his priestly role. The Psalms refer to the Messiah as a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek (Psa.110.4, indicating that Melchizedek's priesthood was seen as a type or foreshadowing of Christ's eternal priesthood). The book of Hebrews expands on this concept, presenting Jesus as a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek (Heb.5.6,10; 6.20; 7.1,10,11,15,17,21). Melchizedek's unique priesthood, which combined royalty and priestly service to God Most High, is seen as a precedent for Jesus' eternal priesthood and kingship.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.18 referred to as Melchizedek (מַלְכִּי־צֶ֫דֶק), or Melchizedek (Μελχισεδέκ).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 제사장. Gen.14.18에 처음 언급되며 '멜기세덱'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 살렘 왕이며 지극히 높으신 하나님의 제사장인 멜기세덱은 아브라함을 축복했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
persons.short: Melea, mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
persons.article: Melea is a name that appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.31). He is listed as an ancestor of Jesus, but no further information about his life or role is provided in the biblical text. His name suggests he was likely of Jewish descent.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.31 only referred to as Melea (Μελεᾶς); a son of Menna; father of Eliakim.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.31에 처음 언급되며 '멜레아'라 불림. 멘나의 아들. 엘리야김의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 멜레아는 누가복음의 예수님 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of King Saul.
persons.short: Melech, a descendant of King Saul mentioned in the genealogies of Benjamin.
persons.article: Melech is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in the First Book of Chronicles (1Ch.8.35; 9.41). He is listed as a descendant of King Saul, the first king of Israel. The genealogies indicate that Melech was the son of Micah and the father of Tarea.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.35 only referred to as Melech (מֶ֫לֶךְ); son of Micah; a brother of Pithon, Tarea and Ahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.35에 처음 언급되며 '멜렉'이라 불림. 미가의 아들. 비돈, 다레아와 아하스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 멜렉은 베냐민 족보에 언급된 사울 왕의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Babylonian official in charge of Daniel and his friends.
persons.short: Melzar, the steward appointed by the chief eunuch to oversee Daniel and his companions.
persons.article: Melzar, also referred to as "the steward," was a Babylonian official appointed by Ashpenaz, the chief eunuch, to oversee Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Dan.1.11). He was responsible for providing them with their daily provisions and monitoring their well-being. When Daniel requested a diet of vegetables and water instead of the king's food and wine, Melzar initially hesitated, fearing for his own life if the young men's appearance suffered (Dan.1.11). However, he agreed to a ten-day test, and when Daniel and his friends appeared healthier than those who ate the king's food, Melzar allowed them to continue with their chosen diet (Dan.1.16).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Dan.1.11 only referred to as Melzar (מֶלְצָר). ; also translated "steward";
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Dan.1.11에 처음 언급되며 '관리인'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 멜사르는 환관장이 다니엘과 그 동료들을 감독하도록 임명한 청지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
persons.short: Memucan, a wise prince who advised King Ahasuerus to depose Queen Vashti.
persons.article: Memucan was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who served as advisors to King Ahasuerus (Est.1.14). When Queen Vashti refused to appear before the king and his guests during a royal feast, Memucan was the one who advised the king on how to handle the situation (Est.1.16). He suggested that Vashti's behavior could set a precedent for other women in the kingdom to disrespect their husbands. Memucan proposed that the king issue a decree deposing Vashti and selecting a new queen, to serve as an example to all women to honor their husbands (Est.1.16,21). The king followed Memucan's advice, and Vashti was removed from her position as queen (Est.1.21).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Memucan (מְמוּכָן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '므무간'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 지혜로운 방백 므무간은 아하수에로 왕에게 와스디 왕비를 폐위하도록 조언했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel who reigned for ten years.
persons.short: Menahem, king of Israel, known for his cruelty and for paying tribute to Assyria.
persons.article: Menahem was the son of Gadi and became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum, who had reigned for only one month (2Ki.15.14). Menahem reigned for ten years in Samaria (2Ki.15.17). During his reign, he was known for his cruelty, particularly for his brutal treatment of the city of Tiphsah, where he ripped open pregnant women (2Ki.15.16). When Pul, the king of Assyria, invaded Israel, Menahem paid him a thousand talents of silver to withdraw and to strengthen his own hold on the kingdom (2Ki.15.19-20). To raise this tribute, Menahem exacted fifty shekels of silver from each wealthy man in Israel (2Ki.15.20). Menahem died and was succeeded by his son Pekahiah (2Ki.15.22).
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.14 only referred to as Menahem (מְנַחֵם); a son of Gadi; father of Pekahiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.14에 처음 언급되며 '므나헴'이라 불림. 가디의 아들. 브가히야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므나헴은 잔인함과 앗수르에게 조공을 바친 것으로 알려진 이스라엘 왕이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
persons.short: Menna, mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
persons.article: Menna is a name that appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in the Gospel of Luke (Luk.3.31). He is listed as an ancestor of Jesus, but no additional information about his life or role is provided in the biblical text. His name suggests he was likely of Jewish descent.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Luk.3.31 only referred to as Menna (Μαϊνάν); a son of Mattatha; father of Melea.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Luk.3.31에 처음 언급되며 '멘나'라 불림. 맛다다의 아들. 멜레아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 멘나는 누가복음의 예수님 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: People from Menuh(?)
persons.brief: A clan descended from Caleb.
persons.short: Menuhoth, a clan descended from Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Menuhoth is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, specifically in the lineage of Caleb, the son of Hur (1Ch.2.52). The text states that Caleb's sons included the clans of Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites, and that from these clans came the people of Zorah and Eshtaol. Menuhoth is listed among these clans, suggesting that they were a family group descended from Caleb.
persons.summary: People from Menuh(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.2.52 only referred to as Menuhoth (מָנַ֫חַת); a brother of Haroeh.
persons.summary_ko: 므누홋 사람. 1Ch.2.52에 처음 언급되며 '마나핫'이라 불림. 소발의 자녀. 하로에의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 므누홋은 갈렙의 후손인 가문으로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Othniel and father of Ophrah.
persons.short: Meonothai, son of Othniel, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Meonothai is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.4.14). He was the son of Othniel, who was the younger brother of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh. Meonothai was the father of Ophrah, but no further information about his life or role is provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.14 only referred to as Meonothai (מְעוֹנֹתַי); son of Othniel(?) whose wife was Achsah; a brother of Hathath(?); father of Ophrah.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.4.14에 처음 언급되며 '므오노대'라 불림. 옷니엘과 악사의 아들. 하닷의 형제. 오브라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므오노대는 옷니엘의 아들로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Malchi-shua@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Merab@1Sa.14.49-2Sa, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch, Armoni@2Sa.21.8
persons.brief: Son of Saul and Rizpah, given to the Gibeonites.
persons.short: Mephibosheth, son of Saul and Rizpah, was given to the Gibeonites for execution.
persons.article: Mephibosheth was a son of King Saul and his concubine Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah (2Sa.21.8). He was one of the seven descendants of Saul who were handed over to the Gibeonites to be executed, as a means of atonement for Saul's attempt to annihilate the Gibeonites (2Sa.21.8). This event occurred during David's reign, when a three-year famine prompted David to seek the Lord's guidance. The Gibeonites requested seven of Saul's descendants to be handed over to them, and Mephibosheth was among those chosen. He was put to death along with his brothers and the five sons of Merab, Saul's daughter (2Sa.21.8).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.21.8 only referred to as Mephibosheth (מְפִיבֹשֶׁת); son of Saul and Rizpah; a brother of Armoni; half-brother of: Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchi-shua, Merab, Michal and Ish-bosheth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.21.8에 처음 언급되며 '므비보셋'이라 불림. 사울과 리스바의 아들. 요나단, 아비나답, 말기수아, 메랍, 미갈, 이스보셋과 알모니의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사울과 리스바의 아들 므비보셋은 기브온 사람들에게 처형되도록 넘겨졌다.

persons.description: Jonathan's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.
persons.short: Mephibosheth, also called Merib-baal, was the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.
persons.article: Mephibosheth, also known as Merib-baal, was the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul (1Ch.8.34; 9.40). He was five years old when his father and grandfather died in battle at Mount Gilboa (2Sa.4.4). During the panic following their deaths, Mephibosheth's nurse picked him up to flee, but he fell and became lame in both feet (2Sa.4.4). Years later, when David had established his kingdom, he sought to show kindness to Mephibosheth for the sake of his father Jonathan (2Sa.9.6). David restored to him all the land that had belonged to Saul and allowed him to eat at the king's table regularly (2Sa.9.6,10,11,13). Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica (2Sa.9.12). During Absalom's rebellion, Mephibosheth's servant Ziba falsely accused him of disloyalty to David (2Sa.16.1,4). After Absalom's death, Mephibosheth met David and explained that Ziba had deceived him (2Sa.19.24,25). David divided Saul's land between Mephibosheth and Ziba (2Sa.19.30). Later, when the Gibeonites demanded seven of Saul's descendants to avenge Saul's attempt to annihilate them, David spared Mephibosheth because of his oath to Jonathan (2Sa.21.7).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.4.4 referred to as Mephibosheth (מְפִיבֹשֶׁת), or Merib-baal (מְרִיב בַּ֫עַל), or Merib-baal (מְרִי בַעַל); a son of Jonathan; father of Micah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 요나단의 아들. 2Sa.4.4에 처음 언급되며 '므비보셋'이라 불림. 요나단의 아들. 미가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므비보셋(므립바알이라고도 함)은 요나단의 아들이며 사울 왕의 손자였다.
persons.article_ko: 므비보셋(므립바알이라고도 함)은 요나단의 아들이며 사울 왕의 손자였다(대상 8:34; 9:40). 그는 아버지와 할아버지가 길보아산 전투에서 죽었을 때 다섯 살이었다(삼하 4:4). 그들의 죽음 이후의 공황 속에서 므비보셋의 유모는 도망치기 위해 그를 안았으나 그가 떨어져 두 발이 다 절게 되었다(삼하 4:4). 여러 해 후 다윗이 자기 왕국을 세웠을 때 그는 요나단을 위해 므비보셋에게 은혜를 베풀고자 했다(삼하 9:6). 다윗은 사울에게 속했던 모든 땅을 그에게 회복시켜주고 왕의 상에서 정기적으로 먹도록 허락했다(삼하 9:6, 10-11, 13). 므비보셋에게는 미가라는 어린 아들이 있었다(삼하 9:12). 압살롬의 반역 동안 므비보셋의 종 시바는 그가 다윗에게 불충하다고 거짓 고발했다(삼하 16:1, 4). 압살롬이 죽은 후 므비보셋은 다윗을 만나 시바가 그를 속였다고 설명했다(삼하 19:24-25). 다윗은 사울의 땅을 므비보셋과 시바에게 나누었다(삼하 19:30). 후에 기브온 사람들이 그들을 멸하려 한 사울의 시도에 대한 보복으로 사울의 후손 일곱 명을 요구했을 때 다윗은 요나단에게 한 맹세 때문에 므비보셋을 살려주었다(삼하 21:7).

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jonathan@1Sa.13.2-1Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Malchi-shua@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch, Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch, Armoni@2Sa.21.8, Mephibosheth@2Sa.21.8
persons.brief: Eldest daughter of King Saul.
persons.short: Merab, the eldest daughter of King Saul, was promised to David but given to Adriel.
persons.article: Merab was the eldest daughter of King Saul (1Sa.14.49). She was initially promised to David as a wife, with the condition that he fight valiantly for Saul and the Lord (1Sa.18.17). However, when the time came for her to be given to David, she was instead given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife (1Sa.18.19). Merab had five sons with Adriel, and these sons were among the seven descendants of Saul who were handed over to the Gibeonites for execution, as a means of atonement for Saul's attempt to annihilate the Gibeonites (2Sa.21.8). This event occurred during David's reign, when a three-year famine prompted David to seek the Lord's guidance.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.14.49 referred to as Merab (מֵרָב), or Merab (מִיכַל); daughter of Saul and Ahinoam; wife of Adriel; a sister of Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchi-shua and Michal; half-sister of: Ish-bosheth, Armoni and Mephibosheth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Sa.14.49에 처음 언급되며 '메랍'이라 불림. 사울과 아히노암의 딸. 요나단, 아비나답, 말기수아, 미갈, 이스보셋, 알모니와 므비보셋의 자매. 아드리엘의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 사울 왕의 맏딸 메랍은 다윗과 약혼했으나 아드리엘에게 주어졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.short: Meraiah, a priest who served during the time of Joiakim the high priest.
persons.article: Meraiah was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim, the high priest in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.12.12). He is mentioned in the list of priests and Levites who went up to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, and Jeshua, the high priest (Neh.12.1). Meraiah is specifically listed among the priests who were heads of their fathers' houses during the days of Joiakim (Neh.12.12).
