persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.12 only referred to as Meraiah (מְרָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.12에 처음 언급되며 '므라야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 메라야는 대제사장 요야김 시대에 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A priest in the lineage of Eleazar.
persons.short: Meraioth, a priest in the lineage of Eleazar, mentioned in genealogies.
persons.article: Meraioth was a priest in the lineage of Eleazar, the son of Aaron (1Ch.6.6,7,52). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the priests and Levites in the books of Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah. In the genealogy of Ezra, a descendant of Meraioth, he is listed as an ancestor of Ezra the scribe (Ezr.7.3). Meraioth is also mentioned in the list of priests who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1Ch.9.11; Neh.11.11).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.6 only referred to as Meraioth (מְרָיוֹת); a son of Zerahiah; father of Amariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 제사장. 1Ch.6.6에 처음 언급되며 '므라욧'이라 불림. 스라히야의 아들. 아마랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므라욧은 엘르아살 계열 제사장으로, 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: The third son of Levi and founder of the Merarites.
persons.short: Merari, the third son of Levi, was the founder of the Merarite clan of Levites.
persons.article: Merari was the third son of Levi and the founder of the Merarite clan, one of the three main divisions of the Levites (Gen.46.11; Exo.6.16,19). The Merarites were responsible for the transportation and maintenance of the tabernacle's framework, pillars, bases, and related equipment during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness (Num.3.36; 4.29,33,42,45). They were also given specific duties in the tabernacle service (Num.7.8; 10.17). In the time of David, the Merarites were assigned various roles in the temple service, including gatekeepers, singers, and assistants to the priests (1Ch.6.44,47; 9.14; 15.6,17; 23.6,21; 24.26,27; 26.10,19). The Merarites were allotted cities in the territories of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun (Jos.21.7,34,40; 1Ch.6.63,77). Members of the Merarite clan, such as Asaiah and Shemaiah, were involved in the reforms and restoration of temple worship during the reigns of Hezekiah and Josiah (2Ch.29.12; 34.12).
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.11 referred to as Merari or Merarite (מְרָרִי), or Merari or Merarite (מְרָרִי); son of Levi; a brother of Gershon, Kohath and Jochebed; father of Mahli, Mushi and Jaaziah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Gen.46.11에 처음 언급되며 '므라리'라 불림. 레위의 아들. 게르손, 그핫과 요게벳의 형제. 마흘리, 무시와 야아시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위의 셋째 아들 므라리는 레위인 므라리 가문의 창설자였다.
persons.article_ko: 므라리는 레위의 셋째 아들이며 레위인의 세 주요 분파 중 하나인 므라리 가문의 창설자였다(창 46:11; 출 6:16, 19). 므라리 사람들은 이스라엘 백성이 광야를 지나는 동안 성막의 틀, 기둥, 받침대 및 관련 장비의 운반과 유지 관리에 대한 책임을 맡았다(민 3:36; 4:29, 33, 42, 45). 그들은 또한 성막 봉사에서 특정 직무를 부여받았다(민 7:8; 10:17). 다윗 시대에 므라리 사람들은 문지기, 노래하는 자, 제사장들의 조수를 포함한 성전 봉사에서 다양한 역할을 부여받았다(대상 6:44, 47; 9:14; 15:6, 17; 23:6, 21; 24:26-27; 26:10, 19). 므라리 사람들은 르우벤, 갓, 스불론 영토에서 성읍들을 분배받았다(수 21:7, 34, 40; 대상 6:63, 77). 아사야와 스마야 같은 므라리 가문의 구성원들은 히스기야와 요시야 통치 기간 동안 성전 예배의 개혁과 회복에 관여했다(대하 29:12; 34:12).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Miriam@1Ch.4.17(?), Shammai@1Ch.4.17(?), Ishbah@1Ch.4.17(?), Jered@1Ch.4.18(?), Heber@1Ch.4.18(?), Jekuthiel@1Ch.4.18(?)
persons.brief: Son of Ezrah from the tribe of Judah.
persons.short: Mered, a son of Ezrah, married Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh.
persons.article: Mered was a son of Ezrah from the tribe of Judah (1Ch.4.17). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in the book of Chronicles. Mered had two wives: one was Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh, and the other was a Judahite woman (1Ch.4.18). The biblical text lists the children born to Mered and his Judahite wife, including Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah (1Ch.4.17).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.4.17 only referred to as Mered (מֶ֫רֶד); son of Ezrah; a brother of Jether, Epher and Jalon; husband of Bithiah(?) and Jehudijah(?); father of Miriam(?), Shammai(?), Ishbah(?), Jered(?), Heber(?) and Jekuthiel(?).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '메렛'이라 불림. 에스라의 아들. 예델, 에벨과 얄론의 형제. 비디아와 여후디야의 남편. 미리암, 삼매, 이스바, 예렛, 헤벨과 여구디엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에스라의 아들 므렛은 바로의 딸 비디아와 결혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Meremoth, an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meremoth is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.36). After Ezra's prayer of confession and call for repentance, the people assembled and agreed to put away their foreign wives and children. Meremoth was among those who had taken foreign wives, but no further information about his specific situation or response to Ezra's call is provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.36 only referred to as Meremoth (מְרֵמוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.36에 처음 언급되며 '므레못'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므레못은 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.short: Meremoth, a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and was involved in the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Meremoth was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile. He was among those who received the silver, gold, and vessels brought back to Jerusalem by Ezra (Ezr.8.33). During the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem under Nehemiah, Meremoth, the son of Uriah, repaired two sections of the wall (Neh.3.4,21). He is also listed among the priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah to follow the Law of God (Neh.10.5). In the lists of priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel, Meremoth is mentioned as the head of a priestly family (Neh.12.3,15).
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.8.33 referred to as Meremoth (מְרֵמוֹת), or Meraioth (מְרָיוֹת); a son of Uriah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.33에 처음 언급되며 '므레못'이라 불림. 우리아의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 므레못은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아와 예루살렘 재건에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
persons.short: Meres, one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advised King Ahasuerus.
persons.article: Meres was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus and were closest to him in rank (Est.1.14). These princes were consulted by the king when he sought advice on how to respond to Queen Vashti's refusal to appear before him and his guests during a royal feast.
persons.summary: A prince of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Meres (מֶ֫רֶס).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '메레스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므레스는 아하수에로 왕에게 조언한 페르시아와 메대의 일곱 방백 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Babylon who sent envoys to Hezekiah.
persons.short: Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, king of Judah.
persons.article: Merodach-baladan was the king of Babylon who sent envoys with letters and a gift to Hezekiah, king of Judah, after hearing of Hezekiah's illness and recovery (2Ki.20.12; Isa.39.1). Hezekiah welcomed the envoys and showed them all his treasures, including silver, gold, spices, and precious oils, as well as his armory and everything in his storehouses. The prophet Isaiah then came to Hezekiah and prophesied that a time would come when all these treasures and even some of Hezekiah's descendants would be carried off to Babylon (2Ki.20.13-18; Isa.39.2-7). This event foreshadowed the future Babylonian conquest of Judah.
persons.summary: A king of Babylon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.20.12 referred to as Merodach-baladan (בְּרֹאדַךְ בַּלְאֲדָן), or Merodach-baladan (מְרֹדַךְ בַּלְאֲדָן); a son of Baladan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.20.12에 처음 언급되며 '부로닥발라단'이라 불림. 발라단의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바벨론 왕 므로닥발라단은 유다 왕 히스기야에게 편지와 선물을 보냈다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Jesher@1Ch.2.18, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Ardon@1Ch.2.18, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Sheva@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: Son of Caleb and founder of Ziph.
persons.short: Mesha, a son of Caleb, was the  father (ie founder) of Ziph.
persons.article: Mesha was a son of Caleb, the son of Hezron from the tribe of Judah. He founded (or fathered) Ziph. (1Ch.2.42).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.42a only referred to as Mesha (מֵישָׁע); son of Caleb and Jerioth(?); a brother of Hur, Jesher, Shobab, Ardon, Haran, Moza, Gazez, Sheber, Tirhanah, Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Shaaph, Sheva and Achsah; father of Mareshah; founder of Ziph.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.42에 처음 언급되며 '메사'라 불림. 갈렙과 여리옷의 아들. 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제. 마레사와 십의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 메사는 갈렙의 아들이며 십의 창설자(아버지)였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jobab@1Ch.8.9, Zibia@1Ch.8.9, Malcam@1Ch.8.9, Jeuz@1Ch.8.10, Sachia@1Ch.8.10, Mirmah@1Ch.8.10, Abitub@1Ch.8.11, Elpaal@1Ch.8.11-
persons.brief: A descendant of Benjamin born in Moab.
persons.short: Mesha, a descendant of Benjamin, was born to Shaharaim in the country of Moab.
persons.article: Mesha is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in the book of Chronicles (1Ch.8.9). He was one of the sons born to Shaharaim in the country of Moab after he had divorced his wives Hushim and Baara.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.9 only referred to as Mesha (מֵישָׁא); son of Shaharaim and Hodesh; a brother of Jobab, Zibia, Malcam, Jeuz, Sachia, Mirmah, Abitub and Elpaal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '메사'라 불림. 사하라임과 호데스의 아들. 요밥, 시비야, 말감, 여우스, 사갸, 미르마, 아비둡과 엘바알의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 메사는 베냐민의 후손으로, 사하라임이 모압 땅에서 낳았다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Moab who rebelled against Israel.
persons.short: Mesha, king of Moab, rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.
persons.article: Mesha was the king of Moab who paid tribute to the kings of Israel. He was a sheep breeder and used to supply the king of Israel with a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams (2Ki.3.4). However, after the death of Ahab, king of Israel, Mesha rebelled against Israelite rule. In response, Jehoram, the king of Israel, allied with Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and the king of Edom to wage war against Moab (2Ki.3.6-7). During the battle, when Mesha saw that the battle was going against him, he took his firstborn son and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall, causing great wrath against Israel and forcing the Israelite army to withdraw (2Ki.3.26-27).
persons.summary: A king in Moab living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.3.4 only referred to as Mesha (מֵישַׁע).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '메사'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 모압 왕 메사는 아합이 죽은 후 이스라엘에 대항하여 반역했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth and grandson of Noah.
persons.short: Meshech, a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, is mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Meshech was one of the sons of Japheth and a grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations (Gen.10.2; 1Ch.1.5). The Table of Nations is a genealogical record of the descendants of Noah's three sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—and their dispersal after the Tower of Babel. Meshech is listed among the sons of Japheth, along with his brothers Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, and Tiras. These sons and their descendants are generally associated with the peoples of the northern and western regions, including Asia Minor and Europe.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Meshech (מֶ֫שֶׁךְ); son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal and Tiras.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '메섹'이라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마곡, 마대, 야완, 두발과 디라스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 메섹은 야벳의 아들이며 노아의 손자로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.offspring: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: A Levite gatekeeper in the time of David.
persons.short: Meshelemiah (also called Shelemiah), a Levite gatekeeper during David's reign.
persons.article: Meshelemiah, also known as Shelemiah, was a Levite gatekeeper who served during the reign of King David. He was the son of Kore, from the clan of Korah (1Ch.9.21; 26.1,14). Meshelemiah had seven sons: Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai (1Ch.26.2). He and his sons were assigned to guard the gates of the tabernacle (1Ch.26.1). Meshelemiah was specifically in charge of the East Gate (1Ch.26.14). His sons and relatives, who were capable men, totaled 62 individuals serving as gatekeepers (1Ch.26.9).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.21 referred to as Meshelemiah (מְשֶׁלֶמְיָהוּ), or Shelemiah (שֶׁלֶמְיָהוּ); father of Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.21에 처음 언급되며 '므셀레먀'라 불림. 스가랴, 여디아엘, 스바댜, 야드니엘, 엘람, 여호하난과 엘여호에내의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므셀레먀(셀레먀라고도 함)는 다윗 왕 시대의 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Meshezabel, one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.article: Meshezabel is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh.10.21). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, the people gathered to hear Ezra read the Book of the Law. They then confessed their sins and made a covenant to follow God's laws. Meshezabel was among the leaders who signed and sealed this covenant, pledging to uphold its terms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.21 only referred to as Meshezabel (מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '므세사벨'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므세사벨은 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A representative of the people to the Persian king.
persons.short: Meshezabel, from the descendants of Judah, was the people's representative to the Persian king.
persons.article: Meshezabel, a descendant of Judah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the people's representative to the Persian king (Neh.11.24). This information is provided in the context of a list of people who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Pethahiah, the son of Meshezabel, was appointed to represent the people in all matters concerning the king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.24 only referred to as Meshezabel (מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל); father of Pethahiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.24에 처음 언급되며 '므세사벨'이라 불림. 브다히야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유다의 후손 므세사벨은 페르시아 왕에게 백성을 대표했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Meshezabel, son of Berechiah, helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Meshezabel, the son of Berechiah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time (Neh.3.4). He worked on a section of the wall next to Meremoth, the son of Uriah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.4 only referred to as Meshezabel (מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל); father of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '므세사벨'이라 불림. 베레갸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브레갸의 아들 므세사벨은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도왔다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Meshillemith (also called Meshillemoth), a priest who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meshillemith, also known as Meshillemoth, was a priest who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. In the book of Chronicles, he is mentioned in the list of priests and Levites who resided in Jerusalem (1Ch.9.12). Meshillemith is described as the son of Immer, indicating his priestly lineage. In the book of Nehemiah, a priest named Meshillemoth, likely the same individual, is mentioned among the priests living in Jerusalem (Neh.11.13).
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 referred to as Meshillemith (מְשִׁלֵּמִית), or Meshillemoth (מְשִׁלֵּמוֹת); a son of Immer; father of Meshullam.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '므실레밋'이라 불림. 임멜의 아들. 므술람의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므실레밋(므실레못이라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: An Ephraimite leader during the reign of Pekah.
persons.short: Meshillemoth, an Ephraimite leader who opposed the enslavement of Judean captives.
persons.article: Meshillemoth was an Ephraimite leader who lived during the reign of Pekah, king of Israel. When Pekah's army defeated Judah and took captives, Meshillemoth, along with other leaders such as Azariah, Berechiah, and Jehizkiah, stood against the army and opposed the enslavement of their fellow Israelites (2Ch.28.12). They urged the army to release the captives, clothe them, and return them to Jericho, citing the Lord's fierce wrath against Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.12 only referred to as Meshillemoth (מְשִׁלֵּמוֹת); father of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.28.12에 처음 언급되며 '무실레못'이라 불림. 베레갸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므실레못은 유다 포로들을 노예로 삼는 것을 반대한 에브라임 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.short: Meshobab, a Simeonite leader during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Meshobab is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in the book of Chronicles (1Ch.4.34). He is listed among the leaders of the Simeonites during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. These leaders, including Meshobab, Jamlech, and Joshah, led a group of Simeonites who destroyed the remaining Amalekites and settled in their land.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.34 only referred to as Meshobab (מְשׁוֹבָב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.34에 처음 언급되며 '메소밥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므소밥은 히스기야 왕 시대의 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Hananiah@1Ch.3.19-, Shelomith@1Ch.3.19, Hashubah@1Ch.3.20, Ohel@1Ch.3.20, Berechiah@1Ch.3.20, Hasadiah@1Ch.3.20, Jushab-hesed@1Ch.3.20, Abiud@Mat.1.13
persons.brief: Son of Zerubbabel, a descendant of David.
persons.short: Meshullam, a son of Zerubbabel, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants in the book of Chronicles (1Ch.3.19). He was one of the sons of Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah who led the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity. Meshullam is listed along with his brothers Hananiah, Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.19 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); son of Zerubbabel; a brother of Hananiah, Shelomith, Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, Jushab-hesed, Abiud.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.19에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 스룹바벨의 아들. 하나냐, 슬로밋, 하수바, 오헬, 베레갸, 하사댜, 유삽헤셋과 아비훗의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 스룹바벨의 아들로, 다윗 후손 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Michael@1Ch.5.13, Sheba@1Ch.5.13, Jorai@1Ch.5.13, Jacan@1Ch.5.13, Zia@1Ch.5.13, Eber@1Ch.5.13
persons.brief: A Gadite leader during the reign of Jotham.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Gadite leader during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad in the book of Chronicles (1Ch.5.13). He is listed among the leaders of the Gadites during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah. These leaders, including Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber, were described as mighty warriors, famous men, and heads of their fathers' houses.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.13 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); son of Abihail; a brother of Michael, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.13에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 아비하일의 아들. 미가엘, 세바, 요래, 야간, 시아와 에벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 유다 왕 요담 시대의 갓 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Eber@1Ch.8.12, Misham@1Ch.8.12, Shemed@1Ch.8.12, Beriah@1Ch.8.13-, Shema@1Ch.8.13, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.17, Hizki@1Ch.8.17, Heber@1Ch.8.17, Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18, Izliah@1Ch.8.18, Jobab@1Ch.8.18
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Elpaal.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Benjamite, was one of the sons of Elpaal.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in the book of Chronicles (1Ch.8.17). He was one of the sons of Elpaal, along with Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.17 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); son of Elpaal; a brother of Eber, Misham, Shemed, Beriah, Shema, Zebadiah, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.17에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 엘바알의 아들. 에벨, 미삼, 세멧, 브리아, 세마, 스바댜, 히스기, 헤벨, 이스므래, 이슬리아와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 베냐민 사람으로 엘바알의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Meshullam (also called Ahzai), a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meshullam, also known as Ahzai, was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. In the book of Chronicles, he is mentioned in the list of priests who settled in Jerusalem (1Ch.9.12). Meshullam is described as the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer. In the book of Nehemiah, a priest named Ahzai, likely the same individual, is mentioned among the priests living in Jerusalem (Neh.11.13). Ahzai is described as the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם), or Ahzai (אַחְזַי); a son of Meshillemith; father of Jahzerah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 므실레밋의 아들. 야세라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므술람(아하새라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Benjamite, was among those who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the list of Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1Ch.9.7). He is listed along with Sallu, Ibneiah, Elah, and Meshullam, who were descendants of Jeshaiah, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.7 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); a son of Hodaviah; father of Sallu.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.7에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 호다위야의 아들. 살루의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Shephathiah.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Benjamite, was the son of Shephathiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the list of Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1Ch.9.8). He was the son of Shephathiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah. This Meshullam is listed separately from the Meshullam mentioned in 1Ch.9.7, indicating that they were two different individuals from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.8 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); a son of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.8에 처음 언급되며 '무술람'이라 불림. 스바댜의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 베냐민 사람으로, 입니야의 아들 르우엘의 아들 스바댜의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite who supervised repairs in Josiah's time.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Levite, was among those who supervised the repairs of the temple during King Josiah's reign.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of 2 Chronicles as one of the Levites who supervised the repairs of the temple during the reign of King Josiah (2Ch.34.12). He is described as a Kohathite, indicating his descent from Kohath, one of the sons of Levi. Meshullam, along with Jahath and Obadiah, who were also Levites, oversaw the workmen and all those doing the work in the various kinds of service. This event took place during Josiah's reforms, which included the restoration of the temple and the renewal of the covenant with God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.12 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.12에 처음 언급되며 '무술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 므술람은 요시야 왕 시대에 성전 수리를 감독하는 일을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Shaphan the scribe during Josiah's reign.
persons.short: Meshullam, the grandfather of Shaphan the scribe, mentioned during King Josiah's reign.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of 2 Kings as the grandfather of Shaphan the scribe (2Ki.22.3). Shaphan played a significant role during the reign of King Josiah of Judah. He was sent by the king to the temple to oversee the temple repairs and the collection of funds. During this process, Hilkiah the high priest discovered the Book of the Law, which Shaphan then brought and read to King Josiah. This event led to Josiah's religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.22.3 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); father of Azaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.22.3에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 아살리야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 요시야 왕 시대에 언급된 서기관 사반의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Opposed Ezra's plan to put away foreign wives.
persons.short: Meshullam, along with Jonathan the son of Asahel, opposed Ezra's plan to put away foreign wives.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of two individuals who opposed Ezra's plan to put away foreign wives (Ezr.10.15). After Ezra had led the people in confessing their sin of intermarriage with foreign women, he proposed a plan for the men to separate from their foreign wives and children. This plan was met with general agreement, but Meshullam and Jonathan the son of Asahel stood against it. The reason for their opposition is not explicitly stated in the text. Despite their dissent, the plan was carried out, and the men put away their foreign wives.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.15 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 아사헬의 아들 요나단과 함께 에스라의 이방인 아내 축출 계획을 반대했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: An Israelite who had married a foreign woman.
persons.short: Meshullam, one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile (Ezr.10.29). After Ezra had led the people in confessing their sin of intermarriage and proposed a plan for the men to separate from their foreign wives, a list of those who had married foreign women was recorded. Meshullam is listed among the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign wives. In response to Ezra's call for repentance and obedience to God's law, Meshullam and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.29 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.29에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader summoned by Ezra to help teach the Law.
persons.short: Meshullam, a leader summoned by Ezra to assist in teaching the Law to the people.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the leaders summoned by Ezra to assist in teaching the Law to the people (Ezr.8.16). Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia. Upon arriving in Jerusalem, Ezra discovered that many of the people, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the surrounding nations and adopted their practices. To address this issue, Ezra called for the leaders, including Meshullam, to help him teach the Law to the people and guide them in repentance and obedience to God's commands.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.16 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 가르치는 것을 돕도록 소집한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A leader who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Meshullam, one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh.10.20). After the public reading of the Law and the people's confession of their sins, the leaders, priests, and Levites entered into a covenant to follow God's Law and uphold its requirements. Meshullam was among the leaders who signed and sealed this covenant, pledging to adhere to its stipulations. The inclusion of Meshullam in this list suggests that he held a position of authority and influence within the community, although his specific role or title is not mentioned.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.20 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.20에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Meshullam, a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah and participated in the dedication of the wall.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh.10.7). After the public reading of the Law and the people's confession of their sins, the leaders, priests, and Levites entered into a covenant to follow God's Law and uphold its requirements. Meshullam was among the priests who signed and sealed this covenant, pledging to adhere to its stipulations. Later, during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, Meshullam is mentioned again as one of the priests who participated in the procession and the dedication ceremonies (Neh.12.33). This suggests that Meshullam held a significant role within the priesthood and actively contributed to the spiritual life of the community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.7 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.7에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 므술람은 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 서명하고 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.7). He is listed among the descendants of Sallu, along with Gabbai and Sallai, who settled in Jerusalem. This information is provided in the context of a list of people who resettled in Jerusalem and other cities of Judah after the exile. The mention of Meshullam in this list indicates that he was part of the group that returned to Jerusalem and contributed to the repopulation and restoration of the city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.7 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); a son of Joed; father of Sallu.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.7에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 요엣의 아들. 살루의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.short: Meshullam, a priest who served during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who served during the high priesthood of Joiakim (Neh.12.13). Joiakim was the son of Jeshua, the high priest who had returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel. In the list of priests and Levites who served during this time, Meshullam is named as the head of the priestly family of Ezra. This suggests that Meshullam was a prominent figure within the priesthood and had a leadership role in his family's priestly duties.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.13 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.13에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 요야김의 대제사장 시절에 섬긴 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.short: Meshullam, head of the priestly family of Ginnethon during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the head of the priestly family of Ginnethon during the high priesthood of Joiakim (Neh.12.16). Joiakim was the son of Jeshua, the high priest who had returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel. In the list of priests and Levites who served during this time, Meshullam is named as the leader of the Ginnethon family. This suggests that Meshullam had a significant role in overseeing the priestly duties and responsibilities of his family.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.16 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.16에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 요야김의 대제사장 시절 긴느돈 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite gatekeeper during Nehemiah's time.
persons.short: Meshullam, a Levite gatekeeper who served during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the Levite gatekeepers who served during Nehemiah's time (Neh.12.25). He is listed along with Talmon, Akkub, and their associates, who were responsible for guarding the gates and storerooms at the gates. The gatekeepers played a crucial role in maintaining the security and order of the temple and its precincts. They ensured that only authorized individuals entered the sacred areas and that the temple's treasures and supplies were protected.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.25 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.25에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므술람은 느헤미야 시대에 섬긴 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Helped repair the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah.
persons.short: Meshullam, son of Berechiah, helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Meshullam, the son of Berechiah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time (Neh.3.4,30). He worked on two sections of the wall, one near the Fish Gate and another near his own house. Meshullam's involvement in the wall reconstruction demonstrates his commitment to the restoration of Jerusalem and the security of its inhabitants. Later in the book, it is mentioned that Meshullam's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, one of Nehemiah's main adversaries (Neh.6.18). This family connection may have complicated Meshullam's role in the ongoing political tensions surrounding the rebuilding of Jerusalem, but no further details are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.3.4 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); a son of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 베레갸의 아들. 므술람의 딸(이름 미상)의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브레갸의 아들 므술람은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Helped repair the Old Gate in Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Meshullam, son of Besodeiah, helped repair the Old Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Meshullam, the son of Besodeiah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who helped repair the Old Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall (Neh.3.6). He worked alongside Joiada, the son of Paseah, to repair and restore this gate. The Old Gate was one of the main entrances to the city of Jerusalem, and its repair was crucial for the security and functionality of the city. Meshullam's participation in this task demonstrates his willingness to contribute to the restoration of Jerusalem and its infrastructure.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.6 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם); a son of Besodeiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.6에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림. 브소드야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 브소드야의 아들 므술람은 예루살렘 성벽 재건 당시 옛 문을 수리하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law.
persons.short: Meshullam, a priest who stood beside Ezra during the public reading of the Law.
persons.article: Meshullam is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who stood beside Ezra during the public reading of the Law (Neh.8.4). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem, the people gathered to hear Ezra read the Book of the Law. Ezra stood on a wooden platform built for this purpose, and beside him stood several priests, including Meshullam. The presence of these priests alongside Ezra emphasizes the importance and solemnity of the occasion, as well as the role of the priesthood in teaching and upholding the Law.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Meshullam (מְשֻׁלָּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '므술람'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 므술람은 에스라가 율법을 공개적으로 낭독할 때 그 곁에 섰다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of Amon, king of Judah.
persons.short: Meshullemeth, the mother of Amon, king of Judah, was from Jotbah.
persons.article: Meshullemeth is mentioned in the Second Book of Kings as the mother of Amon, who became king of Judah (2Ki.21.19). She was the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah, a town whose location is unknown. Meshullemeth's son, Amon, succeeded his father, Manasseh, as king of Judah. However, Amon's reign was short-lived, lasting only two years before he was assassinated by his servants. The biblical text does not provide any further information about Meshullemeth's life, her influence on her son, or her role in the royal court. Her mention serves primarily to identify the maternal lineage of King Amon.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.21.19 only referred to as Meshullemeth (מְשֻׁלֶּ֫מֶת); a daughter of Haruz; wife of Manasseh; mother of Amon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.21.19에 처음 언급되며 '므술레멧'이라 불림. 하루스의 딸. 므낫세의 아내. 아몬의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 므술레멧은 욧바 출신으로 유다 왕 아몬의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: The oldest person mentioned in the Bible.
persons.short: Methuselah, the son of Enoch, was the oldest person mentioned in the Bible, living 969 years.
persons.article: Methuselah, the son of Enoch and the grandfather of Noah, is recognized as the oldest person mentioned in the Bible. He lived an astonishing 969 years (Gen.5.27). Methuselah's father, Enoch, walked with God and was taken by Him at the age of 365 (Gen.5.21-24). Methuselah's long life is seen as a symbol of God's patience and mercy in delaying the judgment of the flood until after his death. His name is mentioned in the genealogies of both Chronicles (1Ch.1.3 and Luke )(Luk.3.37, emphasizing his importance in the lineage of the Messiah). Although little is known about Methuselah's personal life or character, his exceptional longevity stands as a testament to God's sovereignty and the reliability of His word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.5.21 referred to as Methuselah (מְתוּשֶׁ֫לַח), or Methuselah (Μαθουσάλα); a son of Enoch; father of Lamech.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.5.21에 처음 언급되며 '므두셀라'라 불림. 에녹의 아들. 라멕의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 에녹의 아들 므두셀라는 구백육십구 년을 살아 성경에서 가장 오래 산 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: A descendant of Cain; father of Lamech.
persons.short: Methushael, a descendant of Cain, was the father of Lamech.
persons.article: Methushael is mentioned in the book of Genesis as a descendant of Cain, the son of Adam and Eve (Gen.4.18). He was the son of Mehujael and the father of Lamech. Methushael is part of the genealogy that traces the line of Cain, which is separate from the godly line of Seth. The Cainite genealogy is known for the development of various skills and crafts, as well as the increasing wickedness and violence on the earth. Lamech, Methushael's son, is recorded as the first polygamist and a man of violence (Gen.4.19-24). No further details about Methushael's life, character, or achievements are provided in the biblical text. His mention serves to bridge the generations between Cain and Lamech in the genealogical record.
persons.summary: A man living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.4.18 only referred to as Methushael (מְתוּשָׁאֵל); a son of Mehujael; father of Lamech.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 남성. Gen.4.18에 처음 언급되며 '므드사엘'이라 불림. 므후야엘의 아들. 라멕의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므두사엘은 가인의 후손이며 라멕의 아버지였다.

persons.description: People from Mehun(?)
persons.brief: A group of temple servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: The Meunim were a group of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: The Meunim are mentioned in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah as one of the groups of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.50; Neh.7.52). They are listed among the Nethinim, which were a class of people dedicated to assisting the Levites in the service of the temple. The Meunim's specific duties within the temple are not described in the biblical text. Their inclusion in the lists of returning exiles suggests that they played a role in the restoration of temple worship after the exile. The origin and earlier history of the Meunim are not provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: People from Mehun(?), first mentioned at Ezr.2.50 only referred to as Meunim (מְעוּנִים).
persons.summary_ko: 므우님. Ezr.2.50에 처음 언급되며 '므우님'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므우님은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 무리였다.

persons.description: People from Meunit(?)
persons.brief: A people group who were enemies of Israel.
persons.short: The Meunites were a people group who lived near Israel and were enemies of God's people.
persons.article: The Meunites are mentioned in the books of Chronicles as a people group who lived in the vicinity of Israel and were enemies of God's people. In the time of King Hezekiah, the Simeonites attacked and defeated the Meunites, destroying their tents and dwellings (1Ch.4.41). Later, during the reign of King Uzziah, God helped him against the Meunites (2Ch.26.7). In the days of King Jehoshaphat, the Meunites joined with the Moabites and Ammonites to attack Judah, but God caused them to turn against each other, resulting in their defeat (2Ch.20.1, 22-23). The exact location and origin of the Meunites are not specified in the Bible, but they appear to have been a nomadic or semi-nomadic people who lived in the regions east and south of Israel.
persons.summary: People from Meunit(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at 1Ch.4.41 referred to as Meunites or Meunite (מְעוּנִים), or Meunite (עַמּוֹנִי).
persons.summary_ko: 모우님 사람. 1Ch.4.41에 처음 언급되며 '므우님'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므우님 족속은 이스라엘 근처에 살던 민족으로 하나님 백성의 대적이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Edomite king Hadar.
persons.short: Mezahab was the grandfather of Mehetabel, who was the wife of Hadar, an Edomite king.
persons.article: Mezahab is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau in the book of Genesis and the book of Chronicles (Gen.36.39; 1Ch.1.50). He was the father of Matred and the grandfather of Mehetabel, who became the wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom mentioned in these genealogies. No further information is given about Mezahab's life, occupation, or place of origin. His name, which means "waters of gold" or "gold waters" in Hebrew, may suggest some connection to a place known for its gold or water resources, but the Bible does not provide any details to confirm this.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.39 only referred to as Mezahab (מֵי זָהָב); father of Matred.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.39에 처음 언급되며 '메사합'이라 불림. 마드렛의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므사합은 에돔 왕 하달의 아내 므헤다벨의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Warriors from or of Mezoba(?)
persons.brief: The people group of Jaasiel, one of David's warriors.
persons.short: The Mezobaites were the people group of Jaasiel, one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: The Mezobaites are mentioned briefly in the book of 1 Chronicles as the people group to which Jaasiel, one of David's mighty warriors, belonged (1Ch.11.47). Jaasiel is listed among the warriors who came to David at Ziklag and helped him in his battles. No further information is provided about the Mezobaites, their location, or their relationship to Israel. The name "Mezobaite" may refer to a particular place or region, but the Bible does not give any details about its location or significance.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Mezoba(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.11.47 only referred to as Mezobaites (מְצֹבָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 므소바 사람. 1Ch.11.47에 처음 언급되며 '므소바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 므소바 족속은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 야아시엘이 속한 민족이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Hagri.
persons.short: Mibhar, the son of Hagri, was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Mibhar is mentioned in the book of 1 Chronicles as one of David's mighty warriors (1Ch.11.38). He is described as the son of Hagri, but no further details about his family background or place of origin are given. Mibhar is listed among the warriors who supported David and helped him in his military campaigns. The Bible does not record any specific exploits or achievements of Mibhar, but his inclusion in the list of David's mighty warriors suggests that he was a skilled and valiant soldier who demonstrated loyalty to David and played a significant role in his army.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.38 only referred to as Mibhar (מִבְחָר); a son of Hagri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.38에 처음 언급되며 '밉할'이라 불림. 하갈의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하그리의 아들 미브할은 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite, son of Mishma.
persons.short: Mibsam, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Mishma.
persons.article: Mibsam is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in the book of 1 Chronicles (1Ch.4.25). He was the son of Mishma and is listed among the descendants of Shaul. The genealogy in this passage traces the lineage of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. No additional information is given about Mibsam's life, occupation, or role within the Simeonite clan. His mention serves to provide a record of the generations descending from Simeon.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.25 only referred to as Mibsam (מִבְשָׂם); a son of Shallum; father of Mishma.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.25에 처음 언급되며 '밉삼'이라 불림. 살룸의 아들. 미스마의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미브삼은 시므온의 후손으로 미스마의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Massa@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Jetur@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Mahalath@Gen.28.9-
persons.brief: Son of Ishmael, grandson of Abraham.
persons.short: Mibsam was a son of Ishmael and grandson of Abraham.
persons.article: Mibsam is mentioned in the genealogies of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, in the books of Genesis and 1 Chronicles (Gen.25.13; 1Ch.1.29). He was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, who were described as "princes according to their nations" (Gen.25.16). The listing of Ishmael's sons demonstrates the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that He would make Ishmael fruitful and multiply him exceedingly (Gen.17.20).
persons.summary: A man of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.13 only referred to as Mibsam (מִבְשָׂם); son of Ishmael; a brother of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah and Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 아라비아 사람. Gen.25.13에 처음 언급되며 '밉삼'이라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 미스마, 두마, 맛사, 하닷, 데마, 여둘, 나비스, 게드마와 마할랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 미브삼은 이스마엘의 아들이며 아브라함의 손자였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A chief of Edom, descendant of Esau.
persons.short: Mibzar was one of the chiefs of Edom, descended from Esau.
persons.article: Mibzar is mentioned in the lists of the chiefs of Edom in the books of Genesis and 1 Chronicles (Gen.36.42; 1Ch.1.53). He was one of the chiefs who came from the descendants of Esau, Jacob's brother. The Edomites were the offspring of Esau and lived in the region southeast of Israel. The chiefs of Edom are listed to show the political and social structure of the Edomite people. No specific details are provided about Mibzar's life, reign, or achievements. His inclusion in the list of chiefs suggests he held a position of authority and leadership among the Edomites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.42 only referred to as Mibzar (מִבְצָר).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.42에 처음 언급되며 '밉살'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 밉살은 에서의 후손인 에돔 족장 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Mica (or Micah), a Levite, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Mica, also known as Micah, is mentioned in the books of 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah as one of the Levites who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1Ch.9.15; Neh.11.17). He was a descendant of Asaph, one of the three main Levitical singers appointed by David. In the post-exilic period, Mica is described as the son of Zichri and a leader of the Levites. He is also mentioned as being second to Mattaniah in thanksgiving and prayer. These details suggest that Mica played a significant role in the worship and spiritual life of the Jewish community in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.15 referred to as Mica (מִיכָא), or Mica (מִיכָה); a son of Zichri; father of Mattaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.15에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림. 시그리의 아들. 맛다냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미가(미가야라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.short: Mica, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
persons.article: Mica is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh.10.11). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commandments and ordinances. The leaders, Levites, and priests, including Mica, sealed this covenant, pledging to uphold its stipulations. This act demonstrated Mica's commitment to the spiritual renewal and obedience of the Jewish community in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.11 only referred to as Mica (מִיכָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.11에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 미가는 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite leader in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: Mica (or Micaiah), a Levite leader, served in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Mica, also known as Micaiah, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as a Levite leader who served in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.22; 12.35). He was a descendant of Asaph, one of the principal musicians appointed by David. In the post-exilic period, Mica is described as the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem and was responsible for the outside work of the house of God (Neh.11.22). He is also listed among the priests and Levites who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, playing musical instruments (Neh.12.35). These details highlight Mica's significant role in the spiritual and practical affairs of the Jewish community in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.11.22 referred to as Mica (מִיכָא), or Micaiah (מִיכָיָה); father of Mattaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.22에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림. 맛다냐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미가(미가야라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에서 섬긴 레위인 지도자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A Levite, son of Uzziel, during David's reign.
persons.short: Micah, a Levite and son of Uzziel, served during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Micah is mentioned in the book of 1 Chronicles as a Levite who served during the reign of King David (1Ch.23.20; 24.24,25). He was the son of Uzziel, who was a descendant of Kohath, one of the three main branches of the Levites. In the organization of the Levites for temple service, Micah is listed as the head of his father's household (1Ch.24.24). His son, Shamir, is also mentioned in the genealogy (1Ch.24.24). The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the tabernacle and later in the temple. They were also in charge of music, gatekeeping, and other duties related to the worship of God. Although no specific details are given about Micah's role or contributions, his inclusion in these lists suggests that he held a position of responsibility among the Levites during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.20 only referred to as Micah (מִיכָה); son of Uzziel; a brother of Mishael, Elizaphan, Sithri and Isshiah; father of Shamir.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.20에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림. 웃시엘의 아들. 미사엘, 엘사반, 시드리와 잇시야의 형제. 사밀의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시엘의 아들 레위인 미가는 다윗 왕 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Reubenite, descendant of Joel.
persons.short: Micah, a descendant of Joel, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben.
persons.article: Micah is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben in the book of 1 Chronicles (1Ch.5.5). He is listed as a descendant of Joel, who was one of the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in this passage traces the lineage of the Reubenites, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, who settled east of the Jordan River. No additional information is provided about Micah's life, occupation, or role within the Reubenite clan. His mention serves to maintain a record of the generations descending from Reuben.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.5 only referred to as Micah (מִיכָה); a son of Shimei; father of Reaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.5에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 르아야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미가는 요엘의 후손으로, 르우벤 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mephibosheth, grandson of Jonathan.
persons.short: Micah (or Mica), the son of Mephibosheth and grandson of Jonathan, is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Micah, also known as Mica, is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Benjamin in the books of 1 Chronicles and 2 Samuel (1Ch.8.34,35; 9.40,41; 2Sa.9.12). He was the son of Mephibosheth, who was the son of Jonathan, King David's close friend. Mephibosheth was lame in both feet and was shown kindness by David for the sake of his father, Jonathan (2Sa.9.3-13). Micah is listed in the genealogies as a descendant of Saul, the first king of Israel, through Jonathan's line. Apart from his mention in these genealogies, no additional information is provided about Micah's life, character, or role in the biblical narrative.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.9.12 referred to as Micah (מִיכָה), or Mica (מִיכָא); a son of Mephibosheth; father of Pithon, Melech, Tarea and Ahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림. 므비보셋의 아들. 비돈, 멜렉, 다레아와 아하스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미가(므비보셋의 아들이며 요나단의 손자)는 베냐민 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Priest living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: A man from Ephraim who set up idolatrous worship.
persons.short: Micah, a man from the hill country of Ephraim, set up idolatrous worship in his house, which was later adopted by the Danites.
persons.article: Micah is a man from the hill country of Ephraim who is featured in a narrative in the book of Judges (Jdg.17-18). He stole 1,100 pieces of silver from his mother but later returned them. His mother then dedicated 200 pieces of silver to the Lord for Micah to make a carved image and a metal idol (Jdg.17.1-4). Micah set up these idols in his house, along with an ephod and household gods, and installed one of his sons as his priest (Jdg.17.5). Later, a Levite from Bethlehem came to Micah's house, and Micah hired him to be his personal priest (Jdg.17.8-13). The Danites, who were seeking land to settle, sent spies who stayed at Micah's house. They later returned with 600 armed men, stole Micah's idols and his priest, and went on to conquer the city of Laish (Jdg.18.1-29). This narrative highlights the religious and moral decline in Israel during the time of the judges, when "everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (Jdg.17.6; 21.25).
persons.summary: A priest living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.17.1 referred to as Micah (מִיכָה), or Micah (מִיכָֽיְהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 제사장. Jdg.17.1에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 에브라임 산지 사람 미가는 자기 집에 우상 숭배를 세웠고, 후에 단 지파가 그것을 받아들였다.
persons.article_ko: 미가는 에브라임 산지 사람으로 사사기의 한 이야기에 등장한다(삿 17-18장). 그는 어머니에게서 은 천백 개를 훔쳤으나 후에 돌려주었다. 그러자 그의 어머니는 미가가 조각한 형상과 부어 만든 우상을 만들도록 은 이백 개를 여호와께 드렸다(삿 17:1-4). 미가는 이 우상들을 에봇 및 드라빔과 함께 자기 집에 세우고 자기 아들 중 한 사람을 제사장으로 삼았다(삿 17:5). 후에 베들레헴 출신 한 레위인이 미가의 집에 왔고, 미가는 그를 고용하여 자기의 개인 제사장으로 삼았다(삿 17:8-13). 정착할 땅을 찾던 단 지파는 정탐꾼을 보냈고 그들은 미가의 집에 머물렀다. 그들은 후에 무장한 남자 육백 명과 함께 돌아와 미가의 우상들과 그의 제사장을 훔쳐 라이스 성을 정복했다(삿 18:1-29). 이 이야기는 '각자가 자기 소견에 옳은 대로 행하던' 사사 시대의 이스라엘의 종교적, 도덕적 쇠퇴를 부각시킨다(삿 17:6; 21:25).

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet from Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
persons.short: Micah, a prophet from Moresheth, prophesied during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
persons.article: Micah was a prophet from Moresheth, a town in the Shephelah region of Judah, who prophesied during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (Mic.1.1). His prophetic ministry likely spanned from around 750 to 700 BC. Micah's prophecies focused on the judgment of Samaria and Jerusalem for their idolatry, injustice, and oppression of the poor. He also foretold the coming of the Messiah and the restoration of God's people (Mic.5.2). Micah's prophecy that Zion would be plowed like a field and Jerusalem would become ruins (Mic.3.12 was remembered over a century later during the time of Jeremiah )(Jer.26.18). This reference to Micah's prophecy helped spare Jeremiah's life when he faced the threat of death for prophesying against Jerusalem. The book of Micah, which bears his name, preserves his prophetic messages and is part of the Minor Prophets in the Old Testament.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.26.18 referred to as Micah (מִיכָה), or Micah (מִיכָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. Jer.26.18에 처음 언급되며 '미가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 모레셋 출신 선지자 미가는 유다 왕 요담, 아하스, 히스기야 시대에 예언했다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A prophet who foretold King Ahab's death.
persons.short: Micaiah (or Micahu), a prophet, foretold the death of King Ahab of Israel in battle against the Arameans.
persons.article: Micaiah, also referred to as Micahu, was a prophet who lived during the reign of King Ahab of Israel (1Ki.22; 2Ch.18). When Ahab and King Jehoshaphat of Judah planned to go to war against the Arameans at Ramoth-gilead, they sought the counsel of prophets. While the false prophets assured victory, Micaiah was summoned to provide a true word from the Lord. Initially, Micaiah sarcastically affirmed the false prophets' message, but when pressed by Ahab, he delivered a vision of Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd, indicating Ahab's impending death (1Ki.22.17; 2Ch.18.16). Micaiah also revealed that the Lord had put a lying spirit in the mouth of the false prophets to entice Ahab to his doom (1Ki.22.19-23; 2Ch.18.18-22). Angered by this prophecy, Ahab ordered Micaiah to be imprisoned and fed only bread and water until his safe return (1Ki.22.26-27; 2Ch.18.25-26). However, Micaiah declared that if Ahab returned safely, then the Lord had not spoken through him (1Ki.22.28; 2Ch.18.27). Ahab disguised himself in battle but was killed by a random arrow, fulfilling Micaiah's prophecy (1Ki.22.29-40; 2Ch.18.28-34). Micaiah's unwavering commitment to speaking the truth, even in the face of opposition and personal risk, stands as an example of a faithful prophet of God.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.8 referred to as Micaiah (מִיכָֽיְהוּ), or Micahu (מִיכָֽיְהוּ), or Micaiah (מִיכָה); a son of Imlah.
persons.short_ko: 미가야는 아합 왕에게 거짓 선지자들과 달리 패전을 예언한 참 선지자다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 1Ki.22.8에 처음 언급되며 '미가야'라 불림. 이믈라의 아들.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law.
persons.short: Micaiah, a Levite, was among those sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Micaiah is mentioned in the book of 2 Chronicles as one of the Levites commissioned by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah (2Ch.17.7). In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat sent officials, Levites, and priests to instruct the people in the Law of the Lord. Micaiah is listed among the Levites who participated in this educational mission, along with Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah. This initiative demonstrates Jehoshaphat's commitment to spiritual reform and the importance of teaching God's word to the people. Micaiah's inclusion in this group suggests that he was a trusted Levite, knowledgeable in the Law, and capable of teaching others.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.7 only referred to as Micaiah (מִיכָיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.7에 처음 언급되며 '미가야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 미가야는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite sent by King Josiah to inquire of the Lord.
persons.short: Micaiah (or Micah), a Levite, was sent by King Josiah to inquire of the Lord after the discovery of the Book of the Law.
persons.article: Micaiah, also known as Micah, was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Josiah of Judah (2Ki.22.12; 2Ch.34.20). When the Book of the Law was discovered during the repair of the temple, Josiah sent a delegation, which included Micaiah, to inquire of the Lord concerning the words of the book. The delegation went to the prophetess Huldah, who delivered a message of judgment for Judah's disobedience but also affirmed that Josiah's repentance had been heard by the Lord (2Ki.22.14-20; 2Ch.34.22-28). Micaiah's inclusion in this delegation suggests that he was a trusted Levite in Josiah's court. His role in seeking the Lord's guidance demonstrates the importance of inquiring of God and heeding His word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.22.12 referred to as Micaiah (מִיכָיָה), or Micah (מִיכָה); father of Achbor.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.22.12에 처음 언급되며 '미가야'라 불림. 악볼의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 미가야(미가라고도 함)는 율법책 발견 이후 요시야 왕이 여호와께 여쭙도록 보낸 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Gemariah, reported Baruch's reading of Jeremiah's scroll.
persons.short: Micaiah, the son of Gemariah, reported to the officials about Baruch's reading of Jeremiah's scroll to the people.
persons.article: Micaiah, the son of Gemariah, appears briefly in the book of Jeremiah during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah (Jer.36.11,13). When Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, read the prophet's scroll in the temple, Micaiah was present and heard the words of warning and judgment against Judah (Jer.36.10-11). Micaiah then went to the royal palace and reported to the officials all that he had heard from the scroll (Jer.36.12-13). His report prompted the officials to send for Baruch and have him read the scroll to them (Jer.36.14). Micaiah's actions led to the officials' awareness of Jeremiah's prophetic message, although King Jehoiakim ultimately burned the scroll and sought to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch (Jer.36.20-26). Micaiah's role in this narrative highlights the importance of bearing witness to God's word and the potential impact of an individual's actions in bringing that word to the attention of those in authority.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.36.11 only referred to as Micaiah (מִיכָֽיְהוּ); a son of Gemariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.11에 처음 언급되며 '미가야'라 불림. 그마랴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 그마랴의 아들 미가야는 바룩이 백성에게 예레미야의 두루마리를 읽었다는 것을 관리들에게 보고했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.short: Micaiah, a priest, participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Micaiah is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the priests who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh.12.41). After the completion of the wall's reconstruction under Nehemiah's leadership, a great celebration was held to dedicate the wall. Two large choirs were appointed to give thanks and walk on top of the wall in opposite directions (Neh.12.31,38). Micaiah is listed among the priests who went with the second choir, along with Zechariah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani (Neh.12.41). These priests blew trumpets as part of the celebration and thanksgiving to God. Micaiah's participation in this event highlights his role as a priest and his involvement in the spiritual life of the Jewish community in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.41 only referred to as Micaiah (מִיכָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.41에 처음 언급되며 '미가야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 미가야는 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Manassite who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.short: Michael, a Manassite, was one of the men who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.
persons.article: Michael is mentioned in the book of 1 Chronicles as one of the Manassites who joined David at Ziklag (1Ch.12.20). When David was fleeing from King Saul, a group of warriors from various tribes came to support him. Among them were seven men from the tribe of Manasseh, including Michael, Jozabad, Jediael, Elihu, and Zillethai. These men are described as captains of the thousands of Manasseh, suggesting they held leadership positions within their tribe (1Ch.12.20). The Manassites who joined David were skilled warriors and played a significant role in his military campaigns. No further details about Michael's specific role, exploits, or relationship with David are provided in the biblical text. His mention serves to highlight the support David received from various tribes during his time of need.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.20 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.20에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 미가엘은 므낫세 사람으로, 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A leader of the tribe of Issachar under David.
persons.short: Michael, the son of Omri, was the leader of the tribe of Issachar during King David's reign.
persons.article: Michael is mentioned in the book of 1 Chronicles as the leader of the tribe of Issachar during King David's reign (1Ch.27.18). He is described as the son of Omri, although no further details about his father are provided. In the context of 1Chronicles 27, David organizes his administration and appoints leaders over various aspects of the kingdom, including the tribes of Israel. Michael is listed among the tribal leaders, representing Issachar. The fact that he held this position suggests that he was a prominent figure within his tribe and had the necessary leadership skills to oversee the affairs of Issachar.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.18 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל); father of Omri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.18에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림. 오므리의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 옴리의 아들 미가엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 잇사갈 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Meshullam@1Ch.5.13, Sheba@1Ch.5.13, Jorai@1Ch.5.13, Jacan@1Ch.5.13, Zia@1Ch.5.13, Eber@1Ch.5.13
persons.brief: A Gadite chief during the reign of Jotham.
persons.short: Michael, a Gadite chief, is mentioned among the leaders of the tribe of Gad during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah.
persons.article: Michael is listed in the book of 1 Chronicles as one of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah (1Ch.5.13). He is mentioned alongside his brothers: Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber. These seven Gadite chiefs are described as brave warriors, famous men, and heads of their fathers' houses (1Ch.5.14). The Gadites settled in the land of Bashan, east of the Jordan River, and were known for their valor and military prowess (1Ch.5.18-22). No further details about Michael's specific role, accomplishments, or lineage are provided in the biblical text. His mention serves to highlight the leadership structure and notable figures within the tribe of Gad during this period in Israel's history.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.13 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל); son of Abihail; a brother of Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.13에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림. 아비하일의 아들. 므술람, 세바, 요래, 야간, 시아와 에벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 미가엘은 유다 왕 요담 시대의 갓 지파 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Gadite chief, descendant of Abihail.
persons.short: Michael, a descendant of Abihail, was one of the Gadite chiefs mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.
persons.article: Michael is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad in the book of 1 Chronicles (1Ch.5.14). He is listed as a descendant of Abihail, along with his relatives: Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber. These seven men are described as chiefs of the Gadites, brave warriors, famous men, and heads of their fathers' houses (1Ch.5.13-14). The Gadites were known for their military skill and settled in the land of Bashan, east of the Jordan River (1Ch.5.18-22). No additional information about Michael's life, exploits, or role within the Gadite community is provided in the biblical text. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to trace the lineage and leadership of the tribe of Gad.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.14 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל); a son of Jeshishai; father of Gilead.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림. 여시새의 아들. 길르앗의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비하일의 후손 미가엘은 갓 지파 족보에 언급된 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Levite musician, son of Baaseiah.
persons.short: Michael, a Levite and descendant of Merari, was the son of Baaseiah and is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levitical musicians.
persons.article: Michael is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in the book of 1 Chronicles, specifically in the lineage of the Merarites (1Ch.6.40). He is listed as the son of Baaseiah, who was a descendant of Merari, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. The Merarites were responsible for the tabernacle's framework, pillars, bases, and other structural elements (Num.3.36). In the context of 1Chronicles 6, the focus is on the Levitical musicians appointed by David to serve in the temple worship. Although Michael is not explicitly described as a musician, his inclusion in this genealogy suggests that he may have been part of the Levitical musical tradition or that his descendants played a role in the temple music.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.40 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל); a son of Baaseiah; father of Shimea.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.40에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림. 바아세야의 아들. 시므아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바아세야의 아들이며 므라리 계열 레위인 미가엘은 레위인 음악가 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Uzzi, a descendant of Issachar.
persons.short: Michael, a descendant of Issachar, was one of the sons of Uzzi.
persons.article: Michael is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar in the book of 1 Chronicles (1Ch.7.3). He is listed as one of the sons of Uzzi, along with his brothers: Izrahiah, Joel, Ishiah, and Obadiah. These five men are described as mighty men of valor, and their father's house had 22,600 troops ready for battle (1Ch.7.4-5). The genealogy emphasizes the military strength and numerical significance of Issachar's descendants. No further details about Michael's life, exploits, or role within the tribe of Issachar are provided in the biblical text. His mention serves to highlight the descendants of Issachar and their contribution to Israel's armed forces.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.3 only referred to as Michael (מִיכָאֵל); son of Izrahiah; a brother of Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.3에 처음 언급되며 '미가엘'이라 불림. 이스라히야의 아들. 오바댜, 요엘과 잇시야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 미가엘은 잇사갈의 후손으로 웃시의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Arad@1Ch.8.15, Ahio@1Ch.8.14, Shashak@1Ch.8.14-, Jeremoth@1Ch.8.14, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.15, Eder@1Ch.8.15, Ishpah@1Ch.8.16, Joha@1Ch.8.16
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Beriah.
persons.short: Michael, a Benjamite, was one of the sons of Beriah mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
