persons.short: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the tribe of Issachar during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.article: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Israelite tribe of Issachar during the wilderness wanderings under Moses (Num.1.8). He was appointed to help take the census (Num.1.8 and made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle )(Num.7.18,23). Nethanel and the men of Issachar marched under their tribal standard as part of the camp of Judah, on the east side of the tabernacle (Num.2.5). His name means "given of God."
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.8 only referred to as Nethanel (נְתַנְאֵל); a son of Zuar.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.8에 처음 언급되며 '느다넬'이라 불림. 수리알의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 수알의 아들 느다넬은 광야 시절 잇사갈 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Musician in David's time, descended from Asaph
persons.short: Nethaniah was a musician in David's time, brother of Asharelah (or 'Asarelah').
persons.article: Nethaniah was a Levite musician who served during the reign of King David. He was the brother of Asharelah (or 'Asarelah', also called Jesharelah), who was one of the musicians appointed by David to prophesy with lyres, harps and cymbals (1Ch.25.2,12). These musicians were set apart for the ministry of prophesying, under the supervision of the king.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.2 only referred to as Nethaniah (נְתַנְיָ֫הוּ); son of Asaph; a brother of Zaccur, Joseph and Asharelah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.2에 처음 언급되며 '느다냐'라 불림. 아삽의 아들. 삭굴, 요셉과 아사렐라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 느다냐는 다윗 시대의 음악가로 아사렐라(아사렐라라고도 함)의 형제였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent to teach
persons.short: Nethaniah was a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in Judah.
persons.article: Nethaniah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He was one of the Levites that Jehoshaphat sent out to teach the Book of the Law in all the towns of Judah (2Ch.17.8). As a Levite, teaching the people God's laws would have been one of his key roles. This mission by Jehoshaphat was part of his reforms to turn the people back to God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Nethaniah (נְתַנְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '느다냐'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 느다냐는 여호사밧이 유다에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Ishmael
persons.short: Nethaniah was the father of Ishmael, the assassin of Gedaliah the governor.
persons.article: Nethaniah was the father of Ishmael, a man of royal blood who assassinated Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem (2Ki.25.23,25; Jer.40.8,14,15; 41.1-18). Ishmael's mother was the daughter of Elnathan, an official in Jerusalem (2Ki.24.8). After the murder of Gedaliah, Ishmael fled to the Ammonites. Nethaniah is only mentioned in reference to his son Ishmael.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.23 only referred to as Nethaniah (נְתַנְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Elishama; father of Ishmael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.25.23에 처음 언급되며 '느다니야'라 불림. 엘리사마의 아들. 이스마엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 느다냐는 총독 그달랴를 암살한 이스마엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Official under Jehoiakim
persons.short: Nethaniah was the father of Jehudi, an official in King Jehoiakim's court.
persons.article: Nethaniah was the father of Jehudi, an official in the court of King Jehoiakim of Judah (Jer.36.14). Jehudi was sent by the officials to summon Baruch to read the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies to them. The officials then told Jehudi to bring the scroll to the king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.14 only referred to as Nethaniah (נְתַנְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Shelemiah; father of Jehudi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.14에 처음 언급되며 '느다냐'라 불림. 셀레마의 아들. 여후디의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 느다냐는 여호야김 왕궁의 관리 여후디의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants
persons.short: Neziah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Neziah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (also known as Nethinim) who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.54; Neh.7.56). The temple servants assisted the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. Neziah's descendants were among those who settled in Jerusalem after the return (Neh.11.21).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.54 only referred to as Neziah (נְצִיחַ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.54에 처음 언급되며 '느시야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느시아는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: One of seven deacons
persons.short: Nicanor was one of the seven men chosen to assist the apostles in the early Jerusalem church.
persons.article: Nicanor was one of the seven men chosen by the early church in Jerusalem to assist the apostles in the daily distribution of food to the widows (Act.6.5). He was selected along with Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas. These men, who were known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom, were appointed to this task so that the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word. Nicanor was a Greek name, suggesting he may have been a Hellenistic Jew.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.6.5 only referred to as Nicanor (Νικάνωρ).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '니가노르'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 니가노르는 초대 예루살렘 교회에서 사도들을 돕도록 선택된 일곱 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Pharisee who visited Jesus
persons.short: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council who had several encounters with Jesus.
persons.article: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council, the Sanhedrin (Jhn.3.1). He came to Jesus at night, likely to avoid being seen, and engaged in a discussion about the need to be born again to enter the kingdom of God (Jhn.3.1-21). Later, Nicodemus defended Jesus before the Sanhedrin, reminding them that the law required a person to be heard before being judged (Jhn.7.50-51). After the crucifixion, Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes to anoint Jesus' body for burial, demonstrating his devotion to Jesus (Jhn.19.39-40). Though initially coming to Jesus in secret, Nicodemus grew to be a follower of Christ.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Jhn.3.1 only referred to as Nicodemus (Νικόδημος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Jhn.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '니고데모'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 니고데모는 바리새인이며 유대 최고 의회 일원으로, 예수님과 여러 번 만남을 가졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Proselyte chosen as deacon
persons.short: Nicolaus was a proselyte from Antioch chosen as one of the seven deacons in the early church.
persons.article: Nicolaus was one of the seven men chosen by the early church in Jerusalem to assist the apostles in the daily distribution of food to the widows (Act.6.5). He was a proselyte from Antioch, meaning he was a Gentile convert to Judaism before becoming a follower of Christ. Nicolaus, along with the other six chosen men, was known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. His selection as a deacon highlights the inclusive nature of the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.6.5 only referred to as Nicolaus (Νικόλαος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '니골라'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 니골라는 안디옥 출신 개종자로, 초대교회 일곱 집사 중 한 사람으로 선택되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Mighty hunter, built cities
persons.short: Nimrod was a mighty hunter and ruler who built several notable cities, including Babel and Nineveh.
persons.article: Nimrod was a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham (Gen.10.8). He was described as a mighty hunter before the Lord, indicating his prowess and skill (Gen.10.9). Nimrod became a powerful ruler, establishing a kingdom that included the cities of Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar (Gen.10.10). He also expanded his kingdom to Assyria, where he built the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah, and Resen (Gen.10.11-12). The land of Assyria is referred to as the land of Nimrod (Mic.5.6, further emphasizing his influence and power in the region).
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.8 only referred to as Nimrod (נִמְרֹד); son of Cush; a brother of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.8에 처음 언급되며 '니므롯'이라 불림. 구스의 아들. 스바, 하윌라, 삽다, 라아마와 삽드가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 니므롯은 강력한 사냥꾼이며 통치자로, 바벨과 니느웨를 포함한 여러 유명한 성읍을 세웠다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Grandfather of Jehu
persons.short: Nimshi was the grandfather of Jehu, the king of Israel who overthrew the dynasty of Ahab.
persons.article: Nimshi was the grandfather of Jehu, who became king of Israel (2Ki.9.2). Jehu was often referred to as "the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi" (2Ki.9.14, 20; 2Ch.22.7). Nimshi's son Jehoshaphat was the father of Jehu. The prophet Elijah was instructed by God to anoint Jehu as king of Israel (1Ki.19.16, a task that was later carried out by Elisha's servant )(2Ki.9.1-10). Jehu went on to overthrow the dynasty of Ahab and Jezebel, fulfilling the prophecies against them.
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.19.16 only referred to as Nimshi (נִמְשִׁי); father of Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.19.16에 처음 언급되며 '님시'라 불림. 여호사밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 님시는 아합 왕조를 무너뜨린 이스라엘 왕 예후의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite in charge of treasuries
persons.short: Noadiah was a Levite entrusted with the oversight of the treasuries during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Noadiah was a Levite who lived during the time of Ezra, after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was one of the Levites entrusted with the oversight of the treasuries of the house of God (Ezr.8.33). These treasuries contained the items that had been brought back from Babylon for use in the rebuilt temple in Jerusalem. Noadiah, along with other leaders, was responsible for ensuring the safe storage and proper use of these treasures.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.33 only referred to as Noadiah (נוֹעַדְיָה); a son of Binnui.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.33에 처음 언급되며 '노아댜'라 불림. 빈누이의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 노아댜는 에스라 시대에 곳간 관리를 맡은 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: False prophetess opposed Nehemiah
persons.short: Noadiah was a false prophetess who opposed Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
persons.article: Noadiah was a false prophetess who lived during the time of Nehemiah, when the walls of Jerusalem were being rebuilt (Neh.6.14). She, along with other false prophets, tried to intimidate and discourage Nehemiah from his work. These prophets had been hired by Tobiah and Sanballat, enemies of Nehemiah, to hinder the rebuilding efforts. Nehemiah, however, recognized their deceit and prayed for strength to continue his work despite their opposition.
persons.summary: A prophetess living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.14 only referred to as Noadiah (נוֹעַדְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Neh.6.14에 처음 언급되며 '노아댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 노아댜는 느헤미야의 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 반대한 거짓 여선지자였다.

persons.description: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
persons.brief: Righteous man, built ark, survived flood
persons.short: Noah was a righteous man who built the ark and survived the great flood with his family.
persons.article: Noah was the son of Lamech, a descendant of Seth (Gen.5.29-30). He was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God (Gen.6.9). When God saw the wickedness of humanity, He chose Noah to build an ark to save his family and representatives of all animals from the coming flood (Gen.6.13-22). Noah obeyed God and built the ark, and he and his family entered it along with the animals (Genesis 7). After the flood, Noah built an altar and made sacrifices to God (Gen.8.20). God blessed Noah and his sons, establishing a covenant with them and setting the rainbow as a sign of His promise never to destroy the earth by flood again (Genesis 9). Noah lived for 950 years (Gen.9.29). He is remembered as an example of faith (Heb.11.7 and righteousness )(Ezk.14.14, 20; 2Pe.2.5).
persons.summary: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood, first mentioned at Gen.5.29 referred to as Noah (נֹחַ), or Noah (Νῶε); husband of Naamah(?); a son of Lamech; father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
persons.summary_ko: 홍수 이전시대 홍수 생존자. Gen.5.29에 처음 언급되며 '노아'라 불림. 라멕의 아들. 나아마의 남편. 셈, 함과 야벳의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 노아는 의로운 사람으로, 방주를 지어 가족과 함께 대홍수에서 살아남았다.
persons.article_ko: 노아는 셋의 후손인 라멕의 아들이었다(창 5:29-30). 그는 의로운 사람이며 당대 사람들 가운데 흠이 없었고 하나님과 동행했다(창 6:9). 하나님이 인류의 악함을 보셨을 때 그분은 다가올 홍수로부터 그의 가족과 모든 동물의 대표들을 구원하도록 방주를 짓게 하려고 노아를 택하셨다(창 6:13-22). 노아는 하나님께 순종하여 방주를 지었고, 그와 그의 가족은 동물들과 함께 그 안에 들어갔다(창세기 7장). 홍수 이후 노아는 제단을 쌓고 하나님께 제사를 드렸다(창 8:20). 하나님은 노아와 그의 아들들을 축복하시며 그들과 언약을 세우시고, 다시는 홍수로 땅을 멸하지 않으시겠다는 약속의 표징으로 무지개를 두셨다(창세기 9장). 노아는 구백오십 년을 살았다(창 9:29). 그는 믿음(히 11:7)과 의로움(겔 14:14, 20; 벧후 2:5)의 본보기로 기억된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad
persons.short: Noah was one of the daughters of Zelophehad who received an inheritance in the Promised Land.
persons.article: Noah was one of the daughters of Zelophehad, a descendant of Manasseh (Num.26.33). She had four sisters: Mahlah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah (Num.27.1). When their father died without any sons, the daughters of Zelophehad approached Moses and Eleazar the priest, requesting to receive an inheritance among their father's relatives (Num.27.1-4). God instructed Moses to grant their request, establishing a legal precedent for daughters to inherit property when there were no sons (Num.27.5-11). As a result, Noah and her sisters were given an inheritance among the clans of Manasseh (Jos.17.3-6).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.33 only referred to as Noah (נֹעָה); daughter of Zelophehad; a sister of Mahlah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Num.26.33에 처음 언급되며 '노아'라 불림. 슬로브핫의 딸. 말라, 호글라, 밀가와 디르사의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 노아는 슬로브핫의 딸 중 한 사람으로 약속의 땅에서 유산을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Captured Kenath, renamed it Nobah
persons.short: Nobah was an Israelite who captured the town of Kenath and renamed it after himself.
persons.article: Nobah was an Israelite from the tribe of Manasseh who lived during the time of the conquest of Canaan. He captured the town of Kenath and its surrounding settlements, renaming the town after himself (Num.32.42). Kenath was located in the region of Gilead, east of the Jordan River. The renaming of the town to Nobah was a common practice in ancient times, reflecting the conquest and ownership of the area by the victor.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.32.42 only referred to as Nobah (נֹ֫בַח).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.32.42에 처음 언급되며 '노바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 노바는 그낫 성읍을 점령하고 자기 이름을 따서 지은 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: Son of David
persons.short: Nogah was one of King David's sons born in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Nogah was one of the sons of King David born to him in Jerusalem (1Ch.3.7; 14.6). He was born after David had established his reign in Jerusalem and had taken more wives and concubines. The name Nogah means "brightness" or "splendor" in Hebrew.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.3.7 only referred to as Nogah (נֹ֫גַהּ); son of David; a brother of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 1Ch.3.7에 처음 언급되며 '노가'라 불림. 다윗과 예루살렘의 아내들의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛과 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 노가는 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗 왕의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Joshua
persons.short: Nun was the father of Joshua, Moses' assistant and successor as leader of Israel.
persons.article: Nun was an Israelite from the tribe of Ephraim, best known as the father of Joshua (Exo.33.11). His son Joshua was Moses' assistant from his youth (Num.11.28 and was chosen by God to succeed Moses as the leader of Israel )(Num.27.18; Deu.31.23). Nun's name is often mentioned in connection with Joshua, emphasizing the importance of family lineage and the faithfulness passed down through generations. Joshua is referred to as "Joshua the son of Nun" throughout the Bible (e.g., Num.14.6, 30; Jos.1.1; 2.1). As the father of a prominent leader, Nun's legacy was remembered long after his lifetime (1Ki.16.34; Neh.8.17).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.33.11 only referred to as Nun (נוּן); a son of Elishama; father of Joshua.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Exo.33.11에 처음 언급되며 '눈'이라 불림. 엘리사마의 아들. 여호수아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 눈은 모세의 조수이며 후계자인 여호수아의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 눈은 에브라임 지파 출신 이스라엘 사람으로, 여호수아의 아버지로 가장 잘 알려져 있다(출 33:11). 그의 아들 여호수아는 어릴 때부터 모세의 조수였고(민 11:28) 하나님이 그를 모세를 이어 이스라엘의 지도자로 택하셨다(민 27:18; 신 31:23). 눈의 이름은 종종 여호수아와 관련하여 언급되며, 가족의 혈통과 여러 세대에 걸쳐 전해진 신실함의 중요성을 강조한다. 여호수아는 성경 전체에서 '눈의 아들 여호수아'로 지칭된다(예: 민 14:6, 30; 수 1:1; 2:1). 저명한 지도자의 아버지로서 눈의 유산은 그의 생애가 지난 후에도 오랫동안 기억되었다(왕상 16:34; 느 8:17).

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Hosted a church in her house
persons.short: Nympha was a woman who hosted a church in her house in Laodicea.
persons.article: Nympha was a Christian woman who lived in Laodicea during the time of Paul's ministry. She hosted a church in her house (Col.4.15). House churches were common in the early Christian era, as believers often gathered in homes for worship, prayer, and fellowship. Paul sent greetings to Nympha and the church that met in her home, indicating her significant role in the Christian community of Laodicea. The fact that the church is mentioned in connection with her name suggests that she was a prominent member and possibly a leader of the congregation.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Col.4.15 only referred to as Nympha (Νυμφᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Col.4.15에 처음 언급되며 '눔바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 님바는 라오디게아 자기 집에서 교회를 대접한 여인이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite warrior who joined David
persons.short: Obadiah was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul.
persons.article: Obadiah was one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul (1Ch.12.9). He was described as a mighty man of valor, indicating his military prowess and bravery. The Gadites who joined David were skilled in battle and known for their courage and loyalty. They played a significant role in supporting David during his time of exile and helped him establish his kingdom. Obadiah's presence among these warriors demonstrates the widespread support David had from various tribes of Israel, even before he became king.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.9 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.9에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 갓 지파 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ruler over Zebulun in David's time
persons.short: Obadiah was the ruler over the tribe of Zebulun during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Obadiah was the ruler over the tribe of Zebulun during the reign of King David (1Ch.27.19). He was appointed by David to oversee the administration and organization of the tribe. As a ruler, Obadiah's responsibilities likely included managing resources, resolving disputes, and ensuring the well-being of the people under his authority. The mention of Obadiah in the list of tribal leaders demonstrates David's effective governance and the structure he established throughout Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.19 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ); father of Ishmaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.19에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 이스마야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 다윗 왕 시대에 스불론 지파를 다스리는 자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of David
persons.short: Obadiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.
persons.article: Obadiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants (1Ch.3.21). He was the son of Arnan and the father of Shecaniah. No further details about his life or role are provided in the Bible. His inclusion in the genealogy highlights the importance of family lineage and the continuation of David's dynasty.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.21 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ); son of Hananiah; a brother of Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan and Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.21에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 하나냐의 아들. 블라댜, 여사야, 르바야, 아르난과 스가냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 다윗 왕의 후손으로, 그 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Azel
persons.short: Obadiah was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of King Saul.
persons.article: Obadiah was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin (1Ch.8.38; 9.44). His brothers were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, and Hanan. The mention of Obadiah and his brothers in the genealogy of Saul emphasizes the importance of family records and the preservation of lineage, even for those who were not part of the royal line of David.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.3 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ); son of Izrahiah; a brother of Michael, Joel and Isshiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.3에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 이스라히야의 아들. 미가엘, 요엘과 잇시야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 사울 왕의 후손인 아셀의 여섯 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Izrahiah
persons.short: Obadiah was one of the five sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar.
persons.article: Obadiah was one of the five sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar (1Ch.7.3). His brothers were Michael, Ishiah, Joel, and Ishiah. The sons of Izrahiah were described as mighty men of valor in their generations, indicating their strength and military prowess. No further details about Obadiah's life or role are provided in the Bible. His mention in the genealogy of Issachar highlights the importance of family records and the preservation of tribal heritage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.38 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ); son of Azel; a brother of Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah and Hanan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.38에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 아셀의 아들. 아스리감, 보그루, 이스마엘, 스아랴와 하난의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 잇사갈의 후손인 이스라히야의 다섯 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Gatekeeper, descendant of Jeduthun
persons.short: Obadiah, also known as Abda, was a gatekeeper and descendant of Jeduthun who served in the temple.
persons.article: Obadiah, also known as Abda, was a gatekeeper in the temple during the post-exilic period (1Ch.9.16; Neh.12.25). He was a descendant of Jeduthun, one of the three principal musicians appointed by David (1Ch.16.41-42). Obadiah's duties as a gatekeeper likely included guarding the entrance to the temple, maintaining order, and ensuring that only authorized individuals entered the sacred space. He was also a singer and was involved in the musical aspects of temple worship (Neh.11.17). His service in the temple highlights the importance of the Levitical roles in maintaining the proper functioning of the temple and its worship.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.16 referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ), or Abda (עַבְדָּא); a son of Shemaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.16에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 스마야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜(압다라고도 함)는 여두둔의 후손으로 성전에서 섬긴 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ahab's palace administrator, protected prophets
persons.short: Obadiah was a palace administrator under King Ahab who feared the Lord and protected a hundred prophets during Jezebel's persecution.
persons.article: Obadiah was a palace administrator during the reign of King Ahab of Israel (1Ki.18.3). He was described as a devout believer in the Lord (1Ki.18.3). When Jezebel, Ahab's wife, was killing off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them in two caves, supplying them with food and water (1Ki.18.4). During a severe famine, Ahab sent Obadiah to search for grass to keep the horses and mules alive (1Ki.18.5-6). While on this mission, Obadiah encountered the prophet Elijah and helped arrange a meeting between Elijah and Ahab (1Ki.18.7-16). Obadiah's actions demonstrate his courage and commitment to God, even while serving in a high position under a king who had turned away from the Lord.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.18.3 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.18.3에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 아합 왕의 궁내 대신으로, 여호와를 경외하여 이세벨의 박해 기간 동안 백 명의 선지자를 보호했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent to teach in Judah
persons.short: Obadiah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Obadiah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah (2Ch.17.7). He was one of the Levites sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. This educational mission was part of Jehoshaphat's reforms to strengthen the spiritual life of the nation and ensure that the people were instructed in the ways of the Lord. As a Levite, Obadiah's role in teaching the Law was in line with the Levitical responsibility of instructing the people in matters of faith and religious practice.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.7 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.7에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 오바댜는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite overseer of temple repairs
persons.short: Obadiah was a Levite who served as an overseer during the temple repairs under King Josiah.
persons.article: Obadiah was a Levite who served as an overseer during the repairs of the temple in the reign of King Josiah of Judah (2Ch.34.12). He was one of the Levites appointed to supervise the workmen and ensure that the repairs were carried out according to the king's instructions. The temple had fallen into disrepair during the reigns of previous kings who had turned away from the Lord. Josiah's initiative to restore the temple was a significant step in his reforms to bring Judah back to the worship of the true God. Obadiah's role as an overseer demonstrates the involvement of the Levites in the practical aspects of maintaining the temple and supporting the king's religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.12 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.12에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 오바댜는 요시야 왕 시대에 성전 수리를 감독했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Returnee from Babylon
persons.short: Obadiah was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile with Ezra.
persons.article: Obadiah was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile along with Ezra (Ezr.8.9). He was a descendant of Joab, indicating his lineage from the tribe of Judah. Obadiah was among those who joined Ezra in his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem, which took place during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia. The return led by Ezra aimed to restore the worship and practices of the Jewish faith in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.9 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Jehiel.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림. 여히엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 에스라와 함께 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Signatory to Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Obadiah was one of the leaders who signed the covenant of faithfulness during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Obadiah was one of the leaders who signed the covenant of faithfulness during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.10.5). The covenant was a solemn agreement made by the people of Israel to follow the Law of God and to uphold the practices of their faith. By signing the covenant, Obadiah and the other leaders demonstrated their commitment to God and their willingness to lead the people in obedience to His commands. This event took place after the completion of the walls of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.5 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.5에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜는 느헤미야 시대에 신실함의 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prophet who prophesied against Edom
persons.short: Obadiah was a prophet who delivered a message of judgment against the nation of Edom.
persons.article: Obadiah was a prophet who delivered a message of judgment against the nation of Edom (Oba.1.1). The book of Obadiah, the shortest book in the Old Testament, contains his prophecy. Obadiah's message focused on the pride and cruelty of Edom, a nation descended from Esau, who had mistreated the people of Judah. He foretold the destruction of Edom and the restoration of Israel. The prophecy emphasizes God's justice and sovereignty over the nations. The exact date of Obadiah's ministry is uncertain, but it likely took place sometime after the Babylonian conquest of Judah.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Oba.1.1 only referred to as Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Oba.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '오바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 오바댜는 에돔 민족에 대한 심판의 메시지를 전했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Joktan
persons.short: Obal was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Obal was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah (Gen.10.28; 1Ch.1.22). He is mentioned in the Table of Nations, which lists the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. Obal and his brothers were the ancestors of various Arabian tribes. The exact location and identity of the tribes descended from Obal are uncertain, but they likely settled in the southern regions of the Arabian Peninsula.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.28 referred to as Obal (עוֹבָל), or Obal (עֵיבָל); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.28에 처음 언급되며 '오발'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오발은 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ishmaelite warrior in David's army
persons.short: Obed was an Ishmaelite warrior who fought in David's army.
persons.article: Obed was an Ishmaelite warrior who fought in David's army (1Ch.11.47). He is mentioned among the list of mighty men who supported David, which includes warriors from various backgrounds and regions. As an Ishmaelite, Obed likely descended from Ishmael, Abraham's son. His presence in David's army demonstrates the diversity of support David received during his reign.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.47 only referred to as Obed (עוֹבֵד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.47에 처음 언급되며 '오벳'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오벳은 다윗 군대에서 싸운 이스마엘 사람 용사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah
persons.short: Obed was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.
persons.article: Obed was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel (1Ch.2.37-38). He was the son of Ephlal and the father of Jehu. Obed is mentioned in the genealogy of Jerahmeel, which is part of the larger genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.37 only referred to as Obed (עוֹבֵד); a son of Ephlal; father of Jehu.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.37에 처음 언급되며 '오벳'이라 불림. 에블랄의 아들. 예후의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오벳은 여라므엘 계열을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gatekeeper, son of Shemaiah
persons.short: Obed was a gatekeeper in the temple, the son of Shemaiah.
persons.article: Obed was a gatekeeper in the temple during the time of King David (1Ch.26.7). He was the son of Shemaiah, a Korahite Levite. As a gatekeeper, Obed's responsibilities likely included guarding the entrance to the temple, maintaining order, and ensuring that only authorized individuals entered the sacred space. The mention of Obed in the list of gatekeepers highlights the importance of this role in the temple service.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.7 only referred to as Obed (עוֹבֵד); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Othni, Rephael, Elzabad, Elihu and Semachiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.7에 처음 언급되며 '오벳'이라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 오드니, 르바엘, 엘사밧, 엘리후와 스마갸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오벳은 스마야의 아들이며 성전 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Azariah
persons.short: Obed was the father of Azariah, one of the captains who supported Joash in overthrowing Athaliah.
persons.article: Obed was the father of Azariah, one of the captains who supported Joash in overthrowing Queen Athaliah of Judah (2Ch.23.1). Athaliah had seized the throne and killed many of the royal heirs, but Joash, the rightful heir, was hidden and protected. When Joash was seven years old, the priest Jehoiada and the captains, including Azariah son of Obed, made a covenant to crown Joash as king and remove Athaliah from power. The mention of Obed as Azariah's father suggests that he was a person of some influence and that his family played a role in the political events of the time.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.23.1 only referred to as Obed (עוֹבֵד); father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.23.1에 처음 언급되며 '오벳'이라 불림. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오벳은 여호야다를 도와 아달랴를 폐한 지휘관 중 한 사람인 아사랴의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Boaz and Ruth
persons.short: Obed was the son of Boaz and Ruth, and the grandfather of King David.
persons.article: Obed was the son of Boaz and Ruth, born in Bethlehem (Rut.4.17). His birth was a significant event in the story of Ruth, as it marked the restoration of Naomi's family line and the continuation of the lineage that would eventually lead to King David. Obed was the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David (Rut.4.21-22; 1Ch.2.12; Mat.1.5; Luk.3.32). His name means "servant" or "worshiper," possibly reflecting his family's devotion to God. Obed's life is not detailed in the Bible, but his role in the genealogy of David and ultimately Jesus Christ highlights the importance of his place in God's plan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.4.17 referred to as Obed (עוֹבֵד), or Obed (Ὠβήδ); a son of Boaz and Ruth; father of Jesse.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Rut.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '오벳'이라 불림. 보아스와 룻의 아들. 이새의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오벳은 보아스와 룻의 아들이며 다윗 왕의 할아버지였다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.offspring: Shemaiah@1Ch.26.4-, Jehozabad@1Ch.26.4, Joah@1Ch.26.4, Sachar@1Ch.26.4, Nethanel@1Ch.26.4, Ammiel@1Ch.26.5, Issachar@1Ch.26.5, Peullethai@1Ch.26.5
persons.brief: Gittite who housed the Ark
persons.short: Obed-edom was a Gittite in whose house the Ark of the Covenant stayed for three months, bringing blessings to his household.
persons.article: Obed-edom was a Gittite in whose house the Ark of the Covenant stayed for three months after the death of Uzzah (2Sa.6.10-12; 1Ch.13.13-14). When David attempted to bring the Ark to Jerusalem, Uzzah was struck down by God for touching the Ark. Fearful of further divine judgment, David left the Ark in the house of Obed-edom. During its stay, Obed-edom's household was blessed by God (1Ch.13.14). Later, when David brought the Ark to Jerusalem, Obed-edom and his family were appointed as gatekeepers and musicians in the tabernacle (1Ch.15.18, 21, 24; 16.5, 38). Obed-edom had eight sons, all of whom served in the tabernacle (1Ch.26.4-8). He is also mentioned as a Levite in the context of the temple treasuries (2Ch.25.24). Obed-edom's faithfulness and the blessings he received highlight the importance of reverence for the Ark and the presence of God.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.6.10 referred to as Obed-edom (עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם), or Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); son of Jeduthun; a brother of Mattithiah, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah and Hashabiah; father of Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar and Peullethai.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 노래하는 자. 2Sa.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '오벧에돔'이라 불림. 여두둔의 아들. 맛디디야, 그달리야, 스리, 여사야와 하사뱌의 형제. 스마야, 여호사밧, 요아, 사갈, 느다넬, 암미엘, 잇사갈과 브울래대의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 가드 사람 오벧에돔의 집에는 언약궤가 석 달간 머물며 그 집안에 복을 가져다주었다.
persons.article_ko: 오벧에돔은 가드 사람으로, 웃사가 죽은 후 언약궤가 그의 집에서 석 달간 머물렀다(삼하 6:10-12; 대상 13:13-14). 다윗이 궤를 예루살렘으로 옮기려 했을 때 웃사는 궤를 만진 것 때문에 하나님께 죽임을 당했다. 더 이상의 신적 심판을 두려워한 다윗은 궤를 오벧에돔의 집에 두었다. 그것이 머무는 동안 오벧에돔의 집안은 하나님께 복을 받았다(대상 13:14). 후에 다윗이 궤를 예루살렘으로 가져왔을 때 오벧에돔과 그의 가족은 성막에서 문지기와 음악가로 임명되었다(대상 15:18, 21, 24; 16:5, 38). 오벧에돔에게는 여덟 아들이 있었고, 그들 모두 성막에서 섬겼다(대상 26:4-8). 그는 또한 성전 곳간과 관련하여 레위인으로 언급된다(대하 25:24). 오벧에돔의 신실함과 그가 받은 축복은 궤에 대한 경외와 하나님의 임재의 중요성을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of David's camels
persons.short: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of King David's camels.
persons.article: Obil was an Ishmaelite who served as the overseer of King David's camels (1Ch.27.30). He was one of the officials appointed by David to manage various aspects of his royal holdings. As an Ishmaelite, Obil likely had extensive knowledge of camels, which were important for transportation and trade in the region. His role demonstrates the diversity of David's administration and the king's willingness to employ skilled individuals from various backgrounds.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.30 only referred to as Obil (אוֹבִיל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.30에 처음 언급되며 '오빌'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 이스마엘 사람 오빌은 다윗 왕의 낙타들을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Pagiel
persons.short: Ochran was the father of Pagiel, a leader from the tribe of Asher during the Exodus.
persons.article: Ochran was an Israelite from the tribe of Asher. He was the father of Pagiel, who was chosen as the leader of the tribe during the Exodus (Num.1.13; 2.27). Pagiel represented Asher in the census (Num.1.13, in the arrangement of the tribal camps )(Num.2.27, and in the offerings presented at the dedication of the tabernacle )(Num.7.72, 77). He also led the tribe in the order of march (Num.10.26). Ochran's name is mentioned in connection with his son's leadership role, highlighting the importance of family lineage in the tribal structure of Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.13 only referred to as Ochran (עׇכְרָן); father of Pagiel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.13에 처음 언급되며 '오그란'이라 불림. 바기엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오그란은 출애굽 당시 아셀 지파 지도자 바기엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet, father of Azariah
persons.short: Oded was a prophet and the father of Azariah, who prophesied during the reign of King Asa of Judah.
persons.article: Oded was a prophet who lived during the reign of King Asa of Judah. He was the father of Azariah, another prophet (2Ch.15.1). Azariah, inspired by the Spirit of God, delivered a message to King Asa, encouraging him to seek the Lord and reminding him of the consequences of forsaking God (2Ch.15.1-7). This prophecy prompted Asa to initiate religious reforms in Judah, removing idols and repairing the altar of the Lord (2Ch.15.8). Although Oded himself is not recorded as delivering a prophecy, his role as the father of Azariah suggests that he may have been influential in his son's prophetic ministry.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.15.1 only referred to as Oded (עֹדֵד); father of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.15.1에 처음 언급되며 '오뎃'이라 불림. 아사랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 오뎃은 유다 왕 아사 시대에 예언한 아사랴의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet who confronted victorious Israelite army
persons.short: Oded was a prophet who confronted the Israelite army returning from a victory over Judah, urging them to release their Judean captives.
persons.article: Oded was a prophet from Samaria who lived during the reign of King Pekah of Israel. When the Israelite army returned from a successful campaign against Judah, bringing back 200,000 captives, Oded confronted them (2Ch.28.9-11). He rebuked the army for their intention to enslave their fellow Israelites, reminding them of their own sins against God. Oded warned them of God's fierce wrath if they proceeded with this plan. As a result of his intervention, the Israelite leaders released the captives, provided for their needs, and sent them back to Judah (2Ch.28.12-15). Oded's bold prophecy demonstrates the role of prophets in calling the people to repentance and upholding the principles of justice and compassion.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.28.9 only referred to as Oded (עֹדֵד).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. 2Ch.28.9에 처음 언급되며 '오뎃'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 오뎃은 유다를 이기고 돌아오는 이스라엘 군대에게 유다 포로들을 풀어주라고 촉구했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: King of Bashan, defeated by Israel
persons.short: Og was the Amorite king of Bashan who was defeated by the Israelites during their journey to the Promised Land.
persons.article: Og was the Amorite king of Bashan during the time of the Israelites' journey from Egypt to the Promised Land (Num.21.33; Deu.3.1). He ruled over the region of Bashan, which was known for its fertile land and fortified cities (Deu.3.4-5). Og and his army confronted the Israelites, but God delivered him into the hands of Moses and the Israelites (Num.21.34; Deu.3.3). The Israelites defeated Og, conquered his territory, and allocated it to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh (Num.32.33; Deu.3.12-13; Jos.13.30-31). Og was renowned for his great size, and his iron bedstead was mentioned as a symbol of his stature (Deu.3.11). The defeat of Og was remembered as a significant victory for the Israelites and a testament to God's power and faithfulness (Deu.31.4; Jos.2.10; 9.10; Psalm Jos.135.11; 136.20).
persons.summary: A king of Bashan living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.21.33 only referred to as Og (עוֹג).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.21.33에 처음 언급되며 '옥'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 옥은 바산의 아모리 왕으로, 이스라엘이 약속의 땅으로 가는 여정 중에 그들에게 패했다.
persons.article_ko: 옥은 이스라엘 백성이 애굽에서 약속의 땅으로 가는 여정 당시 바산의 아모리 왕이었다(민 21:33; 신 3:1). 그는 비옥한 땅과 요새화된 성읍들로 알려진 바산 지역을 다스렸다(신 3:4-5). 옥과 그의 군대는 이스라엘 백성을 대적했으나, 하나님은 그를 모세와 이스라엘 백성의 손에 넘기셨다(민 21:34; 신 3:3). 이스라엘 백성은 옥을 물리치고 그의 영토를 정복하여 르우벤, 갓, 므낫세 반 지파에게 분배했다(민 32:33; 신 3:12-13; 수 13:30-31). 옥은 그의 거대한 몸집으로 유명했으며, 그의 철 침상이 그의 체구를 상징하는 것으로 언급된다(신 3:11). 옥의 패배는 이스라엘 백성에게 중요한 승리이자 하나님의 능력과 신실하심의 증거로 기억되었다(신 31:4; 수 2:10; 9:10; 시 135:11; 136:20).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Simeon
persons.short: Ohad was one of the sons of Simeon, as listed in the genealogies.
persons.article: Ohad was one of the sons of Simeon, the second son of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.46.10; Exo.6.15). He is mentioned in the genealogies of Simeon, which were recorded when the Israelites were in Egypt and during the Exodus. No further details about Ohad's life or descendants are provided in the Bible. His name is listed among his brothers as part of the family record, highlighting the importance of genealogies in the Israelite tradition.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.10 only referred to as Ohad (אֹ֫הַד); son of Simeon; a brother of Jemuel, Jamin, Jachin, Zerah and Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '오핫'이라 불림. 시므온과 시므온의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 여무엘, 야민, 야긴, 세라와 사울의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오핫은 족보에 기록된 시므온의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Meshullam@1Ch.3.19, Hananiah@1Ch.3.19-, Shelomith@1Ch.3.19, Hashubah@1Ch.3.20, Berechiah@1Ch.3.20, Hasadiah@1Ch.3.20, Jushab-hesed@1Ch.3.20, Abiud@Mat.1.13
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah
persons.short: Ohel was a descendant of Judah through the line of Zerubbabel.
persons.article: Ohel was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Zerubbabel (1Ch.3.20). Zerubbabel was a prominent figure in the return of the Jews from Babylonian exile and the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem. Ohel is listed among the sons of Zerubbabel, indicating his place in the royal lineage of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.20 only referred to as Ohel (אֹ֫הֶל); son of Zerubbabel; a brother of Meshullam, Hananiah, Shelomith, Hashubah, Berechiah, Hasadiah, Jushab-hesed, Abiud.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.20에 처음 언급되며 '오헬'이라 불림. 스룹바벨의 아들. 므술람, 하나냐, 슬로밋, 하수바, 베레갸, 하사댜, 유삽헤셋과 아비훗의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오헬은 스룹바벨 계열을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Symbolic name for Samaria
persons.short: Oholah was a symbolic name given to Samaria, representing the northern kingdom of Israel in Ezekiel's prophecy.
persons.article: Oholah is a symbolic name used by the prophet Ezekiel to represent Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel (Ezk.23.4). In Ezekiel's allegorical prophecy, Oholah and her sister Oholibah (representing Jerusalem) are portrayed as promiscuous women who engaged in idolatry and sought alliances with foreign nations (Ezk.23.5-44). The name Oholah likely means "her tent," possibly referring to the unauthorized places of worship established in the northern kingdom. Through this allegory, Ezekiel condemns the unfaithfulness of Israel and Judah, highlighting their spiritual adultery and the consequences they would face as a result of their actions.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezk.23.4 only referred to as Oholah (אׇהֳלָה); a sister of Oholibah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Ezk.23.4에 처음 언급되며 '오홀라'라 불림. 오홀리바의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 오홀라는 에스겔의 예언에서 북이스라엘 왕국을 상징하는 사마리아에게 지어진 이름이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Skilled craftsman for the tabernacle
persons.short: Oholiab was a skilled craftsman from the tribe of Dan who was appointed to work on the construction of the tabernacle.
persons.article: Oholiab was a skilled craftsman from the tribe of Dan who was appointed by God to work alongside Bezalel in the construction of the tabernacle (Exo.31.6; 35.34; 36.1-2; 38.23). He was filled with the Spirit of God and given wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship (Exo.35.34). Oholiab and Bezalel were responsible for overseeing the work of the tabernacle and creating the sacred furnishings and garments according to the divine instructions given to Moses (Exo.36.1). Their skillful work was essential in establishing a place of worship for the Israelites during their journey in the wilderness.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.31.6 only referred to as Oholiab (אׇהֳלִיאָב); a son of Ahisamach.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Exo.31.6에 처음 언급되며 '오홀리압'이라 불림. 아히사막의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오홀리압은 단 지파 출신 숙련된 장인으로, 성막 건축 작업을 맡도록 임명되었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Symbolic name for Jerusalem
persons.short: Oholibah was a symbolic name given to Jerusalem, representing the southern kingdom of Judah in Ezekiel's prophecy.
persons.article: Oholibah is a symbolic name used by the prophet Ezekiel to represent Jerusalem, the capital of the southern kingdom of Judah (Ezk.23.4). In Ezekiel's allegorical prophecy, Oholibah and her sister Oholah (representing Samaria) are portrayed as promiscuous women who engaged in idolatry and sought alliances with foreign nations (Ezk.23.11-44). The name Oholibah likely means "my tent is in her," possibly referring to the presence of the temple and God's dwelling place in Jerusalem. Through this allegory, Ezekiel condemns the unfaithfulness of Judah, highlighting their spiritual adultery and the consequences they would face as a result of their actions, including judgment and destruction by the hands of their former lovers (Ezk.23.22-35).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezk.23.4 only referred to as Oholibah (אׇהֳלִיבָה); a sister of Oholah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Ezk.23.4에 처음 언급되며 '오홀리바'라 불림. 오홀라의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 오홀리바는 에스겔의 예언에서 남유다 왕국을 상징하는 예루살렘에게 지어진 이름이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Esau
persons.short: Oholibamah was one of Esau's wives, a descendant of Seir the Horite.
persons.article: Oholibamah was one of the wives of Esau, the son of Isaac and Rebekah (Gen.36.2). She was the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon, both descendants of Seir the Horite (Gen.36.2, 14). Oholibamah bore three sons to Esau: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Gen.36.5, 14, 18). She is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau, which list his wives, descendants, and the chiefs of Edom (Gen.36.18, 41; 1Ch.1.52). As one of Esau's wives, Oholibamah played a role in the establishment of the Edomite nation, which descended from Esau.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.2 only referred to as Oholibamah (אׇהֳלִיבָמָה); a daughter of Anah; wife of Esau; mother of Jeush, Jalam and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.36.2에 처음 언급되며 '오홀리바마'라 불림. 아나의 딸. 디손의 자매. 에서의 아내. 여우스, 얄람과 고라의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 오홀리바마는 에서의 아내 중 한 사람으로, 세일 사람 호리의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer greeted by Paul
persons.short: Olympas was a believer in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.
persons.article: Olympas was a Christian believer who lived in Rome during the time of the apostle Paul. In Paul's letter to the Romans, he sends greetings to Olympas and others, indicating that they were part of the Christian community in Rome (Rom.16.15). The fact that Paul mentions Olympas by name suggests that he was a prominent or well-known member of the church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.15 only referred to as Olympas (Ὀλυμπᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.15에 처음 언급되며 '올름바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 올름바는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 신자였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Teman@Gen.36.11-Job, Zepho@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Amalek@Gen.36.12-, Korah@Gen.36.16
persons.brief: Son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau
persons.short: Omar was a son of Eliphaz and a grandson of Esau, mentioned in the genealogies of Edom.
persons.article: Omar was one of the sons of Eliphaz and a grandson of Esau (Gen.36.11, 15; 1Ch.1.36). He is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau, which list the descendants of Esau and the chiefs of Edom. As a grandson of Esau, Omar was part of the Edomite clan and likely held a position of influence within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.11 only referred to as Omar (אוֹמָר); son of Eliphaz; a brother of Teman, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Amalek and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.11에 처음 언급되며 '오말'이라 불림. 엘리바스와 엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 데만, 스보, 가담, 그나스, 아말렉과 고라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오말은 엘리바스의 아들이며 에서의 손자로, 에돔 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Chief of the tribe of Issachar
persons.short: Omri was the chief of the tribe of Issachar during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Omri was the chief of the tribe of Issachar during the reign of King David (1Ch.27.18). He is mentioned in the list of the leaders of the tribes of Israel who served in David's administration. As the chief of Issachar, Omri would have been responsible for overseeing the affairs of his tribe and representing their interests before the king. The fact that he held this position indicates that he was a respected and influential figure within his tribe.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.18 only referred to as Omri (עׇמְרִי); a son of Michael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.18에 처음 언급되며 '오므리'라 불림. 미가엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오므리는 다윗 왕 시대의 잇사갈 지파 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Zemirah@1Ch.7.8, Joash@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: Descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Omri was a descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.
persons.article: Omri was a descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe (1Ch.7.8). He was the son of Becher, one of Benjamin's sons. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 lists the heads of families and clans within the tribe of Benjamin. Omri's mention in this context suggests that he was a significant figure within his clan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Omri (עׇמְרִי); son of Becher; a brother of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '오므리'라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 스미라, 요아스, 엘리에셀, 에료에내, 여레못, 아비야, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오므리는 베냐민의 후손으로, 그 지파의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah in Jerusalem
persons.short: Omri was a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Omri was a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (1Ch.9.4). He is mentioned in the list of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, which includes people from various tribes who resettled in the city. Omri's mention in this context suggests that he was among the first generation of returnees who helped repopulate Jerusalem and restore the Jewish community there.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.4 only referred to as Omri (עׇמְרִי); a son of Imri; father of Ammihud.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '오므리'라 불림. 이므리의 아들. 암미훗의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오므리는 유다의 후손으로 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel; father of Ahab
persons.short: Omri was the sixth king of Israel who established Samaria as the capital and founded a powerful dynasty.
persons.article: Omri was the sixth king of Israel, who reigned for 12 years (1Ki.16.23). He came to power after a period of political instability and established Samaria as the new capital of Israel (1Ki.16.24). Omri was a powerful ruler who expanded Israel's territory and made alliances with neighboring kingdoms, including Phoenicia through the marriage of his son Ahab to Jezebel (1Ki.16.31). However, Omri did evil in the eyes of the Lord and followed the sins of Jeroboam (1Ki.16.25-26). The dynasty he founded, known as the "house of Omri," became notorious for its wickedness, particularly during the reign of his son Ahab (1Ki.16.30; Mic.6.16). Omri's reign was significant in the history of Israel, as he strengthened the kingdom politically and economically, but also led the nation further into idolatry and disobedience to God.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.16 only referred to as Omri (עׇמְרִי); father of Ahab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.16.16에 처음 언급되며 '오므리'라 불림. 아합의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오므리는 이스라엘의 여섯 번째 왕으로 사마리아를 수도로 세우고 강력한 왕조를 세웠다.
persons.article_ko: 오므리는 이스라엘의 여섯 번째 왕으로 십이 년간 다스렸다(왕상 16:23). 그는 정치적 불안정 시기 이후 권력을 잡았고 사마리아를 이스라엘의 새 수도로 세웠다(왕상 16:24). 오므리는 강력한 통치자로 이스라엘의 영토를 확장하고 그의 아들 아합과 이세벨의 결혼을 통해 페니키아를 포함한 이웃 왕국들과 동맹을 맺었다(왕상 16:31). 그러나 오므리는 여호와 보시기에 악을 행하며 여로보암의 죄를 따랐다(왕상 16:25-26). 그가 세운 왕조인 '오므리 가문'은 특히 그의 아들 아합의 통치 기간 동안 악함으로 악명이 높아졌다(왕상 16:30; 미 6:16). 오므리의 통치는 이스라엘 역사에서 중요했는데, 그는 왕국을 정치적, 경제적으로 강화시켰으나 동시에 그 민족을 우상숭배와 하나님께 대한 불순종으로 더욱 이끌었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Reubenite involved in Korah's rebellion
persons.short: On was a Reubenite who joined Korah in his rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
persons.article: On was a Reubenite who joined Korah, a Levite, in his rebellion against the leadership of Moses and Aaron (Num.16.1). Along with Dathan and Abiram, also Reubenites, On supported Korah's challenge to the divinely appointed authority of Moses and Aaron. The rebellion was motivated by a desire for greater power and influence within the Israelite community. However, God intervened and punished the rebels, causing the earth to open up and swallow them and their households (Num.16.31-33). On's participation in this rebellion highlights the importance of submitting to God-ordained leadership and the consequences of rebelling against it.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.16.1 only referred to as On (אוֹן); a son of Peleth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '온'이라 불림. 벨렛의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 온은 르우벤 사람으로, 모세와 아론을 대적한 고라의 반역에 가담했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah, son of Jerahmeel
persons.short: Onam was a descendant of Judah, the son of Jerahmeel, and had two sons, Shammai and Jada.
persons.article: Onam was a descendant of Judah, the son of Jerahmeel (1Ch.2.26, 28). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which lists the descendants of Judah's sons. Onam was the son of Jerahmeel and had two sons of his own, Shammai and Jada (1Ch.2.28). The genealogy of Judah in 1Chronicles 2 provides insight into the family lines and clans within the tribe of Judah. Onam's mention in this genealogy suggests that he was a significant figure within the Jerahmeelite clan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.26 only referred to as Onam (אוֹנָם); son of Jerahmeel and Atarah; a brother of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah; father of Shammai and Jada.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.26에 처음 언급되며 '오남'이라 불림. 여라므엘과 아다라의 아들. 람, 브나, 오렌, 오셈과 아히야의 형제. 삼매와 야다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오남은 유다의 후손 여라므엘의 아들로, 삼매와 야다 두 아들을 두었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Descendant of Seir the Horite
persons.short: Onam was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Edom.
persons.article: Onam was a descendant of Seir the Horite, a group that inhabited the land of Edom before Esau's descendants (Gen.36.23; 1Ch.1.40). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the Horites, which are recorded in the context of Esau's family history. The Horites were a people group that lived in the region of Seir, which later became known as Edom. Onam's mention in these genealogies suggests that he was a significant figure among the Horites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.23 only referred to as Onam (אוֹנָם); son of Shobal; a brother of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal and Shepho.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.23에 처음 언급되며 '오남'이라 불림. 소발의 아들. 알완, 마나핫, 에발과 스보의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오남은 세일 사람 호리의 후손으로, 에돔 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Judah
persons.short: Onan was the second son of Judah, who was punished by God for his wicked actions.
persons.article: Onan was the second son of Judah and his Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shua (Gen.38.4; 1Ch.2.3). After the death of his older brother Er, Judah instructed Onan to marry Er's widow, Tamar, and produce an heir for his brother (Gen.38.8). However, Onan, knowing that the child would not be his own, practiced coitus interruptus to avoid providing an heir for his brother (Gen.38.9). This act was displeasing to the Lord, and as a result, God put Onan to death (Gen.38.10). Onan's death left Tamar without an heir and set the stage for the unusual events that followed, which ultimately led to the birth of Perez and Zerah, twin sons of Judah and Tamar (Gen.38.27-30). Onan is also mentioned in the genealogies of Judah (Gen.46.12; Num.26.19; 1Ch.2.3).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.38.4 only referred to as Onan (אוֹנָן); son of Judah and Bath-shua ; a brother of Er and Shelah; half-brother of: Perez and Zerah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.38.4에 처음 언급되며 '오난'이라 불림. 유다와 딸의 아들. 엘, 셀라, 베레스와 세라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오난은 유다의 둘째 아들로, 그 악한 행동으로 인해 하나님께 벌을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Runaway slave, convert of Paul
persons.short: Onesimus was a runaway slave who became a Christian through Paul's ministry and was the subject of Paul's letter to Philemon.
persons.article: Onesimus was a slave who belonged to Philemon, a Christian from Colossae (Col.4.9). He ran away from his master and, in some way, came into contact with the apostle Paul while Paul was in prison (Phm.1.10). Through Paul's ministry, Onesimus became a Christian and proved to be a valuable companion and helper to Paul (Phm.1.11-13). Paul sent Onesimus back to Philemon with a personal letter, urging Philemon to receive Onesimus back, not as a slave, but as a beloved brother in Christ (Phm.1.16-17). Paul also offered to pay any debt that Onesimus might owe to Philemon (Phm.1.18-19). The letter to Philemon is a powerful example of Christian love, forgiveness, and the transforming power of the gospel in human relationships. Onesimus is also mentioned as a faithful and beloved brother in Paul's letter to the Colossians (Col.4.9).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Col.4.9 referred to as Onesimus (Ὀνήσιμος).
persons.short_ko: 오네시모는 빌레몬에게서 도망친 종이었으나 바울을 통해 회심하고 다시 주인에게 돌아갔다.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Col.4.9에 처음 언급되며 '오네시모'라 불림.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Friend and supporter of Paul
persons.short: Onesiphorus was a friend of Paul who often refreshed him and was not ashamed of his imprisonment.
persons.article: Onesiphorus was a Christian friend and supporter of the apostle Paul (2Ti.1.16). He is mentioned in Paul's second letter to Timothy as someone who often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains (2Ti.1.16). This suggests that Onesiphorus visited Paul during his imprisonment and provided him with comfort and support. Paul expresses his gratitude for Onesiphorus' kindness and asks the Lord to grant mercy to his household (2Ti.1.16). In the final chapter of the letter, Paul sends greetings to the household of Onesiphorus (2Ti.4.19, indicating that Onesiphorus and his family were well-known to the Christian community). The example of Onesiphorus highlights the importance of supporting and encouraging those who are facing hardship or persecution for their faith.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at 2Ti.1.16 only referred to as Onesiphorus (Ὀνησίφορος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Ti.1.16에 처음 언급되며 '오네시보로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오네시보로는 바울의 친구로, 그를 자주 격려하며 그의 투옥을 부끄러워하지 않았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Joktan
persons.short: Ophir was a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Ophir was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem through Eber (Gen.10.29; 1Ch.1.23). He is mentioned in the Table of Nations, which lists the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. Joktan's descendants, including Ophir, are said to have settled in the region "from Mesha all the way to Sephar, the eastern hill country" (Gen.10.30). The exact location of this region is uncertain, but it is generally believed to be in the southern part of the Arabian Peninsula. The name Ophir is also associated with a land famous for its wealth and gold (e.g., 1Ki.9.28; 10.11; 22.48; 1Ch.29.4; 2Ch.8.18; 9.10; Job.22.24; 28.16; Psalm 45.9; Isa.13.12, but it is unclear if this land was named after Joktan's son or another individual).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.29 only referred to as Ophir (אוֹפִיר); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.29에 처음 언급되며 '오빌'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 우살, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오빌은 셈의 후손 욕단의 아들로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Meonothai
persons.short: Ophrah was the son of Meonothai, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Ophrah was the son of Meonothai, a descendant of Judah through the line of Caleb (1Ch.4.14). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which lists the descendants of Judah's sons and grandsons. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 4 provides insight into the family lines and clans within the tribe of Judah. Ophrah's mention in this genealogy suggests that he was a significant figure within his family or clan. However, no further details about Ophrah's life or role are provided in the Bible. It is worth noting that there are other individuals and places in the Bible that share the name Ophrah, but they are not related to this particular Ophrah, the son of Meonothai.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.14 only referred to as Ophrah (עׇפְרָה); a son of Meonothai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.14에 처음 언급되며 '오브라'라 불림. 므오노대의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오브라는 유다의 후손인 므오노대의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Midianite prince, killed by Ephraimites
persons.short: Oreb was a Midianite prince who was killed by the Ephraimites during the time of Gideon.
persons.article: Oreb was a prince of Midian who, along with another prince named Zeeb, led the Midianite army against Israel during the time of Gideon (Jdg.7.25). After Gideon and his 300 men defeated the Midianites, the Ephraimites captured and killed Oreb and Zeeb (Jdg.7.25; 8.3). The Ephraimites brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon as a trophy of their victory (Jdg.7.25). The rock where Oreb was killed became known as the "rock of Oreb" (Jdg.7.25). The defeat of Oreb and Zeeb was a significant victory for Israel and a testament to God's power and deliverance (Psalm Jdg.83.11). The prophet Isaiah later used the "rock of Oreb" as a symbol of God's judgment against the Assyrians (Isa.10.26).
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.7.25 only referred to as Oreb (עֹרֵב).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '오렙'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오렙은 기드온 시대에 에브라임 사람들에게 죽임을 당한 미디안 방백이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jerahmeel
persons.short: Oren was a son of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Oren was one of the sons of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Judah (1Ch.2.25). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which lists the descendants of Judah's sons and grandsons. Jerahmeel was the son of Hezron, who was the son of Perez, one of Judah's twin sons born to Tamar (1Ch.2.5, 9). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 provides insight into the family lines and clans within the tribe of Judah. Oren's mention in this genealogy suggests that he was a significant figure within the Jerahmeelite clan. However, no further details about Oren's life or role are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.25 only referred to as Oren (אֹ֫רֶן); son of Jerahmeel; a brother of Ram, Bunah, Ozem, Ahijah and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.25에 처음 언급되며 '오렌'이라 불림. 여라므엘과 여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 람, 브나, 오셈, 아히야와 오남의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오렌은 유다의 후손인 여라므엘의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Jebusite, sold threshing floor to David
persons.short: Ornan (Araunah) was a Jebusite who sold his threshing floor to King David, which later became the site of Solomon's temple.
persons.article: Ornan, also known as Araunah, was a Jebusite who owned a threshing floor in Jerusalem during the reign of King David (2Sa.24.16; 1Ch.21.15). After David sinned by taking a census of Israel, God sent a plague that killed 70,000 people (2Sa.24.15; 1Ch.21.14). When the angel of the Lord was about to destroy Jerusalem, God commanded the angel to stop at Ornan's threshing floor (2Sa.24.16; 1Ch.21.15). David was instructed by the prophet Gad to build an altar to the Lord on Ornan's threshing floor (2Sa.24.18; 1Ch.21.18). Ornan offered to give David the threshing floor and the oxen for the sacrifice, but David insisted on paying the full price (2Sa.24.21-24; 1Ch.21.22-25). David purchased the threshing floor and the oxen for 50 shekels of silver (2Sa.24.24 or 600 shekels of gold )(1Ch.21.25). The threshing floor became the site where David built an altar and offered sacrifices to the Lord (2Sa.24.25; 1Ch.21.26). This location later became the site of Solomon's temple (2Ch.3.1).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.24.16 referred to as Ornan (אׇרְנָן), or Araunah or Araunah (אֲרַוְנָה).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.24.16에 처음 언급되며 '오르난'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오르난(아라우나)은 여부스 사람으로, 그의 타작마당을 다윗 왕에게 팔았고 그곳이 후에 솔로몬 성전 터가 되었다.

persons.description: Woman living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Naomi's daughter-in-law, stayed in Moab
persons.short: Orpah was Naomi's daughter-in-law who stayed in Moab after the death of her husband, while Ruth accompanied Naomi to Bethlehem.
persons.article: Orpah was the daughter-in-law of Naomi and the wife of Chilion, one of Naomi's sons (Rut.1.4). She was a Moabite woman who married into a Hebrew family that had settled in Moab due to a famine in Judah (Rut.1.1-2). After the deaths of Naomi's husband and sons, Naomi decided to return to Bethlehem (Rut.1.6-7). Initially, both Orpah and Ruth, Naomi's other daughter-in-law, insisted on accompanying her (Rut.1.10). However, Naomi urged them to return to their own families in Moab (Rut.1.11-13). Orpah eventually agreed to stay in Moab, but Ruth remained steadfast in her commitment to Naomi (Rut.1.14). Orpah's decision to stay in Moab is contrasted with Ruth's loyalty and devotion to Naomi and her God (Rut.1.16-17). While Orpah is not mentioned again in the Bible, her brief appearance in the story of Ruth highlights the significant choice that Ruth made in following Naomi and embracing the God of Israel.
persons.summary: A woman of the Moabites living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.1.4 only referred to as Orpah (עׇרְפָּה); wife of Chilion.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 여성. Rut.1.4에 처음 언급되며 '오르바'라 불림. 기룐의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 오르바는 나오미의 며느리로, 남편이 죽은 후 모압에 남았으며 룻은 나오미와 함께 베들레헴으로 갔다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Assyrian king who settled people in Samaria
persons.short: Osnappar (probably Ashurbanipal) was an Assyrian king who brought people from various regions and settled them in Samaria.
persons.article: Osnappar is mentioned in the Bible as the king who brought people from various regions and settled them in the cities of Samaria (Ezr.4.10). He is not mentioned elsewhere in the Bible, but many scholars identify him as Ashurbanipal, one of the last great kings of the Assyrian Empire. Ashurbanipal ruled from 668 to 627 BC and was known for his military campaigns and his extensive library in Nineveh. The resettlement of people in Samaria was a common practice of the Assyrian kings to prevent rebellions and maintain control over conquered territories. The people who were brought to Samaria came from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim (Ezr.4.9-10). These foreign settlers intermarried with the remaining Israelites in Samaria, creating a mixed population that became known as the Samaritans (2Ki.17.24-41). The Samaritans developed their own religious practices, which combined elements of Israelite and pagan traditions, and were often in conflict with the Jews who returned from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.4.1-5; Neh.4.1-3).
persons.summary: A king of Assyria living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.4.10 only referred to as Osnappar (אָֽסְנַפַּר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 왕. Ezr.4.10에 처음 언급되며 '오스납발'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 오스납발(아마도 앗수르바니팔)은 여러 지역 사람들을 사마리아로 데려와 정착시킨 앗수르 왕이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shemaiah, gatekeeper of the ark
persons.short: Othni was a son of Shemaiah and served as a gatekeeper for the ark of the covenant.
persons.article: Othni was one of the sons of Shemaiah, a Levite from the family of Obed-Edom (1Ch.26.7). He is mentioned in the context of the organization of the gatekeepers who were responsible for guarding the entrances to the temple and the storerooms containing the sacred items. Othni and his brothers were described as capable men with the strength to do their work (1Ch.26.7). They were assigned to serve as gatekeepers for the ark of the covenant, ensuring its security and proper handling. The mention of Othni in this passage highlights the importance of the Levites' roles in maintaining the sacred spaces and objects in the temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.7 only referred to as Othni (עׇתְנִי); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu and Semachiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.7에 처음 언급되며 '오드니'라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 르바엘, 오벳, 엘사밧, 엘리후와 스마갸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 옷니는 스마야의 아들로 언약궤의 문지기로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: First judge of Israel, Caleb's nephew
persons.short: Othniel, Caleb's nephew, was the first judge of Israel who delivered the people from Cushan-Rishathaim.
persons.article: Othniel was the son of Kenaz and the nephew of Caleb, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Jos.15.17; Jdg.1.13; 1Ch.4.13). He is described as the first judge of Israel, who delivered the people from the oppression of Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia (Jdg.3.9-10). Othniel's story begins when Caleb offers his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever captures the city of Debir (also known as Kiriath-Sepher) (Jos.15.16; Jdg.1.12). Othniel successfully takes the city and marries Achsah (Jos.15.17; Jdg.1.13).
