Later, when the Israelites fall into sin and are oppressed by Cushan-Rishathaim, they cry out to the Lord for help (Jdg.3.8-9). God raises up Othniel as a deliverer, and the Spirit of the Lord comes upon him (Jdg.3.10). Othniel goes to war against Cushan-Rishathaim and prevails, bringing peace to the land for forty years until his death (Jdg.3.10-11). Othniel is also mentioned as the leader of the tribe of Judah during the reign of King David (1Ch.27.15).
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.15.17 only referred to as Othniel (עׇתְנִיאֵל); son of Kenaz; a brother of Seraiah; husband of Achsah; father of Hathath and Meonothai(?).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jos.15.17에 처음 언급되며 '옷니엘'이라 불림. 그나스의 아들. 스라야의 형제. 악사의 남편. 하닷과 므오노대의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 갈렙의 조카 옷니엘은 이스라엘의 첫 사사로, 백성을 구산리사다임에게서 구원했다.

persons.description: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Brother of David
persons.short: Ozem was one of David's brothers, a son of Jesse.
persons.article: Ozem was one of the sons of Jesse and a brother of King David (1Ch.2.15). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which lists the descendants of Jesse. Ozem is named as the sixth son of Jesse, with his brothers being Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, and David (1Ch.2.13-15). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 provides insight into the family background of David, Israel's most famous king. However, no further details about Ozem's life or role are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.15 only referred to as Ozem (אֹ֫צֶם); son of Jesse; a brother of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Shimeah, Nethanel, Raddai, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 형제. 1Ch.2.15에 처음 언급되며 '오셈'이라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 아들. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 삼마, 느다넬, 랏대, 엘리후, 스루야와 아비가일의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오셈은 다윗의 형제 중 한 사람으로 이새의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Nephew of Caleb
persons.short: Ozem was a son of Jerahmeel and a nephew of Caleb.
persons.article: Ozem was one of the sons of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Judah (1Ch.2.25). He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, which lists the descendants of Judah's sons and grandsons. Jerahmeel was the son of Hezron, who was the son of Perez, one of Judah's twin sons born to Tamar (1Ch.2.5, 9). As a son of Jerahmeel, Ozem was a nephew of Caleb, another prominent figure in the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.18, 42). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 provides insight into the family lines and clans within the tribe of Judah. Ozem's mention in this genealogy suggests that he was a significant figure within the Jerahmeelite clan. However, no further details about Ozem's life or role are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.25 only referred to as Ozem (אֹ֫צֶם); son of Jerahmeel; a brother of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ahijah and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.25에 처음 언급되며 '오셈'이라 불림. 여라므엘과 여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 람, 브나, 오렌, 아히야와 오남의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 오셈은 여라므엘의 아들이며 갈렙의 조카였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men
persons.short: Paarai the Arbite was one of David's mighty men, known for his military prowess.
persons.article: Paarai the Arbite was one of King David's mighty men, a group of elite warriors known for their military skills and bravery (2Sa.23.35). He is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men, which includes some of the most renowned warriors who fought alongside David during his reign. The epithet "the Arbite" suggests that Paarai was from the city of Arab, although the exact location of this city is unknown. Being included in the list of David's mighty men indicates that Paarai was a skilled fighter and played a significant role in David's military campaigns. However, no further details about Paarai's specific accomplishments or life are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.35 only referred to as Paarai (פַּעֲרַי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.35에 처음 언급되며 '바아래'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아릅 사람 바아래는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람으로 군사적 기량으로 알려졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants
persons.short: Padon was an ancestor of a group of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Padon is mentioned in the lists of the people who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.44; Neh.7.47). He was an ancestor of a group of temple servants, also known as the Nethinim, who were assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. The Nethinim were considered a distinct group among the returnees and were listed separately from the other Israelites. The mention of Padon in these lists suggests that he was a significant figure among the temple servants, possibly a leader or a prominent ancestor. However, no further details about Padon's life or specific role are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.44 only referred to as Padon (פָּדוֹן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.44에 처음 언급되며 '바돈'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바돈은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader of the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Pagiel, son of Ochran, was the leader of the tribe of Asher during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.article: Pagiel, son of Ochran, was the leader of the tribe of Asher during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings (Num.1.13). He is mentioned several times in the book of Numbers as one of the leaders who assisted Moses in the census and organization of the Israelite camp (Num.1.13; 2.27; 7.72, 77; 10.26). In the census, Pagiel was responsible for counting the men of military age in his tribe (Num.1.41). He also brought an offering on behalf of his tribe during the dedication of the tabernacle (Num.7.72, 77). As the leader of Asher, Pagiel would have been responsible for overseeing the affairs of his tribe, settling disputes, and representing their interests before Moses and the other tribal leaders. His presence in the various lists and events in Numbers highlights the importance of the tribal structure and leadership in the organization and governance of the Israelite community during their journey through the wilderness.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.13 only referred to as Pagiel (פַּגְעִיאֵל); a son of Ochran.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.13에 처음 언급되며 '바기엘'이라 불림. 오그란의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 오그란의 아들 바기엘은 광야 시절 아셀 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Group of returnees from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Pahath-moab was a group of people who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile, some of whom married foreign women.
persons.article: Pahath-moab is the name of a group of people who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.6; Neh.7.11). They are mentioned in the lists of the returnees, which suggests that they were a significant group among the exiles who chose to return to their homeland. The name "Pahath-moab" may indicate that they were descendants of Moabites who had been taken captive by the Babylonians or that they had some connection to the land of Moab. Some members of the Pahath-moab group were among those who had married foreign women during the exile, which was a violation of God's law (Ezr.10.30). This led to a crisis in the community, and the people were required to separate from their foreign wives to maintain the purity of the Israelite nation. The presence of the Pahath-moab group in the lists of returnees and in the account of the marriage crisis highlights the challenges faced by the Jewish community as they sought to rebuild their lives and maintain their identity after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.6 only referred to as Pahath-moab (פַּ֫חַת מוֹאָב); father of Jeshua, Joab.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.6에 처음 언급되며 '바핫모압'이라 불림. 예수아와 요압의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 무리로, 그중 일부는 이방인 아내와 결혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Signatory of the covenant
persons.short: Pahath-moab was one of the leaders who signed the covenant of renewal during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Pahath-moab is listed among the leaders who signed the covenant of renewal during the time of Nehemiah (Neh.10.14). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel entered into a covenant to obey God's commandments and to separate themselves from the surrounding nations. The leaders of the people, including Pahath-moab, signed this covenant on behalf of their families and clans, pledging to follow God's law and to support the temple service. The presence of Pahath-moab's name among the signatories indicates that he was a prominent leader within the community and that he represented a significant group of people. This covenant signing was a crucial moment in the history of the Jewish people, as it marked a renewed commitment to God and a determination to maintain their identity as a covenant community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.14 only referred to as Pahath-moab (פַּ֫חַת מוֹאָב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '바핫모압'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압은 느헤미야 시대에 언약 갱신에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repairer of the wall of Jerusalem
persons.short: Pahath-moab was one of the people who repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership.
persons.article: Pahath-moab is mentioned as one of the individuals who participated in the repair of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership (Neh.3.11). He is described as repairing a section of the wall, along with Hashub, the son of Pahath-moab. This suggests that Pahath-moab was not only an individual but also the head of a family or clan that bore his name. The repair of the wall was a significant event in the history of the Jewish people, as it symbolized the restoration of Jerusalem and the renewal of the covenant community after the Babylonian exile. Pahath-moab's participation in this project demonstrates his commitment to the well-being of the community and his willingness to contribute to the rebuilding efforts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.11 only referred to as Pahath-moab (פַּ֫חַת מוֹאָב); father of Hasshub.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.11에 처음 언급되며 '바핫모압'이라 불림. 핫숩의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압은 느헤미야의 지도 아래 예루살렘 성벽의 한 구역을 수리한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Uzai, repaired Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Palal, son of Uzai, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near the Parbar during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Palal, son of Uzai, is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the people who participated in repairing the wall of Jerusalem (Neh.3.25). He was responsible for repairing a section of the wall near the Parbar, which was likely a complex of buildings or a court near the temple. Palal's contribution to the restoration of Jerusalem's wall highlights the importance of community involvement and individual effort in the rebuilding process. The repair of the wall was a significant event in the history of the Jewish people, as it symbolized the restoration of Jerusalem and the renewal of the covenant community after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.25 only referred to as Palal (פָּלָל); a son of Uzai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '발랄'이라 불림. 우새의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 우새의 아들 발랄은 느헤미야 시대에 바르발 근처 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Reuben, ancestor of the Palluites
persons.short: Pallu was a son of Reuben and the ancestor of the Palluite clan within the tribe of Reuben.
persons.article: Pallu was one of the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.46.9; Exo.6.14; 1Ch.5.3). He is mentioned in the genealogies of Reuben, which list the descendants of Reuben and their clans. Pallu's descendants formed the Palluite clan within the tribe of Reuben (Num.26.5, 8). The Palluites were one of the clans that made up the tribe of Reuben during the wilderness wanderings and the settlement of the Promised Land. The mention of Pallu and his descendants in these genealogies highlights the importance of family lineage and tribal identity in the organization and history of the Israelite community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.9 referred to as Pallu (פַּלּוּא), or Palluite (פַּלֻּאִי); son of Reuben; a brother of Hanoch, Hezron and Carmi; father of Eliab.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.9에 처음 언급되며 '발루'라 불림. 르우벤의 아들. 하녹, 헤스론과 갈미의 형제. 엘리압의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 발루는 르우벤의 아들이며 르우벤 지파 발루 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Michal's husband from Gallim
persons.short: Palti (Paltiel), son of Laish, was Michal's husband from Gallim before she was taken back by David.
persons.article: Palti, also known as Paltiel, was the son of Laish from Gallim (1Sa.25.44; 2Sa.3.15). He was married to Michal, the daughter of King Saul and the first wife of David. After David fled from Saul, Saul gave Michal to Palti in marriage (1Sa.25.44). However, when David became king over all Israel, he demanded that Michal be returned to him as part of a political agreement with Abner, the commander of Saul's army (2Sa.3.12-16). Palti was forced to relinquish his wife, and he followed her weeping as far as Bahurim before being sent back by Abner (2Sa.3.16). The story of Palti and Michal highlights the complex political and personal relationships during the transition of power from Saul to David and the challenges faced by individuals caught in the midst of these events.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.25.44 referred to as Palti (פַּלְטִי), or Paltiel (פַּלְטִיאֵל); a son of Laish; husband of Michal.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.25.44에 처음 언급되며 '발디'라 불림. 라이스의 아들. 미갈의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 라이스의 아들 발디(발디엘)는 미갈이 다윗에게 되돌아가기 전 갈림에서 그녀의 남편이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Raphu, spy from Benjamin
persons.short: Palti, son of Raphu, was the spy from the tribe of Benjamin sent to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Palti, son of Raphu, was the representative of the tribe of Benjamin among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num.13.9). The spies were chosen from each of the twelve tribes of Israel to assess the land, its inhabitants, and its resources. After forty days of exploration, the spies returned with their report. While Caleb and Joshua encouraged the people to trust in God and take possession of the land, the other ten spies, including Palti, brought back a discouraging report, emphasizing the strength of the inhabitants and the challenges they faced (Num.13.31-33). As a result, the people rebelled against Moses and refused to enter the land, leading to a forty-year period of wandering in the wilderness. Palti's role as one of the spies highlights the importance of faith and obedience in the face of challenges and the consequences of unbelief and disobedience.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.9 only referred to as Palti (פַּלְטִי); a son of Raphu.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.9에 처음 언급되며 '발디'라 불림. 라부의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 라부의 아들 발디는 모세가 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 베냐민 지파 정탐꾼이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader from Issachar, helped divide Canaan
persons.short: Paltiel, son of Azzan, was the leader from the tribe of Issachar who helped divide the land of Canaan.
persons.article: Paltiel, son of Azzan, was the leader from the tribe of Issachar appointed by Moses to help divide the land of Canaan among the Israelite tribes (Num.34.26). After the conquest of Canaan under Joshua's leadership, the land was to be allocated to the tribes according to their size and needs. Moses, before his death, selected a leader from each tribe to assist Eleazar the priest and Joshua in this task. Paltiel was chosen to represent the tribe of Issachar in this process. His appointment demonstrates the importance of tribal representation and the involvement of leaders from each tribe in the decision-making process. The division of the land was a significant event in the history of Israel, as it marked the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to His people and the establishment of the tribal territories.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.26 only referred to as Paltiel (פַּלְטִיאֵל); a son of Azzan.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.26에 처음 언급되며 '발디엘'이라 불림. 앗산의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 앗산의 아들 발디엘은 가나안 땅 분배를 도운 잇사갈 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Parshandatha@Est.9.7, Dalphon@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9, Vaizatha@Est.9.9
persons.brief: Son of Haman, killed by the Jews
persons.short: Parmashta was one of Haman's ten sons killed by the Jews in Susa during the events of Purim.
persons.article: Parmashta was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews in the book of Esther (Est.9.9). After Haman's plot to destroy the Jews was exposed and he was executed, the king granted the Jews the right to defend themselves against their enemies. On the appointed day, the Jews in Susa, led by Mordecai and Esther, fought against those who sought to harm them. Among those killed were Haman's ten sons, including Parmashta. The deaths of Haman's sons served as a powerful symbol of the complete defeat of the enemies of the Jews and the reversal of Haman's evil plans. The story of Parmashta and his brothers is commemorated during the Jewish festival of Purim, which celebrates the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's plot.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.9.9 only referred to as Parmashta (פַּרְמַשְׁתָּא); son of Haman; a brother of Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.9.9에 처음 언급되며 '바마스다'라 불림. 하만과 세레스의 아들. 바산다다, 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 아리새, 아리대와 왜사다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바르마스다는 부림절 사건 중 유대인들에게 죽임을 당한 하만의 열 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: One of the seven deacons
persons.short: Parmenas was one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to serve as deacons in the early church.
persons.article: Parmenas was one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to serve as deacons in the early church in Jerusalem (Act.6.5). As the number of believers grew, the apostles recognized the need for assistance in the daily distribution of food and care for the widows in the community. They instructed the believers to select seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, to take on this responsibility. Parmenas was among those chosen, along with Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, and Nicolas. The selection of these seven men, including Parmenas, marked an important step in the organization and growth of the early church, as it allowed the apostles to focus on prayer and the ministry of the word while ensuring that the practical needs of the community were met.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.6.5 only referred to as Parmenas (Παρμενᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '바메나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바메나는 사도들이 초대교회 집사로 섬기도록 선택한 일곱 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Elizaphan, leader from Zebulun
persons.short: Parnach was the father of Elizaphan, the leader from the tribe of Zebulun who helped divide the land of Canaan.
persons.article: Parnach is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Elizaphan, the leader from the tribe of Zebulun appointed by Moses to help divide the land of Canaan among the Israelite tribes (Num.34.25). Elizaphan was chosen to represent the tribe of Zebulun in the process of allocating the land to the tribes according to their size and needs. The mention of Parnach as Elizaphan's father highlights the importance of family lineage and the role of the father in the identification and status of individuals in Israelite society.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.25 only referred to as Parnach (פַּרְנָךְ); father of Elizaphan.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.25에 처음 언급되며 '바르낙'이라 불림. 엘사반의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바르낙은 가나안 땅 분배를 도운 스불론 지파 지도자 엘리사반의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Family that returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Parosh was the head of a family that returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile, some of whom married foreign women.
persons.article: Parosh is the name of a family that returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.3; Neh.7.8). The family is mentioned in the lists of the returnees, which suggests that they were a significant group among the exiles who chose to return to their homeland. The return from exile marked a crucial moment in the history of the Jewish people, as it signaled the end of the Babylonian captivity and the beginning of the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple. Some members of the Parosh family were among those who had married foreign women during the exile, which was a violation of God's law (Ezr.10.25). This led to a crisis in the community, and the people were required to separate from their foreign wives to maintain the purity of the Israelite nation. The presence of the Parosh family in the lists of returnees and in the account of the marriage crisis highlights the challenges faced by the Jewish community as they sought to rebuild their lives and maintain their identity after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.3 only referred to as Parosh (פַּרְעֹשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.3에 처음 언급되며 '바로스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바로스는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 한 가문의 우두머리였으며, 그중 일부는 이방인 아내와 결혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader who returned with Zerubbabel
persons.short: Parosh was a leader who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, bringing a group of his descendants.
persons.article: Parosh is mentioned as one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, after the Babylonian exile (Ezr.8.3). He is described as bringing a group of his descendants with him, indicating that he was the head of a family or clan. The return of Parosh and his family, along with other leaders and their families, was part of the second wave of Jewish exiles who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Ezra the scribe. This group of returnees played a significant role in the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple, as well as the spiritual and social renewal of the Jewish community. The mention of Parosh as a leader among the returnees highlights the importance of family and clan leadership in the organization and governance of the Jewish community during this period of restoration.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.3 only referred to as Parosh (פַּרְעֹשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '바로스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바로스는 스룹바벨과 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자로, 그 후손 무리를 데려왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A clan leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Parosh, a clan leader who sealed the covenant of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Parosh was a clan leader in the time of Nehemiah who is listed in Neh.10.14 as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant Nehemiah established. The covenant pledged that the people would obey God's law given through Moses, including regulations about marriage, Sabbath keeping, debt cancellation, and financial support of the temple. Parosh represented his clan in affirming this commitment to follow God's ways.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.14 only referred to as Parosh (פַּרְעֹשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '바로스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바로스는 느헤미야의 언약에 서명한 가문 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A man involved in repairing Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Parosh, a man who made repairs near the house of Pedaiah son of Parosh.
persons.article: Parosh was a man mentioned in Neh.3.25 who made repairs to the wall of Jerusalem. He worked on the section of wall near the house of Pedaiah son of Parosh, which was next to the angle and the tower projecting from the upper palace near the court of the guard.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.25 only referred to as Parosh (פַּרְעֹשׁ); father of Pedaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '바로스'라 불림. 브다야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바로스는 바로스의 아들 브다야의 집 근처를 수리한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Dalphon@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Parmashta@Est.9.9, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9, Vaizatha@Est.9.9
persons.brief: Son of Haman killed by the Jews
persons.short: Parshandatha, one of the ten sons of Haman killed by the Jews.
persons.article: Parshandatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, who was killed when the Jews defended themselves from their enemies, as recorded in Est.9.7. After Haman plotted to destroy the Jews throughout the Persian empire, they were granted permission by King Xerxes to fight back against anyone who attacked them. On the appointed days, the 13th and 14th of the month of Adar, the Jews struck down their enemies, including Parshandatha and his brothers.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.9.7 only referred to as Parshandatha (פַּרְשַׁנְדָּתָא); son of Haman; a brother of Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.9.7에 처음 언급되며 '바산다다'라 불림. 하만과 세레스의 아들. 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새, 아리대와 왜사다의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바산다다는 유대인들에게 죽임을 당한 하만의 열 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: People living in Parthia
persons.brief: People group present at Pentecost
persons.short: Parthians, one of the people groups present in Jerusalem at Pentecost.
persons.article: The Parthians were one of the people groups present in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost when the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples, as recorded in Act.2.9. They heard the disciples miraculously speaking in their own language, testifying to God's mighty works. The Parthians were likely Jews or proselytes originally from the Parthian empire east of the Roman empire, in what is now northeastern Iran and Turkmenistan. Their presence in Jerusalem for the feast of Pentecost reflects the widespread dispersion of the Jewish people in the ancient world.
persons.summary: People living in Parthia, only mentioned at Act.2.9 only referred to as Parthians (Πάρθος).
persons.summary_ko: 바대(파르티아) 사람. Act.2.9에 처음 언급되며 '바대인'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바대인은 오순절 때 예루살렘에 있던 민족 중 하나였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of one of Solomon's district governors
persons.short: Paruah, the father of Jehoshaphat, who was one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
persons.article: Paruah was the father of Jehoshaphat, who served as one of the twelve district governors under King Solomon, according to 1Ki.4.17. Each governor was responsible for providing provisions for the royal household for one month of the year. Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was assigned to the hill country of Ephraim.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.17 only referred to as Paruah (פָּרוּחַ); father of Jehoshaphat.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.17에 처음 언급되며 '바루아'라 불림. 여호사밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바루아는 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 한 사람인 여호사밧의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Japhlet from the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Pasach, a son of Japhlet, who was a descendant of Asher.
persons.article: Pasach was a son of Japhlet according to 1Ch.7.33. Japhlet was a descendant of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Pasach was listed among Japhlet's sons, who also included Bimhal and Ashvath.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.33 only referred to as Pasach (פָּסַךְ); son of Japhlet; a brother of Bimhal and Ashvath.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.7.33에 처음 언급되며 '바삭'이라 불림. 야블렛의 아들. 빔할과 아스왓의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바삭은 아셀의 후손인 야블렛의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Eshton from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Paseah, a son of Eshton, who was from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Paseah was a son of Eshton, as listed in the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.4.12. Eshton was the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah and Tehinnah, who was the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah, a clan within the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.12 only referred to as Paseah (פָּסֵחַ); son of Eshton; a brother of Beth-rapha , Tehinnah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.12에 처음 언급되며 '바세아'라 불림. 에스돈의 아들. 베드라바와 드힌나의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바세아는 유다 지파 에스돈의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from exile
persons.short: Paseah, whose descendants were among the temple servants that returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Paseah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile, according to Ezr.2.49 and Neh.7.51. The temple servants were a group of people assigned to assist the Levites in the work of the temple. Paseah's descendants were among those who returned to Jerusalem and Judah to rebuild the temple and restore worship there after the Babylonian captivity ended in 539 BC.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.49 only referred to as Paseah (פָּסֵחַ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.49에 처음 언급되며 '바세아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바세아의 후손은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 중에 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Joiada, who repaired the Old Gate
persons.short: Paseah the father of Joiada (or 'Jehoiada'), who helped repair the Old Gate of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Paseah was the father of Joiada (or 'Jehoiada'), who worked on repairing the Old Gate during the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem, according to Neh.3.6. Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate, laying its beams and putting its doors and bolts and bars in place. The Old Gate was one of the gates in Jerusalem's wall north of the temple. Paseah is not mentioned apart from being named as Jehoiada's father.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.6 only referred to as Paseah (פָּסֵחַ); father of Joiada.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.6에 처음 언급되며 '바세아'라 불림. 요야다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바세아는 예루살렘 옛 문을 수리하는 것을 도운 요야다(여호야다)의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Head of a priestly family that returned from exile
persons.short: Pashhur, the ancestor of a priestly family that returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Pashhur was the ancestor of a priestly family that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile. In Ezr.2.38 and Neh.7.41, the descendants of Pashhur are listed among the priests who returned to Jerusalem. 1Ch.9.12 mentions Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, as one of the priests who settled in Jerusalem. Neh.11.12 also lists Adaiah the son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, among the priests living in Jerusalem. In Ezr.10.22, descendants of Pashhur are named among those who had married foreign women, which was a violation of the Law. The Pashhur family was one of the important priestly clans in the post-exilic community in Judah.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.12 only referred to as Pashhur (פַּשְׁחוּר); a son of Malchijah; father of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.12에 처음 언급되며 '바스훌'이라 불림. 말기야의 아들. 스가랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바스훌은 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 제사장 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest who opposed Jeremiah and was renamed Magor-missabib
persons.short: Pashhur, a priest who opposed Jeremiah and was renamed Magor-missabib, meaning "terror on every side."
persons.article: Pashhur was a priest, the son of Immer, who opposed the prophet Jeremiah, according to Jeremiah 20. He held the position of chief officer in the temple. When he heard Jeremiah prophesying that Jerusalem would be destroyed, Pashhur had Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks. The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah, the prophet told him that God had renamed him Magor-missabib, which means "terror on every side." Jeremiah prophesied that Pashhur and his friends would go into captivity and die in Babylon as punishment for their false prophecies and leading the people astray.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.20.1 referred to as Pashhur (פַּשְׁחוּר), or Terror on Every Side (מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.20.1에 처음 언급되며 '바스훌'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 바스훌은 예레미야를 대적했으며, 그로 인해 마골밋사빕('사방으로 두려움'이라는 뜻)이라는 이름으로 개명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest sent by Zedekiah to inquire of Jeremiah
persons.short: Pashhur, a priest King Zedekiah sent to inquire of Jeremiah.
persons.article: Pashhur son of Malchiah was a priest during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, according to Jer.21.1 and Jer.38.1. When Jerusalem was under attack by the Babylonians, Zedekiah sent Pashhur and Zephaniah the priest to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord for them, hoping for a miraculous deliverance. Later, Pashhur was among the officials who heard Jeremiah's message that the people should surrender to the Babylonians and urged the king to put Jeremiah to death for demoralizing the people. Pashhur's actions show him to be opposed to Jeremiah's prophetic message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.21.1 only referred to as Pashhur (פַּשְׁחוּר); a son of Malchiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.21.1에 처음 언급되며 '바스훌'이라 불림. 말기야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바스훌은 시드기야 왕이 예레미야에게 여쭙도록 보낸 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Gedaliah, an official who opposed Jeremiah
persons.short: Pashhur, the son of Gedaliah, one of the officials who opposed Jeremiah.
persons.article: Pashhur son of Gedaliah was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah prophesying that the people should surrender to the Babylonians, according to Jer.38.1. Along with other officials, he urged King Zedekiah to put Jeremiah to death for demoralizing the soldiers and the people with his message. This Pashhur is only mentioned in this one verse and is distinct from the priest Pashhur son of Malchiah who is mentioned in the same passage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.38.1a only referred to as Pashhur (פַּשְׁחוּר); father of Gedaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.38.1에 처음 언급되며 '바스훌'이라 불림. 그달리야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 그달랴의 아들 바스훌은 예레미야를 대적한 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Pashhur, one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Pashhur was a priest who was among those who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah, according to Neh.10.3. The covenant was a commitment to follow the Law of God, including regulations about marriage, Sabbath observance, and financial support of the temple. As a priest, Pashhur would have had a significant role in the religious life of the community and in teaching and upholding the Law.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.3 only referred to as Pashhur (פַּשְׁחוּר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '바스훌'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바스훌은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 제사장 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: People from Pathrus(?)
persons.siblings: Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Anamim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch, Casluhim@Gen.10.14-1Ch, Caphtorim@Gen.10.14-1Ch
persons.brief: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
persons.short: Pathrusim, a People from Mizraim, son of Ham, according to <ref="Genesis 10:14">Genesis 10:14</ref>.
persons.article: The Pathrusim were a people group listed among the descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham, in Gen.10.14 and 1Ch.1.12. Mizraim was the ancestor of the Egyptians and other related peoples. The Pathrusim are mentioned only in these genealogical lists and are not referred to elsewhere in the Bible. They were probably inhabitants of the region of Pathros in Upper Egypt, which is mentioned several times in the prophets as a place where Jews had settled (Isa.11.11; Jer.44.1,15; Ezk.29.14; 30.14).
persons.summary: People from Pathrus(?) of the Egyptians, first mentioned at Gen.10.14 only referred to as Pathrusim (פַּתְרֻסִים); descended from Egypt along with Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Casluhim and Caphtorim.
persons.summary_ko: 바드루심. Gen.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '바드루심'이라 불림. 미스라임의 자녀. 루딤, 아나밈, 르하빔, 납두힘, 가슬루힘과 갑도림의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 바드루심은 창세기 10장 14절에 따르면 함의 아들 미스라임에서 나온 민족이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
persons.short: Patrobas, a believer in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.
persons.article: Patrobas was a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in Rom.16.14. He is mentioned along with several others, including Hermes, Hermas, and Philologus, suggesting he was part of the Christian community in Rome. His inclusion in Paul's greetings indicates he was known and appreciated by the apostle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.14 only referred to as Patrobas (Πατροβᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.14에 처음 언급되며 '바드로바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바드로바는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 신자였다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Apostle to the Gentiles, author of many NT epistles
persons.short: Paul, also known as Saul, the apostle to the Gentiles and author of many New Testament epistles.
persons.article: Paul, also known as Saul, was one of the most influential figures in early Christianity. He was born in Tarsus as a Roman citizen and trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel. Initially a persecutor of the church, Paul had a dramatic conversion experience on the road to Damascus, where the risen Jesus appeared to him. After this, he became a zealous preacher of the gospel, undertaking several missionary journeys throughout the Mediterranean world. Paul played a key role in spreading Christianity among the Gentiles and in articulating its theological foundations. He wrote many of the epistles in the New Testament, providing guidance and instruction to the early churches. Paul faced numerous challenges, including opposition from Jewish leaders, internal disputes among believers, and physical hardships. He was eventually arrested and taken to Rome, where tradition holds that he was martyred during the reign of Nero. Paul's life and teachings had a profound impact on the development of Christian thought and practice.
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.7.58 referred to as Paul, Paul (Παῦλος), or Saul (Σαούλ), or Saul (Σαῦλος), or Saul (Σαῦλος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Act.7.58에 처음 언급되며 '바울'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 바울(사울이라고도 함)은 이방인의 사도이며 신약성경의 많은 서신서를 저술했다.
persons.article_ko: 바울(사울이라고도 함)은 초대 그리스도교에서 가장 영향력 있는 인물 중 한 사람이었다. 그는 다소에서 로마 시민으로 태어났으며 가말리엘 문하에서 바리새인으로 훈련받았다. 처음에는 교회를 박해하는 자였던 바울은 다메섹 도상에서 극적인 회심을 경험했는데, 그곳에서 부활하신 예수님이 그에게 나타나셨다. 그 후 그는 복음을 열정적으로 전하는 자가 되어 지중해 세계 전역을 여러 번 선교여행 했다. 바울은 이방인들 사이에 그리스도교를 전파하고 그 신학적 기초를 정립하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다. 그는 신약의 많은 서신서를 저술하여 초대교회들에게 지침과 가르침을 제공했다. 바울은 유대 지도자들의 반대, 신자들 사이의 내부 분쟁, 육체적 고난 등 수많은 어려움에 직면했다. 결국 그는 체포되어 로마로 압송되었고, 전승에 따르면 네로 통치 기간에 순교했다. 바울의 삶과 가르침은 그리스도교 사상과 실천의 발전에 지대한 영향을 미쳤다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Leader from Naphtali appointed to divide Canaan
persons.short: Pedahel, son of Ammihud, the leader from Naphtali appointed to help divide Canaan.
persons.article: Pedahel son of Ammihud was the leader from the tribe of Naphtali appointed to help divide the land of Canaan among the Israelites, according to Num.34.28. He was one of the twelve leaders, one from each tribe, chosen to assist Eleazar the priest and Joshua in allocating the tribal territories after the conquest of Canaan. Pedahel's inclusion in this group suggests he was a respected leader within his tribe.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.28 only referred to as Pedahel (פְּדַהְאֵל); a son of Ammihud.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.28에 처음 언급되며 '브다헬'이라 불림. 암미훗의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗의 아들 브다헬은 가나안 땅 분배를 돕도록 임명된 납달리 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Gamaliel, leader from Manasseh
persons.short: Pedahzur, father of Gamaliel, the leader from the tribe of Manasseh during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.article: Pedahzur was the father of Gamaliel, who was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during Israel's wilderness wanderings. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was counted as the leader of Manasseh (Num.1.10; 2.20). When the Israelites made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle, Gamaliel brought his tribe's offering on the eighth day (Num.7.54,59). Gamaliel also led the tribe of Manasseh when the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai (Num.10.23). Pedahzur is only mentioned in reference to his son's leadership role.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.1.10 only referred to as Pedahzur (פְּדָהצוּר); father of Gamaliel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '브다술'이라 불림. 가말리엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브다술은 광야 시절 므낫세 지파 지도자 가말리엘의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Pedaiah, son of Parosh, an officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in King David's administration.
persons.article: Pedaiah son of Parosh was an officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in King David's administration, according to 1Ch.27.20. He was one of the twelve officers, each representing a tribe or half-tribe, who were responsible for providing resources for the king's household. Each officer was in charge of supplying provisions for one month of the year. Pedaiah's role suggests he was a trusted leader within his tribe and had organizational and administrative skills.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.20 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ); father of Joel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.20에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림. 요엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바로스의 아들 브다야는 다윗 왕 행정부에서 므낫세 반 지파를 관리하는 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of King Jehoiachin of Judah
persons.short: Pedaiah, a descendant of King Jehoiachin of Judah born during the Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Pedaiah was a descendant of King Jehoiachin (also known as Jeconiah) of Judah, according to 1Ch.3.18-19. He was born during the Babylonian captivity after Jehoiachin was deposed and exiled by Nebuchadnezzar. Pedaiah's brothers included Shealtiel, Malchiram, and Shenazzar. Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel, who led the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem. However, 1Ch.3.19 also lists Zerubbabel as the son of Pedaiah, suggesting that Pedaiah may have been Zerubbabel's legal father, possibly due to a levirate marriage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.3.18 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ); son of Shealtiel(?); a brother of Malchiram, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah; father of Zerubbabel and Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.18에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림. 스알디엘의 아들. 말기람, 세낫살, 여가먀, 호사마와 느다뱌의 형제. 스룹바벨과 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브다야는 바벨론 포로 기간 동안 태어난 유다 왕 여호야긴의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Zebidah, mother of King Jehoiakim
persons.short: Pedaiah, father of Zebidah, who was the mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah.
persons.article: Pedaiah was the father of Zebidah, who was the mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah, according to 2Ki.23.36. Zebidah was from Rumah, but no other details are given about Pedaiah. Jehoiakim was placed on the throne by Pharaoh Necho of Egypt after he deposed Jehoiakim's younger brother Jehoahaz. Jehoiakim's reign was characterized by political turmoil, as Judah came under the domination of Egypt and then Babylon. The brief mention of Pedaiah provides some genealogical background for Jehoiakim.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.23.36 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ); father of Zebidah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.23.36에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림. 스비다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브다야는 유다 왕 여호야김의 어머니 스비다의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Pedaiah, a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Pedaiah was a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, according to Neh.11.7. He is mentioned in a list of people from various tribes who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile. The resettlement of Jerusalem was an important step in the restoration of Jewish life and worship in the post-exilic period. Pedaiah's inclusion in this list suggests he was part of the initial group that returned to establish a presence in the city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.7 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ); a son of Kolaiah; father of Joed.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.7에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림. 골라야의 아들. 요엣의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브다야는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착한 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite appointed as a treasurer by Nehemiah
persons.short: Pedaiah, a Levite Nehemiah appointed as a treasurer over the storehouses.
persons.article: Pedaiah was a Levite whom Nehemiah appointed as one of the treasurers over the storehouses, according to Neh.13.13. After discovering that the Levites had not been receiving their portions, Nehemiah appointed reliable men, including Pedaiah, to oversee the distribution of tithes and offerings to the Levites. This appointment suggests that Pedaiah was known for his integrity and trustworthiness. His role as a treasurer involved ensuring that the Levites received their due support for their service in the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.13.13 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 브다야는 느헤미야가 곳간의 재무관으로 임명했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of a man who repaired Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Pedaiah, father of a man who made repairs to the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Pedaiah was the father of a man who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah, according to Neh.3.25. The text mentions "the house of Pedaiah son of Parosh" as a reference point for the section of wall being repaired by Pedaiah's unnamed son. This suggests that Pedaiah's family had a significant presence in Jerusalem and may have been involved in the restoration efforts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.25 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ); a son of Parosh.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림. 바로스의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 브다야는 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽을 수리한 사람의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
persons.short: Pedaiah, a Levite who stood with Ezra when he read the Law to the people.
persons.article: Pedaiah was a Levite who assisted Ezra when he read the Law to the people in Jerusalem, according to Neh.8.4. After the completion of the wall, the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate to hear Ezra read from the Book of the Law. Ezra stood on a high wooden platform along with several others, including Pedaiah. The presence of Levites like Pedaiah suggests that they had a role in teaching and interpreting the Law to the people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Pedaiah (פְּדָיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '브다야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 브다야는 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 낭독할 때 그 곁에 섰다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel who reigned for 20 years
persons.short: Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel who reigned for 20 years.
persons.article: Pekah son of Remaliah was the king of Israel for 20 years, according to 2Kings 15. He came to power by conspiring against and assassinating King Pekahiah. During his reign, Pekah allied with Rezin king of Aram to attack Judah, but they were unsuccessful in capturing Jerusalem (2Ki.16.5; Isa.7.1). However, Pekah did inflict heavy casualties on Judah, killing 120,000 in one day (2Ch.28.6). Pekah's reign ended when Hoshea conspired against him, killed him, and succeeded him as king. Pekah's reign was marked by political instability and conflict with Judah.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.25 only referred to as Pekah (פֶּ֫קַח); a son of Remaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.25에 처음 언급되며 '베가'라 불림. 르말랴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 르말랴의 아들 베가는 이스라엘 왕으로 이십 년간 다스렸다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Israel who reigned for 2 years
persons.short: Pekahiah, son of Menahem, king of Israel who reigned for 2 years before being assassinated.
persons.article: Pekahiah son of Menahem was king of Israel for 2 years, according to 2Ki.15.22-23. He succeeded his father Menahem but continued in his father's sinful ways. Pekahiah's reign was cut short when his officer Pekah son of Remaliah conspired against him and assassinated him in the citadel of the king's palace in Samaria (2Ki.15.25). Pekah then became king in his place. Pekahiah's short reign reflects the political instability and moral decline of the northern kingdom of Israel.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.22 only referred to as Pekahiah (פְּקַחְיָה); a son of Menahem.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.22에 처음 언급되며 '브가히야'라 불림. 므나헴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 므나헴의 아들 브가히야는 이스라엘 왕으로 이 년간 다스리다가 암살당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Hodaviah@1Ch.3.24, Eliashib@1Ch.3.24, Akkub@1Ch.3.24, Johanan@1Ch.3.24, Delaiah@1Ch.3.24, Anani@1Ch.3.24
persons.brief: Descendant of King David
persons.short: Pelaiah, a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 3.
persons.article: Pelaiah is mentioned in the genealogy of King David's descendants in 1Ch.3.24. He is listed as one of the six sons of Elioenai, who was a descendant of David through the line of Solomon and Jehoiachin. This genealogy traces David's lineage after the Babylonian exile, suggesting that Pelaiah lived in the post-exilic period. However, no other details are provided about Pelaiah's life or role. His inclusion in the genealogy may serve to demonstrate the continuation of David's line even after the exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.24 only referred to as Pelaiah (פְּלָיָה); son of Elioenai; a brother of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.24에 처음 언급되며 '블라야'라 불림. 에료에내의 아들. 호다위야, 엘리아십, 악굽, 요하난, 들라야와 아나니의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 블라야는 다윗 왕의 후손으로, 역대상 3장 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who helped explain the Law and signed the covenant
persons.short: Pelaiah, a Levite who helped explain the Law to the people and signed Nehemiah's covenant.
persons.article: Pelaiah was a Levite who played a role in the religious reforms of Ezra and Nehemiah. In Neh.8.7, he is listed among the Levites who helped the people understand the Law as Ezra read it. They explained the meaning of the readings, suggesting that Pelaiah had knowledge and teaching skills. Later, in Neh.10.10, Pelaiah is among the Levites who signed the covenant Nehemiah established. This covenant committed the people to follow God's Law and support the temple. Pelaiah's involvement in both teaching and signing the covenant indicates he was an active participant in the spiritual renewal of the post-exilic community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.8.7 only referred to as Pelaiah (פְּלָאיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '블라야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 블라야는 백성에게 율법을 설명하는 것을 돕고 느헤미야의 언약에 서명했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Pelaliah, a priest who lived in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Pelaliah was a priest who resided in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah, according to Neh.11.12. He was the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah. This lineage indicates that Pelaliah belonged to a priestly family. As a priest living in Jerusalem, he would have had duties related to the temple service and worship.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.12 only referred to as Pelaliah (פְּלַלְיָה); a son of Amzi; father of Jeroham.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. Neh.11.12에 처음 언급되며 '블라야'라 불림. 암시의 아들. 여로함의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 블라야는 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘에 거주한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of King Solomon
persons.short: Pelatiah, a descendant of King Solomon mentioned in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 3.
persons.article: Pelatiah is listed in the genealogy of King Solomon's descendants in 1Ch.3.21. He is mentioned as one of the sons of Hananiah, along with his brother Jeshaiah. Hananiah was a descendant of Solomon through the line of King Jehoiachin. This genealogy traces the royal line of Judah after the Babylonian exile, suggesting that Pelatiah lived in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.21 only referred to as Pelatiah (פְּלַטְיָ֫הוּ); son of Hananiah; a brother of Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah and Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.21에 처음 언급되며 '블라댜'라 불림. 하나냐의 아들. 여사야, 르바야, 아르난, 오바댜와 스가냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 블라댜는 솔로몬 왕의 후손으로, 역대상 3장 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite leader who attacked the Amalekites
persons.short: Pelatiah, a Simeonite leader who joined in an attack against the Amalekites.
persons.article: Pelatiah was one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon who participated in an attack against the Amalekites, according to 1Ch.4.42. Along with his fellow leaders Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, Pelatiah led a group of 500 Simeonites to Mount Seir. There they attacked and destroyed the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped earlier defeats. This event likely took place after the Babylonian exile, as the Simeonites sought to reclaim their territory. Pelatiah's leadership role suggests he was a capable warrior and commander.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.42 only referred to as Pelatiah (פְּלַטְיָ֫הוּ); son of Ishi; a brother of Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.42에 처음 언급되며 '블라댜'라 불림. 이시의 아들. 느아랴, 르바야와 웃시엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 블라댜는 아말렉 사람들을 공격하는 데 가담한 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Prince of Israel whom Ezekiel saw in a vision
persons.short: Pelatiah, a prince of Israel whom Ezekiel saw in a vision, and who died as Ezekiel prophesied.
persons.article: Pelatiah son of Benaiah was one of the twenty-five princes of Israel whom the prophet Ezekiel saw in a vision, according to Ezk.11.1. These princes were described as wicked men who gave evil advice in the city. As Ezekiel was prophesying, he saw Pelatiah die, causing him to fall on his face and cry out to God, asking if He would destroy the remnant of Israel (Ezk.11.13). Pelatiah's death in the vision served as a sign of the judgment that would come upon the leaders who had led the people astray. The vision emphasizes the responsibility of leaders and the consequences of their actions.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezk.11.1 only referred to as Pelatiah (פְּלַטְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Benaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezk.11.1에 처음 언급되며 '블라댜'라 불림. 브나야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 블라댜는 에스겔이 환상 중에 본 이스라엘의 방백으로, 에스겔이 예언한 대로 죽었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who signed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Pelatiah, a priest who signed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Pelatiah was one of the priests who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah, according to Neh.10.22. The covenant was a commitment by the people to follow God's law and support the temple service. As a priest, Pelatiah would have had a significant role in the religious life of the community. His signing of the covenant indicates his support for the spiritual reforms and his dedication to upholding the law.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.22 only referred to as Pelatiah (פְּלַטְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.22에 처음 언급되며 '블라댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 블라댜는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Descendant of Shem, ancestor of Abraham
persons.short: Peleg, a descendant of Shem and ancestor of Abraham, during whose time the earth was divided.
persons.article: Peleg was a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah, and an ancestor of Abraham, according to the genealogies in Gen.10.25, 11:16-19, and 1Ch.1.19,25. He was the son of Eber and the brother of Joktan. Peleg lived 239 years and became the father of Reu at the age of 30. The name Peleg means "division," and Gen.10.25 states that in his days the earth was divided. This event is not described in detail, but it may refer to the division of languages and peoples described in the Tower of Babel story (Gen.11.1-9). Peleg is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in Luk.3.35, emphasizing his role in the ancestral line of the Messiah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.25 referred to as Peleg (פֶּ֫לֶג), or Peleg (Φάλεκ); son of Eber; a brother of Joktan; father of Reu.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.25에 처음 언급되며 '벨렉'이라 불림. 에벨의 아들. 욕단의 형제. 르우의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 벨렉은 셈의 후손이며 아브라함의 조상으로, 그의 시대에 땅이 나뉘었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
persons.short: Pelet, a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag, along with his brother Berachah.
persons.article: Pelet was a Benjamite warrior who, along with his brother Berachah, joined David at Ziklag, according to 1Ch.12.3. They were among the mighty warriors who helped David in battle and were known for their skill with the bow. The brothers were sons of Azmaveth, suggesting they came from a family of warriors. Their support of David likely came during the time when he was fleeing from King Saul and gathering a loyal following. The mention of Pelet and his brother highlights the diverse group of warriors who supported David and helped him establish his kingdom.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.3 only referred to as Pelet (פֶּ֫לֶט); son of Azmaveth; a brother of Jeziel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '벨렛'이라 불림. 아스마의 아들. 여시엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 벨렛은 베냐민 용사로, 형제 브라가와 함께 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch(?), Jesher@1Ch.2.18(?), Shobab@1Ch.2.18(?), Ardon@1Ch.2.18(?), Mesha@1Ch.2.42(?), Haran@1Ch.2.46(?), Moza@1Ch.2.46(?), Gazez@1Ch.2.46a(?), Sheber@1Ch.2.48(?), Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48(?), Shaaph@1Ch.2.49(?), Sheva@1Ch.2.49(?), Achsah@1Ch.2.49(?)
persons.brief: Son of Jahdai, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Pelet, a son of Jahdai, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1Chronicles 2.
persons.article: Pelet was a son of Jahdai, according to the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.2.47. He is listed among the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron. No other information is provided about Pelet's life or role. His mention in the genealogy suggests that he was part of the tribe of Judah and lived during the period of Israel's settlement in Canaan or the early monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.47 only referred to as Pelet (פֶּ֫לֶט); son of Caleb and Jahdai; a brother of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Ephah, Shaaph, Hur(?), Jesher(?), Shobab(?), Ardon(?), Mesha(?), Haran(?), Moza(?), Gazez(?), Sheber(?), Tirhanah(?), Shaaph(?), Sheva(?) and Achsah(?).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '벨렛'이라 불림. 갈렙과 야대의 아들. 레겜, 요담, 게산, 에바, 사압, 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 벨렛은 야대의 아들로, 역대상 2장 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jonathan, descendant of Jerahmeel
persons.short: Peleth, a son of Jonathan and descendant of Jerahmeel, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Peleth was a son of Jonathan and a descendant of Jerahmeel, according to the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.2.33. Jerahmeel was the firstborn son of Hezron, who was a grandson of Judah. Peleth is listed along with his brother Zaza as sons of Jonathan. No further details are provided about Peleth's life or role. His inclusion in the genealogy indicates he was part of the tribe of Judah and lived during the period of Israel's settlement in Canaan or the early monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.33 only referred to as Peleth (פֶּ֫לֶת); son of Jonathan; a brother of Zaza.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.33에 처음 언급되며 '벨렛'이라 불림. 요나단의 아들. 사사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 벨렛은 요나단의 아들이며 여라므엘의 후손으로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Reubenite, father of On who rebelled against Moses
persons.short: Peleth, a Reubenite; father of On who joined Korah's rebellion against Moses.
persons.article: Peleth was a Reubenite, the father of On, who was involved in Korah's rebellion against Moses, according to Num.16.1. Korah, a Levite, led a group of 250 leaders in challenging the authority of Moses and Aaron. On son of Peleth was one of the rebels, along with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab. However, On is not mentioned again in the story, and some scholars suggest he may have withdrawn from the rebellion. The rebellion was a serious challenge to Moses' leadership and resulted in God's judgment on the rebels. Peleth's mention as On's father highlights the involvement of Reubenites in this significant event.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.16.1 only referred to as Peleth (פֶּ֫לֶת); father of On.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '벨렛'이라 불림. 온의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 벨렛은 르우벤 사람으로, 모세를 대적한 고라의 반역에 가담한 온의 아버지였다.

persons.description: People from Pelath(?)
persons.brief: Elite military unit loyal to King David
persons.short: The Pelethites, along with the Cherethites, were an elite military unit loyal to King David.
persons.article: The Pelethites were an elite military unit that served as part of King David's personal guard and army, often mentioned alongside the Cherethites (2Sa.8.18; 15.18; 20.7,23; 1Ki.1.38,44; 1Ch.18.17). They were known for their loyalty to David and played a significant role in supporting him during his reign. The Pelethites and Cherethites were likely foreign mercenaries, possibly of Philistine origin, who had pledged their allegiance to David. They were involved in key events, such as helping David quell Absalom's rebellion (2Sa.15.18 and supporting Solomon's claim to the throne )(1Ki.1.38,44). The presence of these elite warriors demonstrates David's military strength and the diversity of his army.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Pelath(?), first mentioned at 2Sa.8.18 only referred to as Pelethites (פְּלֵתִי).
persons.summary_ko: 블렛 사람. 2Sa.8.18에 처음 언급되며 '블렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 블렛 사람들은 그렛 사람들과 함께 다윗 왕에게 충성스러운 정예 군대였다.

persons.description: Warriors from or of Pelon or Palet(?)
persons.brief: Designation for two of David's mighty warriors
persons.short: Pelonite or Paltite, a designation for two of David's mighty warriors, Helez and Ahijah.
persons.article: Pelonite or Paltite is a designation used for two of David's mighty warriors. Helez the Pelonite (also called the Paltite) is mentioned in 1Ch.11.27 and 1Ch.27.10 as one of David's thirty mighty warriors and the leader of the seventh division of David's army, which served in the seventh month. Ahijah the Pelonite is mentioned in 1Ch.11.36 as another of David's mighty warriors. The term Pelonite or Paltite likely refers to their place of origin or clan affiliation, though the exact location is uncertain. The inclusion of these warriors in the lists of David's mighty men highlights their exceptional military skills and their loyalty to the king.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Pelon or Palet(?), first mentioned at 2Sa.23.26 referred to as Pelonites (פְּלוֹנִי), or Paltite (פַּלְטִי).
persons.summary_ko: 벨론 또는 발렛 출신 용사들(추정). 2Sa.23.26에 처음 언급되며 '블론'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 블로니(발디라고도 함)는 다윗의 용사 헬레스와 아히야 두 사람을 가리키는 호칭이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Elkanah's wife, rival of Hannah
persons.short: Peninnah, one of Elkanah's two wives and the rival of Hannah, Samuel's mother.
persons.article: Peninnah was one of the two wives of Elkanah, an Ephraimite man, and the rival of Hannah, according to 1Sa.1.2. Peninnah had children, while Hannah was initially barren. Elkanah would give portions of the sacrificial meat to Peninnah and her children, but he would give a double portion to Hannah because he loved her (1Sa.1.4-5). Peninnah would provoke and irritate Hannah because of her barrenness, causing Hannah great distress (1Sa.1.6-7). This rivalry between the two wives highlights the challenges of polygamy and the importance of children in ancient Israelite society. Peninnah's actions also serve as a contrast to Hannah's faith and prayerful response to her situation.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.1.2 only referred to as Peninnah (פְּנִנָּה); wife of Elkanah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Sa.1.2에 처음 언급되며 '브닌나'라 불림. 엘가나의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 브닌나는 엘가나의 두 아내 중 한 사람으로, 사무엘의 어머니 한나의 경쟁자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch, Shobal@1Ch.2.50-, Salma@1Ch.2.51-, Hareph@1Ch.2.51, Jezreel@1Ch.4.3, Ishma@1Ch.4.3, Idbash@1Ch.4.3, Hazzelelponi@1Ch.4.3, Ezer@1Ch.4.4
persons.brief: Son of Hur, descendant of Judah
persons.short: Penuel, a son of Hur and descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 4.
persons.article: Penuel was a son of Hur, according to the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.4.4. He is listed as one of the descendants of Hur, who was the firstborn of Ephrathah. No other details are provided about Penuel's life or role. His mention in the genealogy suggests that he was part of the tribe of Judah and lived during the period of Israel's settlement in Canaan or the early monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.4 only referred to as Penuel (פְּנוּאֵל); son of Hur; a brother of Uri, Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Jezreel, Ishma, Idbash, Hazzelelponi and Ezer; a founder of Gedor.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.4.4에 처음 언급되며 '브누엘'이라 불림. 훌의 아들. 우리, 소발, 살마, 하렙, 이스르엘, 이스마, 잇바스, 하술렐보니와 에셀의 형제. 그돌의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 브누엘은 훌의 아들이며 유다의 후손으로, 역대상 4장 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ishpan@1Ch.8.22, Eber@1Ch.8.22, Eliel@1Ch.8.22, Abdon@1Ch.8.23, Zichri@1Ch.8.23, Hanan@1Ch.8.23, Hananiah@1Ch.8.24, Elam@1Ch.8.24, Anthothijah@1Ch.8.24, Iphdeiah@1Ch.8.25
persons.brief: Son of Shashak, descendant of Benjamin
persons.short: Penuel, a son of Shashak and descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 8.
persons.article: Penuel was a son of Shashak, according to the genealogy of Benjamin in 1Ch.8.25. He is listed among the descendants of Jeroham, who was a descendant of Benjamin through his son Bela. No further information is given about Penuel's life or role. His inclusion in the genealogy indicates that he was part of the tribe of Benjamin and lived during the period of Israel's settlement in Canaan or the early monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.25 only referred to as Penuel (פְּנוּאֵל); son of Shashak; a brother of Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah and Iphdeiah; founder of Gedor.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.25에 처음 언급되며 '브누엘'이라 불림. 사삭의 아들. 이스반, 에벨, 엘리엘, 압돈, 시그리, 하난, 하나냐, 엘람, 안도디야와 이브드야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 브누엘은 사삭의 아들이며 베냐민의 후손으로, 역대상 8장 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Machir, grandson of Manasseh
persons.short: Peresh, a son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, mentioned in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 7.
persons.article: Peresh was a son of Machir, according to the genealogy of Manasseh in 1Ch.7.16. Machir was the son of Manasseh, who was one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Israel). Peresh is mentioned alongside his brother Sheresh. No other details are provided about Peresh's life or role. His inclusion in the genealogy suggests that he was part of the tribe of Manasseh and lived during the period of Israel's settlement in Canaan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.16 only referred to as Peresh (פֶּ֫רֶשׁ); son of Machir and Maacah; a brother of Gilead, Sheresh and Hammolecheth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.16에 처음 언급되며 '베레스'라 불림. 마길과 마아가의 아들. 길르앗, 마길의 딸(이름 미상), 세레스와 함몰레겟의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 베레스는 마길의 아들이며 므낫세의 손자로, 역대상 7장 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Judah, ancestor of David and Jesus
persons.short: Perez, son of Judah and Tamar, was an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Perez was the son of Judah and Tamar, born in unusual circumstances described in Genesis 38. He was the twin brother of Zerah and was named Perez (meaning "breach" or "breaking forth") because he broke out first during the delivery (Gen.38.29). Perez became the ancestor of a prominent clan within the tribe of Judah (Num.26.20-21). He is mentioned in the genealogy of King David (Rut.4.12,18; 1Ch.2.4-5 and is an ancestor of several notable figures, including Hezron, Caleb, and Nahshon )(1Ch.2.5,9,10). The descendants of Perez were among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.4,6). Most significantly, Perez is listed in the genealogies of Jesus Christ in both Mat.1.3 and Luk.3.33, highlighting his important role in the lineage of the Messiah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.38.29 referred to as Perez (פֶּ֫רֶץ), or Perezite (פַּרְצִי), or Perez (Φάρες); son of Judah and Tamar; a brother of Zerah; half-brother of: Er, Onan and Shelah; father of Hezron and Hamul.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.38.29에 처음 언급되며 '베레스'라 불림. 유다와 다말의 아들. 엘, 오난, 셀라와 세라의 형제. 헤스론과 하물의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베레스는 유다와 다말의 아들로, 다윗 왕과 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.
persons.article_ko: 베레스는 유다와 다말의 아들로, 창세기 38장에 기록된 특이한 상황에서 태어났다. 그는 세라의 쌍둥이 형제였고 출산 중 먼저 나왔기 때문에 '터짐' 또는 '갈라짐'을 의미하는 베레스라는 이름이 지어졌다(창 38:29). 베레스는 유다 지파 안의 저명한 가문의 조상이 되었다(민 26:20-21). 그는 다윗 왕의 족보에 언급되며(룻 4:12, 18; 대상 2:4-5) 헤스론, 갈렙, 나손을 포함한 여러 저명한 인물들의 조상이다(대상 2:5, 9, 10). 베레스의 후손은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착한 사람 중에 속했다(느 11:4, 6). 가장 중요한 것은, 베레스가 마태복음 1:3과 누가복음 3:33 모두의 예수 그리스도 족보에 열거되어 메시아 혈통에서 그의 중요한 역할을 부각시킨다는 것이다.

persons.description: People from Periz(?)
persons.brief: Canaanite people group living in the land of Canaan
persons.short: The Perizzites, a Canaanite people group that inhabited the land of Canaan before the Israelite conquest.
persons.article: The Perizzites were one of the Canaanite people groups that inhabited the land of Canaan before the Israelite conquest. They are first mentioned in Gen.13.7 as living in the land alongside the Canaanites during the time of Abraham. God promised to give the land of the Perizzites to Abraham's descendants (Gen.15.20). The Perizzites are often listed among the Canaanite nations that the Israelites were to dispossess and drive out (Exo.3.8,17; 23.23; 33.2; 34.11; Deu.7.1; 20.17; Jos.3.10; 9.1; 11.3; 12.8). During the conquest of Canaan, the Perizzites were among the groups defeated by the Israelites (Jos.24.11; Jdg.1.4-5). However, some Perizzites remained in the land, and the Israelites intermarried with them (Jdg.3.5-6). The Perizzites, along with other Canaanite groups, were subjected to forced labor during the reigns of Solomon and later kings (1Ki.9.20-21; 2Ch.8.7-8). Remnants of the Perizzites were still present in the land after the Babylonian exile (Ezr.9.1; Neh.9.8).
persons.summary: People from Periz(?), first mentioned at Gen.13.7 only referred to as Perizzites (פְּרִזִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 브리스 사람. Gen.13.7에 처음 언급되며 '브리스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 브리스 사람은 이스라엘 정복 이전 가나안 땅에 살던 가나안 족속이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Female Christian in Rome greeted by Paul
persons.short: Persis, a beloved female Christian in Rome whom Paul greeted in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Persis was a female Christian mentioned by Paul in his greetings to the church in Rome (Rom.16.12). Paul describes her as "the beloved Persis, who has worked hard in the Lord." This brief mention suggests that Persis was a dedicated and hardworking member of the Christian community in Rome. The fact that Paul specifically mentions her and commends her for her work in the Lord indicates that she played a significant role in the church, possibly in serving or ministering to others. The name Persis suggests that she may have been of Persian origin or descent.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.12 only referred to as Persis (Περσίς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Rom.16.12에 처음 언급되며 '버시'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 버시는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 사랑받는 로마의 여성 신자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants
persons.short: Peruda or Perida, the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Peruda, also known as Perida, was the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile. The family is mentioned in the lists of returnees in both Ezr.2.55 and Neh.7.57. Solomon's servants were likely descendants of the Canaanites who had been subjected to forced labor during Solomon's reign (1Ki.9.20-21). The return of Peruda's family, along with other families of Solomon's servants, shows that they had maintained their identity and were part of the Jewish community even during the exile. The variations in the name (Peruda in Ezra and Perida in Nehemiah) may be due to differences in spelling or transcription.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.55 referred to as Peruda or Perida (פְּרוּדָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.55에 처음 언급되며 '브루다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 브루다(브리다라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 솔로몬의 종들 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Apostle of Jesus, leader in the early church
persons.short: Peter, also known as Simon, Cephas, or Simon Bar-Jonah, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus and a prominent leader in the early Christian church.
