These men, representing various churches, were likely entrusted with delivering the collection for the poor in Jerusalem that Paul had gathered from the Gentile churches (Rom.15.25-28). Pyrrhus, being from Berea, was probably a member of the church there, which was known for its diligent study of the Scriptures (Act.17.10-12).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.20.4 only referred to as Pyrrhus (Πύρρος); father of Sopater.
persons.summary_ko: Act.20.4에 처음 언급되며 '아리스다고와'라 불림. 소바더의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 부로는 아시아로 가는 여정에서 바울과 동행한 베뢰아 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: A Christian brother in Corinth who sent greetings to Rome
persons.short: Quartus, a Christian brother in Corinth, sent greetings to the believers in Rome through Paul's letter.
persons.article: Quartus is mentioned briefly in Paul's letter to the Romans as a Christian brother who sent greetings to the believers in Rome (Rom.16.23). He was likely a member of the church in Corinth, where Paul was writing from at the time. Paul's inclusion of Quartus' greeting suggests that he was a well-known and respected member of the Corinthian church. His mention in Paul's letter indicates that he was an active participant in the early Christian community and had a connection to the believers in Rome.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.23 only referred to as Quartus (Κούαρτος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.23에 처음 언급되며 '구아도'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 구아도는 고린도의 그리스도인 형제로, 바울의 편지를 통해 로마의 신자들에게 문안했다.

persons.description: Queen living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A queen who visited Solomon and praised his wisdom
persons.short: The Queen of Sheba visited King Solomon, tested him with questions, and praised his wisdom and prosperity.
persons.article: The Queen of Sheba, whose kingdom was likely located in modern-day Yemen or Ethiopia, heard about the fame and wisdom of King Solomon and traveled to Jerusalem to meet him (1Ki.10.1-13; 2Ch.9.1-12). She brought a large entourage and expensive gifts, including gold, spices, and precious stones. The queen tested Solomon with difficult questions, and he answered them all, demonstrating his God-given wisdom. Impressed by his wisdom, wealth, and the organization of his court, the Queen of Sheba praised Solomon and his God, acknowledging that his wisdom and prosperity were divine blessings. She gave Solomon many gifts, and he reciprocated, giving her all she desired. Jesus later referenced the Queen of Sheba's visit, noting that she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, and yet someone greater than Solomon was present in Jesus himself (Mat.12.42; Luk.11.31).
persons.summary: A queen of the country Sheba living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.10.1 referred to as Queen of Sheba (מַלְכָּה), or Queen of/ the South (βασίλισσα).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕비. 1Ki.10.1에 처음 언급되며 '스바 여왕'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바 여왕은 솔로몬 왕을 방문하여 어려운 질문으로 그를 시험했고 그의 지혜와 번영을 칭송했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Governor of Syria during a census mentioned in Luke
persons.short: Quirinius was the governor of Syria when a census was taken, as mentioned in Luke's Gospel.
persons.article: Quirinius was the governor of Syria at the time of a census that took place around the birth of Jesus (Luk.2.2). This census, ordered by Caesar Augustus, required everyone to return to their ancestral towns to be registered. As a result, Joseph and Mary traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born. The mention of Quirinius helps to provide a historical context for the birth of Christ. However, the exact date of this census and Quirinius' governorship have been the subject of much scholarly debate, as there are some apparent discrepancies between the biblical account and other historical records.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.2.2 only referred to as Quirinius (Κυρήνιος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.2.2에 처음 언급되며 '구레뇨'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 구레뇨는 누가복음에 언급된 인구조사가 실시될 당시 시리아 총독이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Cush, grandson of Ham, great-grandson of Noah
persons.short: Raamah was a son of Cush, grandson of Ham, and great-grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Raamah is mentioned in the genealogy of the nations in Genesis 10, also known as the Table of Nations (Gen.10.7; 1Ch.1.9). He was a son of Cush, who was a son of Ham, making Raamah a grandson of Ham and a great-grandson of Noah. The Table of Nations records the descendants of Noah's sons and their dispersal after the Tower of Babel. Raamah's sons, Sheba and Dedan, are also mentioned, suggesting that they became ancestors of tribes or nations. Some scholars associate Raamah with a region in southern Arabia, based on the connection with Sheba and Dedan, which are often linked to Arabian tribes. However, the exact location and identity of Raamah and his descendants remain uncertain.
persons.summary: A man of the Cushites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.7 referred to as Raamah or Raama (רַעְמָה); son of Cush; a brother of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Sabteca and Nimrod; father of Sheba and Dedan.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.7에 처음 언급되며 '라아마'라 불림. 구스의 아들. 스바, 하윌라, 삽다, 삽드가와 니므롯의 형제. 세바와 드단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라아마는 구스의 아들이며 함의 손자이자 노아의 증손자로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem
persons.short: Rab-mag, a Babylonian official, was present at the capture of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar's army.
persons.article: Rab-mag is mentioned as one of the Babylonian officials present at the capture of Jerusalem by the army of King Nebuchadnezzar (Jer.39.3, 13). The name "Rab-mag" is likely a title rather than a personal name, possibly meaning "chief of the magi" or "chief soothsayer." The presence of Rab-mag, along with other officials. His name was either Nergal-sharezer or he was accompanied by Nergal-sharezer together with Samgar-nebo, and Nebushazban, indicates that he was a high-ranking member of the Babylonian military or administrative hierarchy. After the city fell, these officials took up residence at the Middle Gate, a prominent location within Jerusalem. The specific duties and responsibilities of Rab-mag are not elaborated upon in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.39.3 only referred to as Rab-mag (רַב־מָג).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.39.3에 처음 언급되며 '우두머리'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 랍마그는 느부갓네살 군대가 예루살렘을 함락시킬 때 있었던 바벨론 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Babylonian official sent by King Sennacherib to Jerusalem
persons.short: Rab-saris was one of the Babylonian officials sent by King Sennacherib to Jerusalem during his campaign against Judah.
persons.article: Rab-saris is mentioned as one of the Babylonian officials sent by King Sennacherib of Assyria to Jerusalem during his campaign against Judah (2Ki.18.17). The name "Rab-saris" is likely a title meaning "chief eunuch" or "chief officer." His name was either Tartan or he was accompanied by Tartan, together with Rabshakeh, two other high-ranking Assyrian officials. Their mission was to intimidate King Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem into surrendering. The presence of Rab-saris, along with the other officials, underscores the gravity of the situation and the might of the Assyrian army threatening Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.18.17 only referred to as Rab-saris (רַב־סָרִיס).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.18.17에 처음 언급되며 '랍사리스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 랍사리스는 산헤립 왕이 유다를 공격할 때 예루살렘으로 보낸 바벨론 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem
persons.short: Rab-saris, a Babylonian official, was present at the capture of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar's army.
persons.article: Rab-saris is mentioned as one of the Babylonian officials present at the capture of Jerusalem by the army of King Nebuchadnezzar (Jer.39.3, 13). The name "Rab-saris" is likely a title meaning "chief eunuch" or "chief officer." After the city fell, Rab-saris, along with other officials such as Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, and Nebushazban, took up residence at the Middle Gate, a prominent location within Jerusalem. The presence of these high-ranking officials demonstrates the complete subjugation of Jerusalem to Babylonian authority. The specific duties and responsibilities of Rab-saris are not elaborated upon in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.39.3 only referred to as Rab-saris (רַב־סָרִיס).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.39.3에 처음 언급되며 '랍사리스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 랍사리스는 느부갓네살 군대가 예루살렘을 함락시킬 때 있었던 바벨론 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Babylonian official who taunted Hezekiah and Jerusalem's people
persons.short: Rabshakeh was a Babylonian official who tried to intimidate Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem into surrendering.
persons.article: Rabshakeh was a high-ranking Assyrian official who served as the spokesman for King Sennacherib during his campaign against Judah (2Kings 18-19; Isaiah 36-37). He was sent, along with Tartan and Rab-saris, to intimidate King Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem. Rabshakeh delivered a threatening message, urging them to surrender and not trust in Hezekiah or God to deliver them. He spoke in Hebrew, intending to frighten the people on the city wall. Hezekiah's representatives, Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah, asked Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic, but he refused and continued to speak in Hebrew to undermine the people's morale. Rabshakeh mocked Hezekiah's faith in God and boasted of Assyria's power. When Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went to the temple to pray. Isaiah the prophet reassured Hezekiah that God would protect Jerusalem. Rabshakeh returned to Sennacherib, who had left Lachish to fight against Libnah. Despite Rabshakeh's threats and Sennacherib's letter, Hezekiah trusted in God, and the Assyrian army was ultimately defeated by divine intervention.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.17 only referred to as Rabshakeh (רַבְשָׁקֵה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.18.17에 처음 언급되며 '랍사게'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 랍사게는 히스기야와 예루살렘 백성을 겁박하여 항복시키려 한 바벨론 관리였다.
persons.article_ko: 랍사게는 유다를 대적하는 원정 동안 산헤립 왕의 대변인으로 섬긴 고위 앗수르 관리였다(열왕기하 18-19장; 이사야 36-37장). 그는 다르단, 랍사리스와 함께 히스기야 왕과 예루살렘 백성을 겁박하도록 보내졌다. 랍사게는 위협적인 메시지를 전달하며 그들에게 항복하고 히스기야나 하나님이 그들을 구원하실 것을 신뢰하지 말라고 촉구했다. 그는 성벽 위의 백성을 두렵게 하려는 의도로 히브리어로 말했다. 히스기야의 대표자들인 엘리야김, 셉나, 요아는 랍사게에게 아람어로 말해달라고 요청했으나 그는 거절하고 백성의 사기를 꺾기 위해 계속 히브리어로 말했다. 랍사게는 히스기야의 하나님에 대한 믿음을 조롱하며 앗수르의 권세를 자랑했다. 히스기야는 그 보고를 듣고 자기 옷을 찢고 굵은 베를 입고 기도하러 성전으로 갔다. 선지자 이사야는 히스기야에게 하나님이 예루살렘을 보호하실 것이라고 확신시켰다. 랍사게는 립나를 대적하여 싸우기 위해 라기스를 떠났던 산헤립에게로 돌아갔다. 랍사게의 위협과 산헤립의 편지에도 불구하고 히스기야는 하나님을 신뢰했고, 앗수르 군대는 결국 신적 개입으로 패배했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Jacob; mother of Joseph and Benjamin
persons.short: Rachel was the beloved wife of Jacob, and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
persons.article: Rachel was the daughter of Laban and the younger sister of Leah (Gen.29.16). She became the beloved wife of Israel (or 'Jacob'), who worked for Laban for fourteen years to marry her (Gen.29.18-30). Rachel was initially unable to conceive, while Leah bore several children (Gen.29.31-35). In her distress, Rachel gave her maidservant Bilhah to Jacob, and Bilhah bore Dan and Naphtali (Gen.30.1-8). Eventually, God remembered Rachel, and she gave birth to Joseph (Gen.30.22-24). When Jacob left Laban, Rachel stole her father's household idols (Gen.31.19). She later hid them and deceived her father when he came searching for them (Gen.31.34-35). As Jacob's family journeyed to Ephrath (Bethlehem), Rachel went into labor and gave birth to Benjamin, but she died during childbirth (Gen.35.16-20). Jacob buried her on the way to Ephrath and set up a pillar on her grave (Gen.35.20). Rachel's sons, Joseph and Benjamin, became two of the twelve tribes of Israel (Gen.46.19-22). Her tomb became a landmark (1Sa.10.2 and is mentioned in Jer.31.15, where her weeping is used as a symbol for Israel's mourning during the Babylonian exile). This passage is also quoted in Mat.2.18 in relation to Herod's massacre of the innocents.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.29.6 referred to as Rachel (רָחֵל), or Rachel (Ῥαχήλ); daughter of Laban; a sister of Leah; wife of Israel; mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.29.6에 처음 언급되며 '라헬'이라 불림. 라반의 딸. 레아의 자매. 이스라엘의 아내. 요셉과 베냐민의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 라헬은 야곱의 사랑받는 아내이며 요셉과 베냐민의 어머니였다.
persons.article_ko: 라헬은 라반의 딸이며 레아의 여동생이었다(창 29:16). 그녀는 이스라엘(야곱)이 사랑하는 아내가 되었는데, 야곱은 그녀와 결혼하기 위해 라반을 위해 십사 년간 일했다(창 29:18-30). 라헬은 처음에 잉태하지 못했고 레아는 여러 자녀를 낳았다(창 29:31-35). 고통 중에 라헬은 자기 여종 빌하를 야곱에게 주었고, 빌하는 단과 납달리를 낳았다(창 30:1-8). 마침내 하나님이 라헬을 기억하셔서 그녀는 요셉을 낳았다(창 30:22-24). 야곱이 라반을 떠날 때 라헬은 아버지의 집안 우상들을 훔쳤다(창 31:19). 그녀는 후에 그것들을 숨기고 아버지가 그것들을 찾으러 왔을 때 그를 속였다(창 31:34-35). 야곱의 가족이 에브랏(베들레헴)으로 여행하는 동안 라헬은 산고를 겪으며 베냐민을 낳았으나 출산 중에 죽었다(창 35:16-20). 야곱은 에브랏으로 가는 길에 그녀를 묻고 그녀의 무덤에 비석을 세웠다(창 35:20). 라헬의 아들들인 요셉과 베냐민은 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 두 지파가 되었다(창 46:19-22). 그녀의 무덤은 이정표가 되었고(삼상 10:2) 예레미야 31:15에 언급되는데, 그곳에서 그녀의 울음은 바벨론 포로 시대 이스라엘의 애곡을 상징하는 데 사용된다. 이 구절은 헤롯의 유아 학살과 관련하여 마태복음 2:18에도 인용된다.

persons.description: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: One of David's brothers, son of Jesse
persons.short: Raddai was one of David's brothers, a son of Jesse.
persons.article: Raddai is mentioned in the genealogy of David as one of his brothers, a son of Jesse from Bethlehem (1Ch.2.14). He is listed among David's seven brothers, including Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethaneel, Ozem, and the unnamed seventh brother. Raddai was likely born and raised in Bethlehem, where Jesse's family lived. However, no further information is provided about Raddai in the Bible, and he is not mentioned in the narrative of David's life or reign. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to establish David's family background and lineage.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.14 only referred to as Raddai (רַדַּי); son of Jesse; a brother of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Shimeah, Nethanel, Ozem, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 형제. 1Ch.2.14에 처음 언급되며 '랏대'라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 아들. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 삼마, 느다넬, 오셈, 엘리후, 스루야와 아비가일의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 랏대는 이새의 아들이며 다윗의 형제 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: A Canaanite woman who helped the Israelite spies in Jericho
persons.short: Rahab, a Canaanite woman from Jericho, hid the Israelite spies and was spared during the city's destruction.
persons.article: Rahab was a Canaanite woman who lived in Jericho at the time of the Israelites' conquest of the Promised Land (Jos.2.1). She is described as a prostitute who provided lodging for the two Israelite spies sent by Joshua to survey the city. When the king of Jericho ordered Rahab to hand over the spies, she hid them on her roof and misdirected the king's men (Jos.2.3-7). Rahab acknowledged the God of Israel and asked for protection for herself and her family when the city would be taken (Jos.2.8-13). The spies agreed to spare her if she would tie a scarlet cord in her window (Jos.2.14-21). During the conquest of Jericho, Rahab and her family were saved as promised (Jos.6.17, 23, 25). Rahab's faith and actions are commended in the New Testament (Heb.11.31; Jam 2.25). She is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus, indicating that she married Salmon and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ (Mat.1.5).
persons.summary: A woman living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.2.1 referred to as Rahab (רָחָב), or Rahab (Ῥαάβ), or Rahab (Ῥαχάβ); mother of Boaz(?).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 여성. Jos.2.1에 처음 언급되며 '라합'이라 불림. 살마의 아내. 보아스의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여리고의 가나안 여인 라합은 이스라엘 정탐꾼들을 숨겨주었고, 성이 멸망할 때 목숨을 건졌다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shema and founder of Jorkeam, of Judah
persons.short: Raham was the son of Shema and the father or founder of Jorkeam, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Raham is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.44). He was the son of Shema and the father or founder of Jorkeam. No additional information is provided about Raham in the Bible. His mention in the genealogy serves to trace the lineage of certain families within the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.44 only referred to as Raham (רַ֫חַם); a son of Shema; father or founder of Jorkeam.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.44에 처음 언급되며 '라함'이라 불림. 세마의 아들. 요르그암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라함은 세마의 아들이며 유다 지파 요르그암의 아버지 또는 창설자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Sheresh, of the tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Rakem was a son of Sheresh, from the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Rakem is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh (1Ch.7.16). He was the son of Sheresh, who was a descendant of Manasseh through his son Machir. No further details are provided about Rakem in the Bible. His inclusion in the genealogy helps to establish the family lines within the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.16 only referred to as Rakem (רֶ֫קֶם); son of Sheresh; a brother of Ulam.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.16에 처음 언급되며 '라겜'이라 불림. 세레스의 아들. 울람의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 라겜은 세레스의 아들이며 므낫세 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Firstborn son of Jerahmeel, of the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Ram was the firstborn son of Jerahmeel, from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Ram is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as the firstborn son of Jerahmeel (1Ch.2.25, 27). Jerahmeel was a descendant of Judah through his son Hezron. Ram had two brothers, Bunah and Oren, and a half-brother named Onam. The genealogy also mentions Ram's sons, Maaz, Jamin, and Eker. No further details are provided about Ram or his descendants in the Bible. The inclusion of Ram in the genealogy serves to document the family lines within the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.25 only referred to as Ram (רָם); son of Jerahmeel; a brother of Bunah, Oren, Ozem, Ahijah and Onam; father of Maaz, Jamin and Eker.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.25에 처음 언급되며 '람'이라 불림. 여라므엘과 여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 브나, 오렌, 오셈, 아히야와 오남의 형제. 마아스, 야민과 에겔의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 람은 유다 지파 여라므엘의 맏아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Ancestor of Elihu, who spoke to Job
persons.short: Ram was an ancestor of Elihu, one of the men who spoke to Job.
persons.article: Ram is mentioned in the book of Job as an ancestor of Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram (Job.32.2). Elihu was one of the men who came to comfort Job during his affliction and ended up speaking to him about God's justice and sovereignty. The mention of Ram in Elihu's lineage suggests that he was from a respected family. However, no further details are provided about Ram himself in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Job.32.2 only referred to as Ram (רָם); progenitor of Buzites.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Job.32.2에 처음 언급되며 '람'이라 불림. 부스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 람은 욥에게 말한 사람 중 한 사람인 엘리후의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hezron, ancestor of David and Jesus
persons.short: Ram was the son of Hezron and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Ram, also known as Aram or Arni, was the son of Hezron and a descendant of Judah (Rut.4.19; 1Ch.2.9; Mat.1.3; Luk.3.33). He was the father of Amminadab and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ. Ram is mentioned in the genealogies of David and Jesus, highlighting the lineage from the tribe of Judah to the Messiah. His inclusion in these genealogies underscores the importance of tracing the ancestry of key biblical figures, particularly in relation to the fulfillment of God's promises through the line of David.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.4.19 referred to as Ram (רָם), or Ram (Ἀράμ), or Admin (Ἀδμίν), or Admin (Ἀρνὶ); son of Hezron; a brother of Jerahmeel, Caleb, Segub and Ashhur; father of Amminadab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Rut.4.19에 처음 언급되며 '람'이라 불림. 헤스론과 에브랏의 아들. 여라므엘, 갈렙, 스굽과 아스훌의 형제. 암미나답의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 람은 헤스론의 아들이며 다윗 왕과 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: People from Ramath(?)
persons.brief: People from Ramah who tended King David's vineyards
persons.short: The Ramathites were people from Ramah who were in charge of King David's vineyards.
persons.article: The Ramathites are mentioned briefly in the context of King David's administration (1Ch.27.27). They were people from the city of Ramah who were appointed to oversee the king's vineyards. This suggests that Ramah was known for its viticulture and that its inhabitants were skilled in tending vineyards. The mention of the Ramathites in this passage highlights the various roles and responsibilities assigned to different groups within David's kingdom.
persons.summary: People from Ramath(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.27.27 only referred to as Ramathites (רָמָתִי).
persons.summary_ko: 라마 사람. 1Ch.27.27에 처음 언급되며 '라마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 라마 사람들은 다윗 왕의 포도원을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the men who married foreign women
persons.short: Ramiah was one of the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Ramiah is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the men who had married foreign women (Ezr.10.25). This occurred during the time when Ezra, a priest and scribe, led a religious reform among the Jewish people who had returned from Babylonian exile. Ezra called for the people to separate themselves from the foreign wives they had married, as these marriages were considered a violation of God's law. Ramiah was among those who had taken foreign wives, but no further details are provided about him or his specific situation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.25 only referred to as Ramiah (רַמְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.25에 처음 언급되며 '라먀'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 라먀는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Philistine giants; his descendants fought against David's warriors.
persons.short: Rapha was the ancestor of several Philistine giants who fought against David and his mighty warriors.
persons.article: Rapha is mentioned in 2Samuel 21 and 1Chronicles 20 as the ancestor of several Philistine giants who fought against King David and his mighty warriors. The name "Rapha" is used to describe these giants as descendants of the Rephaim, a people known for their great stature and strength (Deu.2.11, 20-21). In 2Sa.21.16, Ishbi-benob, one of the descendants of Rapha, wielded a bronze spear and threatened to kill David, but Abishai came to David's aid and killed the giant. Another descendant of Rapha, Saph (also called Sippai in 1Ch.20.4, was killed by Sibbecai the Hushathite )(2Sa.21.18). In 2Sa.21.20 and 1Ch.20.6, another descendant of Rapha is described as a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. This giant was killed by Jonathan, the son of Shimea, David's brother (2Sa.21.21; 1Ch.20.7). These battles against the descendants of Rapha are summarized in 2Sa.21.22 and 1Ch.20.8, emphasizing that they were defeated by David and his servants. The mention of Rapha and his descendants highlights the ongoing conflict between the Israelites and the Philistines, as well as the bravery and skill of David and his warriors in facing and defeating these formidable enemies. The victory over the giants also demonstrates God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promise to give the Israelites victory over their enemies and to establish David's kingdom.
persons.summary: A gigantic man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.21.16 referred to as Rapha (רָפָה), or Raphaite (רְפָאִים); father of Goliath, Ishbi-benob, Saph, Lahmi, huge man.
persons.summary_ko: 2Sa.21.16에 처음 언급되며 'Rapha'라 불림. 골리앗, 이스비브놉, 삽, 라흐미와 거인의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라바는 다윗과 그의 용사들을 대적하여 싸운 여러 블레셋 거인들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Binea, a descendant of King Saul
persons.short: Raphah (or Rephaiah) was a son of Binea and a descendant of King Saul.
persons.article: Raphah, also known as Rephaiah, is mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul's descendants (1Ch.8.37; 9.43). He was the son of Binea and a member of the tribe of Benjamin. The genealogy traces Saul's lineage after his death, showing that his family line continued even though he was no longer king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.37 referred to as Raphah (רָפָא), or Rephaiah (רְפָיָה); son of Binea; a brother of Eleasah and Azel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.37에 처음 언급되며 '라바'라 불림. 비느아의 아들. 엘르아사와 아셀의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 라바(르바야라고도 함)는 비느아의 아들이며 사울 왕의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Palti, a spy sent by Moses
persons.short: Raphu was the father of Palti, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Raphu is mentioned in the book of Numbers as the father of Palti, who was from the tribe of Benjamin (Num.13.9). Palti was one of the twelve spies chosen by Moses to explore the land of Canaan before the Israelites were to enter it. Each spy was a leader from his respective tribe. The spies were sent to assess the land, its people, and its resources. After forty days, they returned with their report, but only Joshua and Caleb gave a positive assessment. The other ten spies, including Palti, discouraged the people by emphasizing the challenges they would face. As a result, the Israelites rebelled against God and were punished with forty years of wandering in the wilderness.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.9 only referred to as Raphu (רָפוּא); father of Palti.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.9에 처음 언급되며 '라부'라 불림. 발디의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 라부는 모세가 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 한 사람인 발디의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Reubenite, son of Micah
persons.short: Reaiah was a Reubenite, the son of Micah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben.
persons.article: Reaiah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben (1Ch.5.5). He was the son of Micah and a member of the Reubenite clan. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 5 traces the descendants of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel (or 'Jacob'), and provides a record of the families and clans within the tribe. No further details are given about Reaiah's life or role within the tribe. His mention in the genealogy serves to document the lineage of the Reubenites.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.5 only referred to as Reaiah (רְאָיָה); a son of Micah; father of Baal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.5에 처음 언급되며 '르아야'라 불림. 미가의 아들. 바알의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르우벤 사람 르아야는 미가의 아들로, 르우벤 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Reaiah was an ancestor of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Reaiah is mentioned in the lists of people who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.47; Neh.7.50). He was an ancestor of a group of temple servants, also known as the Nethinim, who were assigned to assist the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. The Nethinim were descendants of the Gibeonites who had been appointed by Joshua to serve in the tabernacle (Jos.9.27). Reaiah's descendants were among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem to help rebuild the temple and restore worship practices. The mention of Reaiah in these lists highlights the importance of the temple servants in the restoration of Jewish worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.47 only referred to as Reaiah (רְאָיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '르아야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르아야는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 성전 봉사자의 조상이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A Midianite king killed by the Israelites
persons.short: Reba was one of the five Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.
persons.article: Reba was one of the five kings of Midian who were defeated and killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses (Num.31.8; Jos.13.21). The Midianites were a nomadic people who lived in the desert regions south and east of Canaan. They had engaged in hostilities against Israel and had led the Israelites into idolatry and immorality (Numbers 25). As a result, God commanded Moses to carry out a war of vengeance against the Midianites. The Israelite army, led by Phinehas, defeated the Midianites and killed their five kings, including Reba. The victory over the Midianites was seen as a judgment against their wickedness and a protection of Israel's spiritual and moral purity. The death of Reba and the other Midianite kings marked the end of a significant threat to Israel's existence and integrity.
persons.summary: A king of Midian living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.31.8 only referred to as Reba (רֶ֫בַע).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.31.8에 처음 언급되며 '레바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레바는 모세 시대에 이스라엘 사람들에게 죽임을 당한 다섯 미디안 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau
persons.short: Rebekah was the wife of Isaac and the mother of Jacob and Esau.
persons.article: Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel and the granddaughter of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Gen.22.23). She became the wife of Isaac after a servant of Abraham was sent to find a suitable bride for him (Genesis 24). Rebekah was a beautiful woman and was chosen by God to be Isaac's wife (Gen.24.15-67). She was barren for many years, but Isaac prayed for her, and she conceived twins (Gen.25.21). During her pregnancy, the Lord revealed to Rebekah that two nations were in her womb and that the older would serve the younger (Gen.25.23). Rebekah gave birth to Esau and Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen.25.24-26). She favored Jacob over Esau and helped him deceive Isaac into giving him the firstborn's blessing (Genesis 27). This led to a conflict between the brothers, and Jacob had to flee to escape Esau's anger (Gen.27.41-45). Rebekah's deception had consequences for the family, but God's plan for Jacob prevailed. Rebekah's nurse, Deborah, died and was buried near Bethel (Gen.35.8). Rebekah died and was buried in the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham and Sarah were also buried (Gen.49.31). In the New Testament, Paul uses Rebekah's story to illustrate God's sovereignty in election (Rom.9.10-12).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.22.23 referred to as Rebekah (רִבְקָה), or Rebekah (Ῥεβέκκα); daughter of Bethuel; a sister of Laban; wife of Isaac; mother of Esau and Israel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.22.23에 처음 언급되며 '리브가'라 불림. 브두엘의 딸. 라반의 자매. 이삭의 아내. 에서와 이스라엘의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 리브가는 이삭의 아내이며 야곱과 에서의 어머니였다.
persons.article_ko: 리브가는 브두엘의 딸이며 아브라함의 형제 나홀의 손녀였다(창 22:23). 그녀는 아브라함의 종이 이삭에게 적합한 신부를 찾도록 보내진 후 이삭의 아내가 되었다(창세기 24장). 리브가는 아름다운 여인이었고 하나님에 의해 이삭의 아내로 선택되었다(창 24:15-67). 그녀는 여러 해 동안 잉태하지 못했으나 이삭이 그녀를 위해 기도했고, 그녀는 쌍둥이를 잉태했다(창 25:21). 임신 중 여호와는 리브가에게 두 민족이 그녀의 태 속에 있으며 형이 동생을 섬길 것이라고 알려주셨다(창 25:23). 리브가는 에서와 이스라엘(야곱)을 낳았다(창 25:24-26). 그녀는 에서보다 야곱을 편애하여 그가 이삭을 속여 맏아들의 축복을 받도록 도왔다(창세기 27장). 이는 형제 사이의 갈등으로 이어졌고, 야곱은 에서의 분노를 피해 도망쳐야 했다(창 27:41-45). 리브가의 속임수는 가족에게 결과를 가져왔으나 야곱을 위한 하나님의 계획은 이루어졌다. 리브가의 유모 드보라는 죽어서 벧엘 근처에 묻혔다(창 35:8). 리브가는 죽어서 아브라함과 사라도 묻힌 막벨라 굴에 묻혔다(창 49:31). 신약에서 바울은 리브가의 이야기를 하나님의 선택에 있어서의 주권을 설명하는 데 사용한다(롬 9:10-12).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of the Rechabites, who were faithful to God
persons.short: Rechab was the ancestor of the Rechabites, a nomadic tribe known for their faithfulness to God's commands.
persons.article: Rechab was the father of Jehonadab (2Ki.10.15 and the ancestor of the Rechabites, a nomadic tribe known for their strict adherence to God's commands )(Jeremiah 35). The Rechabites were descendants of the Kenites, who were associated with the Israelites since the time of Moses (Jdg.1.16). Jehonadab, son of Rechab, supported Jehu in his purge of Baal worship in Israel (2Ki.10.15-23). The Rechabites were known for their obedience to the commands of their ancestor Jonadab, which included abstaining from wine, not building houses, not sowing seed, and not planting vineyards (Jer.35.6-7). When the prophet Jeremiah tested their obedience by offering them wine, they refused, demonstrating their commitment to their ancestral vows (Jer.35.1-11). God commended the Rechabites for their faithfulness and promised that they would always have a descendant to serve Him (Jer.35.18-19). The example of the Rechabites stands as a model of obedience and devotion to God in the midst of a society that had largely abandoned His ways.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.10.15 referred to as Rechab (רֵכָב), or Rechabite (רֵכָבִי); a son of Hammath; father of Jonadab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '레갑'이라 불림. 함맛의 아들. 여호나답의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레갑은 하나님의 명령에 대한 신실함으로 알려진 유목 부족인 레갑 족속의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A captain of Ishbosheth's army, with his brother Baanah
persons.short: Rechab and his brother Baanah were captains in Ishbosheth's army during the time of David.
persons.article: Rechab is mentioned in 2 Samuel as the brother of Baanah, both captains in the army of Ishbosheth, the son of Saul (2Sa.4.2). After the death of Saul, Ishbosheth was made king over Israel, while David reigned over Judah (2Sa.2.8-10). Baanah and Rechab, who were from the tribe of Benjamin, betrayed Ishbosheth by sneaking into his house while he was resting and murdering him (2Sa.4.5-7). They brought Ishbosheth's head to David, hoping to gain favor with him (2Sa.4.8). However, David condemned their treacherous act and ordered their execution (2Sa.4.9-12). The actions of Rechab's sons contributed to the downfall of Ishbosheth and the eventual unification of Israel under David's rule. The story highlights the political instability and violence that characterized the early days of David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.4.2 only referred to as Rechab (רֵכָב); son of Rimmon; a brother of Baanah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '레갑'이라 불림. 림몬의 아들. 바아나의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레갑과 그의 형제 바아나는 다윗 시대에 이스보셋의 군대에서 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Malchijah, who repaired the Dung Gate
persons.short: Rechab was the father of Malchijah, who repaired the Dung Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
persons.article: Rechab is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the father of Malchijah, one of the people who helped repair the walls of Jerusalem (Neh.3.14). During the time of Nehemiah, the walls of Jerusalem were in disrepair, leaving the city vulnerable to attack. Nehemiah, who was serving as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia, received permission to return to Jerusalem and oversee the rebuilding of the walls (Neh.2.1-8). Various individuals and families were assigned to repair specific sections of the wall. Malchijah, son of Rechab, was responsible for repairing the Dung Gate, which was likely located on the southern side of the city and used for removing refuse (Neh.3.14). The mention of Rechab in this context highlights the participation of families in the restoration of Jerusalem's defenses and the importance of each person's contribution to the overall project.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.14 only referred to as Rechab (רֵכָב); father of Malchijah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.14에 처음 언급되며 '레갑'이라 불림. 말기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레갑은 예루살렘 성벽 재건 당시 분문을 수리한 말기야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel
persons.short: Reelaiah (or Raamiah) was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Reelaiah, also known as Raamiah, is mentioned in the lists of leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.2; Neh.7.7). Following the decree of King Cyrus of Persia, which allowed the Jews to return to their homeland and rebuild the temple (Ezr.1.1-4, a group of exiles led by Zerubbabel made the journey back to Jerusalem). Reelaiah (Raamiah) is listed among the leaders of this group, along with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and others. The returning exiles faced the challenge of rebuilding the temple and reestablishing Jewish worship in Jerusalem. The mention of Reelaiah (Raamiah) in these lists emphasizes the significant role played by various leaders in the restoration of Jewish life and faith after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.2 referred to as Reelaiah (רְעֵלָיָה), or Raamiah (רַעַמְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.2에 처음 언급되며 '르엘라야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르엘라야(라아먀라고도 함)는 바벨론 포로에서 스룹바벨과 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch(?), Jesher@1Ch.2.18(?), Shobab@1Ch.2.18(?), Ardon@1Ch.2.18(?), Mesha@1Ch.2.42(?), Haran@1Ch.2.46(?), Moza@1Ch.2.46(?), Gazez@1Ch.2.46a(?), Sheber@1Ch.2.48(?), Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48(?), Shaaph@1Ch.2.49(?), Sheva@1Ch.2.49(?), Achsah@1Ch.2.49(?)
persons.brief: Son of Jahdai, of the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Regem was a son of Jahdai, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Regem is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.47). He was one of the sons of Jahdai, who was a descendant of Judah through Caleb, the son of Hezron. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of several prominent families within the tribe of Judah. No additional information is provided about Regem or his role within the tribe. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and descendants of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.47 only referred to as Regem (רֶ֫גֶם); son of Caleb and Jahdai; a brother of Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, Shaaph, Hur(?), Jesher(?), Shobab(?), Ardon(?), Mesha(?), Haran(?), Moza(?), Gazez(?), Sheber(?), Tirhanah(?), Shaaph(?), Sheva(?) and Achsah(?).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.47에 처음 언급되며 '레겜'이라 불림. 갈렙과 야대의 아들. 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레겜은 야대의 아들로, 유다 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A messenger sent to inquire of the Lord
persons.short: Regem-melech was one of the messengers sent to the house of God to inquire of the Lord.
persons.article: Regem-melech is mentioned in the book of Zechariah as one of the messengers sent by the people of Bethel to inquire of the Lord (Zec.7.2). The context suggests that this event took place after the return of the Jews from Babylonian exile and during the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem. The people of Bethel sent Regem-melech and his companions to the house of God (the temple) to pray and to ask the priests and prophets a question regarding fasting and mourning (Zec.7.3). The people wanted to know if they should continue to observe the fasts they had established during the exile, now that the temple was being rebuilt. In response, the Lord spoke through Zechariah, emphasizing that true obedience and justice were more important than formal fasting (Zec.7.4-14). The mention of Regem-melech highlights the people's desire for guidance and their willingness to seek the Lord's direction through the priests and prophets.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Zec.7.2 only referred to as Regem-melech (רֶ֫גֶם מֶ֫לֶךְ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.7.2에 처음 언급되며 '레겜멜렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레겜멜렉은 여호와께 여쭙도록 하나님의 집에 보내진 전령 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Eliezer, grandson of Moses, a Levite
persons.short: Rehabiah was the son of Eliezer and grandson of Moses, a Levite with many descendants.
persons.article: Rehabiah was the son of Eliezer and grandson of Moses (1Ch.23.17). He was a Levite and had many descendants who were also Levites (1Ch.23.17). The Levites were responsible for assisting the priests in the temple service and had various duties assigned to them. Rehabiah's descendants were among the Levites who served during the reign of King David (1Ch.24.21). They were also among the Levites who were appointed as treasurers and other officials (1Ch.26.25). The multiple mentions of Rehabiah and his descendants in the genealogies and lists of Levites highlight the importance of their role in maintaining the worship and service of God in the temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.17 only referred to as Rehabiah (רְחַבְיָהוּ); a son of Eliezer; father of Isshiah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.17에 처음 언급되며 '르하뱌'라 불림. 엘리에셀의 아들. 잇시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르하뱌는 엘리에셀의 아들이며 모세의 손자로, 많은 후손을 둔 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah
persons.short: Rehob was the father of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, who was defeated by King David.
persons.article: Rehob is mentioned as the father of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah (2Sa.8.3, 12). Zobah was an Aramean kingdom located northeast of Israel, in the region of modern-day Syria. During the reign of King David, Hadadezer and his allies were defeated by David's army when they attempted to extend their influence to the Euphrates River (2Sa.8.3-4). David captured a large amount of gold, silver, and bronze from Hadadezer's cities, which he dedicated to the Lord (2Sa.8.11-12). The defeat of Hadadezer and the Arameans of Zobah was a significant victory for David, establishing his dominance in the region and expanding the boundaries of his kingdom. The mention of Rehob as Hadadezer's father provides additional context to the political situation of the time.
persons.summary: A man of Zobah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.3 only referred to as Rehob (רְחוֹב); father of Hadadezer.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '르흡'이라 불림. 하닷에셀의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르홉은 다윗 왕에게 패배한 소바 왕 하닷에셀의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the leaders who sealed the covenant
persons.short: Rehob was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Rehob is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the leaders who sealed the covenant (Neh.10.11). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commands and to separate themselves from the surrounding nations (Nehemiah 9-10). The leaders of the people, including priests, Levites, and heads of families, sealed this covenant as a sign of their commitment (Neh.10.1-27). Rehob was among these leaders, representing his family or clan. The sealing of the covenant was a significant moment in the spiritual renewal of the Jewish people after their return from Babylonian exile, and it demonstrated their dedication to obeying God's laws and maintaining their distinct identity as His chosen people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.11 only referred to as Rehob (רְחוֹב).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.11에 처음 언급되며 '르홉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르홉은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Abijah@1Ki.14.31-Mat, Jeush@2Ch.11.19, Shemariah@2Ch.11.19, Zaham@2Ch.11.19, Attai@2Ch.11.20, Ziza@2Ch.11.20, Shelomith@2Ch.11.20, Tekoa@2Sa.14.2-Amo(f)
persons.brief: Son of Solomon, first king of Judah
persons.short: Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and the first king of Judah after the division of the kingdom.
persons.article: Rehoboam was the son of King Solomon and Naamah, an Ammonite woman (1Ki.14.21, 31). He became king of Judah after Solomon's death (1Ki.11.43). When Rehoboam went to Shechem to be crowned, the people, led by Jeroboam, asked him to lighten the heavy yoke that Solomon had placed on them (1Ki.12.1-4). Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father, but he rejected their advice to be a servant to the people (1Ki.12.6-8). Instead, he followed the counsel of the young men who had grown up with him and threatened to make the people's yoke even heavier (1Ki.12.9-14). As a result, the ten northern tribes rebelled against Rehoboam and made Jeroboam their king, leaving only the tribes of Judah and Benjamin loyal to Rehoboam (1Ki.12.16-20). Rehoboam intended to fight against the northern tribes, but God sent a prophet to stop him (1Ki.12.21-24). During Rehoboam's reign, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and took away the treasures of the temple and the royal palace (1Ki.14.25-28; 2Ch.12.1-12). Rehoboam did evil in the eyes of the Lord and allowed idol worship to spread in Judah (1Ki.14.22-24). He reigned for 17 years and was succeeded by his son Abijah (1Ki.14.21, 31; 2Ch.12.16). Rehoboam's story is a cautionary tale about the consequences of foolish decisions and disobedience to God.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.11.43 referred to as Rehoboam (רְחַבְעָם), or Rehoboam (Ῥοβοάμ); son of Solomon and Naamah; a brother of Taphath and Basemath; husband of Maacah, Mahalath and Abihail; father of Abijah, Jeush, Shemariah, Zaham, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith; founder of Tekoa.
persons.summary_ko: 통일·분열왕국시대 왕. 1Ki.11.43에 처음 언급되며 '르호보암'이라 불림. 솔로몬과 나아마의 아들. 다밧과 바스맛의 형제. 마아가, 마할랏과 아비하일의 남편. 아비야, 여우스, 스마랴, 사함, 앗대, 시사, 슬로밋과 Tekoa의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르호보암은 솔로몬의 아들이며 왕국이 분열된 후 유다의 첫 왕이었다.
persons.article_ko: 르호보암은 솔로몬 왕과 암몬 여인 나아마의 아들이었다(왕상 14:21, 31). 그는 솔로몬이 죽은 후 유다 왕이 되었다(왕상 11:43). 르호보암이 왕위에 오르기 위해 세겜으로 갔을 때 여로보암이 이끄는 백성은 솔로몬이 그들에게 지운 무거운 멍에를 가볍게 해달라고 요청했다(왕상 12:1-4). 르호보암은 아버지를 섬겼던 원로들과 상의했으나 백성의 종이 되라는 그들의 조언을 거부했다(왕상 12:6-8). 대신 그는 자기와 함께 자란 젊은이들의 조언을 따라 백성의 멍에를 더 무겁게 하겠다고 위협했다(왕상 12:9-14). 그 결과 북부 열 지파는 르호보암에게 반역하여 여로보암을 그들의 왕으로 세웠고, 유다와 베냐민 지파만 르호보암에게 충성했다(왕상 12:16-20). 르호보암은 북부 지파들을 대적하여 싸우려 했으나 하나님이 선지자를 보내 그를 막으셨다(왕상 12:21-24). 르호보암의 통치 기간 동안 애굽 왕 시삭이 예루살렘을 침공하여 성전과 왕궁의 보물들을 가져갔다(왕상 14:25-28; 대하 12:1-12). 르호보암은 여호와 보시기에 악을 행하며 유다에 우상숭배가 퍼지도록 허용했다(왕상 14:22-24). 그는 십칠 년간 다스렸고 그의 아들 아비야가 뒤를 이었다(왕상 14:21, 31; 대하 12:16). 르호보암의 이야기는 어리석은 결정과 하나님께 대한 불순종의 결과에 대한 경고가 된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel
persons.short: Rehum (or Harim or Nehum) was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Rehum, also known as Harim or Nehum, is mentioned in the lists of leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile (Ezr.2.2; Neh.7.7; 12.3). Following the decree of King Cyrus of Persia, which allowed the Jews to return to their homeland and rebuild the temple (Ezr.1.1-4, a group of exiles led by Zerubbabel made the journey back to Jerusalem). Rehum (Harim or Nehum) is listed among the leaders of this group, along with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others. The returning exiles faced the challenge of rebuilding the temple and reestablishing Jewish worship in Jerusalem. In the book of Nehemiah, Rehum (Harim) is also mentioned as one of the priests who sealed the covenant to follow God's law (Neh.10.5). The mention of Rehum (Harim or Nehum) in these passages highlights the significant role played by various leaders and priests in the restoration of Jewish life and faith after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.2 referred to as Rehum (רְחוּם), or Harim (חָרִם), or Nehum (נְחוּם).
persons.short_ko: 르훔은 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 귀환한 지도자 중 한 명이다.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.2에 처음 언급되며 '르훔'이라 불림.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Persian official who wrote to King Artaxerxes
persons.short: Rehum was a Persian official who wrote to King Artaxerxes, attempting to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Rehum is mentioned in the book of Ezra as a high-ranking Persian official who held the title of "commander" (Ezr.4.8, 9, 17, 23). When the enemies of the Jews learned that they had begun rebuilding the temple and the city walls of Jerusalem, they wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes to persuade him to stop the work (Ezr.4.7-16). Rehum was one of the officials who signed this letter, along with Shimshai the scribe and others (Ezr.4.9). In the letter, they accused the Jews of rebuilding a rebellious and wicked city that had a history of causing trouble for kings (Ezr.4.12-16). As a result, Artaxerxes ordered the work to be stopped until further notice (Ezr.4.17-22). Rehum and his associates then went to Jerusalem and forcibly made the Jews stop building (Ezr.4.23). This opposition delayed the completion of the temple and the city walls until the reign of King Darius (Ezr.4.24). Rehum's actions demonstrate the political challenges faced by the Jews as they sought to rebuild Jerusalem after returning from Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.4.8 only referred to as Rehum (Aramiac רְחוּם).
persons.short_ko: 르훔은 사마리아의 방백으로 예루살렘 성전 재건을 방해하는 글을 왕에게 올렸다.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.4.8에 처음 언급되며 '르훔'이라 불림.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
persons.short: Rehum was one of the individuals who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Rehum is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals who sealed the covenant (Neh.10.25). After the completion of the wall of Jerusalem and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commands and to separate themselves from the surrounding nations (Nehemiah 9-10). The leaders of the people, including priests, Levites, and heads of families, sealed this covenant as a sign of their commitment (Neh.10.1-27). Rehum was among these individuals, likely representing his family or clan. The sealing of the covenant was a significant moment in the spiritual renewal of the Jewish people after their return from Babylonian exile, and it demonstrated their dedication to obeying God's laws and maintaining their distinct identity as His chosen people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.25 only referred to as Rehum (רְחוּם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.25에 처음 언급되며 '르훔'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르훔은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Levite who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem
persons.short: Rehum was a Levite who helped repair a section of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Rehum is briefly mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the Levites who helped repair a section of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh.3.17). During the time of Nehemiah, the walls of Jerusalem were in disrepair, leaving the city vulnerable to attack. Nehemiah, who was serving as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia, received permission to return to Jerusalem and oversee the rebuilding of the walls (Neh.2.1-8). Various individuals and families were assigned to repair specific sections of the wall. Rehum, along with other Levites, worked on a portion of the wall (Neh.3.17). The mention of Rehum in this context highlights the participation of the Levites in the restoration of Jerusalem's defenses and the importance of each person's contribution to the overall project.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.17 only referred to as Rehum (רְחוּם); a son of Bani.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.17에 처음 언급되며 '르훔'이라 불림. 바니의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 르훔은 느헤미야 시대에 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: A supporter of Solomon during Adonijah's rebellion
persons.short: Rei was one of the people who remained loyal to King Solomon during Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne.
persons.article: Rei is mentioned briefly in the book of 1 Kings as one of the people who did not join Adonijah in his attempt to become king (1Ki.1.8). Adonijah was one of King David's sons who tried to seize the throne near the end of David's life, even though David had promised the succession to his son Solomon (1Ki.1.5-10). Rei, along with Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and others, remained loyal to Solomon (1Ki.1.8). They did not attend the feast where Adonijah declared himself king (1Ki.1.9-10). When David was informed of Adonijah's actions, he ordered Solomon to be anointed as king, with the support of those who had remained loyal (1Ki.1.32-40). Rei's loyalty to Solomon during this critical time helped ensure a smooth transition of power and the fulfillment of David's choice of successor.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.1.8 only referred to as Rei (רֵעִי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.1.8에 처음 언급되며 '레이'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레이는 아도니야가 왕위를 찬탈하려 할 때 솔로몬 왕에게 신실하게 남은 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hebron, of the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Rekem was a son of Hebron, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Rekem is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah (1Ch.2.43, 44). He was one of the sons of Hebron, who was a descendant of Caleb, the son of Hezron. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of several prominent families within the tribe of Judah. Rekem is listed alongside his brothers Jorkeam, Shammai, and Shema (1Ch.2.44). No additional information is provided about Rekem or his role within the tribe. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and descendants of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.43 only referred to as Rekem (רֶ֫קֶם); son of Hebron; a brother of Korah, Tappuah and Shema; father of Shammai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.43에 처음 언급되며 '레겜'이라 불림. 헤브론의 아들. 고라, 답부아와 세마의 형제. 삼매의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레겜은 헤브론의 아들로, 유다 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: A Midianite king killed by the Israelites
persons.short: Rekem was one of the five Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.
persons.article: Rekem was one of the five kings of Midian who were defeated and killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses (Num.31.8; Jos.13.21). The Midianites were a nomadic people who lived in the desert regions south and east of Canaan. They had engaged in hostilities against Israel and had led the Israelites into idolatry and immorality (Numbers 25). As a result, God commanded Moses to carry out a war of vengeance against the Midianites. The Israelite army, led by Phinehas, defeated the Midianites and killed their five kings, including Rekem (Num.31.1-12). The victory over the Midianites was seen as a judgment against their wickedness and a protection of Israel's spiritual and moral purity. The death of Rekem and the other Midianite kings marked the end of a significant threat to Israel's existence and integrity. The land that had belonged to these kings was later allocated to the tribes of Reuben and Gad as part of their inheritance in the Promised Land (Jos.13.21).
persons.summary: A king of Midian living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.31.8 only referred to as Rekem (רֶ֫קֶם).
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.31.8에 처음 언급되며 '레겜'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레겜은 모세 시대에 이스라엘 사람들에게 죽임을 당한 다섯 미디안 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Pekah, king of Israel
persons.short: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, who became king of Israel and reigned for 20 years.
persons.article: Remaliah is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Pekah, who became king of Israel (2Ki.15.25, 27, 30, 32, 37; 16.1, 5; 2Ch.28.6; Isa.7.1, 4, 5, 9; 8.6). Pekah, son of Remaliah, was a captain in the army of King Pekahiah of Israel. He conspired against Pekahiah, killed him, and seized the throne (2Ki.15.25). Pekah reigned as king of Israel for 20 years (2Ki.15.27). During his reign, Pekah formed an alliance with King Rezin of Aram (Syria) and attacked Judah (2Ki.15.37; 16.5; Isa.7.1). However, their attack was unsuccessful, and the prophet Isaiah foretold the downfall of both Pekah and Rezin (Isa.7.4-9; 8.6). Pekah was eventually assassinated by Hoshea, who became the next king of Israel (2Ki.15.30). The frequent mention of Pekah as "son of Remaliah" in the biblical text suggests that Remaliah was not a prominent figure himself, but rather was known primarily as the father of King Pekah.
persons.summary: A man of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.25 only referred to as Remaliah (רְמַלְיָ֜הוּ); father of Pekah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.15.25에 처음 언급되며 '르말랴'라 불림. 베가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르말랴는 이스라엘 왕이 되어 이십 년간 다스린 베가의 아버지였다.
persons.article_ko: 르말랴는 성경에서 이스라엘 왕이 된 베가의 아버지로 언급된다(왕하 15:25, 27, 30, 32, 37; 16:1, 5; 대하 28:6; 사 7:1, 4-5, 9; 8:6). 르말랴의 아들 베가는 이스라엘 왕 브가히야 군대의 지휘관이었다. 그는 브가히야를 대적하여 음모를 꾸며 그를 죽이고 왕위를 찬탈했다(왕하 15:25). 베가는 이스라엘 왕으로 이십 년간 다스렸다(왕하 15:27). 그의 통치 기간 동안 베가는 아람(시리아) 왕 르신과 동맹을 맺어 유다를 공격했다(왕하 15:37; 16:5; 사 7:1). 그러나 그들의 공격은 성공하지 못했고, 선지자 이사야는 베가와 르신 둘 다의 몰락을 예언했다(사 7:4-9; 8:6). 베가는 결국 호세아에게 암살당했고, 호세아가 이스라엘의 다음 왕이 되었다(왕하 15:30). 성경 본문에서 베가가 자주 '르말랴의 아들'로 언급되는 것은 르말랴 자신이 저명한 인물이 아니라 주로 베가 왕의 아버지로만 알려졌음을 시사한다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A gatekeeper of the temple during David's reign
persons.short: Rephael was one of the gatekeepers of the temple during the reign of King David.
persons.article: Rephael is briefly mentioned in the book of 1 Chronicles as one of the gatekeepers of the temple during the reign of King David (1Ch.26.7). He was a descendant of Obed-Edom, who was a Levite entrusted with the care of the Ark of the Covenant (1Ch.13.13-14; 26.4-8). The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the temple and ensuring that only authorized individuals were allowed to enter (1Ch.9.17-27). They also had duties related to the maintenance and organization of the temple. The mention of Rephael as a gatekeeper highlights the importance of this role in maintaining the sanctity and security of the temple, which was the center of worship for the Israelites.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.7 only referred to as Rephael (רְפָאֵל); son of Shemaiah; a brother of Othni, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu and Semachiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.7에 처음 언급되며 '르바엘'이라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 오드니, 오벳, 엘사밧, 엘리후와 스마갸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 르바엘은 다윗 왕 시대에 성전 문지기 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, of the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Rephah was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
persons.article: Rephah is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1Ch.7.25). He was one of the sons of Beriah, who was a descendant of Asher, the eighth son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 traces the lineage of the tribe of Asher and lists several of its prominent families and individuals. No additional information is provided about Rephah or his role within the tribe. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and descendants of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.25 only referred to as Rephah (רֶ֫פַח); son of Beriah; a brother of Sheerah and Resheph.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '레바'라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 세에라와 레셉의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레바는 브리아의 아들로, 아셀 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A descendant of King David
persons.short: Rephaiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.
persons.article: Rephaiah is mentioned in the genealogy of King David's descendants (1Ch.3.21). He was a descendant of David through the line of Solomon. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 3 traces the royal line of David, listing the kings of Judah and their offspring. The mention of Rephaiah in this genealogy indicates that he was part of the extended royal family, although he did not become king himself. No additional information is provided about Rephaiah or his life. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the continuation of David's lineage and the preservation of the Davidic dynasty.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.21 only referred to as Rephaiah (רְפָיָה); son of Hananiah; a brother of Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Arnan, Obadiah and Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.21에 처음 언급되며 '르바야'라 불림. 하나냐의 아들. 블라댜, 여사야, 아르난, 오바댜와 스가냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 르바야는 다윗 왕의 후손으로, 그 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A Simeonite leader who attacked the Amalekites
persons.short: Rephaiah was a Simeonite leader who led an attack against the Amalekites during the time of Hezekiah.
persons.article: Rephaiah is mentioned in 1Ch.4.42 as one of the leaders of the Simeonites who led an expedition against the Amalekites during the reign of King Hezekiah. The Simeonites, descendants of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, sought to expand their territory. Rephaiah, along with Pelatiah, Neariah, and Uzziel, led 500 men to Mount Seir, where they attacked and defeated the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped earlier conflicts with Israel. The Simeonites then settled in the conquered territory. This event demonstrates the ongoing conflicts between Israel and its enemies and the efforts of the tribes to secure their inheritance in the Promised Land.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.42 only referred to as Rephaiah (רְפָיָה); son of Ishi; a brother of Pelatiah, Neariah and Uzziel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.42에 처음 언급되며 '르바야'라 불림. 이시의 아들. 블라댜, 느아랴와 웃시엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 르바야는 히스기야 시대에 아말렉 사람들을 공격하는 것을 이끈 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Tola, of the tribe of Issachar
persons.short: Rephaiah was a son of Tola, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar.
persons.article: Rephaiah is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar (1Ch.7.2). He was one of the sons of Tola, who was a descendant of Issachar, the ninth son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 lists the main families and clans within the tribe of Issachar. Rephaiah and his brothers, Uzzi, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, were described as brave warriors and heads of their families. The tribe of Issachar was known for its warriors and its men of understanding (1Ch.12.32).
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.2 only referred to as Rephaiah (רְפָיָה); son of Tola; a brother of Uzzi, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.2에 처음 언급되며 '르바야'라 불림. 돌라의 아들. 웃시, 여리엘, 야매, 입삼과 스므엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 르바야는 돌라의 아들로, 잇사갈 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Hur, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Rephaiah was the son of Hur and ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, who helped repair a section of the city wall.
persons.article: Rephaiah, the son of Hur, is mentioned in Neh.3.9 as one of the people who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. He was the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, indicating that he held a position of authority in the city. Nehemiah, who served as the governor of Judah under the Persian Empire, led the effort to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, which had been destroyed during the Babylonian conquest. Various individuals and families were assigned to repair specific sections of the wall. Rephaiah was responsible for repairing a section adjacent to the one repaired by Jedaiah, son of Harumaph. The mention of Rephaiah's involvement in the wall's reconstruction highlights the collective effort of the Jewish community to restore and fortify Jerusalem after their return from exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.9 only referred to as Rephaiah (רְפָיָה); a son of Hur.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.9에 처음 언급되며 '르바야'라 불림. 훌의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 훌의 아들 르바야는 예루살렘 지역 절반을 다스리며 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: People from Repha(?)
persons.brief: A race of giants who inhabited Canaan
persons.short: The Rephaim, also known as Zamzummin, were a race of giants who inhabited parts of Canaan before the Israelite conquest.
persons.article: The Rephaim, also referred to as Zamzummin by the Ammonites (Deu.2.20, were a race of giants who inhabited parts of Canaan before the Israelite conquest). They are first mentioned in Gen.14.5, where they were defeated by Chedorlaomer and his allies in Ashteroth-karnaim. The Rephaim were one of the groups that inhabited the land promised to Abraham's descendants (Gen.15.20). They were known for their great stature and strength, and their land was characterized by large, fortified cities (Deu.3.11, 13). The Rephaim were gradually dispossessed of their land by the Israelites during the conquest of Canaan. The Ammonites drove them out of the territory east of the Jordan River (Deu.2.20-21, while the Israelites, under Joshua's leadership, defeated Og, the king of Bashan, who was described as the last of the Rephaim )(Jos.12.4; 13.12). Despite their formidable reputation, the Israelites were able to overcome the Rephaim with God's help and claim their inheritance in the Promised Land (Jos.17.15).
persons.summary: People from Repha(?), first mentioned at Gen.14.5 referred to as Rephaim (רְפָאִים), or Zamzummin (זַמְזֻמִּים).
persons.summary_ko: 르바 족속. Gen.14.5에 처음 언급되며 '르바임'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 르바 족속(삼숨민이라고도 함)은 이스라엘 정복 이전 가나안 일부 지역에 살던 거인 족속이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, of the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Resheph was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
persons.article: Resheph is mentioned briefly in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher (1Ch.7.25). He was the son of Beriah, who was a descendant of Asher, the eighth son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 traces the lineage of the tribe of Asher and lists several of its prominent families and individuals. No additional information is provided about Resheph or his role within the tribe. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and descendants of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.25 only referred to as Resheph (רֶ֫שֶׁף); son of Beriah; a brother of Sheerah and Rephah; father of Telah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '레셉'이라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 세에라와 레바의 형제. 델라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레셉은 브리아의 아들로, 아셀 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Peleg, ancestor of Abraham
persons.short: Reu was the son of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham, living to the age of 239 years.
persons.article: Reu, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis 11, 1Chronicles 1, and Luke 3, was the son of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham. He was born when Peleg was 30 years old (Gen.11.18 and lived for a total of 239 years )(Gen.11.20-21). Reu fathered Serug at the age of 32 and lived an additional 207 years, having other sons and daughters (Gen.11.19-21). He is listed as one of the descendants of Shem, the son of Noah, and is part of the lineage that traces from Adam to Abraham, and ultimately to Jesus Christ (Luk.3.35). The name Reu means "friend" or "associate" in Hebrew. His inclusion in the genealogies emphasizes the continuity of the godly line from which the Messiah would eventually come.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.11.18 referred to as Reu (רְעוּ), or Reu (Ῥαγαῦ); a son of Peleg; father of Serug.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.11.18에 처음 언급되며 '르우'라 불림. 벨렉의 아들. 스룩의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르우는 벨렉의 아들이며 아브라함의 조상으로, 이백삼십구 세까지 살았다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Dan@Gen.30.6-1Ch, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev, Asher@Gen.30.13-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Zebulun@Gen.30.20-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev
persons.brief: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah
persons.short: Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
persons.article: Reuben was the firstborn son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah (Gen.29.32). As the firstborn, he held a position of prominence and was entitled to a double portion of the inheritance (Gen.49.3; Deu.21.17). However, Reuben lost his birthright due to his sin of sleeping with his father's concubine, Bilhah (Gen.35.22; 49.3-4; 1Ch.5.1). Despite this, Reuben showed concern for his younger brother Joseph and tried to save him from their brothers' plot to kill him (Gen.37.21-22, 29). Later, he offered to bear the blame if harm came to Benjamin on their journey to Egypt (Gen.42.37). When Jacob blessed his sons, he described Reuben as "unstable as water" and declared that he would not excel because of his past actions (Gen.49.3-4). The tribe of Reuben, along with the tribes of Gad and half of Manasseh, settled in the land east of the Jordan River (Numbers 32; Jos.13.15-23). They assisted the other tribes in conquering Canaan before returning to their inheritance (Joshua 22). In the time of the judges, the tribe of Reuben was criticized for not assisting Deborah and Barak in the fight against Sisera (Jdg.5.15-16). The tribe of Reuben is mentioned in the visions of Ezekiel and Revelation, symbolizing its place among the restored tribes of Israel (Ezk.48.6-7, 31; Rev.7.5).
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Reuben living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.29.32 referred to as Reuben or Reubenite (רְאוּבֵן), or Reubenite or Reuben (רְאוּבֵנִי), or Reuben (Ῥουβήν); son of Israel and Leah; a brother of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah; half-brother of: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.29.32에 처음 언급되며 '르우벤'이라 불림. 이스라엘과 레아의 아들. 시므온, 레위, 유다, 단, 납달리, 갓, 아셀, 잇사갈, 스불론, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 하녹, 발루, 헤스론과 갈미의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르우벤은 야곱과 레아의 맏아들로, 그 후손이 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나를 이루었다.
persons.article_ko: 르우벤은 이스라엘(야곱)과 레아의 맏아들이었다(창 29:32). 맏아들로서 그는 중요한 지위를 가졌고 기업의 두 몫을 받을 권리가 있었다(창 49:3; 신 21:17). 그러나 르우벤은 아버지의 첩 빌하와 동침한 죄로 인해 장자권을 잃었다(창 35:22; 49:3-4; 대상 5:1). 그럼에도 르우벤은 동생 요셉에 대해 염려를 보이며 형제들의 살해 음모에서 그를 구하려 했다(창 37:21-22, 29). 후에 그는 애굽으로 가는 여정에서 베냐민에게 해가 생기면 자신이 책임지겠다고 제안했다(창 42:37). 야곱이 아들들을 축복할 때 그는 르우벤을 '물의 끓음 같음'으로 묘사하며 과거의 행동 때문에 뛰어나지 못할 것이라고 선언했다(창 49:3-4). 르우벤 지파는 갓과 므낫세 반 지파와 함께 요단강 동편 땅에 정착했다(민 32장; 수 13:15-23). 그들은 가나안 정복을 도운 후 자기 기업으로 돌아갔다(수 22장). 사사 시대에 르우벤 지파는 드보라와 바락이 시스라를 대적하여 싸울 때 돕지 않았다는 이유로 비판받았다(삿 5:15-16). 르우벤 지파는 에스겔과 요한계시록의 환상에서 회복된 이스라엘 지파들 가운데 자리를 상징하며 언급된다(겔 48:6-7, 31; 계 7:5).

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: A Benjamite, son of Ibnijah
persons.short: Reuel was a Benjamite mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Reuel is briefly mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin (1Ch.9.8). He was the son of Ibnijah, who was a descendant of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 9 lists some of the prominent families and individuals who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. It is possible that Reuel and his family were among those who returned to Jerusalem and settled there. However, no additional information is provided about Reuel's life or specific role within the tribe of Benjamin. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to document the family lines and descendants of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.8 only referred to as Reuel (רְעוּאֵל); a son of Ibnijah; father of Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.8에 처음 언급되며 '르우엘'이라 불림. 이브니야의 아들. 스바댜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르우엘은 베냐민 족보에 언급된 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Esau and Basemath, a chief of Edom
persons.short: Reuel was a son of Esau and Basemath, and he became a chief in the land of Edom.
persons.article: Reuel was one of the sons of Esau, Jacob's brother, and Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael (Gen.36.4, 10, 13, 17; 1Ch.1.35, 37). He was born in Canaan before Esau moved his family to the hill country of Seir, which later became known as Edom (Gen.36.8-9). Reuel became one of the chiefs of Edom, indicating that he held a position of authority and influence among the Edomites (Gen.36.17; 1Ch.1.37). His sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah (Gen.36.13, 17; 1Ch.1.37). The Edomites, descendants of Esau, lived in the region south of the Dead Sea and were often in conflict with the Israelites throughout their history. The mention of Reuel and his descendants in the genealogies of Esau demonstrates the fulfillment of God's promise to make Esau into a nation (Gen.25.23 and provides insight into the early history and leadership of the Edomites).
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.4 only referred to as Reuel (רְעוּאֵל); a son of Esau and Mahalath; half-brother of: Eliphaz, Jeush, Jalam and Korah; father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.4에 처음 언급되며 '르우엘'이라 불림. 에서와 마할랏의 아들. 엘리바스, 여우스, 얄람과 고라의 형제. 나핫, 세라, 삼마와 미사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 르우엘은 에서와 바스맛의 아들로, 에돔 땅의 족장이 되었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother
persons.short: Reumah was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and she bore him four sons.
persons.article: Reumah is mentioned in Gen.22.24 as the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother. Nahor was the grandfather of Rebekah, who would later become the wife of Isaac, Abraham's son (Gen.24.15, 24). Reumah bore four sons to Nahor: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. This information is provided in the context of listing Nahor's descendants, which include both the children of his wife, Milcah, and those of his concubine, Reumah. In ancient Near Eastern culture, it was not uncommon for men to have both wives and concubines. Concubines held a lower social status than wives but were still considered a part of the family. The mention of Reumah and her sons in the genealogy of Nahor shows the breadth of his family and the various branches that would have descended from him. It also provides background information on the extended family of Abraham and the relatives of Rebekah, who would become an important figure in the history of Israel.
persons.summary: A concubine living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.24 only referred to as Reumah (רְאוּמָה); ; concubine of Nahor mother of Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.22.24에 처음 언급되며 '르우마'라 불림. 나홀의 아내. 데바, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 르우마는 아브라함의 형제 나홀의 첩으로, 그에게 네 아들을 낳아주었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Aram (Syria) during the reign of Ahaz
persons.short: Rezin was the king of Aram (Syria) who allied with Pekah, king of Israel, against Ahaz, king of Judah.
persons.article: Rezin was the king of Aram (Syria) during the reign of Ahaz, king of Judah (2Ki.15.37; 16.5-6, 9; Isa.7.1, 4, 8; 8.6; 9.11). He formed an alliance with Pekah, king of Israel, to attack Judah (Isa.7.1). Their goal was to replace Ahaz with a king who would join their coalition against the growing threat of the Assyrian Empire (Isa.7.6). The alliance between Rezin and Pekah caused great distress to Ahaz and the people of Judah (Isa.7.2).
