persons.short_ko: 레위인 스마야는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에서 노래를 이끌었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Shemaiah, a Levite who made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall near his house.
persons.article: Shemaiah was a Levite who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall under the leadership of Nehemiah. According to Neh.3.29, Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah (or 'Shechaniah'), the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs to a section of the wall next to his house. This was part of a larger effort to restore the walls and gates of Jerusalem, which had been damaged during the Babylonian conquest. Shemaiah's contribution, along with that of many others, helped to fortify the city and provide a sense of security for the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.29 only referred to as Shemaiah (שְׁמַעְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Shecaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.29에 처음 언급되며 '스마야'라 불림. 스가냐의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스마야는 자기 집 근처 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: False prophet who opposed Nehemiah
persons.short: Shemaiah, a false prophet who tried to intimidate Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Shemaiah was a false prophet who opposed Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall. In Neh.6.10, Nehemiah describes an encounter with Shemaiah, who was shut up in his house. Shemaiah claimed to have received a prophecy that Nehemiah should hide in the temple to avoid being killed by his enemies. However, Nehemiah recognized this as a false prophecy intended to intimidate him and discredit his leadership. Nehemiah refused to flee, stating that a man in his position should not enter the temple to save his life. This incident highlights the challenges and opposition Nehemiah faced while trying to restore Jerusalem and the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.10 only referred to as Shemaiah (שְׁמַעְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Delaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '스마야'라 불림. 들라야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 스마야는 예루살렘 성벽 재건 기간 동안 느헤미야를 위협하려 한 거짓 선지자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite warrior who joined David
persons.short: Shemariah, a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul.
persons.article: Shemariah was a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag while David was hiding from King Saul. According to 1Ch.12.5, Shemariah was among the Benjamites, along with Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, and Shephatiah, who were described as brave warriors, expert with the bow, and able to shoot arrows or sling stones right-handed or left-handed. These skilled warriors aligned themselves with David and provided him with valuable military support during his time of exile and conflict with Saul.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.5 only referred to as Shemariah (שְׁמַרְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.5에 처음 언급되며 '스마랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 용사 스마랴는 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Abijah@1Ki.14.31-Mat, Jeush@2Ch.11.19, Zaham@2Ch.11.19, Attai@2Ch.11.20, Ziza@2Ch.11.20, Shelomith@2Ch.11.20
persons.brief: Son of Rehoboam and Abihail
persons.short: Shemariah, a son of King Rehoboam and Abihail, the daughter of Eliab.
persons.article: Shemariah was a son of King Rehoboam of Judah and his wife Abihail, the daughter of Eliab. According to 2Ch.11.19, Shemariah was born to Rehoboam along with his brothers Jeush and Zaham. Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, was the first king of the southern kingdom of Judah after the division of the united monarchy. The mention of Shemariah and his brothers highlights the royal lineage of Rehoboam and the continuation of the Davidic dynasty in Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.11.19 only referred to as Shemariah (שְׁמַרְיָ֫הוּ); son of Rehoboam and Mahalath; a brother of Jeush and Zaham; half-brother of: Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '스마랴'라 불림. 르호보암과 마할랏의 아들. 아비야, 여우스, 사함, 앗대, 시사와 슬로밋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스마랴는 르호보암 왕과 엘리압의 딸 아비하일의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Shemariah, an Israelite who was among those who had married foreign women during the exile.
persons.article: Shemariah is mentioned in Ezr.10.32 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. This was part of a larger issue facing the Jewish community after their return to Jerusalem, as many had intermarried with the surrounding peoples. Ezra, a priest and scribe, called for the people to separate themselves from their foreign wives and children to maintain the purity and integrity of the Jewish faith. Shemariah, along with the other Israelites who had married foreign women, agreed to put away their wives in obedience to Ezra's directive.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.32 only referred to as Shemariah (שְׁמַרְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.32에 처음 언급되며 '스마랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스마랴는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Shemariah, another Israelite who was among those who had married foreign women during the exile.
persons.article: Shemariah is mentioned in Ezr.10.41 as another Israelite who had married a foreign woman during the Babylonian exile. This verse is part of a list of men who had taken foreign wives, which was a significant issue addressed by Ezra after the return of the exiles to Jerusalem. Ezra called for the people to separate themselves from their foreign wives and children to preserve the identity and religious purity of the Jewish community. Shemariah, like the other men on this list, agreed to put away his foreign wife in compliance with Ezra's instruction.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.41 only referred to as Shemariah (שְׁמַרְיָ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.41에 처음 언급되며 '스마랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 또 다른 스마랴도 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Zeboiim
persons.short: Shemeber, the king of Zeboiim, who joined the battle against Chedorlaomer and his allies.
persons.article: Shemeber was the king of Zeboiim, one of the five cities of the plain, during the time of Abraham. According to Gen.14.2, Shemeber allied himself with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and the king of Bela (Zoar) to engage in battle against Chedorlaomer king of Elam and his confederate kings. The battle, known as the Battle of the Valley of Siddim, resulted in the defeat of the kings of the plain and the capture of Lot, Abraham's nephew. This event prompted Abraham to mount a rescue mission, ultimately leading to the recovery of Lot and his possessions.
persons.summary: A king in Canaan living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.14.2 only referred to as Shemeber (שֶׁמְאֵ֫בֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.2에 처음 언급되며 '세메벨'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스메벨은 스보임 왕으로, 그돌라오멜과 그 동맹을 대적하는 전투에 가담했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Eber@1Ch.8.12, Misham@1Ch.8.12, Beriah@1Ch.8.13-, Shema@1Ch.8.13, Zebadiah@1Ch.8.17, Meshullam@1Ch.8.17, Hizki@1Ch.8.17, Heber@1Ch.8.17, Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18, Izliah@1Ch.8.18, Jobab@1Ch.8.18
persons.brief: Son of Elpaal, a Benjamite
persons.short: Shemed, a son of Elpaal, who built Ono and Lod with its towns.
persons.article: Shemed was a Benjamite, the son of Elpaal, mentioned in 1Ch.8.12. He is credited with building the cities of Ono and Lod, along with their surrounding towns. This brief mention of Shemed highlights the role of certain individuals in the development and expansion of settlements during the time of the chronicler's account.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.12 only referred to as Shemed (שָׁ֫מֶד); son of Elpaal; a brother of Eber, Misham, Beriah, Shema, Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.12에 처음 언급되며 '세멧'이라 불림. 엘바알의 아들. 에벨, 미삼, 브리아, 세마, 스바댜, 므술람, 히스기, 헤벨, 이스므래, 이슬리아와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세멧은 엘바알의 아들로, 오노와 롯 및 그 주변 마을들을 세웠다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the family of Merari
persons.short: Shemer, a Levite of the family of Merari, an ancestor of Ethan the singer.
persons.article: Shemer was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari, as recorded in 1Ch.6.46. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Ethan, a prominent Levitical singer during the time of King David. Shemer is listed as the son of Mahli and the father of Bani, indicating his place within the lineage of Merari. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and, later, in the temple. However, no specific details are given about Shemer's role or contributions as a Levite.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.46 only referred to as Shemer (שֶׁ֫מֶר); a son of Mahli; father of Bani.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.46에 처음 언급되며 '세멜'이라 불림. 마흘리의 아들. 바니의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세멜은 므라리 가문 레위인으로, 노래하는 자 에단의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Original owner of Samaria
persons.short: Shemer, the original owner of the hill of Samaria, which Omri bought from him.
persons.article: Shemer was the original owner of the hill of Samaria, which would later become the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel. According to 1Ki.16.24, Omri, the king of Israel, bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. Omri then built a city on the hill and named it Samaria, after Shemer, the previous owner of the land. This transaction marked the establishment of a new capital for the northern kingdom, which would play a significant role in the history of Israel. Apart from this land sale, no other information is provided about Shemer's life or background.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.24 only referred to as Shemer (שֶׁ֫מֶר).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.16.24에 처음 언급되며 '세멜'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 세멜은 사마리아 산의 원래 소유주로, 오므리가 그에게서 그 산을 샀다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Gilead, great-grandson of Manasseh
persons.short: Shemida, a son of Gilead and great-grandson of Manasseh, who was the ancestor of the Shemidaite clan.
persons.article: Shemida was a son of Gilead and a great-grandson of Manasseh, as mentioned in Num.26.32, Jos.17.2, and 1Ch.7.19. He was one of the descendants of Joseph through Manasseh, and his clan, the Shemidaites, is listed among the families of Manasseh who received an inheritance in the Promised Land. In the census conducted in the plains of Moab (Numbers 26), the Shemidaites are counted among the clans of Manasseh. Shemida's descendants are also mentioned in the context of the division of the land under Joshua (Jos.17.2, where they are allocated a portion of the territory assigned to Manasseh). Beyond these genealogical and territorial references, no further details are provided about Shemida's life or his role in the history of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.32 referred to as Shemida (שְׁמִידָ֑ע), or Shemidaite (שְׁמִידָעִי); son of Gilead; a brother of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem and Hepher; father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.32에 처음 언급되며 '스미다'라 불림. 길르앗의 아들. 아비에셀, 헬렉, 아스리엘, 세겜과 헤벨의 형제. 아히안, 세겜, 릭히와 아니암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스미다는 길르앗의 아들이며 므낫세의 증손자로, 스미다 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician during David's reign
persons.short: Shemiramoth, a Levite appointed by David to play the harp and lyres in the procession of the ark.
persons.article: Shemiramoth was a Levite who served as a musician during the reign of King David. He is mentioned in 1Ch.15.18, 20, and 1Ch.16.5 in the context of the transportation of the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. In 1Ch.15.18, Shemiramoth is listed among the Levites appointed by David to play the lyres and harps in the procession of the ark. He is specifically named among those who were to play the harps (1Ch.15.20). Later, in 1Ch.16.5, Shemiramoth is mentioned as one of the Levites who ministered before the ark of the Lord with musical instruments after it had been brought to Jerusalem. These references highlight Shemiramoth's role as a skilled musician and his participation in the significant event of bringing the ark to its new resting place in the capital city.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Shemiramoth (שְׁמִירָמוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '스미라못'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스미라못은 다윗이 언약궤 행렬에서 수금과 비파를 연주하도록 임명한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who taught the Law
persons.short: Shemiramoth, a Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in Judah.
persons.article: Shemiramoth was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. According to 2Ch.17.8, he was among the Levites sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. This educational mission was part of Jehoshaphat's reforms to strengthen the spiritual foundation of his kingdom. Shemiramoth, along with other Levites and officials, traveled throughout Judah, instructing the people in the Law of the Lord. This initiative highlighted the importance of religious education and the role of the Levites in preserving and transmitting the knowledge of God's commandments.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Shemiramoth (שְׁמִירָמוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '스미라못'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스미라못은 여호사밧이 유다에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Tola, a leader of Issachar
persons.short: Shemuel, a son of Tola and a leader of the tribe of Issachar during David's reign.
persons.article: Shemuel was a son of Tola and a leader of the tribe of Issachar, as mentioned in 1Ch.7.2. He is listed among the descendants of Issachar who were described as valiant men of might and heads of their fathers' houses. The passage states that during the reign of King David, the number of these mighty men from the tribe of Issachar was 22,600. Shemuel's inclusion in this list suggests that he was a prominent figure within his tribe and a respected warrior during David's time.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.2 only referred to as Shemuel (שְׁמוּאֵל); son of Tola; a brother of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai and Ibsam.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.2에 처음 언급되며 '스므엘'이라 불림. 돌라의 아들. 웃시, 르바야, 여리엘, 야매와 입삼의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스무엘은 돌라의 아들이며 다윗 왕 시대에 잇사갈 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Simeonite leader for land allotment
persons.short: Shemuel, the son of Ammihud, appointed as the leader of the tribe of Simeon for land allotment.
persons.article: Shemuel, the son of Ammihud, was a leader of the tribe of Simeon during the time of the allotment of the Promised Land. In Num.34.20, he is designated as the representative of his tribe who would assist Eleazar the priest and Joshua in dividing the land of Canaan among the nine and a half tribes settling west of the Jordan River. This appointment highlights Shemuel's leadership role within the tribe of Simeon and his responsibility in ensuring a fair distribution of the land inheritance among his people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.34.20 only referred to as Shemuel (שְׁמוּאֵל); a son of Ammihud.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.34.20에 처음 언급되며 '스므엘'이라 불림. 암미훗의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 암미훗의 아들 스무엘은 땅 분배를 위해 시므온 지파 지도자로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah
persons.short: Shenazzar, a descendant of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah, born during the Babylonian captivity.
persons.article: Shenazzar was a descendant of King Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin) of Judah, as recorded in 1Ch.3.18. He was born during the Babylonian captivity, after Jeconiah had been deported to Babylon by King Nebuchadnezzar. Shenazzar is mentioned alongside his brothers Salathiel (Shealtiel), Malchiram, Pedaiah, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. Being a descendant of the royal line of David, Shenazzar was part of the exiled Judean nobility in Babylon. However, no further details are provided about his life or any specific role he may have played during or after the exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.18 only referred to as Shenazzar (שֶׁנְאַצַּ֑ר); son of Shealtiel(?); a brother of Malchiram, Pedaiah, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.18에 처음 언급되며 '세낫살'이라 불림. 스알디엘의 아들. 말기람, 브다야, 여가먀, 호사마와 느다뱌의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스나살은 바벨론 포로 기간 동안 태어난 유다 왕 여고냐(여호야긴)의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite warrior who joined David
persons.short: Shephatiah, a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul.
persons.article: Shephatiah was a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag while David was hiding from King Saul, as recorded in 1Ch.12.5. He is listed among the Benjamites who were described as brave warriors, expert with the bow, and able to shoot arrows or sling stones right-handed or left-handed. These skilled warriors aligned themselves with David and provided him with valuable military support during his time of exile and conflict with Saul. Shephatiah's presence among David's followers demonstrates the loyalty and courage of those who rallied around the future king.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.5 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.5에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 베냐민 용사로, 다윗이 사울을 피해 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ruler of the Simeonites under David
persons.short: Shephatiah, the son of Maacah, appointed as the ruler over the tribe of Simeon during David's reign.
persons.article: Shephatiah, the son of Maacah, was the appointed ruler over the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King David, as mentioned in 1Ch.27.16. This passage lists the leaders of the tribes of Israel who served under David's administration. As the ruler of the Simeonites, Shephatiah would have been responsible for overseeing the affairs of his tribe and representing their interests before the king. This appointment highlights the organization and structure of David's kingdom, with each tribe having a designated leader to manage their specific concerns and maintain order within their territory.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.16 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); a son of Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.16에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 마아가의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 마아가의 아들 스바댜는 다윗 왕 시대에 시므온 지파를 다스리는 자로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem
persons.short: Shephatiah, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, descended from Jeroham.
persons.article: Shephatiah is mentioned in 1Ch.9.8 as one of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem. He is described as a descendant of Jeroham. This passage lists the inhabitants of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, indicating that Shephatiah was among those who resettled in the city. Being a Benjamite, he belonged to one of the tribes of Israel that had traditionally inhabited the area around Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.8 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); a son of Reuel; father of Meshullam.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.8에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 르우엘의 아들. 므술람의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 여로함의 후손으로, 예루살렘에 거주한 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jehoram@1Ki.22.50-Mat, Azariah@2Ch.21.2, Jehiel@2Ch.21.2, Zechariah@2Ch.21.2, Azariahu@2Ch.21.2, Michael@2Ch.21.2
persons.brief: Son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah
persons.short: Shephatiah, one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, who received gifts from his father.
persons.article: Shephatiah was one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, as recorded in 2Ch.21.2. He is mentioned alongside his brothers Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azaryahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. The passage states that Jehoshaphat gave his sons many gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, along with fortified cities in Judah. However, the kingdom was given to Jehoram, Jehoshaphat's firstborn son. The fact that Shephatiah and his brothers received gifts from their father suggests that they held positions of importance within the royal family, even though they did not inherit the throne.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.21.2 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); son of Jehoshaphat; a brother of Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu and Michael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.21.2에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 여호사밧의 아들. 여호람, 아사랴, 여히엘, 스가랴, 아사랴와 미가엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 유다 왕 여호사밧의 아들 중 한 사람으로, 아버지에게 선물을 받았다.

persons.description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: Son of David and Abital
persons.short: Shephatiah, the fifth son of David, born to him and his wife Abital in Hebron.
persons.article: Shephatiah was the fifth son of King David, born to him and his wife Abital during his reign in Hebron, as mentioned in 2Sa.3.4 and 1Ch.3.3. He was born before David's ascension to the throne over all Israel and the establishment of Jerusalem as the capital. Shephatiah is listed among David's six sons born in Hebron, along with Amnon, Chileab (Daniel), Absalom, Adonijah, and Ithream. Each of these sons was born to a different wife of David. Beyond his birth and lineage, no other details are provided about Shephatiah's life or any significant role he may have played in the kingdom.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.4 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); a son of David and Abital; half-brother of: Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 아들. 2Sa.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 다윗과 아비달의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 다윗의 다섯째 아들로, 헤브론에서 아내 아비달에게서 태어났다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
persons.short: Shephatiah, whose descendants were among the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
persons.article: Shephatiah is mentioned in Ezr.2.4, 8:8, and Neh.7.9 as an ancestor of some of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. In Ezr.2.4 and Neh.7.9, the descendants of Shephatiah are listed among the people who came back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town. The number of Shephatiah's descendants is given as 372 in both passages. In Ezr.8.8, Shephatiah's descendants are mentioned again among those who returned with Ezra to Jerusalem, with a slightly different count of 300 males. These references highlight the presence of Shephatiah's family line among the returnees from the Babylonian exile and their contribution to the repopulation of Jerusalem and the surrounding areas.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.4 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.4에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜의 후손은 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 포로 중에 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from exile
persons.short: Shephatiah, whose descendants were among Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
persons.article: Shephatiah is mentioned in Ezr.2.57 and Neh.7.59 as an ancestor of some of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. The descendants of these servants are listed among the people who came back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town. The presence of Shephatiah's descendants among Solomon's servants suggests that his family line had been employed in the service of the royal household during the time of King Solomon and continued this role even after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.57 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.57에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜의 후손은 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 솔로몬의 종들 중에 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Official during King Zedekiah's reign
persons.short: Shephatiah, the son of Mattan, an official during King Zedekiah's reign who opposed Jeremiah.
persons.article: Shephatiah, the son of Mattan, was an official during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, as mentioned in Jer.38.1. Along with other officials named Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashhur, Shephatiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to the people, urging them to surrender to the Babylonians to save their lives. The officials, including Shephatiah, reported Jeremiah's words to King Zedekiah and accused the prophet of discouraging the soldiers and the people. They requested permission to put Jeremiah to death, which the king granted. This incident highlights Shephatiah's opposition to Jeremiah's prophetic message and his role in the persecution of the prophet.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.38.1 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); a son of Mattan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.38.1에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 맛단의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 맛단의 아들 스바댜는 시드기야 왕 시대의 관리로 예레미야를 대적했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Judahite who settled in Jerusalem after exile
persons.short: Shephatiah, a descendant of Judah who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Shephatiah, a descendant of Judah, is mentioned in Neh.11.4 as one of the people who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is described as a son of Mahalalel, from the descendants of Perez, who was a son of Judah. This passage lists the inhabitants of Jerusalem who were chosen by lot to live in the city, with one out of ten settling there while the remaining nine stayed in other towns. Shephatiah's presence in Jerusalem indicates his involvement in the repopulation and restoration of the city after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.4 only referred to as Shephatiah (שְׁפַטְיָהוּ); a son of Mahalalel; father of Amariah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.4에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 마할랄렐의 아들. 아마랴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 유다의 후손으로 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착했다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Horite chief, son of Shobal
persons.short: Shepho, a Horite chief, the son of Shobal, who lived in the land of Seir.
persons.article: Shepho was a Horite chief mentioned in 1Ch.1.40 and Gen.36.23. He was the son of Shobal and lived in the land of Seir, which was later inhabited by the Edomites. The Horites were the original inhabitants of Seir before the descendants of Esau (the Edomites) displaced them. Shepho is listed among the chiefs of the Horites, indicating his position of authority within their tribal structure. These genealogical records provide insight into the early inhabitants of the region and their leadership.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.23 referred to as Shepho (שְׁפוֹ, שְׁפִי); son of Shobal; a brother of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal and Onam.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.23에 처음 언급되며 '스보'라 불림. 소발의 아들. 알완, 마나핫, 에발과 오남의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스보는 세일 땅에 살던 호리 사람 족장으로 소발의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who assisted Ezra and Nehemiah
persons.short: Sherebiah, a Levite who played a significant role in assisting Ezra and Nehemiah in their respective missions.
persons.article: Sherebiah was a prominent Levite who actively assisted Ezra and Nehemiah in their efforts to restore and rebuild the Jewish community after the Babylonian exile. In Ezr.8.18, he is mentioned as one of the Levites sent to Ezra by the chief men at Casiphia to serve in the house of God. Later, in Ezr.8.24, Sherebiah is listed among the twelve leaders of the priests entrusted with the task of safeguarding the offerings and vessels for the temple during the journey to Jerusalem. In Neh.8.7, Sherebiah is named as one of the Levites who helped the people understand the Law as Ezra read it aloud. He, along with other Levites, explained the meaning of the Law to the people, ensuring their comprehension. Furthermore, in Neh.9.4-5, Sherebiah is mentioned among the Levites who led the people in confession and worship during the ceremony of repentance and covenant renewal. These references highlight Sherebiah's significant role as a Levitical leader and his involvement in the religious and social restoration of the Jewish community after the exile. He contributed to the teaching of the Law, the proper handling of sacred offerings, and the spiritual guidance of the people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.8.18 only referred to as Sherebiah (שֵׁרֵֽבְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.18에 처음 언급되며 '세레뱌'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스레뱌는 에스라와 느헤미야 각자의 사명을 돕는 데 중요한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who sealed the covenant and led worship
persons.short: Sherebiah, a Levite who sealed the covenant and led worship during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Sherebiah was a Levite who played a significant role during the time of Nehemiah. In Neh.10.12, he is listed among the Levites who sealed the covenant, pledging to follow the Law of God. This covenant was a solemn commitment made by the people to obey God's commandments and maintain their identity as a holy nation. In Neh.12.8, Sherebiah is mentioned as one of the Levites who led the thanksgiving psalms during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. He, along with other Levites, was involved in the joyous celebration and worship that accompanied this significant event in the restoration of Jerusalem. Furthermore, in Neh.12.24, Sherebiah is named as one of the heads of the Levites, along with Hashabiah, who was responsible for leading the songs of thanksgiving and praise. This leadership role indicates Sherebiah's importance in the Levitical order and his contribution to the worship practices of the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.10.12 only referred to as Sherebiah (שֵׁרֵֽבְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.12에 처음 언급되며 '세레뱌'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스레뱌는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명하고 예배를 인도했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Machir and Maacah
persons.short: Sheresh, a son of Machir and Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Manasseh.
persons.article: Sheresh is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.7.16 as a son of Machir and Maacah. He appears in the genealogical record of the tribe of Manasseh, which is one of the tribes of Israel. Machir, his father, was the firstborn son of Manasseh and is described as the father of Gilead.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.16 only referred to as Sheresh (שָׁ֑רֶשׁ); son of Machir and Maacah; a brother of Gilead, Peresh and Hammolecheth; father of Ulam and Rakem.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.16에 처음 언급되며 '세레스'라 불림. 마길과 마아가의 아들. 길르앗, 마길의 딸(이름 미상), 베레스와 함몰레겟의 형제. 울람과 라겜의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세레스는 마길과 마아가의 아들로, 므낫세 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Anakite giant defeated by Caleb
persons.short: Sheshai, one of the Anakite giants, was defeated by Caleb during the conquest of Canaan.
persons.article: Sheshai was one of the Anakite giants who inhabited the land of Canaan before the Israelite conquest. In Num.13.22, he is mentioned along with his brothers Ahiman and Talmai as descendants of Anak, living in Hebron. The Anakites were known for their great stature and strength, which greatly intimidated the Israelite spies who were sent to scout out the land. In Jos.15.14 and Jdg.1.10, Sheshai is again mentioned as one of the three Anakite giants defeated by Caleb during the conquest of Hebron. Caleb, one of the faithful spies who had encouraged the Israelites to trust in God's power, was given Hebron as his inheritance. He successfully drove out Sheshai and his brothers, claiming the land for the tribe of Judah. The defeat of Sheshai and the other Anakites was a significant victory for the Israelites and a testament to Caleb's faith and courage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.13.22 only referred to as Sheshai (שֵׁשַׁי); son of Anak; a brother of Ahiman and Talmai.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.22에 처음 언급되며 '세새'라 불림. 아낙의 아들. 아히만과 달매의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세새는 아낙 족속의 거인 중 한 사람으로, 가나안 정복 당시 갈렙에게 패했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Jerahmeelite whose daughter married his Egyptian servant
persons.short: Sheshan, a Jerahmeelite who gave his daughter in marriage to his Egyptian servant, Jarha.
persons.article: Sheshan was a member of the Jerahmeelite clan, which was part of the tribe of Judah. He is mentioned in the genealogical record of 1Chronicles 2. Sheshan had no sons, only daughters (v. 34). Faced with the prospect of his lineage ending, Sheshan took an unconventional step. He gave one of his daughters in marriage to his Egyptian servant, Jarha (v. 35). This act allowed Sheshan's line to continue through his daughter and his servant. The passage goes on to list the descendants of Sheshan through this union, indicating that his decision had a lasting impact on his family line. This account highlights the importance of preserving one's lineage and the measures taken to ensure its continuation, even if it meant crossing social boundaries.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.31 only referred to as Sheshan (שֵׁשָׁן); a son of Ishi; father of Ahlai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.31에 처음 언급되며 '세산'이라 불림. 이시의 아들. 알래의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 여라므엘 사람 세산은 자기 딸을 애굽인 종 야하에게 시집보냈다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian noble in King Ahasuerus's court
persons.short: Shethar, one of the seven Persian nobles who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence.
persons.article: Shethar was one of the seven Persian nobles who served in the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) during the events described in the Book of Esther. In Est.1.14, he is mentioned along with the other nobles—Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan—as being closest to the king and holding the highest positions in the kingdom. These nobles had access to the king's presence and were consulted for their expertise in law and justice. When King Ahasuerus sought advice regarding Queen Vashti's refusal to appear before him, Shethar and the other nobles were called upon to provide counsel. Their advice led to the king's decree that Vashti be removed from her position and replaced, setting in motion the events that would lead to Esther becoming queen. Shethar's presence among the king's closest advisors indicates his high status and influence within the Persian court.
persons.summary: A prince of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Shethar (שֵׁתָר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '세달'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 세달은 아하수에로 왕을 알현할 수 있었던 페르시아의 일곱 방백 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian official who questioned the Jews' temple rebuilding
persons.short: Shethar-bozenai, a Persian official who questioned the legitimacy of the Jews' efforts to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Shethar-bozenai was a Persian official who, along with Tattenai the governor and their associates, questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem (Ezr.5.3). They sent a letter to King Darius, inquiring about the legitimacy of the Jews' actions (Ezr.5.6). In response, Darius issued a decree confirming the Jews' right to rebuild the temple and instructing Shethar-bozenai and his colleagues not to interfere (Ezr.6.6). Upon receiving the king's decree, Shethar-bozenai and the others diligently carried out the order, allowing the Jews to continue their work on the temple (Ezr.6.13). Shethar-bozenai's actions demonstrate the challenges faced by the Jews in their efforts to restore their religious and cultural identity after the Babylonian exile, as well as the role of Persian authorities in shaping the course of Jewish history during this period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.5.3 only referred to as Shethar-bozenai (שְׁתַר בּוֹזְנַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.5.3에 처음 언급되며 '스달보스내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스달보스내는 예루살렘 성전 재건을 위한 유대인들의 노력의 정당성에 의문을 제기한 페르시아 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Jesher@1Ch.2.18, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Ardon@1Ch.2.18, Mesha@1Ch.2.42, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: Son of Caleb's concubine Maacah
persons.short: Sheva, a son of Caleb's concubine Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Sheva is briefly mentioned in 1Ch.2.49 as a son of Caleb's concubine Maacah. He appears in the genealogical record of the tribe of Judah, specifically within the family line of Caleb.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.49 only referred to as Sheva (שְׁוָא); son of Caleb and Maacah; a brother of Sheber, Tirhanah and Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Shaaph; half-brother of: Hur, Jesher, Shobab, Ardon, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez and Achsah; father or founder of Machbenah and Gibea.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.49에 처음 언급되며 '스와'라 불림. 갈렙과 마아가의 아들. 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 디르하나, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압과 악사의 형제. 막베나와 기브아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세와는 갈렙의 첩 마아가의 아들로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of King Jehoshaphat's mother
persons.short: Shilhi, the father of Azubah, who was the mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
persons.article: Shilhi is mentioned in 1Ki.22.42 and 2Ch.20.31 as the father of Azubah, who was the mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. Jehoshaphat, the son of Asa, became king of Judah at the age of thirty-five and reigned for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. The mention of Shilhi in these passages serves to provide genealogical information about Jehoshaphat's maternal lineage, highlighting the importance of family connections in the royal line of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.42 only referred to as Shilhi (שִׁלְחִי); father of Azubah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.22.42에 처음 언급되며 '실히'라 불림. 아수바의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 실히는 유다 왕 여호사밧의 어머니 아수바의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Naphtali, ancestor of the Shillemites
persons.short: Shillem (or Shallum), a son of Naphtali and ancestor of the Shillemite clan.
persons.article: Shillem, also known as Shallum, was a son of Naphtali, as mentioned in Gen.46.24, Num.26.49, and 1Ch.7.13. He is listed among the sons of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Israel (or 'Jacob') and his family. In Num.26.49, the descendants of Shillem are referred to as the Shillemite clan, indicating that he was the ancestor of a distinct family group within the tribe of Naphtali. The inclusion of Shillem in these genealogical records emphasizes the importance of tracing one's lineage and maintaining family connections within the Israelite community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Naphtali living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.24 referred to as Shillem (שִׁלֵּם), or Shallum (שַׁלּוּם), or Shillemite (שִׁלֵּמִי); son of Naphtali; a brother of Jahzeel, Guni and Jezer.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.24에 처음 언급되며 '실렘'이라 불림. 납달리의 아들. 야스엘, 구니와 예셀의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 실렘(살룸이라고도 함)은 납달리의 아들이며 실렘 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: A name in Jacob's blessing on Judah
persons.short: Shiloh, a term used in Jacob's prophetic blessing on Judah, possibly referring to a future ruler or a place of rest.
persons.article: Shiloh is a term that appears in Gen.49.10 as part of Jacob's prophetic blessing on his son Judah. The verse states, "The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples." The exact meaning of "Shiloh" in this context is debated among scholars. Some interpret it as a reference to a future Messianic figure, a descendant of Judah who would rule over the nations. Others understand it as a place name, possibly referring to the city of Shiloh, where the tabernacle was once set up. In this interpretation, the verse would mean that Judah's leadership would continue until the coming of a time of rest or peace. Regardless of the specific interpretation, the mention of Shiloh in this passage underscores the importance and prominence of the tribe of Judah in the prophetic vision of Israel's future.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.49.10 only referred to as Shiloh (שִׁילֹה).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.49.10에 처음 언급되며 '실로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 실로는 야곱이 유다에게 준 예언적 축복에서 사용된 용어로, 미래의 통치자나 안식의 장소를 가리키는 것으로 보인다.

persons.description: People from Shelah@Gen.38.5-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Descendants of Judah living in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.short: The Shilonites or Shiloni were descendants of Judah living in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: The Shilonites or Shiloni were a group of People from Judah who lived in Jerusalem following the return from Babylonian captivity (Neh. 11:5). They are mentioned in the context of a list of leaders and people who resettled in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: People living at Shiloh or descended from Shelah(?), only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Shilonites (שִׁלֹנִי); progenitors of Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 셀라 자손(추정). Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '실로'라 불림. 스가랴의 부모.
persons.short_ko: 실로 사람들(실로니라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Suah@1Ch.7.36, Harnepher@1Ch.7.36, Shual@1Ch.7.36-, Beri@1Ch.7.36, Imrah@1Ch.7.36, Bezer@1Ch.7.37, Hod@1Ch.7.37, Shamma@1Ch.7.37, Ithran@1Ch.7.37-, Beera@1Ch.7.37
persons.brief: Son of Zophah, a descendant of Asher.
persons.short: Shilshah was a son of Zophah and a descendant of Asher.
persons.article: Shilshah is mentioned in 1Ch.7.37 as a son of Zophah, who was a descendant of Asher. He is listed among the genealogy of the tribe of Asher, but no additional information is provided about his life or role within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.37 only referred to as Shilshah (שִׁלְשָׁה); son of Zophah; a brother of Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Ithran and Beera.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.37에 처음 언급되며 '실사'라 불림. 소바의 아들. 수아, 하르네벨, 수알, 베리, 이므라, 베셀, 홋, 사마, 이드란과 브에라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 실사는 소바의 아들이며 아셀의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the family of Merari during David's reign.
persons.short: Shimea was a Levite of the family of Merari who served during King David's reign.
persons.article: Shimea was a Levite who belonged to the family of Merari (1Ch. 6:30). He is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites during the time of King David. As a Levite, he would have had duties related to the tabernacle or temple service, although his specific role is not elaborated upon in the text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.30 only referred to as Shimea (שִׁמְעָא, שִׁמְעָה); a son of Uzzah; father of Haggiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.30에 처음 언급되며 '시므아'라 불림. 웃사의 아들. 학기야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므아는 다윗 왕 시대에 섬긴 므라리 가문 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite singer appointed by David for temple worship.
persons.short: Shimea was a Levite singer appointed by David to lead worship in the temple.
persons.article: Shimea was a Levite appointed by King David to serve as a singer in the temple worship (1Ch. 6:39). He is listed among the descendants of Asaph, who were known for their musical abilities and roles in leading worship. As a temple singer, Shimea would have been responsible for providing musical accompaniment and leading the people in praising God.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.39 only referred to as Shimea (שִׁמְעָא, שִׁמְעָה); a son of Michael; father of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.39에 처음 언급되며 '시므아'라 불림. 미가엘의 아들. 베레갸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므아는 다윗이 성전 예배를 인도하도록 임명한 레위인 노래하는 자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Mikloth and nephew of Ner in Benjamin's genealogy.
persons.short: Shimeah (or Shimeam) was a Benjamite, son of Mikloth and nephew of Ner.
persons.article: Shimeah, also known as Shimeam, was a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies found in 1Ch.8.32 and 1Ch.9.38. He was the son of Mikloth and the nephew of Ner, who was the father of Kish and grandfather of King Saul. The genealogies in these passages trace the ancestry and descendants of Saul, indicating that Shimeah was part of the royal family of Israel from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.32 referred to as Shimeah (שִׁמְאָה), or Shimeam (שִׁמְאָם); a son of Mikloth.
persons.short_ko: 시므아는 베냐민 지파 미글롯의 아들이다.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.32에 처음 언급되며 '시므아'라 불림. 미글롯의 아들.

persons.description: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Zeruiah@1Sa.26.6-1Ch, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?)
persons.brief: Brother of David; father of Jonadab (or 'Jonathan').
persons.short: Shimeah (also known as Shimei, Shammah, or Shimea) was a brother of King David and the father of Jonadab (or 'Jonathan').
persons.article: Shimeah, also referred to as Shimei, Shammah, or Shimea, was one of King David's brothers (1Ch. 2:13). He was the son of Jesse and is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah. Shimeah had a son Jonadab (or 'Jonathan'). Jonathan is described as a skilled warrior who killed a Philistine giant (2Sa. 21:21; 1Ch. 20:7), while Jonadab is portrayed as a crafty man who helped Amnon, David's son, to deceive and rape his half-sister Tamar (2Sa. 13:3, 32).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.16.9 referred to as Shimeah (שִׁמְעָה), or Shimei (שִׁמְעִי), or Shammah (שַׁמָּה), or Shimea (שִׁמְעָא); son of Jesse; a brother of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, Zeruiah, Abigail(?) and Elihu; father of Jonadab.
persons.short_ko: 시므아(삼마)는 다윗의 형으로 이새의 셋째 아들이며 요나답의 아버지다.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 형제. 1Sa.16.9에 처음 언급되며 '삼마'라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 아들. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 엘리후, 스루야와 아비가일의 형제. 여호나답의 아버지.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of Jozacar, one of King Joash's assassins.
persons.short: Shimeath was an Ammonitess, the mother of Jozacar (or 'Jozachar'), one of the assassins of King Joash of Judah.
persons.article: Shimeath was an Ammonite woman mentioned in 2Ki.12.21 and 2Ch.24.26 as the mother of Jozacar (or 'Jozachar') (or Zabad), one of the two servants who conspired against and assassinated King Joash of Judah. The biblical text identifies her as an Ammonitess, indicating that she was a foreigner from the nation of Ammon. Apart from her son's infamous act, no other details about Shimeath's life are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A woman of the Ammonites living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.12.21 only referred to as Shimeath (שִׁמְעָת); mother of Jozacar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.12.21에 처음 언급되며 '시므앗'이라 불림. 시므앗의 남편(이름 미상)의 아내. 요사갈의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 시므앗은 암몬 여인으로, 유다 왕 요아스를 암살한 여사갈(요사갈)의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of King David's vineyards from Ramah.
persons.short: Shimei from Ramah was the overseer of King David's vineyards.
persons.article: Shimei from Ramah is mentioned in 1Ch.27.27 as the overseer of King David's vineyards. This chapter lists the various officials and administrators responsible for managing the king's assets and resources. As the overseer of the vineyards, Shimei would have been responsible for the cultivation, maintenance, and production of the royal vineyards. His association with Ramah, a city in the territory of Benjamin, suggests that he may have originated from that area.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.27 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.27에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 라마 사람 시므이는 다윗 왕의 포도원을 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Pedaiah and nephew of King Jeconiah.
persons.short: Shimei was the son of Pedaiah and nephew of King Jeconiah, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in 1Ch.3.19 as a son of Pedaiah and a brother of Zerubbabel. He is listed in the genealogy of King David's descendants, particularly in the line of King Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin). This genealogy traces the royal lineage after the Babylonian exile, suggesting that Shimei was born during or after the exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.19 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); son of Pedaiah; a brother of Zerubbabel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.19에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 브다야의 아들. 스룹바벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 브다야의 아들이며 여고냐 왕의 조카로, 다윗 후손 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah through Mishma.
persons.short: Shimei was a descendant of Judah through Mishma, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah's posterity.
persons.article: Shimei is listed in 1Ch.4.26-27 as a descendant of Judah through the line of Mishma. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah's posterity, along with his sons Hanan, Zaccur, and Shimei. The passage notes that Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, indicating that he had a large family. However, the text also states that his brothers did not have many children, suggesting that Shimei's lineage was more prominent or numerous compared to other branches of his family.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.4.26 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Zaccur.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.26에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 삭굴의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 미스마를 통한 유다의 후손으로, 유다 자손 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Reuben and son of Gog.
persons.short: Shimei was a descendant of Reuben and the son of Gog, mentioned in the genealogy of the Reubenites.
persons.article: Shimei, the son of Gog, is mentioned in 1Ch.5.4 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben. He is listed among the descendants of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). The genealogy in this chapter traces the lineage of the Reubenites, emphasizing their ancestry and descendants. Apart from being mentioned in this genealogical record, no other details about Shimei's life or role within the tribe are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.4 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Gog; father of Micah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.4에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 곡의 아들. 미가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 르우벤의 후손이며 곡의 아들로, 르우벤 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the family of Merari.
persons.short: Shimei was a Levite of the family of Merari, mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in 1Ch.6.29 as part of the genealogy of the Levites, specifically within the family of Merari. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the Kohathites and Gershonites. As a Levite, Shimei would have had duties related to the tabernacle or temple service, although his specific role is not detailed in the text. The genealogy in this chapter focuses on tracing the lineage of the Levites and their respective families.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.29 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Libni; father of Uzzah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.29에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 립니의 아들. 웃사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 므라리 가문 레위인으로, 레위인 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the family of Ladan during David's reign.
persons.short: Shimei was a Levite of the family of Ladan who served during King David's reign.
persons.article: Shimei was a Levite who belonged to the family of Ladan, also known as Libni (1Ch. 6:42; 23:9). He lived during the reign of King David and is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites. In 1Ch.23.9, Shimei is listed along with his brothers Shelomoth and Haziel as heads of their fathers' households. As Levites, they would have had responsibilities related to the service of the tabernacle or temple, although their specific duties are not detailed in the text.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.39 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Jehiel; father of Zimmah, Shelomith, Haziel, Haran.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.42에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 여히엘의 아들. 심마, 슬로못, 하시엘과 하란의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 라단 가문 레위인으로, 다윗 왕 시대에 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.offspring: Jakim@1Ch.8.19, Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Zabdi@1Ch.8.19, Elienai@1Ch.8.20, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Eliel@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21, Shimrath@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: Benjamite descendant of Shimei, son of Elpaal.
persons.short: Shimei was a Benjamite descendant of Shimei, the son of Elpaal.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in 1Ch.8.21 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He is listed as a descendant of Shimei, who was the son of Elpaal. This genealogy traces the lineage of several Benjamite families, particularly those who lived in Jerusalem. Apart from being mentioned in this genealogical record, no other details about this specific Shimei's life or role within the tribe are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.21 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); father of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.21에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 야김, 시그리, 삽디, 엘리에내, 실르대, 엘리엘, 아다야, 브라야와 시므랏의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 엘바알의 아들 시므이를 통한 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Influential figure during Solomon's reign; son of Ela.
persons.short: Shimei was an influential figure during Solomon's reign and the son of Ela.
persons.article: Shimei, the son of Ela, was an important figure during the reign of King Solomon. In 1Ki.1.8, he is mentioned alongside Zadok the priest, Benaiah, and others as not siding with Adonijah in his attempt to become king, suggesting his loyalty to Solomon. Later, in 1Ki.4.18, Shimei is listed as one of the twelve officers appointed by Solomon to provide food for the king and his household, indicating his trusted position within the royal administration.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.1.8 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Ela.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.1.8에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 엘라의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 솔로몬 통치 기간의 영향력 있는 인물로 엘라의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped purify the temple under King Hezekiah.
persons.short: Shimei was a Levite who assisted in purifying the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in 2Ch.29.14 as one of the Levites who participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He is listed alongside other Levites from the families of Kohath and Merari who responded to Hezekiah's call to consecrate themselves and cleanse the temple. The purification process involved removing all the unclean items from the temple and restoring proper worship practices. As a Levite, Shimei would have had specific duties related to the temple service and played a role in this important religious reform.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.14 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); son of Heman; a brother of Jehuel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 2Ch.29.14에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 여후엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 시므이는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite appointed as an overseer of temple contributions.
persons.short: Shimei was a Levite appointed as an overseer of the contributions brought to the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in 2Ch.31.12-13 as one of the Levites appointed to oversee the contributions brought to the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. After the temple was purified and proper worship was restored, the people brought tithes and dedicated gifts to support the priests and Levites. Shimei, along with Conaniah, Shemaiah, Amariah, and others, was entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing the storage and distribution of these contributions. This appointment demonstrates Shimei's trustworthiness and administrative capabilities in managing the temple resources.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.31.12 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a brother of Conaniah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.31.12에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 고나냐의 아버지(이름 미상)의 아들. 고나냐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 시므이는 히스기야 시대에 성전에 가져온 헌물을 감독하도록 임명되었다.

persons.description: David's adversary living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.
persons.short: Shimei was a Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion but later sought the king's forgiveness.
persons.article: Shimei was a Benjamite from the family of Saul who encountered King David during Absalom's rebellion (2Sa. 16:5). As David fled Jerusalem, Shimei cursed him, threw stones at him, and accused him of being a murderer and a wicked man (2Sa. 16:7, 13). After Absalom's defeat, Shimei met David at the Jordan River, seeking forgiveness for his actions (2Sa. 19:16, 18). Although Abishai, one of David's men, wanted to kill Shimei, David spared his life (2Sa. 19:21, 23). However, on his deathbed, David instructed his son Solomon to deal with Shimei, suggesting that he should not be left unpunished (1Ki. 2:8-9). Solomon later confined Shimei to Jerusalem and warned him that leaving the city would result in his death, a condition Shimei initially accepted (1Ki. 2:36-38). However, when Shimei violated this agreement by leaving Jerusalem to retrieve his runaway servants, Solomon ordered his execution (1Ki. 2:39-46).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.16.5 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Gera.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 대적자. 2Sa.16.5에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 게라의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 사람 시므이는 압살롬의 반역 때 다윗을 저주했으나 후에 왕의 용서를 구했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Benjamite ancestor of Mordecai.
persons.short: Shimei was a Benjamite, an ancestor of Mordecai, who lived in Susa during the Persian Empire.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in Est.2.5 as an ancestor of Mordecai, the cousin and guardian of Queen Esther. He is described as a Benjamite who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. This information provides background on Mordecai's lineage and explains how he came to be living in Susa, the capital of the Persian Empire, during the time of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). Shimei's inclusion in the genealogy highlights Mordecai's connection to the tribe of Benjamin and his Jewish heritage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.2.5 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי); a son of Kish; father of Jair.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.2.5에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 기스의 아들. 야일의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베냐민 사람 시므이는 페르시아 제국 시대에 수산에 살았던 모르드개의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Gershon and grandson of Levi.
persons.short: Shimei was a son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, and his descendants formed a Levitical clan.
persons.article: Shimei was the son of Gershon and the grandson of Levi (Num. 3:18; Ex. 6:17; 1Ch. 6:17). He was one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the descendants of Kohath and Merari. The Shimites, his descendants, formed a clan within the Levites (Num. 3:21) and were responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and temple service. In the time of David, the Shimites were among the Levites appointed to serve in the house of the Lord (1Ch. 23:7, 10). The clan of Shimei is also mentioned in the prophetic vision of Zechariah, where they are listed among the Levitical families that will mourn and seek cleansing from sin (Zec. 12:13).
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.17 referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי), or Shimeite or Shimeite (שִׁמְעִי); son of Gershon; a brother of Libni; father of Jahath, Zizah, Jeush and Beriah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 레위인. Exo.6.17에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림. 게르손의 아들. 립니의 형제. 야핫, 시사, 여우스와 브리아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 게르손의 아들이며 레위의 손자로, 그 후손이 레위 지파의 한 가문을 이루었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who married a foreign wife during the exile.
persons.short: Shimei was a Levite who had married a foreign wife during the Babylonian exile and agreed to send her away.
persons.article: Shimei is mentioned in Ezr.10.23 as one of the Levites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. After the return to Jerusalem, Ezra the scribe led a religious reform that required the Israelites to separate themselves from their foreign wives to maintain the purity of the nation. Shimei, along with several other Levites, priests, and leaders, was found to have married a foreign woman. As part of the reform, Shimei agreed to send away his foreign wife and children, demonstrating his commitment to following God's law and maintaining the religious and cultural identity of the Israelites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.23 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.23에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 시므이는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그녀를 내보내기로 동의했다.

persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife during the exile.
persons.short: Shimei was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Babylonian exile and agreed to send her away.

Shimei, along with several other Israelites, was found to have married a foreign woman. As part of the reform, Shimei agreed to send away his foreign wife, demonstrating his commitment to following God's law and maintaining the religious and cultural identity of the Israelites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.33 only referred to as Shimei (שִׁמְעִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.33에 처음 언급되며 '시므이'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 시므이는 바벨론 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 그녀를 내보내기로 동의한 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Judah and descendant of Caleb.
persons.short: Shimon was a son of Judah and a descendant of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Shimon is mentioned in 1Ch.4.20 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He is listed as one of the sons of Judah and a descendant of Caleb, the son of Hur. The genealogy in this chapter traces the lineage of several prominent families within the tribe of Judah, highlighting their descendants and their settlements. Apart from being mentioned in this genealogical record, no other details about Shimon's life or role within the tribe are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.20 only referred to as Shimon (שִׁימוֹן); father of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, Tilon.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.20에 처음 언급되며 '시몬'이라 불림. 암논, 린나, 벤하난과 딜론의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시몬은 유다의 아들이며 갈렙의 후손으로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jakim@1Ch.8.19, Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Zabdi@1Ch.8.19, Elienai@1Ch.8.20, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Eliel@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: Benjamite descendant of Shimei, son of Elpaal.
persons.short: Shimrath was a Benjamite descendant of Shimei, the son of Elpaal.
persons.article: Shimrath is mentioned in 1Ch.8.21 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. He is listed as a descendant of Shimei, who was the son of Elpaal. This genealogy traces the lineage of several Benjamite families, particularly those who lived in Jerusalem. Apart from being mentioned in this genealogical record, no other details about Shimrath's life or role within the tribe are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.21 only referred to as Shimrath (שִׁמְרָת); son of Shimei; a brother of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah and Beraiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.21에 처음 언급되며 '시므랏'이라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 야김, 시그리, 삽디, 엘리에내, 실르대, 엘리엘, 아다야와 브라야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시므랏은 엘바알의 아들 시므이를 통한 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.short: Shimri was one of David's mighty warriors from the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Shimri is mentioned in 1Ch.11.45 as one of the mighty warriors who joined David during his reign as king of Israel. He is described as a Benjamite, indicating that he belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. The passage lists several of David's mighty men, who were known for their bravery, military prowess, and loyalty to the king. As one of these warriors, Shimri would have played a significant role in David's military campaigns and in protecting the kingdom. However, no specific details about his individual exploits are provided in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.45 only referred to as Shimri (שִׁמְרִי); father of Jediael, Joha.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.45에 처음 언급되며 '시므리'라 불림. 여디아엘과 요하의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므리는 베냐민 지파 출신 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign, son of Hosah.
persons.short: Shimri was a Levite gatekeeper during David's reign and the son of Hosah.
persons.article: Shimri is mentioned in 1Ch.26.10 as a Levite who served as a gatekeeper during the reign of King David. He is described as the son of Hosah, who was also a gatekeeper. The passage lists the divisions of the gatekeepers and their responsibilities in guarding the entrances to the temple and its courtyards. Although Shimri is not explicitly mentioned as the firstborn, the text notes that his father appointed him as the chief, suggesting that he held a leadership role among the gatekeepers. As a gatekeeper, Shimri would have been responsible for maintaining the security and order of the temple premises.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.10 only referred to as Shimri (שִׁמְרִי); son of Hosah; a brother of Hilkiah, Tebaliah and Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.26.10에 처음 언급되며 '시므리'라 불림. 호사의 아들. 힐기야, 드발리야와 스가랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시므리는 다윗 왕 시대의 레위인 문지기이며 호사의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite descendant of Shimei in Hezekiah's time.
persons.short: Shimri was a Simeonite descendant of Shimei who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Shimri is mentioned in 1Ch.4.37 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon. He is listed as a descendant of Shimei and is described as one of the Simeonites who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. The passage suggests that Shimri and his fellow Simeonites were involved in expanding their territory by conquering and settling in the region of Gedor, which was previously inhabited by the Hamites. This event likely took place during Hezekiah's reign, indicating that Shimri was a contemporary of this king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.37 only referred to as Shimri (שִׁמְרִי); a son of Shemaiah; father of Jedaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.37에 처음 언급되며 '시므리'라 불림. 스마야의 아들. 여다야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므리는 히스기야 왕 시대에 살았던 시므온 지파 시므이의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped purify the temple under King Hezekiah.
persons.short: Shimri was a Levite who assisted in purifying the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Shimri is mentioned in 2Ch.29.13 as one of the Levites who participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah. He is listed alongside other Levites from the families of Elizaphan and Asaph who responded to Hezekiah's call to consecrate themselves and cleanse the temple. The purification process involved removing all the unclean items from the temple and restoring proper worship practices. As a Levite, Shimri would have had specific duties related to the temple service and played a role in this important religious reform.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.13 only referred to as Shimri (שִׁמְרִי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.13에 처음 언급되며 '시므리'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 시므리는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Issachar and progenitor of the Shimronites.
persons.short: Shimron was a son of Issachar and the progenitor of the Shimronite clan within the tribe of Issachar.
persons.article: Shimron is mentioned in Gen.46.13, Num.26.24, and 1Ch.7.1 as one of the sons of Issachar who went down to Egypt with Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is listed among the 70 members of Jacob's family who migrated to Egypt during the time of Joseph. Shimron became the progenitor of the Shimronite clan within the tribe of Issachar. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.24, the descendants of Shimron, known as the Shimronites, were counted among the clans of Issachar). This census was conducted to determine the military strength and organization of the Israelites before their entry into the Promised Land.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.13 referred to as Shimron (שִׁמְרוֹן), or Shimronite (שִׁמְרֹנִי); son of Issachar; a brother of Tola, Puah and Jashub.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.13에 처음 언급되며 '시므론'이라 불림. 잇사갈의 아들. 돌라, 부와와 야숩의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시므론은 잇사갈의 아들이며 잇사갈 지파 시므론 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Scribe who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
persons.short: Shimshai was a scribe who, along with Rehum the commander, wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes opposing the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Shimshai is mentioned in Ezr.4.8, 9, 17, and 23 as a scribe who, together with Rehum the commander, opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia. Shimshai and Rehum wrote a letter to the king, accusing the Jews of rebuilding the city and its walls, and claiming that this would lead to rebellion against the Persian Empire. In response to their letter, Artaxerxes ordered the work on the city to cease until further notice. Shimshai and Rehum, along with their associates, then went to Jerusalem and forcibly stopped the Jews from rebuilding the city. This opposition temporarily halted the reconstruction efforts until the reign of King Darius, who later allowed the Jews to resume their work on the temple and the city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.4.8 only referred to as Shimshai (שִׁמְשַׁי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.4.8에 처음 언급되며 '심새'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 서기관 심새는 지휘관 르훔과 함께 아닥사스다 왕에게 예루살렘 재건을 반대하는 편지를 썼다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Admah who rebelled against Chedorlaomer.
persons.short: Shinab was the king of Admah who, along with other kings, rebelled against Chedorlaomer, king of Elam.
persons.article: Shinab is mentioned in Gen.14.2 as the king of Admah, one of the five cities in the Valley of Siddim (the Salt Sea or Dead Sea region). He, along with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (Zoar), engaged in a rebellion against Chedorlaomer, the king of Elam, to whom they had been subject for twelve years. In the thirteenth year, these kings fought against Chedorlaomer and his allies in the Battle of the Valley of Siddim. The outcome of the battle is not explicitly stated for Shinab, but it is known that the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell into the tar pits, while the rest fled to the mountains.
persons.summary: A king of the city Admah living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.14.2 only referred to as Shinab (שִׁנְאָב).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.2에 처음 언급되며 '시납'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 시납은 아드마 왕으로, 다른 왕들과 함께 엘람 왕 그돌라오멜을 대적하여 반역했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite descendant of Ziza in Hezekiah's time.
persons.short: Shiphi was a Simeonite descendant of Ziza who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Shiphi is mentioned in 1Ch.4.37 as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon. He is listed as a descendant of Ziza and is described as one of the Simeonites who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. The passage suggests that Shiphi and his fellow Simeonites were involved in expanding their territory by conquering and settling in the region of Gedor, which was previously inhabited by the Hamites. This event likely took place during Hezekiah's reign, indicating that Shiphi was a contemporary of this king.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.37 only referred to as Shiphi (שִׁפְעִי); a son of Allon; father of Ziza.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.37에 처음 언급되며 '시비'라 불림. 알론의 아들. 시사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 십비는 히스기야 왕 시대에 살았던 시므온 지파 시사의 후손이었다.

persons.description: People from Shiphm(?)
persons.brief: People from Siphmoth who oversaw David's vineyards.
persons.short: The Shiphmites were people from Siphmoth who were in charge of King David's vineyards.
persons.article: The Shiphmites are mentioned in 1Ch.27.27 as the people from Siphmoth who were responsible for overseeing King David's vineyards.
