persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.5.14 referred to as Solomon (שְׁלֹמֹה), or Jedidiah (יְדִידְיָה), or Solomon (Σολομών, Σαλωμών); son of David and Bathsheba; a brother of Shammua, Shobab and Nathan; half-brother of: Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Tamar, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth; husband of daughter of Pharaoh and Naamah; father of Taphath, Basemath and Rehoboam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 2Sa.5.14에 처음 언급되며 '솔로몬'이라 불림. 다윗과 밧세바의 아들. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 다말, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 형제. 바로의 딸(이름 미상), 나아마와 솔로몬의 아내(이름 미상)의 남편. 다밧, 바스맛과 르호보암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 솔로몬(여디디야라고도 함)은 다윗과 밧세바의 아들로, 아버지를 이어 이스라엘 왕이 되었으며 지혜와 부, 예루살렘 첫 성전 건축으로 유명했다.
persons.article_ko: 솔로몬(여디디야라고도 함)은 다윗 왕과 밧세바의 아들이며 이스라엘의 세 번째 왕이었다(삼하 12:24; 대상 3:5). 그는 예루살렘에서 태어나 부모에 의해 솔로몬이라 이름 지어졌으나, 선지자 나단은 그를 '여호와께 사랑받는 자'라는 뜻의 여디디야라고 불렀다(삼하 12:25). 솔로몬은 아버지 다윗이 죽은 후 형 아도니야와의 권력 다툼 끝에 왕위에 올랐다(왕상 1-2장). 왕이 된 솔로몬은 백성을 다스릴 지혜를 구했고, 하나님은 그에게 뛰어난 지혜와 총명과 지식을 주셨다(왕상 3:1-15; 대하 1:1-12). 그의 지혜는 같은 아기를 주장하는 두 여인에 대한 유명한 재판 같은 공정한 판결을 통해 드러났다(왕상 3:16-28). 그의 통치 기간 동안 솔로몬은 야심찬 건축 사업을 벌였는데, 가장 유명한 것은 칠 년이 걸려 완성된 예루살렘의 첫 성전 건축이었다(왕상 6장; 대하 3-4장). 그는 또한 자신을 위한 왕궁을 짓고, 성읍들을 요새화하고, 강력한 군사력을 세웠다(왕상 7장; 9:15-19; 10:26-29; 대하 8:1-6; 9:25-28). 솔로몬의 통치는 번영과 부와 국제적 명성으로 특징지어졌다. 그는 이웃 왕국들과 동맹을 맺고, 광범위한 무역에 종사했으며, 외국 통치자들에게 조공을 받았다(왕상 5장; 대하 9:26-28; 10:1-29; 8:17-18; 9:1-28). 스바 여왕은 그의 지혜를 시험하러 솔로몬을 방문했고 그의 지식과 궁정의 화려함에 감명받고 떠났다(왕상 10:1-13; 대하 9:1-12). 그러나 솔로몬의 말년은 하나님께 대한 신실함의 쇠퇴로 특징지어졌다. 그는 많은 이방 여인과 결혼했고 그들의 종교 관습이 그에게 영향을 미치도록 허용하여 거짓 신들을 숭배하게 되었다(왕상 11:1-8). 그 결과 하나님은 솔로몬이 죽은 후 왕국이 나뉠 것이라고 선언하셨다(왕상 11:9-13). 솔로몬은 전통적으로 잠언, 전도서, 아가서를 포함한 여러 성경책의 저자로 여겨진다(잠 1:1; 전 1:1; 아 1:1). 그의 지혜와 잠언은 널리 칭송받고 연구되었다(왕상 4:29-34; 잠 1:1; 10:1; 25:1). 사십 년의 통치 후 솔로몬은 죽었고 그의 아들 르호보암이 뒤를 이었다(왕상 11:41-43; 대하 9:29-31). 예언된 대로 그가 죽은 직후 왕국은 북이스라엘 왕국과 남유다 왕국으로 나뉘었다(왕상 12장; 대하 10장).

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Companion of Paul from Berea, greeted the Roman church.
persons.short: Sopater (or Sosipater) was a companion of Paul from Berea who accompanied him on his journey to Jerusalem and later sent greetings to the church in Rome.
persons.article: Sopater, also known as Sosipater, was a Christian mentioned in the New Testament as a companion of the apostle Paul. He is first mentioned in Act.20.4 as a Berean who accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem, along with several others, including Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius, Timothy, Tychicus, and Trophimus. This journey took place during Paul's third missionary journey, as he was returning to Jerusalem with an offering for the believers there (Act.24.17). Sopater's inclusion in this group suggests that he was a trusted member of the early Christian community and a close associate of Paul. As a Berean, he likely came from the city of Berea (modern-day Veria) in Macedonia, where Paul had previously preached the gospel and found the people to be open-minded and receptive to his message (Act.17.10-12). Later, in Rom.16.21, a Sosipater is mentioned among those sending greetings to the church in Rome, along with Timothy, Lucius, Jason, and others. While it is not explicitly stated, it is likely that this Sosipater is the same person as Sopater from Berea, as both names were used interchangeably in ancient times. The mention of Sopater/Sosipater in these two passages highlights the close-knit nature of the early Christian community and the importance of personal relationships in the spread of the gospel. As a companion of Paul and a member of the delegation carrying the offering to Jerusalem, Sopater played a role in the practical support and unity of the church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.20.4 referred to as Sopater (Σώπατρος), or Sosipater (Σωσίπατρος); a son of Pyrrhus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.20.4에 처음 언급되며 '소바더'라 불림. 아리스다고와의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 소바더(소시바더라고도 함)는 베뢰아 출신 바울의 동행자로, 예루살렘 여정에 그와 동행하고 후에 로마 교회에 문안했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Sophereth (or Hassophereth) was the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
persons.article: Sophereth (or Hassophereth) is mentioned in Ezr.2.55 and Neh.7.57 as the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. Solomon's servants were a group of people who were assigned to work for King Solomon and his descendants, possibly as craftsmen, laborers, or officials. The name Sophereth appears in the list of returning exiles in the book of Ezra, while in the parallel passage in Nehemiah, the name is recorded as Hassophereth. This variation may be due to differences in spelling or transcription over time. The descendants of Sophereth are listed among the exiles who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, and Jeshua.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.55 referred to as Sophereth or Hassophereth (סֹפֶ֫רֶת).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.55에 처음 언급되며 '하소베렛'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 소베렛(핫소베렛이라고도 함)은 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 솔로몬의 종들 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Synagogue ruler in Corinth, co-sender of 1 Corinthians.
persons.short: Sosthenes was a synagogue ruler in Corinth who was beaten by a mob and later became a co-sender of Paul's first letter to the Corinthians.
persons.article: Sosthenes is mentioned twice in the New Testament, first in Act.18.17 and later in 1Co.1.1. In Acts, Sosthenes is identified as the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth during the time when Paul was preaching there. After the proconsul Gallio dismissed the charges brought against Paul by the Jews, the crowd seized Sosthenes and beat him in front of the tribunal. It is not clear whether Sosthenes was targeted because of his position or because he had shown sympathy toward Paul's message. Later, in 1Co.1.1, a Sosthenes is mentioned as a co-sender of Paul's letter to the Corinthian church, along with Paul himself. It is likely, though not certain, that this is the same Sosthenes who was beaten in Corinth. If so, this would indicate that Sosthenes had become a believer and was now working alongside Paul in the ministry. The inclusion of Sosthenes as a co-sender of 1 Corinthians suggests that he was a respected figure in the early church and had a significant role in the Corinthian congregation. His presence in the letter's opening greeting would have lent added authority and credibility to Paul's message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.18.17 only referred to as Sosthenes (Σωσθένης).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.18.17에 처음 언급되며 '소스데네'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 소스데네는 고린도의 회당장으로, 무리에게 매를 맞았고 후에 바울의 고린도전서 공동 발신인이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who returned from exile.
persons.short: Sotai was the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
persons.article: Sotai is mentioned in Ezr.2.55 and Neh.7.57 as the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. Solomon's servants were a group of people who were assigned to work for King Solomon and his descendants, possibly as craftsmen, laborers, or officials. The descendants of Sotai are listed among the exiles who returned to Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, and Jeshua, the high priest. This return took place around 538 BC, after the Persian king Cyrus issued a decree allowing the Jews to return to their homeland and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. The mention of Sotai and his descendants in the lists of returning exiles highlights the importance of maintaining family records and genealogies among the Israelites, even during the Babylonian captivity. It also shows that not only the prominent families but also the servants and workers were included in the return to Jerusalem and the rebuilding of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.55 only referred to as Sotai (סוֹטַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.55에 처음 언급되며 '소대'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 소대는 바벨론 포로에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 솔로몬의 종들 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Believer in Rome, greeted by Paul as a beloved friend.
persons.short: Stachys was a believer in Rome whom Paul greeted as his beloved friend.
persons.article: Stachys is mentioned briefly in Rom.16.9 as one of the individuals in Rome to whom Paul sends his greetings. Paul refers to Stachys as "my beloved" (Greek: ton agapēton mou), indicating a close personal relationship and affection between the two. The context of this greeting is found in the final chapter of Paul's letter to the Romans, where he extends personal greetings to various members of the church in Rome. This suggests that Stachys was a part of the Christian community in Rome and was known to Paul, either through personal interaction or by reputation. Although no further information is provided about Stachys in the biblical text, his inclusion in Paul's greetings indicates that he was a respected and valued member of the early church. The fact that Paul singles him out as a beloved friend suggests a strong bond of Christian love and fellowship between them.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.9 only referred to as Stachys (Στάχυς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.9에 처음 언급되며 '스다구'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스다구는 바울이 사랑하는 친구로 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 신자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Corinthian believer, baptized by Paul, sent to visit him.
persons.short: Stephanas was a believer from Corinth who, along with his household, was baptized by Paul and later visited Paul to provide support and encouragement.
persons.article: Stephanas was a member of the church in Corinth who is mentioned in 1Co.1.16 and 1Co.16.15-17. He and his household were among the first converts in Achaia (the region of Greece where Corinth was located) and were baptized by Paul himself (1Co.1.16). In 1Co.16.15, Paul commends the household of Stephanas for their dedication to the service of the saints. This suggests that Stephanas and his family were actively involved in ministering to the needs of the believers in Corinth and had distinguished themselves through their devotion and service. Later in the same chapter, Paul mentions that Stephanas, along with Fortunatus and Achaicus, had visited him and provided comfort and encouragement (1Co.16.17-18). Their presence was a source of joy and refreshment for Paul, who was facing challenges and opposition in his ministry. Paul urges the Corinthian church to submit to and acknowledge leaders like Stephanas, who had devoted themselves to the work of the ministry (1Co.16.16). This indicates that Stephanas was a respected leader in the Corinthian church, known for his service and commitment to the gospel. Overall, Stephanas emerges as an exemplary member of the early church, whose faith, service, and support were highly valued by Paul and the Corinthian believers.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at 1Co.1.16 referred to as Stephanas (Στεφανᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 1Co.1.16에 처음 언급되며 '스데바나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스데바나는 고린도 신자로, 그의 집안 사람들과 함께 바울에게 세례를 받았고 후에 바울을 방문하여 지지와 격려를 제공했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: One of seven deacons, full of faith, performed miracles, martyred.
persons.short: Stephen, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church, was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, performed miracles, and became the first Christian martyr after his powerful testimony before the Sanhedrin.
persons.article: Stephen was one of the seven men chosen by the early church in Jerusalem to serve as deacons, responsible for the daily distribution of food to widows (Act.6.1-6). He is described as being full of faith, wisdom, and the Holy Spirit (Act.6.5, 8). As Stephen continued to perform wonders and signs among the people, he faced opposition from members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen, who disputed with him (Act.6.9). However, they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke (Act.6.10). Consequently, they brought false charges against Stephen, accusing him of blasphemy against Moses and God (Act.6.11-14). When brought before the Sanhedrin (the Jewish high court), Stephen's face was said to have appeared like the face of an angel (Act.6.15). In his defense, Stephen delivered a powerful speech recounting Israel's history and their rejection of God's prophets, culminating in their rejection of Jesus as the Righteous One (Act.7.1-53). He accused his hearers of resisting the Holy Spirit and persecuting the prophets, just as their fathers had done (Act.7.51-52). Enraged by his words, the members of the Sanhedrin gnashed their teeth at Stephen, but he, full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God (Act.7.54-55). When he declared this vision, they dragged him out of the city and stoned him to death, with a young man named Saul (later known as Paul) guarding the garments of those who carried out the execution (Act.7.56-60). As he was being stoned, Stephen called out to the Lord Jesus to receive his spirit and, echoing Jesus' words on the cross, asked God not to hold this sin against his persecutors (Act.7.59-60). Devout men buried Stephen and lamented deeply over him (Act.8.2). Stephen's martyrdom marked a significant turning point in the early church, as it sparked a great persecution against the church in Jerusalem, leading to the dispersion of believers throughout Judea and Samaria (Act.8.1, 11:19). This dispersion ultimately led to the spread of the gospel beyond Jerusalem, fulfilling Jesus' command to be his witnesses to the ends of the earth (Act.1.8).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.6.5 only referred to as Stephen (Στέφανος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '스데반'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스데반은 초대교회가 선택한 일곱 집사 중 한 사람으로, 믿음과 성령이 충만하여 기적을 행했으며 산헤드린 앞에서 강력한 증언을 한 후 최초의 그리스도교 순교자가 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Harnepher@1Ch.7.36, Shual@1Ch.7.36-, Beri@1Ch.7.36, Imrah@1Ch.7.36, Bezer@1Ch.7.37, Hod@1Ch.7.37, Shamma@1Ch.7.37, Shilshah@1Ch.7.37, Ithran@1Ch.7.37-, Beera@1Ch.7.37
persons.brief: Son of Zophah, from the tribe of Asher
persons.short: Suah, a descendant of Asher mentioned in a genealogy.
persons.article: Suah is mentioned in 1Ch.7.36 as a son of Zophah, who was a descendant of Asher. No other details are provided about Suah in the biblical text. He is listed in a genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Asher living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.36 only referred to as Suah (סוּחַ); son of Zophah; a brother of Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran and Beera.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.36에 처음 언급되며 '수아'라 불림. 소바의 아들. 하르네벨, 수알, 베리, 이므라, 베셀, 홋, 사마, 실사, 이드란과 브에라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 수아는 족보에 언급된 아셀의 후손이었다.

persons.description: People from Sukki(?)
persons.brief: African people who invaded Judah under Shishak
persons.short: The Sukkiim were an African people who joined Shishak's invasion of Judah.
persons.article: The Sukkiim are mentioned in 2Ch.12.3 as part of the army that invaded Judah under Shishak king of Egypt during the reign of Rehoboam. They are listed along with the Lubim and Cushites, indicating they were likely an African people. No other details are provided about the Sukkiim in the Bible. They may have been Libyan mercenaries or allies of the Egyptians.
persons.summary: People from Sukki(?), only mentioned at 2Ch.12.3 only referred to as Sukkiim (סֻכִּיִּים).
persons.summary_ko: 숙. 2Ch.12.3에 처음 언급되며 '숙'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 숙 족속은 시삭의 유다 침공에 합류한 아프리카 민족이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Woman who helped support Jesus and his disciples
persons.short: Susanna was one of the women who provided for Jesus out of her resources.
persons.article: Susanna is mentioned in Luk.8.3 as one of the women who accompanied Jesus and the twelve disciples and helped support them out of her own resources. She is listed along with Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and many other women. This suggests Susanna was a woman of some means who generously contributed to the material needs of Jesus' ministry.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Luk.8.3 only referred to as Susanna (Σουσάννα).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Luk.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '수산나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 수산나는 자기 재산으로 예수님을 섬긴 여인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of the Manassite spy Gaddi
persons.short: Susi was the father of Gaddi, the spy from the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Susi is mentioned in Num.13.11 as the father of Gaddi, who was the man chosen from the tribe of Manasseh to spy out the land of Canaan. Susi is not mentioned again in the Bible. His name suggests he was likely a member of the tribe of Manasseh, but no other details are given about his background or life.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.11 only referred to as Susi (סוּסִי); father of Gaddi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.11에 처음 언급되며 '수시'라 불림. 갓디의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 수시는 므낫세 지파 정탐꾼 갓디의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Woman in the Philippian church whom Paul exhorted
persons.short: Syntyche was a prominent woman in Philippi whom Paul urged to reconcile with Euodia.
persons.article: Syntyche was a woman in the church at Philippi. In Php.4.2, Paul specifically names her and Euodia, and urges them to reconcile and be of the same mind in the Lord. This exhortation suggests the two women may have been in a conflict of some kind. That they are named and addressed personally indicates Syntyche and Euodia were prominent members of the Philippian congregation. Paul describes them as women who labored with him in the gospel.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Php.4.2 only referred to as Syntyche (Συντύχη).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Php.4.2에 처음 언급되며 '순두게'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 순두게는 빌립보의 저명한 여성으로, 바울이 유오디아와 화해하도록 권면했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Family of temple servants who returned from exile
persons.short: The Tabbaoth were a family of temple servants who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: The Tabbaoth are mentioned in Ezr.2.43 and Neh.7.46 as one of the families of temple servants who returned to Judah from Babylonian captivity. They are listed along with the Nephisim, Keros, Siaha, Padon, Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub, Hagab, Shamlai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Asnah, Meunim, Nephusim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha. No other details are provided about the specific duties or history of the Tabbaoth family. As temple servants, they likely assisted the Levites in the maintenance and operation of the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.43 only referred to as Tabbaoth (טַבָּעוֹת).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.43에 처음 언급되며 '답바욧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 답바옷은 바벨론 포로에서 유다로 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Man whom Syria and Ephraim wanted to make king of Judah
persons.short: Tabeal was the man Syria and Ephraim conspired to make king of Judah in place of Ahaz.
persons.article: Tabeal is mentioned in Isa.7.6 as the man whom Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel (Ephraim) planned to install as king of Judah in place of Ahaz. This was part of their plot to invade Judah and replace Ahaz with a puppet ruler. The name Tabeal is Aramaic and may mean "Good is God" or "God is good." No other details are provided about Tabeal's identity or background. The conspiracy of Syria and Ephraim against Judah was part of the Syro-Ephraimite War, which occurred around 735-732 BC. However, their plot did not succeed, as Ahaz appealed to Assyria for help, and the Assyrian king defeated Syria and Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Isa.7.6 only referred to as Tabeal (טָֽבְאַ֑ל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Isa.7.6에 처음 언급되며 '다브엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다브엘은 시리아와 에브라임이 아하스를 대신하여 유다 왕으로 세우려 했던 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian official involved in accusing the Jews to Artaxerxes
persons.short: Tabeel was a Persian official who joined in writing an accusation against the Jews to Artaxerxes.
persons.article: Tabeel is mentioned in Ezr.4.7 as one of the Persian officials who wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes accusing the Jews of rebuilding Jerusalem. He is listed along with Bishlam and Mithredath. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated. No other details are provided about Tabeel's background or role. As a Persian official in the province Beyond the River, he would have had some authority in the region. His accusation against the Jews aimed to stop their efforts to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.4.7 only referred to as Tabeel (טָֽבְאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.4.7에 처음 언급되며 '다브엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다브엘은 아닥사스다에게 유대인을 고발하는 편지를 쓰는 데 가담한 페르시아 관리였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Charitable woman in Joppa whom Peter raised from the dead
persons.short: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a beloved disciple in Joppa known for her charitable works, whom Peter raised from the dead.
persons.article: Tabitha, also known by her Greek name Dorcas, was a disciple who lived in Joppa. Act.9.36 describes her as a woman full of good works and acts of charity. When she became ill and died, the disciples in Joppa sent for Peter, who was in nearby Lydda. They showed him the tunics and garments Dorcas had made for the widows while she was with them, attesting to her life of service. Peter sent everyone out of the room, knelt down, and prayed. Then he told Tabitha to arise, and she opened her eyes and sat up. Peter presented her alive to the saints and widows, and this miracle became known throughout Joppa, causing many to believe in the Lord. The name Tabitha in Aramaic and Dorcas in Greek both mean "gazelle." Tabitha is an example of a faithful disciple who was beloved for her practical service and generosity to those in need.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.9.36 referred to as Tabitha (Ταβιθά), or Dorcas (Δορκάς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Act.9.36에 처음 언급되며 '다비다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다비다(도르가라고도 함)는 욥바의 사랑받는 제자로 자선 사업으로 알려졌으며, 베드로가 그녀를 죽음에서 살렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Ben-hadad I, king of Syria
persons.short: Tabrimmon was the father of Ben-hadad I, the king of Syria who was an ally of Asa king of Judah.
persons.article: Tabrimmon is mentioned in 1Ki.15.18 as the father of Ben-hadad I, who was the king of Syria in Damascus during the reign of Asa king of Judah. Asa made a treaty with Ben-hadad I and sent him silver and gold from the temple treasuries to persuade him to break his treaty with Baasha king of Israel. Ben-hadad I agreed and attacked the northern cities of Israel, forcing Baasha to stop building Ramah. No other details are provided about Tabrimmon. His name may mean "good is Rimmon," referring to a Syrian deity. As the father of Ben-hadad I, Tabrimmon was likely also a king of Syria before his son succeeded him on the throne.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.15.18 only referred to as Tabrimmon (טַבְרִמּוֹן); a son of Hezion; father of Ben-hadad.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '다브림몬'이라 불림. 헤시온의 아들. 벤하닷의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 다브림몬은 유다 왕 아사와 동맹한 시리아 왕 벤하닷 1세의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Telah, from the tribe of Ephraim
persons.short: Tahan was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Telah and father of Ladan.
persons.article: Tahan is mentioned in 1Ch.7.25 as a descendant of Ephraim. He was the son of Telah and the father of Ladan. This genealogy traces the descendants of Ephraim, showing the generations between Ephraim and Joshua. No other details are provided about Tahan's life or role in the tribe. He lived during the time the Israelites were in Egypt.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.25 only referred to as Tahan (תַּ֫חַן); a son of Telah; father of Ladan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '다한'이라 불림. 델라의 아들. 라단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 다한은 델라의 아들이며 에브라임의 후손으로, 라단의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Ephraim, ancestor of the Tahanites clan
persons.short: Tahan was a son of Ephraim and the ancestor of the Tahanites clan.
persons.article: Tahan is mentioned in Num.26.35 as a son of Ephraim and the ancestor of the Tahanites clan. The Tahanites were one of the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, descended from Tahan. No other details are provided about Tahan's life or role in the tribe. As a son of Ephraim, he would have been born in Egypt before the Exodus.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.26.35 referred to as Tahan (תַּ֫חַן), or Tahanite (תַּחֲנִי); son of Ephraim; a brother of Shuthelah, Becher, Ezer, Elead and Beriah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.35에 처음 언급되며 '다한'이라 불림. 에브라임의 아들. 수델라, 베겔, 에셀, 엘르앗과 브리아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다한은 에브라임의 아들이며 다한 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor and Reumah
persons.short: Tahash was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.
persons.article: Tahash is mentioned in Gen.22.24 as a son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah. Nahor was Abraham's brother, making Tahash Abraham's nephew. Tahash is listed along with his brothers Tebah, Gaham, and Maacah. No other details are provided about Tahash's life or descendants. As a son of Nahor, he was born in Mesopotamia, where Abraham and his family originated.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.24 only referred to as Tahash (תַּ֫חַשׁ); son of Nahor and Reumah; a brother of Tebah, Gaham and Maacah; half-brother of: Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, Bethuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.24에 처음 언급되며 '다하스'라 불림. 나홀과 르우마의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 가함과 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다하스는 아브라함의 형제 나홀이 첩 르우마를 통해 얻은 아들이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the Kohathite clan, son of Assir
persons.short: Tahath was a Levite of the Kohathite clan, the son of Assir and father of Uriel.
persons.article: Tahath is mentioned in 1Ch.6.24,37 as a Levite of the Kohathite clan. He was the son of Assir and the father of Uriel. This genealogy lists the descendants of Levi, tracing the ancestry of the prophet Samuel and his sons. As a Kohathite Levite, Tahath would have been involved in the transportation and care of the sacred objects of the tabernacle.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.24 only referred to as Tahath (תַּ֫חַת); a son of Assir; father of Uriel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.24에 처음 언급되며 '다핫'이라 불림. 앗실의 아들. 우리엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 다핫은 아실의 아들이며 웃시엘의 아버지인 고핫 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Ephraim
persons.short: Tahath, a descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.
persons.article: Tahath was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Joseph, mentioned in the genealogy found in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Bered and the father of Eleadah. This genealogy traces the lineage of the tribe of Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, demonstrating the importance of family lines and tribal affiliations in ancient Israelite society.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.20a only referred to as Tahath (תַּ֫חַת); a son of Bered; father of Eleadah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.20a에 처음 언급되며 '다핫'이라 불림. 베렛의 아들. 엘르아다의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 다핫은 족보에 언급된 에브라임의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Another descendant of Ephraim
persons.short: Tahath, another descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.
persons.article: Tahath was a second descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy found in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Eleadah and the father of Zabad. The repetition of the name Tahath within the same genealogy suggests that it may have been a common name within the tribe of Ephraim or that naming children after ancestors was a common practice. The inclusion of both Tahaths in the genealogy highlights the importance of preserving and recording family lineages in ancient Israelite culture.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.20b only referred to as Tahath (תַּ֫חַת); a son of Eleadah; father of Zabad.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.20b에 처음 언급되며 '다핫'이라 불림. 엘르아다의 아들. 사밧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 또 다른 다핫도 족보에 언급된 에브라임의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Egyptian queen who raised Hadad the Edomite
persons.short: Tahpenes was the queen of Egypt who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite.
persons.article: Tahpenes is mentioned in 1Ki.11.19-20 as the queen of Egypt during the time when Hadad the Edomite fled there to escape from King Solomon. Pharaoh gave Hadad his sister-in-law, the sister of Queen Tahpenes, in marriage. Queen Tahpenes raised Hadad's son Genubath in Pharaoh's palace among the princes of Egypt. No other details are provided about Tahpenes' life or reign as queen. Her actions in arranging the marriage and raising Genubath show the favor Hadad found with the Egyptian royal family.
persons.summary: A woman of the Egyptians living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.11.19 only referred to as Tahpenes (תַּחְפְּנֵיס); wife of Pharaoh; mother of daughter of Pharaoh.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '다브네스'라 불림. 다브네스의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 다브네스의 자매(이름 미상)의 자매. 바로의 아내. 바로의 딸(이름 미상)의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 다브네스는 애굽의 왕비로, 자기 자매를 에돔 사람 하닷과 결혼시켰다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Geshur; father of David's wife Maacah
persons.short: Talmai was the king of Geshur and father of Maacah, one of David's wives and mother of Absalom.
persons.article: Talmai is mentioned in 2Sa.3.3 and 1Ch.3.2 as the father of Maacah, who was one of David's wives and the mother of Absalom. Talmai was the king of Geshur, an Aramean city-state to the northeast of Israel. After Absalom murdered his half-brother Amnon, he fled to Geshur and stayed with his grandfather King Talmai for three years before Joab brought about his reconciliation with David (2Sa.13.37).
persons.summary: A king of the Ammonites living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.3.3 only referred to as Talmai (תַּלְמַי); a son of Ammihud; father of Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 2Sa.3.3에 처음 언급되며 '달매'라 불림. 암미훗의 아들. 마아가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 달매는 그술 왕이며 다윗의 아내 중 한 사람이자 압살롬의 어머니인 마아가의 아버지였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Anakim king of Hebron, defeated by Judah
persons.short: Talmai was one of the Anakim kings of Hebron defeated by Caleb and the men of Judah.
persons.article: Talmai is mentioned in Num.13.22, Jos.15.14, and Jdg.1.10 as one of the Anakim who were the pre-Israelite inhabitants of Hebron. The Anakim were giants, descendants of Anak, and were feared by the Israelite spies. Talmai, along with Sheshai and Ahiman, was a king of Hebron. After the conquest of Canaan, Caleb drove out these three Anakim kings when the city was allotted to him and the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A king living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.13.22 only referred to as Talmai (תַּלְמַי); son of Anak; a brother of Ahiman and Sheshai.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 왕. Num.13.22에 처음 언급되며 '달매'라 불림. 아낙의 아들. 아히만과 세새의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 달매는 갈렙과 유다 사람들에게 패배한 헤브론의 아낙 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylonian exile
persons.short: Talmon was a Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylon and served at the temple.
persons.article: Talmon is mentioned in 1Ch.9.17, Ezr.2.42, Neh.7.45, 11:19, and Neh.12.25 as a Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylonian captivity. He and his descendants were responsible for guarding the gates and storerooms of the temple. The gatekeepers were organized by families and rotated their duties. Talmon is listed along with Akkub, Shallum, and Ahiman as the chief gatekeepers. His descendants continued to serve faithfully in this role in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.17 only referred to as Talmon (טַלְמוֹן).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. 1Ch.9.17에 처음 언급되며 '달몬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 달몬은 바벨론에서 돌아와 성전에서 섬긴 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: David's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Amnon@2Sa.3.2-1Ch, Chileab@2Sa.3.3-1Ch, Absalom@2Sa.3.3-Psa, Adonijah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Shephatiah@2Sa.3.4-1Ch, Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch, Shammua@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Shobab@2Sa.5.14-1Ch, Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk, Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act, Ibhar@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishua@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Nepheg@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Japhia@2Sa.5.15-1Ch, Elishama@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliada@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Eliphelet@2Sa.5.16-1Ch, Elpelet@1Ch.3.6-, Nogah@1Ch.3.7-, Jerimoth@2Ch.11.18
persons.brief: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon
persons.short: Tamar was David's daughter who was raped by her half-brother Amnon, leading to tragic consequences.
persons.article: Tamar was the beautiful daughter of King David and full sister of Absalom (2Sa.13.1; 1Ch.3.9). She was raped by her half-brother Amnon, who then rejected her (2Sa.13.1-19). Tamar's tragedy led to Absalom's murder of Amnon and eventual rebellion against David (2Sa.13.20-39). Her story illustrates the dysfunctional relationships and violence within David's family.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.13.1 only referred to as Tamar (תָּמָר); daughter of David and Maacah; a sister of Amnon, Chileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, Elpelet, Nogah and Jerimoth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 다윗의 딸. 2Sa.13.1에 처음 언급되며 '다말'이라 불림. 다윗과 마아가의 딸. 암논, 길르압, 압살롬, 아도니야, 스바댜, 이드르암, 삼무아, 소밥, 나단, 솔로몬, 입할, 엘리수아, 네벡, 야비아, 엘리사마, 엘랴다, 엘리벨렛, 엘리벨렛, 노가와 여레못의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 다말은 다윗의 딸로, 이복형제 암논에게 강간당해 비극적인 결과를 초래했다.
persons.article_ko: 다말은 다윗 왕의 아름다운 딸이며 압살롬의 친누이였다(삼하 13:1; 대상 3:9). 그녀는 이복형제 암논에게 강간당한 후 거부당했다(삼하 13:1-19). 다말의 비극은 압살롬이 암논을 살해하고 결국 다윗을 대적하여 반역하는 것으로 이어졌다(삼하 13:20-39). 그녀의 이야기는 다윗 가족 내의 역기능적인 관계와 폭력을 보여준다.

persons.description: Absalom's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Absalom's beautiful daughter
persons.short: Tamar was the beautiful daughter of Absalom, named after his tragic sister.
persons.article: Tamar is mentioned in 2Sa.14.27 as the beautiful daughter of Absalom. She was likely named after Absalom's full sister Tamar, who was tragically raped by their half-brother Amnon.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.14.27 only referred to as Tamar (תָּמָר); a daughter of Absalom; wife of Uriel; mother of Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 압살롬의 딸. 2Sa.14.27에 처음 언급되며 '다말'이라 불림. 압살롬의 딸. 우리엘의 아내. 마아가의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 다말은 압살롬의 아름다운 딸로, 그의 비극적인 자매의 이름을 따서 지어졌다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Judah's daughter-in-law who bore Perez and Zerah
persons.short: Tamar was Judah's daughter-in-law who, after being wronged by him, bore twin sons Perez and Zerah.
persons.article: Tamar was the daughter-in-law of Judah, married first to his son Er and then to Onan (Gen.38.6-11). After being wronged by Judah, Tamar disguised herself as a prostitute and conceived twins by him (Gen.38.13-24). She gave birth to Perez and Zerah, who became ancestors of the tribe of Judah (Gen.38.29-30; Rut.4.12; 1Ch.2.4). Tamar is praised for her righteousness in contrast to Judah (Gen.38.26). She is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat.1.3).
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.38.6 referred to as Tamar (תָּמָר), or Tamar (Θάμαρ); wife of Judah and Er; mother of Perez and Zerah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.38.6에 처음 언급되며 '다말'이라 불림. 유다와 엘의 아내. 베레스와 세라의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 다말은 유다의 며느리로, 그에게 부당한 대우를 받은 후 쌍둥이 아들 베레스와 세라를 낳았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Supporter of Gedaliah after Jerusalem's fall
persons.short: Tanhumeth the Netophathite was one of the leaders who supported Gedaliah's governorship after Jerusalem's fall.
persons.article: Tanhumeth the Netophathite is mentioned in 2Ki.25.23 and Jer.40.8 as one of the leaders of the forces who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah after the fall of Jerusalem. Along with Ishmael, Johanan, Seraiah, and the sons of Ephai, Tanhumeth supported Gedaliah, whom the Babylonians had appointed governor over Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.23 only referred to as Tanhumeth (תַּנְחֻ֫מֶת); father of Seraiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.25.23에 처음 언급되며 '단후멧'이라 불림. 스라야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 느도바 사람 단후멧은 예루살렘 함락 후 그달랴의 총독직을 지지한 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Solomon; wife of Ben-abinadab
persons.short: Taphath was a daughter of Solomon who married Ben-abinadab, one of Solomon's district governors.
persons.article: Taphath is mentioned in 1Ki.4.11 as a daughter of King Solomon. She was given in marriage to Ben-abinadab, who was one of Solomon's twelve district governors responsible for providing food for the royal household. Ben-abinadab's district was Naphoth-dor.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.11 only referred to as Taphath (טָפַת); daughter of Solomon; a sister of Basemath and Rehoboam; wife of Ben-abinadab.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '다밧'이라 불림. 솔로몬과 솔로몬의 아내(이름 미상)의 딸. 바스맛과 르호보암의 자매. 벤아비나답의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 다밧은 솔로몬의 딸로, 솔로몬의 지방관 중 한 사람인 벤아비나답과 결혼했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hebron from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Tappuah was a son of Hebron, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Tappuah is mentioned in 1Ch.2.43 as one of the sons of Hebron. Hebron was a descendant of Judah through Caleb, making Tappuah a member of the tribe of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.43 only referred to as Tappuah (תַּפֻּחַ); son of Hebron; a brother of Korah, Rekem and Shema.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.43에 처음 언급되며 '답부아'라 불림. 헤브론의 아들. 고라, 레겜과 세마의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 답부아는 헤브론의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth
persons.short: Tarea, also called Tahrea, was a son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth.
persons.article: Tarea, also known as Tahrea, is mentioned in 1Ch.8.35 and 1Ch.9.41 as a son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth. Mephibosheth was a son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul. These passages list the descendants of Saul, tracing the genealogy of his son Jonathan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.35 referred to as Tarea (תַּאֲרֵעַ), or Tahrea (תַּחֲרֵעַ); son of Micah; a brother of Pithon, Melech and Ahaz.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.35에 처음 언급되며 '다레아'라 불림. 미가의 아들. 비돈, 멜렉과 아하스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다레아(다흐레아라고도 함)는 미가의 아들이며 므비보셋의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jeush@1Ch.7.10, Benjamin@1Ch.7.10, Ehud@1Ch.7.10, Chenaanah@1Ch.7.10, Zethan@1Ch.7.10, Ahishahar@1Ch.7.10
persons.brief: Son of Bilhan from the tribe of Benjamin
persons.short: Tarshish was a son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Tarshish is mentioned in 1Ch.7.10 as a son of Bilhan. Bilhan was a descendant of Benjamin, making Tarshish a member of the tribe of Benjamin. This passage lists the sons of Jediael, tracing the genealogy of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.10 only referred to as Tarshish (תַּרְשִׁישׁ); son of Bilhan; a brother of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan and Ahishahar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.10에 처음 언급되며 '다시스'라 불림. 빌한의 아들. 여우스, 베냐민, 에훗, 그나아나, 세단과 아히사할의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다시스는 빌한의 아들이며 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
persons.short: Tarshish was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom.
persons.article: Tarshish is mentioned in Est.1.14 as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who served as advisors to King Ahasuerus (also known as Xerxes I). These seven princes had special access to the king's presence and were the most prominent officials in the Persian Empire. The context of Esther 1 describes a grand feast held by King Ahasuerus in the third year of his reign. During this feast, the king summoned his wife, Queen Vashti, to appear before him and his guests, but she refused. Angered by her refusal, the king consulted his wise men, including Tarshish, to determine the appropriate course of action according to the law. Tarshish, along with the other princes, advised the king to issue a royal decree proclaiming that Vashti would never again enter the king's presence and that her royal position would be given to another woman. This decree was intended to discourage other women in the kingdom from defying their husbands' authority. Apart from his role as one of the seven princes and his involvement in advising the king regarding Vashti's disobedience, no other information is provided about Tarshish's personal life, background, or subsequent actions in the book of Esther.
persons.summary: A prince of Persia living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.14 only referred to as Tarshish (תַרְשִׁישׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 페르시아 사람. Est.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '다시스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다시스는 아하수에로 왕을 알현할 수 있었던 페르시아와 메대의 일곱 방백 중 한 사람으로, 나라에서 가장 높은 지위에 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Javan, great-grandson of Noah
persons.short: Tarshish was a son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah, associated with the ancient city of Tarshish.
persons.article: Tarshish is mentioned in Gen.10.4 and 1Ch.1.7 as a son of Javan and grandson of Noah. He was born after the flood and is listed among the descendants of Japheth. Tarshish is associated with the ancient city of Tarshish, a distant port known for its wealth and maritime trade. His descendants likely settled in or near this city, which some identify with Tartessos in Spain or Tarsus in Cilicia.
persons.summary: A man of the Greeks living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.4 only referred to as Tarshish (תַּרְשִׁישׁ); son of Javan; a brother of Elishah, Kittim and Dodanim.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.4에 처음 언급되며 '달시스'라 불림. 야완의 아들. 엘리사, 깃딤과 도다님의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 다시스는 야완의 아들이며 노아의 증손자로, 고대 다시스 성읍과 관련이 있다.

persons.description: Leader's title
persons.brief: Title of an Assyrian military commander
persons.short: The Tartan was a high-ranking Assyrian military commander who led campaigns against Ashdod and Jerusalem.
persons.article: The Tartan is mentioned in 2Ki.18.17 and Isa.20.1 as a title of a high-ranking Assyrian military commander. In 2 Kings, the Tartan, along with the Rabsaris and the Rabshakeh, was sent by King Sennacherib of Assyria to Jerusalem to intimidate King Hezekiah and demand his surrender. In Isaiah, the Tartan was sent by Sargon king of Assyria to attack the city of Ashdod. The Tartan was likely second in command to the king and led major military campaigns. The title is of Akkadian origin and refers to the commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army.
persons.summary: Title of a leader, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.17 referred to as Tartan or "chief" (תַּרְתָּן).
persons.summary_ko: 지도자 칭호. 2Ki.18.17에 처음 언급되며 '다르단'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 다르단은 아스돗과 예루살렘을 대적하는 원정을 이끈 앗수르의 고위 군사령관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian governor who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild
persons.short: Tattenai was the Persian governor of the province Beyond the River who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple.
persons.article: Tattenai is mentioned in Ezr.5.3,6 and Ezr.6.6,13 as the governor of the province Beyond the River during the reign of Darius king of Persia. When the Jews resumed rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem, Tattenai and his associates questioned their authority to do so and wrote to Darius to investigate the matter. After Darius confirmed Cyrus' decree authorizing the rebuilding, Tattenai allowed the work to continue and even provided support for it from the royal treasury. Tattenai's actions reflect the Persian policy of respecting the religious practices of subject peoples while maintaining oversight of their activities.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.5.3 only referred to as Tattenai (תַּתְּנַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.5.3에 처음 언급되며 '닷드내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 닷드내는 강 건너편 지방의 페르시아 총독으로, 유대인들이 성전을 재건할 권한이 있는지 의문을 제기했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Uz@Gen.22.21, Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor and Reumah
persons.short: Tebah was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.
persons.article: Tebah is mentioned in Gen.22.24 as a son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah. Nahor was Abraham's brother, making Tebah Abraham's nephew. Tebah is listed along with his brothers Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. No other details are provided about Tebah's life or descendants. As a son of Nahor, he was born in Mesopotamia, where Abraham and his family originated.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.24 only referred to as Tebah (טֶ֫בַח); son of Nahor and Reumah; a brother of Gaham, Tahash and Maacah; half-brother of: Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.24에 처음 언급되며 '데바'라 불림. 나홀과 르우마의 아들. 우스, 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 데바는 아브라함의 형제 나홀이 첩 르우마를 통해 얻은 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper, son of Hosah
persons.short: Tebaliah was a Levite gatekeeper, the third son of Hosah.
persons.article: Tebaliah is mentioned in 1Ch.26.11 as the third son of Hosah, a Levite gatekeeper. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the temple and its courtyards. They were organized by families and assigned to different gates. Hosah and his sons, including Tebaliah, were assigned to the Shallecheth Gate on the west side of the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.11 only referred to as Tebaliah (טְבַלְיָ֫הוּ); son of Hosah; a brother of Shimri, Hilkiah and Zechariah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.26.11에 처음 언급되며 '드발리야'라 불림. 호사의 아들. 시므리, 힐기야와 스가랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 드발리야는 호사의 셋째 아들이며 레위인 문지기였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Ir-nahash from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Tehinnah was the father of Ir-nahash and a descendant of Chelub from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Tehinnah is mentioned in 1Ch.4.12 as the father of Ir-nahash. He was a descendant of Chelub from the tribe of Judah. The name Ir-nahash means "city of serpents," but it is unclear whether this refers to an actual city or is a symbolic name. No other details are provided about Tehinnah's life or role in the tribe. He is listed in the genealogy of Judah, which traces the descendants of Jacob's son Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.12 only referred to as Tehinnah (תְּחִנָּה); son of Eshton; a brother of Beth-rapha and Paseah; father or founder of Ir-nahash.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.12에 처음 언급되며 '드힌나'라 불림. 에스돈의 아들. 베드라바와 바세아의 형제. Ir-nahash의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 드힌나는 이르나하스의 아버지이며 유다 지파 글룹의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Resheph from the tribe of Ephraim
persons.short: Telah was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Resheph and father of Tahan.
persons.article: Telah is mentioned in 1Ch.7.25 as a descendant of Ephraim. He was the son of Resheph and the father of Tahan. This genealogy traces the descendants of Joseph's son Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. No other details are provided about Telah's life or role in the tribe. He lived during the time the Israelites were in Egypt or in the early years after the Exodus.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.25 only referred to as Telah (תֶּ֫לַח); a son of Resheph; father of Tahan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '델라'라 불림. 레셉의 아들. 다한의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 델라는 에브라임의 후손으로, 레셉의 아들이며 다한의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Temple servant who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Telem was a temple servant who married a foreign wife during the Exile and later divorced her.
persons.article: Telem is mentioned in Ezr.10.24 as one of the temple servants who had married foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. Under Ezra's leadership, the returned exiles agreed to divorce their foreign wives to maintain the purity of the Jewish community. Telem is listed among those who complied with this decision.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.24 only referred to as Telem (טֶ֫לֶם).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.24에 처음 언급되며 '델렘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 델렘은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했다가 후에 그녀와 이혼한 성전 봉사자였다.

persons.description: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa, Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk, Adbeel@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mibsam@Gen.25.13-1Ch, Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Dumah@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Massa@Gen.25.14-1Ch, Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Jetur@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch, Mahalath@Gen.28.9-
persons.brief: Son of Ishmael, associated with an Arabian city
persons.short: Tema was a son of Ishmael and is associated with the ancient Arabian city of Tema.
persons.article: Tema is mentioned in Gen.25.15 and 1Ch.1.30 as one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar. He is listed among the "princes according to their nations" that descended from Ishmael. Tema is associated with the ancient city of Tema, an important oasis and caravan stop in northwestern Arabia. His descendants likely settled in or around this city.
persons.summary: A man of the Arabs living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.25.15 only referred to as Tema (תֵּימָא); son of Ishmael; a brother of Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah and Mahalath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 아라비아 사람. Gen.25.15에 처음 언급되며 '데마'라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들. 느바욧, 게달, 앗브엘, 밉삼, 미스마, 두마, 맛사, 하닷, 여둘, 나비스, 게드마와 마할랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 데마는 이스마엘의 아들이며 고대 아라비아 성읍 데마와 관련이 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
persons.short: Temah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Temah is mentioned in Ezr.2.53 and Neh.7.55 as the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. The temple servants were a group of non-Israelites who assisted the Levites in the maintenance and service of the temple. Temah's descendants were among those who returned with Zerubbabel to help rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.53 only referred to as Temah (תָּ֑מַח).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.53에 처음 언급되며 '데마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드마는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Omar@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Zepho@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Amalek@Gen.36.12-, Korah@Gen.36.16
persons.brief: Grandson of Esau, associated with an Edomite clan
persons.short: Teman was a grandson of Esau and is associated with an important Edomite clan known for its wisdom.
persons.article: Teman is mentioned in Gen.36.11,15,42 and 1Ch.1.36,53 as a son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau. He was one of the chiefs of Edom. The name Teman is also associated with a prominent Edomite clan (Gen.36.34; 1Ch.1.45 and a region in Edom known for its wisdom )(Jer.49.7; Oba.1.9). Several individuals from Teman are mentioned in the Book of Job, including Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends (Job.2.11; 4.1; 15.1; 22.1; 42.7,9). The Temanites were renowned for their wisdom, though Eliphaz's counsel to Job was ultimately misguided. Teman represents the wisdom and power of Edom, which was still inferior to the wisdom of God.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.11 referred to as Teman (תֵּימָן), or Temanite (תֵּימָנִי); son of Eliphaz; a brother of Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Amalek and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.11에 처음 언급되며 '데만'이라 불림. 엘리바스와 엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 오말, 스보, 가담, 그나스, 아말렉과 고라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 데만은 에서의 손자이며 지혜로 알려진 중요한 에돔 가문과 관련이 있다.
persons.article_ko: 데만은 창세기 36:11, 15, 42와 역대상 1:36, 53에서 엘리바스의 아들이며 에서의 손자로 언급된다. 그는 에돔 족장 중 한 사람이었다. 데만이라는 이름은 저명한 에돔 가문(창 36:34; 대상 1:45)과 지혜로 알려진 에돔의 한 지역(렘 49:7; 옵 1:9)과도 관련이 있다. 욥의 세 친구 중 한 사람인 데만 사람 엘리바스를 포함해 데만 출신 여러 사람이 욥기에 언급된다(욥 2:11; 4:1; 15:1; 22:1; 42:7, 9). 데만 사람들은 지혜로 유명했으나, 욥에게 한 엘리바스의 조언은 결국 잘못된 것이었다. 데만은 에돔의 지혜와 능력을 대표하지만, 그것은 여전히 하나님의 지혜보다 열등했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Hepher@1Ch.4.6, Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6, Zereth@1Ch.4.7, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Ethnan@1Ch.4.7, Koz@1Ch.4.8
persons.brief: Son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Temeni was a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Temeni is mentioned in 1Ch.4.6 as one of the sons of Ashhur (or 'Ashur'). He was a descendant of Judah through Hezron and is described as the "father of Tekoa," likely referring to his role as the founder or leader of the city. Temeni is listed along with his brothers Haahashtari, Hepher, and Ahuzzam.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.6 only referred to as Temeni (תֵּימְנִי); son of Ashhur and Naarah; a brother of Ahuzzam, Hepher and Haahashtari; half-brother of: Zereth, Izhar, Ethnan and Koz.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.6에 처음 언급되며 '데므니'라 불림. 아스훌과 나아라의 아들. 아훗삼, 헤벨, 하아하스타리, 세렛, 이스할, 에드난과 고스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 드므니는 아스훌(아술이라고도 함)의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Abraham's father who settled in Haran
persons.short: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who left Ur to settle in Haran.
persons.article: Terah was the son of Nahor and the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran (Gen.11.24-26). He lived in Ur of the Chaldeans, where he worshipped idols (Jos.24.2). At age 70, he became the father of his three sons (Gen.11.26). After Haran died in Ur, Terah took Abraham, Sarah, and Lot and set out for Canaan, but they settled in the city of Haran instead (Gen.11.31). Terah died in Haran at the age of 205 (Gen.11.32). Jewish tradition portrays Terah as an idolater who turned to God. The Bible does not provide further details about his life, but his significance lies in being the father of Abraham, the recipient of God's covenant promises.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.11.24 referred to as Terah (תֶּ֫רַח), or Terah (Θάρα); a son of Nahor; father of Abraham, Nahor, Haran and Sarah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.11.24에 처음 언급되며 '데라'라 불림. 나홀의 아들. 아브라함, 나홀, 하란과 사라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 데라는 아브라함, 나홀, 하란의 아버지로, 우르를 떠나 하란에 정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Persian official who plotted against King Ahasuerus
persons.short: Teresh was one of two Persian officials who plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus but were discovered by Mordecai.
persons.article: Teresh is mentioned in Est.2.21 and Est.6.2 as one of two eunuchs who served at the door of King Ahasuerus' palace. Along with Bigthan, Teresh plotted to assassinate the king for unknown reasons. However, their plot was discovered by Mordecai, who informed Queen Esther. The matter was investigated and found to be true, leading to the execution of Bigthan and Teresh on the gallows. Mordecai's deed was recorded in the king's chronicles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.2.21 only referred to as Teresh (תֶּ֫רֶשׁ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.2.21에 처음 언급되며 '데레스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 데레스는 아하수에로 왕을 암살하려 음모를 꾸몄으나 모르드개에게 발각된 두 페르시아 관리 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Paul's scribe who wrote the Epistle to the Romans
persons.short: Tertius served as Paul's scribe, writing down the Epistle to the Romans.
persons.article: Tertius is mentioned in Rom.16.22 as the scribe who wrote down the Epistle to the Romans on behalf of the Apostle Paul. Paul likely dictated the letter to Tertius, who then penned it in his own hand. In the closing of the epistle, Tertius inserts his own personal greeting to the recipients, indicating his close association with Paul and the Christian community in Rome. No other details are provided about Tertius' background or role in the early church. His service as a scribe highlights the collaborative nature of Paul's ministry and the importance of written communication in spreading the gospel message.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.22 only referred to as Tertius (Τέρτιος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.22에 처음 언급되며 '더디오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 더디오는 바울의 서기관으로 섬기며 로마서를 받아썼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Lawyer who accused Paul before Governor Felix
persons.short: Tertullus was a lawyer hired by the Jewish authorities to accuse Paul before the Roman governor Felix.
persons.article: Tertullus is mentioned in Act.24.1-2 as a lawyer or orator hired by the Jewish high priest and elders to present their case against the Apostle Paul before the Roman governor Felix in Caesarea. Tertullus began his speech with flattery, praising Felix's reforms and administration. He then accused Paul of being a troublemaker, stirring up riots among the Jews, and profaning the temple. Tertullus aimed to persuade Felix to condemn Paul, but Paul defended himself by denying the charges and asserting his innocence. The outcome of the trial is not directly stated, but Paul remained in custody for two years until Felix's successor Porcius Festus took office.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.24.1 only referred to as Tertullus (Τέρτυλλος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.24.1에 처음 언급되며 '더둘로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 더둘로는 유대 지도자들이 로마 총독 벨릭스 앞에서 바울을 고발하기 위해 고용한 변호사였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Recipient of Luke's Gospel and Acts
persons.short: Theophilus was the recipient of Luke's Gospel and the Book of Acts, likely a Christian of high social standing.
persons.article: Theophilus is mentioned in Luk.1.3 and Act.1.1 as the recipient of these two books written by Luke. He is addressed as "most excellent Theophilus," indicating a person of high social or political standing, possibly a Roman official or a wealthy benefactor of the church. Luke states that he wrote his Gospel to provide Theophilus with an orderly account of the life and teachings of Jesus, based on eyewitness testimonies. The Book of Acts, also addressed to Theophilus, continues the narrative of the early church's growth and mission. The dedication suggests that Theophilus was a Christian who had received some instruction in the faith but needed a more comprehensive understanding. No other details are provided about Theophilus' background, conversion, or role in the church. His identity remains unknown, but his mention reflects the importance of written accounts in transmitting and confirming the gospel message for believers.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.1.3 only referred to as Theophilus (Θεόφιλος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.1.3에 처음 언급되며 '데오빌로'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 데오빌로는 누가복음과 사도행전의 수신자로, 아마 사회적 지위가 높은 그리스도인이었을 것이다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Jewish rebel leader killed by Roman authorities
persons.short: Theudas was a Jewish rebel leader who was killed, and his followers scattered, by the Roman authorities.
persons.article: Theudas is mentioned in Act.5.36 as an example of a failed messianic pretender. According to Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee, Theudas rose up claiming to be somebody important and gathered about four hundred men to follow him. However, he was killed, and his followers were dispersed, resulting in the failure of his movement. Gamaliel used Theudas and another rebel named Judas the Galilean as cautionary examples to dissuade the Jewish council from persecuting the apostles. He argued that if the apostles' movement was of human origin, it would fail like those of Theudas and Judas.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.5.36 only referred to as Theudas (Θευδᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.5.36에 처음 언급되며 '드다'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드다는 유대인 반역 지도자로, 로마 당국에 의해 죽임을 당하고 그의 추종자들은 흩어졌다.

persons.description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: One of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting
persons.short: Thomas, also called Didymus, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting Jesus' resurrection until he saw him in person.
persons.article: Thomas, also known as Didymus (meaning "twin"), was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus Christ. He is mentioned in all four Gospels and the Book of Acts (Mat.10.3; Mrk.3.18; Luk.6.15; Jhn.11.16; 14.5; 20.24-29; 21.2; Act.1.13). Thomas is best known for his doubt about Jesus' resurrection, earning him the nickname "Doubting Thomas." When Jesus appeared to the disciples after his resurrection, Thomas was absent and refused to believe unless he could see and touch Jesus' wounds (Jhn.20.24-25). A week later, Jesus appeared again, inviting Thomas to touch his wounds. Thomas then confessed, "My Lord and my God!" (Jhn.20.26-28). Jesus praised those who believe without seeing (Jhn.20.29). Thomas also showed devotion to Jesus, willing to die with him (Jhn.11.16 and asking questions during the Last Supper )(Jhn.14.5). According to tradition, Thomas later preached the gospel in India, where he was martyred. His initial doubt and later confession serve as an encouragement for believers who struggle with doubts.
persons.summary: An apostle living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.10.3 referred to as Thomas (Θωμᾶς), or Twin (Δίδυμος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 사도. Mat.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '도마'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 도마(디두모라고도 함)는 예수님의 열두 제자 중 한 사람으로, 예수님을 직접 볼 때까지 부활을 의심한 것으로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 도마(디두모라고도 함, '쌍둥이'라는 뜻)는 예수 그리스도의 열두 제자 중 한 사람이었다. 그는 네 복음서와 사도행전 모두에 언급된다(마 10:3; 막 3:18; 눅 6:15; 요 11:16; 14:5; 20:24-29; 21:2; 행 1:13). 도마는 예수님의 부활에 대한 의심으로 가장 잘 알려져 있어 '의심하는 도마'라는 별명을 얻었다. 예수님이 부활 후 제자들에게 나타나셨을 때 도마는 그 자리에 없었고 예수님의 상처를 보고 만지지 않으면 믿지 않겠다고 거부했다(요 20:24-25). 일주일 후 예수님이 다시 나타나셔서 도마에게 그의 상처를 만지라고 초청하셨다. 그러자 도마는 '나의 주님이시요 나의 하나님이시니이다'라고 고백했다(요 20:26-28). 예수님은 보지 않고 믿는 자들을 칭찬하셨다(요 20:29). 도마는 또한 예수님과 함께 죽을 각오를 보이며(요 11:16) 최후의 만찬 동안 질문을 하는 등 헌신을 보였다(요 14:5). 전승에 따르면 도마는 후에 인도에서 복음을 전하다가 순교했다. 그의 처음의 의심과 나중의 고백은 의심과 씨름하는 신자들에게 격려가 된다.

persons.description: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and death
persons.short: Tiberius was the Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and crucifixion, mentioned in several Gospel accounts.
persons.article: Tiberius, also referred to as Caesar, was the Roman emperor during the ministry and death of Jesus Christ. He is mentioned in several passages in the Gospels and once in the Book of Acts (Luk.3.1; Mat.22.17-21; Mrk.12.14-17; Luk.20.22-25; 23.2; Jhn.19.12,15). Tiberius ruled from 14 to 37 AD, succeeding Augustus. His reign provided the historical and political context for the events of the New Testament. In Luk.3.1, Tiberius is mentioned to date the beginning of John the Baptist's ministry. The Gospels also record Jesus' response to the question of paying taxes to Caesar (Tiberius), affirming the legitimacy of secular authority while prioritizing obedience to God (Mat.22.17-21; Mrk.12.14-17; Luk.20.22-25). During Jesus' trial, the Jewish leaders accused him of opposing payment of taxes to Caesar and claiming to be a king, which Pontius Pilate recognized as a challenge to Tiberius' authority (Luk.23.2; Jhn.19.12,15). Tiberius' reign was marked by growing unrest in Judea, leading to the appointment of Pontius Pilate as governor. The New Testament portrays Tiberius as the embodiment of secular power, contrasting with Jesus' spiritual authority.
persons.summary: An emperor of Rome living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.22.17 referred to as Tiberius (Τιβέριος), or Caesar (Καῖσαρ).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 황제. Mat.22.17에 처음 언급되며 '디베료'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 디베료는 예수님의 사역과 십자가 처형 당시 로마 황제로, 여러 복음서에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Rival to Omri for the throne of Israel
persons.short: Tibni was a rival to Omri for the throne of Israel, leading to a divided kingdom until his death.
persons.article: Tibni is mentioned in 1Ki.16.21-22 as a rival to Omri for the throne of Israel. After King Zimri's death, the people of Israel were divided, with half following Tibni son of Ginath and the other half following Omri. The conflict between the two factions lasted for about four years, during which time Israel was effectively a divided kingdom. Eventually, Omri's supporters proved stronger, and Tibni died, allowing Omri to consolidate his power and establish a new dynasty that ruled the northern kingdom of Israel. No other details are provided about Tibni's background, his claim to the throne, or the circumstances of his death. His brief mention in the biblical narrative highlights the political instability and power struggles that characterized the period of the divided monarchy in Israel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.16.21 only referred to as Tibni (תִּבְנִי); a son of Ginath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.16.21에 처음 언급되며 '디브니'라 불림. 기낫의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 디브니는 오므리와 이스라엘 왕위를 다투었고, 이로 인해 그가 죽을 때까지 왕국이 분열되었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Goiim, ally of Chedorlaomer
persons.short: Tidal, king of Goiim, was one of the four kings allied with Chedorlaomer in the battle against the five kings of the plain.
persons.article: Tidal, described as king of Goiim, is mentioned in Gen.14.1 and Gen.14.9 as one of the four kings who joined forces with Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a battle against the five kings of the cities of the plain, including Sodom and Gomorrah. The name "Tidal" is of uncertain origin, and "Goiim" may refer to a region or a group of people. In the biblical account, Tidal and his allies engaged in a military campaign in Canaan, ultimately defeating the five kings and taking captives, including Abraham's nephew Lot. In response, Abraham and his 318 trained men pursued the victorious kings, defeated them, and rescued Lot and the other captives (Gen.14.14-16). No other details are provided about Tidal's background, the extent of his kingdom, or his fate after the battle. His participation in the alliance with Chedorlaomer suggests a significant political and military role in the ancient Near East, but the exact historical and geographical context remains uncertain.
persons.summary: A king living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.14.1 only referred to as Tidal (תִּדְעָל).
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.14.1에 처음 언급되며 '디달'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고임 왕 디달은 평지 다섯 왕과의 전투에서 그돌라오멜과 동맹한 네 왕 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel
persons.short: Tiglath-pileser, also known as Pul, was an Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel and received tribute from King Menahem.
persons.article: Tiglath-pileser, also referred to as "the great" or "Pul," was a powerful Assyrian king who reigned from 745 to 727 BC. He is mentioned in several passages in the Old Testament (2Ki.15.19,29; 16.7,10; 1Ch.5.6,26; 2Ch.28.20; Hos.5.13; 10.6). Tiglath-pileser's reign marked the beginning of the Neo-Assyrian Empire's expansion and dominance in the ancient Near East. He is known for his military conquests and political reforms. In the biblical account, Tiglath-pileser received tribute from King Menahem of Israel (2Ki.15.19 and later conquered parts of Israel, including Gilead, Galilee, and Naphtali, deporting the inhabitants to Assyria )(2Ki.15.29; 1Ch.5.26). King Ahaz of Judah sought Tiglath-pileser's help against the kings of Israel and Syria, but this alliance ultimately led to Judah's subjugation and religious compromises (2Ki.16.7-10; 2Ch.28.20). The prophet Hosea denounced Israel's reliance on Assyria, symbolized by Tiglath-pileser, as futile and contrary to trust in God (Hos.5.13; 10.6). Tiglath-pileser's reign marked a significant turning point in the history of Israel and Judah, as the Assyrian Empire's expansion posed an increasing threat to their sovereignty and independence.
persons.summary: A king of Assyria living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.19 referred to as Tiglath-pileser (תִּגְלַת פִּלְאֶ֫סֶר), or "great" (יָרֵב), or Pul (פּוּל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.15.19에 처음 언급되며 '디글랏'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 디글랏빌레셋(불이라고도 함)은 이스라엘 일부를 정복하고 므나헴 왕에게서 조공을 받은 앗수르 왕이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Shallum, husband of Huldah the prophetess
persons.short: Tikvah, also known as Tokhath, was the father of Shallum and the father-in-law of Huldah the prophetess.
persons.article: Tikvah, also referred to as Tokhath, is mentioned in 2Ki.22.14 and 2Ch.34.22 as the father of Shallum. Shallum was the husband of Huldah, a prophetess who lived in Jerusalem during the reign of King Josiah. When Josiah ordered the repair of the temple, the high priest Hilkiah discovered the Book of the Law. Josiah then sent a delegation, including Shallum, to consult Huldah regarding the words of the book. Huldah prophesied that God would bring judgment upon Judah for their unfaithfulness but that Josiah would be spared because of his repentance. No other details are provided about Tikvah's life or role. His mention serves to identify Shallum and, by extension, Huldah, who played a significant role in Josiah's religious reforms.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.22.14 referred to as Tikvah (תִּקְוָה), or Tokhath (תּוֹקַהַת); a son of Harhas; father of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.22.14에 처음 언급되며 '디과'라 불림. 할하스의 아들. 살룸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 딕와(도가라고도 함)는 살룸의 아버지이며 여선지자 훌다의 시아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Opposed Ezra's reforms regarding foreign wives
persons.short: Tikvah was one of two men who opposed Ezra's reforms requiring Jewish men to divorce their foreign wives.
persons.article: Tikvah is mentioned in Ezr.10.15 as one of two men who opposed Ezra's reforms concerning Jewish men who had married foreign women. After the Babylonian exile, Ezra led a religious revival among the returned exiles, which included separating from foreign influences. When it was discovered that many Jewish men, including priests and Levites, had married women from other nations, Ezra called for a assembly and urged the people to confess their sin and divorce their foreign wives. The assembly agreed to Ezra's proposal, with the exception of Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, who opposed the plan. Despite their opposition, the reforms were carried out, and the foreign wives were sent away.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.15 only referred to as Tikvah (תִּקְוָה); father of Jahzeiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.15에 처음 언급되며 '디과'라 불림. 야스야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 딕와는 에스라가 유대 남자들에게 이방인 아내와 이혼하도록 요구한 개혁을 반대한 두 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Shimon from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Tilon was a son of Shimon, a descendant of Judah.
persons.article: Tilon is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.20 as one of the sons of Shimon, along with his brothers Amnon, Rinnah, and Ben-hanan. Shimon was a descendant of Judah through Perez and Hezron. No other details are provided about Tilon's life or role in the tribe of Judah. His mention serves to trace the genealogy of Judah and demonstrate the continuity of the tribe from the time of the patriarchs to the period of the divided monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.20 only referred to as Tilon (תִּילוֹן); son of Shimon; a brother of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.20에 처음 언급되며 '딜론'이라 불림. 시몬의 아들. 암논, 린나와 벤하난의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 딜론은 시몬의 아들이며 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Father of Bartimaeus, a blind man healed by Jesus
persons.short: Timaeus was the father of Bartimaeus, a blind beggar who was healed by Jesus near Jericho.
persons.article: Timaeus is mentioned in Mrk.10.46 as the father of Bartimaeus, a blind beggar who encountered Jesus on the road to Jericho. The name Bartimaeus literally means "son of Timaeus," indicating that he was known primarily by his relationship to his father. In the biblical account, Bartimaeus was sitting by the roadside when he heard that Jesus was passing by. He cried out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" Despite the crowd's attempts to silence him, Bartimaeus persisted in calling out to Jesus. Jesus stopped and called for Bartimaeus to come to him. When asked what he wanted, Bartimaeus replied, "Rabbi, I want to see." Jesus then healed him, saying, "Go, your faith has healed you." Immediately, Bartimaeus received his sight and followed Jesus.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Mrk.10.46 only referred to as Timaeus (Τιμαῖος); father of Bartimaeus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mrk.10.46에 처음 언급되며 '디매오'라 불림. 바디매오의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 디매오는 여리고 근처에서 예수님에게 고침받은 눈먼 거지 바디매오의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Lotan@Gen.36.20-1Ch, Shobal@Gen.36.20-1Ch, Zibeon@Gen.36.2-1Ch, Dishon@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Ezer@Gen.36.21-1Ch, Dishan@Gen.36.21-1Ch
persons.brief: Concubine of Eliphaz; mother of Amalek
persons.short: Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, son of Esau, and the mother of Amalek.
persons.article: Timna is mentioned in Gen.36.12 as a concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau. She gave birth to Amalek, who became the ancestor of the Amalekites, a nomadic tribe that lived in the Negev and Sinai desert regions. The Amalekites later became enemies of the Israelites during their wilderness wanderings and the period of the judges and early monarchy. No other details are provided about Timna's life or her relationship with Eliphaz. Timna is also mentioned in Gen.36.40 and 1Ch.1.51 as one of the chiefs of Edom, a nation descended from Esau. This probably indicates they are descenced from this concubine, though this is not certain.
persons.summary: A concubine living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.12 only referred to as Timna (תִּמְנָע); daughter of Seir; a sister of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan; concubine of Eliphaz; mother of Amalek.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.36.12에 처음 언급되며 '딤나'라 불림. 세일의 딸. 로단, 소발, 시브온, 디손, 에셀과 디산의 자매. 엘리바스의 아내. 아말렉의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 딤나는 에서의 아들 엘리바스의 첩이며 아말렉의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
