persons.brief: One of the seven chosen to serve the church
persons.short: Timon was one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows in the early church.
persons.article: Timon is mentioned in Act.6.5 as one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to address the needs of Greek-speaking Jewish widows in the early church in Jerusalem. As the church grew, there was a complaint that these widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food. The apostles asked the believers to choose seven men known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom to oversee this task. Timon, along with Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Parmenas, and Nicolas, was selected and appointed to this role, allowing the apostles to focus on prayer and the ministry of the word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.6.5 only referred to as Timon (Τίμων).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '디몬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 디몬은 사도들이 초대교회에서 과부들에게 매일 음식을 나누어주는 일을 감독하도록 선택한 일곱 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Paul's young disciple and co-worker
persons.short: Timothy was a young disciple and co-worker of Paul, who accompanied him on his missionary journeys and later served as a pastor.
persons.article: Timothy was a young disciple and close companion of the Apostle Paul. He is mentioned frequently in the New Testament, both in the book of Acts and in Paul's epistles. Timothy was from Lystra, the son of a Greek father and a Jewish mother named Eunice (Act.16.1). He was well-respected by the believers in his hometown and in Iconium (Act.16.2). Paul invited Timothy to join him on his missionary journeys, and he became a valuable assistant and co-worker (Act.16.3; 17.14-15; 18.5; 19.22; 20.4). Paul referred to Timothy as his "true son in the faith" (1Ti.1.2 and sent him on important missions to churches in Macedonia, Achaia, and Ephesus )(Act.19.22; 1Co.4.17; 16.10; Php.2.19). Timothy was with Paul during his first Roman imprisonment and is named as a co-sender of several of Paul's letters (Php.1.1; Col.1.1; Phm.1.1). Paul also wrote two personal letters to Timothy, providing guidance and encouragement for his pastoral ministry (1Ti.1.2; 2Ti.1.2). These letters, along with the letter to Titus, are known as the Pastoral Epistles. According to Heb.13.23, Timothy was imprisoned at some point but later released. Tradition holds that Timothy served as the bishop of Ephesus in his later years. Timothy's life and ministry exemplify the importance of mentoring, discipleship, and faithful service in the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.16.1 referred to as Timothy (Τιμόθεος); his mother was Eunice.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '디모데'라 불림. 디모데의 아버지(이름 미상)와 유니게의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 디모데는 바울의 젊은 제자이며 동역자로, 그의 선교여행에 동행하고 후에 목회자로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 디모데는 사도 바울의 젊은 제자이며 가까운 동반자였다. 그는 사도행전과 바울의 서신서 모두에서 자주 언급된다. 디모데는 루스드라 출신으로, 그리스인 아버지와 유니게라는 유대인 어머니 사이에서 태어났다(행 16:1). 그는 자기 고향과 이고니온의 신자들에게 존경받았다(행 16:2). 바울은 디모데를 그의 선교여행에 초청했고, 그는 귀중한 조수이며 동역자가 되었다(행 16:3; 17:14-15; 18:5; 19:22; 20:4). 바울은 디모데를 믿음 안에서 참 아들이라 불렀고(딤전 1:2) 마게도냐, 아가야, 에베소의 교회들에 중요한 사명을 위해 그를 보냈다(행 19:22; 고전 4:17; 16:10; 빌 2:19). 디모데는 바울의 첫 번째 로마 투옥 동안 그와 함께 있었고 바울의 여러 편지의 공동 발신인으로 이름이 올라 있다(빌 1:1; 골 1:1; 몬 1:1). 바울은 또한 디모데에게 두 개의 개인적인 편지를 써서 그의 목회 사역을 위한 지도와 격려를 제공했다(딤전 1:2; 딤후 1:2). 이 편지들은 디도서와 함께 목회 서신으로 알려져 있다. 히브리서 13:23에 따르면 디모데는 한때 투옥되었으나 후에 풀려났다. 전승에 따르면 디모데는 말년에 에베소의 감독으로 섬겼다. 디모데의 삶과 사역은 초대교회에서 멘토링, 제자훈련, 신실한 섬김의 중요성을 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth, grandson of Noah
persons.short: Tiras was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, listed among the nations descended from Noah after the flood.
persons.article: Tiras is mentioned in Gen.10.2 and 1Ch.1.5 as one of the sons of Japheth, along with Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, and Meshech. Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah, and his descendants are listed in the Table of Nations (Genesis 10), which traces the spread of the nations after the flood. The descendants of Japheth are generally associated with the peoples of Europe and Asia Minor. No specific details are provided about Tiras or his descendants, but some ancient historians and Jewish traditions have attempted to identify them with various ethnic groups, such as the Thracians or the Etruscans. However, these identifications remain speculative and cannot be confirmed from the biblical text alone.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Tiras (תִּירָ֑ס); son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal and Meshech.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '디라스'라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마곡, 마대, 야완, 두발과 메섹의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 디라스는 야벳의 아들이며 노아의 손자로, 홍수 이후 노아의 후손 민족 명단에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Cush (Ethiopia) who opposed Sennacherib
persons.short: Tirhakah, the king of Cush (Ethiopia), opposed Sennacherib's invasion of Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah.
persons.article: Tirhakah, also known as Taharqa, was the king of Cush (Ethiopia) who opposed the Assyrian king Sennacherib during his invasion of Judah (2Ki.19.9; Isa.37.9). He is mentioned as coming to the aid of King Hezekiah, who was under attack by Sennacherib. Tirhakah was the fourth pharaoh of the Twenty-Fifth (Ethiopian) Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from approximately 690 to 664 BC. There is a chronological difficulty in the biblical account, as the events described are believed to have taken place around 701 BC, before Tirhakah's ascension to the throne. Some scholars suggest that Tirhakah may have been acting as a military commander under his predecessor, Pharaoh Shabaka, or that the biblical authors may have combined accounts of two separate campaigns by Sennacherib. Assyrian records also mention Tirhakah's conflict with the Assyrians. Tirhakah's successful opposition to Assyria is recorded on the walls of a temple at Medinet Habu in Egypt.
persons.summary: A king of Cush living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.19.9 only referred to as Tirhakah (תִּרְהָקָה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.19.9에 처음 언급되며 '디르하가'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 구스(에티오피아) 왕 디르하가는 히스기야 왕 시대에 산헤립의 유다 침공을 대적했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Hur@Exo.17.10-2Ch, Jesher@1Ch.2.18, Shobab@1Ch.2.18, Ardon@1Ch.2.18, Mesha@1Ch.2.42, Haran@1Ch.2.46, Moza@1Ch.2.46, Gazez@1Ch.2.46a, Sheber@1Ch.2.48, Regem@1Ch.2.47, Jotham@1Ch.2.47, Geshan@1Ch.2.47, Pelet@1Ch.2.47, Ephah@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.47, Shaaph@1Ch.2.49, Sheva@1Ch.2.49, Achsah@1Ch.2.49
persons.brief: Son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah
persons.short: Tirhanah was a son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Tirhanah is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.2.48 as one of the sons of Caleb by his concubine Maacah. He is listed along with his brothers Sheber and Shaaph. Caleb was a prominent figure from the tribe of Judah, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num.13.6). The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the descendants of Judah, including Caleb's family.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.48 only referred to as Tirhanah (תִּרְחֲנָה); son of Caleb and Maacah; a brother of Ardon, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez, Sheber, Regem(?), Jotham(?), Geshan(?), Pelet(?), Ephah(?), Shaaph(?), Shaaph and Sheva; half-brother of: Hur, Jesher, Shobab, Ardon, Mesha, Haran, Moza, Gazez and Achsah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.2.48에 처음 언급되며 '디르하나'라 불림. 갈렙과 마아가의 아들. 훌, 예셀, 소밥, 아르돈, 메사, 하란, 모사, 가세스, 세벨, 레겜, 요담, 게산, 벨렛, 에바, 사압, 사압, 스와와 악사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 디르하나는 갈렙이 첩 마아가를 통해 낳은 아들로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jehallelel from the tribe of Judah
persons.short: Tiria was a son of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
persons.article: Tiria is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.4.16 as one of the sons of Jehallelel, along with his brothers Ziph, Ziphah, and Asarel. Jehallelel was a descendant of Judah, and his sons are listed in the genealogy of Judah. No further details are provided about Tiria's life or role in the tribe of Judah. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles trace the lineage of the tribes of Israel, particularly focusing on the descendants of Judah and Levi.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.16 only referred to as Tiria (תִּירְיָא); son of Jehallelel; a brother of Ziph, Ziphah and Asarel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.16에 처음 언급되며 '디리아'라 불림. 여할렐렐의 아들. 십, 시바와 아사렐의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 디리아는 여할렐렐의 아들이며 유다의 후손으로, 유다 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad, granted inheritance rights
persons.short: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who were granted inheritance rights in the absence of male heirs.
persons.article: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, a descendant of Manasseh (Num.26.33; 27.1; 36.11; Jos.17.3). Zelophehad had no sons, and his daughters (Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah) approached Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of Israel to seek the right to inherit their father's property. Moses brought their case before the Lord, who instructed him to grant the daughters the right to inherit their father's property in the absence of male heirs (Num.27.1-11). This ruling set a precedent for inheritance rights in Israel. Later, when the Israelites were preparing to enter the Promised Land, the heads of the clan of Manasseh raised concerns about the potential loss of tribal land if the daughters were to marry outside their tribe. In response, the Lord commanded that the daughters of Zelophehad must marry within their father's tribal clan to keep the inheritance within the tribe (Num.36.1-12). Tirzah and her sisters complied with this ruling (Num.36.11). The story of Tirzah and her sisters highlights the importance of inheritance rights and the preservation of tribal allotments in ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.33 only referred to as Tirzah (תִּרְצָה); daughter of Zelophehad; a sister of Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah and Milcah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. Num.26.33에 처음 언급되며 '디르사'라 불림. 슬로브핫의 딸. 말라, 노아, 호글라와 밀가의 자매.
persons.short_ko: 디르사는 슬로브핫의 다섯 딸 중 한 사람으로, 남자 상속자가 없어 유산 상속권을 받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Gentile convert and companion of Paul
persons.short: Titus was a Gentile convert and a trusted companion of Paul, who accompanied him on missionary journeys and served as his delegate to the church in Corinth.
persons.article: Titus was a Gentile convert and a close companion of the Apostle Paul. He is mentioned several times in Paul's epistles, particularly in 2 Corinthians and the letter addressed to him, the Epistle to Titus. Titus was one of Paul's trusted delegates and was involved in his ministry to the churches. Paul refers to Titus as his "true son in the faith" (Tit.1.4, indicating a close spiritual relationship). Titus accompanied Paul to Jerusalem for the council that discussed the inclusion of Gentiles in the church (Gal.2.1-3). He was not compelled to be circumcised, which supported Paul's stance that Gentile converts did not need to adhere to Jewish law. Titus played a significant role in Paul's relationship with the church in Corinth. He was sent by Paul to Corinth to address issues within the church and to encourage the believers (2Co.7.6-7, 13-14; 8.6, 16, 23). Titus' visit brought comfort and reassurance to Paul regarding the Corinthians' response to his earlier letter. Paul also entrusted Titus with the task of collecting an offering for the believers in Jerusalem (2Co.8.6, 16-24). The Epistle to Titus, written by Paul, provides insight into Titus' role as a church leader. Paul had left Titus in Crete to oversee the churches there, appointing elders and dealing with false teachers (Tit.1.5). The letter offers guidance on sound doctrine, qualifications for church leaders, and the importance of good works. According to 2Ti.4.10, Titus later traveled to Dalmatia (modern-day Croatia). Church tradition holds that Titus served as the first bishop of Crete. Titus' life exemplifies the important role that Gentile converts played in the early church and the trust Paul placed in them as fellow ministers of the gospel.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at 2Co.2.13 referred to as Titus (Τίτος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. 2Co.2.13에 처음 언급되며 '디도'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 디도는 이방인 개종자이며 바울의 신뢰받는 동역자로, 그의 선교여행에 동행하고 고린도 교회에 대한 그의 대리인으로 섬겼다.
persons.article_ko: 디도는 이방인 개종자이며 사도 바울의 가까운 동반자였다. 그는 바울의 서신에서 여러 번 언급되는데, 특히 고린도후서와 그에게 보낸 서신인 디도서에서 그렇다. 디도는 바울의 신뢰받는 대리인 중 한 사람이었고 교회들에 대한 그의 사역에 관여했다. 바울은 디도를 '믿음 안에서 참 아들'이라 부르며(딛 1:4) 가까운 영적 관계를 나타낸다. 디도는 교회에서 이방인의 포용에 대해 논의한 회의를 위해 바울과 함께 예루살렘으로 동행했다(갈 2:1-3). 그는 할례를 강요받지 않았는데, 이는 이방인 개종자들이 유대인의 율법을 따를 필요가 없다는 바울의 입장을 지지했다. 디도는 고린도 교회와의 관계에서 바울에게 중요한 역할을 했다. 그는 교회 내의 문제를 다루고 신자들을 격려하기 위해 바울에 의해 고린도로 보내졌다(고후 7:6-7, 13-14; 8:6, 16, 23). 디도의 방문은 이전 편지에 대한 고린도 사람들의 반응에 대해 바울에게 위안과 안심을 주었다. 바울은 또한 예루살렘의 신자들을 위한 헌금을 모으는 임무를 디도에게 맡겼다(고후 8:6, 16-24). 바울이 쓴 디도서는 교회 지도자로서의 디도의 역할에 대한 통찰을 제공한다. 바울은 디도를 그레데에 남겨두어 그곳의 교회들을 감독하며 장로들을 임명하고 거짓 교사들을 다루도록 했다(딛 1:5). 그 편지는 건전한 교리, 교회 지도자의 자격, 선한 행위의 중요성에 대한 지침을 제공한다. 디모데후서 4:10에 따르면 디도는 후에 달마디아(오늘날의 크로아티아)로 여행했다. 교회 전승은 디도가 그레데의 첫 감독으로 섬겼다고 전한다. 디도의 삶은 초대교회에서 이방인 개종자들이 담당한 중요한 역할과 바울이 그들을 동료 복음 사역자로서 신뢰한 것을 잘 보여준다.

persons.description: Warriors from or of Tiz(?)
persons.brief: Clan from the tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: The Tizites were a clan from the tribe of Manasseh, mentioned among the mighty warriors who joined David at Ziklag.
persons.article: The Tizites are mentioned briefly in 1Ch.11.45 as one of the clans from the tribe of Manasseh who sent mighty warriors to join David at Ziklag, when he was hiding from King Saul. The Tizites are listed along with other clans such as the Korahites and the sons of Hashem the Gizonite. No further details are provided about the Tizites or their role in supporting David. The mention of the Tizites highlights the diverse group of warriors who rallied around David during his time of exile and later helped establish his kingdom.
persons.summary: A group of warriors from Tiz(?), only mentioned at 1Ch.11.45 only referred to as Tizites (תִּיצִי).
persons.summary_ko: 디스 사람. 1Ch.11.45에 처음 언급되며 '디스'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 디스 족속은 므낫세 지파 가문으로, 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 합류한 용맹한 용사 중에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Tobadonijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Tobadonijah is mentioned in 2Ch.17.8 as one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat of Judah to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. He was part of a delegation that included other Levites, such as Shemaiah, Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, as well as the priests Elishama and Jehoram. This teaching mission was part of Jehoshaphat's reforms to strengthen the spiritual and moral foundation of his kingdom. The Levites were responsible for instructing the people in the Law of God and ensuring that they understood and followed its precepts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Tobadonijah (טוֹב אֲדֹנִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '도바도니야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 도바도니야는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of returned exiles unable to prove lineage
persons.short: Tobiah was an ancestor of some returned exiles who were unable to prove their Israelite lineage and were excluded from the priesthood.
persons.article: Tobiah is mentioned in Ezr.2.60 and Neh.7.62 as an ancestor of some of the returned exiles from Babylon who were unable to prove their Israelite lineage. These individuals were among the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, who sought to be registered as priests but were excluded because their names could not be found in the genealogical records. As a result, they were considered unclean and disqualified from serving as priests. The mention of Tobiah in this context highlights the importance of genealogical records in determining priestly eligibility and the challenges faced by some returning exiles in establishing their Israelite identity.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.60 only referred to as Tobiah (טוֹבִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.60에 처음 언급되며 '도비야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 도비야는 이스라엘 혈통을 증명하지 못해 제사장직에서 제외된 일부 포로 귀환자들의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Nehemiah's adversary living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding efforts
persons.short: Tobiah was an Ammonite official who, along with Sanballat the Horonite, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Tobiah, described as an Ammonite official, was one of the main opponents of Nehemiah during the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh.2.10, 19; 4.3, 7; 6.1, 12, 14, 17, 19; 13.4, 7, 8). Along with Sanballat the Horonite and Geshem the Arab, Tobiah mocked and threatened Nehemiah and the Jews, trying to discourage and intimidate them from completing the work. Tobiah had close ties with some of the Jewish nobles, who kept him informed about Nehemiah's activities (Neh.6.17-19). He even had a room in the temple courts, which Nehemiah later cleared out (Neh.13.4-8). Despite the opposition and threats, Nehemiah persevered in rebuilding the walls, trusting in God's protection and strength. Tobiah's actions demonstrate the political and social challenges faced by Nehemiah in his efforts to restore Jerusalem and reform the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man of the Ammonites living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Neh.2.10 only referred to as Tobiah (טוֹבִיָּ֫הוּ); husband of daughter of Shecaniah; father of Jehohanan.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 느헤미야의 대적자. Neh.2.10에 처음 언급되며 '도비야'라 불림. 스가냐의 딸(이름 미상)의 남편. 여호하난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 암몬 관리 도비야는 호론 사람 산발랏과 함께 느헤미야의 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 반대했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Tobijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Tobijah is mentioned in 2Ch.17.8 as one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat of Judah to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah. He was part of a delegation that included other Levites, such as Shemaiah, Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, as well as the priests Elishama and Jehoram. This teaching mission was part of Jehoshaphat's reforms to strengthen the spiritual and moral foundation of his kingdom. The Levites were responsible for instructing the people in the Law of God and ensuring that they understood and followed its precepts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Tobijah (טוֹבִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '도비야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 도비야는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Postexilic Jew who provided silver and gold for crowns
persons.short: Tobijah was a postexilic Jew who, along with others, provided silver and gold to make crowns for Joshua the high priest.
persons.article: Tobijah is mentioned in Zec.6.10 and Zec.6.14 as one of the postexilic Jews who provided silver and gold to make crowns for Joshua the high priest. He is described as one of the exiles, along with Heldai and Jedaiah, who came from Babylon to Jerusalem. The crowns were to be placed in the temple as a memorial and a symbol of God's blessing upon Joshua and the future Messiah, the Branch. Tobijah's contribution to this prophetic act demonstrates the participation and support of the returned exiles in the restoration of the temple and the spiritual life of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Zec.6.10 only referred to as Tobijah (טוֹבִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '도비야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 도비야는 포로 이후 시대의 유대인으로, 다른 이들과 함께 대제사장 여호수아의 면류관을 만들 은과 금을 제공했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Gomer, grandson of Japheth
persons.short: Togarmah was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Togarmah is mentioned in Gen.10.3 and 1Ch.1.6 as one of the sons of Gomer and grandsons of Japheth. He is listed in the Table of Nations, which records the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. The descendants of Japheth are generally associated with the peoples of Europe and Asia Minor. Some ancient Jewish traditions and historians have attempted to identify Togarmah with various regions or ethnic groups, such as Armenia or Phrygia, but these connections remain speculative. The mention of Togarmah in the genealogy serves to emphasize the diversity and spread of the nations descended from Noah.
persons.summary: A man of the Gomerians living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.3 only referred to as Togarmah (תֹּגַרְמָה); son of Gomer; a brother of Ashkenaz and Riphath.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.3에 처음 언급되며 '도갈마'라 불림. 고멜의 아들. 아스그나스와 리밧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 도갈마는 고멜의 아들이며 야벳의 손자로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of the prophet Samuel
persons.short: Tohu, also known as Nahath or Toah, was an ancestor of the prophet Samuel, mentioned in his genealogy.
persons.article: Tohu, also referred to as Nahath or Toah, is mentioned in the genealogies of the prophet Samuel (1Sa.1.1; 1Ch.6.26, 34). He was the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite, and an ancestor of Samuel. The genealogy in 1Sa.1.1 traces Samuel's lineage back to Tohu, emphasizing his Ephraimite heritage. In 1Ch.6.26 and 1Ch.6.34, Tohu is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites, specifically the descendants of Kohath. This suggests that Samuel's family had both Ephraimite and Levitical connections.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.1.1 referred to as Tohu (תֹּחוּ), or Nahath (נַ֫חַת), or Toah (תּוֹחַ); a son of Zuph; father of Elihu.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Sa.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '도후'라 불림. 숩의 아들. 엘리후의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 도후(나핫 또는 도아라고도 함)는 선지자 사무엘의 조상으로, 그의 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: King living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Hamath who sent his son to David
persons.short: Toi, also known as Tou, was the king of Hamath who sent his son Joram to congratulate David on his victory over Hadadezer.
persons.article: Toi, also referred to as Tou, was the king of Hamath, a city-state located in present-day Syria (2Sa.8.9-10; 1Ch.18.9-10). After David defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, Toi sent his son Joram (called Hadoram in 1 Chronicles) to congratulate David and bring gifts of silver, gold, and bronze. Toi's gesture was motivated by his own conflict with Hadadezer, as Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. By sending his son to honor David, Toi sought to establish friendly relations with the rising power of Israel and secure an ally against their common enemy. The gifts brought by Joram were dedicated by David to the Lord, along with the silver and gold he had captured from various nations. This episode demonstrates David's growing reputation as a military leader and the diplomatic relationships he established with neighboring kingdoms.
persons.summary: A king of Syria living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.9 referred to as Toi or Tou (תֹּ֫עִי, תֹּעוּ); father of Joram.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 왕. 2Sa.8.9에 처음 언급되며 '도이'라 불림. 요람의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 도이(도우라고도 함)는 하맛 왕으로, 아들 요람을 보내 다윗이 하닷에셀을 이긴 승리를 축하했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.offspring: Uzzi@1Ch.7.2-, Rephaiah@1Ch.7.2, Jeriel@1Ch.7.2, Jahmai@1Ch.7.2, Ibsam@1Ch.7.2, Shemuel@1Ch.7.2
persons.brief: Son of Issachar, ancestor of the Tolaites
persons.short: Tola was a son of Issachar and the ancestor of the Tolaite clan.
persons.article: Tola was one of the sons of Issachar, mentioned in Gen.46.13, Num.26.23, and 1Ch.7.1-2. He was born to Issachar during the family's time in Canaan and went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. Tola became the ancestor of the Tolaite clan within the tribe of Issachar. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, the Tolaite clan numbered 22,600 men (Num.26.23). Tola's descendants were among the Israelites who received an inheritance in the Promised Land. The mention of Tola in the genealogies highlights the growth and development of the tribe of Issachar from the time of the patriarchs to the settlement in Canaan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.13 referred to as Tola (תּוֹלָע), or Tolaite (תּוֹלָעִי); son of Issachar; a brother of Puah, Jashub and Shimron; father of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.13에 처음 언급되며 '돌라'라 불림. 잇사갈의 아들. 부와, 야숩과 시므론의 형제. 웃시, 르바야, 여리엘, 야매, 입삼과 스므엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 돌라는 잇사갈의 아들이며 잇사갈 지파 돌라 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Judge living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Judge of Israel who succeeded Abimelech
persons.short: Tola, the son of Puah, was a judge of Israel who ruled for 23 years after Abimelech's death.
persons.article: Tola was a judge of Israel who succeeded Abimelech and ruled for 23 years (Jdg.10.1-2). He was the son of Puah and the grandson of Dodo from the tribe of Issachar. Tola lived and was buried in Shamir, located in the hill country of Ephraim. His name means "crimson worm" or "scarlet stuff." Despite being one of the judges, the biblical account provides no details about Tola's deeds or accomplishments during his leadership. The brief mention of his reign serves as a transition between the tumultuous rule of Abimelech and the subsequent judge, Jair.
persons.summary: A Judge living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at Jdg.10.1 only referred to as Tola (תּוֹלָע); a son of Puah.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 사사. Jdg.10.1에 처음 언급되며 '돌라'라 불림. 부와의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 부아의 아들 돌라는 아비멜렉이 죽은 후 이스라엘의 사사로 이십삼 년간 다스렸다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Gentile Christian from Ephesus, companion of Paul
persons.short: Trophimus was a Gentile Christian from Ephesus who accompanied Paul on his missionary journeys and was falsely accused of defiling the temple in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Trophimus was a Gentile Christian from Ephesus who accompanied the Apostle Paul on his missionary journeys (Act.20.4). He was one of several individuals who traveled with Paul from Greece to Asia Minor, carrying the collection for the poor in Jerusalem. In Jerusalem, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul in the temple and falsely accused him of bringing Trophimus, a Gentile, into the restricted areas of the temple (Act.21.29). This incident led to Paul's arrest and eventual imprisonment. Later, in his second letter to Timothy, Paul mentions that he had left Trophimus sick in Miletus (2Ti.4.20). Trophimus' presence with Paul highlights the inclusion of Gentiles in the early church and the challenges faced by Paul and his companions as they ministered in various cultural contexts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.20.4 only referred to as Trophimus (Τρόφιμος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.20.4에 처음 언급되며 '드로비모'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드로비모는 에베소 출신 이방인 그리스도인으로, 바울의 선교여행에 동행했으며 예루살렘 성전을 더럽혔다고 거짓 고발당했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul
persons.short: Tryphaena was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Tryphaena is mentioned briefly in Rom.16.12 as one of the Christian women in Rome to whom Paul sends greetings. She is described as one who "worked hard in the Lord," indicating her dedication and service to the church. Paul's greeting suggests that Tryphaena was a prominent member of the Roman Christian community and had labored diligently for the cause of Christ. No other details are provided about her background or specific role in the church. The mention of Tryphaena, along with other women such as Tryphosa and Persis, highlights the significant contributions of women in the early church and their partnership in the gospel ministry.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.12 only referred to as Tryphaena (Τρύφαινα).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Rom.16.12에 처음 언급되며 '드루배나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드루배나는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인 여성이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul
persons.short: Tryphosa was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
persons.article: Tryphosa is mentioned briefly in Rom.16.12 as one of the Christian women in Rome to whom Paul sends greetings. She is described as one who "worked hard in the Lord," indicating her dedication and service to the church. Paul's greeting suggests that Tryphosa was a prominent member of the Roman Christian community and had labored diligently for the cause of Christ. No other details are provided about her background or specific role in the church. The mention of Tryphosa, along with other women such as Tryphaena and Persis, highlights the significant contributions of women in the early church and their partnership in the gospel ministry.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.12 only referred to as Tryphosa (Τρυφῶσα).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Rom.16.12에 처음 언급되며 '드루보사'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 드루보사는 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인 여성이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk, Magog@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Madai@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Javan@Gen.10.2-Col, Meshech@Gen.10.2-1Ch, Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Japheth, grandson of Noah
persons.short: Tubal was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: Tubal is mentioned in Gen.10.2 and 1Ch.1.5 as one of the sons of Japheth and grandsons of Noah. He is listed in the Table of Nations, which records the descendants of Noah's sons after the flood. The descendants of Japheth are generally associated with the peoples of Europe and Asia Minor. Some ancient historians and Jewish traditions have attempted to identify Tubal with various regions or ethnic groups, such as the Tabali or the Iberians, but these connections remain speculative. The mention of Tubal in the genealogy serves to emphasize the diversity and spread of the nations descended from Noah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.2 only referred to as Tubal (תּוּבַל); son of Japheth; a brother of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Meshech and Tiras.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.2에 처음 언급되며 '두발'이라 불림. 야벳의 아들. 고멜, 마곡, 마대, 야완, 메섹과 디라스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 두발은 야벳의 아들이며 노아의 손자로, 민족 계보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Descendant of Cain, first metalworker
persons.short: Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain, was the first metalworker mentioned in the Bible, forging tools out of bronze and iron.
persons.article: Tubal-cain is mentioned in Gen.4.22 as a descendant of Cain, the son of Lamech and Zillah. He is described as a forger of all instruments of bronze and iron, making him the first metalworker mentioned in the Bible. The name Tubal-cain consists of two elements meaning "producer" and "smith," emphasizing his role as a craftsman. No other details are provided about his life or specific works. Tubal-cain's skills in metalworking represent the development of civilization and technology among the descendants of Cain before the flood. His story illustrates God's grace in allowing cultural advancements even among those who had turned away from Him.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.4.22 only referred to as Tubal-cain (תּוּבַל־קַ֫יִן); son of Lamech and Zillah; a brother of Jabal, Jubal and Naamah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.4.22에 처음 언급되며 '두발가인'이라 불림. 라멕과 씰라의 아들. 야발, 유발과 나아마의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 두발가인은 가인의 후손으로, 성경에 처음 언급된 금속 세공사이며 놋과 철로 기구를 만들었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Faithful companion and messenger of Paul
persons.short: Tychicus was a faithful companion of Paul who served as his messenger to the churches in Asia Minor.
persons.article: Tychicus was a faithful companion and fellow worker of the Apostle Paul, mentioned several times in the New Testament (Act.20.4; Eph.6.21; Col.4.7; 2Ti.4.12; Tit.3.12). He was from the province of Asia (modern-day western Turkey) and accompanied Paul on his third missionary journey. Paul entrusted Tychicus with important missions, sending him as a messenger to the churches in Ephesus (Eph.6.21 and Colossae )(Col.4.7 to deliver letters and bring news of Paul's circumstances). In these letters, Paul describes Tychicus as a beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord. Later, Paul sent Tychicus to Ephesus to relieve Timothy (2Ti.4.12 and planned to send him to Crete to assist Titus )(Tit.3.12). Tychicus' frequent appearances in Paul's letters and his role as a trusted messenger demonstrate his significance in the early church and his close relationship with the apostle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Act.20.4 referred to as Tychicus (Τυχικός).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.20.4에 처음 언급되며 '두기고'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 두기고는 바울의 신실한 동행자로, 소아시아 교회들에게 전령으로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Ephesian teacher who hosted Paul's discussions
persons.short: Tyrannus was a teacher in Ephesus who allowed Paul to use his lecture hall for daily discussions about the gospel.
persons.article: Tyrannus is mentioned briefly in Act.19.9 as a teacher in Ephesus who hosted the Apostle Paul's daily discussions about the gospel. When some Jews in the synagogue became stubborn and spoke evil of the Way, Paul withdrew from the synagogue and began teaching in the lecture hall of Tyrannus. This arrangement continued for two years, allowing all the residents of Asia, both Jews and Greeks, to hear the word of the Lord. The name Tyrannus means "tyrant" or "sovereign" in Greek, possibly indicating his profession as a teacher or rhetorician. By providing a venue for Paul's teaching, Tyrannus played a role in the spread of the gospel in Ephesus and the surrounding region, even if inadvertently.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.19.9 only referred to as Tyrannus (Τύραννος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Act.19.9에 처음 언급되며 '두란노'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 두란노는 에베소의 교사로, 바울이 자신의 강당을 사용하여 날마다 복음에 대해 강론하도록 허락했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Recipient of Agur's wisdom in Proverbs 30
persons.short: Ucal is mentioned in <ref="Proverbs 30:1">Proverbs 30:1</ref> as one of the recipients of the wise sayings of Agur son of Jakeh.
persons.article: Ucal is mentioned in Pro.30.1 as one of the recipients, along with Ithiel, of the wise sayings of Agur son of Jakeh. The name Ucal is of uncertain meaning, with some scholars suggesting it could be translated as "I am weary" or "I am consumed." Others propose that Ucal and Ithiel are not proper names but rather phrases expressing Agur's humility and the intended audience of his teachings. The sayings of Agur, found in Proverbs 30, cover various topics, including the wisdom of trusting in God, the danger of pride, and the importance of integrity. Beyond this mention, no other information is provided about Ucal in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at Pro.30.1 only referred to as Ucal (אֻכָל).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. Pro.30.1에 처음 언급되며 '우갈'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우갈은 잠언 30장 1절에 야게의 아들 아굴의 지혜로운 말을 받은 사람 중 한 사람으로 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife
persons.short: Uel was one of the Israelites who agreed to put away his foreign wife during the time of Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Uel is mentioned briefly in Ezr.10.34 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. During the time of Ezra's reforms, when the Israelites were called to repent and return to obedience to God's law, Uel was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives. This action was part of a larger effort to restore the spiritual purity of the Jewish community and prevent the influence of pagan practices. No other details are provided about Uel's background or his specific family situation. His inclusion in this list highlights the widespread nature of the issue of intermarriage and the collective response of the people to Ezra's call for repentance.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.34 only referred to as Uel (אוּאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.34에 처음 언급되며 '우엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우엘은 에스라의 개혁 시대에 이방인 아내를 내보내기로 동의한 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Sheresh, great-grandson of Manasseh
persons.short: Ulam was a son of Sheresh and great-grandson of Manasseh, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh.
persons.article: Ulam is mentioned in 1Ch.7.16-17 as a son of Sheresh and great-grandson of Manasseh. He is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh, along with his brother Rakem. Ulam's mother was Maacah, the wife of Manasseh. No other details are provided about Ulam's life or role within the tribe. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 traces the descendants of Manasseh, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, highlighting the continuity of the family line from the time of the patriarchs to the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.7.16 only referred to as Ulam (אוּלָם); son of Sheresh; a brother of Rakem; father of Bedan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.16에 처음 언급되며 '울람'이라 불림. 세레스의 아들. 라겜의 형제. 브단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 울람은 세레스의 아들이며 므낫세의 증손자로, 므낫세 지파 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Benjamin, known for his numerous descendants
persons.short: Ulam was a descendant of Benjamin known for his numerous descendants, including many skilled archers.
persons.article: Ulam is mentioned in 1Ch.8.39-40 as a descendant of Benjamin. He was the firstborn son of Eleasah (or 'Eshek'), who was a descendant of Saul, the first king of Israel. Ulam is noted for his numerous descendants, which included 150 sons and grandsons. His descendants were known for their skill in archery, as they are described as "mighty men of valor, archers." The large number of Ulam's descendants and their military prowess suggest that he and his family played a significant role in the tribe of Benjamin during their time. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 traces the lineage of Saul and highlights the prominence of certain individuals within the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.39 only referred to as Ulam (אוּלָם); son of Eleasah; a brother of Jeush and Eliphelet.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.39에 처음 언급되며 '울람'이라 불림. 엘르아사의 아들. 여우스와 엘리벨렛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 울람은 베냐민의 후손으로, 활 쏘는 데 능숙한 많은 후손을 두었던 것으로 알려졌다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician during David's reign
persons.short: Unni was a Levite musician who played the harp and participated in the procession when the ark was brought to Jerusalem during David's reign.
persons.article: Unni is mentioned in 1Ch.15.18, 20 as one of the Levite musicians during the reign of King David. He was appointed, along with other skilled musicians, to play the harp during the procession when the ark of the covenant was brought to Jerusalem. Unni was part of the second group of musicians, led by Zechariah, who accompanied the ark with lyres according to alamoth, which may refer to a high pitch or a specific musical term. The inclusion of Unni in this list highlights the importance of music and worship in the transportation of the ark and the establishment of proper worship practices in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18 only referred to as Unni (עֻנִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.15.18에 처음 언급되며 '운니'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 운니는 다윗 왕 시대에 언약궤가 예루살렘으로 옮겨질 때 수금을 연주한 레위인 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Postexilic Levite who assisted in the temple
persons.short: Unni was a postexilic Levite who assisted in the temple during the time of Nehemiah.
persons.article: Unni is mentioned briefly in Neh.12.9 as one of the Levites who assisted in the temple during the post-exilic period, specifically during the time of Nehemiah. He is listed alongside Bakbukiah as a leader who supervised the thanksgiving hymns. This suggests that Unni had a role in organizing and overseeing the musical aspects of worship in the rebuilt temple. The mention of Unni in this context highlights the restoration of proper worship practices and the involvement of the Levites in the religious life of the Jewish community after their return from Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.9 only referred to as Unni (עֻנִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.9에 처음 언급되며 '운노'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 운니는 느헤미야 시대에 성전에서 섬긴 포로 이후 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Ur was the father of Eliphal, one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Ur is mentioned briefly in 1Ch.11.35 as the father of Eliphal, one of David's mighty men. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors who played a significant role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. Eliphal, son of Ur, is listed among these elite soldiers, suggesting that he was known for his military prowess and loyalty to King David. No other details are provided about Ur himself, as the focus is on his son's inclusion in the list of mighty men. The mention of Ur serves to identify Eliphal and highlight the family connections within David's military ranks.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.35 only referred to as Ur (אוּר); father of Eliphal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.11.35에 처음 언급되며 '울'이라 불림. 엘리발의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우르는 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람인 엘리발의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian in Rome greeted by Paul
persons.short: Urbanus was a Christian in Rome whom Paul called a fellow worker in Christ and to whom he sent greetings.
persons.article: Urbanus is mentioned in Rom.16.9 as a member of the Christian community in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings. Paul refers to Urbanus as "our fellow worker in Christ," indicating that he was actively involved in ministry and well-known among the believers. The name Urbanus was common in ancient Roman times, particularly among slaves and freedmen. No other details are provided about Urbanus' background or specific role in the church. The inclusion of his name in Paul's greetings highlights the diversity of the early Christian community in Rome and the apostle's personal concern for the individuals within the church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Rom.16.9 only referred to as Urbanus (Οὐρβανός).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Rom.16.9에 처음 언급되며 '우르바노'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우르바노는 바울이 그리스도 안의 동역자라고 부르며 문안한 로마의 그리스도인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Geber, one of Solomon's officers
persons.short: Uri was the father of Geber, one of the twelve officers appointed by Solomon to provide for the king and his household.
persons.article: Uri is briefly mentioned in 1Ki.4.19 as the father of Geber, one of the twelve officers appointed by King Solomon to provide for the king and his household. Each officer was responsible for supplying provisions for one month out of the year. Geber, the son of Uri, was assigned the region of Gilead, which included the territory of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan. No other information is given about Uri or his background. The mention of Uri serves to identify Geber and his father's lineage, highlighting the administrative structure of Solomon's kingdom.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.19 only referred to as Uri (אוּרִי); father of Geber.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.19에 처음 언급되며 '우리'라 불림. 게벨의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우리는 솔로몬이 왕과 왕실을 위한 물자를 공급하도록 임명한 열두 관리 중 한 사람인 게벨의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Shobal@1Ch.2.50-, Salma@1Ch.2.51-, Hareph@1Ch.2.51, Jezreel@1Ch.4.3, Ishma@1Ch.4.3, Idbash@1Ch.4.3, Hazzelelponi@1Ch.4.3, Penuel@1Ch.4.4, Ezer@1Ch.4.4
persons.brief: Father of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman
persons.short: Uri was the father of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman chosen by God to construct the tabernacle and its furnishings.
persons.article: Uri, the son of Hur from the tribe of Judah, is mentioned in Exo.31.2, 35:30, and Exo.38.22, as well as 1Ch.2.20, as the father of Bezalel. Bezalel was the skilled craftsman chosen by God and filled with the Spirit of God to construct the tabernacle and its furnishings, including the ark of the covenant. Uri's grandson, Bezalel, is also mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1Ch.2.20, emphasizing the family's important role in the construction of the tabernacle. Apart from being the father of Bezalel, no other details are provided about Uri's life or his own role in the community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.31.2 only referred to as Uri (אוּרִי); son of Hur; a brother of Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Jezreel, Ishma, Idbash, Hazzelelponi, Penuel and Ezer; father of Bezalel.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Exo.31.2에 처음 언급되며 '우리'라 불림. 훌의 아들. 소발, 살마, 하렙, 이스르엘, 이스마, 잇바스, 하술렐보니, 브누엘과 에셀의 형제. 브살렐의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우리는 하나님이 성막과 그 기구들을 만들도록 택하신 숙련된 장인 브살렐의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Postexilic Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife
persons.short: Uri was one of the postexilic Israelites who agreed to put away his foreign wife during the time of Ezra's reforms.
persons.article: Uri is mentioned briefly in Ezr.10.24 as one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile. During the time of Ezra's reforms, when the Israelites were called to repent and return to obedience to God's law, Uri was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives. This action was part of a larger effort to restore the spiritual purity of the Jewish community and prevent the influence of pagan practices. No other details are provided about Uri's background or his specific family situation. His inclusion in this list highlights the widespread nature of the issue of intermarriage and the collective response of the people to Ezra's call for repentance.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.24 only referred to as Uri (אוּרִי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.24에 처음 언급되며 '우리'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우리는 에스라의 개혁 시대에 이방인 아내를 내보내기로 동의한 포로 이후 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest during the reign of King Ahaz
persons.short: Uriah was a priest during the reign of King Ahaz who followed the king's instructions in building a new altar based on a pagan model from Damascus.
persons.article: Uriah was a priest who served during the reign of King Ahaz of Judah (2Ki.16.10-16; Isa.8.2). When Ahaz visited Damascus to meet with the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser, he saw a pagan altar that impressed him. Ahaz sent a model of the altar to Uriah, instructing him to build a replica in Jerusalem. Uriah faithfully followed the king's instructions and built the altar. Upon Ahaz's return, the king made offerings on the new altar and modified the temple's ritual to accommodate it, displacing the bronze altar prescribed by God. Uriah's compliance with the king's orders, despite their departure from proper worship, reflects the religious compromise and syncretism that characterized Ahaz's reign. The prophet Isaiah mentions Uriah as a witness to his prophecy about the coming Immanuel (Isa.8.2, suggesting that Uriah was a recognized figure in Jerusalem's priestly community).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.16.10 referred to as Uriah (אוּרִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.16.10에 처음 언급되며 '우리아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우리야는 아하스 왕 시대의 제사장으로, 왕의 지시에 따라 다메섹의 이방 모델을 본뜬 새 제단을 만들었다.

persons.description: Bathsheba's husband living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Hittite soldier; husband of Bathsheba
persons.short: Uriah was a Hittite soldier in David's army, the husband of Bathsheba, who was killed in battle as part of David's plan to cover up his adultery with Bathsheba.
persons.article: Uriah, often referred to as Uriah the Hittite, was a soldier in King David's army (2Samuel 11; 12:9-10, 15; 23:39; 1Ki.15.5; 1Ch.11.41; Mat.1.6). He was married to Bathsheba, with whom David committed adultery while Uriah was away fighting in battle. When Bathsheba became pregnant, David attempted to cover up his sin by summoning Uriah back from the battle and encouraging him to sleep with his wife. However, Uriah's loyalty and sense of duty prevented him from enjoying the comforts of home while his fellow soldiers were in battle. David then sent Uriah back to the front lines with a letter instructing the commander, Joab, to place Uriah in the fiercest part of the battle and then withdraw, ensuring his death. After Uriah's death, David took Bathsheba as his wife, but the Lord was displeased with David's actions. The prophet Nathan confronted David about his sin, and David faced severe consequences, including the death of the child conceived through adultery. Uriah's loyalty and righteousness stand in stark contrast to David's abuse of power and moral failure, serving as a reminder of the importance of integrity and the consequences of sin.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.11.3 referred to as Uriah (אוּרִיָּה), or Uriah (Οὐρίας); husband of Bathsheba.
persons.short_ko: 우리아는 헷 사람으로 밧세바의 남편이었으나 다윗의 계략으로 전장에서 죽었다.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 밧세바의 남편. 2Sa.11.3에 처음 언급되며 '우리아'라 불림. 밧세바의 남편.
persons.article_ko: 우리야(헷 사람 우리야라고도 함)는 다윗 왕 군대의 군인이었다(사무엘하 11장; 12:9-10, 15; 23:39; 왕상 15:5; 대상 11:41; 마 1:6). 그는 밧세바와 결혼했는데, 우리야가 전투에 나가 있는 동안 다윗은 그녀와 간음했다. 밧세바가 임신했을 때 다윗은 우리야를 전투에서 불러들여 자기 아내와 동침하도록 격려함으로써 자기 죄를 은폐하려 했다. 그러나 우리야의 충성심과 의무감은 그의 동료 군인들이 전투 중일 때 집의 안락함을 누리지 못하게 했다. 그러자 다윗은 지휘관 요압에게 우리야를 전투의 가장 치열한 곳에 배치했다가 물러나게 하여 그의 죽음을 확실히 하도록 지시하는 편지와 함께 그를 최전선으로 돌려보냈다. 우리야가 죽은 후 다윗은 밧세바를 아내로 삼았으나, 여호와께서는 다윗의 행동을 기뻐하지 않으셨다. 선지자 나단은 그의 죄에 대해 다윗을 대면했고, 다윗은 간음으로 잉태된 아이의 죽음을 포함한 심각한 결과에 직면했다. 우리야의 충성심과 의로움은 다윗의 권력 남용과 도덕적 실패와 극명한 대조를 이루며, 정직의 중요성과 죄의 결과에 대한 상기가 된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Postexilic priest involved in rebuilding the wall
persons.short: Uriah was a postexilic priest who participated in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem and was entrusted with the temple treasures.
persons.article: Uriah is mentioned in Neh.3.4, 21 and Ezr.8.33 as a priest who played a role in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall and the restoration of the temple during the post-exilic period. In Nehemiah 3, Uriah is listed among those who repaired sections of the wall, with his name appearing twice, suggesting that he was responsible for repairing two different sections. In Ezr.8.33, Uriah is one of the priests entrusted with the weighing and recording of the temple treasures brought back from Babylon. These references highlight Uriah's involvement in the physical and spiritual restoration of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, both in rebuilding the city's defenses and in ensuring the proper handling of the temple's sacred objects.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.8.33 referred to as Uriah (אוּרִיָּה); a son of Hakkoz; father of Meremoth.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.33에 처음 언급되며 '우리아'라 불림. 학고스의 아들. 므레못의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우리야는 포로 이후 시대의 제사장으로, 예루살렘 성벽 재건에 참여하고 성전 보물을 맡았다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied against Jerusalem
persons.short: Uriah was a prophet from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied against Jerusalem and Judah during the reign of King Jehoiakim, and was killed for his message.
persons.article: Uriah, the son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, was a prophet who lived during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah (Jer.26.20-23). He prophesied against Jerusalem and Judah, speaking words similar to those of the prophet Jeremiah. When King Jehoiakim heard about Uriah's prophecies, he sought to kill him. Uriah fled to Egypt, but the king sent men to bring him back. Upon his return, Jehoiakim had Uriah executed and his body thrown into the burial place of the common people. Uriah's death illustrates the danger faced by prophets who spoke out against the sins of their nation and the resistance they encountered from those in power. His story is recounted by Jeremiah as an example of the persecution faced by true prophets of God.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.26.20 only referred to as Uriah (אוּרִיָּ֫הוּ); a son of Shemaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. Jer.26.20에 처음 언급되며 '우리아'라 불림. 스마야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 기럇여아림 출신 선지자 우리야는 여호야김 왕 시대에 예루살렘과 유다를 대적하여 예언하다가 그 메시지 때문에 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
persons.short: Uriah was one of the priests who assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people during the religious revival in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Uriah is mentioned briefly in Neh.8.4 as one of the priests who stood beside Ezra when he read the Book of the Law to the assembled people in Jerusalem. This event took place during a time of religious revival and renewal, as the Israelites sought to reestablish their covenant relationship with God after returning from Babylonian exile. Uriah, along with other priests and Levites, supported Ezra in his role as a teacher and spiritual leader, helping to make the Law clear and understandable to the people. The presence of Uriah and the other priests alongside Ezra demonstrates the importance of religious leadership and the collaborative effort involved in guiding the people in their renewed commitment to God's commands.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Uriah (אוּרִיָּה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '우리아'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우리야는 에스라가 예루살렘의 영적 부흥기에 백성에게 율법을 낭독하는 것을 도운 제사장 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Kohathite leader who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem
persons.short: Uriel, a Kohathite leader, assisted in bringing the ark to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Uriel was a leader of the Kohathite clan during the reign of King David. He is mentioned as one of the Levites whom David summoned to help bring the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. Uriel, along with other Levite leaders, consecrated themselves to carry the ark on the second attempt after the first failed. He played an important role in this sacred task of transporting the ark to its new resting place in the City of David.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.5 only referred to as Uriel (אוּרִיאֵל).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.15.5에 처음 언급되며 '우리엘'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 고핫 계열 지도자 우리엘은 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮기는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Kohathite Levite, ancestor of the prophet Samuel
persons.short: Uriel, also known as Zephaniah, was a Kohathite Levite and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel.
persons.article: Uriel, also referred to as Zephaniah, is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in 1Ch.6.24 and 1Ch.6.36. He was a descendant of Kohath, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. Uriel is listed as the son of Tahath and the father of Uzziah (called Azariah in verse 36). He is identified as an ancestor of the prophet Samuel, who was also a descendant of Kohath. The dual names Uriel and Zephaniah may indicate that he was known by both names or that there was some variation in the historical records. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles trace the lineage of important figures in Israel's history, highlighting the continuity of the Levitical priesthood and the family lines of significant individuals like Samuel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.24 referred to as Uriel (אוּרִיאֵל), or Zephaniah (צְפַנְיָהוּ); a son of Tahath; father of Uzziah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.24에 처음 언급되며 '우리엘'이라 불림. 다핫의 아들. 웃시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우리엘(스바냐라고도 함)은 고핫 계열 레위인으로 선지자 사무엘의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of mother of Abijah, king of Judah
persons.short: Uriel was the father of the mother of Abijah, king of Judah.
persons.article: Uriel, of Gibeah, was the father of Maacah, wife of Rehoboam, king of Judah, and mother of Abijah, who succeeded Rehoboam as king. She is mentioned by name only once in the genealogy of the kings of Judah. No other details are provided about her life or character. Her mention establishes the lineage of King Abijah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.13.2 only referred to as Uriel (אוּרִיאֵל); husband of Tamar; father of Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.13.2에 처음 언급되며 '우리엘'이라 불림. 다말의 남편. 마아가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우리엘은 유다 왕 아비야의 어머니의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Judahite who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Uthai, a descendant of Perez, resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Uthai was a descendant of Perez, son of Judah. He is listed among the first Judahites to resettle in Jerusalem after returning from Babylonian captivity. Uthai belonged to the clan of Perez, one of the two main Judahite clans along with Zerah. His mention helps establish that members of Judah were among the first returnees to reinhabit Jerusalem and begin rebuilding Jewish life there after the exile.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.4 only referred to as Uthai (עוּתַי); a son of Ammihud.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.4에 처음 언급되며 '우대'라 불림. 암미훗의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 베레스의 후손 우대는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 재정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Exile who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra
persons.short: Uthai, along with Zabbud, led a group returning to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Uthai was one of the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon with Ezra the scribe. He, along with Zabbud, is recorded as leading a group of 70 males of the descendants of Bigvai in this return journey. This took place during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, who commissioned Ezra to lead a group back to Judah to reestablish worship and law according to the Torah. Uthai was part of this important group helping to restore Jewish life in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.14 only referred to as Uthai (עוּתַי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.14에 처음 언급되며 '우대'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 우대는 삽붓과 함께 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 무리를 이끌었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Aram, grandson of Shem
persons.short: Uz, son of Aram and grandson of Shem, was an early Semitic patriarch.
persons.article: Uz was the son of Aram and grandson of Shem, son of Noah. He is mentioned twice in the Table of Nations which records the descendants of Noah's sons who spread out and populated the earth after the flood. Uz was an early post-flood patriarch whose descendants likely settled in the region that bore his name, the land of Uz. This area was probably located east of the Jordan River in what is now northern Saudi Arabia. The Book of Job identifies the land of Uz as Job's homeland. Uz's mention helps trace the Semitic peoples descended from Shem.
persons.summary: A man of the Syrians living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.23 only referred to as Uz (עוּץ); son of Aram; a brother of Hul, Gether and Mash.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.23에 처음 언급되며 '우스'라 불림. 아람의 아들. 훌, 게델과 마스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 우스는 아람의 아들이며 셈의 손자로, 초기 셈족 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Buz@Gen.22.21, Kemuel@Gen.22.21, Chesed@Gen.22.22, Hazo@Gen.22.22, Pildash@Gen.22.22, Jidlaph@Gen.22.22, Bethuel@Gen.22.22-, Tebah@Gen.22.24, Gaham@Gen.22.24, Tahash@Gen.22.24, Maacah@Gen.22.24
persons.brief: Son of Nahor, Abraham's brother
persons.short: Uz, son of Nahor and nephew of Abraham, was an Aramean.
persons.article: Uz was the son of Nahor, who was the brother of Abraham. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Abraham's family, which lists the descendants of his brother Nahor. Uz was one of Nahor's sons born to his wife Milcah in Paddan-aram, the region where Abraham originally came from. As Abraham's nephew, Uz was part of the extended family that formed the early Semitic peoples living in Mesopotamia.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.22.21 only referred to as Uz (עוּץ); son of Nahor and Milcah; a brother of Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel; half-brother of: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.22.21에 처음 언급되며 '우스'라 불림. 나홀과 밀가의 아들. 부스, 그무엘, 게셋, 하소, 빌다스, 이들랍, 브두엘, 데바, 가함, 다하스와 마아가의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 우스는 나홀의 아들이며 아브라함의 조카로, 아람 사람이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Dishan, a Horite chief
persons.short: Uz, a Horite, was the son of Dishan, a chief in Seir.
persons.article: Uz was a Horite man, the son of Dishan, who was one of the chiefs of the Horites living in the land of Seir. The Horites were the original inhabitants of Seir before the Edomites displaced them. Uz is listed in the genealogy of the chiefs of Edom, which includes Horite and Edomite rulers. His mention helps trace the peoples living in Seir and Edom in the time of Esau and his descendants.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.28 only referred to as Uz (עוּץ); son of Dishan; a brother of Aran.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.28에 처음 언급되며 '우스'라 불림. 디산의 아들. 아란의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 우스는 호리 사람으로 디산의 아들이며 세일의 족장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Palal, who repaired Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Uzai was the father of Palal, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Uzai is mentioned only as the father of Palal, who was one of the people responsible for repairing a section of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah. Palal repaired the section next to Pedaiah son of Parosh.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.25 only referred to as Uzai (אוּזַי); father of Palal.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.25에 처음 언급되며 '우새'라 불림. 발랄의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 우새는 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도운 발랄의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Almodad@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Sheleph@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hazarmaveth@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Jerah@Gen.10.26-1Ch, Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Diklah@Gen.10.27-1Ch, Obal@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Abimael@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Sheba@Gen.10.28-1Ch, Ophir@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Havilah@Gen.10.29-1Ch, Jobab@Gen.10.29-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
persons.short: Uzal, a descendant of Shem, was one of Joktan's sons.
persons.article: Uzal was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Shem's descendants, which traces the lineage of the Semitic peoples. Uzal and his brothers were said to have settled in the region "from Mesha toward Sephar, in the eastern hill country." Uzal likely settled and gave his name to an area in ancient Yemen, as the ancient name for the Yemeni city of Sanaa was also Uzal.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.10.27 only referred to as Uzal (אוּזָל); son of Joktan; a brother of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '우살'이라 불림. 욕단의 아들. 알모닷, 셀렙, 하살마웻, 예라, 하도람, 디글라, 오발, 아비마엘, 세바, 오빌, 하윌라와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 우살은 셈의 후손으로 욕단의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Benjamite exile born in Moab
persons.short: Uzza was a Benjamite born in Moab during the exile.
persons.article: Uzza was a Benjamite man who was born in the land of Moab. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin, which includes those who were born during the time when many Israelites were living in Moab. The context suggests this was likely during the Babylonian exile. Uzza and his brothers Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera were all born in Moab before Gera moved the family away from there.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living before Israel's Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.7 only referred to as Uzza (עֻזָּא); son of Ehud; a brother of Naaman, Ahijah, Gera and Ahihud.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. 1Ch.8.7에 처음 언급되며 '웃사'라 불림. 에훗의 아들. 나아만, 아히야, 게라와 아히훗의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃사는 포로 시대에 모압 땅에서 태어난 베냐민 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylon
persons.short: Uzza was an ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Uzza is mentioned as an ancestor of some of the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian captivity. These servants were likely descendants of people who had been assigned by David and the leaders to assist the Levites in the temple service. The list in Ezra and Nehemiah records those who came back to help rebuild Jerusalem and restore the temple worship after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.49 only referred to as Uzza (עֻזָּא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.49에 처음 언급되며 '웃사'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 웃사는 바벨론 포로에서 돌아온 성전 봉사자의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the clan of Merari
persons.short: Uzzah, a Levite of the Merarite clan, was the son of Shimei.
persons.article: Uzzah was a Levite who belonged to the clan of Merari, one of the three main Levite clans. He was the son of Shimei. This Uzzah is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites, which lists the descendants of Levi who were responsible for assisting the priests and maintaining the tabernacle and temple.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.29 only referred to as Uzzah (עֻזָּה); a son of Shimei; father of Shimea.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.29에 처음 언급되며 '웃사'라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 시므아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃사는 므라리 가문 레위인이며 시므이의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Died while moving the ark; place named after him
persons.short: Uzzah died while moving the ark; the place was named Perez-uzzah.
persons.article: Uzzah was a man who died while transporting the ark of the covenant. He and his brother Ahio were guiding the cart carrying the ark when the oxen stumbled. Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, but God struck him down for his irreverent act, and he died there beside the ark. The place where this occurred was named Perez-uzzah, which means "outbreak against Uzzah," and David was angry and afraid because of this divine judgment. The ark was then taken aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.6.3 referred to as Uzzah (עֻזָּא), or Perez-uzzah (פֶּרֶץ עֻזָּא); son of Abinadab; a brother of Eleazar and Ahio.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 2Sa.6.3에 처음 언급되며 '웃사'라 불림. 아비나답의 아들. 엘르아살과 아효의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃사는 언약궤를 옮기던 중 죽었고, 그 장소는 베레스웃사라 불리게 되었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: High priest in the line of Eleazar
persons.short: Uzzi was a high priest in the lineage of Eleazar, son of Aaron.
persons.article: Uzzi was a high priest who served in the line of Eleazar, the third son of Aaron. He was the son of Bukki and the father of Zerahiah. Uzzi is mentioned in the genealogy of the high priests who descended from Eleazar. This lineage was important for establishing the legitimate succession of high priests. Ezra, the priest and scribe who led a return from Babylon, was also a descendant of Uzzi according to his recorded genealogy.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.5 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי); a son of Bukki; father of Zerahiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 제사장. 1Ch.6.5에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림. 북기의 아들. 스라히야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시는 아론의 아들 엘르아살 계열의 대제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Tola, grandson of Issachar
persons.short: Uzzi, a grandson of Issachar, was one of the sons of Tola.
persons.article: Uzzi was a descendant of Issachar, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. He was the son of Tola and one of the clan heads of Issachar. Uzzi and his brothers Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Samuel were all described as brave warriors and outstanding leaders. Their descendants were numerous and powerful during the time of King David. This Uzzi helped establish the strength and influence of the tribe of Issachar.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Issachar living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at 1Ch.7.2 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי); son of Tola; a brother of Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel; father of Izrahiah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.2에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림. 돌라의 아들. 르바야, 여리엘, 야매, 입삼과 스므엘의 형제. 이스라히야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시는 잇사갈의 손자이며 돌라의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ard@Num.26.40, Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Ezbon@1Ch.7.7, Uzziel@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abihud@1Ch.8.3, Abishua@1Ch.8.4, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin
persons.short: Uzzi, a grandson of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Bela.
persons.article: Uzzi was a descendant of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. He was the son of Bela, who was one of Benjamin's sons. Uzzi is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, along with his brothers Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all described as heads of their families and mighty warriors. This Uzzi was part of the fighting strength of the Benjamites.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.7 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי); son of Bela; a brother of Ard, Naaman, Ezbon, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 용사. 1Ch.7.7에 처음 언급되며 '우시'라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 아릇, 나아만, 에스본, 웃시엘, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비훗, 아비수아와 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃시는 베냐민의 손자이며 벨라의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem
persons.short: Uzzi, a Benjamite, was one of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
persons.article: Uzzi was a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem. He is mentioned in the list of the first inhabitants of Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. This list includes people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh who settled in the city. Uzzi's mention indicates that he was one of the Benjamites who took up residence in Jerusalem to help repopulate the city after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at 1Ch.9.8 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי); a son of Michri; father of Elah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. 1Ch.9.8에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림. 미그리의 아들. 엘라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시는 베냐민 사람으로 예루살렘 주민 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite overseer in Jerusalem
persons.short: Uzzi, a Levite, was an overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem.
persons.article: Uzzi was a Levite who served as an overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem. He is mentioned in the list of people who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. Uzzi was the son of Bani, from the descendants of Asaph, one of the main Levite clans responsible for music and singing in temple worship. As an overseer, Uzzi likely had leadership responsibilities for the Levites serving in the city and at the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.22 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי); a son of Bani.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.22에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림. 바니의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 웃시는 예루살렘 레위인의 감독이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priestly leader in the days of Joiakim
persons.short: Uzzi was a leader of the priestly family of Jedaiah during Joiakim's time.
persons.article: Uzzi was a priest who served as the head of the priestly family of Jedaiah during the time of Joiakim. Joiakim was the son of Jeshua, the high priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel. Uzzi is mentioned in the list of priestly family heads during this period of rebuilding after the exile. As a leader of the Jedaiah family, Uzzi would have had important responsibilities in the priestly service at the newly rebuilt temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.19 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.19에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 웃시는 요야김 시대에 여다야 제사장 가문의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Uzzi, a priest, participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Uzzi was one of the priests who participated in the dedication ceremony for the rebuilt wall of Jerusalem. After the wall was completed under Nehemiah's leadership, a great celebration was held to dedicate the wall and give thanks to God. Uzzi is listed among the priests who were present and took part in this joyful occasion, along with other priests, Levites, and leaders. His participation signifies the important role of the priests in the restoration of Jerusalem's religious life.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.42 only referred to as Uzzi (עֻזִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.42에 처음 언급되며 '웃시'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 웃시는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ashterathite, one of David's mighty warriors
persons.short: Uzzia the Ashterathite was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Uzzia the Ashterathite is mentioned in the list of David's mighty warriors, also known as David's "Thirty." This list includes the most elite and skilled soldiers who fought alongside David. Uzzia is described as an Ashterathite, which likely indicates he was from the city of Ashtaroth, a Levitical city in the territory of Manasseh.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.44 only referred to as Uzzia (עֻזִּיָּא).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.44에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아스드랏 사람 웃시아는 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of King David's storehouses
persons.short: Uzziah was in charge of King David's storehouses.
persons.article: Uzziah was one of the officials in charge of King David's storehouses. He is mentioned in the list of people appointed over various aspects of David's administration. The storehouses were used to store agricultural produce, goods, and treasures collected by the king. Uzziah's role was to oversee and manage these royal storehouses, ensuring proper storage and distribution of the items as needed.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.25 only referred to as Uzziah (עֻזִּיָּהוּ); father of Jonathan.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.25에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림. 요나단의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야는 다윗 왕의 곳간을 관리했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite musician in the time of David
persons.short: Uzziah (Azariah) was a Levite musician during David's reign.
persons.article: Uzziah, also known as Azariah, was a Levite who served as a musician during the reign of King David.
