He is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites, specifically in the lineage of Heman, the king's seer. Uzziah was a descendant of Kohath, one of the three main Levite clans. As a Levite musician, he would have been involved in providing music for worship at the tabernacle and later in the preparations for the temple services.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.24 referred to as Uzziah (עֻזִּיָּהוּ), or Azariah (עֲזַרְיָ֫הוּ); a son of Uriel; father of Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.24에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림. 우리엘의 아들. 사울의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야(아사랴라고도 함)는 다윗 왕 시대의 레위인 음악가였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: King of Judah, reigned 52 years
persons.short: Uzziah (Azariah) was king of Judah, known for his long and prosperous reign.
persons.article: Uzziah, also called Azariah, was a king of Judah who reigned for 52 years. He became king at the age of 16 and did what was right in God's sight, seeking Him during the days of Zechariah. God made him prosper, and he had success in wars against the Philistines and Arabs. Uzziah built towers and fortified Jerusalem, assembled a well-equipped army, and developed agricultural projects. However, when he became strong, pride led to his downfall. He entered the temple to burn incense, a task reserved for priests, and God struck him with leprosy until his death. Uzziah was a contemporary of the prophets Isaiah, Amos, and Hosea. He is also included in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.14.21 referred to as Uzziah (עֻזִּיָּהוּ), or Azariah (עֲזַרְיָה), or Azariah (עֲזַרְיָ֫הוּ), or Uzziah (Ὀζίας); a son of Amaziah and Jecoliah; husband of Jerusha; father of Jotham.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.14.21에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림. 아마샤와 여골리아의 아들. 여루사의 남편. 요담의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야(아사랴라고도 함)는 유다 왕으로, 길고 번영한 통치로 알려졌다.
persons.article_ko: 웃시야(아사랴라고도 함)는 오십이 년간 다스린 유다 왕이었다. 그는 십육 세에 왕이 되었고 하나님 보시기에 정직한 것을 행하며 스가랴 시대에 하나님을 찾았다. 하나님은 그를 형통하게 하셔서 그는 블레셋과 아라비아를 대적하는 전쟁에서 성공을 거두었다. 웃시야는 망대를 세우고 예루살렘을 요새화하며 잘 갖추어진 군대를 조직하고 농업 사업을 발전시켰다. 그러나 그가 강성해졌을 때 교만이 그의 몰락을 초래했다. 그는 제사장에게만 허락된 직무인 분향을 하러 성전에 들어갔고, 하나님은 그를 나병으로 치셔서 그가 죽을 때까지 낫지 않았다. 웃시야는 선지자 이사야, 아모스, 호세아와 동시대 인물이었다. 그는 또한 마태복음의 예수님 족보에도 포함되어 있다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Uzziah was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Uzziah is mentioned in the list of men who had taken foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This was discovered when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and found that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land. Uzziah was one of those who had violated God's command not to intermarry with foreigners. In response to Ezra's call for repentance, Uzziah and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives and children to maintain the purity of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.21 only referred to as Uzziah (עֻזִּיָּהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Judahite who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Uzziah, a descendant of Judah, resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Uzziah was a descendant of Perez, son of Judah. He is mentioned in the list of people who resettled in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian captivity. Uzziah is described as a valiant warrior, indicating he was a man of strength and skill. He was among the first Judahites to resettle in Jerusalem and help rebuild the city and its community after the exile.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.4 only referred to as Uzziah (עֻזִּיָּהוּ); a son of Zechariah; father of Athaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.4에 처음 언급되며 '웃시야'라 불림. 스가랴의 아들. 아다야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 웃시야는 유다의 후손으로 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에 재정착했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Bukkiah@1Ch.25.4-, Mattaniah@1Ch.25.4-, Shebuel@1Ch.25.4-, Jerimoth@1Ch.25.4-, Hananiah@1Ch.25.4-, Hanani@1Ch.25.4-, Eliathah@1Ch.25.4-, Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-, Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-, Joshbekashah@1Ch.25.4-, Mallothi@1Ch.25.4-, Hothir@1Ch.25.4-, Mahazioth@1Ch.25.4-
persons.brief: Levite musician in the time of David
persons.short: Uzziel (Azarel), a Levite musician, served during David's reign.
persons.article: Uzziel, also called Azarel, was a Levite musician who served during the reign of King David. He was one of the sons of Heman, the king's seer, who were appointed to provide music and praise in the house of the Lord. Uzziel and his brothers were trained and skilled in singing to the Lord, and they served under the direction of their father Heman. They were part of the Levitical choir that led worship and gave thanks to God with musical instruments and songs.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.4 referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל), or Azarel (עֲזַרְאֵל); son of Heman; a brother of Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.4에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 헤만의 아들. 북기야, 맛다냐, 스브엘, 여레못, 하나냐, 하나니, 엘리아다, 깃달디, 로암디에셀, 요스브가사, 말로디, 호딜과 마하시옷의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃시엘(아사렐이라고도 함)은 다윗 왕 시대에 섬긴 레위인 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite leader who attacked the Amalekites
persons.short: Uzziel, a Simeonite leader, joined in an attack against the Amalekites.
persons.article: Uzziel was a leader from the tribe of Simeon. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Simeon as one of the sons of Ishi. Uzziel, along with his brothers Pelatiah, Neariah, and Rephaiah, led a group of 500 Simeonite men in an attack against the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped to Mount Seir. They struck down the Amalekites and took possession of their land, where they settled and lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon(?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.42 only referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל); son of Ishi; a brother of Pelatiah, Neariah and Rephaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.42에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 이시의 아들. 블라댜, 느아랴와 르바야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃시엘은 아말렉 사람들을 공격하는 데 가담한 시므온 지파 지도자였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Ard@Num.26.40, Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch, Ezbon@1Ch.7.7, Uzzi@1Ch.7.7, Jerimoth@1Ch.7.7, Iri@1Ch.7.7, Addar@1Ch.8.3, Gera@1Ch.8.3, Abihud@1Ch.8.3, Abishua@1Ch.8.4, Ahoah@2Sa.23.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin
persons.short: Uzziel, a grandson of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Bela.
persons.article: Uzziel was a descendant of Benjamin, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. He was the son of Bela, Benjamin's firstborn son. Uzziel is listed in the genealogy of Benjamin along with his brothers Ezbon, Uzzi, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all described as heads of their families and mighty warriors, indicating their strength and leadership within the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A warrior from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.7 only referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל); son of Bela; a brother of Ard, Naaman, Ezbon, Uzzi, Jerimoth, Iri, Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua and Ahoah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 용사. 1Ch.7.7에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 벨라의 아들. 아릇, 나아만, 에스본, 웃시, 여레못, 이리, 앗달, 게라, 아비훗, 아비수아와 아호아의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 웃시엘은 베냐민의 손자이며 벨라의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped cleanse the temple under Hezekiah
persons.short: Uzziel, a Levite, assisted in cleansing the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Uzziel was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. He was the son of Jeduthun. When Hezekiah ordered the cleansing and rededication of the temple, which had been neglected under previous kings, Uzziel was among the Levites who gathered to help. He, along with other Levites, worked to clean and purify the temple, remove the unclean items, and prepare it for proper worship once again.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.14 only referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל); son of Jeduthun; a brother of Shemaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 2Ch.29.14에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 여두둔의 아들. 스마야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 웃시엘은 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Aaron's uncle living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Kohath, uncle of Moses and Aaron
persons.short: Uzziel, son of Kohath, was an uncle of Moses and Aaron.
persons.article: Uzziel was a Levite, the son of Kohath and grandson of Levi. He was the brother of Amram, making him the uncle of Moses and Aaron. Uzziel had three sons: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri. His descendants, the Uzzielites, were one of the Levite clans responsible for the care and transportation of the tabernacle. Uzziel's son Elzaphan and his brother Mishael were called by Moses to carry away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu after they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. The descendants of Uzziel were also counted in the census of the Levites and given specific duties in the service of the tabernacle.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Exo.6.18 referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל), or Uzzielite (עׇזִּיאֵלִי); son of Kohath; a brother of Amram, Izhar and Hebron; father of Mishael, Elizaphan, Sithri, Micah and Isshiah; father of Aaron.
persons.short_ko: 웃시엘은 고핫의 아들로 모세와 아론의 삼촌뻘 되는 레위인이다.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 아론의 삼촌. Exo.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 그핫의 아들. 아므람, 이스할과 헤브론의 형제. 미사엘, 엘사반, 시드리, 미가와 잇시야의 아버지.
persons.article_ko: 웃시엘은 고핫의 아들이며 레위의 손자인 레위인이었다. 그는 아므람의 형제였고, 이는 그가 모세와 아론의 삼촌임을 의미한다. 웃시엘에게는 미사엘, 엘사반, 시드리 세 아들이 있었다. 그의 후손인 웃시엘 사람들은 성막의 관리와 운반을 담당한 레위인 가문 중 하나였다. 웃시엘의 아들 엘사반과 그의 형제 미사엘은 나답과 아비후가 여호와 앞에 허가받지 않은 불을 드린 후 모세에게 부름을 받아 그들의 시신을 옮겼다. 웃시엘의 후손은 또한 레위인 인구조사에 계수되었고 성막 봉사에서 특정 직무를 부여받았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Goldsmith who helped repair Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Uzziel, a goldsmith, was one of the people who repaired Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Uzziel was a goldsmith who participated in repairing the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. He is mentioned as one of the people who worked on restoring the city's fortifications after the Babylonian exile. Uzziel, along with Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired a section of the wall next to the work of Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph. The involvement of goldsmiths and perfumers in the wall's repair shows the community-wide effort in rebuilding Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.8 only referred to as Uzziel (עֻזִּיאֵל); a son of Harhaiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.8에 처음 언급되며 '웃시엘'이라 불림. 할해야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 금장색 웃시엘은 예루살렘 성벽을 수리한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Parshandatha@Est.9.7, Dalphon@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Parmashta@Est.9.9, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9
persons.brief: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
persons.short: Vaizatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.
persons.article: Vaizatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the chief enemy of the Jews in the book of Esther. Haman plotted to destroy all the Jews in the Persian Empire, but his plan was thwarted by Queen Esther and her cousin Mordecai. After Haman's downfall and execution, the king granted the Jews the right to defend themselves against their enemies. On the appointed day, the Jews defeated those who sought to harm them, and they also killed Haman's ten sons, including Vaizatha. The bodies of Haman's sons were hanged on the gallows, demonstrating the complete defeat of those who opposed the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.9.9 only referred to as Vaizatha (וַיְזָתָא); son of Haman; a brother of Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai and Aridai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.9.9에 처음 언급되며 '왜사다'라 불림. 하만과 세레스의 아들. 바산다다, 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새와 아리대의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 바이사다는 유대인의 원수 하만의 열 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Vaniah was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Vaniah is mentioned in the list of men who had taken foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This was discovered when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and found that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land. Vaniah was one of those who had violated God's command not to intermarry with foreigners. In response to Ezra's call for repentance, Vaniah and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives and children to maintain the purity of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.36 only referred to as Vaniah (וַנְיָה).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.36에 처음 언급되며 '와냐'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 와냐는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Queen of Persia, deposed by King Ahasuerus (Xerxes)
persons.short: Vashti, queen of Persia, was deposed by King Ahasuerus for disobeying his command.
persons.article: Vashti was the queen of Persia and the wife of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). She is introduced in the book of Esther during a great feast the king held for his officials and servants. On the seventh day of the feast, when the king was drunk, he commanded Vashti to appear before him and his guests wearing her royal crown, to display her beauty. However, Vashti refused to come at the king's command, which greatly angered him. After consulting with his wise men, the king decided to remove Vashti as queen and give her royal position to another. This decision led to the selection of Esther as the new queen, setting the stage for her role in saving the Jewish people from Haman's plot. Vashti's refusal to appear before the king and her subsequent removal from her position is a key event in the early part of the book of Esther.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.1.9 only referred to as Vashti (וַשְׁתִּי); wife of Ahasuerus; mother of Darius and Artaxerxes.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Est.1.9에 처음 언급되며 '와스디'라 불림. 아하수에로의 아내. 다리오와 아닥사스다의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 와스디는 페르시아 왕비로, 아하수에로 왕의 명령에 불순종하여 폐위되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Father of Nahbi, the Naphtalite spy
persons.short: Vophsi was the father of Nahbi, the man chosen to represent the tribe of Naphtali as a spy.
persons.article: Vophsi is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Nahbi, the man selected from the tribe of Naphtali to be one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. Each tribe provided one man for this mission. Vophsi's son Nahbi was chosen to represent Naphtali. No other details are provided about Vophsi himself. His name is of uncertain meaning, and the text is considered doubtful by some scholars, with variations found in ancient manuscripts.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.14 only referred to as Vophsi (וׇפְסִי); father of Nahbi.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.14에 처음 언급되며 '웝시'라 불림. 나비의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 봅시는 정탐꾼으로 납달리 지파를 대표하도록 선택된 납비의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Horite chief, descendant of Seir the Horite
persons.short: Zaavan, a Horite chief, was a descendant of Seir the Horite.
persons.article: Zaavan was a Horite chief mentioned in the genealogies of Esau and Seir the Horite. He was one of the sons of Ezer, who was a son of Seir. The Horites were the original inhabitants of the land of Seir, which was later inhabited by the Edomites. Zaavan is listed among the chiefs of the Horites, indicating his position of leadership within the tribe. The Bible provides no further details about his life or role as a chief.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.27 only referred to as Zaavan (זַעֲוָן); son of Ezer; a brother of Bilhan and Akan.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.27에 처음 언급되며 '사아완'이라 불림. 에셀의 아들. 빌한과 야아간의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사아완은 세일 사람 호리의 후손인 호리 사람 족장이었다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty warriors
persons.short: Zabad, the son of Ahlai, was one of David's mighty warriors.
persons.article: Zabad, the son of Ahlai, is listed among the mighty warriors who supported David. These warriors were known for their bravery, skill in battle, and loyalty to King David. Zabad is mentioned in the list of David's mighty men, indicating his status as an elite soldier. The Bible does not provide any specific details about Zabad's individual exploits or achievements, but his inclusion in this list suggests he was a valiant and capable warrior who contributed to David's military success.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.11.41 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד); a son of Ahlai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 용사. 1Ch.11.41에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림. 알래의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아흘래의 아들 사밧은 다윗의 용맹한 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Descendant of Judah through Jerahmeel
persons.short: Zabad was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.
persons.article: Zabad is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically in the line of Jerahmeel. He was the son of Nathan and the father of Ephlal. Zabad is listed as part of the descendants of Sheshan, who had no sons and gave his daughter in marriage to his Egyptian servant Jarha. This genealogy shows the intermarriage between Israelites and non-Israelites.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.2.36 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד); a son of Nathan; father of Ephlal.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.36에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림. 나단의 아들. 에블랄의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사밧은 여라므엘 계열을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Ephraim, killed by men of Gath
persons.short: Zabad, a son of Ephraim, was killed by the men of Gath.
persons.article: Zabad was one of the sons of Ephraim, the son of Joseph. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim. According to the account, Zabad and his brother Shuthelah were killed by the men of Gath, who were native inhabitants of the land. This incident occurred when Ephraim's descendants attempted to raid the livestock of the Gathites. The death of Zabad and his brother was a tragedy for the tribe of Ephraim.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Ephraim living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.21 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד); a son of Tahath; father of Shuthelah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.21에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림. 다핫의 아들. 수델라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사밧은 에브라임의 아들로, 가드 사람들에게 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Zabad, son of Zattu, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Zabad, the son of Zattu, is mentioned in the list of men who had taken foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This was discovered when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and found that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land. Zabad was one of those who had violated God's command not to intermarry with foreigners. In response to Ezra's call for repentance, Zabad and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives and children to maintain the purity of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.27 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.27에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삿두의 아들 사밧은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Zabad, son of Hashum, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Zabad, the son of Hashum, is listed among the men who had taken foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This issue came to light when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and discovered that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land, contrary to God's command. Zabad was one of those who had married a foreign woman. When Ezra called for repentance, Zabad and the others agreed to separate from their foreign wives and children to preserve the holiness of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.33 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.33에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 하숨의 아들 사밧은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Zabad, son of Nebo, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Zabad, the son of Nebo, is mentioned in the list of men who had married foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This problem was discovered when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and found that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land, violating God's command. Zabad was among those who had taken a foreign wife. In response to Ezra's call for repentance, Zabad and the others agreed to put away their foreign wives and children to maintain the purity of the Jewish people. He is also referred to as "Zabadeas" in 1Es 9.35.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.43 only referred to as Zabad (זָבָד).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.43에 처음 언급되며 '사밧'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 느보의 아들 사밧은 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
persons.short: Zabbai, of the sons of Bebai, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.
persons.article: Zabbai, of the sons of Bebai, is listed among the men who had taken foreign wives during the Babylonian exile. This issue was brought to light when Ezra, the priest and scribe, returned to Jerusalem and discovered that many Israelites had intermarried with the pagan peoples of the land, going against God's command. Zabbai was one of those who had married a foreign woman. When Ezra called for repentance, Zabbai and the others agreed to separate from their foreign wives and children to maintain the holiness of the Jewish people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.28 only referred to as Zabbai (זַבַּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.28에 처음 언급되며 '삽배'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 브배의 후손 삽배는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repairer of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Zabbai, son of Baruch, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Zabbai, the son of Baruch, is mentioned in the account of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. He is listed among the people who worked on repairing the wall after the Babylonian exile. Zabbai repaired a section of the wall, specifically the second section from the house of Eliashib the high priest. His participation in the wall's restoration demonstrates the community-wide effort to rebuild and fortify Jerusalem after the return from exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.20 only referred to as Zabbai (זַבַּי); father of Baruch.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.20에 처음 언급되며 '삽배'라 불림. 바룩의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바룩의 아들 삽배는 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Overseer of King David's wine cellars
persons.short: Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of King David's wine cellars.
persons.article: Zabdi the Shiphmite was one of the officials in King David's administration. He was appointed as the overseer of the wine cellars, responsible for the storage and distribution of wine in the royal household. Zabdi's role indicates the importance of wine production and consumption in ancient Israelite society, particularly in the context of the king's court. His designation as a Shiphmite suggests he may have originated from the town of Shepham, although the exact location is uncertain.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.27 only referred to as Zabdi (זַבְדִּי).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.27에 처음 언급되며 '삽디'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 십못 사람 삽디는 다윗 왕의 포도주 창고를 관리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jakim@1Ch.8.19, Zichri@1Ch.8.19, Elienai@1Ch.8.20, Zillethai@1Ch.8.20, Eliel@1Ch.8.20, Adaiah@1Ch.8.21, Beraiah@1Ch.8.21, Shimrath@1Ch.8.21
persons.brief: Son of Shimei, a Benjamite
persons.short: Zabdi was a son of Shimei (or 'Shimhi'), a Benjamite, mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul.
persons.article: Zabdi is listed as one of the sons of Shimei (or 'Shimhi') in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin. This genealogy traces the lineage of King Saul, Israel's first king, who came from the tribe of Benjamin. Zabdi is mentioned alongside his brothers, but no further information is provided about his life or role within the tribe. His inclusion in the genealogy highlights the importance of family lineage in Israelite society.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.19 only referred to as Zabdi (זַבְדִּי); son of Shimei; a brother of Jakim, Zichri, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.19에 처음 언급되며 '삽디'라 불림. 시므이의 아들. 야김, 시그리, 엘리에내, 실르대, 엘리엘, 아다야, 브라야와 시므랏의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 삽디는 베냐민 사람 시므이(심히라고도 함)의 아들로, 사울 왕 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of Achan, who sinned against Israel
persons.short: Zabdi (Zimri), son of Zerah, was an ancestor of Achan, who took forbidden plunder during the conquest of Jericho.
persons.article: Zabdi, also known as Zimri, was a descendant of Judah and an ancestor of Achan. Achan, from the tribe of Judah, violated God's command by taking forbidden plunder from Jericho during Israel's conquest of the city. As a result, Israel suffered a defeat at Ai. When Achan's sin was discovered through a process of elimination, he and his family were stoned and burned. Zabdi is mentioned in Achan's genealogy, highlighting the connection between an individual's sin and its impact on the entire community.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.7.1 referred to as Zabdi (זַבְדִּי), or Zimri (זִמְרִי); son of Zerah; a brother of Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara; father of Carmi.
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jos.7.1에 처음 언급되며 '삽디'라 불림. 세라의 아들. 에단, 헤만, 갈골과 다라의 형제. 갈미의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삽디(시므리)는 세라의 아들로, 여리고 정복 당시 금지된 전리품을 취한 아간의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jashobeam, commander of David's army
persons.short: Zabdiel was the father of Jashobeam, a commander in King David's army.
persons.article: Zabdiel is mentioned as the father of Jashobeam, who was a commander in King David's army. Jashobeam was in charge of the first division of 24,000 men, serving the king in the first month of each year. He is described as a mighty warrior and a leader among David's "Thirty" elite soldiers. Zabdiel's son played a significant role in maintaining the military strength and security of David's kingdom, although no further details are provided about Zabdiel himself.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.2 only referred to as Zabdiel (זַבְדִּיאֵל); father of Jashobeam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.2에 처음 언급되며 '삽디엘'이라 불림. 야소브암의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삽디엘은 다윗 왕 군대의 지휘관 야소브암의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest and leader in post-exilic Jerusalem
persons.short: Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was a priest and leader in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zabdiel, the son of Haggedolim, was a priest and leader in Jerusalem during the post-exilic period. After the Babylonian captivity, Nehemiah led a group of Jews back to Jerusalem to rebuild the city walls and restore Jewish community life. Zabdiel is listed among the priests and Levites who settled in Jerusalem, indicating his role in reestablishing religious practices and worship in the city. As a leader, he likely had responsibilities in teaching the law and overseeing various aspects of the restored Jewish community.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.14 only referred to as Zabdiel (זַבְדִּיאֵל); a son of Haggedolim.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.14에 처음 언급되며 '삽디엘'이라 불림. 하그돌림의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 학그돌림의 아들 삽디엘은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘의 제사장이며 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Nathan, priest and king's friend
persons.short: Zabud, son of Nathan, served as a priest and was a close friend of King Solomon.
persons.article: Zabud was the son of Nathan, who was likely the prophet and advisor to King David. Zabud held a significant position in the court of King Solomon, serving both as a priest and as the king's friend. His dual role as a religious leader and a trusted companion to the king highlights the close relationship between the monarchy and the priesthood in ancient Israel. Zabud's presence in the king's inner circle suggests he provided spiritual guidance and counsel to Solomon throughout his reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.4.5 only referred to as Zabud (זָבוּד); son of Nathan; a brother of Azariah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.4.5에 처음 언급되며 '사붓'이라 불림. 나단의 아들. 아사랴의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 나단의 아들 사붓은 제사장으로 섬기며 솔로몬 왕의 절친한 친구였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of returning exiles
persons.short: Zaccai was the ancestor of a family that returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zaccai is mentioned in the lists of Jewish exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. In the accounts found in both Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Zaccai are enumerated among the families who made the journey back to their homeland. The Ezra account records 760 members of Zaccai's family, while Nehemiah's list mentions 760. These numbers suggest that the family of Zaccai was a significant group among the returning exiles who helped rebuild Jerusalem and restore Jewish community life in the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.9 only referred to as Zaccai (זַכַּי).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.9에 처음 언급되며 '삭개'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삭개는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘으로 돌아온 한 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Tax collector who hosted Jesus in Jericho
persons.short: Zacchaeus, a wealthy tax collector, hosted Jesus in his home and experienced a transformative encounter.
persons.article: Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector in the city of Jericho. He was a wealthy man, likely due to his profession, which was often associated with corruption and extortion in ancient Roman-occupied Israel. When Jesus passed through Jericho, Zacchaeus sought to see him but was hindered by his short stature and the crowd. He climbed a sycamore tree to catch a glimpse of Jesus. Noticing Zacchaeus, Jesus called him down and declared his intention to stay at his house. This encounter led to a profound change in Zacchaeus, who pledged to give half of his possessions to the poor and to repay fourfold anyone he had cheated. Jesus affirmed Zacchaeus's transformation, declaring that salvation had come to his house and that the Son of Man had come to seek and save the lost.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.19.2 only referred to as Zacchaeus (Ζακχαῖος).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.19.2에 처음 언급되며 '삭개오'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삭개오는 부유한 세리로, 자기 집에 예수님을 대접하며 변화를 경험했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Merarite Levite, son of Jaaziah
persons.short: Zaccur was a Merarite Levite, one of the sons of Jaaziah.
persons.article: Zaccur was a Levite belonging to the family of Merari. He was one of the sons of Jaaziah, as listed in the genealogy of the Levites during the time of King David. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the Kohathites and Gershonites. They were responsible for the tabernacle's structural components and transportation during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. Zaccur's mention in this genealogy highlights the importance of the Levitical lineage and their roles in Israelite worship.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.27 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); son of Jaaziah; a brother of Beno, Shoham and Ibri.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.24.27에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 야아시야의 아들. 아들, 소함과 이브리의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 삭굴은 야아시야의 아들들인 므라리 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Asaph, a musician in David's time
persons.short: Zaccur, a son of Asaph, was a musician during the reigns of David and Solomon.
persons.article: Zaccur was one of the sons of Asaph, a prominent Levitical musician during the reigns of King David and King Solomon. Asaph was a leader of the Levitical singers and musicians appointed by David to serve in the tabernacle and later in the temple. Zaccur, along with his brothers, was trained in music and participated in the musical worship services. In the time of Nehemiah, after the Babylonian exile, a descendant of Zaccur named Zacchur is mentioned among the musicians who played at the dedication of the rebuilt wall of Jerusalem. This suggests that Zaccur's family continued to serve as musicians in the temple for generations.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.2 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); son of Asaph; a brother of Joseph, Nethaniah and Asharelah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.2에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 아삽의 아들. 요셉, 느다니야와 아사렐라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 아삽의 아들 삭굴은 다윗과 솔로몬 통치 기간의 음악가였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Simeonite descendant of Mishma
persons.short: Zaccur was a Simeonite mentioned in the genealogy of Mishma.
persons.article: Zaccur is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon, specifically as a descendant of Mishma. Mishma was one of the sons of Shaul, who was a son of Simeon. Zaccur is mentioned along with his brothers Hammuel and Zacchur as the sons of Mishma. No further details are provided about Zaccur's life or role within the tribe of Simeon. The inclusion of his name in the genealogical record highlights the importance of family lineage and tribal identity in ancient Israelite society.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.26 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); a son of Hammuel; father of Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.26에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 함무엘의 아들. 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삭굴은 미스마의 족보에 언급된 시므온 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader of returning exiles with Shecaniah
persons.short: Zaccur, along with Shecaniah, led a group of returning exiles to Jerusalem.
persons.article: Zaccur is mentioned in the list of leaders who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem after the exile. He, along with Shecaniah, led a group of men from the descendants of Bigvai. The text records that Ezra gathered these leaders and their families at the river that flows to Ahava, where they camped for three days before setting out for Jerusalem. Ezra had called for a fast to seek God's protection for their journey. The inclusion of Zaccur in this list suggests he was a respected leader among the returning exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.14 referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר), or Zaccur (זָבוּד).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.14에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삭굴은 스가냐와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 포로 무리를 이끌었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Zaccur, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Zaccur is listed among the priests who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. After the completion of the wall and the reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commandments and to maintain the temple worship. The leaders, including priests, Levites, and heads of families, sealed this covenant. Zaccur's presence among the priests who sealed the covenant indicates his role in the spiritual leadership of the post-exilic Jewish community and his commitment to upholding the Law and the proper worship of God.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.12 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.12에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 삭굴은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest appointed as a treasurer
persons.short: Zaccur, a priest, was appointed as one of the treasurers by Nehemiah.
persons.article: Zaccur, a priest, was one of the individuals appointed by Nehemiah to serve as a treasurer for the storehouses. These storehouses were used to collect the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil that were brought by the people for the support of the Levites and priests. Nehemiah chose Zaccur, along with Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, because they were considered trustworthy. Their responsibility was to oversee the distribution of the offerings to their fellow Levites and priests.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.13.13 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); a son of Mattaniah; father of Hanan.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 맛다냐의 아들. 하난의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 삭굴은 느헤미야가 임명한 재무관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Son of Imri, helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Zaccur, son of Imri, participated in rebuilding a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Zaccur, the son of Imri, is mentioned in the account of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. He is listed among the people who worked on repairing the wall after the Babylonian exile. Zaccur and the men of Jericho built the section next to the portion completed by the high priest Eliashib and his fellow priests. Zaccur's participation in the wall's restoration demonstrates the community-wide effort to rebuild and fortify Jerusalem after the return from exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.2 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); a son of Imri.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.2에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 이므리의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 임리의 아들 삭굴은 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역 재건에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Reubenite spy sent to Canaan
persons.short: Zaccur, son of Shammua, was the Reubenite representative among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
persons.article: Zaccur, the son of Shammua, was a member of the tribe of Reuben. He was chosen as one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan before the Israelites entered it. Each tribe was represented by a leader in this scouting mission. Zaccur and the other spies were tasked with assessing the land, its inhabitants, and its resources. After forty days, the spies returned with their report. While Zaccur's specific role in the mission is not detailed, the majority of the spies, except for Joshua and Caleb, delivered a discouraging report that led to the Israelites' refusal to enter the land, resulting in forty years of wandering in the wilderness.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Num.13.4 only referred to as Zaccur (זַכּוּר); father of Shammua.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.13.4에 처음 언급되며 '삭굴'이라 불림. 삼무아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 삼무아의 아들 삭굴은 가나안을 정탐하도록 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 르우벤 지파 대표였다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Postexilic high priest, descendant of Zadok
persons.short: Zadok was a high priest who served in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zadok is mentioned as a high priest who lived and served in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is listed in the genealogies of the priests in the books of Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah. Zadok was a descendant of the earlier high priest Zadok who served during the reigns of David and Solomon. In the postexilic period, Zadok is described as the son of Meraioth and the father of Meshullam. He was part of the priestly lineage that returned to Jerusalem to help rebuild the temple and reestablish the worship of God. The mention of Zadok in these genealogies emphasizes the continuity of the priestly line and the importance of the priesthood in the restoration of Jewish religious life after the exile.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.12 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק); a son of Ahitub; father of Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 제사장. 1Ch.6.12에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 아히둡의 아들. 살룸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에서 섬긴 대제사장이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Father of Jerusha, wife of King Uzziah
persons.short: Zadok was the father of Jerusha, who was the wife of King Uzziah (Azariah) of Judah.
persons.article: Zadok is mentioned as the father of Jerusha, who was the wife of King Uzziah (also known as Azariah) of Judah. Jerusha's mother is not named in the biblical text. Zadok's daughter, Jerusha, became queen when she married Uzziah, and their son, Jotham, succeeded Uzziah as king. The mention of Zadok in this context provides information about the royal family of Judah during Uzziah's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.33 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק); father of Jerusha.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.15.33에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 여루사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독은 유다 왕 웃시야(아사랴)의 아내 여루사의 아버지였다.

persons.description: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
persons.short: Zadok was a prominent high priest who served during the reigns of King David and King Solomon.
persons.article: Zadok was a significant figure in the history of Israel, serving as a high priest during the reigns of King David and King Solomon. He first appears in the biblical narrative as one of the two priests mentioned alongside Ahimelech during David's reign. Zadok remained loyal to David during the rebellion of Absalom, and he played a key role in anointing Solomon as king. After Solomon's accession to the throne, Zadok was appointed as the sole high priest, replacing Abiathar. Zadok's descendants continued to serve as high priests in the temple in Jerusalem, and they are mentioned in the visions of Ezekiel regarding the future restoration of the temple and its services. The "sons of Zadok" are described as faithful priests who will serve in the restored temple. Zadok's lineage and role emphasize the importance of the priesthood in maintaining the worship of God and the spiritual leadership of the nation.
persons.summary: A high priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.17 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק); a son of Ahitub; father of Ahimaaz.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 대제사장. 2Sa.8.17에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 아히둡의 아들. 아히마아스의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독은 다윗 왕과 솔로몬 왕 시대에 섬긴 저명한 대제사장이었다.
persons.article_ko: 사독은 다윗 왕과 솔로몬 왕 통치 기간 동안 대제사장으로 섬긴 이스라엘 역사의 중요한 인물이었다. 그는 다윗 통치 기간 동안 아히멜렉과 함께 언급된 두 제사장 중 한 사람으로 성경 이야기에 처음 등장한다. 사독은 압살롬의 반역 동안 다윗에게 충성했고 솔로몬에게 기름을 부어 왕으로 세우는 데 중요한 역할을 했다. 솔로몬이 왕위에 오른 후 사독은 아비아달을 대신하여 유일한 대제사장으로 임명되었다. 사독의 후손은 계속해서 예루살렘 성전에서 대제사장으로 섬겼고, 그들은 성전과 그 예배의 미래 회복에 관한 에스겔의 환상에 언급된다. '사독의 자손'은 회복된 성전에서 섬길 신실한 제사장들로 묘사된다. 사독의 혈통과 역할은 하나님 예배와 그 민족의 영적 지도력을 유지하는 데 있어 제사장직의 중요성을 강조한다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus Christ
persons.short: Zadok is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy recorded by Matthew.
persons.article: Zadok is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in the Gospel of Matthew. He is listed as the son of Azor and the father of Achim. This genealogy traces the lineage of Jesus from Abraham through His legal father, Joseph. Zadok's inclusion in this genealogy highlights the connection between Jesus and the royal line of David, as well as the fulfillment of messianic prophecies.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Mat.1.14 only referred to as Zadok (Σαδώκ); a son of Azor; father of Achim.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Mat.1.14에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 아소르의 아들. 아킴의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 사독은 마태복음 족보에 기록된 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Zadok was one of the leaders of Israel who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Zadok is listed among the leaders of Israel who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. After the completion of Jerusalem's wall and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commandments and maintain proper worship. The leaders, including Zadok, sealed this covenant, pledging their commitment to uphold the Law and the religious practices of the community. Zadok's presence among the leaders who sealed the covenant indicates his influential position within the post-exilic Jewish society.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.21 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.21에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 사독은 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 이스라엘 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest appointed as a treasurer
persons.short: Zadok, a priest, was appointed as one of the treasurers by Nehemiah.
persons.article: Zadok, a priest, was one of the individuals appointed by Nehemiah to serve as a treasurer for the storehouses. These storehouses were used to collect the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil that were brought by the people for the support of the Levites and priests. Nehemiah chose Zadok, along with Shelemiah the priest, Pedaiah of the Levites, and Hanan, because they were considered trustworthy. Their responsibility was to oversee the distribution of the offerings to their fellow Levites and priests.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.13.13 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.13.13에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 사독은 느헤미야가 임명한 재무관 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Zadok, son of Immer, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near his house.
persons.article: Zadok, the son of Immer, is recorded as one of the individuals who participated in repairing Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding project. He is specifically mentioned as having made repairs opposite his house. This detail suggests that Zadok lived in Jerusalem and had a personal stake in the city's restoration. His contribution to the wall's repair highlights the community-wide involvement in the rebuilding efforts led by Nehemiah after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.29 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק); a son of Immer.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.29에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 임멜의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 임멜의 아들 사독은 자기 집 근처 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Zadok, son of Baana, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding project.
persons.article: Zadok, the son of Baana, is mentioned in the list of people who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. After the Babylonian exile, Nehemiah led a group of Jews back to Jerusalem to rebuild the city walls and restore the community. Zadok was responsible for repairing a section of the wall, demonstrating his participation in the collective effort to fortify Jerusalem and reestablish Jewish presence in the city.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.4 only referred to as Zadok (צָדוֹק); a son of Baana.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.4에 처음 언급되며 '사독'이라 불림. 바아나의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 바아나의 아들 사독은 느헤미야의 재건 사업 당시 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Abijah@1Ki.14.31-Mat, Jeush@2Ch.11.19, Shemariah@2Ch.11.19, Attai@2Ch.11.20, Ziza@2Ch.11.20, Shelomith@2Ch.11.20
persons.brief: Son of King Rehoboam
persons.short: Zaham was one of the sons born to King Rehoboam of Judah.
persons.article: Zaham is mentioned as one of the sons of King Rehoboam, who ruled over Judah after the division of the kingdom following Solomon's death. Zaham's mother was Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth, son of David, and of Abihail, daughter of Eliab, son of Jesse. The listing of Zaham among Rehoboam's sons provides insight into the royal family of Judah during the early years of the divided monarchy.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.11.19 only referred to as Zaham (זָ֑הַם); son of Rehoboam and Mahalath; a brother of Jeush and Shemariah; half-brother of: Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '사함'이라 불림. 르호보암과 마할랏의 아들. 아비야, 여우스, 스마랴, 앗대, 시사와 슬로밋의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사함은 유다 왕 르호보암의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Father of Hanun, who repaired Jerusalem's wall
persons.short: Zalaph was the father of Hanun, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Zalaph is mentioned as the father of Hanun, one of the individuals who participated in repairing Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership. After the Babylonian exile, Nehemiah led a group of Jews back to Jerusalem to rebuild the city walls and restore the community. Hanun, son of Zalaph, is recorded as having made repairs on another section of the wall, along with Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph. This suggests that Zalaph's family was actively involved in the restoration efforts in Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.3.30 only referred to as Zalaph (צָלָף); father of Hanun.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.3.30에 처음 언급되며 '살랍'이라 불림. 하눈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 살랍은 예루살렘 성벽 한 구역을 수리한 하눈의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: One of David's mighty men
persons.short: Zalmon, also known as Ilai, was one of King David's mighty men, hailing from Ahlai.
persons.article: Zalmon, also referred to as Ilai, is listed among the mighty men of King David. These mighty men were renowned warriors who demonstrated exceptional bravery and military prowess. Zalmon is specifically mentioned as being from Ahlai, which is likely a reference to his place of origin or his family lineage. His inclusion in the list of David's mighty men indicates that he was a skilled fighter and played a significant role in David's military campaigns. The variation in his name between Zalmon and Ilai may be due to different textual traditions or translations.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.28 referred to as Zalmon (צַלְמוֹן), or Ilai (עִילַי).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.28에 처음 언급되며 '살몬'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 살몬(일래라고도 함)은 아흘래 출신 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Midianite king defeated by Gideon
persons.short: Zalmunna was a Midianite king who was defeated and killed by Gideon during the time of the judges.
persons.article: Zalmunna was one of the two Midianite kings, along with Zebah, who oppressed Israel during the time of the judges. The Midianites, in alliance with the Amalekites and other eastern peoples, regularly raided Israel and destroyed their crops. God raised up Gideon to deliver Israel from the Midianites. After a decisive battle, Gideon pursued the fleeing Midianite army and captured Zalmunna and Zebah. Gideon questioned them about the men they had killed at Tabor, and upon learning that they were his brothers, he executed Zalmunna and Zebah. The defeat of these Midianite kings brought about a period of peace for Israel. The psalmist later refers to Zalmunna and Zebah as examples of God's enemies who were defeated and destroyed.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.8.5 only referred to as Zalmunna (צַלְמֻנָּע).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.8.5에 처음 언급되며 '살문나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 살문나는 미디안 왕으로, 사사 시대에 기드온에게 패하여 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of returning exiles
persons.short: Zattu was the ancestor of a family that returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zattu is mentioned in the lists of Jewish exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon. In the accounts found in Ezra and Nehemiah, the descendants of Zattu are enumerated among the families who made the journey back to their homeland. The Ezra account records 945 members of Zattu's family, while Nehemiah's list mentions 845. These numbers suggest that the family of Zattu was a significant group among the returning exiles who helped rebuild Jerusalem and restore Jewish community life in the post-exilic period. Additionally, some members of Zattu's family are mentioned among those who had married foreign women and agreed to separate from them in response to Ezra's call for spiritual reformation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.2.8 only referred to as Zattu (זַתּוּא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.2.8에 처음 언급되며 '삿두'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삿두는 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘으로 돌아온 한 가문의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
persons.short: Zattu was one of the leaders of Israel who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
persons.article: Zattu is listed among the leaders of Israel who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah. After the completion of Jerusalem's wall and the public reading of the Law, the people of Israel made a covenant to follow God's commandments and maintain proper worship. The leaders, including Zattu, sealed this covenant, pledging their commitment to uphold the Law and the religious practices of the community. Zattu's presence among the leaders who sealed the covenant indicates his influential position within the post-exilic Jewish society.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.14 only referred to as Zattu (זַתּוּא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.14에 처음 언급되며 '삿두'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 삿두는 느헤미야 시대에 언약에 서명한 이스라엘 지도자 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jonathan, descendant of Jerahmeel
persons.short: Zaza was a son of Jonathan and a descendant of Jerahmeel from the tribe of Judah.
persons.article: Zaza is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah, specifically as a son of Jonathan and a descendant of Jerahmeel. Jerahmeel was one of the sons of Hezron, who was a grandson of Judah. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 2 traces the lineage of Judah's descendants, including the family line of Jerahmeel. Zaza is listed along with his brother Peleth as the sons of Jonathan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.33 only referred to as Zaza (זָזָא); son of Jonathan; a brother of Peleth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.2.33에 처음 언급되며 '사사'라 불림. 요나단의 아들. 벨렛의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 사사는 요나단의 아들이며 여라므엘을 통한 유다의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Gadite warrior who joined David
persons.short: Zebadiah was a Gadite warrior who joined David's forces at Ziklag.
persons.article: Zebadiah is listed among the Gadite warriors who joined David's army when he was seeking refuge from King Saul at Ziklag. The Gadites were known for their bravery and skill in battle. Zebadiah, along with his fellow Gadites, is described as a brave warrior and a commander in the army. They joined David's forces and provided military support during his time of need. Zebadiah's presence among David's followers demonstrates the loyalty and support he received from various tribes during his rise to power.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.12.7 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); son of Jeroham; a brother of Joelah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.12.7에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 여로함의 아들. 요엘라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 갓 지파 용사로, 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그의 군대에 합류했다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Zechariah@1Ch.9.21-, Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper
persons.short: Zebadiah was the firstborn son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper in the time of David.
persons.article: Zebadiah is mentioned as the firstborn son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite who served as a gatekeeper in the time of King David. The Korahites were a Levitical family assigned to various duties in the tabernacle and later in the temple. Meshelemiah and his sons, including Zebadiah, were responsible for guarding the gates and entrances to the sacred areas. Being the firstborn son, Zebadiah would have held a position of responsibility and leadership among his brothers in their role as gatekeepers.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.2 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Zechariah, Jediael, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.26.2에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 스가랴, 여디아엘, 야드니엘, 엘람, 여호하난과 엘여호에내의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 다윗 시대 고라 사람 문지기 므셀레먀의 맏아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Asahel, commander of David's army
persons.short: Zebadiah, son of Asahel, was the commander of the fourth division of David's army, serving during the fourth month.
persons.article: Zebadiah, the son of Asahel, was a commander in King David's army. He was in charge of the fourth division, which served during the fourth month of the year. Asahel, Zebadiah's father, was the brother of Joab, who was the commander of David's entire army. The fact that Zebadiah held this position suggests that he was a capable military leader. His division consisted of 24,000 men, indicating the significant size of David's military force. The rotation of army divisions allowed for a well-organized and efficient military structure during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.7 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); a son of Asahel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.7에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 아사헬의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 아사헬의 아들 스바댜는 다윗 군대에서 넷째 달에 섬긴 넷째 반의 지휘관이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Arad@1Ch.8.15, Ahio@1Ch.8.14, Shashak@1Ch.8.14-, Jeremoth@1Ch.8.14, Eder@1Ch.8.15, Michael@1Ch.8.16, Ishpah@1Ch.8.16, Joha@1Ch.8.16
persons.brief: Son of Beriah, a Benjamite
persons.short: Zebadiah was a greandson of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Zebadiah is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Beriah, son of Elpaal, a descendant of Shaharaim, who was among the Benjamites living in Moab. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 records the descendants of Benjamin, including the family of Elpaal. Zebadiah is mentioned along with his brothers, but no additional details are provided about his life or any specific role he may have played within the tribe.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.15 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); son of Beriah; a brother of Arad, Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Eder, Michael, Ishpah and Joha.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.8.15에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 브리아의 아들. 아랏, 아효, 사삭, 여레못, 에델, 미가엘, 이스바와 요하의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 엘바알의 손자이며 베냐민 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Eber@1Ch.8.12, Misham@1Ch.8.12, Shemed@1Ch.8.12, Beriah@1Ch.8.13-, Shema@1Ch.8.13, Meshullam@1Ch.8.17, Hizki@1Ch.8.17, Heber@1Ch.8.17, Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18, Izliah@1Ch.8.18, Jobab@1Ch.8.18
persons.brief: Son of Elpaal, a Benjamite
persons.short: Zebadiah was a son of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.article: Zebadiah is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of the sons of Elpaal. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 8 lists the descendants of Benjamin, including the family of Elpaal.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.8.17 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); son of Elpaal; a brother of Eber, Misham, Shemed, Beriah, Shema, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.17에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 엘바알의 아들. 에벨, 미삼, 세멧, 브리아, 세마, 므술람, 히스기, 헤벨, 이스므래, 이슬리아와 요밥의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 엘바알의 아들이며 베냐민 지파에 속했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Zebadiah was one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law throughout Judah.
persons.article: Zebadiah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. As part of Jehoshaphat's reforms, he sent out Levites and priests to teach the Book of the Law to the people throughout the cities of Judah. Zebadiah was among the Levites chosen for this task, along with Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah. They were accompanied by the priests Elishama and Jehoram. This educational initiative aimed to instruct the people in the ways of the Lord and strengthen their faith. Zebadiah's participation in this mission highlights the importance of the Levites' role in teaching and preserving the Law.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.8에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 전역에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Chief priest in matters of the Lord
persons.short: Zebadiah, son of Ishmael, was appointed as the leader in all matters concerning the king during Jehoshaphat's reign.
persons.article: Zebadiah, the son of Ishmael, held a significant position during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He was appointed as the leader in all matters concerning the king, working alongside Amariah, the chief priest, who oversaw matters related to the Lord. This dual leadership structure suggests a separation of duties between religious and civil affairs. Zebadiah's role likely involved overseeing administrative and judicial matters on behalf of the king. The mention of his father, Ishmael, may indicate that he came from a prominent family. Zebadiah's appointment reflects Jehoshaphat's efforts to establish a well-organized and efficient government.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.19.11 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); a son of Ishmael.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.19.11에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 이스마엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 이스마엘의 아들 스바댜는 여호사밧 왕 시대에 왕과 관련된 모든 일의 지도자로 임명되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Zebadiah, one of the priests, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Zebadiah is mentioned in the list of priests who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from the Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was contrary to the Law of Moses and posed a threat to the spiritual purity of the community. Ezra called for a assembly where the people confessed their sin and agreed to separate from their foreign wives. Zebadiah, along with the other priests who had married foreign women, pledged to put away their wives and offer a ram as a guilt offering for their transgression.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.20 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.20에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스바댜는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 제사장 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Leader of returning exiles with Shecaniah
persons.short: Zebadiah, son of Michael, led a group of 80 men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zebadiah, the son of Michael, was one of the leaders who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem after the exile. He led a group of 80 men from the descendants of Shephatiah. The text records that Ezra gathered these leaders and their families at the river that flows to Ahava, where they camped for three days before setting out for Jerusalem. Ezra had called for a fast to seek God's protection for their journey. The inclusion of Zebadiah in this list suggests he was a respected leader among the returning exiles.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.8 only referred to as Zebadiah (זְבַדְיָהוּ); a son of Michael.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.8에 처음 언급되며 '스바댜'라 불림. 미가엘의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 미가엘의 아들 스바댜는 바벨론 포로 이후 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아온 팔십 명을 이끌었다.

persons.description: King living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Midianite king defeated by Gideon
persons.short: Zebah was a Midianite king who, along with Zalmunna, was defeated and killed by Gideon during the time of the judges.
persons.article: Zebah was one of the two Midianite kings who led a vast army that invaded and oppressed Israel during the time of the judges. For seven years, the Midianites, along with the Amalekites and other eastern peoples, would come up against Israel, destroying crops and livestock, forcing many Israelites to seek shelter in caves. God raised up Gideon to deliver Israel from the Midianites. After a decisive victory, Zebah and Zalmunna fled with a remnant of their army, but Gideon pursued them across the Jordan River and overtook them at Karkor. The kings were captured and brought back to Israel, where they confessed to killing Gideon's brothers. As a result, Gideon executed them. The name Zebah is related to the Hebrew word for "sacrifice," while Zalmunna may contain a reference to a heathen deity. Their defeat is remembered as a demonstration of God's judgment and glory.
persons.summary: A king of Midia living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.8.5 only referred to as Zebah (זֶ֫בַח).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 왕. Jdg.8.5에 처음 언급되며 '세바'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 세바는 살문나와 함께 사사 시대에 기드온에게 패하여 죽임을 당한 미디안 왕이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Father of the apostles James and John
persons.short: Zebedee was the father of James and John, two of Jesus' twelve apostles, and was a fisherman by trade.
persons.article: Zebedee was a fisherman from Galilee and the father of two of Jesus' disciples, James and John. He worked alongside his sons in the fishing business and was present when Jesus called them to follow Him. His wife was Salome, according to hints at Matt 27.56 with Mrk.15.40. Zebedee's wife, the mother of James and John, is mentioned as one of the women who followed Jesus and supported His ministry. She also made a bold request for her sons to sit at Jesus' right and left hand in His kingdom, revealing her high aspirations for them. Zebedee is not mentioned as a follower of Jesus himself, but he did not hinder his sons from leaving their fishing trade to become disciples. The fact that Zebedee had hired servants suggests that he ran a successful fishing operation. His sons, James and John, along with Peter, formed Jesus' inner circle of disciples and were present at significant events such as the Transfiguration and Jesus' prayers in Gethsemane.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.4.21 only referred to as Zebedee (Ζεβεδαῖος); father of James, John.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Mat.4.21에 처음 언급되며 '세베대'라 불림. 살로매의 남편. 야고보와 요한의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세베대는 예수님의 열두 사도 중 두 사람인 야고보와 요한의 아버지이며 어부였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah
persons.short: Zebidah, daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah, was the mother of Jehoiakim, king of Judah.
persons.article: Zebidah is mentioned in the biblical record as the mother of Jehoiakim, who became king of Judah. She was the daughter of Pedaiah from the town of Rumah. Zebidah's husband was Josiah, the king of Judah who instituted significant religious reforms. After Josiah's death, their son Jehoiakim ascended to the throne at the age of twenty-five and reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem. However, Jehoiakim did not follow in his father's footsteps and did evil in the sight of the Lord.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.23.36 only referred to as Zebidah (זְבוּדָה); a daughter of Pedaiah; wife of Josiah; mother of Jehoiakim.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 2Ki.23.36에 처음 언급되며 '스비다'라 불림. 브다야의 딸. 요시야의 아내. 여호야김의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 루마 사람 브다야의 딸 스비다는 유다 왕 여호야김의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Zebina was one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.
persons.article: Zebina is mentioned in the list of Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra. After the return from the Babylonian exile, Ezra discovered that many of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, had intermarried with the neighboring peoples. This was contrary to the Law of Moses and posed a threat to the spiritual purity of the community. Ezra called for an assembly where the people confessed their sin and agreed to separate from their foreign wives. Zebina, along with the other men who had married foreign women, pledged to put away their wives and offer a ram as a guilt offering for their transgression. This act of repentance and obedience was crucial in preserving the identity and faith of the Israelites after the exile.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.43 only referred to as Zebina (זְבִינָא).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.43에 처음 언급되며 '스비내'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스비나는 에스라 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Governor of Shechem under Abimelech
persons.short: Zebul was the governor of Shechem who served under Abimelech, the son of Gideon, during his reign as king.
persons.article: Zebul was the governor of the city of Shechem during the reign of Abimelech, the son of Gideon, who had declared himself king over Israel. When Gaal, son of Ebed, came to Shechem and incited the people against Abimelech, Zebul remained loyal to Abimelech and informed him of the rebellion. Acting on Abimelech's instructions, Zebul challenged Gaal to fight against Abimelech's forces. In the ensuing battle, Gaal and his followers were defeated, and Abimelech took control of the city. Zebul then drove out Gaal and his brothers from Shechem. Zebul's actions demonstrate his loyalty to Abimelech and his role in quelling the rebellion and maintaining Abimelech's authority over the city of Shechem. The narrative highlights the political tensions and power struggles that existed during the period of the judges.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.9.28 only referred to as Zebul (זְבֻל).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.9.28에 처음 언급되며 '스불'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스불은 기드온의 아들 아비멜렉이 왕으로 다스릴 때 그 밑에서 섬긴 세겜의 성주였다.

persons.description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev, Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev, Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev, Judah@Gen.29.35-Rev, Dan@Gen.30.6-1Ch, Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev, Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev, Asher@Gen.30.13-Rev, Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev, Dinah@Gen.30.21-, Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev, Benjamin@Gen.35.18-Rev
persons.brief: Israelite tribe, son of Jacob and Leah
persons.short: Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob, the sixth and last of Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
persons.article: Zebulun was the tenth son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and the sixth and last son of Leah. He was born in Paddan-aram, and his name is derived from the Hebrew word meaning "honor" or "dwelling." The tribe of Zebulun played a significant role in Israel's history, being one of the twelve tribes that settled in the Promised Land. During the wilderness wanderings, the tribe of Zebulun was led by Eliab, son of Helon, and was positioned with the tribes of Judah and Issachar on the east side of the tabernacle. In the census taken in the wilderness, the tribe of Zebulun numbered 57,400 men of fighting age. The territory allotted to Zebulun was in the northern part of Canaan, bordered by Asher, Naphtali, and Issachar. It included the fertile plain of Jezreel and the coastal region along the Mediterranean Sea. The tribe of Zebulun was commended for their bravery and willingness to fight, as evidenced by their participation in the battles against Sisera and the Midianites. They were also known for their maritime skills and engaged in trade and commerce. Notable members of the tribe of Zebulun include Elon, who judged Israel for ten years, and Ibzan of Bethlehem, who was buried in the territory of Zebulun. The prophet Jonah also hailed from Gath-hepher, a town within Zebulun's borders. In the future distribution of the land described by Ezekiel, Zebulun is allocated a portion in the far north of Israel, with its boundaries stretching from the Mediterranean Sea to the Jordan River. The tribe of Zebulun is also mentioned in the book of Revelation as one of the twelve tribes sealed by God.
persons.summary: A man who founded the tribe of Zebulun living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.30.20 referred to as Zebulun (זְבוּלֻן), or Zebulunite (זְבוּלֹנִי), or Zebulun (Ζαβουλών); son of Israel and Leah; a brother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Dinah; half-brother of: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph and Benjamin; father of Sered, Elon and Jahleel.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 야곱의 아들. Gen.30.20에 처음 언급되며 '스불론'이라 불림. 이스라엘과 레아의 아들. 르우벤, 시므온, 레위, 유다, 단, 납달리, 갓, 아셀, 잇사갈, 디나, 요셉과 베냐민의 형제. 세렛, 엘론과 얄르엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스불론은 야곱의 열 번째 아들이며 레아의 여섯째이자 막내아들로, 그 후손이 이스라엘 열두 지파 중 하나를 이루었다.
persons.article_ko: 스불론은 이스라엘(야곱)의 열째 아들이며 레아의 여섯째이자 막내아들이었다. 그는 밧단아람에서 태어났으며, 그의 이름은 '영예' 또는 '거처'를 뜻하는 히브리어에서 유래했다. 스불론 지파는 약속의 땅에 정착한 열두 지파 중 하나로 이스라엘 역사에서 중요한 역할을 했다. 광야 방랑 기간 동안 스불론 지파는 헬론의 아들 엘리압이 이끌었고 성막 동편에 유다, 잇사갈 지파와 함께 배치되었다. 광야에서 실시된 인구조사에서 스불론 지파는 전투 연령의 남자가 오만 칠천사백 명이었다. 스불론에게 분배된 영토는 가나안 북부에 있었고 아셀, 납달리, 잇사갈과 경계를 이루었다. 그곳에는 비옥한 이스르엘 평야와 지중해를 따르는 해안 지역이 포함되었다. 스불론 지파는 시스라와 미디안을 대적하는 전투 참여에서 볼 수 있듯이 용맹함과 기꺼이 싸우려는 의지로 칭찬받았다. 그들은 또한 해양 기술로 알려졌으며 무역과 상업에 종사했다. 스불론 지파의 저명한 인물로는 이스라엘을 십 년간 다스린 엘론과 스불론 영토에 묻힌 베들레헴 사람 입산이 있다. 선지자 요나 또한 스불론 경계 안에 있던 성읍 가드헤벨 출신이었다. 에스겔이 묘사한 미래의 땅 분배에서 스불론은 이스라엘 극북 지역의 한 부분을 분배받으며, 그 경계는 지중해에서 요단강까지 뻗어 있다. 스불론 지파는 요한계시록에서도 하나님이 인치신 열두 지파 중 하나로 언급된다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Isshiah, a Levite
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Isshiah, was a Levite mentioned in the genealogical records of the Levites during the reign of David.
persons.article: Zechariah, the son of Isshiah, is mentioned in the genealogical records of the Levites during the time of King David. He belonged to the family of Kohath, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. The Kohathites were responsible for the care and transportation of the sacred objects of the tabernacle. In the organization of the Levitical duties by David, the descendants of Kohath were assigned specific roles and responsibilities.
