Zechariah's mention in this context suggests that he and his family line were part of the Levitical service in the tabernacle during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.24.25 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Isshiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.24.25에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 잇시야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 잇시야의 아들 스가랴는 다윗 왕 시대의 레위인 족보 기록에 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Hosah, a Merarite
persons.short: Zechariah was the fourth son of Hosah, a Merarite.
persons.article: Zechariah is listed as the fourth son of Hosah, a Merarite. The Korahites were a clan within the tribe of Levi, descendants of Korah. The Merarites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the Kohathites and Gershonites. They were responsible for the tabernacle's structural components and transportation during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. Zaccur's mention in this genealogy highlights the importance of the Levitical lineage and their roles in Israelite worship.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.26.11 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); son of Hosah; a brother of Shimri, Hilkiah and Tebaliah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.26.11에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 호사의 아들. 시므리, 힐기야와 드발리야의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 므라리 사람 호사의 넷째 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Obadiah, was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during the reign of David.
persons.article: Zechariah, the son of Obadiah, is mentioned as the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during the reign of King David. The half-tribe of Manasseh, along with Reuben and Gad, settled in the region east of the Jordan River, known as Gilead. Zechariah's role as a leader suggests he had administrative and military responsibilities over the territory and people of Manasseh in Gilead. His father, Obadiah, is not mentioned elsewhere in the Bible, but Zechariah's leadership position indicates he came from a family of influence within the tribe. The mention of Zechariah in this context highlights the organization and structure of the tribes during David's reign.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.27.21 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); father of Iddo.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.27.21에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 잇도의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 오바댜의 아들 스가랴는 다윗 왕 시대에 길르앗에 있는 므낫세 반 지파의 지도자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Reubenite chief during the reign of Jotham
persons.short: Zechariah was a chief of the tribe of Reuben during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah.
persons.article: Zechariah is mentioned as one of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah. He is listed along with Jeiel as a leader of the Reubenites. The tribe of Reuben, along with Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, settled in the region east of the Jordan River. During the reign of Jotham, who was known for his righteous rule, these tribes were recognized as having valiant men, skilled in warfare. Zechariah's inclusion among the chiefs suggests he held a position of authority and responsibility within the tribe of Reuben.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Reuben living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.7 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.7에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 유다 왕 요담 시대의 르우벤 지파 족장이었다.

persons.description: Singer living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Jediael@1Ch.26.2, Zebadiah@1Ch.26.2, Jathniel@1Ch.26.2, Elam@1Ch.26.3, Jehohanan@1Ch.26.3, Eliehoenai@1Ch.26.3
persons.brief: Levite gatekeeper and musician during David's reign
persons.short: Zechariah, a Levite, served as a gatekeeper and musician in the tabernacle during the time of King David.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King David. He held various responsibilities related to the tabernacle and its service. Zechariah is mentioned as one of the gatekeepers who guarded the entrance to the tabernacle. He was also a skilled musician and was appointed by David to play the lyre and harp during the transportation of the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. Zechariah's musical abilities were recognized, and he was among the Levites chosen to lead the music and singing when the ark was brought into the tent David had pitched for it. He also participated in the musical celebration when the ark was finally brought into the temple built by Solomon. In addition to his musical duties, Zechariah was entrusted with the responsibility of distributing the offerings and tithes among his fellow Levites. He was known for his integrity and fairness in this role. Zechariah's descendants continued to serve as gatekeepers in the temple, with his son Meshelemiah being appointed as the chief gatekeeper during David's reign. The faithful service of Zechariah and his family in the tabernacle and temple highlights the important role the Levites played in maintaining the worship and service of God.
persons.summary: A musician from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.21 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); son of Meshelemiah; a brother of Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan and Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 노래하는 자. 1Ch.9.21에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 므셀레먀의 아들. 여디아엘, 스바댜, 야드니엘, 엘람, 여호하난과 엘여호에내의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스가랴는 다윗 왕 시대에 성막에서 문지기이며 음악가로 섬겼다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
persons.short: Zechariah was one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. As part of Jehoshaphat's reforms to strengthen the spiritual life of the nation, he sent out Levites and priests to teach the Book of the Law to the people in the cities of Judah. Zechariah was among the Levites chosen for this important task, along with Ben-hail, Obadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah. They were accompanied by the priests Elishama and Jehoram. This educational mission aimed to instruct the people in the ways of the Lord and ensure that they understood and followed the commandments given in the Law. Zechariah's participation in this endeavor highlights the role of the Levites as teachers and spiritual guides for the nation.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.7 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.17.7에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 여호사밧 왕이 유다 성읍들에서 율법책을 가르치도록 보낸 레위인 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign
persons.short: Zechariah, a Levite who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah. He was the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah. During a time of crisis, when a great multitude came against Judah, the Spirit of the Lord came upon Zechariah in the midst of the assembly. He prophesied, encouraging the people not to fear, for the battle belonged to God. This Zechariah is only mentioned in this single passage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.20.14 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Benaiah; father of Jahaziel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.20.14에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 브나야의 아들. 야하시엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스가랴는 여호사밧 왕 시대에 예언했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jehoram@1Ki.22.50-Mat, Azariah@2Ch.21.2, Jehiel@2Ch.21.2, Azariahu@2Ch.21.2, Michael@2Ch.21.2, Shephatiah@2Ch.21.2
persons.brief: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah
persons.short: Zechariah, one of the sons of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
persons.article: Zechariah was one of the sons of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah. His brothers were Azariah, Jehiel, Michael, and Shephatiah. Jehoshaphat gave his sons many gifts of silver, gold, and valuable possessions, along with fortified cities in Judah. However, he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, Zechariah's eldest brother, because he was the firstborn.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.21.2 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); son of Jehoshaphat; a brother of Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.21.2에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 여호사밧의 아들. 여호람, 아사랴, 여히엘, 아사랴, 미가엘과 스바댜의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 유다 왕 여호사밧의 아들 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest murdered in the temple court
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada the priest, was murdered in the temple court.
persons.article: Zechariah was the son of Jehoiada the priest during the reign of Joash, king of Judah. After the death of Jehoiada, Joash listened to the princes of Judah and they abandoned the house of the Lord. Zechariah was filled with the Spirit of God and stood above the people, admonishing them for forsaking God. However, the people conspired against Zechariah and, at the king's command, stoned him to death in the court of the temple. Jesus later references the murder of Zechariah, son of Berechiah (likely referring to Jehoiada), as an example of the persecution of the prophets.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ch.24.20 referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ), or Zechariah (Ζαχαρίας); a son of Jehoiada.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 제사장. 2Ch.24.20에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 여호야다와 여호세바의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 여호야다의 아들 스가랴는 성전 뜰에서 살해당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet who instructed King Uzziah
persons.short: Zechariah, a prophet who instructed King Uzziah in the fear of God.
persons.article: Zechariah was a prophet who lived during the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah. He had understanding in the visions of God. As long as Uzziah sought the Lord, God made him prosper. Zechariah instructed Uzziah in the fear of God. Under his guidance, Uzziah became mighty, built towers and fortifications, and had a large well-equipped army. However, after Uzziah became strong, he grew proud, leading to his downfall. This Zechariah is only mentioned in this single passage.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.26.5 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.26.5에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 선지자 스가랴는 웃시야 왕에게 하나님 경외하는 법을 가르쳤다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite during Hezekiah's temple cleansing
persons.short: Zechariah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, helped cleanse the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite of the sons of Asaph who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah. When Hezekiah began to restore and cleanse the temple, Zechariah was among the Levites who gathered to help. The Levites took all the unclean things from the inner part of the temple and brought them out to be disposed of. They sanctified the temple and the altar, preparing to restart the service of the Lord that had been neglected under the previous kings.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.29.13 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.29.13에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 아삽 자손 레위인 스가랴는 히스기야 왕 시대에 성전을 정결하게 하는 것을 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite who helped repair the temple under Josiah
persons.short: Zechariah, a Levite who helped repair the temple during Josiah's reign.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the reign of King Josiah of Judah. When Josiah ordered the repair and restoration of the temple, Zechariah was among the Levites appointed to oversee the workmen. He, along with other Levites, acted faithfully in this task. This Zechariah is only mentioned in this single passage, and no other details are provided about him.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.34.12 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.34.12에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스가랴는 요시야 왕 시대에 성전 수리를 도왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Leader who contributed to Josiah's Passover
persons.short: Zechariah, a leader who generously contributed to Josiah's Passover celebration.
persons.article: Zechariah was one of the leaders of the people during the reign of King Josiah of Judah. When Josiah directed the celebration of a grand Passover feast, Zechariah, along with Hilkiah and Jehiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave 2,600 Passover offerings and 300 cattle to the priests for the Passover sacrifices. This generous contribution helped make Josiah's Passover one of the greatest in Israel's history.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.35.8 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.35.8에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 지도자 스가랴는 요시야 왕의 유월절 행사에 아낌없이 기여했다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Last king of the northern kingdom of Israel
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Jeroboam II, was the last king of the northern kingdom of Israel, reigning for only six months before being assassinated.
persons.article: Zechariah was the son of Jeroboam II and the last king of the northern kingdom of Israel. He ascended to the throne after the death of his father, who had reigned for forty-one years. However, Zechariah's reign was short-lived, lasting only six months. During his brief reign, Zechariah did evil in the sight of the Lord, following in the footsteps of his predecessors. He continued the idolatrous practices that had plagued the northern kingdom since its inception. Zechariah's reign came to a violent end when he was conspired against and assassinated by Shallum, son of Jabesh. This assassination fulfilled the prophecy given to Jehu, stating that his descendants would sit on the throne of Israel for four generations. The death of Zechariah marked the end of the dynasty of Jehu and the beginning of a period of political instability in the northern kingdom. Shallum, who had killed Zechariah, assumed the throne but was himself assassinated just one month later. This turmoil and the lack of a stable leadership contributed to the eventual downfall and captivity of the northern kingdom at the hands of the Assyrians.
persons.summary: A king of Northern Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.14.29 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Jeroboam.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.14.29에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 여로보암의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여로보암 2세의 아들 스가랴는 북이스라엘 왕국의 마지막 왕으로, 육 개월만 다스리다 암살당했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Mentioned in the genealogy of King Hezekiah
persons.short: Zechariah is mentioned as the father of Abijah (or Abi), the mother of King Hezekiah of Judah.
persons.article: Zechariah is briefly mentioned in the genealogical record of King Hezekiah of Judah. He is identified as the father of Abijah (or Abi), who was the mother of Hezekiah. Apart from this genealogical reference, no further information is provided about Zechariah's life or his role in the history of Judah. His inclusion in the genealogy serves to establish the lineage of King Hezekiah and to highlight the importance of family records in the biblical narrative. The fact that Zechariah is mentioned by name suggests that he may have been a person of some significance or from a notable family. However, without additional details, it is difficult to make any definitive statements about his life or character. The mention of Zechariah in the genealogy of Hezekiah also underscores the interconnectedness of the royal families and the significance of marital alliances in the history of Judah. Hezekiah's mother, Abijah, would have played a crucial role in his upbringing and in shaping his character as a king who sought to restore proper worship and obedience to God in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.18.2 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); father of Abi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.18.2에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 아비의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 유다 왕 히스기야의 어머니 아비야(아비라고도 함)의 아버지로 언급된다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman
persons.short: Zechariah, an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile.
persons.article: Zechariah was an Israelite who lived during the time of Ezra the scribe, after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was among the men who had married foreign women, which was contrary to God's law. When Ezra called the people to repentance and required them to separate from their foreign wives, Zechariah was one of those listed as having done so. This act demonstrated his willingness to obey God's commands and purify the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.10.26 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.10.26에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 포로 시대에 이방인 아내와 결혼했던 이스라엘 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Post-exilic prophet who wrote the book of Zechariah
persons.short: Zechariah, a post-exilic prophet and priest who wrote the book bearing his name.
persons.article: Zechariah was a prophet and priest who lived in Judah after the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel. Zechariah began his prophetic ministry in the second year of Darius, king of Persia, delivering messages to encourage the people to rebuild the temple. His prophecies, recorded in the biblical book bearing his name, are known for their rich use of visions and symbolism, similar to the books of Daniel and Revelation. Zechariah's ministry likely extended into the reign of Xerxes I, the king who made Esther queen of Persia. As both a prophet and priest, Zechariah would have had intimate knowledge of Jewish religious practices.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Ezr.5.1 referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ), or Zechariah (Aramiac זְכַרְיָה); a son of Berechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 선지자. Ezr.5.1에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 베레갸의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 포로 이후 시대의 선지자이며 제사장으로, 그의 이름을 딴 책을 저술했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Bebai who returned with Ezra
persons.short: Zechariah, a descendant of Bebai, who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Zechariah was a descendant of Bebai who lived during the time of Ezra the scribe. He was among the group of exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon under Ezra's leadership. In the list of those who returned, Zechariah is mentioned under the descendants of Bebai. The text records that 28 males of the descendants of Bebai returned with Ezra, but no other specific information is given about this particular Zechariah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.11 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Bebai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.11에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 브배의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 브배의 후손으로 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite sent by Ezra to find ministers
persons.short: Zechariah, a man of understanding, sent by Ezra to find ministers for the house of God.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the time of Ezra the scribe. When Ezra was preparing to lead a group of exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon, he sent for Zechariah and other leaders to find ministers for the house of God. Zechariah is described as a man of understanding, indicating his wisdom and discernment. Ezra's trust in sending him on this important mission suggests that Zechariah was a respected figure among the Levites.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.16 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.16에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 명철한 사람 스가랴는 하나님의 집에서 섬길 자들을 찾도록 에스라가 보낸 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Parosh who returned with Ezra
persons.short: Zechariah, a descendant of Parosh, who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Zechariah was a descendant of Parosh who lived during the time of Ezra the scribe. When Ezra led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon, Zechariah was among them. He is mentioned in the list of the men who returned with Ezra, grouped under the descendants of Parosh.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.3 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.3에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 바로스의 후손으로 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Witness to Isaiah's prophecy about Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Jeberechiah, was a faithful witness to Isaiah's prophecy about his son Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.
persons.article: Zechariah, the son of Jeberechiah, was a witness to the prophet Isaiah's writing concerning the birth and naming of his son, Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz. God instructed Isaiah to record this prophecy and have it witnessed by faithful witnesses, one of whom was Zechariah. The name of Isaiah's son was symbolic, meaning "quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil," and signified the coming judgment on Syria and Israel by Assyria. Zechariah's role as a witness indicates his trustworthiness and possibly his prominence in the community. He is described as a faithful witness, suggesting his commitment to God and His word.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Isa.8.2 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Jeberechiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Isa.8.2에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 여베레기야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 여베레갸의 아들 스가랴는 그 아들 마헬살랄하스바스에 관한 이사야의 예언에 신실한 증인이 되었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Priest, father of John the Baptist
persons.short: Zechariah, a priest of the division of Abijah, was the father of John the Baptist and husband of Elizabeth.
persons.article: Zechariah was a priest who served in the temple during the reign of Herod the Great. He belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and his wife, Elizabeth, was also a descendant of Aaron. Zechariah and Elizabeth are described as righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and statutes of the Lord. Despite their righteousness, Zechariah and Elizabeth were childless, and both were advanced in years. While performing his priestly duties in the temple, Zechariah was chosen by lot to enter the sanctuary and burn incense. During this time, an angel of the Lord appeared to him and announced that his prayer had been heard, and that Elizabeth would bear a son named John. Zechariah doubted the message due to their old age, and as a result, he was struck mute until the birth of his son. When Elizabeth gave birth, Zechariah confirmed that the child's name should be John, as the angel had instructed. Upon doing so, his speech was restored, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit, prophesying about the role his son would play in preparing the way for the Messiah. Zechariah's prophecy, known as the Benedictus, speaks of God's mercy and the coming of the Messiah, who would bring salvation and deliverance to His people. He also foretold that his son, John, would be called the prophet of the Most High and would go before the Lord to prepare His ways.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Luk.1.5 only referred to as Zechariah (Ζαχαρίας); husband of Elizabeth; father of John.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '사가랴'라 불림. 엘리사벳의 남편. 요한의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 아비야 반차의 제사장 스가랴는 세례 요한의 아버지이며 엘리사벳의 남편이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
persons.short: Zechariah, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, was the son of Pashhur (or 'Pashur').
persons.article: Zechariah was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Pashhur (or 'Pashur'), from the priestly family of Malchijah. Zechariah is mentioned in the list of priests and Levites who settled in Jerusalem, indicating his role in reestablishing the spiritual life of the community. As a priest, he would have been involved in the temple service and religious ceremonies.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.12 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Pashhur; father of Amzi.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 레위인. Neh.11.12에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 바스훌의 아들. 암시의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 스가랴는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 바스훌(바술이라고도 함)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Perez who lived in Jerusalem
persons.short: Zechariah, a descendant of Perez, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Zechariah was a descendant of Perez, the son of Judah, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel. Zechariah is mentioned in the list of the people who resettled in Jerusalem, which was a smaller population compared to the wider region of Judah. His presence in Jerusalem suggests his commitment to restoring the city and its spiritual life.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.4 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Amariah; father of Uzziah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.4에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 아마랴의 아들. 웃시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 베레스의 후손 스가랴는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Shelah who lived in Jerusalem
persons.short: Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
persons.article: Zechariah was a descendant of Shelah, the son of Judah, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni. Like the Zechariah mentioned in Neh.11.4, this Zechariah is listed among the people who resettled in Jerusalem. His decision to live in the city demonstrates his commitment to the restoration of Jerusalem and the religious life of the community. The text provides no further details about this specific Zechariah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.11.5 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); a son of Shiloni; father of Joiarib.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.11.5에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 실로의 아들. 요야립의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 셀라의 후손 스가랴는 포로 이후 예루살렘에 정착했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Head of the priestly family of Iddo
persons.short: Zechariah was the head of the priestly family of Iddo during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
persons.article: Zechariah was the head of the priestly family of Iddo during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua, who served as high priest after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the list of priestly family heads during Joiakim's time. As the head of his family, Zechariah would have had a leadership role among the priests and been responsible for his family's service in the temple. This may be the same Zechariah mentioned as the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah (Zec.1.1, though this is not certain).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.16 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.16에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 스가랴는 요야김 대제사장 시절 잇도 제사장 가문의 우두머리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.siblings: Shemaiah@Neh.12.36, Azarel@Neh.12.36, Milalai@Neh.12.36, Gilalai@Neh.12.36, Maai@Neh.12.36, Nethanel@Neh.12.36, Judah@Neh.12.36, Hanani@Neh.12.36
persons.brief: Priest who played a trumpet in the procession
persons.short: Zechariah, son of Jonathan, was a priest who played a trumpet in the procession at Jerusalem's wall dedication.
persons.article: Zechariah, the son of Jonathan, was a priest who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah. He is specifically mentioned as one of the priests who played trumpets during the celebratory procession around the newly built wall. Zechariah's role in playing the trumpet highlights his musical skill and his involvement in the worship and celebrations of the community. He was the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph. This lineage connects him to Asaph, one of the chief musicians appointed by David.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.35 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); son of Jonathan; a brother of Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.35에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림. 요나단의 아들. 스마야, 아사렐, 밀랄래, 길랄래, 마애, 느다넬, 유다와 하나니의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 요나단의 아들 제사장 스가랴는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식 행렬에서 나팔을 불었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who participated in the wall dedication
persons.short: Zechariah, a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
persons.article: Zechariah was one of the priests who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after its completion in the time of Nehemiah. He was among the priests who blew trumpets during the joyful celebration and procession around the city wall. His presence at this significant event indicates his role in the religious life of the community and his support for Nehemiah's leadership in rebuilding the city.
persons.summary: A musician living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.12.41 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.12.41에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 스가랴는 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식에 참여했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
persons.short: Zechariah, a Levite who stood beside Ezra when he read the Law to the people.
persons.article: Zechariah was a Levite who lived during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, after the return from the Babylonian exile. When Ezra read the Book of the Law to the assembled people, Zechariah was one of the Levites who stood beside him on the platform. This public reading of the Law was a significant event in the spiritual reformation of the Jewish community. Zechariah's presence on the platform with Ezra indicates his status as a respected Levite and his involvement in the religious life of the community.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.8.4 only referred to as Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '스가랴'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 레위인 스가랴는 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 낭독할 때 그 곁에 섰다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act, Ner@1Sa.14.50-1Ch, Abdon@1Ch.8.30-, Zur@1Ch.8.30-, Baal@1Ch.8.30-, Nadab@1Ch.8.30-, Gedor@1Ch.8.31-, Ahio@1Ch.8.31-, Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-
persons.brief: Son of Abiel, founder of Gibeon
persons.short: Zecher (or Zechariah), a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the father (and founder) of Gibeon.
persons.article: Zecher, also known as Zechariah, was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the father (and founder) of Gibeon. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles. Zecher had several brothers, including Ner, the grandfather of King Saul. The genealogy suggests that Zecher was an ancestor of some of the Benjamites who lived in Gibeon, a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.8.31 referred to as Zecher (זֶ֫כֶר), or Zechariah (זְכַרְיָהוּ); son of Abiel and Maacah; a brother of Kish, Ner, Abdon, Zur, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio and Mikloth.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.8.31에 처음 언급되며 '세겔'이라 불림. 아비엘과 마아가의 아들. 기스, 넬, 압돈, 술, 바알, 나답, 그돌, 아효와 미글롯의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세겔(스가랴라고도 함)은 기브온의 창설자(아버지) 아비엘(여이엘)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jeconiah, king of Judah
persons.short: Zedekiah, a son of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), king of Judah.
persons.article: Zedekiah was a son of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), the king of Judah who was deported to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar. He is mentioned in the genealogy of the kings of Judah in 1 Chronicles. Zedekiah had a brother named Assir.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.3.16 only referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ); son of Jehoiachin; a brother of Shealtiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.3.16에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림. 여호야긴의 아들. 스알디엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시드기야는 유다 왕 여고냐(여호야긴)의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: False prophet who opposed Micaiah
persons.short: Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, was a false prophet who opposed Micaiah and encouraged Ahab to attack Ramoth-gilead.
persons.article: Zedekiah, the son of Chenaanah, was a false prophet during the reign of King Ahab of Israel. When Ahab sought advice about attacking Ramoth-gilead, Zedekiah, along with other prophets, encouraged the king to go to war, promising victory. He made iron horns and symbolically declared that Ahab would gore the Syrians. However, the prophet Micaiah contradicted their message, prophesying Ahab's defeat and death. Zedekiah struck Micaiah and accused him of lying. Micaiah responded by saying that Zedekiah would hide in an inner chamber when his false prophecy was revealed. Ahab listened to Zedekiah and the other false prophets, leading to his death in battle.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.22.11 only referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ); a son of Chenaanah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ki.22.11에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림. 그나아나의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 그나아나의 아들 시드기야는 미가야를 대적하고 아합이 길르앗 라못을 공격하도록 부추긴 거짓 선지자였다.

persons.description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile
persons.short: Zedekiah, originally named Mattaniah, was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile.
persons.article: Zedekiah, originally named Mattaniah, was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile. He was the son of Josiah and the uncle of Jehoiachin. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, appointed him as a vassal king after deporting Jehoiachin. Zedekiah reigned for 11 years, but he did evil in the sight of the Lord. Despite the warnings of the prophet Jeremiah, Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, leading to the siege and destruction of Jerusalem. During the siege, Zedekiah sought counsel from Jeremiah but did not heed his advice to surrender. When the city fell, Zedekiah attempted to flee but was captured. His sons were killed before his eyes, and then he was blinded and taken to Babylon in chains. Zedekiah's reign ended in tragedy, marking the fall of the kingdom of Judah and the beginning of the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A king of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.24.17 referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ), or Mattaniah (מַתַּנְיָ֫הוּ); son of Josiah and Hamutal; a brother of Jehoahaz; half-brother of: Jehoiakim and Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 왕. 2Ki.24.17에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림. 요시야와 하무달의 아들. 여호아하스, 여호야김과 살룸의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 원래 이름이 맛다냐였던 시드기야는 바벨론 포로 이전 유다의 마지막 왕이었다.
persons.article_ko: 시드기야(원래 이름은 맛다냐)는 바벨론 포로 이전 유다의 마지막 왕이었다. 그는 요시야의 아들이며 여호야긴의 삼촌이었다. 바벨론 왕 느부갓네살은 여호야긴을 유배시킨 후 그를 봉신왕으로 세웠다. 시드기야는 십일 년간 다스렸으나 여호와 보시기에 악을 행했다. 선지자 예레미야의 경고에도 불구하고 시드기야는 바벨론을 대적하여 반역하여 예루살렘의 포위와 파괴를 초래했다. 포위 기간 동안 시드기야는 예레미야에게 조언을 구했으나 항복하라는 그의 충고를 따르지 않았다. 성이 함락되었을 때 시드기야는 도망치려 했으나 사로잡혔다. 그의 아들들은 그의 눈앞에서 죽임을 당했고, 그런 다음 그는 눈이 멀게 되어 사슬에 묶여 바벨론으로 끌려갔다. 시드기야의 통치는 비극으로 끝났으며, 이는 유다 왕국의 멸망과 바벨론 포로의 시작을 나타냈다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: False prophet in Babylon during the exile
persons.short: Zedekiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, was denounced by Jeremiah for his lies and immorality.
persons.article: Zedekiah was a false prophet who, along with another named Ahab, prophesied among the exiles in Babylon during the time of Jeremiah. They falsely predicted an early return from captivity, contradicting Jeremiah's prophecies. Jeremiah sternly rebuked them, not only for their false and reckless predictions but also for their immoral and adulterous lives. He declared that their fate at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar would become proverbial in Israel, with people using their names as a curse, saying, "May the Lord make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire." This Zedekiah is not to be confused with the king of the same name.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.29.21 only referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ); a son of Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.29.21에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림. 마아세야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 시드기야는 바벨론 포로들 가운데 있던 거짓 선지자로, 예레미야가 그의 거짓과 부도덕함을 규탄했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Official during the reign of King Jehoiakim
persons.short: Zedekiah, the son of Hananiah, was an official during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah.
persons.article: Zedekiah, the son of Hananiah, was an official during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah. He is mentioned in the context of the scroll containing Jeremiah's prophecies, which was read before the king. When the scroll was read in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, Zedekiah was among the officials present, along with Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, Gemariah, and others. After hearing the words of the scroll, the officials advised Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, to hide along with Jeremiah. They then reported the matter to the king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.36.12 only referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ); a son of Hananiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. Jer.36.12에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림. 하나냐의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 하나냐의 아들 시드기야는 유다 왕 여호야김 시대의 관리였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
persons.short: Zedekiah, a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah after the exile.
persons.article: Zedekiah was a priest who lived in the time of Nehemiah, after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned among the priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. In this covenant, the people pledged to follow the Law of God, to avoid intermarriage with the surrounding nations, to keep the Sabbath, and to support the temple and its services. Zedekiah's presence among the signatories indicates his leadership role in the priestly community and his commitment to the spiritual reformation led by Nehemiah.
persons.summary: A priest living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.10.1 only referred to as Zedekiah (צִדְקִיָּ֫הוּ).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Neh.10.1에 처음 언급되며 '시드기야'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 제사장 시드기야는 포로 이후 느헤미야와 언약에 서명했다.

persons.description: Man living before Israel's Monarchy
persons.brief: Midianite prince defeated by Gideon
persons.short: Zeeb, a prince of Midian, was captured and killed by the Ephraimites during Gideon's victory over the Midianites.
persons.article: Zeeb was a prince of Midian during the time of the judges in Israel. When Gideon and his 300 men defeated the Midianite army, the Ephraimites captured Zeeb and another prince named Oreb at the winepress of Zeeb. They killed both princes and brought their heads to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan. The victory over Oreb and Zeeb was celebrated as a significant part of Gideon's triumph over the Midianites, who had been oppressing Israel. The Psalmist later refers to their defeat, asking God to make the enemies of Israel like Oreb and Zeeb.
persons.summary: A man living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jdg.7.25 only referred to as Zeeb (זְאֵב).
persons.summary_ko: 사사시대 남성. Jdg.7.25에 처음 언급되며 '스엡'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 미디안 방백 스엡은 기드온이 미디안을 이긴 승리 중 에브라임 사람들에게 사로잡혀 죽임을 당했다.

persons.description: Warrior Ammonite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ammonite, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: Zelek the Ammonite was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: Zelek was an Ammonite who was counted among David's mighty men, the elite group of warriors who fought alongside him. He is mentioned in the lists of David's mighty men in both 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles. The fact that an Ammonite was included among David's most trusted soldiers is significant, as the Ammonites were often enemies of Israel. Zelek's presence in this group suggests that he had proven his loyalty and skill in battle.
persons.summary: A warrior of the Ammonites living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.23.37 only referred to as Zelek (צֶ֫לֶק).
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 암몬 용사. 2Sa.23.37에 처음 언급되며 '셀렉'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 암몬 사람 셀렉은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Israelite whose daughters received his inheritance
persons.short: Zelophehad, a descendant of Manasseh, had no sons, so his daughters appealed for and received his inheritance.
persons.article: Zelophehad was a man from the tribe of Manasseh during the time of Moses. He had five daughters - Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah - but no sons. After the census in the wilderness, Zelophehad's daughters came before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the congregation, asking for a possession among their father's brothers, since Zelophehad had died without a male heir. Moses brought their case before the Lord, who commanded that the daughters be given their father's inheritance. This ruling set a precedent for cases where a man died without a son. Later, when the Israelites were preparing to enter Canaan, the heads of the fathers' houses of Manasseh raised a concern that if Zelophehad's daughters married outside their tribe, their inheritance would be lost to the tribe. Moses then commanded that they could marry whom they thought best, but only within their father's tribal clan, to keep the inheritance within the tribe. Zelophehad's daughters did as the Lord commanded and married sons of their father's brothers. This event is significant in establishing the rights of inheritance for women in ancient Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Num.26.33 only referred to as Zelophehad (צְלׇפְחָד); a son of Hepher; father of Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Num.26.33에 처음 언급되며 '슬로브핫'이라 불림. 헤벨의 아들. 말라, 노아, 호글라, 밀가와 디르사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 슬로브핫은 므낫세의 후손으로 아들이 없어, 그의 딸들이 유산을 청원하여 받았다.

persons.description: People from Zemar(?)
persons.siblings: Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch, Heth@Gen.10.15-Ezk, Jebusites@Gen.10.16-Zec, Amorites@Gen.10.16-Amo, Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh, Hivites@Gen.10.17-2Ch, Arkites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch, Arvadites@Gen.10.18-1Ch, Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch
persons.brief: Canaanite people group
persons.short: The Zemarites were a Canaanite people group mentioned in the Table of Nations.
persons.article: The Zemarites were a Canaanite people group mentioned in the Table of Nations in Genesis 10 and 1Chronicles 1. They are listed between the Arvadites and Hamathites, suggesting they lived in the northern region of Phoenicia. The name may be associated with the town of Sumra, located on the coast between Tripolis and Arvad, about 1.5 miles north of the Nahr el-Kebir River. This town is likely the same as Cumur, which is mentioned in the Tell el-Amarna Letters along with Arvad. The exact extent and history of the Zemarites is unknown, as they are only mentioned in these genealogical passages.
persons.summary: People from Zemar(?) of the Canaanites, first mentioned at Gen.10.18 only referred to as Zemarites (צְמָרִי); descended from Canaan along with Sidon, Heth, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites and Hamathites.
persons.summary_ko: 스말 족속. Gen.10.18에 처음 언급되며 '스말'이라 불림. 가나안의 자녀. 시돈, 헷, 여부스, 아모리, 기르가스, 히위, 알가, 신, 아르왓과 하맛의 동기.
persons.short_ko: 스말 족속은 민족 계보에 언급된 가나안 족속이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.siblings: Joash@1Ch.7.8, Eliezer@1Ch.7.8, Elioenai@1Ch.7.8, Omri@1Ch.7.8, Jeremoth@1Ch.7.8, Abijah@1Ch.7.8, Anathoth@1Ch.7.8, Alemeth@1Ch.7.8
persons.brief: Son of Becher, a Benjamite
persons.short: Zemirah was a son of Becher and grandson of Benjamin.
persons.article: Zemirah was a son of Becher, who was a son of Benjamin, according to the genealogy in 1Chronicles 7. He is mentioned along with his brothers Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.8 only referred to as Zemirah (זְמִירָה); son of Becher; a brother of Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. 1Ch.7.8에 처음 언급되며 '스미라'라 불림. 베겔의 아들. 요아스, 엘리에셀, 에료에내, 오므리, 여레못, 아비야, 아나돗과 알레멧의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스미라는 베겔의 아들이며 베냐민의 손자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Christian lawyer whom Paul commended
persons.short: Zenas, a lawyer, was commended by Paul and was to be sent on his journey with Apollos.
persons.article: Zenas was a Christian lawyer mentioned by Paul in his letter to Titus. Paul instructs Titus to help Zenas and Apollos on their journey, ensuring that they have everything they need. The fact that Paul refers to Zenas as a lawyer suggests he may have had training in Jewish or Roman law. His association with Apollos, a learned and eloquent teacher, may indicate that Zenas was also involved in teaching or preaching. Paul's commendation of Zenas demonstrates his importance in the early Christian community, although no other details about his life or ministry are provided in the Bible.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Tit.3.13 only referred to as Zenas (Ζηνᾶς).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Tit.3.13에 처음 언급되며 '세나'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 율법교사 세나는 바울에게 칭찬받았으며 아볼로와 함께 여행길에 보내지기로 되어 있었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest during the reign of Zedekiah
persons.short: Zephaniah, a priest during King Zedekiah's reign, was taken captive to Babylon.
persons.article: Zephaniah was a priest who served during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah. He is mentioned several times in the books of Jeremiah and 2 Kings. Zephaniah was the son of Maaseiah and held the position of second priest, subordinate to the high priest Seraiah. King Zedekiah sent Zephaniah, along with others, to inquire of the Lord through the prophet Jeremiah concerning the Babylonian threat. Zephaniah is also mentioned in a letter from Shemaiah, a false prophet in Babylon, who accused Zephaniah of not rebuking Jeremiah for his prophecies. After the fall of Jerusalem, Zephaniah was among the captives taken to Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had him executed.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.25.18 only referred to as Zephaniah (צְפַנְיָהוּ); a son of Maaseiah.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ki.25.18에 처음 언급되며 '스바니야'라 불림. 마아세야의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 스바냐는 시드기야 왕 시대의 제사장으로, 바벨론으로 포로로 끌려갔다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the men in Zechariah's prophecy
persons.short: Zephaniah was one of the men in whose crown was to be placed in the temple as a memorial.
persons.article: Zephaniah is mentioned in the book of Zechariah as one of the men who came from Babylon to Jerusalem. He, along with Heldai and Tobijah, brought silver and gold, which was to be used to make a crown. This crown was to be placed on the head of Joshua the high priest and then kept in the temple as a memorial. The event was symbolic of the Messiah, the Branch, who would build the temple of the Lord and rule as both priest and king.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Zec.6.10 only referred to as Zephaniah (צְפַנְיָהוּ); father of Josiah.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Zec.6.10에 처음 언급되며 '스바니야'라 불림. 요시야의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스바냐는 그의 면류관을 성전에 기념물로 두게 될 사람 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Prophet, son of Cushi, descendant of Hezekiah
persons.short: Zephaniah, the prophet who wrote the book bearing his name, was the son of Cushi and descendant of Hezekiah.
persons.article: Zephaniah was a prophet of Judah who ministered during the reign of King Josiah, likely in the late 7th century BC. He was the son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah. This genealogy suggests that Zephaniah may have been a descendant of King Hezekiah of Judah. The book of Zephaniah, the ninth book of the Minor Prophets, is attributed to him. In his prophecies, Zephaniah addresses the judgment coming upon Judah and the surrounding nations, as well as the future restoration of God's people. His message emphasizes the Day of the Lord, a time of both judgment and salvation. The book concludes with a promise of hope and joy for the remnant of Israel.
persons.summary: A prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Zep.1.1 only referred to as Zephaniah (צְפַנְיָהוּ); a son of Cushi.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 선지자. Zep.1.1에 처음 언급되며 '스바니야'라 불림. 구시의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 자기 이름을 딴 책을 쓴 선지자 스바냐는 구시의 아들이며 히스기야의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.siblings: Teman@Gen.36.11-Job, Omar@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Amalek@Gen.36.12-, Korah@Gen.36.16
persons.brief: Son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau
persons.short: Zepho, a son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau, was a chief of Edom.
persons.article: Zepho was a son of Eliphaz and a grandson of Esau. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1. Zepho was one of the chiefs of Edom, indicating his prominent position within the Edomite clan. The Edomites were the descendants of Esau who settled in the region of Seir.
persons.summary: A man of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.11 referred to as Zepho (צְפוֹ, צְפִי); son of Eliphaz; a brother of Teman, Omar, Gatam, Kenaz, Amalek and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람. Gen.36.11에 처음 언급되며 '스보'라 불림. 엘리바스와 엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 데만, 오말, 가담, 그나스, 아말렉과 고라의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스보는 엘리바스의 아들이며 에서의 손자로, 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Levite of the Gershonite clan
persons.short: Zerah, a Levite of the Gershonite clan, was the son of Iddo.
persons.article: Zerah was a Levite who belonged to the clan of Gershon. He was the son of Iddo and is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in 1Chronicles 6. These genealogies trace the lineage of the Levitical families, who were responsible for the religious duties in the temple. As a Gershonite, Zerah would have been part of the Levitical family that was tasked with the care of the tabernacle and its furnishings during the wilderness wanderings.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.21 only referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח); a son of Iddo; father of Jeatherai.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.6.21에 처음 언급되며 '세라'라 불림. 잇도의 아들. 여아드래의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세라는 게르손 계열 레위인으로 잇도의 아들이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Ethiopian commander who invaded Judah
persons.short: Zerah the Ethiopian led a vast army against Judah but was defeated by King Asa.
persons.article: Zerah the Ethiopian (or Cushite) was a military commander who led a massive invasion force against Judah during the reign of King Asa. According to 2Chronicles 14, Zerah's army numbered over a million men and included 300 chariots. They advanced as far as Mareshah before encountering Asa's forces in the Valley of Zephathah. Asa called upon the Lord for help, and the Ethiopians were defeated and pursued as far as Gerar. The exact identity of Zerah is uncertain. Some scholars suggest he may have been Usarken II, an Egyptian pharaoh, while others propose he was an Arabian leader. Whoever he was, his defeat was a significant victory for Judah and a demonstration of God's power on behalf of His people.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.14.9 only referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח).
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 2Ch.14.9에 처음 언급되며 '세라'라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 구스 사람 세라는 유다를 대적하는 대군을 이끌었으나 아사 왕에게 패했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Son of Reuel, grandson of Esau
persons.short: Zerah, a son of Reuel and grandson of Esau, was a chief of Edom.
persons.article: Zerah was a son of Reuel and a grandson of Esau. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Esau in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1. Like his cousin Zepho, Zerah was also a chief of Edom, reflecting his leadership position within the Edomite tribe. The Edomites were the descendants of Esau who settled in the region of Seir.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.13 only referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח); son of Reuel; a brother of Nahath, Shammah and Mizzah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성. Gen.36.13에 처음 언급되며 '세라'라 불림. 르우엘의 아들. 나핫, 삼마와 미사의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세라는 르우엘의 아들이며 에서의 손자로, 에돔 족장이었다.

persons.description: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: King of Edom
persons.short: Zerah, from Bozrah, was a king of Edom before Israel had a king.
persons.article: Zerah was a king of Edom, mentioned in the lists of Edomite kings in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1. He was from the city of Bozrah, an important Edomite center. The list of kings in which Zerah appears is chronologically placed before the time of Israel's monarchy, indicating that he ruled during the period of the judges. The Edomites were the descendants of Esau who settled in the region of Seir.
persons.summary: A king of Edom living at the time of the Patriarchs, first mentioned at Gen.36.33 only referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח); father of Jobab.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 왕. Gen.36.33에 처음 언급되며 '세라'라 불림. 요밥의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 보스라 출신 세라는 이스라엘에 왕이 있기 전 에돔 왕이었다.

persons.description: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Judah, twin of Perez
persons.short: Zerah, son of Judah and Tamar, was the twin brother of Perez and ancestor of Achan.
persons.article: Zerah was the son of Judah and Tamar, and the twin brother of Perez. His birth is recorded in Genesis 38, where it is noted that he put out his hand first during delivery, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on his wrist. However, his brother Perez was actually born first, breaking out before him. Zerah's descendants are mentioned in various genealogies throughout the Old Testament. Most notably, Achan, the man who sinned by taking the devoted things during the conquest of Jericho, was from the tribe of Judah and the family of Zerah. The descendants of Zerah are also mentioned among those who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. In 1Chronicles 27, it is recorded that Shamhuth, from the clan of Zerah, was in charge of the fifth division of David's army. His descendants the Izrahites or Ezrahites included very wise men (1Ki.4.31). Ethan is also credited with composing Psalm 89 (Psalm 1Ki.89.1). Another notable Ezrahite was Heman, who was a singer and musician in the time of David and is mentioned as the author of Psalm 88 (Psalm 1Ki.88.1; 1Ch.6.33). Zerah is also included in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew 1, highlighting his significance in the lineage of the Messiah.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.38.30 referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח), or Izrahite (יִזְרָ֑ח), or Zerah (Ζαρά); son of Judah and Tamar; a brother of Perez; half-brother of: Er, Onan and Shelah; father of Zabdi, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 유다의 아들. Gen.38.30에 처음 언급되며 '세라'라 불림. 유다와 다말의 아들. 엘, 오난, 셀라와 베레스의 형제. 삽디, 에단, 헤만, 갈골과 다라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세라는 유다와 다말의 아들이며 베레스의 쌍둥이 형제로, 아간의 조상이었다.
persons.article_ko: 세라는 유다와 다말의 아들이며 베레스의 쌍둥이 형제였다. 그의 출생은 창세기 38장에 기록되어 있는데, 그가 출산 중 먼저 손을 내밀어 산파가 그의 손목에 홍색 실을 매었다고 기록한다. 그러나 그의 형제 베레스가 실제로 먼저 그를 앞질러 태어났다. 세라의 후손은 구약 전체의 여러 족보에 언급된다. 가장 주목할 만한 것은, 여리고 정복 당시 온전히 바친 물건을 취하여 죄를 지은 아간이 유다 지파이자 세라 가문 출신이었다는 것이다. 세라의 후손은 또한 포로 이후 예루살렘에 거주한 사람들 가운데도 언급된다. 역대상 27장에는 세라 가문 출신 삼훗이 다윗 군대의 다섯 번째 반을 담당했다고 기록되어 있다. 그의 후손인 이스라 사람들 또는 에스라 사람들에는 매우 지혜로운 사람들이 포함되었다(왕상 4:31). 에단은 시편 89편을 지은 것으로 인정받는다(시 89:1). 또 다른 저명한 에스라 사람은 헤만으로, 다윗 시대의 노래하는 자이며 음악가였고 시편 88편의 저자로 언급된다(시 88:1; 대상 6:33). 세라는 또한 마태복음 1장의 예수님 족보에도 포함되어 있어, 메시아 혈통에서 그의 중요성을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Son of Simeon; ancestor of the Zerahites
persons.short: Zerah (or Zohar), a son of Simeon, was the ancestor of the Zerahite clan.
persons.article: Zerah, also known as Zohar, was one of the sons of Simeon, the second son of Israel (or 'Jacob') and Leah. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Simeon in Gen.46.10, Exo.6.15, Num.26.13, and 1Ch.4.24. Zerah's descendants formed the Zerahite clan within the tribe of Simeon. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai (Num.26.20, the Zerahites were counted among the clans of Simeon). The Zerahites are also mentioned in the story of Achan (Jos.7.17, who was from the tribe of Judah but was identified as a descendant of Zerah). In 1Ch.27.11,13, Sibbecai, one of David's military commanders, is described as a Zerahite. The repeated mention of Zerah and his descendants in various contexts highlights the importance of family lineage and clan identity within the tribes of Israel.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, first mentioned at Gen.46.10 referred to as Zerah (זֶ֫רַח), or Zerahite (זַרְחִי), or Zohar (צֹ֫חַר); son of Simeon; a brother of Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin and Shaul.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '소할'이라 불림. 시므온과 시므온의 아내(이름 미상)의 아들. 여무엘, 야민, 오핫, 야긴과 사울의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세라(소할이라고도 함)는 시므온의 아들이며 세라 족속의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Priest, ancestor of Ezra
persons.short: Zerahiah (or Ahitub), a priest, was an ancestor of Ezra the scribe.
persons.article: Zerahiah, also known as Ahitub, was a priest mentioned in the genealogies of the priestly families in 1 Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah. He was an ancestor of Ezra the scribe, who played a significant role in the spiritual reformation of the Jews after their return from Babylonian exile. In the genealogies, Zerahiah is listed as the son of Uzzi and the father of Meraioth. He was part of the line of priests descending from Eleazar, the son of Aaron. As a priest, Zerahiah would have served in the temple and carried out the religious duties prescribed for the Levitical priesthood. His inclusion in the genealogies of Ezra emphasizes the scribe's priestly lineage and authority.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.6.6 referred to as Zerahiah (זְרַחְיָה), or Ahitub (אֲחִיטוּב); a son of Uzzi; father of Meraioth.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 제사장. 1Ch.6.6에 처음 언급되며 '스라히야'라 불림. 웃시의 아들. 므라욧의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 세라야(아히둡이라고도 함)는 제사장으로 서기관 에스라의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Descendant of Pahath-Moab who returned with Ezra
persons.short: Zerahiah, a descendant of Pahath-Moab, led 200 men in the return to Jerusalem with Ezra.
persons.article: Zerahiah was a descendant of Pahath-Moab, one of the clans that returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile with Ezra. In Ezra 8, which lists the family heads and the number of men who accompanied Ezra, Zerahiah is mentioned as the leader of 200 men of Pahath-Moab. This indicates that he held a position of responsibility and leadership within his clan. The return led by Ezra was significant in the history of Israel, as it marked a renewed commitment to the Law of Moses and the restoration of Jewish worship in Jerusalem. Zerahiah's participation in this journey demonstrates his devotion to God and his support for Ezra's mission.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Ezr.8.4 only referred to as Zerahiah (זְרַחְיָה); father of Eliehoenai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Ezr.8.4에 처음 언급되며 '스라히야'라 불림. 엘여호에내의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 바핫모압의 후손 스라히야는 에스라와 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아오는 이백 명을 이끌었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.offspring: Vaizatha@Est.9.9, Parshandatha@Est.9.7, Dalphon@Est.9.7, Aspatha@Est.9.7, Poratha@Est.9.8, Adalia@Est.9.8, Aridatha@Est.9.8, Parmashta@Est.9.9, Arisai@Est.9.9, Aridai@Est.9.9
persons.brief: Wife of Haman, enemy of the Jews
persons.short: Zeresh, the wife of Haman, advised him to have Mordecai hanged on a gallows.
persons.article: Zeresh was the wife of Haman, the chief antagonist in the Book of Esther. When Haman became enraged at Mordecai's refusal to bow down to him, Zeresh and Haman's friends advised him to have a gallows built and to ask the king's permission to hang Mordecai on it. This plan reveals Zeresh's support for her husband's evil schemes and her own animosity towards the Jews. However, after Haman was humiliated by having to honor Mordecai, Zeresh and his wise men predicted Haman's downfall, stating that he could not prevail against Mordecai if he was of Jewish descent. Zeresh's words proved true, as Haman was ultimately hanged on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. The story of Zeresh and Haman serves as a warning against pride, hatred, and the consequences of plotting evil against others.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Est.5.10 only referred to as Zeresh (זֶ֫רֶשׁ); wife of Haman; mother of Vaizatha, Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai and Aridai.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성. Est.5.10에 처음 언급되며 '세레스'라 불림. 하만의 아내. 왜사다, 바산다다, 달본, 아스바다, 보라다, 아달리야, 아리다다, 바마스다, 아리새와 아리대의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 하만의 아내 세레스는 그에게 모르드개를 교수대에 매달라고 조언했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Ahuzzam@1Ch.4.6, Hepher@1Ch.4.6, Temeni@1Ch.4.6, Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6, Izhar@1Ch.4.7, Ethnan@1Ch.4.7, Koz@1Ch.4.8
persons.brief: Son of Ashhur, founder of Tekoa
persons.short: Zereth, a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and Helah, was a Judahite.
persons.article: Zereth was a Judahite, the son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and his wife Helah. Ashhur was the father (ie founder) of Tekoa, a town in Judah. Zereth is mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1Chronicles 4, along with his brothers Zohar and Ethnan.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.4.7 only referred to as Zereth (צֶ֫רֶת); son of Ashhur and Helah; a brother of Haahashtari, Izhar, Ethnan and Koz; half-brother of: Ahuzzam, Hepher and Temeni.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.4.7에 처음 언급되며 '세렛'이라 불림. 아스훌과 헬라의 아들. 아훗삼, 헤벨, 데므니, 하아하스타리, 이스할, 에드난과 고스의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세렛은 아스훌(아술이라고도 함)과 헬라의 아들로 유다 사람이었다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jeduthun, a temple musician
persons.short: Zeri (or Izri), a son of Jeduthun, was a temple musician during the reign of David.
persons.article: Zeri, also known as Izri, was one of the sons of Jeduthun, a Levite who served as a temple musician during the reign of King David. Zeri and his brothers were appointed by David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. They were part of the group of Levites tasked with providing music for worship in the tabernacle. In the organizational structure of the temple musicians, Zeri and his brothers were under the supervision of their father Jeduthun.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.25.3 referred to as Zeri (צְרִי), or Izri (יִצְרִי); son of Jeduthun; a brother of Obed-edom, Mattithiah, Gedaliah, Jeshaiah and Hashabiah.
persons.short_ko: 스리는 여두둔의 아들로 성전에서 수금을 연주하며 찬양을 담당했다.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.25.3에 처음 언급되며 '스리'라 불림. 여두둔의 아들. 오벧에돔, 맛디디야, 그달리야, 여사야와 하사뱌의 형제.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Ancestor of King Saul
persons.short: Zeror, a Benjamite, was an ancestor of King Saul.
persons.article: Zeror was a Benjamite mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul, Israel's first monarch. He was the father of Abiel (or Jeiel) and the grandfather of Kish, Saul's father. This genealogical note appears in the context of introducing Saul and providing information about his family background. As an ancestor of Saul, Zeror belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Sa.9.1 only referred to as Zeror (צְרוֹר); a son of Becorath; father of Abiel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.9.1에 처음 언급되며 '스롤'이라 불림. 베고랏의 아들. 아비엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스로르는 베냐민 사람으로 사울 왕의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Mother of Jeroboam, first king of Israel
persons.short: Zeruah was the mother of Jeroboam, who became the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
persons.article: Zeruah was the mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the division of the united monarchy. She is mentioned in the account of Jeroboam's rise to power in 1Kings 11. Zeruah was a widow, and her son Jeroboam was an official in Solomon's administration. Jeroboam rebelled against Solomon and fled to Egypt. After Solomon's death, Jeroboam returned and was made king over the ten northern tribes, fulfilling a prophecy given to him by Ahijah the Shilonite. Zeruah's mention in this context highlights Jeroboam's background and family situation.
persons.summary: A woman of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.11.26 only referred to as Zeruah (צְרוּעָה); wife of Nebat; mother of Jeroboam.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.11.26에 처음 언급되며 '스루아'라 불림. 느밧의 아내. 여로보암의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 스루아는 북이스라엘 왕국의 첫 왕이 된 여로보암의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Governor living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.offspring: Meshullam@1Ch.3.19, Hananiah@1Ch.3.19-, Shelomith@1Ch.3.19, Hashubah@1Ch.3.20, Ohel@1Ch.3.20, Berechiah@1Ch.3.20, Hasadiah@1Ch.3.20, Jushab-hesed@1Ch.3.20, Abiud@Mat.1.13
persons.brief: Leader of the first Jewish exiles from Babylon
persons.short: Zerubbabel (or Sheshbazzar), a descendant of David, led the first group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon and oversaw the rebuilding of the temple.
persons.article: Zerubbabel, also known as Sheshbazzar, was a descendant of King David who played a crucial role in the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon and the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem. He is mentioned in various books of the Old Testament, including 1 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, and Zechariah. Zerubbabel led the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem under the decree of Cyrus, king of Persia. He is listed among the leaders who returned and is credited with laying the foundation of the temple. Despite facing opposition from the Samaritans and others, Zerubbabel, along with the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, encouraged the people to complete the rebuilding of the temple. He is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Matthew, emphasizing his importance in the messianic lineage. Zerubbabel's leadership and dedication were instrumental in reestablishing Jewish worship in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: Governor from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.3.19 referred to as Zerubbabel (זְרֻבָּבֶ֫ל), or Zerubbabel (Aramiac זְרֻבָּבֶ֫ל), or Sheshbazzar (שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר), or Sheshbazzar (Aramiac שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר), or Zerubbabel (Ζοροβάβελ); son of Pedaiah; a brother of Shimei; father of Meshullam, Hananiah, Shelomith, Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, Jushab-hesed and Abiud.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 총독. 1Ch.3.19에 처음 언급되며 '스룹바벨'이라 불림. 브다야의 아들. 시므이의 형제. 므술람, 하나냐, 슬로밋, 하수바, 오헬, 베레갸, 하사댜, 유삽헤셋과 아비훗의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스룹바벨(세스바살이라고도 함)은 다윗의 후손으로, 바벨론에서 유대인 포로 첫 무리를 이끌고 예루살렘으로 돌아와 성전 재건을 감독했다.
persons.article_ko: 스룹바벨(세스바살이라고도 함)은 다윗 왕의 후손으로, 바벨론에서 유대인 포로들이 돌아오고 예루살렘 성전을 재건하는 데 중대한 역할을 했다. 그는 역대상, 에스라, 느헤미야, 학개, 스가랴 등 구약의 여러 책에 언급된다. 스룹바벨은 페르시아 왕 고레스의 조서에 따라 포로들의 첫 무리를 이끌고 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다. 그는 돌아온 지도자 명단에 올라 있으며 성전의 기초를 놓은 것으로 인정받는다. 사마리아 사람들과 다른 이들의 반대에도 불구하고 스룹바벨은 선지자 학개와 스가랴와 함께 백성이 성전 재건을 완성하도록 격려했다. 그는 또한 마태복음의 예수 그리스도 족보에 언급되어, 메시아 혈통에서 그의 중요성을 강조한다. 스룹바벨의 지도력과 헌신은 바벨론 포로 이후 예루살렘에서 유대인 예배를 재확립하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Ancestor of Jesus
persons.short: Zerubbabel, a descendant of David, was an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
persons.article: Zerubbabel is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Luke 3. He was a descendant of King David and an ancestor of Joseph, the husband of Mary. In the genealogy, Zerubbabel is listed as the son of Shealtiel and the father of Rhesa. This Zerubbabel is likely the same person as the prominent figure who led the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon and oversaw the rebuilding of the temple in the 6th century BC. His inclusion in Jesus' genealogy underscores the Messiah's connection to the royal line of David and the fulfillment of God's promises to His people.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Luk.3.27 only referred to as Zerubbabel (Ζοροβάβελ); a son of Shealtiel; father of Rhesa.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Luk.3.27에 처음 언급되며 '스룹바벨'이라 불림. 스알디엘의 아들. 레사의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스룹바벨은 다윗의 후손이며 예수 그리스도의 조상이었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.siblings: David@Rut.4.17-Rev, Eliab@1Sa.16.6-2Ch, Abinadab@1Sa.16.8-1Ch, Nethanel@1Ch.2.14, Raddai@1Ch.2.14, Ozem@1Ch.2.15, Elihu@1Ch.27.18, Abigail@2Sa.17.25-1Ch(?), Shimeah@1Sa.16.9-1Ch
persons.brief: Sister of David; mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel
persons.short: Zeruiah, David's sister, was the mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel, who were among David's mighty men and military leaders.
persons.article: Zeruiah was the sister of King David and the mother of three of his most prominent military leaders: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Her sons played significant roles throughout David's reign, both in military campaigns and in political matters. Joab served as the commander of David's army, while Abishai and Asahel were also known for their bravery and skill in battle. Zeruiah's sons were fiercely loyal to David, though their actions sometimes brought them into conflict with the king. For example, Joab murdered Abner and Amasa, two of David's rivals, without the king's consent. Despite these tensions, David recognized the importance of Zeruiah's sons in establishing and maintaining his kingdom. The fact that Zeruiah is consistently mentioned as their mother highlights her significance in the family and her influence on her sons' roles in David's court.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Sa.26.6 only referred to as Zeruiah (צְרוּיָה); daughter of Jesse and Nahash; a sister of David, Eliab, Abinadab, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, Abigail(?) and Elihu, Shimeah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Sa.26.6에 처음 언급되며 '스루야'라 불림. 이새와 나하스의 딸. 다윗, 엘리압, 아비나답, 느다넬, 랏대, 오셈, 엘리후, 아비가일과 삼마의 자매. 스루야의 남편(이름 미상)의 아내. 아비새, 요압과 아사헬의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 다윗의 누이 스루야는 다윗의 용사이며 군 지도자였던 요압, 아비새, 아사헬의 어머니였다.
persons.article_ko: 스루야는 다윗 왕의 누이이며 그의 가장 저명한 군 지휘관 세 사람인 요압, 아비새, 아사헬의 어머니였다. 그녀의 아들들은 다윗의 통치 기간 동안 군사 작전과 정치적 문제 모두에서 중요한 역할을 했다. 요압은 다윗 군대의 지휘관으로 섬겼고, 아비새와 아사헬도 전투에서의 용맹함과 기량으로 알려졌다. 스루야의 아들들은 다윗에게 철저히 충성했으나, 그들의 행동은 때때로 왕과의 갈등을 초래했다. 예를 들어, 요압은 왕의 동의 없이 다윗의 경쟁자였던 아브넬과 아마사를 살해했다. 이러한 긴장에도 불구하고 다윗은 그의 왕국을 세우고 유지하는 데 있어 스루야의 아들들의 중요성을 인정했다. 스루야가 그들의 어머니로 일관되게 언급된다는 사실은 가족 내에서 그녀의 중요성과 다윗 궁정에서 아들들의 역할에 대한 그녀의 영향력을 부각시킨다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Laadan, a Gershonite Levite
persons.short: Zetham, a son of Laadan, was a Gershonite Levite during the time of David.
persons.article: Zetham was a Levite of the Gershonite clan, mentioned in the genealogies and organizational lists of the Levites during the reign of King David. He was a son of Laadan and is listed along with his brothers Jehiel and Joel. In David's organization of the Levites, Zetham and his brothers were appointed as treasurers and officials over the treasuries of the house of the Lord. This suggests that they held positions of responsibility in managing the resources and wealth associated with the tabernacle and later the temple.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.23.8 only referred to as Zetham (זֵתָם); son of Libni ; a brother of Joel and Jehiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 레위인. 1Ch.23.8에 처음 언급되며 '세담'이라 불림. 립니의 아들. 여히엘과 요엘의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 스담은 라단의 아들이며 다윗 시대의 게르손 계열 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Jeush@1Ch.7.10, Benjamin@1Ch.7.10, Ehud@1Ch.7.10, Chenaanah@1Ch.7.10, Tarshish@1Ch.7.10, Ahishahar@1Ch.7.10
persons.brief: Son of Bilhan, a Benjamite
persons.short: Zethan was a son of Bilhan and a descendant of Benjamin.
persons.article: Zethan was a Benjamite mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin in 1Chronicles 7. He was a son of Bilhan and a descendant of Jediael, one of the sons of Benjamin. Zethan is listed along with his brothers Jeush and Benjamin. This genealogical record provides insight into the family structure and lineage of the tribe of Benjamin.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.10 only referred to as Zethan (זֵיתָן); son of Bilhan; a brother of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Tarshish and Ahishahar.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.7.10에 처음 언급되며 '세단'이라 불림. 빌한의 아들. 여우스, 베냐민, 에훗, 그나아나, 달시스와 아히사할의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 세단은 빌한의 아들이며 베냐민의 후손이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: One of the seven eunuchs of King Ahasuerus
persons.short: Zethar was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus of Persia.
persons.article: Zethar was one of the seven eunuchs who served in the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) of Persia, as recorded in the Book of Esther. He is mentioned by name along with the other eunuchs: Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, and Carcas. In the story, King Ahasuerus commanded these seven eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti before him during a royal feast, so that he could display her beauty to the guests. This incident led to Vashti's refusal and subsequent removal as queen, setting the stage for Esther to become the new queen. As a eunuch, Zethar would have been a trusted servant in the royal court, with responsibilities related to the king's personal affairs and harem.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Est.1.10 only referred to as Zethar (זֵתַר).
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 남성. Est.1.10에 처음 언급되며 '세달'이라 불림.
persons.short_ko: 세달은 페르시아 왕 아하수에로를 섬긴 일곱 내시 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.siblings: Michael@1Ch.5.13, Meshullam@1Ch.5.13, Sheba@1Ch.5.13, Jorai@1Ch.5.13, Jacan@1Ch.5.13, Eber@1Ch.5.13
persons.brief: Gadite clan leader during the reign of Jotham
persons.short: Zia was a Gadite clan leader during the reigns of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel.
persons.article: Zia was a clan leader of the tribe of Gad during the reigns of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel. He is mentioned in the genealogical record of the Gadites in 1Chronicles 5. This record lists the clan leaders and their families who lived in the region of Gilead. Zia is named along with his fellow clan leaders, including Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, and Beba.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Gad living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.13 only referred to as Zia (זִיעַ); son of Abihail; a brother of Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan and Eber.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성. 1Ch.5.13에 처음 언급되며 '시아'라 불림. 아비하일의 아들. 미가엘, 므술람, 세바, 요래, 야간과 에벨의 형제.
persons.short_ko: 시아는 유다 왕 요담과 이스라엘 왕 여로보암 시대의 갓 지파 가문 지도자였다.

persons.description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Servant of Saul's household, later served David
persons.short: Ziba, a servant of Saul's household, became a servant of David and played a role in the conflict between David and Mephibosheth.
persons.article: Ziba was a servant of Saul's household who later became a servant of King David. He first appears in the narrative when David inquires about any remaining members of Saul's family to whom he can show kindness. Ziba informs David about Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, who was lame in both feet. David grants Mephibosheth all of Saul's land and appoints Ziba, along with his fifteen sons and twenty servants, to manage the property on Mephibosheth's behalf. Later, during Absalom's rebellion, Ziba meets David with supplies and falsely claims that Mephibosheth had hoped to regain the kingdom. David then grants Ziba all of Mephibosheth's possessions.
