persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: The wife of Caiaphas the high priest.
persons.short: A reference to the unnamed wife of Caiaphas, the high priest who condemned Jesus.
persons.article: Jhn.18.13 makes a passing reference to the wife of Caiaphas, the Jewish high priest at the time of Jesus' trial and crucifixion. Caiaphas presided over the Sanhedrin council that condemned Jesus and turned him over to Pontius Pilate for execution. No other details are provided in Scripture about Caiaphas' wife. As the wife of the high priest, she would have been a prominent woman in Jerusalem's aristocratic circles. However, her name and any other information about her life are unknown.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Jhn.18.13 only referred to as a wife of Caiaphas (.); unnamed daughter of: Annas; wife of Caiaphas.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Jhn.18.13에 처음 언급되며 '안나스의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 안나스의 딸. 가야바의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 이는 예수님을 정죄한 대제사장 가야바의 이름 없는 아내를 가리킨다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness - unnamed daughter of Machir
persons.brief: Married Hezron, bore Segub
persons.short: The daughter of Machir married Hezron and gave birth to Segub.
persons.article: The daughter of Machir is mentioned in 1Ch.2.21 as the wife of Hezron, who married her in his old age. Machir was the son of Manasseh, and his daughter's marriage to Hezron, a descendant of Judah, represents an inter-tribal union. She gave birth to a son named Segub. This brief mention in the genealogy of Judah highlights the connection between the tribes of Judah and Manasseh through this marriage.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Manasseh living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at 1Ch.2.21 only referred to as daughter of Machir; unnamed daughter of: Machir; a sister of Gilead, Peresh, Sheresh and Hammolecheth; wife of Hezron; mother of Segub.
persons.description_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 마길의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 마길의 이름 없는 딸. 1Ch.2.21에 처음 언급되며 '마길의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 마길과 마아가의 딸. 길르앗, 베레스, 세레스와 함몰레겟의 자매. 헤스론의 아내. 스굽의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 마길의 딸은 헤스론과 결혼하여 스굽을 낳았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return - unnamed daughter of Meshullam
persons.brief: Married Jehohanan, son of Tobiah the Ammonite
persons.short: The daughter of Meshullam was married to Jehohanan, the son of Tobiah the Ammonite.
persons.article: The daughter of Meshullam is mentioned in Neh.6.18 as the wife of Jehohanan, the son of Tobiah the Ammonite. Tobiah was one of the adversaries who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. The marriage between Meshullam's daughter and Tobiah's son highlights the complex relationships and alliances that existed among the Jewish nobles and their neighboring tribes. This connection likely contributed to the challenges Nehemiah faced in his mission to restore Jerusalem and its community.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.6.18 only referred to as daughter_of_Meshullam (.); unnamed daughter of: Meshullam; wife of Jehohanan.
persons.description_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 므술람의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 므술람의 이름 없는 딸. Neh.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '므술람의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 므술람의 딸. 여호하난의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 므술람의 딸은 암몬 사람 도비야의 아들 여호하난과 결혼했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy - unnamed daughter of Pharaoh
persons.brief: Daughter of Pharaoh - Wife of King Solomon
persons.short: Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, forming a political alliance with Egypt.
persons.article: The daughter of Pharaoh, unnamed in the biblical text, was one of King Solomon's wives. Their marriage, mentioned in 1Ki.3.1, was likely a political alliance between Israel and Egypt. Solomon brought her to the City of David until he finished building his palace and the Temple. The marriage to Pharaoh's daughter demonstrates Solomon's growing power and influence, as well as his willingness to form alliances with foreign nations. However, it also foreshadows Solomon's eventual downfall, as his many foreign wives led him astray from worshiping the one true God (1Ki.11.1-8).
persons.summary: A woman of the Egyptians living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.3.1 only referred to as daughter of Pharaoh; unnamed daughter of: Pharaoh and Tahpenes; wife of Solomon.
persons.description_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성 - 바로의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성 - 바로의 이름 없는 딸. 1Ki.3.1에 처음 언급되며 '바로의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 바로와 다브네스의 딸. 솔로몬의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 솔로몬은 바로의 딸과 결혼하여 애굽과 정치적 동맹을 맺었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness - unnamed daughter of Pharaoh
persons.brief: Daughter of Pharaoh - Rescued and adopted Moses
persons.short: Pharaoh's daughter rescued the infant Moses from the Nile and adopted him as her son.
persons.article: The daughter of Pharaoh, unnamed in the biblical text, played a significant role in the early life of Moses. When Moses was born, his mother hid him for three months to protect him from Pharaoh's decree to kill all Hebrew male infants. When she could no longer hide him, she placed him in a basket and set it among the reeds of the Nile River. Pharaoh's daughter discovered the basket while bathing in the Nile and recognized the child as a Hebrew. Moses' sister Miriam, who was watching nearby, offered to find a Hebrew woman to nurse the child, and Pharaoh's daughter agreed. Miriam brought Moses' mother, who was then hired by Pharaoh's daughter to nurse the child. When Moses grew older, Pharaoh's daughter adopted him as her son and named him Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water" (Exo.2.5-10). This event set the stage for Moses' upbringing in the Egyptian royal court and his eventual role as the deliverer of the Israelites from Egyptian bondage.
persons.summary: A woman of the Egyptians living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Exo.2.5 only referred to as daughter of Pharaoh; unnamed daughter of: Pharaoh; adoptive mother of: Moses.
persons.description_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 바로의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 바로의 이름 없는 딸. Exo.2.5에 처음 언급되며 '바로의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 바로의 딸.
persons.short_ko: 바로의 딸은 아기 모세를 나일강에서 구해내 자기 아들로 입양했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness - unnamed daughter of Putiel
persons.brief: Daughter of Putiel - Wife of Eleazar the priest
persons.short: The daughter of Putiel was the wife of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest.
persons.article: The daughter of Putiel, whose name is not given in the biblical text, was the wife of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest (Exo.6.25). Eleazar was one of the first priests of Israel, serving alongside his father Aaron and his brothers Nadab, Abihu, and Ithamar. The only information provided about Putiel's daughter is her marriage to Eleazar, which highlights the priestly lineage of Aaron's family.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, only mentioned at Exo.6.25 only referred to as daughter of Putiel; unnamed daughter of: Putiel; wife of Eleazar; mother of Phinehas.
persons.description_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 부디엘의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성 - 부디엘의 이름 없는 딸. Exo.6.25에 처음 언급되며 '부디엘의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 부디엘의 딸. 엘르아살의 아내. 비느하스의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 부디엘의 딸은 제사장 아론의 아들 엘르아살의 아내였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return - unnamed daughter of Sanballat
persons.brief: Married to a grandson of the high priest Eliashib
persons.short: The daughter of Sanballat the Horonite was married to a grandson of the high priest Eliashib.
persons.article: The daughter of Sanballat is mentioned in Neh.13.28 as being married to a grandson of the high priest Eliashib. Sanballat was the governor of Samaria and an opponent of Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild Jerusalem. This marriage between a member of the high priestly family and the daughter of a prominent adversary was considered a serious breach of the covenant and a defilement of the priesthood. Nehemiah took decisive action by driving the offending priest away from Jerusalem.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, inferred at Neh.13.28; only referred to as daughter of Sanballat; unnamed daughter of: Sanballat; wife of son of Joiada.
persons.description_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 산발랏의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 산발랏의 이름 없는 딸. Neh.13.28에 처음 언급되며 '산발랏의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 산발랏의 딸. 요야다의 아들(이름 미상)의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 호론 사람 산발랏의 딸은 대제사장 엘리아십의 손자와 결혼했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return - unnamed daughter of Shecaniah
persons.brief: Married to one of Tobiah's sons
persons.short: The daughter of Shecaniah was married to one of Tobiah the Ammonite's sons.
persons.article: The daughter of Shecaniah is mentioned in Neh.6.18 as being married to one of the sons of Tobiah the Ammonite. Tobiah was an adversary who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. The marriage alliance between Shecaniah's daughter and Tobiah's son highlights the complex relationships and connections that existed among the Jewish nobles and their neighboring tribes during the post-exilic period.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Exile and Return, inferred at Neh.6.18; only referred to as daughter of Shecaniah; unnamed daughter of: Shecaniah; wife of Tobiah.
persons.description_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 스가냐의 이름 없는 딸
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 여성 - 스가냐의 이름 없는 딸. Neh.6.18에 처음 언급되며 '스가냐의 딸(이름 미상)'라 불림. 스가냐의 딸. 도비야의 아내. 여호하난의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 스가냐의 딸은 암몬 사람 도비야의 아들 중 한 사람과 결혼했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs - unnamed older daughter of Lot
persons.brief: Elder daughter of Lot; mother of Moab
persons.short: Lot's unnamed elder daughter, who bore Moab after the destruction of Sodom.
persons.article: Gen.19.30-38 recounts the story of Lot's two unnamed daughters after the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The elder daughter, believing that they were the only survivors and that there were no men to father their children, devised a plan to sleep with their father. She got Lot drunk and lay with him, conceiving a son named Moab. Moab became the ancestor of the Moabite people. The Bible does not provide further details about the elder daughter's life or character, but her actions reflect the desperation and moral decay of the time.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, inferred at Gen.19.30a; only referred to as daughter1 of Lot; unnamed older daughter of: Lot; daughter of Lot; mother of Moab; a sister of daughter2 of Lot.
persons.description_ko: 족장시대 여성 - 롯의 이름 없는 큰딸
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성 - 롯의 이름 없는 큰딸. Gen.19.37에 처음 언급되며 '롯의 딸 1(이름 미상)'라 불림. 롯과 롯의 아내(이름 미상)의 딸. 롯의 딸(이름 미상)의 자매. 롯의 아내. 모압의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 롯의 이름 없는 맏딸은 소돔 멸망 후 모압을 낳았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs - unnamed younger daughter of Lot
persons.brief: Younger daughter of Lot; mother of Ben-ammi
persons.short: Lot's unnamed younger daughter, who bore Ben-ammi after the destruction of Sodom.
persons.article: Gen.19.30-38 tells the story of Lot's two unnamed daughters following the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The younger daughter, like her elder sister, believed that they were the only survivors and that there were no men to father their children. She followed her sister's plan to sleep with their father. After getting Lot drunk, she lay with him and conceived a son named Ben-ammi, who became the ancestor of the Ammonite people. The Bible does not provide additional information about the younger daughter's life or character, but her actions, like those of her sister, reflect the desperation and moral decay of the time.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, inferred at Gen.19.30b; only referred to as daughter2 of Lot; unnamed younger daughter of: Lot; mother of Ben-ammi ; a sister of daughter1 of Lot.
persons.description_ko: 족장시대 여성 - 롯의 이름 없는 작은딸
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성 - 롯의 이름 없는 작은딸. Gen.19.38에 처음 언급되며 '롯의 딸 2(이름 미상)'라 불림. 롯과 롯의 아내(이름 미상)의 딸. 롯의 딸(이름 미상)의 자매. 롯의 아내. 벤암미의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 롯의 이름 없는 작은딸은 소돔 멸망 후 벤암미를 낳았다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of the New Testament - unnamed father of Barnabas
persons.brief: A close relative of John Mark.
persons.short: A reference to the grandfather or other close relative of John Mark.
persons.article: Col.4.10 mentions the father of John Mark in passing. The verse states that Barnabas was John Mark's cousin (or nephew, in some translations). By extension then, John Mark's unnamed father was the uncle of Barnabas. No other details are provided about this man. As Barnabas was a Levite from Cyprus (Act.4.36, his uncle may have also been a Levite and lived on Cyprus, but this is not specified in Scripture). John Mark became an important early church leader who accompanied Paul and Barnabas on missionary journeys (Act.12.25, 13:5, Act.15.37-39 and later aided Peter as well )(1Pe.5.13).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, inferred at Col.4.10; only referred to as father of Barnabas (.); unnamed father of: Barnabas and Mary.
persons.description_ko: 신약시대 레위인 - 바나바의 이름 없는 아버지
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 레위인 - 바나바의 이름 없는 아버지. Col.4.10에 처음 언급되며 '바나바의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 바나바와 마리아의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이는 요한 마가의 할아버지 또는 다른 가까운 친척을 가리킨다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy - unnamed father
persons.brief: Father of Conaniah, a Levite in charge of offerings
persons.short: The father of Conaniah, a Levite who supervised the offerings during King Hezekiah's reign.
persons.article: The father of Conaniah is mentioned in 2Ch.31.12 as the father of a Levite named Conaniah, who served during the reign of King Hezekiah. Conaniah and his brother Shimei were appointed to oversee the contributions, tithes, and dedicated gifts brought to the temple. They were entrusted with the responsibility of ensuring the proper distribution of these offerings among the priests and Levites. Although the name of Conaniah's father is not stated, his son's position indicates that he likely belonged to a family of Levites dedicated to temple service.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, inferred at 2Ch.31.12; only referred to as father of Conaniah; unnamed father of: Conaniah and Shimei.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. 2Ch.31.12에 처음 언급되며 '고나냐의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 고나냐와 시므이의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 고나냐의 아버지는 히스기야 왕 시대에 헌물을 감독한 레위인이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: The wife of Zechariah and mother of John the Baptist.
persons.short: Elizabeth was the wife of Zechariah, a priest, and the mother of John the Baptist.
persons.article: Elizabeth was the wife of Zechariah, a priest from the division of Abijah, and the mother of John the Baptist (Luk.1.5,13). She was a descendant of Aaron, making her a Levite (Luk.1.5). Elizabeth and her husband were described as righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and statutes of the Lord (Luk.1.6). Despite their righteousness, Elizabeth was barren, and both she and Zechariah were advanced in years (Luk.1.7). An angel appeared to Zechariah and announced that Elizabeth would bear a son, who was to be named John (Luk.1.13). When Elizabeth conceived, she remained in seclusion for five months, praising God for His favor (Luk.1.24-25). During her sixth month of pregnancy, her relative Mary, who was carrying Jesus, visited her (Luk.1.36,39-40). Upon hearing Mary's greeting, the baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb, and she was filled with the Holy Spirit, blessing Mary and her child (Luk.1.41-45). After the birth of John, Elizabeth and Zechariah had him circumcised and named on the eighth day, according to the angel's instructions (Luk.1.59-63). The Bible does not provide further details about Elizabeth's life after these events.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Levi through Aaron, living at the time of the New Testament, not named in the Bible but implied at Luk.1.36; father of Elizabeth (Ἐλισάβετ) and the wife of Heli (?).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성. Luk.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '엘리사벳의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 엘리사벳과 헬리의 아내(이름 미상)의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 엘리사벳은 제사장 사가랴의 아내이며 세례 요한의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament - unnamed father of Eunice
persons.brief: Father of Eunice - Grandfather of Timothy
persons.short: Eunice's father, unnamed in the Bible, was the maternal grandfather of Timothy.
persons.article: The father of Eunice, mentioned in 2Ti.1.5, is not named in the biblical text. He was the maternal grandfather of Timothy, Paul's young disciple and companion. Eunice, along with her mother Lois, was commended by Paul for her sincere faith, which they had passed on to Timothy. Although no further information is provided about Eunice's father, his legacy of faith appears to have had a significant impact on his daughter and grandson, who both became followers of Christ and influential members of the early church.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, inferred at 2Ti.1.5; only referred to as father_of_Eunice (.); unnamed father of Eunice@2Ti.1.5.
persons.description_ko: 신약시대 남성 - 유니게의 이름 없는 아버지
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성 - 유니게의 이름 없는 아버지. 2Ti.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '유니게의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 로이스의 남편. 유니게의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 유니게의 성경에 이름이 나오지 않는 아버지는 디모데의 외할아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy - unnamed father
persons.brief: Father of Hilkiah, Jeremiah's cousin
persons.short: The father of Hilkiah, who was the cousin of the prophet Jeremiah.
persons.article: The father of Hilkiah is mentioned in Jer.32.7 as the father of the prophet Jeremiah's cousin. Hilkiah approached Jeremiah with an offer to buy a field in Anathoth, their ancestral town, as a matter of right of redemption. This incident occurred during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem, and the purchase of the field served as a symbolic act of hope and trust in God's promise of future restoration for the people of Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, inferred at Jer.32.7; only referred to as father of Hilkiah; unnamed father of: Hilkiah and Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. Jer.32.7에 처음 언급되며 '힐기야의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 힐기야와 살룸의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 힐기야의 아버지는 선지자 예레미야의 사촌이었다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy - unnamed father
persons.brief: Father of Hodiah and Naham
persons.short: An unnamed man, the father Naham and his sister Hodiah
persons.article: 1Ch.4.19 mentions an unnamed man who was the father of Naham and his sister Hodiah. No further details are provided about his life, character, or lineage. His inclusion in the genealogy of Judah highlights the importance of family connections and marital relationships in ancient Israelite society.
persons.summary: A man from the tribe of Judah(?) living at the time of United Monarchy, inferred at 1Ch.4.19; only referred to as father of Hodiah; unnamed father of: Hodiah and Naham.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. 1Ch.4.19에 처음 언급되며 '호디야의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 호디야와 나함의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 이 이름 없는 사람은 나함과 그 자매 호디야의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament - unnamed father
persons.brief: The father of Mary, Martha and Lazarus of Bethany.
persons.short: The unnamed father of Mary, Martha and Lazarus, who lived in Bethany.
persons.article: The father of Mary, Martha and Lazarus is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Luk.10.38-42. This passage records Jesus visiting the home of Martha in Bethany. It notes that Martha had a sister named Mary. Jhn.11.1-2 specifies that Mary, Martha and Lazarus were siblings. Therefore, the unnamed man was the father of these three. No other details are provided about him in Scripture. He likely lived in Bethany along with his children.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, inferred at Luk.10.39; only referred to as father of Lazarus (.); unnamed father of: Martha, Mary and Lazarus.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. Luk.10.39에 처음 언급되며 '나사로의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 마르다, 마리아와 나사로의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마리아, 마르다, 나사로의 이름 없는 아버지는 베다니에 살았다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs - unnamed father
persons.brief: Father of Mamre - Amorite, ally of Abraham
persons.short: Mamre's father, an Amorite, was an ally of Abraham during the battle against Chedorlaomer.
persons.article: The father of Mamre, an Amorite, is mentioned briefly in Gen.14.13. His name is not provided in the biblical text. Mamre, along with his brothers Eshcol and Aner, was an ally of Abraham during the time when Abraham lived near the terebinth trees of Mamre in Hebron. When Abraham learned that his nephew Lot had been captured by Chedorlaomer and his allies, he gathered his 318 trained servants and pursued them. Mamre and his brothers joined Abraham in this pursuit, demonstrating their loyalty and support for Abraham and his family (Gen.14.24).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, inferred at Gen.14.13; only referred to as father of Mamre; unnamed father of: Mamre, Eshcol and Aner.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. Gen.14.13에 처음 언급되며 '마므레의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 마므레, 에스골과 아넬의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마므레의 아버지는 아모리 사람으로, 그돌라오멜과의 전투에서 아브라함의 동맹자였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy - unnamed father
persons.brief: Father of Nathan, one of David's mighty men
persons.short: The father of Nathan, one of King David's mighty men.
persons.article: The father of Nathan is mentioned in 1Ch.11.38 as the father of one of King David's mighty men. Nathan is listed among the thirty-seven warriors who were renowned for their bravery and military prowess in David's army. Although the name of Nathan's father is not provided, his mention in this context suggests that he was a significant figure, as his son was recognized as one of David's elite soldiers.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, inferred at 1Ch.11.38; only referred to as father of Nathan; unnamed father of: Nathan and Joel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. 1Ch.11.38에 처음 언급되며 '나단의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 나단과 요엘의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 나단의 아버지는 다윗 왕의 용사 중 한 사람의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy - unnamed father
persons.brief: Egyptian Pharaoh who gave his daughter to Hadad
persons.short: The father of Tahpenes, an Egyptian Pharaoh who gave his daughter in marriage to Hadad the Edomite.
persons.article: The father of Tahpenes is mentioned in 1Ki.11.19 as the Egyptian Pharaoh who showed favor to Hadad, an Edomite prince who fled to Egypt after King David's conquest of Edom. The Pharaoh welcomed Hadad and provided for him, even giving him his sister-in-law, the sister of Queen Tahpenes, as a wife. This marriage alliance demonstrates the Pharaoh's support for Hadad and his willingness to grant him refuge in Egypt. The name of this Pharaoh is not specified in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, inferred at 1Ki.11.19; only referred to as father of Tahpenes; unnamed father of: Tahpenes and sister of Tahpenes.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성 - 이름 없는 아버지. 1Ki.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '다브네스의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 다브네스와 다브네스의 자매(이름 미상)의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 다브네스의 아버지는 에돔 사람 하닷에게 자기 딸을 시집보낸 애굽 바로였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of the New Testament - unnamed father of Timothy
persons.brief: Father of Timothy - Greek man; husband of Eunice
persons.short: Timothy's father was a Greek man, and his mother was a believing Jewish woman named Eunice.
persons.article: The father of Timothy, the young disciple and companion of Paul, is mentioned briefly in Act.16.1. His name is not given, but he is described as a Greek man. Timothy's mother, Eunice, was a Jewish woman who believed in Jesus Christ. This mixed-race background may have contributed to Timothy's ability to relate to both Jewish and Gentile believers in the early church. Although Timothy's father was Greek, it seems that he did not hinder his wife Eunice and mother-in-law Lois from raising Timothy in the Jewish faith and teaching him the Scriptures from childhood (2Ti.1.5; 3.15).
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, inferred at Act.16.1; only referred to as father of Timothy (.); unnamed father of Timothy.
persons.description_ko: 신약시대 남성 - 디모데의 이름 없는 아버지
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 남성 - 디모데의 이름 없는 아버지. Act.16.1에 처음 언급되며 '디모데의 아버지(이름 미상)'라 불림. 유니게의 남편. 디모데의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 디모데의 아버지는 그리스 사람이었고, 어머니는 믿는 유대인 여인 유니게였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness - unnamed husband of Hammolecheth
persons.brief: Husband of Hammolecheth - Father of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah
persons.short: Hammolecheth's husband, unnamed in the Bible, was the father of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
persons.article: The husband of Hammolecheth is not named in the biblical text. He is mentioned indirectly in 1Ch.7.18 as the father of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah. Hammolecheth, whose name means "the queen," was the sister of Gilead, a descendant of Manasseh. The genealogy in 1Chronicles 7 lists the descendants of Manasseh, including Hammolecheth and her children.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, inferred at 1Ch.7.18; only referred to as husband of Hammolecheth; unnamed husband of: Hammolecheth.
persons.description_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성 - 함몰레겟의 이름 없는 남편
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 남성 - 함몰레겟의 이름 없는 남편. 1Ch.7.18에 처음 언급되며 '함몰레겟의 남편(이름 미상)'라 불림. 함몰레겟의 남편. 이스홋, 아비에셀과 말라의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 함몰레겟의 이름 없는 남편은 이스홋, 아비에셀, 마흘라의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Levite living at the time of the New Testament  - unnamed husband of Mary
persons.brief: Husband of Mary - John Mark's father
persons.short: Mary's husband, unnamed in the Bible, was the father of John Mark.
persons.article: The husband of Mary, the mother of John Mark, is mentioned indirectly in Act.12.12. His name is not provided in the biblical text. Mary was a prominent member of the early Christian community in Jerusalem, and her house served as a gathering place for prayer and fellowship. When Peter was miraculously released from prison, he went to Mary's house, where many believers were praying for him. The fact that the house is described as belonging to Mary suggests that her husband may have been deceased at the time.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the New Testament, inferred at Act.12.12; only referred to as husband of Mary (.); unnamed father of: Mark; husband of Mary.
persons.description_ko: 신약시대 레위인 - 마리아의 이름 없는 남편
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 레위인 - 마리아의 이름 없는 남편. Act.12.12에 처음 언급되며 '마리아의 남편(이름 미상)'라 불림. 마리아의 남편. 마가의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 마리아의 이름 없는 남편은 요한 마가의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs - unnamed husband of Matred
persons.brief: Husband of Matred, of Edomite royalty
persons.short: Matred's mother was Mezahab, the grandmother of Mehetabel, who was the wife of an Edomite king.
persons.article: The husband of Matred is mentioned in Gen.36.39 as Mezahab. He was the father of Mehetabel, who became the wife of Hadar, one of the kings of Edom. This information is provided in the context of the genealogy of the Edomite kings, which lists the succession of rulers in the land of Edom before the Israelites had their own kings.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of the Patriarchs, inferred at Gen.36.39; only referred to as husband of Matred; unnamed husband of: Matred.
persons.description_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람 - 마드렛의 이름 없는 남편
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 에돔 사람 - 마드렛의 이름 없는 남편. Gen.36.39에 처음 언급되며 '마드렛의 남편(이름 미상)'라 불림. 마드렛의 남편. 므헤다벨의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 므헤다벨의 어머니는 므사합의 딸이며, 에돔 왕의 아내 므헤다벨의 할머니였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy - unnamed husband of Shimeath
persons.brief: Husband of Shimeath - Father of King Joash's assassins
persons.short: Shimeath's husband, unnamed in the Bible, was the father of Jozachar, one of the assassins of King Joash.
persons.article: The husband of Shimeath, an Ammonitess, is not named in the biblical text. He is mentioned indirectly in 2Ki.12.21 as the father of Jozachar (or Zabad, according to 2Ch.24.26, one of the two servants who conspired against King Joash of Judah and assassinated him). Jozachar's mother, Shimeath, is identified as an Ammonitess, indicating that her husband may have also been an Ammonite or that she married an Israelite.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, inferred at 2Ki.12.21; only referred to as husband of Shimeath; unnamed husband of: Shimeath.
persons.description_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성 - 시므앗의 이름 없는 남편
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 남성 - 시므앗의 이름 없는 남편. 2Ki.12.21에 처음 언급되며 '시므앗의 남편(이름 미상)'라 불림. 시므앗의 남편. 요사갈의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 시므앗의 이름 없는 남편은 요아스 왕을 암살한 자 중 한 사람인 여사갈의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Husband of Zeruiah; father of Abishai and Joab
persons.short: The unnamed husband of Zeruiah, who was the father of David's mighty men, Abishai and Joab.
persons.article: The Bible does not directly name the husband of Zeruiah, who was the sister of King David. However, 1Sa.26.6 mentions Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, suggesting that she was married and had children. 2Sa.2.18 also mentions Joab and Asahel as sons of Zeruiah. The fact that Zeruiah's sons are consistently referred to as "sons of Zeruiah" rather than by their father's name suggests that he may have died before they rose to prominence or that Zeruiah herself was a notable figure. Although the Bible does not provide further details about Zeruiah's husband, his marriage to David's sister and the military prowess of his sons indicate that he was likely a member of a prominent family in Judah.
persons.summary: A man living at the time of United Monarchy, inferred at 1Sa.26.6; only referred to as husband of Zeruiah; unnamed husband of Zeruiah; father of Abishai, Joab, Asahel.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 남성. 1Sa.26.6에 처음 언급되며 '스루야의 남편(이름 미상)'라 불림. 스루야의 남편. 아비새, 요압과 아사헬의 아버지.
persons.short_ko: 스루야의 이름 없는 남편은 다윗의 용사 아비새와 요압의 아버지였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Mother-in-law of Peter, healed by Jesus
persons.short: Peter's unnamed mother-in-law, whom Jesus healed of a fever.
persons.article: The New Testament mentions an unnamed woman who was the mother-in-law of the apostle Peter. In Mat.8.14, we learn that she was suffering from a fever when Jesus visited Peter's house in Capernaum. Jesus touched her hand, and the fever left her, demonstrating His power to heal and His compassion for those who were sick. The fact that Peter had a mother-in-law living with him suggests that he was married, although no further details are given about his wife or their relationship. This brief account of Jesus healing Peter's mother-in-law highlights the personal nature of Jesus' ministry and His care for the families of His disciples.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.8.14 only referred to as motherInLaw of Peter (.); unnamed mother-in-law of: Peter.
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Mat.8.14에 처음 언급되며 '베드로의 장모(이름 미상)'라 불림. 베드로의 아내(이름 미상)의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 베드로의 이름 없는 장모는 예수님이 열병을 고쳐주셨다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Egyptian queen, given in marriage to Hadad
persons.short: The sister of Tahpenes, an Egyptian queen, was given in marriage to Hadad the Edomite by Pharaoh.
persons.article: The sister of Tahpenes is mentioned in 1Ki.11.19 as an Egyptian queen who was given in marriage to Hadad, an Edomite prince who fled to Egypt after King David's conquest of Edom. Pharaoh, the father of Tahpenes, showed favor to Hadad and provided for him, even giving him the queen's sister as a wife. This marriage alliance demonstrates the Pharaoh's support for Hadad and his willingness to grant him refuge in Egypt. The name of Tahpenes' sister is not specified in the biblical text.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ki.11.19 only referred to as sister of Tahpenes; unnamed sister of: Tahpenes; wife of Hadad; mother of Genubath.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.11.19에 처음 언급되며 '다브네스의 자매(이름 미상)'라 불림. 다브네스의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 다브네스의 자매. 하닷의 아내. 그누밧의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 애굽 왕비 다브네스의 자매는 바로가 에돔 사람 하닷에게 시집보냈다.

persons.description: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Son of Jashen - One of David's mighty men
persons.short: The son of Jashen, unnamed in the Bible, was one of David's mighty men.
persons.article: The son of Jashen is mentioned in 2Sa.23.32 as one of David's mighty men. His name is not given in the biblical text. The mighty men were a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside David and played significant roles in his military campaigns. They were known for their bravery, strength, and loyalty to David. The son of Jashen is listed among these warriors, indicating his prowess in battle and his dedication to serving King David.
persons.summary: A warrior living at the time of United Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Sa.23.32 only referred to as son of Jashen; unnamed son of: Jashen.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 용사. 2Sa.23.32에 처음 언급되며 '야센의 아들(이름 미상)'라 불림. 야센의 아들.
persons.short_ko: 야센의 이름 없는 아들은 다윗의 용사 중 한 사람이었다.

persons.description: Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
persons.brief: Grandson of Eliashib, married Sanballat's daughter
persons.short: The son of Joiada, a grandson of the high priest Eliashib, married the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite.
persons.article: The son of Joiada is mentioned in Neh.13.28 as a grandson of the high priest Eliashib who married the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite. Sanballat was a prominent adversary of Nehemiah and the governor of Samaria. This marriage alliance between a member of the high priestly family and the daughter of an enemy of Jerusalem was considered a serious violation of the covenant. Nehemiah responded by driving the offending priest away from Jerusalem, demonstrating his commitment to maintaining the purity and integrity of the Jewish community.
persons.summary: A priest from the tribe of Levi living at the time of Exile and Return, only mentioned at Neh.13.28 only referred to as son of Joiada; unnamed son of: Joiada; a brother of Johanan; husband of daughter of Sanballat.
persons.summary_ko: 포로·귀환시대 제사장. Neh.13.28에 처음 언급되며 '요야다의 아들(이름 미상)'라 불림. 요야다의 아들. 요하난의 형제. 산발랏의 딸(이름 미상)의 남편.
persons.short_ko: 요야다의 아들은 대제사장 엘리아십의 손자로, 호론 사람 산발랏의 딸과 결혼했다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: The unnamed grandmother of Jesus.
persons.short: The wife of Heli was sister of Elizather who mothered John the Baptist.
persons.article: The unnamed wife of Heli shared a father with John ther Baptist's mother Elizabeth who was descended from Aaron, making her a Levite (Luk.1.5). This is inferred from the fact that John was related to Jesus who's male ancestral line came from the tribe of Judah. Elizabeth and her husband were described as elderly when Jesus and John were born (Luk.1.7, so she likely was from Mary's mother's generation). This creates the simples possible explanation for the fact that John and Jesus were related and yet were from different tribes.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Levi(?) living at the time of the New Testament, implied at Luk.1.5; ; mother of Mary and Salome (?).
persons.summary_ko: 신약시대 여성. Luk.1.5에 처음 언급되며 '헬리의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 엘리사벳의 아버지(이름 미상)의 딸. 헬리의 아내. 마리아와 살로매의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 헬리의 아내는 엘리사벳의 자매로 세례 요한의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.offspring: Teman@Gen.36.11-Job, Omar@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Zepho@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch, Korah@Gen.36.16
persons.brief: Wife of Eliphaz and mother of Teman.
persons.short: Wife or concubine of Eliphaz, was the mother of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
persons.article: Wife or concubine of Eliphaz is mentioned in Genesis 36 and 1Chronicles 1 as the mother of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. Eliphaz was the firstborn son of Esau. As a concubine, she would have a lower social status than a primary wife but was still considered a legitimate partner.
persons.summary: A woman of the Edomites living at the time of the Patriarchs, implied at Gen.36.11; only referred to as a wife of Eliphaz; unnamed wife of Eliphaz; mother of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz and Korah.
persons.summary_ko: Gen.36.11에 처음 언급되며 '엘리바스의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 엘리바스의 아내. 데만, 오말, 스보, 가담, 그나스와 고라의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 엘리바스의 아내 또는 첩은 데만, 오말, 스보, 가담, 그나스의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Ezekiel - Died as a sign to Israel
persons.short: Ezekiel's wife died suddenly, and God used her death as a sign to the people of Israel.
persons.article: The wife of the prophet Ezekiel is mentioned briefly in Ezk.24.18. God revealed to Ezekiel that his wife would die suddenly, and he was commanded not to mourn for her openly. Ezekiel's wife died that evening, and the next morning, Ezekiel did as the Lord had commanded him. God used this event as a sign to the people of Israel, indicating that they should not mourn when the Lord's judgment came upon Jerusalem and the temple. The death of Ezekiel's wife served as a powerful object lesson, demonstrating the severity of God's impending judgment and the importance of submitting to His will.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Ezk.24.18 only referred to as a wife of Ezekiel; unnamed wife of: Ezekiel.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. Ezk.24.18에 처음 언급되며 '에스겔의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 에스겔의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 에스겔의 아내는 갑자기 죽었고, 하나님은 그녀의 죽음을 이스라엘 백성에게 표징으로 사용하셨다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
persons.brief: Mother of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb
persons.short: An unnamed wife of Hezron who bore him Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
persons.article: The Bible mentions an unnamed wife of Hezron in 1Ch.2.9. She was the mother of Hezron's three sons: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb. No further information is provided about her in the biblical text. Her inclusion in the genealogy highlights the importance of family lineage and the role of women in bearing children to continue the family line.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness, implied at 1Ch.2.9; only referred to as a_wife_of_Hezron (.); wife of Hezron; an unnamed mother of: Jerahmeel and Caleb.
persons.summary_ko: 출애굽·광야시대 여성. 1Ch.2.9에 처음 언급되며 '헤스론의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 헤스론의 아내. 여라므엘과 갈렙의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 헤스론의 이름 없는 아내는 그에게 여라므엘, 람, 갈렙을 낳아주었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Wife of Jerahmeel; mother of Ram
persons.short: An unnamed wife of Jerahmeel who bore him Bunah, Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
persons.article: 1Ch.2.26 mentions an unnamed wife of Jerahmeel, who was a descendant of Judah. She was the mother of Jerahmeel's sons Bunah, Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. The Bible does not provide any additional details about her life or character. Her presence in the genealogy emphasizes the significance of family relationships and the role of women in producing heirs to carry on the family name.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, implied at 1Ch.2.26; only referred to as a wife of Jerahmeel; unnamed wife of Jerahmeel; mother of Bunah, Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.2.26에 처음 언급되며 '여라므엘의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 여라므엘의 아내. 브나, 람, 오렌, 오셈과 아히야의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 여라므엘의 이름 없는 아내는 그에게 부나, 람, 오렌, 오셈, 아히야를 낳아주었다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
persons.brief: A wife of Josiah; mother of Shallum
persons.short: One of King Josiah's wives was the mother of his son Shallum.
persons.article: A wife of Josiah In 1Ch.3.15, an unnamed wife of King Josiah is mentioned as the mother of his sons Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, who both became kings of Judah after Josiah's death. Josiah, one of Judah's most righteous kings, had multiple wives, as was common for kings at the time. This particular wife gave birth to two sons who played significant roles in the final years of the Kingdom of Judah before the Babylonian exile.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of Divided Monarchy, implied at 1Ch.3.15; only referred to as a_wife_of_Josiah (.); wife of Josiah; mother of:Shallum.
persons.summary_ko: 분열왕국시대 여성. 1Ch.3.15에 처음 언급되며 '요시야의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 요시야의 아내. 살룸의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 요시야 왕의 아내 중 한 사람은 그의 아들 살룸의 어머니였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Lot, daughter-in-law of Terah
persons.short: An unnamed wife of Lot, who was Terah's daughter-in-law.
persons.article: Gen.11.27 mentions an unnamed woman who was the wife of Lot, Abraham's nephew. She was the daughter-in-law of Terah, Abraham's father. The Bible does not provide any further details about her life or her relationship with Lot. Her inclusion in the genealogy of Terah's family establishes Lot's marital status and his connection to Abraham's family.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the Patriarchs, only mentioned at Gen.11.27 only referred to as a wife of Lot; unnamed wife of Lot; mother of: daughter1 of Lot, daughter2 of Lot.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.19.15에 처음 언급되며 '롯의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 롯의 아내. 롯의 딸(이름 미상)와 롯의 딸(이름 미상)의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 롯의 이름 없는 아내는 데라의 며느리였다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persons.brief: Wife of Peter, whose mother Jesus healed
persons.short: Peter's unnamed wife, whose mother Jesus healed of a fever.
persons.article: The New Testament mentions an unnamed woman who was the wife of the apostle Peter. In Mat.8.14, we learn that Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law, who was suffering from a fever. This incident took place in Peter's house in Capernaum. The fact that Peter was married is confirmed by this passage, although no further details are given about his wife or their relationship. Her presence in the Gospel narrative highlights Jesus' compassion and power to heal, as well as the humanity of His disciples, who had families and responsibilities outside of their ministry.
persons.summary: A woman living at the time of the New Testament, first mentioned at Mat.8.14 only referred to as a wife of Peter (.); unnamed wife of: Peter.
persons.note: 익명 인물 (베드로의 아내, 성경에 이름 없음)
persons.summary_ko: Mat.8.14에 처음 언급되며 '베드로의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 베드로의 장모(이름 미상)의 딸. 베드로의 아내.
persons.short_ko: 베드로의 이름 없는 아내는 그 어머니가 예수님께 열병을 고침받았다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
persons.brief: Wife of Simeon, the son of Jacob.
persons.short: An unnamed wife of Simeon, the son of Jacob, is mentioned in the genealogy of Simeon's descendants.
persons.article: A wife of Simeon, the son of Israel (or 'Jacob'), is mentioned in Gen.46.10 as part of the genealogy of Jacob's family. The passage lists the descendants of Jacob who came with him to Egypt during the time of Joseph. Simeon, one of Jacob's twelve sons, is mentioned along with his sons Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul. The text also notes that Shaul was the son of a Canaanite woman, implying that Simeon had married a Canaanite wife. No further details about Simeon's wife are provided in the biblical text, and she remains unnamed. The mention of Simeon's wife in the genealogy serves to provide a complete record of Jacob's family and their descendants, highlighting the growth of the Israelite people even before their settlement in Egypt.
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Simeon living at the time of the Patriarchs, implied at Gen.46.10; only referred to as a_wife_of_Simeon (.); wife of Simeon; presumed mother of: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin and Zerah.
persons.summary_ko: 족장시대 여성. Gen.46.10에 처음 언급되며 '시므온의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 시므온의 아내. 여무엘, 야민, 오핫, 야긴과 세라의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 야곱의 아들 시므온의 이름 없는 아내는 시므온 후손 족보에 언급된다.

persons.description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
persons.brief: Daughter of Abinadab, one of Solomon's wives.
persons.short: One of Solomon's wives was the daughter of Abinadab, who was placed in charge of the district of Dor.
persons.article: In 1Ki.4.11, one of Solomon's wives is mentioned as the daughter of Abinadab. She is not named but is identified by her relation to her father, who was one of Solomon's twelve district governors. Abinadab was in charge of the district of Dor, a region located in the western part of Israel, near the Mediterranean coast. As part of the administrative structure of Solomon's kingdom, each district was responsible for providing provisions for the king and his household for one month of the year (1Ki.4.7). The mention of Abinadab's daughter as Solomon's wife suggests that the king may have arranged marriages with the daughters of his officials to strengthen political ties and loyalty within his kingdom. No further details about this particular wife or her relationship with Solomon are provided in the biblical text. Solomon is known to have had many wives, including foreign women, which eventually led to his downfall and the weakening of his commitment to God (1Ki.11.1-8).
persons.summary: A woman from the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, implied at 1Ki.4.11; only referred to as a_wife_of_Solomon (.); wife of Solomon; mother of Taphath and Basemath.
persons.summary_ko: 통일왕국시대 여성. 1Ki.4.11에 처음 언급되며 '솔로몬의 아내(이름 미상)'라 불림. 솔로몬의 아내. 다밧과 바스맛의 어머니.
persons.short_ko: 솔로몬의 아내 중 한 사람은 돌 지역을 관리하던 아비나답의 딸이었다.
